questions.prompt: What do we learn about American workers from the passage?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） They are rarely in control of many things related to their work.
**题目译文**
从文章中我们对美国工人了解到什么?
A) 他们实际上为自己生产的商品和服务感到自豪。
B) 他们担心与外部世界隔绝。
C) 他们很少能掌控与工作相关的许多事情。
D) 他们渴望分享工作所创造的利润。
**定位** 工人们往往无法掌控自己如何工作、何时工作、他们生产的产品和服务被如何处置、以及他们劳动所创造的利润被如何使用。
**信号** 分点首句"First"后的解释句。本段以 First, work can be alienating. 起头点出第一个问题，紧接着的这句 Workers are often not in control of 就是对该问题的展开说明，是承载答案的句子。
**替换** Workers are often not in control of↔They are rarely in control of many things related to their work often not 改写为 rarely how they work, when they work, what is done with the goods and services they produce, and what is done with the profits↔ many things related to their work罗列细节概括为 many things
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱A 借用录音原词 the goods and services they produce 制造熟悉感，但录音说的是工人"无法掌控"产品去向，A 却说工人"为之自豪"，态度与原文相反。借用原文： what is done with the goods and services they produce
B) 原词陷阱B 盗用录音 work can be alienating 的 alienat- 词根，但录音的"异化"指工人与其劳动/产出相疏离，B 却说成"担心被外部世界孤立"，偷换了概念。借用原文： First, work can be alienating.
D) 原词陷阱D 借用录音原词 the profits made from their work，但录音说的是工人"无法掌控利润去向"，D 却说工人"渴望分享利润"，是录音根本没提的引申。借用原文： what is done with the profits made from their work
questions.quote: Workers are often not in control of how they work, when they work, what is done with the goods and services they produce, and what is done with the profits made from their work.

options.text: They are actually proud of the goods and services they produce.
They are worried about being alienated from the outside world.
They are rarely in control of many things related to their work.
They are longing to share the profits made from their work.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say long working hours contribute to?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） The feeling of being time poor.
**题目译文**
文章认为长时间工作导致了什么?
A) 生产率的持续下降。
B) 对身体健康的不良影响。
C) 时间贫乏的感觉。
D) 经济不平等的加剧。
**定位** 长时间工作会带来"时间贫乏"的感受，这种感受又会对心理健康产生不良影响。
**信号** 因果信号 contribute to。句中 Long working hours contribute to the feeling of "time poverty" 与题干同词出现，contribute to 这个因果信号直接锁定"长工时→时间贫乏"，是答案句。
**替换** the feeling of "time poverty"↔ The feeling of being time poor. time poverty 与 time poor 同根改写
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反A 借录音里出现过的 productivity increases 中的 productivity，但录音说的是"尽管生产率提高"（上升），A 却说"生产率持续下降"，与原文方向相反。借用原文： full time employees work an average of 8.72 hours per day despite productivity increases
B) 偷换概念B 几乎照搬录音 has an adverse effect on psychological well-being 的 adverse effect，却把 psychological（心理）换成 physical（身体）健康，偷改了范围。借用原文： which has an adverse effect on psychological well-being
D) 张冠李戴D 的 economic inequality 出自第3段 driving economic inequality，那是"工资跟不上生产率"的后果，并非长工时的后果，被错搬到本题。借用原文： Real wages have not kept pace with productivity, driving economic inequality
questions.quote: Long working hours contribute to the feeling of "time poverty", which has an adverse effect on psychological well-being.

options.text: The steady decrease in productivity.
The adverse effect on physical health.
The feeling of being time poor.
The rising economic inequality.

questions.prompt: What does automation do, according to the passage?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） It puts jobs and wages at risk.
**题目译文**
根据文章,自动化产生了什么作用?
A) 它改变了工作的结构。
B) 它使工作和工资面临风险。
C) 它将人们从繁琐和费力的工作中解放出来。
D) 它在信息技术行业创造了新的工作机会。
**定位** 第四，自动化使工作岗位和工资面临风险。
**信号** 分点首句直接定调。本段分点句 Fourth, automation puts jobs and wages at risk. 开门见山给 automation 定调，是直接承载答案的主题句。
**替换** automation puts jobs and wages at risk↔ It puts jobs and wages at risk.近乎原句对接
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 张冠李戴A 的 alter the structure of work 借用录音 unless changes are made to the structure of work，但那是"除非改变工作结构"的假设条件，并非 automation 本身所做的事。借用原文： unless changes are made to the structure of work
C) 原词陷阱C 借录音 liberate people from the 40-hour work week 的 liberate，但原文是Technological innovation could in theory liberate——只是"理论上可能"，并被随后的But 推翻，并非自动化实际的作为。借用原文： Technological innovation could in theory liberate people from the 40-hour work week. But unless changes are made
D) 未提及录音只说 automation 会 further diminish work opportunities（进一步减少工作机会），从未说它在IT业创造新岗位，D 属无中生有。
questions.quote: Fourth, automation puts jobs and wages at risk.

options.text: It alters the structure of work.
It puts jobs and wages at risk.
It liberates people from tedious and laborious work.
It creates new work opportunities in the IT industry.

questions.prompt: What do post-work theorists advocate?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （态度观点题） Prioritizing life over work.
**题目译文**
后工作理论家倡导什么?
A) 在工作中寻找意义。
B) 将生活置于工作之上。
C) 改善社区中的关系。
D) 在工作场所实现个人的社会价值。
**定位** 后工作理论家认为，工作不应在我们的生活中占据中心位置，也不应占用我们这么多时间。……因此，生活本身应被视为目的。
**信号** 表态动词 believe 与结论 Thus。The post-work theorists believe that work should not hold a central position in our lives 中的 believe 直接引出主张，段末 Thus, life should be seen as an end in itself. 以 Thus 收束出结论，两处合起来锁定立场。
**替换** work should not hold a central position in our lives or take up so much of our time↔Prioritizing life over work.工作不居中心等于生活优先life should be seen as an end in itself↔Prioritizing life over work.生活本身是目的印证生活优先
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反A 借录音 meaning, purpose and social value reside in the communities and relationships built and sustained outside of the workplace 里的 meaning，但原文明说意义在职场"之外"，A 却说"在工作中找意义"，正话反说。借用原文： meaning, purpose and social value reside in the communities and relationships built and sustained outside of the workplace
C) 原词陷阱C 借录音 the communities and relationships 里的 communities/relationships，但原文是说意义"寓于"社区与关系之中，并非主张"去改善社区关系"，把举例性说明当成了主张。借用原文： meaning, purpose and social value reside in the communities and relationships
D) 与原文相反D 借录音 social value 一词，但原文说社会价值在职场"之外"的社区与关系里实现，D 却说"在职场中实现社会价值"，与原文相反。借用原文： social value reside in the communities and relationships built and sustained outside of the workplace
questions.quote: The post-work theorists believe that work should not hold a central position in our lives or take up so much of our time. ... Thus, life should be seen as an end in itself.

options.text: Finding meaning in work.
Prioritizing life over work.
Improving relationships in the community.
Realizing one's social value in the workplace.

transcript.text: My current research is mainly looking at factors like stress and how it affects our immune system.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They get infections.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Often these infections lead to death.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: So we're trying to slow down that progression to feebleness.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: But this isn't just a problem in Birmingham or even in the UK.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: This is a problem globally.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: People are aging.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: There's a lot more people in the older generation who are living for longer but not necessarily staying healthy for a large part of their lives.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcriptTranslations: 我目前的研究主要关注压力等因素以及它如何影响我们的免疫系统。所以我目前非常感兴趣的项目是关注老年人以及对他们来说重要的因素。
在一个项目中，我们正在研究老年人的髋部骨折，这是一个常见事件，我们试图理解抑郁症的影响。通常髋部骨折住院的人会出现抑郁症，而这些人随后会比其他人更快地变得虚弱。他们会感染疾病。这些感染往往会导致死亡。所以我们试图减缓这种向虚弱发展的进程。因此，如果我们能更好地理解这些因素如何相互作用，那么我们实际上就可以开始采取行动。
我的研究在伯明翰产生的影响，首先显然是针对老年人，因为这些人正在经历髋部骨折并出现抑郁症，我们试图改善他们的健康和生活质量。但这不仅仅是伯明翰甚至英国的问题。这是一个全球性问题。人们正在老龄化。老年群体中有更多的人活得更长，但不一定在他们生命的大部分时间里保持健康。所以他们生命的最后阶段往往充满了疾病，我们试图理解能够影响晚年生活质量的因素。

我认为我的研究最让我兴奋的是它感觉真实且相关。许多学者可能对他们的研究非常兴奋，但它可能与他们周围的人不那么相关。而我觉得我所做的工作与每个人都相关，因为每个人都在衰老。健康是每个人的问题，无论他们的年龄如何,而我试图做的是理解影响健康的因素以及我们如何改善人们的生活质量。所以这是真正让我兴奋的事情之一。另一件事是，我们不是只从一个角度出发，不是仅仅从心理学家的角度来看待衰老和健康，我们现在正在汇集许多不同的技术和许多不同的观点，来实际研究影响健康的各种不同因素。
美国人痴迷于名厨。我们谈论他们，并试图像他们一样饮食。但我们能否从他们那里学到比食谱和技巧更多的东西？
根据市场数据企业的统计,美国人每年在自助和个人组织产品上花费近100亿美元。这个市场巨大,部分原因是大多数大学和研究生院不教授基本的组织方法,但烹饪学校和专业厨房会教。
也许烹饪组织的原则可以延伸到帮助我们这些不是顶级厨师的人。使厨房运转的系统被称为mise-en- place,或字面意思是各就各位。这是一个法语短语,意思是收集和安排烹饪所需的食材和工具。

但对许多专业厨师来说,这个短语意味着更深层的东西。一些厨师称之为他们的信仰。它帮助他们协调大量的劳动和材料,并通过专注和自律改变从业者的生活。美国烹饪学院的学生将其视为一种生活方式。这是一种集中精神的方式,只专注于他们此刻需要处理的方面,摆脱干扰。这是一些学生即使不在厨房时也会保持的习惯。他们mise-en-place他们的生活。他们为上课准备好书籍。他们准备好厨师服。他们擦亮鞋子。他们知道一天中每一步需要的一切。

那么如何达到这种组织水平？高水平组织的关键是心态。厨师可以轻松地为三小时的晚餐班次做六小时的准备。美国烹饪学院的讲师Dwayne Lipuma解释说,mise-en-place迫使厨师对他们的每一分钟时间和每一个动作负责。一道菜的每个组成部分都在一个角落,所以他们的手实际上只移动几英寸。一旦学生设置好他们的工作台,我应该能够蒙住他们的眼睛。他们应该知道他们的刀具总是在这里,他们的油总是在这里,他们的盐和胡椒总是在这里。
但在最高层次上实践时,mise-en-place表明时间是宝贵的,资源是宝贵的,空间是宝贵的,你的自尊和他人的尊重是宝贵的。明智地使用它们。这难道不是我们这个时代的哲学吗？
为什么我们停止为自己制定目标并停止在生活中进步?原因之一是我们相信应该接受自己本来的样子,而不是不断努力提升自己。我们在这方面犯的错误是,虽然自我接纳至关重要,但实际上应该将其作为成长的基础。当我们不成长、不学习、不在生活中寻求改进时,我们往往会停滞不前,接受现状,并停止相信自己可以变得更好。
创建目标和取得进步的一个关键工具是运用我们的想象力。然而,正如常见的情况一样,到我们步入中年时,我们已经停止梦想自己想要实现什么,并对目标设定感到相当消极。我们不再从实现目标中感受到信心、快乐和满足,而是觉得自己总是达不到目标。这导致失望,我们停止梦想。我们停止想象自己想要拥有的生活或想要成为的人,很快就发现自己被现实的痛苦击垮。
到目前为止,除非我们在创意行业工作,否则我们会觉得使用"玩耍"这个概念有点幼稚。在西方,我们大多是用头脑、用理性思维来运作。但人们开始更好地理解这一点,因为使用我们的想象力实际上是我们能做的最强大的事情之一。

发现自己因未能实现目标而恼怒的问题在于,目标总是在变化,无论我们是否意识到,我们总是在适应。因此,结果是我们最终感觉自己永远无法达到目标。这正是导致失败、不满和不快乐的最大误解和原因之一。我们用目标来衡量,而不是用我们的起点来衡量。Dan Sullivan把这称为"差距与收获"。我们总是用目标来衡量,感觉自己永远达不到,而不是用收获来衡量,也就是我们的起点。通过衡量我们从哪里来,而不是我们要去哪里,我们看到了结果。我们看到了那些被我们视为理所当然或未曾注意到的事情。这是一个简单却深刻的认知转变,我喜欢它的地方在于它能立即让我们提升一个档次。它非常非常简单,却对我们的思维产生了立竿见影的积极影响。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say is quite common among older people?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） Hip fracture.
**题目译文**
说话者说在老年人中什么是相当常见的?
A) 慢性抑郁症。
B) 日益虚弱。
C) 髋部骨折。
D) 致命性感染。
**定位** 在一个项目里，我们研究老年人的髋部骨折，这是一种常见的情况，我们想弄清抑郁对它的影响。
**信号** which is a common event 直接点"常见"。答案句里 which is a common event（这是一种常见的情况）紧跟在 hip fracture in older people 之后，which 指代的正是 hip fracture，这个"常见"信号词把答案锁死在髋部骨折上。
**替换** hip fracture in older people, which is a common event↔Hip fracture.原词直接对应＋common 坐实
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱录音确实念到 depression，A 的 Chronic depression. 借此勾人，但原文说的是"骨折后常发展出抑郁"，抑郁是骨折带来的结果，且并未被 common 修饰，也没说是"chronic（慢性）"，答非所问。借用原文： these are the people that then go on to become feeble a lot more quickly
B) 原词陷阱录音说 become feeble a lot more quickly，B 的 Growing feebleness. 取了这个feeble，但原文讲的是骨折＋抑郁导致"更快变虚弱"这一恶化进程，并非在说"老年人中常见的是虚弱"，对不上题干的"常见"。借用原文： become feeble a lot more quickly than others
D) 原词陷阱录音说 They get infections. Often these infections lead to death.，D 的 Fatal infections. 拼合了 infections 和"致命"，但原文 often 修饰的是"感染导致死亡"这一后续后果，处于"骨折→抑郁→虚弱→感染→死亡"链条末端，不是题干问的"常见之事"本身。借用原文： Often these infections lead to death.
questions.quote: In one project we are looking at hip fracture in older people, which is a common event and we're trying to understand the impact of depression.

options.text: Chronic depression.
Growing feebleness.
Hip fracture.
Fatal infections.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker think excites her most about her research?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （态度观点题） It feels real and relevant.
**题目译文**
说话者认为她的研究最令她兴奋的是什么?
A) 它让人感觉真实且切题。
B) 它对心理学有贡献。
C) 它胜过许多学者的研究。
D) 它在Birmingham之外赢得认可。
**定位** 我认为我的研究最让我兴奋的地方，在于它让人感到真实而切身相关。
**信号** excites me most 直接领出答案。答案句 the thing that excites me most about my research is that it feels real and relevant 里 excites me most 与题干 excites her most是同一表态信号，is that 后面那句就是她给出的理由，定位精准。
**替换** it feels real and relevant↔It feels real and relevant.几乎原句搬入选项
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱录音确有 from the perspective of the psychologist，B 的 It contributes to psychology. 借 psychology 勾人，但原文是说"不再只从心理学家的单一视角看"，恰恰在强调超越心理学，而非"为心理学做贡献"，意思反向。借用原文： rather than looking at aging and health just from the perspective of the psychologist
C) 过度推断录音说 Lots of academics are probably very excited about their research, but it might not be that relevant，C 的 It outcompetes lots of academics' research. 借 academics勾人，但原文只是用别的学者作对比来突出"自己的研究更切身相关"，从未说"胜过／outcompete"别人，属过度拔高。借用原文： Lots of academics are probably very excited about their research, but it might not be that relevant to those around them
D) 原词陷阱Birmingham 是录音里反复出现的地名（见 The impact that my research will have in Birmingham），D 的 It wins recognition outside of Birmingham. 借它勾人，但录音从没说研究"在伯明翰之外赢得认可"，只说这是"全球性问题"，把"问题是全球的"偷换成"研究在外地获认可"。借用原文： But this isn't just a problem in Birmingham or even in the UK. This is a problem globally.
questions.quote: I think the thing that excites me most about my research is that it feels real and relevant.

It contributes to psychology.

questions.prompt: How does the speaker approach her research project?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） By combining multiple perspectives.
**题目译文**
说话者如何开展她的研究项目?
A) 通过把年长和年轻的专家聚集在一起。
B) 通过依靠先进的现代技术。
C) 通过充分利用她的专业知识。
D) 通过结合多种视角。
**定位** 与其只采取单一视角，与其只从心理学家的角度看待衰老与健康，我们现在汇集了许多不同的技术和许多不同的观点，来真正审视影响健康的各种因素。
**信号** rather than… we are now bringing together 对比转折。答案句用 rather than just taking one perspective 先否定"单一视角"，再以 we are now bringing together a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints 给出真正做法，"不是A而是B"的对比让 B 半句成为答案落点。
**替换** a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints ↔By combining multiple perspectives. different viewpoints＝multiple perspectives 同义改写bringing together ↔ combining bring together＝combine 同义动词
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱录音确有 bringing together，A 的 By bringing together experts old and young. 借此勾人，但原文汇集的是 different techniques and viewpoints（技术与观点），不是"老少专家"，old and young 是套用别处的 older／young 之类印象，张冠李戴。借用原文： we are now bringing together a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints
B) 过度推断录音说 a lot of different techniques（多种不同的技术手段），B 的 By counting on advanced modern technology. 借 techniques 勾人，但原文只说"多种技术手段"，从没说"依赖先进的现代科技"，advanced modern 是凭空添加的拔高。借用原文： bringing together a lot of different techniques
C) 与原文相反By making full use of her expertise. 即"充分用她自己（心理学家）的专长"，这正是录音用 rather than… just from the perspective of the psychologist 明确否定的单一视角做法，选项取了被否定的那一半，与原文意思相反。借用原文： rather than looking at aging and health just from the perspective of the psychologist
questions.quote: rather than just taking one perspective, so rather than looking at aging and health just from the perspective of the psychologist, we are now bringing together a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints to actually look at the sort of different factors affecting health.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about most colleges and graduate schools in America?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） They don't teach basic organization.
**题目译文**
说话者对美国大多数学院和研究生院有何看法?
A) 它们不教授基本的组织方法。

**信号** 原因状语 because 引出的因果句。答案句由 partly because most colleges and graduate schools don't teach basic organization 这个 because 因果结构托出，讲者在解释“市场为何巨大”时正面说出了学校“不教什么”，这种交代原因的从句往往就是细节答案所在。

questions.tip:

B) 原词陷阱选项 They don't focus on teaching techniques. 借了录音开头 recipes and techniques里的 techniques 制造熟耳感，但讲者从没说学校“不重视教技巧”，学校被说成不教的是organization，不是 techniques，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。借用原文： recipes and techniques
C) 原词陷阱选项 They attach little importance to recipes. 取了开头 recipes and techniques 的recipes，但录音并未说学校“不重视食谱”，更没把 recipes 和大学挂钩，是借原词编出的无中生有。借用原文： recipes and techniques
D) 未提及选项 They hire very few distinguished chefs. 用了贯穿全篇的 chefs 蹭话题，但录音通篇没提“学校聘用名厨多少”，hire very few distinguished chefs 完全是没听到的内容。借用原文： celebrity chefs
questions.quote: The market is huge, partly because most colleges and graduate schools don't teach basic organization, but cooking schools and professional kitchens do.

options.text: They don't teach basic organization.
They don't focus on teaching techniques.
They attach little importance to recipes.
They hire very few distinguished chefs.

questions.prompt: How do students of the culinary institute of America view "mise-en-place" or "put in place"?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （态度观点题） It's a way of life to them.
**题目译文**
美国烹饪学院的学生如何看待"mise-en-place"或"就位"?
A) 这是名厨独有的。
B) 这是一种转变方式。
C) 这对他们要求过高。
D) 对他们来说这是一种生活方式。
**定位** 美国烹饪学院的学生把它视为一种生活方式。
**信号** 被点名群体后紧跟的“view it as…”态度句。讲者点出 Students at the culinary institute of America 这一群体后，紧接 view it as a way of life 直接给出他们的看法，这种“某群人+ view/see it as……”的句子就是态度题的标准答案落点。
**替换** view it as a way of life↔It's a way of life to them. view it as A 改写成 It's A to them
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 偷换概念选项 It's unique to celebrity chefs. 借了开头 celebrity chefs 的熟词，但录音说把它当生活方式的是学生，不是名厨独有；unique（独有）这个范围限定录音根本没说，属偷换概念加原词诱选。借用原文： celebrity chefs
B) 答非所问选项 It's a way of transformation. 取自录音 transforms the lives of its practitioners 的transform，听起来很耳熟，但那句是讲者总述 mise-en-place 的功效，不是“学生怎么看它”的答案；题问的是学生的 view，答案句明确是 a way of life。借用原文： transforms the lives of its practitioners
C) 过度推断选项 It's too demanding for them. 利用 focus and self-discipline 让人联想“很苛刻”，但录音从未说学生觉得它“太苛刻”，反而把它当生活方式正面接纳，too demanding 是凭印象的过度推断。借用原文： focus and self-discipline
questions.quote: Students at the culinary institute of America view it as a way of life.

options.text: It's unique to celebrity chefs.
It's a way of transformation.
It's too demanding for them.
It's a way of life to them.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker advise us to do at the end of the talk?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） Use time and resources in a wise way.
**题目译文**
说话者在讲话结尾建议我们做什么?
A) 尊重他人以获得尊重。
B) 明智地使用时间和资源。
C) 培养自律的习惯。
D) 认真向哲学家学习。
**定位** 但在最高层次上去实践，mise-en-place 告诉我们：时间是宝贵的，资源是宝贵的，空间是宝贵的，你的自尊和对他人的尊重都是宝贵的。要明智地使用它们。
**信号** 结尾的祈使劝告句“Use them wisely”。整段在罗列 time is precious, resources are precious 之后，以祈使句 Use them wisely. 收束，这句独立成句的劝告正是讲者在结尾给出的建议，是答案的落点。
**替换** time is precious, resources are precious↔ Use time and resources in a wise way.把要珍惜的对象同义搬进祈使句Use them wisely. ↔ in a wise way wisely 改写成 in a wise way
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱选项 Respect others so as to be respected. 借了 your self-respect and the respect of others are precious 里的 respect，但录音只把“尊重”列为“宝贵之物”之一，最后的劝告是Use them wisely（明智使用），并非“尊重别人以换取被尊重”，且 so as to be respected是录音没有的因果，属原词陷阱加过度推断。借用原文： your self-respect and the respect of others are precious
C) 原词陷阱选项 Cultivate a habit of self-discipline. 取自第四段 focus and self-discipline 的 self- discipline，这是前文描述 mise-en-place 作用时的词，不是结尾劝告；题问 at the end，结尾讲者劝的是明智使用时间资源，不是培养自律。借用原文： focus and self-discipline
D) 偷换概念选项 Learn from philosophers earnestly. 利用结尾 Isn't that a philosophy for our time? 的 philosophy 设套，但那只是反问“这难道不是我们时代的一种哲理吗”，并非叫人“认真向哲学家学习”，philosophers 与 learn from 都是录音没有的捏造。借用原文： Isn't that a philosophy for our time?
questions.quote: But practiced at its highest level, mise-en-place says that time is precious, resources are precious, space is precious, your self-respect and the respect of others are precious. Use them wisely.

options.text: Respect others so as to be respected.
Use time and resources in a wise way.
Cultivate a habit of self-discipline.
Learn from philosophers earnestly.

groups.instructions:
In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks followed by three or four questions. The recordings will be played only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A), B), C) and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet I with a single line through the centre.
Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.prompt: What should self-acceptance be used as according to the speaker?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） The basis for self-improvement.
**题目译文**
根据讲话者的观点,自我接纳应该被用作什么?
A) 努力工作的动机。
B) 停滞不前的理由。
C) 自我提升的基础。
D) 自信的正当理由。
**定位** 我们在这件事上犯的错误是：尽管自我接纳至关重要，但它其实应当被用作成长的基础。
**信号** 转折 whilst + 定性结构 used as。答案句先用让步 whilst self-acceptance is imperative（尽管自我接纳重要）退一步，再用 it should actually be used as the basis for growth给出真正主张，actually 加重了转折后的落点，正是这句对 self-acceptance 做了定性。
**替换** used as the basis for growth↔ The basis for self-improvement. growth = self-improvement 同义替换
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及The motive for hard work. 把 self-acceptance 说成『努力工作的动机』，原文只讲它是成长的基础，从未提 hard work，也未提 motive，属无中生有。
B) 原词陷阱The reason for stagnation. 借用了原文 we tend to stagnate 的同根词 stagnation 制造耳熟，但原文说『不成长才会停滞』，stagnation 是不接纳成长的后果，绝非 self- acceptance 被用作的角色，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。借用原文： we tend to stagnate
D) 偷换概念The justification for self-confidence. 利用 self- 前缀与 C 的 self-improvement 混淆，但原文落点是 growth/improvement，不是 self-confidence，且 justification（理由）也非原文的 basis，属偷换概念。借用原文： the basis for growth
questions.quote: The mistake we make with this is that whilst self-acceptance is imperative, it should actually be used as the basis for growth.

options.text: The motive for hard work.
The reason for stagnation.
The basis for self-improvement.
The justification for self-confidence.

questions.prompt: What do people tend to do when they have reached midlife?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） Stop imagining further progress in life.
**题目译文**
当人们步入中年时,他们往往会做什么?
A) 感到自信、幸福和满足。
B) 相信他们已经实现了人生目标。
C) 使用一个关键工具来设定雄心勃勃的目标。
D) 停止想象人生中的进一步进步。
**定位** 然而正如常见的那样，到我们步入中年时，我们已经不再梦想自己想要实现什么，并对设定目标抱有相当负面的感受。……我们不再去想象自己想过的生活或想成为的人。
**信号** 转折 Yet + midlife 时间锚 + 重复 stop。Yet as is so often the case, by the time we've reached midlife 用 Yet 转折并点出时间锚 midlife，随后 we've stopped dreaming 与We stop imagining the life we'd like to have 两次出现 stop，反复强调的负向行为正是答案落点。
**替换** We stop imagining the life we'd like to have or the person we'd like to be↔Stop imagining further progress in life. stop imagining 原词 + 概括化we've stopped dreaming about what we want to achieve↔Stop imagining further progress in life. stop dreaming = stop imagining progress
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反Feel confidence, happiness and satisfaction. 三个词全部来自原文 Instead of feeling confidence, happiness and satisfaction from achieving our goals，但原文前面是Instead of（而不是），意思恰恰是人们没有这些感受，选项却取了被否定的内容，是典型听到原词就选的陷阱。借用原文： Instead of feeling confidence, happiness and satisfaction from achieving our goals
B) 与原文相反Believe they have achieved their life goals. 说人们相信已达成人生目标，而原文说中年时人们 feel we are always falling short（总觉得没达到），方向完全相反，属无中生有又反向。借用原文： we feel we are always falling short
C) 张冠李戴Use a key tool for setting ambitious goals. 里 a key tool 来自第 2 段开头 A key tool for creating goals and progressing, is using our imagination，但那是作者讲『工具是什么』，并非说中年人会去用它；原文恰恰说中年时人们停止了想象，选项张冠李戴。借用原文： A key tool for creating goals and progressing, is using our imagination
questions.quote: Yet as is so often the case, by the time we've reached midlife, we've stopped dreaming about what we want to achieve and feel quite negatively about goal setting. ... We stop imagining the life we'd like to have or the person we'd like to be.

options.text: Feel confidence, happiness and satisfaction.
Believe they have achieved their life goals.
Use a key tool for setting ambitious goals.
Stop imagining further progress in life.

questions.prompt: Why do we find ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） We have to adapt to the ever-changing goal.
**题目译文**
为什么我们会因未能达成目标而感到恼怒?
A) 我们觉得自己总是落后于他人。
B) 我们必须适应不断变化的目标。
C) 关于目标设定存在各种误解。
D) 最初设定的目标总是存在问题。
**定位** 我们因没达成目标而恼火，问题在于：目标总在变化，而无论我们是否意识到，我们也总在不断适应。
**信号** 因果结构 The problem with … is because。The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal is because the goal always changes 用 The problem … is because 直接给出原因，because 后的 the goal always changes and we're always adapting 就是答案句核心。
**替换** the goal always changes and we're always adapting↔We have to adapt to the ever-changing goal. always changes + always adapting → ever-changing + adapt
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 偷换概念We feel we are always falling behind others. 借了原文反复出现的 always 与 falling 的语感（如 we feel we are always falling short），但加了 others（落后于他人）。原文讲的是和自己的目标比、和来路比，从未说和别人比，others 是凭空添加。借用原文： we feel we are always falling short
C) 原词陷阱There are various misconceptions about goal setting. 搬用了原文 herein lies one of the biggest misconceptions 的 misconceptions，听着耳熟，但题目问的是『恼火的原因』，原因是 the goal always changes，而非泛泛地说『存在各种误解』，属听到原词就选的陷阱。借用原文： herein lies one of the biggest misconceptions
D) 偷换概念There are always problems with the goal originally set. 借了原文 The problem with…的 problem 一词，但原文说的是『恼火这件事的问题在于目标在变』，不是说『当初设的目标本身有毛病』，把问题归错了对象。借用原文： The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal
questions.quote: The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal is because the goal always changes and we're always adapting, whether we realize it or not.

options.text: We feel we are always falling behind others.
We have to adapt to the ever-changing goal.
There are various misconceptions about goal setting.
There are always problems with the goal originally set.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say has an immediate positive impact on our thinking?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） Measuring where we've come from instead of measuring against the goal.
**题目译文**
讲话者说什么对我们的思维有立即的积极影响?
A) 要实现的目标数量发生明显变化。
B) 总是根据差距而非收获来衡量。
C) 衡量我们从哪里来而不是根据目标来衡量。
D) 对我们在努力实现目标时未能注意到的事物有恰当的理解。
**定位** 我们对着目标来衡量，而不是衡量自己走过了多远。……当我们衡量自己走过了多远、而非衡量离要去的地方还差多少时，我们就看到了成果。……这是一种简单却深刻的认知转变……却对我们的思维有着即时而正面的影响。
**信号** 正面评价 profound/positive impact 指向 measuring where we've come from。has an immediate, positive impact on our thinking 这句的『它』回指前文反复强调的 In measuring where we've come from, rather than where we're trying to get to，作者用profound、positive impact 正面定性的正是这种衡量来路的做法。
**替换** measuring where we've come from, rather than where we're trying to get to ↔Measuring where we've come from instead of measuring against the goal. rather than = instead of，goal = where we're trying to get to
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及A noticeable change in the number of goals to achieve. 说『要达成的目标数量发生明显变化』，原文谈的是衡量基准的转变（量来路 vs 量目标），从未提目标的数量变化，属未提及。
B) 与原文相反Measuring always against the gap rather than the gain. 搬用了原文术语 We measure always against the goal 与 gap/gain，但作者批评的恰恰是『总对着 gap/goal 量』、推崇的是量 gain（来路）。选项说『量 gap 而非 gain』正好取了被否定的一面，与原文相反。借用原文： We measure always against the goal
D) 偷换概念A proper conception of what we fail to notice in trying to achieve our goals. 借了原文 things we've taken for granted, or not noticed 的 not noticed，拼成『对我们没注意到之物的正确认知』，但原文说有即时正面影响的是『衡量来路这一做法』本身，不是某种conception，属偷换概念/过度拼凑。借用原文： things we've taken for granted, or not noticed
questions.quote: We measure against the goal, rather than where we've come from. ... In measuring where we've come from, rather than where we're trying to get to, we see results. ... It's a simple, yet profound change in perception ... yet has an immediate, positive impact on our thinking.

options.text: A noticeable change in the number of goals to achieve.
Measuring always against the gap rather than the gain.
Measuring where we've come from instead of measuring against the goal.
A proper conception of what we fail to notice in trying to achieve our goals.

确实,这点值得注意。谢谢。另外,Rachel的面试表现很好。我觉得她给人的印象是聪明又机敏。
是的。她问了一些关于这个职位和公司的很好的问题,这让我觉得她对这份工作非常感兴趣。
我也这么想。现在,我们来看看Peter的面试表现。我觉得他也表现得很好。他给人的印象是有礼貌、很专业,你说呢?沉着冷静。就他这个年龄来说非常成熟。
没错。在我的笔记里,我写道他看起来很镇定,能控制好自己的情绪。我觉得他看起来肯定比Rachel更成熟。
有意思。所以,我们都认为Rachel显得缺乏经验,不如Peter成熟,尽管两位候选人年龄相同,而且几乎都没有工作经验。
如果把他们放在一起比较的话,是的,Peter看起来更自信一些。也许是他们肢体语言方面的某些差异吧。
当然。也许他只是不那么紧张而已。
也许吧。谁知道呢?说实话,我觉得我更喜欢Rachel。
嗯。真的吗?我觉得我更喜欢Peter。
啊,好吧。如果打成平手,我们无法达成一致,那我们就把这个问题交给John,让他来投决定性的一票。
我们今天请到了私人时装品牌 L'Orange 的首席设计师 Clementine Ortega，来聊聊她的最新系列。Ortega 女士，您会如何描述这一季的风格？
说实话，我偏爱的风格一直都是比较模糊的那种，我觉得这个系列更是如此。我尽量不去遵循社会规范和期望。相反，我总是试图在我的美学中融入一些略带荒诞的东西。
这个系列中各种配饰的组合对评论家产生了相当大的影响。比如在秀场最后展示的那件炫目的披风，就让观众席上的许多人感到困惑。这件作品的灵感来源是什么？
夏天的时候，我去亚洲各地的乡村山区旅行，寻找手工艺品来装饰我的新工作室。有个村子里的女人们做的刺绣实在太精美了。我一直忘不了。试图重现她们的设计是徒劳的。所以我采用了自己古怪的方法。我用闪粉在天鹅绒披风上画出类似的复杂图案。最后就有了为秀场收尾的那个华丽夺目的造型。
确实很有气势，然而，我能说吗，同时又带着一种男性气质。
嗯，是的，这是有意为之。我喜欢融合那些通常处于时尚光谱两端的风格。因此，闪亮的披风搭配了你通常会在商务场合看到的传统职业套装。恕我直言，效果非常轰动。
确实壮观！整场秀都令人惊艳。打破刻板印象、融入本土元素，再加上您标志性的底层触感，让这个系列成为本季的宣言。您证明了自己是一位了不起的年轻设计师，我们迫不及待想看到您接下来会创作出什么作品。

questions.prompt: Why does the man think it is difficult to make the decision?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） Both candidates are quite competitive.
**题目译文**
为什么男士认为很难做出决定?
A) 他们必须在今天结束前做出选择。
B) 两位候选人都非常渴望得到这份工作。
C) 他们对程序持有不同看法。
D) 两位候选人都很有竞争力。
**定位** 男：是啊，但这不是个容易做的选择。两位申请者都相当强。
**信号** 男士应答里的转折 + 给因。这是男士对女士「今天得定」的直接应答，but it isn't an easy choice to make 用 but 转出「不好选」，紧接 Both applicants are quite strong 给出原因——两人都很强，正是「难选」的答案句。
**替换** Both applicants are quite strong↔Both candidates are quite competitive近义改写 strong→competitive、applicants→candidates
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱A 取自女士开场 we need to decide by the end of the day 的「by the end of the day」，但那是「期限」而非「难以抉择的原因」；问的是 Why difficult，时间紧不是男士给出的理由，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。借用原文： we need to decide by the end of the day
B) 张冠李戴「很想要这份工作」对应录音后面 she is very keen about the job，那是评价 Rachel的，且只针对一人；本题问男士为何觉得难选，他给的因是「两人都强」，不是「都很想要」，B 张冠李戴又答非所问。借用原文： she is very keen about the job
C) 未提及录音里两人对「流程」并无分歧，finalize this whole procedure 只是说要走完流程，并没有说「对 procedure 持不同看法」；C 借 procedure 一词虚构了一个原文没有的分歧。借用原文： finalize this whole procedure
questions.quote: M: Yes, but it isn't an easy choice to make. Both applicants are quite strong.

options.text: They have to make a choice by the end of the day.
Both candidates are very keen on getting the job.
They hold different views on the procedure.
Both candidates are quite competitive.

questions.prompt: What do the speakers say may be worth noting?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） Rachel scored moderately higher grades than Peter at school.
**题目译文**
说话者认为什么可能值得注意?
A) Rachel和Peter都表现得既尊重他人又很专业。
B) Rachel在学校的成绩略高于Peter。
C) Rachel和Peter在学业追求上都很出色。
D) Peter在体格上似乎略强于Rachel。
**定位** 男：唯一也许值得一提的差别，是看起来 Rachel 在整个高中和大学的成绩略好一些。但正如我说的，只比 Peter 高出一点点。
**信号** 明示标记 difference worth noting。男士直接说 The only difference worth noting，与题干 worth noting 字面对应，是教科书式的答案信号；其后 Rachel scored moderately stronger grades 加上 only a tiny bit higher than Peter 就是要抓的内容。
**替换** Rachel scored moderately stronger grades throughout high school and university↔Rachel scored moderately higher grades than Peter at school stronger grades=higher grades，程度词原样保留only a tiny bit higher than Peter↔moderately higher grades than Peter a tiny bit higher印证「略高」
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱A 的 respectful and professional 直接取自女士评 Peter 的 He came across as respectful and professional，是真听到的原词；但那是夸 Peter 一人的面试表现，并非两人都如此，且不是被点为「worth noting」的那点，属原词陷阱。借用原文： He came across as respectful and professional
C) 与原文相反录音强调 only a tiny bit higher，仅是「略高」；C 的 excelled（出类拔萃）且说「两人都」学业杰出，把程度从「略」拔高到「极」、把范围从「Rachel 略胜」改成「两人皆优」，与原文程度相反。借用原文： only a tiny bit higher than Peter
D) 未提及录音通篇比的是成绩、面试表现、成熟度，从未提到 physically（体格）；D 把 stronger偷换成「身体上更强」，是录音根本没说的维度。
questions.quote: M: The only difference worth noting, perhaps, is that it looks like Rachel scored moderately stronger grades throughout high school and university. But as I said, only a tiny bit higher than Peter.

options.text: Both Rachel and Peter came across as respectful and professional.
Rachel scored moderately higher grades than Peter at school.
Both Rachel and Peter excelled in their academic pursuit.
Peter appeared slightly stronger than Rachel physically.

questions.prompt: According to the man, what might account for Peter appearing somewhat more self- assured than Rachel?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） His use of body language.
**题目译文**
根据男士的说法,什么可能是Peter看起来比Rachel更自信的原因?
A) 他对肢体语言的使用。
B) 他积累的经验。
C) 他不寻常的精神状态。
D) 他对公司的了解。
**定位** 男：把他们并排比较时，是的，Peter 不知怎的显得更自信。也许跟他们的肢体语言有关。
**信号** 男士的归因句 Maybe it was…。这是男士亲口给出的归因——Peter seemed more self- assured somehow 之后紧跟 Maybe it was something about their body language，用Maybe it was… 引出原因，正是 account for 所问的答案句。
**替换** Maybe it was something about their body language↔His use of body language body language原词同指其运用
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱B 的 experience 来自录音 practically no work experience，但原文说的是「两人几乎都没有工作经验」，恰恰不是经验造成差异；B 把「没有经验」偷成「经验的积累」，听到experience 就选即落坑。借用原文： practically no work experience
C) 偷换概念录音说 Peter 显得 composed and in control of his emotions（沉着、控制情绪），是正面的镇定，并非 unusual state of mind（异常心态）；C 把镇定歪曲成「异常」，且不是男士给的归因，原文未提此因。借用原文： composed and in control of his emotions
D) 张冠李戴D 的 knowledge about the company 化用录音 asked some very good questions about the position and the company，但那是说 Rachel 问了好问题、显得很想要这份工作，针对的是 Rachel、回答的是「是否 keen」，与本题问 Peter 自信的归因无关。借用原文： asked some very good questions about the position and the company
questions.quote: M: When comparing them side by side, yes, Peter seemed more self-assured somehow. Maybe it was something about their body language.

options.text: His use of body language.
His accumulation of experience.
His unusual state of mind.
His knowledge about the company.

questions.prompt: What does the man say they will do if they can't reach an agreement?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） Let John make the final decision.
**题目译文**
男士说如果他们无法达成一致意见会怎么做?
A) 再次并列比较候选人。
B) 请董事会投决定性的一票。
C) 下次找个办法打破平局。
D) 让John做最终决定。
**定位** 男：啊，好吧。如果出现平局、我们没法达成一致，那我们就把它交给 John，让他来投决定票。
**信号** 条件句 If…then 的对策落点。男士用 If there's a tie, and we can't come to an agreement, then we'll take it to John 给出明确的 If…then 对策；句中专有人名 John 是强定位信号，then 后的动作即答案。
**替换** take it to John and let him cast the deciding vote↔Let John make the final decision cast the deciding vote=make the final decision
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱A 的 compare side by side 取自男士早前的 When comparing them side by side，确是原词；但那是描述他们之前已做的对比，而非「谈不拢时的对策」，问的是 if can't agree怎么办，A 时态与问点都不符。借用原文： When comparing them side by side
B) 偷换概念B 的 cast the deciding vote 正是录音原词 cast the deciding vote，极具迷惑；但录音里投决定票的是 John 一个人，B 却说交给 the board（董事会）投票，把「个人 John」偷换成「集体 board」。借用原文： take it to John and let him cast the deciding vote
C) 偷换概念C 的 break the tie 借用录音 If there's a tie 的 tie 一词，但录音对平局的对策是「这次就交给 John」，C 却说「找办法在下次打破平局」，把「当下交 John」偷改成「留待下次」，时点与做法都对不上。借用原文： If there's a tie, and we can't come to an agreement
questions.quote: M: Ah, well. If there's a tie, and we can't come to an agreement, then we'll take it to John and let him cast the deciding vote.

options.text: Compare the candidates side by side again.
Ask the board to cast the deciding vote.
Find a way to break the tie next time.
Let John make the final decision.

questions.prompt: What are the speakers mainly talking about?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （主旨题） The woman's latest collection.
**题目译文**
说话者主要在讨论什么?
A) 自有品牌"L'Orange"
B) 女士的最新系列
C) 本季的新时尚
D) 首席设计师的角色
**定位** 我们今天请到了私人时装品牌 L'Orange 的首席设计师 Clementine Ortega，来聊聊她的最新系列。
**信号** 开场引入语点题。记者开场白 to discuss her latest collection 直接交代了"今天来谈什么"，访谈类对话的中心话题几乎都由开场引入句给出，这就是答案句。
**替换** to discuss her latest collection↔The woman's latest collection. her=the woman 指代对应
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱录音确实念到品牌名 the private fashion label L'Orange，但它只是介绍设计师身份时的背景，全程没有围绕"这个品牌"展开，是听到原词就想选的原词陷阱。借用原文： the private fashion label L'Orange
C) 偷换概念记者后面问过 this season's look，C 借这个词把话题偷换成"本季新潮流"这种行业泛论；可对话谈的始终是"她个人的这一系列"，不是整个时尚界的趋势。借用原文： this season's look
D) 未提及录音用 head designer 介绍她的职位，D 借此说成"首席设计师的职责"；但全段没有一句在谈"这个职位要干什么"，是抓住头衔词的过度发挥。借用原文： head designer
questions.quote: We're here with Clementine Ortega, head designer of the private fashion label L'Orange, to discuss her latest collection.

options.text: The private label "L'Orange".
The woman's latest collection.
This season's new fashion.
The head designer's role.

questions.prompt: What does the woman say she always tries to incorporate into her aesthetic?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） Something slightly absurd.
**题目译文**
女士说她总是试图将什么融入她的美学风格?
A) 反映社会规范的东西
B) 符合公众期望的东西
C) 略微荒诞的东西
D) 有点模糊的东西
**定位** 相反，我总是试着把一点略显荒诞的东西融入我的审美。
**信号** I always try to 是直接应答。被问者女设计师用 I always try to incorporate something slightly absurd 直接讲出她总加入的东西，主语+always 的自述句正是题干所问，是答案句。
**替换** something slightly absurd↔ Something slightly absurd.近乎原句对应
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反录音里 I try not to adhere to social norms 是她要"避开"的东西，A 却说她要加入"反映社会规范"的东西，正好把否定听成了肯定。借用原文： I try not to adhere to social norms
B) 与原文相反原文 expectations 与 social norms 并列，都在 I try not to adhere to 的否定范围内；B说她要做"符合公众期待"的东西，与她的本意相反。借用原文： social norms and expectations
D) 原词陷阱录音里 my preferred style has always been on the ambiguous side 说的是她整体风格偏"含糊"，D 借 ambiguous 这个原词来答"她加入了什么"，但题问的是 incorporate 进去的具体东西（absurd），答非所问。借用原文： my preferred style has always been on the ambiguous side
questions.quote: Rather, I always try to incorporate something slightly absurd into my aesthetic.

options.text: Something reflecting the social norms.
Something meeting public expectations.
Something slightly absurd.
Something a bit ambiguous.

questions.prompt: What does the woman say she likes to do?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） Merge styles often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum.
**题目译文**
女士说她喜欢做什么?
A) 融合通常处于时尚光谱两端的风格
B) 向亚洲乡村山区村民的设计学习
C) 让天鹅绒斗篷看起来既威严又阳刚
D) 在传统正装西服上绘制复杂的图案
**定位** 我喜欢把那些常常处于时尚光谱两端的风格融合到一起。
**信号** I like to 直陈偏好。I like to merge styles that are often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum 用 I like to 直接说出她的偏好，正中题干，是答案句。
**替换** merge styles that are often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum↔Merge styles often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum.省略定语从句的同义压缩
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 与原文相反录音里她去亚洲山村看了刺绣，但明说 Trying to recreate their designs would have been futile——照搬他们的设计是徒劳的，所以她没"学他们的设计"，B 把"放弃模仿"说反成"向他们学习"。借用原文： Trying to recreate their designs would have been futile
C) 张冠李戴majestic 和 masculine 是男主持人 masculine at the same time 给出的观感评价，C 盗用这两个原词，把"别人对作品的评价"伪装成"她喜欢做的事"，张冠李戴。借用原文： masculine at the same time
D) 原词陷阱I drew similar intricate patterns onto the velvet cape 是她做那件斗篷时的一次具体操作，D 把这个一次性细节冒充成她长期"喜欢做"的事，可题问的是她声明的偏好（merge styles），层级对不上。借用原文： I drew similar intricate patterns onto the velvet cape
questions.quote: I like to merge styles that are often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum.

options.text: Merge styles often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum.
Learn from the designs of the Asian rural mountain villagers.
Make velvet capes look both majestic and masculine.
Draw intricate patterns onto a traditional power suit.

questions.prompt: What is the man looking forward to?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） Seeing the woman's new creations.
**题目译文**
男士期待什么?
A) 获得女士的签名
B) 看到女士的新作品
C) 将本土元素融入他的作品
D) 下次与女士分享更多想法
**定位** 我们迫不及待想看看你接下来会创作出什么新作品。
**信号** 结尾 can't wait 表期待。男方在结尾说 we can't wait to see what creations you come up with next，can't wait to see 就是"期待"的强信号，是答案句。
**替换** to see what creations you come up with next↔ Seeing the woman's new creations. come up with next=new creations
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 偷换概念录音 your underlying signature touch 里 signature 指她"标志性"的风格印记，A 却理解成"获取她的签名"，把一词多义的 signature 偷换了义项，且男方根本没说要签名。借用原文： your underlying signature touch
C) 原词陷阱the incorporation of indigenous aspects 是男方对本季作品已完成之处的称赞，描述的是过去做成的事；C 盗用 indigenous 这个原词，把"已经做到"说成"他期待去做"，时间和主体都错位。借用原文： the incorporation of indigenous aspects
D) 未提及录音结尾的 next 是接在 what creations you come up with next（下次的作品）上的，D借这个"下次"感造出"下次多分享想法"，可对话从没提"再聊/分享想法"，是无中生有。
questions.quote: we can't wait to see what creations you come up with next.

options.text: Obtaining the woman's signature.
Seeing the woman's new creations.
Incorporating indigenous aspects into his work.
Sharing more ideas with the woman next time.

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Recent studies show that self-control and persistence increase academic outcomes, independence of IQ.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Even our personal beliefs about efforts can affect academic outcomes.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Children who think effort leads to achievement outperform those who believe ability is a fixed trait.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Given the link between persistence and academic success, decisions about efforts are particularly important in childhood.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Yet, relatively little research has explored how young children learn what's worth the effort.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: We all know that infants are keen observers of the social world, but they're not just idly watching; they are tiny learning machines.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They can generalize such abstract concepts as causal relationships and social roles from just a few examples.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Even a 15-month-old infant can outperform a high level computer in such tasks.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Could infants also make broad generalizable inferences from a few examples when it comes to effort?
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: If so, then maybe persistence isn't simply a character trait.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Maybe it's flexible and adaptable based on social context.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: To explore this question, we showed 15-month-old babies one of two things—an experimenter working hard to achieve two different goals, or an experimenter who effortlessly reached each goal.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Then we introduced the baby to a novel music toy that seemed as if it could be activated by pushing a big button on top.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The button could be pressed down, but didn't actually activate anything.

transcript.text: Then analysts who didn't know which condition each baby was in, watched video tapes of the experiment and counted how many times babies tried to activate the toy by pressing the button.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Across one study and a pre-registered duplication, babies who had seen an adult persist and succeed push the button about twice as many times as those who saw an adult effortlessly succeed.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In other words, babies learned that effort was valuable after watching just two examples of an adult working hard and succeeding.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Part of what's exciting about this finding is that the babies didn't just imitate the adult's actions.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Instead, they generalized the value of effort to a novel task.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The experimenter never demonstrated pushing a button or trying to make music.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Instead, the babies learned from different examples of effortful actions that the new toy probably also required persistence.

transcript.text: If chronic lateness has taken over your life and turned into a defining trait of who you are, it's likely that you're losing out on job offers, recreational opportunities, friendships, and more.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: If you are showing up late to your own life, get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: When you have to be somewhere, try to arrive 15 to 30 minutes before you need to.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: If you always run late, that means you must be failing to account for something you always do.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Anticipate that by giving yourself extra time to arrive.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Keep track of whether or not you actually do arrive early.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: You might find that leaving early gets you to places exactly on time.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Set two alarms.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Set one alarm that lets you know it's time to drop what you're doing and a second alarm that means you need to walk out the door.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Obey the alarms.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: As soon as the first alarm goes off, stop what you're doing.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: If it's something you'll be coming back to, like a project for work, make a note to remind yourself where you left off.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Grab everything you need and make sure you know how to get where you're going.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Aim to be out the door and on your way before the second alarm rings.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: This will only work if you take the alarms seriously, so make sure you react as soon as you hear them.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Prepare for the day ahead.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Have all of your notes and materials organized well in advance of each event, so that all you have to do is grab them and go when it's the actual day.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: If mornings are a struggle for you, do as much as you can to ready yourself the night before.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Before you go to bed, lay out your clothes and pack your bag for the next day.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: It soon becomes unbearable to shift between one meeting and another without space in between.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: If you overschedule yourself, however, you'll arrive late as soon as you hit a bump.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: As well as giving you space, this time also acts as a buffer between events, which can be borrowed from, should you be held up in a prior meeting, allowing you to still get to the next one on time.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Calculate transit time between activities and then add 10 to 30 minutes for unexpected delays.

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Do you find other cities to be more or less polite?
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Different cities have different feels for visitors.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Some are friendly and open; some are formal and distant.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Boston tends to seem hurried and sometimes a little rude.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: That's what some tourists have said.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: One study found that people here are less willing to volunteer to help strangers than those residents of other U.S. cities.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Take a close look next time you're in Boston, and here are some of the things you'll probably see: people smoking in the subway stations despite the frequent reminders not to do so; pedestrians walking when the crosswalk lights say not to do so, ignoring the cars; car drivers speeding, making a loud noise with the horn and occasionally cursing at each other.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Drivers who can't be bothered to find a place to park, but instead simply turn on their blinker and stop in the middle of the street.

transcript.text: Sometimes Bostonians seem like they're just too busy to be polite.

transcript.text: That culture has carried down to the present day, he believes.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: That's given Boston a sense of clannishness and reserve, he thinks.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The idea of a stranger greeting another stranger is simply not part of the local culture, he says.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: People will begin a conversation with someone they know, but not with a stranger.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Ralph Whitehead, a professor of journalism at the University of Massachusetts at Amherst, thinks it's because Boston's upper class used manners to make class distinctions.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: By being snobbish about manners, Proper Bostonians made other people scornful of courtesy, he says.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Some say that's just the way Boston is and that the city will never change.

transcript.text: Still, other cities with reputations for worse rudeness are trying hard to change their images.

transcript.text: Paris is one example where people are trying to be friendly.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: New York City is another.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: There, the city is trying to persuade subway riders to be more considerate.

transcript.text: If those cities can make the effort, maybe Boston should as well.

transcriptTranslations: 近期研究表明,自我控制和坚持不懈能够提高学业成绩,且独立于智商之外。甚至我们对努力的个人信念也会影响学业成绩。那些认为努力会带来成就的儿童表现优于那些相信能力是固定特质的儿童。鉴于坚持不懈与学业成功之间的联系,关于努力的决策在儿童时期尤为重要。
然而,关于幼儿如何学习什么值得努力的研究相对较少。我们都知道婴儿是社会世界的敏锐观察者,但他们不只是无所事事地观看,他们是微小的学习机器。他们仅从几个例子就能概括出因果关系和社会角色等抽象概念。即使是15个月大的婴儿在此类任务中也能胜过高级计算机。婴儿在涉及努力时是否也能从几个例子中做出广泛的可概括推断?如果可以,那么也许坚持不懈并非单纯的性格特质,也许它是灵活的,可以根据社会情境进行调整。

为了探索这个问题,我们向15个月大的婴儿展示两种情况之一——一个实验者努力工作以实现两个不同的目标,或者一个实验者毫不费力地达成每个目标。然后我们向婴儿介绍一个新奇的音乐玩具,看起来似乎可以通过按压顶部的大按钮来激活。这个按钮可以被按下,但实际上不会激活任何东西。在婴儿看不见的地方,我们用一个隐藏按钮打开音乐玩具,让他们听到玩具发出音乐。我们把音乐玩具给婴儿,然后离开房间。接着,不知道每个婴儿处于哪种条件的分析人员观看实验录像带,并计算婴儿尝试通过按压按钮来激活玩具的次数。

在一项研究及一次预先注册的重复实验中,看到成人坚持并成功的婴儿按压按钮的次数大约是看到成人毫不费力就成功的婴儿的两倍。换句话说,婴儿仅通过观看成人努力工作并成功的两个例子就学会了努力是有价值的。这一发现令人兴奋的部分原因在于,婴儿不只是模仿成人的行为。相反,他们将努力的价值概括到了一项新任务中。实验者从未演示过按压按钮或试图制造音乐。相反,婴儿从不同的努力行为例子中学到,这个新玩具可能也需要坚持不懈。
如果长期迟到已经接管了你的生活并成为你的一个标志性特征,那么你很可能正在失去工作机会、娱乐机会、友谊等等。如果你总是迟到于自己的人生,那就要组织好自己,优先考虑守时,并解决任何潜在的原因。
当你必须去某个地方时,尽量在需要到达的时间前15到30分钟到达。如果你总是迟到,那意味着你肯定没有把某些你总会做的事情考虑在内。通过给自己额外的时间到达来预见这一点。记录你是否真的提前到达了。你可能会发现提前出发让你恰好准时到达目的地。
设置两个闹钟。设置一个闹钟让你知道该放下手头的事情了,再设置第二个闹钟意味着你需要走出门。服从闹钟。第一个闹钟一响,就停下你正在做的事情。如果是你会回来继续做的事情,比如工作项目,做个笔记提醒自己做到哪里了。拿上你需要的所有东西,确保你知道如何到达目的地。争取在第二个闹钟响起之前出门上路。这只有在你认真对待闹钟时才会奏效,所以确保你一听到闹钟就做出反应。
为即将到来的一天做好准备。提前把每个活动的所有笔记和材料整理好,这样到了真正的那天你只需要拿起它们就走。如果早晨对你来说很困难,那就尽可能在前一晚做好准备。睡觉前,把第二天的衣服摆好,把包收拾好。
学会在任务和会议之间留出时间。在一个会议和另一个会议之间没有空隙地转换很快就会变得难以忍受。然而,如果你把自己的日程安排得过满,一旦遇到障碍你就会迟到。除了给你空间,这段时间还充当活动之间的缓冲,如果你在前一个会议中被耽搁了,可以从中借用时间,让你仍然能准时到达下一个会议。计算活动之间的交通时间,然后为意外延误增加10到30分钟。

你认为波士顿人会铺开欢迎垫吗?你觉得其他城市更礼貌还是更不礼貌?不同的城市给访客的感觉不同。有些友好开放,有些正式疏远。波士顿往往显得匆忙,有时还有点粗鲁。这是一些游客说的。一项研究发现,这里的人比美国其他城市的居民更不愿意主动帮助陌生人。下次你在波士顿时仔细观察一下,你可能会看到以下一些情况:人们在地铁站吸烟,尽管有频繁的提醒不要这样做;行人在人行横道灯指示不要通行时仍然穿行,无视车辆;汽车司机超速行驶,大声按喇叭,偶尔还互相咒骂。司机懒得找地方停车,而是直接打开转向灯,停在街道中间。

有时波士顿人似乎只是太忙而无暇礼貌。为什么他们的城市是这样的?美国前众议员Chester Atkins说,这是因为清教徒创始人本身就没有耐心、脾气暴躁,没有时间讲礼貌。他认为这种文化一直延续至今。Boston College教授Thomas O'Connor认为一个促成因素是波士顿作为一个城市的历史,每一批新移民都受到怀疑和排斥。他认为这让波士顿有了一种宗派意识和保守性。陌生人向另一个陌生人打招呼的想法根本不是当地文化的一部分,他说。人们会和认识的人开始交谈,但不会和陌生人交谈。马萨诸塞大学Amherst分校新闻学教授Ralph Whitehead认为,这是因为波士顿的上层阶级用礼仪来区分阶级。他说,通过对礼仪的势利态度,正统波士顿人让其他人蔑视礼貌。
有些人说这就是波士顿的样子,这座城市永远不会改变。不过,其他以更粗鲁著称的城市正在努力改变形象。巴黎就是一个人们试图变得友好的例子。纽约市是另一个例子。在那里,该市正在努力说服地铁乘客更加体贴周到。如果那些城市能够做出努力,也许波士顿也应该这样做。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say even our personal beliefs about effort can do?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） Impact academic achievements.
**题目译文**
说话者说，即使是我们个人关于努力的信念也能做什么?
A) 影响我们对新任务的态度。
B) 在社会世界中使我们与众不同。
C) 在重要性上超过智商。
D) 影响学业成就。
**定位** 甚至连我们对努力的个人信念，都能影响学业成果。
**信号** 题干原词复现 + Even 强调。录音 Even our personal beliefs about efforts can affect academic outcomes. 几乎照搬了题干的 personal beliefs about effort，又用 Even 加重语气提示"这点尤其值得注意"——题干关键词原样出现加上 Even 的强调，就是答案句的信号。
**替换** affect academic outcomes↔ Impact academic achievements.近义词整体替换
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 张冠李戴Affect our attitude to novel tasks. 盗用了录音后文 a novel music toy / a novel task 里的 novel（新的）一词，但那是讲婴儿对"新玩具 / 新任务"，和本题"个人信念能做什么"无关，属张冠李戴。借用原文： a novel music toy
B) 原词陷阱Distinguish us in the social world. 借了录音 keen observers of the social world 里的social world，但原文是说"婴儿是社会世界的敏锐观察者"，根本没说个人信念能"在社会中区分我们"，是盗用原词的答非所问。借用原文： keen observers of the social world
C) 偷换概念Outweigh IQ in importance. 抓住了录音里的 IQ，但原文说自控力与坚持是independence of IQ（独立于 IQ、与 IQ 无关），并没有说"比 IQ 更重要"，把"无关"偷换成了"更重要"，是与原文不符的偷换。借用原文： independence of IQ
questions.quote: Even our personal beliefs about efforts can affect academic outcomes.

options.text: Affect our attitude to novel tasks.
Distinguish us in the social world.
Outweigh IQ in importance.
Impact academic achievements.

questions.prompt: How did the researchers turn on the music toy in their experiment?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） By pressing a hidden button.
**题目译文**
研究人员在他们的实验中是如何打开音乐玩具的?
A) 通过按下一个隐藏的按钮。
B) 通过按下顶部的一个大按钮。
C) 通过同时按下两个按钮。
D) 通过帮助婴儿按下正确的按钮。
**定位** 在婴儿看不到的地方，我们用一个隐藏的按钮打开了音乐玩具，好让他们听到玩具发出音乐。
**信号** 题干动词 turned on 原样复现。录音 we turned on the music toy with a hidden button 把题干的 turn on the music toy 原样念出，紧跟 with a hidden button 交代方式——题干动作短语原样出现的那句，就是答案句。
**替换** turned on the music toy with a hidden button↔By pressing a hidden button. with a hidden button 概括为 by pressing it
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱By pushing a big button on top. 整句盗自录音 pushing a big button on top，但原文说这个顶上的大按钮"按得下去却其实不启动任何东西"（didn't actually activate anything），它是给婴儿试的假按钮，不是研究者打开玩具的方式，是典型原词陷阱。借用原文： a big button on top, but didn't actually activate anything
C) 未提及By pressing two buttons at the same time. 里"同时按两个按钮"在录音中完全没有出现——原文只有一个隐藏按钮和一个假的大按钮，没有"两个一起按"的说法，属未提及。
D) 与原文相反By helping the babies push the right button. 与录音相反：原文是研究者 Out of sight of the babies（背着婴儿）自己用隐藏按钮打开，并非"帮婴儿按对按钮"，把"偷偷开"歪曲成"协助婴儿按"，与原文不符。借用原文： Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button
questions.quote: Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button so that they heard the toy making music.

questions.prompt: What could the infants do in the experiment according to the speaker?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） Make generalizable inferences about persistence from a few examples.
**题目译文**
根据说话者的说法，婴儿在实验中能做什么?
A) 仅通过观察成人的行为就能成功完成困难的任务。
B) 从少数例子中对坚持做出可推广的推断。
C) 使自己适应不同的社会环境。
D) 努力与实验者互动。
**定位** 他们能仅凭少数几个例子，就归纳出因果关系、社会角色这类抽象概念。那么，当涉及努力时，婴儿是否也能从少数例子中做出宽泛而可推广的推断呢？
**信号** 选项长句原话复现 generalizable inferences from a few examples。录音 make broad generalizable inferences from a few examples 几乎照搬了选项 B 的措辞，from just a few examples 又反复强调"只凭少数例子"——选项学术长句在录音原话里成段复现，就是答案信号；第4段 they generalized the value of effort 进一步证实婴儿确实做到了这种推广。
**替换** make broad generalizable inferences from a few examples ↔Make generalizable inferences about persistence from a few examples.近乎原词复现 + persistence 同义补足
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 过度推断Perform difficult tasks successfully just by observing how adults acted. 借了录音keen observers / observing 的"观察"之意，但原文说的是婴儿从观察中"做出推断、推广努力的价值"，并没说他们"光靠看就成功完成难任务"；successfully、just by 把原意夸大了一截，是过度推断。借用原文： infants are keen observers of the social world
C) 偷换概念Adapt themselves to different social contexts. 盗用录音 based on social context 的social context，但原文是说"坚持也许是灵活的、随社会情境而变"（指坚持这一特质的性质），不是说"婴儿能让自己适应不同社会情境"，主体和意思都被偷换。借用原文： it's flexible and adaptable based on social context
D) 张冠李戴Work hard to interact with experimenters. 借了录音里反复出现的 experimenter（实验者）和 effort / work hard 之意，但原文说"努力工作"的是录像里的成人 an adult working hard，婴儿是观察者，录音从没说婴儿"努力去和实验者互动"，是张冠李戴。借用原文： an adult working hard
questions.quote: They can generalize such abstract concepts as causal relationships and social roles from just a few examples. Could infants also make broad generalizable inferences from a few examples when it comes to effort?

options.text: Perform difficult tasks successfully just by observing how adults acted.
Make generalizable inferences about persistence from a few examples.
Adapt themselves to different social contexts.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's purpose of giving this talk?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （目的题） Offering advice on overcoming habitual lateness.
**题目译文**
演讲者发表这次讲话的目的是什么?
A) 就克服习惯性迟到提供建议。
B) 举例说明各种休闲娱乐机会。
C) 审视个人的决定性特征。
D) 建议设定优先事项的方法。
**定位** 如果长期迟到已经占据了你的生活、变成你这个人的一个鲜明特征,那你很可能正在失去工作机会、休闲机会、友谊等等。如果你连自己的人生都总是迟到,那就把自己安排好、把准时放在首位、并解决背后的根本原因。
**信号** 篇首点题句。目的题的答案信号是"开头的总起句":首段先点出"chronic lateness"(长期迟到)的危害,再用祈使句 get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes 给出全篇要教的方向,后面各段(设两个闹钟、前一晚准备、中间留时间)都是这句的展开,故它统领全篇、就是目的所在。
**替换** chronic lateness↔ habitual lateness同义词替换get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes↔Offering advice on overcoming详述概括为"给建议"
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱Exemplifying various recreational opportunities. 盗用了首段的原词 recreational:录音里recreational opportunities 只是迟到会"失去"的东西之一,被一笔带过,讲话根本不是在"举例各种休闲机会",属于把局部细节当主旨。借用原文： recreational opportunities
C) 原词陷阱Scrutinizing individuals' defining traits. 盗用了首段的 a defining trait of who you are:录音只是说"长期迟到会变成你的一个鲜明特征",并非要去"剖析人的个性特质",方向完全跑偏。借用原文： a defining trait of who you are
D) 偷换概念Suggesting ways for setting priorities. 借了 prioritize punctuality(把准时放首位)里的"priorit-"做文章:录音只把"优先准时"作为众多建议中的一句,全篇并非教"如何排优先级",以偏概全。借用原文： prioritize punctuality
questions.quote: If chronic lateness has taken over your life and turned into a defining trait of who you are, it's likely that you're losing out on job offers, recreational opportunities, friendships, and more. If you are showing up late to your own life, get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes.

options.text: Offering advice on overcoming habitual lateness.
Exemplifying various recreational opportunities.
Scrutinizing individuals' defining traits.
Suggesting ways for setting priorities.

questions.prompt: What should you do if mornings are a struggle for you?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） Get prepared the night before.
**题目译文**
如果早上对你来说很困难,你应该怎么做?
A) 把早餐做得更简单。
B) 认真对待闹钟。
C) 在清晨做好准备。
D) 前一天晚上做好准备。
**定位** 如果早晨对你来说很吃力,那就尽量在前一晚把自己准备好。睡觉前,把衣服摆好、把第二天的包收拾好。
**信号** 条件句原话复现+其后应对。答案信号是题干条件句在录音里的几乎原话复现:录音 If mornings are a struggle for you 与题干一字不差,紧跟其后的 do as much as you can to ready yourself the night before 就是给出的做法,据"条件句之后即答案"锁定此句。
**替换** ready yourself the night before↔Get prepared the night before.近义短语替换
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及Make the breakfast simpler. 听着像应对"早晨吃力"的合理办法,但录音讲早晨那段只说"前一晚摆衣服、收包",从未提及早餐或把它简化,属凭常识脑补、原文未提。
B) 张冠李戴Take the alarms seriously. 盗用了第三段的 take the alarms seriously:那是"设两个闹钟"那条建议里的话,和本题"早晨吃力怎么办"不是同一条,被错接到这道题上。借用原文： take the alarms seriously
C) 与原文相反Ready yourself in the early dawn. 把 ready yourself 的时间偷改成"清晨(early dawn)",而录音明说是 ready yourself the night before(前一晚),时间点正好相反,正中第一步预读标出的 C/D 对立陷阱。借用原文： ready yourself the night before
questions.quote: If mornings are a struggle for you, do as much as you can to ready yourself the night before. Before you go to bed, lay out your clothes and pack your bag for the next day.

options.text: Make the breakfast simpler.
Take the alarms seriously.
Ready yourself in the early dawn.
Get prepared the night before.

questions.prompt: According to the speaker, what can we do to combat unexpected delays?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） Leave time in between activities.
**题目译文**
根据演讲者所说,我们可以做什么来应对意外延误?
A) 提前30分钟完成前一项任务。
B) 避免自己遇到障碍。
C) 在各项活动之间留出时间。
D) 尽量避免可能的耽搁。
**定位** 学会在各项任务和会议之间留出时间。这段时间除了给你余地,还在各项活动之间起到缓冲作用——万一前一场会议把你拖住了,可以从这段时间里挪用,让你仍能准时赶到下一场。
**信号** 段首主张句+buffer 缓冲解释。答案信号是第五段段首的核心主张 Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings,其后用 acts as a buffer(充当缓冲)解释它正好能对付"被前一场拖住"的意外延误,与题干 combat unexpected delays 对上,据此锁定段首这句主张。
**替换** leave time in between tasks and meetings ↔ Leave time in between activities.上位词概括替换acts as a buffer between events ↔ Leave time in between activities.缓冲机制印证该做法
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱Finish the prior task 30 minutes earlier. 盗用了末句的数字 add 10 to 30 minutes for unexpected delays 里的"30 minutes":录音是说"为意外延误额外加留 10 到 30 分钟",并不是"把前一项任务提前 30 分钟完成",数字念到了、事却拼错了。借用原文： add 10 to 30 minutes for unexpected delays
B) 与原文相反Keep ourselves from hitting a bump. 盗用了 you'll arrive late as soon as you hit a bump 里的"hit a bump":录音是说"一旦把日程排太满,碰到颠簸就会迟到",讲的是过度排期的后果,而非教你"避免碰到颠簸";颠簸是无法避免的,要做的是留缓冲,选项把原意拧反了。借用原文： you'll arrive late as soon as you hit a bump
D) 偷换概念Try to avoid possible hold-ups. 只是把题干目标"应对意外延误"换个说法重述一遍(avoid hold-ups),并未给出录音真正提出的可操作做法;且录音 should you be held up 把"被拖住"当成会发生、需用缓冲化解的事,而非教你"避免"它,这是空泛复述目标的陷阱。借用原文： should you be held up
questions.quote: Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings. As well as giving you space, this time also acts as a buffer between events, which can be borrowed from, should you be held up in a prior meeting, allowing you to still get to the next one on time.

options.text: Finish the prior task 30 minutes earlier.
Keep ourselves from hitting a bump.
Leave time in between activities.
Try to avoid possible hold-ups.

questions.prompt: What do visitors find about the cities they've been to?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） They have different feels.
**题目译文**
游客对他们去过的城市有什么发现?
A) 它们的生活方式各不相同。
B) 它们的特征各不相同。
C) 它们有不同的习俗。
D) 它们有不同的感觉。
**定位** 不同的城市带给游客不同的感受。
**信号** 开篇点题句。这是第一段抛出两个问句后给出的第一句陈述 Different cities have different feels for visitors.，独白常在开头先点主题，它直接对应题干问的"游客的发现"，是答案句。
**替换** different feels for visitors↔They have different feels.近乎原句保留 feels
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 偷换概念Their lifestyles vary. 把"feels"偷换成 lifestyles（生活方式），原文谈的是"感受"不是"生活方式"，属偷换概念。
B) 偷换概念Their traits vary. 用 traits（特征）顶替原文的 feels，原文从未说城市"特征"不同，是换词制造的干扰。
C) 未提及They have different customs. 的 customs（习俗）原文没有出现，属无中生有的替换项。
questions.quote: Different cities have different feels for visitors.

options.text: Their lifestyles vary.
Their traits vary.
They have different customs.
They have different feels.

questions.prompt: What did one study find about Bostonians compared with residents of other U.S. cities?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） They are not as willing to help strangers.
**题目译文**
一项研究发现,与美国其他城市的居民相比,Boston人有什么特点?
A) 他们不太愿意帮助陌生人。
B) 他们彼此之间不太有耐心。
C) 他们更频繁地违反交通规则。
D) 他们在公共场合更容易被激怒。
**定位** 一项研究发现，与美国其它城市的居民相比，这里的人更不愿意主动帮助陌生人。
**信号** study found 信号词。句首 One study found that 是题干 one study 的直接对应锚点，其后跟的就是研究结论，是答案句。
**替换** less willing to volunteer to help strangers↔They are not as willing to help strangers. less=not as 同义改写
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 答非所问not as patient with one another 里的 patient 来自后文 too busy to be polite 的语境联想，但研究句说的是"帮陌生人"不是"彼此有无耐心"，把别处内容安到研究结论上，属答非所问。借用原文： Sometimes Bostonians seem like they're just too busy to be polite.
C) 原词陷阱violate traffic rules more frequently 盗用第一段后半罗列的现象——pedestrians walking when the crosswalk lights say not to、car drivers speeding，但这些是说话人列举的所见，不是 one study 的结论，属原词陷阱。借用原文： car drivers speeding, making a loud noise with the horn
D) 过度推断more easily irritated in public 由后文 cursing、rude 的氛围引申而来，但研究句并未说波士顿人"更易动怒"，是顺着语气过度推断。借用原文： occasionally cursing at each other
questions.quote: One study found that people here are less willing to volunteer to help strangers than those residents of other U.S. cities.

options.text: They are not as willing to help strangers.
They are not as patient with one another.
They violate traffic rules more frequently.
They become more easily irritated in public.

questions.prompt: What does Thomas O'Connor say about the idea of strangers greeting one another?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） It is not part of Boston's local culture.
**题目译文**
Thomas O'Connor对陌生人互相问候这一想法有何看法?
A) 这是Boston建城先辈们践行的做法。
B) 正统Boston人并不认为这是异域风俗。
C) 这被Boston上层阶级所采纳。
D) 这不是Boston地方文化的一部分。
**定位** 他说，陌生人跟陌生人打招呼这种事，根本就不属于本地文化。
**信号** he says 归属信号。这句以 he says 收尾，he 回指本段正在论述的 Thomas O'Connor，把观点准确归到他名下；其内容直接回答"陌生人打招呼"与文化的关系，是答案句。
**替换** simply not part of the local culture↔It is not part of Boston's local culture. near-原句对应
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 张冠李戴practiced by Boston's founding fathers 盗用了 the Puritan founding fathers，但那是Chester Atkins 的说法、且讲的是性情急躁，与 O'Connor 谈"陌生人打招呼"无关，属张冠李戴。借用原文： the Puritan founding fathers were themselves impatient and bad-tempered
B) 原词陷阱not deemed exotic by Proper Bostonians 把 Proper Bostonians 这个原词拼到不存在的exotic 上，Proper Bostonians 出自 Whitehead 谈"以礼仪划阶级"的论述，原文从无"是否异域风"之说，属原词陷阱。借用原文： Proper Bostonians made other people scornful of courtesy
C) 张冠李戴adopted by Boston's upper class 盗用 Boston's upper class used manners to make class distinctions，那是 Whitehead 的说法、讲的是上层用礼仪划分阶级，并非O'Connor 论"陌生人打招呼"，属张冠李戴。借用原文： Boston's upper class used manners to make class distinctions
questions.quote: The idea of a stranger greeting another stranger is simply not part of the local culture, he says.

options.text: It was practiced by Boston's founding fathers.
It is not deemed exotic by Proper Bostonians.
It was adopted by Boston's upper class.
It is not part of Boston's local culture.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker think Boston should do?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （推断题） Follow the examples set by Paris and New York City.
**题目译文**
说话者认为Boston应该做什么?
A) 坚持自己对陌生人表示礼貌的方式。
B) 效仿Paris和New York City树立的榜样。
C) 学习世界主要城市在推广旅游方面的做法。
D) 为其历史感到自豪并坚守其文化传统。
**定位** 巴黎就是一个例子，那里的人在努力变得友善。纽约也是，那座城市正设法说服地铁乘客多为他人着想。如果这些城市都能努力，那么也许波士顿也应该这么做。
**信号** 末句 maybe…should 表态。结尾 If those cities can make the effort, maybe Boston should as well. 用条件句含蓄给出说话人的建议——既然巴黎、纽约都在努力改，波士顿也应仿效，是承载态度的答案句。
**替换** Paris is one example ↔ Follow the examples set by Paris and New York City.举例即榜样maybe Boston should as well ↔ Follow the examples should as well=该照做
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反Stick to its own way of showing courtesy to strangers 是"保持原样"，恰与说话人"也该努力改"的劝告相反；它呼应的是上文 the city will never change，但那是"some say"的观点、被 Still 一转否掉了。借用原文： Some say that's just the way Boston is and that the city will never change.
C) 未提及Learn from the world's major cities in promoting tourism 借用了"向大城市学"的影子，但原文谈的是变友善、有礼，从未提"promoting tourism（推广旅游）"，属未提及。
D) 与原文相反Take pride in its history and adhere to its cultural tradition 盗用前文 Boston's history等词，主张"守住历史与传统"，与说话人"该像巴黎纽约一样去改"正好相反，属与原文相反。借用原文： Boston's history as a city where each new group of immigrants was treated with suspicion
questions.quote: Paris is one example where people are trying to be friendly. New York City is another. There, the city is trying to persuade subway riders to be more considerate. If those cities can make the effort, maybe Boston should as well.

options.text: Stick to its own way of showing courtesy to strangers.
Follow the examples set by Paris and New York City.
Learn from the world's major cities in promoting tourism.
Take pride in its history and adhere to its cultural tradition.

我明白了。不过你要知道,我们经理对你们这么久才来很不满。我理解这可能不是你的错,但不管怎样,你应该了解我们这边的感受。
我理解,对造成的任何不便我表示抱歉。我会尽快尽好地解决你们的电脑问题。具体是什么问题,在哪台机器上?
就是这台机器。它之前运行就挺慢的,我觉得,然后越来越糟。上周二它就彻底不工作了。你开机就能看到我说的情况。
好的。你知道有没有备份吗?
备份?
我是说,你知不知道它的内容有没有被复制保存到别的地方?
我不知道。
嗯,这要看接下来的操作情况,如果我需要清空系统目录来重新配置默认协议的话,那我首先要做的就是尽可能仔细地提取所有数据。否则,硬盘上存储的所有数据都会永久丢失。
我们经理会知道。我去叫他过来。
你对学习法律有更多想法了吗？
我一直在认真考虑，是的。实际上，这就是我想跟您谈谈的原因。我想多了解一下学法律是什么样的。
在我看来，法律职业是一件美好的事情。很多人会说这是个枯燥的领域，但我不同意。事实是法律有很多不同的分支，也有很多不同的工作。
您是做建筑和施工方面的，对吧？
没错。我是一名律师，专攻房地产领域。我的大部分工作涉及调解土地纠纷。
您介意给我举个例子吗？
当然。在很多情况下，我受雇于在两个冲突方之间进行仲裁。比如说，有两个土地所有者在某件事上存在棘手的分歧，比如他们相邻地块的边界问题。可能有人会雇用我来打破僵局，解决争端。我的工作通常涉及协商协议，简单明了。
所以您是说，您做的很多工作是解决人们的法律问题，比如您试图找到一个对每个人都有利的解决方案，防止问题升级。
完全正确，说得好。你需要记住，法院和所有官僚机构一样，可能会非常混乱、令人沮丧，而且费用昂贵。因此，只要有可能，最好在法庭外解决问题。
我明白了。所以除了对法律了如指掌，您还需要良好的人际交往技能，对吗？
当然。任何涉及与人打交道的工作都需要良好的人际交往技能，而且任何法律专业人士都需要非常善于清晰地阐述论点。
对。所以我一直在考虑学习刑法。我觉得听起来非常有趣。
嗯，是的。我会说房地产法更赚钱，但刑法的风险更高。我能理解你为什么会觉得它更有趣。

questions.prompt: What did the woman do last Tuesday?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） Called the man's company.
**题目译文**
这位女士上周二做了什么?
A) 见了电脑技术员。

**定位** 我上周二跟你们那边一位女士通过话，到现在已经十天了。我讲得很清楚这是急事，请尽快派人来。

questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱选项盗用了对话开头出现的 computer technician 一词，但她见到这位技术员是今天上门这一刻，并非上周二；上周二她做的是打电话，时间对不上，属答非所问。借用原文： I'm the computer technician
B) 张冠李戴上周二她是给公司打电话，电话那头是 a lady，而男士本人这周才接到任务上门，上周二两人根本没接触，把通话对象说成 the man 是张冠李戴。借用原文： I spoke to a lady there last Tuesday
D) 原词陷阱选项盗用男士自报的 Alpha Maintenance，但那是他工作的公司名，女士只是打电话过去，并没有亲自上门拜访，visited 这个动作无中生有。借用原文： I work for Alpha Maintenance
questions.quote: I spoke to a lady there last Tuesday, which is now 10 days ago. I made it clear it was an urgent matter and please send someone as soon as possible.

questions.prompt: What does the man say he did when he got the call?
questions.explanation:

**题目译文**
这位男士说他接到电话后做了什么?
A) 咨询了负责人。

**定位** 抱歉，调度安排不归我管，我确实不清楚。我能告诉你的就是，我这周接到电话，已经尽快赶过来了。
**信号** 被问者的直接应答句 All I can tell you is。女士追问他能不能早点来，男士的应答里 All I can tell you is I got the call this week and came as soon as I could 用 All I can tell you is 把重点框出来，这句他亲口交代自己接电话后的动作，是答案句。
**替换** came as soon as I could↔Came as soon as possible尽我所能快换成尽可能快
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反选项的 in charge 直接盗用原文 I'm not in charge of scheduling all logistics，但原文是否定，他强调调度不归他负责、自己也不清楚，根本没说去请示负责人，正好与原文相反。借用原文： I'm not in charge of scheduling all logistics
C) 张冠李戴central office 来自男士早先的推测 someone from your office called our central office，那是女方办公室的人打给总部，不是他接电话后做的；把别人的动作安到他头上，是张冠李戴。借用原文： someone from your office called our central office
D) 原词陷阱designated an engineer 盗用 I'm the engineer designated to your case，那是他猜测自己被指派的过程、动作发出方是公司，不是他本人接电话后所为，属答非所问。借用原文： I'm the engineer designated to your case

questions.prompt: What is the feeling about the problem around the woman's workplace?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （态度观点题） Indignation.
**题目译文**
这位女士的工作场所周围对这个问题的感受是什么?
A) 沮丧。
B) 恐惧。
C) 绝望。
D) 愤慨。
**定位** 这么说吧，我得让你知道，我的经理对你们拖这么久才来相当愤慨。
**信号** 评价性形容词 indignant。女士说 my manager is rather indignant that it's taken you this long to come，indignant 是直接的情绪形容词，又被 rather 加重，正是描述工作场所对这件事感受的答案句。
**替换** my manager is rather indignant↔Indignation形容词 indignant 转成名词 Indignation
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及Frustration 是常见情绪词的合理猜测，但原文用的明确是 indignant（愤慨），二者程度和指向不同：indignant 是对怠慢的气愤，不是单纯的受挫，原文并未表达 frustration。
B) 未提及Intimidation 指被威胁、被吓住，对话里女方是在抱怨对方来得慢，没有任何被恐吓的内容，与原文情绪不符，属未提及。
C) 过度推断Desperation 表示绝望、走投无路，程度远超原文。女方只是不满拖延、表达气愤，并未到绝望地步，属过度推断。
questions.quote: Well, I'll have you know, my manager is rather indignant that it's taken you this long to come.

Intimidation.
Desperation.
Indignation.

questions.prompt: What does the woman say her manager would know?
questions.explanation:

这位女士说她的经理会知道什么?

C) 原词陷阱选项盗用男士那句 all data that was stored on its hard drive will be forever lost，但那是他对不备份后果的假设性说明，并不是女士说经理会知道的内容；经理会知道的是有没有备份，不是数据是否已全丢，属答非所问。借用原文： all data that was stored on its hard drive will be forever lost
D) 原词陷阱wipe the system directories clean 直接取自 if I need to wipe the system directories clean，那是男士对自己后续可能操作的描述，是他要不要做的事，不是女士说经理会知道的内容，属答非所问。借用原文： if I need to wipe the system directories clean in order to reconfigure default protocols

questions.prompt: What will many people say about a career in law?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （态度观点题） It's boring.
**题目译文**
许多人会如何评价法律职业?
A) 它很无聊。
B) 它很有挑战性。
C) 它是一件美好的事情。
D) 它不同于大多数工作。
**定位** 在我看来，从事法律是件美好的事。许多人会说这是个枯燥的领域，但我不同意。
**信号** 归属信号 Many people will say。答案落点不在 a beautiful thing in my opinion，而在Many people will say it's a boring field 这句——题干问的是 many people，必须抓住Many people will say 这个明确的归属信号，它后面跟的才是『许多人』的说法。
**替换** a boring field↔It's boring.同义浓缩
questions.tip:
**排除**
C) 张冠李戴It's a beautiful thing. 盗用了录音原话 a beautiful thing in my opinion，但那是男士『我个人』的看法，题干问的是 many people 怎么说——把说话人的观点安到『许多人』头上，归属错位。借用原文： a beautiful thing in my opinion
B) 未提及It's challenging. 听上去合理，但录音里无论是 many people 还是说话人，都没说过从事法律『有挑战性』，属凭常识脑补、原文无据。

questions.prompt: What does the man say most of his work involves?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） Mediating land disputes.
**题目译文**
这位男士说他的大部分工作涉及什么?
A) 在意见不一的律师之间进行仲裁。
B) 防止争议升级。
C) 买卖房产。
D) 调解土地纠纷。
**定位** 我是一名事务律师，专攻房地产。我的工作大部分涉及调解土地纠纷。
**信号** 限定信号 Most of my work。录音 Most of my work involves mediating land disputes与题干的 most of his work 用词几乎一致，Most of my work 就是定位信号，它后面跟的动作即答案。
**替换** mediating land disputes↔Mediating land disputes.近乎原词对应
questions.tip:
**排除**
C) 原词陷阱Buying and selling property. 蹭了录音 specializing in real estate 的房地产话题，听到『房产』就想选；但男士说的主要工作是 mediating land disputes，不是买卖房产，属答非所问的原词陷阱。借用原文： specializing in real estate
A) 偷换概念Arbitrating between disagreeing solicitors. 借用了后文 arbitrate between two clashing parties 的 arbitrate，但把对象偷换成 disagreeing solicitors(意见不合的律师)；录音里仲裁的对象是两个地主/当事人，不是律师，对象错位。借用原文： arbitrate between two clashing parties
B) 答非所问Preventing disputes from escalating. 对应后文 prevents a problem from escalating，但那是女士事后归纳男士工作意义的话，且题干问的是 most of his work 的具体内容；用『防止问题升级』这个意义层面的概括来答『主要做什么』，答非所问。借用原文： prevents a problem from escalating
questions.quote: I'm a solicitor, specializing in real estate. Most of my work involves mediating land disputes.

Preventing disputes from escalating.
Buying and selling property.
Mediating land disputes.

questions.prompt: Why does the man say it's usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） Courts can be frustrating and expensive.
**题目译文**
为什么这位男士说在可能的情况下最好在法庭外解决问题?
A) 法庭是用来解决重大法律纠纷的。
B) 法庭正变得过于官僚化而无法运作。
C) 法庭可能令人沮丧且费用高昂。
D) 法庭可能令人恐惧且武断。
**定位** 你要记住，法庭和所有官僚机构一样，可能非常混乱、令人沮丧而且昂贵。正因如此，能在庭外解决问题通常更好。
**信号** 因果信号 For this reason。For this reason 是明确的因果连接词，它前面那句courts...can be very messy, frustrating, and expensive 就是『为什么庭外解决更好』的原因，顺着 For this reason 往前一句即定位到答案。
**替换** frustrating, and expensive↔ Courts can be frustrating and expensive.原词提取，去掉多余特征
questions.tip:
**排除**
D) 偷换概念Courts can be frightening and arbitrary. 与正确项仅差两个形容词，但录音说的是frustrating(沮丧)和 expensive(昂贵)，不是 frightening(可怕)和 arbitrary(武断)；这两个词录音根本没念，是替换掉真实形容词的近形陷阱。
A) 答非所问Courts are intended for fixing major legal disputes. 说的是法庭的用途，录音里男士并没有用『法庭是用来解决重大纠纷的』来解释为何庭外更好，方向不符。
B) 过度推断Courts are getting too bureaucratic to function. 蹭了录音 like all bureaucracies 的bureaucracy，但录音只是把法庭比作官僚机构、说它混乱昂贵，从没说法庭『过于官僚以致无法运转』，属由原词过度推断。借用原文： like all bureaucracies
questions.quote: You need to remember that courts, like all bureaucracies really, can be very messy, frustrating, and expensive. For this reason, it's usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible.

options.text: Courts are intended for fixing major legal disputes.
Courts are getting too bureaucratic to function.
Courts can be frustrating and expensive.
Courts can be frightening and arbitrary.

questions.prompt: What does the man think is required of any law professional?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） The ability to express themselves clearly and forcefully.
**题目译文**
这位男士认为任何法律专业人士需要具备什么?
A) 以独特方式进行论证的能力。
B) 防止相关各方之间冲突的技能。
C) 预见工作中任何潜在利害关系的技能。

**定位** 任何与人打交道的工作都需要良好的人际交往能力，而任何法律从业者都需要非常善于清楚地表达论点。
**信号** 要求信号 needs to be。题干问 required of any law professional，录音 any law professional needs to be very eloquent at articulating that argument 用 needs to 直接回应，needs to be 就是要求信号，其后描述的能力即答案。
**替换** eloquent at articulating that argument↔The ability to express themselves clearly and forcefully.同义替换
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱The skill of preventing conflicts between parties concerned. 蹭了前文 prevents a problem from escalating 与调解纠纷的整段话题，听上去和这职业最贴；但题干问 any law professional 被要求的能力，录音对此的回答是 eloquent at articulating，不是预防冲突，属答非所问的原词陷阱。借用原文： prevents a problem from escalating
A) 偷换概念The ability to make arguments in a unique way. 借了录音 articulating that argument的 argument，但录音只说要 eloquent(善于表达)，从未说要『以独特的方式』论辩，unique 是凭空加上的限定。借用原文： articulating that argument
C) 张冠李戴The skill of foreseeing any potential stakes in their work. 盗用了结尾 the stakes are higher in criminal law 的 stakes，但那是男士比较两类法律时说的话，与『法律从业者被要求的能力』无关，且录音从没说要『预见潜在利害』。借用原文： the stakes are higher in criminal law
questions.quote: Any job that involves people requires good interpersonal skills, and any law professional needs to be very eloquent at articulating that argument.

The skill of preventing conflicts between parties concerned.

transcript.text: Humans are aspirational goal-seeking beings.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Each of us, according to research, has an inborn drive to acquire.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The "dark side" of this drive to acquire is being mindlessly driven to possess more and more "things" and to socially compare our "stuff" with all the stuff other people have in their lives.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: So the question is, how do we ensure we tap into our drive to acquire in positive ways that will benefit our well-being?
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: One way is to become more intentionally aspirational.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: To be intentionally aspirational includes consciously aspiring to be the person you need to be to succeed in your professional and personal life.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: It also includes consciously aspiring to acquire things in your life that will positively impact your sense of well-being.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: If you're not consciously, mindfully and intentionally harnessing this inborn drive to acquire, you might be mindlessly pursuing all the wrong things.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: While your intentional aspirational goals will include pursuit of acquiring things that will increase your sense of well-being, they ought to also include goals to help other people in your various life roles.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Your intentional aspirational goals will also include striving to be your personal best—a person of "good" character, integrity, and trustworthiness.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Think about this from a practical, rather than theoretical viewpoint.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: If you're not pursuing intentional aspirational goals, you have nothing to strive for.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: If you have nothing to strive for, you're putting yourself in the dangerous position of simply drifting through life, and you will not be able to experience, live and enjoy all that life has to offer.

transcriptTranslations: 长期以来，幼儿看电视时间增加一直与某些发展领域的进步较差相关联。抵消这些负面影响的一个可能方法是在看屏幕时交谈。正如一项新研究表明的那样,父母在看电视期间与学龄前儿童交谈越多,这些儿童在进入幼儿园时拥有更高好奇心水平的可能性就越大。这对于社会经济条件不利的儿童尤其如此。

密歇根大学健康C.S. Mott儿童医院的首席作者Prachi Shah说:"我们的研究结果强化了父母交谈对促进幼儿发展和好奇心的重要性。"研究人员评估了1500名学龄前儿童每天看电视的小时数和父母在屏幕时间交谈的频率,然后测量了幼儿园时期的早期儿童好奇心。该研究特别关注好奇心水平,这与幼儿园阶段阅读和数学方面的学习增强和更高学业成就相关,以及行为发展方面的益处,特别是对来自社会经济地位较低家庭的儿童。虽然现在许多幼儿通过平板电脑和手机等移动设备接触数字媒体而成长,但电视仍然是主要的屏幕活动,占所有屏幕时间的72%。98%的家庭都有电视,使得电视接触成为幼儿发展背景中的一个相关因素。
过度接触媒体,包括电视,可能会取代探索性活动,如游戏和亲子互动,而这些被认为是培养儿童好奇心的关键。Shah说:"我们的研究结果表明,父母在与幼儿的日常生活中寻找机会促进对话交流的重要性——包括在看电视时。"
人类是有抱负、追求目标的生物。根据研究，我们每个人都有一种与生俱来的获取驱动力。这种获取驱动力的"阴暗面"是无意识地被驱使去拥有越来越多的"东西",并将我们的"物品"与其他人生活中拥有的所有物品进行社会比较。所以问题是,我们如何确保以积极的方式利用我们的获取驱动力,从而有益于我们的幸福感?
一种方法是变得更有意识地怀有抱负。有意识地怀有抱负包括有意识地渴望成为你在职业和个人生活中取得成功所需要成为的那个人。它还包括有意识地渴望在生活中获得能够积极影响你幸福感的事物。如果你没有有意识地、用心地、有意图地驾驭这种与生俱来的获取驱动力,你可能正在无意识地追求所有错误的东西。
虽然你有意的抱负目标将包括追求获得能增加你幸福感的事物,但它们也应该包括在你各种生活角色中帮助他人的目标。你有意的抱负目标还将包括努力成为最好的自己——一个具有"良好"品格、正直和值得信赖的人。
从实践而非理论的角度来思考这个问题。如果你不追求有意的抱负目标,你就没有可以努力争取的东西。如果你没有可以努力争取的东西,你就将自己置于简单地随波逐流度过人生的危险境地,你将无法体验、生活和享受生活所提供的一切。
