questions.prompt: What is the question the woman asked Mr. Grimm after the introduction?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） How he has led people of Berkton to change the village radically.
**题目译文**
这位女士在介绍之后向Grimm先生提出了什么问题?
A) 他如何使自己成为广受欢迎的Berkton市长。
B) 居民将如何把Berkton变成旅游胜地。
C) 他本人认为Berkton村有多迷人。
D) 他如何带领Berkton的人们彻底改变了这个村庄。
**定位** Berkton 已成为全国最受欢迎的旅游目的地之一，而这一切就发生在你的任期之内。你究竟是怎么做到这一点的呢？
**信号** 主持人在介绍后抛出的直接提问句。答案句的信号是主持人(W)在开场介绍之后说出的那句直接发问 Just how did you achieve this?——"this" 回指上一句 "Berkton 变成热门旅游地"，所以她问的正是 "你如何促成了这场转变"。对话题里，主持人 "介绍之后的第一个问句" 就是答案落点。
**替换** how did you achieve this↔ How he has led people of Berkton to change the village radically this＝把村子变旅游地，即 "彻底改变村庄" this has happened under your watch↔he has led people of Berkton "在你任期内发生"＝市长带领大家做成
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱A 用了原文反复出现的 popular as the mayor of Berkton 这些原词，但主持人问的是 "如何改变村子"，不是 "市长本人如何变得受欢迎"；原文 popular tourist destinations 说的是 "村子" 受欢迎，A 偷换成 "市长" 受欢迎，听到 popular 就选会中招。借用原文： Berkton has become one of the most popular tourist destinations in the country
B) 张冠李戴B 说的是 the residents will turn Berkton into a tourist attraction，主语是居民、且是"将要" 做的将来事；可主持人问的是 "你(市长)如何做到了已经发生的转变"，B 张冠李戴(把焦点从市长换成居民)又错了时态。借用原文： The achievement belongs to all the residents of Berkton.
C) 原词陷阱C 说 How charming he himself considers the village of Berkton to be，借用了原文this charming village 里的 charming 一词；但 charming 是主持人介绍时用的，且主持人问的是 "如何做到转变"，不是 "市长觉得村子多迷人"，C 把客观描述偷换成 "市长的主观评价"。借用原文： overseeing this charming village
questions.quote: Berkton has become one of the most popular tourist destinations in the country, and this has happened under your watch. Just how did you achieve this?

options.text: How he has made himself popular as the mayor of Berkton.
How the residents will turn Berkton into a tourist attraction.
How charming he himself considers the village of Berkton to be.
How he has led people of Berkton to change the village radically.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about Berkton 10 years ago?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） It was relatively unknown to the outside.
**题目译文**
关于10年前的Berkton我们了解到什么?
A) 它的开发程度很有限。
B) 它完全与世隔绝,是个沉睡的村庄。
C) 它在外界相对不为人知。
D) 它拥有稀有的自然资源。
**定位** 大约 10 年间，Berkton 从一个相对默默无闻的沉睡小村，变成了一个必看的旅游胜地。
**信号** "from…to…" 中 from 后即 10 年前的状态。答案信号是主持人这句 gone from a relatively unheard-of sleepy village to a must-see destination 里的 "from…to…" 结构：from 后面 a relatively unheard-of sleepy village 正是 "10 年前" 的起点状态，to 后面才是现在。问 "10 年前"，答案就在 from 之后。
**替换** a relatively unheard-of sleepy village↔ It was relatively unknown to the outside unheard-of＝unknown，同义替换
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及A 说 developed only to a limited extent(只在有限程度上被开发)，但原文只说村子 "没名气/沉睡"，从没说它 "被开发到有限程度"；这是凭 "沉睡村" 的印象自行脑补的开发说法，原文无据。
B) 原词陷阱B 用了原文原词 sleepy village，但把 relatively unheard-of(相对没名气)夸大成 totally isolated(完全孤立)；relatively(相对)被偷换成 totally(完全)，程度被拔高，与原文不符。借用原文： a relatively unheard-of sleepy village
D) 原词陷阱D 说 endowed with rare natural resources，借用了原文 endowed with such a beautiful natural allure 的 endowed 与 natural；但原文说的是 "自然之美(allure)" 而非"罕见资源(resources)"，且这句讲的不是 "10 年前的状态"，与题问的时间也不对。借用原文： Berkton was always fortunate to be endowed with such a beautiful natural allure.
questions.quote: In about 10 years, Berkton has gone from a relatively unheard-of sleepy village to a must- see destination.

options.text: It was developed only to a limited extent.
It was totally isolated as a sleepy village.
It was relatively unknown to the outside.
It was endowed with rare natural resources.

questions.prompt: What resulted from the passing of the legislative proposal "Motion 836"?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） All the houses in Berkton looked aesthetically similar.
**题目译文**
立法提案"836号动议"的通过产生了什么结果?
A) Berkton的所有房产都由同一位建筑师设计。
B) 大多数居民与邻居和睦相处。
C) 大多数居民享有舒适的住房条件。
D) Berkton的所有房屋在美学上看起来相似。
**定位** 这项立法提案本质上是要统一 Berkton 所有房屋的外观审美。其设想是：如果所有房产都按某种方式、带着共同的设计特征呈现，那么整个村庄看起来会更美。而它奏效了。
**信号** 提案后紧跟的 "统一外观"＋"奏效了"。答案信号有两处：一是紧跟提案的目的句harmonize the aesthetic appearance of all the houses(统一所有房子的外观)，二是收尾的 And it worked.(它奏效了)——"奏效" 确认了这个 "外观统一" 的效果真的实现了，正是提案带来的结果。
**替换** harmonize the aesthetic appearance of all the houses in Berkton↔All the houses in Berkton looked aesthetically similar "统一外观"＝"外观看起来相似" shared design features↔ aesthetically similar "共同设计特征"＝外观相似
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱A 说 designed by the same architect，借用了原文 shared design features 里的design；但原文说的是 "共同的设计特征"，从没说 "出自同一个建筑师"，A 把 "设计相似"偷换成 "同一人设计"，是听到 design 就选的陷阱。借用原文： if all the properties looked a certain way with shared design features
B) 偷换概念B 说 lived in harmony with their neighbours(邻里和睦相处)，疑似借了原文harmonize(统一)与 an overwhelming majority of neighbors voted 里 neighbors 的影子；但原文是说邻居们 "投票通过提案"，harmonize 指 "统一房屋外观" 而非 "邻里关系和睦"，B 偷换了概念。借用原文： an overwhelming majority of neighbors voted in favor of "Motion 836"
C) 未提及C 说 enjoyed cosy housing conditions(享受舒适的居住条件)，但原文谈的是房子 "外观是否统一、村子是否更美"，从没谈居民住得舒不舒适；cosy(舒适)是凭 "漂亮房子" 联想出来的，原文无据。
questions.quote: This legislative proposal essentially set out to harmonize the aesthetic appearance of all the houses in Berkton. The idea was that if all the properties looked a certain way with shared design features, then a village as a whole would look more beautiful. And it worked.

options.text: All the properties in Berkton were designed by the same architect.
The majority of residents lived in harmony with their neighbours.
The majority of residents enjoyed cosy housing conditions.
All the houses in Berkton looked aesthetically similar.

questions.prompt: Why does the man say the tourists are a blessing to Berkton?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） They have helped boost the local economy.
**题目译文**
为什么这位男士说游客是Berkton的福音?
A) 他们帮助促进了当地经济。
B) 他们使居民感到异常自豪。
C) 他们为其知名度做出了相当大的贡献。
D) 他们给村里的每个人都带来了快乐。
**定位** 我们接待的游客是一种福气，因为他们彻底重振了我们当地的经济。
**信号** 因果词 as 之后即原因。答案信号是因果连词 as：它前面是判断 The tourists we receive are a blessing，后面 they have completely revitalized our local economy 才是 "为什么是福气" 的真正原因。问 Why，答案就在 as 引出的从句里。
**替换** they have completely revitalized our local economy ↔They have helped boost the local economy revitalize＝boost，同义替换
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 张冠李戴B 说 made the residents unusually proud，借用了原文前面 Great pride 的 pride；但那是回答 "邻居们现在感受如何" 时说的居民对 "村子变美" 的自豪，不是 "游客" 带来的、也不是 "游客是福气" 的原因，B 张冠李戴、错配了问题。借用原文： Great pride, I would say.
C) 原词陷阱C 说 contributed considerably to its popularity，借了原文反复出现的popular/popularity 影子；但说话人给出的 "福气" 原因是 "重振经济"，不是 "游客提升了知名度"，C 把答案换到了名气这条线，与 as 后的原因不符。借用原文： Berkton has become one of the most popular tourist destinations in the country
D) 过度推断D 说 brought happiness to everyone in the village，疑似从 Every visitor is warmly welcome 的友好氛围里推出来；但原文只说 "重振经济/欢迎游客"，没说 "给村里每个人带来快乐"，everyone/happiness 都是脑补放大，过度推断。借用原文： Every visitor is warmly welcome.
questions.quote: The tourists we receive are a blessing, as they have completely revitalized our local economy.

options.text: They have helped boost the local economy.
They have made the residents unusually proud.
They have contributed considerably to its popularity.
They have brought happiness to everyone in the village.

transcript.text: Different people use different strategies for managing conflicts.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: These strategies are learned in childhood.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Usually, we are not aware of how we act in conflict situations.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: We just do whatever seems to come naturally.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: But we do have a personal strategy, and because it is learned, we can always change it by learning new and more effective ways of managing conflicts.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: When you get involved in a conflict, there are two major concerns you have to take into account: achieving your personal goals and keeping a good relationship with the other person.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: How important your personal goals are and how important the relationship is to you affect how you act in a conflict.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Given these two concerns, five styles of managing conflicts can be identified.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The turtle.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Turtles withdraw into their shells to avoid conflicts.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They give up their personal goals and relationships.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They believe it is easier to withdraw from a conflict than to face it.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The shark.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Sharks try to overpower opponents by forcing them to accept their solution to the conflict.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They seek to achieve their goals at all costs.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Sharks assume that conflicts are settled by one person winning and one person losing.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Winning gives sharks a sense of pride and achievement.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Losing gives them a sense of weakness, inadequacy, and failure.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The teddy bear.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Teddy bears want to be accepted and liked by other people.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They think that conflict should be avoided in favor of harmony, and believe that conflicts cannot be discussed without damaging relationships.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They give up their goals to preserve the relationship.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The fox.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Foxes are moderately concerned with their own goals and about their relationships with other people.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They give up part of their goals and persuade the other person in a conflict to give up part of his goals.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They seek a solution to conflicts where both sides gain something.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The owl.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Owls view conflicts as problems to be solved.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They see conflicts as improving relationships by reducing tension between two people.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They try to begin a discussion that identifies the conflict as a problem.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: By seeking solutions that satisfy both themselves and the other person, owls maintain the relationship.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Owls are not satisfied until a solution is found that achieves their own goals and the other person's goals, and they are not satisfied until the tensions and negative feelings have been fully resolved.

transcript.text: Question 25. How can we solve pressing environmental and societal problems according to Professor Tom Oliver?
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcriptTranslations: 不同的人使用不同的策略来管理冲突。这些策略是在童年时期学会的。通常,我们并不知道自己在冲突情境中是如何行事的。我们只是做任何看似自然而然的事情。但我们确实有个人策略,而且因为它是习得的,我们总是可以通过学习新的、更有效的冲突管理方式来改变它。当你卷入冲突时,你必须考虑两个主要关切:实现你的个人目标和与他人保持良好关系。你的个人目标有多重要以及这段关系对你有多重要,会影响你在冲突中的行为方式。基于这两个关切,可以识别出五种冲突管理风格。
海龟型。海龟缩进壳里以避免冲突。他们放弃个人目标和关系。他们认为退出冲突比面对冲突更容易。
鲨鱼型。鲨鱼试图通过强迫对手接受他们对冲突的解决方案来压倒对手。他们不惜一切代价寻求实现自己的目标。鲨鱼认为冲突是通过一方获胜、一方失败来解决的。获胜给鲨鱼带来自豪感和成就感。失败则让他们感到软弱、无能和失败。
泰迪熊型。泰迪熊希望被他人接受和喜欢。他们认为应该避免冲突以维护和谐,并相信冲突无法在不损害关系的情况下讨论。他们为了保持关系而放弃自己的目标。
狐狸型。狐狸对自己的目标和与他人的关系都适度关注。他们放弃部分目标,并说服冲突中的对方也放弃部分目标。他们寻求让双方都有所收获的冲突解决方案。
猫头鹰型。猫头鹰将冲突视为需要解决的问题。他们认为冲突通过减少两人之间的紧张关系来改善关系。他们试图发起讨论,将冲突确定为一个问题。通过寻求既满足自己又满足对方的解决方案,猫头鹰维持了关系。猫头鹰只有在找到既实现自己目标又实现对方目标的解决方案时才会满意,只有在紧张和负面情绪得到完全化解时才会满意。
地球上现存的全部150万个已知动植物物种的基因密码将被绘制成图谱,以帮助拯救濒危物种并促进人类健康。科学家希望破解动植物的基因密码能够帮助发现传染病的新疗法、延缓衰老、改良农业作物并创造新型生物材料。
在英国,包括自然历史博物馆、邱园皇家植物园和Wellcome Sanger研究所在内的多家机构联手对英国的66000个动植物物种进行基因测序。该项目被称为达尔文生命之树项目,预计耗时10年,耗资1亿英镑。项目完成后,所有信息将向研究人员公开。
许多科学家认为地球现已进入第六次大灭绝,人类正在制造栖息地丧失、污染和气候变化的有毒混合体,这已导致自1500年以来至少77种哺乳动物和140种鸟类灭绝。这是自6600万年前恐龙灭绝以来最大规模的物种丧失。科学家表示,对每个物种进行测序将彻底改变人们对生物学和进化的理解,并加强保护、维护和恢复生物多样性的努力。
自然历史博物馆生命科学部主任Tim Littlewood博士说:"无论你关心的是食物还是疾病,地球上每个生物体如何适应其环境的历史都记录在它的基因组成中。如何利用这些信息取决于你理解它的能力。我们将使用现代方法来深入了解现在和过去。当然,了解过去也为未来提供了一个前瞻性模型。"

Wellcome科学主任Jim Smith爵士说:"无论我如何努力,我都想不出比这更激动人心、更相关、更及时或更具国际启发性的项目了。自1970年以来,人类已经消灭了60%的动物种群。在调查的80000个物种中,约23000个正在走向灭绝。我们正处于地球上第六次物种大灭绝事件之中,这不仅威胁着野生物种,也危及全球粮食供应。作为科学家,我们都意识到我们迫切需要现在就为我们脆弱的星球上的生命编目。我认为我们正在创造历史。"
17世纪英国诗人约翰·多恩写道："没有人是一座孤岛，可以自全；每个人都是大陆的一片，是整体的一部分。"现在,一位英国学者声称,人类的个体性确实只是一种幻觉,因为社会在心理、生理和文化层面的相互联系远比人们意识到的要紧密得多。雷丁大学生态与进化研究小组的研究员汤姆·奥利弗教授在他的新书《自我的错觉》中指出,不存在所谓的"自我",甚至连我们的身体也不是真正的"我们"。

正如哥白尼意识到地球不是宇宙的中心一样,奥利弗教授表示,社会迫切需要一场类似哥白尼式的革命,以理解人们不是独立的存在,而是一个相互联系的整体的一部分。他写道:"人类思维文化演变中的一个重要里程碑是接受地球不是宇宙的中心,即所谓的哥白尼革命。然而,我们还有一个重大的神话需要破除:我们作为独立的自我存在于主观宇宙的中心。你可能觉得自己是一个独立的个体,在世界上自主行动;你有一个贯穿一生的不变的内在自我,作为一个中心锚点,而世界在你周围变化。这就是我试图揭穿的幻觉。我们与周围的世界紧密相连。"
奥利弗教授认为,人体内大约有37万亿个细胞,但大多数细胞的寿命只有几天或几周,因此物质层面的"我们"在不断变化。事实上,你身体的任何部分都不曾存在超过10年。"由于我们的身体基本上每隔几周就会重新生成,仅凭其中的物质显然不足以解释身份认同的持续性线索。"
奥利弗教授声称,个人主义实际上对社会有害,只有认识到我们是一个更大整体的一部分,我们才能解决紧迫的环境和社会问题。通过自私的过度消费,我们正在破坏自然世界,并以越来越快的速度使用不可再生资源。他说:"作为一个物种,我们正处于一个关键的十字路口,必须迅速改革我们的思维方式和行为,以更少自私的方式行事。所以让我们睁开眼睛,看到我们周围隐藏的联系。"

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker say strategies for managing conflicts can always be changed?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） Because they are learned.
**题目译文**
为什么说话者说管理冲突的策略总是可以改变的?
A) 因为它们是习得的。
B) 因为它们是自然而然产生的。
C) 因为它们必须被适当地个性化。
D) 因为可能存在更有效的策略。
**定位** 但我们确实有一套个人策略，而正因为它是后天习得的，我们总能通过学习新的、更有效的冲突处理方式来改变它。
**信号** because 直接交代原因。这句里 because it is learned, we can always change it 是赤裸裸的因果结构："because + 原因"紧跟着"can always change"。原因题听到 because 就锁这句，不必再听后文。
**替换** because it is learned↔Because they are learned.几乎原句搬到选项
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱录音确实说过 We just do whatever seems to come naturally，但那是讲"我们平时不自觉、顺其自然地行事"，并非"策略能被改变的原因"。B 把这个原词搬来当原因，恰恰用反了——天生自然反而是难改的那一面。借用原文： We just do whatever seems to come naturally
C) 偷换概念录音提到策略是 a personal strategy（个人的），C 顺势造出 they have to be properly personalized（必须妥善个性化）。但录音从没说"必须被个性化"是它能改变的原因，这是把"个人的"偷换成"必须个性化"的无中生有。借用原文： a personal strategy
D) 答非所问录音末尾确有 more effective ways，D 据此说 there can be more effective strategies。但"有更有效的策略"在录音里是"改变之后能达到的效果/途径"，不是"能改变"的原因；真正的原因是它习得（learned）。D 把结果当成了原因。借用原文： more effective ways of managing conflicts
questions.quote: But we do have a personal strategy, and because it is learned, we can always change it by learning new and more effective ways of managing conflicts.

options.text: Because they are learned.
Because they come naturally.
Because they have to be properly personalized.
Because there can be more effective strategies.

questions.prompt: What is said to affect the way one acts in a conflict?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） The importance of one's goals and of the relationship.
**题目译文**
什么被认为会影响一个人在冲突中的行为方式?
A) 双方之间差异和相似的程度。
B) 对另一方所持特定期望的了解。
C) 一个人的目标和关系的重要性。
D) 一个人采用的冲突管理方法。
**定位** 你的个人目标有多重要、以及这段关系对你有多重要，这两点影响你在冲突中如何行事。
**信号** 原句直接出现 affect。这句的主干就是 How important your personal goals are and how important the relationship is to you affect how you act，动词 affect 与题干affect 同词出现，谓语前的两个主语（目标重要性、关系重要性）即所求，是教科书式的"信号词同词复现"定位点。
**替换** How important your personal goals are and how important the relationship is to you↔The importance of one's goals and of the relationship.句子改名词化
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及A 说 The extent of difference and of similarity between the two sides.（双方差异与相似的程度）听上去很学术，但录音通篇没说"差异/相似程度"会影响行为。这是凭"冲突=双方有分歧"的常识脑补出来的，原文无据。
B) 原词陷阱B 说 The knowledge of the specific expectation the other side holds.（了解对方的具体期待）。录音确实反复说到"the other person"，但从没说"知道对方期待什么"会影响你的行为，影响行为的是你自己目标和关系的重要性。B 借了"对方"这个原词，却安了个录音没说的内容。借用原文： keeping a good relationship with the other person
D) 原词陷阱D 说 The approaches one adopts to conflict management.（处理冲突所采取的方法）。这正是整篇的大主题词 managing conflicts，但题目问的是"什么影响你的做法"，而"做法本身"不能影响"做法"，逻辑上自指。D 盗用了贯穿全文的话题词来冒充答案。借用原文： strategies for managing conflicts
questions.quote: How important your personal goals are and how important the relationship is to you affect how you act in a conflict.

options.text: The extent of difference and of similarity between the two sides.
The knowledge of the specific expectation the other side holds.
The importance of one's goals and of the relationship.
The approaches one adopts to conflict management.

questions.prompt: Of the five styles the speaker discusses, which views conflicts as problems to be solved?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） The owl.
**题目译文**
在说话者讨论的五种风格中,哪一种将冲突视为需要解决的问题?
A) 狐狸型。
B) 猫头鹰型。
C) 鲨鱼型。
D) 乌龟型。
**定位** 猫头鹰。猫头鹰把冲突视为有待解决的问题。
**信号** 原句逐字复述特征。第 6 段开头先报名字 The owl，紧接着 Owls view conflicts as problems to be solved 与题干 views conflicts as problems to be solved 几乎一字不差。匹配题里，题干特征在哪段被原样念出，那段的主角就是答案。
**替换** Owls view conflicts as problems to be solved ↔ The owl.特征绑定到名字
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 答非所问A 是 The fox.。狐狸的特征是 both sides gain something（双方各让一步、各得一点），属于折中妥协，录音没说狐狸"把冲突看作待解决的问题"。它和 owl 都偏正面，最易混，但定性不同。借用原文： They seek a solution to conflicts where both sides gain something.
C) 与原文相反C 是 The shark.。鲨鱼的特征是 overpower opponents by forcing them to accept their solution（强压对方、逼其接受），与"把冲突当问题来解决"正相反。鲨鱼追求一方赢一方输，绝非协商解决。借用原文： Sharks try to overpower opponents by forcing them to accept their solution
D) 与原文相反D 是 The turtle.。乌龟的特征是 withdraw into their shells to avoid conflicts（缩进壳里逃避冲突），它连面对都不愿意，更谈不上"把冲突当问题来解决"，与题干特征截然相反。借用原文： Turtles withdraw into their shells to avoid conflicts.
questions.quote: The owl. Owls view conflicts as problems to be solved.

options.text: The fox.
The owl.
The shark.
The turtle.

questions.prompt: What do scientists hope to do by cracking the genetic code of plants and animals?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） Help save species from extinction and boost human health.
**题目译文**
科学家希望通过破解动植物的遗传密码来做什么?
A) 帮助拯救物种免于灭绝并促进人类健康。
B) 了解动植物在过去是如何灭亡的。
C) 帮助收集研究人员可公开获取的信息。
D) 找出英国66000个物种灭绝的原因。
**定位** 地球上全部 150 万已知动植物物种的基因密码都将被绘制出来，以帮助拯救物种免于灭绝、并提升人类健康。
**信号** 目的信号 to help 后面接落点。答案句靠目的状语 to help save species from extinction and boost human health 中的 to help 锁定——"做基因测序"的目的正写在 to help 之后，这正是题干 hope to do 要的那一层。
**替换** save species from extinction and boost human health↔Help save species from extinction and boost human health.选项几乎原句搬来，只在前面加 Help
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 答非所问本项 Understand how plants and animals perished over the past. 借了"动植物消亡"的料（呼应录音第 3 段大量物种灭绝的描述），但说的是"理解过去它们如何消亡"，而录音目的是"拯救现在的物种"，把"救（未来）"偷换成"懂（过去）"，答非所问。借用原文： has already led to the loss of at least 77 species of mammals and 140 types of birds since 1500
C) 原词陷阱Help gather information publicly available to researchers. 直接搬了录音 all the information will be publicly available to researchers，但那是说"项目完成后信息将公开给研究者"，是项目的副产品，不是"破解基因码"这一动作的目的，典型原词陷阱。借用原文： all the information will be publicly available to researchers
D) 原词陷阱Find out the cause of extinction of Britain's 66, 000 species. 搬了录音 Britain's 66,000 species 这个醒目数字，又拼上"找灭绝原因"，但录音从没说目的是"查灭绝原因"，且66,000 是英国测序的物种数、与"破解基因码的目的"是两码事，原词＋无中生有。借用原文： Britain's 66,000 species of animals and plants
questions.quote: The genetic code of all 1.5 million known species of animals and plants living on earth will be mapped to help save species from extinction and boost human health.

options.text: Help save species from extinction and boost human health.
Understand how plants and animals perished over the past.
Help gather information publicly available to researchers.
Find out the cause of extinction of Britain's 66, 000 species.

questions.prompt: What do many scientists believe with regard to earth?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） It has entered the sixth mass extinction.
**题目译文**
许多科学家对地球持什么看法?
A) 它曾经由恐龙统治。
B) 它已进入第六次大灭绝。
C) 它的前景取决于人类未来的行为。
D) 它的气候变化因人类而加剧。
**定位** 许多科学家相信，地球如今已进入第六次大规模物种灭绝，人类制造出栖息地丧失、污染和气候变化交织而成的有毒组合。
**信号** 观点信号 Many scientists believe 直接引出。答案句由 Many scientists believe that earth has now entered the sixth mass extinction 这个观点引导句锁定——题干 believe与原文 believe 对齐，believe 后的 that 从句就是"许多科学家相信什么"的答案。
**替换** earth has now entered the sixth mass extinction↔ It has entered the sixth mass extinction. earth→It，其余原句保留
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱It was once dominated by dinosaurs. 蹭录音里的 dinosaurs，但原文说的是 the biggest loss of species since the dinosaurs were wiped out 66 million years ago——恐龙是被灭绝来做"损失之大"的参照，录音从没说"地球曾被恐龙统治"，纯属听到dinosaurs 就想选的陷阱。借用原文： since the dinosaurs were wiped out 66 million years ago
C) 偷换概念Its prospects depend on future human behaviour. 说"地球前景取决于未来人类行为"，录音第 4 段虽提到 a window on the future，但那是讲项目能模型化未来，并非"许多科学家相信地球前景取决于人类未来行为"，把别处的零碎拼成新断言，无中生有。借用原文： a window on the past gives you a prospective model on the future
D) 原词陷阱Its climate change is aggravated by humans. 抓住录音 habitat loss, pollution and climate change 里的 climate change 单独放大，但原文是"栖息地丧失、污染、气候变化"三者并列、共同构成有毒组合，单拎一项当作"科学家相信地球如何"，以偏概全。借用原文： a toxic mix of habitat loss, pollution and climate change
questions.quote: Many scientists believe that earth has now entered the sixth mass extinction, with humans creating a toxic mix of habitat loss, pollution and climate change.

options.text: It was once dominated by dinosaurs.
It has entered the sixth mass extinction.
Its prospects depend on future human behaviour.
Its climate change is aggravated by humans.

questions.prompt: How does Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome, describe the Darwin Tree of Life Project?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （态度观点题）It is the most exciting, most relevant, most timely and most internationally inspirational.
**题目译文**
Wellcome科学主任Jim Smith爵士如何描述生命之树计划?
A) 它使地球上所有其他保护、保护和恢复生物多样性的努力都相形见绌。
B) 它启动成本高昂,需要数千名科学家的共同努力。
C) 它可以帮助恢复已经灭绝的大量动植物。
D) 它是最激动人心、最相关、最及时和最具国际启发性的。
**定位** Wellcome 科学总监 Jim Smith 爵士说："无论我怎么想，都想不出还有比这更激动人心、更切题、更及时、更具国际启发性的项目。"
**信号** 评价语气：I can't think of a more… 是变相最高级。答案句靠 I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project 这个"想不出更…的"否定结构锁定——"想不出比它更…的"等于"它是最…的"，是说话人对项目的最高评价。
**替换** I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project↔ It is the most exciting, most relevant, most timely and most internationally inspirational. "想不出更…的"="最…的"，比较级转最高级
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱It dwarfs all other efforts to conserve, protect and restore biodiversity on earth. 蹭了录音 conserve as well as protect and restore biodiversity 的原词，但说"它使其它一切保护努力相形见绌"是录音没有的比较，且这是 Jim Smith 的评价题，A 拼的是别处第 3 段的料，张冠李戴。借用原文： bolster efforts to conserve as well as protect and restore biodiversity
B) 答非所问It is costly to get started and requires the joint efforts of thousands of scientists. 蹭了录音 cost £100 million 与众多科学家协作的料，但这是讲项目的成本与规模，是客观事实，不是 Jim Smith"如何形容/评价"项目，答非所问。借用原文： it is expected to take 10 years and cost £100 million
C) 过度推断It can help to bring back the large numbers of plants and animals that have gone extinct. 用了录音常出现的"动植物灭绝"原词，但录音只说项目能助保护、记录生命，从没说能"把已灭绝物种带回来"，明显过度推断。借用原文： we desperately need to catalogue life on our fragile planet now
questions.quote: Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome, said, "Try as I might, I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project."

options.text: It dwarfs all other efforts to conserve, protect and restore biodiversity on earth.
It is costly to get started and requires the joint efforts of thousands of scientists.
It can help to bring back the large numbers of plants and animals that have gone extinct.
It is the most exciting, most relevant, most timely and most internationally inspirational.

questions.prompt: What is indeed just an illusion according to Professor Tom Oliver?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） Human individuality.
**题目译文**
根据Tom Oliver教授的观点,什么实际上只是一种幻觉?
A) 文化身份。
B) 社会演化。
C) 哥白尼革命。
D) 人类个体性。
**定位** 如今，一位英国学者声称，人的个体独立性其实只是一种幻觉，因为社会在心理、生理和文化层面上的相互联系远比人们意识到的紧密。
**信号** 原句直陈定性。答案句直接用 human individuality is indeed just an illusion 把某概念点定为"幻觉"，is just an illusion 这种判定句就是信号，听到"X 其实只是个幻觉"就锁定 X。
**替换** human individuality ↔ Human individuality.原词直接对应
questions.tip:
**排除**
C) 原词陷阱The Copernican revolution. 盗用了录音第二段反复出现的 Copernican，但哥白尼革命是讲者用来作类比的"参照"，不是被称为幻觉的对象，属听到 Copernican 就想选的原词陷阱。借用原文： the so-called Copernican Revolution
B) 原词陷阱Social evolution. 借了录音 the cultural evolution of human minds 里的 evolution 一词，但"社会／文化演化"是讲者描述心智发展的背景，并未被定性为幻觉。借用原文： A significant milestone in the cultural evolution of human minds
A) 偷换概念Cultural identity. 与录音 cultural level 的 cultural 沾边，但讲者说的是"文化层面的联系"，从未把"文化身份"称为幻觉，属偷换概念。借用原文： at a mental, physical, and cultural level
questions.quote: Now, a British academic has claimed that human individuality is indeed just an illusion, because societies are far more interconnected at a mental, physical, and cultural level than people realise.

options.text: Cultural identity.
Social evolution.
The Copernican revolution.
Human individuality.

questions.prompt: What does Professor Tom Oliver think of the idea that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （态度观点题） It is a delusion to be disposed of.
**题目译文**
Tom Oliver教授如何看待我们作为独立自我存在于主观宇宙中心这一观念?
A) 这是一种应当被摒弃的错觉。
B) 即使在学术界这种观念也很普遍。
C) 这是一个由John Donne的诗歌传播的谬误。
D) 这根植于17世纪的思维模式。
**定位** 然而，我们还有一个大迷思需要破除：即我们以为自己是独立的自我、处在一个主观宇宙的中心。
**信号** 转折However后是真意。句首 However 转折之后才是讲者真正要表达的态度，他把那个想法称为 one more big myth to dispose of（又一个要破除的迷思），处置动词 dispose of直接给出否定态度。
**替换** one more big myth to dispose of↔a delusion to be disposed of myth=delusion同义替换
questions.tip:
**排除**
D) 原词陷阱rooted in the mindset of the 17th century 盗用了录音开头 wrote in the 17th century的时间词，但 17 世纪说的是 John Donne 写诗的年代，讲者从未说那个"独立自我"的想法植根于 17 世纪心态，属原词陷阱。借用原文： wrote in the 17th century
C) 张冠李戴a myth spread by John Donne's poem 把"迷思"归因到 John Donne 的诗，盗用了开头出现的 John Donne，但讲者引 Donne 的诗恰恰是支持"人互相连接"，并非说这首诗散布了迷思，属张冠李戴。借用原文： every man is a piece of the continent, a part of the main
B) 未提及prevalent even among academics（连学者中都很普遍）原文从未提及，讲者只说这是普遍的 illusion，没有专门强调"在学者中尤其普遍"，属未提及。
questions.quote: However, we have one more big myth to dispose of: that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe.

options.text: It is a delusion to be disposed of.
It is prevalent even among academics.
It is a myth spread by John Donne's poem.
It is rooted in the mindset of the 17th century.

questions.prompt: Why does Professor Tom Oliver claim that the material "us" is constantly changing?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） He contends most of our body cells can only live a few days or weeks.
**题目译文**
为什么Tom Oliver教授声称物质层面的"我们"在不断变化?
A) 他信奉哥白尼关于宇宙的哲学学说。
B) 他在Reading大学获得了充分的科学证据。
C) 他发现我们的内在自我与物质自我是相互关联的。
D) 他认为我们身体的大部分细胞只能存活几天或几周。
**定位** 奥利弗教授指出，人体内约有37万亿个细胞，但大多数细胞的寿命只有几天或几周，因此物质意义上的"我们"在不断变化。
**信号** 因果so前是原因。句中 so the material "us" is constantly changing 的 so 是结果标志，so 之前的 most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks 就是讲者给出的原因，正是Why 题要找的依据句。
**替换** most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks ↔most of our body cells can only live a few days or weeks lifespan改写为can only live
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱ample scientific evidence at the University of Reading 盗用了录音第一段介绍学者时的the University of Reading，但那只是说明他的任职单位，原文从未说他在该校获得了大量科学证据，属原词陷阱。借用原文： Professor Tom Oliver, a researcher in the Ecology and Evolution group at the University of Reading
A) 答非所问He believes in Copernican philosophical doctrines about the universe. 又借Copernican 一词，但本题问的是"物质之我为何在变"，答案是细胞寿命，与哥白尼无关，属答非所问。借用原文： Just as Copernicus realised the Earth is not the centre of the universe
C) 偷换概念He has found that our inner self and material self are interconnected. 听上去与全篇"互相连接"主旨呼应，但原文并未以"内在自我与物质自我相连"来解释物质之我为何变化，是偷换概念、答非所问。借用原文： We are intimately connected to the world around us.
questions.quote: Professor Oliver argues there are around 37 trillion cells in the body but most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks, so the material "us" is constantly changing.

options.text: He believes in Copernican philosophical doctrines about the universe.
He has gained ample scientific evidence at the University of Reading.
He has found that our inner self and material self are interconnected.
He contends most of our body cells can only live a few days or weeks.

questions.prompt: How can we solve pressing environmental and societal problems according to Professor Tom Oliver?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） By becoming aware that we are part of a bigger world.
**题目译文**
根据Tom Oliver教授的观点,我们如何才能解决紧迫的环境和社会问题?
A) 通过认识到这些问题已经变得多么具有破坏性。
B) 通过意识到我们都可以在这些努力中尽自己的一份力。
C) 通过认识到我们是更大世界的一部分。
D) 通过坚决而持续地共同努力。
**定位** 奥利弗教授声称，个人主义其实对社会有害，只有意识到我们是更大整体的一部分，我们才能解决紧迫的环境与社会问题。
**信号** only by引出唯一途径。句中 only by realising we are part of a bigger entity 用 only by引出唯一解决途径，only by 这种限定条件结构是答案信号，听到"只有……才能解决……"就锁定 by 后面的办法。
**替换** realising we are part of a bigger entity↔becoming aware that we are part of a bigger world entity改写为world
questions.tip:
**排除**
D) 未提及By making joint efforts resolutely and persistently（坚定持久地共同努力）听上去正确且积极，但原文给的办法是"意识到自己属于更大整体"，并未说靠"坚定持久的共同努力"，属未提及的正确话陷阱。
B) 偷换概念By realising that we all can do our own bit in such endeavours（意识到人人能尽一份力）借了 realising 一词，但原文 realising 后接的是"我们是更大整体的一部分"，不是"人人能尽一份力"，属偷换概念。借用原文： only by realising we are part of a bigger entity
A) 未提及By coming to see how disruptive such problems have got to be（认清这些问题有多具破坏性）原文并未把"看清问题严重"作为解决之道，讲者给的解法是意识到自己属于更大整体，属未提及。
questions.quote: Professor Oliver claims that individualism is actually bad for society, and only by realising we are part of a bigger entity can we solve pressing environmental and societal problems.

options.text: By coming to see how disruptive such problems have got to be.
By realising that we all can do our own bit in such endeavours.
By becoming aware that we are part of a bigger world.
By making joint efforts resolutely and persistently.

transcriptTranslations: 谢谢你这么短时间内就和我见面，Stephen。
没问题，Margaret。现在，请给我一些好消息吧。你同意我上次的提案了吗？
我确实同意了。我希望签署这份协议，只需要对合同做一个小小的修改。
Margaret，我们为这事来来回回、反复修改已经快一年了。你到底确定要不要为你的客户做这个赞助协议？我这么问是因为，坦白说，我这边有些人已经失去耐心了。
我理解你的担忧。但我相信你也明白，我们把客户的最佳利益放在首位。因此我们会仔细审查所有合同的细节，请放心，我们都很感激贵公司的耐心。
好吧，行。那你想做什么修改？
基本上，我们希望新协议把中东地区排除在外。就这样。
中东？为什么？
我的客户有几个来自中东公司的其他潜在营销协议。这些协议如果成交的话，将专门在中东地区使用我客户的形象。因此，为了避免任何冲突，我们需要确保两个营销活动在地理上不重叠。
我们这里说的中东是哪个行业？
房地产。
那应该没问题。只要产品与我们的食品饮料市场有很大不同，就不会有利益冲突。不过，我还是得让我的人过一遍。我预计不会有什么问题。中东对我们来说是个微不足道的市场，但我仍然需要和几个部门确认一下。
接下来，我们有一条特别的科学相关新闻。Paula Hancocks 在 Denver 天文台。Paula，那边有什么大新闻？
嗨，John。是的，这里现场的所有天文学家都非常兴奋。事实上，整个北美和北半球其他地区的太空爱好者今晚都会聚集在山顶上观看夜空。
为什么？有什么大事件吗？是不是很快有日食发生？
今晚，地球将与 Oppenheimer 彗星近距离接触。这是我们的星球在一百多年来与这种现象最接近的一次。因此，预计今晚将有成千上万的人仰望天空，以观看这个令人敬畏的天体。
这颗彗星有多远？人们能用肉眼看到它吗？
Oppenheimer 彗星仍将在数百万英里之外，在我们银河系的边缘。但尽管如此，这是一个相对较近的距离，近到足以让人们通过望远镜详细观察。没有望远镜的话，人们只能看到一个模糊的影像。不过，这并不意味着需要专业设备。即使是最普通的望远镜也应该足以让人们观察并惊叹于这个飞行的天体。
我们的许多观众会想知道他们如何也能参与这个千载难逢的事件。这颗彗星会在天空的什么位置？人们怎么找到它？
这颗彗星几乎正好在正北方，在赤道上方 60 度。不过，找到这颗彗星确实非常棘手。这里的科学家告诉我，有很多手机应用程序可以帮助实现这一点。
太棒了！谢谢你，Paula，提供这些信息。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say she will do?

**答案** B （细节题） Sign the agreement if one small change is made to it.
**题目译文**
女士说她将做什么?
A) 在短时间内回复男士的最新提议。
B) 如果对协议做一处小的修改就签署协议。
C) 在会议上为她的客户达成一项赞助协议。

**定位** 女：我确实同意了。而且我希望签署这份协议，前提是合同里做一处小改动。
**信号** 被问者的直接应答 + I wish to 表态。上一句男方问 Have you agreed to my last proposal?，女方紧接着应答 I have, indeed. And I wish to sign the agreement pending one small change，这句既是被问者的直接回应，又含 I wish to 的明确表态，正是答案句。

D) 原词陷阱D 的 Give the man some good news regarding the contract. 盗了男方那句 please give me some good news，那是男方的请求 / 期待，女方并没说 "我要给你好消息"，她说的是愿意签约。借用原文： please give me some good news

**题目译文**

A) 他们正变得不耐烦。
B) 他们担心时间不多了。
C) 他们习惯于做出修改。
D) 他们关注细节。
**定位** 男：我之所以这么问，是因为坦白说，我这边有些人快没耐心了。
**信号** 因果 because 后给出他对己方人员的真实描述。他用 because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience，because 引出对 "我这边的人" 的实情描述，frankly（坦白说）更是加重语气的强调信号，这句就是答案句。
**替换** running out of patience↔ becoming impatient running out of patience = impatient，同义改写
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱B 的 time is running out 盗用了录音 running out of patience 里的 running out，却把宾语偷换成 time。录音里耗尽的是耐心，不是时间，B 在 running out 后面动了手脚。借用原文： running out of patience
C) 答非所问C 的 used to making alterations 取自录音 making alterations，但那是男方说双方 "这一年来回改来改去" 的背景，不是在描述 "我方那些人现在什么状态"，答非所问。借用原文： we've been through this for almost a year now, back and forth, making alterations
D) 张冠李戴D 的 concerned about the details 实际对应女方后面说的 We therefore comb through the fine details of all contracts，那是女方一边推敲细节，与男方所说 "我那边的人没耐心" 是两拨人、两回事。借用原文： We therefore comb through the fine details of all contracts
questions.quote: M: I ask this, because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience.

options.text: They are becoming impatient.
They are afraid time is running out.
They are used to making alterations.
They are concerned about the details.

questions.prompt: What reason does the woman give for the new deal to exclude the Middle East?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） To avoid any conflict of interest.
**题目译文**
女士给出了什么理由说明新协议要排除中东地区?
A) 为了防止地域歧视。
B) 为了开拓食品和饮料市场。
C) 为了避免任何利益冲突。
D) 为了减少不公平竞争。
**定位** 女：因此，为了避免任何冲突，我们需要确保两个营销活动在地域上不重叠。
**信号** in order to / therefore 双因果信号引出真目的。她先讲客户在中东另有营销意向，再用Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically，therefore 与 in order to 双双标出这是给理由的句子，正是答案句。
**替换** in order to avoid any conflict↔To avoid any conflict of interest. avoid any conflict 与选项几乎原义对应both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically↔ conflict of interest两活动地域不重叠 = 不产生利益冲突
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱A 的 To prevent geographical discrimination. 蹭了录音 overlap geographically 里的geographically，造出 "地域歧视"。原文讲的是两个营销活动地域别重叠，与 "歧视" 毫不相干，是借词造假。借用原文： both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically
B) 答非所问B 的 To tap the food and beverage market. 用了录音 our food and beverage market，但那是男方在第12段说自家所属行业，与女方排除中东的理由无关；她的理由是避免冲突，不是去开发某市场。借用原文： So long as the product is very different from our food and beverage market
D) 未提及D 的 To reduce unfair competition. 听着像商务套话，但录音通篇没说要减少不公平竞争，她讲的是避免客户形象在同一地域撞车的利益冲突，competition 一词原文压根没出现。
questions.quote: W: Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically.

options.text: To prevent geographical discrimination.
To tap the food and beverage market.
To avoid any conflict of interest.
To reduce unfair competition.

questions.prompt: What does the man say about the Middle East?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） It is a negligible market for his company.
**题目译文**
男士关于中东地区说了什么?
A) 它是食品和饮料的潜在市场。
B) 它对房地产开发商很有吸引力。
C) 对他的公司来说它是一个微不足道的市场。
D) 它与其他市场非常不同。
**定位** 男：中东对我们来说是个可以忽略的市场，不过我还是得跟几个部门核实一下。
**信号** 他对中东的直接评价句 + 形容词 negligible。他直说 The Middle East is a negligible market for us，主系表结构直接给出评价形容词 negligible，是对中东的正面定性句，正是答案句；后半 but 起的只是补充程序，不改这句评价。
**替换** a negligible market for us ↔ a negligible market for his company for us = for his company，几乎原义
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反A 的 It is a potential market for food and beverage. 把中东说成 "有潜力"，与他原话 a negligible market（可忽略）正好相反；food and beverage 又是蹭了他讲己方行业的熟词，双重误导。借用原文： The Middle East is a negligible market for us
B) 张冠李戴B 的 It is very attractive for real estate developers. 借了女方说的中东 Real estate，但那是女方客户在中东另有房地产营销意向，并非男方对中东市场的评价，张冠李戴。借用原文： Real estate
D) 偷换概念D 的 It is very different from other markets. 盗用了 the product is very different from our food and beverage market 里的 very different，但原文说的是 "产品" 与食饮市场不同，不是说 "中东市场" 与别的市场不同，主语被偷换。借用原文： So long as the product is very different from our food and beverage market
questions.quote: M: The Middle East is a negligible market for us, but I still need to check this with a couple of departments.

options.text: It is a potential market for food and beverage.
It is very attractive for real estate developers.
It is a negligible market for his company.
It is very different from other markets.

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about all the astronomers at the Denver Observatory?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） They are thrilled by a rare astronomic phenomenon.
**题目译文**
关于丹佛天文台的所有天文学家,这位女士说了什么?
A) 他们对一种罕见的天文现象感到兴奋。
B) 他们正在山顶庆祝一个重大事件。
C) 他们对与科学相关的重大新闻充满热情。
D) 北美各地的天文学家都加入了他们。
**定位** 是的，在这里现场的所有天文学家都非常兴奋。
**信号** 被问者的直接应答。男士在 what is the big story over there? 抛出问题，女士开口第一句all the astronomers on site here are very excited 就是直接应答，对话题的答案落在回答方，这句即落点。
**替换** all the astronomers on site here are very excited↔They are thrilled by a rare astronomic phenomenon. excited 同义改写为 thrilled
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 张冠李戴录音 congregating on mountain tops 确实念到"山顶"，但那是"聚集去观星"，不是celebrating a big event on mountain tops 的"在山顶庆祝"，且主语是北美各地爱好者，非天文台的天文学家。借用原文： congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night's sky
C) 原词陷阱开头 a special science-related news story 念到"科学相关"，C 项 enthusiastic about big science-related stories 直接搬这串词，但录音说的是天文学家"为这次天象兴奋"，不是"热衷各种科学新闻故事"，把对一次具体天象的兴奋偷换成对科学故事的泛泛热衷。借用原文： a special science-related news story
D) 张冠李戴录音 space enthusiasts all across North America 说的是"北美各地的爱好者要聚集"，D项 joined by astronomers all across North America 把它改成"天文台的天文学家被北美各地天文学家加入"，主语和事件都被偷换，原文没有这层意思。借用原文： space enthusiasts all across North America and the rest of the Northern Hemisphere will be congregating
questions.quote: Yes, all the astronomers on site here are very excited.

options.text: They are thrilled by a rare astronomic phenomenon.
They are celebrating a big event on mountain tops.
They are enthusiastic about big science-related stories.
They are joined by astronomers all across North America.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the conversation about the Oppenheimer comet?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） It will come closest to Earth in more than one hundred years.
**题目译文**
从对话中我们了解到关于Oppenheimer彗星的什么信息?
A) 它将是一个多世纪以来同类中最壮观的。
B) 它将在一百多年来最接近地球。
C) 它将使人类历史上许多其他此类事件黯然失色。
D) 从丹佛的山顶将最清楚地看到它。
**定位** 今晚，地球将与奥本海默彗星近距离接近。这是一百多年来我们的星球离这样一种天象最近的一次。
**信号** 正面定性句 + 时间数字。女士直接给彗星定性 It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years，"closest…in over 100 years" 把"距离最近"和"百年"绑在一起，是带数字的定性句，正是答案落点。
**替换** the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years↔It will come closest to Earth in more than one hundred years.主被动对调 + 数字同义
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱录音后文 this formidable object 确有 "formidable"，A 项 the most formidable of its kind in over a century 便把"百年"嫁接到"最厉害"上；但原文里"百年"修饰的是"距离最近"，从没说它是百年来"最厉害"的，是把数字按到了错的形容词上。借用原文： in order to see this formidable object
C) 过度推断eclipse many other such events in human history 借"eclipse"（此处作动词"使相形见绌"）和前文 Is there an eclipse happening soon? 的"日食"玩文字游戏，原文从没说这颗彗星"使人类历史上其他天象相形见绌"，属凭空拔高。借用原文： Is there an eclipse happening soon?
D) 原词陷阱seen most clearly from Denver's mountain tops 把前文 the Denver Observatory的"丹佛"和 mountain tops 的"山顶"拼到一起，但原文只说爱好者会聚到山顶观星，从没说"从丹佛的山顶看得最清楚"，是把零散原词攒成一句没说过的话。借用原文： congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night's sky
questions.quote: Tonight, the Earth will come into close proximity with the Oppenheimer comet. It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years.

options.text: It will be the most formidable of its kind in over a century.
It will come closest to Earth in more than one hundred years.
It will eclipse many other such events in human history.
It will be seen most clearly from Denver's mountain tops.

questions.prompt: What does the woman say people will only see in the sky without a telescope?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） blur.
**题目译文**
这位女士说人们在没有望远镜的情况下在天空中只能看到什么?
A) 模糊的影像。
B) 星星。
C) 我们星系的边缘。
D) 一个普通的飞行物体。
**定位** 没有望远镜的话，人们只会看到模糊的一团。
**信号** 条件 without one + only 直陈。这句用 without one（one 指代上文 telescope）锁定"不用望远镜"的前提，再用 only see a blur 直说看到什么，前提和结果都摆明，是答案句。
**替换** People will only see a blur without one↔blur.原句直取，前提一致
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 未提及录音通篇没说不用望远镜会看到"星星"，Stars. 是凭"看星空"的常识脑补出来的，原文只说看到"一团模糊"。
C) 原词陷阱on the edge of our galaxy 念到"星系边缘"，但那是说彗星"所在的位置"，不是"不用望远镜看到的东西"，C 项 The edge of our galaxy. 把"它在哪"偷换成"看到什么"。借用原文： The Oppenheimer comet will still be millions of miles away, on the edge of our galaxy
D) 与原文相反wonder at this flying object 念到 "flying object"，但那是"用普通望远镜能观赏到的彗星"，D 项 An ordinary flying object. 把它挪到"不用望远镜"的前提下——条件正好反了，不用望远镜只见模糊团，看不清是个"飞行物"。借用原文： Even the most ordinary of telescopes should be conducive for people to observe and wonder at this flying object
questions.quote: People will only see a blur without one.

options.text: blur.
Stars.
The edge of our galaxy.
An ordinary flying object.

questions.prompt: What do scientists at the Denver Observatory advise amateurs do to facilitate their observation?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） Make use of phone apps.
**题目译文**
丹佛天文台的科学家们建议业余爱好者做什么来便于他们的观测?
A) 使用专业设备。
B) 爬到附近的高处。
C) 将目光固定在正北方。
D) 使用手机应用程序。
**定位** 这里的科学家告诉我，有很多手机应用程序可以帮上这个忙。
**信号** 建议句 + 与题干同词 facilitate。女士转述科学家的建议 there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this，"scientists…told me"对应题干的"scientists advise"，"facilitate"与题干 facilitate their observation 同词，是答案句。
**替换** there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this↔Make use of phone apps.存在句 → 祈使建议
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反录音 that does not mean one needs professional equipment 明确说"并不需要专业设备"，A 项 Use professional equipment. 直接搬这串原词却把否定改成肯定，意思正好反了。借用原文： that does not mean one needs professional equipment
B) 原词陷阱录音 congregating on mountain tops 念到"山顶"，B 项 Climb to the nearby heights.（爬到附近高处）借此设套，但那是说爱好者去哪儿聚集，不是科学家"为方便观测给的建议"，问的根本不是同一件事。借用原文： will be congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night's sky
C) 原词陷阱录音 The comet will be almost exactly due north 念到"正北"，那是在说彗星"在天上的位置"，C 项 Fix their eyes due north. 把"它在正北方"偷换成"建议人们眼睛盯着正北"，而科学家给的方便观测的办法是用 app，不是"盯着北方"。借用原文： The comet will be almost exactly due north, at 60 degrees above the equator
questions.quote: And scientists here have told me there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this.

options.text: Use professional equipment.
Climb to the nearby heights.
Fix their eyes due north.
Make use of phone apps.

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Climate scientists predict that many parts of the world will be increasingly prone to floods.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: This is a serious risk to human lives and property.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: So understanding and accurately forecasting flood risks is a key challenge for vulnerable cities around the globe.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: It uses a smartphone app to collect the data of ordinary citizens during high tides.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: He'll use those data to validate and improve his mathematical flooding model, called TideWatch.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcriptTranslations: 有许多因素影响我们的健康。这些因素包括我们的财务状况、情绪以及工作方式。教育就是其中一个因素。研究表明，较高的教育水平可以带来更好的健康状况，甚至更长的寿命。但配偶的教育水平又如何呢?新的研究试图回答这个问题。研究人员使用了一项纵向研究的数据。这些数据来自1957年首次对高中毕业生进行的调查。调查于2011年结束。研究团队发现,配偶教育水平较高的人往往报告健康状况更好。在调整其他因素后,这一情况依然成立,这些因素包括参与者自身的教育水平、社会背景以及婚前婚后的健康状况。作者认为,高教育水平提供了共享的社会、智力、情感和财务资源。这些包括更高水平的情商、特定技能或知识,或者更多的金钱。研究人员承认,个人自身的教育水平对其健康显然很重要,但他们断言,个人也可以从配偶的教育中获益。值得注意的是,这种影响因性别而异。对女性而言,健康状况与配偶教育水平的相关性比男性更密切。研究团队认为这可能与研究的时间段有关。该样本中的女性教育水平和职业成就均低于男性。研究人员的假设是,这使得丈夫的资源更有可能产生共享影响。

气候科学家预测，世界许多地区将越来越容易发生洪水。这对人类生命和财产构成严重威胁。因此，了解并准确预测洪水风险是全球脆弱城市面临的关键挑战。2017年，弗吉尼亚海洋科学研究所的Derek Loftis启动了一个名为Catch the King的项目。该项目使用智能手机应用程序在涨潮期间收集普通公民的数据。他将使用这些数据来验证和改进他的数学洪水模型TideWatch。Loftis的使命是在水到达之前就知道水会流向哪里。但收集必要的数据并足够快地处理这些信息以做出可用的预测绝非易事。准确的洪水预测需要了解实地情况。到21世纪初，超级计算技术已经足够先进，科学家们可以将天气预报模型与此类测量数据相结合。但他们仍然没有实时预测快速移动洪水这一至关重要的能力。因此，在2017年，Loftis及其同事在弗吉尼亚州诺福克这个洪水风险社区设置了一组28个联网水位传感器。新传感器将关于水位高度和流动的粗略测量数据传输到弗吉尼亚研究所的计算机。除了这些传感器，数百名当地居民拍摄涨潮照片并将其实时传输到研究所。科学家们希望这些公民收集的数据能够帮助提高准确预测破坏性洪水发生时间和地点的能力。

questions.prompt: What does research suggest about a higher level of education?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） It can enable us to live a healthier and longer life.
**题目译文**
研究表明较高的教育水平会带来什么?
A) 它可以影响我们的心境和情绪。
B) 它可以使我们过上更健康、更长寿的生活。
C) 它可以显著改善我们的经济状况。
D) 它可以帮助我们取得更好的工作表现。
**定位** 研究表明，更高的教育水平能带来更好的健康状况，甚至更长的寿命。
**信号** 题干原词在原文的复现句。录音里 Research suggests that higher levels of education 几乎逐字复述了题干 What does research suggest about a higher level of education 的措辞，这种'题干怎么问、原文就怎么开头'的句子就是答案句，紧跟其后的 can lead to better health and even greater longevity 即为结论。
**替换** better health and even greater longevity↔live a healthier and longer life名词换成形容词、同义改写
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱录音开头确实念到 our emotions，但那是在列举'影响健康的诸多因素'时提到的，并非说'教育能影响情绪'。选项 have an impact on our moods and emotions 把这个原词搬来，答的却不是题干问的'教育带来什么'。借用原文： our finances, our emotions and the way we work
C) 原词陷阱录音里 our finances 同样只是被列为'影响健康的因素'之一，原文从未说'教育能显著改善财务'。选项 improve our financial status significantly 借 finances 这个原词设套，与题干所问无关。借用原文： our finances, our emotions and the way we work
D) 原词陷阱录音说 the way we work 是影响健康的因素之一，并未说'教育能带来更好的工作表现'。选项 achieve better work performance 用 work 这个原词制造熟悉感，但属无中生有。借用原文： the way we work
questions.quote: Research suggests that higher levels of education can lead to better health and even greater longevity.

options.text: It can have an impact on our moods and emotions.
It can enable us to live a healthier and longer life.
It can improve our financial status significantly.
It can help us achieve better work performance.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the finding of the new research?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） The spouse's level of education can impact one's health.
**题目译文**
我们从这项新研究的发现中了解到什么?
A) 一个人的健康状况在婚前和婚后往往有所不同。
B) 一个人的健康状况与其社会背景有关。
C) 配偶越富有,一个人就越健康。
D) 配偶的教育水平可以影响一个人的健康。
**定位** 研究团队发现，配偶受教育水平更高的人，往往报告自己的健康状况更好。
**信号** The team found 引出研究结论。The team found that 是典型的'结论引导句'，篇章里凡以'研究团队发现……'开头的话，几乎必是某道题的答案句；其后整句就是这项新研究的核心发现。
**替换** a person whose spouse had a higher level of education tended to report better health↔The spouse's level of education can impact one's health'配偶教育高→健康好'概括为'配偶教育影响健康'
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱录音里 health status before and after marriage 是作者明确列出的'被调整掉的其他因素'之一，意在说'即便排除它结论依然成立'，根本不是研究发现。选项 One's health tends to differ before and after marriage 反把这个被排除项当成结论。借用原文： adjusting for other factors, such as participants' own education, social background and health status before and after marriage
B) 原词陷阱social background 与上一项一样，是被作者 adjusting for 排除掉的干扰因素，原文没说'健康与社会背景有关'是新发现。选项 One's health status is related to one's social background 把被排除项伪装成结论。借用原文： adjusting for other factors, such as participants' own education, social background and health status before and after marriage
C) 偷换概念研究讲的是配偶'教育'影响健康，C 却说 The wealthier one's spouse is, the healthier one becomes，把'教育'偷换成'财富'。虽然录音后文提到教育能带来 more money 等资源，但那是教育的衍生好处，原文从未把'配偶越富→本人越健康'立为结论。借用原文： more money
questions.quote: The team found that a person whose spouse had a higher level of education tended to report better health.

options.text: One's health tends to differ before and after marriage.
One's health status is related to one's social background.
The wealthier one's spouse is, the healthier one becomes.
The spouse's level of education can impact one's health.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about the men in the sample of the new research?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） They had more education than their spouses.
**题目译文**
文章关于新研究样本中的男性说了什么?
A) 他们从自己的职业成就中受益匪浅。
B) 他们对配偶的职业表现出兴趣。
C) 他们与配偶有很多共同点。
D) 他们比配偶受过更多教育。
**定位** 该样本中的女性，其受教育水平和职业成就都低于男性。
**信号** 比较句 lower…than the men 反推男性更高。答案句以女性为主语作比较——Women in this sample had lower levels of education…than the men，说女性教育水平低于男性，等于反过来说男性教育水平高于女性。问 men 的题，答案藏在'拿 women 跟 men 比'的这句里，需做一次方向反推。
**替换** Women in this sample had lower levels of education…than the men↔They had more education than their spouses'女低于男'与'男多于女'肯否方向对调、等值
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱录音 lower occupational achievements 里确有 achievements 一词，但它是用来说女性'职业成就低'的，并没说男性'从事业成就中获益良多'。选项 benefited a lot from their career achievements 借 achievements 设套，且把描述对象错安到'获益'这一原文没有的意思上。借用原文： lower occupational achievements
B) 原词陷阱录音里与 occupation 沾边的只有 occupational achievements，原文从未说男性'对配偶的职业感兴趣'。选项 showed interest in their spouse's occupations 用 occupations 这个原词凑出一个原文没有的行为。借用原文： lower occupational achievements
C) 与原文相反原文恰恰在讲男女'教育与职业成就有差距'（女性更低），而 They had much in common with their spouses 说男性'与配偶有很多共同点'，方向正好相反，原文也根本没提共同点。
questions.quote: Women in this sample had lower levels of education and lower occupational achievements than the men.

options.text: They benefited a lot from their career achievements.
They showed interest in their spouse's occupations.
They had much in common with their spouses.
They had more education than their spouses.

questions.prompt: What is said to be a key challenge for cities prone to floods?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） Forecasting flood risks accurately.
**题目译文**
据说对于易发洪水的城市而言，一个关键挑战是什么?
A) 消除洪水的根本原因。
B) 准确预测洪水风险。
C) 识别城市的地质特征。
D) 找出不断变化的气候模式。
**定位** 因此，理解并准确预报洪水风险，对全球易受灾的城市来说是一项关键挑战。
**信号** 原句直接出现 key challenge。这句直接含题干核心名词 a key challenge for vulnerable cities around the globe，且前面有 So 引出结论，是明确的答案句信号——题干名词在录音里几乎原样出现的那一句，就是落点。
**替换** accurately forecasting flood risks↔Forecasting flood risks accurately同词换序，意思全等
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及Eliminating their root cause 谈"消除洪水的根源"，录音通篇讲的是"理解和预报"风险，从未提到消除根源，属凭常识臆想的方向。
C) 答非所问Identifying the cities' geological features 说挑战是"识别城市地质特征"，录音里challenge 后面跟的是"预报洪水风险"，根本没提地质特征，方向被岔开。
D) 原词陷阱Finding out the changing climate patterns 借了录音开头 Climate scientists predict 里的 climate 制造熟耳感，但那只是引出背景的"气候科学家预测"，挑战并非"弄清气候模式变化"，是典型听到原词就想选的陷阱。
questions.quote: So understanding and accurately forecasting flood risks is a key challenge for vulnerable cities around the globe.

options.text: Eliminating their root cause.
Forecasting flood risks accurately.
Identifying the cities' geological features.
Finding out the changing climate patterns.

questions.prompt: For what purpose does Derek Loftis collect the data of ordinary citizens during high tides?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （目的题） To improve his mathematical flooding model.
**题目译文**
Derek Loftis在大潮期间收集普通市民的数据是出于什么目的?
A) 验证他关于洪水严重程度的假设。
B) 确定引发洪水的大潮发生频率。
C) 改进他的洪水数学模型。
D) 了解他的洪水项目的可行性。
**定位** 他将用这些数据去验证并改进他那个名为 TideWatch 的数学洪水模型。
**信号** use those data to 引出目的。这句的 use those data to validate and improve his mathematical flooding model 正是目的信号 use… to…，to 后面的动作就是采集数据的目的，是答案句无疑。
**替换** improve his mathematical flooding model ↔ To improve his mathematical flooding model几乎原句对应
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱To validate his hypothesis about the gravity of floods 借了录音原词 validate and improve，但录音 validate 的宾语是"数学洪水模型"，不是"关于洪水严重性的假设"——盗了动词、换了宾语。
B) 原词陷阱To determine the frequency of high tides causing floods 盗用 high tides，但录音里high tides 是"采集数据的时机"，目的并非"测高潮致洪的频率"，把时间状语硬说成目的。
D) 未提及To see the feasibility of his project on flooding 说目的是"看项目可行性"，录音从未提feasibility 或"看可行性"，纯属添加。
questions.quote: He'll use those data to validate and improve his mathematical flooding model, called TideWatch.

options.text: To validate his hypothesis about the gravity of floods.
To determine the frequency of high tides causing floods.
To improve his mathematical flooding model.
To see the feasibility of his project on flooding.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say is Derek Loftis's mission?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） To forecast rapid floods in real time.
**题目译文**
文章说Derek Loftis的使命是什么?
A) 研究大潮对洪水淹没地区的后果。
B) 教当地市民如何收集即将到来的洪水的数据。
C) 实时预报快速洪水。
D) 对处理过的洪水数据进行分类。
**定位** Loftis 的使命是：在水流到某处之前，就知道它会去哪里。……但他们仍不具备实时预报快速移动洪水这一至关重要的能力。
**信号** mission is to + 后文同义解释。信号句 Loftis's mission is to know where the water goes before it goes there 直接点出使命；它较抽象，录音随后用 forecast fast-moving floods in real time 把这一使命具体化，两处合起来锁定答案。
**替换** to know where the water goes before it goes there↔To forecast rapid floods in real time形象说法换成专业说法forecast fast-moving floods in real time↔To forecast rapid floods in real time fast-moving=rapid，近义词替换
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱To study the consequences of high tides on flooded areas 借了录音的 high tides，但录音说的使命是"实时预报"，不是"研究高潮对淹没区的后果"，study consequences 是录音没有的动作。
B) 张冠李戴To teach local citizens how to collect data of incoming floods 盗用 citizens、collect data，但录音是"市民帮他采数据"，从没说他的使命是"教市民怎么采数据"——角色与动作都被偷换。
D) 原词陷阱To classify the flooding data processed 借了录音 processing that information 里的"处理数据"概念，但录音从没说使命是"给处理过的洪水数据分类"，classify 是凭空添加的动作。
questions.quote: Loftis's mission is to know where the water goes before it goes there. ... But they still didn't have the critically important ability to forecast fast-moving floods in real time.

options.text: To study the consequences of high tides on flooded areas.
To teach local citizens how to collect data of incoming floods.
To forecast rapid floods in real time.
To classify the flooding data processed.

questions.prompt: What did Loftis and his colleagues do to obtain data about water height and movement?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） They set up Internet-connected water-level sensors.
**题目译文**
Loftis和他的同事们做了什么来获取有关水位高度和水流运动的数据?
A) 他们安装了联网的水位传感器。
B) 他们用摄像机追踪涨潮情况。
C) 他们使用了新开发的超级计算设施。
D) 他们现场观察水流方向。
**定位** 于是，2017 年，Loftis 和同事们在弗吉尼亚州诺福克的涝灾社区各处架设了一组共 28 个联网水位传感器。这些新传感器把关于水位高度和水流移动的粗略测量数据传回弗吉尼亚研究所的一台计算机。
**信号** set up sensors + 紧跟 water height and movement。答案句信号是动作动词 set up a group of 28 Internet-connected water-level sensors，紧接着下一句出现题干的对象词water height and movement，两句锁死"靠装传感器拿水位数据"。
**替换** set up a group of 28 Internet-connected water-level sensors ↔They set up Internet-connected water-level sensors略去数量，核心动作器材全留
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 偷换概念They tracked the rising tides with video-cameras 看似对应录音 take photos of rising tides，但那是"市民用（手机）拍照"，不是"用 video-cameras 追踪"，且这是采图片、不是题干问的"水位与水流"数据，器材和数据类型都被换。
C) 原词陷阱They used newly-developed supercomputing facilities 借了录音 supercomputing had advanced，但录音说超算是用来"整合天气预报模型"的背景能力，不是他们获取水位数据的手段，原词被搬错了位置。
D) 未提及They observed the direction of water flow on the spot 说他们"实地观察水流方向"，录音获取水流靠的是传感器测量，从没说"实地肉眼观察方向"，属添加动作。
questions.quote: So, in 2017, Loftis and colleagues set up a group of 28 Internet-connected water-level sensors throughout the flood risk community of Norfolk, Virginia. The new sensors relayed rough measurements about water height and movement to a computer at the Virginia Institute.

options.text: They set up Internet-connected water-level sensors.
They tracked the rising tides with video-cameras.
They used newly-developed supercomputing facilities.
They observed the direction of water flow on the spot.

transcriptTranslations: Kate Atkinson 于1951年出生于英格兰约克郡。她努力获得了作为作家的资历。她在苏格兰的大学学习英国文学。1974年毕业后,她研究了美国文学博士学位。后来,她在毕业的大学任教,并于1981年开始写短篇小说。1986年赢得Woman's Own短篇小说大赛后,她开始为女性杂志撰稿。她的第一部小说《博物馆幕后》赢得了1995年英国年度图书奖。这本书以约克郡为背景,已被改编为广播剧、舞台剧和电视剧。她为爱丁堡的一家剧院创作了两部戏剧——第一部名为《Nice》,第二部是《Abandonment》,于2000年8月作为爱丁堡艺术节的一部分上演。

无论Atkinson写什么体裁,她的书都触及爱与失去以及如何继续前行的主题。它们总是以巧妙和邪恶的幽默感呈现。她的书往往充斥着古怪、有时有罪且通常有缺陷的怪人,这些人物因被如此充分地刻画而变得可信。她的书经常被描述为风俗喜剧。也就是说,这种喜剧再现了时尚社交圈中流行的复杂而精致的行为准则,在那里外表比真正的道德品格更重要。风俗喜剧倾向于奖励其聪明和狡诈的角色,而不是惩罚他们的恶行。风俗喜剧的幽默依赖于言辞机智和戏谑的调侃。

为什么适应能力是职场中需要锻炼的一项重要技能？简单来说，适应能力是雇主越来越看重的一项技能。当你花时间学习一项新任务而不是抗拒它时，你的生产力就会提高。你还可以为那些可能在适应方面遇到困难的同事树立榜样，并帮助引领你的团队前进。战略顾问Dorie Clark这样向我们解释。"我认为适应能力在职场中是一项重要技能，因为坦率地说，环境会变化。竞争对手推出新产品,经济可能陷入衰退,客户偏好随时间而变化,等等。如果你对着天空挥拳说为什么不能保持不变,那不会有什么用。相反,你需要认识到环境何时发生了变化,这样你就可以根据实际情况采取适当的行动,而不是根据你希望世界成为的样子。这使你能够做出更准确、更明智和更有效的选择。"
此外,职场本身也一直在演变。当今的工作文化和管理风格通常基于团队合作,而不是僵化的等级制度。头脑风暴需要创造力、灵活性和情商,是一种典型的解决问题的技巧。不能或不愿意参与的员工将不会轻易在公司中获得晋升。灵活的员工也展现出其他技能。当变化发生时,他们可以迅速重新确定优先级,并在某些事情不奏效时提出额外的修改建议。当挫折发生时,他们还可以迅速重整旗鼓,自信地适应新情况而不会反应过度。

questions.prompt: When did Kate Atkinson begin to write for women's magazines?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） After winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition.
**题目译文**
Kate Atkinson 是什么时候开始为女性杂志撰稿的?
A) 当她开始在苏格兰爱丁堡大学任教时。
B) 在她攻读美国文学博士学位期间。
C) 在出版她的第一部小说《博物馆幕后》之后。
D) 在赢得1986年《女性周刊》短篇小说大赛之后。
**定位** 她在赢得 1986 年《Woman's Own》短篇小说大赛之后,开始为女性杂志写作。
**信号** after 时间标志词直接锁定时点。答案句里 after winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition 的 after 是明确的时间定向词,把"开始为女性杂志写作"这一动作精确挂在"获奖"事件之后——听到"writing for women's magazines"紧跟 after,就锁定这一句。
**替换** after winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition ↔After winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition.原文与选项近乎逐字同形,只需对住事件
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱When she started teaching at Edinburgh University in Scotland. 盗用了原文 she taught at the university she graduated from 这一真实事件来诱选,但任教在前(1981写短篇之前),并非"为女性杂志写作"的时点;且原文是"母校"而非 Edinburgh University,地点也被偷改。借用原文： Later, she taught at the university she graduated from
B) 原词陷阱While she was doing her doctoral studies on American Literature. 借原文 she researched a doctorate on American Literature 设套,读博发生在 1974 年毕业后、远早于 1986 年,并非为女性杂志写作的时间。借用原文： After graduating in 1974, she researched a doctorate on American Literature
C) 原词陷阱After publishing her first novel Behind the Scenes at the Museum. 借原文 Her first novel, Behind the Scenes at the Museum, won the 1995 UK Book of the Year award设套;出版在 1995 年、晚于为女性杂志写作的 1986 年,时序正好反了。借用原文： Her first novel, Behind the Scenes at the Museum, won the 1995 UK Book of the Year award
questions.quote: She began writing for women's magazines after winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition.

options.text: When she started teaching at Edinburgh University in Scotland.
While she was doing her doctoral studies on American Literature.
After publishing her first novel Behind the Scenes at the Museum.

questions.prompt: What did Kate Atkinson's books touch on?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） The themes of love and loss.
**题目译文**
Kate Atkinson 的书涉及了什么?
A) 爱与失去的主题。
B) 人类行为的准则。
C) 古怪之人的罪过和缺陷。
D) 上流社会的礼仪。
**定位** 无论写什么体裁,阿特金森的书都触及爱与失、以及如何继续生活下去这些主题。
**信号** 题干同词 touch on 领起主题,直给答案。答案句 her books touch on the themes of love and loss 用的动词与题干 touch on 完全同款,等于原文亲口把答案领出来——听到 "her books touch on…" 就锁这句,后面紧跟的主题即答案。
**替换** the themes of love and loss↔ The themes of love and loss.主题表述逐字对应
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 答非所问The code of human behaviour. 取自原文后文 the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour,但那是在解释"风尚喜剧"这一文类的定义,不是回答"her books touch on 什么主题"的内容,答非所问。借用原文： the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour current in fashionable circles of society
C) 答非所问The sins and flaws of eccentrics. 拼自原文 sometimes sinful, and generally flawed eccentrics,但那句讲的是书里"住着哪类人物形象",而题目问的是 touch on 的"主题",混淆了"登场人物"与"核心主题"。借用原文： populated by odd, sometimes sinful, and generally flawed eccentrics
D) 答非所问The manners of fashionable circles. 取自原文 code of behaviour current in fashionable circles of society 与 comedies of manners,这些是解释"风尚喜剧"文类标签的措辞,而非她书的 touch on 主题。借用原文： comedies that represent the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour current in fashionable circles of society
questions.quote: Whatever genre Atkinson writes in, her books touch on the themes of love and loss and how to carry on.

options.text: The themes of love and loss.
The code of human behaviour.
The sins and flaws of eccentrics.
The manners of fashionable circles.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the clever and deceitful characters in a comedy of manners?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） They often get rewarded instead of being punished.
**题目译文**
关于风尚喜剧中聪明而狡诈的角色,我们了解到什么?
A) 他们通常对复杂的人际关系一无所知。
B) 他们成功地模仿名人的举止。
C) 他们经常得到奖赏而不是受到惩罚。
D) 他们在社会上普遍受到轻视。
**定位** 风尚喜剧往往奖赏它那些聪明而狡诈的角色,而不是惩罚他们的恶行。
**信号** reward…rather than punish 的对比定向句。答案句用 reward its clever and deceitful characters, rather than punish their bad deeds 这一"奖赏 A、而非惩罚 B"的对比结构直接交代结局——rather than 是关键定向词,把方向钉死在"受赏"一边;听到 reward…rather than punish 就锁这句。
**替换** reward its clever and deceitful characters, rather than punish their bad deeds↔They often get rewarded instead of being punished.主动→被动 + rather than=instead of 同义改写
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱They are usually ignorant of complex human relations. 把原文 the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour 里的 complex 一词揪出来拼成"对复杂人际无知",但原文从未说这些角色"无知",纯属据片词臆造。借用原文： the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour
B) 未提及They successfully imitate the manners of celebrities. 借原文 manners 一词造势,但原文只字未提这些角色"成功模仿名人",imitate/celebrities 都无出处,属凭空添加。
D) 与原文相反They are generally looked down upon in society. 取了"受罚/负面"的方向,正好与原文reward…rather than punish 的"受赏不受罚"相反——原文明说是被奖赏,本项却说被社会看轻,极性反了。借用原文： rather than punish their bad deeds
questions.quote: A comedy of manners tends to reward its clever and deceitful characters, rather than punish their bad deeds.

options.text: They are usually ignorant of complex human relations.
They successfully imitate the manners of celebrities.
They often get rewarded instead of being punished.
They are generally looked down upon in society.

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker say adaptability is an important skill to exercise in the workplace?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） It is what employers are increasingly seeking after.
**题目译文**
为什么说话者认为适应能力是在职场中需要锻炼的一项重要技能?
A) 这是成员用来缓解团队紧张气氛的能力。
B) 这是雇主日益寻求的能力。
C) 这有助于度过经济衰退。
D) 这是学习新任务所必需的。
**定位** 简单说，适应力是一种雇主越来越看重的技能。
**信号** Simply put 引出总论断。开篇自问 Why 之后紧跟 Simply put, adaptability is a skill employers are increasingly looking for，Simply put 是抛出核心结论的信号词，这句就是对 Why 的直接回答。
**替换** employers are increasingly looking for↔employers are increasingly seeking after looking for 同义于 seeking after
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及alleviate tension in a team 在录音里根本没出现，适应力被说成雇主看重的技能而非用来化解团队紧张的工具，属凭空捏造。
C) 原词陷阱录音后文确念了 economy might enter a recession，但那是举例说明环境会变，并非说适应力有助于度过衰退；C 盗用 recession 制造听到就想选的诱惑，答非所问。借用原文： economy might enter a recession
D) 原词陷阱录音里 learning a new task 是说学新任务时生产力会上升，并非说适应力对学新任务必不可少；D 把这个原词搬来当重要性的理由，错位。借用原文： When you spend time learning a new task rather than resisting it, your productivity goes up.
questions.quote: Simply put, adaptability is a skill employers are increasingly looking for.

questions.prompt: What does adaptability enable us to do according to strategy consultant Dorie Clark?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） Make better choices.
**题目译文**
根据战略顾问Dorie Clark的说法,适应能力使我们能够做什么?
A) 做出更好的选择。
B) 追随创新理念。
C) 及时获得认可。
D) 积累工作经验。
**定位** 这使你能够做出更准确、更明智、更有效的选择。
**信号** enables you to 的因果落点。Dorie Clark 一番话的收尾句 That enables you to make more accurate, informed and effective choices，enables you to 正是题干 enable us to do 的对应信号，结论就在这句。
**替换** make more accurate, informed and effective choices↔Make better choices.三个褒义形容词概括为 better
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 未提及Follow innovative ideas. 在 Dorie Clark 的话里没有依据，她讲的是认清变化、做出选择，未提跟随创新想法。
C) 未提及Achieve recognition duly. 谈获得认可，录音从未涉及，是凭空添加的职场正能量诱饵。
D) 答非所问录音说环境会变、要据实采取行动，并未提积累经验；Accumulate work experience. 借职场话题诱你联想，但答案句讲的是做选择，并非攒经验。借用原文： you can take appropriate action based on what is, rather than how you wish the world would be
questions.quote: That enables you to make more accurate, informed and effective choices.

options.text: Make better choices.
Follow innovative ideas.
Achieve recognition duly.
Accumulate work experience.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about today's work culture from the passage?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） People often work in teams.
**题目译文**
从文中我们对当今的工作文化了解到什么?
A) 员工表现出更高的情商。
B) 员工更多使用脑力而非体力。
C) 人们通常采用弹性工作时间。
D) 人们经常以团队形式工作。
**定位** 如今的工作文化和管理方式往往建立在团队合作之上，而非僵化的等级制度。
**信号** Today's work culture 直接点题。第二段开头 Today's work culture and management style is often based on teamwork 与题干用词几乎一致，是直接点题句，答案就在 based on teamwork。
**替换** based on teamwork ↔ People often work in teams.名词 teamwork 转为动作 work in teams
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱录音确念了 emotional intelligence，但那是说头脑风暴需要情商，并非说工作者展现出更多情商；A 把这个原词搬来当工作文化特征，安错了对象。借用原文： Brainstorming, which requires creativity, flexibility, and emotional intelligence
B) 未提及Workers use brains more than muscles. 这种脑力对体力的对比录音从没说，是凭空臆造的常识性诱饵。
C) 原词陷阱录音多次出现 flexibility、flexible，但讲的是员工要灵活应变，并未说大家弹性工时；People usually work flexible hours. 借 flexible 同根词诱你联想到工时，无据。借用原文： Employees who are flexible demonstrate other skills too.
questions.quote: Today's work culture and management style is often based on teamwork, rather than a rigid hierarchy.

options.text: Workers show more emotional intelligence.
Workers use brains more than muscles.
People usually work flexible hours.
People often work in teams.

questions.prompt: What are employees with adaptability able to do when changes occur?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） Decide on new priorities speedily.
**题目译文**
当变化发生时,具有适应能力的员工能够做什么?
A) 尽快离开团队。
B) 提前充分预见挫折。
C) 迅速决定新的优先事项。
D) 自信地坚持原有目标。
**定位** 当变化发生时，他们能迅速重新排定优先级，并在某些做法行不通时提出额外的调整。
**信号** when changes occur 条件句应答。They can reprioritize quickly when changes occur与题干 when changes occur 逐词对应，reprioritize quickly 就是对该情形的直接应答，是答案句。
**替换** reprioritize quickly ↔ Decide on new priorities speedily. reprioritize=decide on new priorities，quickly=speedily
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反录音说有适应力的人遇变化会迅速重排优先级、自信适应，Leave the group as soon as possible. 的尽快离队是逃避态度，与原文取向相反，且 leave the group 录音未提。
B) 原词陷阱录音后句确念了 regroup quickly when a setback occurs，但说的是挫折发生时迅速重整，并非 well in advance 提前预判；Anticipate setbacks well in advance. 盗用 setback又把时间偷换成事前。借用原文： They can also regroup quickly when a setback occurs
D) 与原文相反录音说 adapting to the new situation confidently，confidently 是修饰适应新情况；Stick to original goals confidently. 搬走 confidently 却接上坚持原目标，恰与适应力相反。借用原文： adapting to the new situation confidently and without overreacting
questions.quote: They can reprioritize quickly when changes occur and suggest additional modifications when something is not working.

Anticipate setbacks well in advance.
Decide on new priorities speedily.
Stick to original goals confidently.

transcript.text: Now, it's become something of a ritual to debate the value of a college degree, but as Current Population Survey data show, there has been a sharp decline in employment among men without college degrees compared with those who have them.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: This decline began in the 1960s and has become more serious over time.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: What has actually caused this decline?
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Well, economists have been working to ascertain the roots of the decline for decades and have come up with several theories.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: One popular theory is that it's a case of too low wages for jobs that don't require a degree.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: An alternate theory is that there were more jobs not requiring a college degree in the past than now.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: A recent working paper from the National Bureau of Economic Research reviewed those theories and put forward additional hypotheses about the causes of the problem.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Let's look at that paper now.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: First, the researchers considered the issue of wages.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: As the wage gap has grown between those with college degrees and those without, economists have suggested that men aren't as interested in taking some of the less lucrative jobs.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: While the authors of the paper found truth in this explanation, they assert that low wages can't be the only factor, as wages for men without college degrees, adjusting for inflation, haven't changed much since the 1960s, making it hard to see why fewer men seem willing to accept those wages.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: This leads to the second theory, that more jobs require a college degree today than in the past.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Indeed, that theory seems valid, because in America today, 2/3 of jobs are filled by workers with at least some college education.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: However, the authors of the paper argue that there are other factors amplifying the problem.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They identified two new potential explanations: the first being the tremendous decline in marriage among men without college degrees since the 1960s; and the second being the increase in women participating in the workforce that was concurrent with the decline in marriage.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: These two changes mean that men might not have families to support, or if they do, their wives might be doing more of the providing, both of which might remove the financial incentive to work.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The authors of the paper concede that research on the subject isn't complete, but they argue that their work supports the value of a college education.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: While an increasing number of people are trying to eat less meat, a market research team has found in its latest fashion and sustainability report that the trend is now spreading from kitchen to closet.

transcript.text: It found animal welfare came top of a list of issues that people considered before buying clothes, with 42% saying it was important to them.

transcript.text: As well as being on trend, and with a much better ring to it than synthetic leather, the vegan label does convey an important extra distinction.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: If you label something as vegan, then the whole product needs to be animal free.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: That means checking things like the glue that holds the shoe together, for example, and the chemicals used for finishing them.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: At the top end, some of the world-renowned fashion designers have avoided leather and fur for some time.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In fact, some of the companies are now exploring a leather substitute and a silk replacement made from mushrooms.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The Animal Free Product Society says they've seen a boom in products registered with the vegan trademark.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In 2018, there were 119.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: So far this year, it says an unprecedented 1,956 have been registered.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: New products are being added daily.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: There are fur coats that are vegan, plastic vegan belts and shoes made from tree bark or natural rubber labelled vegan.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: These new products aren't coming at an extra cost to consumers though.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Vegan boots cost the same as the leather originals.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: New Look, one of the first reputable store chains to use the vegan trademark, prices ballet shoes at £7.99 and a vegan laptop handbag at £29.99, comparable with its other products.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: This signifies a change.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In the past, ethical products, whether they were fair trade or organic, came at a premium.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: However, it is unclear whether these new products can be considered ethical.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The debate over durability, crop-growing impacts, pollution and recyclability is a complicated one, not to mention the ethics around the working conditions for people making the products, whatever the component materials.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Environmental campaigners advise that the best approach is to buy less, never mind what the item is made of.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: By the end of 2016, anyone who had been paying even passing attention to the news headlines was highly likely to conclude that everything was terrible, and that the world was going to hell.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: It was easy to feel depressed by the wars in different parts of the world, the spread of deadly viruses or terror attacks.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Yet, 2016 was the best year in the history of humanity.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Child mortality was roughly half what it was as recently as 1990.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: And 300,000 more people gained access to electricity each day.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Every single measure of material and environmental welfare in America, Europe, Asia, Africa and the world as a whole has improved rather than deteriorated.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: We are living in history's most peaceful era, with violence of all kinds in steep decline.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Those are the facts.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: So why aren't we all optimists?
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In a 2015 survey for YouGov, 65% of British people and 81% of the French said they thought the world was getting worse.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: However, according to numerous sensible statistics, these people are simply wrong.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Nobody in their right mind should wish to have lived in a previous century.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Yet people do.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Why?
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Our prevailing mood of despair is irrational.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: It says more about us than it does about how things really are.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: It is best explained as the result of various psychological biases that served a purpose for our evolutionary ancestors—but now, in a media-saturated era, constantly mislead us.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Once upon a time, it was of great survival value to be worried about everything that could go wrong.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: This is what makes bad news especially compelling.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In our evolutionary past, it was a very good thing that our attention could be easily seized by negative information, since it might well indicate a dangerous risk to our own survival.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The caveman who always assumed there was a lion behind the next rock would usually be wrong, but he'd be much more likely to survive and reproduce than one who always assumed the opposite.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: But that was all before newspapers, television and the internet.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In today's hyper connected times, our addiction to bad news just leads us to vacuum up depressing or enraging stories from across the globe.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Whether these news stories threaten us or not, we conclude that things are much worse than they actually are.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Really good news, on the other hand, can be a lot harder to spot in a newspaper because predictable daily events by definition aren't news.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcriptTranslations: 如今，辩论大学学位的价值已经成为一种惯例，但正如现行人口调查数据所显示的，与拥有大学学位的男性相比，没有大学学位的男性的就业率出现了急剧下降。这种下降始于20世纪60年代，并且随着时间的推移变得更加严重。
究竟是什么导致了这种下降？嗯，几十年来经济学家一直在努力确定这种下降的根源，并提出了几种理论。一种流行的理论是，不需要学位的工作工资过低。另一种理论是，过去不需要大学学位的工作比现在更多。

美国国家经济研究局最近的一篇工作论文审视了这些理论，并提出了关于问题成因的其他假设。现在让我们看看那篇论文。首先,研究人员考虑了工资问题。随着拥有大学学位者与没有大学学位者之间的工资差距扩大,经济学家认为男性对接受一些收入较低的工作不那么感兴趣。虽然论文作者认为这一解释有其道理,但他们断言低工资不可能是唯一因素,因为没有大学学位的男性的工资,经通货膨胀调整后,自20世纪60年代以来并没有太大变化,这使得很难理解为什么似乎越来越少的男性愿意接受这些工资。
这引出了第二种理论,即如今需要大学学位的工作比过去更多。确实,这一理论似乎是有效的,因为在今天的美国,三分之二的工作由至少接受过一些大学教育的工人担任。然而,论文作者认为还有其他因素在放大这个问题。
他们确定了两个新的潜在解释:第一个是自20世纪60年代以来没有大学学位的男性结婚率大幅下降;第二个是与结婚率下降同时发生的女性劳动力参与率的增加。这两个变化意味着男性可能没有家庭需要供养,或者即使有,他们的妻子可能承担更多的供养责任,这两种情况都可能消除工作的经济激励。论文作者承认关于这一主题的研究尚未完成,但他们认为他们的工作支持大学教育的价值。
虽然越来越多的人正在尝试少吃肉，但一个市场研究团队在其最新的时尚与可持续发展报告中发现，这一趋势现在正在从厨房蔓延到衣橱。报告发现，动物福利在人们购买衣服前考虑的问题清单中位居首位，42%的人表示这对他们很重要。该团队的研究人员预测，明年将出现无动物成分鞋履系列的繁荣，因为他们听到各个年龄段的购物者都表示会购买标注为"纯素"的鞋类，这意味着这些商品在生产过程中没有使用任何动物或动物部位。
纯素标签不仅符合潮流趋势，而且比合成革听起来好得多，它确实传达了一个重要的额外区别。如果你将某物标注为纯素，那么整个产品都需要不含动物成分。这意味着要检查诸如将鞋子粘合在一起的胶水，以及用于修整鞋子的化学品等细节。在高端领域，一些世界知名的时装设计师已经有一段时间避免使用皮革和毛皮。事实上，一些公司现在正在探索用蘑菇制成的皮革替代品和丝绸替代品。

Animal Free Product Society表示，他们看到注册纯素商标的产品出现了激增。2018年有119个。该组织称，今年迄今为止已有前所未有的1,956个产品注册。每天都在增加新产品。有纯素皮草大衣、塑料纯素腰带以及由树皮或天然橡胶制成并标注为纯素的鞋子。不过，这些新产品并没有给消费者带来额外成本。纯素靴子的价格与原版皮革靴子相同。New Look是首批使用纯素商标的知名连锁店之一,其芭蕾舞鞋售价7.99英镑,纯素笔记本电脑手提包售价29.99英镑,与其其他产品价格相当。
这标志着一种变化。过去，无论是公平贸易还是有机产品，道德产品都要溢价。然而,这些新产品是否可以被视为道德产品尚不清楚。关于耐用性、作物种植影响、污染和可回收性的争论是复杂的,更不用说围绕制造这些产品的人的工作条件的伦理问题,无论组成材料是什么。环保活动人士建议,最好的做法是少买,无论这件物品是用什么制成的。
到2016年底,任何稍微关注新闻头条的人都极有可能得出这样的结论:一切都很糟糕,世界正走向毁灭。世界各地的战争、致命病毒的传播或恐怖袭击很容易让人感到沮丧。
然而,2016年是人类历史上最好的一年。儿童死亡率大约是1990年的一半。每天有30万人获得电力供应。美国、欧洲、亚洲、非洲和整个世界的物质和环境福祉的每一项指标都在改善而非恶化。我们生活在历史上最和平的时代,各种暴力行为都在急剧下降。这些都是事实。那么为什么我们不都是乐观主义者呢?
在2015年YouGov的一项调查中,65%的英国人和81%的法国人表示他们认为世界正在变得更糟。然而,根据众多可靠的统计数据,这些人完全错了。没有一个头脑正常的人会希望生活在前几个世纪。然而人们确实这样希望。为什么?
我们普遍的绝望情绪是不理性的。它更多地反映了我们自身,而非事物的真实状况。最好的解释是,这是各种心理偏见的结果,这些偏见曾对我们进化中的祖先有用,但现在在一个媒体饱和的时代,却不断误导我们。曾几何时,担心可能出错的一切事情具有极大的生存价值。这就是坏消息特别引人注目的原因。

在我们的进化历史中,我们的注意力很容易被负面信息吸引是一件非常好的事情,因为它很可能预示着对我们自身生存的危险风险。那个总是假设下一块岩石后面有狮子的穴居人通常会判断错误,但他比总是做相反假设的人更有可能生存和繁衍。但那都是在报纸、电视和互联网出现之前。在当今这个高度互联的时代,我们对坏消息的沉迷只会导致我们从全球各地吸收令人沮丧或愤怒的故事。无论这些新闻是否威胁到我们,我们都会得出结论:事情比实际情况糟糕得多。另一方面,真正的好消息在报纸上可能更难发现,因为可预测的日常事件从定义上讲不是新闻。
