transcript.text: If you visit the Great Smoky Mountains National Park, chances are you will remember the roadside or campground bears above all else.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Bears are the most popular animals in a number of our national parks.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In these mountains, where the population of bears runs into the hundreds, opportunities to observe these large wild animals are plentiful during the summer.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Since national parks are wildlife sanctuaries where no disturbance of the native animals is allowed, years of protection have served to break down the wild bears' fear of humans.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Now, instead of depending on their own resources for a living, many bears patrol park roads and campgrounds.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They give the garbage cans a frequent going over.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: An occasional offer of food from a park visitor, an illegal and dangerous practice, makes beggars of them.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Bears are very often hungry and since they will feed on almost any kind of plant or animal, garbage is quite acceptable.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Feeding them, however, represents misguided kindness because the bears come to expect such generosity from everyone and consequently, trouble could lie ahead.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Park rules prohibit the feeding of bears.

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Why do we form opinions or attitudes about someone or something without really knowing much about them?
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Just hearing something good or bad about a person, a place or thing can influence our opinions positively or negatively.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: But letting the opinions of another person determine what our opinions will be is dangerous.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Forming opinions about someone or something before really knowing them well is called prejudice.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: "Pre-" means before, and "judice" refers to judgment.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Hence, prejudice means to judge before having adequate knowledge.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: We can be prejudiced toward or against someone or something.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In either case, we are only allowing ourselves to see half of the picture.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Very few people or things in this world are all good or all bad.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Prejudiced attitudes are usually based on myths, half-truths or incorrect information, and they are dangerous because they can keep us from learning the truth about someone or something.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: People form prejudices against others for many reasons—differences in their race, religion, gender, or occupation.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Prejudices keep people apart.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They keep us from really knowing and understanding each other.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: We should feel proud of who we are and the group of people we represent.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: If feelings of pride begin to turn to feelings of superiority when we think that our group or our beliefs are better than those around us, however, then we begin to develop prejudiced attitudes that can be harmful.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: For example, the prejudiced attitudes of one group may keep another group from attending certain schools, from living in any neighborhood they want, or from getting a job or a promotion.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Extreme feelings of prejudice have caused the deaths of innocent people.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: We are responsible for our own thoughts and opinions.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: When we let someone else tell us what to think about someone or something, we are giving up some control of our own lives.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Before you form an attitude or opinion, find out for yourself about the person or the thing in question.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Sometimes we don't realize that we hold prejudiced attitudes toward or against someone or something.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: We need to carefully examine our lives and our fears, and to ask ourselves whether our attitudes come from our personal knowledge and experience or from rumors and fear of the unknown.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The good news about prejudice is that we are not born with it.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Prejudiced attitudes and opinions develop over time.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: But with education and knowledge, we can replace our prejudices with cooperation and understanding.

transcript.text: When I started high school, it was a shock.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: I had been a big, tough 8th grader and suddenly I was a lonely 9th grader bullied by the big, tough 12th grade seniors who ran the high school.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: I realized then that it's nice to strive for something, but that you also have to enjoy the moment you're in and be happy where you are.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Rock and roll had always been an important part of my life.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: I remember my friends and I used to drive around until the late hours of the nights listening to the music of Rock and Roll legends.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Most people that age think the same thing, but people drift apart.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Jobs, families and tragedies separate people from those lasting friendships.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: A year after I graduated from high school, I left for Vietnam.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: I came back, burned out, and tired, as though I had lived 10 lifetimes in the short span of 14 months, the 14 months I was in the war.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: I couldn't relate to the friends I had had in high school.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They still seemed childish, concerned with childish things that weren't important to me.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: I was still trying to cope with the death, destruction and evil I had seen in Vietnam.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: I felt like we had done terrible things to innocent people there and in turn, I had seen terrible things done to my friends.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: I withdrew from my friends and started college.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Then I quit college and took many different jobs.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: I spent a lot of my time and money on alcohol and other drugs.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Finally, in an effort to get my life going in the right direction again, I sold everything and took what little money I had and bought myself an airplane ticket to Israel.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: While studying at Haifa University, I met my wife, who was also an American student.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: I now teach in a high school back in America.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcriptTranslations: 如果你访问大烟山国家公园,你很可能会对路边或营地的熊印象最为深刻。熊是我们许多国家公园中最受欢迎的动物。在这些山区,熊的数量达到数百只,夏季有充足的机会观察这些大型野生动物。
由于国家公园是野生动物保护区,不允许对本地动物进行任何干扰,多年的保护已经消除了野熊对人类的恐惧。现在,许多熊不再依靠自己的能力谋生,而是在公园道路和营地巡游。它们经常翻找垃圾桶。游客偶尔提供的食物——这是一种违法且危险的行为——使它们变成了乞讨者。熊经常很饿,由于它们几乎以任何种类的植物或动物为食,垃圾是完全可以接受的。
然而,喂食它们代表着错误的善意,因为熊会期待每个人都如此慷慨,因此可能会带来麻烦。公园规定禁止喂熊。违反者将被逮捕。每年,在公园附近开诊所的医生都会治疗一些熊咬伤和熊抓伤的病例。一些事故以奇怪的方式发生。
一名男子正在喂食两只小熊崽,这时母熊出现了并坚持要吃一些食物。这名男子用一只手把大熊推到一边,继续喂小熊,突然他的脸上遭到猛烈一击。一只熊受到一位女士不断提供的食物的诱惑,进入了这位慷慨的人所坐的汽车。她试图把熊推出车外,结果受了伤。一名男子在用点燃的香烟触碰熊的鼻子后需要医疗救治。另一名男子试图把一只熊推到他汽车的前座上,以便拍摄熊坐在他妻子旁边的照片,他妻子当时在驾驶座上。
由于熊偏爱道路和营地,徒步旅行者在公园小径上遇到熊的可能性很小,但总有这种可能,因为熊似乎知道你是否携带午餐或糖果棒。它甚至可能坚持要拿走它。
为什么我们会在对某人或某事并不真正了解的情况下形成看法或态度？仅仅听到关于一个人、一个地方或一件事的好话或坏话就能积极或消极地影响我们的看法。但让他人的看法决定我们的看法是危险的。在真正了解某人或某事之前就对其形成看法被称为偏见。"Pre-"意为之前，"judice"指判断。因此，偏见意味着在拥有充分知识之前就进行判断。
我们可以对某人或某事持有支持或反对的偏见。无论哪种情况,我们都只允许自己看到事物的一半。这个世界上很少有人或事是完全好或完全坏的。带有偏见的态度通常基于神话、半真半假的说法或不正确的信息,它们是危险的,因为它们会阻止我们了解关于某人或某事的真相。人们出于许多原因对他人形成偏见——种族、宗教、性别或职业方面的差异。偏见使人们彼此分离。它们阻止我们真正认识和理解彼此。

我们应该为自己是谁以及我们所代表的群体感到自豪。然而,如果自豪感开始转变为优越感,当我们认为我们的群体或我们的信仰优于周围的人时,我们就开始形成可能有害的偏见态度。例如,一个群体的偏见态度可能会阻止另一个群体进入某些学校、居住在他们想要的任何社区,或者获得工作或晋升。极端的偏见情绪导致了无辜者的死亡。我们要为自己的思想和观点负责。当我们让别人告诉我们该如何看待某人或某事时,我们正在放弃对自己生活的部分控制权。
在你形成态度或观点之前,请亲自了解所讨论的人或事。有时我们没有意识到自己对某人或某事持有偏见态度。我们需要仔细审视我们的生活和恐惧,并扪心自问我们的态度是来自个人知识和经验,还是来自谣言和对未知事物的恐惧。关于偏见的好消息是我们并非生来就有偏见。偏见态度和观点是随着时间发展而来的。但通过教育和知识,我们可以用合作和理解取代我们的偏见。

当我开始上高中时，这是一个冲击。我曾花了八年时间奋力成为天主教学校学生群体中最受欢迎的孩子。我曾是一个高大强壮的八年级学生，突然间我变成了一个孤独的九年级学生，被那些掌控高中的高大强壮的十二年级学长欺负。那时我意识到，努力争取某样东西固然很好,但你也必须享受当下的时刻,对自己所处的位置感到快乐。摇滚乐一直是我生活中的重要部分。我记得我和朋友们常常开车四处转悠,直到深夜,聆听摇滚传奇人物的音乐。在那些青少年时期,我建立了我以为会持续一生的友谊。那个年纪的大多数人都这样想,但人们会渐行渐远。工作、家庭和悲剧使人们与那些长久的友谊分离。
让我永远与朋友们分离的悲剧是越南战争。高中毕业一年后,我去了越南。我回来时精疲力竭、疲惫不堪,仿佛在短短14个月里经历了10次人生,那14个月就是我在战争中度过的时间。我无法与高中时的朋友产生共鸣。他们似乎仍然幼稚,关心着对我来说并不重要的幼稚事情。我仍在努力应对我在越南见到的死亡、毁灭和邪恶。我觉得我们在那里对无辜的人做了可怕的事情,而反过来,我也见到了对我朋友们做的可怕事情。
我远离了朋友们,开始上大学。然后我退学了,做了许多不同的工作。我把大量时间和金钱花在酒精和其他毒品上。最后,为了让我的生活重新走上正轨,我卖掉了所有东西,用仅有的一点钱给自己买了一张去以色列的机票。我去那里学习历史。在海法大学学习期间,我遇到了我的妻子,她也是一名美国学生。
我现在在美国的一所高中教书。我看着我的学生们,看到他们正在与许多年前我曾挣扎过的事情作斗争。作为一名教师,我尽我所能帮助他们度过艰难时期。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about the bears in national parks now?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） They are unafraid of humans.
**题目译文**
讲话者对国家公园里的熊的现状有何评价?
A) 它们对人类相当友好。
B) 它们的数量正在减少。
C) 它们不怕人类。
D) 它们特别喜欢垃圾。
**定位** 由于国家公园是禁止任何打扰本地动物的野生动物保护区，多年的保护已经逐渐瓦解了野生熊对人类的恐惧。
**信号** 因果句的结果落点。years of protection have served to break down the wild bears' fear of humans 是"多年保护"导致的结果，"瓦解了对人的恐惧"正是对熊现状的概括，这种"原因—结果"句的结果端就是答案落点。
**替换** break down the wild bears' fear of humans↔They are unafraid of humans. "瓦解恐惧"="不再害怕"
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 过度推断原文只说熊 break down the wild bears' fear of humans（不再怕人），但"不怕"不等于"友好"——后文讲熊咬人抓人，恰恰说明它们并不友好。They are quite friendly to humans. 是把"不怕"硬升级成"友好"，推过了头。借用原文： break down the wild bears' fear of humans
B) 与原文相反录音里只在第一段说 the population of bears runs into the hundreds（熊有成百上千），根本没说数量在减少。They are shrinking in numbers. 与原文给出的"数量众多"印象相反，属与原文相反。借用原文： the population of bears runs into the hundreds
D) 原词陷阱录音确实念到 garbage is quite acceptable（垃圾它们也吃），They are especially fond of garbage. 就盗用了 garbage 这个原词。但原文是说熊"几乎什么都吃，垃圾也接受"，并非"特别偏爱垃圾"，更不是对熊"现状"的总概括，是答非所问的原词陷阱。借用原文： garbage is quite acceptable
questions.quote: Since national parks are wildlife sanctuaries where no disturbance of the native animals is allowed, years of protection have served to break down the wild bears' fear of humans.

options.text: They are quite friendly to humans.
They are shrinking in numbers.
They are unafraid of humans.
They are especially fond of garbage.

C) 这是人类慷慨的表现。
D) 只允许在特定区域这样做。
**定位** 公园游客偶尔给熊喂食，这是一种违法又危险的行为，会把熊变成乞食者。
**信号** 插入语直接定性 illegal。an illegal and dangerous practice 是夹在句中的插入语，直接给"游客喂食"贴上"违法且危险"的定性标签，这种紧贴行为的评判性插入语就是答案信号；第三段 Park rules prohibit the feeding of bears. 再次印证。
**替换** an illegal and dangerous practice↔It is strictly forbidden. illegal/prohibit = strictly forbidden
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 答非所问原文说游客喂食只是 An occasional offer of food（偶尔给食），但整段都在讲熊巡逻、讨食、被喂出问题，可见这事并不罕见；题问的也是"喂熊"的性质（违法），而非它"常不常见"。It is an uncommon sight. 答非所问。借用原文： An occasional offer of food from a park visitor
C) 与原文相反录音第三段确实出现 misguided kindness（误导的善意），并提到熊指望"这种慷慨"，generosity 一词录音真念过，于是 It is a gesture of human generosity. 把它正面化。但作者明说这是"misguided（错误的）"善意，是正话反说，并非赞许喂熊是慷慨之举。借用原文： misguided kindness
D) 与原文相反原文是 Park rules prohibit the feeding of bears.（规定禁止喂熊），全面禁止、没有任何"某些区域可以喂"的说法。It is allowed only in certain areas. 凭空造出"分区允许"，与原文相反。借用原文： Park rules prohibit the feeding of bears.
questions.quote: An occasional offer of food from a park visitor, an illegal and dangerous practice, makes beggars of them.

options.text: It is strictly forbidden.
It is an uncommon sight.
It is a gesture of human generosity.
It is allowed only in certain areas.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's advice to people who carry some food while hiking on a park trail?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） Be prepared to run into a hungry bear.
**题目译文**
讲话者对在公园小径徒步时携带食物的人有什么建议?
A) 与看到的熊分享食物。
B) 做好遇到饥饿的熊的准备。
C) 尽量与遇到的熊友好相处。
D) 避免逗弄带幼崽的熊。
**定位** 由于熊更喜欢马路和营地，徒步者在公园小径上遇到熊的可能性很小，但总有那么一点几率，因为熊似乎能察觉你是否带着午餐或糖果。它甚至可能非要把它抢走。
**信号** 转折 but 之后才是真意。前半 the possibility of a hiker meeting up with a bear along park trails is small 是铺垫，but there's always that chance 的 but 一转，才点出"仍有可能遇上、且熊会盯上你的食物甚至抢走"——转折后这层提醒就是 advice 的落点。
**替换** there's always that chance ↔ Be prepared to run into a hungry bear. "总有机会遇上"="要有遇熊的准备" He may even insist on taking it ↔ a hungry bear "非要抢食"印证"饿熊"
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反Share their food with the bear they see. 是"主动喂熊"，但全文反复说喂熊违法危险（an illegal and dangerous practice、Park rules prohibit the feeding of bears.），作者绝不会建议分食物给熊，与原文立场相反。借用原文： Park rules prohibit the feeding of bears.
C) 与原文相反Try to be friendly with the bear they meet. 让人主动亲近熊，但录音通篇在讲熊咬人抓人、会抢食，提醒的是"提防"而非"友好"。这是把第 16 题埋的 friendly 一词挪过来制造的诱惑，与作者本意相反。借用原文： He may even insist on taking it
D) 原词陷阱录音第四段确有带幼崽的母熊伤人的例子（the mother bear appeared），cubs 的画面录音真出现过，Refrain from teasing bears with cubs. 就借此设套。但那只是"事故举例"，作者末段给徒步者的建议并不是"别逗带崽的熊"，属答非所问的原词陷阱。借用原文： One man was in the process of feeding two small cubs
questions.quote: Because bears prefer roads and campgrounds, the possibility of a hiker meeting up with a bear along park trails is small, but there's always that chance, for a bear seems to know if you are carrying a lunch or a candy bar. He may even insist on taking it.

options.text: Share their food with the bear they see.
Be prepared to run into a hungry bear.
Try to be friendly with the bear they meet.
Refrain from teasing bears with cubs.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about prejudice?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） It means making judgments without adequate knowledge.
**题目译文**
说话者关于偏见说了什么?
A) 它指的是激进且广泛存在的观点。
B) 它意味着在没有充分了解的情况下做出判断。
C) 它指的是关于某人或某事的根深蒂固的信念。
D) 它意味着即使被证明是错误的也坚持自己的判断。
**定位** 在真正了解某人或某物之前就对其形成看法，这叫作偏见。"Pre-"意为"之前"，"judice"指"判断"。因此，偏见就是在没有足够认识之前就下判断。
**信号** 定义标志is called与Hence总结。is called prejudice 给出概念名称、紧接 Hence, prejudice means to judge before having adequate knowledge 用 Hence 收束成一句完整定义，这个"下定义+总结"信号让它成为答案句。
**替换** to judge before having adequate knowledge↔ making judgments without adequate knowledge judge=making judgments且before=without
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱opinions that are radical and widespread 借了录音里的 opinions 一词，但原文从未说偏见是"激进而广泛的（radical and widespread）"观点，激进/广泛是凭空加的限定，属听到 opinions 就想选的原词陷阱。借用原文： hearing something good or bad about a person, a place or thing can influence our opinions
C) 偷换概念deep-rooted beliefs about someone or something 蹭了原文反复出现的 about someone or something，但把偏见说成"根深蒂固的信念"，而原文定义强调的是"了解/认识之前"就下判断，时间点完全不同，属偷换概念。借用原文： Forming opinions about someone or something before really knowing them well
D) 答非所问sticking to one's judgments even when proved wrong 用了 judgments 一词，但说的是"被证明错了仍坚持"，是事后固执；原文定义说的是"了解之前"就下判断，是事前，与原文相反/错位。借用原文： prejudice means to judge before having adequate knowledge
questions.quote: Forming opinions about someone or something before really knowing them well is called prejudice. "Pre-" means before, and "judice" refers to judgment. Hence, prejudice means to judge before having adequate knowledge.

options.text: It refers to opinions that are radical and widespread.
It means making judgments without adequate knowledge.
It refers to deep-rooted beliefs about someone or something.
It means sticking to one's judgments even when proved wrong.

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker say prejudiced attitudes are dangerous?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） They prevent us from getting to the truth.
**题目译文**
说话者为什么说带有偏见的态度是危险的?
A) 它们常常导致宗教团体之间的战争。
B) 它们阻碍某些职业的繁荣发展。
C) 它们使神话和半真半假的说法长期存在。
D) 它们阻止我们了解真相。
**定位** 偏见态度通常建立在谬误、半真半假的说法或错误信息之上，它们之所以危险，是因为它们会妨碍我们了解关于某人或某物的真相。
**信号** dangerous because因果信号。they are dangerous because they can keep us from learning the truth 里 dangerous 后跟 because，因果信号直接把"危险的原因"端出来，because 之后那半句就是答案句。
**替换** keep us from learning the truth↔prevent us from getting to the truth keep from=prevent from且learning=getting to
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱war between religious groups 借了原文 religion/后文 religious 的影子，但原文此处说危害是"妨碍了解真相"，并未说偏见"导致宗教群体间的战争"；战争是过度引申，原文只说极端偏见 caused deaths，没说"宗教群体间开战"。借用原文： differences in their race, religion, gender, or occupation
B) 张冠李戴keep certain occupations from thriving 蹭了原文 occupation 一词，但原文说偏见 keep people apart（让人彼此疏远），第三段说妨碍人 getting a job or a promotion（找工作/晋升），从没说让"某些职业无法繁荣"，属张冠李戴。借用原文： from getting a job or a promotion
C) 原词陷阱allow myths and half-truths to persist 直接盗用原文 myths, half-truths，极具迷惑性；但原文说偏见是"基于（based on）myths/half-truths"，谬误是偏见的成因/来源，不是because 后给出的"危险原因"，答非所问。借用原文： Prejudiced attitudes are usually based on myths, half-truths or incorrect information
questions.quote: Prejudiced attitudes are usually based on myths, half-truths or incorrect information, and they are dangerous because they can keep us from learning the truth about someone or something.

options.text: They often lead to war between religious groups.
They keep certain occupations from thriving.
They allow myths and half-truths to persist.
They prevent us from getting to the truth.

questions.prompt: When does the speaker say we begin to develop prejudiced attitudes?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） When we start to feel superior.
**题目译文**
说话者说我们什么时候开始形成带有偏见的态度?
A) 当我们开始感到优越时。
B) 当我们与有偏见的人交往时。
C) 当我们生活在一个封闭的社区时。
D) 当我们试图跟上周围的人时。
**定位** 如果自豪感开始转变为优越感——当我们认为自己的群体或信念比周围人更好时——然而，那时我们就开始发展出可能有害的偏见态度。
**信号** If…turn to superiority条件信号。If feelings of pride begin to turn to feelings of superiority 用 If 引出条件、then we begin to develop prejudiced attitudes 给出结果，这个"条件→产生偏见"的因果/条件信号让它成为答案句。
**替换** feelings of pride begin to turn to feelings of superiority ↔ When we start to feel superior turn to feelings of superiority=start to feel superior
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 未提及When we mix with prejudiced people（与有偏见的人来往时）听上去合理，但原文给的触发条件是"自豪转为优越感"，从没说"和有偏见的人相处"会让我们产生偏见，属未提及。
C) 原词陷阱live in an isolated neighborhood 盗用了原文 living in any neighborhood 的neighborhood 一词；但原文里 neighborhood 出现在"偏见使某群体无法随意居住"的危害举例中，是偏见的后果，不是产生偏见的条件，张冠李戴。借用原文： from living in any neighborhood they want
D) 与原文相反When we try to keep up with those around us（努力跟上周围人）与原文 better than those around us（觉得自己比周围人更好）方向相反：原文是"自觉高人一等"，选项却是"努力追赶别人"，与原文相反。借用原文： our group or our beliefs are better than those around us
questions.quote: If feelings of pride begin to turn to feelings of superiority when we think that our group or our beliefs are better than those around us, however, then we begin to develop prejudiced attitudes that can be harmful.

options.text: When we start to feel superior.
When we mix with prejudiced people.
When we live in an isolated neighborhood.
When we try to keep up with those around us.

questions.prompt: How did the speaker feel when he started high school?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （态度观点题） Shocked.
**题目译文**
说话者刚上高中时感觉如何?
A) 有动力的。
B) 失望的。
C) 困惑的。
D) 震惊的。
**定位** 我上高中的时候，那真是一记冲击。
**信号** 直陈感受句 it was a shock。开篇第一句 it was a shock 就用 it was + 情绪名词直接定调入学感受，这种讲者自陈心情的句子就是态度题的答案句。
**替换** it was a shock↔ Shocked.名词 shock 转形容词 Shocked
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反Motivated. 是被激励的积极情绪，而原文 it was a shock 是负面冲击，方向相反。借用原文： it was a shock
B) 偷换概念Disappointed. 是失望，原文是 shock（震惊冲击），二者都偏负面但情绪类型不同，原文没有“期望落空”的意思。
C) 偷换概念Perplexed. 是困惑、想不明白，原文 shock 强调的是突然的强烈冲击，并非智力上的困惑。
questions.quote: When I started high school, it was a shock.

options.text: Motivated.
Disappointed.
Perplexed.
Shocked.

questions.prompt: What did the speaker once think of teenage friendships?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） They would last a lifetime.
**题目译文**
说话者曾经如何看待青少年时期的友谊?
A) 它们会随着时间的流逝而改变。
B) 它们会对年轻人的成年生活有益。
C) 它们会帮助孩子们成长。
D) 它们会持续一生。
**定位** 在那些青少年岁月里，我建立了一些我以为会维系一辈子的友谊。
**信号** I thought 引出当初的判断。that I thought would last a lifetime 里的 I thought（我当初以为）正对题干的 once think，是讲者亲口给出的当年看法，定为答案句。
**替换** would last a lifetime↔They would last a lifetime.几乎原句照搬
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反They would change with the passage of time. 说友谊会随时间改变，这恰恰是讲者后来才发现的现实（people drift apart），不是他当初 thought 的看法，张冠李戴了时间点。借用原文： people drift apart
B) 未提及They would benefit young people's adult life. 谈友谊对成年生活的好处，录音只说他以为友谊会持久，从未谈“对成年生活有益”，属无中生有。
C) 未提及They would help kids grow. 说友谊帮孩子成长，录音里讲者对青少年友谊的判断只有“会持续一辈子”，没有“助成长”这一层。
questions.quote: During those teenage years, I built friendships that I thought would last a lifetime.

options.text: They would change with the passage of time.
They would benefit young people's adult life.
They would help kids grow.
They would last a lifetime.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the speaker when he returned from the Vietnam War?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （推断题） He had become mature.
**题目译文**
关于说话者从越南战争返回时,我们了解到什么?
A) 他已经变得成熟了。
B) 他健康状况不佳。
C) 他有很多故事要讲。
D) 他后悔离开越南。
**定位** 我没法再和高中时的那些朋友产生共鸣了。他们在我看来还是很幼稚，只在意一些对我而言已不重要的幼稚事情。
**信号** 以朋友的“幼稚”反衬自己的成熟。讲者说朋友 still seemed childish、还在关心 childish things that weren't important to me，用对方的幼稚反衬出自己已经变了——经历战争后心智超前于同龄人，这处对比就是归纳点。
**替换** They still seemed childish, concerned with childish things that weren't important to me↔He had become mature. “别人幼稚”反向等于“我成熟”
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱讲者说自己 burned out, and tired，He suffered poor health. 盗用这种“累、垮”的字眼当身体得病，但 burned out 指心力交瘁，原文并未说他身体患病。借用原文： burned out, and tired
C) 过度推断He had lots of stories to tell. 看似贴合“经历越战、活了十辈子”，但原文 as though I had lived 10 lifetimes 是形容沧桑成熟，不是说他爱讲故事、有谈资，答非所问。借用原文： as though I had lived 10 lifetimes
D) 未提及He regretted leaving Vietnam. 说他后悔离开越南，原文只讲他对在越南的所见所为感到痛苦，从没说后悔离开那里，属无中生有且方向也不对。
questions.quote: I couldn't relate to the friends I had had in high school. They still seemed childish, concerned with childish things that weren't important to me.

options.text: He had become mature.
He suffered poor health.
He had lots of stories to tell.
He regretted leaving Vietnam.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker try to do as a teacher?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （目的题） Help his students get through the growing pains.
**题目译文**
说话者作为一名教师试图做什么?
A) 与他的学生交朋友。
B) 向他的学生展示如何尽力而为。
C) 帮助他的学生度过成长的烦恼。
D) 与他的学生分享他的个人经历。
**定位** 我看着我的学生，看到他们正为许多当年我也挣扎过的同样的事而苦苦挣扎。作为一名老师，我尽我所能帮他们渡过那些艰难的关口。
**信号** As a teacher, I try to… 的收束主句。结尾 As a teacher, I try to help them over the rough spots 用 I try to help… 直陈自己当老师的做法，是全篇落点句，正对题干 try to do。
**替换** help them over the rough spots↔ Help his students get through the growing pains. rough spots = growing pains struggling with many of the very things I struggled with↔Help his students get through the growing pains.学生的挣扎即成长之痛
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及Make friends with his students. 说和学生交朋友，结尾只说 I try to help them over the rough spots（帮他们渡难关），从没说要与学生做朋友，无中生有。
B) 偷换概念Show his students how to do their best. 说教学生如何做到最好，原文是 help…over the rough spots（帮他们渡过难关），偏向陪伴扶持，不是示范如何取得最好表现，偷换了做法。
D) 原词陷阱Share his personal experience with his students. 借前文大段个人经历制造诱惑，但结尾的做法是 help them over the rough spots，是“帮”不是“讲给学生听”，他回顾经历只为解释自己懂学生的处境，并未说要把经历分享给学生，答非所问。借用原文： I look at my students and see them struggling with many of the very things I struggled with many years ago
questions.quote: I look at my students and see them struggling with many of the very things I struggled with many years ago. As a teacher, I try to help them over the rough spots as best I can.

options.text: Make friends with his students.
Show his students how to do their best.
Help his students get through the growing pains.
Share his personal experience with his students.

transcript.text: Section A. Directions: In this section, you will hear two long conversations. At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions. transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Welcome to the Book Club.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: Today's guest is Susan Lane, the author of a new book on personal finances that has already sold half a million copies.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: Hi, Susan, your book is extremely successful.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: Why do you think that is?
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: I think that's because of my message, which is making happiness a priority over money.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: So many of us in my generation have spent decades trying to earn more money, just to consume more, but it made us more miserable.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: You yourself were once caught in that cycle, working for two decades as an executive and earning a high salary, but still accumulating debt.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: I most certainly was.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: I earned millions, but by the time I quit my job four years ago to become a writer, I owed over $30,000.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: So how did you escape that pattern?
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: And what would you advise other people to do?
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: The first change is in what we value.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: We need to emphasize things that actually make us happy, like relationships, the environment or even our hobbies.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: Once we make the right things our priority, our goals will change and so will our financial behavior.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: How does that translate into practical action?
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: Can you give our audience examples of what you are talking about on an everyday basis?
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: The major areas for action are usually housing, food and transportation.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: So people might share a home with friends instead of living on their own, bring lunch from home instead of going to restaurants, and use public transport instead of owning a car.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: Those sound like major sacrifices, I could never share my home, I need my own space.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: But they aren't sacrifices.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: So in the example of housing, if we value relationships, sharing a home isn't depriving ourselves of space, but giving us an opportunity to spend more time with our loved ones.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: Indeed it is.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcriptTranslations: 欢迎来到读书俱乐部。今天的嘉宾是Susan Lane,她是一本个人理财新书的作者,这本书已经卖出了50万册。你好,Susan,你的书非常成功。你觉得这是为什么呢?
我觉得是因为我传达的理念,就是把幸福放在金钱之上。我们这一代有太多人花了几十年时间想挣更多钱,只是为了消费更多,但这让我们更痛苦。
你自己也曾陷入那种循环,做了20年高管,拿着高薪,但还是欠了一身债。
我确实是。我挣了几百万,但四年前当我辞职去当作家的时候,我还欠着3万多美元。
那你是怎么摆脱那种模式的?你会建议其他人怎么做呢?
首先要改变的是我们看重什么。我们需要强调那些真正让我们快乐的东西,比如人际关系、环境,甚至我们的爱好。一旦我们把正确的东西放在首位,我们的目标就会改变,我们的财务行为也会随之改变。
那在实际行动中怎么体现呢?你能给我们的听众举些日常生活中的例子吗?
主要的行动领域通常是住房、食物和交通。所以人们可以和朋友合租而不是独自住,从家里带午饭而不是去餐馆,使用公共交通而不是买车。
这些听起来像是很大的牺牲,我永远做不到合租,我需要自己的空间。
但这些不是牺牲。当人们改变他们的价值观时,他们的愿望也会改变。所以拿住房来说,如果我们重视人际关系,合租不是剥夺我们的空间,而是给我们机会和所爱的人在一起更多时间。
确实如此。
谢谢你邀请我来画廊,Christopher。自从你前任的退休招待会之后我就没来过这里了。
你想先看看我们馆藏的最新藏品吗,Catherine?
是Danielle Gregory的那些风景画吗?我特别喜欢她的作品。
第一幅作品是艺术家本人赠送给画廊的,非常精美。
我喜欢她描绘荒凉景色的方式。色彩搭配得非常完美。
你能从画中感受到那种荒凉。这幅作品的灵感来自Gregory最近的戈壁沙漠之旅。
那你们是怎么得到她这边的另一幅作品的?
是一位匿名收藏家在拍卖会上购买的,然后借给画廊展出。这幅是她最受赞誉的画作之一。
那位收藏家买这幅画肯定花了一大笔钱。
显然我不能透露他支付的具体金额,但确实很可观。
这幅画有太多细节了。我感觉自己真的能沉浸在这个场景中。我特别喜欢山在湖中的倒影所形成的对称感。
这幅作品就是被提名Gateway Award的那幅。我很幸运能作为Gregory的客人参加了颁奖典礼。
所以你和她私下认识。我猜她是个很古怪的艺术家吧。
恰恰相反。事实上,她一点都不古怪。我觉得她是我认识的人中最随和、最聪明的人之一。
我很想见见她。我有好多问题想问。
真巧!我今晚要和她一起吃晚饭。你想一起来吗?
我很乐意。谢谢你。

questions.prompt: What message does the woman convey in her book?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） Prioritizing happiness over money.
**题目译文**
这位女士在她的书中传达了什么信息?
A) 把幸福置于金钱之上。
B) 加入俱乐部以获得她的新书。
C) 明智地管理个人财务。
D) 只有在挣得更多时才消费更多。
**定位** 我想那是因为我书里的核心讯息——把幸福置于金钱之上。
**信号** my message is 自报主旨。女方用 that's because of my message, which is making happiness a priority over money 亲口点出 my message（我的核心讯息），这种受访者自报观点的句子就是答案信号，无需再推。
**替换** making happiness a priority over money↔Prioritizing happiness over money短语换说法、意思全等
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 未提及录音里男方说 Welcome to the Book Club 又提 a new book，B 借「book/club」这两个原词诱你联想「入会拿书」，但全篇没有任何「加入俱乐部以获取她新书」的内容，是凭原词拼出的假选项。借用原文： Welcome to the Book Club
C) 原词陷阱Managing one's personal finances wisely 用了书的主题词 personal finances（原文 a new book on personal finances），听着像那么回事，但女方的核心讯息是「幸福优先于金钱」这个价值排序，而非笼统的「明智理财」，C 用原词把观点稀释成了空泛口号。借用原文： a new book on personal finances
D) 与原文相反Consuming more only when earning more 盗用原文 trying to earn more money, just to consume more 的 earn / consume，但那是女方批判的旧循环（结果让人更痛苦），不是她要传达的讯息，正话被反着取了。借用原文： trying to earn more money, just to consume more, but it made us more miserable
questions.quote: I think that's because of my message, which is making happiness a priority over money.

options.text: Prioritizing happiness over money.
Joining the club to get her new book.
Managing one's personal finances wisely.
Consuming more only when earning more.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the woman before she became a writer?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） She was in debt.
**题目译文**
关于这位女士成为作家之前的情况,我们了解到什么?
A) 她负债累累。
B) 她是一名理财顾问。
C) 她每月挣3万美元。
D) 她享有幸福的生活。
**定位** 我挣过数百万，但等到四年前我辞职去当作家时，我已欠债超过 3 万美元。
**信号** 转折 but 后才是真处境。句中 I earned millions, but by the time I quit my job…I owed over \$30,000 用 but 转折，前半「挣过数百万」是铺垫，转折后的「欠债三万」才是她当作家前的真实处境，转折后即落点。
**替换** I owed over \$30,000↔ She was in debt owe 概括为 in debt
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 偷换概念She was a financial adviser 借书谈 personal finances 的「financial」联想出「理财顾问」，但原文说她过去是 working for two decades as an executive（高管），不是理财顾问，职业被张冠李戴。借用原文： working for two decades as an executive
C) 原词陷阱She earned \$30,000 a month 直接搬来原文数字 \$30,000，但原文 \$30,000 是 I owed over \$30,000 的「欠债额」，不是月收入；她的收入原文说的是 earned millions。数字对、名目全错。借用原文： I owed over \$30,000
D) 与原文相反She enjoyed a happy life 与原文相反：女方说当年那段循环 made us more miserable（更痛苦），过去并不幸福，D 反了极性。借用原文： but it made us more miserable
questions.quote: I earned millions, but by the time I quit my job four years ago to become a writer, I owed over $30,000.

options.text: She was in debt.
She was a financial adviser.
She earned $30,000 a month.
She enjoyed a happy life.

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about one's financial behavior?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） It changes with one's goals in life.
**题目译文**
关于个人理财行为,这位女士说了什么?
A) 它反映一个人的挣钱能力。
B) 它随一个人所处的环境而变化。
C) 它反映一个人的幸福感。
D) 它随一个人的人生目标而改变。
**定位** 一旦我们把对的事情当作优先项，我们的目标就会改变，财务行为也随之改变。
**信号** Once…and so will 的因果链。Once we make the right things our priority, our goals will change and so will our financial behavior 用 Once（一旦）引导条件、so will 承接连锁：目标改变带动财务行为改变，财务行为是被「目标」牵着走的，因果链尾即答案。
**替换** our goals will change and so will our financial behavior↔It changes with one's goals in life so will 还原成 changes with goals
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 偷换概念It reflects one's earning power 蹭了全篇 earn / earned 的高频词，但原文说财务行为由goals 决定，从未说它「反映挣钱能力」，归因对象被换掉了。借用原文： trying to earn more money
B) 原词陷阱It varies with one's environment 的 environment 确实在原文出现过——但那是relationships, the environment or even our hobbies 里「值得珍视的事物」之一，不是决定财务行为的因素，词对、关系错。借用原文： like relationships, the environment or even our hobbies
C) 未提及It varies with one's environment 与 B 同样把 environment 当成变量来源，原文从未说财务行为随环境变化，纯属拼词造句。借用原文： like relationships, the environment or even our hobbies
questions.quote: Once we make the right things our priority, our goals will change and so will our financial behavior.

options.text: It reflects one's earning power.
It varies with one's environment.
It mirrors one's sense of well-being.
It changes with one's goals in life.

questions.prompt: What does the man say about sharing a home?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （态度观点题） It would mean major sacrifices for him.
**题目译文**
关于合住,这位男士说了什么?
A) 这会让他有更多时间陪伴所爱的人。
B) 这对重视人际关系的人有好处。
C) 这对他来说意味着重大牺牲。
D) 这会剥夺他的个性。
**定位** 那些听起来像是重大的牺牲，我绝不可能跟人合住，我需要自己的空间。
**信号** 男方直接应答表态。在女方讲完合住等做法后，男方紧接着应答 Those sound like major sacrifices, I could never share my home, I need my own space，这是被问者本人的直接表态，态度题的答案就落在这句应答上。
**替换** Those sound like major sacrifices↔ It would mean major sacrifices for him几乎原词、补出主语 for him
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 张冠李戴It would give him more time to be with his loved ones 来自女方 giving us an opportunity to spend more time with our loved ones，那是女方反驳时说的合住好处，不是男方的看法，主体说反了。借用原文： giving us an opportunity to spend more time with our loved ones
B) 张冠李戴It would be good for those who value relationships 对应女方观点 if we value relationships, sharing a home isn't depriving ourselves of space，仍是女方的论调而非男方所说，归属错位。借用原文： if we value relationships, sharing a home isn't depriving ourselves of space
D) 原词陷阱It would deprive him of his individuality 蹭了女方原文 sharing a home isn't depriving ourselves of space 的 depriving，但原文说的是「不会剥夺空间」且是女方所言，D 既盗词又把否定说成肯定、还安到男方头上。借用原文： sharing a home isn't depriving ourselves of space
questions.quote: Those sound like major sacrifices, I could never share my home, I need my own space.

options.text: It would give him more time to be with his loved ones.
It would be good for those who value relationships.
It would mean major sacrifices for him.
It would deprive him of his individuality.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about one of the newest additions to the gallery's collection?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） It was donated by the artist herself.
**题目译文**
关于画廊藏品中最新增添的作品之一,我们了解到什么?
A) 这是该艺术家的第一幅风景画。
B) 这是Christopher的一幅画作。
C) 这是由艺术家本人捐赠的。
D) 这在一次退休派对上展出过。
**定位** 这第一幅是艺术家本人赠送给画廊的，相当精美。
**信号** 被问者对新藏品的直接交代。女士问要不要看新藏品后，男士直接介绍 This first piece was a gift to the gallery from the artist herself——这是被问者对该画来历的正面应答，就是答案句。
**替换** a gift to the gallery from the artist herself↔donated by the artist herself a gift = donated 同义改写
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱录音里女士提到 those the landscapes by Danielle Gregory，男士又说 This first piece，选项 A 把 first 与 landscape 拼成『这是她的第一幅风景画』，但 first 只是『第一幅展品』之序，原文从未说是画家生涯首作。借用原文： This first piece
B) 张冠李戴Christopher 是开头女士称呼的画廊负责人（Thank you for inviting me to the gallery, Christopher.），画作者是 Danielle Gregory；选项 B 把这画说成 Christopher 所画，属张冠李戴。借用原文： Christopher
D) 原词陷阱录音里女士说上次来还是 your predecessor's retirement function（前任的退休活动），与这幅画的展示毫无关系；选项 D 把这个退休场合搬来当画作展出地，纯属错配。借用原文： your predecessor's retirement function
questions.quote: This first piece was a gift to the gallery from the artist herself, and it's quite exquisite.

options.text: It was the artist's first landscape.
It was a painting by Christopher.
It was donated by the artist herself.
It was displayed at a retirement party.

questions.prompt: What does the man say about one of the most acclaimed paintings by Danielle Gregory?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） It is owned by an anonymous collector.
**题目译文**
关于Danielle Gregory最受赞誉的画作之一,男士说了什么?
A) 正是这幅画让她立刻变得富有。
B) 他花了很多钱来购买它。
C) 这是画廊最近购入的。
D) 它为一位匿名收藏家所有。
**定位** 它是由一位匿名收藏家在拍卖会上买下的，那人把它借给画廊展出。这幅作品是她最受赞誉的画作之一。
**信号** 被问者对『这画怎么来的』的直接应答。女士问 how did you obtain her other piece over here?，男士应答 purchased at auction by an anonymous collector who lent it to the gallery——问归属、答归属，就是答案句。
**替换** purchased at auction by an anonymous collector who lent it to the gallery↔owned by an anonymous collector买下并出借 = 仍归其所有
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及选项 A 说这画让『她』瞬间致富，录音通篇没提画家因此画暴富；倒是后文说藏家花了 it was substantial 一大笔钱，但那是藏家花钱，不是画家致富，属未提及。
B) 张冠李戴录音确实说买这画花了一大笔（cost that collector a small fortune、it was substantial），但花钱的是匿名藏家，不是男士本人；选项 B 用 cost him 把买家偷换成男士。借用原文： It must have cost that collector a small fortune
C) 与原文相反录音原句确有 purchased at auction，但买家是匿名藏家，不是画廊；选项 C 把『画廊近期购入』套上 purchased 一词，恰与原文相反（画廊只是借展、并未买）。借用原文： purchased at auction by an anonymous collector
questions.quote: It was purchased at auction by an anonymous collector who lent it to the gallery for display. This composition is one of her most acclaimed paintings.

options.text: It was the painting that instantly made her rich.
It has cost him a lot of money to purchase it.
It was recently purchased by the gallery.
It is owned by an anonymous collector.

questions.prompt: Why does the woman say she can feel immersed in the scene in the painting?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） It contains ample details.
**题目译文**
为什么女士说她能感到自己沉浸在画中的场景里?
A) 它反映了她的情感。
B) 它包含大量细节。
C) 它看起来完全对称。
D) 它描绘了荒凉之美。
**定位** 这幅画里有这么多细节。我感觉自己真能沉浸到画面之中。
**信号** 感受句前的原因陈述。女士先说 There's so much detail in this painting，紧接着才说 I can really immerse myself in the scene——『大量细节』是她能沉浸的原因，先因后果，前句即落点。
**替换** There's so much detail in this painting↔contains ample details so much detail = ample details
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及录音里只有 You can sense the desolation 这类气氛话，且女士谈沉浸时给的理由是细节多，不是『画反映她的情感』；选项 A 的 emotions 录音并未作为沉浸之由提出，属未提及。
C) 答非所问女士确实说了 I particularly like the symmetry created by the reflection，但那是她另外补充喜欢的一点，不是『能沉浸』的原因；本题问的沉浸之由是前一句的 so much detail，选项 C 把相邻却不同句的对称搬来顶替。借用原文： the symmetry created by the reflection of the mountain in the lake
D) 原词陷阱荒凉之美 You can sense the desolation in the picture 是男士谈另一幅戈壁画作时的话，与女士此处『因细节多而沉浸』无关；选项 D 把 desolation 搬来当沉浸理由，属答非所问。借用原文： You can sense the desolation in the picture
questions.quote: There's so much detail in this painting. I feel like I can really immerse myself in the scene.

options.text: It reflects her emotions.
It contains ample details.
It appears perfectly symmetrical.
It depicts the beauty of desolation.

questions.prompt: How does the man describe Danielle Gregory?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （态度观点题） She is a very nice and intelligent artist.
**题目译文**
男士如何描述Danielle Gregory?
A) 她像任何其他艺术家一样古怪。
B) 她是一位非常好且聪明的艺术家。
C) 她像任何受赞誉的艺术家一样幸运。
D) 她是最多产的艺术家之一。
**定位** 恰恰相反。事实上，她一点也不古怪。我会说她是我认识的最随和、最聪明的人之一。
**信号** 转折否定后才是真评价。女士猜她古怪，男士先 Quite the opposite、再 not at all eccentric 把猜测顶回去，转折否定之后的 easygoing and intelligent 才是他的真实评价，正是答案句。
**替换** she's one of the most easygoing and intelligent people I know↔She is a very nice and intelligent artist. easygoing = nice，intelligent 原义保留

A) 与原文相反eccentric 录音里确实出现，但男士是 she's not at all eccentric 加以否定的；选项 A 取了被否定掉的那个词，与男士本意正好相反。借用原文： she's not at all eccentric
C) 张冠李戴录音里 I was lucky enough to attend the award ceremony 说的是男士自己幸运，不是画家幸运；选项 C 把 lucky 挪到对画家的评价上，属张冠李戴。借用原文： I was lucky enough to attend the award ceremony
D) 未提及录音说她最受赞誉、随和聪明，但从未说她是最高产的画家；选项 D 的 most productive录音里没有对应，属未提及。

transcript.text: In last week's lecture, we talked about the problems caused by poor eating habits, focusing on how medical professionals are trying to solve these problems.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Today, we'll continue with the topic, but focus on research from a different field—marketing.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Now, what can marketing tell us about improving nutrition?
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Well, a team of marketing professors has studied the importance of the visual aspect of food and how that influences food choices.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Those marketing experts assert that the impact of the appearance of food is greater than we might presume, and might hold the key to encouraging better eating.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: So how important is the appearance of food?
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Research shows that just seeing an appealing photograph of a hamburger in an advertisement, for example, can cause individuals to imagine the taste or smell of that hamburger.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: This can make them more likely to purchase and consume it.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Of course, that's the point of advertisements.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: So isn't that a good thing?
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Well, the marketing professors argue that this is actually a problem, because the combination of pleasing aesthetics of and easy access to unhealthy foods, such as hamburgers and pizza, may be contributing to a worldwide health crisis.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In fact, statistics show that 39% of all adults in the world weigh too much and another 13% are obese.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Now, as we discussed last time, medical professionals have tried to fight the obesity epidemic by focusing on the nutrients found in different foods, emphasizing things like carbohydrate, fat, sugar and calorie content.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: But they've had limited success.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The marketing professors believe that the real solution to obesity is making food look appealing and focusing on the pleasure of both looking at and eating that food.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: That pleasure can be used as a tool to promote healthy food choices.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In fact, the research done by the team showed that associating healthy food with pleasant images, experiences and emotions led to greater interest in purchasing or eating it.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: "This is a better strategy," they claim, than reminding consumers that a certain food is good for them.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: But are they right?
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Well, the researchers cited a marketing campaign designed to reverse the sales decline of carrots.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The campaign didn't emphasize the carrots' healthy qualities, but embraced their beauty and the pleasure derived from eating them.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: For example, the ads focused on the bright, beautiful orange color and crisp texture of the carrots.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The campaign led to an impressive increase in product sales of more than 10%.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The researchers believe that other companies could bolster sales of healthy foods with similar ads, depicting their products as attractive and a source of pleasure.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The household cleaning products industry really began to take off in the 1950s.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Prior to that, resourceful housewives who had grown up in a less prosperous era relied on substances that they used in their kitchens such as vinegar used to clean windows.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Today, the household cleaning products industry is worth billions of dollars a year and is dominated by large global companies.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In recent years, however, many countries have witnessed a surge in the number of small businesses and companies offering more environment-friendly cleaning products, and they're doing good business too.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: One reason for this is that consumers are becoming more aware of environment and sustainability issues.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They also want to make their home a safe place, free from toxic chemicals.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The third reason is people's awareness of and knowledge about technology has never been greater.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In the past, people might have been skeptical of a new product claimed to be able to achieve amazing cleaning results, but they now have faith in technology's ability to do what was once thought impossible.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The company claims its cloth lifts, traps and removes dirt and bacteria.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: And considering that people don't see these products in shops, or advertised on TV or in the press, it has been a pretty steep rise.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Many of the people behind these companies began testing the viability of their products by selling them at local markets.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Then, in many cases, customers are doing the marketing for these products by leaving threads of comments on social media, praising their virtues.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: There are also TV shows and books dedicated to maintaining home tidiness and cleanliness and the benefits of having a clean home.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Having a safe and clean home might be one thing people feel they can control in an increasingly out- of-control world.

transcript.text: And there are social media celebrities.

transcript.text: Throwing spare change into a fountain is a time-honored ritual: throw a penny into the water, and your wish might come true.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: But all that money has to go somewhere.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Otherwise, the growing piles of pennies, quarters and euros could clog up the fountains' works.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Today, I'm going to talk about where all the coins go.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Well, the coins collected can go to all sorts of different places—from fountain maintenance to charity or public service.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In New York City, for example, coins collected from fountains in public parks often go towards the fountains' maintenance itself, though entrepreneurs who don't mind getting their hands wet often get to it first.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: There are over 50 beautiful decorative display fountains in New York City parks.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They are cleaned by the parks' staff every few weeks.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: But most of the coins have already been removed by entrepreneurial New Yorkers and there is not a significant amount left to be collected.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Other cities, though, can pull in a much more serious haul.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Take for example, Rome's famous Trevi fountain: for hundreds of years, visitors have thrown coins over their shoulder into the fountain to ensure that they will return.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: So many tourists toss in coins that Roman officials have the fountain cleaned every night, reportedly getting as much as $4,000 in loose change from around the world each day.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Most of the money collected each night goes towards running a supermarket for the needy.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: And collecting that cash is serious business.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Roman officials have been known to be tough on anyone caught skimming coins from the fountain.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In one case in 2005, police arrested four fountain cleaners after they were spotted slipping coins into their own pockets after collecting them.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Authorities finally caught one notorious thief named Thomas Morgan and banned him from the fountain after he fished out thousands of dollars in change over 34 years using a magnetic stick.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: For the most part, money collected from privately-owned fountains in the United States also goes to charity.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The fountain in New York City's Bryant Park is owned and operated by a not-for-profit corporation, which puts the cash collected by cleaners towards the fountain's own maintenance.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Tens of thousands of dollars in coins removed from wishing wells, fountains and ponds in Florida's Walt Disney World are donated each year to support foster children living in the state.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Whether or not your wish comes true after tossing a coin into a fountain, you can rest assured knowing that the change is likely going to someone who needs it.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcriptTranslations: 在上周的讲座中,我们谈到了不良饮食习惯造成的问题,重点讨论了医疗专业人员如何努力解决这些问题。今天,我们将继续这个话题,但会聚焦于来自不同领域的研究——市场营销。
那么,市场营销能告诉我们什么关于改善营养的信息呢?一个市场营销教授团队研究了食物视觉方面的重要性,以及它如何影响食物选择。
这些市场营销专家断言,食物外观的影响力比我们想象的要大,并且可能是鼓励更好饮食的关键。那么食物的外观有多重要呢?
研究表明,仅仅是在广告中看到一张诱人的汉堡照片,就能让人们想象那个汉堡的味道或气味。这会使他们更有可能购买和食用它。当然,这就是广告的目的。那么这难道不是一件好事吗?
然而,这些市场营销教授认为这实际上是个问题,因为不健康食品(如汉堡和披萨)令人愉悦的美感与便捷的获取途径相结合,可能正在导致一场全球性的健康危机。事实上,统计数据显示,全世界39%的成年人超重,另有13%肥胖。
正如我们上次讨论的,医疗专业人员试图通过关注不同食物中的营养成分来对抗肥胖流行病,强调碳水化合物、脂肪、糖和卡路里含量等内容。但他们取得的成效有限。
这些市场营销教授认为,解决肥胖问题的真正办法是让食物看起来诱人,并关注观看和食用食物的愉悦感。这种愉悦感可以作为促进健康食物选择的工具。事实上,该团队进行的研究表明,将健康食品与愉快的图像、体验和情感联系起来,会增加人们购买或食用它的兴趣。他们声称,"这是一个更好的策略",而不是提醒消费者某种食物对他们有益。但他们说得对吗?
研究人员引用了一个旨在扭转胡萝卜销售下滑的市场营销活动。该活动没有强调胡萝卜的健康品质,而是展现了它们的美感以及食用它们带来的愉悦。例如,广告聚焦于胡萝卜明亮美丽的橙色和爽脆的质地。该活动使产品销量大幅增长了10%以上。研究人员认为,其他公司可以通过类似的广告来提升健康食品的销量,将其产品描绘成具有吸引力且能带来愉悦的来源。
家庭清洁产品行业真正开始腾飞是在20世纪50年代。在此之前,在不太富裕时代长大的精打细算的家庭主妇们依赖她们在厨房中使用的物质,如用醋来清洁窗户。
如今,家庭清洁产品行业每年价值数十亿美元,并由大型跨国公司主导。然而近年来,许多国家见证了提供更环保清洁产品的小企业和公司数量激增,而且它们的生意也很好。
原因之一是消费者对环境和可持续发展问题的意识越来越强。他们还希望让自己的家成为一个安全的地方,远离有毒化学物质。第三个原因是人们对技术的认识和了解从未如此之高。过去,人们可能会对声称能够达到惊人清洁效果的新产品持怀疑态度,但他们现在相信技术有能力做到曾经认为不可能的事情。
也许没有比一家公司销售的专利布更好的例子了,它显著地只使用水而不是传统清洁产品。该公司声称其布料能够提起、捕获和去除污垢和细菌。考虑到人们在商店里看不到这些产品,也没有在电视或报刊上看到广告,这已经是一个相当陡峭的增长了。
这些公司背后的许多人开始通过在当地市场销售来测试其产品的可行性。然后,在许多情况下,顾客通过在社交媒体上留下大量评论来为这些产品做营销,称赞它们的优点。还有专门讲述保持家庭整洁和清洁以及拥有干净家庭的好处的电视节目和书籍。
在一个日益失控的世界中,拥有一个安全干净的家可能是人们觉得自己能够控制的一件事。还有社交媒体名人。英国一位女性因其清洁技巧页面而成为社交媒体轰动人物,拥有超过两百万粉丝。
向喷泉中投掷零钱是一项历史悠久的仪式:将一枚硬币扔进水中,你的愿望就有可能实现。但所有这些钱必须有去处。否则,不断堆积的便士、两角五分硬币和欧元可能会堵塞喷泉的运作系统。今天,我将谈谈所有这些硬币的去向。
收集到的硬币可以流向各种不同的地方——从喷泉维护到慈善或公共服务。例如在纽约市,从公共公园喷泉中收集的硬币通常用于喷泉本身的维护,尽管不介意弄湿双手的创业者往往会抢先一步。纽约市公园里有50多座美丽的装饰性展示喷泉。它们每隔几周就由公园工作人员清理一次。但大部分硬币已经被有创业精神的纽约人拿走了,剩下可供收集的数量并不多。

然而,其他城市的收获可能要丰厚得多。以罗马著名的Trevi喷泉为例:数百年来,游客们将硬币从肩膀上方抛入喷泉以确保他们会再次回来。有如此多的游客投掷硬币,以至于罗马官员每天夜里都要清理喷泉,据报道每天能收集到来自世界各地价值高达4000美元的零钱。每晚收集到的大部分钱用于运营一家为贫困人群服务的超市。收集这些现金是一项严肃的工作。罗马官员对任何被抓到从喷泉中私拿硬币的人都会严厉处理。在2005年的一个案例中,警方逮捕了四名喷泉清洁工,因为他们被发现在收集硬币后将硬币偷偷塞进自己的口袋。当局最终抓获了一名叫Thomas Morgan的臭名昭著的小偷,并禁止他靠近喷泉,此前他在34年间使用磁棒从喷泉中捞取了数千美元的零钱。
在美国,从私人拥有的喷泉中收集的钱大部分也流向了慈善机构。纽约市Bryant公园的喷泉由一家非营利公司拥有和运营,该公司将清洁工收集的现金用于喷泉自身的维护。佛罗里达州Walt Disney World的许愿井、喷泉和池塘中取出的数万美元硬币每年都被捐赠用于支持该州的寄养儿童。无论你向喷泉投掷硬币后愿望是否实现,你都可以放心,这些零钱很可能会流向需要它的人。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say a team of marketing professors has studied?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） The importance of the appearance of food.
**题目译文**
说话者说一个营销学教授团队研究了什么?
A) 增加健康食品供应的关键。
B) 改进营销研究的最佳方法。
C) 广告对消费的影响。
D) 食物外观的重要性。
**定位** 嗯，一组营销学教授研究了食物视觉方面的重要性，以及它如何影响食物选择。
**信号** 题干原词 studied 在原文直接出现。录音 a team of marketing professors has studied the importance of the visual aspect of food 与题干同用 studied，是对研究对象的直接交代，定位信号明确，无需转折或推断。
**替换** the importance of the visual aspect of food↔The importance of the appearance of food. visual aspect 同义改写为 appearance
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱选项把录音多次提到的 healthy 拼成 increasing healthy food supply，但录音研究的是外观对选择的影响，从未谈增加健康食品的供给量，属听到 healthy 就想选的原词陷阱。借用原文： promote healthy food choices
B) 原词陷阱选项借用录音里的 marketing 拼成 improve marketing research，但讲者说的是营销学者拿来研究外观，而非研究如何改进市场调研本身，属答非所问。借用原文： a team of marketing professors
C) 原词陷阱录音确实在 seeing an appealing photograph of a hamburger in an advertisement 提到广告，但那是用来举例说明外观如何起作用，不是这组学者研究的对象；选项把举例细节当成研究主题，属原词陷阱。借用原文： an appealing photograph of a hamburger in an advertisement
questions.quote: Well, a team of marketing professors has studied the importance of the visual aspect of food and how that influences food choices.

options.text: The key to increasing healthy food supply.
The best way to improve marketing research.
The impact of advertisements on consumption.
The importance of the appearance of food.

questions.prompt: How have medical professionals tried to fight obesity?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） By focusing on the nutrients in different foods.
**题目译文**
医疗专业人员如何努力对抗肥胖?
A) 通过关注不同食物中的营养成分。
B) 通过强调食物的多样性。
C) 通过强调食物赏心悦目的美感。
D) 通过赢得营销学教授的支持。
**定位** 医学专家曾试图通过关注不同食物中的营养成分来对抗肥胖流行病，强调诸如碳水化合物、脂肪、糖和卡路里含量之类的东西。
**信号** 主体词 medical professionals 领出做法句。录音 medical professionals have tried to fight the obesity epidemic by focusing on the nutrients 主体与题干完全一致，by focusing on 直接给出做法，是该主体名下的答案句信号。
**替换** by focusing on the nutrients found in different foods↔By focusing on the nutrients in different foods.几乎原句对应仅省略 found
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 未提及选项 By emphasizing the diversity of food. 的 diversity 在录音里从未出现，医学专家强调的是营养成分而非食物多样性，属无中生有。
C) 张冠李戴强调美感 By stressing pleasing aesthetics of food. 确是录音里的做法，但那是营销学者的主张，不是医学专家的做法；选项把营销学者的招安到医学专家头上，属张冠李戴。借用原文： the combination of pleasing aesthetics
D) 原词陷阱选项 By winning the support of marketing professors. 借用录音里的 marketing professors，但录音从没说医学专家去争取营销教授的支持，二者只是讲座中并列对比的两方，属原词陷阱。借用原文： a team of marketing professors

questions.prompt: What can other companies learn from the example of the carrot promotion campaign?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （推断题） They can boost sales of healthy foods by making them visually appealing.
**题目译文**
其他公司能从胡萝卜促销活动的例子中学到什么?
A) 它们可以用产品的健康品质吸引顾客。
B) 它们可以通过使健康食品在视觉上更吸引人来提升销量。
C) 它们可以向营销学教授寻求建议。
D) 它们可以依靠广告进行促销。
**定位** 研究者认为，其他公司可以用类似的广告来提升健康食品的销量，把它们的产品描绘得有吸引力、是一种愉悦的来源。
**信号** 结尾外推句 could+similar 给出启示。录音结尾 other companies could bolster sales of healthy foods with similar ads 用 could 与 similar 把胡萝卜案例外推到其他公司，正是题干所问的启示落点。
**替换** bolster sales of healthy foods with similar ads, depicting their products as attractive ↔They can boost sales of healthy foods by making them visually appealing. bolster=boost、attractive=visually appealing
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反选项 They can attract customers with the healthy qualities of their products. 借用录音didn't emphasize the carrots' healthy qualities 的原词，但录音明说该案例恰恰没强调健康属性，选项把否定说成肯定，属与原文相反。借用原文： The campaign didn't emphasize the carrots' healthy qualities
C) 原词陷阱选项 They can turn to marketing professors for advice. 借用录音里的 marketing professors，但讲者说的是公司可用类似广告，从没说让公司去求助营销教授，属原词陷阱。借用原文： a team of marketing professors
D) 偷换概念选项 They can rely on advertising for sales promotion. 借用录音的 ads，但录音强调的是靠把产品拍得有吸引力、令人愉悦的广告，而非泛泛依赖广告；选项丢掉视觉吸引这一关键限定，属偷换概念。借用原文： bolster sales of healthy foods with similar ads, depicting their products as attractive and a source of pleasure
questions.quote: The researchers believe that other companies could bolster sales of healthy foods with similar ads, depicting their products as attractive and a source of pleasure.

options.text: They can attract customers with the healthy qualities of their products.
They can boost sales of healthy foods by making them visually appealing.
They can turn to marketing professors for advice.
They can rely on advertising for sales promotion.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about the cleaning products industry in recent years?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） It has seen more small businesses offering environment-friendly products.
**题目译文**
说话者关于近年来清洁产品行业说了什么?
A) 该行业需求出现了惊人的激增。
B) 该行业受到了环保主义者的诸多批评。
C) 该行业出现了更多提供环保产品的小企业。
D) 该行业经历了全球公司之间日益激烈的竞争。
**定位** 然而近年来，许多国家见证了提供更环保清洁用品的小企业和公司数量激增，而且它们的生意还相当不错。
**信号** 时间标志 in recent years + 转折 however。In recent years, however 同时给出题干要的时间窗和一个转折信号——however 把话锋从前句"大公司主导"转向"小企业崛起"，转折之后才是答案落点。
**替换** a surge in the number of small businesses and companies offering more environment-friendly cleaning products↔ more small businesses offering environment-friendly products a surge in the number of = more 的同义概括
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱录音确实念了 surge，但原文是 a surge in the number of small businesses（企业数量激增），选项 a spectacular surge in demand 把它偷换成"需求激增"，听到 surge 就选会中招。借用原文： a surge in the number of small businesses and companies
B) 未提及选项 much criticism from environmentalists 在录音里找不到任何对应——原文讲的是环保产品走红、生意红火，从无"被批评"之说，属凭空捏造。
D) 原词陷阱录音第2段确有 large global companies，选项 fierce competition among global companies 借这个词造出"全球公司竞争加剧"，可原文只说大公司"主导"行业，没说它们之间竞争更激烈。借用原文： dominated by large global companies
questions.quote: In recent years, however, many countries have witnessed a surge in the number of small businesses and companies offering more environment-friendly cleaning products, and they're doing good business too.

options.text: It has witnessed a spectacular surge in demand.
It has met much criticism from environmentalists.
It has seen more small businesses offering environment-friendly products.
It has experienced increasingly fierce competition among global companies.

questions.prompt: Why are newly developed cleaning products selling well?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） Consumers now know much more about technology.
**题目译文**
为什么新开发的清洁产品卖得很好?
A) 消费者现在对技术了解得多得多。
B) 它们的大规模生产大幅降低了价格。
C) 消费者倾向于青睐一切新颖的东西。
D) 它们的质量得到了极大改善。
**定位** 第三个原因是，人们对技术的认知和了解从未像现在这样深。过去人们可能会怀疑一款号称能达到惊人清洁效果的新产品，但如今他们相信技术有能力做到曾被认为不可能的事。
**信号** 明示标志 The third reason + 对应题干"new products"。The third reason is people's awareness of and knowledge about technology has never been greater 用 The third reason 直接挂出一条理由；题干问的是 newly developed products，对应的正是这条"人们更懂技术、因而信任新产品"的原因。
**替换** people's awareness of and knowledge about technology has never been greater↔Consumers now know much more about technology knowledge…never been greater = know much more 的同义改写
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 未提及选项 mass production has sharply reduced the price 听上去顺理成章，但录音讲好卖的原因是环保意识、安全、懂技术，从头到尾没提"量产降价"，是用生活常识替代原文。
C) 过度推断选项 favor all that is novel（偏爱一切新奇）看似贴近"新产品"，但录音说的是人们 have faith in technology（信任技术能力），不是"凡新必爱"，把"信任技术"推成"盲目追新"推过了头。借用原文： they now have faith in technology's ability to do what was once thought impossible
D) 偷换概念选项 quality has been greatly improved 录音并未提及——原文讲的是消费者对技术的"认知与信任"，而非产品"质量本身"提高了，二者不能混为一谈。
questions.quote: The third reason is people's awareness of and knowledge about technology has never been greater. In the past, people might have been skeptical of a new product claimed to be able to achieve amazing cleaning results, but they now have faith in technology's ability to do what was once thought impossible.

options.text: Consumers now know much more about technology.
Their mass production has sharply reduced the price
Consumers tend to favor all that is novel.
Their quality has been greatly improved.

questions.prompt: What are some customers doing to help promote non-traditional cleaning products?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） Writing positive comments about them on social media.
**题目译文**
一些顾客正在做什么来帮助推广非传统清洁产品?
A) 只购买这类产品用于家庭清洁。
B) 在社交媒体上撰写关于它们的正面评论。
C) 在电视上演示这些产品有多有效。
D) 相互告知它们无可比拟的优点。
**定位** 然后，很多情况下，是顾客在为这些产品做营销——他们在社交媒体上留下一串串评论，称赞产品的优点。
**信号** 主语对应 customers + 动作 doing the marketing。customers are doing the marketing for these products 的主语正是题干的 customers、目的正是 help promote（做营销=帮推广），后面 by leaving… 直接交代了具体做法，是答案句。
**替换** leaving threads of comments on social media, praising their virtues↔Writing positive comments about them on social media leaving…comments, praising = writing positive comments 的同义改写
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及选项 Purchasing only this kind of products 里的 only（只买这一种）录音没有任何依据——原文讲顾客帮做营销、写评论，从没说他们"只"用这类产品。
C) 原词陷阱录音第4段提过 TV（advertised on TV）、第5段提过 TV shows，选项 Demonstrating on TV 借这些 TV 造"上电视演示"，可原文恰恰说这类产品没在电视宣传、且"上电视演示"是节目而非顾客所为，听到 TV 就选会中招。借用原文： people don't see these products in shops, or advertised on TV or in the press
D) 原词陷阱选项 Telling one another about their incomparable virtues 用了录音的 virtues，但原文顾客是"在社交媒体写评论"称赞，而非 Telling one another（互相口头转告）；盗了对的词、错在渠道。借用原文： leaving threads of comments on social media, praising their virtues
questions.quote: Then, in many cases, customers are doing the marketing for these products by leaving threads of comments on social media, praising their virtues.

options.text: Purchasing only this kind of products for home cleaning.
Writing positive comments about them on social media.
Demonstrating on TV how effective these products are.
Telling one another about their incomparable virtues.

questions.prompt: What problem might be caused by the growing piles of coins in fountains?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） Blocking the fountains' works.
**题目译文**
喷泉中不断堆积的硬币可能会造成什么问题?
A) 增加清洁工的工作量。
B) 堵塞喷泉的运作装置。
C) 破坏一项由来已久的仪式。
D) 污染喷泉的水。
**定位** 否则，越堆越多的便士、25 美分和欧元硬币可能会堵塞喷泉的运作机件。
**信号** Otherwise 引出假设后果。信号是 Otherwise（否则）——它引出"如果钱不被运走会怎样"的假设性后果，正对题干问的"会造成什么问题"，紧跟其后的 could clog up the fountains' works 就是答案句的核心。
**替换** clog up the fountains' works↔ Blocking the fountains' works clog up = Blocking 同义替换
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱选项 Increasing cleaners' workload 里的 cleaners 在后文确实反复出现（喷泉由 staff 清理），但录音从没说"硬币堆积会加重清洁工负担"，是借后文的"清洁"话题诱你听到cleaners 就选。借用原文： They are cleaned by the parks' staff every few weeks.
C) 原词陷阱选项 Breaking a time-honored ritual 直接搬了录音第一句的 time-honored ritual，但那句是说"投币许愿是个老传统"，是引入话题，根本不是在讲"硬币堆积造成的问题"——典型的把开头原词拿来骗。借用原文： Throwing spare change into a fountain is a time-honored ritual
D) 未提及选项 Polluting the fountains' water 听起来"硬币泡水里好像会污染"很合常识，但录音通篇没提水质污染，是用生活常识替文本作答的典型坑。
questions.quote: Otherwise, the growing piles of pennies, quarters and euros could clog up the fountains' works.

options.text: Increasing cleaners' workload.
Blocking the fountains' works.
Breaking a time-honored ritual.
Polluting the fountains' water.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about the coins collected from New York City's park fountains?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） They are mostly used for the fountains' maintenance.
**题目译文**
说话者关于从纽约市公园喷泉中收集的硬币说了什么?
A) 它们偶尔会被好奇的游客取走。
B) 它们定期捐赠给慈善组织。
C) 它们大多用于喷泉的维护。
D) 它们通常用作喷泉清洁工的工资。
**定位** 但大部分硬币已经被有生意头脑的纽约人捞走了，剩下能被收走的已所剩无几。
**信号** 转折 But 后才是真意。信号是 But——前半句说"市政人员每几周清理一次"是表面信息，转折 But 之后的 most of the coins have already been removed by entrepreneurial New Yorkers 才是录音真正想强调的实情，这正是答案落点。
**替换** go towards the fountains' maintenance itself↔used for the fountains' maintenance go towards=used for 同指用途
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 张冠李戴选项 occasionally retrieved by curious tourists 看似对上"硬币被人提前取走"，但录音说取走硬币的是 entrepreneurial New Yorkers（有生意头脑的纽约人），不是 curious tourists（好奇游客）——把取走者的身份偷换了，属张冠李戴。借用原文： most of the coins have already been removed by entrepreneurial New Yorkers
B) 张冠李戴选项 donated to charity organizations 里的 charity 录音确有（罗马的钱办惠民超市、迪士尼捐寄养儿童），但那是罗马和迪士尼喷泉的事，不是本题问的纽约公园喷泉——张冠李戴。借用原文： Tens of thousands of dollars in coins removed from wishing wells, fountains and ponds in Florida's Walt Disney World are donated each year to support foster children
D) 未提及选项 used as wages for fountain cleaners 里 cleaners / staff 录音确有（喷泉由公园staff 清理），但录音从没说硬币被"当作清洁工的工资"，是借"清洁"话题拼出的无中生有。借用原文： They are cleaned by the parks' staff every few weeks.
questions.quote: But most of the coins have already been removed by entrepreneurial New Yorkers and there is not a significant amount left to be collected.

options.text: They are occasionally retrieved by curious tourists.
They are regularly donated to charity organizations.
They are mostly used for the fountains' maintenance.
They are usually used as wages for fountain cleaners.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the money collected from Rome's Trevi Fountain?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） It is used to run a supermarket for the needy.
**题目译文**
关于从罗马许愿池收集的钱,我们了解到什么?
A) 它被投资于一系列生意。
B) 它专门用于该喷泉的维护。
C) 它被用来经营一家为贫困者服务的超市。
D) 它估计每月约为40000美元。
**定位** 每晚收上来的钱，大部分用于运营一家面向困难群体的超市。
**信号** goes towards 点明用途。信号是表用途的 goes towards（用于……）——它直接交代这笔钱的去向，紧跟其后的 running a supermarket for the needy 就是答案。听到 goes towards 这类"用于"的短语就锁定其后内容。
**替换** running a supermarket for the needy↔ run a supermarket for the needy running→run 仅词形微调
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱选项 invested in a series of businesses 里 business(es) 一词录音确有（serious business 指"收钱是件正经事"），但那是形容"这事很严肃"，根本不是说钱拿去"投资做生意"——盗用 business 一词制造误会。借用原文： collecting that cash is serious business
B) 张冠李戴选项 used exclusively for its maintenance 描述的"专门用于喷泉维护"是录音里纽约公园喷泉和 Bryant Park 喷泉的处置，不是罗马许愿池的，张冠李戴；且 exclusively（专门、唯一）程度过死，罗马的钱是"大部分"办超市。借用原文： which puts the cash collected by cleaners towards the fountain's own maintenance
D) 与原文相反选项 about $40,000 a month 把数字改了：录音说的是 as much as $4,000 in loose change from around the world each day（每天约 4000 美元），选项改成"每月 4万"——金额和时间单位都被动了手脚，是典型数字陷阱。借用原文： getting as much as $4,000 in loose change from around the world each day
questions.quote: Most of the money collected each night goes towards running a supermarket for the needy.

options.text: It is invested in a series of businesses.
It is used exclusively for its maintenance.
It is used to run a supermarket for the needy.
It is estimated to be about $40,000 a month.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about Thomas Morgan?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） He stole a lot of money from a fountain with a magnetic stick.
**题目译文**
说话者关于Thomas Morgan说了什么?
A) 他因从四名喷泉清洁工那里偷钱而被逮捕。
B) 他被判处34年监禁。
C) 他收集来自世界各地的稀有硬币。
D) 他用磁棒从喷泉中偷了很多钱。
**定位** 当局最终抓获一名臭名昭著、名叫 Thomas Morgan 的小偷，并禁止他靠近喷泉——此前他用一根磁棒在 34 年间钓走了数千美元的零钱。
**信号** 人名 + 其后动作链。信号是人名 named Thomas Morgan 一出现就锁定本句，重点在它后面的动作链 fished out thousands of dollars in change over 34 years using a magnetic stick——"用磁棒钓走数千美元"就是答案核心。
**替换** fished out thousands of dollars in change↔stole a lot of money from a fountain fished out=stole 概括偷取using a magnetic stick↔ with a magnetic stick using=with 同指工具
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 张冠李戴选项 arrested for stealing money from four fountain cleaners 里的 four fountain cleaners 录音确有，但那是 2005 年警方抓的"四名监守自盗的清洁工"，是另一桩案子，跟Thomas Morgan 无关——把别人的事安到他头上，还把"四名清洁工"从"被抓的人"偷换成"被偷的对象"。借用原文： police arrested four fountain cleaners after they were spotted slipping coins into their own pockets
B) 原词陷阱选项 sentenced to 34 years' imprisonment 盗用录音的数字 34 years，但录音说的是他over 34 years 间一直作案，结果只是被 banned from the fountain（禁入喷泉），并没有"判刑 34 年"——把"作案时长"偷换成"刑期"。借用原文： banned him from the fountain after he fished out thousands of dollars in change over 34 years
C) 原词陷阱选项 collected rare coins from around the world 里 from around the world 录音确有（罗马许愿池收来自世界各地的零钱），但那是说硬币来源广，不是说 Morgan"收藏稀有硬币"——他是偷钱不是藏币，纯属拼凑别处原词造的无中生有。借用原文： as much as $4,000 in loose change from around the world each day
questions.quote: Authorities finally caught one notorious thief named Thomas Morgan and banned him from the fountain after he fished out thousands of dollars in change over 34 years using a magnetic stick.

options.text: He was arrested for stealing money from four fountain cleaners.
He was sentenced to 34 years' imprisonment.
He collected rare coins from around the world.
He stole a lot of money from a fountain with a magnetic stick.

transcript.text: That's very modest of you to say, considering that your four books have sold a total of seven million copies worldwide, and they've been translated into 12 different languages.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: What makes people so fascinated with your work?
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: Well, people read my books because more than 60% of Americans are overweight, or obese.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: And other countries are facing similar problems.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: Basically, we all want to know how to fix things.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: We certainly do.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: I've read your new book, and it's fabulous, especially when it comes to the way you make difficult science easy for laymen to understand.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: That's no small achievement.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: I'm glad to hear you find my work accessible, because I was worried when I wrote it that discussing the science might make the book more suited for a specialist audience.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: My last book was written primarily for the medical community.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: But this time, I want to help ordinary people take control of their weight.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: And how do you suggest they do that?
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: Can you give us the basics of your advice for people who want to lose weight?
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: Briefly, I argue that every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body's needs.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: I don't advocate one single diet.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: Some people should eat more carbohydrates than others.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: And different people need different amounts of protein and fat.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: But you do have some recommendations for everyone, including eating ten servings of vegetables and three of fruit a day.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: We'll talk about those recommendations next, but now we need to take a short break for a message from our sponsor.
transcript.speaker: W

transcriptTranslations: 你的论文进展怎么样了？我正在校对初稿，明天要提交给我的教授。
哦，我甚至还没开始写呢，所以我真的很担心能不能在下学期末之前完成。
你是说你还一点都没开始吗？终稿五个月后就要交了。
我当然已经开始了，但还没法进入写作阶段，因为我还没找到足够的资料可用，所以我还在研究这个课题。
也许问题出在你做研究的方式上。我一开始就跟我的教授聊了去哪里找信息，基于他的建议，我在图书馆找到了书籍，还在网上找到了很多可靠的期刊文章。
我都试过了，但还是不够写论文，因为我们系要求最少70页。我觉得问题在于我的选题不可行。说实话，我的教授一开始就警告过我可能找不到足够的材料。但我对这个课题太感兴趣了，没有听他的劝告。
那我建议你换个新课题。毕竟，我们的教授是来指导我们的，所以最好听他们的。
现在回想起来，我真希望当时听了他的话，但我没听。现在我不想放弃我的课题，因为我已经投入了那么多时间和精力。
如果你坚持现在的课题，也许你可以做些调整，而不是完全放弃它。你的课题是什么？
是"本国南方民间传说中的女性形象描绘"。
这个范围挺窄的。如果你把课题范围扩大一些，也许能找到更多材料，比如可以纳入其他类型的描绘。
扩大课题范围是个好主意，我会从纳入本国其他地区的民间传说开始。
今天在《书谈》节目中,我们非常幸运地邀请到了 John Robbins,来讨论他的新书《为什么美国人肥胖以及我们如何减肥》。John 不仅是一位受人尊敬的作家,他还是当今少数几位撰写科学题材的名人作家之一。
谢谢你邀请我,Rebecca,但我算不上什么名人。
你这么说真是太谦虚了,要知道你的四本书在全球总共售出了七百万册,并且被翻译成了12种不同的语言。是什么让人们对你的作品如此着迷呢?
嗯,人们读我的书是因为超过60%的美国人超重或肥胖。而其他国家也面临着类似的问题。基本上,我们都想知道如何解决这些问题。
我们确实想知道。我读了你的新书,它太棒了,尤其是你把艰深的科学知识变得通俗易懂的方式。这可不是件容易的事。
很高兴听到你觉得我的作品通俗易懂,因为我在写作时还担心讨论科学内容会让这本书更适合专业读者。我上一本书主要是写给医学界的。但这一次,我想帮助普通人控制他们的体重。
那你建议他们怎么做呢?你能给我们介绍一下你对想要减肥的人的基本建议吗?
简单来说,我认为每个人都需要考虑自己的新陈代谢,吃适合自己身体需求的食物。我不主张单一的饮食方案。有些人应该比其他人摄入更多的碳水化合物。而且不同的人需要不同量的蛋白质和脂肪。
但你确实对所有人都有一些建议,包括每天吃十份蔬菜和三份水果。我们接下来会谈谈这些建议,但现在我们需要短暂休息一下,播放赞助商的广告。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about her dissertation?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） She hasn't started writing it.
**题目译文**
女士对她的论文说了什么?
A) 她还没有开始写。
B) 她还没有确定题目。
C) 她正在校对初稿。
D) 她正在整理参考文献。
**定位** 女：哦，我连写都还没开始呢，所以我真的很担心能不能在下学期末之前完成。
**信号** 被问者的直接应答。男生先问 How's your dissertation going，女生张口第一句 I haven't even started writing mine yet 就是对提问的直接应答，对话题的答案就落在被问者这第一反应上。
**替换** I haven't even started writing mine yet↔She hasn't started writing it.去掉 even 的同义压缩
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 偷换概念She hasn't decided on a topic. 听着也像『没进展』，但女生说的是还没开始写，topic 在后文 I'm still researching the topic 里指『还在查资料』，并非『没定下题目』，属偷换概念。借用原文： I'm still researching the topic
C) 张冠李戴She is proofreading the first draft. 里 proofreading the first draft 确在录音中出现，但说这话的是男生 I'm proofreading my first draft，不是女生，张冠李戴。借用原文： I'm proofreading my first draft
D) 未提及She is working on the references. 说她在弄参考文献，意味着正文已近完成，与她『还没动笔』完全矛盾，录音里也没说她在做文献，属未提及。
questions.quote: W: Oh, I haven't even started writing mine yet, so I'm really worried about finishing by the end of next semester.

options.text: She hasn't started writing it.
She hasn't decided on a topic.
She is proofreading the first draft.
She is working on the references.

questions.prompt: What does the man say about his professor?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） He offered the man advice on resource hunting
**题目译文**
男士对他的教授说了什么?
A) 他借给男士许多书供参考。
B) 他就资源搜寻向男士提供了建议。
C) 他在多个知名期刊上发表了大量文章。
D) 他告诉男士在使用电子资源时要有选择性。
**定位** 男：我一开始是去找我教授聊该上哪儿找资料，在这个基础上，我在图书馆找到了书，还在网上找到很多有声望的期刊文章。
**信号** 经过句里的求助动作。男生回顾自己怎么做研究，关键在 I started by talking to my professor about where to look for information——他教授给的正是『去哪找资料』的指点，这句叙述里藏着教授的作为。
**替换** talking to my professor about where to look for information↔He offered the man advice on resource hunting把『聊去哪找资料』概括为『给找资料建议』
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱He lent many books to the man for reference. 里 books 确在录音出现，但 I found books in the library 是男生自己在图书馆找到的书，不是教授借给他的，原词陷阱。借用原文： I found books in the library
C) 原词陷阱He published a lot in a number of reputable journals. 用了原词 reputable journal，但a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet 说的是男生在网上找到这些文章来读，而非教授在期刊上发表论文，原词陷阱兼无中生有。借用原文： a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet
D) 未提及He told the man to be selective when using e-resources. 说教授叮嘱『用电子资源要有选择』，但录音里教授只指点了去哪找，从未提『要挑着用』，selective 是未提及。
questions.quote: M: I started by talking to my professor about where to look for information, and based on that, I found books in the library and a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet.

options.text: He lent many books to the man for reference.
He offered the man advice on resource hunting
He published a lot in a number of reputable journals.
He told the man to be selective when using e-resources.

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about her professor?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） He didn't think her dissertation topic viable.
**题目译文**
女士对她的教授说了什么?
A) 他认为她的论文题目不可行。
B) 他对她的论文题目不感兴趣。
C) 他不希望她仓促完成论文。
D) 他没有具体说明她的论文篇幅。
**定位** 女：说实话，我教授一开始就警告过我，我可能找不到足够的材料。
**信号** 引述动词 warn 引出原话。女生用 my professor did warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material 转述教授当初的警告，引述动词 warn 后面那句就是教授的态度，是答案句。
**替换** warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material↔He didn't think her dissertation topic viable.『找不到材料』即『选题不可行』
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 张冠李戴He wasn't interested in her dissertation topic. 把 interested 安在教授身上，但录音里 I was so interested in the topic 说有兴趣的是女生自己，教授只是警告找不到料，张冠李戴又偷换。借用原文： I was so interested in the topic
C) 未提及He didn't want her to rush through her dissertation. 说教授不想她赶工，但教授只警告材料不够，从没说过快慢、赶不赶的事，未提及。
D) 原词陷阱He wasn't specific about the length of her dissertation. 提到 length，录音里 length出现在 my department's minimum length is 70 pages，那是系里的规定，与教授说没说清篇幅无关，原词陷阱。借用原文： my department's minimum length is 70 pages
questions.quote: W: And honestly, my professor did warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material.

options.text: He didn't think her dissertation topic viable.
He wasn't interested in her dissertation topic.
He didn't want her to rush through her dissertation.
He wasn't specific about the length of her dissertation.

questions.prompt: What do we learn the woman will do to complete her dissertation?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） Follow the man's advice.
**题目译文**
我们了解到女士将做什么来完成她的论文?
A) 改变她的研究方法。
B) 缩小她的论文题目范围。
C) 多咨询她的教授。
D) 听从男士的建议。
**定位** 女：把题目扩大是个好主意，我打算先把全国其他地区的民间传说也纳进来。
**信号** 结尾采纳建议的应答。男生上一句建议 You could find more material if you made the topic broader，女生末句 Broadening the topic is a great idea 当即采纳，结尾这句『接受建议』就是答案句。
**替换** Broadening the topic is a great idea ↔ Follow the man's advice.采纳男生提议=照他建议办
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱Change her research methodology. 沾了男生那句 Maybe the problem is the way you're doing your research，但女生最终决定的是扩大题目，并没说要换研究方法，原词陷阱。借用原文： Maybe the problem is the way you're doing your research
B) 与原文相反Narrow down her dissertation topic. 与女生的决定正好相反——男生说题目 That's pretty narrow，建议 made the topic broader，女生要做的是 broaden（扩大）而非narrow（缩小），与原文相反。借用原文： That's pretty narrow
C) 原词陷阱Consult her professor more. 里 professor 全程反复出现，诱人选；但女生采纳的是男生当下的建议，并未表示要再去多问教授，原词陷阱。借用原文： our professors are here to guide us
questions.quote: W: Broadening the topic is a great idea, I'll start by including folklore from other regions of the country.

options.text: Change her research methodology.
Narrow down her dissertation topic.
Consult her professor more.
Follow the man's advice.
