transcript.text: We've talked recently about the importance of sustainable energy.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: We've also talked about the different theories on how that can be done.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: So far, our discussions have all been theoretical.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Now I have a practical question for you all.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Can you run a 140,000 kilogram train on just the steam generated by solar power?
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Well, one engineer, Tim Castleman, believes it's possible.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: And his home city of Sacramento, California should see the technology's first test.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: As part of the upgrading of its rail yard, Castleman, who is an inventor and self-proclaimed steam visionary, is campaigning for a new steam train that runs without any fire and could run on an existing 10-kilometre line, drawing tourists and perhaps offering city commuters a green alternative to their cars.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Castleman wants to build an array of solar magnifying mirrors at one end of the line to collect and focus heat onto water-filled tubes.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: This would generate steam that could be used to fill tanks on a small steam train without the use of fire.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: "Supplying power to trains in this way would offer the shortest distance from well to wheels," he says, "with the least amount of energy lost."
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: According to Harry Valentine, a Canadian engineer who is researching modern steam technology, a special tank measuring 2 by 10 metres could store over 750 kilowatt-hours of energy as high-pressure steam, enough to pull a two-car train for an hour or so.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Energy to drive a steam locomotive can be stored in other materials besides water.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: For example, a team at Tohoku University in Japan has studied materials that can store large amounts of heat.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: When heated, these materials turn from a solid into a liquid absorbing energy as they change phase.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The liquid is maintained above its melting point until steam is required, at which point the liquid is allowed to turn back into a solid, releasing its stored energy.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Another team at Nagoya University in Japan has tested calcium compound as an energy storage material.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Heating this chemical compound drives off carbon dioxide gas, leaving calcium oxide.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The gas can be stored under pressure in a tank.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: To recover the energy, the gas is fed back over the calcium oxide.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: "In theory," says Valentine, "this can create a high enough temperature to generate superheated steam."
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Today's crisis in care for older people in England has two main causes.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: First, people are living longer with a lot more complex needs.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Second, they rely on a system that has long been marked by a poor relation between national health and social care services.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Current services originate in two key measures.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They are the National Health Service and the 1948 National Assistance Act.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: This required local governments to provide residential accommodation for older people and supervise care homes run by independent organizations.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They also provided home and community services, including meals, day centres and home helpers and other subsidized services.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The National Health Service was free and wholly publicly provided.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: It delivered the best health care for all.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: No such vision guided residential and community care though.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The care was substantially provided by voluntary services which worked together with local authorities as they long had, with eligibility based on income.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Today, life expectancy has risen from 66 for a male at best in 1948 to around 80 now.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In addition, there is better overall health and improved medical knowledge in care.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: This means an unprecedented number of people are surviving longer in conditions requiring experts' support.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Families provide at least as much care as they ever did.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Even so, they can rarely, without subsidized support, address serious personal needs.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Care for older people faced persistent criticism as these trends became apparent.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: From the early 1960s, local authorities were required to plan health and welfare services.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The aim was to enable older people to remain in their own homes for as long as possible.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: But this increased concern about the lack of coordination between free health and paid-for social care.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Through the 1970s, a number of measures sought to improve matters.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: However, at a time of financial crisis, funding diminished and little changed.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In the 1980s, the government cut spending.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Meanwhile, preference for private over public services made management even more difficult.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Simultaneously, the number of sick older people grew.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Governments emphasized the need to improve services.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They did so, though, while doing little to stop the erosion of available aid.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Services were irregular across authorities.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Unless you were prepared to pay, they were increasingly difficult to obtain for any but the most severely disabled.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Why has 60 years of criticism produced so little change?
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Discrimination against older people has a long history.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Additionally, those affected by inadequate health and social care are too vulnerable to launch the protests that have addressed other forms of discrimination.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcriptTranslations: 这是我的侄女Sarah。她的妈妈是一名医生,她的爸爸是一名律师。等Sarah上大学的时候,她父母所从事的工作将会看起来截然不同。

2013年,牛津大学的研究人员对未来工作进行了一项研究。他们得出结论,几乎每两个工作中就有一个面临被机器自动化的高风险。机器学习是造成这种颠覆的主要技术。它是人工智能中最强大的分支。它使机器能够从数据中学习并模仿人类能做的一些事情。我的公司Kaggle在机器学习的前沿领域运营。我们召集了数十万专家来解决工业界和学术界的重要问题。这使我们对机器能做什么、不能做什么以及它们可能使哪些工作自动化或受到威胁有独特的见解。
机器学习在90年代初开始进入工业领域。它从相对简单的任务开始。它从评估贷款申请的信用风险、通过识别手写邮政编码分拣邮件等事情开始。在过去几年里,我们取得了巨大的突破。机器学习现在能够完成复杂得多的任务。2012年,Kaggle向其社区发起挑战,要求构建一个能够为高中作文评分的程序。获胜的程序能够与人类教师给出的分数相匹配。
现在,只要有合适的数据,机器在这类任务上的表现将超过人类。一位教师在40年的职业生涯中可能会阅读1万篇作文。而机器可以在几分钟内阅读数百万篇作文。在频繁的、大批量的任务上,我们没有机会与机器竞争。
但有些事情我们能做而机器不能。机器在处理新情况方面进展甚微。机器无法处理它们以前没有见过很多次的事情。机器学习的根本局限在于它需要从大量的过去数据中学习。但人类不需要。我们有能力将看似不同的线索联系起来,解决我们从未见过的问题。
我们最近讨论了可持续能源的重要性。我们也讨论了关于如何实现这一目标的不同理论。到目前为止,我们的讨论都是理论性的。现在我有一个实际问题要问大家。你能仅靠太阳能产生的蒸汽来驱动一列14万公斤重的火车吗?工程师Tim Castleman认为这是可能的。

他的家乡加州Sacramento应该会见证这项技术的首次测试。作为铁路调车场升级改造的一部分,Castleman——一位发明家和自称的蒸汽梦想家——正在倡导建造一种不需要任何火的新型蒸汽火车,它可以在现有的10公里线路上运行,吸引游客,或许还能为城市通勤者提供一种替代汽车的绿色选择。Castleman想在线路一端建造一组太阳能聚光镜阵列,将热量收集并聚焦到充满水的管道上。这将产生蒸汽,可以在不使用火的情况下为小型蒸汽火车的储罐注入蒸汽。他说:"以这种方式为火车供电将提供从井到车轮的最短距离,能量损失最少。"根据研究现代蒸汽技术的加拿大工程师Harry Valentine的说法,一个2米乘10米的特殊储罐可以以高压蒸汽的形式储存超过750千瓦时的能量,足以牵引一列双节车厢的火车运行大约一小时。

驱动蒸汽机车的能量可以储存在水以外的其他材料中。例如,日本东北大学的一个团队研究了可以储存大量热量的材料。这些材料在加热时会从固态变成液态,在相变过程中吸收能量。液体保持在其熔点以上,直到需要蒸汽时,液体被允许重新变回固体,释放其储存的能量。日本名古屋大学的另一个团队测试了钙化合物作为储能材料。加热这种化合物会释放出二氧化碳气体,留下氧化钙。气体可以在储罐中加压储存。为了回收能量,将气体反馈到氧化钙上。Valentine说:"理论上,这可以产生足够高的温度来生成过热蒸汽。
当今英格兰老年人护理危机有两个主要原因。首先，人们寿命更长，需求也更加复杂。其次，他们依赖的系统长期以来一直以国家医疗服务与社会护理服务之间的不良关系为特征。

目前的服务起源于两项关键措施。它们是国家医疗服务体系和1948年国家援助法案。该法案要求地方政府为老年人提供住宿设施，并监督由独立组织运营的护理院。它们还提供家庭和社区服务,包括膳食、日间中心、家庭帮手以及其他补贴服务。国家医疗服务是免费的,完全由公共部门提供。它为所有人提供最好的医疗保健。然而,没有这样的愿景来指导住宿和社区护理。护理主要由志愿服务提供,这些服务像长期以来一样与地方当局合作,资格基于收入。
如今,预期寿命已从1948年男性最高66岁上升到现在约80岁。此外,整体健康状况更好,护理方面的医学知识也有所改善。这意味着前所未有数量的人在需要专家支持的状况下存活更长时间。家庭提供的护理至少与以往一样多。即便如此,没有补贴支持,他们也很少能够满足严重的个人需求。随着这些趋势变得明显,老年人护理面临持续批评。
从20世纪60年代初开始,地方当局被要求规划医疗和福利服务。目标是使老年人尽可能长时间地留在自己家中。但这增加了人们对免费医疗与付费社会护理之间缺乏协调的担忧。整个70年代,许多措施试图改善状况。
然而,在金融危机时期,资金减少,几乎没有改变。在20世纪80年代,政府削减开支。与此同时,对私人服务而非公共服务的偏好使管理变得更加困难。同时,患病老年人的数量增加。政府强调需要改善服务。不过,他们这样做的同时,几乎没有采取措施阻止可用援助的减少。
各地方当局的服务参差不齐。除非你准备付费,否则除了最严重残疾的人之外,其他人越来越难以获得服务。
为什么60年的批评产生的变化如此之少?对老年人的歧视有着悠久的历史。此外,受到医疗和社会护理不足影响的人太过脆弱,无法发起已解决其他形式歧视的抗议。

questions.prompt: What did the researchers at Oxford University conclude?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） About half of current jobs might be automated.
**题目译文**
牛津大学的研究人员得出了什么结论?
A) 目前约半数工作可能会被自动化。
B) 医生和律师的工作将受到威胁。
C) 就业市场正变得有些难以预测。
D) 机器学习将在2013年前证明具有颠覆性。
**定位** 他们得出结论：几乎每两份工作里就有一份面临被机器自动化取代的高风险。
**信号** 结论动词 concluded 领出落点。原文 They concluded that 直接对应题干的 conclude，这种"下结论"的标志动词后面紧跟的就是答案句；听到 concluded/found/argued 这类词，后面那句基本就是考点。
**替换** almost one in every two jobs↔About half of current jobs "二分之一"= about half has a high risk of being automated by machines↔might be automated高风险=might（可能）
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 张冠李戴录音开头确实念到 Her mom is a doctor and her dad is a lawyer，但那是讲小侄女父母的引子，并非"牛津研究的结论"；选项把这两个原词搬来冒充结论，是答非所问。借用原文： Her mom is a doctor and her dad is a lawyer
C) 未提及原文结论是"约一半工作有被自动化的高风险"，是个明确的比例判断，并没有说就业市场"变得难以预测（unpredictable）"；这层意思录音从未表达，属凭印象推出来的。
D) 偷换概念录音里 In 2013, researchers at Oxford University did a study 中的 2013 是"做研究的年份"，选项却说"机器学习到 2013 年将具颠覆性"，把这个年份偷换成了"颠覆发生/达成的时间"，时间含义被改了。借用原文： In 2013, researchers at Oxford University did a study on the future of work
questions.quote: They concluded that almost one in every two jobs has a high risk of being automated by machines.

options.text: About half of current jobs might be automated.
The jobs of doctors and lawyers would be threatened.
The job market is becoming somewhat unpredictable.
Machine learning would prove disruptive by 2013.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about Kaggle company's winning programs?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） They could grade high-school essays just like human teachers.
**题目译文**
关于Kaggle公司的获胜程序,我们了解到什么?
A) 它们广泛适用于大规模开放在线课程。
B) 它们现在正被众多高中教师使用。
C) 它们能在一分钟内阅读多达10,000篇论文。
D) 它们能像人类教师一样给高中论文评分。
**定位** 那些获胜的程序能够给出与人类老师所打分数相符的成绩。
**信号** 主体词 winning programs 直接出现。原文 The winning programs were able to 与题干主体逐字对上，主体词出现处就是答案句；这种"题干主体在原文原样念出"的情况，紧跟其后的能力描述即落点。
**替换** match the grades given by human teachers↔ grade high-school essays just like human teachers "分数相符"= 像老师一样评分grade high-school essays↔ grade high-school essays评高中作文（原任务对象）
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及录音谈的是批高中作文，从未提到"massive open online courses（慕课）"，更没说这些程序广泛适用于网课；这是凭"网课也涉及作文"的联想脑补出来的。
B) 张冠李戴录音确有 human teachers 一词，但说的是"程序的分与老师相符"，并非"许多高中老师在使用这些程序"；选项把 teachers 从"被对标的人"偷换成"使用者"，张冠李戴。借用原文： match the grades given by human teachers
C) 原词陷阱"一分钟读一万篇"是把后文 A teacher might read 10,000 essays over a 40-year career和 A machine can read millions of essays within minutes 的数字拼凑改造而来，且讲的是"读得快/多"，而本题问 winning programs 的本事在于"评得准"，答非所问。借用原文： A teacher might read 10,000 essays over a 40-year career
questions.quote: The winning programs were able to match the grades given by human teachers.

options.text: They are widely applicable for massive open online courses.
They are now being used by numerous high school teachers.
They could read as many as 10,000 essays in a single minute.
They could grade high-school essays just like human teachers.

questions.prompt: What is the fundamental limitation of machine learning?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） It has to rely on huge amounts of previous data.
**题目译文**
机器学习的根本局限是什么?
A) 它在整个过程中都需要指令。
B) 它在频繁、大量的任务上表现不佳。
C) 它必须依赖大量先前数据。
D) 它在追踪新事物时速度缓慢。
**定位** 机器学习的根本局限在于：它必须从大量的历史数据中学习。
**信号** 原词 fundamental limitation + 转折 But 后落点。本段以 But there are things we can do that machines cannot 转折开场，随后 The fundamental limitation of machine learning is that 与题干逐字呼应，这种"转折后 + 原话点题"的句子就是答案句。
**替换** it needs to learn from large volumes of past data↔It has to rely on huge amounts of previous data整句几乎逐词同义替换
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 过度推断录音从未说机器学习"全过程都需要人给指令"；它强调的是"需要从历史数据中学习"，而非"需要指令"。throughout the process 这种绝对化说法是凭印象加上去的。
B) 与原文相反录音说 We have no chance of competing against machines on frequent, high- volume tasks——高频海量任务上人类根本拼不过机器，即机器在此最强；选项却说机器在"frequent, high-volume tasks"上"做得差"，把强项说成短板，正话反说。借用原文： We have no chance of competing against machines on frequent, high-volume tasks
D) 偷换概念录音确实说 Where machines have made very little progress is in tackling novel situations——机器在应对新情境上进展甚微，但题问的是"根本局限"，原文给的根本局限是"必须依赖旧数据"；而且选项说"追踪新事物时'慢'（slow）"，原文说的是"进展很少/处理不了"，并非"慢"，含义被改。借用原文： Where machines have made very little progress is in tackling novel situations
questions.quote: The fundamental limitation of machine learning is that it needs to learn from large volumes of past data.

options.text: It needs instructions throughout the process.
It does poorly on frequent, high-volume tasks.
It has to rely on huge amounts of previous data.
It is slow when it comes to tracking novel things.

questions.prompt: What has the speaker previously talked about?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） The theoretical aspects of sustainable energy.
**题目译文**
说话者之前谈论了什么?
A) 太阳能发电的工程问题。
B) 用最新技术产生蒸汽。
C) 探索新能源的重要性。
D) 可持续能源的理论方面。
**定位** 我们最近谈过可持续能源的重要性。我们也谈过关于如何实现它的各种理论。到目前为止，我们的讨论都还停留在理论层面。
**信号** 完成时回顾句 We've talked + 收束句 all been theoretical。We've also talked about the different theories 是完成时回顾，紧接着 our discussions have all been theoretical一句把之前内容定性为理论，这句收束语就是答案信号——它一句话概括了前情。
**替换** the different theories on how that can be done ↔ The theoretical aspects of sustainable energy theories 改写为 theoretical aspects the importance of sustainable energy ↔ sustainable energy话题词 sustainable energy 原样对应
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱The engineering problems with solar power 借了录音里 one engineer 及后文工程内容的影子，但工程实践是说话人即将转入的 practical question，不是 previously（之前）讲的内容，时间点错位。借用原文： one engineer, Tim Castleman, believes it's possible
B) 原词陷阱The generation of steam with the latest technology 借了录音后面反复出现的 steam 和technology，但用蒸汽这套技术是说话人转向的 practical question（实践问题），属于现在要讲、不是之前讲过的，答非所问。借用原文： run a 140,000 kilogram train on just the steam generated by solar power
C) 偷换概念The importance of exploring new energy sources 看似贴主题，但录音回顾的是 the importance of sustainable energy（可持续能源的重要性）和各种理论，并没有讲探索新能源的重要性，exploring new energy sources 是无中生有的拔高。借用原文： the importance of sustainable energy
questions.quote: We've talked recently about the importance of sustainable energy. We've also talked about the different theories on how that can be done. So far, our discussions have all been theoretical.

options.text: The engineering problems with solar power.
The generation of steam with the latest technology.
The importance of exploring new energy sources.
The theoretical aspects of sustainable energy.

questions.prompt: What is Tim Castleman trying to do in Sacramento?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） Drive trains with solar energy.
**题目译文**
Tim Castleman 在 Sacramento 试图做什么?
A) 用太阳能驱动火车。
B) 升级该市的火车设施。
C) 建造一条新的十公里铁路线。
D) 削减该市的能源消耗。
**定位** 卡斯尔曼正在倡导一种不用任何明火、能在现有 10 公里线路上运行的新型蒸汽火车。卡斯尔曼想在线路一端建一组太阳能聚光镜，收集并把热量聚焦到充水的管道上。这会产生蒸汽，用来给一列小型蒸汽火车的水箱充气，而无需用火。
**信号** 人物意图句 Castleman wants to build... 及整套目标描述。Castleman wants to build an array of solar magnifying mirrors 是直接的人物意图句（wants to），加上前面 a new steam train that runs without any fire，整段都在说他想用太阳能产蒸汽来跑火车，这就是答案信号。
**替换** build an array of solar magnifying mirrors↔Drive trains with solar energy建聚光镜产蒸汽 = 用太阳能驱动火车steam generated by solar power↔ solar energy solar power 改写为 solar energy
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱Upgrade the city's train facilities 借了录音 the upgrading of its rail yard（铁路调车场升级）这个词，但升级是这件事发生的背景，Castleman 本人的目标是建太阳能蒸汽火车，不是去升级设施，答非所问。借用原文： As part of the upgrading of its rail yard
C) 与原文相反Build a new ten-kilometre railway line 借了原文 ten-kilometre 这个数字，但录音说的是 an existing 10-kilometre line（现有的 10 公里线路），他要在现有线上跑车，不是新建一条线，与原文相反。借用原文： could run on an existing 10-kilometre line
D) 过度推断Cut down the city's energy consumption 沾了录音 a green alternative（绿色替代方案）的环保意味，但录音只说这可能给通勤者一个绿色选择，没说他的目标是削减全城能耗，属拔高推断。借用原文： offering city commuters a green alternative to their cars
questions.quote: Castleman is campaigning for a new steam train that runs without any fire and could run on an existing 10-kilometre line. Castleman wants to build an array of solar magnifying mirrors at one end of the line to collect and focus heat onto water-filled tubes. This would generate steam that could be used to fill tanks on a small steam train without the use of fire.

options.text: Drive trains with solar energy.
Upgrade the city's train facilities.
Build a new ten-kilometre railway line.
Cut down the city's energy consumption.

questions.prompt: What has a Japanese research team tried to do?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） Find a new material for storing energy.
**题目译文**
日本研究团队试图做什么?
A) 建造一个用于保存氧化钙的容器。
B) 找到一种储存能量的新材料。
C) 回收过热蒸汽。
D) 收集二氧化碳气体。
**定位** 驱动蒸汽机车的能量，除了水之外还可以储存在别的材料里。例如，日本东北大学的一个团队研究了能储存大量热量的材料。
**信号** 总起句 stored in other materials + 例证 has studied materials。本段开头 Energy ... can be stored in other materials besides water 是总起句，点明本段主题是寻找别的储能材料；紧接着 a team at Tohoku University in Japan has studied materials that can store large amounts of heat 给出团队的具体做法，这两句合起来就是答案信号。
**替换** stored in other materials besides water ↔ Find a new material for storing energy用水以外的材料储能 = 找新储能材料
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱Build a tank for keeping calcium oxide 借了原文 calcium oxide（氧化钙）这个词，但录音说罐子里存的是 The gas can be stored under pressure in a tank（气体存在罐中），剩下的 calcium oxide 是留在原处的固体、不是被存进罐里的，对象张冠李戴。借用原文： The gas can be stored under pressure in a tank, leaving calcium oxide
C) 原词陷阱Recover super-heated steam 借了原文末句 generate superheated steam，但那是Valentine 说的理论上能达到的效果，且是 recover the energy 的过程，不是日本团队尝试做的事本身，答非所问。借用原文： this can create a high enough temperature to generate superheated steam
D) 偷换概念Collect carbon dioxide gas 借了原文 drives off carbon dioxide gas，二氧化碳确实被存进罐子，但这只是名古屋团队储能流程里的一步手段，题问的是团队尝试做什么——核心是找钙化合物作储能材料，而非单纯收集二氧化碳，以偏概全。借用原文： Heating this chemical compound drives off carbon dioxide gas
questions.quote: Energy to drive a steam locomotive can be stored in other materials besides water. For example, a team at Tohoku University in Japan has studied materials that can store large amounts of heat.

options.text: Build a tank for keeping calcium oxide.
Find a new material for storing energy.
Recover super-heated steam.
Collect carbon dioxide gas.

questions.prompt: What is one cause of the current crisis in care for the elderly in England?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） The poor relation between national health and social care services.
**题目译文**
英格兰老年人护理当前危机的一个原因是什么？
A) 国家和地方政府缺乏监管。
B) 国内外当前经济危机的影响。
C) 日间照料中心和家庭帮助服务的管理不善。
D) 国家医疗服务与社会护理服务之间的关系不佳。
**定位** 第二，他们依赖于一套长期以来以国家医疗服务与社会照护服务之间衔接不良为特征的体系。
**信号** 并列信号 Second 引出第二条原因。首段以 two main causes 起头，用 First 与 Second罗列两条原因；Second 之后这句正是其中一条成因。
**替换** a poor relation between national health and social care services↔The poor relation between national health and social care services.近乎原句保留的关键表述
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱A 借用录音里反复出现的 local governments 制造熟耳感，但录音说的两条原因是"人活得更久、需求更复杂"与"体系衔接差"，从未把"国家与地方政府监管缺失"列为危机原因。借用原文： supervise care homes run by independent organizations
B) 原词陷阱录音第 5 段确有 a time of financial crisis，但那是讲 1980 年代资金减少的背景，不是当前老年护理危机的两条主因之一；B 把别处的"经济危机"挪来当成因。借用原文： at a time of financial crisis, funding diminished and little changed
C) 原词陷阱C 里的 day centres and home help services 直接取自录音第 2 段 day centres and home helpers，但原文只是在介绍服务种类，没说"这些服务管理不善"是当前危机的原因。借用原文： meals, day centres and home helpers and other subsidized services
questions.quote: Second, they rely on a system that has long been marked by a poor relation between national health and social care services.

options.text: The lack of supervision by both the national and local governments.
The impact of the current economic crisis at home and abroad.
The poor management of day centres and home help services.
The poor relation between national health and social care services.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about residential and community care?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） It was mainly provided by voluntary services.
**题目译文**
说话者关于住院护理和社区护理说了什么？
A) 它主要由志愿服务提供。
B) 它主要满足特权阶层的需求。
C) 它需要足够数量的志愿者。
D) 在过去六十年里它已经恶化了。
**定位** 然而，居家与社区照护却没有这样的理念指引。这种照护主要由志愿服务提供，它们一如既往地与地方当局协作，资格依据收入而定。
**信号** 对象名出现+核心动词 provided by。句子点名 residential and community care，紧接着用 substantially provided by voluntary services 说明它的供给来源，正是题目所问。
**替换** substantially provided by voluntary services↔It was mainly provided by voluntary services. substantially=mainly 的同义替换
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 与原文相反录音说 eligibility based on income（按收入定资格），B 却说服务"特权阶层"(the privileged)，方向相反——按收入往往是照顾低收入者，并非偏向特权者。借用原文： with eligibility based on income
C) 原词陷阱C 里的 volunteers 蹭录音的 voluntary services，但原文只说服务"由"志愿组织提供，没有说"呼吁要足够多志愿者"(called for a sufficient number)，属凭空添加。借用原文： provided by voluntary services
D) 原词陷阱D 的 deteriorated over the past sixty years 蹭了末段 60 years of criticism 里的时间跨度，但那是讲"批评了 60 年"，本题问的是这种照护的供给来源，原文没说它"在 60 年里恶化"。借用原文： Why has 60 years of criticism produced so little change?
questions.quote: No such vision guided residential and community care though. The care was substantially provided by voluntary services which worked together with local authorities as they long had, with eligibility based on income.

options.text: It was mainly provided by voluntary services.
It mainly caters to the needs of the privileged.
It called for a sufficient number of volunteers.
It has deteriorated over the past sixty years.

questions.prompt: What made management of care for the elderly more difficult in the 1980s?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） Their preference for private services.
**题目译文**
是什么使得20世纪80年代老年人护理的管理变得更加困难？
A) 他们更长的寿命。
B) 可用的家庭帮助人员更少。
C) 他们对私人服务的偏好。
D) 他们中更多人患有严重疾病。
**定位** 在 1980 年代，政府削减开支。与此同时，对私营服务而非公共服务的偏好使管理变得更加困难。
**信号** 时间 1980s + made…difficult 直接点题。句中 In the 1980s 锁定年代，made management even more difficult 与题干 made management…more difficult 几乎逐词对应，紧贴其前的 preference 即致因。
**替换** preference for private over public services↔Their preference for private services.压缩式同义改写
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 答非所问A 的 longer lifespans 对应录音第 3 段 life expectancy has risen，那是讲危机的大背景，不是本题"1980 年代使管理更难"的直接原因。借用原文： life expectancy has risen from 66 for a male at best in 1948 to around 80 now
B) 答非所问录音确有 doing little to stop the erosion of available aid 暗示援助在减少，但本题致因句明确指向"偏好私营服务"，B 把别处的"帮手变少"挪来顶替。借用原文： the erosion of available aid
D) 原词陷阱D 的 serious illnesses 蹭录音 the number of sick older people grew，但那句是与致因并列的另一现象（病人增多），用 Simultaneously 引出，并非"made management difficult"所修饰的原因。借用原文： Simultaneously, the number of sick older people grew
questions.quote: In the 1980s, the government cut spending. Meanwhile, preference for private over public services made management even more difficult.

options.text: Their longer lifespans.
Fewer home helpers available.
Their preference for private services.
More of them suffering serious illnesses.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about older people in England?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） They have long been discriminated against.
**题目译文**
说话者关于英格兰的老年人说了什么？
A) 他们无力支付医疗服务费用。
B) 他们长期以来一直受到歧视。
C) 他们容易患病和疾病。
D) 他们为社会做出了巨大贡献。
**定位** 对老年人的歧视由来已久。此外，那些受不足的医疗与社会照护影响的人太过脆弱，无法发起像针对其他歧视形式那样的抗议。
**信号** 结尾收束句直接定性。末段以设问 Why has 60 years of criticism produced so little change? 收束，随后 Discrimination against older people has a long history. 直接对老人这一群体下定性，是说话人的总结表态。
**替换** Discrimination against older people has a long history↔They have long been discriminated against.名词化↔主被动转换
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱A 的"付不起医疗费"蹭了录音 Unless you were prepared to pay 的 pay，但那是讲服务难获取的条件，原文没说老人"无力支付"，更不是结尾对群体的定性。借用原文： Unless you were prepared to pay
C) 原词陷阱C 的 vulnerable to illnesses and diseases 蹭录音末段 too vulnerable to launch the protests 的 vulnerable，但原文 vulnerable 指老人"脆弱到无力发起抗议"，不是"易患病"，被偷换了对象。借用原文： are too vulnerable to launch the protests
D) 未提及D 说老人"对社会贡献很大"，全篇围绕照护困境与歧视，从未提到老人对社会的贡献，属无中生有。
questions.quote: Discrimination against older people has a long history. Additionally, those affected by inadequate health and social care are too vulnerable to launch the protests that have addressed other forms of discrimination.

options.text: They are unable to pay for health services.
They have long been discriminated against.
They are vulnerable to illnesses and diseases.
They have contributed a great deal to society.

transcriptTranslations: 嘿，我刚读了一本很棒的物理学书。我觉得你会喜欢的。书名叫《世界的物理学》，作者是一位名叫Sylvia Mundus的科学家。
哦，我读过那本书。非常棒。作者是一位温暖而称职的向导，带领读者探索物理学的奥秘。我觉得任何读者都能从中获益，无论是对科学知之甚少的人，还是职业物理学家。
能看到一位坚强、好奇、聪慧的女性在这个传统上由男性主导的领域发出自己的声音，真是令人耳目一新。我认为她值得称赞，因为她努力加入了一些不太为人所知的女科学家的轶事。你知道，她们常常是"一个坚信女人的位置就在家里的时代"的受害者。
我喜欢这本书写得很清晰，每一章都因为一些引人入胜的知识而生动起来。比如，在其中一章她揭穿了一个我听大学物理教授讲过的谬误。我经常听说中世纪的玻璃窗底部更厚是因为玻璃像流体一样"流动"。她证明了这不是真的。这种变形实际上是由于玻璃制造工艺的特殊性造成的。
是啊，我喜欢她通过提供大量动手实验来培养科学参与感，这些实验展示了支配从太阳系到你家餐桌上一切事物的经典物理学的基本原理。从利用复杂的物理定律测试旋转的鸡蛋是否煮熟，到通过举起一片硬纸板来测量大气压，她的实践例子让这本书成为真正互动的读物。
是的。我必须说这本没有方程式的书是所有类型科学家、任何教授科学的人甚至不喜欢物理学的人的理想读物。
嗨，教授。如果您不太忙的话，我想占用您一点时间。我在开始写论文时遇到了一些问题，希望您能给我一些建议，告诉我该如何着手。
当然可以。不过我有很多学生。你能提醒我一下你的题目是什么吗？
我选择的总体题目是美学，但我就只到这一步了。我真不知道接下来该怎么做。
是的。这个题目太大了。你真的需要缩小范围，使它更容易处理。否则，你就是在写一本书了。
没错。这正是我想问您的。我希望能换个题目。相比美，我其实对自然更感兴趣。
恐怕你必须坚持指定的题目。不过，如果你对自然感兴趣，那当然可以融入到你的论文中。我们之前在课上讨论过休谟，对吧？
哦，对。他就是那位写关于我们美的观念从何而来的哲学家。
没错。我建议你去图书馆找一本他的传记。从那里开始，但记住要遵守作业的要求。这篇论文占你总成绩的很大一部分，所以一定要按照说明来做。如果你看看他的传记，就能很好地了解他的生活经历是如何体现在他的美学理论中的，特别是他将自然视为我们认为美的事物之源泉的方式。
太好了！谢谢您花时间回答我的问题，教授。我不打扰您上课了。
如果你还有什么需要的，随时来我办公室找我。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about the book the man recommended?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （态度观点题） It can benefit professionals and non-professionals alike.
**题目译文**
女士对男士推荐的那本书有什么看法?
A) 它对专业人士和非专业人士都同样有益。
B) 它列出了物理学家们正面临的各种挑战。
C) 它描述了物理学的一些谜团是如何被解开的。
D) 它是有史以来最引人入胜的物理学书籍之一。
**定位** 我认为它能让任何读者都有收获，从对科学知之甚少的人，到职业物理学家。
**信号** 被问者女士的直接评价句。本题问 the woman 的看法，定位就锁女士的话。她说 it promises enrichment for any reader, from those who know little about science to the career physicist，这句「面向任何读者」的概括评价正是答案句。
**替换** from those who know little about science to the career physicist↔professionals and non-professionals alike「外行到职业」概括为「专业与非专业都」it promises enrichment for any reader↔It can benefit promises enrichment = benefit
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱B说书「列出物理学家面临的种种挑战」，借了 physicists 这个全篇高频词诱你选，但录音里女士说的是适合各类读者，从未说本书在「罗列挑战」，属答非所问。借用原文： the career physicist
C) 原词陷阱C说书「描述了某些物理之谜是如何被解开的」，盗用了女士口中的 mysteries 一词，但她只说作者是引领读者了解物理之谜的「向导」，没说书在讲「谜题被解开的过程」，偷换了概念。借用原文： the mysteries of physics
D) 过度推断D说它是「有史以来最引人入胜的物理书之一」，女士确实夸了书（great），但绝没说「史上最…之一」这种最高级定位，属过度推断、把一般称赞拔成顶级评价。
questions.quote: I think it promises enrichment for any reader, from those who know little about science to the career physicist.

options.text: It can benefit professionals and non-professionals alike.
It lists the various challenges physicists are confronting.
It describes how some mysteries of physics were solved.
It is one of the most fascinating physics books ever written.

questions.prompt: What can we find in the book the man recommended?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） Stories about some female physicists.
**题目译文**
在男士推荐的书中我们能找到什么?
A) 物理学家对人类的贡献。
B) 关于一些女性物理学家的故事。
C) 现代物理学的历史演变。
D) 女性对物理学态度的变化。
**定位** 我认为她值得称赞，因为她努力收入了关于鲜为人知的女科学家的轶事。
**信号** 明示「书中收入了…」的内容句。男士说 making an effort to include anecdotes about little-known female scientists，include（收入、包含）直接回应题干「书里能找到什么」，是承载答案的内容句。
**替换** anecdotes about little-known female scientists↔Stories about some female physicists anecdotes=Stories，scientists≈physicists
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及A说「物理学家对人类的贡献」，听着很正能量、像物理书该有的内容，但录音通篇没说书在讲谁对人类有何贡献，属未提及的想当然。
C) 原词陷阱C说「现代物理的历史演变」，借了贯穿全篇的 physics 话题词，但录音从没讲物理学如何一步步演变的历史线，属未提及。借用原文： the mysteries of physics
D) 偷换概念D说「女性对物理态度的转变」，盗用了 P3 里 the woman's place 这类涉及女性的词，但录音说的是收入女科学家的故事，而非讲女性「态度如何变化」，张冠李戴、偷换了主题。借用原文： the woman's place was in the home
questions.quote: I think she is to be commended for making an effort to include anecdotes about little-known female scientists.

options.text: Physicists' contribution to humanity.
Stories about some female physicists.
Historical evolution of modern physics.
Women's changing attitudes to physics.

questions.prompt: How does the author bring her book to life?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） By including lots of fascinating knowledge.
**题目译文**
作者如何让她的书生动起来?
A) 通过揭露物理学中的许多误解。
B) 通过描述她自己的生活经历。
C) 通过包含大量引人入胜的知识。
D) 通过讲述关于著名教授的趣闻轶事。
**定位** 我喜欢这本书写得清晰，每一章都被一个个引人入胜的知识点带得活灵活现。
**信号** 题干原话 brought to life 的对应句。题干问 bring her book to life，录音几乎原话出现each chapter brought to life by pieces of fascinating knowledge，by 引出的正是手段，是答案句。
**替换** brought to life by pieces of fascinating knowledge↔By including lots of fascinating knowledge by…fascinating knowledge=By including…fascinating knowledge
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱A说「靠揭穿物理学中的大量迷思」让书生动，盗用了 P4 里 a myth（迷思）一词，但录音里「揭穿迷思」只是举的一个例子，并非女士点明的「让书生动」的总手段；且原文是 a myth（单个）而非 a lot of myths（大量），张冠李戴又夸大了数量。借用原文： she exposes a myth that I've heard taught by university physics professors
B) 未提及B说「靠描述她自己的人生经历」，听着像作者会用的招，但录音从没说书里写了作者的个人经历，属未提及。
D) 张冠李戴D说「靠讲名教授的逸事」让书生动，盗用了 P4 里 university physics professors 一词，但原文是说「她揭穿了一个连大学物理教授都在教的迷思」，并非「讲教授的逸事」，把教授的角色彻底安错了。借用原文： I've heard taught by university physics professors
questions.quote: I like how the book is clearly written with each chapter brought to life by pieces of fascinating knowledge.

options.text: By exposing a lot of myths in physics.
By describing her own life experiences.
By including lots of fascinating knowledge.
By telling anecdotes about famous professors.

questions.prompt: How does the book cultivate readers' interest in physics?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） It provides experiments they can do themselves.
**题目译文**
这本书如何培养读者对物理学的兴趣?
A) 它避免详细阐述物理学的抽象概念。
B) 它包含大量引人思考的问题。
C) 它展示了他们如何能够成为物理学家。
D) 它提供了他们可以自己动手做的实验。
**定位** 我喜欢她通过提供大量可自己动手做的实验来培养读者对科学的投入，这些实验呈现了经典物理同样的基础原理。
**信号** 题干同源词 cultivate + by 引出做法。录音 cultivates scientific engagement by providing a host of do-it-yourself experiments 与题干 cultivate 同词，by 后引出的「提供可自己动手做的实验」正是答案句。
**替换** do-it-yourself experiments↔ experiments they can do themselves do-it-yourself=they can do themselves hands-on examples make her book a truly interactive read↔It provides experiments they can do themselves. hands-on/interactive 印证「亲自做」
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 过度推断A说书「避免详述物理的抽象概念」，看似呼应末句 equation-free（无公式），但「不含公式」不等于「回避讲抽象概念」，且这也不是录音回答「如何培养兴趣」的那句话，属过度推断。借用原文： this equation-free book is an ideal read
B) 未提及B说书「含大量发人深省的问题」，是想当然的科普书套路，但录音说的是提供动手实验，从没说书里设有大量问题，属未提及。
C) 原词陷阱C说书「展示读者如何能成为物理学家」，盗用了全篇高频的 physicist 一词，但录音只说书让读者动手参与、产生兴趣，绝没说能教人「成为物理学家」，过度拔高了书的功能。借用原文： the career physicist
questions.quote: I like how she cultivates scientific engagement by providing a host of do-it-yourself experiments that bring the same foundational principles of classical physics.

options.text: It avoids detailing abstract concepts of physics.
It contains a lot of thought-provoking questions.
It demonstrates how they can become physicists.
It provides experiments they can do themselves.

questions.prompt: What is the man's problem?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） He has no idea how to proceed with his dissertation.
**题目译文**
这位男士的问题是什么?
A) 他太忙了,无法按时完成作业。
B) 他不知道该写什么样的主题。
C) 他不理解教授的指示。
D) 他不知道如何着手写论文。
**定位** 我在着手写毕业论文上遇到了点麻烦，希望您能给我点建议，告诉我该怎么起步。
**信号** 求助者开口自报处境。对话一开场，男生就用 I'm having some problems getting started on my dissertation 直接交代自己卡在哪——"开口自报处境"就是 problem 题的答案信号，不必等后文。
**替换** getting started on my dissertation ↔ how to proceed with his dissertation起步=怎么往下推进I'm having some problems ↔ He has no idea有麻烦=没头绪
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及选项说他 too busy to finish his assignment in time（太忙赶不及），可男生从头到尾没说自己忙、也没提时间紧，他说的是不知怎么起步，属无中生有。
B) 原词陷阱选项说他 does not know what kind of topic to write on（不知写什么主题）。男生其实已选定主题（后文 aesthetics），问题是选好后"不知怎么往下"，不是没题目，这里借了后文反复出现的 topic 一词来误导。借用原文： The general topic I chose is aesthetics
C) 原词陷阱选项说他 does not understand the professor's instructions。"instructions"确在录音里出现，但那是后文教授叮嘱 follow the instructions，跟男生当前"不会起步"的问题无关，是把别处的词搬来凑。借用原文： make sure to follow the instructions
questions.quote: I'm having some problems getting started on my dissertation, and I was hoping you could give me some advice on how to begin.

options.text: He is too busy to finish his assignment in time.
He does not know what kind of topic to write on.
He does not understand the professor's instructions.
He has no idea how to proceed with his dissertation.

questions.prompt: What does the professor think of the man's topic?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （态度观点题） It is too broad.
**题目译文**
教授认为这位男士的主题怎么样?
A) 太宽泛了。
B) 有点过时了。
C) 有挑战性。
D) 很有趣。
**定位** 这题目太大了。你真得把它缩小，才好驾驭。
**信号** 评价者直接下断语。教授应答时一句 That's much too large a topic 直接给出评价，紧接着 narrow it down（缩小范围）又印证"太大"——评价者直接下断语，就是态度题的答案信号。
**替换** much too large a topic↔too broad太大=太宽泛narrow it down↔ too broad需缩小↔现太宽
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 未提及选项说题目 a bit outdated（有点过时），但教授评的是"太大"，全程没提时间新旧，属无中生有。
C) 偷换概念选项说 It is challenging.（有挑战）。教授嫌它"太大需缩小"，并非夸它有难度有价值，challenging 把负面评价偷换成中性偏褒，方向不符。借用原文： much too large a topic
D) 与原文相反选项说 It is interesting.（有趣）是正面评价，但教授给的是负面评价（太大），极性正好相反，是想当然往好处想的人会掉的坑。借用原文： much too large a topic
questions.quote: That's much too large a topic. You really need to narrow it down in order to make it more accessible.

options.text: It is too broad.
It is a bit outdated.
It is challenging.
It is interesting.

questions.prompt: What is the man really more interested in?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） Nature.
**题目译文**
这位男士真正更感兴趣的是什么?
A) 传记。
B) 自然。
C) 哲学。
D) 美。
**定位** 我本来还希望能换个题目。比起美，我其实更感兴趣的是自然。
**信号** more...than 比较句点出取舍。男生说 I'm really more interested in nature than beauty，一个 more...than 把两样东西摆上天平、明确偏向 nature——比较句就是"更喜欢哪个"的答案信号。
**替换** more interested in nature↔Nature原句取 more 后那项
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱选项 Biography 确在录音里出现，但那是教授让他去图书馆借的 get a copy of his biography，是"该读的材料"，不是男生"更感兴趣的东西"，张冠李戴。借用原文： get a copy of his biography
C) 原词陷阱选项 Philosophy 蹭了录音里 He's the philosopher 的 philosopher 一词，但那是在介绍Hume 的身份，男生并没说更喜欢哲学，是借音近词设的坑。借用原文： He's the philosopher who wrote about where our ideas of beauty come from
D) 与原文相反选项 Beauty 是比较句里 than 后面那一项——正是被比下去的一方。录音确实念了beauty，但男生说的是更喜欢 nature 而非 beauty，取错了天平的另一端。借用原文： more interested in nature than beauty
questions.quote: I was hoping it would be possible for me to change topics. I'm really more interested in nature than beauty.

options.text: Biography.
Nature.
Philosophy.
Beauty.

questions.prompt: What does the professor say the man has to do?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） Stick to the topic assigned.
**题目译文**
教授说这位男士必须做什么?
A) 提高他的累计成绩。
B) 培养他的阅读能力。
C) 坚持布置的主题。
D) 先列出参数。
**定位** 恐怕你得守着那个被指定的题目（不能换）。
**信号** have to 引出硬性要求。教授一句 you have to adhere to the assigned topic，have to（必须）就是"被要求做什么"的答案信号，紧跟其后的动作即答案。
**替换** adhere to the assigned topic↔Stick to the topic assigned adhere to=stick to
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱选项 Improve his cumulative grade. 蹭了录音里 This paper is a large part of your cumulative grade，但那只是解释"为什么要照做"的背景，不是教授要他做的动作，把背景目的偷换成任务。借用原文： This paper is a large part of your cumulative grade
B) 未提及选项 Develop his reading ability. 录音根本没要求他提升阅读能力，他只是被叫去图书馆借本传记，属无中生有。
D) 原词陷阱选项 List the parameters first. 蹭了录音里 stick to the parameters of the assignment的 parameters，但原文是"守住作业的各项规定"，不是"先把参数列出来"，把"遵守"偷换成"列出"。借用原文： remember to stick to the parameters of the assignment
questions.quote: I'm afraid you have to adhere to the assigned topic.

options.text: Improve his cumulative grade.
Develop his reading ability.
Stick to the topic assigned.
List the parameters first.

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Growing up in New Zealand, everything was always calm and slow.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: People enjoyed the tranquility of a slower pace of life.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: But after I moved to Tokyo and lived there for a number of years, I got used to having a pile of to-do lists and my calendar always looked like a mess, with loads of things to do written across it.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: I found myself filling my time up with endless work meetings and social events, rushing along as busy as a bee.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Then, one day, I came across a book called In Praise of Slowness and realized that being busy is not only detrimental, but also has the danger of turning life into an endless race.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: So I started practicing the various practical steps mentioned by the author in the book, and began to revolt against the very idea of being too busy.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: It doesn't mean that my to-do lists no longer exist, but I've become more aware of the importance of slowing down and making sure that I enjoy the daily activities as I carry them out.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: From now on, when someone asks you how your life is, try responding with words like "exciting and fun" instead of the cultural norm that says "busy."
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: See if you experience the tranquility that follows.

transcriptTranslations: 密西西比河长约2300英里,是美国最长的河流。Mackenzie河长约1000英里,是加拿大最长的河流。但这些水道与世界上两条最长的河流——尼罗河和亚马逊河相比,显得微不足道。
尼罗河发源于非洲中部,向北流淌4100多英里注入地中海,其沿岸孕育了世界上伟大的古代文明之一。尼罗河一年中大部分时间平静祥和,过去每年都会泛滥,从而为附近的农田创造、灌溉并带来新的表层土壤,古埃及正是依靠这些农田为生。作为交通工具,这条河流承载着各种船只往来于河道之上。如今沿着这条水道畅通无阻的部分旅行,会经过壮丽的帝王谷,那里矗立着许多古代君主的陵墓,已有3000多年的历史。
亚马逊河与伟大文明和密集定居几乎没有关联。然而这条长达4000英里的南美河流携带着世界上约20%的淡水——比密西西比河、尼罗河和长江的总和还要多。其他统计数据同样令人震惊。亚马逊河在某些地段如此宽阔,以至于从河中心看不到任何一岸。亚马逊河每秒向大西洋注入约5500万加仑的水;在其入海口,有一座比瑞士还大的岛屿。最重要的是,亚马逊河灌溉着地球上最大的热带雨林。
你多久会对别人说"我很忙"或"我没时间做那个"？一个不可避免的事实是，我们所有人都生活在快车道上，尽管我们知道忙碌并不总是特别健康。
在新西兰长大时，一切总是平静而缓慢。人们享受着慢节奏生活的宁静。但在我搬到东京并在那里生活了几年之后,我习惯了堆积如山的待办事项清单，我的日历看起来总是一团糟，上面写满了要做的事情。我发现自己把时间填满了无休止的工作会议和社交活动，像蜜蜂一样忙碌地奔波着。
然后，有一天，我偶然读到一本名为《慢活哲学》的书，意识到忙碌不仅有害，而且有把生活变成无休止竞赛的危险。于是我开始实践书中作者提到的各种实用步骤，并开始反抗过于忙碌这一理念本身。这并不意味着我的待办事项清单不再存在，但我更加意识到放慢脚步的重要性，并确保在进行日常活动时享受它们。
从现在开始，当有人问你生活怎么样时，试着用"令人兴奋和有趣"这样的词来回应，而不是说"忙碌"这个文化常态。看看你是否会体验到随之而来的宁静。

questions.prompt: What can be found in the Valley of the Kings?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） Tombs of ancient rulers.
**题目译文**
在帝王谷可以发现什么?
A) 成片的农田。
B) 典型的埃及动物农场。
C) 古代统治者的陵墓。
D) 毁灭性洪水留下的废墟。
**定位** 今天，沿这条河可通航的河段航行，会经过壮丽的帝王谷，那里矗立着许多古代帝王的陵墓，已逾三千年。
**信号** 关键词 Valley of the Kings 后紧跟 where 引出存在物。答案句由专有地名信号 the splendid Valley of the Kings 触发，其后 where the tombs of many of these ancient monarchs have stood for over 3,000 years 用 where 引导出该地存在的事物——陵墓，这就是题目问的有什么的落点。
**替换** the tombs of many of these ancient monarchs ↔ Tombs of ancient rulers. monarchs=rulers 同义替换
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱选项 Stretches of farmland. 盗用了原文 the nearby farmland on which ancient Egypt depended 里的 farmland，但那是讲尼罗河洪水滋养沿岸农田，并不在帝王谷里能找到，地点对错位了。借用原文： carrying new topsoil to the nearby farmland on which ancient Egypt depended
B) 未提及选项 Typical Egyptian animal farms. 借 Egyptian 与 farm 的关联诱选，原文只提埃及依赖农田耕作，从未说帝王谷里有典型的埃及动物农场，属凭埃及二字硬凑、原文无对应内容。
D) 原词陷阱选项 Ruins left by devastating floods. 盗用原文 the Nile used to flood annually 的flood，但原文洪水是滋养农田的正面作用，根本不是 devastating（毁灭性）的废墟，且废墟也不在帝王谷，词对、语义与地点全错。借用原文： the Nile used to flood annually, thereby creating, irrigating and carrying new topsoil
questions.quote: A journey through the unobstructed part of this waterway today would pass by the splendid Valley of the Kings, where the tombs of many of these ancient monarchs have stood for over 3,000 years.

options.text: Stretches of farmland.
Typical Egyptian animal farms.
Tombs of ancient rulers.
Ruins left by devastating floods.

questions.prompt: In what way is the Amazon different from other big rivers?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） It is hardly associated with great civilizations.
**题目译文**
亚马孙河在哪方面不同于其他大河?
A) 它为更多原始部落提供栖息地。
B) 它几乎不与伟大文明相关联。
C) 它尚未被完全勘探和开发。
D) 它从许多热带雨林汇集水源。
**定位** 伟大的文明与密集的人类定居几乎与亚马孙河无缘。
**信号** 段首否定 hardly 标出反常之处。答案句是第 3 段开门第一句，用否定词 Great civilizations and intensive settlement are hardly associated with the Amazon 直接点出亚马孙河的反常——别的大河多孕育文明，它却几乎没有，这种段首突出的否定式断言正是它与众不同的信号。
**替换** Great civilizations and intensive settlement are hardly associated with the Amazon↔It is hardly associated with great civilizations.近乎原句保留，仅省去 settlement
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及选项 It provides habitats for more primitive tribes. 里 more primitive tribes（更原始的部落）原文从未提及，原文末句只说它 irrigates the largest tropical rain forest on earth，是灌溉雨林而非为原始部落提供栖息地，属凭雨林联想硬加。
C) 偷换概念选项 It has not yet been fully explored and exploited. 借开发/探索的话题诱选，但原文谈的是文明与定居稀少，从未说它尚未被充分开发利用，是把没文明偷换成没开发，原文无此层意思。
D) 与原文相反选项 It gathers water from many tropical rain forests. 盗用原文 irrigates the largest tropical rain forest on earth 的 tropical rain forest，但原文是亚马孙河灌溉雨林（河给雨林水），选项却说它从多片雨林汇水（雨林给河水），施受方向正好相反。借用原文： the Amazon irrigates the largest tropical rain forest on earth
questions.quote: Great civilizations and intensive settlement are hardly associated with the Amazon.

options.text: It provides habitats for more primitive tribes.
It is hardly associated with great civilizations.
It has not yet been fully explored and exploited.
It gathers water from many tropical rain forests.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about the Amazon?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） It carries about one fifth of the world's fresh water.
**题目译文**
说话者关于亚马孙河说了什么?
A) 它携带着世界上约五分之一的淡水。
B) 它的两岸有众多人类定居点。
C) 它的宽度仅次于密西西比河。
D) 它的长度相当于尼罗河和长江加起来的长度。
**定位** 然而这条长达四千英里的南美河流，携带着全球约百分之二十的淡水——比密西西比河、尼罗河和长江加起来还多。
**信号** 数据信号 about 20% 与 more than…combined。答案句以转折 Yet 引出关键数据carries about 20% of the world's fresh water，并补一句 more than the Mississippi, Nile, and Yangtze combined，含百分比与多于…相加，正是数据题该锁定的统计落点。
**替换** carries about 20% of the world's fresh water↔It carries about one fifth of the world's fresh water. 20%=one fifth 数字换算等值
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 与原文相反选项 It has numerous human settlements along its banks. 说沿岸有众多定居点，但原文 intensive settlement are hardly associated with the Amazon 恰恰说密集定居几乎与它无缘，选项与原文极性相反。借用原文： Great civilizations and intensive settlement are hardly associated with the Amazon
C) 原词陷阱选项 It is second only to the Mississippi River in width. 盗用原文真念过的 Mississippi和 wide，但原文 more than the Mississippi, Nile, and Yangtze combined 是说水量多于它们，so wide at some points that…neither shore can be seen 是说它极宽、从未说宽度仅次于密西西比河，把不同的量与排名硬凑在一起。借用原文： The Amazon is so wide at some points that from its center neither shore can be seen.
D) 原词陷阱选项 It is as long as the Nile and the Yangtze combined. 盗用原文 more than the Mississippi, Nile, and Yangtze combined 里的 Nile、Yangtze、combined，但原文这串河名比的是淡水量（carries…more than），不是长度，选项把比较的对象量从水量偷换成long（长度）。借用原文： carries about 20% of the world's fresh water—more than the Mississippi, Nile, and Yangtze combined
questions.quote: Yet this 4,000-mile-long South American river carries about 20% of the world's fresh water—more than the Mississippi, Nile, and Yangtze combined.

options.text: It carries about one fifth of the world's fresh water.
It has numerous human settlements along its banks.
It is second only to the Mississippi River in width.
It is as long as the Nile and the Yangtze combined.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker think is an inevitable truth?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） We are always in a rush to do various things.
**题目译文**
说话者认为什么是不可避免的事实？
A) 快节奏的生活方式会带来成功。
B) 我们总是匆匆忙忙地做各种事情。
C) 对宁静的追求已经成为一种趋势。
D) 我们所有人实际上都渴望缓慢而平静的生活。
**定位** 有一个无可回避的事实：我们所有人都过着快节奏的生活，尽管我们都知道忙碌并不总是那么健康。
**信号** 题干词原文复现。信号是题干里的 inevitable truth 在 It's an inevitable truth that all of us live a life in the fast lane 中原话出现，that 引导的从句就是这个"事实"的具体内容，即答案所在。
**替换** all of us live a life in the fast lane↔We are always in a rush to do various things.比喻短语转直白同义
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱A 借用了原文里的 fast lane 让人耳熟，但原文只说大家都过快节奏生活，从没说"快节奏leads to success（带来成功）"，这个因果是选项凭空加上的。借用原文： all of us live a life in the fast lane
C) 答非所问"对平静的追求成了一种潮流"在原文里并没有作为"inevitable truth"被说出；原文提到平静（tranquility）是讲她个人的转变和结尾的建议，不是说它已成趋势，本题问的是那个"事实"，对不上。
D) 过度推断原文说大家"过着快节奏生活，尽管知道忙不健康"，并没说"所有人其实都向往慢而平静的生活"；D 是把说话人结尾的个人主张夸大成"全体的内心渴望"，与那句"事实"的本意相反。借用原文： being busy is not always particularly healthy
questions.quote: It's an inevitable truth that all of us live a life in the fast lane, even though we know that being busy is not always particularly healthy.

options.text: Living a life in the fast lane leads to success.
We are always in a rush to do various things.
The search for tranquility has become a trend.
All of us actually yearn for a slow and calm life.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about her life in Tokyo?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） She was accustomed to tight schedules.
**题目译文**
说话者如何描述她在东京的生活？
A) 她在平衡家庭和工作方面遇到了困难。
B) 她喜欢各种社交活动。
C) 她习惯于紧凑的日程安排。
D) 她把所有闲暇时间都用来写书。
**定位** 但搬到东京、在那儿住了好些年之后，我习惯了堆成一摞的待办清单，我的日程表总是乱成一团，上面密密麻麻写满了要做的事。
**信号** 转折 But 后引出东京生活。信号是段首的转折词 But after I moved to Tokyo——前面讲新西兰的慢生活，But 之后才转到东京，这正是本题问的"东京生活"落点，紧跟的描述就是答案句。
**替换** I got used to having a pile of to-do lists↔She was accustomed to tight schedules.短语换近义词 + 具象换概括
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及原文讲东京生活只说待办多、日程乱、忙得像蜜蜂，从没提"难以平衡家庭与工作"；balancing family and work 是文中根本没出现的内容。
B) 原词陷阱B 借了原文里的 social events 让人耳熟，但原文是说她被无尽的会议和社交活动"填满时间、忙得团团转"，是负担，不是"enjoyed（享受）"；选项把忙碌偷换成了享受。借用原文： filling my time up with endless work meetings and social events, rushing along as busy as a bee
D) 张冠李戴原文东京段只讲忙，没说"闲暇全用来写书"；book 一词虽在第三段出现，但那是她"读到"一本书 I came across a book，不是她写书，更不在东京段，D 把无关且改写错的细节塞了进来。借用原文： I came across a book called In Praise of Slowness
questions.quote: But after I moved to Tokyo and lived there for a number of years, I got used to having a pile of to-do lists and my calendar always looked like a mess, with loads of things to do written across it.

options.text: She had trouble balancing family and work.
She enjoyed the various social events.
She was accustomed to tight schedules.
She spent all her leisure time writing books.

questions.prompt: What made the speaker change her lifestyle?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） Reading a book about slowing down.
**题目译文**
是什么让说话者改变了她的生活方式？
A) 可能毁掉她的家庭。
B) 意识到自己的健康状况在下降。
C) 快节奏生活带来的疲惫。
D) 读了一本关于放慢生活节奏的书。
**定位** 后来有一天，我偶然读到一本叫《赞美慢》的书，意识到忙碌不仅有害，还有把生活变成无尽赛跑的危险。
**信号** 时间转折 Then, one day 引出起因。信号是 Then, one day 这个时间转折——它标志故事从"一直很忙"拐向"开始改变"，紧跟的"读到一本书并意识到……"就是促成改变的那件事，即答案。
**替换** I came across a book called In Praise of Slowness↔Reading a book about slowing down.动词与书名的同义改写
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及原文从没说她担心"忙碌会毁掉家庭"；ruining her family 是文中完全没有的原因，属凭日常想象添加的选项。
B) 偷换概念原文说她意识到忙"detrimental（有害）"、可能让生活变成 endless race，但这是读书后的领悟，并非"察觉自己健康在下滑"这一亲身体验；B 把抽象的"有害"偷换成具体的"健康下滑"，且颠倒了"先读书才醒悟"的顺序。借用原文： being busy is not only detrimental
C) 原词陷阱C 里的快节奏生活确是全篇背景，但原文促成改变的直接起因是"读到那本书"，而非"被快节奏累垮"；选项盗用主题词 fast-paced life 制造耳熟，却把背景错当成了导火索。借用原文： rushing along as busy as a bee
questions.quote: Then, one day, I came across a book called In Praise of Slowness and realized that being busy is not only detrimental, but also has the danger of turning life into an endless race.

options.text: The possibility of ruining her family.
Becoming aware of her declining health.
The fatigue from living a fast-paced life.
Reading a book about slowing down.

questions.prompt: What happened after the speaker changed her lifestyle?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） She came to enjoy doing everyday tasks.
**题目译文**
说话者改变生活方式后发生了什么？
A) 她开始遵循文化规范。
B) 她开始享受做日常事务。
C) 她学会了使用更礼貌的表达方式。
D) 她不再使用待办事项清单和日历。
**定位** 这并不是说我的待办清单从此不存在了，而是我更意识到放慢节奏的重要，并确保自己在做日常事务时是享受其中的。
**信号** but 后的 I've become 落出真意。信号有两处：前半 It doesn't mean that my to-do lists no longer exist 先排除"完全弃用清单"这一误解，转折词 but 之后的 I enjoy the daily activities 才是改变后的真实结果，转折后才是落点。
**替换** I enjoy the daily activities as I carry them out↔She came to enjoy doing everyday tasks.近义词逐一对应
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反原文结尾建议大家别用 the cultural norm that says "busy"，主张反其道而行，而不是"开始顺从文化习惯"；A 与原文的主张正好相反。借用原文： instead of the cultural norm that says "busy"
C) 未提及原文结尾让人改用 exciting and fun 来回答，那是为了体现"不再以忙为常态"，不是为了"更礼貌"；用语更礼貌 polite expressions 是文中没有的说法。
D) 原词陷阱D 借了原文真出现的 to-do lists，但原文明确说 It doesn't mean that my to-do lists no longer exist——清单并没有不存在；D 把"没那么依赖"夸大成"彻底停用"，被前半句直接否掉。借用原文： It doesn't mean that my to-do lists no longer exist
questions.quote: It doesn't mean that my to-do lists no longer exist, but I've become more aware of the importance of slowing down and making sure that I enjoy the daily activities as I carry them out.

options.text: She started to follow the cultural norms.
She came to enjoy doing everyday tasks.
She learned to use more polite expressions.
She stopped using to-do lists and calendars.

transcript.text: One very important code was never broken.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: It was used during World War II by the Americans.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: It was a spoken code never written down.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: And it was developed and used by Navajo Indians.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They were called "the Navajo code talkers".
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The Navajos created the code in their own language.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Navajo is hard to learn and only a few people know it.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: So it was pretty certain that the enemy would not be able to understand the code talkers.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: In addition, the talkers used code words.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They called a submarine an iron fish and a small bomb thrown by hand a potato.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: If they wanted to spell something, they used code words for letters of the alphabet.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: For instance, the letter A was ant or apple or ax.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The code talkers worked mostly in the islands in the Pacific.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: One or two would be assigned to a group of soldiers.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They would send messages by field telephone to the code talker in the next group.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: And he would relay the information to his commander.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The code talkers played an important part in several battles.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They helped troops coordinate their movements and attacks.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: After the war, the U.S. government honored them for what they had accomplished.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Theirs was the most successful wartime code ever used.

transcriptTranslations: 许多人喜欢密码。密码越难，就有越多的人试图破解它。在战时，密码尤其重要。它们帮助军队传送有关战斗和敌军规模的消息。任何一方都不希望自己的密码被对方破解。

有一种非常重要的密码从未被破解。它在第二次世界大战期间被美国人使用。这是一种口头密码，从未被写下来。它由Navajo印第安人开发和使用。他们被称为"Navajo密码通讯员"。Navajo人用他们自己的语言创造了这种密码。Navajo语很难学，只有少数人懂得它。因此几乎可以肯定敌人无法理解密码通讯员的内容。此外,通讯员还使用了代码词。他们把潜艇称为铁鱼,把手榴弹称为土豆。如果他们想拼写什么,就使用字母表中字母的代码词。例如,字母A是蚂蚁、苹果或斧头。
密码通讯员主要在太平洋的岛屿上工作。一到两名通讯员会被分配到一组士兵中。他们通过野战电话向下一组的密码通讯员发送消息。然后他会将信息传达给他的指挥官。密码通讯员在几次战斗中发挥了重要作用。他们帮助部队协调行动和进攻。战后,美国政府为他们所取得的成就授予了荣誉。他们的密码是战时使用过的最成功的密码。
如果你正年轻并在思考自己的职业生涯，你会想知道可以在哪里谋生。
在未来20年里，大量知识密集型工作将被技术取代,特别是在劳动力队伍中拥有专业技能的两个最大部门。一个是教育,另一个是医疗保健。将会有许多应用程序、软件和平台进入这两个领域提供信息和服务,这意味着大量医疗保健和教育部门将发生根本性变化,许多工作岗位将会消失。
那么,新的工作岗位将在哪里出现呢?经济中有一个部门是即使智能技术也无法轻易复制的,那就是护理部门——个人护理部门。也就是说,你无法真正让机器人做出很好的按摩或物理治疗,或者你无法获得治疗或任何其他个人服务所需的那种个人关注。可能会有非常高端的个人服务。治疗师确实收费很高。我认为如果人们负担得起,他们想要的个人关注和个人护理是没有限度的。
但未来真正的问题是,如果人们没有钱,他们怎么能负担得起这些东西,因为他们找不到薪酬足够高的工作。这就是我写这本书的原因,这本书讲述的是当技术给我们过去认为的高收入工作带来破坏性变化时,如何为未来重组经济。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say many people enjoy doing?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） Decoding secret messages.
**题目译文**
说话者说许多人喜欢做什么?
A) 了解他人的秘密。
B) 搜索信息。
C) 破译秘密信息。
D) 传播耸人听闻的新闻。
**定位** 很多人喜欢密码。密码越难，有些人越想把它破解出来。
**信号** 开篇点题句，enjoy 直接对上题干 enjoy doing。录音第一句就是 Many people enjoy secret codes，题干问 enjoy doing，这里 enjoy 原词出现，是直接应答型信号；紧接的try to figure it out 进一步说明他们享受的是把密码破解出来这件事。
**替换** try to figure it out↔ Decoding secret messages. figure out a code = decode，同义改写
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 偷换概念Learning others' secrets. 借了原文 secret codes 里的 secret 制造熟悉感，但原文讲的是figure out 密码本身，不是打探别人的隐私秘密，属偷换概念。借用原文： secret codes
B) 未提及Searching for information. 在录音里找不到对应表述，原文只说人们享受破解密码，没有谈搜集或查找信息，属无中生有。
D) 张冠李戴Spreading sensational news. 与开篇 enjoy 那句无关；录音后文虽提到 They help the army send news about battles，但那是讲密码在战时的用途、不是人们喜欢做的事，本项把 news 张冠李戴还加上原文没有的 sensational。借用原文： They help the army send news about battles
questions.quote: Many people enjoy secret codes. The harder the code, the more some people will try to figure it out.

options.text: Learning others' secrets.
Searching for information.
Decoding secret messages.
Spreading sensational news.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the Navajo code talkers?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） They helped the U.S. army in World War Ⅱ.
**题目译文**
关于Navajo密码通信员我们了解到什么?
A) 他们在第二次世界大战中帮助了美国军队。
B) 他们能够迅速写下口头密码。
C) 他们被指派破译敌方信息。
D) 他们擅长破解敌方密码。
**定位** 有一种非常重要的密码从未被破译。它在二战期间被美国人使用。它是由纳瓦霍印第安人创造并使用的。
**信号** 直接陈述句，点出二战、美国、由 Navajo 使用。录音用一组陈述句交代事实：It was used during World War II by the Americans 与 it was developed and used by Navajo Indians，明确这套密码服务于二战中的美国一方，是描述该群体的关键事实句；第三段They helped troops coordinate their movements and attacks 再次佐证他们帮的是己方部队。
**替换** It was used during World War II by the Americans↔They helped the U.S. army in World War Ⅱ. the Americans 用此码 = 帮 U.S. army，World War II 原词对上They helped troops coordinate their movements and attacks↔They helped the U.S. army in World War Ⅱ. helped troops coordinate = helped the U.S. army，详述被概括
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 与原文相反They could write down spoken codes promptly. 借了原文 It was a spoken code never written down 里 spoken、written 的字眼，但原文恰恰强调这套密码从不写下来，本项却说他们能迅速写下，与原文相反。借用原文： It was a spoken code never written down
C) 原词陷阱They were assigned to decode enemy messages. 堆了 decode、enemy、messages一串原文热词制造熟悉感；assigned 也确在原文 One or two would be assigned to a group of soldiers 出现过。但原文说的是 Navajo 用自己创造的密码发消息帮己方，不是被派去破译敌方密码，方向完全相反。借用原文： One or two would be assigned to a group of soldiers
D) 原词陷阱They were good at breaking enemy secret codes. 借了原文反复出现的 code、broken（如 One very important code was never broken）；但原文是说他们的密码没人能破，不是他们擅长去破敌方密码，方向被偷换。借用原文： One very important code was never broken
questions.quote: One very important code was never broken. It was used during World War II by the Americans. And it was developed and used by Navajo Indians.

options.text: They helped the U.S. army in World War Ⅱ.
They could write down spoken codes promptly.
They were assigned to decode enemy messages.
They were good at breaking enemy secret codes.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker mainly talking about?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （主旨题） A military code that was never broken.
**题目译文**
说话者主要在谈论什么?
A) 太平洋战争中的重要战役。
B) 战时秘密信息的破译。
C) 一种从未被破解的军事密码。
D) Navajo印第安人对密码破译的贡献。
**定位** 有一种非常重要的密码从未被破译。它在二战期间被美国人使用。……他们的密码是有史以来最成功的战时密码。
**信号** 开头点题 never broken + 结尾收束 most successful 首尾呼应。第二段开篇 One very important code was never broken 立即点题，第三段结尾 Theirs was the most successful wartime code ever used 用最高级收束，首尾都在强调这是一套从未被破、最成功的密码，是典型的主旨信号。
**替换** One very important code was never broken ↔ A military code that was never broken. never broken 原意保留，code 加限定为 military Theirs was the most successful wartime code ever used ↔A military code that was never broken. most successful wartime code = military code，结尾印证主旨
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱Important battles fought in the Pacific War. 借了原文 The code talkers worked mostly in the islands in the Pacific 与 battles 等词，但原文只把太平洋战役当作密码发挥作用的背景，没展开讲具体战役，本项以局部细节冒充主旨。借用原文： The code talkers worked mostly in the islands in the Pacific
B) 过度推断Decoding of secret messages in war times. 借了 codes、war 等主题词，但全文重点是Navajo 用自家密码而非破译密码，且这一概括过于宽泛，没扣住从未被破这一独特点，属以偏概全兼方向偏。借用原文： In wartime, codes are especially important
D) 偷换概念Navajo Indians' contribution to code breaking. 用了 Navajo、code 这两个全文核心词，极具迷惑性；但原文讲的是 Navajo 创造并使用一套不可破的密码（编码、保密），不是他们去破译别人的密码（code breaking），主旨方向被偷换。借用原文： The Navajos created the code in their own language
questions.quote: One very important code was never broken. It was used during World War II by the Americans. ... Theirs was the most successful wartime code ever used.

options.text: Important battles fought in the Pacific War.
Decoding of secret messages in war times.
A military code that was never broken.
Navajo Indians' contribution to code breaking.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say will happen in the next 20 years?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） A lot of knowledge-intensive jobs will be replaced.
**题目译文**
说话者说在未来20年里将会发生什么?
A) 所有服务都将个性化。
B) 许多知识密集型工作将被取代。
C) 技术将彻底改变所有工业部门。
D) 将有更多信息可供使用。
**定位** 嗯，在未来 20 年里，会出现对大量知识密集型工作的技术性替代，尤其是在劳动力中两个最大的、需要专业技能的领域。
**信号** 时间标志 in the next 20 years 直接对题。这句出现了题干同款时间标志 in the next 20 years，又紧跟全段开头的 Well 起话，是说话人对"未来 20 年"下的核心判断，正是答案句。
**替换** a technological replacement of a lot of knowledge-intensive jobs ↔A lot of knowledge-intensive jobs will be replaced.名词化转主动+被动改写
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱A 说 All services will be personalized.，蹭了原文 provide information and service 里的 service 一词，但原文从没说"所有服务都将个性化"，是听到 service 就联想个性化的原词陷阱，且 All 范围过绝。借用原文： provide information and service
C) 偷换概念C 说 Technology will revolutionize all sectors of industry.，原文只点了 the two largest sectors of the labor force"两个最大领域"，C 把"两个"夸成"所有行业"，属范围程度偷改。借用原文： the two largest sectors of the labor force
D) 原词陷阱D 说 More information will be available.，蹭了原文 provide information and service的 information，但原文是说应用软件"提供信息和服务"来替代工作，并非说"信息会变多"，听到 information 就选即落坑。借用原文： provide information and service
questions.quote: Well, there's going to be a technological replacement of a lot of knowledge-intensive jobs in the next 20 years, particularly in the two largest sectors of the labor force with professional skills.

options.text: All services will be personalized.
A lot of knowledge-intensive jobs will be replaced.

questions.prompt: Where will young people have more chances to find jobs?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） In the personal care sector.
**题目译文**
年轻人在哪里会有更多机会找到工作?
A) 在机器人行业。
B) 在信息服务业。
C) 在个人护理行业。
D) 在高端制造业。
**定位** 那么，新的工作会在哪里出现呢？嗯，经济中唯一一个连智能技术都不易复制的领域，就是看护领域——个人护理领域。
**信号** 设问自答 where…+ the one sector…is。录音先自设问 where will the new jobs be found?，随即用 the one sector…is the personal care sector 自答，设问句后紧跟的答句正是答案落点，信号极强。
**替换** the personal care sector↔ In the personal care sector.几乎原词，仅加介词 In
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱A 说 In the robotics industry.，原文确实念到 you can't really get a robot to do a great massage，但 robot 是被当作"做不了护理"的反例提的，绝非新工作所在领域，听到 robot就选即中招。借用原文： you can't really get a robot to do a great massage
B) 与原文相反B 说 In the information service.，蹭的是上一段 provide information and service 的information service，但那是被技术替代的旧领域，不是新工作领域，正好与题意相反。借用原文： provide information and service
D) 原词陷阱D 说 In high-end manufacturing.，蹭了原文 There could be very high-end personal services. 的 high-end，但原文 high-end 修饰的是"个人服务"，根本没提"制造业"，是拼词造出的陷阱。借用原文： There could be very high-end personal services.
questions.quote: Now, where will the new jobs be found? Well, the one sector of the economy that can't be easily duplicated by even smart technologies is the caring sector—the personal care sector.

options.text: In the robotics industry.
In the information service.
In the personal care sector.
In high-end manufacturing.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about therapists?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） They charge high prices.
**题目译文**
说话者对治疗师说了什么?
A) 他们收费很高。
B) 他们需要大量培训。
C) 他们迎合年轻人的需求。
D) 他们关注客户的具体需求。
**定位** 治疗师确实收费很高。
**信号** 强调助动词 do + 点名 Therapists。这句直接点名 Therapists 并用强调助动词 do（do charge）加重"确实收费高"的语气，是说话人对治疗师的明确评述，答案句无疑。
**替换** Therapists do charge a lot of money↔ They charge high prices. a lot of money = high prices 同义替换
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 未提及B 说 They need lots of training.，原文谈治疗师只说收费高，从未提及他们"需要大量培训"，是凭"专业人士想必要培训"的常识硬加，原文无据。
C) 原词陷阱C 说 They cater to the needs of young people.，young 蹭自开头 If you are young and thinking about your career，但那是对听众说的，与治疗师服务对象无关，听到young 就联想即落坑。借用原文： If you are young and thinking about your career
D) 原词陷阱D 说 They focus on customers' specific needs.，蹭了原文 the kind of personal attention you need 的"个人需求"语境，但原文这话是讲护理服务的不可替代性，并非评价治疗师"专注客户具体需求"，是预读就标记过的"听着顺"的分流项。借用原文： the kind of personal attention you need
questions.quote: Therapists do charge a lot of money.

options.text: They charge high prices.
They need lots of training.
They cater to the needs of young people.
They focus on customers' specific needs.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's book about?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （主旨题） The disruption caused by technology in traditionally well-paid jobs.
**题目译文**
说话者的书是关于什么的?
A) 未来20年教育和医疗保健领域不断增长的需求。
B) 技术对传统高薪工作造成的冲击。
C) 新技术将给人们生活带来的巨大变化。
D) 人们想要获得的惊人数量的个人关注。
**定位** 这就是我写这本书的原因——这本书讲的是，当技术给我们过去视为高收入的工作带来破坏性变化时，如何为未来重新组织经济。
**信号** 结尾收束 That's why…this book is about。末段用 That's why I wrote this book which is about… 直接收束并点出书的主题，That's why 是结论信号、which is about 直接给出书的内容，是主旨答案句。
**替换** technology brings about destructive changes to what we used to consider high income work↔The disruption caused by technology in traditionally well-paid jobs. destructive changes=disruption，high income=well-paid
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 答非所问A 说 The rising demand in education and healthcare in the next 20 years.，蹭了第二段 teaching and the other, healthcare 和 the next 20 years，但那是中段铺垫的细节，且原文说这两领域是"被替代、岗位流失"而非"需求上升"，既以偏概全又方向反了。借用原文： teaching and the other, healthcare
C) 过度推断C 说 The tremendous changes new technology will bring to people's lives.，蹭了changes、technology 等高频词，但"给人们生活带来的巨变"比书的实际主题（如何为未来重组经济以应对高薪工作受冲击）宽泛太多，是预读标记的范围过宽陷阱。借用原文： technology brings about destructive changes

transcript.text: Governments, private groups and individuals spend billions of dollars a year trying to root out non- native organisms that are considered dangerous to ecosystems, and to prevent the introduction of new intruders.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: But a number of scientists question the assumption that the presence of alien species can never be acceptable in a natural ecosystem.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They say that portraying introduced species as inherently bad is an unscientific approach.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Distinctions between exotic and native species are artificial, said Dr.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Michael Rosenzweig, a professor of evolutionary biology at the University of Arizona, because they depend on picking a date and calling the plants and animals that show up after that date exotic.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Ecosystems free of species defined as exotic are, by default, considered the most natural.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: "You can't roll back the clock and remove all exotics or fix habitats," Dr.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Rosenzweig said.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: "Both native and exotic species can become invasive, and so they all have to be monitored and controlled when they begin to get out of hand."
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: At its core, the debate is about how to manage the world's remaining natural ecosystems and about how, and how much, to restore other habitats.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Species that invade a territory can harm ecosystems, agriculture and human health.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: They can threaten some native species or even destroy and replace others.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Next to habitat loss, these invasive species represent the greatest threat to biodiversity worldwide, many ecologists say.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Ecologists generally define an alien species as one that people, accidentally or deliberately, carried to its new location.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Across the American continents, exotic species are those introduced after the first European contact.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: That date, rounded off to 1500 AD, represents what ecologists consider to have been a major shift in the spread of species, including crops and livestock, as they began to migrate with humans from continent to continent.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Of the 7,000 alien species in the United States—out of a total of 150,000 species—only about 10 percent are invasive, he pointed out.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The other 90 percent have fit into their environments and are considered naturalized.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Yet appearances can deceive, ecologists caution, and many of these exotics may be considered acceptable only because no one has documented their harmful effects.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: What is more, non-native species can appear harmless for decades, then turn invasive.

transcriptTranslations: 政府、私人团体和个人每年花费数十亿美元试图根除被认为对生态系统有危害的非本地物种,并防止新入侵者的引入。
但一些科学家质疑外来物种的存在在自然生态系统中永远不可接受这一假设。他们说,将引入物种描述为本质上有害是一种不科学的方法。
外来物种和本地物种之间的区分是人为的,亚利桑那大学进化生物学教授Michael Rosenzweig博士说,因为它们取决于选择一个日期,并将该日期之后出现的动植物称为外来物种。没有被定义为外来物种的生态系统默认被认为是最自然的。
Rosenzweig博士说:"你无法让时光倒流并清除所有外来物种或修复栖息地。本地物种和外来物种都可能成为入侵物种,因此当它们开始失控时,都必须对它们进行监测和控制。"
从根本上说,这场辩论关乎如何管理世界上现存的自然生态系统,以及如何以及在多大程度上恢复其他栖息地。入侵一个地区的物种可能会危害生态系统、农业和人类健康。它们可能威胁一些本地物种,甚至摧毁并取代其他物种。许多生态学家表示,仅次于栖息地丧失,这些入侵物种是全球生物多样性面临的最大威胁。
生态学家通常将外来物种定义为人们意外或故意携带到新地点的物种。在美洲大陆,外来物种是指首次与欧洲接触后引入的物种。这个日期约为公元1500年,代表了生态学家认为物种传播的重大转变,包括农作物和家畜,它们开始随人类从一个大陆迁移到另一个大陆。

田纳西大学生态学和进化生物学教授Don Smith说,只有一小部分外来物种在其新栖息地造成问题。他指出,在美国的7000种外来物种中——总共15万种物种——只有大约10%是入侵性的。其他90%已经适应了它们的环境,被认为是归化的。然而生态学家警告说,表象可能具有欺骗性,这些外来物种中的许多可能被认为是可接受的,只是因为没有人记录它们的有害影响。更重要的是,非本地物种可能在数十年内看起来无害,然后变成入侵性的。

女士们、先生们,早上好。欢迎来到我们"海外经商"系列商务研讨会的第三讲。今天我们将探讨跨文化意识,也就是说,并非每个人都是英国人,并非每个人都说英语,并非每个人都以英国方式做生意。他们为什么要这样做呢?如果海外商务人士向我们销售产品,那么他们会尽一切努力说英语,尊重我们的传统和方法。当我们拜访他们时,我们也应该这样做,这是基本的礼貌。这不仅仅是礼貌问题。如果我们想向海外销售英国产品,这是至关重要的。
首先,来做一个小测验。让我们看看你们的跨文化意识如何。问题1:在每月的第一天和第七天,你绝对不能在哪里饮酒?问题2:你永远不应该在哪里赞美主人的财物?问题3:在曼谷的商务午餐中,你应该如何招呼服务员?问题4:你应该在哪里尽量把所有约会安排在下午2点之前或5点半之后?

好的。大家都有机会做些笔记了吗?好。下面是答案——尽管我确信这些信息同样适用于我所选择的国家以外的其他国家。第1题,在印度,每月的第一天和第七天不能饮酒。在国际酒店,你可能会发现供应酒精饮料,但如果你与印度同事共进餐,如果你的到访恰逢这些日期之一,记得不要点啤酒。第2题,在阿拉伯国家,人们的礼貌和慷慨是无与伦比的。如果你赞美同事漂亮的金碗,你很可能会发现它们被作为礼物送给你。然而,这不是一种廉价的购物方式,因为你的主人会理所当然地期望你回赠一份价值和美感相当的礼物。在泰国,打响指、拍手或只是喊"服务员!"会让你的主人、其他用餐者、服务员本人,尤其是你自己感到尴尬!应该手掌朝下,做一个不显眼的挥手动作,这会立即产生令人满意的效果。最后,在西班牙,一些企业保持工作到大约2点,然后从5点半到晚上8点、9点或10点返回办公室的模式。

1984年George Grune接管Reader's Digest Association后不久,打开了公司的董事会会议室,并宣布这个房间现在对员工开放。这是一个象征性的举动,表明在Grune的领导下,Reader's Digest将会有所不同。Grune确实信守诺言,改变了这里的文化。要了解我们所说的文化,可以看看Grune开放的这间董事会会议室。它拥有世界上任何博物馆都想收藏的艺术品,包括Monet和Picasso等许多世界著名艺术家的画作。其总部收藏了约3000件艺术品。主楼顶部是一座Georgian塔楼,上面有四座神话中带翼飞马的雕塑,这是该杂志的企业标志。它坐落在127英亩修剪整齐的草坪上。

编辑办公室曾经由创始人DeWitt Wallace使用,他与妻子Lila Acheson Wallace于1922年创办了Reader's Digest,刊登其他出版物的精简文章。它已成为世界上阅读最广泛的杂志,每月以17种语言和41个不同版本销售2800万册。Wallace夫妇都是教会牧师的子女,为他们的"小杂志"制定了明确的方针,Reader's Digest最初的副标题就是如此。文章要短小、易读且令人振奋。选题旨在启发或娱乐。Wallace夫妇直到1955年才在美国版接受广告,即使那时他们也不允许香烟、酒类或药品的任何广告。Wallace夫妇对他们想要的工作场所也有清晰的认识。它开始时是夫妻店式的经营,没有子女的Wallace夫妇始终将员工视为家人。员工们至今还在讲述Wallace夫妇如何照顾遭遇不幸的员工,他们给予员工不同寻常的福利,比如感恩节的火鸡和五月份的周五休假。
这种温馨的工作场所在这里已不复存在。Wallace夫妇都在1980年代初九十多岁时去世。George Grune是一位前广告推销员,1960年加入Reader's Digest,他的目光聚焦在利润底线上。在短短几年内,他彻底改变了这本杂志。他解雇了数百名员工。受打击尤其严重的是蓝领和粉领部门,如订阅履行部门。

questions.prompt: What assumption about introduced species is challenged by a number of scientists?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） They pose a threat to the local ecosystem.
**题目译文**
关于引入物种的哪一假设受到了一些科学家的质疑?
A) 它们会彻底根除本地物种。
B) 它们有助于地区生物多样性。
C) 它们对当地生态系统构成威胁。
D) 它们会与本地物种杂交。
**定位** 但有一些科学家质疑这样一个假设：外来物种出现在自然生态系统中永远是不可接受的。
**信号** 转折 But + 题干同词 question the assumption。答案句由转折词 But 领起，且与题干assumption 用同一个词 question the assumption，转折后正是被质疑的那条假设；听力里 But 之后才是真意，加上题干原词复现，这句必是答案句。
**替换** the presence of alien species can never be acceptable in a natural ecosystem↔They pose a threat to the local ecosystem永不可接受=被视为对生态的威胁
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱录音第一段确有 root out non-native organisms（铲除外来生物），选项把 root out 搬来却改成 root out native species altogether（彻底铲除本地物种）——铲除的对象是外来物种、不是本地物种，且 altogether 这种绝对化也无据，是典型听到原词就想选的陷阱。借用原文： root out non-native organisms
B) 张冠李戴外来物种有益、有助生物多样性是后面科学家反驳时的立场，而非题干要的被质疑的假设；选项 contribute to a region's biodiversity 方向正相反，且 biodiversity 一词出现在第五段讲威胁时 the greatest threat to biodiversity，借这个词制造熟悉感，实为张冠李戴。借用原文： the greatest threat to biodiversity
D) 未提及选项说外来物种会与本地物种 crossbreed with native species（杂交），录音通篇讨论的是威胁、控制、归化，从未提到杂交这一点，属凭常识臆造、原文无对应的未提及项。
questions.quote: But a number of scientists question the assumption that the presence of alien species can never be acceptable in a natural ecosystem.

options.text: They will root out native species altogether.
They contribute to a region's biodiversity.
They pose a threat to the local ecosystem.
They will crossbreed with native species.

questions.prompt: What does Dr. Michael Rosenzweig think of exotic and native species?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （态度观点题） Their distinctions are artificial.
**题目译文**
Michael Rosenzweig 博士如何看待外来物种和本地物种?
A) 它们的分类是有意义的。
B) 它们的相互作用难以界定。
C) 它们的定义是可变的。
D) 它们的区别是人为的。
**定位** 外来物种与本地物种之间的区分是人为的，亚利桑那大学进化生物学教授 Michael Rosenzweig 博士说，因为这种区分取决于挑一个日期、把此后出现的动植物称作外来物种。
**信号** 人名 said Dr. Rosenzweig 直接领出本人观点。答案句中 said Dr. Michael Rosenzweig把发言人锁定为题干问的那个人，他亲口给出的判断 Distinctions between exotic and native species are artificial 就是观点句；态度题紧跟人名找他说的评价句即可定位。
**替换** Distinctions between exotic and native species are artificial↔Their distinctions are artificial几乎原句压缩，artificial 评价一致
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反Rosenzweig 明说区分是 artificial（人为、不真实），选项却说分类 Their classifications are meaningful（有意义、站得住），与他的立场完全相反，是把观点极性反转的陷阱。借用原文： Distinctions between exotic and native species are artificial
B) 偷换概念选项说它们的 interactions are hard to define（相互作用难界定），但原文谈的是distinctions（区分）人为，且说难以界定的不是 interactions；选项借 species 的话题感把 distinction 偷换成 interaction，答非所问。借用原文： Distinctions between exotic and native species are artificial
C) 过度推断选项说 Their definitions are changeable（定义可变），原文虽提到区分取决于 picking a date（挑个日期），但 Rosenzweig 的核心判断是这条区分本身人为，而非强调定义会变；changeable 看似沾边，却不是他给出的定性，属偏离重心。借用原文： picking a date and calling the plants and animals that show up after that date exotic
questions.quote: Distinctions between exotic and native species are artificial, said Dr. Michael Rosenzweig, a professor of evolutionary biology at the University of Arizona, because they depend on picking a date and calling the plants and animals that show up after that date exotic.

Their interactions are hard to define.
Their definitions are changeable.
Their distinctions are artificial.

questions.prompt: What does Professor Don Smith say about alien species?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） Only a few of them cause problems to native species.
**题目译文**
Don Smith 教授关于外来物种说了什么?
A) 它们中只有少数对本地物种造成问题。
B) 它们可能最终对当地环境有益。
C) 它们中很少能在新栖息地存活。
D) 它们中只有百分之十能够归化。
**定位** 只有一小部分外来物种会在新栖息地造成问题，田纳西大学生态与进化生物学教授 Don Smith 说。
**信号** 人名 said Don Smith + 数量限定 Only a small percentage。答案句由 said Don Smith锁定发言人，开头的数量限定 Only a small percentage 正是他给出的核心事实；题干问某人 say about，紧跟人名的这句限定数量的陈述就是答案句。
**替换** Only a small percentage of alien species cause problems in their new habitats ↔Only a few of them cause problems to native species a small percentage = a few，同义换说
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 与原文相反选项说外来物种 may turn out to benefit the local environment（可能有益于本地环境），但原文末尾 Smith 的真意恰相反——他提醒 non-native species can appear harmless for decades, then turn invasive（看似无害多年后会转为入侵），强调的是别被表象骗，而非可能有益；选项把警示反向曲解。借用原文： non-native species can appear harmless for decades, then turn invasive
C) 原词陷阱选项 Few of them can survive in their new habitats（少有能存活）借用了原文 in their new habitats 这一原词，但 Smith 说的是少数会惹问题、九成已 fit into their environments 适应良好，恰恰是大多数能存活；选项把适应说成不能存活，与原文相反。借用原文： fit into their environments and are considered naturalized
D) 原词陷阱原文确有 only about 10 percent are invasive——10% 是入侵的比例；选项 Only 10 percent of them can be naturalized 把数字搬对，却说成只有 10% 能归化，与原文 The other 90 percent…are considered naturalized（九成才是归化）正好颠倒，是典型听到数字就想选的陷阱。借用原文： only about 10 percent are invasive
questions.quote: Only a small percentage of alien species cause problems in their new habitats, said Don Smith, professor of ecology and evolutionary biology at the University of Tennessee.

options.text: Only a few of them cause problems to native species.
They may turn out to benefit the local environment.
Few of them can survive in their new habitats.
Only 10 percent of them can be naturalized.

questions.prompt: What should you do when doing business with foreigners?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） Respect their traditional culture.
**题目译文**
与外国人做生意时你应该做什么?
A) 尊重他们的传统文化。
B) 参加他们的商务研讨会。
C) 研究他们的具体需求。
D) 采用正确的商业策略。
**定位** 我们去拜访他们时，做到同样这一点才算有礼貌。这还不只是礼貌问题，如果我们想把英国产品卖到海外，这是必不可少的。
**信号** 强调句 It is essential 标出讲者的核心建议。讲者先说对方卖给我们时会努力说英语、尊重我们的传统方法，紧接着用 It is only polite for us to do the same 要求我们反过来也这样，并用 It is essential if we want to sell British products overseas 加重语气——“essential（必不可少）”这种强调用词，就是答案句的信号。
**替换** respect our traditions and methods↔Respect their traditional culture traditions and methods 概括成 traditional culture do the same when we visit them↔Respect their traditional culture. do the same 指代前句的“尊重对方传统”
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱录音开头有 our series of business seminars，选项 Attend their business seminars. 正是盗用了 seminars 这个原词。但“seminars”指的是讲者自己办的这场系列讲座，根本不是“和外国人做生意该做什么”的答案，纯靠耳熟骗选。借用原文： our series of business seminars
C) 未提及Research their specific demands.（研究他们的具体需求）听起来像很专业的商务建议，但录音里讲者给的总纲是“尊重对方传统”，全程没有讲“研究具体需求”。这是把一个看似合理的商务套话强加进来，原文未提及。
D) 偷换概念Adopt the right business strategies.（采取正确的商业策略）是个很笼统的大词，看似稳妥。但讲者明确给的建议是“尊重对方传统方法”这一具体点，而非泛泛的“正确策略”；用一个更大更空的概念把原文的具体主张换掉了。
questions.quote: It is only polite for us to do the same when we visit them. It is not only polite. It is essential if we want to sell British products overseas.

options.text: Respect their traditional culture.
Attend their business seminars.
Research their specific demands.
Adopt the right business strategies.

questions.prompt: What must you avoid doing with your Indian colleague?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） Drinking alcohol on certain days of a month.
**题目译文**
与你的印度同事交往时必须避免做什么?
A) 向他们展示你的手掌。
B) 赠送他们贵重的礼物。
C) 在一个月中的某些日子饮酒。
D) 在他们面前大声打响指。
**定位** 那么第一题，在印度，每月的一号和七号你绝不能喝酒。
**信号** 禁止语气 must not + 国家名 India 双重信号。这句同时出现 you must not drink alcohol 的强禁止语气和定位锚 in India，问“必须避免做什么 + 印度同事”，正好对上must not 和 India 两个信号，定位非常稳。
**替换** drink alcohol on the first and seventh of the month↔Drinking alcohol on certain days of a month the first and seventh 概括成 certain days
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 张冠李戴Showing them your palm. 里的“手掌 palm”来自录音讲泰国如何叫服务员那段：Place your palm downward and make an inconspicuous waving gesture。那是泰国的“正确做法”，不是印度的禁忌，被搬到印度题里张冠李戴。借用原文： Place your palm downward and make an inconspicuous waving gesture
B) 张冠李戴Giving them gifts of great value. 里的“贵重礼物”取自讲阿拉伯国家那段 presenting him with a gift of equal worth and beauty。那是阿拉伯礼俗，且并非“必须避免”，被错挂到印度同事头上。借用原文： presenting him with a gift of equal worth and beauty
D) 张冠李戴Clicking your fingers loudly in their presence. 来自泰国段 In Thailand, clicking the fingers, clapping your hands, or just shouting "Waiter!", will embarrass your hosts。这是泰国叫服务员的禁忌，不是印度同事的禁忌，国家对错了。借用原文： In Thailand, clicking the fingers, clapping your hands, or just shouting "Waiter!", will embarrass your hosts
questions.quote: So No. 1, you must not drink alcohol on the first and seventh of the month in India.

options.text: Showing them your palm.
Giving them gifts of great value.
Drinking alcohol on certain days of a month.
Clicking your fingers loudly in their presence.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about some Spanish business people?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） They have a break from 2:00 to 5:30 p.m.
**题目译文**
关于一些西班牙商人我们了解到什么?
A) 他们很容易满足。
B) 他们有很强的自我价值感。
C) 他们往往友好而热情。
D) 他们下午2点到5点半休息。
**定位** 最后，在西班牙，有些企业保持这样的作息：工作到大约两点，然后从下午五点半再回办公室，一直工作到晚上八点、九点或十点。
**信号** 国家名 Spain + 数字时间是定位与答案信号。in Spain 是定位锚，紧跟的数字 working until about 2 o'clock and then returning to the office from 5:30 是答案承载点——听到国家名加一串时间数字，就是本题的落点。
**替换** working until about 2 o'clock and then returning to the office from 5:30 ↔They have a break from 2:00 to 5:30 p.m. “干到2点、5点半再回”推出“2点到5点半休息”
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及They are very easy to satisfy.（很容易满足）录音里关于西班牙人压根没说过，属于自己脑补的性格评价，原文只讲了作息时间，没有任何关于“是否容易满足”的内容。
B) 原词陷阱They have a strong sense of worth. 里的“worth（价值）”呼应的是阿拉伯段 a gift of equal worth and beauty 中的 worth，被移植成对西班牙人的性格判断。原文讲西班牙只说了作息，没有这种评价。借用原文： a gift of equal worth and beauty
C) 张冠李戴They tend to be friendly and enthusiastic.（友好热情）对应的是录音讲阿拉伯人那段the politeness and generosity of the people are without parallel。这是阿拉伯人的特点，被张冠李戴给了西班牙人。借用原文： the politeness and generosity of the people are without parallel
questions.quote: And finally, in Spain, some businesses maintain the pattern of working until about 2 o'clock and then returning to the office from 5:30 to 8:00, 9:00 or 10:00 in the evening.

options.text: They are very easy to satisfy.
They have a strong sense of worth.
They tend to be friendly and enthusiastic.
They have a break from 2:00 to 5:30 p.m.
