questions.prompt: What does the speaker do?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） He is a sociologist.
**题目译文**
说话者是做什么的?
A) 他是一位政治家。
B) 他是一位商人。
C) 他是一位社会学家。
D) 他是一位经济学家。
**定位** （贫困）不仅关乎我们这些社会学家，也关乎经济学家、政治家和商人。
**信号** us+职业的自我归类。关键信号是 us sociologists 里的 us（我们）——说话人用“我们社会学家“把自己算进 sociologists 这一类，这就是自我定位。后面 economists, politicians and business people 用 also（也）领出，是“别人”，不是说话人自己。
**替换** us sociologists↔ He is a sociologist. us+职业=本人即该职业
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱He is a politician. 盗用了录音里念到的 politicians，但那是用 also 领出的“也关乎的对象”，是别人，不是说话人本人，听到 politicians 就选即中陷阱。借用原文： economists, politicians and business people
B) 原词陷阱He is a businessman. 对应录音 business people，同样是 also 后面列举的“也关心此事的人”，并非说话人自指。借用原文： also economists, politicians and business people
D) 原词陷阱He is an economist. 是最迷惑的——economists 紧跟在 also 之后第一个被念到（but also economists），与社会学家是研究相近领域的近邻，容易混；但它前面是 also，仍属“也关乎的对象”，说话人本人是 us sociologists。借用原文： but also economists
questions.quote: It concerns not only us sociologists, but also economists, politicians and business people.

options.text: He is a politician.
He is a businessman.
He is a sociologist.
He is an economist.

questions.prompt: Where does the speaker say we can find extreme poverty?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） In developing countries.
**题目译文**
说话者说我们在哪里可以发现极端贫困?
A) 在贫民窟。
B) 在非洲。
C) 在前工业社会。
D) 在发展中国家。
**定位** 极端贫困发生在哪里？嗯，你只能在发展中国家找到它。
**信号** 自问自答+occur/find in。录音先自抛设问 Where does extreme poverty occur?，紧接着自答 you can find it only in developing countries——设问句后的那句应答就是答案句，地点触发词 find it … in 后面紧跟的地名即为落点。
**替换** in developing countries↔In developing countries.原词直接复现
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及In slums.（贫民窟）听上去与“贫困“语义相关，很容易凭常识脑补，但录音讲极端贫困地点时只说 developing countries，从未出现 slums 一词，属考生用常识替代文本。
B) 未提及In Africa. 同样未在录音中出现。考生易把“极端贫困“与非洲挂钩，但这是背景常识，不是录音内容，全篇没念 Africa。
C) 未提及In pre-industrial societies.（前工业社会）是个像模像样的学术说法，但录音通篇没说极端贫困发生在前工业社会，属凭“听着专业“误选。
questions.quote: Where does extreme poverty occur? Well, you can find it only in developing countries.

options.text: In slums.
In Africa.
In pre-industrial societies.
In developing countries.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about American people living in relative poverty?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） Their income is less than 50% of the national average family income.
**题目译文**
关于生活在相对贫困中的美国人,我们了解到什么?
A) 他们无法获得医疗保健,更不用说娱乐或休闲了。
B) 他们的收入低于全国平均家庭收入的50%。
C) 他们需要加班工作来满足基本需求。
D) 他们的孩子上不起私立学校。
**定位** 例如，在美国，如果一个家庭的收入低于全国家庭平均收入的50%，就可以被视为贫困。
**信号** 美国举例+50%数字。信号有二：一是 in the United States 正好点中题干限定的“美国”；二是数字 50% 出现（less than 50% of the national average family income）——预读时已标星的数字落点在此兑现，数字句几乎必是答案句。
**替换** their income is less than 50% of the national average family income↔Their income is less than 50% of the national average family income.原句几乎逐字搬入选项
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱They have no access to health care, let alone entertainment or recreation. 重组了本段后文 they lack access to cultural guts, entertainment and recreation 与 do not have access to quality health care 的原词，确实在讲相对贫困者，但题目问的是“我们了解到什么“中与判定标准对应的那条，A 偷换了状况侧面，且把“缺乏优质医疗“夸大成“完全没有医疗”。借用原文： they lack access to cultural guts, entertainment and recreation. They also do not have access to quality health care
C) 张冠李戴They work extra hours to have their basic needs met. 听着像贫困者的常态，但录音讲相对贫困者从未提“加班才够基本需求”；basic needs 一词是前文讲极端、中度贫困时反复用的（cannot meet basic needs、basic needs are met），被挪来安到美国相对贫困者头上，属张冠李戴。借用原文： basic needs are met but barely
D) 未提及Their children cannot afford to go to private schools. 里的 private schools 全篇没出现；录音讲极端贫困时说 cannot afford education for their children，考生可能把“供不起教育“脑补成“上不起私校”，属无中生有式过度具体化。借用原文： They cannot afford education for their children.
questions.quote: For example, in the United States, a family can be considered poor if their income is less than 50% of the national average family income.

transcriptTranslations: Ishiguro先生,您有没有在二手书店发现过自己的书?
有的。那种情况挺难受的。如果他们那儿有我的书,我会想,"哎呀,这真是侮辱!有人不想留着我的书!"但如果没有,我也觉得受到了侮辱。我会想,"为什么没人转卖我的书?为什么这家店里没有?"
当作家需要脸皮厚吗?
是的,比如说,我妻子有时会非常严厉。我在2004年开始写最新的书《被掩埋的巨人》,但在我给妻子看了一小部分后就停笔了。她觉得那部分写得很糟糕。
即使在您获得布克奖之后?
她完全不怕我,批评我的方式跟我刚开始写作、还没出版时一模一样。
但您绝不会在自己的构想上妥协。
不,我绝不会在本质的东西上妥协,比如想法或主题。这其实不是我妻子想批评我的地方。她总是针对执行层面。
那您为什么把《被掩埋的巨人》搁置了那么久?显然您十多年前就开始写了。
我经常会停下一本书的写作,放上几年。等我回过头来时,它可能已经变了。通常我的想象力已经转移了,我能想到不同的背景或不同的处理方式。
当您终于完成一本书时是什么感觉?
你这么问挺有意思的,因为我从来没有过那种"啊,我完成了!"的时刻。你知道,我看足球运动员比赛结束时,哨声一响,他们赢了或输了。在那之前他们倾尽全力,而在那一刻他们知道结束了。对作家来说很有意思。永远不会有终场哨声。
根据一项关于教育中的种族与平等的研究，全国各地的黑人运动员正以惊人的速度从大学退学。今天和我们一起讨论这项研究结果的是《华盛顿邮报》专栏作家Kevin Blackstone。早上好!
早上好。你好吗?
很好,谢谢。你在这项研究中发现了什么新内容?
嗯,这是Shaun Harper的研究。他指出,在全国各大学校园里,黑人男性占本科生入学人数的比例不到3%。然而,当你看他们在创收型运动队——橄榄球队和篮球队——中的人数或百分比时,他们占到了这些队伍的50%到60%。所以问题是,他们实际上是作为校园里创收型运动员工人阶级的一部分存在,而不一定是像其他群体的大多数学生那样作为受教育阶级的一部分。
与其他群体相比,我想这个群体在那65所学校的数据是,黑人男性运动员的毕业率只有刚过一半。
没错。这件事真正糟糕的地方在于,这些运动员理应至少得到一样东西,作为他们所有血汗的回报。那就是大学学位,当你谈到向上流动时,这在我们社会中可以是一个改变命运的工具。这才是这件事真正令人不安的部分。
嗯,这个问题近年来真的被讨论得太多了。为什么还没有改变呢?
嗯,我认为它没有改变的原因之一是因为真的没有经济压力来改变这一点。所有的激励机制实际上都在于场上或球场上的输赢。教练们不一定有让球员毕业的激励。

questions.prompt: How would the man feel if he found his book in a second-hand bookstore?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （态度观点题） He would feel insulted.
**题目译文**
如果这个男人在二手书店发现了自己的书,他会有什么感受?
A) 他会感到被侮辱。
B) 他会感到非常难过。
C) 他会感到尴尬。
D) 他会感到失望。
**定位** 如果他们那儿有我的书，我会想："嗯，这是一种侮辱！有人不想留着我的书！"
**信号** 被问者的直接应答。女主持问到二手书店见到自己的书，男方（被采访者）开口应答 this is an insult，被问者的这句直接回应就是答案落点，听力对话题的答案几乎总在被问的那个人嘴里。
**替换** this is an insult↔He would feel insulted.名词转形容词
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) He would feel very sad. 听上去是合理的负面情绪，但录音里他说的是 this is an insult（被侮辱），从未提到 sad，是把"被侮辱"想当然换成了"悲伤"。C) He would be embarrassed. 的"尴尬"看似贴合"在二手店见到自己的书"的场景，但录音里他给的反应是 insult 而非 embarrassed，原文并无此情绪。D) He would be disappointed. 的"失望"同样是另起的情绪，录音中他的反应是被侮辱（insult），并未说失望，属于另换情绪的干扰。
questions.quote: If they've got my book there, I think, "Well, this is an insult! Somebody didn't want to keep my book!"

options.text: He would feel insulted.
He would feel very sad.
He would be embarrassed.
He would be disappointed.

questions.prompt: What does the man's wife think of his books?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （态度观点题） They need improvement.
**题目译文**
这个男人的妻子如何看待他的书?
A) 它们值得获奖。
B) 它们没什么价值。
C) 它们适合阅读。
D) 它们需要改进。
**定位** 我2004年开始写我最新的书《被掩埋的巨人》，但给妻子看了一小段后就停下了。她觉得那是垃圾。
**信号** 妻子的评价用词。男方转述妻子的看法时落在 She thought it was rubbish，rubbish 是带强烈贬义的评价词，这种评判性用词就是"问看法"题的答案信号。
**替换** She thought it was rubbish↔They need improvement.贬义概括为需改进
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) They are worthy of a prize. 是高度肯定，与妻子 rubbish 的强烈否定恰好相反；题中虽提到 Booker Prize，但那是他获过奖、并非妻子认为书"配得奖"，属把否定听成肯定。借用原文： She thought it was rubbish B) They are of little value.（几乎没价值）方向虽是贬义，但等于全盘否定整本书的价值；妻子批评的其实只是 It's always about execution.（写法、执行），并非说书毫无价值，程度被夸大。借用原文： It's always about execution. C) They make good reading.（很好读、好看）是正面评价，与妻子说的 rubbish 完全相反，是把否定评价反向理解。借用原文： She thought it was rubbish
questions.quote: I began working on my latest book, The Buried Giant, in 2004 but I stopped after I showed my wife a little section. She thought it was rubbish.

options.text: They are worthy of a prize.
They are of little value.
They make good reading.
They need improvement.

questions.prompt: What does the man do when he engages in writing?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） He seldom writes a book straight through.
**题目译文**
这个男人在写作时会做什么?
A) 他很少从头到尾一气呵成地写完一本书。
B) 他同时写好几本书。
C) 他借鉴自己的真实生活经历。
D) 他经常向妻子寻求帮助。
**定位** 我常常会停下一本书的写作，把它搁置好几年。等我再回头去写时，它可能已经变了。
**信号** 频率词 often 领出习惯。他用 I've often stopped writing a book and left it for a few years，频率词 often＋"停笔搁置几年"直接交代了写作习惯，这种描述常态做法的句子就是本题答案句。
**替换** I've often stopped writing a book and left it for a few years↔He seldom writes a book straight through.肯否转换说同一事
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) He writes several books simultaneously. 像是对"停一本写别的"的合理联想，但录音只说他停下一本、搁置几年再回来 left it for a few years，从没说同时写好几本，是凭印象多推一步。借用原文： left it for a few years C) He draws on his real-life experiences. 听起来很像作家常态，但录音里他谈的是"停笔、搁置、回来再改"的流程，全程没提从真实生活取材，属未提及。
D) 原词陷阱He often turns to his wife for help. 盗用了前文 my wife 这个原词，但妻子在文中是批评他写法（rubbish）的人，不是他写作时求助的对象，把"妻子批评"偷换成"向妻子求助"。借用原文： I showed my wife a little section
questions.quote: I've often stopped writing a book and left it for a few years. And by the time I come back to it, it may have changed.

He writes several books simultaneously.
He draws on his real-life experiences.
He often turns to his wife for help.

questions.prompt: What does the man want to say by mentioning the football match?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （推断题） Unlike a football match, there is no end to writing a book.
**题目译文**
这个男人提到足球比赛想要表达什么?
A) 写书就像看足球比赛。
B) 作家实际上和足球运动员一样努力工作。
C) 他喜欢在完成一本书后看足球比赛。
D) 与足球比赛不同,写书没有尽头。
**定位** 我看球员在比赛结束时……那一刻他们知道结束了。对作家来说就很奇怪。（写作）从来没有一声终场哨。
**信号** 对比后的落脚句。他先讲球员有终场哨、知道比赛结束，随即用 It's funny for an author. There's never a finishing whistle. 把话锋转到作家身上——这句对比后的落脚句才是他真正想说的，是答案信号。
**替换** There's never a finishing whistle↔Unlike a football match, there is no end to writing a book.形象说法转直白It's funny for an author↔ Unlike a football match对比关系对位
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) Writing a book is just like watching a football match. 盗用了 football match 原词，但他的本意恰是"写书与球赛不同"（没有终场哨），说成"就像看球赛"把对比关系弄反了。借用原文： It's funny for an author B) Writers actually work every bit as hard as footballers. 借了 footballers 原词，并把话题引到"作家和球员一样辛苦"；但他对比的是"有没有终点"，根本没谈谁更辛苦，属另起话题。借用原文： I watch footballers at the end of the match C) He likes watching a football match after finishing a book. 盗用 watch／football match 原词，编出"写完书爱看球"的个人爱好；录音里 watch footballers 只是打比方，他并未表达"完书后喜欢看球"。借用原文： I watch footballers at the end of the match
questions.quote: I watch footballers at the end of the match... at that moment they know it's over. It's funny for an author. There's never a finishing whistle.

questions.prompt: What is the new finding about black male athletes in this study?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） They make money for the college but often fail to earn a degree.
**题目译文**
这项研究关于黑人男性运动员的新发现是什么?
A) 他们在各种比赛中都展现出极大的天赋。
B) 他们更擅长体育运动而非学业。
C) 他们难以找到完成学业的资金。
D) 他们为大学赚钱,但往往无法获得学位。
**定位** 然而，看他们在足球、篮球这些创收球队上的人数或比例，却高达那些球队的 50-60%。所以这个意思是，他们其实是被当作校园里创收的「劳动者」运动员，而不一定是像其他多数学生那样属于受教育的群体。
**信号** 转折 Yet 后是落点。被问方先说招生占比不到 3%，紧接一个转折信号 Yet，转折之后才是研究的真正发现——他们在创收球队占 50-60%、是来「挣钱」而非「受教育」的。转折后那部分才是答案落点。
**替换** revenue-generating sports teams↔ make money for the college术语转大白话not necessarily there to be part of the educating class↔often fail to earn a degree含蓄表达转明确结果
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及display great talent in every kind of game（在每种比赛都极有天赋）录音从未说，原文只提足球、篮球两类创收项目，every kind（每种）属夸大杜撰。
B) 偷换概念better at sports than at academic work（更擅长运动而非学业）是常识刻板印象，但录音说的是制度把他们当「劳动者」用、没给他们受教育机会，并非他们「学习能力差」，归因被偷换。
C) 原词陷阱difficulty finding money to complete their studies（凑不出钱读完）借了录音的「钱」氛围（revenue、money）制造耳熟，但录音从没说他们缺钱读书，恰恰相反——是他们替学校挣钱。盗词却把因果方向弄反。借用原文： revenue-generating working class of athletes

So the idea is that they are really there to be part of the revenue-generating working class of athletes on campus and not necessarily there to be part of the educating class.

questions.prompt: What is the graduation rate of black male athletes?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） Slightly over 50%.
**题目译文**
黑人男性运动员的毕业率是多少?
A) 大约15%。
B) 大约40%左右。
C) 略高于50%。
D) 大约70%。
**定位** 和其他群体相比，我觉得这个群体在那 65 所学校的数字大概是——只有勉强过半的黑人男运动员最终能毕业。
**信号** graduate 旁的比例词。答案数字不是直接念出百分号，而是用文字描述 just barely more than half ... graduate（勉强过半才毕业）。锁定的信号是「比例词紧贴 graduate（毕业）」——题干问毕业率，就抓 graduate 旁边那个量。
**替换** just barely more than half↔Slightly over 50%文字比例转百分数
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 答非所问About 15% 没有原文依据，是用一个偏小的数迷惑；录音里偏小的数是 less than 3 percent（招生占比），但那不是毕业率，A 既非原数也非所问。
B) 与原文相反Around 40% 把「勉强过半」往下挪到四成，just barely more than half 明确是「过半」，40% 是没过半，与原文程度不符。借用原文： barely more than half
D) 原词陷阱Approximately 70% 把毕业率抬到七成，与「勉强过半」相差甚远；录音里偏高的数是50-60 percent（球队占比），D 既非该数也答非所问。借用原文： 50-60 percent of those teams
questions.quote: Compared with other groups, I think the numbers in this group at those 65 schools are something like just barely more than half of the black male athletes graduate at all.

options.text: About 15%.
Around 40%.
Slightly over 50%.
Approximately 70%.

questions.prompt: What accounts for black athletes' failure to obtain a college degree according to the man?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） Coaches lack the incentive to graduate them.
**题目译文**
根据该男士的说法,黑人运动员未能获得大学学位的原因是什么?
A) 教练缺乏让他们毕业的动力。
B) 大学学位对他们来说不太重要。
C) 他们对学业没有什么兴趣。
D) 学校不认为这是一个严重的问题。
**定位** 嗯，我觉得它之所以没改变，原因之一是确实没有经济上的压力去改变它。所有的激励都在赛场上赢球、别输球，教练并不一定有让球员毕业的动力。
**信号** one of the reasons...because。男士回答 why 时连用因果信号 one of the reasons it hasn't changed is because，明确引出原因；其后 Coaches do not necessarily have the incentive to graduate players 把责任落到「教练缺乏让球员毕业的动力」上，这是答案落点。
**替换** Coaches do not necessarily have the incentive to graduate players↔Coaches lack the incentive to graduate them近乎原句的同义改写
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 与原文相反College degrees do not count much to them（学位对他们不值钱）录音从未说；男士恰恰强调学位是 a transformative tool（能改变命运的工具），即学位很重要，与 B 相反。借用原文： a college degree, which can be a transformative tool
C) 偷换概念They have little interest in academic work（学生对学业没兴趣）是最符合刻板印象、最易误选的项，但男士给的原因是「制度上没有经济压力、教练没动力」，归因在制度/教练，不在学生主观意愿。
D) 张冠李戴Schools do not deem it a serious problem（学校不当回事）盗用了录音 economic pressure、incentive 的「制度」氛围，但男士把责任明确落在 coaches（教练），不是schools（学校），把对象换了人。借用原文： Coaches do not necessarily have the incentive to graduate players
questions.quote: Well, I think one of the reasons it hasn't changed is because there is really no economic pressure to change this. All of the incentive is really on winning and not losing on the field or on the court. Coaches do not necessarily have the incentive to graduate players.

options.text: Coaches lack the incentive to graduate them.
College degrees do not count much to them.
They have little interest in academic work.
Schools do not deem it a serious problem.

transcriptTranslations: 嗯，我目前的研究主要是关于消费者行为的。所以最近我研究了年轻人的饮酒问题，这显然是政府目前非常关注的问题。我还研究了老年人在媒体中是如何被呈现的。同样，随着老年人在英国乃至世界社会中所占比例越来越大，这也是当前的重大关注点。我还对消费者如何在线上运作以及这种线上行为与他们去商店时的线下行为有何不同感兴趣。
嗯，我认为这里重要的是要真正从消费者的角度理解正在发生的事情。企业乃至政府组织经常做不到的一件事就是真正从消费者的角度看待正在发生的事情。例如，在年轻人饮酒的案例中，我发现的一点是，对于18到24岁之间的人来说，饮酒完全是关于社交活动的。很多政府广告都是关于个人责任的，但实际上理解饮酒在很大程度上是关于社交活动，并找到帮助年轻人安全回家而不是最终住院的方法，是我们试图在那里提出的事情之一。

关于消费者行为的关键在于它很大程度上是关于消费者如何变化的。市场总是比营销变化得更快，所以我们必须关注消费者在做什么。目前我给二年级本科生教授消费者行为，我们研究消费者行为的各个方面，特别是消费者在广告中是如何被呈现的。所以他们通过观察广告参与进来，真正批判性地评估其中的消费者行为方面，并参与其中，有时还进行初级研究。例如，去年我的学生花了一周时间观察他们自己的购买行为，并从购物到他们与零售银行和移动电话供应商的关系进行详细分析。我认为他们发现这非常有用，这也帮助他们确定了自己有什么样的预算。事实是，那里有一系列有趣的研究。而且我认为随着时间的推移，我们将有更多的东西需要考虑，当然学生也将有更多的东西可以参与其中。
瑞典是第一个印刷和使用纸币的欧洲国家,但它可能很快就会废除实物货币。银行通过转向无现金系统可以节省大量资金并避免监管方面的麻烦,还可以避免银行抢劫、盗窃和脏钱。
《金融时报》Money版块的编辑Claer Barrett表示,西方世界正在走向一个没有实物货币的世界。英格兰银行首席经济学家Andy Holder建议英国转向政府支持的数字货币。但无现金社会真的具有良好的经济意义吗?"现金从社会中被抽离这一事实,与其说是我们日常生活的特征,不如说是电子支付的便利性。这实际上是否让我们在不知不觉中花了更多的钱?"
Barrett想要弄清楚实物货币的缺失是否确实会导致一个人花更多的钱,所以她决定在几个月前进行一项实验。她决定尝试在两周内只使用现金来进行所有必要的购物,看看这会对她的消费产生什么影响。她发现自己确实花的钱少得多,因为很难预测自己需要多少现金——她不停地从取款机取钱。几个月后,她仍然在裤子口袋和手提包的口袋里发现塞着的现金。
在实验期间,Barrett乘坐了一次火车。途中,有一则广播通知餐车目前不接受信用卡支付。车厢里充满了抱怨声,因为许多乘客出行时没有携带现金。
"这恰恰说明了上一代人以来事情发生了多大的变化,"Barrett说。我的父母年轻的时候,习惯通过把钱放进信封来做预算——他们拿到工资后会立即把现金分成几堆并放进信封里,这样他们就知道每周有多少钱可以花。这对他们来说是一种非常有效的记账方式。
如今,我们都在使用信用卡,进行网上购物,钱某种程度上正在变成一种不那么实体化而更加虚拟的东西,我们无法真正掌握它。
为什么你应该考虑在大学修一门人口学课程?你将在婴儿潮一代步入退休和死亡的时代成长。你将面临人口老龄化带来的前所未有的问题。你会越来越多地听到关于国家之间、农村地区与城市之间人口迁移的讨论。作为公民、纳税人和选民,你需要理解这些争论背后的真相。

我想告诉你们人类人口的过去、现在和未来,那么让我们从几个问题开始。现在,有十亿人长期处于饥饿状态。这意味着他们醒来时饿着,一整天都饿着,睡觉时也饿着。有十亿人生活在贫民窟,不是同一批十亿人,但有一些重叠。生活在贫民窟意味着他们没有基础设施来清运垃圾。他们没有安全的饮用水供应。近十亿人是文盲。试着想象你的生活如果不识字会是什么样。你无法阅读超市里瓶子上的标签,如果你能去超市的话。这些文盲中有三分之二是女性,大约有2亿到2.5亿女性无法获得她们想要的生育控制手段,以便她们能够控制自己的生育能力。这不仅是发展中国家的问题;全球大约有一半的怀孕是非意愿的。所以这些都是人口问题的例子。

人口学为你提供了理解和解决这些问题的工具。它不仅研究人类人口,还研究非人类物种的种群,包括病毒,如流感,你肠道中的细菌,你吃的植物,你喜欢的或为你提供肉类的动物。人口学还包括对非生命物体的研究,如灯泡、出租车和建筑物,因为这些也是种群。它使用定量数据和数学模型作为分析工具,研究这些种群的过去、现在和未来。我认为人口学是与经济学相关的核心学科。它是更明智、更有效地干预现实世界的手段,不仅改善你自己的福祉,尽管这可能很重要,而且改善你周围人的福祉以及与我们共享这个星球的其他物种的福祉。

**定位** 就青年饮酒而言，我所发现的一点是，对于大约 18 到 24 岁的人来说，饮酒完全是关于社交活动的。
**信号** I've identified 引出的发现判定句。录音用 one of the things that I've identified is that drinking … is all about the social activity 给出明确发现，identified 与题干 found 同义、is all about 是下定性的强判定结构，正是这句把饮酒定性为社交，是答案落点。
**替换** drinking for people, say, between the ages of 18 and 24 is all about the social activity↔It is an act of socialising. social activity 同义改写为 act of socialising
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及A 项 It is the cause of many street riots. 是凭『青年喝酒』的刻板印象联想出来的负面后果，录音里既没出现 riots，也从未说饮酒导致骚乱，属于录音根本没提的内容。
B) 张冠李戴B 项 It is a chief concern of parents. 借用了录音 a major concern to government 的concern 一词，却把担忧的主体由 government（政府）偷换成 parents（家长），主体一换就成了张冠李戴。借用原文： a major concern to government
C) 过度推断C 项 It is getting worse year by year. 是从『政府很担忧』过度推断出的恶化趋势，但录音只说它是 concern、是 social activity，从未说饮酒一年比一年严重，year by year 的趋势是录音没有的推断。
questions.quote: in the case of young people's drinking, one of the things that I've identified is that drinking for people, say, between the ages of 18 and 24 is all about the social activity.

options.text: It is the cause of many street riots.
It is a chief concern of parents.
It is getting worse year by year.
It is an act of socialising.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say that his students did last year?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） They spent a week studying their own purchasing behavior.
**题目译文**
说话者说他的学生去年做了什么?
A) 他们花了一周时间研究自己的购买行为。
B) 他们研究了手机对年轻人的影响。
C) 他们分析了多年来的家庭预算。
D) 他们对广告进行了彻底研究。
**定位** 去年我的学生们花了一周时间审视他们自己的购买行为，并从购物到他们与零售银行、手机运营商的关系，进行了详细分析。
**信号** last year 时间词直接对应题干。录音里 last year my students spent a week looking at their own purchasing 的 last year 与题干 last year 逐字对应，spent a week 又与某选项的 a week 呼应，是顺时间词即可锁定的答案句。
**替换** spent a week looking at their own purchasing↔They spent a week studying their own purchasing behavior. looking at 同义为 studying，purchasing 扩为 purchasing behavior
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱B 项 They researched the impact of mobile phones on young people. 借用了录音mobile phone providers 的 mobile phone 一词，但原文只是说学生分析自己购买行为时涉及与手机运营商的关系，并非研究『手机对青年的影响』，研究对象被偷换。借用原文： mobile phone providers
C) 原词陷阱C 项 They analysed their family budgets over the years. 拼用了录音里的 budgets 与years，但原文 helped them identify just what kind of budgets they had 说的是这次活动顺带帮学生看清自己的预算，并非『多年来分析家庭预算』，family、over the years 都是凑出来的。借用原文： helped them identify just what kind of budgets they had
D) 原词陷阱D 项 They conducted a thorough research on advertising. 借用了录音 how consumers are presented in advertising 的 advertising，但广告是说话人课堂教学讨论的内容，去年学生具体做的研究是审视自己的购买行为，把课堂内容当成学生去年所做的研究是张冠李戴。借用原文： how consumers are presented in advertising
questions.quote: last year my students spent a week looking at their own purchasing and analysed it in detail from shopping to the relationship that they have with their retail banks and their mobile phone providers.

options.text: They spent a week studying their own purchasing behavior.
They researched the impact of mobile phones on young people.
They analysed their family budgets over the years.
They conducted a thorough research on advertising.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about Sweden?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） It is likely to give up paper money in the near future.
**题目译文**
关于瑞典我们了解到什么？
A) 它正在帮助其银行提高效率。
B) 它正在努力消除脏钱。
C) 它是世界上第一个使用信用卡的国家。
D) 它很可能在不久的将来放弃纸币。
**定位** 瑞典是欧洲第一个印制并使用纸币的国家，但它可能很快就要废弃实体货币了。
**信号** 转折 but 后才是真意。这句以 but 把语义拐了向：前半 the first European country to print and use paper money 是背景铺垫，转折后的 it may soon do away with physical currencies 才是录音真正要点出的关于瑞典的现状，答案落在 but 之后。
**替换** it may soon do away with physical currencies↔It is likely to give up paper money in the near future. do away with = give up，soon = near future
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及录音讲银行好处时提到省钱、避监管，但没说瑞典在帮银行 improve efficiency，"提升效率"是把"省钱避麻烦"过度引申，原文未提。
B) 原词陷阱录音确实念到 dirty money，但那是说改用无现金系统能"避免"脏钱，并非说瑞典在"努力清除"脏钱，选项 trying hard to do away with dirty money 借这个原词制造"听到就想选"，实则答非所问。借用原文： they can also avoid bank robberies, theft, and dirty money
C) 与原文相反录音说瑞典是 the first European country to print and use paper money（第一个用纸币），选项 the first country to use credit cards 保留了 the first 这个最高级框架，却把paper money 换成 credit cards，并把范围从 European 扩成 in the world，与原文不符。借用原文： Sweden was the first European country to print and use paper money
questions.quote: Sweden was the first European country to print and use paper money, but it may soon do away with physical currencies.

options.text: It is helping its banks to improve efficiency.
It is trying hard to do away with dirty money.
It is the first country to use credit cards in the world.
It is likely to give up paper money in the near future.

questions.prompt: What did Claer Barrett want to find out with her experiment?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （目的题） Whether the absence of physical currency causes a person to spend more.
**题目译文**
Claer Barrett想通过她的实验弄清楚什么？
A) 不携带任何实物货币旅行是否可能。
B) 预测一个人将要花费多少钱是否可能。
C) 缺少实物货币是否会导致一个人花费更多。
D) 缺少实物货币是否会影响日常生活。
**定位** 巴雷特想弄清楚，没有实体货币是否真的会导致一个人花更多钱，于是几个月前她决定做一个实验。
**信号** find out if 后即验证目标。录音用 wanted to find out if 直接挑明实验目的，紧跟其后的the absence of physical currency does indeed cause a person to spend more 就是她要验证的命题，这是答案句的明确信号。
**替换** the absence of physical currency does indeed cause a person to spend more↔Whether the absence of physical currency causes a person to spend more.几乎同句，仅去掉 does indeed
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 答非所问选项 travel without carrying any physical currency 虽与火车那段"很多人没带现金"沾边，但那是实验过程中的插曲，并非她想"验证"的命题，答非所问。借用原文： many of the passengers were traveling without cash
B) 原词陷阱录音确实念到 hard to predict how much cash one is going to need，但那是实验的"结果/发现"，不是她一开始"想验证"的命题；选项 predict how much money one is going to spend 借 predict 这个原词把发现偷换成目的。借用原文： it is incredibly hard to predict how much cash one is going to need
D) 偷换概念录音里 less a feature of our everyday lives 出现过 everyday life，选项 affect everyday life 借此把验证目标放大成"是否影响日常生活"，比她实际要验证的"是否让人花更多"范围大得多。借用原文： less a feature of our everyday lives
questions.quote: Barrett wanted to find out if the absence of physical currency does indeed cause a person to spend more, so she decided to conduct an experiment a few months ago.

options.text: Whether it is possible to travel without carrying any physical currency.
Whether it is possible to predict how much money one is going to spend.
Whether the absence of physical currency causes a person to spend more.
Whether the absence of physical currency is going to affect everyday life.

questions.prompt: What did Claer Barrett find on her train ride?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） The restaurant car accepted cash only.
**题目译文**
Claer Barrett在火车上发现了什么？
A) 火车上没有餐饮服务。
B) 火车上的服务不好。
C) 餐车只接受现金。
D) 她手提包里的现金不见了。
**定位** 途中，广播通知说餐车目前不接受信用卡。车厢里一片抱怨声，因为许多乘客出行都没带现金。
**信号** announcement 引出关键事件。there was an announcement that 引出火车上发生的关键事件 the restaurant car was not currently accepting credit cards，后一句 because many of the passengers were traveling without cash 解释了为何引发抱怨，事件落点清晰。
**替换** the restaurant car was not currently accepting credit cards↔The restaurant car accepted cash only.不收信用卡 = 只收现金
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反录音说的是餐车 not currently accepting credit cards（只是不收卡），并非 no food service（没有餐食服务）；餐车照常营业，只是付款方式受限，与"没有餐食"相反。借用原文： the restaurant car was not currently accepting credit cards
B) 未提及录音只说餐车不收信用卡、乘客抱怨，没有评价 service on the train was not good（服务好不好）；抱怨是因为没带现金付不了，不是因为服务差。
D) 张冠李戴录音第 3 段提到她 still finding cash stuffed in her trouser pockets and the pockets of her handbags，handbag 与 cash 出现过，但说的是"手袋里还塞着现金"，并非 cash in her handbag was missing（手袋里的现金不见了），更不在火车那段。借用原文： she was still finding cash stuffed in her trouser pockets and the pockets of her handbags
questions.quote: On the way, there was an announcement that the restaurant car was not currently accepting credit cards. The train cars were filled with groans because many of the passengers were traveling without cash.

options.text: There was no food service on the train.
The service on the train was not good.
The restaurant car accepted cash only.
The cash in her handbag was missing.

questions.prompt: How did people of the last generation budget their spending?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） By putting money into envelopes.
**题目译文**
上一代人如何安排他们的开支预算？
A) 通过把钱放进信封里。
B) 通过每周取钱。
C) 通过限制他们的日常开支。
D) 通过拒绝赊账购买任何东西。
**定位** 我父母年轻时常常这样做预算：把钱放进信封里——一发工资就立刻把现金分成几摞放进信封，这样他们就知道每周该花多少。
**信号** budget by 后即方法动作。budget by putting money into envelopes 用 by 直接点出方法动作，是这道"问方式"题的答案信号；其后 put them in envelopes 进一步坐实"装信封"这一做法。
**替换** budget by putting money into envelopes↔ By putting money into envelopes.几乎原句保留
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱录音念到 they knew what they had to spend week by week，week by week 是"按周心里有数"的结果，并非 drawing money week by week（按周取钱）这个动作；选项借week by week 这个原词制造"听到就想选"，实则把方法说错了。借用原文： so they knew what they had to spend week by week
C) 过度推断装信封的结果是控制了花销，但录音的方法是"放进信封"，并非直接说 limiting their day- to-day spending（限制日常开支）这种笼统做法；这是把具体方法过度概括成一个泛泛说法。
D) 原词陷阱录音说上一代用信封管钱，contrast 的是 nowadays, we're all on credit cards（如今我们都刷信用卡），但并没有说他们"拒绝任何赊账"；refusing to buy anything on credit 是借 credit 这个原词凭空安给上一代的做法。借用原文： we're all on credit cards
questions.quote: My parents, when they were younger, used to budget by putting money into envelopes—they'd get paid and they'd immediately separate the cash into piles and put them in envelopes, so they knew what they had to spend week by week.

options.text: By putting money into envelopes.
By drawing money week by week.
By limiting their day-to-day spending.
By refusing to buy anything on credit.

questions.prompt: What is one of the problems the speaker mentions in his talk?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） Chronic hunger.
**题目译文**
演讲者在讲话中提到的问题之一是什么?
A) 人口爆炸。
B) 长期饥饿。
C) 珍稀物种灭绝。
D) 环境恶化。
**定位** 现在，有十亿人长期处于饥饿之中。这意味着他们醒来时是饿的、整天都是饿的、睡觉时还是饿的。
**信号** 举例罗列问题的首项。讲者用 so let's start with a few problems 开启问题清单，紧接着 a billion people are chronically hungry 就是罗列的第一个问题，这种以 start with / a few problems 引出的并列举例，每一项都是答案候选，chronically hungry 正是其中一项。
**替换** a billion people are chronically hungry ↔ Chronic hunger.形容词短语改名词短语
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱全篇主题是人口（population），考生易把 Population explosion.（人口爆炸）当成必然提到的问题，但录音从未说人口爆炸，讲的是 aging of the population（人口老龄化）和具体困境，A 属听到 population 就想选的原词陷阱。借用原文： the aging of the population
C) 原词陷阱Extinction of rare species.（珍稀物种灭绝）里 species 在第三段确实念到，但那是讲demography 也研究非人类物种，并非把物种灭绝列为问题；C 盗用 species 一词张冠李戴。借用原文： the populations of non-human species
D) 未提及Environmental deterioration.（环境恶化）是谈人口最容易联想到的问题，很合常识，但录音列举的问题是饥饿、贫民窟、文盲、意外怀孕，从未提环境恶化，属于凭常识脑补的未提及项。
questions.quote: Right now, a billion people are chronically hungry. That means they wake up hungry, they are hungry all day and they go to sleep hungry.

options.text: Population explosion.
Chronic hunger.
Extinction of rare species.
Environmental deterioration.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about pregnancies?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） About half of them are unintended.
**题目译文**
演讲者关于怀孕说了什么?
A) 它们导致人口过剩。
B) 约一半是意外怀孕。
C) 它们已得到控制。
D) 大多数往往会中途结束。
**定位** 这不仅仅是发展中国家的问题；全球大约一半的怀孕都是意外（非计划内）的。
**信号** 锚词 pregnancies 直接出现。答案句直接念出题目锚词 about half of all pregnancies globally are unintended，且带量化词 about half，正是预读时预备要记的比例数字，听到 pregnancies 配 half 即可锁定。
**替换** about half of all pregnancies globally are unintended↔About half of them are unintended.近乎同形＋代词替换
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 过度推断They contribute to overpopulation. 把意外怀孕推向导致人口过剩，是常识联想；录音只说一半怀孕是意外，从未说怀孕导致人口过剩，且 overpopulation 一词录音也没出现，属脑补的因果。
C) 与原文相反录音明说 This is not only a problem in developing countries，意思是问题没被局限、没被解决；They have been brought under control.（已被控制）与之相反，录音传达的恰是问题仍普遍存在。借用原文： This is not only a problem in developing countries
D) 偷换概念The majority of them tend to end halfway. 把 half（一半）偷换成 majority（大多数），又把 unintended（意外）换成 end halfway（半途结束），数字和论断都被改，录音没有半途结束这一说。
questions.quote: This is not only a problem in developing countries; about half of all pregnancies globally are unintended.

options.text: They contribute to overpopulation.
About half of them are unintended.
They have been brought under control.
The majority of them tend to end halfway.

questions.prompt: How does the speaker view the study of the populations?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （态度观点题） It is essential to the wellbeing of all species on earth.
**题目译文**
演讲者如何看待人口研究?
A) 它对地球上所有物种的福祉至关重要。
B) 它正成为跨学科研究的课题。
C) 它在许多发展中国家被忽视。
D) 它开始吸引研究生的关注。
**定位** 它（人口学）是更明智、更有效地干预现实世界的手段，用以增进福祉——不只是你自己的福祉（尽管那也很重要），还有你周围人的福祉，以及与我们共享这颗星球的其他物种的福祉。
**信号** 结尾总结定性句。讲者在末段以 I see demography as a central subject 起评，再用 to improve the well being … of other species with whom we share the planet 收束，这种 I see … as / the means to 的总结定性正是态度题的答案落点。
**替换** improve the well being not only of yourself … but of people around you and of other species with whom we share the planet↔ It is essential to the wellbeing of all species on earth.列举范围概括为 all species I see demography as a central subject↔ It is essential central 与 essential 同义定性
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱It is becoming a subject of interdisciplinary research. 借录音里 demography is …related to economics 的跨学科气息编出 interdisciplinary research，但讲者只说它与经济学相关，从未说它正成为一门跨学科研究的对象，是原词联想的拼凑。借用原文： a central subject related to economics
C) 张冠李戴developing countries 在第二段确实念到（not only a problem in developing countries），但那是讲意外怀孕，不是讲人口研究被忽视；neglected in many of the developing countries 把该地点词挪来安到研究头上，张冠李戴。借用原文： not only a problem in developing countries
D) 偷换概念录音开头讲 taking a course in demography in college，是劝大学生选修；It is beginning to attract postgraduates' attention. 把 college 学生悄悄换成postgraduates（研究生），且讲者问的是看法而非谁在关注，属偷换加未提及。借用原文： taking a course in demography in college
questions.quote: It is the means to intervene more wisely and more effectively in the real world to improve the well being not only of yourself, important as that may be, but of people around you and of other species with whom we share the planet.

options.text: It is essential to the wellbeing of all species on earth.
It is becoming a subject of interdisciplinary research.
It is neglected in many of the developing countries.
It is beginning to attract postgraduates' attention.

title: Section A 长对话

transcript.text: Section A. Directions: In this section, you will hear two long conversations. At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions. Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A), B), C) and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Welcome to Work Place, and in today's program we are looking at the results of two recently published surveys, which both deal with the same topic—happiness at work.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: John, tell us about the first survey.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: Well, this was done by a human resources consultancy who interviewed more than 1,000 workers and established a top 10 of the factors which make people happy at work.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: The most important factor, for the majority of the people interviewed, was having friendly, supportive colleagues.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: In fact, 73% people interviewed put their relationship with colleagues as the key factor contributing to happiness at work, which is a very high percentage.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: The second most important factor was having work that is enjoyable.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: The two least important factors were having one's achievements recognized and rather surprisingly, earning a competitive salary.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: So, we are not mainly motivated by money?
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: Apparently not.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: Any other interesting information in the survey?
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: Yes.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: For example, 25% of the working people interviewed described themselves as very happy at work.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: However, 20% of employees described themselves as being unhappy.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: That's quite a lot of unhappy people at work every day.
transcript.speaker: W

transcript.text: It is, isn't it?
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: And there were several more interesting conclusions revealed by the survey.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: First of all, small is beautiful.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: People definitely prefer working for smaller organizations or companies with less than 100 staff.
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: We also find out that, generally speaking, women were happier in their work than men.
transcript.speaker: M

transcriptTranslations: 欢迎收看《职场》节目,在今天的节目中,我们将关注最近发表的两项调查结果,这两项调查都涉及同一个话题——工作中的幸福感。John,跟我们说说第一项调查吧。
好的,这项调查是由一家人力资源咨询公司完成的,他们采访了1000多名员工,并确立了让人们在工作中感到幸福的十大因素。对大多数受访者来说,最重要的因素是拥有友好、supportive的同事。事实上,73%的受访者把与同事的关系作为促进工作幸福感的关键因素,这是一个非常高的百分比。第二重要的因素是拥有令人愉快的工作。最不重要的两个因素是成就得到认可,以及相当令人意外的是,获得有竞争力的薪水。
所以,我们主要不是被金钱所驱动的?
显然不是。
调查中还有其他有趣的信息吗?
有的。比如,25%的受访职场人士形容自己在工作中非常幸福。然而,20%的员工形容自己是不幸福的。
那就是说每天有相当多的人在工作中不开心。
确实是这样,不是吗?调查还揭示了其他几个有趣的结论。首先,小即是美。人们明显更喜欢为员工少于100人的小型组织或公司工作。我们还发现,总的来说,女性在工作中比男性更幸福。
是的,我们确实是,不是吗?
而且每天只工作4到5小时的兼职员工比全职员工更幸福。研究人员得出结论,这可能是因为工作与生活平衡得更好。
老板比他们的员工更幸福吗?
是的。也许并不令人意外,人们在公司中的职位越高,他们就越幸福。所以高级管理人员比他们手下的人更享受自己的工作。
De Keyzer先生，我非常喜欢您的书《洪水来临前的瞬间》。您能告诉我们您最初是如何对这个主题产生兴趣的吗？
2006年，Bruges市音乐厅邀请我为一个以水为主题的新音乐季目录拍摄一些照片，我发现自己在比利时海岸线工作。由于媒体上有大量关于气候灾难即将发生的警示文章，我开始以非常不同的方式看待大海和海滩——这个我童年时度过无数美好时光的地方。这种对迫在眉睫的危险的恐惧成为了一个大型摄影项目的主题。
您在书中写道"我不想拍摄灾难；我想拍摄即将发生的灾难。"您能谈谈这个吗？
现在很清楚，整个欧洲海岸线消失在水下只是时间问题。世界各地的许多大城市也是如此。我的想法是在为时已晚之前拍摄这条美丽而独特的、富有历史的海岸线——作为最后的见证者。
您能谈谈历史在这个项目中扮演的角色吗？
当然。这个项目也是关于欧洲历史的，看着大海，想着下一个敌人何时会出现。在这些影像中，你会看到各种可能的防御工事，用来抵挡罗马人、德国人、维京人，而现在大自然成了头号敌人。比如，有一张通向大海的桥的照片，拍摄于Normandy D-Day登陆地点。还有Venice，这座永远受到大海威胁的城市，每天早上都必须搭建木制通道，让游客能够到达他们的酒店。
谢谢您，De Keyzer先生。今天很高兴您能来到我们这里。

In this section, you will hear two long conversations. At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions. Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A), B), C) and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What is the number one factor that made employees happy according to the survey?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） Having friendly colleagues.
**题目译文**
根据调查，让员工感到快乐的首要因素是什么？
A) 做令人愉快的工作。
B) 拥有友好的同事。
C) 获得有竞争力的薪水。
D) 为支持自己的上司工作。
**定位** 对受访者中的大多数人来说，最重要的因素是拥有友好、给予支持的同事。
**信号** 最高级定第一。排序信号词 The most important factor（最重要的因素）直接点出"排第一"，紧跟其后的 having friendly, supportive colleagues 就是答案。听到 the most important 这类最高级，就锁定它后面带出的那个对象。
**替换** having friendly, supportive colleagues↔Having friendly colleagues.删修饰留同义
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱录音说 The second most important factor was having work that is enjoyable，Doing enjoyable work. 确被提到，但它是"第二重要"，题目问"第一"，盗用 enjoyable work 这个原词来骗"听到就选"。借用原文： The second most important factor was having work that is enjoyable
C) 与原文相反录音明说 The two least important factors were … earning a competitive salary，薪水是"最不重要"之一，选项 Earning a competitive salary. 却被摆来当"第一"，方向正好相反。借用原文： The two least important factors were having one's achievements recognized and rather surprisingly, earning a competitive salary
D) 张冠李戴排第一的是"同事"colleagues，Working for supportive bosses. 借用了原文 supportive这个词，却把对象从"同事"偷换成"老板"，是张冠李戴。借用原文： having friendly, supportive colleagues
questions.quote: The most important factor, for the majority of the people interviewed, was having friendly, supportive colleagues.

options.text: Doing enjoyable work.
Having friendly colleagues.
Earning a competitive salary.
Working for supportive bosses.

questions.prompt: What is the percentage of the people surveyed who felt unhappy at work?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） 20%.
**题目译文**
在接受调查的人中，感到工作不快乐的比例是多少？
A) 31%。
B) 20%。
C) 25%。
D) 73%。
**定位** 25% 的受访在职人员形容自己在工作中非常开心。然而，20% 的员工形容自己不开心。
**信号** 转折后接目标数据。转折词 However 把句子分成两半：前半 25% … very happy 说开心的人，后半 20% of employees … unhappy 才是"不开心"的人。题目问 unhappy，要取转折后的 20%。
**替换** 20% of employees described themselves as being unhappy↔ 20%.数字直接对应
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及 31% 在整段录音里根本没出现过，纯属凑数干扰，没有任何原文支撑。
C) 原词陷阱录音 25% … described themselves as very happy at work，25% 说的是"很开心"的人，25%. 盗用了这个真被念到的数字，却答非所问——题目问的是"不开心"的人。借用原文： 25% of the working people interviewed described themselves as very happy at work
D) 原词陷阱73% 来自第2段 73% people interviewed put their relationship with colleagues as the key factor，说的是把同事关系当首要因素的人，与"不开心"无关，是远处搬来的原词陷阱。借用原文： 73% people interviewed put their relationship with colleagues as the key factor
questions.quote: 25% of the working people interviewed described themselves as very happy at work. However, 20% of employees described themselves as being unhappy.

questions.prompt: What kind of companies are popular with employees?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） Those of a small size.
**题目译文**
什么样的公司受员工欢迎？
A) 规模较小的公司。
B) 由女性经营的公司。
C) 管理良好的公司。
D) 充满熟练工人的公司。
**定位** 首先，小即是美。人们明显更偏爱为规模较小的机构、或员工少于 100 人的公司工作。
**信号** 偏好词prefer点题。偏好信号 People definitely prefer working for smaller organizations 里的 prefer（更偏爱）直接点出受欢迎的类型是"较小的公司"，加重词definitely 进一步强调。听到 prefer 就锁定其后的特征。
**替换** smaller organizations or companies with less than 100 staff↔Those of a small size.具体数概括为小
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱录音确有 women were happier in their work than men，但说的是"女性比男性更开心"，并非"女性经营的公司受欢迎"。Those run by women. 盗用 women 这个词，偷换成了"公司由女性经营"。借用原文： women were happier in their work than men
C) 未提及"管理得好"听起来天然正确，但全段并未说员工偏爱管理好的公司，Those that are well managed. 是凭常识想当然、原文无据。
D) 未提及录音从未提到"员工技能高的公司"，Those full of skilled workers. 无任何原文支撑，属凭空编造。
questions.quote: First of all, small is beautiful. People definitely prefer working for smaller organizations or companies with less than 100 staff.

options.text: Those of a small size.
Those run by women.
Those that are well managed.
Those full of skilled workers.

questions.prompt: What is the possible reason for people on part-time contracts to be happier?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） They can better balance work and life.
**题目译文**
兼职合同员工更快乐的可能原因是什么？
A) 他们可以轻松地从一份工作跳到另一份工作。
B) 他们的工作能够获得认可。
C) 他们可以更好地平衡工作和生活。
D) 他们可以从事不止一份工作。
**定位** 而每天只工作 4 到 5 小时的兼职合同工，比全职工作的人更开心。研究者得出结论，这很可能是由于他们有更好的工作与生活平衡。
**信号** 因果due to给原因。因果信号 this is probably due to a better work-life balance 里的due to（由于）直接点出原因。题干的 possible reason 正对应原文的 probably due to，听到 due to 就锁定其后的内容为答案。
**替换** a better work-life balance↔They can better balance work and life.名词化转动词句
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及录音从没说兼职者"换工作容易"，They can hop from job to job easily. 是凭"兼职=灵活"的常识想象出来的，原文无据。
B) 原词陷阱"获得认可"对应的是第2段 having one's achievements recognized，且那里说它是最不重要的因素之一，与"兼职者为何更开心"毫不相干，是远处搬来的原词陷阱。借用原文： The two least important factors were having one's achievements recognized
D) 过度推断录音说的是兼职者每天 only work 4 or 5 hours a day（工时短），从未说他们"兼好几份工"。They can take on more than one job. 把"工时少"曲解成"工作多"，方向相反且原文无此意。借用原文： workers on part-time contracts who only work 4 or 5 hours a day
questions.quote: And workers on part-time contracts who only work 4 or 5 hours a day are happier than those who work full time. The researchers concluded that this is probably due to a better work- life balance.

options.text: They can hop from job to job easily.
They can win recognition of their work.
They can better balance work and life.
They can take on more than one job.

questions.prompt: What does the man say about the book Moments Before the Flood?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） It is a collection of photos.
**题目译文**
关于《洪水来临之前的时刻》这本书，男士说了什么?
A) 这是一本欧洲历史书。
B) 这是一本音乐入门书。
C) 这是关于布鲁日这座城市的。
D) 这是一本摄影集。
**定位** 这种对迫近危险的恐惧，成了一个大型摄影项目的主题。
**信号** 受访者给作品定性的句子。对话题答案在被问者的应答里。男士在介绍这本书来历时，用became the subject of a large-scale photo project 给作品做了归类——"摄影项目"这个定性就是答案信号，它直接回答了"这是一本什么书"。
**替换** photo project ↔ a collection of photos "摄影项目"="照片集"，同义概括
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱原文确实多次提到欧洲历史 rich in history，但那是说海岸"历史悠久"，并非说这本书是历史书；选项 a book of European history 拿"history"这个真听到的词来诱选，答非所问。借用原文： rich in history
B) 原词陷阱原文出现 the concert hall of the city of Bruges(音乐厅)、concert season，选项 an introduction to music 借"concert/音乐"这层听到的字眼诱你以为书与音乐有关，但音乐厅只是他接活拍照的地点，书本身与音乐无关。借用原文： the concert hall of the city of Bruges
C) 原词陷阱原文出现 the city of Bruges，选项 about the city of Bruges 直接搬这个地名诱选，但Bruges 只是邀请他拍照的城市，书的内容是海岸/海洋，并非"写布鲁日这座城"。借用原文： the city of Bruges
questions.quote: This fear of a looming danger became the subject of a large-scale photo project.

options.text: It is a book of European history.
It is an introduction to music.
It is about the city of Bruges.
It is a collection of photos.

questions.prompt: When did the man get his idea for the work?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） When taking pictures for a concert catalogue.
**题目译文**
男士是什么时候产生这部作品的想法的?
A) 在为布鲁日音乐厅绘画时。
B) 在意大利某个海滨城市度假时。
C) 在为一本音乐会目录拍照时。
D) 在撰写关于比利时海岸地区的文章时。
**定位** 2006年，布鲁日市的音乐厅请我为新一季以"水"为主题的音乐会目录拍一些照片，我于是来到比利时海岸沿线工作。
**信号** 时间状语 In 2006 + when…引出的事件。受访者用 In 2006, when the concert hall…asked me to take some pictures for a catalogue 这个明确的时间+事件状语，交代了想法萌芽的时刻——"为音乐会目录拍照"这件事，正是答案信号。
**替换** take some pictures for a catalogue for a new concert season↔taking pictures for a concert catalogue "为音乐会季目录拍照"="拍音乐会目录的照片"，详述↔概括
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱原文有 the concert hall of the city of Bruges，选项 When painting the concert hall of Bruges. 把这个真听到的"布鲁日音乐厅"搬来，却把动作偷换成 painting(绘画)——他做的是拍照不是画画，动作错了。借用原文： the concert hall of the city of Bruges
B) 未提及想法产生于2006年为音乐会目录拍照、沿比利时海岸工作时，原文从未说他在"意大利海滨城市度假"；选项 When vacationing in an Italian coastal city. 利用后文出现的意大利城市Venice 让人误以为想法起于那里，实则未提。
D) 原词陷阱原文是 working along the Belgian coastline(沿比利时海岸拍照工作)，选项 When writing about Belgium's coastal regions. 借"比利时海岸"这个真听到的地点，却把动作换成 writing(写作)——他是拍照不是写文章，且想法起于拍照那件事。借用原文： working along the Belgian coastline
questions.quote: In 2006, when the concert hall of the city of Bruges asked me to take some pictures for a catalogue for a new concert season around the theme of water, I found myself working along the Belgian coastline.

options.text: When painting the concert hall of Bruges.
When vacationing in an Italian coastal city.
When taking pictures for a concert catalogue.
When writing about Belgium's coastal regions.

questions.prompt: What will happen when the climate catastrophe occurs?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） The entire European coastline will be submerged.
**题目译文**
当气候灾难发生时会发生什么?
A) 整个欧洲海岸线都将被淹没。
B) 欧洲的丰富遗产将完全消失。
C) 欧洲的海水将受到严重污染。
D) 欧洲主要景点将会消失。
**定位** 现在已经很清楚，整条欧洲海岸线没入水下只是时间问题。
**信号** 断言式后果句 it's a matter of time before…。男士用 it's a matter of time before the entire European coastline disappears under water 这种"早晚会发生"的强断言，直接给出灾难后果——"整条欧洲海岸线没入水下"，这就是答案信号。
**替换** the entire European coastline disappears under water↔The entire European coastline will be submerged. "没入水下"="被淹没"，主被动+同义词替换
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 过度推断原文说海岸 rich in history(历史悠久)，选项 The rich heritage of Europe will be lost completely. 借"rich/history"这层听到的字眼，却把后果夸成"欧洲的丰富遗产将彻底丧失"——原文只说海岸线会被淹，没说"遗产完全消失"，completely 是过度推断。借用原文： rich in history
C) 未提及原文讲的是海岸线被海水淹没，选项 The seawater of Europe will be seriously polluted.借"sea/water"的听感联想到"海水污染"，但原文从头到尾说的是"淹没"不是"污染"，属无中生有。
D) 偷换概念原文是 the entire European coastline disappears under water(整条海岸线没入水下)，选项 The major European scenic spots will disappear. 借真听到的 disappear，却把范围从"整条海岸线"偷换成"主要景点"——范围被改小，主语对不上。借用原文： the entire European coastline disappears under water
questions.quote: It is clear now that it's a matter of time before the entire European coastline disappears under water.

options.text: The entire European coastline will be submerged.
The rich heritage of Europe will be lost completely.
The seawater of Europe will be seriously polluted.
The major European scenic spots will disappear.

questions.prompt: What does the man say about Venice?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） Tourists use wooden paths to reach their hotels in the morning.
**题目译文**
关于威尼斯，男士说了什么?

transcriptTranslations: 鸟类以携带物品而闻名。有些鸟类，如信鸽,可以被训练来传递信息和包裹。其他鸟类则会在不知情的情况下携带附着在它们身上搭便车的种子。
加拿大科学家发现了一个令人担忧的新例子,说明鸟类在传播物质方面具有强大的力量。在遥远的加拿大北极地区,海鸟正在海洋中捡拾危险化学物质,并将它们带到鸟类栖息地附近的池塘中。
约10,000对被称为管鼻鹱的鸟类(一种北极海鸟)在北极圈以北的Devon Island筑巢。管鼻鹱会飞越约400公里的海域寻找食物。当它们返回家园时,它们的粪便最终散落在筑巢地点周围,包括附近的池塘中。
此前,科学家注意到污染物随风到达北极地区。鲑鱼在河流和海洋之间洄游时也会携带危险化学物质。鱼类和其他肉食动物的体内可能会积累高浓度的化学物质。
为了测试管鼻鹱的污染能力,研究人员从Devon Island的11个池塘中采集了沉积物样本。结果显示,在距离鸟群最近的池塘中,污染物的含量远高于受鸟类影响较小的池塘。池塘中的污染物似乎来自管鼻鹱在海上觅食时吃的鱼类。
研究人员表示,在鸟类聚居地附近生活、狩猎或捕鱼的人需要小心。鸟类无意造成伤害,但它们携带的化学物质可能会造成重大问题。
近年来,美国百岁老人——年龄达到或超过100岁的人——的死亡率有所下降,从2008年到2014年,女性下降了14%,男性下降了20%。这个年龄组的主要死因也在发生变化。
2000年,百岁老人的前五大死因是心脏病、中风、流感、癌症和阿尔茨海默病。但到2014年,这个年龄组因阿尔茨海默病导致的死亡率增加了一倍多——从3.8%上升到8.5%——使这种进行性脑部疾病成为百岁老人的第二大死因。
这个群体中阿尔茨海默病死亡人数上升的一个原因可能是,即使人们战胜了死于癌症等其他疾病的可能性,患上这种疾病的风险仍然存在。身体足够强健能够存活超过100年的人,最终还是会屈服于阿尔茨海默病等影响思维和认知功能的疾病。换句话说,他们的大脑似乎比身体更早衰竭。
另一方面,流感的死亡率从2000年的7.4%下降到2014年的4.1%。这使流感从第三大死因降至第五位。
总体而言,百岁老人的总数在增加。2014年有72197名百岁老人,而2000年为50281名。但由于这一人口群体在扩大,该群体的死亡人数也在增加——2000年有18434名百岁老人死亡,而2014年有25914名死亡。

questions.explanation:

**题目译文**

A) 它们可以在紧急情况下被用来传递信息。

C) 它们携带植物种子并将其传播到遥远的地方。

**定位** 加拿大科学家发现了一个令人担忧的新例子，显示了鸟类四处散播东西的能力。在加拿大北极地区的最北端，海鸟正从海洋中沾取危险的化学物质，并把它们带到鸟类居住地附近的池塘里。
**信号** have found 后紧跟的应答句。题干问 found，录音 Canadian scientists have found 原样出现，紧跟其后的 seabirds are picking up dangerous chemicals in the ocean and delivering them to ponds 就是这个发现的具体内容，是承载答案的句子。
**替换** dangerous chemicals in the ocean ↔ pollutants from the ocean危险化学物=污染物delivering them to ponds near where the birds live ↔ to their nesting sites鸟居住地附近=筑巢地
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱选项 deliver messages 盗用了录音开头 can be trained to deliver messages and packages 的原词，但那只是引出话题的旧例子，不是加拿大科学家的新发现，答非所问。借用原文： can be trained to deliver messages and packages
C) 原词陷阱选项 carry plant seeds 盗用了 carry seeds that cling to them 的原词，同样是开头列举鸟会搬运的旧现象，不是本段讲的新发现，答非所问。借用原文： carry seeds that cling to them for the ride
D) 未提及选项说鸟因污染濒临灭绝，录音通篇只讲鸟搬运污染物，从没说鸟自身濒危或灭绝，属无中生有；预读时已警惕的极端词果然落空。
questions.quote: Canadian scientists have found a worrisome, new example of the power that birds have to spread stuff around. Way up north in the Canadian Arctic, seabirds are picking up dangerous chemicals in the ocean and delivering them to ponds near where the birds live.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about Alzheimer's disease?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） It is now the second leading cause of death for centenarians.
**题目译文**
说话者关于阿尔茨海默病说了什么?

B) 它现在是百岁老人的第二大死因。

questions.prompt: What is characteristic of people who live up to 100 years and beyond?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） Their minds fall before their bodies do.

活到100岁及以上的人有什么特点?

B) 他们的生活质量迅速恶化。

D) 他们比以往任何时候都更珍惜生命。
**定位** 身体硬朗到能活过100岁的人，最终还是会败给阿尔茨海默病这类影响心智和认知功能的疾病。换句话说，看起来他们的心智先于身体垮掉。
**信号** 总结提示语 In other words 引出点题句。In other words 是典型的换言归纳信号，它后面那句 their minds give out before their bodies do 是对前文的提炼，正是文章对百岁老人特征的结论。

questions.tip:

questions.prompt: What does Devils Tower look like?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） The stump of a giant tree.
**题目译文**
Devils Tower 看起来像什么?
A) 一棵巨树的树桩。
B) 一块巨大的岩石。
C) 一座山的山峰。
D) 一座高耸的烟囱。
**定位** 魔鬼塔，美国第一座国家纪念碑，几乎会被错看成一棵巨树的树桩。
**信号** “被错看成”即外形比喻信号。could almost be mistaken for（几乎会被错看成）是一个明确的“像什么”信号词，听到它后面紧跟的那个比喻对象，就是本题答案落点。
**替换** the stump of an enormous tree↔ The stump of a giant tree. enormous = giant 近义替换
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱录音确实多处出现 rock（如 the massive column of rock），B 的 A huge piece of rock.盗用了这个原词诱你“听到 rock 就选”；但题目问“看上去像什么”，原文给的比喻是“树桩”而非“一块巨石”，rock 只是它的材质而非它“像”的东西。借用原文： the massive column of rock
C) 偷换概念原文提到它矗立在平原之上、有 flat summit（平顶），让人联想到山，C 的 The peak of a mountain. 借“山峰/顶”的语境诱选；但原文从未说它“像一座山峰”，比喻对象明确是“树桩”。借用原文： the flat summit
D) 未提及A tall chimney.（高烟囱）这一比喻在原文中根本没有出现，纯属编造，虽然柱状高耸的形状会让人觉得“也挺像”，但听力以原文说了什么为准。
questions.quote: Devils Tower, the first national monument in America, could almost be mistaken for the stump of an enormous tree.

options.text: The stump of a giant tree.
A huge piece of rock.
The peak of a mountain.
A tall chimney.

questions.prompt: What caused the volcano's outer layers to wear away?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） Wind and water.
**题目译文**
是什么导致火山的外层被侵蚀掉?
A) 人类活动。
B) 风和水。
C) 化学过程。
D) 烈火与狂怒。
**定位** 魔鬼塔生于烈火与狂暴之中，随后被风与水缓慢而轻柔的作用所塑造。火山的外层逐渐被磨蚀殆尽，直到坚硬的内核完全裸露出来。
**信号** shaped by + worn away 的施动者。shaped by the slow, gentle work of wind and water 里的 shaped by 点出真正的施动力量；紧接着 The outer layers of the volcano were worn away 用被动语态说外层被磨蚀——“被…塑造/被磨蚀”的施动者就是答案信号。
**替换** wind and water↔ Wind and water.原词直接对应
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及Human activity.（人类活动）在原文里完全没有提到，魔鬼塔的塑造全是自然力量；这一项靠常识里“景观破坏常与人类有关”的联想骗选。
C) 偷换概念原文讲 the rock cooled and hardened（岩石冷却硬化）涉及物理变化，C 的 Chemical processes.（化学过程）借“岩石变化”语境偷换成“化学过程”；但磨蚀外层的是风与水的物理作用，非化学过程。借用原文： the rock cooled and hardened
D) 原词陷阱录音里 Born in fire and fury 确有 fire and fury 一词，D 的 Fire and fury. 原样盗用，诱你“听到就选”；但“烈火与狂暴”说的是它“诞生（born in）”时的力量，问的却是“外层被磨蚀”的原因，张冠李戴、答非所问。借用原文： Born in fire and fury
questions.quote: Born in fire and fury, Devils Tower was then shaped by the slow, gentle work of wind and water. The outer layers of the volcano were worn away, until the hard core stood completely exposed.

options.text: Human activity.
Wind and water.

Fire and fury.

questions.prompt: What does an Indian legend say about Devils Tower?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） It was created by supernatural powers.
**题目译文**
印第安传说对 Devils Tower 有何说法?
A) 它是一座历史纪念碑。
B) 它建于古代。
C) 它是印第安人崇拜的圣地。
D) 它是由超自然力量创造的。
**定位** 难怪一则印第安传说把魔鬼塔描述为由超自然力量所形成。
**信号** legend described…as 引出传说界定。an Indian legend described Devils Tower as being formed by supernatural powers 里的 legend described…as（传说把它描述为…）是明确的“传说怎么说”信号，as 后面的内容就是传说的界定，即答案落点。
**替换** being formed by supernatural powers↔ It was created by supernatural powers. formed = created 近义、被动同构
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱录音开头说它是 the first national monument in America，A 的 It is a historical monument. 盗用 monument 一词诱选；但 monument 是“国家纪念地”的官方身份，题目问的是“传说怎么说”，传说讲的是超自然力量，不是“历史纪念碑”。借用原文： the first national monument in America
B) 与原文相反It was built in ancient times.（古时人工建造）与传说“由超自然力量形成”相反——传说强调的恰是“非人力所及”，built（人建）正好反了向；它借“ancient/古老”的氛围诱选。借用原文： being formed by supernatural powers
C) 原词陷阱录音多次出现 Indian（如 an Indian legend），C 的 It is Indians' sacred place for worship. 盗用 Indian 诱选；但原文只说“印第安传说”提到它，从未说它是印第安人“供奉/朝拜的圣地”，sacred place for worship 属编造。借用原文： an Indian legend
questions.quote: Small wonder that an Indian legend described Devils Tower as being formed by supernatural powers.

options.text: It is a historical monument.

It was created by supernatural powers.

questions.prompt: How did the Rock God help the seven girls in the Indian legend?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） By lifting them well above the ground.
**题目译文**
在印第安传说中,岩石之神如何帮助那七个女孩?
A) 在洞穴中庇护她们。
B) 杀死袭击的熊。
C) 把她们举到远离地面的高处。
D) 把她们带到山顶。
**定位** 岩神让岩石长高，把女孩们高高托到地面之上，而岩石的侧面则被愤怒的熊用爪子抓出道道划痕。
**信号** caused the rock to…lift 的施救动作。The god caused the rock to grow and to lift the girls far above the ground 直接说出岩神所做的事——让岩石长高、把女孩托离地面，这句“岩神 + 动作”就是 How 题的答案落点。
**替换** lift the girls far above the ground↔ By lifting them well above the ground. lift…far/well above the ground 近义替换
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及By sheltering them in a cave.（把她们藏进山洞）在原文里没有出现，岩神是“让岩石长高托起她们”而非“藏入山洞”；这项靠“躲避熊”的常识联想骗选。

D) 偷换概念原文是让岩石长高、把女孩 lift the girls far above the ground（托到地面之上），D 的By taking them to the top of a mountain. 把它偷换成“带到山顶”；岩神是“就地把岩石升高”而非“带她们去某座山顶”，似是而非。借用原文： lift the girls far above the ground

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about extravagances?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （态度观点题） They can bring only temporary pleasures.
**题目译文**
说话者关于奢侈消费说了什么?
A) 它们只能带来短暂的快乐。
B) 它们是为极其富有的人准备的。
C) 应该彻底摒弃它们。
D) 它们最终可能会使人破产。
**定位** 遗憾的是，奢侈消费带来的快乐往往在账单还没还清之前就早早消失了。
**信号** 评价词 Sadly + 主语 pleasure…disappears。信号是句首带态度的副词 Sadly（遗憾地）加上正面评价奢侈消费的主句 the pleasure that comes from extravagances often disappears，这正是说话人对 extravagances 的定性句。
**替换** the pleasure that comes from extravagances often disappears long before the bills do↔bring only temporary pleasures快乐很快消失=只带短暂快乐
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 与原文相反选项 meant for the extremely wealthy 说奢侈只为极富者，但录音明说 hard-working men and women 这些普通辛劳者也会奢侈消费，与“只给富人”相反。借用原文： hard-working men and women C)选项 done away with altogether（应彻底取消）把话说过头，录音恰恰承认 They do deserve such indulgences（他们确实配享受这些），只是提醒别忘了更重要的东西，并没主张取消，属过度推断、与原文相反。借用原文： They do deserve such indulgences D)选项 drive one to bankruptcy 借预读就警惕过的极端词 bankruptcy 诱选，但录音只说快乐消失、账单难还（constant stress, tension, even fear about money），从未说会导致破产，是把后果夸大、过度推断。借用原文： constant stress, tension, even fear about money
questions.quote: Sadly, the pleasure that comes from extravagances often disappears long before the bills do.

They are meant for the extremely wealthy.
They should be done away with altogether.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker want to show by the example of the Chicago woman?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （推断题） Small daily savings can make a big difference in one's life.
**题目译文**
说话者想通过芝加哥女性的例子说明什么?
A) 社交的好方法是每天与同事共进午餐。
B) 退休储蓄应该是家庭预算的首要考虑。
C) 如果每周存20美元,度假就能负担得起。
D) 每天小额储蓄能对人的生活产生很大影响。
**定位** 比如一位芝加哥女士发现每天和同事在外吃午饭一年要花她两千美元，于是改成自己带饭；她说“现在我每周往度假基金里存二十美元，再往退休储蓄里存二十美元。”
**信号** for example 引例，例后承接全段主旨。信号是 for example 标明这是个例子，而它紧跟在全段主旨句 The solution—set priorities, add up the annual cost of each item 之后，是为印证“算清每项开销、攒小钱”这一主张而举，故例子意图要回到该主旨。
**替换** daily lunches with coworkers cost her $2000 a year↔Small daily savings每天省小钱累成一年大数put $20 a week into my vacation fund and another 20 into retirement savings↔make a big difference in one's life攒成度假与退休金即大不同
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱选项 have daily lunch with one's colleagues 把录音原词 daily lunches with coworkers直接搬来诱选，但她恰恰是“不再天天一起吃、改带饭”，选项却说成是好的社交方式，与原文相反。借用原文： daily lunches with coworkers
B) 原词陷阱选项 Retirement savings should come first 借录音原词 retirement savings 诱选，但例子只是把省下的钱同时投入度假与退休两处，并未说退休储蓄要“排第一”，属答非所问、过度推断。借用原文： retirement savings C)选项 saves 20 dollars a week 抓住录音数字 $20 a week 诱选，但录音是说她每周往度假基金存 20、往退休存 20，并非“每周省 20 就能负担一次度假”这种因果，属偷换概念、张冠李戴。借用原文： $20 a week into my vacation fund
questions.quote: One Chicago woman, for example, discovered that daily lunches with coworkers cost her$2000 a year; she decided to take lunch to work instead. "I now put $20 a week into my vacation fund and another 20 into retirement savings."

Retirement savings should come first in one's family budgeting.
A vacation will be affordable if one saves 20 dollars a week.

transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.text: So let's get started.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: And to start things off I think what we need to do is consider a definition.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: I'm going to define what love is but then most of the experiments I'm going to talk about are really focused more on attraction than love.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: And I'm going to pick a definition from a former colleague, Robert Sternberg, who is now the dean at Tufts University but was here on our faculty at Yale for nearly thirty years.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: And he has a theory of love that argues that it's made up of three components: intimacy, passion, and commitment, or what is sometimes called decision-commitment.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: And these are relatively straightforward.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: He argued that you don't have love if you don't have all three of these elements.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Intimacy is the feeling of closeness, of connectedness with someone, of bonding.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Operationally, you could think of intimacy as you share secrets, you share information with this person that you don't share with anybody else.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Okay.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: That's really what intimacy is, the bond that comes from sharing information that isn't shared with other people.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The second element is passion.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Passion is the drive that leads to romance.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: You can think of it as physical attraction.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: And Sternberg argues that this is a required component of a love relationship.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: The third element of love in Sternberg's theory is what he calls decision/commitment, the decision that one is in a love relationship, the willingness to label it as such, and a commitment to maintain that relationship at least for some period of time.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Sternberg would argue it's not love if you don't call it love and if you don't have some desire to maintain the relationship.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: So if you have all three of these, intimacy, passion and commitment, in Sternberg's theory, you have love.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: Now what's interesting about the theory is what do you have if you only have one out of three or two out of three?
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: What do you have and how is it different if you have a different two out of three?
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: What's interesting about this kind of theorizing is it gives rise to many different combinations that can be quite interesting when you break them down and start to look them carefully.
transcript.speaker: Speaker

transcript.text: So what I've done is I've taken Sternberg's three elements of love, intimacy, passion and commitment, and I've listed out the different kinds of relationships you would have if you had zero, one, two or three out of the three elements.

亲密是亲近感,是与某人联结的感觉,是一种纽带。从操作层面讲,你可以把亲密理解为你分享秘密,你与这个人分享你不会与其他任何人分享的信息。好的。这就是亲密的真正含义,即来自分享不与他人分享的信息而产生的纽带。第二个要素是激情。激情是导向浪漫的驱动力。你可以把它看作身体上的吸引。Sternberg认为这是爱情关系的必要组成部分。Sternberg理论中爱的第三个要素是他所说的决定/承诺,即认定自己处于一段爱情关系中的决定,愿意将其标记为这样一段关系,以及至少在一段时间内维持这段关系的承诺。Sternberg会认为,如果你不称之为爱,如果你没有某种维持这段关系的愿望,那就不是爱。所以如果你拥有所有这三者,亲密、激情和承诺,在Sternberg的理论中,你就拥有了爱。
现在这个理论有趣的地方在于,如果你只拥有三者中的一个或三者中的两个,你会拥有什么?你拥有什么,如果你拥有三者中不同的两个,又有什么不同?这种理论化的有趣之处在于,当你将它们分解并开始仔细观察时,它会产生许多可能相当有趣的不同组合。所以我所做的是,我采用了Sternberg关于爱的三个要素,亲密、激情和承诺,我列出了如果你在三个要素中拥有零个、一个、两个或三个时你会拥有的不同类型的关系。

你好!我是Elizabeth Hoffler,社会工作硕士。我是一名社会工作者、一名游说者,也是全国社会工作者协会执行主任的特别助理。今天我们将要讨论成为一名社会工作者。社会工作是助人的职业。其首要使命是提升人类福祉,帮助满足所有人的基本需求,尤其关注那些弱势群体、受压迫者以及生活在贫困中的人们。我们常常处理复杂的人类需求。社会工作不同于其他职业,因为我们关注人与环境。我们处理影响个人处境和前景的外部因素。我们创造评估和干预的机会,帮助服务对象和社区有效应对他们的现实,并在必要时改变这一现实。
社会工作者以成千上万种方式帮助他人,帮助来自各个年龄段、各种背景、全国各地的人们。无论何处有需要,社会工作者都会前来帮助。这一职业最为人所知的方面是社会安全网。我们帮助引导人们获取关键资源,并就改变人生的决定向他们提供咨询。全国有超过60万名专业社会工作者,我们都拥有社会工作学士学位、硕士学位或博士学位。受过临床训练的社会工作者比受过临床训练的精神科医生、心理学家和精神科护士的总和还要多。

今天，我想谈谈当名人榜样倡导健康习惯的同时又推广垃圾食品时会发生什么。目前，Michelle Obama的"动起来！"运动正受到越来越多的批评，该运动通过鼓励青少年更多地参与体育活动来对抗儿童肥胖，并签约了歌手Beyoncé和篮球运动员Shaquille O'Neal，而这两人也都代言汽水，而汽水正是肥胖流行病的主要推动因素之一。现在有更多证据表明，名人——尤其是职业运动员——在影响儿童行为方面有多么强大的力量。

在Yale大学Rudd食品政策与肥胖中心发布的一份报告中，研究人员研究了100名职业运动员及其代言合同。该团队将重点放在运动员身上，因为从理论上讲，他们是儿童积极健康生活方式的最佳榜样。在按类别对交易进行分类后，他们确定在与运动员相关的512个品牌中，大多数涉及体育用品，紧随其后的是食品和饮料品牌。运动饮料通常含糖量和热量都很高，在食品和饮料交易中占据了大部分，其余部分则由软饮料和快餐填补。在职业运动员代言的46种饮料中，93%的热量完全依赖糖分。
高知名度运动员能够影响儿童的饮食行为并不令人意外，但科学家们能够量化这些代言在儿童环境中的普遍程度。以职业运动员及其代言产品为特色的广告往往能获得令人印象深刻的曝光度，出现在电视、广播、印刷品和网络上。2010年，研究人员报告称，12至17岁的儿童看到的运动员代言食品和饮料品牌广告比成年人更多。
任何宣传活动都想要一位受欢迎的名人代言人，原因之一是无论他们在做什么，孩子们都会被他们所吸引。我们不能指望孩子们在同一个人销售糖分时关闭这种崇拜。在最好的情况下，孩子们可能会感到困惑。在最坏的情况下，他们会认为关于汽水的信息与关于水的信息是一样的，但这两种饮料并不相同。
如果儿童将运动员视为榜样，那么他们的偶像保持一致性符合他们的最佳利益。积极行为的一致性信息传递将为孩子们展示更健康的生活方式以供效仿。

B) 原词陷阱录音确有 a former colleague, Robert Sternberg 和 here on our faculty at Yale，但这是介绍提出理论的那位学者的背景，不是说 "实验是他在 Yale 做的"；选项把 "学者在 Yale" 偷换成 "实验由 Yale 同事做"，听到 Yale 就选会中招。借用原文： a former colleague, Robert Sternberg, who is now the dean at Tufts University but was here on our faculty at Yale
C) 原词陷阱nearly thirty years 在原文修饰 Sternberg "在 Yale 任教近三十年"，与实验进行了多久毫无关系；选项把这个时长扣到 the experiments "做了三十年" 头上，是典型听到数字就误选。借用原文： was here on our faculty at Yale for nearly thirty years
D) 张冠李戴录音中 a theory of love 是 Sternberg 提出的爱情理论，讲者并未说那些实验 "构成其理论的基础"；选项盗用 theory of love 字样，却让实验充当理论根基，与原文不符。借用原文： he has a theory of love that argues that it's made up of three components
questions.quote: I'm going to define what love is but then most of the experiments I'm going to talk about are really focused more on attraction than love.

options.text: They are focused more on attraction than love.
They were done by his former colleague at Yale.
They were carried out over a period of some thirty years.
They form the basis on which he builds his theory of love.

questions.prompt: What does Robert Sternberg argue about love?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） It is not love if you don't wish to maintain the relationship.
**题目译文**
Robert Sternberg对爱情持何观点?
A) 如果没有激情,这段关系就不能持久。
B) 亲密关系是必要的,但对爱情而言并非绝对不可或缺。
C) 如果你不希望维持这段关系,那就不是爱。
D) 没有相互理解就不可能有浪漫。
**定位** Sternberg 会主张：如果你不把它称为爱、并且没有某种维持这段关系的意愿，那它就不是爱。
**信号** 主张标记 argue + 否定条件强判断句。句首 Sternberg would argue 是明确的 "主张" 信号，正对题干 argue；其后 it's not love if you don't have some desire to maintain the relationship 是 "否定+条件" 的强判断，正是他的核心论点所在。
**替换** it's not love if you don't have some desire to maintain the relationship↔It is not love if you don't wish to maintain the relationship. wish=have some desire，句式同构
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 偷换概念录音说 Sternberg argues that this is a required component（passion 是爱的必需成分），并没说 "没有 passion 关系就不能持久"；选项 cannot last long if no passion 把"是构成要素之一" 偷换成 "决定关系能否长久"，听到 passion 就选会错。借用原文： Sternberg argues that this is a required component of a love relationship
B) 与原文相反原文讲三要素 you don't have love if you don't have all three，intimacy 是缺一不可的成分；选项 essential but not absolutely indispensable 给 intimacy 留了 "可有可无" 的口子，与 "三者缺一不可" 直接矛盾。借用原文： He argued that you don't have love if you don't have all three of these elements
D) 未提及录音确说 Passion is the drive that leads to romance，选项借了 romance 一词；但"romance 离不开 mutual understanding" 在原文中根本没有讲过，是凭空添加的断言。借用原文： Passion is the drive that leads to romance
questions.quote: Sternberg would argue it's not love if you don't call it love and if you don't have some desire to maintain the relationship.

options.text: The relationship cannot last long if no passion is involved.
Intimacy is essential but not absolutely indispensable to love.
It is not love if you don't wish to maintain the relationship.
Romance is just impossible without mutual understanding.

questions.prompt: What question does the speaker think is interesting about Sternberg's three elements of love?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） How the relationship is to be defined if any one is missing.
**题目译文**
关于Sternberg的爱情三要素,说话者认为什么问题很有趣?
A) 其中哪一个被认为是最重要的。
B) 没有承诺是否算真爱。
C) 缺少任何一个要素何时不会影响这段关系。
D) 如果缺少任何一个要素,这段关系该如何定义。
**定位** 那么这个理论有意思的地方在于：如果你只拥有三个里的一个、或三个里的两个，你拥有的是什么？
**信号** 态度标记 what's interesting 引出的追问。what's interesting about the theory is 是讲者亲口给出的 "有意思" 信号，正对题干 interesting；其后 what do you have if you only have one out of three or two out of three 就是他认为有意思的那个问题——缺了部分要素时还剩下什么。
**替换** what do you have if you only have one out of three or two out of three↔How the relationship is to be defined if any one is missing. "只有一个/两个"="缺了某个"，"剩下什么"="如何定义"
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及讲者只说三要素 "缺一就不是爱"，三者地位并列，从未讨论 most important（哪个最重要）；最高级是凭空添加的比较，原文没有这层意思。
B) 原词陷阱录音三要素含 decision/commitment，commitment 是真念过的词；但讲者觉得有意思的是 "缺其一或其二（泛指）" 时关系算什么，并非单问 "缺 commitment 算不算真爱"。选项把泛指的缺失窄化成只缺 commitment 一项，范围偏了。借用原文： The third element of love in Sternberg's theory is what he calls decision/commitment
C) 答非所问讲者的追问是缺项后 "你拥有的是什么、它有何不同"，关注的是 "变成哪种关系"，并非When the absence… doesn't affect the relationship（什么时候缺一个也不影响关系）；原文从未说缺要素 "不影响"，反而强调缺了就不是爱。借用原文： What do you have and how is it different if you have a different two out of three?
questions.quote: Now what's interesting about the theory is what do you have if you only have one out of three or two out of three?

options.text: Which of them is considered most important.
Whether it is true love without commitment.
When the absence of any one doesn't affect the relationship.
How the relationship is to be defined if any one is missing.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker mainly talk about?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （主旨题） Social work as a profession.
**题目译文**
说话者主要讨论什么?
A) 社会工作作为一种职业。
B) 社会工作的历史。
C) 社会工作申请者所需的学术学位。
D) 全国社会工作者协会的目标。
**定位** 今天我们要谈的是如何成为一名社会工作者。社会工作是一种助人的职业。
**信号** 开头点题句 talking about。答案句的信号是开头的点题宣告 Today we are going to be talking about becoming a social worker.，紧接 Social work is the helping profession.给社工下定义——讲座开篇的"今天要讲X"+"X 是…"正是主旨所在。
**替换** Social work is the helping profession. ↔ Social work as a profession. the helping profession 概括为 a profession
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 未提及原文确实念到 the rich history of social work，但那是 throughout this series you will learn 里"系列后续会涉及"的诸多内容之一，不是本段主旨；选项 The history of social work. 盗用 history 这个原词以偏概全。借用原文： the rich history of social work
C) 原词陷阱原文提到社工 have a bachelor's degree, a master's degree, or a PhD in Social Work，选项 Academic degrees required of social work applicants. 借"degree"原词把这一处细节拔高成主旨，属以偏概全。借用原文： a bachelor's degree, a master's degree, or a PhD in Social Work
D) 原词陷阱原文结尾才说 Our mission is to promote, protect, and advance the social work profession.，选项 The aim of the National Association of Social Workers. 盗用National Association 这个高频专名，把结尾一句话的协会宗旨当成整篇主旨，仍是以偏概全。借用原文： The National Association of Social Workers
questions.quote: Today we are going to be talking about becoming a social worker. Social work is the helping profession.

options.text: Social work as a profession.
The history of social work.
Academic degrees required of social work applicants.
The aim of the National Association of Social Workers.

questions.prompt: What do social workers mainly do?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） They help enhance the well-being of the underprivileged.
**题目译文**
社会工作者主要做什么?
A) 他们试图改变人们的社会行为。
B) 他们帮助提升弱势群体的福祉。
C) 他们提高人们的环境意识。
D) 他们为失业者创造大量机会。
**定位** 它的首要使命是提升人类福祉、帮助满足所有人的基本需求，并尤其关注那些脆弱、受压迫和生活贫困的人群。
**信号** 使命定义句 primary mission。答案句的信号是 Its primary mission is to enhance human well-being 里的 primary mission（首要使命）——"主要做什么"的正面定义句，正落在这种"使命是…"的判断句上。
**替换** enhance human well-being ↔ help enhance the well-being well-being 近乎原词对应those who are vulnerable, oppressed, and living in poverty↔the underprivileged三类弱势人群上提为 underprivileged
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 偷换概念原文说社工 focus on the person and environment、应对影响处境的外部因素，选项They try to change people's social behavior. 借"person""environment"的语境编出"改变人的社会行为"，原文从未说改变 behavior，是偷换概念。借用原文： we focus on the person and environment
C) 原词陷阱原文 focus on the person and environment 里的 environment 指"人所处的（社会）环境"，选项 They raise people's awareness of the environment. 盗用 environment 把它曲解成"自然环境/环保意识"，是熟词僻义被反向利用的偷换。借用原文： the person and environment
D) 原词陷阱原文确说 we create opportunity for assessment and intervention（为评估与干预创造机会），选项 They create a lot of opportunities for the unemployed. 盗用 create opportunity 这个原词，却把受益对象偷换成 the unemployed（失业者），原文从没提失业者。借用原文： we create opportunity for assessment and intervention
questions.quote: Its primary mission is to enhance human well-being and help meet the basic needs of all people, with a particular focus on those who are vulnerable, oppressed, and living in poverty.

options.text: They try to change people's social behavior.
They help enhance the well-being of the underprivileged.
They raise people's awareness of the environment.
They create a lot of opportunities for the unemployed.

questions.prompt: What do professional social workers have in common, according to the speaker?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题） They all have an academic degree in social work.
**题目译文**
根据说话者所述,专业社会工作者有什么共同点?
A) 他们都接受过严格的临床培训。
B) 他们都拥有社会工作学术学位。
C) 他们都是全国协会的成员。
D) 他们都通过自己的工作产生了影响。
**定位** 全国有超过六十万名职业社会工作者，我们全都拥有社会工作的学士、硕士或博士学位。
**信号** 全称句 we all either…。答案句的信号是 we all either have a bachelor's degree, a master's degree, or a PhD in Social Work 里的 we all——这正是预读盯住的全称表述，"全都拥有社工学位"就是共同点。
**替换** we all either have a bachelor's degree, a master's degree, or a PhD in Social Work↔They all have an academic degree in social work三种学位概括为 an academic degree
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反原文只说 There are more clinically trained social workers than clinically trained psychiatrists, psychologists, and psychiatric nurses combined.——讲的是"临床训练的社工"人数多，并未说"所有社工都受过临床训练"；选项 They have all received strict clinical training. 盗用 clinical training 原词，再硬加一个 all，与原文不符。借用原文： There are more clinically trained social workers than clinically trained psychiatrists, psychologists, and psychiatric nurses combined.
C) 原词陷阱原文 The National Association of Social Workers represents nearly 145,000 social workers，而全国有 more than 600,000 professional social workers——协会只代表其中一部分，远非全体；选项 They are all members of the National Association. 盗用高频专名再加 all，与数字明显矛盾。借用原文： The National Association of Social Workers represents nearly 145,000 social workers
D) 原词陷阱原文里 how you can make a difference by becoming a social worker 是对听众的鼓励"你能带来改变"，不是陈述"所有社工都已做出改变"这一共同属性；选项 They have all made a difference through their work. 盗用 make a difference 原词，答非所问。借用原文： how you can make a difference by becoming a social worker
questions.quote: There are more than 600,000 professional social workers in the country, and we all either have a bachelor's degree, a master's degree, or a PhD in Social Work.

options.text: They have all received strict clinical training.
They all have an academic degree in social work.
They are all members of the National Association.
They have all made a difference through their work.

questions.prompt: What is Mel Wilson going to talk about in the series?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） Social workers' job options and responsibilities.
**题目译文**
Mel Wilson将在系列节目中讨论什么?
A) 提升社会工作者的社会地位。
B) 社会工作者培训的重要性。
C) 社会工作者满足人们需求的方法。
D) 社会工作者的工作选择和职责。
**定位** Mel 会告诉你，拿到社工学位之后你有哪些选择，以及社会工作者必须恪守的高标准职责。
**信号** 人名后紧跟 will tell you about。答案句的信号是人名 Mel 后紧跟 Mel will tell you about the range of options——"某人 will tell you about…"正是该人负责话题的标志，挨着 Mel 的就是他要讲的。
**替换** the range of options you have once you get your social work degree ↔ job options range of options 概括为 job options the high standards of responsibility that social workers must adhere to ↔ responsibilities responsibility 近乎原词对应
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 未提及原文从未说 Mel 要讲社工的社会地位提升，选项 The promotion of social workers' social status. 里的"social status"原文未提；它或借 promote, protect, and advance the social work profession 的 promote 引人联想，但 promote profession 不等于 promote social status。借用原文： promote, protect, and advance the social work profession
B) 张冠李戴原文里与"流程/步骤"相关的是 Stacy 讲 the step-by-step process of becoming a social worker，与培训沾边的话题不归 Mel；选项 The importance of training for social workers. 把不属于 Mel 的话题安到他头上，且"training 的重要性"原文也未强调。借用原文： Stacy is going to walk you through the step-by-step process of becoming a social worker
C) 原词陷阱原文里 needs 出现在第一段 help meet the basic needs of all people，讲的是社工总体职责，并非 Mel 将讲的内容；选项 Ways for social workers to meet people's needs. 盗用 needs 原词，张冠李戴到 Mel 头上。借用原文： help meet the basic needs of all people
questions.quote: Mel will tell you about the range of options you have once you get your social work degree, as well as the high standards of responsibility that social workers must adhere to.

options.text: The promotion of social workers' social status.
The importance of training for social workers.
Ways for social workers to meet people's needs.
Social workers' job options and responsibilities.

questions.prompt: What is the aim of Michelle Obama's campaign?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题） To fight childhood obesity.
**题目译文**
Michelle Obama的运动目标是什么?
A) 对抗儿童肥胖。
B) 帮助弱势儿童。
C) 鼓励孩子们多参加体育运动。
D) 敦促孩子们效仿他们的榜样。
**定位** 目前，米歇尔·奥巴马的"动起来！"计划正受到越来越多的批评，该计划通过鼓励青少年增加身体活动来对抗儿童肥胖。
**信号** which 定语从句直陈宗旨。答案信号是计划名后紧跟的定语从句 which fights childhood obesity——录音介绍一个 campaign 后立刻用 which 说明它"做什么、为什么"，这就是目的说明句，一听到"计划名 + which + 动词"就锁定。
**替换** which fights childhood obesity↔To fight childhood obesity.从句转不定式表目的
questions.tip:
**排除**
C) 原词陷阱C To encourage kids to play more sports. 盗用了录音 encouraging youngsters to become more physically active 里的"鼓励/更多运动"之意，听着很对。但"鼓励多运动"在原文里只是"对抗肥胖"的手段（by encouraging…），不是计划的最终目的；题问 aim，手段当目的就是答非所问。借用原文： by encouraging youngsters to become more physically active
B) 未提及B To help disadvantaged kids. 里的"弱势儿童"录音通篇没有出现，计划针对的是"所有儿童的肥胖"，不是"弱势群体"。属凭"公益计划=帮弱势"的常识臆造，文本无据。
D) 张冠李戴D To urge kids to follow their role models. 里的 role models 确实是录音的关键词，但"名人是榜样"是整篇讨论的背景，不是 "Let's Move!" 计划的目的；该计划目的是对抗肥胖，把全篇话题安到这个计划头上即张冠李戴。借用原文： celebrity role models
questions.quote: Currently, there's mounting criticism of Michelle Obama's "Let's Move!" campaign, which fights childhood obesity by encouraging youngsters to become more physically active.

options.text: To fight childhood obesity.
To help disadvantaged kids.
To encourage kids to play more sports.
To urge kids to follow their role models.

questions.prompt: What does research find about advertisements featuring professional athletes?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） They impress kids more than they do adults.
**题目译文**
关于以职业运动员为主角的广告,研究发现了什么?
A) 当在网上投放时,它们最能促进产品销售。
B) 当在电视上播出时,它们最有效。
C) 它们变得越来越普遍。
D) 它们给孩子们留下的印象比给成年人留下的印象更深。
**定位** 而且在 2010 年，研究人员报告说，12 至 17 岁的儿童看到的由运动员代言的食品饮料品牌广告比成人看到的更多。
**信号** researchers reported 引出结论。答案信号是 the researchers reported that——这是研究方正式给出结论的标志句，题问 research find，这句就是直接应答；其后的 children…more…than adults 即发现内容。
**替换** children ages 12 to 17 saw more athlete-endorsed food and beverage brand commercials than adults↔ They impress kids more than they do adults.看得更多改写为印象更深
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 原词陷阱B They are most effective when appearing on TV. 抓住了录音 on TV, radio, in print and online 里念到的 TV，让人误以为"电视最有效"。但原文只是并列罗列广告出现的各种渠道，从没说哪个渠道"最有效"，B 凭空加了"most effective"和"单挑 TV"。借用原文： on TV, radio, in print and online
A) 原词陷阱A They best boost product sales when put online. 同样借了 online 这个真念到的渠道词，再编出"放网上最能促进销量"。录音只说广告在网上等渠道"曝光大"，全篇没讲过"销量"，更没说网上最促销，属添油加醋。借用原文： online
C) 原词陷阱C They are becoming more and more prevalent. 里的 prevalent 确实是录音 how prevalent these endorsements are 念到的词，极诱人。但原文只是说研究"量化了这些代言在儿童环境中有多普遍"，是陈述"普遍程度"，并没有说"越来越（more and more）"这个"上升趋势"；C 把"普遍"偷换成"日益普遍"，且这不是本题问的"研究发现"的落点。借用原文： how prevalent these endorsements are in the children's environment
questions.quote: And in 2010, the researchers reported that children ages 12 to 17 saw more athlete-endorsed food and beverage brand commercials than adults.

options.text: They best boost product sales when put online.
They are most effective when appearing on TV.
They are becoming more and more prevalent.
They impress kids more than they do adults.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker think kids' idols should do?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （态度观点题） Message positive behaviors at all times.
**题目译文**
说话者认为孩子们的偶像应该做什么?
A) 始终把孩子们的利益放在首位。
B) 做他们在公开场合所倡导的事。
C) 始终传递积极的行为。
D) 注意他们在儿童面前的形象。
**定位** 如果孩子们把运动员当作榜样，那么偶像保持言行一致才最符合孩子们的利益。始终如一地传递正面行为，会向孩子们展示更健康的生活方式，供他们效仿。
**信号** 结尾建议句 it's in their best interest。答案信号是末段的 it's in their best interest if their idols are consistent——录音收尾用"最符合孩子利益的是……"这种价值判断句给出主张，正是说话人 think 的落点；紧接的 Consistent messaging of positive behaviors 把主张说得更具体。
**替换** Consistent messaging of positive behaviors↔Message positive behaviors at all times.名词化转祈使且 consistent=at all times
questions.tip:
**排除**

transcriptTranslations: 你猜怎么着?我吃过的最难吃的食物是在法国。
真的吗?这太奇怪了。我还以为法国人都是好厨师呢。
是的。没错。不过我觉得其实哪儿都一样。你知道的,有些地方好,有些地方差。但这其实都是我们自己的错。
你什么意思?
嗯,那是我第一次去法国。好多年前了,我还在上学的时候,我跟我爸爸学校的朋友一起去的。他们租了辆大巴去瑞士。
学校组织的旅行?
对。他们大多数人以前都没出过国。我们是晚上穿过英吉利海峡的,然后就穿过法国出发了,到了早餐时间,大巴司机安排我们在一家小咖啡馆停下来。我们所有人都在那儿,又累又饿,然后我们就有了这个重大发现。
什么发现?
培根加鸡蛋。
太棒了!地道的英式早餐。
是啊。反正我们也不懂——所以就吃了,然后,呃……!
什么样的?恶心吗?
哦,简直难以置信!他们就拿个碗,放点儿油进去。然后把培根放进油里,在上面打个鸡蛋,把整个东西放进烤箱烤了大概十分钟。
放烤箱里!你在开玩笑吧。培根加鸡蛋怎么能用烤箱做!
嗯,他们肯定是那么做的。是热的,但没熟。就是鸡蛋在大量的油里漂着,还有生培根。
你真的吃了吗?
没有!谁都没吃。他们都想掉头回家。你知道的,回去喝袋泡茶、吃炸鱼薯条。也真不能怪他们。反正第二天晚上我们又吃到了另一道外国特色菜。
是什么?
蜗牛。那真是彻底把他们击垮了。多美好的假期啊!
你说你的店经营得不错。能不能用一些实际的数据和数字来说明一下"经营得不错"是什么意思？
嗯，"经营得不错"的意思是大约7年来平均每周收入1200英镑或更多，总共赚了差不多25万英镑。而且"经营得不错"意味着你的收入在增长。去年我们的营业额略高于5万英镑，今年我们希望能超过6万英镑。所以，如果我们能继续增长的话，这很好。
现在，我想那是毛收入吧。那你们的开支呢？
是的，那是毛收入。开支当然在稳步上升。而且自从我们搬到这个新店以来，开支大幅增加了，因为这是一个大得多的店面。所以我说不准我们的开支到底是多少。大概在每年六七千英镑左右，这不算高。从商业角度来说，这是相当低的，我们尽量把开支控制得越低越好。
而且你们的价格比周围店铺的同类商品低得多。当地的店主们对于在他们中间有这样一家生意这么好的店是什么感受？

也许他们中的很多人并不知道我们做得有多好，因为我们不会刻意去宣传。这是我们很早就学到的教训。我们和所有当地店主都很友好，有一次我们碰巧向一个当地店主提到我们那周赚了多少钱。他非常不高兴，之后就再也没那么友好了。所以我们特意不去宣传我们赚了多少钱。但我们和所有店铺的关系都很好。他们中没有人抱怨过我们抢了他们的生意或类似的事情。我觉得这是一种友好的关系。也许如果他们真的知道我们赚了多少，可能就不会那么友好了。

questions.prompt: What did the woman think of the French?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （态度观点题） They were all good at cooking.
**题目译文**
这位女士对法国人有什么看法？
A) 他们都擅长烹饪。
B) 他们对食物很讲究。
C) 他们为自己的菜肴感到自豪。
D) 他们喜欢培根和鸡蛋。
**定位** 真的吗？那可奇怪了。我一直以为法国人个个都是好厨子。
**信号** 女士本人「I thought…」的直接表态。答案句是女士自己说的 I thought the French were all good cooks.，题目问女士的看法，信号就是她用第一人称 I thought 直接说出的判断——对话题里谁的看法就听谁开口说的那句。
**替换** the French were all good cooks↔They were all good at cooking. good cooks = good at cooking 同义换说法
questions.tip:
**排除**
B) 未提及They were particular about food. 说法国人「对食物挑剔」，女士全程只说了 good cooks，从未提他们挑不挑嘴，属凭「法国人讲究吃」的常识硬套，原文未提。
C) 过度推断They were proud of their cuisine. 把「会做菜」拔高成「为自家菜系自豪」，是一种心理状态的过度推断，女士只评价了厨艺水平，没说他们自豪，原文未提。
D) 原词陷阱They were fond of bacon and eggs. 里的 bacon and eggs 确实在录音后段被念到，但那是男士讲的那顿难吃早餐，与女士对法国人的看法毫不相干，是把原词搬来骗「听到就选」。借用原文： Bacon and eggs.
questions.quote: Really? That's odd. I thought the French were all good cooks.

questions.prompt: Who did the man travel with on his first trip to Switzerland?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题） His parents' friends.
**题目译文**
这位男士第一次去瑞士旅行时和谁一起去的？
A) 他的父母。
B) 他的朋友。
C) 他的同学。
D) 他父母的朋友。
**定位** 嗯，那是我第一次去法国。好多年前了，我还在上学，我是跟我父母的朋友一起去的，是我父亲学校的人。
**信号** 「I went there with…」直接交代同行人。信号是男士用 I went there with my parents' friends 直接把「和谁去」说了出来，with 后面跟的就是答案所在；细节题要抓住这种把问题点一句答清的句子。
**替换** my parents' friends↔ His parents' friends. my → His 仅人称转换，其余照搬
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱His parents. 抓住了原话里的 parents，但原话是 my parents' friends（父母的「朋友」），不是父母本人。只听到 parents 就选，正中陷阱。借用原文： my parents' friends
B) 偷换概念His friends. 听上去也沾 friends，但原话是「父母的朋友」，不是他自己的朋友；少了parents' 这层限定，对象就完全变了。借用原文： my parents' friends
C) 原词陷阱His schoolmates. 来自原文反复出现的 school（when I was at school、my father's school），但那是说他当时在上学、以及是父亲学校组织的，并非和同学同行，属听到school 就联想成「同学」。借用原文： my father's school

questions.prompt: What does the man say about the breakfast at the little French café?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题） No one of the group ate it.
**题目译文**
这位男士对那家法国小咖啡馆的早餐有什么看法？
A) 餐食没有配茶。
B) 那是真正的英式早餐。
C) 这群人中没有人吃它。
D) 它有点煮过头了。
**定位** 没有！没人吃。他们都想掉头回家。
**信号** 对女士「有没有吃」之问的直接应答。上一段女士问 Did you actually eat it?，男士回答No! Nobody did.——这是被问者对关键问题的直接应答，信号是这个加重的否定 No 和Nobody did，正好回答了「这顿早餐怎么了」。
**替换** Nobody did ↔ No one of the group ate it. Nobody did = No one … ate it 同义还原
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 原词陷阱No tea was served with the meal. 说这顿没配茶，但男士描述早餐时只讲了油、培根、鸡蛋怎么做，全程没提茶；tea 一词虽在 back to teabags 出现，却是讲「想回家喝茶」，与这顿早餐配不配茶无关，原文未提。借用原文： back to teabags and fish and chips
B) 张冠李戴It was the real English breakfast. 几乎照搬女士那句 The real English breakfast.，但那是女士看到 bacon and eggs 时的期待，紧接着就被男士的实际遭遇推翻（没熟、没人吃），并非男士对这顿早餐的定性。借用原文： The real English breakfast.
D) 与原文相反It was a little overcooked. 说「有点煮过头」，但男士明说 It was hot, but it wasn't cooked.——热是热，却没熟，蛋还泡在油里、培根是生的。实际是欠火，选项说成过火，方向正相反。借用原文： It was hot, but it wasn't cooked.

questions.prompt: What did the man think of his holiday in France?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （态度观点题） It was rather disappointing.
**题目译文**
这位男士对他在法国的假期有什么看法？
A) 它充满了兴奋感。
B) 它真的很不同寻常。
C) 它是一次冒险的经历。
D) 它相当令人失望。
**定位** 蜗牛。那简直把他们彻底整崩溃了。真是个「美好」的假期啊！
**信号** 结尾反语「Lovely holiday」加全篇负面基调。答案信号是结尾那句 Lovely holiday that was!——表面夸 lovely，但前文一路是「最难吃」「没熟」「没人吃」「把他们整崩溃」，结合这股基调可知 lovely 是反话，真意是这假期糟透了。态度题要靠语气加上下文判反话。
**替换** Lovely holiday that was! ↔ It was rather disappointing.反语 Lovely 实指失望The worst food I've ever had was in France. ↔ It was rather disappointing.全篇基调「最难吃」佐证失望
questions.tip:
**排除**
A) 与原文相反It was full of excitement. 说假期「充满兴奋」，恰是被结尾 Lovely holiday that was! 字面骗了；那句是反讽，全篇都在吐槽食物，并无兴奋之意。借用原文： Lovely holiday that was!
B) 偷换概念It was really extraordinary. 看似呼应男士那句 it was incredible!，但 incredible 在这里是「难以置信地糟」，而 extraordinary 偏中性甚至褒义，把负面情绪洗成了「了不起」，没答出「失望」这个态度。借用原文： it was incredible!
C) 过度推断It was a risky experience. 把「吃到难吃的食物」联想成「有风险的经历」，但男士说的是失望、难吃，从未表达「危险/有风险」，属顺着情节脑补出的态度，原文未提。
questions.quote: Snails. That really finished them off. Lovely holiday that was!

It was a risky experience.
