questions.prompt: Besides social media companies, what factors contribute to young people's psychological health problems?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
除了社交媒体公司之外，还有哪些因素导致年轻人的心理健康问题？
A) 资金不足的学校和医疗服务。
B) 政客们急于转移公众注意力。
C) 对数字媒体巨头不完善的法定监管。
D) 他们父母的教育背景和生活状况。
**判型** Besides social media companies, what factors contribute to young people's psychological health problems? 问文中列举了哪些其他成因，有明确的列举句可查，属细节题。
**拆句** Q50 主干 what factors contribute to young people's psychological health problems，句首 Besides social media companies 是介词短语作排除限定。contribute to 表示'促成'，问的是成因；Besides 是全题题眼，决定答案不能落在社交媒体公司头上。
**定位** 当然，社交媒体公司并非我们所有问题的根源，而且它们很容易成为政客们的靶子——政客热衷于借此转移人们对投入不足的学校和医疗服务的关注。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确inadequately resourced schools and health services↔Poorly financed schools and health services.预判候选'投入不足的学校与医疗服务'与 Poorly financed schools and health services. 仅修饰语有别，主体名词逐字相同，且它确属'社交媒体公司以外'的因素，锁定 A。
B) 答非所问Politicians' eagerness to divert public attention. 取自 politicians keen to divert attention，但政客转移视线是对问题的掩盖手段，不是导致年轻人心理问题的成因；题干问的是 contribute to 心理问题的因素，此项答非所问。
C) 答非所问Bad statutory regulation of digital media giants. 借自 P4 Statutory regulation of the digital media giants is long overdue.——监管缺位针对的正是数字媒体巨头本身，属于'社交媒体公司'这一条线，而题干用 Besides social media companies 明确把这条线排除在外；且 P5 列举的其他原因里也根本没有它。
D) 偷换概念原文的另一成因是 increasing pressure to succeed in education and in life more broadly——年轻人自己在教育和人生上的成功压力；Their parents' educational background and life. 把 education and life 的原词留下，却硬是安上 parents' 这个原文没有的主体，把'自身压力'偷换成'父母背景'。
questions.quote: Of course, social media companies are not the source of all our ills, and can offer a too- easy target for politicians keen to divert attention from inadequately resourced schools and health services.

options.text: Poorly financed schools and health services.
Politicians' eagerness to divert public attention.
Bad statutory regulation of digital media giants.
Their parents' educational background and life.

title: Two proposals are before the state legislature that…

sentences.text: Two proposals are before the state legislature that look to put some limits on ever-increasing rent prices, which some lawmakers say are contributing to rising homelessness rates.

passage.translation: 州议会目前正在审议两项提案，旨在对不断上涨的租金设置一些限制。一些议员表示，租金上涨正在导致无家可归率上升。

sentences.text: The proposals (26)____ caps on rent increases, preventing landlords in the state from raising rent more than the rate of inflation in most cases.
There are exceptions for buildings less than 10 years old, public housing, improvements beyond maintenance, and a hardship (27)____ .

passage.translation: 这些提案对租金涨幅设定上限，在大多数情况下，禁止该州房东将租金涨幅提高到超过通货膨胀率的水平。例外情况包括建成未满10年的建筑、公共住房、维护之外的改造，以及因困难而获得的豁免。

sentences.text: In a 2020 study, researchers at the U.S.
Government Accountability Office estimated that every $100 in rent increase is (28)____ to a 9% rise in homelessness.
Rent increases have an even more detrimental effect on some demographic groups, such as racial minorities.

passage.translation: 在2020年的一项研究中，美国政府问责署的研究人员估计，租金每上涨100美元，就与无家可归率上升9%相关。租金上涨对某些人口群体的影响更加不利，例如少数族裔。

sentences.text: Representative Alex Ramel explained why he thought that this kind of legislation was so important, telling the story of a (29)____ struggling to live in the community.

passage.translation: 亚历克斯·拉梅尔议员讲述了一名努力在当地社区生活的选民的故事，并解释了他为何认为这类立法如此重要。

sentences.text: Ramel pointed out the (30)____ effect of double-digit rent increases, saying that he made the decision to introduce the legislation while talking to a young man in Bellingham.
"He's a recent graduate from Western Washington University and just got a new job," Ramel said.
"He was leaving our community because his landlord (31)____ him that his rent was going to go up by $600 a month."

passage.translation: 拉梅尔指出，两位数租金涨幅会造成毁灭性影响。他说，自己是在与贝灵厄姆的一名年轻人交谈时决定提出这项立法的。拉梅尔说：“他刚从西华盛顿大学毕业，最近找到了一份新工作。他正要离开我们的社区，因为他的房东通知他，租金每月要上涨600美元。”

sentences.text: The Rental Housing Association of Washington opposes the legislation.
The association (32)____that the policy won't actually solve the problem of rental prices.
Instead, it will punish small landlords and allow wealthy renters easy access to cheap housing.

passage.translation: 华盛顿州租赁住房协会反对这项立法。该协会声称，这项政策实际上无法解决租金问题，反而会惩罚小房东，让富裕租户轻易获得廉价住房。

sentences.text: "The rent control policy has failed everywhere it has been (33)____ in this county.
It has not fixed one housing problem (34)____ .
It also does not distinguish between rich and poor when (35)____ who gets the benefits of rent control," said Chester Baldwin with the Rental Housing Coalition.

passage.translation: 租赁住房联盟的切斯特·鲍德温说：“租金管制政策在这个国家所有实施过的地方都失败了。它没有在任何地方解决一个住房问题。在决定谁能从租金管制中受益时，它也不区分富人和穷人。”

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
Two proposals are before the state legislature that look to put some limits on ever-increasing rent prices, which some lawmakers say are contributing to rising homelessness rates.

The proposals {{26}} caps on rent increases, preventing landlords in the state from raising rent more than the rate of inflation in most cases. There are exceptions for buildings less than 10 years old, public housing, improvements beyond maintenance, and a hardship {{27}} .

In a 2020 study, researchers at the U.S. Government Accountability Office estimated that every $100 in rent increase is {{28}} to a 9% rise in homelessness. Rent increases have an even more detrimental effect on some demographic groups, such as racial minorities.

Representative Alex Ramel explained why he thought that this kind of legislation was so important, telling the story of a {{29}} struggling to live in the community.

Ramel pointed out the {{30}} effect of double-digit rent increases, saying that he made the decision to introduce the legislation while talking to a young man in Bellingham. "He's a recent graduate from Western Washington University and just got a new job," Ramel said. "He was leaving our community because his landlord {{31}} him that his rent was going to go up by $600 a month."

The Rental Housing Association of Washington opposes the legislation. The association {{32}}that the policy won't actually solve the problem of rental prices. Instead, it will punish small landlords and allow wealthy renters easy access to cheap housing.

"The rent control policy has failed everywhere it has been {{33}} in this county. It has not fixed one housing problem {{34}} . It also does not distinguish between rich and poor when {{35}} who gets the benefits of rent control," said Chester Baldwin with the Rental Housing Coalition.

options.text: anywhere
exemption
asserts
impose
constituent
notified
correlated
notwithstanding
determining
presume
devastating
rehabilitation
enacted
reproaching
entails

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) impose 动词
**词性槽** 复数主语 proposals 之后缺谓语，需动词原形（一般现在时）
**依据** impose caps/limits on 是政策语域的固定搭配，「对……设限」The proposals __(26)__ caps on rent increases, preventing landlords in the state from raising rent more than the rate of inflation in most cases.——提案「对租金涨幅设上限」，呼应首段 put some limits on ever-increasing rent prices，impose caps on 与put limits on 是同义改写，这正是六级最爱考的「换说法不换意思」。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) presume presume 意为「假定」，与 caps 不构成搭配且逻辑相反presume 是「假定、推测」，presume caps 不是英语搭配；且提案是「实际设限」而非「假定存在上限」，代入后与后半句 preventing landlords…（实际阻止房东涨租）矛盾。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 M) —— presume 与 impose 同为原形动词，「提案假定上限」粗读似乎也通。The proposals __(26)__ caps on rent increases 中 presume 形态合格，且考生若只认识 presume 不认识 impose，容易用「熟悉的词」填。防坑：盯住宾语搭配——caps/limits 的舞伴是 impose（impose caps on），presume 后接的是「事实从句」；再回看首段 put some limits on ever-increasing rent prices，同义改写的锚点直接指向 impose。

questions.explanation:
**答案** I) exemption 名词
**词性槽** 不定冠词 a + 名词作定语的 hardship 之后，需单数可数名词
**依据** hardship exemption「困难豁免」是政策文本的固定说法，且与 exceptions 同义呼应There are exceptions for buildings less than 10 years old, public housing, improvements beyond maintenance, and a hardship __(27)__.——列举的都是「不适用该限制的豁免情形」，a hardship exemption（因困难而获得的豁免）与句首 exceptions同义复现，政策语域用词精准。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) constituentconstituent「选民」不能与 hardship 构成政策豁免概念a hardship constituent 字面上是「一位困难的选民」，但本句列举的是例外「情形/类别」（建筑、公屋、改良工程），不是人；且选民不属于租金管制条例的豁免条款范畴，语义场不合。
N) rehabilitationrehabilitation 意为「康复/修复」，与 hardship 搭配不成立hardship rehabilitation（困难修复）不是英语里的政策术语；rehabilitation 多指罪犯改造、病人康复或建筑翻修，与「豁免条款」的语境无关。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) correlated 动词
**词性槽** be 动词 is 之后、介词 to 之前，需过去分词构成 be done 表语结构
**依据** be correlated to 是固定搭配，意为「与……相关」，严丝合缝研究语境 researchers at the U.S. Government Accountability Office estimated that every $100 in rent increase is __(28)__ to a 9% rise in homelessness：租金每涨 100 美元「对应/关联」无家可归率上升 9%——这正是相关性表述，be correlated to/with 是六级阅读与选词填空的高频固定搭配，语义与搭配双契合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) enacted enact 的搭配对象是法律而非数据关系enacted 意为「颁布（法律）」，其主语应是立法机构、宾语是法案；「租金上涨被颁布成无家可归率上升 9%」语义不通，且 enact 不与 to 构成表语搭配。
K) notified notify 的对象必须是人notify sb of/that… 意为「通知某人」，被通知方是人；这里主语是 every $100 in rent increase（物），「租金上涨被通知给无家可归率」不成立，也不与 to 搭配。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) constituent 名词
**词性槽** 不定冠词 a 之后、分词短语 struggling… 之前，需单数可数名词指人
**依据** 议员讲「选民」的艰难故事，身份与语境严丝合缝Representative Alex Ramel explained why he thought that this kind of legislation was so important, telling the story of a __(29)__ struggling to live in the community.——说话者是 Representative（众议员），议员为自己的立法辩护时讲的是「选区选民」的故事；constituent 正是「（选区的）选民」，且下一段 he made the decision to introduce the legislation while talking to a young man in Bellingham 的 a young man 就是这个 constituent 的具体化。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
N) rehabilitationrehabilitation 是抽象事物名词，不能「挣扎着生活」rehabilitation（康复/修复）是物不是人，无法充当 struggling to live 的逻辑主语；「一个挣扎着住在社区里的康复」语义荒谬，直接排除。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) devastating 形容词
**词性槽** 定冠词 the 与名词 effect 之间，需形容词作定语
**依据** devastating effect 是高频搭配，且与「两位数涨幅」的负面语境吻合上下文 Ramel pointed out the __(30)__ effect of double-digit rent increases 与 Rent increases have an even more detrimental effect on some demographic groups 呼应：说话者是立法支持者，强调租金暴涨的「毁灭性」影响，devastating effect（毁灭性的影响）搭配与感情色彩双双贴合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) constituent constituent 作形容词意为「组成的」，与 effect 不搭constituent 虽有形容词用法（组成的、构成整体的），但 constituent effect 不是英语搭配；其名词义「选民」也与本空语法槽（名词前的定语形容词）语义不合。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) notified 动词
**词性槽** his landlord 后缺谓语，且后接双宾 him + that 从句，需及物动词过去式
**依据** notify sb that… 「通知某人……」，房东通知涨租正是此场景He was leaving our community because his landlord __(31)__ him that his rent was going to go up by $600 a month.——他要搬离，因为房东「通知」他月租要涨 600 美元。notify sb that 从句句型严丝合缝，因果链（被通知涨租 → 被迫搬走）完全通顺。

**答案** B) asserts 动词
**词性槽** 单数主语 The association 后缺谓语，需三单动词接 that 从句
**依据** assert that… 「坚称」，正是机构表态反对的措辞The Rental Housing Association of Washington opposes the legislation. The association __(32)__ that the policy won't actually solve the problem of rental prices.——协会反对立法，「坚称」该政策解决不了租金问题。assert 接 that 从句表强硬主张，与前句 opposes 的反对立场无缝衔接。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) entailsentail 是及物动词接名词性成分，不接 that 从句entails 意为「使必要、涉及」，用法是 A entails B（B 为名词/动名词），如 The job entails travel；它没有 entail that 从句表「声称」的用法，代入后句法不成立。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— entails 与 asserts 同为三单，形态零区分度，最易凭模糊词义选错。The association __(32)__ that the policy won't actually solve the problem of rental prices. 中 entails 词性、时态全部合格，「涉及问题」的字面意思又和语境沾边，是最强干扰。防坑口诀：空后是 that 从句时先问动词能不能带宾语从句——entail 只能接名词性宾语，assert 才能接 that 从句表「坚称」，句法门槛一过见分晓。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) enacted 动词
**词性槽** has been 之后需过去分词，构成现在完成被动语态
**依据** 法律政策「被颁布实施」用 enact，法案语域的专属动词The rent control policy has failed everywhere it has been __(33)__ in this county.——租金管控政策「凡是在本县被实施过的地方都失败了」。enact 专用于「颁布法律、实施政策」，与 policy 构成最自然的被动搭配，也是说话者（反对派）论证政策无效的语义所需。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
K) notified notify 的对象是人，政策不能被「通知」notified 意为「被通知」，其逻辑主语必须是人（sb be notified of/that…）；it 指 policy（物），「政策被通知」语义不通。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) anywhere 副词
**词性槽** 句子主干完整（It has not fixed one housing problem），空在句尾作状语，需副词
**依据** 否定句 + anywhere = 「在任何地方都不」，承接上句 everywhere The rent control policy has failed everywhere it has been __(33)__ in this county. It has not fixed one housing problem __(34)__.——上句说政策「处处失败」，本句递进「它在任何地方都没能解决哪怕一个住房问题」。not…anywhere 是英语否定的标准搭配，与 everywhere 形成语义对仗，语气一气呵成。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
L) notwithstanding notwithstanding 表让步「尽管如此」，与本句递进逻辑冲突notwithstanding 作副词意为「尽管如此」（表让步转折），而本句与上句是递进强调（处处失败 → 一个问题都没解决），不是让步；且 notwithstanding 通常不单独置于句尾修饰否定陈述句，代入后逻辑和句法双不通。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) determining 动词
**词性槽** when 引导的省略状语从句 when (it is) doing，需现在分词
**依据** determine who gets the benefits「决定谁受益」，与 distinguish 的批评逻辑一致It also does not distinguish between rich and poor when __(35)__ who gets the benefits of rent control——批评者说该政策「在决定谁享受租金管控的好处时不区分贫富」。determine + 宾语从句（决定……）搭配自然，且与前文 it will punish small landlords and allow wealthy renters easy access to cheap housing 的批评（富人也能占便宜）完全同向。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
O) reproaching reproach 意为「责备」，其对象是人且与 who gets… 从句不搭reproach 的用法是 reproach sb (for sth)，宾语是被责备的人；「在责备谁获得好处时不区分贫富」语义拧巴——政策不会去「责备」受益人，批评的对象错位，逻辑不通。

title: The History and Meaning of Colored Traffic Lights

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Timed traffic lights are set according to schedules that are supposed to coordinate with peak traffic hours.
Cities need to monitor and update signal light time schedules at least every two years to keep these systems effective.
In Los Angeles, California, an ambitious project to go a step further and synchronize(使同步) every red light in Los Angeles cost over 400 million dollars.
Ask a resident of the city and they are likely to agree that saving time on the road is well worth it.
If implemented nationwide, synchronization could shave 10% off traffic congestion(堵塞) and 20% off air pollution.
Congestion costs time, money, and lives.
Big data can help improve how millions of people safely share the road.
However, none of this would be possible without the traffic light!

passage.translation: 定时交通信号灯根据应当与高峰交通时段相协调的时刻表进行设置。城市需要至少每两年监测和更新信号灯时间安排,以保持这些系统的有效性。在加利福尼亚州洛杉矶,一项更进一步同步洛杉矶每个红灯的雄心勃勃的项目耗资超过4亿美元。问问这座城市的居民,他们很可能会认为节省道路上的时间非常值得。如果在全国范围内实施,同步化可以减少10%的交通拥堵和20%的空气污染。拥堵浪费时间、金钱和生命。大数据可以帮助改善数百万人安全共享道路的方式。然而,如果没有交通信号灯,这一切都不可能实现!

passage.label: B

sentences.text: The first traffic light was invented in London in the 1860's, but it was hardly recognizable — or effective.
It had been adapted from the railroad signal system by a railway manager, John Peak Knight, in 1868.
The railroads used red gas lights at night to signal stops and green gas lights during the daytime.
Knight installed a similar gas light, semaphore(臂板信号) system near London's Westminster Bridge in December of 1868.

passage.translation: 第一个交通信号灯于19世纪60年代在伦敦发明,但它几乎无法辨认——也不有效。1868年,铁路管理者John Peak Knight将铁路信号系统进行了改造。铁路在夜间使用红色气灯来示意停车,白天则使用绿色气灯。Knight于1868年12月在伦敦威斯敏斯特桥附近安装了一套类似的气灯臂板信号系统。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: The life of the first traffic light signal was short-lived.
A gas leak caused one of the signal lights to explode on its police officer operator within a month of being installed.

passage.translation: 第一个交通信号灯的寿命很短。在安装后不到一个月,煤气泄漏导致其中一个信号灯在其警察操作员身上爆炸。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: Automating traffic signals stalled after the London incident.
Forty years passed before cars crowding city streets urged the development of traffic lights in the United States.
London would not see another traffic light until 1929.

passage.translation: 伦敦事故后,交通信号自动化陷入停滞。四十年过去了,拥挤城市街道的汽车才促使美国发展交通信号灯。伦敦直到1929年才再次出现交通信号灯。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: The United States is a car culture like no other country.
Unlike most European cities that started urban planning when horses were high-tech, many cities in the United States were designed around urban sprawl, suburban tracts, and motor cars.

passage.translation: 美国的汽车文化不同于任何其他国家。与大多数欧洲城市在马匹还是高科技时代就开始城市规划不同,美国的许多城市是围绕城市扩张、郊区地带和机动车辆设计的。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: As traffic and cities grew, so did the race to solve growing traffic problems.
The first traffic signals were semaphores.
Semaphores are towers with moving arms signaling for traffic to stop or go.
They could be manual or automatic.
There was no consistent design.
Various models were invented and put into place in cities as the need arose.

passage.translation: 随着交通和城市的发展,解决日益严重的交通问题的竞赛也在进行。最早的交通信号是臂板信号。臂板信号是带有移动臂的塔,示意交通停止或通行。它们可以是手动的或自动的。没有统一的设计。随着需求的出现,各种型号被发明并安装在城市中。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: In 1912, Lester Wire was a police officer exhausted by traffic at Main Street and 200 South.
He developed a manually switched stop light.
The four-sided box, raised on a ten-foot pole, looked like a birdhouse and was operated manually by an officer.
The officer would flip a switch to change between the dipped red and green lights.

passage.translation: 1912年,Lester Wire是一名因Main Street和200 South的交通而疲惫不堪的警察。他开发了一种手动切换的停车灯。这个四面的盒子安装在十英尺高的杆子上,看起来像鸟屋,由警察手动操作。警察会拨动开关在倾斜的红灯和绿灯之间切换。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Like the 1910 semaphore, the first electric signal used words.
However, the words were no longer written on arms that raised and fell.
The words "stop" or "move" were on lights.
The posts lit up on each of four corner-posts around an intersection(十字路口).
It was not automated, though.
A booth with an operator was required to flip the switches.

passage.translation: 与1910年的臂板信号一样,第一个电子信号使用文字。然而,文字不再写在升降的臂上。'停止'或'通行'的字样在灯上。灯柱在十字路口周围的四个角柱上点亮。但它不是自动化的。需要一个带操作员的岗亭来拨动开关。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: The system allowed police officers to move from the middle of the street to a corner.
From that vantage(有利地位), an officer could oversee the crowd.
If an emergency vehicle came, the officer could flip a switch and clear the intersection by triggering all red lights.
The emergency vehicle could now pass effortlessly.
Finally, in San Francisco the first red and green electric light system that could be operated automatically (or manually) was introduced in 1917.

passage.translation: 该系统使警察能够从街道中间移动到角落。从那个有利位置,警察可以监督人群。如果有紧急车辆到来,警察可以拨动开关,通过触发所有红灯来清空十字路口。紧急车辆现在可以毫不费力地通过。最后,1917年在旧金山引入了第一个可以自动(或手动)操作的红绿电子灯系统。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: In 1920, the first three-color light system was introduced in Detroit — also known as Motor City, USA.
The evolution of traffic light signals could not have a more appropriate context than Motor City.
Ford Motor Company was founded in Detroit in 1903 (and other motor companies followed).
Ford made cars affordable for more common people, rather than the wealthy, by creating larger scale factory production.

passage.translation: 1920年,第一个三色灯系统在底特律引入——也被称为美国汽车城。交通信号灯的演变在汽车城这个背景下再合适不过了。福特汽车公司于1903年在底特律成立(其他汽车公司随后跟进)。福特通过创建更大规模的工厂生产,使汽车对更普通的人而非富人来说变得可负担。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: Stop and go were insufficient for the new volumes of cars zooming through intersections.
Streets were full of new numbers of cars in addition to delivery wagons, bustling crowds, bicycles, horse- drawn carriages, and street cars.
The introduction of the cautionary yellow light helped increase driver safety, decreasing accidents that come from running red lights.

passage.translation: 对于呼啸通过十字路口的新增车辆数量来说,停止和通行是不够的。街道上除了满载的新车数量外,还有送货马车、熙攘的人群、自行车、马车和有轨电车。警示黄灯的引入有助于提高驾驶员安全性,减少闯红灯造成的事故。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: Stop lights were incredibly important in chaotic city streets.
Crosswalks weren't even introduced until 1951.
The first pedestrian fatality in the United States was in 1899.

passage.translation: 停车灯在混乱的城市街道上极其重要。人行横道甚至直到1951年才被引入。美国第一起行人死亡事故发生在1899年。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: The development of the modern traffic light may have started in London, but it grew up in the United States.
In Cleveland, an African-American inventor named Garrett Morgan came up with an affordable, patented traffic signal.
The yellow light made intersections safer than the old stop and go system.
The new design was inexpensive enough that it allowed the installation of a lot more lights.

passage.translation: 现代交通信号灯的发展可能始于伦敦,但它在美国成长起来。在克利夫兰,一位名叫Garrett Morgan的非裔美国发明家提出了一种经济实惠、获得专利的交通信号。黄灯使十字路口比旧的停止和通行系统更安全。新设计足够便宜,使得可以安装更多的灯。

passage.label: N

sentences.text: Morgan sold the patent to General Electric — and the spread of the traffic light was green lighted.
Green means go.
It is that simple, but it's still best to check both ways for oncoming traffic that may not be paying attention or is running the light.
Yellow means slow down and prepare to stop.
It does not mean full-throttle(全速) ahead.
While you may get away with gunning it into the intersection, running a yellow can lead to tickets and dangerous accidents.
Red lights are a clear and consistent warning to stop.
Even where right turns are allowed on red lights, you must come to a complete stop before turning right.
You must also yield to any through traffic, which has the right of way.
In most states and cities, you can take a right on red unless otherwise indicated.
New York City does not allow a right on red.

passage.translation: Morgan将专利出售给通用电气——交通信号灯的推广获得了绿灯。绿色意味着通行。就这么简单,但最好还是向两边查看可能没有注意或正在闯灯的迎面而来的车辆。黄色意味着减速并准备停车。它不意味着全速前进。虽然你可能侥幸冲进十字路口,但闯黄灯可能导致罚单和危险事故。红灯是明确且一致的停车警告。即使在允许红灯右转的地方,你也必须在右转前完全停车。你还必须让行任何直行车辆,它们拥有通行权。在大多数州和城市,除非另有说明,你可以在红灯时右转。纽约市不允许红灯右转。

passage.label: O

sentences.text: Red arrows mean you cannot turn right on a red in most states.
The green arrow, in these cases, is the only time you can make the turn.

However, you can take a right on a red arrow after a full stop in the states of Illinois, Kansas, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, New Hampshire, North Dakota, Oregon, South Carolina, Utah, Washington State and Wyoming.

passage.translation: 在大多数州,红色箭头意味着你不能在红灯时右转。在这些情况下,只有绿色箭头才是你可以转弯的时机。然而,在伊利诺伊州、堪萨斯州、路易斯安那州、马里兰州、密歇根州、新罕布什尔州、北达科他州、俄勒冈州、南卡罗来纳州、犹他州、华盛顿州和怀俄明州,你可以在完全停车后在红色箭头时右转。

passage.label: P

sentences.text: Flashing Red is the same as a stop sign, generally used at four-way intersections where there is minimal traffic.
When arriving at a flashing red light, make a full and complete stop.
Flashing Red Arrows similarly mean to stop and then proceed to take the turn.
Flashing Yellow lights mean yield or signal caution, like outside of a fire station.
There are no all-direction flashing yellow lights, since it is prohibited in the United States.
If you have a flashing yellow light, you are to yield to oncoming traffic.

passage.translation: 闪烁红灯与停车标志相同,通常用于交通流量最小的四向十字路口。当遇到闪烁红灯时,要完全彻底地停车。闪烁红色箭头同样意味着停车然后继续转弯。闪烁黄灯意味着让行或示意谨慎,就像在消防站外一样。美国没有全向闪烁黄灯,因为这是被禁止的。如果你有闪烁黄灯,你应该让行迎面而来的车辆。

passage.label: Q

sentences.text: Flashing Yellow Arrows are part of a four-signal traffic light.
These are used in some states after a protected green turn signal, or arrow, but before a steady yellow arrow.
When a flashing yellow arrow is shown, you can take the turn after yielding to pedestrians and traffic.
Steady Yellow Arrows maintain the normal yellow light caution in three-light signals, meaning to stop or prepare to stop.
In a four-signal system that has a flashing yellow arrow, the steady yellow arrow is a signal that the yield period is ending.
The red arrow is about to start.
Vehicles should stop if safely possible.
Traffic tickets are possible for running a steady yellow arrow.

passage.translation: 闪烁黄色箭头是四信号交通灯的一部分。在一些州,这些在受保护的绿色转向信号或箭头之后但在稳定黄色箭头之前使用。当显示闪烁黄色箭头时,你可以在让行行人和车辆后转弯。稳定黄色箭头在三灯信号中保持正常的黄灯警示,意味着停车或准备停车。在具有闪烁黄色箭头的四信号系统中,稳定黄色箭头是让行期结束的信号。红色箭头即将开始。车辆应该在安全的情况下停车。闯稳定黄色箭头可能导致交通罚单。

passage.label: R

sentences.text: Traffic light meaning is fairly consistent across the board with various deviations.
Green means it's safe to proceed (though you should still exercise caution).
Yellow means caution and yield.
Red means danger and stop.
Always drive defensively and obey traffic signals.

passage.translation: 交通灯的含义在各个方面相当一致,只有各种偏差。绿色意味着可以安全通行(尽管你仍应谨慎行事)。黄色意味着谨慎和让行。红色意味着危险和停车。始终进行防御性驾驶并遵守交通信号。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: Upon seeing a flashing yellow arrow, a driver should let pedestrians and traffic pass first before taking the turn.
questions.explanation:
**答案** Q 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
看到闪烁的黄色箭头时,驾驶员应该先让行人和车辆通过,然后再转弯。
**锚点** 闪烁黄色箭头 + 先让行后转弯
**定位** 出现闪烁的黄色箭头时，你可以在先给行人和过往车辆让行之后再转弯。
**改写** flashing yellow arrow ↔ flashing yellow arrow术语原样复现let pedestrians and traffic pass first before taking the turn ↔you can take the turn after yielding to pedestrians and traffic yield = 让行的同义改写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
P P 段同样出现 flashing yellow 等词，但讨论的是 Flashing Yellow lights mean yield or signal caution 这类整盏闪黄灯，没有提“先让行后转弯”这一动作链条，所以不是题36 的源头段。Flashing Yellow lights mean yield or signal caution, like outside of a fire station
questions.quote: When a flashing yellow arrow is shown, you can take the turn after yielding to pedestrians and traffic.

questions.prompt: The red and green automatic traffic light system originated in an American city.
questions.explanation:
**答案** I 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
红绿灯自动交通信号系统起源于一个美国城市。
**锚点** 首套自动红绿信号 + 美国城市
**定位** 最后，在旧金山，首套可自动（或手动）运行的红绿电灯系统于 1917 年问世。
**改写** red and green automatic traffic light system ↔the first red and green electric light system that could be operated automatically (or manually) automatic 与 automatically 同根改写originated in an American city ↔ in San Francisco下位地名替上位描述
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
J J 段同样讲美国城市 Detroit 与首次出现，但所述是 the first three-color light system 而非题干的 “red and green automatic”，少了“两色 + 自动”这关键限定，覆盖不全。In 1920, the first three-color light system was introduced in Detroit G G 段虽也讲红绿灯 between the dipped red and green lights，但明确说 operated manually by an officer，不是 automatic，故不是题 37 源头段。He developed a manually switched stop light
questions.quote: Finally, in San Francisco the first red and green electric light system that could be operated automatically (or manually) was introduced in 1917.

questions.prompt: Residents of an American city tend to share the opinion that time saved on the road justifies the cost of upgrading its traffic light system.
questions.explanation:
**答案** A 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
一个美国城市的居民倾向于认为在道路上节省的时间证明升级其交通信号系统的成本是合
理 的 。
**锚点** 美国某市居民认为省时间值回升级成本
**定位** 你去问问这座城市的居民，他们多半会同意：在路上省下的时间，绝对值回投入。
**改写** Residents of an American city tend to share the opinion ↔Ask a resident of the city and they are likely to agree复数与单数态度的同义改写time saved on the road justifies the cost of upgrading its traffic light system ↔saving time on the road is well worth it well worth it = 物有所值
questions.quote: Ask a resident of the city and they are likely to agree that saving time on the road is well worth it.

questions.prompt: Mass production of cars made it possible for ordinary people to buy them.
questions.explanation:
**答案** J 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
汽车的大规模生产使普通人能够购买汽车。
**锚点** 汽车的大规模生产让普通人买得起
**定位** 福特通过创立更大规模的工厂生产，使汽车不再只属于富人，而是变成普通人也买得起的东西。
**改写** Mass production of cars ↔ creating larger scale factory production工厂规模化生产 = 大规模生产made it possible for ordinary people to buy them ↔made cars affordable for more common people, rather than the wealthy affordable = made it possible to buy
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E E 段虽提及 The United States is a car culture like no other country 等汽车扩张背景，但并未陈述“大规模生产让普通人买得起汽车”这一具体机制。many cities in the United States were designed around urban sprawl, suburban tracts, and motor cars
questions.quote: Ford made cars affordable for more common people, rather than the wealthy, by creating larger scale factory production.

questions.prompt: What a traffic light means is almost the same everywhere despite some variations.
questions.explanation:
**答案** R 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
尽管存在一些差异,交通信号灯的含义在各地几乎相同。
**锚点** 信号灯含义到处几乎一样、有些差异
**定位** 总体来看，红绿灯的含义大体上保持一致，只是存在一些差异。
**改写** almost the same everywhere ↔ fairly consistent across the board across the board = everywhere despite some variations ↔ with various deviations with = despite 的让步同义
questions.quote: Traffic light meaning is fairly consistent across the board with various deviations.

questions.prompt: Pedestrian crossings came into being only in the mid-twentieth century.
questions.explanation:
**答案** L 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
人行横道仅在二十世纪中叶才出现。
**锚点** 人行横道仅在 20 世纪中叶才出现
**定位** 人行横道甚至直到 1951 年才出现。
**改写** Pedestrian crossings ↔ Crosswalks同义词替换came into being only in the mid-twentieth century ↔ weren't even introduced until 1951 until 1951 = 直到 20 世纪中叶才
questions.quote: Crosswalks weren't even introduced until 1951.

questions.prompt: People raced to address increasing traffic problems along with the expansion of cities and traffic.
questions.explanation:
**答案** F 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
随着城市和交通的扩张,人们竞相解决日益严重的交通问题。
**锚点** 城市与交通扩张 + 解决交通问题的竞赛
**定位** 随着交通和城市的扩张，解决日益严重的交通问题的竞赛也愈演愈烈。
**改写** People raced to address increasing traffic problems ↔so did the race to solve growing traffic problems race + address ≈ race + solve along with the expansion of cities and traffic ↔ As traffic and cities grew expansion 是 grew 的名词化
questions.quote: As traffic and cities grew, so did the race to solve growing traffic problems.

questions.prompt: When the warning yellow light was introduced, driving became safer and traffic accidents reduced.
questions.explanation:
**答案** K 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
当黄色警告灯被引入时,驾驶变得更加安全,交通事故减少了。
**锚点** 黄灯被引入后驾驶更安全、事故减少
**定位** 警示性黄灯的引入帮助提高了驾驶者的安全，减少了因闯红灯导致的事故。
**改写** the warning yellow light was introduced ↔ The introduction of the cautionary yellow light warning = cautionary 同义形容词driving became safer and traffic accidents reduced ↔helped increase driver safety, decreasing accidents increase driver safety = 驾驶变安全；decreasing = reduced
questions.quote: The introduction of the cautionary yellow light helped increase driver safety, decreasing accidents that come from running red lights.

questions.prompt: The signal system on the railroad served as the basis for the first traffic light.
questions.explanation:
**答案** B 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
铁路上的信号系统是第一个交通信号灯的基础。
**锚点** 铁路信号系统是首盏红绿灯的基础
**定位** 它是 1868 年由铁路经理 John Peak Knight 仿照铁路信号系统改造而来的。
**改写** The signal system on the railroad ↔ the railroad signal system of/on 与定语顺序的等价served as the basis for the first traffic light ↔It had been adapted from the railroad signal system adapted from = served as the basis for
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
F F 段把最早信号灯描述为 The first traffic signals were semaphores，并没有提到“railroad signal system” 作为基础，故不是题 44 源头段。The first traffic signals were semaphores
questions.quote: It had been adapted from the railroad signal system by a railway manager, John Peak Knight, in 1868.

questions.prompt: Even though a green light signals "go", attention should be paid to traffic on either side in case some driver is being careless or ignoring a red light.
questions.explanation:
**答案** N 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
即使绿灯表示"通行",也应注意两侧的交通情况,以防某些驾驶员粗心大意或无视红灯。
**锚点** 绿灯也要留意两侧、防有人闯红
**定位** 绿灯表示通行。就这么简单，但最好还是双向都看一下，留意那些可能心不在焉、或者正在闯灯的对向车辆。
**改写** Even though a green light signals "go" ↔ Green means go. It is that simple “signals go” 与 “means go” 同义attention should be paid to traffic on either side ↔it's still best to check both ways for oncoming traffic both ways = either side，check = pay attention in case some driver is being careless or ignoring a red light ↔may not be paying attention or is running the light running the light = ignoring a red light；not paying attention = careless
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
R R 段虽提及 Green means it's safe to proceed (though you should still exercise caution)，但没有具体说“两侧来车”和“有人闯红灯”，覆盖不到题干这两个关键细节。Green means it's safe to proceed (though you should still exercise caution)
questions.quote: Green means go. It is that simple, but it's still best to check both ways for oncoming traffic that may not be paying attention or is running the light.

title: Do You Know When to Quit Wisely?

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Projects, relationships, and jobs don't always work out as planned — and it's not always clear when to give up.
We've all repeatedly heard the saying that "quitters never win", but sometimes the best decision is to cut our losses.

passage.translation: 项目、关系和工作并不总是按计划进行——而且并不总是清楚何时应该放弃。我们都反复听过"放弃者永远不会成功"这句话,但有时最好的决定是及时止损。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: Think about that relationship you held on to even after it had run its course or the job you stayed in despite your boss making you miserable.
Many of us try to hold onto the last ray of hope, thinking we can make it work, whatever "it" is.
And while perseverance is generally an excellent quality, it may also incline you to over-invest in something that is no longer a good idea.

passage.translation: 想想那段你即使在它已经走到尽头后仍坚持的关系,或者那份尽管老板让你痛苦不堪却仍留守的工作。我们中的许多人试图抓住最后一线希望,认为我们可以让它成功,无论"它"是什么。虽然坚持不懈通常是一种优秀的品质,但它也可能使你过度投资于一件不再明智的事情。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: As an executive coach, I work with numerous passionate and hard-working leaders who don't want to "quit".
But the smartest leaders learn to discern the difference between quitting too soon and holding onto something that they shouldn't.

passage.translation: 作为一名高管教练,我与许多充满热情和勤奋工作的领导者共事,他们不想"放弃"。但最聪明的领导者学会辨别过早放弃和坚持不该坚持的事情之间的区别。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: We are all susceptible to the sunk-cost delusion, an unconscious bias that leads us to persist in an endeavor we have already invested time, effort, or money into — even when abandoning it would be more beneficial.

We realize that we can't get back the resources we've given, so we persevere —investing in a project that should be halted, staying in a relationship that should be over, or finishing a book we no longer enjoy and should put down, because we're already halfway through it.
If quitting is "not your thing", you may be especially susceptible to this bias.

passage.translation: 我们都容易受到沉没成本谬误的影响,这是一种无意识的偏见,导致我们坚持已经投入了时间、精力或金钱的事业——即使放弃它会更有益。我们意识到无法收回已经付出的资源,所以我们坚持下去——投资于应该停止的项目,待在应该结束的关系中,或者读完我们不再喜欢、应该放下的书,因为我们已经读了一半。如果放弃"不是你的风格",你可能特别容易受到这种偏见的影响。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: The sunk-cost delusion causes us to overly worry about what we'll lose if we move on and not think enough about the costs of not moving on.
To offset this bias, deliberately refocus your thinking on the gains so you can more objectively weigh the alternatives.
Ask yourself: What might I gain by cutting my losses now?
Will you be happier or have time for another (better) opportunity?
Then ask yourself: What will it cost me to soldier on?
For example, is it possible that you'll be throwing more good money after what you've already lost?
Or that you won't have the energy to capitalize on other promising possibilities?

passage.translation: 沉没成本谬误使我们过分担心如果继续前进会失去什么,而没有充分考虑不继续前进的成本。为了抵消这种偏见,有意识地将思维重新聚焦于收益,这样你就能更客观地权衡各种选择。问问自己:现在及时止损我可能获得什么?你会更快乐还是会有时间去把握另一个(更好的)机会?然后问自己:坚持下去会让我付出什么代价?例如,你是否可能在已经损失的基础上投入更多好钱?或者你是否没有精力去利用其他有前景的可能性?

passage.label: F

sentences.text: The illusion of control can also interfere with our best judgment, leading us to overestimate our ability to control events and attain a positive outcome.
This bias gives us a sense of agency and can promote mental health.
However, the bias can also result in escalating commitment to a losing course of action.
Especially when combined with an "I'm not a quitter" mentality, feeling like we have more control over an event or person than we do puts us at risk of doubling down when we should pull out.

passage.translation: 控制幻觉也会干扰我们的最佳判断,导致我们高估自己控制事件和获得积极结果的能力。这种偏见给我们一种掌控感,可以促进心理健康。然而,这种偏见也可能导致对失败行动方针的不断升级投入。特别是当与"我不是放弃者"的心态结合时,感觉我们对事件或他人的控制力比实际更强,会使我们在应该退出时加倍投入,从而面临风险。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: To counteract this bias, consider your situation and make a simple two-column list of what's in your control and what's not.
Think rigorously.
While you may be able to influence other people and various circumstances, you can't force them to change or go your way.

passage.translation: 为了抵消这种偏见,考虑你的情况并列一个简单的两栏清单,列出什么在你的控制之内,什么不在。严格思考。虽然你可能能够影响其他人和各种情况,但你不能强迫他们改变或按你的方式行事。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Getting clear on what you can control and what you can't is essential to making a quality decision about whether to call it quits or persevere.
With a written list in hand, you can ensure you focus on what you can control and better assess whether your continued efforts are worth the expense.
Expending effort and emotion on things you can't control can be both draining and disempowering.

passage.translation: 弄清楚你能控制什么和不能控制什么,对于就是否放弃还是坚持做出高质量决策至关重要。有了书面清单在手,你可以确保专注于你能控制的事情,并更好地评估你的持续努力是否值得付出代价。在你无法控制的事情上花费精力和情感既会令人疲惫又会使人丧失力量。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Research indicates that people link their self-identity and social status to their commitments.
And because we identify with our commitments, withdrawing from one can feel like a threat to our identity or status.

passage.translation: 研究表明,人们将自我认同和社会地位与他们的承诺联系在一起。因为我们认同自己的承诺,从一项承诺中退出可能感觉像是对我们身份或地位的威胁。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: Take my client Ryan, a leader at a technology company.
Ryan had invested two years and a lot of effort in a design project that wasn't delivering the needed outcomes, but the thought of abandoning it after all she had put in was hard to bear.
As Ryan and I explored whether she should cancel the initiative she'd been leading or continue to persevere, she stated, "The thing is, I'm not a quitter."
This singular, fixed sense of self was clouding her judgment and limiting her choices for action.

passage.translation: 以我的客户Ryan为例,她是一家科技公司的领导者。Ryan在一个设计项目上投入了两年时间和大量精力,但该项目没有产生所需的成果,然而在投入了这么多之后放弃它的想法让她难以承受。当Ryan和我探讨她是否应该取消她一直领导的这个项目还是继续坚持时,她说:"问题是,我不是一个放弃者。"这种单一、固定的自我意识正在影响她的判断并限制她的行动选择。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: Our self-concept and identity are mental concepts that influence our behavior.
If you strongly identify as not being a quitter, you can end up staying stuck in a course of action due to your narrow and rigid self-concept.
To overcome this kind of internal obstacle, recall your other positive traits and personality characteristics.
Ask yourself: What additional strengths do I have (or aspire to have) that would be helpful to employ here?
For example, when I asked Ryan what other positive qualities from her personality she needed to leverage for decision making, she replied, "Discernment and bravery."

passage.translation: 我们的自我概念和身份是影响我们行为的心理概念。如果你强烈认同自己不是一个放弃者,你最终可能会因为狭隘和僵化的自我概念而困在某个行动方针中。为了克服这种内在障碍,回想你的其他积极特质和性格特征。问问自己:我还有(或渴望拥有)什么额外的优势可以在这里运用?例如,当我问Ryan她需要利用自己性格中的哪些其他积极品质来进行决策时,她回答说:"辨别力和勇气。"

passage.label: L

sentences.text: Now, examine your situation through the lens of each of these facets of yourself.
What does the discerning part of you say?
The brave part?
Considering your decision through these different characteristics will enable you to see that you have more choices.
It's also helpful to seek external sources of information, rather than relying solely on your thinking and instincts.
But it's important to think through whose opinions you solicit.

passage.translation: 现在,通过你自己的这些不同方面来审视你的情况。你有辨别力的那一面说什么?勇敢的那一面呢?通过这些不同的特征来考虑你的决定将使你看到你有更多选择。寻求外部信息来源也很有帮助,而不是仅仅依赖于你的思考和直觉。但重要的是要考虑清楚你征求谁的意见。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: Ideally, seek out people who are less invested in your decision than you are.
If you're considering whether to shut down your entrepreneurial venture, for instance, reach out to other founders as opposed to just your business partner.
Similarly, if you're looking for love advice, ask someone removed from the ups and downs of your relationship instead of relying only on your best friend.
In all cases, I recommend describing your situation and following up with a question like: "How would you manage this situation?"

passage.translation: 理想情况下,寻找那些对你的决定投入程度不如你的人。例如,如果你正在考虑是否关闭你的创业企业,请联系其他创始人,而不是仅仅联系你的商业伙伴。同样,如果你在寻求爱情建议,问一个与你关系起伏保持距离的人,而不是仅仅依赖你最好的朋友。在所有情况下,我建议描述你的情况,然后提出这样的问题:"你会如何处理这种情况?"

passage.label: N

sentences.text: Alternately, you could also seek out hard data that illuminates your real chance of success in whatever endeavor you are contemplating.
Sticking with the example of the entrepreneurial venture, numbers are your best friend.
Use them to remove yourself from the love you have for this idea and consider your burn rate relative to growth plan, industry growth rates, and other factors that predict start-up success.
External sources of information can help you see angles and possibilities you might not have considered.

passage.translation: 或者,你也可以寻求能够揭示你在正在考虑的任何事业中真正成功机会的硬数据。继续以创业企业为例,数字是你最好的朋友。用它们来让自己摆脱对这个想法的热爱,考虑你的烧钱率相对于增长计划、行业增长率以及预测初创企业成功的其他因素。外部信息来源可以帮助你看到你可能没有考虑过的角度和可能性。

passage.label: O

sentences.text: When something that seemed so promising at the start doesn't turn out the way we imagined, we can become overly self-critical.
Nobody likes to feel that they've made a poor decision, especially if making intelligent decisions is a quality you hold in high esteem.
The most effective strategy here is to give yourself a break.
Practicing self-compassion increases your resilience(韧性), emotional intelligence, compassion toward others, and can boost your performance as well as help you develop a growth mindset.

passage.translation: 当一开始看起来很有希望的事情没有按我们想象的方式发展时,我们可能会变得过度自我批评。没有人喜欢感觉自己做出了糟糕的决定,特别是如果做出明智决策是你高度重视的品质。这里最有效的策略是放自己一马。练习自我同情可以增强你的韧性、情商、对他人的同情心,还可以提升你的表现并帮助你培养成长型思维。

passage.label: P

sentences.text: Instead of deliberating and criticizing yourself, focus instead on what you can learn from this situation.
For example, Ryan recognized she had developed various new skills and leadership capabilities from leading the design project.
And despite ultimately deciding to drop it, she was still happy she had tried and grateful for what the experience taught her.

passage.translation: 与其深思和批评自己,不如专注于你可以从这种情况中学到什么。例如,Ryan认识到她从领导设计项目中培养了各种新技能和领导能力。尽管最终决定放弃它,但她仍然为自己尝试过而感到高兴,并对这段经历教给她的东西心怀感激。

passage.label: Q

sentences.text: Undeniably, perseverance can help us succeed.
But for your well-being, it's important to learn how to distinguish quitting too soon and clinging to a losing course of action.
While letting go can be difficult, it will free up your time, energy, and mental space to imagine new possibilities and pursue new opportunities.

passage.translation: 不可否认,坚持不懈可以帮助我们成功。但为了你的幸福,学会如何区分过早放弃和坚持失败的行动方针是很重要的。虽然放手可能很难,但它会释放你的时间、精力和心理空间,让你想象新的可能性并追求新的机会。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: Feeling like they have more control over something or someone than they do, people get more committed to their pursuit when they should give up.
questions.explanation:
**答案** F 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
当人们感觉自己对某事或某人的控制力比实际情况更强时,他们会在本应放弃的时候对追求变得更加执着。
**锚点** 高估掌控感导致继续投入
**定位** 尤其当与"我不是放弃者"的心态结合时，觉得自己对某件事或某个人有比实际更多的掌控感，会让我们在本该退出时反而加码投入。
**改写** Feeling like they have more control over something or someone than they do ↔feeling like we have more control over an event or person than we do代词与名词的同义替换get more committed to their pursuit when they should give up ↔doubling down when we should pull out口语短语的解释式改写
questions.quote: Especially when combined with an "I'm not a quitter" mentality, feeling like we have more control over an event or person than we do puts us at risk of doubling down when we should pull out.

questions.prompt: If you regard yourself as one who never quits, you may end up trapped in your course of action.
questions.explanation:
**答案** K 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
如果你把自己看作一个从不放弃的人,你可能最终会被困在自己的行动路线中。
**锚点** 自认从不放弃者会被困住
**定位** 如果你强烈地把自己认同为不是一个放弃者，那么你会因为狭隘僵化的自我概念，最终被困在某一行动路线里。
**改写** If you regard yourself as one who never quits ↔ If you strongly identify as not being a quitter动词与短语同义替换trapped in your course of action ↔ staying stuck in a course of action近义动词同义替换
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
F F段出现了I'm not a quitter这一相同表述，容易让人误以为是源头段；但它的核心论点是控制错觉与该心态叠加导致doubling down，并不是题干所说的trapped in your course of action。Especially when combined with an "I'm not a quitter" mentality, feeling like we have more control over an event or person than we do puts us at risk of doubling down when we should pull out.
questions.quote: If you strongly identify as not being a quitter, you can end up staying stuck in a course of action due to your narrow and rigid self-concept.

questions.prompt: One of the author's clients found it hard to give up a design project, in which she had put in a lot of time and effort.
questions.explanation:
**答案** J 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
作者的一位客户发现很难放弃一个设计项目,她在这个项目上投入了大量时间和精力。
**锚点** 客户与设计项目的难放手
**定位** Ryan在一个迟迟拿不出预期成果的设计项目上投入了两年时间和大量精力，但一想到要在投入这么多之后放弃它就难以承受。
**改写** One of the author's clients ↔ my client Ryan专名与泛指对应found it hard to give up a design project ↔the thought of abandoning it after all she had put in was hard to bear形容词短语同义替换in which she had put in a lot of time and effort ↔invested two years and a lot of effort in a design project具体时长概括为时间
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
P P段同样提到leading the design project，但内容是Ryan从中获得new skills and leadership capabilities并感激这段经历；它叙述的是后续学习与释怀，不是题干强调的found it hard to give up这一时刻。Ryan recognized she had developed various new skills and leadership capabilities from leading the design project.
questions.quote: Ryan had invested two years and a lot of effort in a design project that wasn't delivering the needed outcomes, but the thought of abandoning it after all she had put in was hard to bear.

questions.prompt: The author suggests that one should direct their thoughts to the gains of quitting timely so as to move on.
questions.explanation:
**答案** E 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
作者建议人们应该将思绪转向及时放弃所能获得的收益,以便继续前进。
**锚点** 把思考转向及时放弃的收益
**定位** 为抵消这一偏差，要刻意把思考重心转向收益，这样你才能更客观地权衡各种选择。
**改写** direct their thoughts to the gains ↔ refocus your thinking on the gains动词与名词同义替换the gains of quitting timely ↔ What might I gain by cutting my losses now?及时止损的同义表达so as to move on ↔ so you can more objectively weigh the alternatives目的状语的概括式改写
questions.quote: To offset this bias, deliberately refocus your thinking on the gains so you can more objectively weigh the alternatives.

questions.prompt: When making a decision, you'd better ask for opinions of those who have less stake in your decision.
questions.explanation:
**答案** M 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
在做决定时,你最好征求那些在你的决定中利益关系较小的人的意见。
**锚点** 向利益相关度低的人征询
**定位** 理想情况下，要找那些比你在这项决定中投入度更低的人征询意见。
**改写** ask for opinions of those who have less stake in your decision ↔seek out people who are less invested in your decision than you are动词与利益关系词同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
L L段只说seek external sources of information, rather than relying solely on your thinking and instincts并提示要think through whose opinions you solicit，把谁来征询这一具体回答推到下一段；它没有less stake这层意思，因此不是源头段。It's also helpful to seek external sources of information, rather than relying solely on your thinking and instincts. But it's important to think through whose opinions you solicit.
questions.quote: Ideally, seek out people who are less invested in your decision than you are.

questions.prompt: For people associating their identity with their commitments, quitting can feel like their identity is threatened.
questions.explanation:
**答案** I 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
对于那些将身份认同与承诺联系在一起的人来说,放弃可能会让他们感觉自己的身份认同受到了
威 胁 。
**锚点** 身份与承诺挂钩
**定位** 研究表明，人们会把自我认同与社会地位与自己的承诺挂钩。正因为我们把自己等同于这些承诺，退出其中一项就会让人觉得像是对身份或地位的威胁。
**改写** associating their identity with their commitments ↔people link their self-identity and social status to their commitments动词同义替换quitting can feel like their identity is threatened ↔withdrawing from one can feel like a threat to our identity or status动名词被动改写
questions.quote: Research indicates that people link their self-identity and social status to their commitments. And because we identify with our commitments, withdrawing from one can feel like a threat to our identity or status.

questions.prompt: People who regard highly the quality of making wise decisions do not feel good when they make a bad one.
questions.explanation:
**答案** O 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
高度重视做出明智决策这一品质的人在做出错误决定时不会感觉良好。
**锚点** 看重明智决策者面对坏决定的感受
**定位** 没有人喜欢觉得自己做了一个糟糕的决定，尤其当你把做出明智决定视为自己很看重的品质时。
**改写** regard highly the quality of making wise decisions ↔making intelligent decisions is a quality you hold in high esteem动词短语与形容词同义do not feel good when they make a bad one ↔Nobody likes to feel that they've made a poor decision否定改写+近义形容词
questions.quote: Nobody likes to feel that they've made a poor decision, especially if making intelligent decisions is a quality you hold in high esteem.

questions.prompt: The wisest leaders learn to distinguish between giving up too soon and sticking with something irrationally.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
最明智的领导者学会区分过早放弃和非理性地坚持某事。
**锚点** 最聪明领导者懂得分辨
**定位** 但最聪明的领导者会学着分辨过早放弃与不该坚持却继续坚持之间的差别。
**改写** The wisest leaders ↔ the smartest leaders近义形容词最高级distinguish between giving up too soon and sticking with something irrationally ↔discern the difference between quitting too soon and holding onto something that they shouldn't动词与短语的同义概括
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
Q Q段出现learn how to distinguish quitting too soon and clinging to a losing course of action这一与题干高度相似的并置，是最容易让人误选的相邻段；但它谈的对象是普遍意义的人，并未限定The wisest leaders这一主语，故不是源头段。But for your well-being, it's important to learn how to distinguish quitting too soon and clinging to a losing course of action.
questions.quote: But the smartest leaders learn to discern the difference between quitting too soon and holding onto something that they shouldn't.

questions.prompt: When people are thinking of an endeavor, they should dig out reliable data that tells them how likely they are to succeed.
questions.explanation:
**答案** N 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
当人们考虑一项事业时,他们应该挖掘能够告诉他们成功可能性有多大的可靠数据。
**锚点** 用可靠数据评估成功概率
**定位** 或者，你也可以去寻找能够照亮你成功真实概率的硬数据，无论你在考虑哪种事业。
**改写** dig out reliable data ↔ seek out hard data动词与形容词同义how likely they are to succeed ↔ your real chance of success名词短语改写为从句When people are thinking of an endeavor ↔ in whatever endeavor you are contemplating近义动词替换
questions.quote: Alternately, you could also seek out hard data that illuminates your real chance of success in whatever endeavor you are contemplating.

questions.prompt: Having a clear view of what's in your control and what's not is vital to making a good decision regarding whether to give up or stick it out.
questions.explanation:
**答案** H 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
清楚地了解什么在你的控制范围内、什么不在你的控制范围内,对于就是否放弃还是坚持做出正确决定至关重要。
**锚点** 看清可控与否对决策至关重要

**改写** Having a clear view of what's in your control and what's not↔Getting clear on what you can control and what you can't动名词短语同义vital to making a good decision↔ essential to making a quality decision近义形容词同义whether to give up or stick it out↔whether to call it quits or persevere并置短语整体同义

G G段聚焦工具：make a simple two-column list of what's in your control and what's not；它没有vital to making a good decision这层论点，因此不是源头段。To counteract this bias, consider your situation and make a simple two-column list of what's in your control and what's not.
questions.quote: Getting clear on what you can control and what you can't is essential to making a quality decision about whether to call it quits or persevere.

title: Restaurants Are Now Employing Robots — Should Chefs Be Worried?

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Like most chefs, Flippy is not afraid of hard work.
Since last summer, that has meant 11 am until 7 pm shifts at Caliburger in Pasadena, California, as well as short assignments at Chick-N-Tots at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles.
These are long hours of repetitive work, where the boss demands absolute consistency.
But you won't hear Flippy complain or say anything, in fact.
For Flippy is a robot — a cloud-connected mechanical arm with 3D thermal scanners for eyes — that can flip burgers or fry 80 baskets of food an hour, monitor that food and even clean up afterwards.

passage.translation: 和大多数厨师一样,Flippy不惧怕辛苦工作。自去年夏天以来,这意味着在加利福尼亚州帕萨迪纳的Caliburger餐厅从上午11点工作到晚上7点,以及在洛杉矶道奇体育场的Chick-N-Tots短期值班。这些都是长时间的重复性工作,老板要求绝对的一致性。但你不会听到Flippy抱怨或说任何话,事实上。因为Flippy是一个机器人——一个云连接的机械臂,配有3D热扫描仪作为眼睛——它可以翻转汉堡或每小时油炸80篮食物,监控食物,甚至之后清理。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: Flippy was created by Miso Robotics, part of the Cali Group, which is described by its CEO, John Miller, as: "A technology company that happens to sell cheeseburgers."
Cali creates new machines that it road-tests in its Caliburger restaurants across the world, into which Flippy will be deployed this year.
And Flippy is not alone.
Also in California, Bear Robotics has developed a self-guiding robot, Penny, which has so far served 40,000 diners.

passage.translation: Flippy由Miso Robotics创造,该公司是Cali Group的一部分,其首席执行官John Miller将其描述为:"一家恰好销售芝士汉堡的科技公司。"Cali创造新机器,并在其遍布全球的Caliburger餐厅进行路测,Flippy将于今年部署到这些餐厅。而且Flippy并不孤单。同样在加利福尼亚,Bear Robotics开发了一个自导航机器人Penny,迄今为止已为4万名食客提供服务。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: Ten years ago, robot-chefs and waiters were pure science fiction.
Today, they are a reality, and at prices that make them a plausible investment.
From May, Penny will be shipped on a subscription basis that offers "an immediate return", says Bear Robotics' chief operating officer, Juan Higueros.
Flippy will cost a reported $60,000 to $100,000.
Fully automated burger restaurants managed with minimal human oversight — where customers order at screens, pay electronically, and eat food cooked and delivered by robots — are now a possibility.

passage.translation: 十年前,机器人厨师和服务员纯属科幻小说。今天,它们成为现实,而且价格使它们成为合理的投资。Bear Robotics的首席运营官Juan Higueros说,从5月起,Penny将以订阅方式发货,提供"即时回报"。据报道Flippy的成本将在6万至10万美元之间。由最少人工监督管理的全自动汉堡餐厅——顾客在屏幕上点餐,电子支付,食用由机器人烹饪和配送的食物——现在已成为可能。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: The technology exists; it just needs knitting together cost-effectively and in a way diners buy into.
In an industry keen to slash labor costs and increase profits, further automation seems inevitable.
After an eight-month test at Kang Nam Tofu House in California, Bear Robotics credited Penny with driving a 28% increase in sales.
Meanwhile, in US trials, the self-ordering screens that McDonald's is currently installing at its 1,300 UK restaurants yielded a reported 30% rise in order values.

passage.translation: 技术已经存在;它只需要以经济有效的方式整合在一起,并以食客接受的方式呈现。在一个热衷于削减劳动力成本和增加利润的行业中,进一步自动化似乎是不可避免的。在加利福尼亚江南豆腐屋进行为期八个月的测试后,Bear Robotics认为Penny推动了销售额增长28%。与此同时,在美国的试验中,麦当劳目前正在其英国1300家餐厅安装的自助点餐屏幕据报道使订单价值增长了30%。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Personalisation is seen as key to the appeal of this technology, alongside its ability to reliably push so-called "upsells" (meal deals, extras, larger drinks) to customers.

Soon when you log into a restaurant app, it will be able to use your data and purchasing history to recommend dishes to you— factoring in everything from the weather to, if you are ordering at a screen that can read your face, your mood.

passage.translation: 个性化被视为这项技术吸引力的关键,以及它能够可靠地向顾客推送所谓"追加销售"(套餐,额外食品,更大份饮料)的能力。很快,当你登录餐厅应用程序时,它将能够使用你的数据和购买历史向你推荐菜肴——从天气到,如果你在可以读取你面部表情的屏幕上点餐,你的心情,都会被考虑在内。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: "Right now people compromise on choice.
We're presented with a one-size-fits-all menu.
Ultimately, technology can allow us to make personal choices.
You love spicy food and chicken?
Here's the dish people like you mostly order," says Tom Weaver, CEO at the hospitality tech company Flyt.
He talks enthusiastically about the Helsinki pop-up Take-In, a full-service restaurant where diners ordered dishes in from various delivery services.
"For the first time in a few hundred years, digital is allowing us to create new versions of restaurants."

passage.translation: "现在人们在选择上妥协。我们面对的是一刀切的菜单。最终,技术可以让我们做出个人选择。你喜欢辣味食物和鸡肉?这是像你这样的人最常点的菜,"酒店科技公司Flyt的首席执行官Tom Weaver说。他热情地谈论赫尔辛基的快闪餐厅Take-In,这是一家全方位服务餐厅,食客从各种配送服务订购菜肴。"几百年来第一次,数字技术让我们能够创造新版本的餐厅。"

passage.label: G

sentences.text: If high-street fast food is automation-ready, its impact on high-end restaurants is likely to be subtler and slower.
"It'll probably be a very long time before we see a five-star robot-chef," says Noel Sharkey, professor of AI and robotics at the University of Sheffield.
"Apart from the AI creativity gap, great cooking involves a subtle understanding of ingredients and delicate cooking that would be enormously challenging for robots.
Placing fragile foods on plates would be incredibly slow."

passage.translation: 如果街头快餐已为自动化做好准备,那么它对高端餐厅的影响可能会更微妙、更缓慢。"我们可能要很长时间才能看到五星级机器人厨师,"谢菲尔德大学人工智能和机器人技术教授Noel Sharkey说。"除了人工智能的创造力差距之外,出色的烹饪涉及对食材的微妙理解和精细烹饪,这对机器人来说将是极具挑战性的。将易碎的食物摆放在盘子上会非常缓慢。"

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Currently, robots have limited functionality.
A human needs to load Penny with plates that diners lift off themselves.
At the robot-powered US pizza-delivery company Zume, the more difficult jobs, such as topping pizzas, are still done by humans.
But Moley, which will launch soon, offers an idea of the sophistication to come.
Modelled on the movements of a MasterChef contest winner, Tim Anderson, its robotic arms are fixed over a stove and programmed to prepare dishes from raw ingredients.
It is designed for domestic use, but a commercial version is planned that opens up the possibility of restaurant kitchens automating even highly technically challenging tasks.

passage.translation: 目前,机器人的功能有限。需要人类为Penny装载盘子,食客自己取下。在机器人驱动的美国披萨配送公司Zume,更困难的工作,如在披萨上添加配料,仍由人类完成。但即将推出的Moley提供了未来复杂性的想法。其机械臂以MasterChef比赛获胜者Tim Anderson的动作为模型,固定在炉灶上方,并编程从原材料准备菜肴。它是为家庭使用而设计的,但计划推出商业版本,这为餐厅厨房自动化甚至高度技术性挑战的任务提供了可能性。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: For now, the kitchen technology that QSR Automations supplies to Mitchells & Butlers' pubs or KFC is less glamorous.
Rather than having a chef shouting out diners' orders, the QSR system automatically distributes those orders across screens.
The kitchen screens then tell chefs when to start cooking each dish, so that your plate of fish, chips and peas comes together at the right time.

passage.translation: 目前,QSR Automations向Mitchells & Butlers酒吧或肯德基提供的厨房技术没那么引人注目。QSR系统不是让厨师大声喊出食客的订单,而是自动将这些订单分配到各个屏幕上。然后厨房屏幕告诉厨师何时开始烹饪每道菜,这样你的鱼、薯条和豌豆就能在合适的时间一起上桌。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: The restaurant industry is currently suffering a severe shortage of skilled chefs — a deficit of 11,000, according to the skills agency People 1st.
"Automation systems designed to make the process more idiot-proof are trying to bridge that gap," says Stefan Chomka, the editor of Restaurant magazine.

passage.translation: 餐饮业目前正遭受熟练厨师的严重短缺——根据技能机构People 1st的数据,缺口为1.1万人。"旨在使流程更加简单易行的自动化系统正试图弥合这一差距,"《餐厅》杂志编辑Stefan Chomka说。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: In terms of simplifying or enhancing the customer experience, online restaurant booking has been the easily-won success of the internet age.
Automated at-table ordering and payment is seen as the next landmark.
Until then, early adopters, such as the Manchester bar owner Andy Smith, who uses the Ordoo app at his venue 33 Oldham Street, may well experience growing but "lower than expected" acceptance.

passage.translation: 就简化或增强顾客体验而言,在线餐厅预订一直是互联网时代轻松获得的成功。桌边自动点餐和支付被视为下一个里程碑。在那之前,早期采用者,如曼彻斯特酒吧老板Andy Smith,他在其场所33 Oldham Street使用Ordoo应用程序,很可能会经历不断增长但"低于预期"的接受度。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: Embarrassing failures in restaurant tech frequently hit the headlines.
The TGI Fridays drone(无人机) that injured a Brooklyn Daily photographer; US burger chain Shake Shack having to retreat from plans for entirely cashless ordering sites.
But, says Chomka, such technology could miss the mark if it only offers "solutions to problems that don't really exist".
"Payments being automatic" could be useful, he adds.
But, in an expensive restaurant, "how quick do you need dinner to be?"

passage.translation: 餐厅技术中的尴尬失败经常登上头条。TGI Fridays的无人机伤害了Brooklyn Daily的摄影师;美国汉堡连锁店Shake Shack不得不放弃完全无现金点餐站点的计划。但是,Chomka说,如果这种技术只提供"对实际上不存在的问题的解决方案",它可能会偏离目标。他补充说,"支付自动化"可能是有用的。但是,在一家昂贵的餐厅,"你需要晚餐有多快?"

passage.label: M

sentences.text: That attachment to the human art of hospitality will be heartening for staff who see automation as a threat to jobs.
"Unite is concerned that without safeguards, any benefits will bypass workers in low- paying jobs, such as waiters," says the union's London regional officer, Dave Turnbull.
"We're urging Members of Parliament to ensure automation does not just benefit a wealthy few like previous industrial revolutions."

passage.translation: 对人类待客艺术的这种依恋将让那些将自动化视为工作威胁的员工感到鼓舞。"Unite担心,如果没有保障措施,任何好处都将绕过低薪工作的工人,如服务员,"该工会的伦敦地区官员Dave Turnbull说。"我们敦促国会议员确保自动化不会像以前的工业革命那样只让少数富人受益。"

passage.label: N

sentences.text: The industry principle is that automation will allow it to redeploy staff more effectively.
Jobs will change, if not immediately decrease in number.
"Self-order screens mean more demand for people front-of-house.
Last year, we recruited 1,000 new managers," says McDonald's COO, Jason Clark.
Caliburger has a programme to retrain staff as robot engineers or "chef techs".

passage.translation: 行业原则是自动化将使其能够更有效地重新部署员工。工作将发生变化,即使数量不会立即减少。"自助点餐屏幕意味着对前台人员的更多需求。去年,我们招聘了1000名新经理,"麦当劳首席运营官Jason Clark说。Caliburger有一个项目将员工重新培训为机器人工程师或"厨师技术员"。

passage.label: O

sentences.text: But ultimately the chance to reduce overheads(管理费用) by employing fewer people or at lower rates will be what attracts big brands to technology.
Invariably, over the next 10 years, jobs will go in conventional bricks-built restaurants, not least because automation will boost their rapidly growing rival: delivery.
Companies such as Domino and Just Eat have both experimented with robot and drone delivery, which is already legal in Reykjavik, Iceland.
"Robot food deliveries are the future," says Noel Sharkey.
"Small, 4 mph ground robots are safe and will work 24 hours a day."

passage.translation: 但最终,通过雇用更少的人或以更低的薪酬来减少管理费用的机会将是吸引大品牌采用技术的原因。在未来10年,传统实体餐厅的工作岗位将不可避免地减少,尤其是因为自动化将促进其快速增长的竞争对手:配送。Domino和Just Eat等公司都尝试过机器人和无人机配送,这在冰岛雷克雅未克已经合法。"机器人食品配送是未来,"Noel Sharkey说。"小型、时速4英里的地面机器人是安全的,将24小时工作。"

passage.label: P

sentences.text: Combined with machine learning of anticipated order volumes and the minute-by-minute cooking data generated by systems such as QSR, that robot fleet could deliver almost instantly.
"Restaurants will prepare food ahead of orders coming in," predicts Just Eat's director of engineering, Daniel Richardson.
"I'll be able to say 'Let's have pizza' to my family, my intelligent assistant will hear and 10 minutes later the food will be at my door."
No one is putting an exact date on it yet.
But in the dining room and on your doorstep, the robots are coming.

passage.translation: 结合对预期订单量的机器学习以及QSR等系统生成的逐分钟烹饪数据,该机器人车队几乎可以即时配送。"餐厅将在订单到来之前准备食物,"Just Eat的工程总监Daniel Richardson预测。"我可以对我的家人说'我们吃披萨吧',我的智能助理会听到,10分钟后食物就会送到我家门口。"还没有人给出确切的日期。但在餐厅和你家门口,机器人即将到来。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
