**辨邻**
N 该段是 Jobs will change, if not immediately decrease in number，落点在岗位结构而非"人性化待客带来的宽慰"。The industry principle is that automation will allow it to redeploy staff more effectively
questions.quote: That attachment to the human art of hospitality will be heartening for staff who see automation as a threat to jobs.

questions.prompt: There is an acute shortage of experienced chefs in the catering industry and automated cooking is expected to fill the gap.
questions.explanation:
**答案** J 段（弱锚点）
**题目译文**
餐饮业存在经验丰富的厨师严重短缺的问题,自动化烹饪有望填补这一空白。
**锚点** 厨师严重短缺＋自动化补缺
**定位** 餐饮业目前正遭遇熟练厨师的严重短缺——据技能机构 People 1st 称缺口达 11000 人。《Restaurant》杂志编辑 Stefan Chomka 说："旨在让流程更傻瓜化的自动化系统正试图弥合这一缺口。"
**改写** an acute shortage of experienced chefs ↔ a severe shortage of skilled chefs成对近义词替换automated cooking is expected to fill the gap ↔Automation systems … are trying to bridge that gap近义动词替换
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
N 该段是 more demand for people front-of-house，与题干"短缺＋补缺"不是同一命题。Self-order screens mean more demand for people front-of-house
questions.quote: The restaurant industry is currently suffering a severe shortage of skilled chefs — a deficit of 11,000, according to the skills agency People 1st. "Automation systems designed to make the process more idiot-proof are trying to bridge that gap," says Stefan Chomka, the editor of Restaurant magazine.

questions.prompt: Over the coming decade, many jobs in traditional restaurants will disappear due to robot delivery.
questions.explanation:
**答案** O 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
在未来十年中,由于机器人配送,传统餐厅的许多工作岗位将会消失。
**锚点** 十年内传统餐厅岗位因送餐消失
**定位** 无可避免地，未来十年，传统砖砌实体餐厅里的岗位将会消失，尤其因为自动化会助推它们快速增长的对手——外卖配送。
**改写** Over the coming decade, many jobs in traditional restaurants will disappear ↔over the next 10 years, jobs will go in conventional bricks-built restaurants近义词替换due to robot delivery ↔ automation will boost their rapidly growing rival: delivery因果还原
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
P 该段是 that robot fleet could deliver almost instantly，落点在送达速度，无题干的"岗位消失"。Restaurants will prepare food ahead of orders coming in N 该段是 Jobs will change, if not immediately decrease in number，与题干"will disappear"立场相反。Jobs will change, if not immediately decrease in number
questions.quote: Invariably, over the next 10 years, jobs will go in conventional bricks-built restaurants, not least because automation will boost their rapidly growing rival: delivery.

questions.prompt: According to an expert in AI and robotics, it may be quite some time before a master robot-chef appears.
questions.explanation:
**答案** G 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
根据一位人工智能和机器人技术专家的说法,可能还需要相当长的时间才会出现大师级机器人
厨 师 。
**锚点** AI 专家称大师机器人厨师尚远
**定位** "我们要见到五星级机器人厨师，恐怕还得很久很久，"谢菲尔德大学的 AI 与机器人学教授Noel Sharkey 说。
**改写** an expert in AI and robotics ↔ professor of AI and robotics上位词替换quite some time before a master robot-chef appears ↔a very long time before we see a five-star robot-chef近义词替换
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
O 该段是 Robot food deliveries are the future，话题为配送，与题干"机器人厨师尚远"无关。Robot food deliveries are the future H 该段是 offers an idea of the sophistication to come，与题干"还要很久"的判断方向不同。Moley, which will launch soon, offers an idea of the sophistication to come
questions.quote: "It'll probably be a very long time before we see a five-star robot-chef," says Noel Sharkey, professor of AI and robotics at the University of Sheffield.

title: The other day I had to log into…

sentences.text: The other day I had to log into a service I hadn't used before.
Since I was a new user, the website decided that it needed to check I wasn't a robot and so set me a Captcha test to determine whether the user is a person or a machine.

passage.translation: 前几天我不得不登录一个之前从未使用过的服务。由于我是新用户,该网站决定需要检查我不是机器人,于是让我完成一项验证码测试来确定用户是人还是机器。

sentences.text: I was presented with an image of a roadside scene over which was laid a grid.
My "challenge" was to click on each cell in the grid that contained a traffic sign.
I did so, a bit irritated.
Then I was presented with another image and another grid — also with a request to identify road signs.
Like a lamb, I complied, after which the website accepted my input.

passage.translation: 我看到一张路边场景的图片,上面覆盖着一个网格。我的"挑战"是点击网格中包含交通标志的每个单元格。我有点恼火地照做了。然后我又看到另一张图片和另一个网格——同样要求识别道路标志。我像只羔羊一样顺从了,之后网站接受了我的输入。

sentences.text: And then I realised what I had been doing was adding to a dataset for training the machine- learning software that guides self-driving cars.
So, to gain access to an automated service that will benefit financially from my input, I first have to do some unpaid labor to help improve the performance of autonomous vehicles.

passage.translation: 然后我意识到我一直在做的事情是为训练指导自动驾驶汽车的机器学习软件添加数据集。所以,为了获得一项将从我的输入中获得经济利益的自动化服务,我首先必须做一些无偿劳动来帮助提高自动驾驶车辆的性能。

sentences.text: Neat, eh?
But note also the delicious additional irony that the Captcha is described as an "automated Turing test".
The Turing test was conceived, you may recall, as a way of enabling humans to determine whether a machine could respond in such a way that one couldn't tell whether it was a human or a robot.
So we have wandered into a world in which machines make us do tricks to prove that we are humans!

passage.translation: 巧妙,是吧?但也请注意额外的绝妙讽刺,验证码被描述为"自动化图灵测试"。你可能记得,图灵测试的设想是一种让人类能够确定机器是否能以一种无法分辨它是人还是机器人的方式做出反应的方法。所以我们已经步入了一个机器让我们做把戏来证明我们是人类的世界!

sentences.text: The strangest aspect of this unparalleled shift is how under-discussed it has been.
The metaphor of the boiling frog comes to mind.
Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don't see what's been happening to us?
Have we been conditioned to accept a world governed by "smart" tech, trading convenience to the point where we become a bit like machines ourselves?

passage.translation: 这一史无前例转变最奇怪的方面是它讨论得如此之少。温水煮青蛙的比喻浮现在脑海中。我们是否已经被数字技术如此微妙地训化,以至于我们看不到发生在我们身上的事情?我们是否已经被训化到接受一个由"智能"技术统治的世界,为了便利而交易到我们自己都变得有点像机器的地步?

sentences.text: In a recent startling and thoughtful book, two scholars — Brett Frischmann, a law professor, and Evan Selinger, a philosopher — argue that the answer to that question is "yes".

passage.translation: 在最近一本令人震惊且发人深省的书中,两位学者——法学教授Brett Frischmann和哲学家Evan Selinger——认为这个问题的答案是"是的"。

sentences.text: And they're right.
There's nothing technophobic(技术恐惧的) about that.
We shape our tools and then our tools shape us.
Technology is supposed to provide tools that serve human ends.
But, as the machine-learning Captcha demonstrates, a significant proportion of digital tech now sees (and uses) humans as means to ends that are not ours.
In the process, they reduce us to the status of cheery rats running on treadmills(踏⻋) designed by people who do not have our interests at heart.
So back to the frog metaphor.
Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late?
You don't even have to Google it to know the answer.

passage.translation: 他们是对的。这并没有任何技术恐惧的成分。我们塑造我们的工具,然后我们的工具塑造我们。技术本应提供服务于人类目的的工具。但是,正如机器学习验证码所展示的,相当大比例的数字技术现在将人类视为(并利用为)达成并非我们自己目的的手段。在这个过程中,它们把我们降低到快乐地在由不以我们利益为重的人设计的踏车上奔跑的老鼠的地位。所以回到青蛙的比喻。我们是否足够聪明在为时已晚之前跳出来?你甚至不必谷歌搜索就知道答案。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A) , B) , C) and D) . You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: How did the author respond to the Captcha test?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者是如何回应验证码测试的?
A) 他随机点击了单元格。
B) 他欣然接受了挑战。
C) 他自信地完成了测试。
D) 他顺从地完成了测试。
**判型** How did the author respond to the Captcha test? 问的是作者在原文里具体做了什么、什么态度，需要回到原文找事实，而不是推断或概括。
**拆句** How did the author respond to the Captcha test? 句式平铺直叙，主谓宾清楚，无陷阱。
**定位** 我像一只羔羊一样照办了，之后网站接受了我的输入。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念clicked on the cells randomly 说作者随机点，但原文 My "challenge" was to click on each cell in the grid that contained a traffic sign. I did so 显示作者是按规则点含交通标志的格子，并不是随机。
B) 与原文相反accepted the challenge readily 说"欣然接受"，但原文 I did so, a bit irritated 明示作者是带着不快接受的，二者情绪极性相反。
C) 无中生有completed it confidently 说"自信地完成"，但原文从未描写作者的信心，只说他不情愿地照办；自信纯属添加。
D) ✓ 正确Like a lamb, I complied ↔ submissively预判要的就是"顺从地照做"，He worked on it submissively. 是唯一把这层顺从语气保留下来的选项。
questions.quote: Like a lamb, I complied, after which the website accepted my input.

options.text: He clicked on the cells randomly.
He accepted the challenge readily.
He completed it confidently.
He worked on it submissively.

questions.prompt: What is ironic about the Captcha test?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
验证码测试的讽刺之处是什么?
A) 机器能像人类一样回应测试。
B) 机器在物体识别方面的表现能超过人类。
C) 一项原本设计用来测试机器的测试现在被机器用来测试人类。
D) 一项原本用于区分人类和机器人的测试现在能做人类做不到的事情。
**判型** What is ironic about the Captcha test? 要求回到原文找出作者点明讽刺的那一句，是事实层细节。
**拆句** What is ironic about the Captcha test? 结构简单，is 后跟形容词作表语，无陷阱。
**定位** 但还要注意一个绝妙的额外讽刺：Captcha 被称作"自动化的图灵测试"。你或许记得，图灵测试当初的设想，是让人类来判断机器能否做出让人分不清是人还是机器人的回应。结果，我们如今竟漂入了这样一个世界——机器反过来让我们耍把戏，以证明我们是人类！
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问A machine can respond to the test as well as humans do 是"机器答得和人一样好"，但原文讽刺的是"角色反转"，不是机器表现优秀。
B) 无中生有A machine can outperform humans in object identification 说"机器在物体识别上胜过人类"，但原文没做这种性能比较，纯属添加。
C) ✓ 正确The Turing test was conceived, you may recall, as a way of enabling humans to determine whether a machine could respond↔ A test designed to test machines machines make us do tricks to prove that we are humans↔now used by machines to test humans预判要的就是"测机器→测人"的角色反转，A test designed to test machines is now used by machines to test humans. 一句话把这一组对调说清楚。
D) 张冠李戴A test conceived to tell a human from a robot can now do tricks humans can't说"测试现在能耍出人耍不出的把戏"，主体被换成了"测试"，但原文是 machines make us do tricks——机器让我们耍把戏，主体错位。
questions.quote: But note also the delicious additional irony that the Captcha is described as an "automated Turing test". The Turing test was conceived, you may recall, as a way of enabling humans to determine whether a machine could respond in such a way that one couldn't tell whether it was a human or a robot. So we have wandered into a world in which machines make us do tricks to prove that we are humans!

options.text: A machine can respond to the test as well as humans do.
A machine can outperform humans in object identification.
A test designed to test machines is now used by machines to test humans.
A test conceived to tell a human from a robot can now do tricks humans can't.

questions.prompt: Why does the author use the metaphor of the boiling frog?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （推断题）
**题目译文**
作者为什么使用温水煮青蛙的比喻?
A) 为了表明人类不愿意用便利换取对智能技术的控制。
B) 为了表明人类没有意识到智能技术带来的潜在危险。
C) 为了质疑人类是否习惯于接受数字技术。
D) 为了质疑人类是否像被煮的青蛙一样脆弱。
**判型** Why does the author use the metaphor of the boiling frog? 问的是"作者为什么用"这个比喻，需要从比喻所在语境向上提炼一步作者意图。
**拆句** Why does the author use the metaphor of the boiling frog? 标准疑问句结构，of 短语作 metaphor 的后置定语，无陷阱。
**定位** 脑海里浮现出"温水煮青蛙"的比喻。我们是不是已经被数字技术悄悄驯化，以至于看不到自己身上正在发生什么？
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反humans are unwilling to trade convenience for control by smart tech 说人"不愿"用便利换控制，但原文 trading convenience to the point where we become a bit like machines ourselves 显示人正在交换，不是不愿；极性翻转。
B) ✓ 正确Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don't see what's been happening to us?↔ humans are unaware of the potential danger brought by smart tech so subtly conditioned by digital technology ↔ potential danger brought by smart tech温水煮青蛙寓意的核心就是"察觉不到"，To show that humans are unaware of the potential danger brought by smart tech. 同时覆盖"潜在危险"与"未察觉"两层，最贴合作者意图。
C) 偷换概念To question whether humans are conditioned to accept digital tech 说作者"质疑"人是否被驯化，但原文虽用反问，立场是倾向于"已被驯化"，并不是中立质疑。
D) 偷换概念To question whether humans are as vulnerable as the boiling frog 把比喻意图框成"人是否像青蛙一样脆弱"，但温水煮青蛙寓意的核心是"察觉不到"而非"脆弱"，焦点跑偏。
questions.quote: The metaphor of the boiling frog comes to mind. Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don't see what's been happening to us?

options.text: To show that humans are unwilling to trade convenience for control by smart tech.
To show that humans are unaware of the potential danger brought by smart tech.
To question whether humans are conditioned to accept digital tech.
To question whether humans are as vulnerable as the boiling frog.

questions.prompt: Why does the author think that Brett Frischmann and Evan Selinger are right?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**

A) 很大一部分数字技术现在正在利用人类来实现其自身目的。
B) 人类现在正与数字技术展开一场争夺世界控制权的竞赛。
C) 数字技术能以以前认为不可能的方式满足人类需求。
D) 数字技术现在在进行思考,而人类在做重复性工作。
**判型** Why does the author think that Brett Frischmann and Evan Selinger are right? 要求回到原文找作者表态后紧接给出的论据句，属事实细节。
**拆句** Why does the author think that Brett Frischmann and Evan Selinger are right? 是疑问句 + that 引导的宾语从句，think 后省略 that 也成立，主干清晰，无陷阱。
**定位** 他们说得没错。这并不是什么技术恐惧。我们塑造工具，反过来工具也塑造我们。技术本应提供服务于人类目的的工具。但是，正如机器学习版 Captcha 所展示的那样，相当一部分数字技术如今把人类当作（并加以利用为）实现非人类目的之手段。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确a significant proportion of digital tech ↔ A large part of digital tech now sees (and uses) humans as means to ends that are not ours ↔now making use of humans to meet its own ends预判要的是"技术把人当工具达成自身目的"，A large part of digital tech is now making use of humans to meet its own ends. 同时覆盖"相当大一部分"+"利用人"+"达成自身目的"三个要点，与原文逐一吻合。
B) 无中生有Humans are now fast locked in a race against digital tech to control the world说"人在与数字技术赛跑争夺世界控制"，但原文从未把人与技术描绘成赛跑或争控关系。
C) 与原文相反Digital tech can serve human needs in ways previously thought impossible 在赞美技术服务人类的能力，但作者 But 之后说的恰是相反——技术正反过来利用人。
D) 过度推断Digital tech is now doing thinking while humans are doing repetitive work 把人机的工作分工说成"技术思考、人重复劳动"，原文虽然提到作者做了 some unpaid labor，但并未把它对立到"技术负责思考"的层面。
questions.quote: And they're right. There's nothing technophobic about that. We shape our tools and then our tools shape us. Technology is supposed to provide tools that serve human ends. But, as the machine-learning Captcha demonstrates, a significant proportion of digital tech now sees (and uses) humans as means to ends that are not ours.

options.text: A large part of digital tech is now making use of humans to meet its own ends.
Humans are now fast locked in a race against digital tech to control the world.
Digital tech can serve human needs in ways previously thought impossible.
Digital tech is now doing thinking while humans are doing repetitive work.作 者 为 什 么 认 为Brett Frischmann和Evan Selinger是 对 的?

questions.prompt: What does the author imply by asking "Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late?" at the end of the passage?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （推断题）
**题目译文**
作者在文章结尾问"我们是否足够聪明,能在为时已晚之前跳出来?"这暗示了什么?
A) 期望数字技术将人类利益放在心上是不明智的。
B) 很难说技术还是人类会占上风。
C) 我们可能必须搜索网络才能得到这个问题的答案。
D) 我们可能无法及时意识到数字技术对我们构成的危险。
**判型** What does the author imply by asking ... 中的 imply 明确要求由作者的反问句推导言外之意，不能停在字面。
**拆句** What does the author imply by asking "Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late?" at the end of the passage? 主干是 What does the author imply，by asking... 是方式状语，引号内是反问句（rhetorical question），表达否定意味，是理解全题的关键。
**定位** 那么回到青蛙的比喻。我们够聪明，能在为时已晚之前跳出来吗？这个问题，你甚至都不用上网搜就能知道答案。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问It is not sensible to expect digital tech to take humans' interest to heart 在评判"指望技术为人着想是否明智"，对象是技术；但题干反问的主语是 we——问的是人是否够聪明，主体偏移。
B) 偷换概念It is hard to say whether technology or humans will get the upper hand 把作者立场说成"难说人机谁占上风"，但原文反问 + 反讽尾句强烈暗示作者倾向悲观，并非中立。
C) 与原文相反We may have to search the web to get the answer to the question 字面理解了You don't even have to Google it——把"不用搜也知道"反向解成"必须搜才知道"。
D) ✓ 正确Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late?↔We may not awake in time to the danger digital tech poses to us Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don't see what's been happening to us?↔ the danger digital tech poses to us预判要的是"恐怕来不及醒悟"，We may not awake in time to the danger digital tech poses to us. 把"反问 → 否定断言"与"温水煮青蛙 → 数字技术的危险"两层一起兜住，是唯一贴着原文走一步的推断。
questions.quote: So back to the frog metaphor. Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late? You don't even have to Google it to know the answer.

options.text: It is not sensible to expect digital tech to take humans' interest to heart.
It is hard to say whether technology or humans will get the upper hand.
We may have to search the web to get the answer to the question.
We may not awake in time to the danger digital tech poses to us.

title: Mindfulness has been shown to have a number…

sentences.text: Mindfulness has been shown to have a number of meaningful health benefits — it can help reduce anxiety and promote healing in those suffering from chronic illness.

passage.translation: 正念已被证明具有许多重要的健康益处——它可以帮助减少焦虑,并促进慢性疾病患者的康复。

sentences.text: The practice is based on an insight first described in ancient Buddhist texts that human beings have the capacity to observe experience without being caught up in it.

This means simply that it is possible to observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment in a way that amplifies the feeling or sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events.

passage.translation: 这种练习基于古代佛教文本中首次描述的一种洞见,即人类有能力观察体验而不陷入其中。这简单地意味着,我们可以观察自己产生渴望、快乐的想法,甚至可怕的情绪,而不在当下以放大这种感受或使思绪陷入对旧回忆的思考或对未来事件的预期的方式做出反应。

sentences.text: This practice of mindfulness can help calm the mind and the body as we learn not to react to experience with likes and dislikes or judgments of good and bad.
It does not make us cold or indifferent but more fully present.

passage.translation: 这种正念练习可以帮助平静身心,因为我们学会不以好恶或好坏的判断来回应体验。它不会使我们变得冷漠或漠不关心,而是让我们更充分地活在当下。

sentences.text: One of the challenges of practicing mindfulness in our contemporary world is that there has been a profound transformation in human attention.
The artist Jenny Odell argues that in our "attention economy" human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell.
This economy rests on a technological revolution of mobile phones and social media that makes it possible for corporations to target our attention with their content at every moment.

passage.translation: 在当代世界练习正念的挑战之一是人类注意力发生了深刻的转变。艺术家Jenny Odell认为,在我们的"注意力经济"中,人类注意力已经转变为大公司买卖的商品。这种经济依赖于移动电话和社交媒体的技术革命,使公司能够在每时每刻用其内容瞄准我们的注意力。

sentences.text: The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment.
The result is that it can feel as though our ability to focus, and be fully present, has been stolen.
But mindfulness can help us resist the attention economy and relish the things that make life special, like being together with those we love.

passage.translation: 大多数人使用的设备是对当下时刻的永久分散。其结果是,我们的专注能力和充分活在当下的能力似乎被偷走了。但正念可以帮助我们抵制注意力经济,并珍视那些使生活特别的事物,比如与我们所爱的人在一起。

sentences.text: Most mindfulness research focuses on the individual benefits of the practice, but some scholars assert that we can not only practice mindfulness for ourselves but also practice it for others.
It can help us build stronger, healthier relationships.

passage.translation: 大多数正念研究关注这种练习的个人益处,但一些学者断言,我们不仅可以为自己练习正念,也可以为他人练习正念。它可以帮助我们建立更牢固、更健康的关系。

sentences.text: The sad truth is that living in the attention economy, most of us have become bad listeners.
However, just as it is possible to watch ourselves having an experience without reacting, it's possible to watch another person have an experience without getting tied up in reactivity and judgment.

passage.translation: 可悲的事实是,生活在注意力经济中,我们大多数人已经成为糟糕的倾听者。然而,正如我们可以观察自己拥有一种体验而不做出反应一样,我们也可以观察另一个人拥有一种体验而不陷入反应性和判断之中。

sentences.text: The gift of mindfulness is a practice of listening with compassion to others describe their experiences.
To give this gift means putting away your phone, turning off social media, and setting aside other common distractions.
It means practicing being fully present in another person's presence and listening to them with complete attention without judgment, while resisting the urge to make the interaction about you.

passage.translation: 正念的馈赠是一种带着同情心倾听他人描述其体验的练习。给予这份馈赠意味着收起手机,关闭社交媒体,并放下其他常见的干扰。它意味着练习在他人面前充分活在当下,并以完全的注意力倾听他们而不加判断,同时抵制使互动围绕自己的冲动。

sentences.text: If we judge the value of gifts based on their price, this gift may seem worthless, but in a distracted world, it is a precious one.

passage.translation: 如果我们根据价格来判断礼物的价值,这份礼物可能看起来毫无价值,但在一个分心的世界里,它是珍贵的。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A) , B) , C) and D) . You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about practicing mindfulness?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
从文章中我们了解到关于练习正念的什么内容?
A) 它触发我们的思维去反思过去的经历或预期未来的事件。
B) 它将我们的注意力集中在当下时刻而不做评判。
C) 它将我们的思维集中在个人感受上,无论是快乐的还是恐惧的。
D) 它帮助我们的思维在面对他人的评判时保持平静。
**判型** What do we learn from the passage about practicing mindfulness 问的是文章关于mindfulness 的客观陈述，没有 infer/imply/mainly 这类信号，是一道关于 mindfulness本质特征的细节题。
**拆句** What do we learn from the passage about practicing mindfulness? 主干是 What do we learn from the passage，about practicing mindfulness 是介词短语后置补充询问对象，结构直白无陷阱。
**定位** 这意味着，我们可以观察自己产生渴望、愉快念头甚至恐惧情绪，而无需在当下作出反应、不放大该情绪，也不让心思滑向旧时记忆或对未来事件的预期。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反原文 without … sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events 明确把「回想旧事 / 预期未来」放在否定结构里，是正念要避免的，A 把它说成正念的作用，恰好与原文相反。
B) ✓ 正确observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment↔ focuses our attention on the present moment we learn not to react to experience with likes and dislikes or judgments of good and bad ↔without making judgments预判落在「观察当下、不卷入、不评判」三点上，focuses our attention on the present moment without making judgments 把前两点合在一句里全覆盖，是定位句的紧贴改写。
C) 偷换概念原文 observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment 强调观察情绪而不卷入，C 项却说「把注意力集中在个人情绪上」，把「观察」偷换成「集中」，两者一冷静一沉浸，语义错位。
D) 张冠李戴原文谈的是「自己不对体验作好坏评判」（judgments of good and bad），并未涉及「他人评判我们」，D 项把评判主体从「自我」换成「他人」，无原文依据。
questions.quote: This means simply that it is possible to observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment in a way that amplifies the feeling or sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events.

options.text: It triggers our mind to reflect on past experiences or anticipate future events.
It focuses our attention on the present moment without making judgments.
It concentrates our mind on our personal feelings, happy or scary.
It helps our mind to stay calm when facing judgments from others.

questions.prompt: What do we see in today's "attention economy" according to Jenny Odell?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
根据Jenny Odell的说法,我们在当今的"注意力经济"中看到了什么?
A) 对技术进步的关注持续更新着产品和服务。
B) 人们的注意力变成了可以被买卖的东西。
C) 企业通过销售手机和革新社交媒体获利。
D) 人们倾向于不加仔细思考就购买产品和服务。
**判型** What do we see in today's attention economy according to Jenny Odell 用according to 把答案归到 Jenny Odell 名下，是事实归属型细节题。
**拆句** What do we see in today's "attention economy" according to Jenny Odell? 主干What do we see in today's attention economy，according to Jenny Odell 是把观点归属到具体人物的状语，关键在于答案必须落到 Odell 的话上，而不是文章自己说的。
**定位** 艺术家 Jenny Odell 论述道：在我们的「注意力经济」中，人的注意力已经被转化成大公司买卖的商品。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文 This economy rests on a technological revolution of mobile phones and social media that makes it possible for corporations to target our attention with their content at every moment 说技术革命让公司能持续抢占注意力，没说技术让产品/服务持续更新，A 项偷换了技术革命的作用。
B) ✓ 正确human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell ↔People's attention is turned into something that can be bought and sold选项 B 几乎是 Odell 原话的一对一改写，主语、动词、对象、属性四要素全对齐，是according to 型细节题里最干净的同义替换。
C) 偷换概念原文 buy and sell 的宾语是 human attention（人的注意力），C 项把宾语偷换成mobile phones and social media，是把抽象对象偷换成具体技术，正好踩中考生「具象更易接受」的认知偏误。
D) 无中生有原文谈的是公司买卖「人的注意力」，并未谈消费者本身是否冲动消费；D 项关于「人们购买商品不细想」属凭空生造。
questions.quote: The artist Jenny Odell argues that in our "attention economy" human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell.

options.text: Focus on technological advances continuously updates products and services.
People's attention is turned into something that can be bought and sold.
Businesses profit from selling mobile phones and revolutionizing social media.
People tend to purchase products and services without careful thinking.

questions.prompt: What happens with the prevalent use of mobile phones or social media?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
手机或社交媒体的普遍使用会发生什么?
A) 它们不断使用户从此时此地分心。
B) 它们使用户无法抵抗诱惑。
C) 它们剥夺了用户观察体验的能力。
D) 它们诱使用户认同注意力经济。
**判型** What happens with the prevalent use of mobile phones or social media 直接问 What happens，是问客观结果，属于细节题。
**拆句** What happens with the prevalent use of mobile phones or social media? 主干 What happens，with the prevalent use of… 是介词短语作伴随状语，相当于 when… are widely used，结构平实。
**定位** 大多数人使用的这些设备是一种让人持续偏离当下的干扰。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment ↔They keep distracting users from the here and now A 项两个核心语义点（keep distracting、from the here and now）与原文 perpetual diversion、from the present moment 一一对应，是定位句的紧贴改写。
B) 过度推断原文 But mindfulness can help us resist the attention economy 谈的是正念能帮我们抵抗，B 项却说设备让用户「彻底失去抵御诱惑的能力」，把「分心」夸大为「丧失抵抗力」，无原文依据。
C) 张冠李戴原文 our ability to focus, and be fully present, has been stolen 谈被偷走的是「专注、全在当下」的能力，而 capacity to observe experience 才是 observe experience 的能力，C 项把两者混在一起，张冠李戴。
D) 无中生有原文只说设备让人分心、注意力被卖，没说设备诱使用户主动「支持/认同」注意力经济，D 项凭空多出一个「用户主动认同」的环节。
questions.quote: The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment.

options.text: They keep distracting users from the here and now.
They render users incapable of resisting temptation.
They rob users of their ability to observe experience.
They tempt users to endorse the attention economy.

questions.prompt: What benefit can practicing mindfulness bring to us according to some scholars?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
根据一些学者的说法,练习正念能给我们带来什么好处?
A) 它防止我们对他人做出武断的评判。
B) 它将我们的注意力从物质事物转移到精神追求。
C) 它有助于我们建立更好的人际关系。
D) 它有助于恢复我们享受生活中所拥有之物的能力。
**判型** What benefit can practicing mindfulness bring to us according to some scholars 用according to some scholars 归属信息源，是出处型细节题。
**拆句** What benefit can practicing mindfulness bring to us according to some scholars? 主干 What benefit can practicing mindfulness bring to us，according to some scholars是把观点归到学者群体的状语，注意不要把作者自己其它段落的好处当成学者说的。
**定位** 多数正念研究关注其个人层面的益处，但一些学者论断：正念不仅可为己练，也可为他人而练；它能帮我们建立更稳固、更健康的人际关系。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴「不作评判」是 P3 谈 mindfulness 个体效用时的内容，而 Q49 问的是 some scholars 的观点；把 P3 的句子嫁接到学者名下属于张冠李戴，且 prevent us from making arbitrary judgments about others 也夸大了原文「自己不评判体验」的限定。
B) 无中生有原文没有把好处归结为「从物质转向精神追求」，B 项凭空生造一组对立维度。
C) ✓ 正确help us build stronger, healthier relationships ↔conducive to our forging better interpersonal relationships C 项把学者观点收束句 help us build stronger, healthier relationships 完整改写成conducive to our forging better interpersonal relationships，主体、动作、对象逐项对齐。
D) 张冠李戴「重拾享受生活的能力」对应 relish the things that make life special, like being together with those we love，是作者自己的论述而非 some scholars 的观点；嫁接到学者名下属于张冠李戴。
questions.quote: Most mindfulness research focuses on the individual benefits of the practice, but some scholars assert that we can not only practice mindfulness for ourselves but also practice it for others. It can help us build stronger, healthier relationships.

options.text: It prevents us from making arbitrary judgments about others.
It shifts our attention from material things to spiritual pursuits.
It is conducive to our forging better interpersonal relationships.
It is helpful in regaining our ability to enjoy what we have in life.

questions.prompt: What does the author suggest we do in another person's presence?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者建议我们在他人面前做什么?
A) 坦诚而富有同情心地分享彼此的经历。
B) 全神贯注于与他们建立亲密关系。
C) 做专注的倾听者同时避免做出评判。
D) 提醒他们注意来自手机和社交媒体的干扰。
**判型** What does the author suggest we do in another person's presence 问的是作者对一个具体场景给出的具体做法，是建议型细节题。
**拆句** What does the author suggest we do in another person's presence? 主干 What does the author suggest we do，in another person's presence 是地点状语；suggest 后接省略 that 的从句 we do…，注意 suggest 在此为「建议」义、不是「暗示」义。
**定位** 这意味着练习在另一个人面前全然临在，全神贯注地倾听他们，不作评判，同时克制把对话焦点拉回到自己身上的冲动。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反原文 resisting the urge to make the interaction about you 明确要求克制把谈话拉回到「自己」，强调单向倾听对方；A 项却说 share each other's experience 双向分享，与原文要求方向相反。
B) 偷换概念原文要求把全部注意力放在对方的体验上，目的是「以正念之心送出倾听这一礼物」（practicing being fully present in another person's presence）；B 项却把目的偷换成 establishing close relationships with them——这是 Q49 的话题，且原文未把它定为这一场景的目的。
C) ✓ 正确listening to them with complete attention without judgment↔Be attentive listeners while refraining from making judgments C 项把作者建议的两项核心动作（with complete attention、without judgment）都直接对应到选项的两个分句，是同义改写最紧贴的一项。
D) 无中生有原文要求自己 putting away your phone, turning off social media, and setting aside other common distractions，即「自己」放下手机，并未要求去提醒对方；D项把动作主体从「自己」偷换到「提醒他人」，无原文依据。
questions.quote: It means practicing being fully present in another person's presence and listening to them with complete attention without judgment, while resisting the urge to make the interaction about you.

options.text: Share each other's experience frankly and compassionately.
Pay full attention to establishing close relationships with them.
Be attentive listeners while refraining from making judgments.
Remind them of the distraction from mobile phones and social media.

title: It's best to think of an accent as…

sentences.text: It's best to think of an accent as a distinct, systematic and rule-governed way of speaking.
Accent is not a (26)____ for dialect, but it's related.
Dialect is an umbrella term for the way a community pronounces words, creates words, and orders words; accent refers to that first part only.

passage.translation: 最好将口音理解为一种独特的、系统的、有规则支配的说话方式。口音不是方言的同义词,但两者相关。方言是一个总括性术语,指一个社群发音、造词和组词的方式;而口音仅指其中第一部分。

sentences.text: Many (27)____ presume that there is a single standard way of speaking in each country, with one single standard accent, and that this perceived standard is (28)____ the best form of speech, but linguists(语言学家) often point out that the concept of a standard accent is better understood as an ideal rather than a (29)____ .
In other words, no one speaks "standard English"; rather, it is an imagined way of using language that exists only in grammar and style books.

passage.translation: 许多外行人认为每个国家都有一种标准说话方式,配有一种标准口音,并且这种被认为的标准天然就是最佳的言语形式,但语言学家常常指出,标准口音的概念更应被理解为一种理想而非现实。换句话说,没有人说"标准英语";相反,它是一种想象中的语言使用方式,仅存在于语法书和文体书中。

sentences.text: One reason linguists agree there is no one true standard is that, through the years, there have been(30)____ supposed standards, depending on time and place.
The standard for English in British newsreels(新闻片) from the 1950s, for example, differs greatly from the standard found on American national news broadcasts today.
In fact, there has never been a single standard that's been fully agreed upon — and broadcast outlets across the (31)____ have never consistently held to those standards anyway.

passage.translation: 语言学家一致认为不存在唯一真正标准的一个原因是,多年来,根据时间和地点的不同,存在过多种所谓的标准。例如,1950年代英国新闻片中的英语标准与当今美国全国新闻广播中的标准大不相同。事实上,从来就没有一个得到完全认可的单一标准——而且各类广播媒体也从未始终如一地坚持这些标准。

sentences.text: Even so, this idea of a standard accent is (32)____ and many workplace and educational environments perpetuate the idea that accents that (33)____ from the current standard are less appropriate, or even inappropriate.
Scholars have found that southern US accent features are more accepted in (34)____ such as government, law and service-oriented workplaces, but less accepted in the technology sector.
The acceptability of nonstandard accents may (35)____ with differences in class and culture, with newer or higher prestige industries expecting more standard speech in the workplace.

passage.translation: 即便如此,这种标准口音的观念颇具影响力,许多职场和教育环境都在延续这样的观念:偏离当前标准的口音不够恰当,甚至是不恰当的。学者们发现,美国南方口音特征在政府、法律和服务型职场等领域更容易被接受,但在科技行业则较难被接受。非标准口音的可接受程度可能与阶层和文化差异相关,较新或声望较高的行业对职场中的标准言语有更高期待。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
It's best to think of an accent as a distinct, systematic and rule-governed way of speaking. Accent is not a {{26}} for dialect, but it's related. Dialect is an umbrella term for the way a community pronounces words, creates words, and orders words; accent refers to that first part only.

Many {{27}} presume that there is a single standard way of speaking in each country, with one single standard accent, and that this perceived standard is {{28}} the best form of speech, but linguists(语言学家) often point out that the concept of a standard accent is better understood as an ideal rather than a {{29}} . In other words, no one speaks "standard English"; rather, it is an imagined way of using language that exists only in grammar and style books.

One reason linguists agree there is no one true standard is that, through the years, there have been{{30}} supposed standards, depending on time and place. The standard for English in British newsreels(新闻片) from the 1950s, for example, differs greatly from the standard found on American national news broadcasts today. In fact, there has never been a single standard that's been fully agreed upon — and broadcast outlets across the {{31}} have never consistently held to those standards anyway.

Even so, this idea of a standard accent is {{32}} and many workplace and educational environments perpetuate the idea that accents that {{33}} from the current standard are less appropriate, or even inappropriate. Scholars have found that southern US accent features are more accepted in {{34}} such as government, law and service-oriented workplaces, but less accepted in the technology sector. The acceptability of nonstandard accents may {{35}} with differences in class and culture, with newer or higher prestige industries expecting more standard speech in the workplace.

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) synonym 名词
**词性槽** 不定冠词 a 后 + for 介词框架
**依据** a synonym for 固定搭配原文 Accent is not a __(26)__ for dialect, but it's related. Dialect is an umbrella term...; accent refers to that first part only. 说"accent 不是 dialect 的 ___，但相关"，紧接着解释 dialect 是包含 accent 的更大范畴——也就是两者不是同义词。a synonym for X 即"X的同义词"，是英语中固定搭配，语义与逻辑双合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
L) specimen 样品义不合语境specimen 指"标本、样品"，说"accent 不是 dialect 的样品"逻辑不通，且无 a specimen for这一搭配。
J) reality现实义与对比关系不符reality 指"现实"，原文是在做术语对比（accent 与 dialect），并非讨论虚实，且 a reality for在此搭配生硬。
M) spectrum 范围义无法对应同义对比spectrum 指"范围、谱系"，与下文"二者相关但不重合"的同义/上下位对比不匹配。
D) domains 复数形式不匹配冠词 a domains 为复数，与不定冠词 a 不兼容；语义"领域"也不构成 accent 与 dialect 的术语对照。
G) laymen 复数且指人，不合语境laymen 为复数指"外行人"，与 a 不搭，且整句是在定义术语，非指代人群。
I) properties 复数且抽象属性义偏移properties 复数与 a 不兼容；"属性"也无法解释 accent 与 dialect 的术语关系。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) laymen 名词
**词性槽** 形容词 Many 后 + 之后为谓语动词 presume
**依据** 外行人对应"想当然以为"的认知主体Many laymen presume… 即"许多外行人想当然以为……"，恰好与下半句 but linguists(语言学家) often point out that the concept of a standard accent is better understood as an ideal rather than a __(29)__ 中的 linguists 构成"外行 vs 专家"对照，逻辑严丝合缝。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
D) domains 领域无法做"以为"的主体domains 指"领域"，是抽象范畴，不能作 presume 的逻辑主语；且与下句 linguists 的对照对象不符。
I) properties 属性无法做"以为"的主体properties 指"属性、财产"，同样是抽象概念，无法 presume；与对照结构不匹配。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) inherently 副词
**词性槽** be 动词与表语形容词之间的修饰位
**依据** 本质上即最佳，对应"理想型"叙述原文 Many __(27)__ presume that there is a single standard way of speaking in each country, with one single standard accent, and that this perceived standard is __(28)__the best form of speech 描述"外行人以为感知到的标准在本质上就是最佳说话方式"，inherently 表"本质上、生来就是"，正好对应这种被想当然的本体论断言。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
K) reciprocally相互义与单向断言不符reciprocally 表"相互地"，需双向主体；句中只是单方面"被认为是最佳"，无相互关系可言。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 K) —— 副词类目仅二选一，词义辨义易翻车。F) inherently 与 K) reciprocally 同为副词，考生若只看到"副词"就随手填，可能误选 reciprocally；防坑：be+ ___ + the best form of speech 这种单向断言句不存在"相互"关系，必须看断言方向再选副词。

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) reality 名词
**词性槽** rather than 后并列名词位
**依据** an ideal rather than a reality标准口音"更适合被理解为一种理想，而不是现实"，ideal 与 reality 是英语中最经典的反义对子；紧接的下一句 no one speaks "standard English"; rather, it is an imagined way of using language that exists only in grammar and style books. 用"想象的、只存在于语法书中"再次坐实"非现实"，对照成立。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
L) specimen 样品义与理想无反义对应specimen 指"样本、标本"，与 ideal 不构成对照，且语义上说"标准口音是样本"不通。
M) spectrum 范围义与理想不对仗spectrum 指"频谱、范围"，与 ideal 既无反义、也不切下句"想象的语言用法"语境。
I) properties 复数与 a 不兼容properties 复数，违背 a + 单数名词 的语法约束；语义"属性"也不构成与 ideal 的对照。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) multiple 形容词
**词性槽** there have been + 空 + 复数名词
**依据** 多个标准支撑"无统一"论点本段中心是"语言学家认为没有唯一真标准"，紧跟的例子 The standard for English in British newsreels(新闻片) from the 1950s, for example, differs greatly from the standard found on American national news broadcasts today. 用"50 年代英国 vs 当下美国"佐证存在多个标准，multiple supposed standards 切中要害。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
O) unanimous 一致同意与无统一标准矛盾unanimous 表"一致同意的"，若说"存在一致同意的标准"，与下文 there has never been a single standard that's been fully agreed upon 直接打架。

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) spectrum 名词
**词性槽** the + 空 + 介词短语
**依据** across the spectrum 全谱系across the spectrum 是英语固定搭配，表"涵盖各种类型/全谱系"。原文意为"全谱系的广播机构都没有始终如一地坚持那些标准"，正好支持"标准并未统一遵行"的主旨。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
L) specimen 标本义无范围义specimen 指"标本、样品"，不能表"涵盖范围"，across the specimen 不成立搭配。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) influential 形容词
**词性槽** be 动词后的表语位置
**依据** 有影响力解释后文延续效应下文 and many workplace and educational environments perpetuate the idea that accents that __(33)__ from the current standard are less appropriate 说许多职场和教育环境仍在延续这一观念——也就是这一观念"颇有影响力"，influential 正好统摄后文这一果。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
O) unanimous 一致同意与全文论点冲突全文反复强调没有统一公认的标准（there has never been a single standard that's been fully agreed upon），若说"标准口音的观念是一致同意的"，与上下文直接矛盾。
H) multiple 多个无法搭配单数主语属性multiple 表"多种的"，用于修饰可数复数或集合概念；说"this idea is multiple"语义不通。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 O) —— unanimous 看着切题，实则与主旨反向。32 题 this idea of a standard accent is ___ 看见"标准口音"主题，部分考生顺势填 unanimous；防坑：联读后文 and many workplace and educational environments perpetuate the idea，重点是"延续/影响"不是"一致同意"，influential 才对得上。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) deviate 动词
**词性槽** that 从句中缺谓语 + 后接 from
**依据** deviate from 偏离当前标准原文整段在讨论"偏离当下标准的口音被视为不合适"，deviate from the current standard即"偏离当前标准"，词义、搭配、逻辑三处合一。

**答案** D) domains 名词
**词性槽** 介词 in 后 + such as 举例
**依据** 领域作为政府/法律/服务业的上位词government、law、service-oriented workplaces 都是社会职业"领域"，domains 表"领域、范围"正是这些行业的自然上位范畴，搭配 in domains such as ___ 在学术英语里极为常见。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
I) properties 属性义无法囊括行业举例properties 表"属性、财产"，government 等并非"属性"，无法做其上位范畴；搭配 in properties such as government 语义不通。

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) correlate 动词
**词性槽** 情态动词 may 后 + 介词 with
**依据** correlate with 与……相关联correlate with 表"与……相关联"，原句意为"非标准口音的可接受度可能与阶层和文化差异相关"，紧跟的 with newer or higher prestige industries expecting more standard speech in the workplace 进一步说明这种相关性的具体表现，逻辑顺畅。

title: People who repeatedly give unwanted advice can be…

sentences.text: People who repeatedly give unwanted advice can be well-meaning and genuinely want to help.
Others might do this out of a sense of self-worth around the ability to influence others.
One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency.

passage.translation: 反复提供不请自来的建议的人可能出于好意,真心想要帮忙。另一些人这样做可能是出于一种围绕影响他人能力的自我价值感。一项研究发现,权力寻求倾向高的人比倾向相反的人更容易给出建议。

sentences.text: Under the guise(外表) of unselfishness, people may be driven to give you unwanted advice because it makes them feel powerful or in control.
They may not be fully aware of this drive, however.

passage.translation: 在无私的外表下,人们可能被驱使给你提供不想要的建议,因为这让他们感到强大或能够掌控。然而,他们可能并未完全意识到这种驱动力。

sentences.text: These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down.
It is possible that their emotions were only validated in childhood when they were at their loudest, encouraging them to adopt responses to discomfort that are excessive in most situations.

passage.translation: 这些人还可能表现出问题性的情绪脆弱程度,很快变得心烦意乱,需要很长时间才能平静下来。有可能他们的情绪在童年时期只有在最大声时才得到认可,这促使他们采用在大多数情况下都过度的不适应对方式。

sentences.text: When someone is giving advice in order to make themselves feel more powerful, there is underlying anxiety to their behavior that recipients of the advice tend to notice.
It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesired result.

passage.translation: 当某人为了让自己感觉更强大而给出建议时,他们的行为背后有焦虑,建议的接受者往往会注意到这一点。在这种情况下,对建议给予者做出严厉反应并指责他们具有操纵性可能很诱人,但这种方法可能会产生不希望的结果。

sentences.text: If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone's feelings of self-worth, an outright(直率的) rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict.

passage.translation: 如果给出建议的行为正在积极促成某人的自我价值感,直率的拒绝可能被视为一种威胁,激活他们的战斗或逃跑反应,可能导致他们加倍寻求认可的行为,或导致更大的冲突。

sentences.text: The key is to validate without over-identifying.
You can let them know that you have heard them and appreciate where they are coming from without taking on the potentially damaging narrative that you could not have gotten by without their help.
You had better say something like, "Thanks for the idea.
I have my own plan for handling this, but I really appreciate your perspective and will take it into consideration.
Can I let you know when I need help in the future?"

passage.translation: 关键是要认可但不要过度认同。你可以让他们知道你听到了他们的意见,理解他们的出发点,而不必接受那种可能有害的叙事,即没有他们的帮助你就无法做到。你最好说些类似这样的话:'感谢你的想法。我有自己处理这件事的计划,但我真的很感激你的观点,会将它纳入考虑。将来我需要帮助时可以告诉你吗?'

sentences.text: If you have trouble setting boundaries tactfully, prioritize working on your own ability to self- regulate.
As uncomfortable as it may be to continuously receive, if you can respond with compassion, the situation will likely defuse much faster.

passage.translation: 如果你在巧妙地设定界限方面有困难,优先致力于提高自己的自我调节能力。尽管持续接受可能令人不舒服,但如果你能以同情心回应,情况可能会更快缓和。

sentences.text: Though it is usually not the intended outcome of giving unsolicited advice, many who receive it often feel stressed, offended, or simply annoyed by unwanted suggestions.
Setting a boundary in this regard, if you feel you need one, is perfectly reasonable and something that can bring you increased emotional safety.

passage.translation: 尽管这通常不是主动提供建议的预期结果,但许多接受建议的人常常因不想要的建议而感到压力、被冒犯或只是感到恼火。在这方面设定界限,如果你觉得需要,是完全合理的,也是能给你带来更多情感安全的事情。

sentences.text: It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.

passage.translation: 最好以考虑到个人做事的潜在原因的方式设定界限,以避免不必要的冲突和更多压力。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What is the finding of one study about people who keep giving unsolicited advice?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
一项研究关于不断提供主动建议的人有什么发现?
A) 他们原来是出于好意的。
B) 他们确实心地善良。
C) 他们有能力影响他人。
D) 他们倾向于渴望权力。
**判型** 题干 What is the finding of one study 指向某个具体研究的事实性结论，不含 infer/imply/mainly。
**拆句** 题干主干是 What is the finding of one study，about 引导的介词短语修饰 finding，限定研究对象是 people who keep giving unsolicited advice（who 引导定语从句修饰people）。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 一项研究发现，求权欲望强的人比求权欲望相反（低）的人更倾向于给出建议。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问They turn out to be well-meaning 取自首句 can be well-meaning，但那只是 give advice 的一种可能动机的铺垫，并非“研究的发现”。
B) 答非所问They are genuinely kind-hearted 改写自 genuinely want to help，同样位于铺垫句，不是研究结论。
C) 偷换概念They are capable of influencing others 把 self-worth around the ability to influence others 中“自我价值感来自影响他人的能力”误读为“具备影响他人能力”，且这同样不在 study 结论里。
D) ✓ 正确a high tendency to seek power ↔ inclined to crave for power四项中只有 inclined to crave for power 与预判“求权欲强者更爱给建议”形成 1:1 同义对应。
questions.quote: One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency.

options.text: They turn out to be well-meaning.
They are genuinely kind-hearted.
They are capable of influencing others.
They are inclined to crave for power.

questions.prompt: What is the problem with people who are driven to give you unsolicited advice?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
那些被驱使向你提供主动建议的人有什么问题?
A) 他们可能很快就会让别人不高兴。
B) 他们可能在情感上很脆弱。
C) 他们想让自己的声音最响亮。
D) 他们对不适过度反应。
**判型** 题干 What is the problem with 指向一个可在原文中找到具体描述的缺陷。
**拆句** 主干 What is the problem，介词短语 with people who are driven to give you unsolicited advice 修饰 problem；who 引导被动语态定语从句。注意 driven 是被动，表示“被某种力量驱使”，而不是主动选择。
**定位** 这些人还可能表现出某种程度上有问题的情绪脆弱性——很快就情绪激动，且久久不能平复。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴They may be quick to upset others 把原文中“自己易激动”扭曲为“使他人易激动”——动作发出者由 these people 变成对他人施加影响。
B) ✓ 正确a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability ↔ emotionally vulnerable预判的“情绪脆弱”在四项中只与 emotionally vulnerable 对应；A/C/D 都来自定位句的修饰部分。
C) 偷换概念They want their voice to be the loudest 改自 their emotions were only validated in childhood when they were at their loudest，那是对成因的猜测且发生在童年，并非“现在的问题”本身。
D) 答非所问They respond to discomfort excessively 取自 adopt responses to discomfort that are excessive in most situations，那是脆弱情绪导致的“反应方式”，是表现/后果，而题干问的是“问题本身”。
questions.quote: These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down.

options.text: They may be quick to upset others.
They may be emotionally vulnerable.
They want their voice to be the loudest.
They respond to discomfort excessively.

questions.prompt: What is the advice receiver tempted to do when noticing the advice giver's underlying anxiety?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
当注意到建议提供者潜在的焦虑时,建议接受者会倾向于做什么?
A) 揭示他们的方法所带来的不良结果。
B) 以不加掩饰的方式拒绝他们的建议。
C) 将他们的真实动机揭露出来。
D) 指责他们试图控制他人。
**判型** 题干 What is the advice receiver tempted to do 指向一个原文中可直接对应的具体行为。
**拆句** 主干 What is the advice receiver tempted to do，when 引导时间状语从句 when noticing the advice giver’s underlying anxiety（noticing 为分词短语）。注意 tempted to do 不等于“已经做”，而是“被诱使想去做”。
**定位** 在这种情况下，人很容易被诱使去强硬回怼劝告者并指责他们在操控自己，但这种做法可能导致不希望出现的结果。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Reveal the undesired result of their approach 把原文 this approach might produce an undesired result 中“己方做法的结果”硬塞为“揭露对方做法的结果”，且reveal 这一动作原文从未出现。
B) 张冠李戴Refuse their advice in an undisguised manner 取自 an outright rejection 的outright（直率的），属于 Q54 区间内容；与 Q53 问的“被诱使做什么”无关。
C) 无中生有Bring their real motives to the surface 谈“把真实动机暴露出来”，原文虽提到 They may not be fully aware of this drive，但从未说被诱使去把动机带到台面上。
D) ✓ 正确accuse them of being manipulative ↔ Accuse them of trying to control others在 to react harshly 与 to accuse them of being manipulative 两个候选动作里，只有Accuse them of trying to control others 与后者形成精确同义改写。
questions.quote: It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesired result.

options.text: Reveal the undesired result of their approach.
Refuse their advice in an undisguised manner.
Bring their real motives to the surface.
Accuse them of trying to control others.

questions.prompt: How is the advice giver likely to react to the rejection of their advice?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
建议提供者对他们的建议被拒绝可能会有什么反应?
A) 他们可能会将其视为一种威胁。
B) 他们可能会改变自己的行为。
C) 他们为更大的冲突做好准备。
D) 他们开始怀疑自己的自我价值。
**判型** 题干 How is the advice giver likely to react 问的是一个原文中有具体描述的反应方式。
**拆句** 主干 How is the advice giver likely to react，to 引导的介词短语 to the rejection of their advice 表反应对象。likely to 是预测性短语，对应原文的 may/possibly 等情态表达。
**定位** 如果给建议这一行为正主动地构建着对方的自我价值感，那么一次直率的拒绝可能被对方视为威胁，激活其“战或逃”反应，可能导致他们加倍寻求认可，或引发更大的冲突。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确may be perceived as a threat ↔ They may regard it as a threat预判“视为威胁”在四项中只与 They may regard it as a threat 形成 1:1 同义对应；B/C/D 均取自定位句末尾的分词链或脱离原文。
B) 与原文相反They may modify their behavior 暗示劝告者会调整行为；原文却是 double down on their validation-seeking behavior——加倍重复原行为，方向相反。
C) 过度推断They get ready for a larger conflict 描述劝告者“准备好”打更大架；原文是possibly...leading to a larger conflict，只是分词链中可能的下游结果，并非劝告者主动准备。
D) 与原文相反They begin to doubt their self-worth 说劝告者开始怀疑自己；原文方向相反——他们的 self-worth 被威胁后，会更努力地寻求认可（double down on validation- seeking），而不是怀疑。
questions.quote: If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone's feelings of self-worth, an outright rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict.

options.text: They may regard it as a threat.
They may modify their behavior.
They get ready for a larger conflict.
They begin to doubt their self-worth.

questions.prompt: What should the advice receiver do to avoid unnecessary conflict?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
建议接受者应该怎么做才能避免不必要的冲突?
A) 承认该建议是完全合理的。
B) 给出他们不采纳该建议的理由。
C) 理解建议提供者为什么要提供这个建议。
D) 解释他们所选择的处理情况的方式。
**判型** 题干 What should the advice receiver do 指向作者给出的明确建议，文章末段往往有归纳。
**拆句** 主干 What should the advice receiver do，to 引导目的状语 to avoid unnecessary conflict。should 是关键情态动词，意味着答案对应文中明确的建议性陈述，而非可能性陈述。
**定位** 最好以一种顾及当事人行为背后深层动机的方式来设界限，以避免不必要的冲突和更多压力。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴Concede the advice is perfectly reasonable 让步承认建议合理，是放弃自己立场；原文是劝考者“自己设界限是 perfectly reasonable”，主语完全不同。
B) 偷换概念Give their reasons for not taking the advice 让 receiver 说出自己的拒绝理由；原文范本话术 I have my own plan for handling this 谈的是“我自有方案”，并未要求陈述拒绝理由，更不是 P9 给出的总策略。
C) ✓ 正确takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing ↔Understand why the advice giver offers the advice预判“顾及对方深层动机”在四项中只与 Understand why the advice giver offers the advice 形成 1:1 同义对应。
D) 以偏概全Explain their chosen way of handling the situation 描述 receiver 解释自己的处理方式，对应 I have my own plan for handling this 的示范话术之一，但题干问的是“避免冲突的做法”——文末 P9 的总结才是答案。
questions.quote: It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.

options.text: Concede the advice is perfectly reasonable.
Give their reasons for not taking the advice.
Understand why the advice giver offers the advice.
Explain their chosen way of handling the situation.

title: As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of…

sentences.text: As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others.
We like to work with people who are like-minded, with whom we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about.
This is evident in how we have organized ourselves into various collective groups such as nations, regions, communities, organizations, and families.

passage.translation: 作为相互依存的存在，我们无法独立于他人而兴旺发展。我们喜欢与志同道合的人共事，与我们有共同兴趣的人共事，或者与同样相信我们所认真对待的事业的人共事。这在我们如何将自己组织成各种集体群体中表现得很明显，如国家、地区、社区、组织和家庭。

sentences.text: Does the group you belong to have a strong collective consciousness or shared beliefs?
Is there interdependence among its members?
Do you consider this group a significant part of your existence?
If your answers are affirmative, then you are experiencing a micro version of solidarity.

passage.translation: 你所属的群体是否有强烈的集体意识或共同信念？其成员之间是否存在相互依存关系？你是否认为这个群体是你存在的重要组成部分？如果你的答案是肯定的，那么你正在经历团结的微缩版本。

sentences.text: What is solidarity?
Its simplest definition in the dictionary is: "… a unifying opinion, feeling, purpose or interest among a group of people."

passage.translation: 什么是团结？字典中对它最简单的定义是："……一群人之间统一的观点、感受、目的或利益。"

sentences.text: In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labor.

passage.translation: 在我们生活的这个日益多元化的社会中，团结呈现出复杂和多面的特征，因为它在生活于快速变化的环境中并在复杂的劳动分工中工作的独特个体之间形成相互依存的纽带。

sentences.text: One facet of solidarity fits well with the principles of communitarianism(社群主义).
In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good.
However, its strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences and preferences.
Consequently, individuality and autonomy are sacrificed to maintain the unity of the group.

passage.translation: 团结的一个方面与社群主义的原则非常契合。在这种情况下，个人放弃自己的利益来服务于共同利益。然而，它对社会凝聚力和排他性的严格遵守限制了个体差异和偏好的表达和实践。因此，个性和自主性被牺牲以维护群体的团结。

sentences.text: Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice.

It goes against the liberal idea of unrestricted individuals who see society as a hindrance to their freedom to make choices and to act according to what is good for them regardless of how these will affect others.

passage.translation: 团结也被视为对过度强调个人主义和选择自由的一种反应。它反对自由主义关于不受限制的个人的观念，这些个人将社会视为阻碍他们自由做出选择和根据对自己有利的事情行事的障碍，而不管这些会如何影响他人。

sentences.text: But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society.
They believe that for human society to survive as it becomes more diverse, more new bonds need to be formed based on the differences.
In the light of this, they regard a genuine solidarity as more than just shallow relationships based on common interests.
Solidarity is not just a product of strategic calculations of how much it will benefit the self.
It is not an exclusive class founded on the you-and-me-against-the-world principle.
Rather, it is inclusive and is not forced.
Acting out of solidarity means supporting and standing up for each other — in recognition that one's fate is in the fate of the other.
It is a bond characterized by cooperative practices and strengthened by the concern for the well-being of others or the common good.
It fights for the protection of human dignity and listens to and acts on the cries of the most vulnerable.

passage.translation: 但尽管团结有许多方面，社会理论家将团结视为给社会带来秩序和进步的关键因素。他们认为，随着人类社会变得更加多元化，要使其生存下去，就需要基于差异形成更多新的纽带。鉴于此，他们认为真正的团结不仅仅是基于共同利益的肤浅关系。团结不仅仅是关于它将给自我带来多少利益的战略计算的产物。它不是建立在你我对抗世界原则基础上的排他性阶层。相反，它是包容性的，不是强制的。出于团结而行动意味着相互支持和挺身而出——认识到一个人的命运在于另一个人的命运之中。这是一种以合作实践为特征、以对他人福祉或共同利益的关注而得到加强的纽带。它为保护人类尊严而战，倾听并回应最脆弱者的呼声。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about human beings?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者对人类有何看法?
A) 他们若不相互合作就无法繁荣发展。
B) 他们有共同的利益并相信正义的事业。
C) 他们在不同社会群体中的思维和行为方式相似。
D) 他们若不为之抗争就无法获得独立。
**判型** What does the author say about human beings? 问的是作者就 human beings 这一具体对象说了什么，落点在某一具体陈述上而非整篇主旨。
**拆句** What does the author say about human beings? 是常规疑问句结构，主干 "the author say"，关于 human beings，无从句、无否定、无比较，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 作为相互依赖的存在，我们无法脱离他人独自繁荣兴盛。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确thrive ↔ prosper cannot thrive independent of others ↔ cannot prosper without cooperating with each other They cannot prosper without cooperating with each other. 把 cannot thrive independent of others 改写为"必须合作才能兴旺"，正是预判内容的同义转述。
B) 偷换概念They share a common interest and believe in a just cause. 取自 we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about，但原文这是"喜欢和谁一起工作"的举例，不是对 human beings 的总体陈述；且 cause 被偷换为just cause（正义事业）。
C) 过度推断They think and behave alike in different social groups. 声称"在不同群体中想法行为都一样"，原文只说人喜欢和"like-minded"的人共事，并未说人在所有群体中思想行为都相同。
D) 与原文相反They cannot gain independence without fighting for it. 谈"独立要靠斗争争取"，但原文 we cannot thrive independent of others 强调的是"无法独立"而非"为独立而战"，话题相反。
questions.quote: As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others.

options.text: They cannot prosper without cooperating with each other.
They share a common interest and believe in a just cause.
They think and behave alike in different social groups.
They cannot gain independence without fighting for it.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about solidarity in an increasingly diverse society?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于日益多元化社会中的团结,我们了解到什么?
A) 它引发了复杂的劳动分工。
B) 它涉及许多具有高度复杂性的方面。
C) 它随着环境变化将个体凝聚在一起。
D) 它包容不同个体的特征。
**判型** What do we learn about solidarity in an increasingly diverse society? 提问限定在"多元化社会下的 solidarity"这一局部，并非整篇主旨。
**拆句** What do we learn about solidarity in an increasingly diverse society? 主干 "we learn about solidarity"，介词短语 "in an increasingly diverse society" 限定语境，无难句结构。
**定位** 在我们所处的这个日益多元化的社会里，solidarity 呈现出复杂而多面的特征，因为它在快速变化的环境中、在复杂的分工内部，于各不相同的个体之间形成了相互依赖的纽带。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 强加因果It gives rise to a complicated division of labor. 说 solidarity 导致了复杂分工，但原文 working within a complex division of labor 是说 solidarity 发生"在"复杂分工"之内"，分工是背景而非结果。
B) ✓ 正确takes on a complex and multifaceted character ↔involves many aspects with great complexity takes on ↔ involves involves many aspects with great complexity 同时覆盖原文的 complex 和multifaceted 两个核心修饰语，且未做任何额外延伸。
C) 以偏概全It brings individuals together as environment changes. 把"形成相互依赖纽带"窄化为"把个体聚拢"，且偷换了主线——题干问的是"我们关于 solidarity 在多元社会中学到什么"，正确答案应概括其"特征"，C 选了一处细节当主答。
D) 偷换概念It embraces the characteristics of different individuals. 说 solidarity"接纳"个体差异，但原文只说它在 unique individuals 之间形成纽带，并未说它"接纳"或"包含"个体特征。
questions.quote: In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast- changing environment and working within a complex division of labor.

options.text: It gives rise to a complicated division of labor.
It involves many aspects with great complexity.
It brings individuals together as environment changes.
It embraces the characteristics of different individuals.

questions.prompt: What would we witness in the setting of communitarianism?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
在社群主义的背景下我们会看到什么?
A) 社会规范的统治和个性的消除。
B) 强调坚持个体差异。
C) 为了公共利益而牺牲个人利益。
D) 消除个人主义和个人选择。
**判型** What would we witness in the setting of communitarianism? 问的是该情境下会观察到什么，指向文中具体描述句。
**拆句** What would we witness in the setting of communitarianism? 主干 "we would witness"，"in the setting of communitarianism" 限定情境，would 表示一般陈述语气，无难点。
**定位** 在这种情境下，个人放弃自身利益以服务于共同利益。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全Ruling of social norms and ridding of individuality. 把"个体在某情境下放弃个人利益"夸大为"社会规范统治、个性被彻底清除"，原文虽提到 individuality 被牺牲，但用的是 sacrificed（让位）而非 ridding（彻底清除）。
B) 与原文相反Emphasis on the adherence to individual differences. 说社群主义强调坚持个体差异，但原文 strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences 明说它限制了个体差异的表达，完全相反。
C) ✓ 正确individuals give up their own interests ↔ Sacrifice of personal interests to serve the common good ↔ for the common good Sacrifice of personal interests for the common good. 是对 individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good 的完整、保守的名词化改写，与预判完全吻合。
D) 过度推断Elimination of individualism and personal choices. 用 Elimination（彻底消除）描述社群主义的效果，但原文只说 individuality and autonomy are sacrificed（让位/牺牲），并未达到"彻底消除"的程度。
questions.quote: In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good.

options.text: Ruling of social norms and ridding of individuality.
Emphasis on the adherence to individual differences.
Sacrifice of personal interests for the common good.
Elimination of individualism and personal choices.

questions.prompt: What does solidarity entail according to the passage?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
根据文章,团结意味着什么?
A) 对个人差异的限制。
B) 对个人主义的反对。
C) 对社会进步的阻碍。
D) 自由主义追求的必然终结。
**判型** What does solidarity entail according to the passage? 询问 solidarity 本质内涵，对应文中明确陈述句。
**拆句** What does solidarity entail according to the passage? 标准疑问句，谓语动词 entail 是关键考词，"according to the passage" 为状语，结构简单。
**定位** solidarity 也被视为对极端强调个人主义与选择自由的一种反应（反对）。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴A limit to personal differences. 来自 restricts expression and practice of individual differences，那是讲社群主义的代价，不是讲 solidarity 整体的内涵；题干问的是solidarity entail 什么。
B) ✓ 正确a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism ↔ An opposition to individualism the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice ↔ individualism An opposition to individualism 是 a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism 最直接的同义改写，与预判一致。
C) 张冠李戴A hindrance to social advancement. 把 solidarity 说成"社会进步的障碍"，但原文see society as a hindrance to their freedom to make choices 是说"自由派认为社会是其自由的障碍"，hindrance 的主语应为 society 而非 solidarity；并且 P7 明说solidarity 是 order and progress 的关键。
D) 过度推断An inevitable end to liberal pursuits. 说 solidarity 会"不可避免地终结"自由派追求，但原文只说它是对极端个人主义的 reaction（反对/回应），并未说会"终结"或必然成功，且 inevitable 加重了语气。
questions.quote: Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice.

options.text: A limit to personal differences.
An opposition to individualism.
A hindrance to social advancement.
An inevitable end to liberal pursuits.

questions.prompt: What do social theorists think of solidarity?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
社会理论家如何看待团结?
A) 它与最弱势群体尤其相关。
B) 它在保护人类尊严方面最为有效。
C) 它对社会的进步与秩序至关重要。
D) 它对于避免肤浅关系不可或缺。
**判型** What do social theorists think of solidarity? 问的是 social theorists 这一具体群体的看法，定位明确，不是整篇作者主旨。
**拆句** What do social theorists think of solidarity? 主语 "social theorists"，think of 是固定搭配"看待/认为"，结构平铺直叙。
**定位** 但是，尽管 solidarity 有诸多面向，社会理论家们仍把它视为推动社会秩序与进步的关键因素。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全It is especially relevant to the most vulnerable. 取自 listens to and acts on the cries of the most vulnerable，原文这是对 solidarity 内涵的一种延伸描述，且"especially relevant"是干扰项的额外断言；题干问的是社会理论家对 solidarity 的整体看法，而非"它最关乎谁"。
B) 过度推断It is most effective in protecting human dignity. 用 most effective（最有效）做绝对化判断，但原文 It fights for the protection of human dignity 仅说它"为人类尊严而战"，并未与其他事物比较"最有效"。
C) ✓ 正确a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society ↔essential to progress and order in society bringing about order and progress in society ↔ progress and order in society essential to progress and order in society 是 a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society 的标准同义改写，与预判完全对应。
D) 偷换概念It is indispensable to avoiding shallow relationships. 说 solidarity 对"避免肤浅关系"必不可少，但原文 they regard a genuine solidarity as more than just shallow relationships based on common interests 是说"真正的 solidarity 不仅仅是肤浅关系"，是在界定 solidarity 本身，而非说它用于"避免肤浅关系"。
questions.quote: But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society.

options.text: It is especially relevant to the most vulnerable.
It is most effective in protecting human dignity.
It is essential to progress and order in society.
It is indispensable to avoiding shallow relationships.

title: We humans love to believe we are special,…

sentences.text: We humans love to believe we are special, but science and technology have repeatedly proved this conviction wrong.
People (26)____ thought that humans were the only animals to use tools, to form teams or to propagate culture, but science has shown that other animals do each of these things.

passage.translation: 我们人类喜欢相信自己是特殊的，但科学和技术已经反复证明这种信念是错误的。人们曾经认为人类是唯一会使用工具、组建团队或传播文化的动物，但科学已经表明其他动物也会做这些事情。

sentences.text: Meanwhile, technology has quashed(使无效), one by one, claims that (27)____ tasks require a human brain.
The first adding machine was invented in 1623.
This past year, a computer-generated work won an art contest.
I believe the moment when computers meet and (28)____ human intelligence is on the horizon.

passage.translation: 与此同时，技术已经逐一使那些认为认知任务需要人类大脑的说法失效。第一台加法机发明于1623年。今年，一件由计算机生成的作品赢得了艺术竞赛。我相信计算机达到并超越人类智能的时刻即将到来。

sentences.text: How will human intelligence and creativity be valued when machines become smarter and more creative than the brightest people?
There will likely be a spectrum.
In some (29)____ , people still value humans doing things, even if a computer can do it better.
It's been a quarter of a century since a computer beat world champion Garry Kasparov, but human chess hasn't gone away.

passage.translation: 当机器变得比最聪明的人更聪明、更有创造力时，人类的智能和创造力将如何被评价？可能会出现一个范围。在某些领域，人们仍然重视人类做事，即使计算机能做得更好。自计算机击败世界冠军Garry Kasparov以来已经过去了四分之一个世纪，但人类国际象棋并没有消失。

sentences.text: In other fields, human skill will seem costly and (30)____ .

Take illustration for example: most readers don't care whether the graphic (31)____ a magazine article was drawn by a person or a computer — they just want it to be relevant, new and perhaps (32)____ .

passage.translation: 在其他领域，人类技能将显得昂贵而多余。以插图为例：大多数读者并不在乎杂志文章配图是由人还是计算机绘制的——他们只是希望它相关、新颖，或许还有趣。

sentences.text: And, of course, this question isn't black or white.

Many fields will be a (33)____ , where some humans find a lucky place, but most of the work is done by computers, like in manufacturing today, where much of the work is accomplished by robots, but some humans must be there to (34)____ the machines.

passage.translation: 当然，这个问题并非非黑即白。许多领域将是混合的，一些人找到幸运的位置，但大部分工作由计算机完成，就像今天的制造业，大部分工作由机器人完成，但必须有一些人在那里监督机器。

sentences.text: If history is any guide, it's almost certain that advances in AI will cause more jobs to (35)____ , that creative workers with human-only skills will become richer but fewer in number, and that those who own creative technology will become the new ultra-rich.

passage.translation: 如果历史可以作为指引，几乎可以肯定的是，人工智能的进步将导致更多工作消失，拥有人类独有技能的创意工作者将变得更富有但数量更少，而那些拥有创意技术的人将成为新的超级富豪。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
We humans love to believe we are special, but science and technology have repeatedly proved this conviction wrong. People {{26}} thought that humans were the only animals to use tools, to form teams or to propagate culture, but science has shown that other animals do each of these things.

Meanwhile, technology has quashed(使无效), one by one, claims that {{27}} tasks require a human brain. The first adding machine was invented in 1623. This past year, a computer-generated work won an art contest. I believe the moment when computers meet and {{28}} human intelligence is on the horizon.

How will human intelligence and creativity be valued when machines become smarter and more creative than the brightest people? There will likely be a spectrum. In some {{29}} , people still value humans doing things, even if a computer can do it better. It's been a quarter of a century since a computer beat world champion Garry Kasparov, but human chess hasn't gone away.

In other fields, human skill will seem costly and {{30}} . Take illustration for example: most readers don't care whether the graphic {{31}} a magazine article was drawn by a person or a computer — they just want it to be relevant, new and perhaps {{32}} .

And, of course, this question isn't black or white. Many fields will be a {{33}} , where some humans find a lucky place, but most of the work is done by computers, like in manufacturing today, where much of the work is accomplished by robots, but some humans must be there to {{34}} the machines.

If history is any guide, it's almost certain that advances in AI will cause more jobs to {{35}} , that creative workers with human-only skills will become richer but fewer in number, and that those who own creative technology will become the new ultra-rich.
