questions.explanation:
**答案** I) once 副词
**词性槽** 主语与谓语之间的状语位
**依据** 与 but 后的 has shown 构成今昔对比People __(26)__ thought that humans were the only animals to use tools, to form teams or to propagate culture, but science has shown that other animals do each of these things. 前半句过去时 thought、后半句现在完成时 has shown，典型 "过去曾以为 /如今已证明" 结构，填 once（曾经）正好咬合这条时间逻辑。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
N) tentatively 语义指向不对，是 "试探性地" 而非 "曾经" tentatively 意为 "暂时地、试探性地"，强调态度不坚定。但原文说人们 "长久以为人类是唯一会用工具的动物"，这是一种**坚信**而非试探，与下句被 but 反转的语气不匹配。

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) cognitive 形容词
**词性槽** 名词 tasks 前的前置定语
**依据** 与 "require a human brain" 同义呼应claims that __(27)__ tasks require a human brain——能 require a human brain（需要人脑）的任务，正是 cognitive tasks（认知性的任务、需要思维加工的任务）。下一句又用 adding machine、computer-generated art、computer matches human intelligence 反复指向 "智力/认知"，B 与上下文构成最稳同义网。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) intuitive"直觉的" 与 "人脑认知" 范围不符intuitive 指 "凭直觉的"，强调非理性、不依靠分析。而本段下文举例（加法机、AI 绘画、计算机匹敌人类智能）恰恰是**理性认知**任务被机器接管，与 intuitive 的语义指向相反。
D) entertaining"有趣的" 偏娱乐，与 "需要人脑" 不沾边entertaining 指 "令人愉快的、有娱乐性的"，与 require a human brain（需要人脑）这一论点完全脱节，纯属词性诱饵。
K) redundant "多余的任务" 与原意南辕北辙redundant 是 "多余的、被裁掉的"——"多余的任务需要人脑" 在逻辑上根本说不通；况且 K 后文 30 题正等着它。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— 看到 AI 话题就联想 "直觉"。intuitive 词性对、又与 AI 话题表面沾边（"机器没有直觉"），最易让考生误填。防坑：claims that __(27)__ tasks require a human brain 里同句锚词是 a human brain，"需要人脑的任务" = cognitive（认知性的），而非 intuitive（直觉的）。"找同句同义锚" 是六级选词填空的必修招式。

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) surpass 动词
**词性槽** and 并列谓语：computers meet and __ human intelligence
**依据** "匹敌并超越" 是 AI 论述的固定搭配I believe the moment when computers meet and __(28)__ human intelligence is on the horizon.——meet（达到/匹敌）+ surpass（超越）是 AI 话题里最常见的递进搭配，且呼应第三段 when machines become smarter and more creative than the brightest people（变得比最聪明的人更聪明、更有创造力），证实方向就是 "超越"。

**答案** C) domains 名词
**词性槽** 介词 In some 后的名词复数
**依据** "在某些领域里" 与下文 In other fields 形成对照下一段开头 In other fields, human skill will seem costly and __(30)__. 用 In other fields与本段 In some __(29)__ 形成 "在某些领域 / 在另一些领域" 的并列对照；domains（领域）与 fields 同义，正好咬合这条段间对照逻辑。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
L) stances "立场" 与下文 fields 不对应stances 指 "立场、姿态"，是抽象观点。但下段 in other fields 明确把对比维度定在 "领域" 而非 "立场"——填 stances 会让段间对照失锚。
G) impetus 形态不对：单数且不可数impetus 通常作不可数单数（推动力），与 some + 复数名词的结构不合；语义上 "在某些推动力里人们仍重视人类" 也不通。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 L) —— 复数名词形态一致的假同义。stances 与 domains 同为复数名词、同能套进 In some __ 结构，最易混。防坑：盯紧下段段首 In other fields——"领域 vs 立场" 是两条线，fields 同义对应 domains。"段间对照锁名词" 一招直接破。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) redundant 形容词
**词性槽** 并列连词 and 后接形容词，与 costly 并列
**依据** "昂贵 + 多余" 共同描述被淘汰的人类技能本段例 most readers don't care whether the graphic __(31)__ a magazine article was drawn by a person or a computer——读者并不在意是人画的还是机器画的，意味着人类技能既贵又**没必要**，redundant（多余的、被裁掉的）正好把这层负面评价点透。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
D) entertaining 褒义色彩与 costly 不同向entertaining（有趣的）偏褒，而 costly 偏负面——并列时色彩不一致，逻辑上 "昂贵且有趣"也无法描述被市场淘汰的人类劳动。
H) intuitive"直觉的" 与 "被淘汰" 主线不沾intuitive 指 "直觉的"，并不直接传递价值高低、是否被取代的信息，与本段 "人类技能将变得不值" 的论点错位。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) accompanying 形容词
**词性槽** the graphic __ a magazine article：现在分词作后置定语
**依据** "配文插图" 是固定搭配the graphic __(31)__ a magazine article was drawn by a person or a computer——graphic accompanying a magazine article 即 "配在杂志文章旁的插图"，accompany 与graphic/article 是新闻出版中的常规搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) evoking "唤起一篇文章" 搭配不成立evoking 是 "唤起、引发"，搭配对象多是 emotion/memory 等抽象名词；evoke a magazine article（唤起一篇杂志文章）语义不通，逻辑上也不是 "插图与文章" 的关系。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) entertaining 形容词
**词性槽** and 并列形容词链：relevant, new and __
**依据** 读者期待 "贴题、新颖、有趣" 三件套they just want it to be relevant, new and perhaps __(32)__.——读者作为大众，对杂志插图的诉求是 relevant（与文章相关）、new（新鲜）、entertaining（有趣）这三件套，构成同色彩并列；perhaps 又留了余地，正合 "有趣" 这种偏锦上添花的属性。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) intuitive "直觉的" 与并列项不同色彩intuitive 偏认知/操作领域（如 intuitive interface 易上手的界面），与读者读杂志插图时的诉求错位；与 relevant、new 也无法构成同色彩并列。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) hybrid 名词
**词性槽** a + __ 单数可数名词位
**依据** where 从句直接定义 "人机混合" Many fields will be a __(33)__, where some humans find a lucky place, but most of the work is done by computers, like in manufacturing today, where much of the work is accomplished by robots, but some humans must be there to __(34)__ the machines.——where 从句里 "some humans … but most of the work is done by computers" 把空名词定义成 "人机混合体"，hybrid 是唯一精准对应词。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) impetus "推动力" 与 "人机混合" 错位impetus 是 "推动力、动力"，无法被 where 从句中 "既有人又有计算机" 的描述合理修饰；"许多领域将成为一种推动力" 在语义上也不通。

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) oversee 动词
**词性槽** must be there to + 动词原形
**依据** "机器为主、人来监管" 正是本段图景much of the work is accomplished by robots, but some humans must be there to__(34)__ the machines. 转折 but 之后明确：活儿主要由机器人干，但仍要有人 "在场"——"在场对机器" 干什么？最贴合的就是 "监督、监管" oversee，与制造业现实经验也一致。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) surpass "超越机器" 与本段 "人辅助机器" 逻辑反向surpass（超越）会把句意变成 "人必须在场以超越机器"，与 but 引出的 "机器为主、人为辅"的图景反向；况且 surpass 已是 28 题的答案。
O) vanish 不及物动词不能带 machines vanish 是不及物动词（消失），其后不能直接接 the machines 作宾语；语义上 "人必须在那里以消失机器" 也不通。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) vanish 动词
**词性槽** cause more jobs to + 动词原形
**依据** AI 会让更多工作消失，对应全段悲观预测advances in AI will cause more jobs to __(35)__, that creative workers with human- only skills will become richer but fewer in number——后半 "人类技能工作者会变少"直接揭示前半 "更多工作 __" 的方向是 "消失"，vanish 正中靶心。

title: During his acceptance speech for the Nobel Peace…

sentences.text: During his acceptance speech for the Nobel Peace Prize, Martin Luther King Jr. said, "I believe that unarmed truth and unconditional love will have the final word in reality."

passage.translation: 在诺贝尔和平奖获奖感言中,小马丁·路德·金说:"我相信,手无寸铁的真理和无条件的爱在现实中终将获胜。"

sentences.text: More than five decades later, our society is still struggling to separate truth from fantasy, fact from fiction.
From disputes over the climate change to debates about how slavery is taught, America is at a crossroads.
And the battle for equity is at the heart of these vital conversations.

passage.translation: 五十多年后,我们的社会仍在努力区分真实与幻想、事实与虚构。从关于气候变化的争论到关于如何教授奴隶制的辩论,美国正处于十字路口。而公平之战正是这些重要对话的核心。

sentences.text: Study after study shows that inequity has had appalling consequences.

A 2020 report by Citi indicated that "Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90 – $113 billion" if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades.

passage.translation: 一项又一项研究表明,不公平已经造成了骇人的后果。花旗集团2020年的一份报告指出,"如果过去二十年高等教育相关的公平问题得到充分解决,黑人学生本可以增加900亿至1130亿美元的终身收入"。

sentences.text: This statistic represents a flood of issues we've failed to confront as a nation.
It also highlights one truth: We're missing out on valuable opportunities to bridge the differences that divide us.
However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.

passage.translation: 这一统计数据代表着我们作为一个国家未能直面的大量问题。它也凸显了一个真相:我们正在错失弥合分歧的宝贵机会。然而,通过传承马丁·路德·金的遗志,我们可以让国家重回通往真正公平的道路。

sentences.text: Students — and adults for that matter — simply cannot understand the conflicts we have today without understanding what caused them in the first place.
That means we have a responsibility to help them make connections between US history and current events.
It also means giving them the tools they need to address inequity and bias in their own lives.
Adherence to these principles, along with a commitment to truthful dialogue, can help every student better appreciate how far we've come and more clearly see the roads we have yet to travel.

passage.translation: 学生——以及成年人——如果不理解最初导致冲突的原因,就根本无法理解我们今天面临的冲突。这意味着我们有责任帮助他们在美国历史与时事之间建立联系。这也意味着要给他们提供在自己生活中应对不公平和偏见所需的工具。遵循这些原则,加上对真实对话的承诺,可以帮助每个学生更好地认识到我们已经走了多远,并更清楚地看到我们尚未踏上的道路。

sentences.text: With more truthful analysis of the need for more qualified, diverse educators, we can improve our recruiting, training, and retention strategies for schools across the country.

passage.translation: 通过更真实地分析对更多合格的、多元化教育工作者的需求,我们可以改进全国各地学校的招聘、培训和留用策略。

sentences.text: Unfortunately, our deeply rooted divisions are delaying these advancements.
A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is "more divided than ever before".
But reports of increased polarization shouldn't persuade us to look away from one another.
Instead, they should compel us to address our shared issues head-on.

passage.translation: 不幸的是,我们根深蒂固的分歧正在延缓这些进步。最近的一项调查发现,77%的美国人认为国家"比以往任何时候都更加分裂"。但关于两极分化加剧的报道不应说服我们将目光从彼此身上移开。相反,它们应该促使我们正面应对我们共同的问题。

sentences.text: We are not, as some would suggest, living in a "post-racial society".
We simply cannot afford to keep our heads buried in the sand when it comes to racial inequity.
Unless we get honest about intolerance, bias, and how these social diseases impact the ways we treat one another, injustice will continue to haunt us.
But our children and our grandchildren deserve better.

passage.translation: 正如一些人所暗示的,我们并非生活在一个"后种族社会"。在种族不平等问题上,我们根本无法继续将头埋在沙子里。除非我们诚实面对不宽容、偏见,以及这些社会疾病如何影响我们彼此对待的方式,否则不公正将继续困扰我们。但我们的子孙后代应该得到更好的未来。

sentences.text: On this Martin Luther King Day and beyond, let's commit to working together to disrupt the status quo.
Let's continue to build a better, more inclusive nation; and in the words of Martin Luther King Jr., "A society at peace with itself, a society that can live with its conscience."

passage.translation: 在这个马丁·路德·金日以及之后的日子里,让我们致力于共同努力打破现状。让我们继续建设一个更美好、更包容的国家;用小马丁·路德·金的话说,"一个与自身和平相处的社会,一个能够心安理得的社会。"

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A) , B) , C) and D) . You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does the author think about today's America?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者对当今美国有何看法?
A) 美国正努力将虚构变为现实。
B) 美国一直是许多重要对话的焦点。
C) 美国在真正实现公平之前还有很长的路要走。
D) 美国已经到了人们在几乎每个问题上都存在分歧的地步。
**判型** 题干 What does the author think about today's America? 问的是作者对一个明确对象的具体看法，不是问全文主旨、不含 infer/imply。
**拆句** 句子结构是 What does the author think about today's America?，主语 the author、谓语 think、介词宾语 today's America；无从句、无否定，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 然而，只要传承（马丁·路德·）金的精神遗产，我们就能让国家重新回到通向真正公平的道路上。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反struggling to transform fiction into reality 的字面义是「努力把虚构变成现实」，与struggling to separate truth from fantasy（努力分清真相与幻象）方向相反——原文是要分开两者，不是把虚构变成现实。
B) 张冠李戴It has been the focus of many vital conversations 把美国当成「对话的焦点」；但the battle for equity is at the heart of these vital conversations 里说的是「公平之战是这些对话的核心」，焦点是 equity，不是美国。
C) ✓ 正确get our country back on the path toward true equity ↔still has a long way to go before equity can be truly realized our society is still struggling to separate truth from fantasy↔ still has a long way to go预判「离真正公平还远」与 still has a long way to go before equity can be truly realized 一一对应，且呼应 still struggling——锁定 C。
D) 以偏概全disagree on nearly every issue 把分歧泛化到「几乎每一个议题」；原文只举了climate change 与 how slavery is taught 等具体议题，且作者关心的核心是 equity，没有「几乎每个议题都有分歧」的论断。
questions.quote: However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.

options.text: It is struggling to transform fiction into reality.
It has been the focus of many vital conversations.
It still has a long way to go before equity can be truly realized.
It has got to a point where people disagree on nearly every issue.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about black students in the past 20 years?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
从文章中我们了解到过去20年中黑人学生的什么情况?
A) 他们在高等教育方面受到了不公平的对待。
B) 他们一直在努力奋斗以解决公平问题。
C) 他们使自己的终身收入增加了数十亿美元。
D) 他们已经认识到种族歧视的后果。
**判型** 题干 What do we learn from the passage about black students in the past 20 years?问从文中「得知」什么，明确锁定群体加时间，是要求回原文复述事实。
**拆句** What do we learn from the passage about black students in the past 20 years? 是What...about... 结构，about 后跟的 black students in the past 20 years 是定位对象；结构清晰，无陷阱。
**定位** 花旗集团 2020 年的一份报告指出：如果过去二十年里高等教育中的公平问题得到了妥善处理，黑人学生本可以多挣 900 亿到 1130 亿美元的终身收入。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades↔ unfairly treated regarding higher education Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90 – $113 billion ↔They have been unfairly treated预判「过去二十年高等教育对黑人学生不公」与 unfairly treated regarding higher education 一一对应——锁定 A。
B) 无中生有battling hard to address equity issues 把「被动遭遇不公」换成「主动奋力解决公平问题」；原文只说公平问题如果被妥善处理黑人学生本可多挣钱，并未说他们自己在奋斗解决。
C) 与原文相反They have boosted their lifetime incomes by billions of dollars 用现在完成时陈述「已经多挣了」；原文是 could have increased 虚拟语气，含义是「本可以但实际没有」——选项把虚拟当作了现实。
D) 偷换概念come to see the consequences of racial discrimination 把话题偷换成「看清种族歧视的后果」；原文谈的是高等教育公平问题与黑人学生的收入损失，并未提及他们「认识到歧视后果」这一心理变化。
questions.quote: A 2020 report by Citi indicated that "Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90 – $113 billion" if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades.

options.text: They have been unfairly treated regarding higher education.
They have been battling hard to address equity issues.
They have boosted their lifetime incomes by billions of dollars.
They have come to see the consequences of racial discrimination.

questions.prompt: How can Americans bridge the differences that divide them?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
美国人如何能够弥合分裂他们的分歧?
A) 通过处理他们面临的棘手问题。
B) 通过抓住每个机会来增进种族和谐。
C) 通过继续追求Martin Luther King Jr.的事业。
D) 通过努力识别极其宝贵的机会。
**判型** 题干 How can Americans bridge the differences that divide them? 问的是「如何做到X」，要求从原文找具体路径，是细节题。
**拆句** How can Americans bridge the differences that divide them? 中 that divide them 是定语从句修饰 differences，等于 the differences which divide Americans；结构稍长，但无否定无比较，逻辑直白。
**定位** 然而，只要传承（马丁·路德·）金的精神遗产，我们就能让国家重新回到通向真正公平的道路上。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问dealing with the thorny issues confronting them 描述的是「直面棘手问题」。原文address our shared issues head-on 这一表述是作者对 polarization 的回应，并非他给出的「弥合分歧」路径；定位句 P4 给出的路径只有 honoring King's legacy。
B) 无中生有seizing every chance to enhance racial harmony 把答案拉到「抓住一切机会促进种族和谐」。原文只谈 equity、bridge differences、honor King's legacy，没有 racial harmony 的提法，也没有 every chance 这种全称量化。
C) ✓ 正确by honoring King's legacy ↔ continuing to pursue Martin Luther King Jr.'s cause in the words of Martin Luther King Jr., "A society at peace with itself, a society that can live with its conscience."↔ Martin Luther King Jr.'s cause预判「继承金的精神遗产」与 By continuing to pursue Martin Luther King Jr.'s cause 一一对应——锁定 C。
D) 偷换概念striving to identify exceedingly valuable opportunities 截取了 missing out on valuable opportunities 中的 valuable opportunities，但原文的语义是「我们正在错失机会」，并非「努力识别极有价值的机会」；选项把「错过」扭成「努力寻找」。
questions.quote: However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.

options.text: By dealing with the thorny issues confronting them.
By seizing every chance to enhance racial harmony.
By continuing to pursue Martin Luther King Jr.'s cause.
By striving to identify exceedingly valuable opportunities.

questions.prompt: How do most Americans view America as a nation according to a recent survey?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
根据最近的一项调查,大多数美国人如何看待美国这个国家?
A) 美国被迫解决其历史性的社会问题。
B) 美国正在推迟朝着种族平等的进步。
C) 美国使自己免于两极分化。
D) 美国已经变得越来越分裂。
**判型** 题干 How do most Americans view America as a nation according to a recent survey? 明确说 according to a recent survey，要求复述调查数据，是细节题。
**拆句** How do most Americans view America as a nation according to a recent survey? 主干是 How do most Americans view America，as a nation 是补足语相当于把 America视作一个国家整体，according to a recent survey 是状语限定信息来源；无陷阱。
**定位** 一项近期调查发现，77% 的美国人认为这个国家「前所未有地分裂」。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴compelled to address its historical social issues 借用了 they should compel us to address our shared issues head-on 的措辞，但那句话是作者对 polarization 报告的回应，不是 most Americans 在调查中表达的看法；本题问的是 most Americans 的看法。
B) 张冠李戴delaying advancements toward racial equality 借用 our deeply rooted divisions are delaying these advancements，但原文里拖延进步的主语是 our deeply rooted divisions（根深蒂固的分裂），且这是作者的判断而非调查结论；本题问的是调查里美国人怎么看美国。
C) 与原文相反has kept itself from polarization 意为「避免了两极分化」。原文 reports of increased polarization 明确说「两极分化在加剧」，且 77% 的美国人认为国家更分裂——选项与调查结论方向相反。
D) ✓ 正确more divided than ever before ↔ increasingly split 77 percent of Americans believe ↔ It has become increasingly split预判「国家越来越分裂」与 has become increasingly split 一一对应——锁定 D。
questions.quote: A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is "more divided than ever before".

options.text: It is compelled to address its historical social issues.
It is delaying advancements toward racial equality.
It has kept itself from polarization.
It has become increasingly split.

questions.prompt: What does the author suggest Americans do?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者建议美国人做什么?
A) 确保他们的子孙后代的福祉。
B) 共同努力解决国家的公平问题。
C) 克制他们的不宽容和歧视。
D) 恢复社会秩序以建立和谐的国家。
**判型** 题干 What does the author suggest Americans do? 问作者建议美国人做什么——是一个落到具体动作的细节题，不是问全文中心。
**拆句** What does the author suggest Americans do? 是宾语从句结构，suggest 后省略that，Americans 是从句主语、do 是从句谓语原形；结构清晰，无陷阱。
**定位** 在马丁·路德·金日及今后，让我们一起承诺携手努力，打破现状。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问Ensure the well-being of their children and grandchildren 借用 our children and our grandchildren deserve better，但那句是说「下一代值得更好」——是作者的忧虑动机，不是他给读者的具体建议；选项把动机当成了行动。
B) ✓ 正确let's commit to working together to disrupt the status quo↔Make joint efforts to tackle the nation's equity issues the path toward true equity↔the nation's equity issues预判「联手打破现状」与 Make joint efforts to tackle the nation's equity issues 一一对应——锁定 B。
C) 偷换概念Restrain their intolerance and discrimination 把答案换成「克制偏狭与歧视」。原文Unless we get honest about intolerance, bias 要求的是「对偏狭与偏见保持诚实」——是承认与谈论，而不是 restrain（克制压抑）。
D) 偷换概念Restore social order for a harmonious nation 借用末段 build a better, more inclusive nation 的「建设国家」色彩，但 restore social order（恢复社会秩序）原文从未提及；原文是「建设更包容」，不是「恢复秩序」。
questions.quote: On this Martin Luther King Day and beyond, let's commit to working together to disrupt the status quo.

options.text: Ensure the well-being of their children and grandchildren.
Make joint efforts to tackle the nation's equity issues.
Restrain their intolerance and discrimination.
Restore social order for a harmonious nation.

title: Many see friendships as a comfort blanket: a…

sentences.text: Many see friendships as a comfort blanket: a shoulder to cry on, a reliable soul to confide in.
However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process.

passage.translation: 许多人将友谊视为一条慰藉的毛毯:一个可以倾诉的肩膀,一个可以信赖的灵魂。然而,更多时候,在我们急于追求个人成功的过程中,我们沿途失去了朋友,而这已成为这一过程的一部分。

sentences.text: The chaos and never-ending turmoil that accompanies everyday life is an aggressive obstacle in the pursuit of stable friendships.
As students, we use this excuse to shrug off losing people who we once thought to be loved ones.

passage.translation: 伴随日常生活而来的混乱和永无止境的动荡是追求稳定友谊的严重障碍。作为学生,我们用这个借口来对失去那些我们曾经认为是挚爱之人的事实不以为意。

sentences.text: Instead of viewing our lives as a race, where everyone is on their own path to some form of success, we must relearn to value the connections we make along the track.
We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom.

passage.translation: 我们不应该将生活视为一场竞赛,每个人都在通往某种形式成功的自己的道路上,而必须重新学会珍视我们在这条轨道上建立的联系。我们必须重新评估激进的个人自由所带来的危害。

sentences.text: Radical individualism elevates the freedom of the individual over the collective.
It argues, for instance, that universal healthcare, an example of collectivism, threatened the dream of many Americans.

passage.translation: 激进个人主义将个人自由置于集体之上。例如,它认为全民医疗保健这一集体主义的例子威胁到了许多美国人的梦想。

sentences.text: Many of us have fallen victim to an individualistic culture.
Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person.

passage.translation: 我们中的许多人已经成为个人主义文化的受害者。社会倾向于颂扬个人成就,并基于这样的假设对其进行赞扬:获胜或成功是比别人更努力工作的结果。

sentences.text: As a society, we idolize the concept of "losing friends on the road to success".
I remember hearing in high school, "Don't worry about losing friendships, just focus on study and getting into college.
That's all that will matter in the long run," a sentiment that is not unique to my experience.
It's preached in many success stories, and it's embedded in the way we see growth.
Motivational speakers will push their audience to be complacent to the inevitable end of losing friends.
Spend too much time with friends?
You're losing time better utilized on your achievements.
Invest time in your relationships?
Invest time in your work instead.

passage.translation: 作为一个社会,我们崇拜"在通往成功的路上失去朋友"这一概念。我记得在高中时听到过:"不要担心失去友谊,只需专注于学习和考上大学。从长远来看,那才是唯一重要的事情。"这种情绪并非我独有的经历。它在许多成功故事中被宣扬,并且嵌入在我们看待成长的方式中。励志演讲者会推动他们的听众对失去朋友这一不可避免的结局感到满足。花太多时间和朋友在一起?你正在浪费本可以更好地用于你的成就上的时间。在你的人际关系上投入时间?把时间投入到你的工作上吧。

sentences.text: This constant need to succeed has blinded us from seeing through the whirlwind of change that accompanies our everyday lives.
We are expected to tangibly succeed, earn awards, get higher positions, earn better grades.
In order to succeed, we lose friends, and that has sadly become normalized.

passage.translation: 这种对成功的持续需求使我们看不清伴随日常生活而来的变化旋涡。我们被期望取得有形的成功,赢得奖项,获得更高的职位,取得更好的成绩。为了成功,我们失去了朋友,而这已可悲地变得正常化了。

sentences.text: We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors.
Yes, pursue success.
Challenge yourself.
Push limits.
But contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts, doing it alone does not make you more successful or any better than someone who achieved it with the help of others.

passage.translation: 我们不能对失去友谊感到满足,因为它们是我们的锚。是的,追求成功。挑战自己。突破极限。但与所有那些自封的成功专家相反,独自做到这一点并不会让你更成功,也不会让你比在他人帮助下实现它的人更优秀。

sentences.text: Put effort into fostering healthy relationships, and maintaining them through your busy schedule that seems like it leaves no time for anyone else.
Although we may be living in a society that treasures the independent pursuit of achievement, having people to support and love you on the way is far more important than any end result.

passage.translation: 努力培养健康的人际关系,并在你那似乎不为任何其他人留出时间的繁忙日程中维持这些关系。尽管我们可能生活在一个珍视独立追求成就的社会中,但在这条路上有人支持和爱你远比任何最终结果都重要得多。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A) , B) , C) and D) . You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What often happens when people are eager to pursue individual success?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
当人们急于追求个人成功时,常常会发生什么?
A) 他们缺少一个可以倾诉的肩膀。
B) 他们没有可以吐露心声的知己。
C) 他们找不到可靠的朋友。
D) 他们忽视了与朋友的联系。
**判型** What often happens when people are eager to pursue individual success? 是 What引导的事实性问句，问 "经常发生什么"，无 infer/imply/suggest 等推断信号。
**拆句** What often happens when people are eager to pursue individual success? 主句What often happens 是 wh- 主语疑问句；when 引导时间状语从句，be eager to do 意为 "急于做某事"。句意 "当人们急于追求个人成功时，常常会发生什么？" 结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 然而，多数情况下，在我们急于追求个人成功的过程中，我们沿途失去了朋友，而这已经成为这一过程的一部分。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问They lack a shoulder to cry on. 把 a shoulder to cry on 这一对友谊功能的比喻直接当作 "人们当下缺什么" 的结论，但原文这一句是描述 "许多人对友谊的看法"，不是 "人们追求个人成功时发生的结果"。
B) 答非所问They have no soul to confide in. 与 A 同套路，把 a reliable soul to confide in 这一对友谊作用的描绘当作题干所问的 "结果"，但原文这是 "友谊在人们眼中的样子"，不是"追求成功时发生的事"。
C) 偷换概念They cannot find reliable friends. 说 "找不到可靠朋友"，但原文 we lose friends 强调的是 "主动放弃/丢失现有朋友"，与 "找不到" 是两种不同动作；原文从未说过 "找不到"。
D) ✓ 正确we lose friends along the way ↔ They ignore their ties with friends.在四项中，只有 They ignore their ties with friends. 与预判 "失去/疏远朋友" 在主谓宾三层都吻合，故选 D。
questions.quote: However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process.

options.text: They lack a shoulder to cry on.
They have no soul to confide in.
They cannot find reliable friends.
They ignore their ties with friends.

questions.prompt: What does the author advise people to do in their pursuit of radical individualism?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者建议人们在追求激进个人主义时做什么?
A) 重新审视其有害影响。
B) 对失去所爱之人不以为意。
C) 避免其中涉及的混乱和动荡。
D) 清除道路上咄咄逼人的障碍。
**判型** What does the author advise people to do in their pursuit of radical individualism?直接问作者建议做什么，是对文中作者表态句的事实性提问，不是推断。
**拆句** What does the author advise people to do in their pursuit of radical individualism? advise sb. to do sth. = 建议某人做某事；their pursuit of radical individualism 是"his/her/their + 名词 + of" 的所属结构，等价于 "when they pursue radical individualism"。句意：作者建议人们在追求极端个人主义时做什么？
**定位** 我们必须重新评估极端个人自由的危害。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom ↔ Reexamine its detrimental effects.在四项中，只有 Reexamine its detrimental effects. 同时覆盖了 "再审视" 与 "危害" 两个语义成分，故选 A。
B) 与原文相反Shrug off the loss of their loved ones. 是 we use this excuse to shrug off losing people who we once thought to be loved ones 里被作者批判的 "错误做法"，并非作者建议。
C) 无中生有Avoid the chaos and turmoil involved. 把 The chaos and never-ending turmoil that accompanies everyday life 这一对生活状态的描述当作作者建议，但原文只是把它列为 "我们丢友谊的借口"，作者既未说要避免也未说要拥抱。
D) 偷换概念Remove aggressive obstacles in the way. 把 an aggressive obstacle in the pursuit of stable friendships 的名词搭配换皮成 "清除前进路上的强劲障碍"，但作者要清除的不是抽象意义上的 "前进路上的障碍"——他要重新评估的是极端个人主义之害。
questions.quote: We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom.

options.text: Reexamine its detrimental effects.
Shrug off the loss of their loved ones.
Avoid the chaos and turmoil involved.
Remove aggressive obstacles in the way.

questions.prompt: What is American society's assumption of personal achievement?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
美国社会对个人成就的假设是什么?
A) 它应当得到适当的庆祝和高度的赞扬。
B) 它是实现个人梦想的可靠途径。
C) 它围绕个人主义文化展开。
D) 它反映了一个人非凡的努力。
**判型** What is American society's assumption of personal achievement? 是 What is 引导的事实性问句，问 "美国社会对个人成就的预设是什么"，无推断信号词。
**拆句** What is American society's assumption of personal achievement? American society's assumption of personal achievement 是双层所属结构：assumption of personal achievement 等于 "对个人成就的预设"；前置 American society's 进一步说明这是 "美国社会的"。句意：美国社会对个人成就的预设是什么？
**定位** 社会倾向于赞美个人成就，并基于一种预设来推崇它，这种预设是：获胜或成功是比别人更努力工作的结果。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问It is to be duly celebrated and highly commended. 把 Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it 的 "社会的做法" 直接当成 "对个人成就的预设"，但题干问的是 the assumption 这个预设本身的内容，不是社会怎么做。
B) 无中生有It is a sure way to fulfill a person's dream. 说 "个人成就是实现梦想的可靠途径"，原文从未将个人成就与 "实现梦想" 直接挂钩；原文涉及 dream 只出现在 threatened the dream of many Americans 中，且是普及医保的对立面，与个人成就的预设无关。
C) 偷换概念It revolves around an individualistic culture. 把 Many of us have fallen victim to an individualistic culture 的上位归类（属于个人主义文化）当作预设本身，但题干问的是 "对个人成就所持的预设"，不是 "个人成就属于哪种文化"。
D) ✓ 正确winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person ↔It reflects a person's exceptional endeavor.四项中只有 It reflects a person's exceptional endeavor. 准确捕捉 "成功背后是个人非凡努力" 这一预设，故选 D。
questions.quote: Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person.

options.text: It is to be duly celebrated and highly commended.
It is a sure way to fulfill a person's dream.
It revolves around an individualistic culture.
It reflects a person's exceptional endeavor.

questions.prompt: What is preached in many success stories?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
许多成功故事中宣扬的是什么?
A) 重视通往成功道路上的学业收获。
B) 把时间投入工作而不是与朋友交往。
C) 在追求个人成功的过程中努力加强友谊。
D) 在学业表现上出类拔萃以进入名牌大学。
**判型** What is preached in many success stories? 问的是 "很多励志故事中宣扬了什么"，是对文中具体表述的事实性追问。
**拆句** What is preached in many success stories? 主语 What 是宾语提前的 wh-；is preached为被动语态，意为 "被宣扬"。句意：很多励志故事中宣扬的是什么？句式简单、无陷阱。
**定位** 励志演讲者会推动听众坦然接受 "失去朋友" 这一不可避免的结局。和朋友花太多时间？你正在浪费本可用于个人成就的时间。把时间投入到人际关系上？不如把时间投入到工作上。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴Attaching importance to academic gains on the road to success. 来自 Don't worry about losing friendships, just focus on study and getting into college，但这是 "高中时听到的话"（作者的个人经历），紧接其后才提到 "a sentiment that is not unique to my experience. It's preached in many success stories"——题干问的是"在 many success stories 中被宣扬的"，即作者随后展开的演讲家观点，不是高中老师的话。
B) ✓ 正确Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead. ↔Investing one's time in work instead of connecting with friends.四项中只有 Investing one's time in work instead of connecting with friends. 同时覆盖 "投入工作" 与 "放弃朋友联系" 两层，故选 B。
C) 与原文相反Trying to strengthen friendships in one's pursuit of personal success. 是作者自己在 P8 P9 提出的反向建议，不是 success stories 所宣扬的内容；many success stories 宣扬的恰恰是放弃友谊。
D) 以偏概全Excelling in academic performance to get into a prestigious college. 同样源自focus on study and getting into college 这句高中老师的话，且把 college 升级为prestigious college（名校）属于无中生有；不属于 many success stories 所宣扬的内容。
questions.quote: Motivational speakers will push their audience to be complacent to the inevitable end of losing friends. Spend too much time with friends? You're losing time better utilized on your achievements. Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead.

options.text: Attaching importance to academic gains on the road to success.
Investing one's time in work instead of connecting with friends.
Trying to strengthen friendships in one's pursuit of personal success.
Excelling in academic performance to get into a prestigious college.

questions.prompt: What can we infer from the passage regarding the pursuit of success?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （推断题）
**题目译文**
从文章中我们可以推断出关于追求成功的什么?
A) 没有人能不突破极限而取得成功。
B) 没有人能够承受忽视亲密朋友的后果。
C) 集体主义优于个人主义。
D) 成功学专家常常把人们引向毁灭。
**判型** What can we infer from the passage regarding the pursuit of success? 中 infer 一词直接亮明题型属性。
**拆句** What can we infer from the passage regarding the pursuit of success? What 作 infer的宾语；regarding = 关于，介词短语作后置定语限定 infer 的范围。句意：关于追求成功，我们可以从本文推断出什么？句式平铺直叙。
**定位** 我们不能对失去友谊袖手旁观，因为朋友是我们的锚。是的，去追求成功，挑战自己，突破极限。但与所有自封的成功专家所言相反，独自一人完成它，并不会让你更成功，也并不比那些借助他人之力成功的人更高一筹。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断No one can succeed without pushing limits. 借 Push limits 一词夸大为 "没有人不突破极限就能成功"，但原文仅说 "是的，去突破极限" 作为肯定后退一步的让步话，并未声明 "不突破极限就不能成功"。
B) ✓ 正确We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors.↔No one can afford to neglect close friends. having people to support and love you on the way is far more important than any end result↔No one can afford to neglect close friends.在四项中，只有 No one can afford to neglect close friends. 是从 P8 P9 两处强表态合理延伸一步得到的结论，故选 B。
C) 过度推断Collectivism is superior to individualism. 把 Radical individualism elevates the freedom of the individual over the collective 与 universal healthcare, an example of collectivism 加工成 "集体主义比个人主义优越" 的全称比较，但原文只反对 "极端"个人主义，并未抬高集体主义本身。
D) 过度推断Success experts often lead people to ruin. 来自 contrary to all the self- proclaimed success experts，作者只是 "与所谓的成功专家相反"，并未宣称 "成功专家把人引向毁灭"——ruin 一词是文外强化。
questions.quote: We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors. Yes, pursue success. Challenge yourself. Push limits. But contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts, doing it alone does not make you more successful or any better than someone who achieved it with the help of others.

options.text: No one can succeed without pushing limits.
No one can afford to neglect close friends.
Collectivism is superior to individualism.
Success experts often lead people to ruin.

title: By now, it is generally accepted that regular…

groups.content:
By now, it is generally accepted that regular exercise comes with an assortment of health benefits for people who maintain the habit over time. But is it {{26}} too late to start?

New research looked at people who increased their exercise levels after their 40s beyond levels they had when they were younger and those individuals showed declines in their risk of early {{27}}which were similar to those of people who exercised consistently throughout their lives. This was a{{28}} of 32% to 35% compared to people who did not exercise. Those who began exercising in middle age also saw reductions in their incidence of {{29}} diseases, such as heart disease and cancer, which were similar to the steady exercisers.

So why bother exercising consistently throughout your life? The authors of the study {{30}} that some might interpret the study's findings to mean that they can delay starting an exercise program but this would be a mistake. There are other benefits, both mental and physical, to staying consistently active that we should not {{31}} . These real health benefits include better {{32}} functioning and lowered risk of gaining weight. The latter is {{33}} important given the global obesity epidemic. In addition, experts assert that starting younger is better because, if you make a habit of exercising when you are young, you are more likely to keep up those {{34}} later in life. It is ideal, then, for people to start exercising when they are children or {{35}} , and it is good to maintain an active lifestyle at all times regardless of your age. However, this study does indicate that, if you have not been active, you can still benefit if you start becoming active in your 40s and 50s.
