**定位** 但如果你想戒掉沉迷电子游戏，仅仅决定去跑步未必有效；你可能需要引入另一种强化手段，比如约朋友一起报一节锻炼课。
**改写** it may not be successful to simply substitute one activity with another to effect a change of habit ↔simply deciding you will go for a run might not be as effective委婉否定同义you may need extra reinforcement ↔ You might need to introduce another reinforcement extra=another（同义替换）
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
F F段说rather than giving up something, think about introducing something in its place——这是"替换有效"的主张，但题干Q40在说"简单替换可能不够"+"还要额外强化"，需要的是H段的进一步推论。rather than giving up something, think about introducing something in its place G G段the system that got you to change one behavior might not work for another是策略不通用的总论，没有another reinforcement这类具体强化手段，因此不是源头段。it's natural to assume that when we do manage to adopt and sustain a desirable behavior, that same strategy will work when we want to make another behavior change. But that's not always the case
questions.quote: But if you want to stop indulging in video games, simply deciding you will go for a run might not be as effective. You might need to introduce another reinforcement, such as meeting a friend and booking an exercise class together.

questions.prompt: One should introduce something new to replace an old habit instead of simply kicking it.
questions.explanation:
**答案** F 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
一个人应该引入新的东西来替代旧习惯,而不是简单地戒掉它。
**锚点** introduce something new to replace an old habit
**定位** 这就是为什么与其放弃某个东西，不如想想引入新东西去取代它。
**改写** One should introduce something new to replace an old habit ↔think about introducing something in its place introduce+in its place=introduce+replace instead of simply kicking it ↔ rather than giving up something instead of=rather than，kick=give up
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E E段This is called your "cue."核心在解释"线索"概念，例子里虽然有"花草茶换售货机"，但段落主张是"设置触发线索"，不是Q41主张的"introduce instead of kicking"。This is called your "cue." Basically, it's a trigger to perform that particular habit
questions.quote: That's why rather than giving up something, think about introducing something in its place.

questions.prompt: Perfectionists focus too much on their big target and neglect celebrating the small gains they make in the process.
questions.explanation:
**答案** J 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
完美主义者过于关注他们的宏大目标,而忽视了庆祝他们在过程中取得的小进步。
**锚点** Perfectionists + big target + small gains
**定位** 完美主义者在尝试建立行为改变时常陷入一个习惯：他们太专注于大目标，没有花时间庆祝过程中的小进步。
**改写** Perfectionists focus too much on their big target ↔ They focus too much on the big goal几乎同形neglect celebrating the small gains they make in the process ↔don't take the time to celebrate the small progress they make in the process neglect=don't take the time to + gains=progress
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
I I段The perfectionist in you might be screaming to abandon your goals altogether讲的是"失败后被劝放弃"，与Q42主张的"忽视小进步"不是一回事，因此不是答案段。The perfectionist in you might be screaming to abandon your goals altogether
questions.quote: There's a habit that many perfectionists tend to fall into when they try to establish a behavior change. They focus too much on the big goal and don't take the time to celebrate the small progress they make in the process.

questions.prompt: It is of great benefit to us in the long term to conquer the inertia that stops us from making behavioral changes.
questions.explanation:
**答案** L 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
从长远来看,克服阻止我们做出行为改变的惰性对我们大有裨益。
**锚点** long term benefit + conquer the inertia
**定位** 记住，克服阻碍我们实施新改变（如健康饮食或运动）的行为惯性，长期来看能让我们受益，并改善身心健康。
**改写** to conquer the inertia that stops us from making behavioral changes ↔overcoming the behavioral inertia that prevents us from implementing new changes conquer=overcome，stops=prevents It is of great benefit to us in the long term ↔ can benefit us in the long run in the long term=in the long run
questions.quote: Remember, overcoming the behavioral inertia that prevents us from implementing new changes, like eating a healthy diet or exercising, can benefit us in the long run and can improve our physical and mental health.

questions.prompt: The strategy that successfully changed one of your behaviors may not work for some other behavior of yours.
questions.explanation:
**答案** G 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
成功改变你某一行为的策略可能对你的其他某些行为不起作用。
**锚点** strategy that changed one behavior may not work for another
**定位** 有时候，让你改变某种行为成功的那个系统，对另一种行为未必有效。
**改写** The strategy that successfully changed one of your behaviors ↔the system that got you to change one behavior strategy=system，successfully changed=got you to change may not work for some other behavior of yours ↔ might not work for another几乎同形
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
K K段the strategies we used to initiate the change will be equally effective in helping us continue the change谈"启动到维持"的策略迁移，对象是同一个行为的两个阶段；Q44要的是"两个不同行为"。the strategies we used to initiate the change will be equally effective in helping us continue the change H H段You might need to introduce another reinforcement给的是替换之外加强化的具体例子，没有像G段那样把"策略不通用"作为主张提出。You might need to introduce another reinforcement, such as meeting a friend and booking an exercise class together
questions.quote: Sometimes, the system that got you to change one behavior might not work for another.

questions.prompt: Without a happy mood, it seems that our wisdom to adopt a different behavior vanishes.
questions.explanation:
**答案** K 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
没有愉快的心情,我们采用不同行为的智慧似乎就会消失。
**锚点** without a happy mood + wisdom vanishes
**定位** 如果心情低落，那种采取另一种行为的智慧仿佛就消失了，我们又会回到多吃少动的状态。
**改写** Without a happy mood ↔ If our mood is low正反条件互换our wisdom to adopt a different behavior vanishes↔the wisdom to behave differently seems to disappear vanish=disappear，adopt a different behavior=behave differently
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
I I段by Friday you found yourself so exhausted and opted to order greasy takeout描述疲惫导致失败，但没有像K段那样把"行为智慧"与"心情"挂钩。by Friday you found yourself so exhausted and opted to order greasy takeout
questions.quote: If our mood is low, the wisdom to behave differently seems to disappear and we go back to eating more and exercising less.

title: The Curious Case of the Tree That Owns Itself

passage.label: A

sentences.text: In the city of Athens, Georgia, there exists a rather curious local landmark—a large white oak that is almost universally stated to own itself.
Because of this, it is considered one of the most famous trees in the world.
So how did this tree come to own itself and the land around it?

passage.translation: 在佐治亚州的雅典市,存在着一个相当奇特的地方地标——一棵大白橡树,几乎所有人都说它拥有自己。因此,它被认为是世界上最著名的树木之一。那么这棵树是如何拥有自己及其周围土地的呢?

passage.label: B

sentences.text: Sometime in the 19th century a Georgian called Colonel William Jackson reportedly took a liking to the said tree and endeavored to protect it from any danger.
As to why he loved it so, the earliest documented account of this story is an anonymously written front page article in the Athens Weekly Banner published on August 12, 1890.
It states, "Col.
Jackson had watched the tree grow from his childhood, and grew to love it almost as he would a human.
Its luxuriant leaves and sturdy limbs had often protected him from the heavy rains, and out of its highest branches he had many a time gotten the eggs of the feathered singers.

He watched its growth, and when reaching a ripe old age he saw the tree standing in its magnificent proportions, he was pained to think that after his death it would fall into the hands of those who might destroy it."

passage.translation: 19世纪的某个时候,一位名叫William Jackson上校的佐治亚人据说喜欢上了这棵树,并努力保护它免受任何危险。至于他为什么如此喜爱它,关于这个故事最早有记载的描述是1890年8月12日发表在《雅典周报》头版的一篇匿名文章。文章写道:"Jackson上校从童年起就看着这棵树成长,并逐渐像爱一个人一样爱上了它。它茂盛的树叶和粗壮的树枝经常为他遮挡暴雨,他曾多次从它最高的树枝上取到鸣禽的蛋。他看着它成长,当他年事已高看到这棵树矗立在那里,呈现出壮丽的姿态时,一想到自己死后它会落入那些可能毁掉它的人手中,他就感到痛苦。"

passage.label: C

sentences.text: Towards this end, Jackson transferred by means of a deed ownership of the tree and a little land around it to the tree itself.
The deed read, "W.
H.

Jackson for and in consideration of the great affection which he bears the said tree, and his great desire to see it protected has conveyed unto the said oak tree entire possession of itself and of all land within eight feet of it on all sides."

passage.translation: 为此,Jackson通过契约的方式将这棵树及其周围的一小块土地的所有权转让给了树本身。契约上写道:"W. H. Jackson出于对该树的深厚感情,以及保护它的强烈愿望,已将该橡树本身以及其四周八英尺内的所有土地的完全所有权转让给该橡树。"

passage.label: D

sentences.text: In time, the tree came to be something of a tourist attraction, known as The Tree That Owns Itself.
However, in the early 20th century, the tree started showing signs of its slow death, with little that could be done about it.
Father time comes for us all eventually, even our often long lived, tall and leafy fellow custodians(看管者) of Earth.
Finally, on October 9, 1942, the over 30 meter tall and 200-400 year old tree fell, rumor has it, as a result of a severe windstorm and/or via having previously died and its roots rotted.

passage.translation: 随着时间推移,这棵树成为了某种旅游景点,被称为"拥有自己的树"。然而,在20世纪初,这棵树开始显现出缓慢死亡的迹象,对此几乎无能为力。时间老人最终会降临到我们所有人身上,即使是我们这些常常长寿、高大且枝繁叶茂的地球守护者同伴也不例外。最终,在1942年10月9日,这棵超过30米高、有200至400年树龄的树倒下了,传闻是由于一场严重的风暴和/或之前已经死亡且根部腐烂所致。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: About four years later, members of the Junior Ladies Garden Club (who'd tended to the tree before its unfortunate death) tracked down a small tree grown from a nut taken from the original tree.

And so it was that on October 9, 1946, under the direction of Professor Roy Bowden of the College of Agriculture at the University of Georgia, this little tree was transplanted to the location of its ancestor.
A couple of months later, an official ceremony was held featuring none other than the Mayor of Athens, Robert L McWhorter, to commemorate the occasion.

passage.translation: 大约四年后,青年女士园艺俱乐部的成员(她们在树不幸死亡前一直照料它)找到了一棵从原树上取下的果实长成的小树。于是,1946年10月9日,在佐治亚大学农学院Roy Bowden教授的指导下,这棵小树被移植到了其祖先所在的位置。几个月后,举行了一场正式仪式,雅典市长Robert L McWhorter出席,以纪念这一时刻。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: This new tree became known as The Son of the Tree That Owns Itself and it was assumed that, as the original tree's heir, it naturally inherited the land it stood on.
Of course, there are many dozens of other trees known to exist descending from the original, as people taking a nut from it to grow elsewhere was a certainty.
That said, to date, none of the original tree's other children have petitioned the courts for their share of the land, so it seems all good.
In any event, The Son of the Tree That Owns Itself still stands today, though often referred to simply as The Tree That Owns Itself.

passage.translation: 这棵新树被称为"拥有自己的树之子",人们认为,作为原树的继承者,它自然继承了它所站立的土地。当然,已知还有许多其他树木是原树的后代,因为人们肯定会从它那里取果实到别处种植。话虽如此,迄今为止,原树的其他子代都没有向法院请求分得它们在这块土地上的份额,所以似乎一切安好。无论如何,"拥有自己的树之子"至今仍然矗立着,尽管常常被简称为"拥有自己的树"。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: This all brings us around to whether Jackson ever actually gave legal ownership of the tree to itself in the first place and whether such a deed is legally binding.

passage.translation: 这一切让我们回到一个问题:Jackson当初是否真的在法律上将树的所有权给了树本身,以及这样的契约是否具有法律约束力。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Well, to begin with, it turns out Jackson only spent about three years of his life in Athens, starting at the age of 43 from 1829 to 1832, sort of dismissing the idea that he loved the tree from spending time under it as a child and watching it grow, and then worrying about what would happen to it after he died.
Further, an extensive search of land ownership records in Athens does not seem to indicate Jackson ever owned the land the tree sits on.

passage.translation: 首先,事实证明Jackson在雅典只生活了大约三年,从1829年到1832年,当时他43岁,这在一定程度上否定了他从小就在树下度过时光、看着它成长、然后担心自己死后它会怎样的说法。此外,对雅典土地所有权记录的广泛搜索似乎并未表明Jackson曾拥有过树所在的那块土地。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: He did live on a lot of land directly next to it for those three years, but whether he owned that land or not isn't clear.
Whatever the case, in 1832 a four acre parcel, which included the land the tree was on and the neighboring land Jackson lived on, among others, was sold to University professor Malthus A Ward.
In the transaction, Ward was required to pay Jackson a sum of $1,200 (about $31, 000 today), either for the property itself or simply in compensation for improvements Jackson had made on the lot.

In the end, whether he ever owned the neighboring lot or was simply allowed to use it while he allegedly worked at the University, he definitely never owned the lot the tree grew on, which is the most important bit for the topic at hand.

passage.translation: 在那三年里,他确实住在紧邻树的一大块土地上,但他是否拥有那块土地尚不清楚。无论如何,1832年,一块四英亩的地块被卖给了大学教授Malthus A Ward,其中包括树所在的土地以及Jackson居住的邻近土地等。在这笔交易中,Ward被要求向Jackson支付1200美元(相当于今天约31000美元),要么是购买房产本身,要么只是补偿Jackson在该地块上所做的改进。最终,无论他是否曾拥有邻近的地块,或只是在据称他在大学工作期间被允许使用它,他肯定从未拥有过树生长的那块地,而这对于我们讨论的话题来说是最重要的一点。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: After Professor Ward purchased the land, Jackson and his family purchased a 655 acre parcel a few miles away and moved there.
Ten years later, in 1844, Jackson seemed to have come into financial difficulties and had his little plantation seized by the Clarke County Sheriff's office and auctioned off to settle the mortgage.
Thus, had he owned some land in Athens itself, including the land the tree sat on, presumably he would have sold it to raise funds or otherwise had it taken as well.

passage.translation: Ward教授购买土地后,Jackson和他的家人在几英里外购买了一块655英亩的地块并搬到了那里。十年后的1844年,Jackson似乎陷入了财务困境,他的小种植园被Clarke县警长办公室查封并拍卖以清偿抵押贷款。因此,如果他在雅典本身拥有一些土地,包括树所在的土地,想必他会卖掉它来筹集资金,或者它也会被收走。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: And whatever the case there, Jackson would have known property taxes needed to be paid on the deeded land for the tree to be truly secure in its future.
Yet no account or record indicates any trust or the like was set up to facilitate this.

passage.translation: 无论那种情况如何,Jackson应该知道需要为契约土地缴纳财产税,以确保树的未来真正安全。然而,没有任何记录或账目表明设立了任何信托或类似机制来促成此事。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: On top of all this, there is no hard evidence such a deed ever existed, despite the fact that deed records in Athens go back many decades before Jackson's death in 1876 and that it was supposed to have existed in 1890 in the archives according to the original anonymous news reporter who claims to have seen it.

passage.translation: 除此之外,没有确凿证据表明这样的契约曾经存在过,尽管雅典的契约记录可以追溯到Jackson 1876年去世前的许多年,而且根据最初的匿名新闻记者的说法,该契约应该在1890年存在于档案中,他声称见过它。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: As you might imagine from all of this, few give credit to this side of the story.
So how did all of this come about then?

passage.translation: 从所有这些来看,你可以想象,很少有人相信故事的这一面。那么这一切是如何产生的呢?

passage.label: N

sentences.text: It is speculated to have been invented by the imagination of the said anonymous author at the Athens Weekly Banner in the aforementioned 1890 front page article titled "Deeded to Itself", which by the way contained several elements that are much more easily proved to be false.

As to why the author would do this, it's speculated perhaps it was a 19th century version of a click-bait thought exercise on whether it would be legal for someone to deed such a non-conscious living thing to itself or not.

passage.translation: 据推测,这是上述匿名作者在1890年《雅典周报》头版文章《契约给自己》中虚构的,顺便说一句,该文章包含了几个更容易被证明是虚假的元素。至于作者为什么要这样做,有人推测这可能是19世纪版本的点击诱饵式思想实验,探讨某人将这样一个无意识的生物契约给它自己是否合法。

passage.label: O

sentences.text: Whatever the case, the next known instance of the Tree That Owns Itself being mentioned wasn't until 1901 in the Centennial Edition of that same paper, the Athens Weekly Banner.
This featured another account very clearly just copying the original article published about a decade before, only slightly reworded.

The next account was in 1906, again in the Athens Weekly Banner, again very clearly copying the original account, only slightly reworded, the 19th century equivalent of re-posts when the audience has forgotten about the original.

passage.translation: 无论如何,下一次提到"拥有自己的树"是在1901年同一份报纸《雅典周报》的百年纪念版上。这又是一篇显然只是复制了大约十年前发表的原始文章的报道,只是措辞稍有不同。下一篇报道是在1906年,仍然在《雅典周报》上,仍然非常明显地复制了原始报道,只是措辞稍有不同,相当于19世纪版本的转发,当时受众已经忘记了原文。

title: Variability is crucially important for learning new skills.…

sentences.text: Variability is crucially important for learning new skills.
Consider learning how to serve in tennis.
Should you always practise serving from the exactly same location on the court, aiming at the same spot?
Although practising in more variable conditions will be slower at first, it will likely make you a better tennis player in the end.
This is because variability leads to better generalisation of what is learned.

passage.translation: 可变性对于学习新技能至关重要。考虑学习网球发球。你应该总是在球场上完全相同的位置练习发球,瞄准同一个点吗?尽管在更多变的条件下练习一开始会比较慢,但最终可能会让你成为更好的网球运动员。这是因为可变性能使所学内容更好地泛化。

sentences.text: This principle is found in many domains, including speech perception and learning categories.
For instance, infants will struggle to learn the category "dog" if they are only exposed to Chihuahuas, instead of many different kinds of dogs.

passage.translation: 这一原理存在于许多领域,包括语音感知和类别学习。例如,如果婴儿只接触吉娃娃,而不是许多不同种类的狗,他们就会难以学习"狗"这个类别。

sentences.text: "There are over ten different names for this basic principle," says Limor Raviv, the senior investigator of a recent study.
"Learning from less variable input is often fast, but may fail to generalise to new stimuli."

passage.translation: 最近一项研究的高级研究员Limor Raviv说:"这个基本原理有十多个不同的名称。从可变性较小的输入中学习通常很快,但可能无法泛化到新的刺激。

sentences.text: To identify key patterns and understand the underlying principles of variability effects, Raviv and her colleagues reviewed over 150 studies on variability and generalisation across fields, including computer science, linguistics, categorisation, visual perception and formal education.

passage.translation: 为了识别关键模式并理解可变性效应的基本原理,Raviv和她的同事回顾了跨领域关于可变性和泛化的150多项研究,包括计算机科学、语言学、分类、视觉感知和正规教育。

sentences.text: The researchers discovered that, across studies, the term variability can refer to at least four different kinds of variability, such as set size and scheduling.
"These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared—which means that we currently don't know which is most effective for learning," says Raviv.

passage.translation: 研究人员发现,在各项研究中,可变性一词至少可以指代四种不同类型的可变性,例如集合大小和调度安排。Raviv说:"这四种可变性从未被直接比较过——这意味着我们目前不知道哪一种对学习最有效。

sentences.text: The impact of variability depends on whether it is relevant to the task or not.
But according to the 'Mr.
Miyagi principle', practising seemingly unrelated skills may actually benefit learning of other skills.

passage.translation: 可变性的影响取决于它是否与任务相关。但根据"宫城先生原理",练习看似无关的技能实际上可能有益于其他技能的学习。

sentences.text: But why does variability impact learning and generalisation?
One theory is that more variable input can highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not.

passage.translation: 但为什么可变性会影响学习和泛化呢?一种理论认为,更多变的输入可以突出显示任务的哪些方面是相关的,哪些是不相关的。

sentences.text: Another theory is that greater variability leads to broader generalisations.
This is because variability will represent the real world better, including atypical(非典型的) examples.

passage.translation: 另一种理论认为,更大的可变性会导致更广泛的泛化。这是因为可变性能更好地代表真实世界,包括非典型的例子。

sentences.text: A third reason has to do with the way memory works: when training is variable, learners are forced to actively reconstruct their memories.

passage.translation: 第三个原因与记忆的工作方式有关:当训练是可变的时,学习者被迫主动重构他们的记忆。

sentences.text: "Understanding the impact of variability is important for literally every aspect of our daily life.
Beyond affecting the way we learn language, motor skills, and categories, it even has an impact on our social lives," explains Raviv.
"For example, face recognition is affected by whether people grew up in a small community or in a larger community.
Exposure to fewer faces during childhood is associated with diminished face memory."

passage.translation: Raviv解释说:"理解可变性的影响对我们日常生活的方方面面都很重要。除了影响我们学习语言、运动技能和类别的方式之外,它甚至对我们的社交生活也有影响。例如,人脸识别会受到人们是在小社区还是在大社区长大的影响。童年时期接触较少的面孔与面孔记忆能力减弱有关。

sentences.text: "We hope this work will spark people's curiosity and generate more work on the topic," concludes Raviv.
"Our paper raises a lot of open questions.
Can we find similar effects of variability beyond the brain, for instance, in the immune system?"

passage.translation: Raviv总结道:"我们希望这项工作能激发人们的好奇心,并在这个主题上产生更多研究。我们的论文提出了许多开放性问题。我们能否在大脑之外找到可变性的类似效应,例如在免疫系统中?

You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about infants learning the category "dog" if they are exposed to Chihuahuas only?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
如果婴儿只接触吉娃娃,文章对婴儿学习"狗"这一类别有何说法?
A) 他们会遇到一定程度的困难。
B) 他们会先尝试对其他物体进行分类。
C) 他们会更喜欢吉娃娃而非其他犬种。
D) 他们会想象吉娃娃在各种情况下的样子。
**判型** What does the passage say about infants learning the category "dog" if they are exposed to Chihuahuas only? 以 What does the passage say about... 起手，要求复述原文事实，没有 infer/suggest 等推断信号。
**拆句** Q51 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，主干 What does the passage say about infants learning the category "dog"，其中 learning the category "dog" 是 v-ing 短语做infants 的后置定语；末尾 if they are exposed to Chihuahuas only 是条件状语从句，被动语态 are exposed to 意为“只接触到”，是理解前提。
**定位** 举例来说，如果婴儿只接触吉娃娃，而不是接触多种不同种类的狗，他们将很难学会“狗”这一类别。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确struggle to learn the category "dog" ↔ encounter some degree of difficulty预判“会有学习困难”与 encounter some degree of difficulty 在语义上严格对应，无需推断，直接锁定 A。
B) 无中生有They will try to categorise other objects first 在 P2 找不到任何对应——原文只说他们 struggle to learn“狗”，未说他们会先去分类别的东西。
C) 偷换概念They will prefer Chihuahuas to other dog species 把原文“只接触到吉娃娃”曲解为“偏好吉娃娃”——原文谈的是输入受限导致学习困难，与个人偏好无关。
D) 张冠李戴They will imagine Chihuahuas in various conditions 把第 1 段“在多变条件下练习”的概念硬塞到婴儿身上——原文中婴儿并不会主动 imagine，“in various conditions”是上一段网球训练的语境。
questions.quote: For instance, infants will struggle to learn the category "dog" if they are only exposed to Chihuahuas, instead of many different kinds of dogs.

options.text: They will encounter some degree of difficulty.
They will try to categorise other objects first.
They will prefer Chihuahuas to other dog species.
They will imagine Chihuahuas in various conditions.

questions.prompt: What does Raviv say about the four different kinds of variability?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
Raviv对四种不同类型的变异性有何说法?
A) 其中哪一种与手头的任务最相关有待确认。
B) 它们为何对学习产生影响远未被理解。
C) 它们为何从未被直接比较过仍是一个谜。
D) 其中哪一种最有利于学习尚待确定。
**判型** What does Raviv say about the four different kinds of variability? 用 say about 句式问 Raviv 对四种 variability 的明确表述，是事实复述而非推断。
**拆句** Q52 主干 What does Raviv say，介词短语 about the four different kinds of variability限定话题范围；句中 the four different kinds of 含定冠词 the，提示原文已先有这“四种”的提及。
**定位** Raviv 说：“这四种 variability 从未被直接比较过——这意味着我们目前还不知道哪种对学习最有效。”
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念Which of them is most relevant to the task at hand is to be confirmed 把原文的most effective for learning（对学习最有效）偷换为 most relevant to the task at hand（对手头任务最相关）——relevant to the task 是第 6 段的话题，不是第 5 段Raviv 引语的内容。
B) 答非所问Why they have an impact on learning is far from being understood 是关于“机制为何”的论断，不是 Raviv 在第 5 段就四种 variability 所说的话；况且第 7–9 段恰恰给出了三种 theory，“远未被理解”与原文也不符。
C) 过度推断Why they have never been directly compared remains a mystery 把原文 These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared 的事实（“未被比较”）扭曲成“为何未被比较仍是谜”——原文从未说“为何未被比较”是个谜。
D) ✓ 正确we currently don't know which is most effective for learning ↔Which of them is most conducive to learning is yet to be identified most effective for learning ↔ most conducive to learning无论是“目前不知→尚待确认”的含蓄否定，还是“最有效→最有助益”的形容词替换，都精准落在 D 项措辞上，锁定 D。
questions.quote: "These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared—which means that we currently don't know which is most effective for learning," says Raviv.

options.text: Which of them is most relevant to the task at hand is to be confirmed.
Why they have an impact on learning is far from being understood.
Why they have never been directly compared remains a mystery.
Which of them is most conducive to learning is yet to be identified.

questions.prompt: How does one of the theories explain the importance of variability for learning new skills?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
其中一种理论如何解释变异性对学习新技能的重要性?
A) 学习者认为变化训练是现实世界中发生情况的典型代表。
B) 接受变化训练的学习者被迫重组其记忆。
C) 学习者关注任务的相关方面并忽略不相关的方面。
D) 学习者专注于相关技能而不是在不相关技能上浪费时间和精力。
**判型** How does one of the theories explain the importance of variability for learning new skills? 问“某个理论怎么解释”，要求复述原文中三个理论之一的具体内容，仍属细节题。
**拆句** Q53 How 引导特殊疑问，主干 How does one of the theories explain the importance，of 短语 of variability for learning new skills 限定 importance，并不影响理解。注意 one of the theories 用单数动词 explain，提示只问其中一个理论。
**定位** 第三个原因与记忆的运作方式有关：当训练具有多变性时，学习者被迫主动地重构他们的记忆。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反Learners regard variable training as typical of what happens in the real world 把variability will represent the real world better, including atypical examples 颠倒——原文是“多变训练能更好地代表真实世界（包含非典型例子）”，并非“学习者把多变训练视为典型”。
B) ✓ 正确learners are forced to actively reconstruct their memories ↔Learners receiving variable training are compelled to reorganise their memories when training is variable ↔ receiving variable training条件状语从句→v-ing 定语、被动词组→被动词组、动词短语→动词短语三层替换齐全，正确项 B 与定位句构成一对一映射。
C) 偷换概念Learners pay attention to the relevant aspects of a task and ignore those irrelevant 把 more variable input can highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not 偷换主语——原文是“多变输入会突显相关/不相关方面”，并非“学习者主动关注/忽略”。
D) 与原文相反Learners focus on related skills instead of wasting time and effort on unrelated ones 把 practising seemingly unrelated skills may actually benefit learning of other skills 的意思颠倒——原文是“练习看似无关的技能也能助益”，选项却说“专注相关技能而不浪费在无关技能上”，恰恰相反。
questions.quote: A third reason has to do with the way memory works: when training is variable, learners are forced to actively reconstruct their memories.

options.text: Learners regard variable training as typical of what happens in the real world.
Learners receiving variable training are compelled to reorganise their memories.
Learners pay attention to the relevant aspects of a task and ignore those irrelevant.
Learners focus on related skills instead of wasting time and effort on unrelated ones.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about face recognition?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
文章对面孔识别有何说法?
A) 在小社区长大的人可能会发现记住熟悉面孔很容易。
B) 面孔识别对我们社会生活的几乎每个方面都有重大影响。
C) 在大社区长大的人能够轻易识别任何个体面孔。
D) 人们成长所在社区的规模影响其面孔识别能力。
**判型** What does the passage say about face recognition? 仍是 What does the passage say about 句式，问原文如何陈述 face recognition 这一事实。
**拆句** Q54 结构与第 51 题同款，主干 What does the passage say about face recognition? 无从句无否定，平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 例如，面孔识别会受到人们是在小社区还是大社区长大这一因素的影响。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反People growing up in a small community may find it easy to remember familiar faces 给“小社区”贴上“易记熟人脸”的标签，但 Exposure to fewer faces during childhood is associated with diminished face memory 恰恰说“接触少→记忆减弱”，与 A 的方向相反；且原文没区分 familiar faces。
B) 张冠李戴Face recognition has a significant impact on literally every aspect of our social lives 把“variability 影响每一方面”安到 face recognition 头上——原文Understanding the impact of variability is important for literally every aspect of our daily life 的主语是 variability，不是 face recognition。
C) 过度推断People growing up in a large community can readily recognise any individual faces 用 any individual faces 把原文中性的“识别能力受影响”夸大为“能轻松识别任何个人面孔”，是绝对化推断。
D) ✓ 正确face recognition is affected by whether people grew up in a small community or in a larger community↔ The size of the community people grow up in impacts their face recognition ability D 既保留了“社区规模→识别能力”的因果，也保留了“人群”层面的中性陈述，没有像 A/C那样把因果方向具体化、特例化，最贴近原文。
questions.quote: For example, face recognition is affected by whether people grew up in a small community or in a larger community.

options.text: People growing up in a small community may find it easy to remember familiar faces.
Face recognition has a significant impact on literally every aspect of our social lives.
People growing up in a large community can readily recognise any individual faces.
The size of the community people grow up in impacts their face recognition ability.

questions.prompt: What does Raviv hope to do with their research work?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
Raviv希望通过其研究工作做什么?
A) 强调任务的哪些方面与学习技能相关、哪些方面不相关。
B) 在教育中运用变异性原则教授看似无关的技能。
C) 激发人们对变异性的兴趣并促进该主题的更多研究。
D) 将变异性原则应用于免疫系统等研究领域。
**判型** What does Raviv hope to do with their research work? 问 Raviv 对其研究的具体期望，要求复述原文具体表述，不需推断。
**拆句** Q55 主干 What does Raviv hope to do，with 短语 with their research work 是状语，说明 do 的对象是 research work。their 在此泛指研究团队，非语法陷阱。
**定位** Raviv 总结说：“我们希望这项工作能激发人们的好奇心，并产生更多关于这一主题的研究。”
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问Highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not to learning a skill 是 more variable input can highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not 中第 1 个理论的措辞，并非 Raviv 在末段表达的研究愿景。
B) 答非所问Use the principle of variability in teaching seemingly unrelated skills in education取自 practising seemingly unrelated skills may actually benefit learning of other skills 的 Mr. Miyagi 原则，也并非 Raviv 末段表达的愿景。
C) ✓ 正确spark people's curiosity↔ Arouse people's interest in variability generate more work on the topic ↔ stimulate more research on the topic C 把原文两个并列愿望 spark...curiosity 与 generate...work 都同义改写并对齐，没有遗漏其中任何一个，符合“并列动作全保留”原则。
D) 过度推断Apply the principle of variability to such fields of study as the immune system 把Can we find similar effects of variability beyond the brain, for instance, in the immune system? 这一开放性问题当成 Raviv 的具体计划——原文是疑问句、是抛出问题，并非“打算应用到免疫系统”。
questions.quote: "We hope this work will spark people's curiosity and generate more work on the topic," concludes Raviv.

options.text: Highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not to learning a skill.
Use the principle of variability in teaching seemingly unrelated skills in education.
Arouse people's interest in variability and stimulate more research on the topic.
Apply the principle of variability to such fields of study as the immune system.

title: Sarcasm and jazz have something surprisingly in common:…

sentences.text: Sarcasm and jazz have something surprisingly in common: You know them when you hear them.
Sarcasm is mostly understood through tone of voice, which is used to portray the opposite of the literal words.
For example, when someone says, "Well, that's exactly what I need right now," their tone can tell you it's not what they need at all.

passage.translation: 讽刺和爵士乐有一个令人惊讶的共同点：当你听到它们时，你就能识别出来。讽刺主要通过语调来理解，语调被用来表达与字面意思相反的含义。例如，当有人说"嗯，这正是我现在需要的"时,他们的语调能告诉你这根本不是他们需要的。

sentences.text: Most frequently, sarcasm highlights an irritation or is, quite simply, mean.

passage.translation: 最常见的是,讽刺凸显一种恼怒,或者说得直白一点,就是刻薄。

sentences.text: If you want to be happier and improve your relationships, cut out sarcasm.
Why?
Because sarcasm is actually hostility disguised as humor.

passage.translation: 如果你想更快乐并改善人际关系,那就戒掉讽刺。为什么?因为讽刺实际上是伪装成幽默的敌意。

sentences.text: Despite smiling outwardly, many people who receive sarcastic comments feel put down and often think the sarcastic person is rude, or contemptible.
Indeed, it's not surprising that the origin of the word sarcasm derives from the Greek word "sarkazein" which literally means "to tear or strip the flesh off."
Hence, it's no wonder that sarcasm is often preceded by the word "cutting" and that it hurts.

passage.translation: 尽管表面上面带笑容,但许多接受讽刺评论的人感到被贬低,并且常常认为讽刺者粗鲁或可鄙。事实上,讽刺一词的起源来自希腊语"sarkazein",其字面意思是"撕扯或剥去皮肉",这并不令人惊讶。因此,难怪讽刺前面常常加上"尖刻"一词,而且它确实伤人。

sentences.text: What's more, since actions strongly determine thoughts and feelings, when a person consistently acts sarcastically it may only serve to heighten their underlying hostility and insecurity.
After all, when you come right down to it, sarcasm can be used as a subtle form of bullying—and most bullies are angry, insecure, or cowardly.

passage.translation: 更重要的是,由于行为强烈地决定思想和感受,当一个人持续以讽刺的方式行事时,这可能只会加剧他们潜在的敌意和不安全感。毕竟,归根结底,讽刺可以被用作一种微妙的欺凌形式——而大多数欺凌者都是愤怒、不安全或懦弱的。

sentences.text: Alternatively, when a person stops voicing negative comments, especially sarcastic ones, they may soon start to feel happier and more self-confident.
Also, other people in their life benefit even more because they no longer have to hear the emotionally hurtful language of sarcasm.

passage.translation: 相反,当一个人停止发表负面评论,尤其是讽刺性评论时,他们可能很快就会开始感到更快乐、更自信。此外,他们生活中的其他人受益更多,因为他们不再需要听到讽刺这种情感上伤人的语言。

sentences.text: Now, I'm not saying all sarcasm is bad.
It may just be better used sparingly—like a potent spice in cooking.
Too much of the spice, and the dish will be overwhelmed by it.
Similarly, an occasional dash of sarcastic wit can spice up a chat and add an element of humor to it.
But a big or steady serving of sarcasm will overwhelm the emotional flavor of any conversation and can taste very bitter to its recipient.

passage.translation: 现在,我并不是说所有讽刺都是不好的。它只是最好节制使用——就像烹饪中的浓烈香料。香料放太多,菜肴就会被它压倒。同样,偶尔来点讽刺的机智可以为聊天增添趣味,并为其增添幽默元素。但大量或持续的讽刺会压倒任何对话的情感基调,并让接收者感到非常苦涩。

sentences.text: So, tone down the sarcasm and work on clever wit instead, which is usually without any hostility and thus more appreciated by those you're communicating with.
In essence, sarcasm is easy while true, harmless wit takes talent.

passage.translation: 所以,减少讽刺,转而在巧妙的机智上下功夫,这种机智通常不带任何敌意,因而更受与你交流的人欣赏。本质上,讽刺很容易,而真正无害的机智需要才华。

sentences.text: Thus, the main difference between wit and sarcasm is that, as already stated, sarcasm is often hostility disguised as humor.
It can be intended to hurt and is often bitter and biting.
Witty statements are usually in response to someone's unhelpful remarks or behaviors, and the intent is to untangle and clarify the issue by emphasizing its absurdities.
Sarcastic statements are expressed in a cutting manner; witty remarks are delivered with undisguised and harmless humor.

passage.translation: 因此,机智和讽刺的主要区别在于,正如已经指出的,讽刺往往是伪装成幽默的敌意。它可能意在伤害,而且往往是尖酸刻薄的。机智的话语通常是对某人无益言行的回应,其意图是通过强调其荒谬性来理清和澄清问题。讽刺性的陈述以尖刻的方式表达;机智的评论则以不加掩饰和无害的幽默传递。

You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: Why does the author say sarcasm and jazz have something surprisingly in common?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者为什么说讽刺和爵士乐有某种令人惊讶的共同点?
A) 两者在被听到时都能被识别出来。
B) 两者有完全相同的语调。
C) 两者的含义都与其表面意思相反。
D) 两者都隐藏着明显的恼怒情绪。
**判型** Q46 用 Why does the author say... 询问作者把 sarcasm 与 jazz 类比的具体依据，不是问主旨也不是问推断。
**拆句** Q46 主干为 Why does the author say + 宾语从句 sarcasm and jazz have something surprisingly in common；宾语从句里 something 是 have 的宾语，surprisingly in common 整体作 something 的后置修饰；结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 讽刺和爵士乐有一个出人意料的共同点：你一听就能认出它们。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确You know them when you hear them. ↔ Both are recognized when heard. Both are recognized when heard. 是 You know them when you hear them. 的标准被动同义改写，与预判完全一致。
B) 无中生有原文只说"sarcasm 借 tone of voice 传达"，从未说 sarcasm 与 jazz 拥有相同语气。
C) 张冠李戴原文 Sarcasm is mostly understood through tone of voice, which is used to portray the opposite of the literal words. 把"言反其意"只归于 sarcasm，与 jazz无关。
D) 张冠李戴Most frequently, sarcasm highlights an irritation 只说 sarcasm 反映 irritation，与jazz 无关。
questions.quote: Sarcasm and jazz have something surprisingly in common: You know them when you hear them.

options.text: Both are recognized when heard.
Both have exactly the same tone.
Both mean the opposite of what they appear to.
Both have hidden in them an evident irritation.

questions.prompt: How do many people feel when they hear sarcastic comments?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
许多人在听到讽刺性评论时有什么感受?
A) 他们对讽刺者感到敌意。
B) 他们感到被贬低和不被尊重。
C) 他们感到强烈的报复冲动。
D) 他们感到无法掩饰自己的恼怒。
**判型** Q47 用 How do many people feel 直接问感受类细节，答案应是原文情绪句的同义改写。
**拆句** Q47 How 引导特殊疑问，主干 do many people feel，when 引导状语从句 they hear sarcastic comments；结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 尽管表面带笑，许多人在听到讽刺的话时仍会感觉被贬低，并常常认为讽刺他们的人粗鲁或可鄙。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴原文 sarcasm is actually hostility disguised as humor 把 hostility 归于讽刺者，不是接收者的感受。
B) ✓ 正确feel put down ↔ They feel belittled and disrespected. think the sarcastic person is rude, or contemptible ↔ disrespected They feel belittled and disrespected. 恰是 feel put down 的双词同义改写，与预判一致。
C) 无中生有原文从未提及接收者想报复，文章主张反而是"停掉讽刺"以缓和关系。
D) 与原文相反Despite smiling outwardly 恰恰是说接收者表面在笑——即"能掩饰"，与 incapable of disguising 相反。
questions.quote: Despite smiling outwardly, many people who receive sarcastic comments feel put down and often think the sarcastic person is rude, or contemptible.

options.text: They feel hostile towards the sarcastic person.
They feel belittled and disrespected.
They feel a strong urge to retaliate.
They feel incapable of disguising their irritation.

questions.prompt: What happens when a person consistently acts sarcastically?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
当一个人持续以讽刺方式行事时会发生什么?
A) 他们感到自己的尊严大大提高。
B) 他们感到越来越不安全和充满敌意。
C) 他们在幽默的伪装下忍受敌意。
D) 他们即使在愉快的互动中也感到苦涩。
**判型** Q48 问"当某人持续讽刺时会发生什么"，是原文一个具体因果陈述，属细节题。
**拆句** Q48 What happens 主干 + when a person consistently acts sarcastically 时间状语从句；副词 consistently 修饰 acts，无陷阱。
**定位** 当一个人一贯地讽刺人，这种行为只会加深他内心潜藏的敌意与不安全感。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反原文加深的是 hostility/insecurity 等负面情绪，而非 dignity（尊严）；正相反，长期讽刺者被视为隐性霸凌者，尊严下滑。
B) ✓ 正确heighten their underlying hostility and insecurity ↔They feel increasingly insecure and hostile. They feel increasingly insecure and hostile. 把"程度加深"用 increasingly 还原，把名词敌意/不安全感转回形容词，恰是预判同义。
C) 张冠李戴原文 hostility disguised as humor 的施事是讽刺者本人；这里把"在 humor 伪装下被迫忍受 hostility"按到讽刺者身上，搞反了角色。
D) 偷换概念原文 can taste very bitter to its recipient 的 bitter 是接收者的感觉，且语境是"过量讽刺"，从未说"持续讽刺者在愉快互动中也尝苦"。
questions.quote: when a person consistently acts sarcastically it may only serve to heighten their underlying hostility and insecurity.

options.text: They feel their dignity greatly heightened.
They feel increasingly insecure and hostile.
They endure hostility under the disguise of humor.
They taste bitterness even in pleasant interactions.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about people quitting sarcastic comments?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者对人们停止讽刺性评论有何看法?
A) 这让其他人更快乐、更自信。
B) 这约束他们不再恼人和欺凌。
C) 这不仅有益于他们自己,也有益于周围的人。
D) 这使他们免受负面评论和公然敌意的影响。
**判型** Q49 用 What does the author say about... 询问作者对"停讽"的具体陈述，属对应一句原文的细节题。
**拆句** Q49 主干 What does the author say + about 介词短语；about 的宾语是动名词短语people quitting sarcastic comments；结构无陷阱。
**定位** 反过来说，当一个人不再说讽刺等负面话语时，他自己很快会更快乐、更自信；而且，他生活中的其他人受益更多，因为他们再也不必听到讽刺这种伤人的话。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全原文 happier and more self-confident 的主语是讽刺者本人，A 只说让 others 更乐更自信，丢掉了"自己"那一半。
B) 无中生有原文虽在 can be used as a subtle form of bullying 提及 bullying，但 P6 描述停讽效果时根本没出现"约束自己别再霸凌"的说法。
C) ✓ 正确they may soon start to feel happier and more self-confident ↔ not only themselves other people in their life benefit even more ↔ but also those around them It benefits not only themselves but also those around them. 用 not only...but also同时呼应 may soon start to feel happier 与 other people in their life benefit even more，与预判一致。
D) 与原文相反原文是"停讽者不再向外发讽刺、让他人不必听到"，并非"屏蔽讽刺者本人免受外界负面话语"，方向相反。
questions.quote: Alternatively, when a person stops voicing negative comments, especially sarcastic ones, they may soon start to feel happier and more self-confident. Also, other people in their life benefit even more because they no longer have to hear the emotionally hurtful language of sarcasm.

options.text: It makes others happier and more self-confident.
It restrains them from being irritating and bullying.
It benefits not only themselves but also those around them.
It shields them from negative comments and outright hostility.

questions.prompt: What is the chief difference between a speaker's wit and sarcasm?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
说话者的机智和讽刺之间的主要区别是什么?
A) 它们的清晰度。
B) 它们的欣赏程度。
C) 它们的侧重点。
D) 它们的意图。
**判型** Q50 直接问"主要区别是什么"，原文有总结句给出，属细节题而非主旨题。
**拆句** Q50 主干 What is the chief difference + 后置介词短语 between a speaker's wit and sarcasm；between 引导比较对象；结构无陷阱。
**定位** 于是，机智与讽刺的主要区别在于：讽刺常是"敌意伪装成幽默"，可能意在伤人；而机智之语意在厘清问题、点出其荒谬之处。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全untangle and clarify the issue 只出现在 wit 一侧；讽刺侧从未谈到 clarity 这一维度。
B) 偷换概念原文 more appreciated by those you're communicating with 谈的是"听者是否欣赏"，是结果而非区别本身。
C) 以偏概全by emphasizing its absurdities 中 emphasizing 仅是 wit 实现意图的手段，不是对比双方共有的维度。
D) ✓ 正确It can be intended to hurt↔ Their intention. the intent is to untangle and clarify the issue↔Their intention. Their intention. 把原文 sarcasm 的 be intended to hurt 与 wit 的 intent is to untangle and clarify 抽象为共同维度 intention，与预判一致。
questions.quote: Thus, the main difference between wit and sarcasm is that, as already stated, sarcasm is often hostility disguised as humor. It can be intended to hurt and is often bitter and biting. Witty statements are usually in response to someone's unhelpful remarks or behaviors, and the intent is to untangle and clarify the issue by emphasizing its absurdities.

options.text: Their clarity.
Their appreciation.
Their emphasis.
Their intention.

title: A rainbow is a multi-colored, arc-shaped phenomenon that…

sentences.text: A rainbow is a multi-colored, arc-shaped phenomenon that can appear in the sky.
The colors of a rainbow are produced by the reflection and (26)____ of light through water droplets(小滴) present in the atmosphere.
An observer may (27)____ a rainbow to be located either near or far away, but this phenomenon is not actually located at any specific spot.
Instead, the appearance of a rainbow depends entirely upon the position of the observer in (28)____ to the direction of light.
In essence, a rainbow is an (29)____ illusion.

passage.translation: 彩虹是一种多彩的弧形现象，可以出现在天空中。彩虹的颜色是由光线通过大气中存在的水滴反射和色散产生的。观察者可能会认为彩虹位于近处或远处，但这种现象实际上并不位于任何特定地点。相反，彩虹的出现完全取决于观察者相对于光线方向的位置。本质上，彩虹是一种光学错觉。

sentences.text: Rainbows present a (30)____ made up of seven colors in a specific order.
In fact, school children in many English-speaking countries are taught to remember the name "Roy G.
Biv" as an aid for remembering the colors of a rainbow and their order.
"Roy G.
Biv" (31)____ for: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet.
The outer edge of the rainbow arc is red, while the inner edge is violet.

passage.translation: 彩虹呈现出由七种颜色按特定顺序组成的光谱。事实上，许多英语国家的学童被教导记住"Roy G. Biv"这个名字，作为记忆彩虹颜色及其顺序的辅助方法。"Roy G. Biv"代表：红、橙、黄、绿、蓝、靛、紫。彩虹弧的外缘是红色，而内缘是紫色。

sentences.text: A rainbow is formed when light (generally sunlight) passes through water droplets (32)____ in the atmosphere.
The light waves change direction as they pass through the water droplets, resulting in two processes: reflection and refraction(折射).
When light reflects off a water droplet, it simply (33)____back in the opposite direction from where it (34)____ .
When light refracts, it takes a different direction.
Some individuals refer to refracted light as "bent light waves."
A rainbow is formed because white light enters the water droplet, where it bends in several different directions.
When these bent light waves reach the other side of the water droplet, they reflect back out of the droplet instead of (35)____passing through the water.
Since the white light is separated inside of the water, the refracted light appears as separate colors to the human eye.

passage.translation: 彩虹是在光线（通常是太阳光）穿过悬浮在大气中的水滴时形成的。光波在穿过水滴时改变方向，导致两个过程：反射和折射。当光从水滴反射时，它只是从其起源处朝相反方向反弹回来。当光发生折射时，它会朝不同的方向前进。有些人将折射光称为"弯曲的光波"。彩虹的形成是因为白光进入水滴，在那里它朝几个不同的方向弯曲。当这些弯曲的光波到达水滴的另一侧时，它们从水滴中反射出来，而不是完全穿过水。由于白光在水内部被分离，折射光在人眼中呈现为不同的颜色。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
A rainbow is a multi-colored, arc-shaped phenomenon that can appear in the sky. The colors of a rainbow are produced by the reflection and {{26}} of light through water droplets(小滴) present in the atmosphere. An observer may {{27}} a rainbow to be located either near or far away, but this phenomenon is not actually located at any specific spot. Instead, the appearance of a rainbow depends entirely upon the position of the observer in {{28}} to the direction of light. In essence, a rainbow is an {{29}} illusion.

Rainbows present a {{30}} made up of seven colors in a specific order. In fact, school children in many English-speaking countries are taught to remember the name "Roy G. Biv" as an aid for remembering the colors of a rainbow and their order. "Roy G. Biv" {{31}} for: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. The outer edge of the rainbow arc is red, while the inner edge is violet.

A rainbow is formed when light (generally sunlight) passes through water droplets {{32}} in the atmosphere. The light waves change direction as they pass through the water droplets, resulting in two processes: reflection and refraction(折射). When light reflects off a water droplet, it simply {{33}}back in the opposite direction from where it {{34}} . When light refracts, it takes a different direction. Some individuals refer to refracted light as "bent light waves." A rainbow is formed because white light enters the water droplet, where it bends in several different directions. When these bent light waves reach the other side of the water droplet, they reflect back out of the droplet instead of {{35}}passing through the water. Since the white light is separated inside of the water, the refracted light appears as separate colors to the human eye.

options.text: bounces
permeates
completely
ponder
dispersion
preceding
eccentric
recklessly
hanging
relation
optical
spectrum
originates
stands
perceive

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) dispersion 名词
**词性槽** and 并列连接：reflection and ___，并列成分要求同性
**依据** reflection and dispersion 是描述彩虹成因的标准搭配The colors of a rainbow are produced by the reflection and dispersion of light through water droplets 光经过水滴时发生「反射 + 色散」是彩虹七色形成的物理原理；与下一段 reflection and refraction（折射）共同呼应「光在水滴中的多重作用」。
questions.tip:
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 N) —— spectrum 也是名词，且与彩虹七色话题强相关，极易抢答26。produced by the reflection and __(26)__ of light through water droplets 26 题若考生没等到 30 题就抢着填，看到「彩虹 + 光」很容易顺手填 N spectrum；但 26 题靠and 并列须填与 reflection 同类的「光学过程」名词（dispersion 色散），spectrum「光谱」属结果性名词，且 spectrum 真正归属 30 题 a ___ made up of seven colors。防坑：严格执行「用过即划 + 先做高把握空」，让 30 题先把 spectrum 划走。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) perceive 动词
**词性槽** 情态动词 may 后接动词原形
**依据** perceive sb/sth to be ... 「察觉/认为……是……」An observer may perceive a rainbow to be located either near or far away perceive后可直接接「宾语 + to be + 状态」，意为「察觉/认为彩虹位于近处或远处」，与下句but this phenomenon is not actually located at any specific spot 形成「主观感知 vs客观事实」的转折。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
J) ponder ponder 表「沉思」，不接「宾语 + to be」ponder 通常作不及物或接 sth/on sth/over sth，不构成「ponder sth to be ...」结构；语义上「观察者沉思彩虹位于近处或远处」也极不自然。

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) relation 名词
**词性槽** 介词 in 后 + to 之前，构成 in ___ to 框架
**依据** 固定短语 in relation to = 「相对于、关于」the appearance of a rainbow depends entirely upon the position of the observer in__(28)__ to the direction of light. 文意是「彩虹出现完全取决于观察者相对于光线方向的位置」，正是 in relation to 的典型用法。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) dispersion 无 in dispersion to 这一搭配dispersion 表「色散」，与「位置 ↔ 光线方向」的相对关系无关，且不构成固定短语 in dispersion to。
N) spectrum spectrum 指「光谱/范围」，搭配错误spectrum 是后文 30 题对应「七色光谱」的名词，与「相对位置」语义不沾边，且无 in spectrum to 短语。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) optical 形容词
**词性槽** 不定冠词 an + 空 + 名词 illusion
**依据** optical illusion = 「视错觉、光学幻象」固定搭配In essence, a rainbow is an optical illusion. 上文已经指出彩虹「并非真实位于某一地点，而是取决于观察者的相对位置」，结论自然是「光学幻象」——optical illusion 是英语中表「视错觉」的标准搭配，与全段论证完全吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
D) eccentric eccentric 表「古怪的」，色彩与语境不符eccentric 多形容人/行为「古怪、反常」，描述彩虹这一自然光学现象时既不准确也不带这种语义色彩；eccentric illusion 并非英语习用搭配。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 D) —— eccentric 形态匹配 an + 形容词 + illusion，最容易抢29。a rainbow is an __(29)__ illusion. eccentric 以元音 /ɪ/ 开头与 an 适配、作前置定语语法完全通；但 optical illusion 才是英语固定搭配「视错觉」，本段全段都在论证「彩虹是观察者视觉上的幻象」，与「光学」直接对应。防坑：见 illusion 先想 optical illusion这一高频固定搭配，再回头比对其它候选。

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) spectrum 名词
**词性槽** 及物动词 present 后 + 不定冠词 a 后
**依据** spectrum = 「光谱」，正对应「七色按特定顺序」Rainbows present a spectrum made up of seven colors in a specific order. 「由七种颜色按特定顺序组成」正是 spectrum（光谱）的定义；下文 Roy G. Biv 口诀也是为了记忆这一光谱顺序。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) dispersion dispersion 强调「色散过程」，非结果性的「七色排列」dispersion 指光被分解的「过程/动作」，而本句 made up of seven colors in a specific order 描述的是一个由七色组成的「结果性序列」——这是 spectrum 的语义，不是 dispersion的语义；且 dispersion 已被 26 题预订（见后）。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) stands 动词
**词性槽** 主语 "Roy G. Biv" 后缺谓语 + 后接 for
**依据** 固定搭配 stand for = 「代表、缩写指代」"Roy G. Biv" __(31)__ for: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. 紧随其后的就是七色英文首字母对应的全称，文意正是「Roy G. Biv 这一串字母代表红橙黄绿蓝靛紫」，stand for 是固定搭配，意为「代表 / 是……的缩写」，与语境完全契合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) originates originate 后不接 for originate 表「起源于」，常搭 originate from/in，无 originate for 这一搭配；语义也讲不通——「Roy G. Biv 起源于红橙黄……」不成立。
H) perceive 形态不符 + 搭配不通perceive 非单三，且 perceive for 不是固定搭配；它的宾语应是被感知的对象（如本文 27 题用法），与此处「代表七色」不符。
I) permeates permeate 意为「渗透」permeate 表液体/气味/影响渗透弥漫，搭配介词通常是 through/into，与「字母代表颜色」毫不相干。
J) ponder 形态不符 + 语义不通ponder 非单三；其义为「沉思」，主语「Roy G. Biv」是个口诀，不会「沉思」，逻辑不成立。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) hanging 形容词
**词性槽** 名词 water droplets 后置修饰 + 空后接 in the atmosphere 介词短语
**依据** hanging in the atmosphere = 「悬浮在大气中」water droplets hanging in the atmosphere 与第 1 段 water droplets(小滴) present in the atmosphere 同义改写，hanging 形象描绘水滴「悬浮 / 飘在」空中的状态，与上下文「光穿过水滴形成彩虹」语境完全一致。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
K) preceding preceding 表「在前的、先前的」，语义与空间状态无关preceding 多用于时间或顺序「前一个、之前的」（如 in the preceding paragraph），不能用来描述水滴「悬浮在大气中」的物理状态。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) bounces 动词
**词性槽** 主语 it（= 光）后缺谓语，且与并列分句时态一致
**依据** bounce back = 「反弹回去」，与 reflect 同义改写When light reflects off a water droplet, it simply bounces back in the opposite direction from where it __(34)__. 上文 reflects 已给出动作，本句用 simply bounces back 同义改写以「反弹回来」的形象语言再说一遍，与 in the opposite direction 表方向反向严丝合缝。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) originates originate 表「起源」，与「反弹回来」语义相反originate 强调「光从某处发源」，与本句 reflect / back / opposite direction 的「返回」语义方向相反，不可选。
I) permeates permeate 是「渗透、弥漫」，与 bounce back 行为完全相反permeate 表向内/向四周扩散，与「沿反方向反弹回去」（in the opposite direction）的物理路径冲突。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) originates 动词
**词性槽** from where 引导的地点从句缺谓语 + 主语 it 单三
**依据** from where it originates = 「从它发源的地方」it simply bounces back in the opposite direction from where it __(34)__. 光被反射后沿反方向回到「它最初出发/发源的方向」——originate 表「起源、发源」与 from 搭配自然（originate from），完美对应「反弹回光线最初来的地方」。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
I) permeates permeate 强调「渗透、弥漫」，与「反弹回起点」语义不符permeate 描述向各方向扩散浸入，无「起点 / 来处」之意；from where it permeates 既不构成习惯表达，也违背物理「光从原方向反弹回去」的描述。

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) completely 副词
**词性槽** instead of 后接动名词 passing，空在 of 与 passing 之间作状语
**依据** completely = 「完全地」，与 instead of 形成「反射 vs 完全穿透」的对照they reflect back out of the droplet instead of __(35)__ passing through the water. 上文说光在水滴另一侧「反射回来」，而非「完全穿过水滴」——completely 强调「彻底/全部」穿过去，与 reflect back 构成自然对比。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
L) recklessly recklessly 含「鲁莽」感情色彩，与物理过程不符recklessly 形容人的行为「不顾后果」，带主观贬义；光是物理对象，无所谓「鲁莽地穿过水」，逻辑荒谬。

title: When someone asks us 'what do you do?'…

sentences.text: When someone asks us 'what do you do?' we nearly always reply with our occupation.
Work, for many of us, is much more than a job.
It is the defining aspect of our identity.
For many of us it is through our job that we can define ourselves.

passage.translation: 当有人问我们"你是做什么的?"时,我们几乎总是用职业来回答。对我们许多人来说,工作远不止是一份职业。它是我们身份认同的决定性方面。对我们许多人而言,正是通过工作我们才能定义自己。

sentences.text: "Without my job I don't know who I am," is a sentence that has been uttered on more than a handful of occasions from my office chair.
Indeed, it can be one of the most challenging aspects I work on with clients who have lost or been forced into changing their jobs.
This loss provokes an identity crisis much greater than the loss of the job itself.

passage.translation: "没有工作我不知道自己是谁",这句话我在办公椅上已经听过不止几次了。事实上,对于那些失去工作或被迫改变工作的客户来说,这可能是我与他们一起处理的最具挑战性的方面之一。这种失落所引发的身份认同危机远比失去工作本身更为严重。

sentences.text: One of the things I have come to understand, however, is that our identity is much more complex than we recognise at first glance.
If we take the time to reflect we might recognise that as well as our work we can also identify as a friend, a spouse, a son or daughter, a parent, a member of a sports team or religious community.
We may recognise that we feel and act differently in these roles and relationships than we do at work.
The passive daughter becomes an assertive leader at work.
Furthermore, our identities at work are not static.
They change over time.
I myself have been a shop assistant, a waitress, a student, a graduate, and a clinical psychologist.
At each stage my ability to adapt to and develop my career identity has been crucial to my wellbeing.
Whilst we like to eliminate uncertainty in our lives at some level we have to manage uncertainty, especially in today's volatile and ever-shifting job market.

passage.translation: 然而,我逐渐理解到的一点是,我们的身份认同远比我们乍看之下所认识到的要复杂得多。如果我们花时间反思,可能会意识到除了工作之外,我们还可以将自己视为朋友、配偶、儿子或女儿、父母、运动队成员或宗教团体成员。我们可能会意识到,在这些角色和关系中,我们的感受和行为方式与在工作中不同。被动的女儿在工作中变成了果断的领导者。此外,我们在工作中的身份认同也不是静态的。它们会随时间而变化。我自己曾经是店员、服务员、学生、毕业生和临床心理学家。在每个阶段,我适应和发展职业身份的能力对我的幸福感都至关重要。虽然我们希望在生活中消除不确定性,但在某种程度上我们必须管理不确定性,尤其是在当今动荡且不断变化的就业市场中。

sentences.text: How we see ourselves is central to the issue of our identity.
When we tell ourselves "I'm good at starting projects but not so great at seeing them through" it can become part of our belief system.
But if you have the unfortunate experience of an enforced job change you will need to examine those beliefs to see how grounded in reality they are.
You will be required to ask yourself how helpful these beliefs are and consider personal change.
We can change our beliefs, behaviours and emotional experience at any time through experimentation, practice and conscious self-discipline.

In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether you can create a new experience of your identity by changing the beliefs you hold about yourself in order to expand your career options.
Ultimately it is you who define who you are.
You are only your job if you let it be so.

passage.translation: 我们如何看待自己是身份认同问题的核心。当我们告诉自己"我擅长启动项目但不太擅长完成它们"时,这可能会成为我们信念系统的一部分。但是,如果你不幸经历了被迫的工作变动,你将需要审视这些信念,看看它们在多大程度上基于现实。你需要问自己这些信念有多大帮助,并考虑个人改变。我们可以随时通过实验、练习和有意识的自我约束来改变我们的信念、行为和情感体验。在一个职业发展可能将我们引向新领域的时代,挑战我们的自我意识并探索是否可以通过改变你对自己持有的信念来创造新的身份体验,从而拓展你的职业选择,变得越来越重要。归根结底,是你定义了你是谁。只有你允许,你才仅仅是你的工作。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about one's loss of a job?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
从文章中我们了解到关于失业的什么信息?
A) 它迫使他们去看临床心理医生。
B) 它为他们提供了扮演不同角色的机会。
C) 它使他们对自己是谁感到困惑。
D) 它迫使他们重新定义人生目标。
**判型** What do we learn from the passage about one's loss of a job? 指向一个具体事实——失业会带来什么——并未问推断或主旨。
**拆句** 主干 What do we learn from the passage 中 we 是主语、learn 是谓语；about one's loss of a job 是 learn 的范围介词短语，指明问的对象是「失去工作这件事」。句式平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 「没有了工作，我就不知道自己是谁」——这话在我办公室的椅子上不止一次被来访者说出。事实上，与那些失去或被迫更换工作的来访者一起处理这种感受，是我工作中最具挑战的部分之一。这种失落所引发的身份危机，要远远大于失业本身。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文只是说作者本人是 clinical psychologist 处理来访者的身份危机，并未要求 visit a clinical psychologist；A 把作者视角偷换成失业者的行为。
B) 张冠李戴原文段 2 并未说失业「提供了扮演不同角色的机会」；段 3 才谈多重身份，但与「失业带来什么」是两个话题。
C) ✓ 正确Without my job I don't know who I am ↔ puzzled about who they are This loss provokes an identity crisis ↔ It renders them puzzled预判的「不知道自己是谁」与 It renders them puzzled about who they are 在主语、谓语致使关系、宾语状态上完全对应，确定 C。
D) 过度推断原文谈的是 identity crisis 与重新审视自我信念，并没有说失业必然要 redefine their life's goals，把身份层面的事推到了「人生目标」的宏大命题上。
questions.quote: "Without my job I don't know who I am," is a sentence that has been uttered on more than a handful of occasions from my office chair. Indeed, it can be one of the most challenging aspects I work on with clients who have lost or been forced into changing their jobs. This loss provokes an identity crisis much greater than the loss of the job itself.

options.text: It compels them to visit a clinical psychologist.
It offers them a chance to play different roles.
It renders them puzzled about who they are.
It forces them to redefine their life's goals.

questions.prompt: What has the author come to understand about our identity?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者对我们的身份认同有了什么理解?
A) 它对我们的情感健康至关重要。
B) 它在生活的许多方面发挥重要作用。
C) 它反映了我们在社会中不断变化的地位。
D) 它比表面看起来更复杂。
**判型** What has the author come to understand about our identity? 指向原文一句明确表述，不要求跨段推理。
**拆句** 完成时 What has the author come to understand 用 has come to understand 强调认知过程已完成；about our identity 指明认知对象。结构简单。
**定位** 然而，我逐渐明白的一件事是：我们的身份远比乍看之下复杂得多。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文段 3 后半句说 my ability to adapt to and develop my career identity has been crucial to my wellbeing，主语是「适应身份的能力」，并非身份本身；A 把「能力对幸福重要」偷换成「身份对情绪幸福重要」。
B) 答非所问原文确实列了多种身份角色，但作者「come to understand」的核心是「身份复杂」这一判断，而非「身份在生活方方面面起作用」；B 只描述现象，未答出认知本身。
C) 过度推断原文 They change over time 谈的是「我们在不同时期的身份变化」（学生、毕业生、咨询师等），并非社会地位的变化；C 偷偷加上了 status in society。
D) ✓ 正确much more complex than we recognise at first glance ↔ more complicated than it appears预判要点「复杂」「超出表面认知」两块在 more complicated than it appears 里一一落地，无遗漏，确定 D。
questions.quote: One of the things I have come to understand, however, is that our identity is much more complex than we recognise at first glance.

options.text: It is crucial to our emotional wellbeing.
It plays a big role in many facets of life.
It reflects our changing status in society.
It is more complicated than it appears.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about our identities at work?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
文章关于我们在工作中的身份认同说了什么?
A) 它们对我们的自尊至关重要。
B) 它们随着时间的推移而演变。
C) 它们凌驾于所有其他自我认知之上。
D) 它们是理解我们自己的关键。
**判型** What does the passage say about our identities at work? 让考生回原文找关于「职场身份」的明示句。
**拆句** What does the passage say about our identities at work：say 是谓语、about 引出宾语对象；our identities at work 中 at work 修饰 identities，限定「工作中的」身份。无难点。
**定位** 此外，我们在工作中的身份并非一成不变。它们会随时间而变化。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有原文谈的是 wellbeing、identity crisis，没有 self-esteem（自尊）的概念，A 属于原文未提的新信息。
B) ✓ 正确They change over time ↔ They evolve with the passage of time预判「随时间而变」直接命中 They evolve with the passage of time，主谓宾全对应，定 B。
C) 与原文相反段 3 强调的是身份的「多元」与「变化」，并未说工作身份压倒其他身份；恰相反，作者承认我们还可作为朋友、配偶等存在。
D) 答非所问「身份是理解自己的关键」与 Q52 的「身份很复杂」更接近，但题问的是 our identities at work 的具体属性；D 没有答出「随时间而变」这一具体属性。
questions.quote: Furthermore, our identities at work are not static. They change over time.

options.text: They are essential to our self-esteem.
They evolve with the passage of time.
They overrule all other self-perceptions.
They are key to understanding ourselves.

questions.prompt: What do we have to do in today's ever-changing job market?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
在当今不断变化的就业市场中我们必须做什么?
A) 努力发展我们的社会身份。
B) 为不同的职业道路做准备。
C) 始终努力保持自信果断。
D) 学会管理不确定性。
**判型** What do we have to do in today's ever-changing job market? 指向原文一句给出具体动作的陈述。
**拆句** What do we have to do in today's ever-changing job market?：do 是询问的动作；in引导的状语 in today's ever-changing job market 限定背景。句式直白。
**定位** 尽管我们倾向于消除生活中的不确定性，但在某种程度上我们必须学会管理不确定性，尤其是在如今这个动荡多变的就业市场中。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文谈 career identity / our identities at work，从未出现 social identity；A 凭空替换了限定语。
B) 张冠李戴「为不同职业路径做准备」更接近段 4 的 career progression / new sectors，但 Q54问的是动荡市场下「必须做的事」，原文给的明确答案是 manage uncertainty。
C) 以偏概全原文只是举例说有人在职场会变得 assertive，并未要求所有人 at all times 都要果断；C 把范围扩到全部场景，与原文不符。
D) ✓ 正确we have to manage uncertainty ↔ Learn to manage uncertainty predict 的「学会管理不确定性」与 Learn to manage uncertainty 字面几乎一致，确定 D。
questions.quote: Whilst we like to eliminate uncertainty in our lives at some level we have to manage uncertainty, especially in today's volatile and ever-shifting job market.

options.text: Strive to develop our social identity.
Prepare for different career paths.
Try to be assertive at all times.
Learn to manage uncertainty.

questions.prompt: What should we do to expand our career options?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
为了拓展职业选择我们应该做什么?
A) 改变我们对自己的认知。
B) 比较各种工作机会。
C) 关注新兴行业领域。
D) 有意识地进行自我约束。
**判型** What should we do to expand our career options? 求一个明确的应对动作。
**拆句** What should we do to expand our career options?：should we do 是主干，to expand our career options 是目的状语，说明动作要服务的目标。结构平铺直叙。
**定位** 在一个职业发展可能把我们带入新行业的时代，挑战我们对自我的认知、并探索是否能通过改变你对自己持有的信念来创造一种新的身份体验、以拓宽你的职业选择，变得越来越重要。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确changing the beliefs you hold about yourself↔Alter our perceptions of ourselves challenge our sense of self↔Alter our perceptions of ourselves预判要点「改变自我信念」在 Alter our perceptions of ourselves 中以同义改写完整呈现，确定 A。
B) 无中生有原文谈的是「改变信念以扩展选择」，并非 Compare various job opportunities；B把心理层面的动作偷换为外部信息搜集行为。
C) 答非所问原文 career progression may lead us into new sectors 只是时代背景描述，作者并未让读者去 Look into newly emerging sectors。
D) 以偏概全原文 through experimentation, practice and conscious self-discipline 只是改变信念的途径之一；题干问的是「为扩展职业选择」最直接该做的事，作者明确给出的是改变信念，而非单独突出自律。
questions.quote: In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether you can create a new experience of your identity by changing the beliefs you hold about yourself in order to expand your career options.

options.text: Alter our perceptions of ourselves.
Compare various job opportunities.
Look into newly emerging sectors.
Exercise self-discipline consciously.

title: The "American Dream" promises that in the Land…

sentences.text: The "American Dream" promises that in the Land of Opportunity, any individual can climb the economic ladder and prosper through hard work and ambition alone.

And yet, young Americans today are struggling to earn more than their parents did at the same age, and upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably to that of other industrialised nations.

passage.translation: "美国梦"承诺，在这片机遇之地，任何个人都可以仅凭努力工作和雄心壮志攀登经济阶梯并获得成功。然而，今天的美国年轻人正努力挣得比他们父母在同龄时更多的收入，而美国的向上流动性实际上与其他工业化国家相比并不理想。

sentences.text: So why does the idea of the American Dream persist?
A new study in the American Journal of Political Science identifies one factor that has been overlooked: the influence of reality TV.

passage.translation: 那么，为什么美国梦的理念依然存在？《美国政治科学杂志》上的一项新研究发现了一个被忽视的因素：真人秀电视节目的影响。

sentences.text: Reality shows have come to dominate US television over the past 20 years, notes Eunji Kim from Vanderbilt University.
And the overwhelming majority of these have a "rags-to-riches" storyline: they feature ordinary Americans who work hard to achieve great economic success.

And while these programmes are regularly among the most-watched shows, news broadcasts—which paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship faced by millions of Americans—get a much smaller proportion of the viewership.

passage.translation: Vanderbilt University 的 Eunji Kim 指出，真人秀节目在过去20年里已经占据了美国电视的主导地位。这些节目中绝大多数都有"白手起家"的故事线：它们展示普通美国人通过努力工作实现巨大经济成功。虽然这些节目经常位列收视率最高的节目之列，但新闻广播——它们描绘了数百万美国人面临的经济困境的更真实景象——却只获得了少得多的收视率份额。

sentences.text: Rags-to-riches stories are ubiquitous(无处不在的) on TV—but does watching these programmes actually convince people that economic mobility is easily attainable?
To find out, Kim's team had participants watch a 5-minute clip from a reality show with a rags-to-riches storyline.
Control participants watched a clip from a reality show that didn't have a rags-to-riches story.
After watching the shows, participants rated how much they agreed with four statements relating to the American Dream.

passage.translation: 白手起家的故事在电视上无处不在——但观看这些节目真的会让人们相信经济流动性很容易实现吗？为了找到答案，Kim 的团队让参与者观看一个5分钟的真人秀片段，该片段具有白手起家的故事线。对照组参与者观看的真人秀片段没有白手起家的故事。观看节目后，参与者对四个与美国梦相关的陈述的认同程度进行评分。

sentences.text: The results showed that those who'd watched a rags-to-riches clip did indeed have a significantly greater belief in the American Dream.

Interestingly, when participants were separated by party affiliation, this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats, suggesting that the kind of messages implicit in these TV shows may play into people's existing socioeconomic beliefs.

passage.translation: 结果显示，那些观看了白手起家片段的人确实对美国梦有显著更强的信念。有趣的是，当参与者按党派归属分开时，这种效应在共和党人中显著，但在民主党人中不显著，这表明这些电视节目中隐含的信息可能会迎合人们现有的社会经济信念。

sentences.text: Kim also conducted a survey of 3,000 US residents.
They also rated the extent to which they believed success in life is related to various internal factors (such as ambition) and external factors (such as family wealth).
Finally, they read a list of TV programmes and indicated which they regularly watched.

passage.translation: Kim 还对3000名美国居民进行了调查。他们还评估了自己在多大程度上相信生活中的成功与各种内在因素（如雄心）和外在因素（如家庭财富）相关。最后，他们阅读了一份电视节目清单，并指出他们经常观看哪些节目。

sentences.text: Participants who were heavy viewers of rags-to-riches programmes or frequent viewers had a stronger belief in the American Dream than those who never watched such shows.

passage.translation: 白手起家节目的重度观众或频繁观众比那些从不观看此类节目的人对美国梦有更强的信念。

sentences.text: Kim concludes that "rags-to-riches entertainment media are an important cultural force that promotes and perpetuates beliefs in upward mobility".

And here's the problem: if people mistakenly believe that hard work is all that is needed for individuals to make a better life for themselves, they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality.

passage.translation: Kim 总结说，"白手起家的娱乐媒体是一种重要的文化力量，它促进并延续了对向上流动性的信念"。问题就在这里：如果人们错误地认为努力工作就是个人改善生活所需的全部，他们可能就不太支持那些真正能够对抗不平等的政策。

sentences.text: "In this era of choice, entertainment media is what captures hearts and minds," Kim writes.
"Its political consequences are anything but trivial".

passage.translation: Kim 写道："在这个选择的时代，娱乐媒体才是真正抓住人心的东西。它的政治后果绝非微不足道。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about young Americans of today?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
从文章中我们了解到当今美国年轻人的什么情况?
A) 他们比父母有更大的抱负。
B) 他们发现实现向上流动很困难。
C) 他们在收入方面已经超过了父母。
D) 他们羡慕其他工业化国家的机会。
**判型** What do we learn from the passage about young Americans of today 明确问的是关于某个具体群体的事实信息，没有出现 infer / imply / mainly about 等推断或主旨信号。
**拆句** 题干主干是 What do we learn from the passage about young Americans of today？about 引导的介宾短语限定 learn 的对象。介词 about 把『青年美国人』锁为定位词，结构平铺无陷阱。
**定位** 然而，今天的美国年轻人正在艰难地试图挣得比父辈同龄时更多的收入，而且美国的向上流动性事实上比其他工业化国家逊色。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有原文只说他们在收入上难超父辈，从未比较两代人的『抱负』。
B) ✓ 正确struggling to earn more than their parents did at the same age ↔find it difficult to achieve upward mobility upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably ↔ upward mobility预判结论是『难以向上流动』，选项 B 几乎是这句话的字面化，二者构成最直接的同义替换。
C) 与原文相反原文说青年正在 struggling to earn more than their parents，意即尚未超过；C 选项却说 overtaken their parents in terms of earnings，恰好相反。
D) 过度推断原文只把美国向上流动与其他工业化国家比较得出『美国更差』，从未提及青年的情绪态度，更未说他们 envy。
questions.quote: And yet, young Americans today are struggling to earn more than their parents did at the same age, and upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably to that of other industrialised nations.

options.text: They have greater ambitions than their parents.
They find it difficult to achieve upward mobility.
They have overtaken their parents in terms of earnings.
They envy the opportunities in other industrialised nations.

questions.prompt: What does Kim's team find about reality TV shows in America?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
Kim的团队对美国真人秀节目有什么发现?
A) 它们重新诠释了流行的白手起家文化的本质。
B) 它们敦促人们通过努力工作获得经济成功。
C) 它们帮助增强人们对美国梦的信念。
D) 它们以普通美国人争取社会认可为特色。
**判型** What does Kim’s team find about reality TV shows in America 问的是研究团队的具体发现，是对原文实验结论的事实性提问。
**拆句** 主干 What does Kim’s team find about reality TV shows，about 引出研究对象。结构干净，无从句无陷阱。
**定位** 结果显示，那些看过『白手起家』短片的人确实显著加深了对美国梦的信仰。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有原文只说真人秀展示 rags-to-riches storyline 并验证其加深观众信仰，从未提到节目在『重新诠释』该文化的本质。
B) 偷换概念they feature ordinary Americans who work hard to achieve great economic success 的主语是节目所呈现的人物在努力，而非节目敦促观众去努力。
C) ✓ 正确significantly greater belief in the American Dream ↔help strengthen people’s conviction in the American Dream预判为『真人秀加深美国梦信仰』，选项 C 把『加深』表达为 help strengthen，把『美国梦信仰』表达为 conviction in the American Dream，二者一一对应。
D) 偷换概念原文明确写 great economic success，与选项的 social recognition 不是一回事。
questions.quote: The results showed that those who'd watched a rags-to-riches clip did indeed have a significantly greater belief in the American Dream.

options.text: They reinterpret the essence of the popular rags-to-riches culture.
They urge people to achieve economic success through hard work.
They help strengthen people's conviction in the American Dream.
They feature ordinary Americans striving for social recognition.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about news broadcasts in America?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者对美国的新闻广播说了什么?
A) 它们吸引的观众远少于真人秀节目。
B) 它们一心报道生活的阴暗面。
C) 它们与真人秀节目形成鲜明对比。
D) 它们关注美国人的经济困境。
**判型** What does the author say about news broadcasts in America 问对某具体对象的陈述，没有 infer / suggest，是事实型细节题。
**拆句** 主干 What does the author say about news broadcasts in America。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 而尽管这些节目（真人秀）经常位列收视率最高的电视节目之列，新闻播报——它们描绘了数以百万计的美国人所面临的经济困境这一更现实的图景——只占据小得多的观众份额。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确get a much smaller proportion of the viewership ↔ attract far fewer viewers than reality TV预判结论是『观众远少于真人秀』，选项 A 把 smaller proportion 改写为 far fewer viewers，把对照对象明示为 reality TV，与定位句的对比关系完全一致。
B) 过度推断paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship 只描述了新闻所呈现的内容，并未对新闻的意图作 be bent on（一心要、决意）这种主观倾向判断。
C) 偷换概念原文用 while 引出对比，但描述对象是『收视份额』，并未对新闻与真人秀做 striking contrast（鲜明反差）的整体定性评价。
D) 以偏概全paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship 是把经济困境作为更真实图景的一部分来呈现，并未说新闻 focus on（聚焦于）经济困境；况且 Q48 问的是作者对新闻的总评，而 D 只是从句里附带说明的内容。
questions.quote: And while these programmes are regularly among the most-watched shows, news broadcasts—which paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship faced by millions of Americans—get a much smaller proportion of the viewership.

options.text: They attract far fewer viewers than reality TV.
They are bent on reporting the dark side of life.
They stand in striking contrast with reality TV.
They focus on Americans' economic hardships.

questions.prompt: What can we infer from the passage about Republicans in general?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （推断题）
**题目译文**
从文章中我们可以推断出共和党人总体上的什么情况?
A) 他们坚信美国梦。
B) 他们努力攀登社会经济阶梯。
C) 他们对自己的党派有很强的归属感。
D) 他们倾向于观看更多白手起家的电视节目。
**判型** What can we infer from the passage about Republicans in general 中明确出现 infer，是典型推断信号。
**拆句** 主干 What can we infer from the passage about Republicans in general。in general提示答案不应是局部小结论，而是适用于该群体的整体性推断。
**定位** 有趣的是，当按党派分组时，这种效应在共和党人中显著、而在民主党人中不显著，这意味着真人秀里隐含的信息可能契合了人们既有的社会经济观念。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats ↔believe strongly in the American Dream play into people’s existing socioeconomic beliefs ↔ believe strongly in the American Dream预判结论是『共和党人本就更信美国梦』，选项 A 是这一推断的标准表达。
B) 无中生有原文只比较了党派对美国梦的信念差异，从未提到任一党派的人在 socio-economic ladder 上的实际行动。
C) 偷换概念when participants were separated by party affiliation 中 party affiliation 只是『按党派分组』的研究操作变量，并未评价共和党人对自己政党的归属感强弱。
D) 过度推断原文只说看了 rags-to-riches 短片后，对美国梦信仰加深的效应在共和党人中显著；并未说共和党人比民主党人更常或更多地观看此类节目。
questions.quote: Interestingly, when participants were separated by party affiliation, this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats, suggesting that the kind of messages implicit in these TV shows may play into people's existing socioeconomic beliefs.

options.text: They believe strongly in the American Dream.
They strive to climb the socio-economic ladder.
They have a very strong affiliation with their party.
They tend to watch more rags-to-riches TV shows.

questions.prompt: What is stated about people who believe in upward mobility?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于相信向上流动的人,文中陈述了什么?
A) 他们可能会因自己的困境而责怪政府。
B) 他们认为政治后果绝非微不足道。
C) 他们尊重努力攀登社会阶梯的个人。
D) 他们不太可能赞成对抗不平等的政策。
**判型** What is stated about people who believe in upward mobility 用 stated 询问对该人群所作的陈述，是细节题。
**拆句** 主干 What is stated about people…？被动语态，who believe in upward mobility 是people 的定语从句，提示要找作者直接说明这类人会怎样的句子。
**定位** 问题就在这里：如果人们错误地以为只要努力工作就足以让个人过上更好的生活，他们就可能更不支持那些其实能对抗不平等的政策。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有P8 只说他们更不支持反不平等政策，从未提到他们指责政府或抱怨自身困境。
B) 张冠李戴Its political consequences are anything but trivial 中代词 Its 指向 entertainment media；选项 B 把这一评价偷塞到『相信向上流动者』身上，属于张冠李戴。
C) 无中生有原文只说他们因为相信努力万能而更不支持反不平等政策，从未提到他们对其他奋斗者的态度（如尊敬）。
D) ✓ 正确they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality↔less likely to approve of policies to fight inequality预判结论『更不支持反不平等政策』与选项 D 完全等义，combat 与 fight 是六级阅读高频可互换词。
questions.quote: And here's the problem: if people mistakenly believe that hard work is all that is needed for individuals to make a better life for themselves, they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality.

options.text: They are likely to blame the government for their plight.
They regard political consequences as anything but trivial.
They respect individuals striving to climb the social ladder.
They are less likely to approve of policies to fight inequality.

title: The Sun Is Also a Star is a…

sentences.text: The Sun Is Also a Star is a truly lovely story of love, romance, fate, and destiny.

passage.translation: 《太阳也是一颗星》是一个关于爱情、浪漫、命运和宿命的真正动人的故事。

sentences.text: Natasha is a Jamaican-born immigrant living (26)____ in America, not by choice exactly.
Her parents brought her over and created the situation she (27)____ to be out of.

passage.translation: Natasha是一位在牙买加出生的移民,非法居住在美国,这并非完全出于她的选择。是她的父母把她带来并造成了她努力想要摆脱的处境。

sentences.text: Daniel is an American born of Korean immigrants.
He believes in true love, fate, and all that other nonsense that Natasha (28)____ through scientific reasoning.

passage.translation: Daniel是在美国出生的韩国移民后代。他相信真爱、命运以及所有那些被Natasha用科学推理驳斥的无稽之谈。

sentences.text: Daniel and Natasha meet by (29)____ on the streets of New York on the day that she is to be(30)____ .
She doesn't tell him that but does allow him to keep her company while he tries to get her to fall in love with him over the course of the day.

passage.translation: Daniel和Natasha在纽约街头偶然相遇,那天正是她将被驱逐出境的日子。她没有告诉他这件事,但确实允许他陪伴她,而他则试图在这一天的时间里让她爱上他。

sentences.text: Natasha is me.
I found her so similar to myself.
She's scientifically-minded, practical, somewhat cynical, and always (31)____ .
Her obsession with the universe through a scientific lens is infectious and I (32)____ Daniel seeing that too.

passage.translation: Natasha就是我。我发现她和我自己非常相似。她具有科学头脑、务实、有些愤世嫉俗,而且总是持怀疑态度。她通过科学视角对宇宙的痴迷具有感染力,我也喜欢Daniel看到这一点。

sentences.text: Daniel is charming and passionate and has a way with words that even (33)____ Natasha's tough outer shell.
By the end of the book I fell in love with both of them.

passage.translation: Daniel富有魅力和激情,他的言语方式甚至能打破Natasha坚硬的外壳。在书的结尾,我爱上了他们两个。

sentences.text: I used to find romance stories to always be cheap or laughable.
I think now I can see the value in escaping into a story of pure optimism.
I got (34)____ in The Sun Is Also a Star and finished it cover to cover in a weekend.
I couldn't wait to get to what I hoped would be a happy ending.

passage.translation: 我曾经总是觉得浪漫故事廉价或可笑。我想现在我能看到逃入一个纯粹乐观的故事中的价值。我沉浸在《太阳也是一颗星》中,并在一个周末就从头到尾读完了它。我迫不及待地想看到我所希望的美好结局。

sentences.text: It's nice every once in a while to give in to magic.
It doesn't have to be a hard fantasy novel with actual spells, it can be the magic found between two people who just have that special something.
That(35)____ that causes them to react and spark when they're near each other.

passage.translation: 偶尔屈服于魔力是件好事。它不必是一部有真实咒语的硬幻想小说,它可以是两个人之间发现的魔力,他们就是有那种特别的东西。那种化学反应使他们在彼此靠近时产生反应和火花。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
The Sun Is Also a Star is a truly lovely story of love, romance, fate, and destiny.

Natasha is a Jamaican-born immigrant living {{26}} in America, not by choice exactly. Her parents brought her over and created the situation she {{27}} to be out of.

Daniel is an American born of Korean immigrants. He believes in true love, fate, and all that other nonsense that Natasha {{28}} through scientific reasoning.

Daniel and Natasha meet by {{29}} on the streets of New York on the day that she is to be{{30}} . She doesn't tell him that but does allow him to keep her company while he tries to get her to fall in love with him over the course of the day.

Natasha is me. I found her so similar to myself. She's scientifically-minded, practical, somewhat cynical, and always {{31}} . Her obsession with the universe through a scientific lens is infectious and I {{32}} Daniel seeing that too.

Daniel is charming and passionate and has a way with words that even {{33}} Natasha's tough outer shell. By the end of the book I fell in love with both of them.

I used to find romance stories to always be cheap or laughable. I think now I can see the value in escaping into a story of pure optimism. I got {{34}} in The Sun Is Also a Star and finished it cover to cover in a weekend. I couldn't wait to get to what I hoped would be a happy ending.

It's nice every once in a while to give in to magic. It doesn't have to be a hard fantasy novel with actual spells, it can be the magic found between two people who just have that special something. That{{35}} that causes them to react and spark when they're near each other.

options.text: adore
illegally
appraise
lost
assaults
perpetually
chemistry
prescribed
coincidence
shrewd
cracks
skeptical
deported
strives
dismisses

questions.explanation:
**答案** I) illegally 副词
**词性槽** living 后缺修饰语，需副词
**依据** 与下句「想脱离的处境」呼应=非法滞留紧接着的 Her parents brought her over and created the situation she __(27)__ to be out of. 说明父母带她过来、造成了她想摆脱的「处境」——这种典型「移民却想脱身」的处境就是「非法居留」。illegally 修饰 living，正好把这条暗线一句话点透。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
K) perpetually 语义不指向她想脱离的困境perpetually=「永久地」只描述时间长度，无法解释她「想 be out of」的那种处境，与后文的脱身意愿不咬合。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) strives 动词
**词性槽** she 后缺谓语 + to be 不定式
**依据** strive to be out of=努力摆脱Natasha 想摆脱「非法居留即将被遣返」的处境，strives to be out of 正好表达「她一直在努力跳出这处境」的奋斗感，与全文中她「practical、cynical、scientifically-minded」的人物形象一致。

**答案** H) dismisses 动词
**词性槽** 定语从句中 Natasha 后缺谓语
**依据** dismiss=不予理会、驳回她对 Daniel 那些「真爱、命运」之类的「nonsense（胡说八道）」用「scientific reasoning（科学推理）」来对待——最贴的就是「dismiss=驳回 / 不予理会」。一个skeptical 的人对超验信念的标准反应就是 dismiss。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) assaults 攻击太过激烈，搭配也不自然assault 一般指人身/语言上的猛烈攻击，「用科学推理 assault 胡话」搭配生硬、语气也过激，不像理性书评的写法。
F) cracks crack 通常指「攻破壳/裂开」，留给 33 题crack 的「击破外壳」义更贴合 33 题 that even __(33)__ Natasha's tough outer shell 那种「攻破她那层硬壳」的形象化表达，把它放在这里会和那条线抢词。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— cracks 极易被误填到 28。cracks 也是 -s 动词、也能搭「攻破 nonsense」，但它真正的家在 33 题的 outer shell；若 28 用了 cracks，33 题就只能勉强配 assaults，全篇逻辑塌方。防坑口诀：看到 outer shell/wall 这种 metaphor 宾语，先把 crack 留给它。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) coincidence 名词
**词性槽** 介词 by 后接名词
**依据** by coincidence=偶然地，固定搭配by coincidence 是英语里非常稳定的方式状语短语，意为「偶然、巧合地」；正好对应The Sun Is Also a Star is a truly lovely story of love, romance, fate, and destiny. 里反复出现的「命运」基调——两个陌生人街头偶遇、命中注定的故事开端。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
D) chemistry 搭配不立 + 语义留给最后一空by chemistry 不是英语固定搭配；而且 chemistry「人与人之间的默契火花」更适合留给 35 题里 That __(35)__ that causes them to react and spark when they're near each other. 那种「化学反应」语义。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) deported 动词
**词性槽** be to be __(30)__ 是被动不定式
**依据** 与 26 题非法居留对应=即将被驱逐26 题已经定下 Natasha 是 Natasha is a Jamaican-born immigrant living __(26)__ in America 非法身份；那么「她今天即将 be __(30)__」最合逻辑的就是「被驱逐出境」（deported），整本书最大的戏剧张力——一日相恋、当晚遣返——也由此而来。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
