questions.prompt: In pursuing perfection, some perfectionists fail to complete their tasks on time.
questions.explanation:
**答案** G 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
在追求完美的过程中,一些完美主义者未能按时完成任务。
**锚点** fail to complete their tasks on time
**定位** 但另一些人反而拖延工作，除非达到完美否则交不出作业。
**改写** some perfectionists fail to complete their tasks on time↔others actually fall behind on work, unable to complete assignments unless they are, well, perfect fall behind 加 unable to complete 等于 fail to complete on time
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
F Meeting them becomes an all or nothing premise 描述心理层的恶性循环，没有fail to complete on time 这一具体行为。make an archive of all their failures
questions.quote: But others actually fall behind on work, unable to complete assignments unless they are, well, perfect.

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Gratitude may be more beneficial than we commonly suppose.
One recent study asked participants to write a note of thanks to someone and then estimate how surprised and happy the recipient would feel—an impact that they consistently underestimated.
Another study assessed the health benefits of writing thank-you notes.
The researchers found that writing as few as three weekly thank-you notes over the course of three weeks improved life satisfaction, increased happy feelings and reduced symptoms of depression.

passage.translation: 感恩可能比我们通常认为的更有益。最近一项研究要求参与者给某人写一封感谢信,然后估计收信人会感到多么惊讶和快乐——他们一贯低估了这种影响。另一项研究评估了写感谢信对健康的益处。研究人员发现,在三周的时间里每周只写三封感谢信,就能提高生活满意度,增加幸福感并减轻抑郁症状。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: While this research into gratitude is relatively new, the principles involved are anything but.
Students of mine in a political philosophy course at Indiana University are reading Daniel Defoe's 300-year- old Robinson Crusoe, often regarded as the first novel published in English.
Left alone on an unknown island with no apparent prospect of rescue or escape, Crusoe has much to lament(悲叹).

But instead of giving in to despair, he makes a list of things for which he is grateful, including the fact that he is the sole survivor from the shipwreck(海难) and has been able to salvage many useful items from the wreckage.

passage.translation: 虽然这项关于感恩的研究相对较新,但其中涉及的原则却绝非如此。我在Indiana University政治哲学课程的学生正在阅读Daniel Defoe三百年前的《鲁滨逊漂流记》,该书通常被认为是用英语出版的第一部小说。独自留在一个陌生的岛屿上,看不到获救或逃脱的明显希望,Crusoe有很多值得悲叹的事情。但他没有屈服于绝望,而是列出了他所感激的事情,包括他是海难中唯一的幸存者这一事实,并且能够从残骸中打捞出许多有用的物品。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: Defoe's masterpiece, which is often ranked as one of the world's greatest novels, provides a portrait of gratitude in action that is as timely and relevant today as it has ever been.
It is also one with which contemporary psychology and medicine are just beginning to catch up.
Simply put, for most of us, it is far more helpful to focus on the things in life for which we can express gratitude than those that incline us toward resentment and lamentation.

passage.translation: Defoe的这部杰作常被列为世界上最伟大的小说之一,它呈现了一幅感恩行动的画像,这幅画像在今天和以往任何时候一样及时而切题。当代心理学和医学也才刚刚开始赶上它。简单地说,对我们大多数人来说,关注生活中我们可以表达感激的事情,远比关注那些使我们倾向于怨恨和悲叹的事情更有帮助。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: When we focus on the things we regret, such as failed relationships, family disputes, and setbacks in career and finance, we tend to become more regretful.
Conversely, when we focus on the things we are grateful for, a greater sense of happiness tends to spread through our lives.

And while no one would argue for cultivating a false sense of blessedness, there is mounting evidence that counting our blessings is one of the best habits we can develop to promote mental and physical health.

passage.translation: 当我们关注我们后悔的事情时,比如失败的关系、家庭纠纷以及事业和财务上的挫折,我们往往会变得更加后悔。相反,当我们关注我们感激的事情时,更强烈的幸福感往往会传播到我们的生活中。虽然没有人会主张培养一种虚假的幸福感,但越来越多的证据表明,细数我们的幸事是我们可以养成的促进心理和身体健康的最佳习惯之一。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Gratitude has long enjoyed a privileged position in many of the world's cultural traditions.

For example, some ancient Western philosophers counsel gratitude that is both enduring and complete, and some Eastern thinkers portray it as not merely an attitude but a virtue to be put into practice.

passage.translation: 感恩长期以来在世界上许多文化传统中享有特权地位。例如,一些古代西方哲学家倡导既持久又完整的感恩,一些东方思想家将其描绘为不仅仅是一种态度,而是一种要付诸实践的美德。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: Recent scientific studies support these ancient teachings.

Individuals who regularly engage in gratitude exercises, such as counting their blessings or expressing gratitude to others, exhibit increased satisfaction with relationships and fewer symptoms of physical illness.
And the benefits are not only psychological and physical.
They may also be moral—those who practice gratitude also view their lives less materialistically and suffer from less envy.

passage.translation: 最近的科学研究支持这些古老的教义。定期进行感恩练习的个人,如细数自己的幸事或向他人表达感激,表现出对人际关系更高的满意度和更少的身体疾病症状。这些益处不仅是心理上和身体上的。它们也可能是道德上的——那些践行感恩的人也较少用物质主义的眼光看待自己的生活,并且较少遭受嫉妒之苦。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: There are multiple explanations for such benefits of gratefulness.
One is the fact that expressing gratitude encourages others to continue being generous, thus promoting a virtuous cycle of goodness in relationships.
Similarly, grateful people may be more likely to reciprocate(回报) with acts of kindness of their own.
Broadly speaking, a community in which people feel grateful to one another is likely to be a more pleasant place to live than one characterized by mutual suspicion and resentment.
The beneficial effects of gratitude may extend even further.
For example, when many people feel good about what someone else has done for them, they experience a sense of being lifted up, with a corresponding enhancement of their regard for humanity.
Some are inspired to attempt to become better people themselves, doing more to help bring out the best in others and bringing more goodness into the world around them.

passage.translation: 对感恩的这些益处有多种解释。一个是这样的事实:表达感激鼓励他人继续慷慨大方,从而促进人际关系中善意的良性循环。同样,心怀感激的人可能更有可能用自己的善举来回报。从广义上讲,一个人们彼此心怀感激的社区,很可能比一个以相互猜疑和怨恨为特征的社区更宜居。感恩的有益影响可能延伸得更远。例如,当许多人对别人为他们所做的事情感到高兴时,他们会体验到一种被提升的感觉,相应地提高了他们对人性的尊重。有些人受到启发,试图成为更好的人,做更多的事来帮助激发他人的优点,并为周围的世界带来更多的善意。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Gratitude also tends to strengthen a sense of connection with others.
When people want to do good things that inspire gratitude, the level of dedication in relationships tends to grow and relationships seem to last longer.
And when people feel more connected, they are more likely to choose to spend their time with one another and demonstrate their feelings of affection in daily acts.

passage.translation: 感恩也往往会加强与他人的联系感。当人们想做激发感激的好事时,人际关系中的投入程度往往会增长,关系似乎会持续更久。当人们感到更紧密联系时,他们更有可能选择共度时光,并在日常行为中表达他们的感情。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Of course, acts of kindness can also foster discomfort.
For example, if people feel they are not worthy of kindness or suspect that some ulterior(别有用心的) motive lies behind it, the benefits of gratitude will not be realized.
Likewise, receiving a kindness can give rise to a sense of indebtedness, leaving beneficiaries feeling that they must now pay back whatever good they have received.
Gratitude can flourish only if people are secure enough in themselves and sufficiently trusting to allow it to do so.
Another obstacle to gratitude is often called a sense of entitlement.
Instead of experiencing a benefaction(善行) as a good turn, people sometimes regard it as a mere payment of what they are owed, for which no one deserves any moral credit.

passage.translation: 当然,善举也可能引发不适。例如,如果人们觉得自己不配得到善意,或怀疑其背后隐藏着某种别有用心的动机,感恩的益处就无法实现。同样,接受善意可能会产生一种负债感,使受益者觉得他们现在必须偿还所得到的任何好处。感恩只有在人们对自己足够有安全感并且有足够的信任允许它这样做时才能蓬勃发展。感恩的另一个障碍通常被称为特权感。人们有时不是将善行视为好意,而是将其视为对自己所应得之物的单纯支付,没有人因此应得任何道德赞誉。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: There are a number of practical steps anyone can take to promote a sense of gratitude.
One is simply spending time on a regular basis thinking about someone who has made a difference, or perhaps writing a thank-you note or expressing such gratitude in person.
Others are found in ancient religious disciplines, such as reflecting on benefactions received from another person or actually praying for the health and happiness of a benefactor.
In addition to benefactions received, it is also possible to focus on opportunities to do good oneself, whether those acted on in the past or hoped for in the future.
Some people are most grateful not for what others have done for them but for chances they enjoyed to help others.

In regularly reflecting on the things in his life he is grateful for, Defoe's Crusoe believes that he becomes a far better person than he would have been had he remained in the society from which he originally set out on his voyage.

passage.translation: 任何人都可以采取许多实际步骤来培养感恩之心。一个是简单地定期花时间思考一个产生过影响的人,或者写一封感谢信或当面表达这种感激。其他方法见于古老的宗教修行,如反思从他人那里得到的善行,或实际为恩人的健康和幸福祈祷。除了收到的善行,还可以关注自己行善的机会,无论是过去付诸行动的还是未来希望做到的。有些人最感激的不是别人为他们做了什么,而是他们享有的帮助他人的机会。在定期反思生活中他所感激的事情时,Defoe笔下的Crusoe相信,他成为了一个比他如果留在他最初出发航行的那个社会中会成为的人要好得多的人。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: Reflecting on generosity and gratitude, the great basketball coach John Wooden once offered two counsels to his players and students.
First, he said, "It is impossible to have a perfect day unless you have done something for someone who will never be able to repay you."
In saying this, Wooden sought to promote purely generous acts, as opposed to those performed with an expectation of reward.
Second, he said, "Give thanks for your blessings every day."

passage.translation: 在反思慷慨和感恩时,伟大的篮球教练John Wooden曾向他的球员和学生提出两条建议。首先,他说:"除非你为一个永远无法报答你的人做了一些事,否则不可能拥有完美的一天。"说这话时,Wooden试图促进纯粹慷慨的行为,而不是那些期待回报的行为。其次,他说:"每天为你的幸事而感恩。"

passage.label: L

sentences.text: Some faith traditions incorporate such practices into the rhythm of daily life.
For example, adherents of some religions offer prayers of thanksgiving every morning before rising and every night before lying down to sleep.
Others offer thanks throughout the day, such as before meals.
Other less frequent special events, such as births, deaths and marriages, may also be heralded by such prayers.

passage.translation: 一些信仰传统将这类实践融入日常生活的节奏中。例如,某些宗教的信徒每天早上起床前和每晚睡觉前都会做感恩祈祷。其他人则全天表达感谢,比如在饭前。其他不太频繁的特殊事件,如出生、死亡和婚姻,也可能通过这样的祈祷来宣告。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: When Defoe depicted Robinson Crusoe making thanksgiving a daily part of his island life, he was anticipating findings in social science and medicine that would not appear for hundreds of years.
Yet he was also reflecting the wisdom of religious and philosophical traditions that extend back thousands of years.
Gratitude is one of the healthiest and most nourishing of all states of mind, and those who adopt it as a habit are enriching not only their own lives but also the lives of those around them.

passage.translation: 当Defoe描绘鲁滨逊·克鲁索使感恩成为他岛屿生活的日常部分时,他预见了数百年后才会出现的社会科学和医学发现。然而,他也反映了延续数千年的宗教和哲学传统的智慧。感恩是所有心理状态中最健康、最滋养的状态之一,那些将其作为习惯的人不仅丰富了自己的生活,也丰富了周围人的生活。

在所有的心理状态中,感恩被认为是最健康和最有益的心态之一。
**锚点** 感恩是最健康、最有益的心态之一
**定位** 感恩是所有心态中最健康、最滋养的心态之一；养成感恩习惯的人，不仅在丰盈自己的生活，也在丰盈身边人的生活。
**改写** Of all states of mind ↔ of all states of mind短语原样复现feeling grateful ↔ Gratitude动名词与抽象名词同义one of the most healthy and beneficial ↔ one of the healthiest and most nourishing最高级框架内的近义形容词替换
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
D counting our blessings is one of the best habits we can develop to promote mental and physical health 中的 one of the best 修饰的是 habits，而陈述句要求of all states of mind 中的最高级修饰对象是“心态”，对象错位即不构成匹配。counting our blessings is one of the best habits we can develop to promote mental and physical health
questions.quote: Gratitude is one of the healthiest and most nourishing of all states of mind, and those who adopt it as a habit are enriching not only their own lives but also the lives of those around them.

questions.prompt: The principles underlying the research into gratitude are nothing new at all.
questions.explanation:
**答案** B 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
感恩研究所依据的原则完全不是什么新事物。
**锚点** 感恩研究背后的原理并不新
**定位** 虽然这类关于感恩的研究相对较新，但其中所涉的原理一点都不新。
**改写** The principles underlying the research into gratitude ↔this research into gratitude is relatively new, the principles involved句式重构与同义替换are nothing new at all ↔ the principles involved are anything but习语级强否定的同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E Gratitude has long enjoyed a privileged position in many of the world's cultural traditions 与 some ancient Western philosophers counsel gratitude 谈的是古代文化态度，没有出现“研究背后的原理一点都不新”这一对照句框架，与陈述句要求错位。Gratitude has long enjoyed a privileged position in many of the world's cultural traditions.
questions.quote: While this research into gratitude is relatively new, the principles involved are anything but.

questions.prompt: Gratitude is likely to enhance one's sense of being connected with other people.
questions.explanation:
**答案** H 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
感恩很可能增强一个人与他人相连的感觉。
**锚点** 增强与他人的连接感
**定位** 感恩也倾向于增强人与他人之间的连接感。
**改写** is likely to enhance ↔ tends to strengthen近义动词与情态副词同义sense of being connected with other people ↔ sense of connection with others动词过去分词与同根名词同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
G a virtuous cycle of goodness in relationships 谈的是 relationships 中的善意循环，并未直接讲“增强连接感”；陈述句的“sense of being connected”需对 H 段的sense of connection 主题句，与 G 段错位。expressing gratitude encourages others to continue being generous, thus promoting a virtuous cycle of goodness in relationships.
questions.quote: Gratitude also tends to strengthen a sense of connection with others.

title: Chimpanzees(黑猩猩), human beings' closest animal relatives, share up…

sentences.text: Chimpanzees(黑猩猩), human beings' closest animal relatives, share up to 98% of our genes.
Yet humans and chimpanzees lead very different lives.
Fewer than 300,000 wild chimpanzees live in a few forested corners of Africa today, while humans have colonized every corner of the globe.
At more than 7 billion, human population dwarfs that of nearly all other mammals—despite our physical weaknesses.

passage.translation: 黑猩猩是人类在动物界最亲近的近亲,与我们共享高达98%的基因。然而人类和黑猩猩过着截然不同的生活。如今只有不到30万只野生黑猩猩生活在非洲少数几个森林角落,而人类已经在全球每个角落定居。人类人口超过70亿,使几乎所有其他哺乳动物的数量相形见绌——尽管我们身体上有弱点。

sentences.text: What could account for our species' incredible evolutionary successes?

passage.translation: 是什么可以解释我们物种令人难以置信的进化成功?

sentences.text: One obvious answer is our big brains.
It could be that our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box, innovating solutions to thorny problems as people migrated across the globe.

passage.translation: 一个显而易见的答案是我们的大脑袋。可能是我们的原始智力赋予了我们前所未有的跳出常规思维的能力,在人们迁徙到全球各地时创新性地解决棘手问题。

sentences.text: But a growing number of cognitive scientists and anthropologists(人类学家) are rejecting that explanation.
They think that, rather than making our living as innovators, we survive and thrive precisely because we don't think for ourselves.
Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others.

passage.translation: 但越来越多的认知科学家和人类学家正在否定这种解释。他们认为,我们之所以能够生存和繁荣,恰恰是因为我们不独立思考,而非靠创新谋生。相反,人们通过仔细模仿他人来应对充满挑战的气候和生态环境。

sentences.text: In a famous study, psychologists Victoria Horner and Andrew Whiten showed two groups of test subjects—children and chimpanzees—a mechanical box with a treat inside.
In one condition, the box was opaque, while in the other it was transparent.
The experimenters demonstrated how to open the box to retrieve the treat, but they also included the irrelevant step of tapping on the box with a stick.

passage.translation: 在一项著名的研究中,心理学家Victoria Horner和Andrew Whiten向两组测试对象——儿童和黑猩猩——展示了一个里面装有奖品的机械盒子。在一种条件下,盒子是不透明的,而在另一种条件下它是透明的。实验者演示了如何打开盒子取出奖品,但他们还包含了用棍子敲击盒子这一无关步骤。

sentences.text: Oddly, the children carefully copied all the steps to open the box, even when they could see that the stick had no practical effect.
That is, they copied irrationally: Instead of doing only what was necessary to get their reward, children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed.

passage.translation: 奇怪的是,即使孩子们能看到棍子没有实际作用,他们也会仔细模仿打开盒子的所有步骤。也就是说,他们进行了非理性的模仿:孩子们不是只做获得奖励所必需的事情,而是机械地模仿他们目睹的每一个动作。

sentences.text: Of course, that study only included three—and four-year-olds.

But additional research has shown that older children and adults are even more likely to mindlessly copy others' actions, and infants are less likely to over-imitate—that is, to precisely copy even impractical actions.

passage.translation: 当然,那项研究只包括三岁和四岁的儿童。但其他研究表明,年龄较大的儿童和成年人更有可能盲目模仿他人的行为,而婴儿较少过度模仿——也就是说,较少精确复制甚至不实用的动作。

sentences.text: By contrast, chimpanzees in the study only over-imitated in the opaque condition.
In the transparent condition—where they saw that the stick was mechanically useless—they ignored that step entirely.
Other research has since supported these findings.

passage.translation: 相比之下,研究中的黑猩猩只在不透明条件下过度模仿。在透明条件下——它们看到棍子在机械上毫无用处——它们完全忽略了那个步骤。其他研究此后也支持了这些发现。

sentences.text: When it comes to copying, chimpanzees are more rational than human children or adults.

passage.translation: 在模仿方面,黑猩猩比人类儿童或成年人更理性。

sentences.text: Where does the seemingly irrational human preference for over-imitation come from?
Anthropologist Joseph Henrich points out that people around the world rely on technologies that are often so complex that no one can learn them rationally.
Instead, people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers.

passage.translation: 人类看似非理性的过度模仿偏好从何而来?人类学家Joseph Henrich指出,世界各地的人们依赖的技术往往非常复杂,以至于没有人能够理性地学会它们。相反,人们必须一步一步地学习它们,相信更有经验的长辈和同伴的智慧。

sentences.text: So the next time you hear someone arguing passionately that everyone should embrace nonconformity and avoid imitating others, you might laugh a little bit.
We're not chimpanzees, after all.

passage.translation: 所以下次当你听到有人热情地主张每个人都应该拥抱不墨守成规并避免模仿他人时,你可能会笑一笑。毕竟,我们不是黑猩猩。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What might explain humans' having the largest population of almost all mammals?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
什么可能解释人类拥有几乎所有哺乳动物中最大的种群数量?
A) 他们具备解决最具挑战性问题的原始力量。
B) 他们比动物亲缘物种更有效地应对外部世界。
C) 他们拥有最杰出的思考能力。
D) 他们知道如何在地球上任何地方生存。
**判型** 题干 What might explain humans' having the largest population of almost all mammals? 指向文章中给出原因解释的某一句，并非全文主旨，属于细节题。
**拆句** 主干是 What might explain X，其中 X 由动名词短语 humans' having the largest population of almost all mammals 充当 explain 的宾语；不定式般的动名词结构是六级常见考点，注意 humans' 是 having 的逻辑主语，不是 population 的所有格。
**定位** 一个显而易见的答案是我们的大脑。可能是我们的纯粹智力赋予了我们一种前所未有的跳出思维定式的能力，让人们在迁徙到全球各处时能够创新性地解决棘手难题。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念选项 equipped with raw strength for solving the most challenging problems 用raw strength 替换原文 raw intelligence，正话反说——文章首段恰恰强调 despite our physical weaknesses，人类身体反而是弱的。
B) 答非所问They cope with the outside world more effectively than their animal relatives 用animal relatives 把题点引向 Chimpanzees, human beings' closest animal relatives——黑猩猩，但 51 题问的是 largest population of almost all mammals 的原因，原因句在 P3 而非 P1。
C) ✓ 正确our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box ↔possess the most outstanding ability to think our big brains ↔ possess预判已锁定卓越的思考能力，C 选项 possess the most outstanding ability to think在词面与语义上都与定位句一一对应，是定位句的标准同义替换。
D) 答非所问They know how to survive everywhere on earth 是 humans have colonized every corner of the globe 的同义改写，但这是现象本身，不是题目所问的解释；题干 What might explain 要的是 原因。
questions.quote: One obvious answer is our big brains. It could be that our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box, innovating solutions to thorny problems as people migrated across the globe.

options.text: They are equipped with raw strength for solving the most challenging problems.
They cope with the outside world more effectively than their animal relatives.
They possess the most outstanding ability to think.
They know how to survive everywhere on earth.

questions.prompt: What accounts for humans' evolutionary successes according to a growing number of cognitive scientists and anthropologists?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
根据越来越多认知科学家和人类学家的观点,什么解释了人类进化的成功?
A) 他们更擅长创新解决方案。
B) 他们通过创造性策略繁荣发展。
C) 他们天生适应生态环境。
D) 他们通过仔细模仿他人来应对挑战。
**判型** 题干 according to a growing number of cognitive scientists and anthropologists 限定了观点来源，要求回原文找到该群体说了什么，属典型署名细节题。
**拆句** 主干 What accounts for humans' evolutionary successes，后接 according to 短语作状语限定信息来源；account for 在此意为解释/导致，是六级高频熟词僻义。
**定位** 他们认为：我们之所以存活下来并蓬勃发展，恰恰不是因为我们以创新者的身份谋生，而恰恰是因为我们不自己思考。相反，人类是通过仔细地模仿他人来应对极具挑战的气候与生态环境的。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴They are better at innovating solutions 来自 innovating solutions to thorny problems——但这是 P4 But 转折之前被驳的旧解释，不是 a growing number of 科学家的观点；题干限定了观点出处，必须取转折之后。
B) 与原文相反They thrive through creative strategies 用 creative——这与 we don't think for ourselves 直接相反，文章明确说人类成功不靠自己思考创新。
C) 无中生有They are naturally adaptive to ecological contexts 把 ecological contexts 抄过来制造熟悉感，但 naturally adaptive（与生俱来的适应性）这种说法在原文没有任何出处——文章强调的是后天模仿。
D) ✓ 正确by carefully copying others ↔ imitating others carefully cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts ↔ meet challenges预判已锁定靠仔细模仿来应对挑战，They meet challenges by imitating others carefully 在结构（meet challenges by + 动名词短语）和措辞上与定位句完全同义。
questions.quote: They think that, rather than making our living as innovators, we survive and thrive precisely because we don't think for ourselves. Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others.

options.text: They are better at innovating solutions.
They thrive through creative strategies.
They are naturally adaptive to ecological contexts.
They meet challenges by imitating others carefully.

questions.prompt: What does the author think is odd about the findings of the study by Victoria Horner and Andrew Whiten?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者认为Victoria Horner和Andrew Whiten的研究发现有什么奇怪之处?
A) 儿童非理性地模仿了实验者的每一个动作。
B) 黑猩猩能够区分透明盒子和不透明盒子。
C) 黑猩猩取得奖励的速度比儿童更快。
D) 儿童省略了用棍子敲击盒子以打开它的步骤。
**判型** 题干问的是作者认为某项研究中 odd 的具体内容，需要回到原文一句话找出对应描述，是细节题而非态度题。
**拆句** 主干 What does the author think is odd about X，think 后跟省略 that 的宾语从句 is odd about the findings，about 短语限定 odd 的范围；考生易把 think is odd 误读成主旨态度题。
**定位** 奇怪的是，儿童仔细地模仿了开盒子的每一步动作，哪怕他们能看出那根木棒并没有任何实际作用。也就是说，他们的模仿是非理性的：他们没有只做获得奖励所必需的动作，而是奴隶般地模仿了所看到的每一个动作。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed ↔Children irrationally imitated every action of the experimenters every action they'd witnessed ↔ every action of the experimenters A 选项 Children irrationally imitated every action of the experimenters 完整对应定位句的两个关键点：irrationally 对应 slavishly/irrationally，every action of the experimenters 对应 every action they'd witnessed。
B) 答非所问Chimpanzees could tell the transparent box from the opaque one 描述黑猩猩能区分透明与不透明盒子——这是 P8 黑猩猩对比段的隐含信息，但题干问的是作者认为odd 的发现，奇怪在儿童这边，不在黑猩猩能不能区分上。
C) 无中生有Chimpanzees could retrieve the treat more quickly than children did 提到黑猩猩比儿童更快取得食物——这种速度比较在文中没有任何描写。
D) 与原文相反Children omitted the step of tapping on the box with a stick to open it 说儿童跳过了敲打这一步——与 children carefully copied all the steps 完全相反，且 P8 显示是黑猩猩在透明条件下才跳过这一步。
questions.quote: Oddly, the children carefully copied all the steps to open the box, even when they could see that the stick had no practical effect. That is, they copied irrationally: Instead of doing only what was necessary to get their reward, children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed.

options.text: Children irrationally imitated every action of the experimenters.
Chimpanzees could tell the transparent box from the opaque one.
Chimpanzees could retrieve the treat more quickly than children did.
Children omitted the step of tapping on the box with a stick to open it.

questions.prompt: What is anthropologist Joseph Henrich's explanation for the human preference for copying?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
人类学家Joseph Henrich对人类偏好模仿的解释是什么?
A) 它源于世界各地人们的理性。
B) 它源于人们学习复杂技术的方式。
C) 它源于人们不信任自己的智慧。
D) 它源于逐步获取知识的愿望。
**判型** 题干 What is anthropologist Joseph Henrich's explanation for the human preference for copying? 明确指向某专家对某行为的解释，属于署名+原因型细节题。
**拆句** 主干 What is anthropologist Joseph Henrich's explanation for the human preference for copying，anthropologist 是 Joseph Henrich 的同位语；preference for copying 名词化结构相当于 prefer to copy。
**定位** 人类学家 Joseph Henrich 指出：世界各地的人都依赖于一些非常复杂的技术，复杂到没有人能够完全理性地学会它们。因此，人们必须一步一步地学习这些技术，并信任那些更有经验的前辈与同伴的智慧。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反It originates in the rationality of people around the world 说模仿源于人们的理性——可文中明确说 no one can learn them rationally，恰恰是 没法理性学 才需要模仿；选项把因果反过来了。
B) ✓ 正确people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers↔ It stems from the way people learn complex technologies technologies that are often so complex ↔ complex technologies rely on technologies ↔ stems from B It stems from the way people learn complex technologies 把 Henrich 的两步因果（技术复杂 → 必须一步步模仿）压缩成 模仿源于学习复杂技术的方式，与预判完全吻合。
C) 过度推断It results from people distrusting their own wisdom——文章里只有 trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers，即信任 前辈与同伴 的智慧，并未说不信任自己的智慧；distrust their own 是过度推断 + 与原文相反的合成。
D) 偷换概念It derives from the desire to acquire knowledge step by step 把 step by step 抄过来，但说成 是因为人有一步步获取知识的欲望——文章是说 因为技术太复杂、不得不一步步学习，并不是出于 欲望。手段被替换成动机。
questions.quote: Anthropologist Joseph Henrich points out that people around the world rely on technologies that are often so complex that no one can learn them rationally. Instead, people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers.

options.text: It originates in the rationality of people around the world.
It stems from the way people learn complex technologies.
It results from people distrusting their own wisdom.
It derives from the desire to acquire knowledge step by step.

questions.prompt: What point does the author want to emphasize when he says "We're not chimpanzees"?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （推断题）
**题目译文**
当作者说"我们不是黑猩猩"时,他想强调什么观点?
A) 每个人是否都应该避免模仿是有争议的。
B) 模仿他人是人类的特征。
C) 信任更有知识的同伴是可取的。
D) 嘲笑拥抱不从众的人是幼稚的。
**判型** What point does the author want to emphasize 询问的是作者借这句反语想强调什么，属典型推断题。
**拆句** 题干主干 What point does the author want to emphasize when he says "We're not chimpanzees"?，when 引导时间状语从句，指明这句话所在的语境；需要把 not chimpanzees 当作对照、推出人类的特征。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念It is arguable whether everyone should avoid imitation 把作者的话理解为 模仿是否该避免是个值得讨论的问题——但作者并没有在讨论 是否该避免，而是直接调侃那些反模仿者；arguable（有争议的）是无中生有的态度。
B) ✓ 正确We're not chimpanzees, after all↔It is characteristic of human beings to copy others carefully copying others↔to copy others B It is characteristic of human beings to copy others 恰好把反语还原为正面陈述：模仿是人类的特征；其余三项要么没抓到反语指向、要么停留在字面。
C) 以偏概全It is desirable to trust in more knowledgeable peers 来自 trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers——这只是 Henrich 一段的局部解释，不是末段反语 We're not chimpanzees 想强调的点；末段强调的是 人类天性模仿，不是 信任前辈这件事好不好。
D) 与原文相反It is naive to laugh at someone embracing nonconformity 说嘲笑追求不从众的人是天真的——可文中作者恰恰说 you might laugh a little bit，即可以笑一笑，作者站的是支持嘲笑那一方；naive（天真的）正话反说。

options.text: It is arguable whether everyone should avoid imitation.
It is characteristic of human beings to copy others.
It is desirable to trust in more knowledgeable peers.
It is naive to laugh at someone embracing nonconformity.

title: If you're someone who has turned to snacking…

sentences.text: If you're someone who has turned to snacking on junk food more in the pandemic(大流行病), you're not alone.
Investigative reporter Michael Moss says processed food is engineered to hook you, not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances.
His 2013 book, Salt Sugar Fat, explored food companies' aggressive marketing of those products and their impact on our health.
In his new book, Hooked, Moss updates the food giants' efforts to keep us eating what they serve, and how they're responding to complaints from consumers and health advocates.

passage.translation: 如果你在疫情期间更频繁地吃垃圾食品零食，你并不孤单。调查记者Michael Moss说，加工食品的设计目的就是让你上瘾，这与酒精、香烟或其他有害物质没什么不同。他2013年的著作《盐糖脂》探讨了食品公司对这些产品的激进营销及其对我们健康的影响。在他的新书《上钩》中,Moss更新了食品巨头让我们继续吃他们提供的食物的努力,以及他们如何回应来自消费者和健康倡导者的投诉。

sentences.text: Processed food is inexpensive, it's legal, and it's everywhere.
Companies' advertising is cueing us to remember those products and we want those products constantly.
So the food environment is one of those key things that makes food even more problematic for so many people.
Memory, nostalgia(怀旧) in particular, plays a big role in the foods we crave.
Soda companies discovered that if they put a soda in the hands of a child when they're at a ball game with their parents, that soda will forever be associated with that joyous moment.
Later in life, when that child wants to experience a joyous moment, they're going to think of soda.
Many people seek comfort in the snacks they remember from childhood.

passage.translation: 加工食品价格低廉、合法且无处不在。公司的广告在提示我们记住这些产品,而我们也不断地想要这些产品。因此,食品环境是使食品对许多人来说更加成问题的关键因素之一。记忆,特别是怀旧,在我们渴望的食物中起着重要作用。碳酸饮料公司发现,如果他们在孩子与父母一起看球赛时把一瓶汽水放到孩子手中,那瓶汽水就会永远与那个快乐时刻联系在一起。在以后的生活中,当那个孩子想要体验快乐时刻时,他们就会想到汽水。许多人在他们记忆中童年时的零食中寻求慰藉。

sentences.text: Moss examines the way companies capitalize on our memories, cravings and brain chemistry to keep us snacking.

passage.translation: Moss研究了公司如何利用我们的记忆、渴望和大脑化学机制来让我们不断吃零食。

sentences.text: One of the reasons I came to think that some of these food products are even more powerful, more troublesome than drugs can be is memory.
What we eat is all about memory.
And we begin forming memories for food at a really early age.
And we keep those memories for a lifetime.
Knowing this, the food industry spends lots of time trying to shape the memories that we have for their products.

One of the features of addiction that scientists studying drug addiction discovered back in the 1990s was that the faster a substance hits the brain, the more apt we are as a result to act impulsively.
There's nothing faster than food in its ability to hit the brain.
For Moss, this puts the notion of "fast food" in an entirely new light as this isn't limited to fast food chains-almost 90% of food products in grocery stores are processed foods.
Everything in the industry is about speed, from manufacturing to packaging.

passage.translation: 我之所以认为其中一些食品甚至比毒品更强大、更麻烦的原因之一就是记忆。我们吃什么完全与记忆有关。我们在很小的时候就开始形成对食物的记忆。而且我们会将这些记忆保留一生。知道这一点后,食品行业花费大量时间试图塑造我们对其产品的记忆。研究药物成瘾的科学家在20世纪90年代发现的成瘾特征之一是,一种物质作用于大脑的速度越快,我们因此冲动行事的可能性就越大。没有什么比食物作用于大脑的能力更快。对Moss来说,这使"快餐"的概念呈现出全新的意义,因为这不仅限于快餐连锁店——杂货店里近90%的食品都是加工食品。行业中的一切都与速度有关,从制造到包装。

sentences.text: Overall, Moss outlines the industry's dependence on making their products inexpensive, super delicious, and incredibly convenient for consumers.

Now that more and more people care about what they put in their bodies and are wanting to eat healthier, these companies are finding it really difficult to meet that new demand because of their own addiction to making these convenience foods.

passage.translation: 总的来说,Moss概述了该行业对使其产品价格低廉、超级美味且对消费者极其方便的依赖。现在越来越多的人关心他们摄入体内的东西,并希望吃得更健康,这些公司发现很难满足这种新需求,因为它们自己对制造这些方便食品上了瘾。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: In what way does Michael Moss think processed food is comparable to alcohol and cigarettes?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
Michael Moss认为加工食品在哪方面可与酒精和香烟相提并论?
A) 它们都会使人上瘾。
B) 它们都是必要之恶。
C) 它们都经过设计以让人享受。
D) 它们的需求都在日益增长。
**判型** In what way does Michael Moss think processed food is comparable to alcohol and cigarettes? 问的是一个明确的可比关系，答案应能从原文一句话直接读出。
**拆句** 主干 does Michael Moss think processed food is comparable to alcohol and cigarettes，从句 that 省略，理解关键是 comparable to 的语义"与……可比"，不是"被比作"。结构平铺直叙、无陷阱。
**定位** 调查记者 Michael Moss 说，加工食品被精心设计来"勾住"你，这一点与酒精、香烟或其他有害物质并无不同。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确engineered to hook you ↔ addictive not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances ↔ They are all addictive.预判"勾住人"对应 addictive，A 即为对定位句双重否定+动词短语的整体重述。
B) 无中生有necessary evils 原文未提及；Moss 全文批评加工食品，没有任何"必要"评价。
C) 偷换概念engineered to be enjoyed 把原文 engineered to hook you 偷换为"为享受而设计"——hook 是"勾住、使上瘾"的强迫语义，与"被享受"的中性愉悦语义不等。
D) 偷换概念increasingly great demand 原文未提及"需求日益增大"；Moss 说的是公司在"积极推销"（aggressive marketing），不是消费者需求暴涨。
questions.quote: Investigative reporter Michael Moss says processed food is engineered to hook you, not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances.

options.text: They are all addictive.
They are all necessary evils.
They are all engineered to be enjoyed.
They are all in increasingly great demand.

questions.prompt: What does the author say plays a key role in the foods we crave?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者认为什么在我们渴望的食物中起着关键作用?
A) 食物环境。
B) 激进的营销。
C) 便利性。
D) 记忆。
**判型** What does the author say plays a key role in the foods we crave? 问的是某个明确因素，答案是原文里一句陈述句的主语或表语。
**拆句** What does the author say plays a key role in the foods we crave? 中 What 既是 say的宾语从句的主语、又是 plays 的主语；the foods we crave 是省略了 that 的定语从句。结构标准、无陷阱。
**定位** 记忆，尤其是怀旧情感，在我们渴求的食物中起着举足轻重的作用。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问The food environment. 出现在 the food environment is one of those key things that makes food even more problematic，原文说的是"让食物对人更具危害"，不是"在我们渴求的食物中起关键作用"。
B) 张冠李戴Aggressive marketing. 来自首段 food companies' aggressive marketing，是 Moss上一本书的话题，不在 Q47 定位句中。
C) 张冠李戴Convenience. 是末段 incredibly convenient for consumers 提到的食品属性之一，与Q47 的"渴求"无直接因果关系。
D) ✓ 正确Memory, nostalgia(怀旧) in particular ↔ Memory.预判的主语 Memory 与 Memory. 原词一致，是最直接的细节复现型答案。
questions.quote: Memory, nostalgia(怀旧) in particular, plays a big role in the foods we crave.

options.text: The food environment.
Aggressive marketing.
Convenience.
Memory.

questions.prompt: What do food companies do to capitalize on consumers' association with their food products?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
食品公司如何利用消费者对其食品产品的联想?
A) 它们努力影响消费者对其产品的记忆方式。
B) 它们试图利用消费者的长期记忆来促进成瘾。
C) 它们试图尽早利用消费者对其产品的记忆。
D) 它们努力找出消费者对其产品的记忆内容。
**判型** What do food companies do to capitalize on consumers' association with their food products? 问的是公司具体做了什么，是原文动作的同义改写。
**拆句** What do food companies do to capitalize on consumers' association with their food products? 中 to capitalize on... 是目的状语；consumers' association with... 是"消费者对……的联想"。结构清晰、无陷阱。
**定位** 明白这一点之后，食品行业花费大量时间，努力塑造我们对其产品所留存的记忆。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确trying to shape the memories that we have for their products ↔strive to influence how consumers remember their products预判的"塑造记忆"与 influence how consumers remember 在动作（塑造/影响）和对象（记忆/如何记住）上双重对应。
B) 过度推断use consumers' long-term memories to promote addiction 把"塑造记忆"曲解为"利用长期记忆推动成瘾"——原文虽然提到 features of addiction，但其语境是说"食物入脑速度快"，并不是把记忆当成瘾工具。
C) 偷换概念exploit consumers' memories for their products as early as possible 把动作偷换为"尽早利用记忆"，并嫁接首段 we begin forming memories for food at a really early age 的"早期"细节——但原文说的是"消费者从小开始形成记忆"，不是"公司尽早去利用"。
D) 偷换概念endeavor to find what consumers remember about their products 把"塑造（shape）"偷换为"查明（find）"——前者是主动改变记忆，后者是被动调查记忆，方向完全相反。
questions.quote: Knowing this, the food industry spends lots of time trying to shape the memories that we have for their products.

options.text: They strive to influence how consumers remember their products.
They attempt to use consumers' long-term memories to promote addiction.
They try to exploit consumers' memories for their products as early as possible.
They endeavor to find what consumers remember about their products.

questions.prompt: How does the food industry operate from manufacturing to packaging, according to Moss?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
根据Moss的说法,食品行业从生产到包装是如何运作的?
A) 将快餐的概念置于全新的视角。
B) 对快餐连锁店的数量不设限制。
C) 专注于工作完成的速度。
D) 优先考虑其产品的质量。
**判型** How does the food industry operate from manufacturing to packaging, according to Moss? 问的是"以什么方式运作"，答案是原文一句话的同义改写。
**拆句** How does the food industry operate from manufacturing to packaging, according to Moss? 中 from...to... 是状语，according to Moss 是引述来源。结构平铺直叙、无陷阱。
**定位** 整个行业的一切都围绕"速度"展开，从生产到包装无一例外。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问Placing the idea of fast food in an entirely new light 是 Moss 对"fast food"概念的重新解读结果，对应 this puts the notion of "fast food" in an entirely new light，但Q49 问的是行业"如何运作"，不是 Moss"如何看待 fast food 概念"。
B) 偷换概念Setting no limit to the number of fast food chains 来自对 isn't limited to fast food chains 的曲解——原文是说"fast food 不限于连锁快餐店（含义=加工食品也算 fast food）"，不是说"快餐连锁店数量没有上限"。
C) ✓ 正确Everything in the industry is about speed ↔ Focusing on how quickly the work is done预判的"以速度为核心"与 Focusing on how quickly the work is done 在核心概念上完全等值。
D) 与原文相反Prioritizing the quality of their products 说"优先考虑质量"，但原文明确说Everything in the industry is about speed——是"速度"优先，不是"质量"优先。
questions.quote: Everything in the industry is about speed, from manufacturing to packaging.

options.text: Placing the idea of fast food in an entirely new light.
Setting no limit to the number of fast food chains.
Focusing on how quickly the work is done.
Prioritizing the quality of their products.

questions.prompt: Why are companies finding it difficult to satisfy consumers' demand for healthier food products?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
为什么公司发现难以满足消费者对更健康食品的需求?
A) 它们认为生产速度比消费者健康更重要。
B) 它们相信没有快餐其行业将会消亡。
C) 它们必须在口味和营养之间取得平衡。
D) 它们沉迷于生产方便食品。
**判型** Why are companies finding it difficult to satisfy consumers' demand for healthier food products? 问的是直接原因，原文必有 because/due to 之类的因果句对应。
**拆句** Why are companies finding it difficult to satisfy consumers' demand for healthier food products? 中 finding it difficult to V 是"find + it（形式宾语）+ difficult + 不定式真宾语"结构；考生若把 it 当作普通代词指代前文事物，就会读偏。
**定位** 如今越来越多的人在意吃进体内的东西、想吃得更健康，这些公司发现自己很难满足这一新需求，原因在于它们自身已经"上瘾"于生产这些便利食品。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断speed of production outweighs consumers' health 把第四段"速度优先"与末段"难满足健康需求"硬串成因果——原文确实说过 about speed，但并未说"速度压倒健康"是公司难以满足新需求的原因。
B) 无中生有their industry would perish without fast foods 完全是凭空想象，原文未涉及行业"消亡"或"存亡"。
C) 过度推断strike a balance between taste and nutrition 把末段 super delicious 和 eat healthier 硬凑成"口味与营养的平衡"——但原文没有任何"平衡"的表述，给出的真正原因是公司自身"上瘾"。
D) ✓ 正确their own addiction to making these convenience foods↔hooked on manufacturing convenience foods making ↔ manufacturing预判的"对制造便利食品上瘾"与 hooked on manufacturing convenience foods 完全等值，且 hooked on 回扣首段 hook 一词，是作者刻意的呼应。
questions.quote: Now that more and more people care about what they put in their bodies and are wanting to eat healthier, these companies are finding it really difficult to meet that new demand because of their own addiction to making these convenience foods.

options.text: They think speed of production outweighs consumers' health.
They believe their industry would perish without fast foods.
They have to strike a balance between taste and nutrition.
They are hooked on manufacturing convenience foods.

title: You might not know yourself as well as…

sentences.text: You might not know yourself as well as you think.
According to a new study, people are (26)____accurate judges of only some of their behaviors.

While most previous studies on how well people know themselves have been done on long-term personality traits, this new study (27)____ how well people understand how they are acting from one moment to the next.
Researchers asked participants to wear audio recorders that automatically (28)____ every 9.5 minutes between 7 a.m. and 2 a.m. to record 30 seconds of audio.
These participants were then emailed surveys four times a day asking them to(29)____ how outgoing, agreeable, or conscientious they were during a particular hour of the day.
The study used data from 248 participants, all of whom answered questions about their behavior for two(30)____ weeks and wore the audio device for one of those weeks.

passage.translation: 你可能并不像自己以为的那样了解自己。根据一项新研究，人们只是对自己某些行为的相对准确的评判者。虽然大多数关于人们有多了解自己的先前研究都是针对长期人格特质进行的,但这项新研究探讨的是人们对自己每时每刻行为表现的理解程度。研究人员要求参与者佩戴录音设备,该设备在上午7点至凌晨2点之间每隔9.5分钟自动启动,记录30秒的音频。随后这些参与者每天会收到四次电子邮件调查,要求他们回忆自己在一天中某个特定小时内的外向程度、随和程度或尽责程度。该研究使用了248名参与者的数据,所有参与者都连续两周回答了关于自己行为的问题,并在其中一周佩戴了音频设备。

sentences.text: Six laboratory assistants rated each participant's audio clips to see how their observations compared with people's (31)____ of themselves.
The six assistants were generally in agreement with one another about how the people they were observing acted.
Further, participants' ratings of their own behaviors agreed with observers' for how outgoing and how conscientious they were being.
But the agreement between participants and outside observers was much smaller for agreeableness.

Some of this (32)____could be because the observers used only audio clips, and thus could not read (33)____ like body language, but there are (34)____ other explanations, as people should be able to hear when a participant is being kind versus being rude.
The weak agreement between how participants thought they were acting and what observers heard could be because people would rather (35)____ rude behavior.

passage.translation: 六名实验室助理对每位参与者的音频片段进行了评分,以了解他们的观察结果与人们对自己的评估相比如何。这六名助理对于他们所观察的人的行为表现总体上彼此意见一致。此外,参与者对自己行为的评分在外向程度和尽责程度方面与观察者的评分是一致的。但参与者与外部观察者之间在随和程度方面的一致性要小得多。造成这种差异的部分原因可能是观察者只使用了音频片段,因此无法解读肢体语言等线索,但可能还有其他解释,因为人们应该能够听出参与者何时表现友善何时表现粗鲁。参与者认为自己的行为表现与观察者所听到的内容之间一致性较弱,可能是因为人们宁愿否认粗鲁的行为。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
You might not know yourself as well as you think. According to a new study, people are {{26}}accurate judges of only some of their behaviors. While most previous studies on how well people know themselves have been done on long-term personality traits, this new study {{27}} how well people understand how they are acting from one moment to the next. Researchers asked participants to wear audio recorders that automatically {{28}} every 9.5 minutes between 7 a.m. and 2 a.m. to record 30 seconds of audio. These participants were then emailed surveys four times a day asking them to{{29}} how outgoing, agreeable, or conscientious they were during a particular hour of the day. The study used data from 248 participants, all of whom answered questions about their behavior for two{{30}} weeks and wore the audio device for one of those weeks.

Six laboratory assistants rated each participant's audio clips to see how their observations compared with people's {{31}} of themselves. The six assistants were generally in agreement with one another about how the people they were observing acted. Further, participants' ratings of their own behaviors agreed with observers' for how outgoing and how conscientious they were being. But the agreement between participants and outside observers was much smaller for agreeableness. Some of this {{32}}could be because the observers used only audio clips, and thus could not read {{33}} like body language, but there are {{34}} other explanations, as people should be able to hear when a participant is being kind versus being rude. The weak agreement between how participants thought they were acting and what observers heard could be because people would rather {{35}} rude behavior.

probes

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) relatively 副词
**词性槽** 空在 are 与 accurate judges 之间，修饰形容词 accurate
**依据** 与 of only some of their behaviors 的"有限/不完全"语义共振句尾 only some of their behaviors 已经把人对自己行为的判断范围限定为"只有部分"，作者要表达的是"对自身行为只能算是相对准确的判断者"，relatively 这种程度副词正好与"only some"形成呼应——不是绝对准确、只是相对准确。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) probably 情态偏"可能性"，与后文"only some"的限定语义错位probably 表"很可能"，强调命题的真假概率；但原句要表达的不是"人可能是准确判断者"，而是"在准确程度上是相对的、有限的"。况且 probably 留给第 34 题更贴——那里 are __ other explanations 需要的正是"很可能还有其他解释"，这个词更值得留给后面。

questions.explanation:
**答案** I) probes 动词
**词性槽** 主语 this new study 后缺谓语
**依据** 研究"深入探究"问题是惯用搭配句意是"这项新研究深入探究人们对自己片刻行为的理解程度"，与前句 While most previous studies on how well people know themselves have been done on long- term personality traits 的对比正好——以前的研究做长期人格、这项新研究则"深入考察"短时行为。a study probes/explores how... 是学术语境的高频表达。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) articulatesarticulate 偏"清晰表达观点"，主语应是人或文章articulates 的典型主语是人/作者/政策文件，意为"清晰阐明（一种立场）"；用在"研究"上多见于"该研究阐明了某结论"，但本句宾语是 how-从句问号式的"研究问题"，与"探究/调查"的语义更贴，与 articulate 的"明确表达已有观点"语义错位。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 B) —— B articulates 三单形态完全合，靠语义才能区分。articulates 在 this new study ___ how... 的位置看似也通，但 articulate 指"清晰表达观点"，主语应是已经形成立场的人或文件；而本句宾语是 how-从句的研究问题，本质是"研究在调查/探究某问题"。一句话防坑：研究＋how 问题＝probe/explore，研究＋that 结论＝articulate/state。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) activated 动词
**词性槽** that 引导定语从句，空作从句谓语
**依据** 录音机"被启动/启动"是描述设备机制的标准表达录音机"每 9.5 分钟自动启动一次以录 30 秒音频"才符合实验设计。activated 在此为过去式作谓语，与全文研究描述的过去时态一致（如 asked、used、were 都是过去时），且automatically activated 是描述自动设备的常见搭配 audio recorders that automatically__(28)__ every 9.5 minutes between 7 a.m. and 2 a.m.。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
I) probes 时态为现在时、且语义不指设备启动probes 是第三人称单数现在时，与复数主语 recorders 不一致；语义上指"探究/调查"，多与人或问题搭配，不与"录音机每 9.5 分钟探究"搭配。
B) articulates 单复数不匹配 + 语义指"清晰表达" articulates 主语应是人（清晰表达），与"录音机"在主谓搭配上严重失配，单复数也与复数recorders 不一致。
K) recall 语义指人的"回忆"，与设备主语冲突recall 的主语通常是人，意为"回忆/想起"；机器"recall every 9.5 minutes"不成立，且 K 在 29题有更刚需的位置（让参与者"回忆"自己当时的行为）。
O) terminate 语义反向："终止"与"启动录音"完全相反若代入 terminate every 9.5 minutes，意为"每 9.5 分钟终止一次"，与后半句 to record 30 seconds of audio（启动后录 30 秒）形成逻辑矛盾。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) recall 动词
**词性槽** asking them to＋空，不定式中的动词原形
**依据** 回忆某时段自己有多外向/友善＝实验任务原句要求参与者评估"自己在某一小时里有多外向、友善或尽责" how outgoing, agreeable, or conscientious they were during a particular hour of the day，这是典型的"回忆性自评"任务，recall 表"回想起"与"a particular hour of the day（白天某一小时）"的过去时间状语精准匹配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) deny 语义反向："否认"自己有多外向不成立ask them to deny how outgoing they were 意为"让他们否认自己当时有多外向"，逻辑荒谬；且 F 在 35 题处有更贴切的位置（参与者"否认"粗鲁行为）。
O) terminate 搭配错误：终止"自己有多外向"不通terminate 通常与活动、合同、过程搭配，不能与 how-从句搭配描述自我评估。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) consecutive 形容词
**词性槽** 数词 two 与名词 weeks 之间的限定位置
**依据** two consecutive weeks＝"连续两周"是高频固定搭配原文说参与者要回答两周的行为问卷、其中一周还要戴录音设备，强调的是"连着进行的两周"。consecutive 与 weeks 是英语里"连续 N 周"的标准说法，语义与研究设计完全吻合answered questions about their behavior for two __(30)__ weeks。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
J) random 与"两周"严密的实验时段矛盾random weeks 意为"随机的（任选的）几周"，但研究是两周连续追踪、并明确其中一周戴录音设备 wore the audio device for one of those weeks，时间是确定段落而非随机选取，与random 的"任意性"冲突。
M) saturated 搭配不成立、语义不通saturated 多用于"饱和脂肪/被…浸透/市场饱和"，从未与"weeks"构成日常表达；语义上也无法解释一段"被饱和的两周"，搭配直接证伪。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 J) —— J random 词性、搭配都看似通。random 是形容词、可修饰 weeks、读起来也顺，但与原文研究设计"连续两周＋其中一周戴录音"的精密时段冲突。一句话防坑：先去原文找时间安排的描述（wore the audio device for one of those weeks），看时段是"连续"还是"随机"再下笔。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) assessment 名词
**词性槽** 形容词性物主代词 people's 后接名词
**依据** 与前文 observations 形成"他评 vs 自评"对比句子在比较"助理们的 observations"与"参与者对自己的 ___"，这正是研究的核心对照——他人观察 vs 自我评估。assessment 意为"评估/判断"，与 observations 在抽象层级上对等，构成"observations of A vs assessment of A"的标准学术对照 how their observations compared with people's __(31)__ of themselves。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) discrepancy discrepancy 是"差异"本身、不是"参与者对自己的判断" discrepancy of themselves 不成立——人不会"对自己有差异"。况且 G 在 32 题处恰好用来描述"自评与他评之间的分歧"，那里才是它的归宿。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) discrepancy 名词
**词性槽** 代词 this 后＋空 → 抽象名词作主语
**依据** 回指上文"自评与他评在 agreeableness 上分歧明显"上句说 But the agreement between participants and outside observers was much smaller for agreeableness. 这正是"分歧/不一致"。this ___ 概括的就是这种agreeableness 上的不一致，discrepancy 恰是"差异/出入"的标准名词，与 agreement 反义构成上下文呼应。

**答案** E) cues 名词
**词性槽** 动词 read 的宾语 + like body language 的同位列举
**依据** cues 与 body language 同属"非语言线索"语义集cues 指"线索/信号"，nonverbal cues / visual cues 与 body language 构成同位列举，语义自然贴合："观察者无法读取诸如肢体语言这类的线索" could not read __(33)__ like body language——正好解释为什么仅听音频会让宜人评分出现偏差。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
N) symptoms symptoms 是"病症"，与"肢体语言"不同类symptoms 多指疾病征候，无法与 body language 构成同位列举；read symptoms 在医学语境可成立，但与本文心理学行为观察主题不符。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) probably 副词
**词性槽** are 与 other explanations 之间的存在句结构
**依据** but 后引出"可能还有别的解释"的推测语气前句 could be because the observers used only audio clips, and thus could not read__(33)__ like body language 给出一种解释（可能因为只听音频），但作者用 but 引出另一种猜测：很可能还有别的解释。probably 恰好承担"作者的推测口吻"，与 could be 的不确定基调一致。

**答案** F) deny 动词
**词性槽** would rather＋空 → 动词原形
**依据** 人们"宁可否认"自己粗鲁——解释自评偏差上文说参与者对"宜人/友善"的自评与外部观察分歧大 the agreement between participants and outside observers was much smaller for agreeableness，作者在此给出心理学解释：人们宁愿"否认"自己当时表现得粗鲁，所以自评偏向"我没那么粗"。deny rude behavior 是"否认粗鲁行为"的标准搭配，正好解释了自我评估和观察之间的落差。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
O) terminate would rather terminate 与心理回避语义不符terminate rude behavior 字面是"终止粗鲁行为"，但上下文重点不是"停止粗鲁"——录音已结束、行为已发生——而是"自评时是否承认"。terminate 也不解释为何观察者听到了"粗鲁"而当事人自评却没有，逻辑不对路。

title: Many oppose workplace surveillance, because of the inherent…

sentences.text: Many oppose workplace surveillance, because of the inherent dehumanizing effect it has and the relentless pressure it brings.
But it's on the rise around the world as firms look to become more efficient by squeezing more productivity from their workers.
More than half of companies with over $750m in annual revenue used "non-traditional" monitoring techniques on staff last year.

passage.translation: 许多人反对工作场所监控，因为它具有内在的去人性化效应，并带来无情的压力。但随着企业寻求通过压榨员工更多生产力来提高效率，这种做法在全球范围内呈上升趋势。去年，年收入超过7.5亿美元的公司中，超过半数对员工使用了"非传统"监控技术。

sentences.text: Monitoring employee performance gives firms the ability to assess how their staff are performing and interacting, which can be good for both the firm and employees themselves.
A growing number of analytics companies offer this service.
They gather "data exhaust" left by employees' email and instant messaging apps, and use name badges equipped with radio-frequency identification devices and microphones.
These can check how much time you spend talking, your volume and tone of voice, even if you do not dominate conversations.
While this may sound intrusive, exponents argue that it can also protect employees against bullying and sexual harassment.

passage.translation: 监控员工绩效使企业能够评估员工的表现和互动方式，这对企业和员工本身都有好处。越来越多的分析公司提供这项服务。它们收集员工电子邮件和即时通讯应用留下的"数据尾气"，并使用配备射频识别设备和麦克风的名牌。这些设备可以检查你说话的时长、音量和语调，甚至检查你是否主导对话。虽然这听起来可能具有侵扰性，但支持者认为它也可以保护员工免受欺凌和性骚扰。

sentences.text: Some of this data analysis can produce unexpected results.

For example, it was found that people who sat at 12-person lunch tables tended to interact, share ideas more and outperform those who regularly sat at four-person tables, a fact that would probably have gone undetected without such data analysis.

passage.translation: 其中一些数据分析可以产生意想不到的结果。例如，研究发现，坐在12人午餐桌旁的人往往更多地互动、分享想法，并且表现优于那些经常坐在4人餐桌旁的人，而这一事实如果没有这样的数据分析可能不会被发现。

sentences.text: Over the last few years a Stockholm co-working space called Epicenter has gone much further and holds popular "chipping parties", where people can have microchips implanted in their hands.
They can use the implants to access electronically-controlled doors, or monitor how typing speed correlates with heart rate.
Implanted chips may seem extreme, but it is a relatively small step from ID cards and biometrics to such devices.

passage.translation: 在过去几年里，斯德哥尔摩一个名为Epicenter的联合办公空间走得更远，举办了受欢迎的"植入芯片派对",人们可以在手中植入微芯片。他们可以使用植入物访问电子控制门，或监测打字速度与心率的相关性。植入芯片可能看起来很极端,但从身份证和生物识别技术到这类设备只是相对较小的一步。

sentences.text: As long as such schemes are voluntary, there will probably be a growing number of convenience-oriented uses so that a substantial number of workers would opt to have a chip inserted.
But if implanted chips are used to reduce slack time or rest breaks, that could prove to be detrimental.
And if surveillance tools take away autonomy, that's when they prove most unpopular.
A lot depends on how such monitoring initiatives are communicated and this could prevent possible revolts being staged.

passage.translation: 只要这些计划是自愿的，可能会有越来越多以便利为导向的用途，以至于相当数量的员工会选择植入芯片。但如果植入芯片被用来减少空闲时间或休息时间，这可能会产生有害影响。如果监控工具剥夺了自主权，那就是它们最不受欢迎的时候。很大程度上取决于如何传达这类监控举措，这可能防止可能发生的反抗。

sentences.text: If bosses don't communicate effectively, employees assume the worst.
But if they're open about the information they're collecting and what they're doing with it, research suggests 46% of employees are generally okay with it.
Although many such monitoring schemes use anonymised data and participation is voluntary, many staffers remain sceptical and fear an erosion of their civil liberties.

passage.translation: 如果老板们不进行有效沟通，员工就会往最坏的方面想。但如果他们对所收集的信息以及如何使用这些信息持开放态度，研究表明46%的员工通常对此表示接受。尽管许多此类监控计划使用匿名数据且参与是自愿的，但许多员工仍持怀疑态度，担心其公民自由受到侵蚀。

sentences.text: So workplace surveillance could be empowering for staff and useful for companies looking to become more efficient and profitable.
But implemented in the wrong way, it could also become an unpopular tool of oppression that proves counterproductive.

passage.translation: 因此，工作场所监控可以增强员工能力，对寻求提高效率和盈利能力的公司也很有用。但如果实施方式不当，它也可能成为一种不受欢迎的压迫工具，结果适得其反。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: Why are many people opposed to monitoring employee performance?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
为什么许多人反对监控员工绩效?
A) 它使员工处于持续的压力之下。
B) 它被普遍认为本质上是反人性的。
C) 它对被监控的员工造成精神和身体上的伤害。
D) 它使企业能够从员工身上榨取最大的生产力。
**判型** 题干Why are many people opposed to monitoring employee performance?直接索取一个被作者写在文中的客观原因,而非作者本人的推断或态度。
**拆句** 题干主干为被动语态are...opposed to,opposed to后接动名词短语monitoring employee performance作介词宾语;句首Why仅起询问原因作用,无陷阱结构。
**定位** 许多人反对工作场所监控,因为它本身具有非人化的效果,并且带来持续不断的压力。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确the relentless pressure it brings↔ puts workers under constant pressure预判中"持续压力"一条被A项constant pressure逐词同义对应,A为定位句两项理由之一的精确改写,在四个选项中是唯一与原文有同义映射的项。
B) 过度推断原文说监控具有inherent dehumanizing effect,只是描述其内在属性,并未声称这一点被普遍认同;B项把它升级为universally deemed anti-human,把"内在属性"偷换为"举世公认"。
C) 无中生有原文只提及dehumanizing effect与relentless pressure,均偏心理与人格层面;C项添加physical harm,原文无任何关于身体伤害的表述。
D) 答非所问squeeze maximal productivity复述的是企业立场——原文firms look to become more efficient by squeezing more productivity from their workers是企业实施监控的动机,而非员工反对的理由,角色彻底错位。
questions.quote: Many oppose workplace surveillance, because of the inherent dehumanizing effect it has and the relentless pressure it brings.

options.text: It puts workers under constant pressure.
It is universally deemed anti-human by nature.
It does both mental and physical harm to employees monitored.
It enables firms to squeeze maximal productivity from employees.

questions.prompt: What is the supporters' argument for workplace surveillance?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
支持者对工作场所监控的论据是什么?
A) 它使员工能够避免主导谈话。
B) 它增强员工对其所在企业的认同感。
C) 它可以提醒员工注意对其隐私的侵犯。
D) 它可以保护员工免受攻击性行为的伤害。
**判型** 题干What is the supporters' argument直接索取支持方在文中明说的一项主张,不要求读者推断弦外之音。
**拆句** 题干为What引导的特殊疑问句,系动词is后接名词短语the supporters' argument for workplace surveillance,for短语作定语限定argument的对象,结构平直无陷阱。
**定位** 尽管这听起来具有侵扰性,支持者主张监控也可以保护员工免受欺凌和性骚扰。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文These can check how much time you spend talking, your volume and tone of voice, even if you do not dominate conversations.是描述"监控能检测谈话占比"的功能,而非支持方提出的argument;A项enables employees to refrain from dominating conversations把"检测是否dominate"扭曲为"使员工避免dominate"。
B) 无中生有B项enhances employees' identification with firms谈的是员工对公司的认同感,原文整段无任何提及"员工认同公司"的语义。
C) 与原文相反原文While this may sound intrusive承认监控"听起来侵犯隐私",但支持者的argument是against bullying而非against intrusion;C项alert employees to intrusion into their privacy反而把"监控可警示员工隐私被侵犯"作为主张,与支持方立场相反。
D) ✓ 正确protect employees against bullying and sexual harassment ↔protect employees against aggressive behavior预判中的"保护员工免受bullying与sexual harassment"被D项以aggressive behavior一词概括,protect...against结构原样保留,是定位句的标准同义替换。
questions.quote: While this may sound intrusive, exponents argue that it can also protect employees against bullying and sexual harassment.

options.text: It enables employees to refrain from dominating conversations.
It enhances employees' identification with firms they work in.
It can alert employees to intrusion into their privacy.
It can protect employees against aggressive behavior.

questions.prompt: What does the author want to show by the example of different numbers of people interacting at lunch tables?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （例证目的题）
**题目译文**
作者想通过午餐桌上不同人数互动的例子说明什么?
A) 数据分析是成功实施工作场所监控的关键。
B) 分析从员工那里收集的数据可以产生意想不到的结果。
C) 更多同事坐在一张午餐桌旁往往有助于互动和想法分享。
D) 没有数据分析,很难决定一张午餐桌应该坐多少人。
**判型** What does the author want to show by the example...中by the example明示题干在追问例子的论证目的而非例子的字面内容。
**拆句** 题干主干What...want to show中by the example为方式状语,后接of介词短语different numbers of people interacting at lunch tables修饰example;considering动名词成分较长,但句意线性无歧义。
**定位** 这种数据分析有时会产生出人意料的结果。例如,研究发现坐12人餐桌的人比坐4人餐桌的人更倾向于互动、分享想法,表现也更好,而这一事实如果没有这种数据分析很可能会被忽略。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断原文从未声称数据分析是监控成功实施的key;论点只是说"数据分析能产生意外结果",而非"数据分析是监控成功的关键";key一词无原文支撑。
B) ✓ 正确Some of this data analysis can produce unexpected results. ↔Analyzing data gathered from workers can yield something unexpected. B项主谓宾三段(Analyzing data/can yield/something unexpected)与原文(this data analysis/can produce/unexpected results)逐成分对应,是论点句的标准同义重写。
C) 答非所问C项More workmates sitting at a lunch table tend to facilitate interaction and idea sharing字面复述了例子内容,但题干问的是例子要说明的论点,不是例子本身,答非所问。
D) 偷换概念原文末尾a fact that would probably have gone undetected without such data analysis强调的是"数据分析揭示了这一事实",而非"数据分析帮助决定餐桌人数";D项把焦点偏到"决定餐桌坐几人"上。
questions.quote: Some of this data analysis can produce unexpected results. For example, it was found that people who sat at 12-person lunch tables tended to interact, share ideas more and outperform those who regularly sat at four-person tables, a fact that would probably have gone undetected without such data analysis.

options.text: Data analysis is key to the successful implementation of workplace surveillance.
Analyzing data gathered from workers can yield something unexpected.
More workmates sitting at a lunch table tend to facilitate interaction and idea sharing.
It is hard to decide on how many people to sit at a lunch table without data analysis.

questions.prompt: What does much of the positive effect of monitoring initiatives depend on?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
监控措施的大部分积极效果取决于什么?
A) 员工被监控的频率。
B) 哪些具体的个人信息被排除在外。
C) 采取了哪些措施来最大限度地减少其有害影响。
D) 老板们如何充分说明其监控目的。
**判型** What does much of the positive effect of monitoring initiatives depend on?问的是文中明确写出的依赖条件,不需推断。
**拆句** 题干主干What does...depend on?中谓语动词是depend on,主语是较长的名词短语much of the positive effect of monitoring initiatives;of短语层层修饰,但语义线性,认出动词短语depend on即可。
**定位** 很多事情取决于这些监控举措是如何被传达的,这种沟通可能阻止潜在的抵制行动发生。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有原文从未提到监控的frequency(频率),只谈how communicated;A项把"如何沟通"偷换为"多频繁地监控",原文无任何对应。
B) 偷换概念原文many such monitoring schemes use anonymised data谈匿名化处理,但语境是"虽然匿名,员工仍恐惧";B项specific personal information is being excluded把焦点偏到"排除哪些信息",且与题干"positive effect depend on"无对应。
C) 过度推断原文确实提到detrimental一词,但句子是"如果用监控减少休息,可能detrimental";题干问的是"positive effect depend on",答案应回到A lot depends on的主句而非detrimental前的条件句;C项把"减少不利影响的步骤"作为positive effect的依赖,属过度推断。
D) ✓ 正确how such monitoring initiatives are communicated ↔How well bosses make known their purpose of monitoring D项核心动词make known精确对应原文communicated,主语bosses合理补出施动者,purpose of monitoring为补全语境的合理增添,语义聚焦于"沟通"这一关键变量。
questions.quote: A lot depends on how such monitoring initiatives are communicated and this could prevent possible revolts being staged.

options.text: How frequently employees are to be monitored.
What specific personal information is being excluded.
What steps are taken to minimize their detrimental impact.
How well bosses make known their purpose of monitoring.

questions.prompt: What concern do monitoring initiatives cause among many staffers?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
监控措施在许多员工中引起了什么担忧?
A) 它们可能过度赋权雇主。
B) 它们可能侵蚀工作场所环境。
C) 它们可能侵犯员工应有的自由。
D) 从长远来看,它们可能会产生适得其反的效果。
**判型** What concern do monitoring initiatives cause among many staffers?问的是员工在原文中明确表达的某项顾虑,不是作者推断。
**拆句** 题干主干What concern do monitoring initiatives cause中concern作cause的宾语前置,among many staffers为范围状语;倒装并未改变句意,主语是monitoring initiatives。
**定位** 尽管许多此类监控方案使用匿名数据且参与是自愿的,许多员工仍持怀疑态度,担心他们的公民自由被侵蚀。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反原文workplace surveillance could be empowering for staff中的empower指的是"赋权员工",而非"赋权雇主";A项empower employers excessively反转了方向,且excessively无原文支撑。
B) 偷换概念原文用an erosion of their civil liberties,erosion的对象是公民自由,而非workplace environment;B项保留了erosion的同根词erode,但把宾语偷换为"工作环境",熟词陷阱。
C) ✓ 正确an erosion of their civil liberties↔infringe upon staffers' entitled freedom预判的"公民自由被侵蚀"被C项以infringe upon...entitled freedom精确改写,主谓宾结构对应,语义内核完整保留。
D) 张冠李戴an unpopular tool of oppression that proves counterproductive是作者在末段的两面性总评,主体是作者而非many staffers;D项把作者的总评搬来作员工的顾虑,主体错位。
questions.quote: Although many such monitoring schemes use anonymised data and participation is voluntary, many staffers remain sceptical and fear an erosion of their civil liberties.

options.text: They may empower employers excessively.
They may erode the workplace environment.
They may infringe upon staffers' entitled freedom.
They may become counterproductive in the long run.

title: How on earth did we come to this?…

sentences.text: How on earth did we come to this?
We protect our children obsessively from every harm; we scrutinize every carer, teacher or doctor with whom they come into contact.
Yet despite all this, one group, which in no way has their best interests at heart, has almost unconstrained access.

passage.translation: 我们究竟是怎么走到这一步的?我们过度保护孩子免受一切伤害;我们仔细审查每一位与他们接触的看护者、教师或医生。然而尽管如此,有一个群体几乎可以不受约束地接触孩子,而这个群体绝不是为了孩子的最大利益着想。

sentences.text: We seem to take it for granted that advertisers and marketers are allowed to condition even the youngest children.

Before children have even developed a proper sense of their own identity, or learned to handle money, they're encouraged to associate status and self-worth with stuff, and to look to external things such as fame and wealth for validation.
We're turning out little consumers rather than young citizens who will value themselves for what they contribute to the society in which they live.

passage.translation: 我们似乎理所当然地认为广告商和营销人员可以影响甚至最年幼的儿童。在孩子们还没有形成对自己身份的正确认识,或学会如何处理金钱之前,他们就被鼓励将地位和自我价值与物品联系起来,并从名望和财富等外在事物中寻求认可。我们正在培养小消费者,而不是培养会因自己对所生活的社会做出贡献而重视自己的年轻公民。

sentences.text: We've reached this point so gradually that many of us have never questioned it.
It's crept up on us in the 60 years since advertisers started to target the young and found that they could recruit them to a commercial assault on their parents.
We've come to know it as "pester power" or the ability of children to pressure parents to make certain purchases.

passage.translation: 我们如此渐进地走到这一步,以至于我们中的许多人从未质疑过它。自从60年前广告商开始瞄准年轻人,并发现他们可以招募年轻人对其父母发动商业攻势以来,这种现象就悄悄向我们袭来。我们已经将其称为"纠缠力量",即儿童迫使父母进行特定购买的能力。

sentences.text: Many psychologists, child development experts and educators point to research suggesting that this emerging cradle-to-grave consumerism is contributing to growing rates of low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness.

passage.translation: 许多心理学家、儿童发展专家和教育工作者指出,研究表明这种新兴的从摇篮到坟墓的消费主义正在导致自卑、抑郁和其他形式的心理疾病发病率上升。

sentences.text: Not all psychologists agree.
There're plenty working hand in glove with a ￡12bn-a-year industry that has turned the manipulation of adult emotions and desires into an art form—often literally.
It's also one that's forever developing new ways to persuade our children to desire material possessions, and because of advertisements' viral effect they only need to infect a few to reach the many.
Advertising and marketing can serve a useful purpose for children.
Marketing may help socialize children as consumers, inform them about products, and help them carve out unique identities as they reach adulthood.

passage.translation: 并非所有心理学家都同意这一观点。有许多心理学家与这个年产值120亿英镑的产业密切合作,该产业已经将操纵成年人的情感和欲望变成了一种艺术形式——往往是字面意义上的艺术形式。这也是一个永远在开发新方法来说服我们的孩子渴望物质财产的产业,而且由于广告的病毒式传播效应,他们只需要感染少数人就能影响多数人。广告和营销可以为儿童服务于有益的目的。营销可能有助于将儿童社会化为消费者,向他们介绍产品信息,并帮助他们在成年时塑造独特的身份。

sentences.text: Then, should we ban all advertising aimed at young children?
I say yes.

passage.translation: 那么,我们应该禁止所有针对幼儿的广告吗?我的答案是肯定的。

sentences.text: Of course there'll be plenty of objections to an outright ban on advertising to the under-11s.
There'll be those who argue that would be a breach of freedom of speech and infringe the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products.

passage.translation: 当然,对于全面禁止针对11岁以下儿童的广告,会有很多反对意见。会有人认为这将侵犯言论自由,侵犯企业对幼儿进行洗脑使其要求购买其产品的权利。

sentences.text: Most parents hate what advertising does to their children, but we do have the power to end it and let our children grow up free from many of the pressures of consumerism until they're old enough to make their own decisions.
And though advertising is only part of an all-pervasive(无处不在的) marketing culture we need to make a start somewhere.
Let's ban all advertising targeting children of primary school age and younger now.

passage.translation: 大多数父母讨厌广告对孩子的影响,但我们确实有能力终止它,让我们的孩子在成长过程中免受消费主义的许多压力,直到他们足够大能够自己做决定。尽管广告只是无处不在的营销文化的一部分,但我们需要从某个地方开始。现在就让我们禁止所有针对小学学龄及更小儿童的广告吧。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: Which group of people does the author say has almost unrestricted access to children?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者说哪一群体几乎可以不受限制地接触儿童?
A) 广告商。
B) 看护者。
C) 教师。
D) 医生。
**判型** Which group of people does the author say has almost unrestricted access to children? 直接询问「哪一群人」，要求在原文里找出对应群体，是典型的事实细节追问。
**拆句** 主干为 Which group of people ... has almost unrestricted access to children，does the author say 是插入语，去掉后剩「哪一群人对孩子有几乎不受限制的接触权」，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 然而尽管如此，有一个群体，他们丝毫不把孩子的最大利益放在心上，却几乎不受限制地接触着孩子。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确advertisers and marketers are allowed to condition even the youngest children ↔ Advertisers预判的「对孩子不友好却不受限制的群体」在 P2 被明示为广告商和营销者，与选项Advertisers 直接对应。
B) 与原文相反Carers 属于 every carer, teacher or doctor with whom they come into contact中被严格审查的一方，是「保护孩子」的角色，与「几乎不受限地接触孩子」的群体相反。
C) 与原文相反Teachers 同样位于 every carer, teacher or doctor 列表中，是被审查的对象，不是「几乎不受限地接触孩子」的群体。
D) 与原文相反Doctors 也是 every carer, teacher or doctor 列表中的被审查对象，原文未把医生列为「几乎不受限接触孩子」的群体。
questions.quote: Yet despite all this, one group, which in no way has their best interests at heart, has almost unconstrained access.

options.text: Advertisers.
Carers.
Teachers.
Doctors.

questions.prompt: What kind of people should we enable children to become according to the author?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
根据作者的观点,我们应该让儿童成为什么样的人?
A) 那些寻求名利以获得外在和终极认可的人。
B) 那些因为对社会的贡献而重视自己的人。
C) 那些将自我价值与处理金钱的能力联系起来的人。
D) 那些已经形成了对自身身份认同的恰当意识的人。
**判型** What kind of people should we enable children to become according to the author?含 according to the author，要求复述原文已写明的内容，不要求跨段综合，仍是细节题。
**拆句** 主干为 What kind of people should we enable children to become，become 后省略表语补足语，由四个选项的 Those who... 补齐；结构清楚，唯一要注意的是 enable children to become＝「让孩子成长为」，主语是 we 不是 children。
**定位** 我们正在培养小消费者，而不是会因自己对所在社会的贡献而看重自身价值的年轻公民。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反Those who look to fame and wealth for external and ultimate validation 对应 to look to external things such as fame and wealth for validation，是作者批判而非倡导的形象。
B) ✓ 正确young citizens who will value themselves for what they contribute to the society in which they live↔ Those who value themselves because of their contribution to society选项 B 在主语「Those who」、动词「value themselves」、原因状语三处与定位句逐项对应，是作者正向倡导项的同义改写。
C) 偷换概念Those who associate self-worth with the ability to handle money 把 learned to handle money 这个被作者列出的「尚未具备」的前提，偷换成孩子应该成为的目标。
D) 偷换概念Those who have developed a proper sense of their own identity 同样取自 Before children have even developed a proper sense of their own identity，仅是作者列出的孩子尚未具备的前提，并非最终倡导项。
questions.quote: We're turning out little consumers rather than young citizens who will value themselves for what they contribute to the society in which they live.

options.text: Those who look to fame and wealth for external and ultimate validation.
Those who value themselves because of their contribution to society.
Those who associate self-worth with the ability to handle money.
Those who have developed a proper sense of their own identity.

questions.prompt: Many child development experts and educators call attention to research that suggests _____.
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
许多儿童发展专家和教育工作者呼吁关注研究,这些研究表明_____。
A) 终身消费主义正在导致越来越多的心理问题病例。
B) 教育日益商业化正在侵蚀许多儿童的自尊。
C) 对财富日益增长的渴望正在导致抑郁症发病率上升。
D) 对购买物质产品的渴望在人的一生中被培养起来。
**判型** Many child development experts and educators call attention to research that suggests _____. 是不完整陈述句，要求选项填入研究的内容，等同于追问该研究的结论事实，归为细节题。
**拆句** 主句 Many child development experts and educators call attention to research，that suggests 后续宾语从句由选项补齐；call attention to＝呼吁关注，是熟词僻义提醒，主语动作就是「指出研究表明……」。
**定位** 许多心理学家、儿童发展专家和教育者援引研究指出：这种正在出现的「从摇篮到坟墓」的消费主义，正在导致低自尊、抑郁和其他形式心理疾病的发生率不断上升。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确this emerging cradle-to-grave consumerism ↔ life-long consumerism growing rates of low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness ↔more and more cases of psychological problems is contributing to ↔ is causing选项 A 的主语「终生消费主义」、谓语「正在导致」、宾语「越来越多心理问题」与定位句三项要点逐一同义对应，是最精确的复述。
B) 无中生有increasing commercialization of education 在原文中完全没有提及，作者批评的是面向孩子的广告与营销，不是教育自身的商业化。
C) 以偏概全the growing desire for wealth 只是原文 fame and wealth 的一半；a rising rate of depression 也只是 low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness的一项。两处都只取了原文的局部。
D) 答非所问the craving for purchasing material things is nurtured throughout one's life 说的是「物欲是如何被培养起来的」，而题干要求复述「研究表明的因果结论」——D 项把因果关系换成了「物欲是如何形成」，与题干追问方向不一致。
questions.quote: Many psychologists, child development experts and educators point to research suggesting that this emerging cradle-to-grave consumerism is contributing to growing rates of low self- esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness.

options.text: life-long consumerism is causing more and more cases of psychological problems.
increasing commercialization of education is eroding many children's self-esteem.
the growing desire for wealth is contributing to a rising rate of depression.
the craving for purchasing material things is nurtured throughout one's life.

questions.prompt: What does the author imply about the impact of advertising?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （推断题）
**题目译文**
关于广告的影响,作者暗示了什么?
A) 它实际上会传染给许多人而不是少数人。
B) 它植根于我们对物质财产的欲望。
C) 它可与病毒的影响相比。
D) 它实际上仅限于儿童。
**判型** What does the author imply about the impact of advertising? 中的 imply 表明本题要求基于原文作推断，而非复述事实。
**拆句** What does the author imply about the impact of advertising? 主干是 What ... the author imply，about the impact of advertising 限定推断对象；句子简洁，需注意imply 是「暗示」而非「明示」。
**定位** 它（广告业）也是这样一个行业：不断开发新方法来诱使我们的孩子渴望物质；而由于广告的病毒式效应，他们只需感染少数即可触及多数。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确they only need to infect a few to reach the many ↔It is actually infectious to many rather than a few they only need to infect a few to reach the many ↔ rather than a few由 infect a few to reach the many 一步推出「广告其实波及多数而非少数」，正好是imply 题所要的「一步推断」型答案。
B) 与原文相反rooted in our desire for material possessions 把因果反过来——原文是「广告诱使孩子产生物欲」（persuade our children to desire material possessions），不是「广告源于物欲」。
C) 过度推断comparable to that of virus 已经超出原文 viral effect 的比喻：原文只说「影响具有病毒式扩散效应」，并没断言「广告影响可与病毒影响相提并论」。两者程度差异明显。
D) 与原文相反literally limited to children 把广告影响范围缩限到「仅限于儿童」，而原文 infect a few to reach the many 恰恰强调影响会扩散到「多数」，并非「仅限于儿童」。
questions.quote: It's also one that's forever developing new ways to persuade our children to desire material possessions, and because of advertisements' viral effect they only need to infect a few to reach the many.

options.text: It is actually infectious to many rather than a few.
It is rooted in our desire for material possessions.
It is comparable to that of virus.
It is literally limited to children.

questions.prompt: What is the opponents' argument against a complete ban on advertising to young children?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
反对者针对完全禁止向幼儿做广告提出了什么论点?
A) 这会剥夺他们了解产品的机会。
B) 这会使他们无法塑造独特的身份认同。
C) 这会侵犯他们作为潜在消费者的自由。
D) 这会侵犯赋予广告商的权利。
**判型** What is the opponents' argument against a complete ban on advertising to young children? 直接问反对者给出的具体论据，对应原文中已写明的让步句，属细节题。
**拆句** 主干 What is the opponents' argument，against a complete ban on advertising to young children 是后置修饰，整体含义是「反对者反对彻底禁广告时给出的理由」；注意against 修饰的是 argument，而非整个句子的否定。
**定位** 会有人辩称（禁止广告）将构成对言论自由的侵犯，并损害企业「向幼儿洗脑、让他们索要产品」的权利。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴deprive them of the chance to learn about products 取自 Marketing may help socialize children as consumers, inform them about products，是作者描述广告「益处」的内容，并非 P7 中的反方论据。
B) 张冠李戴render them unable to carve out unique identities 同样取自 help them carve out unique identities as they reach adulthood，是广告作为「益处」的功能描述，非 P7中反方对禁令的反对理由。
C) 偷换概念breach their freedom as would-be consumers 中 their 指 young children；但 a breach of freedom of speech 中被侵犯的是「言论自由」，主语暗指「企业表达自由」，不是「孩子作为准消费者的自由」。
D) ✓ 正确infringe the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products↔violate the rights endowed upon advertisers the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products↔the rights endowed upon advertisers反方第二条论据「损害企业的权利」被选项 D 完整同义改写为「侵犯广告商被赋予的权利」，且两条论据中只有该条被选项明确复述。
questions.quote: There'll be those who argue that would be a breach of freedom of speech and infringe the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products.

options.text: It would deprive them of the chance to learn about products.
It would render them unable to carve out unique identities.
It would breach their freedom as would-be consumers.
It would violate the rights endowed upon advertisers.

title: Imagine sitting down to a big dinner: a…

sentences.text: Imagine sitting down to a big dinner: a massive steak, a large portion of fried potatoes, and cake for dessert.
After eating so much, you should be too full to eat another bite.

But some people experience a powerful urge to keep eating, even after (26)____ in a huge meal, a behavior that makes little sense, as most adults are well-versed in the dangers of obesity, which researchers have shown correlates with(27)____ health issues and is even linked to increased (28)____ risk.
But some people still keep eating long after they should stop, a phenomenon Dr.
Susan Thompson calls "insatiable(永不满足的) hunger."
It is characterized by two main (29)____ : not being satisfied by eating, and having a desire to stay sedentary(久坐不动的).

passage.translation: 想象一下坐下来享用一顿丰盛的晚餐：一块巨大的牛排、一大份炸土豆，还有蛋糕作为甜点。吃了这么多之后，你应该饱得吃不下任何东西了。但有些人会体验到一种强烈的冲动，想要继续吃，即使在大吃一顿之后也是如此，这种行为毫无道理，因为大多数成年人都非常清楚肥胖的危险，研究人员已经表明肥胖与无数健康问题相关，甚至与死亡风险增加有关。但有些人仍然在应该停止进食很久之后继续吃，Susan Thompson博士将这种现象称为"永不满足的饥饿"。它有两个主要特征：吃东西无法获得满足感，以及有久坐不动的欲望。

sentences.text: This is at (30)____ with how humans are biologically programmed.
When there was a great deal of food available, ancient people would gorge on calories; this massive calorie intake was accompanied by an urge to get active.
Humans were also programmed for something called "compensation," which is the brain's (31)____ mechanism for preventing the accumulation of excess weight.
With compensation, if you eat one large meal in the morning, you are naturally (32)____ to eat less for the rest of the day.

passage.translation: 这与人类的生物学编程相矛盾。当有大量食物可供获取时，古代人会大量摄入卡路里；这种大量的卡路里摄入会伴随着想要活动的冲动。人类还被编程了一种叫做"补偿"的机制，这是大脑防止积累过多体重的调节机制。有了补偿机制，如果你早上吃了一顿大餐，你自然会倾向于在这一天剩余的时间里少吃一些。

sentences.text: But recent studies show that 70% of American adults have lost the ability to naturally compensate for the calories they consume; worse (33)____ , a significant number of them report (34)____ hunger halfway through an eating session, but, by the end of the meal, they feel the same or higher levels of hunger than when they sat down.
Dr.
Thompson argues that the main cause of this phenomenon is the modern diet, which is (35)____ of food high in sugar, carbohydrates and calories.

passage.translation: 但最近的研究表明，70%的美国成年人已经失去了自然补偿所摄入卡路里的能力；更糟糕的是，他们中的很大一部分人报告说在进食过程中饥饿感会减弱一半，但到用餐结束时，他们感到的饥饿程度与坐下来时相同甚至更高。Thompson博士认为，这种现象的主要原因是现代饮食，其由高糖、高碳水化合物和高卡路里的食物组成。

groups.content:
Imagine sitting down to a big dinner: a massive steak, a large portion of fried potatoes, and cake for dessert. After eating so much, you should be too full to eat another bite. But some people experience a powerful urge to keep eating, even after {{26}} in a huge meal, a behavior that makes little sense, as most adults are well-versed in the dangers of obesity, which researchers have shown correlates with{{27}} health issues and is even linked to increased {{28}} risk. But some people still keep eating long after they should stop, a phenomenon Dr. Susan Thompson calls "insatiable(永不满足的) hunger." It is characterized by two main {{29}} : not being satisfied by eating, and having a desire to stay sedentary(久坐不动的).

This is at {{30}} with how humans are biologically programmed. When there was a great deal of food available, ancient people would gorge on calories; this massive calorie intake was accompanied by an urge to get active. Humans were also programmed for something called "compensation," which is the brain's {{31}} mechanism for preventing the accumulation of excess weight. With compensation, if you eat one large meal in the morning, you are naturally {{32}} to eat less for the rest of the day.

But recent studies show that 70% of American adults have lost the ability to naturally compensate for the calories they consume; worse {{33}} , a significant number of them report {{34}} hunger halfway through an eating session, but, by the end of the meal, they feel the same or higher levels of hunger than when they sat down. Dr. Thompson argues that the main cause of this phenomenon is the modern diet, which is {{35}} of food high in sugar, carbohydrates and calories.
