title: Selective colleges and universities in the U.S. are…

sentences.text: Selective colleges and universities in the U.S. are under fire for being too elite and too expensive, and for not training graduates for the world of work.

Such charges ignore the fact that these institutions continue to prepare students for success in their work, for thoughtful engagement in civic life, for lifelong learning, and for understanding the world and those with whom they live.

passage.translation: 美国的选拔性学院和大学正因过于精英化、学费过于昂贵以及未能为毕业生的职场做好培训而饱受批评。这些指责忽视了一个事实,即这些院校持续在为学生的职业成功、公民生活的深思参与、终身学习以及理解世界和与他们共同生活的人做准备。

sentences.text: These colleges and universities must be doing something right.
Applications are at record highs, and their financial aid programs make them more accessible than ever.
This model of education has long played a central role in creating opportunity, driving economic growth, and spurring innovation.

passage.translation: 这些学院和大学一定是在做正确的事情。申请人数创历史新高,它们的助学金项目使其比以往任何时候都更容易进入。这种教育模式长期以来在创造机会、推动经济增长和激发创新方面发挥着核心作用。

sentences.text: Yet, there is growing skepticism about the value of this model.
The recent tax reform bill is a wake-up call that our strongest colleges and universities are under assault by some in government.
The initial proposals would have made education unaffordable for many by taxing tuition waivers for graduate students and ending deductions for student loan interest.
Thankfully, these provisions were ultimately stripped from the bill, but lawmakers let stand a new tax on the investment income of some colleges and universities.

passage.translation: 然而,人们对这种模式的价值日益持怀疑态度。最近的税收改革法案是一记警钟,表明我们最强大的学院和大学正受到一些政府人士的攻击。最初的提案本会通过对研究生的学费减免征税和取消学生贷款利息扣除,使许多人无法负担教育费用。值得庆幸的是,这些条款最终从法案中被剔除,但立法者保留了对一些学院和大学投资收入征收的新税。

sentences.text: While these attacks are motivated by misguided ideas, we need to do a better job of explaining why these claims are false and why what we do is valuable.
We cannot take for granted that any of this is obvious.

passage.translation: 虽然这些攻击是出于错误的观念,但我们需要更好地解释为什么这些说法是错误的,以及我们所做的为什么有价值。我们不能想当然地认为这一切都是显而易见的。

sentences.text: It is often said that elite colleges and universities do not train students, particularly those who study the liberal arts, for the workforce.
But this can be refuted by scholarly research.
The data are clear: a liberal arts education is great career preparation, both for excellent lifetime earnings and for satisfaction with the work.

This education develops the skills of critical thinking, rigorous analysis of data and facts, communication with the written and spoken word, understanding of cultural differences and issues, and the ability to keep learning.
In fact, liberal arts graduates do extremely well in every imaginable field.

passage.translation: 人们常说,精英学院和大学没有为学生,特别是那些学习文科的学生,进行职场培训。但这可以被学术研究所反驳。数据是清楚的:文科教育是极好的职业准备,无论是对于出色的终身收入还是对工作的满意度。这种教育培养批判性思维的技能、对数据和事实的严格分析、书面和口头语言的沟通、对文化差异和问题的理解以及持续学习的能力。事实上,文科毕业生在每个可以想象的领域都表现极其出色。

sentences.text: Access to an education at selective colleges and universities is now more available than ever to low- and middle-income families.

We have built endowments from donations by alumni(校友) and parents who understand and appreciate our mission to provide access and opportunity, and a significant portion of the returns from these endowments is used to fund financial aid.

passage.translation: 在选拔性学院和大学接受教育的机会现在比以往任何时候都更容易为中低收入家庭所获得。我们已经通过理解并赞赏我们提供入学机会和机遇使命的校友和家长的捐赠建立了捐赠基金,这些捐赠基金回报的很大一部分用于资助经济援助。

sentences.text: Ironically, the new tax on endowments drains financial aid funds from the very schools most able to offer opportunity to those who have earned a spot but cannot otherwise afford this education.
Beyond the virtue of access to those who have earned a place at these schools, the diversity of economic backgrounds enhances the education and experience of all of our students.

passage.translation: 具有讽刺意味的是,对捐赠基金征收的新税从那些最有能力为那些赢得了入学资格但无法负担这种教育费用的人提供机会的学校抽走了助学金。除了为那些在这些学校赢得一席之地的人提供入学机会的优点之外,经济背景的多样性增强了我们所有学生的教育和体验。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What fact does the author emphasize concerning selective colleges and universities?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于选择性学院和大学,作者强调了什么事实?
A) 它们一直忽视对毕业生进入职场的培训。
B) 它们一直在确保学生拥有成功未来方面做得很好。
C) 它们一直因过于精英化和过于昂贵而不断受到抨击。
D) 它们一直积极参与校园之外的公民生活。
**判型** What fact does the author emphasize 明确询问作者强调的事实，对应原文某一处具体表述，不要求跨段推断。
**拆句** 主干是 What fact does the author emphasize，concerning selective colleges and universities 是介词短语后置修饰 fact，相当于 about。无否定、无比较，平铺直叙。
**定位** 这些指控忽视了一个事实：这些院校仍在持续地为学生做准备——为他们的事业成功、公民生活的深入参与、终身学习，以及理解世界与共处之人做准备。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反They have been ignoring the training of graduates for the world of work 把“忽视”这一动作扣到了院校头上，正好与原文相反——原文是说指控者忽视了事实，并不是院校忽视培养。
B) ✓ 正确these institutions continue to prepare students for success in their work ↔doing well in ensuring their students a successful future Such charges ignore the fact that ↔ They have been doing well预判说“院校仍在为学生未来成功做准备”，B 项 doing well in ensuring their students a successful future 正是这一表述的同义替换，故选 B。
C) 答非所问They have been constantly attacked for being too elite and too expensive 复述的是 Selective colleges and universities in the U.S. are under fire for being too elite and too expensive 这一事实——但这是别人对院校的指控，不是作者要强调的 fact；题干问 What fact does the author emphasize。
D) 偷换概念They have been actively engaged in civic life beyond the school campus 把原文中“院校培养学生参与公民生活”的对象（学生）偷换成了院校本身参与公民生活，主体被替换。
questions.quote: Such charges ignore the fact that these institutions continue to prepare students for success in their work, for thoughtful engagement in civic life, for lifelong learning, and for understanding the world and those with whom they live.

options.text: They have been ignoring the training of graduates for the world of work.
They have been doing well in ensuring their students a successful future.
They have been constantly attacked for being too elite and too expensive.
They have been actively engaged in civic life beyond the school campus.

questions.prompt: What does the author say in arguing for the model of education in the U.S.?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者在论证美国教育模式时说了什么?
A) 它对国家的整体发展做出了重大贡献。
B) 它成功维持了可持续的财政资助项目。
C) 它优先考虑研究生学习的创新项目。
D) 它在吸引国际申请者方面发挥了核心作用。
**判型** What does the author say 询问作者具体表态了什么，对应一句具体陈述，仍属细节题。
**拆句** 主干 What does the author say，in arguing for the model of education in the U.S. 是介词短语作状语，交代 say 发生的语境。结构简单。
**定位** 这一教育模式长期以来在创造机会、推动经济增长与激发创新方面扮演着核心角色。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确creating opportunity, driving economic growth, and spurring innovation ↔contributed substantially to the nation's overall development has long played a central role ↔ contributed substantially三项并列贡献可统一抽象为 the nation's overall development，A 项正是这一上位概括，故选 A。
B) 偷换概念succeeded in maintaining sustainable financial aid programs 把“该模式的整体贡献”偷换成了“维持可持续的资助项目”——原文 their financial aid programs make them more accessible than ever 只是说援助项目使学校更可及，没说“可持续维持”，更不是作者为之辩护的核心论据。
C) 无中生有given priority to innovative programs for graduate studies 把 spurring innovation中的 innovation 拼接成“研究生项目优先”，但原文从未谈及研究生项目优先级，是凭空捏造。
D) 无中生有played a central role in attracting international applicants 套用了原文 played a central role 的句式，却把宾语换成了 attracting international applicants（吸引国际申请人），但原文从未提国际申请人，是用熟悉句式包装的新内容。
questions.quote: This model of education has long played a central role in creating opportunity, driving economic growth, and spurring innovation.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the initial proposals concerning the recent tax reform bill?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于近期税改法案的初步提案,我们了解到什么?
A) 它们本会剥夺许多学生的人生机会。
B) 它们本会扣除研究生学生贷款利息。
C) 它们本会增加许多学生的经济负担。
D) 它们本会增加学费减免的数量。
**判型** What do we learn about the initial proposals 问关于某物的具体信息，定位句即答案出处，属细节题。
**拆句** 主干 What do we learn about the initial proposals，concerning the recent tax reform bill 是 the initial proposals 的后置修饰。注意虚拟语气 would have made 暗示这些提议未实施，比对选项时四个选项都是 would have，与原文虚拟一致。
**定位** 最初的提议本来会通过对研究生学费减免征税、取消学生贷款利息抵扣，使许多人负担不起教育。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念would have stripped many students of life's chances 把“加重经济负担”夸大为“剥夺人生机会”——原文 unaffordable for many 只到“许多人负担不起”，未到“剥夺人生机会”的程度，且 life's chances 范围过宽。
B) 与原文相反would have deducted graduate student loan interest 把原文 ending deductions for student loan interest 中的“取消抵扣”反过来说成“抵扣”，方向完全相反。
C) ✓ 正确would have made education unaffordable for many ↔would have added to many students' financial burden taxing tuition waivers for graduate students and ending deductions for student loan interest ↔financial burden unaffordable for many 与 added to many students' financial burden 在虚拟语气下完全等值，故选 C。
D) 与原文相反would have increased the number of tuition waivers 与原文 taxing tuition waivers相反——原文是对学费减免征税（变相缩减或削弱），选项却说“增加学费减免数量”，方向相反。
questions.quote: The initial proposals would have made education unaffordable for many by taxing tuition waivers for graduate students and ending deductions for student loan interest.

options.text: They would have stripped many students of life's chances.
They would have deducted graduate student loan interest.
They would have added to many students' financial burden.
They would have increased the number of tuition waivers.

questions.prompt: What do the data show about elite colleges and universities?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
数据显示精英学院和大学有什么特点?
A) 它们的毕业生缺乏进行统计分析所需的严谨性。
B) 它们的学生被证明对未来职业准备不足。
C) 它们对研究的关注有助于培养学生的批判性思维。
D) 它们的博雅教育使毕业生能够在任何领域中表现出色。
**判型** What do the data show 询问数据呈现的客观结论，对应原文具体陈述句，属细节题。
**拆句** 主干 What do the data show about elite colleges and universities，about 短语限定讨论对象。注意题干用的是 data show（data 复数对应原文 The data are clear），属于细节呼应。
**定位** 数据很清楚：博雅教育是出色的职业准备，既能带来优厚的终身收入，也能带来工作满意度。……事实上，博雅毕业生在每一个可以想象的领域都表现极佳。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反Their graduates lack the rigor required for doing statistical analysis 与原文rigorous analysis of data and facts（严谨的数据与事实分析能力）正相反——原文说博雅教育培养这种严谨，选项却说他们缺乏。
B) 与原文相反Their students prove to be inadequately prepared for their future careers 与原文a liberal arts education is great career preparation 正相反——原文说“出色的职业准备”，选项说“准备不充分”。
C) 无中生有Their focus on research is conducive to developing students' critical thinking 借用了 scholarly research 和 critical thinking 两个原文词，拼出“院校以研究为重心、研究有助于培养批判性思维”——但原文只说博雅教育培养批判性思维，并未说研究是其重心，更未谈“研究→批判性思维”的因果。
D) ✓ 正确liberal arts graduates do extremely well in every imaginable field ↔Their liberal arts education enables graduates to excel in whatever field they are in a liberal arts education is great career preparation ↔Their liberal arts education enables graduates to excel预判“在任何领域都表现出色”，D 项 excel in whatever field they are in 是其精准同义替换，故选 D。
questions.quote: The data are clear: a liberal arts education is great career preparation, both for excellent lifetime earnings and for satisfaction with the work. ... In fact, liberal arts graduates do extremely well in every imaginable field.

questions.prompt: What is an advantage of providing financial aid for students?

为学生提供经济资助有什么好处?
A) 每个学生都可以选择他们希望就读的院校。

**拆句** 主干 What is an advantage of providing financial aid for students，of 短语限定advantage 的所属。注意冠词是 an，意为多个优点中的任一个，选项只要原文支持即可，不必是唯一优点。
**定位** 除了让那些凭实力争得席位的人获得入学机会这一价值之外，经济背景的多样性还提升了所有学生的教育与体验。
questions.tip:

B) ✓ 正确the diversity of economic backgrounds enhances the education and experience of all of our students↔ All students can benefit from a diversified student population the diversity of economic backgrounds↔ a diversified student population原文明确说 all of our students 都从多样性中获益，与 B 项 All students can benefit完全对位，故选 B。

title: The city of Bath was founded by the…

sentences.text: The city of Bath was founded by the Romans almost two thousand years ago.
It has been famous for its (26)____ pleasing architecture and healing thermal springs ever since.

passage.translation: 巴斯市由罗马人建立于近两千年前。自那时起,它就以美观宜人的建筑和具有疗效的温泉而闻名。

sentences.text: There are three hot springs in Bath; one is the King's Spring, upon which the Roman Baths and a temple were (27)____ .
The other two are the Cross Spring and the Hetling Spring, close to each other in Hot Bath Street.
Although Bath is (28)____ known as a Roman and Georgian city, many people came in the intervening centuries to make use of the (29)____ waters.

passage.translation: 巴斯有三处温泉;其中一处是国王泉,罗马浴场和一座神庙就建在其上。另外两处是十字泉和Hetling泉,在Hot Bath街彼此相邻。尽管巴斯主要以罗马和乔治时代城市而著称,但在这两个时期之间的几个世纪里,许多人也来此利用这些天然泉水。

sentences.text: While the Georgians made 'taking the waters' or bathing particularly fashionable, it was (30)____generations who paved the way, creating greater interest in Bath and its springs.
Charles II, desperate for an heir and unable to produce a (31)____ son, came to Bath to take the waters in the hope that their magical powers would do something to (32)____ the situation.
Craving for a male heir, James and Mary both came to Bath and soon after produced a son, which bred many conspiracy theories about who was the real father of their (33)____ .
Regardless, the 'miracle' created something of a boom in tourism for Bath and once Queen Anne had paid a visit in 1702, sealing it as the place to be, the whole nation(34)____ to the city.

passage.translation: 虽然乔治时代的人们使"饮用泉水"或沐浴变得尤为流行,但正是前几代人铺平了道路,使人们对巴斯及其温泉产生了更大的兴趣。查理二世急需继承人却无法生育合法的儿子,于是来到巴斯饮用泉水,希望泉水的神奇力量能对这一状况有所补救。渴望男性继承人的詹姆斯和玛丽都来到巴斯,不久之后便生下了一个儿子,这引发了许多关于谁是其后代真正父亲的阴谋论。无论如何,这个"奇迹"为巴斯带来了旅游业的繁荣,而一旦安妮女王在1702年造访,确立了巴斯作为必去之地的地位,全国上下便纷纷涌向这座城市。

sentences.text: Afterwards, the spas(矿泉疗养浴场) in Bath continued to go in and out of fashion for more than 150 years until they closed completely.
The new Bath Spa, which opened in 2006, (35)____ modern architecture with the ancient spring, now the New Royal Bath.

passage.translation: 此后,巴斯的矿泉疗养浴场在150多年里不断经历兴衰起伏,直到完全关闭。2006年开放的新巴斯温泉将现代建筑与古老的泉水相结合,现在被称为新皇家浴场。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
The city of Bath was founded by the Romans almost two thousand years ago. It has been famous for its {{26}} pleasing architecture and healing thermal springs ever since.

There are three hot springs in Bath; one is the King's Spring, upon which the Roman Baths and a temple were {{27}} . The other two are the Cross Spring and the Hetling Spring, close to each other in Hot Bath Street. Although Bath is {{28}} known as a Roman and Georgian city, many people came in the intervening centuries to make use of the {{29}} waters.

While the Georgians made 'taking the waters' or bathing particularly fashionable, it was {{30}}generations who paved the way, creating greater interest in Bath and its springs. Charles II, desperate for an heir and unable to produce a {{31}} son, came to Bath to take the waters in the hope that their magical powers would do something to {{32}} the situation. Craving for a male heir, James and Mary both came to Bath and soon after produced a son, which bred many conspiracy theories about who was the real father of their {{33}} . Regardless, the 'miracle' created something of a boom in tourism for Bath and once Queen Anne had paid a visit in 1702, sealing it as the place to be, the whole nation{{34}} to the city.

Afterwards, the spas(矿泉疗养浴场) in Bath continued to go in and out of fashion for more than 150 years until they closed completely. The new Bath Spa, which opened in 2006, {{35}} modern architecture with the ancient spring, now the New Royal Bath.

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) aesthetically 副词
**词性槽** 修饰形容词 pleasing 的副词
**依据** 审美上令人愉悦 = 建筑美观famous for its __ pleasing architecture 说的是巴斯以"美观的建筑"闻名，aesthetically pleasing 是英文里描述"赏心悦目、审美上令人愉快"的高频固定搭配，与后面"healing thermal springs"（治疗效果）并列，分别从美感和功效两方面定调全城特色。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
K) principally 义为"主要地"，与 pleasing 不搭principally pleasing 意为"主要令人愉悦"，不符合英语习惯搭配；且 principally 通常修饰动词或限定范围（principally known as 等），更适合放在第 28 题修饰 known。
M) rhetorically 修辞地 ≠ 美感rhetorically 指"在修辞表达上"，与建筑外观的视觉美感没有关系，rhetorically pleasing architecture 在英语里不成立。

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) constructed 动词
**词性槽** were ___ → 被动语态过去分词
**依据** 建在泉水之上upon which 引导的定语从句修饰 the King's Spring，意为"罗马浴场和神庙建在国王泉之上"，constructed（建造）正是该语义的标准词。

**答案** K) principally 副词
**词性槽** 修饰过去分词 known 的副词
**依据** "主要被认作罗马 & 乔治亚城"对应 although 让步全句 Although Bath is __(28)__ known as a Roman and Georgian city, many people came in the intervening centuries 用 although 让步："尽管巴斯主要以罗马 / 乔治亚之城闻名，但中间几个世纪也有很多人来"。principally"主要地"恰好建立"主流认知 vs. 例外史实"的对照，是该让步逻辑的标准副词。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) rhetorically修辞地 known 不成立rhetorically known 在英文中不成习惯搭配，且"修辞上被认作"与让步逻辑无关；本句讨论的是事实层面的主流印象，与修辞无关。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 M) —— rhetorically 词性也对、形态也对，唯独搭配不通。副词槽Although Bath is __(28)__ known as a Roman and Georgian city 留下 principally 与rhetorically 两词同时过关词性，词义又都比较"专业"，容易让考生选错。防坑：看although 让步逻辑——只有"主要地"才能与让步对照（虽然主要是 A，但也有 B），rhetorically 没有让步含义。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) natural 形容词
**词性槽** the + 空 + 复数名词 waters → 修饰名词的形容词
**依据** natural waters = 天然温泉上文 healing thermal springs 已点明巴斯的水是"天然温泉"，本句指"中间几个世纪人们来利用这些（天然温泉）水"，natural 直接呼应温泉的天然属性，搭配 natural waters 是英语描述天然泉水的常见说法。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) legitimate "合法的水"语义荒谬legitimate 指"合法的、婚生的"，与温泉水的属性毫不沾边；且 legitimate 在后文 unable to produce a __(31)__ son 里有更贴合的位置（legitimate son = 婚生子）。
O) versatile"多才多艺的水"不通versatile 多形容人或物用途广，搭配 waters 不通顺；且全文没出现需要 versatile 的语境，它是典型的干扰词。

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) previous 形容词
**词性槽** it was ___ generations who paved → 强调结构中修饰复数名词的形容词
**依据** previous generations 与下文乔治亚时代构成时间对照本句让步逻辑是 While the Georgians made 'taking the waters' or bathing particularly fashionable, it was __(30)__ generations who paved the way——虽然是乔治亚人让"浴疗"流行起来，但真正铺路的是"前几代人"。previous generations"前几代人"正好与 the Georgians（乔治亚一代）形成时间上的对照，且与后文查理二世、詹姆士与玛丽这些"前任王朝"事例呼应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
O) versatile"多才多艺的几代人"与铺路逻辑无关versatile generations 既不构成时间对照，也与"paved the way（铺路）"的因果关系无关；versatile 整篇都找不到落脚点，是命题人埋的干扰词。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) legitimate 形容词
**词性槽** a + 空 + 名词 son → 修饰 son 的形容词
**依据** legitimate son = 婚生子（合法继承人）查理二世"desperate for an heir"——急需王位继承人；legitimate son 在英语里专指"婚生子"，即可以合法继承王位的儿子。下文 Craving for a male heir 再次印证关注点在合法男嗣，与 legitimate 完美吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
O) versatile多才多艺与王位继承无关versatile son"多才多艺的儿子"与文意"急需合法继承人"完全错位；查理二世在意的不是儿子才艺，而是儿子是否婚生、是否能继位。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) remedy 动词
**词性槽** do something to + 动词原形 → 不定式动词
**依据** remedy the situation = 补救局面查理二世来巴斯泡温泉 in the hope that their magical powers would do something to__ the situation，希望温泉魔力"做点什么来挽救 / 补救（生不出合法继承人的）局面"。remedy 作动词意为"纠正 / 补救"，remedy the situation 是英语固定搭配，与 desperate的语气一致。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
D) extract "提取局面"语义不通extract 意为"提取 / 抽出"，搭配名词通常是 extract information/data/oil，不能与 situation搭配；且与"求子续嗣"语境无关，是干扰项。

questions.explanation:
**答案** I) offspring 名词
**词性槽** 形容词性物主代词 their 后 → 名词
**依据** their offspring = 他们的子嗣前文 James and Mary both came to Bath and soon after produced a son 明确他们生了一个儿子，本句又紧接"who was the real father of their __"，空处应是"他们的孩子"。offspring 正是"子女、后代"的中性书面词，与上下文阴谋论的语气吻合。

**答案** E) flocked 动词
**词性槽** 主语 the whole nation + 空 + to the city → 过去式动词
**依据** flock to = 蜂拥而至前文铺垫"安妮女王 1702 年访问巴斯，把它坐实为时尚胜地"once Queen Anne had paid a visit in 1702, sealing it as the place to be，后面紧接"全国都___去这座城市"，逻辑上必须是"大规模、公开地涌向"，flocked（成群蜂拥而至）正是描写旅游热的标准词，与前句"created something of a boom in tourism"完美呼应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
N) sneaked 潜行 ≠ 公开蜂拥sneaked 指"偷偷溜走 / 潜行"，是小规模、隐秘的动作，主语是"全国（the whole nation）"时显然不合理；而且与"boom in tourism""the place to be"传递的高调、公开氛围正好相反，属典型反义诱惑项。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 N) —— sneaked 与 flocked 都能搭配 to，词义边界相反。the whole nation __(34)__ to the city 里 sneaked 看似也能填，是典型"正话反说"诱惑。防坑：看主语量级（the whole nation 是大规模、公开的）+ 上文气氛（boom in tourism、the place to be），明显与"偷偷溜走"矛盾。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) incorporates 动词
**词性槽** 主语 The new Bath Spa + 空 → 第三人称单数动词
**依据** incorporate A with B = 把 A 与 B 融合__(35)__ modern architecture with the ancient spring 的搭配框架"___ A with B"暗示"将现代建筑与古泉结合 / 融合"，incorporates"把……融合 / 并入"正是该框架的标准动词，与"new"（新）和"ancient"（古）形成的对比相呼应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) designates designate = "指定 / 命名"，搭配 with 不成立designate 通常搭配 as（designate A as B）或直接接宾语，不与 with 搭配；且语义"指定 / 命名"与"把现代建筑与古泉融合"完全不同，代入读不通。

title: Why facts don't change our minds

passage.label: A

sentences.text: The economist J.
K.
Galbraith once wrote, "Faced with a choice between changing one's mind and proving there is no need to do so, almost everyone gets busy with the proof."

passage.translation: 经济学家J. K. Galbraith曾写道："面对改变自己想法和证明没有必要这样做之间的选择,几乎每个人都忙于证明。"

passage.label: B

sentences.text: Leo Tolstoy was even bolder: "The most difficult subjects can be explained to the most slow-witted man if he has not formed any idea of them already; but the simplest thing cannot be made clear to the most intelligent man if he is firmly persuaded that he knows already, without a shadow of a doubt, what is laid before him."

passage.translation: Leo Tolstoy甚至更大胆地说："如果一个人事先没有形成任何观念,最困难的主题也可以向最迟钝的人解释清楚;但如果一个人坚信自己已经毫无疑问地知道摆在他面前的是什么,那么即使是最简单的事情也无法向最聪明的人说清楚。"

passage.label: C

sentences.text: What's going on here?
Why don't facts change our minds?
And why would someone continue to believe a false or inaccurate idea anyway?
How do such behaviors serve us?
Humans need a reasonably accurate view of the world in order to survive.
If your model of reality is wildly different from the actual world, then you struggle to take effective actions each day.
However, truth and accuracy are not the only things that matter to the human mind.
Humans also seem to have a deep desire to belong.

passage.translation: 这是怎么回事?为什么事实无法改变我们的想法?为什么有人会继续相信一个错误或不准确的观念?这些行为如何服务于我们?人类需要对世界有一个相当准确的认识才能生存。如果你的现实模型与真实世界大相径庭,那么你每天都难以采取有效的行动。然而,真相和准确性并不是人类思维关心的唯一事物。人类似乎也有一种强烈的归属欲望。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: In Atomic Habits, I wrote, "Humans are herd animals.
We want to fit in, to bond with others, and to earn the respect and approval of our peers.
Such inclinations are essential to our survival.
For most of our evolutionary history, our ancestors lived in tribes.
Becoming separated from the tribe—or worse, being cast out—was a death sentence."

passage.translation: 在《原子习惯》中,我写道:"人类是群居动物。我们想要融入群体,与他人建立联系,并赢得同伴的尊重和认可。这种倾向对我们的生存至关重要。在我们大部分进化历史中,我们的祖先生活在部落中。与部落分离——或者更糟的是被驱逐——就是死刑判决。"

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Understanding the truth of a situation is important, but so is remaining part of a tribe.
While these two desires often work well together, they occasionally come into conflict.
In many circumstances, social connection is actually more helpful to your daily life than understanding the truth of a particular fact or idea.

The Harvard psychologist Steven Pinker put it this way, "People are embraced or condemned according to their beliefs, so one function of the mind may be to hold beliefs that bring the belief-holder the greatest number of allies, protectors, or disciples(信徒), rather than beliefs that are most likely to be true."

passage.translation: 理解情况的真相很重要,但保持部落成员身份同样重要。虽然这两种欲望通常协调一致,但它们偶尔会产生冲突。在许多情况下,社会联系实际上比理解某个特定事实或观念的真相对你的日常生活更有帮助。哈佛心理学家Steven Pinker这样说:"人们根据自己的信念被接纳或谴责,因此思维的一个功能可能是持有能为信念持有者带来最多盟友、保护者或信徒的信念,而不是最可能正确的信念。"

passage.label: F

sentences.text: We don't always believe things because they are correct.
Sometimes we believe things because they make us look good to the people we care about.

I thought Kevin Simler put it well when he wrote, "If a brain anticipates that it will be rewarded for adopting a particular belief, it's perfectly happy to do so, and doesn't much care where the reward comes from—whether it's pragmatic(实用主义的) (better outcomes resulting from better decisions), social (better treatment from one's peers), or some mix of the two."

passage.translation: 我们并不总是因为事物正确而相信它们。有时我们相信事物是因为它们让我们在我们关心的人面前显得体面。我认为Kevin Simler说得很好:"如果大脑预期采纳某个特定信念会得到奖励,它就会非常乐意这样做,并且不太在乎奖励来自哪里——无论是实用主义的(更好的决策带来更好的结果)、社会的(同伴的更好对待),还是两者的某种混合。"

passage.label: G

sentences.text: False beliefs can be useful in a social sense even if they are not useful in a factual sense.
For lack of a better phrase, we might call this approach "factually false, but socially accurate."
When we have to choose between the two, people often select friends and family over facts.

This insight not only explains why we might hold our tongue at a dinner party or look the other way when our parents say something offensive, but also reveals a better way to change the minds of others.

passage.translation: 即使错误的信念在事实意义上没有用处,在社会意义上也可能有用。由于缺乏更好的表述,我们可以将这种方法称为"事实上错误,但社会上准确"。当我们必须在两者之间选择时,人们往往选择朋友和家人而非事实。这一洞察不仅解释了为什么我们可能在晚宴上保持沉默或当父母说出冒犯性言论时视而不见,还揭示了改变他人想法的更好方法。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Convincing someone to change their mind is really the process of convincing them to change their tribe.
If they abandon their beliefs, they run the risk of losing social ties.
You can't expect someone to change their mind if you take away their community too.
You have to give them somewhere to go.
Nobody wants their worldview torn apart if loneliness is the outcome.

passage.translation: 说服某人改变想法实际上是说服他们改变部落的过程。如果他们放弃自己的信念,就有失去社会联系的风险。如果你夺走了他们的社群,就不能指望他们改变想法。你必须给他们一个去处。如果孤独是结果,没有人愿意自己的世界观被撕裂。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: The way to change people's minds is to become friends with them, to integrate them into your tribe, to bring them into your circle.
Now, they can change their beliefs without the risk of being abandoned socially.

passage.translation: 改变人们想法的方法是与他们成为朋友,将他们融入你的部落,把他们带入你的圈子。现在,他们可以改变信念而不必冒被社会抛弃的风险。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: Perhaps it is not difference, but distance, that breeds tribalism and hostility.
As proximity increases, so does understanding.
I am reminded of Abraham Lincoln's quote, "I don't like that man.
I must get to know him better."

passage.translation: 也许滋生部落主义和敌意的不是差异,而是距离。随着距离的缩短,理解也会增加。这让我想起Abraham Lincoln的名言:"我不喜欢那个人。我必须更好地了解他。"

passage.label: K

sentences.text: Facts don't change our minds.
Friendship does.
Years ago, Ben Casnocha mentioned an idea to me that I haven't been able to shake: The people who are most likely to change our minds are the ones we agree with on 98 percent of topics.
If someone you know, like, and trust believes a radical idea, you are more likely to give it merit, weight, or consideration.
You already agree with them in most areas of life.
Maybe you should change your mind on this one too.
But if someone wildly different than you proposes the same radical idea, well, it's easy to dismiss them as nuts.

passage.translation: 事实不会改变我们的想法。友谊会。多年前,Ben Casnocha向我提到一个我一直无法摆脱的想法:最有可能改变我们想法的人是那些在98%的话题上与我们意见一致的人。如果你认识、喜欢并信任的人相信一个激进的想法,你更有可能给予它价值、权重或考虑。你已经在生活的大多数领域与他们意见一致。也许你也应该在这个问题上改变想法。但如果一个与你截然不同的人提出同样激进的想法,那么很容易将他们当作疯子而不予理会。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: One way to visualize this distinction is by mapping beliefs on a spectrum.
If you divide this spectrum into 10 units and you find yourself at Position 7, then there is little sense in trying to convince someone at Position 1.
The gap is too wide.
When you're at Position 7, your time is better spent connecting with people who are at Positions 6 and 8, gradually pulling them in your direction.

passage.translation: 可视化这种区别的一种方法是将信念映射到一个光谱上。如果你将这个光谱分成10个单位,而你发现自己处于位置7,那么试图说服位置1的人就没有什么意义。差距太大了。当你处于位置7时,你的时间最好花在与处于位置6和8的人建立联系上,逐渐将他们拉向你的方向。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: The most heated arguments often occur between people on opposite ends of the spectrum, but the most frequent learning occurs from people who are nearby.
The closer you are to someone, the more likely it becomes that the one or two beliefs you don't share will bleed over into your own mind and shape your thinking.
The further away an idea is from your current position, the more likely you are to reject it outright.
When it comes to changing people's minds, it is very difficult to jump from one side to another.
You can't jump down the spectrum.
You have to slide down it.

passage.translation: 最激烈的争论往往发生在光谱两端的人之间,但最频繁的学习发生在附近的人之间。你与某人越接近,你们不共享的一两个信念就越有可能渗透到你自己的思维中并塑造你的思考。一个想法离你当前位置越远,你就越有可能彻底拒绝它。在改变人们想法方面,从一边跳到另一边是非常困难的。你不能跳下光谱。你必须滑下去。

passage.label: N

sentences.text: Any idea that is sufficiently different from your current worldview will feel threatening.
And the best place to ponder a threatening idea is in a non-threatening environment.
As a result, books are often a better vehicle for transforming beliefs than conversations or debates.
In conversation, people have to carefully consider their status and appearance.
They want to save face and avoid looking stupid.
When confronted with an uncomfortable set of facts, the tendency is often to double down on their current position rather than publicly admit to being wrong.
Books resolve this tension.
With a book, the conversation takes place inside someone's head and without the risk of being judged by others.
It's easier to be open-minded when you aren't feeling defensive.

passage.translation: 任何与你当前世界观有足够差异的想法都会让人感到威胁。而思考威胁性想法的最佳场所是在非威胁性的环境中。因此,书籍往往比对话或辩论更能有效地转变信念。在对话中,人们必须仔细考虑自己的地位和形象。他们想要保全面子,避免显得愚蠢。当面对一组令人不适的事实时,往往倾向于加倍坚持自己当前的立场,而不是公开承认错误。书籍解决了这种紧张关系。通过书籍,对话在某人的头脑中进行,没有被他人评判的风险。当你不感到防御时,更容易保持开放的心态。

passage.label: O

sentences.text: There is another reason bad ideas continue to live on, which is that people continue to talk about them.
Silence is death for any idea.
An idea that is never spoken or written down dies with the person who conceived it.
Ideas can only be remembered when they are repeated.
They can only be believed when they are repeated.
I have already pointed out that people repeat ideas to signal they are part of the same social group.
But here's a crucial point most people miss: People also repeat bad ideas when they complain about them.
Before you can criticize an idea, you have to reference that idea.
You end up repeating the ideas you're hoping people will forget—but, of course, people can't forget them because you keep talking about them.
The more you repeat a bad idea, the more likely people are to believe it.

passage.translation: 坏想法继续存在还有另一个原因,那就是人们继续谈论它们。沉默对任何想法来说都是死亡。一个从未被说出或写下的想法会随着构思它的人一起死去。想法只有在被重复时才能被记住。它们只有在被重复时才能被相信。我已经指出,人们重复想法是为了表明他们是同一社会群体的一部分。但这里有一个大多数人忽略的关键点:当人们抱怨坏想法时,他们也在重复它们。在你批评一个想法之前,你必须引用那个想法。你最终重复了你希望人们忘记的想法——但当然,人们无法忘记它们,因为你一直在谈论它们。你越多重复一个坏想法,人们就越有可能相信它。

passage.label: P

sentences.text: Let's call this phenomenon Clear's Law of Recurrence: The number of people who believe an idea is directly proportional to the number of times it has been repeated during the last year—even if the idea is false.

passage.translation: 让我们把这种现象称为Clear重复定律:相信一个想法的人数与它在过去一年中被重复的次数成正比——即使这个想法是错误的。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: According to the author, humans can hardly survive if separated from their community.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
根据作者的观点,如果与群体分离,人类几乎无法生存。
**锚点** 脱离社群难以生存
**定位** 和部落分开——或更糟，被驱逐——等于被判了死刑。
**改写** separated from their community ↔Becoming separated from the tribe—or worse, being cast out community 是 tribe 的上位词can hardly survive ↔ was a death sentence死刑=不能存活的程度化同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
C C 段只讲到 Humans need a reasonably accurate view of the world in order to survive，谈的是生存与世界观的关系，没有 separated/community/death 这条主线，只覆盖陈述句一半。Humans need a reasonably accurate view of the world in order to survive
questions.quote: Becoming separated from the tribe—or worse, being cast out—was a death sentence.

**改写** prioritize social bonds rather than facts ↔ people often select friends and family over facts二选一句式同义改写accept false beliefs ↔False beliefs can be useful in a social sense even if they are not useful in a factual sense采信错误信念在两侧呼应
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
F F 段讲 We don't always believe things because they are correct. Sometimes we believe things because they make us look good，话题与社交动机相邻，但没有friends and family vs facts 这种二选一表态，与题干 prioritize…rather than… 的句式锚不上。Sometimes we believe things because they make us look good to the people we care about E E 段讲 social connection is actually more helpful to your daily life than understanding the truth，侧重日常中社交连接对生活的助益（对应第 41 题），不是题干强调的 accept false beliefs 这条因果。social connection is actually more helpful to your daily life than understanding the truth of a particular fact or idea

questions.prompt: Most often people learn from those close to them.

人们最常从身边亲近的人那里学习。
**锚点** 从亲近者处学到最多

questions.prompt: Sometimes people adopt certain beliefs in order to leave a favorable impression on those dear to them.

**答案** F 段（强锚点）

有时人们采纳某些信念是为了给自己珍视的人留下好印象。

**定位** 有时候我们相信某些事，是因为这些事让我们在我们在乎的人面前显得好看。

questions.quote: Sometimes we believe things because they make us look good to the people we care about.

questions.prompt: Compared with face-to-face communication, books often provide a better medium for changing people's beliefs.

**锚点** 书比面对面交流更利于改变信念
**定位** 结果是，比起对话或辩论，书往往是一种更好的改变信念的载体。
**改写** books often provide a better medium ↔ books are often a better vehicle medium 与 vehicle 同义changing people's beliefs ↔ transforming beliefs changing 与 transforming 同义face-to-face communication ↔ conversations or debates上位概括

questions.prompt: On many occasions in daily life, people benefit more from their social bonds than from knowing the truth.
questions.explanation:
**答案** E 段（强锚点）

在日常生活的许多场合,人们从社会纽带中获得的好处多于了解真相。

**定位** 在许多情形下，社交连接实际上比理解某一具体事实或观念的真相更有助于你的日常生活。
**改写** On many occasions in daily life ↔ In many circumstances频次状语同义对换benefit more from their social bonds than from knowing the truth ↔social connection is actually more helpful to your daily life than understanding the truth of a particular fact or idea比较句式重构
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
C C 段说 truth and accuracy are not the only things that matter to the human mind. Humans also seem to have a deep desire to belong，只提出两种需要并列存在，并未在日常情境下把社交连接置于真相之上。truth and accuracy are not the only things that matter to the human mind. Humans also seem to have a deep desire to belong G G 段强调 When we have to choose between the two, people often select friends and family over facts，是被迫二选一时的选择，不是题干说的 在许多日常情形下 受益更多。When we have to choose between the two, people often select friends and family over facts
questions.quote: In many circumstances, social connection is actually more helpful to your daily life than understanding the truth of a particular fact or idea.

questions.prompt: If you want to change somebody's beliefs, you should first establish social connection with them.
questions.explanation:
**答案** I 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
如果你想改变某人的信念,你应该首先与他们建立社会联系。
**锚点** 想改信念先建立社交连接
**定位** 改变别人想法的方式是与他们成为朋友，把他们融入你的部落，把他们带进你的圈子。
**改写** change somebody's beliefs ↔ change people's minds beliefs 与 minds 在本文同义first establish social connection ↔become friends with them, to integrate them into your tribe, to bring them into your circle上位概括

**辨邻**
H H 段说 You can't expect someone to change their mind if you take away their community too. You have to give them somewhere to go，落脚是 别抽走他的群体，与题干 first establish social connection 的正向先后步骤不一致。You can't expect someone to change their mind if you take away their community too K K 段强调 Facts don't change our minds. Friendship does，回答的是 谁能改变想法（友谊），不是题干问的 想改变想法你应先做什么（先建立社交连接）。Facts don't change our minds. Friendship does
questions.quote: The way to change people's minds is to become friends with them, to integrate them into your tribe, to bring them into your circle.

questions.prompt: Humans cannot survive without a fair knowledge of the actual world.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
人类如果不具备对现实世界相当程度的了解就无法生存。
**锚点** 无对真实世界的认识则无法生存
**定位** 人类要生存，就需要一种对世界相当准确的认识。

questions.tip:
**辨邻**
D D 段说 Becoming separated from the tribe—or worse, being cast out—was a death sentence，落脚是社群关系对生存的意义，与题干 a fair knowledge of the actual world 这一认知层面无关。Becoming separated from the tribe—or worse, being cast out—was a death sentence
questions.quote: Humans need a reasonably accurate view of the world in order to survive.

questions.prompt: Repetition of bad ideas increases their chances of being accepted.
questions.explanation:
**答案** O 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
错误观念的重复增加了它们被接受的可能性。
**锚点** 重复坏想法增加被接受机会
**定位** 你越是重复一个坏想法，人们就越可能相信它。
**改写** Repetition of bad ideas ↔ repeat a bad idea名词化increases their chances of being accepted ↔ the more likely people are to believe it比较句式与可能性同义

P P 段说 The number of people who believe an idea is directly proportional to the number of times it has been repeated during the last year，是把 O 段结论命名为Clear's Law of Recurrence，是 给命题命名 而非首次提出 重复→被接受 这一命题。题干 Q44 表述的是命题本身，首发在 O 段。The number of people who believe an idea is directly proportional to the number of times it has been repeated during the last year

**定位** 如果结果是孤独，没人愿意让自己的世界观被撕裂。

I I 段说 they can change their beliefs without the risk of being abandoned socially，落脚是 提供方法让人能改信念，与题干 Q45 的 没人愿意放弃信念 这一反向心理表述不一致。they can change their beliefs without the risk of being abandoned socially D D 段说 Becoming separated from the tribe—or worse, being cast out—was a death sentence，落脚是 被部落驱逐的生死后果，与题干 Q45 的 不愿放弃信念以免孤立 这一信念—孤立链条不同。Becoming separated from the tribe—or worse, being cast out—was a death sentence
questions.quote: Nobody wants their worldview torn apart if loneliness is the outcome.

title: Do music lessons really make children smarter?

passage.label: A

sentences.text: A recent analysis found that most research mischaracterizes the relationship between music and skills enhancement.

passage.translation: 最近的一项分析发现,大多数研究错误地描述了音乐与技能提升之间的关系。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: In 2004, a paper appeared in the journal Psychological Science, titled "Music Lessons Enhance IQ."

The author, composer and psychologist Glenn Schellenberg had conducted an experiment with 144 children randomly assigned to four groups: one learned the keyboard for a year, one took singing lessons, one joined an acting class, and a control group had no extracurricular training.
The IQ of the children in the two musical groups rose by an average of seven points in the course of a year; those in the other two groups gained an average of 4.3 points.

passage.translation: 2004年,《心理科学》杂志上发表了一篇题为《音乐课程提高智商》的论文。作者Glenn Schellenberg是作曲家兼心理学家,他对144名儿童进行了实验,这些儿童被随机分配到四组:一组学习键盘一年,一组上声乐课,一组参加表演班,对照组没有课外培训。两个音乐组儿童的智商在一年内平均上升了7分;另外两组的儿童平均上升了4.3分。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: Schellenberg had long been skeptical of the science supporting claims that music education enhances children's abstract reasoning, math, or language skills.
If children who play the piano are smarter, he says, it doesn't necessarily mean they are smarter because they play the piano.
It could be that the youngsters who play the piano also happen to be more ambitious or better at focusing on a task.
Correlation, after all, does not prove causation.

passage.translation: Schellenberg长期以来一直对支持音乐教育能增强儿童抽象推理、数学或语言技能这一说法的科学依据持怀疑态度。他说,如果弹钢琴的孩子更聪明,这并不一定意味着他们因为弹钢琴而更聪明。也可能是弹钢琴的孩子恰好更有抱负或更善于专注于任务。毕竟,相关性并不能证明因果关系。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: The 2004 paper was specifically designed to address those concerns.
And as a passionate musician, Schellenberg was delighted when he turned up credible evidence that music has transfer effects on general intelligence.
But nearly a decade later, in 2013, the Education Endowment Foundation funded a bigger study with more than 900 students.
That study failed to confirm Schellenberg's findings, producing no evidence that music lessons improved math and literacy skills.

passage.translation: 2004年的论文就是专门为解决这些担忧而设计的。作为一名充满热情的音乐家,Schellenberg在发现音乐对一般智力有迁移效应的可信证据时感到非常高兴。但将近十年后,在2013年,教育捐赠基金会资助了一项涉及900多名学生的更大规模研究。该研究未能证实Schellenberg的发现,没有产生音乐课程提高数学和读写能力的证据。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Schellenberg took that news in stride while continuing to cast a skeptical eye on the research in his field.

Recently, he decided to formally investigate just how often his fellow researchers in psychology and neuroscience make what he believes are erroneous—or at least premature—causal connections between music and intelligence.
His results, published in May, suggest that many of his peers do just that.

passage.translation: Schellenberg从容地接受了这一消息,同时继续对其研究领域的研究持怀疑态度。最近,他决定正式调查他在心理学和神经科学领域的同行研究者在音乐与智力之间建立他认为错误的——或至少是过早的——因果联系的频率。他在5月发表的结果表明,他的许多同行确实这样做了。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: For his recent study, Schellenberg asked two research assistants to look for correlational studies on the effects of music education.
They found a total of 114 papers published since 2000.
To assess whether the authors claimed any causation, researchers then looked for telltale verbs in each paper's title and abstract, verbs like "enhance," "promote," "facilitate," and "strengthen."

The papers were categorized as neuroscience if the study employed a brain imaging method like magnetic resonance, or if the study appeared in a journal that had "brain," "neuroscience," or a related term in its title.
Otherwise the papers were categorized as psychology.
Schellenberg didn't tell his assistants what exactly he was trying to prove.

passage.translation: 在最近的研究中,Schellenberg让两名研究助理寻找关于音乐教育效果的相关性研究。他们找到了自2000年以来发表的总共114篇论文。为了评估作者是否声称存在任何因果关系,研究人员随后在每篇论文的标题和摘要中寻找标志性动词,如"增强"、"促进"、"促成"和"加强"。如果研究采用了磁共振等脑成像方法,或者研究发表在标题中含有"大脑"、"神经科学"或相关术语的期刊上,论文就被归类为神经科学。否则论文被归类为心理学。Schellenberg没有告诉他的助手他究竟想证明什么。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: After computing their assessments, Schellenberg concluded that the majority of the articles erroneously claimed that music training had a causal effect.

The overselling, he also found, was more prevalent among neuroscience studies, three quarters of which mischaracterized a mere association between music training and skills enhancement as a cause-and-effect relationship.
This may come as a surprise to some.
Psychologists have been battling charges that they don't do "real" science for some time—in large part because many findings from classic experiments have proved unreproducible.
Neuroscientists, on the other hand, armed with brain scans and EEGs(脑电图), have not been subject to the same degree of critique.

passage.translation: 在计算评估结果后,Schellenberg得出结论,大多数文章错误地声称音乐训练具有因果效应。他还发现,这种过度宣传在神经科学研究中更为普遍,其中四分之三的研究将音乐训练与技能提升之间的单纯关联错误地描述为因果关系。这可能会让一些人感到惊讶。心理学家一直在对抗他们不做"真正"科学的指责——很大程度上是因为许多经典实验的发现被证明无法重现。另一方面,拥有脑扫描和脑电图的神经科学家并没有受到同样程度的批评。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: To argue for a cause-and-effect relationship, scientists must attempt to explain why and how a connection could occur.
When it comes to transfer effects of music, scientists frequently point to brain plasticity—the fact that the brain changes according to how we use it.
When a child learns to play the violin, for example, several studies have shown that the brain region responsible for the fine motor skills of the left hand's fingers is likely to grow.

And many experiments have shown that musical training improves certain hearing capabilities, like filtering voices from background noise or distinguishing the difference between the consonants(辅音) 'b' and 'g'.

passage.translation: 要论证因果关系,科学家必须尝试解释为什么以及如何产生联系。在涉及音乐的迁移效应时,科学家经常指出大脑可塑性——即大脑根据我们的使用方式而改变的事实。例如,当儿童学习拉小提琴时,几项研究表明,负责左手手指精细运动技能的大脑区域可能会增长。许多实验表明,音乐训练能提高某些听觉能力,如从背景噪音中过滤声音或区分辅音'b'和'g'之间的差异。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: But Schellenberg remains highly critical of how the concept of plasticity has been applied in his field.
"Plasticity has become an industry of its own," he wrote in his May paper.
Practice does change the brain, he allows, but what is questionable is the assertion that these changes affect other brain regions, such as those responsible for spatial reasoning or math problems.

passage.translation: 但Schellenberg对可塑性概念在其领域的应用方式仍持高度批评态度。他在5月的论文中写道:"可塑性本身已经成为一个产业。"他承认,练习确实会改变大脑,但值得质疑的是这些变化会影响其他大脑区域的断言,如负责空间推理或数学问题的区域。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: Neuropsychologist Lutz Jancke agrees.
"Most of these studies don't allow for causal inferences," he said.
For over two decades, Jancke has researched the effects of music lessons, and like Schellenberg, he believes that the only way to truly understand their effects is to run longitudinal studies.
In such studies, researchers would need to follow groups of children with and without music lessons over a long period of time—even if the assignments are not completely random.
Then they could compare outcomes for each group.

passage.translation: 神经心理学家Lutz Jancke对此表示赞同。"这些研究中的大多数不允许因果推断,"他说。二十多年来,Jancke一直在研究音乐课的效果,和Schellenberg一样,他认为真正了解其效果的唯一方法是进行纵向研究。在这类研究中,研究人员需要长期跟踪有音乐课和没有音乐课的儿童群体——即使分配不是完全随机的。然后他们可以比较每组的结果。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: Some researchers are starting to do just that.
The neuroscientist Peter Schneider from Heidelberg University in Germany, for example, has been following a group of children for ten years now.

Some of them were handed musical instruments and given lessons through a school-based program in the Ruhr region of Germany called Jedem Kind ein Instrument, or "an instrument for every child," which was carried out with government funding.

Among these children, Schneider has found that those who were enthusiastic about music and who practiced voluntarily showed improvements in hearing ability, as well as in more general competencies, such as the ability to concentrate.

passage.translation: 一些研究人员正开始这样做。例如,德国海德堡大学的神经科学家Peter Schneider现在已经跟踪一组儿童十年了。其中一些儿童通过德国鲁尔地区一个名为Jedem Kind ein Instrument(即"每个孩子一件乐器")的学校项目获得了乐器并接受了课程,该项目由政府资助。在这些儿童中,Schneider发现那些对音乐充满热情并自愿练习的人在听觉能力以及更一般的能力方面都有所提高,如专注能力。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: To establish whether effects such as improved concentration are caused by music participation itself, and not by investing time in an extracurricular activity of any kind, Assal Habibi, a psychology professor at the University of Southern California, is conducting a five-year longitudinal study with children from low-income communities in Los Angeles.
The youngsters fall into three groups: those who take after-school music, those who do after-school sports, and those with no structured after- school program at all.

After two years, Habibi and her colleagues reported seeing structural changes in the brains of the musically trained children, both locally and in the pathways connecting different parts of the brain.

passage.translation: 为了确定诸如注意力提高等效果是由音乐参与本身引起的,而不是由投入时间参与任何类型的课外活动引起的,南加州大学心理学教授Assal Habibi正在对洛杉矶低收入社区的儿童进行为期五年的纵向研究。这些孩子分为三组:参加课后音乐活动的、参加课后体育活动的,以及完全没有结构化课后项目的。两年后,Habibi和她的同事报告称,在接受音乐训练的儿童大脑中看到了结构变化,无论是局部还是在连接大脑不同部分的通路中。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: That may seem compelling, but Habibi's children were not selected randomly.
Did the children who were drawn to music perhaps have something in them from the start that made them different but eluded the brain scanners?
"As somebody who started taking piano lessons at the age of five and got up every morning at seven to practice, that experience changed me and made me part of who I am today," Schellenberg said.
"The question is whether those kinds of experiences do so systematically across individuals and create exactly the same changes.
And I think that is that huge leap of faith."

passage.translation: 这似乎很有说服力,但Habibi的儿童不是随机选择的。被音乐吸引的孩子是否从一开始就拥有某些使他们与众不同但脑扫描仪无法捕捉到的东西?Schellenberg说:"作为一个从五岁开始上钢琴课并每天早上七点起床练习的人,那段经历改变了我,使我成为今天的一部分。问题是这类经历是否在个体之间系统性地产生同样的变化。我认为这是一个巨大的信念飞跃。

passage.label: N

sentences.text: Did he have a hidden talent that others didn't have?
Or more endurance than his peers?

Music researchers tend, like Schellenberg, to be musicians themselves, and as he noted in his recent paper, "the idea of positive cognitive and neural side effects from music training (and other pleasurable activities) is inherently appealing."
He also admits that if he had children of his own, he would encourage them to take music lessons and go to university.
"I would think that it makes them better people, more critical, just wiser in general," he said.

passage.translation: 他是否拥有别人没有的隐藏天赋?或者比同龄人更有耐力?音乐研究者往往像Schellenberg一样,本身就是音乐家,正如他在最近的论文中指出的那样,"音乐训练(和其他愉快活动)产生积极认知和神经副作用的想法本质上具有吸引力。"他也承认,如果他有自己的孩子,他会鼓励他们上音乐课和上大学。他说:"我会认为这让他们成为更好的人,更有批判性,总体上更明智。

passage.label: O

sentences.text: But those convictions should be checked at the entrance to the lab, he added.
Otherwise, the work becomes religion or faith.
"You have to let go of your faith if you want to be a scientist."

passage.translation: 但他补充说,这些信念应该在实验室门口被搁置。否则,工作就变成了宗教或信仰。"如果你想成为科学家,就必须放下你的信念。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: Glenn Schellenberg's latest research suggests many psychologists and neuroscientists wrongly believe in the causal relationship between music and IQ.
questions.explanation:
**答案** E 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
Glenn Schellenberg的最新研究表明，许多心理学家和神经科学家错误地相信音乐与智商之间存在因果关系。
**锚点** 强锚·latest research + wrongly believe causal
**定位** 最近，他决定正式调查一下他在心理学和神经科学领域的同行们，多频繁地做出他认为是错误的——或者至少是过早的——关于音乐与智力之间的因果关联。他 5 月发表的结果表明，他的许多同行的确如此。
**改写** Glenn Schellenberg's latest research ↔ Recently, he decided to formally investigate时间副词 + 行为动词改写wrongly believe in the causal relationship between music and IQ ↔erroneous—or at least premature—causal connections between music and intelligence同义词替换 + 范围保留many psychologists and neuroscientists ↔his fellow researchers in psychology and neuroscience同义短语改写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
G G 段 the majority of the articles erroneously claimed that music training had a causal effect 虽然也讲「错称因果」，但题干 36 强调的是「Schellenberg 的最新研究表明 + 同行错信」这一整体判断，落点在 E 段的 His results, published in May, suggest that many of his peers do just that 上。the majority of the articles erroneously claimed that music training had a causal effect
questions.quote: Recently, he decided to formally investigate just how often his fellow researchers in psychology and neuroscience make what he believes are erroneous—or at least premature—causal connections between music and intelligence. His results, published in May, suggest that many of his peers do just that.

questions.prompt: The belief in the positive effects of music training appeals to many researchers who are musicians themselves.

**题目译文**
对音乐训练积极效果的信念吸引了许多本身就是音乐家的研究人员。
**锚点** 强锚·researchers who are musicians themselves
**定位** 音乐研究者们和 Schellenberg 一样，往往自己就是音乐家；正如他在最近的论文里所写：「音乐训练（以及其他令人愉悦的活动）带来正向认知与神经副作用的想法，本身就很有吸引力。」
**改写** The belief in the positive effects of music training ↔the idea of positive cognitive and neural side effects from music training近义词替换 + 概括appeals to many researchers who are musicians themselves ↔Music researchers tend, like Schellenberg, to be musicians themselves is inherently appealing主被动转换 + 同源词替换
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
D D 段 as a passionate musician, Schellenberg was delighted when he turned up credible evidence 是描述他作为音乐家时的个人情绪反应，而非题干的『许多本身是音乐家的研究者被这种正向看法所吸引』。as a passionate musician, Schellenberg was delighted when he turned up credible evidence
questions.quote: Music researchers tend, like Schellenberg, to be musicians themselves, and as he noted in his recent paper, "the idea of positive cognitive and neural side effects from music training (and other pleasurable activities) is inherently appealing."

questions.prompt: Glenn Schellenberg was doubtful about the claim that music education helps enhance children's intelligence.

Glenn Schellenberg对音乐教育有助于提高儿童智力的说法持怀疑态度。
**锚点** 强锚·doubtful + claim that music education helps enhance children's intelligence

questions.tip:

questions.prompt: Glenn Schellenberg came to the conclusion that most of the papers assessed made the wrong claim regarding music's effect on intelligence.

**答案** G 段（强锚点）

Glenn Schellenberg得出结论，大多数被评估的论文在音乐对智力的影响方面做出了错误的
声 明 。

**定位** 在汇总助手们的评估之后，Schellenberg 得出结论：大多数论文错误地宣称音乐训练具有因果效应。
**改写** most of the papers assessed ↔ the majority of the articles近义词替换made the wrong claim regarding music's effect on intelligence ↔erroneously claimed that music training had a causal effect名词短语 ↔ 副词 + 动词 + 因果改写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E E 段 many of his peers do just that 是『许多同行』的程度词，而题干 39 用的是『大多数论文（most of the papers）』这种定量化判决，应当对到 G 段更精确的majority 表述。His results, published in May, suggest that many of his peers do just that
questions.quote: After computing their assessments, Schellenberg concluded that the majority of the articles erroneously claimed that music training had a causal effect.

questions.prompt: You must abandon your unverified beliefs before you become a scientist.
questions.explanation:
**答案** O 段（强锚点）

在你成为科学家之前，你必须放弃未经证实的信念。

**定位** 但他补充说，那些信念应该在走进实验室时就被搁置；否则，研究就会沦为宗教或信仰。「如果你想成为一名科学家，就必须放下你的信念。」
**改写** You must abandon your unverified beliefs ↔ You have to let go of your faith情态动词 + 动词短语同义替换before you become a scientist ↔ if you want to be a scientist条件状语句式转换
questions.quote: But those convictions should be checked at the entrance to the lab, he added. Otherwise, the work becomes religion or faith. "You have to let go of your faith if you want to be a scientist."

questions.prompt: Lots of experiments have demonstrated that people with music training can better differentiate certain sounds.
questions.explanation:
**答案** H 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
大量实验已经证明，接受过音乐训练的人能够更好地区分某些声音。
**锚点** 强锚·music training + differentiate certain sounds
**定位** 并且许多实验已经表明，音乐训练能提升某些听觉能力，比如从背景噪声中过滤人声，或区分辅音 b 和 g 之间的差异。
**改写** Lots of experiments have demonstrated ↔ many experiments have shown数量词 + 动词同义替换people with music training can better differentiate certain sounds ↔musical training improves certain hearing capabilities, like ... distinguishing the difference between the consonants(辅音) 'b' and 'g'上位概括 + 同义动作 + 例证还原
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
K K 段 improvements in hearing ability, as well as in more general competencies, such as the ability to concentrate 是一项追踪研究的整体发现，并未提到『区分某些声音』这种具体辨别动作；这正是 H 段独有的细节。improvements in hearing ability, as well as in more general competencies, such as the ability to concentrate
questions.quote: And many experiments have shown that musical training improves certain hearing capabilities, like filtering voices from background noise or distinguishing the difference between the consonants(辅音) 'b' and 'g'.

questions.prompt: Glenn Schellenberg's findings at the beginning of this century were not supported by a larger study carried out some ten years later.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
Glenn Schellenberg在本世纪初的研究结果未能得到大约十年后进行的一项更大规模研究的
支 持 。
**锚点** 强锚·beginning of this century + larger study ten years later
**定位** 但将近十年后，在 2013 年，Education Endowment Foundation 资助了一项更大规模的研究，受试者超过 900 名学生。那项研究未能证实 Schellenberg 的发现，没能拿出证据表明音乐课提升了数学和读写能力。
**改写** Glenn Schellenberg's findings at the beginning of this century ↔The 2004 paper was specifically designed to address those concerns时间状语的上位概括were not supported by a larger study carried out some ten years later ↔nearly a decade later, in 2013, the Education Endowment Foundation funded a bigger study with more than 900 students时间表达 + 形容词近义替换were not supported by a larger study ↔ That study failed to confirm Schellenberg's findings否定结构同义替换
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段 The IQ of the children in the two musical groups rose by an average of seven points 描述的是 2004 实验的正面结果，并未提及十年后大研究是否支持；题干 42 的关键事件是『未被支持』，应落在 D 段。The IQ of the children in the two musical groups rose by an average of seven points in the course of a year

**题目译文**
一位研究人员认同Glenn Schellenberg的观点，即有必要进行长期发展性研究以了解音乐训练的
效 果 。
**锚点** 强锚·One researcher shares + long-term developmental studies
**定位** 神经心理学家 Lutz Jancke 表示同意。「这些研究大多无法支持因果推断，」他说。二十多年来，Jancke 一直在研究音乐课的效果，并且和 Schellenberg 一样，他认为真正理解其效果的唯一办法是做纵向研究。

questions.quote: Neuropsychologist Lutz Jancke agrees. "Most of these studies don't allow for causal inferences," he said. For over two decades, Jancke has researched the effects of music lessons, and like Schellenberg, he believes that the only way to truly understand their effects is to run longitudinal studies.

questions.prompt: Glenn Schellenberg admits that practice can change certain areas of the brain but doubts that the change can affect other areas.

title: No one in fashion is surprised that Burberry burnt £28 million of stock

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Last week, Burberry's annual report revealed that £28.6 million worth of stock was burnt last year.
The news has left investors and consumers outraged but comes as little surprise to those in the fashion industry.

passage.translation: 上周,Burberry的年度报告披露,去年价值2860万英镑的库存被焚烧。这一消息令投资者和消费者感到愤怒,但对时尚行业内部人士来说却并不意外。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: The practice of destroying unsold stock, and even rolls of unused fabric, is commonplace for luxury labels.
Becoming too widely available at a cheaper price through discount stores discourages full- price sales.
Sending products for recycling leaves them vulnerable to being stolen and sold on the black market.

Jasmine Bina, CEO of brand strategy agency Concept Bureau explains, "Typically, luxury brands rally around exclusivity to protect their business interests, namely intellectual property and preservation of brand equity(资产)."
She stated she had heard rumors of stock burning but not specific cases until this week.

passage.translation: 销毁未售出库存甚至未使用的成卷面料,对于奢侈品牌来说是司空见惯的做法。通过折扣店以更低价格大量销售会抑制全价销售。将产品送去回收会使其面临被盗并在黑市上出售的风险。品牌战略机构Concept Bureau的首席执行官Jasmine Bina解释道:"通常,奢侈品牌围绕排他性来保护其商业利益,即知识产权和品牌资产的保值。"她表示自己之前听说过焚烧库存的传闻,但直到本周才听说具体案例。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: Another reason for the commonplace practice is a financial incentive for brands exporting goods to America.
United States Customs states that if imported merchandise is unused and destroyed under their supervision, 99% of the duties, taxes or fees paid on the merchandise may be recovered.
It is incredibly difficult to calculate how much dead stock currently goes to waste.
While there are incentives to do it, there's no legal obligation to report it.

passage.translation: 这种普遍做法的另一个原因是品牌向美国出口商品时的财务激励。美国海关规定,如果进口商品未经使用并在其监督下销毁,则可退回该商品所支付关税、税费的99%。目前极难计算有多少滞销库存被浪费。虽然有激励措施去做这件事,但并没有报告的法律义务。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: A source, who chose to remain anonymous, shared her experience working in a Burberry store in New York in October 2016.
"My job was to toss items in boxes so they could be sent to be burned.
It was killing me inside because all that leather and fur went to waste and animals had died for nothing.
I couldn't stay there any longer, their business practices threw me off the roof."
In May this year, Burberry announced it was taking fur out of its catwalk shows and reviewing its use elsewhere in the business.
"Even though we asked the management, they refused to give us detailed answers as to why they would do this with their collection," continued the source, who left her role within two weeks.
She has since worked with another high-profile, luxury label.

passage.translation: 一位选择匿名的消息人士分享了她2016年10月在纽约一家Burberry门店工作的经历。"我的工作是把物品扔进箱子里,这样它们就能被送去焚烧。这让我内心备受煎熬,因为所有那些皮革和毛皮都被浪费了,动物们白白死去。我无法再待在那里,他们的商业做法让我彻底崩溃。"今年5月,Burberry宣布将不再在时装秀中使用毛皮,并审查其在业务其他方面的使用情况。"尽管我们询问了管理层,但他们拒绝向我们详细解释为什么要这样处理他们的系列产品,"这位在两周内离职的消息人士继续说道。此后她在另一家知名奢侈品牌工作。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: In an online forum post, which asked if it's true that Louis Vuitton burned its bags, Ahmed Bouchfaa, who claimed to work for Louis Vuitton, responded that the brand holds sales of old stock for staff members twice a year.
Items which have still not sold after several sales are destroyed.
"Louis Vuitton doesn't have public sales.
They either sell a product at a given price or discontinue it.
This is to make sure that everybody pays the same price for an item," he says.
He goes on to disclose the strict guidelines around the employee sales: "You may buy gifts for someone, but they track each item, and if your gift ends up online they know who to ask."
One investor commenting on the Burberry figures was reportedly outraged that the unsold goods were not even offered to investors before they were destroyed.

passage.translation: 在一个在线论坛帖子中,有人问Louis Vuitton是否真的焚烧其手袋,自称为Louis Vuitton工作的Ahmed Bouchfaa回应称,该品牌每年为员工举办两次旧库存促销活动。经过几次促销后仍未售出的物品会被销毁。"Louis Vuitton不进行公开促销。他们要么以给定价格出售产品,要么停产。这是为了确保每个人为同一件商品支付相同的价格,"他说。他接着披露了员工促销的严格准则:"你可以买礼物送人,但他们会追踪每件商品,如果你的礼物最终出现在网上,他们知道该问谁。"据报道,一位对Burberry数据发表评论的投资者对未售出商品在被销毁前甚至没有提供给投资者感到愤怒。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: Richemont, who owns several luxury brands, hit the headlines in May for taking back £437 million of watches for destruction in the last two years to avoid marked-down prices.
It's not just luxury brands either.
In October last year, a Danish TV show exposed H&M for burning 12 tonnes of unsold clothing since 2013.

In a statement, the high street retailer defended itself by saying that the burnt clothing had failed safety tests: "The products to which the media are referring have been tested in external laboratories.
The test results show that one of the products is mold infested and the other product contains levels of lead that are too high.
Those products have rightly been stopped in accordance with our safety routines."
In March, a report revealed that H&M was struggling with $4.3 billion worth of unsold stock.
The brand told The New York Times that the plan was to reduce prices to move the stock, arguably encouraging consumers to buy and throw away with little thought.

passage.translation: 拥有多个奢侈品牌的Richemont在5月份因在过去两年中收回价值4.37亿英镑的手表进行销毁以避免降价而成为头条新闻。不仅仅是奢侈品牌如此。去年10月,一档丹麦电视节目曝光H&M自2013年以来焚烧了12吨未售出服装。在一份声明中,这家快时尚零售商为自己辩护称被焚烧的服装未通过安全测试:"媒体所指的产品已在外部实验室进行了测试。测试结果显示,其中一款产品受到霉菌感染,另一款产品的铅含量过高。根据我们的安全规程,这些产品已被正确拦截。"3月份,一份报告显示H&M正面临价值43亿美元的未售出库存困境。该品牌告诉《纽约时报》,计划是降价以清理库存,这无疑鼓励消费者不假思索地购买和丢弃。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: Over-production is perhaps the biggest concern for Burberry.

While there has been much outrage at the elitist connotation of burning goods rather than making them affordable, executives at the British fashion house are no doubt struggling to defend how they miscalculated production.
The waste has been put down to burning old cosmetic stock to make way for their new beauty range.
However, while the value of destroyed stock is up from £26.9 million last year, it's an even more significant increase from 2016's figure of £18.8 million, highlighting that this is an ongoing issue.

passage.translation: 过度生产或许是Burberry最大的问题。尽管人们对焚烧商品而非使其变得平价的精英主义含义表示强烈愤怒,但这家英国时装公司的高管们无疑难以为他们对生产的错误估算进行辩护。这些浪费被归咎于焚烧旧化妆品库存以为新美妆系列腾出空间。然而,虽然销毁库存的价值从去年的2690万英镑上升,但相比2016年的1880万英镑更是大幅增长,这凸显出这是一个持续存在的问题。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: In September 2016, Burberry switched to a "see now, buy now" catwalk show format.
The move was a switch to leverage on the coverage of their fashion week show to make stock available immediately to consumers.
This is opposed to the traditional format of presenting to the industry, taking orders for production and becoming available in six months' time.

While Burberry announced "record-breaking" online reach and engagement, there has been little evidence to suggest that the strategy has had a significant effect on sales, particularly as the hype(炒作) slows across the season.
In February they made adjustments to the format, dropping some catwalk items immediately and promising that others would launch in the coming months.

passage.translation: 2016年9月,Burberry转向"即看即买"的时装秀形式。此举旨在利用时装周秀场的报道覆盖面,使库存立即向消费者开放。这与传统模式相反,传统模式是向业界展示、接受生产订单并在六个月后上市。尽管Burberry宣布了"破纪录"的在线覆盖率和参与度,但几乎没有证据表明该策略对销售产生了显著影响,特别是随着整个季度炒作热度下降。今年2月,他们对这一形式进行了调整,立即下架部分秀场单品,并承诺其他单品将在未来几个月推出。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: In a statement, Burberry denied that switching to "see now, buy now" has had an impact on waste.

This is a core part of our strategy and we have forged partnerships and committed support to innovative organizations to help reach this goal."

passage.translation: 在一份声明中,Burberry否认转向"即看即买"对浪费产生了影响。一位Burberry发言人进一步表示:"在必须处理产品的情况下,我们会以负责任的方式进行。我们始终在寻求减少和再利用废弃物的方法。这是我们战略的核心部分,我们已经建立了合作伙伴关系并承诺支持创新组织,以帮助实现这一目标。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: One such partnership is with Elvis & Kresse, an accessories brand working with reclaimed materials.

passage.translation: 其中一个合作伙伴是Elvis & Kresse,一个使用回收材料的配饰品牌。联合创始人Kresse Wesling说:"去年年底,我们与Burberry基金会启动了一项雄心勃勃的五年合作伙伴关系。其主要目标是扩大我们的皮革回收项目,从Burberry皮革制品生产的边角料开始。我们正在不懈努力扩展我们的解决方案,并欢迎任何人来我们的工作室参观我们正在做的事情。"目前,该合作伙伴关系仅解决生产阶段的废弃物问题,而非未售出商品。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: While these are honorable schemes, it makes it harder for Burberry to defend these latest figures.

sentences.text: Bina believes that brands need to readdress their exclusivity tactic.

That's the challenge that traditional luxury brands will have to contend with in the mid- to long-term future."
