**题目译文**
多年来一直存在争论,即谁应该为Notre Dame大教堂的修复买单。
**锚点** 多年来争论谁出钱修缮
**定位** 这座大教堂由法国国家所有，多年来一直处于一场长期纠纷的中心：到底应由谁来出资修缮其坍塌的楼梯、剥落的雕像和裂缝的墙体。
**改写** There has been argument over the years ↔ has been at the centre of a years-long dispute同义名词 + 时间表达等值as to who should pay for the restoration of Notre Dame Cathedral ↔over who should finance restoration work动词 finance ↔ pay for 同义 + 介词等值
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
C C 段讲的是 French business leaders and global corporations announced they would donate to a restoration campaign launched by the president，是 周二几个小时内承诺捐款 这种 即时、新发生 的事件；与题干 多年来争论 在时间属性上完全不同。French business leaders and global corporations announced they would donate to a restoration campaign launched by the president, Emmanuel Macron
questions.quote: The cathedral is owned by the French state and has been at the centre of a years-long dispute over who should finance restoration work of the collapsing staircases, crumbling statues and cracked walls.

questions.prompt: News of the Notre Dame Cathedral catastrophe instantly caught media attention throughout the world.
questions.explanation:
**答案** G 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
Notre Dame大教堂灾难的消息立即引起了全世界媒体的关注。
**锚点** 灾难新闻瞬间引起全球媒体关注
**定位** 事实上，几分钟之内，这场大火就占据了全球各大报纸和电视网的头条。
**改写** News of the Notre Dame Cathedral catastrophe ↔ the fire事件 ↔ 事件本身的同义指代instantly caught media attention throughout the world ↔within minutes the fire occupied headlines of every major global newspaper and television network副词 ↔ 时间窗 + 抽象 ↔ 具体改写
questions.quote: Indeed, within minutes the fire occupied headlines of every major global newspaper and television network.

title: How Marconi Gave Us the Wireless World

passage.label: A

sentences.text: A hundred years before iconic figures like Bill Gates and Steve Jobs permeated our lives, an Irish- Italian inventor laid the foundation of the communication explosion of the 21st century.
Guglielmo Marconi was arguably the first truly global figure in modern communication.
Not only was he the first to communicate globally, he was the first to think globally about communication.
Marconi may not have been the greatest inventor of his time, but more than anyone else, he brought about a fundamental shift in the way we communicate.

passage.translation: 在Bill Gates和Steve Jobs这样的标志性人物渗透到我们生活中的一百年前,一位爱尔兰裔意大利发明家为21世纪的通信大爆炸奠定了基础。Guglielmo Marconi可以说是现代通信领域第一位真正具有全球影响力的人物。他不仅是第一个实现全球通信的人,也是第一个从全球视角思考通信问题的人。Marconi也许不是他那个时代最伟大的发明家,但他比任何人都更能促成我们通信方式的根本性转变。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: Today's globally networked media and communication system has its origins in the 19th century, when, for the first time, messages were sent electronically across great distances.
The telegraph, the telephone, and radio were the obvious predecessors of the Internet, iPods, and mobile phones.
What made the link from then to now was the development of wireless communication.
Marconi was the first to develop and perfect this system, using the recently-discovered "air waves" that make up the electromagnetic spectrum.

passage.translation: 当今全球网络化的媒体和通信系统起源于19世纪,那时消息第一次通过电子方式远距离传送。电报、电话和无线电显然是互联网、iPod和移动电话的前身。从那时到现在的联系纽带是无线通信的发展。Marconi是第一个开发并完善这一系统的人,他利用了最近发现的构成电磁波谱的"空气波"。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: Between 1896, when he applied for his first patent in England at the age of 22, and his death in Italy in 1937, Marconi was at the center of every major innovation in electronic communication.

He was also a skilled and sophisticated organizer, an entrepreneurial innovator, who mastered the use of corporate strategy, media relations, government lobbying, international diplomacy, patents, and prosecution.
Marconi was really interested in only one thing: the extension of mobile, personal, long- distance communication to the ends of the earth (and beyond, if we can believe some reports).
Some like to refer to him as a genius, but if there was any genius to Marconi it was this vision.

passage.translation: 从1896年他22岁时在英国申请第一项专利,到1937年在意大利去世,Marconi一直处于电子通信领域每一项重大创新的中心。他还是一位技能娴熟、老练精明的组织者,一位企业家式的创新者,精通企业战略、媒体关系、政府游说、国际外交、专利和诉讼的运用。Marconi真正感兴趣的只有一件事:将移动的、个人的、远距离通信延伸到地球的尽头(如果我们相信某些报道的话,甚至延伸到地球之外)。有些人喜欢称他为天才,但如果说Marconi有什么天才之处,那就是这种愿景。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: In 1901 he succeeded in signaling across the Atlantic, from the west coast of England to Newfoundland in the USA, despite the claims of science that it could not be done.
In 1924 he convinced the British government to encircle the world with a chain of wireless stations using the latest technology that he had devised, shortwave radio.
There are some who say Marconi lost his edge when commercial broadcasting came along; he didn't see that radio could or should be used to frivolous(无聊的) ends.

In one of his last public speeches, a radio broadcast to the United States in March 1937, he deplored that broadcasting had become a one-way means of communication and foresaw it moving in another direction, toward communication as a means of exchange.
That was visionary genius.

passage.translation: 1901年,尽管科学界声称这不可能做到,他还是成功地实现了跨大西洋信号传输,从英国西海岸传到美国纽芬兰。1924年,他说服英国政府用他设计的最新技术——短波无线电,在全球建立一个无线电台链。有人说当商业广播出现时Marconi失去了他的优势;他没有看到无线电可以或应该用于无聊的目的。在他最后一次公开演讲中,即1937年3月向美国进行的一次无线电广播中,他对广播已经成为一种单向通信方式表示遗憾,并预见它将朝另一个方向发展,即通信作为一种交流手段。这是富有远见的天才之举。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Marconi's career was devoted to making wireless communication happen cheaply, efficiently, smoothly, and with an elegance that would appear to be intuitive and uncomplicated to the user- friendly, if you will.

There is a direct connection from Marconi to today's social media, search engines, and program streaming that can best be summed up by an admittedly provocative exclamation: the 20th century did not exist.
In a sense, Marconi's vision jumped from his time to our own.

passage.translation: Marconi的职业生涯致力于使无线通信以廉价、高效、顺畅的方式实现,并且具有一种优雅,这种优雅对用户来说似乎是直观和简单的——如果你愿意的话,可以说是用户友好的。从Marconi到今天的社交媒体、搜索引擎和流媒体节目之间存在着直接的联系,这种联系可以用一句公认具有挑衅性的感叹来概括:20世纪并不存在。从某种意义上说,Marconi的愿景从他的时代跳跃到了我们的时代。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: Marconi invented the idea of global communication—or, more straightforwardly, globally networked, mobile, wireless communication.
Initially, this was wireless Morse code telegraphy(电报通讯), the principal communication technology of his day.
Marconi was the first to develop a practical method for wireless telegraphy using radio waves.

He borrowed technical details from many sources, but what set him apart was a self-confident vision of the power of communication technology on the one hand, and, on the other, of the steps that needed to be taken to consolidate his own position as a player in that field.
Tracing Marconi's lifeline leads us into the story of modern communication itself.
There were other important figures, but Marconi towered over them all in reach, power, and influence, as well as in the grip he had on the popular imagination of his time.
Marconi was quite simply the central figure in the emergence of a modern understanding of communication.

passage.translation: Marconi发明了全球通信的理念——或者更直白地说,全球网络化的、移动的、无线的通信。最初,这是无线摩尔斯电码电报通讯,是他那个时代的主要通信技术。Marconi是第一个开发出利用无线电波进行无线电报通讯的实用方法的人。他从许多来源借鉴了技术细节,但使他与众不同的是,一方面他对通信技术力量有着自信的愿景,另一方面他知道需要采取哪些步骤来巩固自己在该领域的参与者地位。追溯Marconi的人生轨迹会把我们引向现代通信本身的故事。虽然还有其他重要人物,但Marconi在影响范围、权力和影响力方面都凌驾于他们所有人之上,在他那个时代对大众想象力的掌控也是如此。Marconi简直就是现代通信理解形成过程中的核心人物。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: In his lifetime, Marconi foresaw the development of television and the fax machine, GPS, radar, and the portable hand-held telephone.
Two months before he died, newspapers were reporting that he was working on a "death ray," and that he had "killed a rat with an intricate device at a distance of three feet."
By then, anything Marconi said or did was newsworthy.
Stock prices rose or sank according to his pronouncements.
If Marconi said he thought it might rain, there was likely to be a run on umbrellas.

passage.translation: 在他的有生之年,Marconi预见了电视和传真机、GPS、雷达以及便携式手持电话的发展。在他去世前两个月,报纸报道说他正在研制一种"死亡射线",并且他"用一个复杂的装置在三英尺的距离外杀死了一只老鼠"。到那时,Marconi说的或做的任何事情都是有新闻价值的。股票价格会根据他的言论而涨跌。如果Marconi说他认为可能会下雨,很可能就会出现抢购雨伞的情况。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Marconi's biography is also a story about choices and the motivations behind them.
At one level, Marconi could be fiercely autonomous and independent of the constraints of his own social class.
On another scale, he was a perpetual outsider.
Wherever he went, he was never "of" the group; he was always the "other," considered foreign in Britain, British in Italy, and "not American" in the United States.
At the same time, he also suffered tremendously from a need for acceptance that drove, and sometimes stained, every one of his relationships.

passage.translation: Marconi的传记也是一个关于选择及其背后动机的故事。在某种程度上,Marconi可以非常自主,不受自己社会阶层约束的限制。在另一个层面上,他是一个永久的局外人。无论他走到哪里,他都不"属于"那个群体;他总是"他者",在英国被认为是外国人,在意大利被认为是英国人,在美国被认为"不是美国人"。同时,他也极度渴望被接纳,这种需求驱动着,有时也玷污着他的每一段关系。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Marconi placed a permanent stamp on the way we live.

He was the first person to imagine a practical application for the wireless spectrum, and to develop it successfully into a global communication system—in both terms of the word; that is, worldwide and all-inclusive.

He was able to do this because of a combination of factors—most important, timing and opportunity—but the single- mindedness and determination with which he carried out his self-imposed mission was fundamentally character-based; millions of Marconi's contemporaries had the same class, gender, race, and colonial privilege as he, but only a handful did anything with it.

Marconi needed to achieve the goal that was set in his mind as an adolescent; by the time he reached adulthood, he understood, intuitively, that in order to have an impact he had to both develop an independent economic base and align himself with political power.
Disciplined, uncritical loyalty to political power became his compass for the choices he had to make.

passage.translation: Marconi在我们的生活方式上留下了永久的印记。他是第一个想象无线电波谱实际应用的人,并成功地将其发展成为一个全球通信系统——这个词的两层含义都适用,即世界范围的和包容一切的。他之所以能做到这一点,是因为多种因素的结合——最重要的是时机和机遇——但他执行自己强加给自己的使命时的专一和决心从根本上是基于性格的;Marconi的数百万同时代人拥有与他相同的阶级、性别、种族和殖民特权,但只有少数人利用这些做了什么。Marconi需要实现青少年时期就在他脑海中确立的目标;到他成年时,他凭直觉明白,为了产生影响,他必须既发展独立的经济基础,又与政治权力结盟。对政治权力有纪律的、不加批判的忠诚成为他必须做出选择的指南针。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: At the same time, Marconi was uncompromisingly independent intellectually.

Shortly after Marconi's death, the nuclear physicist Enrico Fermi—soon to be the developer of the Manhattan Project—wrote that Marconi proved that theory and experimentation were complementary features of progress.

"Experience can rarely, unless guided by a theoretical concept, arrive at results of any great significance…on the other hand, an excessive trust in theoretical conviction would have prevented Marconi from persisting in experiments which were destined to bring about a revolution in the technique of radio-communications."
In other words, Marconi had the advantage of not being burdened by preconceived assumptions.

passage.translation: 同时,Marconi在智识上是毫不妥协地独立的。Marconi去世后不久,核物理学家Enrico Fermi——很快将成为曼哈顿计划的开发者——写道,Marconi证明了理论和实验是进步的互补特征。"除非有理论概念的指导,经验很少能取得任何重大意义的成果……另一方面,对理论信念的过度信任会阻止Marconi坚持那些注定要给无线电通信技术带来革命的实验。"换句话说,Marconi的优势在于他没有被先入为主的假设所束缚。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: The most controversial aspect of Marconi's life—and the reason why there has been no satisfying biography of Marconi until now—was his uncritical embrace of Benito Mussolini.
At first this was not problematic for him.
But as the regressive(倒退的) nature of Mussolini's regime became clear, he began to suffer a crisis of conscience.

However, after a lifetime of moving within the circles of power, he was unable to break with authority, and served Mussolini faithfully (as president of Italy's national research council and royal academy, as well as a member of the Fascist Grand Council) until the day he died—conveniently—in 1937, shortly before he would have had to take a stand in the conflict that consumed a world that he had, in part, created.

passage.translation: Marconi一生中最具争议的方面——也是直到现在都没有令人满意的Marconi传记的原因——是他对Benito Mussolini不加批判的拥护。起初这对他来说并不成问题。但随着Mussolini政权的倒退本质变得清晰,他开始经历良心危机。然而,在终生游走于权力圈子之后,他无法与权威决裂,并忠实地为Mussolini服务(担任意大利国家研究委员会和皇家学院主席,以及法西斯大议会成员),直到他去世的那一天——恰好——在1937年,就在他不得不在吞噬了一个他在某种程度上创造的世界的冲突中表明立场之前不久。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: Marconi was central to our present-day understanding of communication.
questions.explanation:
**答案** F 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
Marconi对我们当今对通信的理解起到了核心作用。
**锚点** 对现代通信的中心理解
**定位** 马可尼简直就是现代通信理解兴起过程中的中心人物。
**改写** central to our present-day understanding of communication ↔the central figure in the emergence of a modern understanding of communication central 一对一、present-day 等于 modern
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
A A 段虽然也是总评段，但说的是 laid the foundation of the communication explosion 与 the first truly global figure，强调的是奠基者与第一这一身份，并未提到 central to our present-day understanding 中的 central 与 understanding 这一组合。laid the foundation of the communication explosion of the 21st century
questions.quote: Marconi was quite simply the central figure in the emergence of a modern understanding of communication.

questions.prompt: As an adult, Marconi had an intuition that he had to be loyal to politicians in order to be influential.
questions.explanation:
**答案** I 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
作为成年人,Marconi有一种直觉,认为他必须忠于政治家才能具有影响力。
**锚点** 成年时直觉效忠政治家
**定位** 到成年时，他凭直觉就明白：要产生影响，他必须既建立独立的经济基础，又让自己与政治权力结盟。
**改写** As an adult ↔ by the time he reached adulthood成年的两种基础表达had an intuition ↔ understood, intuitively名词与副词的同根转换had to be loyal to politicians in order to be influential ↔in order to have an impact he had to both develop an independent economic base and align himself with political power结盟即忠诚、有影响即有效力
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
K K 段虽然也讲忠诚于政治（served Mussolini faithfully），但陈述句 had an intuition 强调的是认知形成阶段（成年时的直觉判断），K 段讲的是已成定局的具体效忠行为，时间维度与认知维度都不对应。after a lifetime of moving within the circles of power, he was unable to break with authority
questions.quote: by the time he reached adulthood, he understood, intuitively, that in order to have an impact he had to both develop an independent economic base and align himself with political power.

questions.prompt: Marconi disapproved of the use of wireless communication for commercial broadcasting.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
Marconi不赞成将无线通信用于商业广播。
**锚点** 反对将无线用于商业广播
**定位** 有人说当商业广播兴起时，马可尼已经落伍；他不认为广播可以或应该被用作无聊的目的。
**改写** disapproved of the use of wireless communication for commercial broadcasting ↔he didn't see that radio could or should be used to frivolous(无聊的) ends含蓄否定表达不赞成 + radio 即 wireless
questions.quote: There are some who say Marconi lost his edge when commercial broadcasting came along; he didn't see that radio could or should be used to frivolous(无聊的) ends.

questions.prompt: Marconi's example demonstrates that theoretical concepts and experiments complement each other in making progress in science and technology.
questions.explanation:
**答案** J 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
Marconi的例子表明,理论概念和实验在科学技术进步中相辅相成。
**锚点** 理论与实验互补
**定位** 马可尼证明了理论与实验是进步的互补特征。
**改写** theoretical concepts and experiments complement each other ↔theory and experimentation were complementary features of progress complement 同根 + theory/experimentation 同根making progress in science and technology ↔bring about a revolution in the technique of radio-communications进步与革命的同义概括
questions.quote: Marconi proved that theory and experimentation were complementary features of progress.

questions.prompt: Marconi's real interest lay in the development of worldwide wireless communication.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
Marconi真正的兴趣在于发展全球无线通信。
**锚点** 真正兴趣在全球无线通信
**定位** 马可尼真正关心的只有一件事：把移动、个人化、远距离通信延伸到地球的尽头（如果有报道可信的话，甚至更远）。
**改写** Marconi's real interest ↔ Marconi was really interested in only one thing real/really 同根 + only one thing 强化the development of worldwide wireless communication ↔the extension of mobile, personal, long-distance communication to the ends of the earth extension 即 development、to the ends of the earth 即 worldwide
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E E 段说 Marconi's career was devoted to making wireless communication happen cheaply, efficiently, smoothly，描述的是他职业生涯做无线通信的方式与品质标准，并未用 real interest 这种动机性表述去定位他唯一关心的事。Marconi's career was devoted to making wireless communication happen cheaply, efficiently, smoothly
questions.quote: Marconi was really interested in only one thing: the extension of mobile, personal, long- distance communication to the ends of the earth (and beyond, if we can believe some reports).

questions.prompt: Marconi spent his whole life making wireless communication simple to use.
questions.explanation:
**答案** E 段（弱锚点）
**题目译文**
Marconi毕生致力于使无线通信简单易用。
**锚点** 毕生让无线通信易用
**定位** 马可尼的职业生涯致力于让无线通信变得便宜、高效、流畅，且优雅得在用户看来直觉而不复杂——也就是用户友好。
**改写** spent his whole life ↔ Marconi's career was devoted to career devoted 即 spent whole life making wireless communication simple to use ↔making wireless communication happen cheaply, efficiently, smoothly, and with an elegance that would appear to be intuitive and uncomplicated to the user-friendly user-friendly 与 simple to use 完全同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
C C 段 Marconi was really interested in only one thing: the extension of mobile, personal, long-distance communication to the ends of the earth 讲的是把通信延伸到多远，是范围维度；陈述句 simple to use 强调的是让用户用起来简单，是用户体验维度。the extension of mobile, personal, long-distance communication to the ends of the earth
questions.quote: Marconi's career was devoted to making wireless communication happen cheaply, efficiently, smoothly, and with an elegance that would appear to be intuitive and uncomplicated to the user-friendly, if you will.

questions.prompt: Because of his long-time connection with people in power, Marconi was unable to cut himself off from the fascist regime in Italy.
questions.explanation:
**答案** K 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
由于长期与当权者的联系,Marconi无法与意大利的法西斯政权切断关系。
**锚点** 无法与意大利法西斯政权切割
**定位** 然而，经过一生在权力圈中游走，他已无法与权威决裂，忠诚服侍墨索里尼（任意大利国家研究委员会与皇家学院主席、法西斯大议会成员），直到 1937 年他便利地去世——就在他本会被迫表态于那场吞噬世界的冲突之前不久，而这世界一定程度上正是由他参与创造的。
**改写** his long-time connection with people in power ↔a lifetime of moving within the circles of power long-time 等于 lifetime、people in power 等于 circles of power unable to cut himself off from the fascist regime in Italy ↔he was unable to break with authority, and served Mussolini faithfully cut off 等于 break with、fascist regime 等于 Mussolini
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
I I 段 align himself with political power 描述的是马可尼成年时的认知决定（决定要靠拢政治），属于动机层；陈述句 unable to cut himself off 是后期已成定局的无能层，是 K 段才有的内容。align himself with political power
questions.quote: However, after a lifetime of moving within the circles of power, he was unable to break with authority, and served Mussolini faithfully (as president of Italy's national research council and royal academy, as well as a member of the Fascist Grand Council) until the day he died—conveniently—in 1937, shortly before he would have had to take a stand in the conflict that consumed a world that he had, in part, created.

questions.prompt: In his later years, Marconi exerted a tremendous influence on all aspects of people's life.
questions.explanation:
**答案** G 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
在晚年,Marconi对人们生活的各个方面都产生了巨大影响。
**锚点** 晚年对生活各方面巨大影响
**定位** 到那时，马可尼说什么做什么都是新闻；股价随他的言论涨跌；他若说可能下雨，就会有抢购雨伞的风潮。
**改写** In his later years ↔ Two months before he died, newspapers were reporting去世前两月即晚年exerted a tremendous influence on all aspects of people's life ↔Stock prices rose or sank according to his pronouncements. If Marconi said he thought it might rain, there was likely to be a run on umbrellas.抽象概括由两个具体例证承载
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
A A 段 A hundred years before iconic figures like Bill Gates and Steve Jobs permeated our lives 讲的是百年尺度的奠基影响，不是 later years 这一晚年具体时段的影响。A hundred years before iconic figures like Bill Gates and Steve Jobs permeated our lives
questions.quote: By then, anything Marconi said or did was newsworthy. Stock prices rose or sank according to his pronouncements. If Marconi said he thought it might rain, there was likely to be a run on umbrellas.

questions.prompt: What connected the 19th century and our present time was the development of wireless communication.
questions.explanation:
**答案** B 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
连接19世纪和我们当今时代的是无线通信的发展。
**锚点** 无线通信连接 19 世纪与现在
**定位** 把那时和现在连接起来的，正是无线通信的发展。
**改写** What connected the 19th century and our present time ↔ What made the link from then to now connected 等于 made the link、present time 等于 now the development of wireless communication ↔ the development of wireless communication原文整短语逐字复现
questions.quote: What made the link from then to now was the development of wireless communication.

questions.prompt: Despite his autonomy, Marconi felt alienated and suffered from a lack of acceptance.
questions.explanation:
**答案** H 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
尽管拥有自主权,Marconi仍感到疏离并饱受缺乏认同之苦。
**锚点** 自主却疏离、苦于不被接纳
**定位** 一方面，马可尼可以激烈地自主，独立于他自身阶级的束缚；另一方面，他又是永远的外人。无论走到哪儿，他都不属于那个群体；永远是那个他者——在英国被视为外国人、在意大利被视为英国人、在美国被视为非美国人。与此同时，他也极度苦于对被接纳的渴求，这种渴求驱动并有时玷污了他的每一段关系。
**改写** Despite his autonomy ↔Marconi could be fiercely autonomous and independent of the constraints of his own social class autonomy 与 autonomous 同根felt alienated↔he was a perpetual outsider … he was never "of" the group; he was always the "other," outsider/other 即 alienated suffered from a lack of acceptance↔he also suffered tremendously from a need for acceptance渴求接纳即缺乏接纳的正话反说
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
K K 段 he began to suffer a crisis of conscience 讲的是政治选择上的良心冲突，不是alienated 这种社会身份疏离感，也不涉及 lack of acceptance 这种渴求接纳。he began to suffer a crisis of conscience
questions.quote: At one level, Marconi could be fiercely autonomous and independent of the constraints of his own social class. On another scale, he was a perpetual outsider. Wherever he went, he was never "of" the group; he was always the "other," considered foreign in Britain, British in Italy, and "not American" in the United States. At the same time, he also suffered tremendously from a need for acceptance that drove, and sometimes stained, every one of his relationships.

title: Emulating your conversation partner's actions is a common…

sentences.text: Emulating your conversation partner's actions is a common human behavior classified as "mirroring" and has been known and studied by psychologists for years.
We all tend to subconsciously copy gestures of people we like.
But why do we act like this?

passage.translation: 模仿对话伙伴的行为是一种常见的人类行为,被归类为"镜像效应",心理学家多年来一直对此有所了解并进行研究。我们都倾向于下意识地模仿我们喜欢的人的手势。但我们为什么会这样做呢?

sentences.text: As a rule, mirroring means that conversationalists enjoy their communication and that there's a certain level of agreement between them.
The topic of discussion is equally interesting for both and they know their interests meet.

passage.translation: 通常,镜像效应意味着交谈者享受他们的交流,并且他们之间存在一定程度的共识。讨论的话题对双方都同样有趣,他们知道彼此的兴趣相投。

sentences.text: Repeating someone's behavior is typical of talented communicators, not always because the person is sympathetic, but because there is a goal to be achieved.
This way new idols have been brought to the stage: politicians, celebrities, and other big names.
Popular culture makes people want to look popular, and act and speak like popular people.

passage.translation: 重复他人的行为是优秀沟通者的典型特征,并非总是因为这个人富有同情心,而是因为有目标需要实现。通过这种方式,新的偶像被推上了舞台:政治家、名人和其他大人物。流行文化使人们想要看起来受欢迎,并像受欢迎的人那样行事和说话。

sentences.text: Nowadays celebrities steal lyrics from each other and struggle with copyright violation accusations or straightforwardly claim themselves to be the authors, even though all the work was done by other people.

passage.translation: 如今,名人之间相互窃取歌词,并陷入侵犯版权的指控之中,或者直接声称自己是作者,尽管所有工作都是由其他人完成的。

sentences.text: Among celebrities, it's trendy nowadays to use their own speech writers as politicians do.
The so-called "ghostwriting" can take various forms: books, articles, autobiographies, and even social media posts.

passage.translation: 在名人中,如今像政治家那样使用自己的演讲稿撰写人已成为一种潮流。所谓的"代笔"可以采取多种形式:书籍、文章、自传,甚至社交媒体帖子。

sentences.text: Who is a true copycat(抄袭者) and who gets copycatted?
Sometimes, it is a hard nut to crack without an expert's help.
But new authorship defending methods based on identifying individual writing patterns are already here.
Their aim is to protect intellectual property.
Using scientific methods, some of them can define authorship with 85% accuracy.

passage.translation: 谁是真正的抄袭者,谁被抄袭?有时,没有专家的帮助很难弄清楚。但基于识别个人写作模式的新作者身份鉴定方法已经出现。它们的目的是保护知识产权。使用科学方法,其中一些方法可以以85%的准确率确定作者身份。

sentences.text: Writing is not an easy craft to master.
If you want to write like a professional without plagiarism(抄袭), there are a few lessons to learn and the first one is: "Copy from one, it's plagiarism; copy from two, it's research."
The correct interpretation of this statement is not about copying, but rather about creating your own style.
When you study an author's writing style, don't stop on a single one, but explore numerous styles instead.
Examine types of sentences they use, pay attention to their metaphors, and focus on stories you feel you could write a pretty cool sequel(续篇) to.

passage.translation: 写作并非一门容易掌握的技艺。如果你想像专业人士那样写作而不抄袭,有几个教训需要学习,第一个是:"从一个人那里抄袭,那是抄袭;从两个人那里抄袭,那是研究。"对这句话的正确理解不是关于抄袭,而是关于创造自己的风格。当你研究某位作者的写作风格时,不要只停留在一个人身上,而要探索众多风格。审视他们使用的句子类型,关注他们的隐喻,并专注于那些你觉得可以为之写出很酷续篇的故事。

sentences.text: Imitation is rather paradoxical.
As an integral part of learning, it brings about positive changes, making people develop and grow.
However, it may do a lot of harm.
Copying someone's thoughts, ideas or inventions is completely unacceptable.
It infringes on intellectual property rights of others.

passage.translation: 模仿颇具矛盾性。作为学习的一个组成部分,它带来积极的变化,使人们发展和成长。然而,它也可能造成很大的危害。抄袭他人的思想、创意或发明是完全不可接受的。这侵犯了他人的知识产权。

sentences.text: Still, many things we do are about copying others one way or another.
So if you want to compliment someone on the work they have done and imitate it, just make sure you do it the right way to avoid committing plagiarism.

passage.translation: 然而,我们所做的许多事情都以某种方式涉及模仿他人。因此,如果你想赞美某人所做的工作并模仿它,只需确保你以正确的方式进行,以避免犯下抄袭行为。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What do people tend to do while engaging in a conversation?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
人们在进行对话时往往会做什么?
A) 以这样或那样的方式重复对方说的话。
B) 尽可能关注双方共同感兴趣的话题。
C) 在对方不知情的情况下模仿对方的手势。
D) 仔细观察对方如何运用手势。
**判型** 题干 What do people tend to do while engaging in a conversation? 是 What...do 句式，问的是客观行为，无 infer/imply/mainly 等推断或主旨信号词。
**拆句** What do people tend to do while engaging in a conversation? 主干是 What do people tend to do，宾语从句式 What 提问；while engaging in a conversation 是分词短语作时间状语，意为"当处于对话中时"，无陷阱。
**定位** 我们都会下意识地模仿自己喜欢之人的手势。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念Repeat what their partners say one way or another 把原文的 copy gestures（模仿动作）偷换成 Repeat what...say（重复话语），原文谈的是肢体动作而非言语内容。
B) 答非所问Focus as much as possible on topics of mutual interest 是第二段 The topic of discussion is equally interesting for both 的同义改写，属于 52 题的话题范围，与51 题问的"做什么"无关。
C) ✓ 正确subconsciously copy gestures ↔ Imitate their partners' gestures without their knowing it C 项同时复现"模仿手势"与"无意识"两个预判要素，且无额外添加成分，与定位句严格等值。
D) 偷换概念Observe carefully how their partners make use of gestures 把原文动词 copy（模仿）偷换成 Observe（观察）——观察是单方注视、不构成模仿行为，性质完全不同。
questions.quote: We all tend to subconsciously copy gestures of people we like.

options.text: Repeat what their partners say one way or another.
Focus as much as possible on topics of mutual interest.
Imitate their partners' gestures without their knowing it.
Observe carefully how their partners make use of gestures.

questions.prompt: When does mirroring usually take place in a conversation?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
镜像通常在对话中的什么时候发生?
A) 当双方彼此同情时。
B) 当双方有很多共同点时。
C) 当双方都做出有趣的贡献时。
D) 当双方试图寻求共同点时。
**判型** When does mirroring usually take place in a conversation? 用 When 直接问mirroring 发生的条件，是客观事实题。
**拆句** When does mirroring usually take place in a conversation? 一般疑问倒装结构，主语mirroring，谓语 take place，副词 usually 修饰频度；句式平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 一般而言，mirroring 意味着对话双方享受彼此的交流，并且双方之间存在一定程度的共识。讨论的话题对双方同样有趣，他们知道彼此兴趣相合。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反When both sides are sympathetic with each other 利用 not always because the person is sympathetic 制造干扰；原文恰恰说"并非总是因为同情"——A 把这层被否定的说法当成 mirroring 发生的条件，与原文相反。
B) ✓ 正确there's a certain level of agreement between them. The topic of discussion is equally interesting for both and they know their interests meet↔ both sides have a lot of things in common predict 的"双方兴趣/共识相合"正是"have a lot of things in common"的内核，B 同时覆盖"agreement"与"interests meet"两点，匹配度最高。
C) 偷换概念When both sides make interesting contributions 把原文 The topic of discussion is equally interesting（话题本身有趣）偷换为"双方各自贡献有趣的内容"，主语和性质都变了——原文谈的是话题本身的属性，不是参与者的输出。
D) 偷换概念When both sides try to seek common ground 把原文"已存在共识"（there's a certain level of agreement）偷换为"尝试寻求共识"——try to seek 是"过程"，原文是"结果"，时态/状态偷换。
questions.quote: As a rule, mirroring means that conversationalists enjoy their communication and that there's a certain level of agreement between them. The topic of discussion is equally interesting for both and they know their interests meet.

options.text: When both sides are sympathetic with each other.
When both sides have a lot of things in common.
When both sides make interesting contributions.
When both sides try to seek common ground.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about popular culture?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于流行文化我们了解到什么?
A) 它鼓励人们模仿。
B) 它主要吸引知名人士。
C) 它使年轻人熟悉他们的偶像。
D) 它可以改变人们的认知模式。
**判型** What do we learn about popular culture? 表面是"了解到什么"，实质问"原文对该概念是怎么说的"，仍是细节题。
**拆句** What do we learn about popular culture? What 引导宾语从句作问，learn about 介词短语带宾语，结构简单无陷阱。
**定位** 流行文化让人想要看起来很受欢迎，并像受欢迎的人那样行事、说话。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确makes people want to look popular, and act and speak like popular people ↔It encourages people to imitate predict 的"促使/鼓励模仿"正是 A 的字面表达，且 imitate 涵盖 act and speak like popular people 全部具体行为，匹配最严格。
B) 张冠李戴It appeals mostly to big names 把流行文化的影响对象偷换为"big names"（大牌名人），但原文"big names"是被模仿的对象，不是流行文化吸引的对象——主客关系彻底颠倒。
C) 无中生有It acquaints young people with their idols 中"young people"和"acquaint with idols"原文均无对应——原文未限定年龄，也未谈"让人认识偶像"。
D) 过度推断It can change people's mode of cognition 把原文"想模仿名人言行"过度推至"改变认知模式"——认知模式是心理学层面的根本性变化，远超原文"行为/语言层面的模仿"。
questions.quote: Popular culture makes people want to look popular, and act and speak like popular people.

options.text: It encourages people to imitate.
It appeals mostly to big names.
It acquaints young people with their idols.
It can change people's mode of cognition.

questions.prompt: Why is the saying "copy from two, it's research" a lesson to learn?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
为什么"从一个人那里抄袭是剽窃,从两个人那里抄袭是研究"这句话值得学习?
A) 它有助于形成自己的写作风格。
B) 它有助于保护个人的知识产权。
C) 它培养对专业写作的正确理解。
D) 它使人能够为著名故事写出引人入胜的续集。
**判型** Why is the saying “copy from two, it's research” a lesson to learn? 用 Why 直接问原文对该格言的解释，不带 infer/imply，按细节题处理。
**拆句** Why is the saying “copy from two, it's research” a lesson to learn? 主干 Why is the saying a lesson to learn；the saying 后接同位语"copy from two, it's research” 解释 the saying 的内容；a lesson to learn 是表语，to learn 是不定式作后置定语，修饰 lesson。
**定位** "抄一家是抄袭，抄两家是研究。" 这句话的正确解读不是关于抄袭，而是关于创造你自己的风格。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确not about copying, but rather about creating your own style ↔It facilitates the creation of one's own writing style选项 A 抓住 not...but 结构中"but rather"那一层的正面信息，并把动名词转为名词化短语——这是格言题的标准改写。
B) 答非所问It helps to protect one's intellectual property rights 来自 Their aim is to protect intellectual property.——那是讲鉴权工具的目的，不是格言的教益。属相邻话题搬运。
C) 偷换概念It fosters correct interpretation of professional writing 把原文 The correct interpretation 中描述"对该格言的正确解读"反过来当成"格言促进对专业写作的正确解读"——主客颠倒。
D) 以偏概全It enables one to write intriguing sequels to famous stories 利用 focus on stories you feel you could write a pretty cool sequel(续篇) to 的具体例子来冒充格言的教益——sequel 只是"探索写作"的一个具体方式，不是格言的核心。
questions.quote: "Copy from one, it's plagiarism; copy from two, it's research." The correct interpretation of this statement is not about copying, but rather about creating your own style.

options.text: It facilitates the creation of one's own writing style.
It helps to protect one's intellectual property rights.
It fosters correct interpretation of professional writing.
It enables one to write intriguing sequels to famous stories.

questions.prompt: Why does the author say imitation is rather paradoxical?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
为什么作者说模仿相当矛盾?
A) 它容易产生不同的解释。
B) 它总的来说是一种必要之恶。
C) 它可能引发无休止的争论。
D) 它可能既有害又有益。
**判型** Why does the author say imitation is rather paradoxical? 用 Why 问作者为何这样说，原文紧跟该评价后会用 However/but 等显性给出两面性依据。
**拆句** Why does the author say imitation is rather paradoxical? Why 引导原因疑问，宾语从句 imitation is rather paradoxical 作 say 的宾语；rather 副词加强 paradoxical 的程度，意为"相当矛盾"。
**定位** 模仿相当矛盾。作为学习不可或缺的一部分，它带来积极变化，让人成长进步。然而，它也可能造成很多危害。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念It is liable to different interpretations 把"自身两面性"偷换为"被人有不同解读"——原文谈的是 imitation 本身既有好处也有害，不是说人们对它解读不一。
B) 过度推断It is by and large a necessary evil 把原文"利弊并存"过度推断为"必要之恶"——necessary evil 暗含"虽然有害但不可避免"，原文并未说"模仿不可避免"或"必须容忍这种害处"。
C) 无中生有It can give rise to endless disputes 中"无休止争议"在原文中无任何对应——原文只说有害、不说"引发争议"，更未提"无休止"。
D) ✓ 正确it brings about positive changes, making people develop and grow. However, it may do a lot of harm↔ It may do harm as well as good predict 要求"既有利又有害"两面同时落地，D 用 harm as well as good 一次性涵盖，完美贴合 paradoxical 的语义内核。
questions.quote: Imitation is rather paradoxical. As an integral part of learning, it brings about positive changes, making people develop and grow. However, it may do a lot of harm.

options.text: It is liable to different interpretations.
It is by and large a necessary evil.
It can give rise to endless disputes.
It may do harm as well as good.

title: You can't see it, smell it, or hear…

sentences.text: You can't see it, smell it, or hear it, and people disagree on how precisely to define it, or where exactly it comes from.
It isn't a school subject or an academic discipline, but it can be learned.
It is a quality that is required of artists, but it is also present in the lives of scientists and entrepreneurs.
All of us benefit from it and we thrive mentally and spiritually when we are able to wield it.
It is a delicate thing, easily stamped out; in fact, it flourishes most fully when people are playful and childlike.
Meanwhile, it works best in conjunction with deep knowledge and expertise.

passage.translation: 你看不见它，闻不到它，也听不到它，人们对如何准确定义它或它究竟来自何处存在分歧。它不是一门学校科目或学术学科,但它可以被学习。它是艺术家所需的一种品质,但它也存在于科学家和企业家的生活中。我们所有人都从中受益,当我们能够运用它时,我们在精神上和心灵上都会蓬勃发展。它是一种脆弱的东西,容易被扼杀;事实上,当人们充满玩心和童心时,它才能最充分地flourish。与此同时,它与深厚的知识和专业技能相结合时效果最佳。

sentences.text: This mysterious—but teachable—quality is creativity, the subject of a recently-published report by Durham Commission on Creativity and Education.

The report concludes that creativity should not inhabit the school curriculum only as it relates to drama, music, art and other obviously creative subjects, but that creative thinking ought to run through all of school life, infusing(充满) the way humanities and natural sciences are learned.

passage.translation: 这种神秘但可教授的品质就是创造力,这是Durham Commission on Creativity and Education最近发表的一份报告的主题。该报告得出结论,创造力不应仅作为与戏剧、音乐、艺术和其他明显的创意学科相关的内容存在于学校课程中,而应该贯穿整个学校生活,充满人文学科和自然科学的学习方式。

sentences.text: The authors, who focus on education in England, offer a number of sensible recommendations, some of which are an attempt to alleviate the uninspiring and fact-based approach to education that has crept into policy in recent years.
When children are regarded as vessels to be filled with facts, creativity does not prosper; nor does it when teachers' sole objective is coaching children towards exams.

One suggestion from the commission is a network of teacher-led "creativity collaboratives", along the lines of existing maths hubs(中心), with the aim of supporting teaching for creativity through the school curriculum.

passage.translation: 这些作者关注英格兰的教育,提出了一些合理的建议,其中一些试图缓解近年来渗入政策的那种缺乏启发性、以事实为基础的教育方法。当儿童被视为需要填充事实的容器时,创造力不会繁荣;当教师的唯一目标是辅导儿童应对考试时,创造力也不会繁荣。该委员会提出的一项建议是建立由教师主导的"创造力协作网络",类似于现有的数学中心,目的是通过学校课程支持创造力教学。

sentences.text: Nevertheless, it is arts subjects through which creativity can most obviously be fostered.
The value placed on them by the independent education sector is clear.
One only has to look at the remarkable arts facilities at Britain's top private schools to comprehend this.
But in the state sector the excessive focus on English, maths and science threatens to crush arts subjects; meanwhile, reduced school budgets mean diminishing extracurricular activities.
There has been a 28.1% decline in students taking creative subjects at high schools since 2014, though happily, art and design have seen a recent increase.

passage.translation: 然而,艺术学科是最能明显培养创造力的途径。私立教育部门对它们的重视是显而易见的。只需看看英国顶尖私立学校卓越的艺术设施就能理解这一点。但在公立教育部门,对英语、数学和科学的过度关注有可能扼杀艺术学科;与此同时,学校预算削减意味着课外活动减少。自2014年以来,在高中选修创意学科的学生减少了28.1%,不过令人欣慰的是,艺术和设计最近出现了增长。

sentences.text: This discrepancy between state and private education is a matter of social justice.
It is simply wrong and unfair that most children have a fraction of the access to choirs, orchestras, art studios and drama that their more privileged peers enjoy.
As lives are affected by any number of looming challenges—climate crisis, automation in the workplace—humans are going to need creative thinking more than ever.
For all of our sakes, creativity in education, and for all, must become a priority.

passage.translation: 公立教育和私立教育之间的这种差异是一个社会公正问题。大多数儿童只能获得其更优越的同龄人所享有的合唱团、管弦乐队、艺术工作室和戏剧机会的一小部分,这简直是错误和不公平的。随着生活受到各种迫在眉睫的挑战——气候危机、工作场所自动化——的影响,人类将比以往任何时候都更需要创造性思维。为了我们所有人,教育中的创造力,以及面向所有人的创造力,必须成为优先事项。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about creativity?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
从文章中我们了解到关于创造力的什么信息?
A) 当人们在精神上做好准备时,创造力发展得最好。
B) 创造力最常由科学家和企业家运用。
C) 创造力建立在科学知识和分析技能的基础上。
D) 创造力有助于智力发展,但很容易被扼杀。
**判型** What do we learn from the passage about creativity? 问的是关于 creativity 的“我们能了解到什么”，落点在首段对 creativity 多项属性的综合判断。
**拆句** Q46 是简单的特殊疑问句，主干是 What do we learn，about creativity 是状语；句子无陷阱。
**定位** 我们所有人都因它受益，当我们能够驾驭它时，便能在心智与精神上得到滋养。它是一种脆弱之物，极易被扼杀。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念It develops best when people are spiritually prepared. 把原文的“在人们玩乐而童心未泯时最为繁盛”改写成“精神上准备好时才发展最好”，把 playful and childlike 偷换成spiritually prepared。
B) 范围程度偷改原文说创造力“也存在于”科学家和企业家的生活里，It is most often wielded by scientists and entrepreneurs. 却拔高为“最常被科学家和企业家施展”。
C) 偷换概念原文说创造力“与深厚知识和专长协同时效果最好”，It is founded on scientific knowledge and analytical skills. 却改成“建立在科学知识和分析技能之上”，并把 deep knowledge 缩窄为 scientific knowledge。
D) ✓ 正确we thrive mentally and spiritually ↔ contributes to intellectual growth easily stamped out ↔ can easily be killed It contributes to intellectual growth but can easily be killed. 用 but 同时容纳“促进智力成长”和“易被扼杀”两个属性，与预判完全吻合。
questions.quote: All of us benefit from it and we thrive mentally and spiritually when we are able to wield it. It is a delicate thing, easily stamped out;

options.text: It develops best when people are spiritually prepared.
It is most often wielded by scientists and entrepreneurs.
It is founded on scientific knowledge and analytical skills.
It contributes to intellectual growth but can easily be killed.

questions.prompt: What is the conclusion of a recently-published report?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
最近发表的一份报告得出了什么结论?
A) 自然科学应该像人文课程那样进行教学。
B) 创造力的培养应该渗透到整个学校课程中。
C) 艺术课程应该成为所有学生的必修课。
D) 学生应该学习更多明显具有创造性的科目。
**判型** What is the conclusion of a recently-published report? 指向报告里一句明确的判断，是定点细节题。
**拆句** Q47 主干 What is the conclusion，of a recently-published report 是后置定语；结构平铺，无陷阱。
**定位** 该报告得出结论：创造力不应只在戏剧、音乐、美术等明显属于创意类科目中出现于学校课程，相反，创造性思维应贯穿整个校园生活，渗透到人文学科和自然科学的学习方式中。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Natural sciences should be learned the way humanities courses are. 凭空规定自然科学要按人文学科的方式学习——原文只说创造性思维渗透两者的学习方式，并未让一者照搬另一者。
B) ✓ 正确creative thinking ought to run through all of school life ↔Cultivation of creativity should permeate the entire school curriculum. infusing(充满) the way humanities and natural sciences are learned ↔permeate the entire school curriculum B 项把 run through all of school life 改写为 permeate the entire school curriculum，是 but 后内容的精准同义复述。
C) 偷换概念Art courses should be made compulsory for all students. 把原文“创造性思维渗透全部课程”偷换为“艺术课必须成为必修”，原文从未提到 compulsory。
D) 与原文相反Students should learn more obviously creative subjects. 恰好是结论 not A but B中被否定的 A——原文反对“只把创造力限制在明显的创意学科里”，选项却让学生多学这些学科。
questions.quote: The report concludes that creativity should not inhabit the school curriculum only as it relates to drama, music, art and other obviously creative subjects, but that creative thinking ought to run through all of school life, infusing(充满) the way humanities and natural sciences are learned.

options.text: Natural sciences should be learned the way humanities courses are.
Cultivation of creativity should permeate the entire school curriculum.
Art courses should be made compulsory for all students.
Students should learn more obviously creative subjects.

questions.prompt: What does the report say is detrimental to the fostering of creativity?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
报告指出什么不利于创造力的培养?
A) 减轻压力。
B) 教师主导的学校活动。
C) 应试教学。
D) 自主学习。
**判型** What does the report say is detrimental to the fostering of creativity? 问的是报告里点名的具体不利因素，是定点细节。
**拆句** Q48 主干 What does the report say is detrimental to ...；嵌套了 say 引导的宾语从句，从句主语正是答案所指。理解时把 say 看作透明引述即可。
**定位** 当孩子被看作待填装事实的容器时，创造力无法繁荣；当教师的唯一目标是辅导孩子应对考试时，创造力同样无法繁荣。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反Alleviation of pressure. 借用了段中的 alleviate 一词，但原文是说要“缓解”应试取向带来的问题——alleviation 本身是正面行为，不可能是 detrimental。
B) 与原文相反Teacher-led school activities. 取自原文里报告的正面建议 a network of teacher-led “creativity collaboratives”，却被当作有害因素，与原文极性相反。
C) ✓ 正确teachers' sole objective is coaching children towards exams ↔ Test-oriented teaching. the uninspiring and fact-based approach to education ↔ Test-oriented teaching. C 项把段中两处对应内容压缩为 Test-oriented teaching，是报告明确点名的负面教学方式。
D) 无中生有Independent learning. 完全没有原文依据——第三段根本未讨论 independent learning 是否有害。
questions.quote: When children are regarded as vessels to be filled with facts, creativity does not prosper; nor does it when teachers' sole objective is coaching children towards exams.

options.text: Alleviation of pressure.
Teacher-led school activities.
Test-oriented teaching.
Independent learning.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the private schools in the UK?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
我们了解到关于英国私立学校的什么信息?
A) 它们鼓励课外活动。
B) 它们高度重视艺术教育。
C) 它们将艺术科目置于数学和科学之上。
D) 它们面向来自不同家庭背景的学生。
**判型** What do we learn about the private schools in the UK? 问的是某一具体群体的特征，落点在描述该群体的一两句话，是定点细节。
**拆句** Q49 与 46 题同句型，唯一区别是 about 后面换成了具体群体，定位粒度更细；句子无陷阱。
**定位** 尽管如此，最能直接培养创造力的还是艺术类学科。独立教育部门对它们的重视显而易见。只要看看英国顶级私立学校出色的艺术设施，就足以体会这一点。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴They encourage extracurricular activities. 借用了段末 reduced school budgets mean diminishing extracurricular activities，但该句说的是公立学校预算削减导致课外活动减少，主语并不是 private schools。
B) ✓ 正确The value placed on them by the independent education sector is clear ↔They attach great importance to arts education. remarkable arts facilities at Britain's top private schools ↔ arts education B 项把“独立部门给艺术学科赋予的价值”主动化表达为“私立学校非常重视艺术教育”，与定位句完全等值。
C) 过度推断They prioritize arts subjects over maths and sciences. 把“重视艺术”夸大为“把艺术置于数理之上”，原文并未做此比较。
D) 无中生有They cater to students from different family backgrounds. 原文未谈及私立学校生源构成；末段提到的社会公正问题是对公私差距的批评，恰恰说明私立学校并非面向“不同家庭背景”。
questions.quote: Nevertheless, it is arts subjects through which creativity can most obviously be fostered. The value placed on them by the independent education sector is clear. One only has to look at the remarkable arts facilities at Britain's top private schools to comprehend this.

options.text: They encourage extracurricular activities.
They attach great importance to arts education.
They prioritize arts subjects over maths and sciences.
They cater to students from different family backgrounds.

questions.prompt: What should be done to meet the future challenges?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
应该做什么来应对未来的挑战?
A) 增加政府对学校教育的投资。
B) 缩小现有的贫富差距。
C) 为所有儿童提供平等接受艺术教育的机会。
D) 关注满足弱势学生的需求。
**判型** What should be done to meet the future challenges? 表面像主旨，但实质问的是末段给出的对策，是定点细节。
**拆句** Q50 主干 What should be done，to meet the future challenges 是不定式状语，表目的；句子无陷阱。
**定位** 由于人类生活正受各种正在逼近的挑战——气候危机、工作场所自动化——所影响，我们将比以往任何时候都更需要创造性思维。为了我们所有人，教育中的创造力，并惠及所有人，必须成为重中之重。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Increasing government investment in school education. 原文虽提到 reduced school budgets，但末段呼吁的是“惠及所有人”，并未要求增加政府投资——投资是手段，不是作者点名的对策。
B) 以偏概全Narrowing the existing gap between the rich and the poor. 把全文聚焦的“艺术教育机会不平等”放大为整个“贫富差距”，超出作者讨论范围。
C) ✓ 正确creativity in education, and for all, must become a priority ↔Providing all children with equal access to arts education. most children have a fraction of the access to choirs, orchestras, art studios and drama that their more privileged peers enjoy↔ equal access to arts education C 项 all children with equal access 精准对应 for all 与 fraction of the access 的反向均等化，是对末段呼吁最严谨的同义复述。
D) 以偏概全Focusing on meeting the needs of under-privileged students. 只关照弱势群体，与原文 for all（所有人）相悖；作者要的是普惠，不是单向倾斜。
questions.quote: As lives are affected by any number of looming challenges—climate crisis, automation in the workplace—humans are going to need creative thinking more than ever. For all of our sakes, creativity in education, and for all, must become a priority.

options.text: Increasing government investment in school education.
Narrowing the existing gap between the rich and the poor.
Providing all children with equal access to arts education.
Focusing on meeting the needs of under-privileged students.

title: At 43, I've reached the stage where women…

sentences.text: At 43, I've reached the stage where women are warned to watch out for the creeping sadness of middle age.
We're served up an endless stream of advice on "how to survive your 40s", as if we're in the endurance stage of a slow limp toward (26)____ .
This is the age women start to become "invisible"—our value, attractiveness and power supposedly (27)____ by the vanishing of youth.
But I don't feel like I'm fading into (28)____ .
I feel more seen than I ever have, and for the first time in my life, I have a clear-eyed view of myself that is (29)____ , compassionate and accepting.

passage.translation: 43岁的我已经到了女性被警告要当心中年悄然而至的悲伤的阶段。我们被源源不断地灌输关于"如何度过你的40多岁"的建议,仿佛我们正处于缓慢蹒跚走向脆弱的耐力阶段。这是女性开始变得"隐形"的年龄——我们的价值、吸引力和力量据说会因青春的消逝而减弱。但我并不觉得自己正在淡出人们的视野。我感到自己比以往任何时候都更被看见,而且这是我人生中第一次对自己有了清醒的认识,这种认识是真实的、富有同情心的和接纳的。

sentences.text: When I look in the mirror, I'm proud of who I am—even those "broken" parts that for so long seemed impossible to love.
So when advertisers try to sell me ways to "turn back the clock", I have to(30)____ a laugh.
I wouldn't go back to the crippling self-consciousness of my youth if you paid me.
This hard-won sense of self-acceptance is one of the joys of being an older woman.
But it's a narrative often (31)____ out by the shame that marketers rely on to peddle us their diet pills, miracle face creams and breathable yoga pants—as if self-love is a (32)____ commodity.

passage.translation: 当我照镜子时,我为自己是谁而自豪——甚至包括那些长期以来似乎不可能去爱的"破碎"部分。所以当广告商试图向我兜售"让时光倒流"的方法时,我不得不强忍住笑。即使你付钱给我,我也不会回到年轻时那种令人难以忍受的自我意识过剩状态。这种来之不易的自我接纳感是作为年长女性的乐趣之一。但这种叙事常常被营销人员所依赖的羞耻感淹没,他们向我们兜售减肥药、神奇面霜和透气瑜伽裤——仿佛自爱是一种可以购买的商品。

sentences.text: For some women I know, this sense of trust and self-belief later in life gave them the courage to leave dysfunctional relationships or (33)____ on new career paths.

Others talked about enjoying their own company, of growth through (34)____ , deepening bonds of friendships, the ability to be more compassionate, less judgmental and to listen more and appreciate the small pleasures.
Life past 40 is far from smooth sailing, but it's so much more than the reductive (35)____ we see in women's magazines and on the Hollywood big screen.

passage.translation: 对于我认识的一些女性来说,这种在人生后期产生的信任感和自信给了她们勇气去离开功能失调的关系或开启新的职业道路。还有一些人谈到享受独处,在逆境中成长,加深友谊纽带,能够更有同情心、更少评判性,更多倾听并欣赏小小的快乐。40岁以后的生活远非一帆风顺,但它远比我们在女性杂志和好莱坞大银幕上看到的简化描绘丰富得多。

groups.content:
At 43, I've reached the stage where women are warned to watch out for the creeping sadness of middle age. We're served up an endless stream of advice on "how to survive your 40s", as if we're in the endurance stage of a slow limp toward {{26}} . This is the age women start to become "invisible"—our value, attractiveness and power supposedly {{27}} by the vanishing of youth. But I don't feel like I'm fading into {{28}} . I feel more seen than I ever have, and for the first time in my life, I have a clear-eyed view of myself that is {{29}} , compassionate and accepting.

When I look in the mirror, I'm proud of who I am—even those "broken" parts that for so long seemed impossible to love. So when advertisers try to sell me ways to "turn back the clock", I have to{{30}} a laugh. I wouldn't go back to the crippling self-consciousness of my youth if you paid me. This hard-won sense of self-acceptance is one of the joys of being an older woman. But it's a narrative often {{31}} out by the shame that marketers rely on to peddle us their diet pills, miracle face creams and breathable yoga pants—as if self-love is a {{32}} commodity.

For some women I know, this sense of trust and self-belief later in life gave them the courage to leave dysfunctional relationships or {{33}} on new career paths. Others talked about enjoying their own company, of growth through {{34}} , deepening bonds of friendships, the ability to be more compassionate, less judgmental and to listen more and appreciate the small pleasures. Life past 40 is far from smooth sailing, but it's so much more than the reductive {{35}} we see in women's magazines and on the Hollywood big screen.

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) fragility 名词
**词性槽** 介词 toward 后接名词
**依据** "缓慢蹒跚"暗示终点是衰朽a slow limp toward __(26)__描绘中年妇女被刻画成"缓慢瘸行走向 X"，X 必是"衰老、衰朽"类负面终点；fragility（脆弱、衰朽）紧扣"endurance stage""creeping sadness"的衰退主题，呼应作者要反驳的刻板印象。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) adversity义偏"逆境"非"衰朽终点" adversity"逆境"侧重外部困境，而本句喻"朝身体/价值衰退的终点缓慢爬行"，fragility 的"衰朽"更贴。
D) depictions义"描绘"与"走向"不搭toward depictions="朝着描绘"语义不通，且 depictions 留作第35题的答案。
J) obscurity已留给第28题的 fade into 搭配obscurity 与 fade into 是高频搭配，应留给28题；此处用了它就抢走了更稳的搭配位。
K) outlines义"轮廓"无关衰退主题outlines"轮廓/纲要"与中年衰退的喻意无关。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 J) —— toward obscurity 也通顺，但抢了28题铁搭位。a slow limp toward __(26)__里 obscurity 单看能填，但 fade into obscurity 是更稳的铁搭，应让位给28；防坑要诀：通读全文再下笔，发现某词在别处是铁搭就让出来。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) diminished 动词
**词性槽** 过去分词作后置定语/状语
**依据** "价值因青春逝去而被削弱" our value, attractiveness and power supposedly __(27)__ by the vanishing of youth——作者陈述刻板印象：女性的"价值、吸引力和权力"据说会因"青春的消逝"而削减；diminished by"被…削减"语义贴切、与全文反驳的"中年=贬值"刻板印象呼应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) drowned drowned by 与"价值削弱"语义错位drowned 多用于声音/信号"被淹没"，且 F 应留给31题"drowned out by the shame"的固定搭配。
I) neglected neglected"被忽视"主体错位neglected 强调"被忽略未照料"，主语"价值、吸引力、权力"不会"被青春的消逝忽视"，逻辑上vanishing 是"原因"而非"主体"，搭配偏误。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 I) —— neglected 词性与位置都对，却错抓"忽视"含义。our value, attractiveness and power supposedly __(27)__ by the vanishing of youth中 neglected误为"被忽视"，但 by 引导的是"原因"而非"忽视的主体"，正解 diminished"被削减"；防坑要诀：分清 by 的"被动施事"与"被动原因"。

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) obscurity 名词
**词性槽** fade into 后接名词
**依据** fade into obscurity="湮没无名"是铁搭This is the age women start to become "invisible"提示"中年女性=被看不见的"，作者随即反驳"我不觉得自己 fading into __"，对应 obscurity"默默无闻"——与"invisible"互文，形成完整反讽。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) adversity fade into adversity 不成搭配adversity 与 fade into 不构成英语固定表达，且语义"消逝进逆境"也不通。
D) depictions 义"描绘"且为35题铁位depictions"描绘"复数与 fade into 不搭，留给35题 reductive depictions。
K) outlines义偏物理"轮廓"无关outlines 与"消失成无名之辈"的喻意不符。

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) authentic 形容词
**词性槽** 并列形容词中的一员
**依据** 本真、富有同情、接纳——三重自我品质a clear-eyed view of myself that is authentic, compassionate and accepting——authentic（本真的）与 compassionate（富有同情心的）和 accepting（接纳的）共同刻画"对自己清醒、真实、慈悲、接纳"的成熟自我形象，与全篇主旨吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
L) prevalent 义"盛行"非"对自我的品质" prevalent 形容"事物普遍存在"，无法描述"对自己的看法"的内在品质，感情色彩与并列结构脱节。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) suppress 动词
**词性槽** 情态动词 have to + 动词原形
**依据** suppress a laugh="忍住笑"惯用搭配when advertisers try to sell me ways to "turn back the clock", I have to __(30)__ a laugh——作者面对"回到青春"的广告觉得可笑，但出于礼节"忍住笑"。suppress a laugh是英语固定搭配，意为"克制笑出来"。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) convey 义"传达"语义反向convey a laugh"传达一个笑"既不是固定搭配也与上下文反讽语气相反——作者要克制而不是表达。
N) submit submit 通常不及物或接 to submit a laugh 不成立，submit 多用"submit to"或"提交文件"义，与"忍住笑"无关。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) drowned 动词
**词性槽** 过去分词 + out by 固定搭配
**依据** drown out=淹没/盖过（铁搭）a narrative often drowned out by the shame that marketers rely on to peddle us their diet pills——"自我接纳的叙事常被商家所利用的羞耻感所盖过"。drown out 是六级高频固定短语，意为"用更强的声音/力量盖过"。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
I) neglected neglected out by 不是固定搭配neglected 不与 out 构成短语；且"被忽视"无法解释"shame 主动盖过"的力量感。

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) purchasable 形容词
**词性槽** 不定冠词 a + ___ + 名词 commodity
**依据** 讽刺商家把自爱当"可购买商品" marketers rely on to peddle us their diet pills, miracle face creams and breathable yoga pants—as if self-love is a __(32)__ commodity——前文说商家兜售各种产品，as if引出讽刺：仿佛"自爱"是可以买来的商品，purchasable commodity"可购买的商品"对接最严丝合缝。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) authentic 义向相反authentic commodity="真正的商品"是正面陈述，但句子是讽刺商家把自爱商品化，正向词与as if 讽刺语气冲突。
L) prevalent 搭配偏离讽刺焦点prevalent"普遍的"修饰 commodity 在语法上可成立，但作者讽刺的是"自爱被当成可买卖之物"，而非"自爱很普遍"，错过讽刺核心。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) embark 动词
**词性槽** or 并列"to leave / __ on"，需动词原形
**依据** 固定搭配 embark on=踏上（新征程）__(33)__ on new career paths即"踏上新的职业道路"，embark on 是英语里描述"开始一段新旅程/事业"的高频搭配，与前文"leave dysfunctional relationships"语义并列、感情色彩积极。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) convey convey 不与 on 搭配convey 意为"传达"，常接宾语而非"on+名词"，无法表达"踏上职业道路"。
N) submit submit to 而非 submit on，且感情色彩反向submit 常用"submit to=屈服于"，与"勇气离开/开启"的积极语境冲突。
O) suppress suppress 是及物动词不带 on suppress 后直接接宾语（压制某物），不与 on 构成固定搭配，也与"new career paths"语义不合。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) adversity 名词
**词性槽** 介词 through 后接名词
**依据** 经由逆境而成长=英文励志惯用法enjoying their own company, of growth through __(34)__, deepening bonds of friendships列举中年女性的多种正向收获，growth through adversity"在逆境中成长"是英语常用励志表达，与"享受独处""友谊加深"并列自然。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
D) depictions 义"描绘"与"经由…成长"不匹配growth through depictions"经由描绘成长"语义不通；depictions 应留给35题"reductive depictions"。
K) outlines 义"轮廓/纲要"与成长机制无关growth through outlines 不构成习语，无逻辑可言。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) depictions 名词
**词性槽** the + 形容词 + ___
**依据** 杂志和银幕里"狭隘的刻画" it's so much more than the reductive __(35)__ we see in women's magazines and on the Hollywood big screen——作者反驳的正是媒体对中年女性"reductive depictions"（简化的、缩水的刻画），depictions 与"在杂志和银幕上看到"完美对回，与开篇"women are warned…"形成首尾呼应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
K) outlines outlines 偏"概要/轮廓"指代不够具体outlines"概要"在新闻或大纲语境用，描述媒体"刻画形象"更精准的是 depictions；杂志/银幕里看到的是"画面、刻画"而非"概要"。

title: The car has reshaped our cities.…

sentences.text: The car has reshaped our cities.
It seems to offer autonomy for everyone.

There is something almost delightful in the detachment from reality of advertisements showing mass-produced cars marketed as symbols of individuality and of freedom when most of their lives will be spent making short journeys on choked roads.

passage.translation: 汽车重塑了我们的城市。它似乎为每个人提供了自主权。广告中展示的场景与现实脱节,将批量生产的汽车作为个性和自由的象征进行营销,而这些汽车生命中的大部分时间将在拥堵的道路上进行短途行驶,这其中有一种近乎可笑的意味。

sentences.text: For all the fuss made about top speeds, cornering ability and acceleration, the most useful gadgets on a modern car are those which work when you're going very slowly: parking sensors, sound systems, and navigation apps which will show a way around upcoming traffic jams.

This seems to be one of the few areas where the benefit of sharing personal information comes straight back to the sharer: because these apps know where almost all the users are, and how fast they are moving almost all the time, they can spot traffic congestion(堵塞) very quickly and suggest ways round it.

passage.translation: 尽管人们对最高速度、转弯能力和加速性能大做文章,但现代汽车上最有用的装置是那些在你行驶非常缓慢时发挥作用的设备:停车传感器、音响系统,以及能显示绕开前方交通拥堵路线的导航应用程序。这似乎是为数不多的几个领域之一,在这里分享个人信息的好处会直接回馈给分享者:因为这些应用程序几乎始终知道几乎所有用户的位置以及他们的移动速度,它们可以非常快速地发现交通拥堵并建议绕行路线。

sentences.text: The problem comes when everyone is using a navigation app which tells them to avoid everyone else using the same gadget.
Traffic jams often appear where no one has enough information to avoid them.
When a lucky few have access to the knowledge, they will benefit greatly.
But when everyone has perfect information, traffic jams simply spread onto the side roads that seem to offer a way round them.

passage.translation: 问题出现在当每个人都在使用导航应用程序,而该程序告诉他们避开所有其他使用同一装置的人时。交通拥堵常常出现在没有人拥有足够信息来避开它们的地方。当幸运的少数人获得这些知识时,他们将大大受益。但当每个人都拥有完美的信息时,交通拥堵只会蔓延到那些看似提供绕行路线的辅路上。

sentences.text: This new congestion teaches us two things.
The first is that the promises of technology will never be realised as fully as we hope; they will be limited by their unforeseen and unintended consequences.
Sitting in a more comfortable car in a different traffic jam is pleasant but hardly the liberation that once seemed to be promised.
The second is that self-organisation will not get us where we want to go.
The efforts of millions of drivers to get ahead do not miraculously produce a situation in which everyone does better than before, but one in which almost everyone does rather worse.
Central control and collective organisation can produce smoother and fairer outcomes, though even that much is never guaranteed.

passage.translation: 这种新的拥堵给我们带来两点启示。第一点是,技术的承诺永远不会像我们希望的那样完全实现;它们将受到不可预见和意外后果的限制。坐在更舒适的汽车里处于不同的交通拥堵中是令人愉快的,但这很难说是曾经似乎被承诺的解放。第二点是,自我组织不会让我们到达想去的地方。数百万驾驶员争先恐后的努力并不会奇迹般地产生一种每个人都比以前做得更好的局面,而是产生一种几乎每个人都做得相当糟糕的局面。集中控制和集体组织可以产生更顺畅和更公平的结果,尽管即使这一点也永远无法保证。

sentences.text: Similar limits can be foreseen for the much greater advances promised by self-driving cars.
Last week, one operated by the taxi company Uber struck and killed a woman pushing her bicycle across a wide road in Arizona.
This was the first recorded death involving a car which was supposed to be fully autonomous.
Experts have said that it suggests a "catastrophic failure" of technology.

passage.translation: 对于自动驾驶汽车所承诺的更大进步,也可以预见类似的局限性。上周,出租车公司Uber运营的一辆自动驾驶汽车在Arizona的一条宽阔道路上撞死了一名推着自行车过马路的女性。这是有记录以来第一起涉及被认为是完全自主汽车的死亡事故。专家表示,这表明技术出现了"灾难性故障"。

sentences.text: Increasingly, even Silicon Valley has to acknowledge the costs of the intoxicating(令人陶醉的) hurry that characterises its culture.
What traffic teaches us is that reckless and uncontrolled change is as likely to harm us as it is to benefit us, and that thoughtful regulation is necessary for a better future.

passage.translation: 即使是硅谷也越来越不得不承认其文化特征——令人陶醉的匆忙——所带来的代价。交通教给我们的是,鲁莽和不受控制的变革既可能伤害我们,也可能使我们受益,而深思熟虑的监管对于更美好的未来是必要的。

questions.prompt: What does the author say about car advertisements?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者对汽车广告有何看法?
A) 它们描绘了享受道路速度的驾驶者。
B) 它们呈现了汽车所提供自主性的虚假画面。
C) 它们在设计理念上追求个性和独创性。
D) 它们高估了自动驾驶汽车的潜在市场。
**判型** What does the author say about car advertisements 直接问作者对广告的具体表述，无infer/imply 等推断信号，属对原文某句的客观转述。
**拆句** 标准 What does the author say about X 句式，宾语从句结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 广告中那种"脱离现实"的味道几乎让人觉得有趣——量产车被包装成个性与自由的象征，可它们这辈子大多数时间都堵在短途的拥挤路上。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有原文谈的是个性 / 自由的形象与拥堵现实的反差，没有任何句子说广告里的司机享受速度。
B) ✓ 正确detachment from reality of advertisements showing mass-produced cars marketed as symbols of individuality and of freedom↔ They present a false picture of the autonomy cars provide预判要的"广告呈现的自由是失真的"，B 恰好以 false picture + autonomy 两词整齐对应原文，是定位句的同义压缩。
C) 偷换概念原文说广告把车包装为"个性的象征"（marketed as symbols of individuality），不是说广告在"设计理念上追求个性与原创"。
D) 张冠李戴原文谈的是普通量产车广告，autonomous cars（自动驾驶车）要到 P5 才出现，且与广告无关。
questions.quote: There is something almost delightful in the detachment from reality of advertisements showing mass-produced cars marketed as symbols of individuality and of freedom when most of their lives will be spent making short journeys on choked roads.

options.text: They portray drivers who enjoy speed on the road.
They present a false picture of the autonomy cars provide.

They overestimate the potential market of autonomous cars.

questions.prompt: What does the author imply about the various gadgets on cars?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （推断题）
**题目译文**
作者对汽车上的各种装置有何暗示?
A) 它们可以帮助缓解交通拥堵。
B) 它们大多数像广告宣传的那样有效。
C) 只有部分装置能在当前交通状况下投入使用。
D) 它们不断升级以使驾驶更轻松、更安全。
**判型** What does the author imply about the various gadgets on cars 中 imply 是典型推断信号，要求在原文未明说的方向上做一步延伸。
**拆句** What does the author imply about X 标准句式，结构无难度，关键是认出 imply 的题型信号。
**定位** 尽管人们对极速、过弯和加速大谈特谈，但现代车上真正有用的小装置，反而都是在你开得很慢时才派上用场的那些——停车感应、音响、导航。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断原文说导航 apps 能 spot 拥堵并 suggest ways round，但下一段立刻指出这只是把堵车"转移"到 side roads，并未真正缓解（alleviate）。
B) 无中生有原文只罗列 gadgets 哪些有用，并没有把它们与广告所宣传的效果做比较，无从得出"多数与广告一样有效"。
C) ✓ 正确the most useful gadgets on a modern car are those which work when you're going very slowly↔ Only some can be put to use under current traffic conditions预判要的"只有一部分装置真正派用"，C 用 only some 精准对上原文 those which... 的子集限定，是唯一吻合预判的选项。
D) 无中生有原文没有讨论 gadgets "不断升级"，更未涉及"让驾驶更轻松/安全"的整体趋势。

questions.prompt: What does the author say about the use of navigation apps?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者对导航应用程序的使用有何看法?
A) 它可能在其他地方造成交通拥堵。
B) 它在缓解交通拥堵方面帮助很大。
C) 它大幅减少了交通事故的发生率。
D) 它使正在学习驾驶的人受益。
**判型** What does the author say about the use of navigation apps 用 say 而非 imply，属客观转述类细节题。
**拆句** What does the author say about the use of X 标准句式，宾语是动名词短语 the use of navigation apps，平铺无陷阱。
**定位** 但当所有人都掌握完美信息时，堵车只会蔓延到那些看起来能绕开拥堵的次要道路上去。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确traffic jams simply spread onto the side roads that seem to offer a way round them ↔It is likely to create traffic jams in other places预判要的"导航把堵车推到别处"，A 用 create traffic jams + in other places 精准对应spread onto + the side roads，是定位句的同义改写。
B) 与原文相反原文核心是导航 apps 只能把堵车搬走、不能从总量上 ease it；选项却说"对缓解拥堵帮助巨大"，与作者立场相反。
C) 无中生有原文全段讨论的是"避堵"，从未涉及"交通事故发生率"，更没说能 sharply reduce。
D) 偷换概念原文未提"学车人"这一群体，只笼统说 everyone / a lucky few；选项偷换为"对学车者有益"。
questions.quote: But when everyone has perfect information, traffic jams simply spread onto the side roads that seem to offer a way round them.

options.text: It is likely to create traffic jams in other places.
It helps a great deal in easing traffic congestion.
It sharply reduces the incidence of traffic accidents.
It benefits those who are learning to drive.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about technology?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者对技术有何看法?
A) 其后果通常难以评估。
B) 它很少兑现所有承诺的好处。
C) 它取决于应用所需的知识。
D) 其好处由集体智慧保证。
**判型** What does the author say about technology 仍是 say 句式，要求转述作者对technology 的明确表述。
**拆句** What does the author say about technology 标准句式，结构简单；难点不在题干而在technology 在原文的复现密度——需靠 byWords 中的"评价句"通法收敛。
**定位** 第一是，技术的种种承诺永远无法像我们期望的那样被完全兑现；它们总会被那些未曾预料、并非本意的后果所制约。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文说的是"后果未被预见 / 并非本意"（unforeseen and unintended），而非"难以评估"（difficult to assess）。
B) ✓ 正确the promises of technology will never be realised as fully as we hope ↔It seldom delivers all the benefits as promised预判要的"技术承诺难以完全兑现"，B 用 seldom + all ... as promised 精准对应原文的never + as fully as we hope。
C) 无中生有原文未讨论"技术应用是否依赖知识储备"。
D) 与原文相反原文末句明说 even that much is never guaranteed（即使集中管控也无法保证），选项却说"集体智慧保证了技术的好处"，与作者立场相反。
questions.quote: The first is that the promises of technology will never be realised as fully as we hope; they will be limited by their unforeseen and unintended consequences.

options.text: Its consequences are usually difficult to assess.
It seldom delivers all the benefits as promised.
It depends on the required knowledge for application.
Its benefits are guaranteed by collective wisdom.

questions.prompt: What key message does the author try to convey in the passage?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （主旨题）
**题目译文**
作者在文中试图传达什么关键信息?
A) 技术创新的后果无需夸大。
B) 开发技术以创造更美好世界总是要付出代价的。
C) 技术创新应该受到适当监管。
D) 硅谷文化不应被效仿。
**判型** What key message does the author try to convey in the passage 中 key message +in the passage 是典型主旨题双信号。
**拆句** What key message does the author try to convey in the passage——疑问句倒装，主语 the author，谓语 try to convey，宾语 what key message，结构清楚不绕。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反全文核心是要正视技术后果、加以监管，而非"不必夸大后果"——选项的方向与作者完全相反。
B) 以偏概全原文确实承认有代价（unforeseen and unintended consequences），但作者的核心立场不是"代价不可避免"，而是"需要监管"。把局部当作主旨，落点偏移。
C) ✓ 正确thoughtful regulation is necessary for a better future↔Technological innovation should be properly regulated Central control and collective organisation can produce smoother and fairer outcomes↔Technological innovation should be properly regulated预判要的"技术需妥善监管"，C 把 thoughtful regulation 直译为 properly regulated，又覆盖了 central control 这条中段证据，是全文主线的最大公约数。
D) 以偏概全硅谷文化只在 Silicon Valley has to acknowledge the costs of the intoxicating hurry一句被点到，作为例子；全文主旨并非反对硅谷文化本身。

options.text: The consequences of technological innovation need not be exaggerated.
There is always a price to pay to develop technology for a better world.
Technological innovation should be properly regulated.
The culture of Silicon Valley ought not to be emulated.

title: We often think of drawing as something that…

sentences.text: We often think of drawing as something that takes inborn talent, but this kind of thinking stems from our misclassification of drawing as, primarily, an art form rather than a tool for learning.

passage.translation: 我们常常认为绘画需要与生俱来的天赋,但这种想法源于我们对绘画的错误分类,即主要将其视为一种艺术形式,而非学习工具。

sentences.text: Researchers, teachers, and artists are starting to see how drawing can positively impact a wide variety of skills and disciplines.

passage.translation: 研究人员、教师和艺术家开始认识到绘画如何对各种技能和学科产生积极影响。

sentences.text: Most of us have spent some time drawing before, but at some point, most of us stop drawing.
There are people who don't, obviously, and thank God for that: a world without designers and artists would be a very shabby one indeed.

passage.translation: 我们大多数人以前都花过一些时间画画,但在某个时候,我们大多数人停止了绘画。显然,有些人没有停止,感谢上帝:一个没有设计师和艺术家的世界确实会非常寒酸。

sentences.text: Some argue that so many adults have abandoned drawing because we've miscategorized it and given it a very narrow definition.
In his book, Stick Figures: Drawing as a Human Practice, Professor D.
B.
Dowd argues that we have misfiled the significance of drawing because we see it as a professional skill instead of a personal capacity.
We mistakenly think of "good" drawings as those which work as recreations of the real world, as realistic illusions.
Rather, drawing should be recategorized as a symbolic tool.

passage.translation: 一些人认为,如此多的成年人放弃绘画是因为我们对其分类错误并给了它一个非常狭隘的定义。D. B. Dowd教授在其著作《火柴人:作为人类实践的绘画》中指出,我们错误地归档了绘画的意义,因为我们将其视为一种职业技能而非个人能力。我们错误地认为"好的"绘画是那些作为现实世界再现的作品,是逼真的幻象。相反,绘画应该被重新归类为一种符号工具。

sentences.text: Human beings have been drawing for 73,000 years.
It's part of what it means to be human.
We don't have the strength of chimpanzees(大猩猩) because we've given up animal strength to manipulate subtle instruments, like hammers, spears, and—later—pens and pencils.
The human hand is an extremely dense network of nerve endings.
In many ways, human beings are built to draw.

passage.translation: 人类绘画已有73000年的历史。这是人之为人的一部分。我们没有大猩猩的力量,因为我们放弃了动物的力量来操纵精细的工具,如锤子、矛,以及后来的钢笔和铅笔。人类的手是一个极其密集的神经末梢网络。从许多方面来说,人类生来就是为了绘画。

sentences.text: Some researchers argue that doodling(涂画) activates the brain's so-called default circuit—essentially, the areas of the brain responsible for maintaining a baseline level of activity in the absence of other stimuli.
Because of this, some believe that doodling during a boring lecture can help students pay attention.
In one study, participants were asked to listen to a list of names while either doodling or sitting still.
Those who doodled remembered 29 percent more of the names than those who did not.

passage.translation: 一些研究人员认为,涂画激活了大脑的所谓默认回路——本质上是大脑中负责在缺乏其他刺激的情况下维持基线活动水平的区域。因此,一些人认为在无聊的讲座中涂画可以帮助学生集中注意力。在一项研究中,参与者被要求在涂画或静坐时听一串名字。涂画的人比不涂画的人多记住了29%的名字。

sentences.text: There's also evidence that drawing talent is based on how accurately someone perceives the world.
The human visual system tends to misjudge size, shape, color, and angles but artists perceive these qualities more accurately than non-artists.
Cultivating drawing talent can become an essential tool to improve people's observational skills in fields where the visual is important.

passage.translation: 也有证据表明,绘画天赋基于某人对世界感知的准确程度。人类视觉系统往往会错误判断尺寸、形状、颜色和角度,但艺术家比非艺术家更准确地感知这些特质。培养绘画天赋可以成为提高人们在视觉重要领域观察技能的重要工具。

sentences.text: Rather than think of drawing as a talent that some creative people are gifted in, we should consider it as a tool for seeing and understanding the world better—one that just so happens to double as an art form.

Both absent-minded doodling and copying from life have been shown to positively affect your memory and visual perception, so complain loudly the next time your school board slashes the art department's budget.

passage.translation: 与其将绘画视为一些有创造力的人所具有的天赋,我们应该将其视为一种更好地观察和理解世界的工具——一种恰好兼作艺术形式的工具。无论是心不在焉的涂画还是写生,都已被证明对你的记忆和视觉感知产生积极影响,所以下次你的学校董事会削减艺术部门预算时,请大声抗议。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What do people generally think about drawing?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
人们通常如何看待绘画?
A) 它是有创造力的人所被赋予的天赋。
B) 它是通过练习习得的技能。
C) 它是一种被所有人欣赏的艺术形式。
D) 它是每个人都应该培养的能力。
**判型** What do people generally think about drawing? 问的是大众对绘画的普遍认知，属于事实型细节题。
**拆句** What do people generally think about drawing? 是简单的 what 引导特殊疑问句，主语people，谓语 think，宾语为 what，句式直白、无陷阱。
**定位** 我们常把绘画看作需要天生才能的事情，但这种想法源于我们把绘画错误归类——主要把它当作艺术形式而非学习工具。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确something that takes inborn talent ↔ a gift creative people are endowed with预判的"天生才能"与 a gift creative people are endowed with 一一对应，A 项是定位句前半的精准同义替换。
B) 无中生有It is a skill that is acquired with practice. 称绘画是通过练习习得的技能，但 P1 强调的恰恰是"天生才能"而非"练习习得"，文中没有任何句子说大众认为绘画靠练习。
C) 偷换概念It is an art form that is appreciated by all. 称绘画是被所有人欣赏的艺术形式，但our misclassification of drawing as, primarily, an art form 中作者只是引用大众把它归为艺术形式这一错误归类，并未谈及"被所有人欣赏"。
D) 张冠李戴It is an ability everyone should cultivate. 称绘画是人人都应培养的能力，这是作者在we should consider it as a tool for seeing and understanding the world better 中的呼吁，是作者立场而非大众看法。
questions.quote: We often think of drawing as something that takes inborn talent, but this kind of thinking stems from our misclassification of drawing as, primarily, an art form rather than a tool for learning.

options.text: It is a gift creative people are endowed with.
It is a skill that is acquired with practice.
It is an art form that is appreciated by all.
It is an ability everyone should cultivate.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about designers and artists?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于设计师和艺术家我们了解到什么?
A) 他们的数量正在逐渐减少。
B) 他们热衷于改变破旧的环境。
C) 他们为世界增添美感和魅力。
D) 他们一生中的大部分时间都在绘画。
**判型** What do we learn about designers and artists? 问的是我们对这群人的事实性认识。
**拆句** What do we learn about designers and artists? 主谓宾结构 we learn what about X，关于 X 我们学到了什么，句式平直无陷阱。
**定位** 显然有人没有放弃画画，谢天谢地：没有设计师和艺术家的世界，将会是一个非常单调寒酸的世界。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有They are declining gradually in number. 称他们数量在逐渐减少，但 P3 只说"多数人长大后放弃画画、但有人没放弃"，未提"设计师和艺术家"的数量趋势。
B) 偷换概念They are keen on changing shabby surroundings. 称他们热衷于改变 shabby 的环境，但原文 shabby 是用来形容"如果没有他们，世界会怎样"，是一个假设性结果，而非他们当下要改变的对象。
C) ✓ 正确a world without designers and artists would be a very shabby one indeed ↔They add beauty and charm to the world.把"没有他们世界会 shabby"还原为"他们让世界不 shabby、即美丽迷人"，正好对应They add beauty and charm to the world.。
D) 以偏概全They spend most of their lives drawing. 称他们一生大部分时间都在画画，但 P3 只说他们没有像普通人那样停止画画，并未说他们"一生大部分时间都在画画"。
questions.quote: There are people who don't, obviously, and thank God for that: a world without designers and artists would be a very shabby one indeed.

options.text: They are declining gradually in number.
They are keen on changing shabby surroundings.
They add beauty and charm to the world.
They spend most of their lives drawing.

questions.prompt: What does Professor D. B. Dowd argue in his book?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
D. B. Dowd教授在他的书中提出了什么论点?
A) 每个人生来都具有绘画的能力。
B) 绘画是一项需要专门训练的技能。
C) 绘画的价值往往被高估。
D) 绘画应该被重新定义为一种现实主义幻觉。
**判型** What does Professor D. B. Dowd argue in his book? 问具体某人在其书中提出的论点，属事实型细节题。
**拆句** What does Professor D. B. Dowd argue in his book? 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，argue 为关键动词，地点状语 in his book 仅作辅助定位，结构平直。
**定位** 在《火柴人：作为人类实践的绘画》一书中，D. B. Dowd 教授认为，我们把绘画的意义错误归类了，因为我们把它视为一种专业技能，而非一种个人能力。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确a personal capacity ↔ Everybody is born with the capacity to draw. instead of a personal capacity ↔ Everybody is born with the capacity to draw.教授的真正主张是 instead of 后的 a personal capacity（个人能力），其语义内核即"人人都具备"——正好对应 Everybody is born with the capacity to draw.。
B) 与原文相反Drawing is a skill that requires special training. 称绘画是需要专门训练的技能，但we see it as a professional skill instead of a personal capacity 中"专业技能"恰恰是教授要反对的错误归类，B 选项与教授立场南辕北辙。
C) 与原文相反The value of drawing tends to be overestimated. 称绘画的价值常被高估，但 we have misfiled the significance of drawing 中教授说的是"被错误归类"而非"被高估"，且全文基调是"绘画的价值被低估"——教授要为绘画正名。
D) 与原文相反Drawing should be redefined as a realistic illusion. 称绘画应被重新定义为"真实幻象"，但 Rather, drawing should be recategorized as a symbolic tool 明确说应被重新归类为"符号化工具"；而 realistic illusion 是教授要反对的旧定义。
questions.quote: In his book, Stick Figures: Drawing as a Human Practice, Professor D. B. Dowd argues that we have misfiled the significance of drawing because we see it as a professional skill instead of a personal capacity.

options.text: Everybody is born with the capacity to draw.
Drawing is a skill that requires special training.
The value of drawing tends to be overestimated.
Drawing should be redefined as a realistic illusion.

questions.prompt: What have some researchers found from one study about doodling?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
一些研究人员从一项关于涂鸦的研究中发现了什么?
A) 它是维持大脑基本活动水平的必要条件。
B) 它是激活大脑最可靠的刺激物。
C) 它可以把无聊的事情变成有趣的事情。
D) 它有助于提高注意力和记忆力。
**判型** What have some researchers found from one study about doodling? 问研究人员从一项具体研究中发现了什么，是事实细节。
**拆句** What have some researchers found from one study about doodling? 主干researchers have found what，状语 from one study 与 about doodling 双重限定研究对象，句式紧凑无陷阱。
**定位** 正因如此，有人认为在乏味的讲座中涂画可以帮助学生集中注意力。在一项研究中，参与者被要求一边听一串名字一边或涂画或静坐。涂画者比不涂画者多记住 29% 的名字。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全It is a must for maintaining a base level of brain activity. 称涂画是维持大脑基线活动的必要条件（a must），但 doodling activates the brain's so-called default circuit 只说涂画"激活"默认回路，并未说它是"必需的"，且默认回路本身就是在缺乏其他刺激时维持基线活动，不依赖涂画。
B) 无中生有It is the most reliable stimulant to activate the brain. 称涂画是激活大脑最可靠的刺激物，P6 只说"有些研究者认为"涂画能激活默认回路，从未将其与其他刺激物比较或评级。
C) 偷换概念It can turn something boring into something interesting. 称涂画能化无聊为有趣，但 doodling during a boring lecture can help students pay attention 只说在乏味讲座中涂画能助你专注，并未说讲座因此变有趣——是"帮你听下去"，不是"让它变好玩"。
D) ✓ 正确can help students pay attention ↔ It helps improve concentration and memory. Those who doodled remembered 29 percent more of the names than those who did not ↔It helps improve concentration and memory. D 的两个并列成分 concentration / memory 各自由原文两句独立支撑（pay attention/ remembered more），实现完整覆盖。
questions.quote: Because of this, some believe that doodling during a boring lecture can help students pay attention. In one study, participants were asked to listen to a list of names while either doodling or sitting still. Those who doodled remembered 29 percent more of the names than those who did not.

options.text: It is a must for maintaining a base level of brain activity.
It is the most reliable stimulant to activate the brain.
It can turn something boring into something interesting.
It helps improve concentration and memory.

questions.prompt: What is characteristic of people with drawing talent?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
具有绘画天赋的人有什么特点?
A) 对认知刺激的敏感性。
B) 表现的细腻性。
C) 分类的准确性。
D) 视觉感知的精确性。
**判型** What is characteristic of people with drawing talent? 问的是有绘画天赋的人具有什么特征，原文必有明示。
**拆句** What is characteristic of people with drawing talent? 主干 what is characteristic of X，characteristic 在此为形容词，介词 of 引出 X，句式简洁无陷阱。
**定位** 也有证据表明，绘画才能取决于一个人感知世界的准确程度。人类视觉系统常误判大小、形状、颜色和角度，但艺术家能比非艺术家更准确地感知这些特性。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴Sensitivity to cognitive stimulation. 称对认知刺激敏感，但 P7 谈的是视觉感知（visual perception）的准确度，并未涉及对认知刺激（cognitive stimulation）的敏感度——cognitive stimulation 是来自第 6 段涂画/默认回路话题的措辞。
B) 与原文相反Subtlety of representation. 称表现手法精巧，但 We mistakenly think of "good" drawings as those which work as recreations of the real world, as realistic illusions 明确表示"把绘画当作现实再现"是错误归类；且本题问的是绘画者的特征而非作品的特征。
C) 偷换概念Accuracy in categorization. 称分类的准确性，但 P7 说的是感知（perception）的准确性，并非分类（categorization）能力；文章中 categorization 一词只出现在第 4 段讨论绘画的"归类"问题，与艺术家的视觉能力无关。
D) ✓ 正确artists perceive these qualities more accurately than non-artists↔Precision in visual perception. The human visual system tends to misjudge size, shape, color, and angles↔Precision in visual perception.选项 D 把原文"perceive more accurately"整体名词化为"precision in visual perception"，是定位句的最简同义替换。
questions.quote: There's also evidence that drawing talent is based on how accurately someone perceives the world. The human visual system tends to misjudge size, shape, color, and angles but artists perceive these qualities more accurately than non-artists.
