questions.explanation:
**答案** L) realms 名词
**词性槽** in all ___ 介词＋限定词后接复数名词
**依据** in all realms 在所有领域men feel the need to appear competent in all __(26)__ 配合下文 while women worry only about the skills in which they've invested heavily——男性希望在『所有领域』都显得能干，女性只在自己擅长的领域才担心。realms = 领域，正好与 skills 形成范围对照。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) legacies 词义指向遗产、不合语境legacies 意为『遗产、前人遗留之物』，与『男性希望显得 competent（有能力）』毫无逻辑接口；男人不可能希望『在所有遗产里都显得能干』。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) heavily 副词
**词性槽** 动词 invested 后缺修饰副词
**依据** invest heavily 固定搭配＋语义匹配invest heavily（大量投入）是高频搭配，对应 the skills in which they've invested__(27)__ 所要表达的『投入了大量精力的技能』——女性只在自己投入很多的领域才担心是否胜任，逻辑通顺。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
O) viciously 感情色彩冲突viciously 是凶狠地、恶毒地，带强烈贬义色彩，无法修饰中性词 invest，搭配 invest viciously不成立。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) mastering 动词
**词性槽** 介词 for 后接动名词
**依据** mastering a skill 掌握一项技能master a skill（掌握一门技能）是高频搭配；对应 Praise won for mastering a skill suddenly puts one in the position of having everything to lose.——因为掌握一门技能而赢得的赞誉，反而让人陷入『一旦失败就全盘皆输』的处境。与 overview『成功反招失败焦虑』完全对应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
D) heaving heave a skill 搭配不成立heave 意为『用力举起、起伏』，对象多为重物（heave a stone/sigh），不与 skill（技能）搭配；heave a skill 在语义上不可解。

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) fatigue 名词
**词性槽** 并列名词清单中的一员
**依据** fatigue 与 drinking、depression 同属负面身心状态drinking, fatigue, depression 三者都是人们用来自我设限的『缺陷』——酗酒、疲劳、抑郁；fatigue 与 depression 同属健康/心理负面状态，并列自然。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
I) momentum 正向词、并列项语义冲突momentum（动力/势头）是正向词，无法与 drinking、depression 这类负面缺陷并列；放进句中会破坏 many successful people develop a handicap 的 handicap（缺陷）语义。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) hospitalized 动词
**词性槽** 名词后的过去分词作后置定语
**依据** hospitalized for depression 因抑郁住院be hospitalized for + 疾病 是固定表达；对应 An advertising executive hospitalized for depression shortly after winning an award——一位获奖后不久因抑郁住院的广告主管，正好印证前一句『许多成功人士发展出一种缺陷』。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) labeled labeled for 搭配不地道label 常用 be labeled as / be labeled a + 称号，不与 for + 疾病搭配；labeled for depression 表达模糊，不符英语习惯。
J) obsessed obsessed 常与 with 搭配be obsessed with sth 才是固定搭配；obsessed for depression 既不成习惯，也与上文『发展出一种缺陷/疾病』的事件性叙述不符。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 J) —— obsessed for depression 看似可解。30 题考生若不熟hospitalized for sth 这一医学固定搭配，很容易在 hospitalized、labeled、obsessed 三个过去分词里看混；obsessed 在『因抑郁而……』的中文语义里乍读也通，但 obsessed只跟 with、不跟 for，且语义指『痴迷』而非『生病住院』，与下一句的引语『没有抑郁，我就是失败者』完全不接。防坑要点：动词过去分词不仅看词义，更看后接介词是不是固定搭配。

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) obsessed 形容词
**词性槽** those ___ with 形容词作后置定语
**依据** obsessed with success 痴迷于成功be obsessed with sth 是『痴迷于某物』的标准搭配；对应 the people most likely to become chronic excuse makers are those obsessed with success.——最容易长期找借口的，正是那些痴迷成功的人，与下一句 Such people are so afraid of being labeled a failure at anything 因果连贯。

**答案** F) labeled 动词
**词性槽** being ___ a 后需被动分词带宾语
**依据** be labeled a failure 被贴上失败者的标签label sb a failure 是把人贴上『失败者』标签的标准说法，正好对应 Such people are so afraid of being labeled a failure at anything——这些人极度害怕在任何事上被贴上『失败者』的标签，所以才不停找借口。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
J) obsessed obsessed 不带『人＋名号』句型obsess 的固定搭配是 be obsessed with sth（痴迷于某事），不能后接名词作『把某人称作某X』的双宾结构；being obsessed a failure 语法不成立。

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) ruin 名词
**词性槽** lead to 后接名词
**依据** lead to ruin 后果性的负面词Though self-handicapping can be an effective way of coping with performance anxiety now and then, in the end, researchers say, it will lead to __(33)__. 用 though…in the end 形成让步＋强调对比，需要一个负面结果词；ruin（毁灭）正好填进 lead to ruin，对应下文 excuse makers fail to live up to their true potential and lose the status they care so much about——彻底失去地位 = ruin。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) fatigue 语义太弱、承担不了终局fatigue 仅表『疲劳』，远不足以承担 in the end 引出的总结性后果；且下文紧接 lose the status 的彻底失去，与单纯疲倦不匹配。
I) momentum 正向词，与 though…in the end 的反差不符momentum 表『势头、发展动力』，是正向词；放进 lead to momentum 成了好结果，与though self-handicapping can be effective…in the end 这一让步—反差结构所需的『负面终局』背道而驰。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 I) —— lead to momentum 词性正确但情感色彩反向。33 题考生只看 lead to 后接名词、容易在 fatigue、momentum、ruin 之间犹豫；momentum 看似与 lead to 搭配自然，却是正向词，违反 Though…in the end… 的让步逻辑——A 正面、B 必负面。防坑要点：见到 though…in the end…，先判情感色彩再选词。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) potential 名词
**词性槽** 形容词 true 后接名词
**依据** live up to one's potential 实现潜能live up to one's potential 是固定搭配，意为『发挥/不辜负自身潜能』；对应 excuse makers fail to live up to their true __(34)__——爱找借口的人最终无法发挥真正的潜力。语义与搭配双重契合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) fatigue 义为疲惫、与 live up to 不搭fatigue 指疲倦，与 live up to（不辜负、达到……期望）这一动词短语在语义上不构成正面期望，搭配不成立。
I) momentum 动力之意但搭配偏离momentum（势头）虽可与 maintain/gain 搭配，但 live up to one's momentum 并非地道表达；且与 true（真正的）连用语义生硬，远不如 potential 自然。
N) ruin 贬义＋逻辑反向ruin 意为毁灭，是贬义；fail to live up to their true ruin 等于『没能达到真正的毁灭』，逻辑完全相反，原文要说的是『没能发挥潜能』，不是『没能毁掉自己』。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) contrary 名词
**词性槽** to the ___ 介词＋定冠词后必跟名词
**依据** protests to the contrary 整套搭配protests to the contrary 意为『反对的抗议、否认到底的辩白』，对应 despite their protests to the __(35)__, they have only themselves to blame——即便他们极力辩解责任不在自己，事实上还是只能怪自己。逻辑完美自洽。

title: Children Understand Far More About Other Minds Than Long Believed

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Until a few decades ago, scholars believed that young children know very little, if anything, about what others are thinking.
Swiss psychologist Jean Piaget, who is credited with founding the scientific study of children's thinking, was convinced that preschool children cannot consider what goes on in the minds of others.

The interviews and experiments he conducted with kids in the middle of the 20th century suggested that they were trapped in their subjective viewpoints, incapable of imagining what others think, feel or believe.

passage.translation: 直到几十年前,学者们还认为幼儿对他人的想法知之甚少,甚至一无所知。瑞士心理学家Jean Piaget被认为是儿童思维科学研究的奠基人,他确信学龄前儿童无法考虑他人心中所想。他在20世纪中叶对儿童进行的访谈和实验表明,他们被困在自己的主观视角中,无法想象他人的想法、感受或信念。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: Much of the subsequent research on early childhood thinking was highly influenced by Piaget's ideas.
Scholars sought to refine his theory and empirically confirm his views.
But it became increasingly clear that Piaget seemed to have gravely underestimated the intellectual powers of very young kids before they can make themselves understood by speech.
Researchers began to devise ever more ingenious ways of figuring out what goes on in the minds of babies, and the resulting picture of their abilities shows subtle variations.

Consequently, the old view of children's egocentric(自我中心的) nature and intellectual weaknesses has increasingly fallen out of favor and become replaced by a more generous position that sees a budding sense not only of the physical world but also of other minds, even in the "youngest young."

passage.translation: 此后关于幼儿思维的大量研究深受Piaget思想的影响。学者们试图完善他的理论并通过实证证实他的观点。但人们越来越清楚地认识到,Piaget似乎严重低估了幼儿在能够通过语言表达自己之前的智力能力。研究人员开始设计出越来越巧妙的方法来弄清婴儿心中的想法,由此得出的关于他们能力的图景呈现出微妙的差异。因此,关于儿童自我中心本质和智力缺陷的旧观点日益失宠,被一种更宽容的立场所取代,这种立场认为即使在"最小的幼儿"身上,也存在着对物理世界以及他人心智的萌芽意识。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: Historically, children didn't receive much respect for their mental powers.

Piaget not only believed that children were "egocentric" in the sense that they were unable to differentiate between their own viewpoint and that of others; he was also convinced that their thinking was characterized by systematic errors and confusions.
When playing with others, they don't cooperate because they do not realize there are different roles and perspectives.
He was convinced that children literally cannot "get their act together": instead of playing cooperatively and truly together, they play side by side, with little regard for others.
And when speaking with others, a young child supposedly cannot consider the listener's viewpoint but "talks to himself without listening to others."

passage.translation: 从历史上看,儿童的心智能力并未受到太多尊重。Piaget不仅认为儿童是"自我中心的",即他们无法区分自己的视角和他人的视角;他还确信他们的思维以系统性错误和混乱为特征。在与他人玩耍时,他们不会合作,因为他们没有意识到存在不同的角色和视角。他确信儿童简直无法"协调一致":他们不是合作地真正一起玩耍,而是并排玩耍,很少顾及他人。而在与他人交谈时,幼儿据称无法考虑听者的视角,而是"自言自语,不听他人说话"。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: Piaget and his followers maintained that children go through something like a dark age of intellectual development before slowly and gradually becoming enlightened by reason and rationality as they reach school age.
Alongside this enlightenment develops an ever growing understanding of other persons, including their attitudes and views of the world.

passage.translation: Piaget及其追随者坚持认为,儿童在智力发展上经历了类似黑暗时代的阶段,然后在达到学龄时才缓慢渐进地被理性和理智所启蒙。伴随这种启蒙发展的是对他人的理解不断增长,包括对他们的态度和世界观的理解。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Today, a very different picture of children's mental development emerges.
Psychologists continually reveal new insights into the depth of young children's knowledge of the world, including their understanding of other minds.
Recent studies suggest that even infants are sensitive to others' perspectives and beliefs.

passage.translation: 如今,儿童心智发展呈现出截然不同的图景。心理学家不断揭示幼儿对世界认知深度的新见解,包括他们对他人心智的理解。最近的研究表明,即使是婴儿也对他人的视角和信念敏感。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: Part of the motivation to revise some of Piaget's conclusions stemmed from an ideological shift about the origin of human knowledge that occurred in the second half of the 20th century.
It became increasingly unpopular to assume that a basic understanding of the world can be built entirely from experience.

This was in part prompted by theorist Noam Chomsky, who argued that something as complex as the rules of grammar cannot be picked up from exposure to speech, but is supplied by an inborn "language faculty."
Others followed suit and defined further "core areas" in which knowledge allegedly cannot be pieced together from experience but must be possessed at birth.
One such area is our knowledge of others' minds.
Some even argue that a basic knowledge of others' minds is not only possessed by human infants, but must be evolutionarily old and hence shared by our nearest living relatives, the great apes.

passage.translation: 修正Piaget某些结论的部分动机源于20世纪下半叶发生的关于人类知识起源的意识形态转变。假设对世界的基本理解可以完全从经验中建立的观点变得越来越不受欢迎。这在一定程度上是由理论家Noam Chomsky促成的,他认为像语法规则这样复杂的东西不可能仅从接触言语中习得,而是由天生的"语言机能"提供的。其他人纷纷效仿,并定义了更多"核心领域",在这些领域中,知识据称无法从经验中拼凑而成,而必须是与生俱来的。其中一个领域就是我们对他人心智的认知。有些人甚至认为,对他人心智的基本认知不仅为人类婴儿所拥有,而且必定在进化上古老,因此被我们现存的近亲——类人猿所共享。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: To prove that infants know more in this realm than had been acknowledged, researchers needed to come up with innovative ways of showing it.
A big part of why we now recognize so much more of kids' intellectual capacities is the development of much more sensitive research tools than Piaget had at his disposal.

passage.translation: 为了证明婴儿在这个领域的认知超出了此前的认识,研究人员需要想出创新的方法来展示它。我们现在能认识到儿童如此多的智力能力,很大一部分原因在于开发出了比Piaget当时所拥有的更为敏锐的研究工具。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Instead of engaging babies in dialog or having them execute complex motor tasks, the newer methods capitalize on behaviors that have a firm place in infants' natural behavior repertoire: looking, listening, sucking, making facial expressions, gestures and simple manual actions.
The idea of focusing on these "small behaviors" is that they give kids the chance to demonstrate their knowledge implicitly and spontaneously without having to respond to questions or instructions.
For example, children might look longer at an event that they did not expect to happen, or they might show facial expressions indicating that they have sympathetic concern for others.

When researchers measure these less demanding, and often involuntary, behaviors, they can detect a sensitivity to others' mental states at a much younger age than with the more taxing methods that Piaget and his followers deployed.

passage.translation: 新方法没有让婴儿参与对话或让他们执行复杂的运动任务,而是利用了在婴儿自然行为repertoire中占有重要地位的行为:观看、倾听、吮吸、做面部表情、手势和简单的手部动作。关注这些"微小行为"的理念是,它们让儿童有机会隐含地、自发地展示他们的知识,而无需回应问题或指令。例如,儿童可能会对他们没有预料到会发生的事件注视更长时间,或者他们可能会表现出表明他们对他人有同情关切的面部表情。当研究人员测量这些要求较低且往往是非自主的行为时,他们能够在比Piaget及其追随者使用的更费力的方法所能达到的年龄更小的时候,就检测到对他人心理状态的敏感性。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: In the 1980s, these kinds of implicit measures became customary in developmental psychology.
But it took a while longer before these tools were employed to measure children's grasp of the mental lives of others.

passage.translation: 在20世纪80年代,这类隐含测量方法在发展心理学中变得常规化。但又过了一段时间,这些工具才被用来测量儿童对他人心理生活的把握。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: In a set of experiments, my colleagues at the University of Southern California and I found evidence that babies can even anticipate how others will feel when their expectations are disappointed.
We acted out several puppet(木偶) shows in front of two-year-old children.
In these puppet shows, a protagonist (Cookie Monster) left his precious belongings (cookies) on stage and later returned to fetch them.
What the protagonist did not know was that an antagonist had come and messed with his possessions.
The children had witnessed these acts and attentively watched the protagonist return.
We recorded children's facial and bodily expressions.
Children bit their lips, wrinkled their nose or wiggled(扭动) in their chair when the protagonist came back, as if they anticipated the bewilderment and disappointment he was about to experience.
Importantly, children showed no such reactions and remained calm when the protagonist had seen the events himself and thus knew what to expect.
Our study reveals that by the tender age of two, kids not only track what others believe or expect; they can even foresee how others will feel when they discover reality.

passage.translation: 在一系列实验中,我和南加州大学的同事们发现了证据表明,婴儿甚至能够预期当他人的期望落空时他们会有什么感受。我们在两岁儿童面前表演了几出木偶剧。在这些木偶剧中,一个主角(Cookie Monster)把他的珍贵物品(饼干)留在舞台上,后来回来取。主角不知道的是,一个反派角色曾经来过并弄乱了他的物品。儿童目睹了这些行为,并专注地看着主角回来。我们记录了儿童的面部和身体表情。当主角回来时,儿童咬着嘴唇、皱起鼻子或在椅子上扭动,仿佛他们预期到了他即将经历的困惑和失望。重要的是,当主角自己看到了这些事件因而知道会发生什么时,儿童没有表现出这样的反应并保持平静。我们的研究揭示,到两岁这个幼小的年龄,儿童不仅能追踪他人的信念或期望;他们甚至能预见当他人发现现实时会有什么感受。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: Studies like this reveal that there is much more going on in small kids' and even infants' minds than was previously believed.
With the explicit measures used by Piaget and successors, these deeper layers of kids' understanding cannot be accessed.

The new investigative tools demonstrate that kids know more than they can say: when we scratch beneath the surface, we find an emerging understanding of relations and perspectives that Piaget probably did not dream of.

passage.translation: 像这样的研究揭示,幼儿甚至婴儿的心智中发生的事情远比此前认为的要多。使用Piaget及其继任者所用的显性测量方法,无法触及儿童理解的这些深层次。新的调查工具表明,儿童知道的比他们能说出的更多:当我们深入表层之下时,我们发现了Piaget可能做梦都想不到的对关系和视角的新兴理解。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: Despite these obvious advances in the study of young children's thinking, it would be a grave mistake to dismiss the careful and systematic analyses compiled by Piaget and others before the new tests dominated the scene because the original methods revealed essential facts about how children think that the new methods cannot uncover.

passage.translation: 尽管在幼儿思维研究方面取得了这些明显的进步,但如果因此就摒弃Piaget和其他人在新测试主导局面之前所编纂的细致而系统的分析,那将是一个严重的错误,因为原始方法揭示了关于儿童如何思考的基本事实,而这些事实是新方法无法揭示的。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: There's no consensus in today's science community about how much we can infer from a look, a facial expression or a hand gesture.
These behaviors clearly indicate a curiosity about what goes on in the mind of others, and probably a set of early intuitions coupled with a willingness to learn more.
They pave the way to richer and more explicit forms of understanding of the minds of others.
But they can in no way replace the child's growing ability to articulate and refine her understanding of how people behave and why.

passage.translation: 在当今的科学界,对于我们能从一个眼神、一个面部表情或一个手势中推断出多少,尚无共识。这些行为清楚地表明了对他人心中所想的好奇心,可能还有一套早期直觉以及学习更多的意愿。它们为更丰富、更明确的理解他人心智的形式铺平了道路。但它们绝不能取代儿童日益增长的能力,即阐明和完善她对人们如何行为以及为何如此行为的理解。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

**定位** 他在 20 世纪中叶对孩子做的访谈和实验表明，孩子们被困在自己的主观视角里，无法想象他人在想什么、感受什么、相信什么。
**改写** Research conducted by Jean Piaget in the last century ↔The interviews and experiments he conducted with kids in the middle of the 20th century上位词Research涵盖访谈实验babies were insensitive to others' thinking ↔they were trapped in their subjective viewpoints, incapable of imagining what others think, feel or believe形容词凝练与动词短语展开同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
C C 段虽然反复出现 Piaget 与孩子无法考虑他人视角的话题，但用的是 Piaget not only believed that children were "egocentric"，讲的是他的信念与论断，而不是陈述句所要求的'他自己做的研究表明'这一信息来源。Piaget not only believed that children were "egocentric" in the sense that they were unable to differentiate between their own viewpoint and that of others D D 段虽含 Piaget and his followers maintained，但讲的是儿童会经历智力黑暗期再被理性启蒙，没有提到'他做的研究表明婴儿对他人想法不敏感'。Piaget and his followers maintained that children go through something like a dark age of intellectual development
questions.quote: The interviews and experiments he conducted with kids in the middle of the 20th century suggested that they were trapped in their subjective viewpoints, incapable of imagining what others think, feel or believe.

questions.prompt: Our improved understanding of babies' intellectual power is attributable to better research tools.
questions.explanation:
**答案** G 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
我们对婴儿智力能力认识的提高归功于更好的研究工具。
**锚点** 智力理解归功于更好工具
**定位** 我们今天之所以能识别儿童远比过去多得多的智力，很大程度上是因为研究工具比皮亚杰当年所能用到的更敏感得多。
**改写** Our improved understanding of babies' intellectual power ↔we now recognize so much more of kids' intellectual capacities理解提升的同义改写attributable to better research tools ↔the development of much more sensitive research tools than Piaget had at his disposal better与more sensitive同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
H H 段虽然也属于'新方法'话题，但写的是具体操作 looking, listening, sucking, making facial expressions, gestures and simple manual actions，没有明确把'对婴儿智力的更好理解'归因到'更好的工具'这一宏观因果关系。the newer methods capitalize on behaviors that have a firm place in infants' natural behavior repertoire: looking, listening, sucking, making facial expressions, gestures and simple manual actions
questions.quote: A big part of why we now recognize so much more of kids' intellectual capacities is the development of much more sensitive research tools than Piaget had at his disposal.

questions.prompt: It has been found in recent research that even small babies are sensitive to other people's points of view.
questions.explanation:
**答案** E 段（弱锚点）
**题目译文**
最近的研究发现,即使是很小的婴儿也对他人的观点很敏感。
**锚点** 近期研究小婴儿对他人视角敏感
**定位** 近期研究表明，连婴儿也对他人的视角和信念敏感。
**改写** recent research ↔ Recent studies research与studies同义even small babies ↔ even infants small babies与infants同义are sensitive to other people's points of view ↔ are sensitive to others' perspectives and beliefs points of view与perspectives同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
J J 段讲的是 two-year-old children 在木偶实验里的具体表现，没有提出'连 infants 也敏感'这种宽泛断言；且没有 Recent studies 这一总括表达。Children bit their lips, wrinkled their nose or wiggled(扭动) in their chair when the protagonist came back B B 段讲的是 a more generous position that sees a budding sense not only of the physical world but also of other minds 这种宏观观点取代，没有以 Recent studies来报告婴儿对他人视角的敏感这一具体发现。a more generous position that sees a budding sense not only of the physical world but also of other minds, even in the "youngest young."
questions.quote: Recent studies suggest that even infants are sensitive to others' perspectives and beliefs.

questions.prompt: Scientists are still debating what inference can be drawn from certain physical expressions of a child.
questions.explanation:
**答案** M 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
科学家们仍在争论可以从儿童的某些身体表现中得出什么推论。
**锚点** 科学家仍在争论身体表情推断
**定位** 对于从一个眼神、一个面部表情或一个手势中可以推断出多少东西，当今科学界尚无共识。
**改写** Scientists are still debating ↔ There's no consensus in today's science community争论与无共识同义what inference can be drawn from certain physical expressions of a child ↔how much we can infer from a look, a facial expression or a hand gesture physical expressions概括看表情手势
questions.quote: There's no consensus in today's science community about how much we can infer from a look, a facial expression or a hand gesture.

questions.prompt: The newer research methods focus on infants' simple behaviors instead of requiring them to answer questions.
questions.explanation:
**答案** H 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
较新的研究方法关注婴儿的简单行为,而不是要求他们回答问题。
**锚点** 新方法关注简单行为不答问题
**定位** 新方法不是让婴儿参与对话或执行复杂的运动任务，而是利用婴儿天然行为库中固有的那些行为：看、听、吸吮、做面部表情、手势和简单的手部动作。
**改写** The newer research methods ↔ the newer methods新方法名同义复现focus on infants' simple behaviors ↔capitalize on behaviors that have a firm place in infants' natural behavior repertoire focus on与capitalize on同义instead of requiring them to answer questions ↔without having to respond to questions or instructions排斥答问要求的同义改写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
G G 段说研究者必须 come up with innovative ways of showing it，强调需要新工具，但没有具体讲'新方法用什么简单行为代替答问题'这一操作层信息。researchers needed to come up with innovative ways of showing it
questions.quote: Instead of engaging babies in dialog or having them execute complex motor tasks, the newer methods capitalize on behaviors that have a firm place in infants' natural behavior repertoire: looking, listening, sucking, making facial expressions, gestures and simple manual actions.

questions.prompt: With the progress in psychology, the traditional view of children's self-centered nature and limited thinking abilities has become less and less influential.
questions.explanation:
**答案** B 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
随着心理学的进步,关于儿童以自我为中心的天性和有限思维能力的传统观点影响力越来越小。
**锚点** 自我中心旧观点影响力下降
**定位** 结果，那种认为儿童本性自我中心、智力薄弱的旧观点越来越失宠，被一种更宽厚的立场所取代：这种立场认为，即使在'最小的小娃'身上，也已经萌发了对物质世界、乃至他人心智的感知。
**改写** the traditional view of children's self-centered nature and limited thinking abilities ↔the old view of children's egocentric(自我中心的) nature and intellectual weaknesses传统观点与旧观点同义has become less and less influential ↔ has increasingly fallen out of favor影响力下降与失宠同义With the progress in psychology ↔Researchers began to devise ever more ingenious ways of figuring out what goes on in the minds of babies, and the resulting picture of their abilities shows subtle variations心理学进步的同义改写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E E 段也属心理学进步话题，但讲的是 Recent studies suggest that even infants are sensitive to others' perspectives and beliefs 这种新发现，没有直接说'自我中心旧观点越来越没影响力'。Psychologists continually reveal new insights into the depth of young children's knowledge of the world
questions.quote: Consequently, the old view of children's egocentric(自我中心的) nature and intellectual weaknesses has increasingly fallen out of favor and become replaced by a more generous position that sees a budding sense not only of the physical world but also of other minds, even in the "youngest young."

questions.prompt: Even though marked advances have been made, it is wrong to dismiss Piaget's fundamental contributions to the study of kids' cognitive abilities.
questions.explanation:
**答案** L 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
尽管已经取得了显著进展,但否定Piaget对儿童认知能力研究的根本贡献是错误的。
**锚点** 不应否定皮亚杰的根本贡献
**定位** 尽管在儿童思维研究上已有这些显著进展，但若就此否定皮亚杰等人在新方法主导之前所做的细致而系统的分析，那将是严重的错误，因为那些原始方法揭示了新方法所无法揭示的关于儿童思维的本质事实。
**改写** Even though marked advances have been made ↔Despite these obvious advances in the study of young children's thinking Even though与Despite同义让步it is wrong to dismiss Piaget's fundamental contributions to the study of kids' cognitive abilities↔it would be a grave mistake to dismiss the careful and systematic analyses compiled by Piaget and others before the new tests dominated the scene wrong与grave mistake同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
K K 段写的是 we find an emerging understanding of relations and perspectives that Piaget probably did not dream of，态度方向偏向'新方法挖到了皮亚杰没料到的东西'，而非'不应否定皮亚杰'。when we scratch beneath the surface, we find an emerging understanding of relations and perspectives that Piaget probably did not dream of
questions.quote: Despite these obvious advances in the study of young children's thinking, it would be a grave mistake to dismiss the careful and systematic analyses compiled by Piaget and others before the new tests dominated the scene because the original methods revealed essential facts about how children think that the new methods cannot uncover.

title: Is hunting good or bad for the environment?…

sentences.text: Is hunting good or bad for the environment?
Like so many hot button issues, the answer to this question depends upon who you ask.
On the one hand, some say, nothing could be more natural than hunting, and indeed just about every animal species—including humans—has been either predator or prey at some point in its evolution.

And, ironic as it sounds, since humans have wiped out many animal predators, some see hunting as a natural way to reduce the herds of prey animals that now reproduce beyond the environment's carrying capacity.

passage.translation: 狩猎对环境是好是坏？和许多热点问题一样，这个问题的答案取决于你问谁。一方面，有人说，没有什么比狩猎更自然的了，事实上几乎每一个动物物种——包括人类——在其进化过程中的某个时刻都曾是捕食者或猎物。而且，尽管听起来很讽刺，由于人类已经消灭了许多动物捕食者，一些人认为狩猎是减少猎物数量的自然方式，这些猎物现在的繁殖已超出环境承载能力。

sentences.text: On the other hand, many environmental and animal advocates see hunting as savage, arguing that it is morally wrong to kill animals, regardless of practical considerations.

According to Glenn Kirk of the California-based The Animals' Voice, hunting "causes immense suffering to individual wild animals…" and is "irrationally cruel because unlike natural predation(捕⻝), hunters kill for pleasure …" He adds that, despite hunters' claims that hunting keeps wildlife populations in balance, hunters' license fees are used to "manipulate a few game species into overpopulation at the expense of a much larger number of non-game species, resulting in the loss of biological diversity, genetic integrity and ecological balance."

passage.translation: 另一方面，许多环境和动物保护倡导者认为狩猎是野蛮的，主张杀死动物在道德上是错误的,无论实际考虑如何。根据加利福尼亚州The Animals' Voice的Glenn Kirk所说，狩猎"给野生动物个体造成巨大痛苦……"并且"是非理性的残忍，因为与自然捕食不同，猎人为了取乐而杀戮……"他还补充说，尽管猎人声称狩猎使野生动物种群保持平衡，但猎人的许可证费用被用来"操纵少数狩猎物种过度繁殖，而牺牲了数量多得多的非狩猎物种，导致生物多样性、遗传完整性和生态平衡的丧失。"

sentences.text: Beyond moral issues, others contend that hunting is not practical.

According to the Humane Society of the United States, the vast majority of hunted species—such as waterfowl, rabbits, upland birds and mourning doves—"provide minimal nutrition and do not require population control."

passage.translation: 除了道德问题之外，其他人认为狩猎并不实用。根据美国人道协会的说法，绝大多数被猎杀的物种——如水禽、兔子、高地鸟类和哀鸽——"提供的营养极少，并且不需要种群控制。"

sentences.text: Author Gary E.
Varner suggests in his book, In Nature's Interests, that some types of hunting may be morally justifiable while others may not be.

Hunting "designed to secure the aggregate welfare of the target species, the integrity of its ecosystem, or both"—what Varner terms "therapeutic hunting"—is defensible, while subsistence and sport hunting—both of which only benefit human beings—are not.

passage.translation: 作者Gary E. Varner在他的著作《自然的利益》中提出，某些类型的狩猎在道德上可能是正当的，而其他类型则可能不是。"旨在确保目标物种的整体福利、其生态系统的完整性或两者兼顾"的狩猎——Varner称之为"治疗性狩猎"——是可辩护的，而生存狩猎和运动狩猎——这两种都只有利于人类——则不是。

sentences.text: Regardless of one's individual stance, fewer Americans hunt today than in recent history.
Data gathered by the U.
S.
Fish & Wildlife Service in 2006 show that only five percent of Americans—some 12.5 million individuals—consider themselves hunters today, down from nine percent in 2001 and 15 percent in 1996.

passage.translation: 无论个人立场如何，如今狩猎的美国人比近代历史上要少。美国鱼类和野生动物管理局2006年收集的数据显示，只有5%的美国人——约1250万人——认为自己是猎人，低于2001年的9%和1996年的15%。

sentences.text: Public support for hunting, however, is on the rise.

A 2007 survey by Responsive Management Inc. found that eighty percent of respondents agreed that "hunting has a legitimate place in modern society," and the percentage of Americans indicating disapproval of hunting declined from 22 percent in 1995 to 16 percent in 2007.

passage.translation: 然而，公众对狩猎的支持率正在上升。Responsive Management Inc.2007年的一项调查发现，80%的受访者同意"狩猎在现代社会中有其合理地位"，而表示不赞成狩猎的美国人比例从1995年的22%下降到2007年的16%。

sentences.text: Perhaps matching the trend among the public, green leaders are increasingly advocating cooperation between hunters and environmental groups: After all, both deplore urban sprawl and habitat destruction.

passage.translation: 也许与公众的趋势相一致，环保领袖们越来越多地倡导猎人和环保组织之间的合作：毕竟，双方都痛惜城市扩张和栖息地破坏。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does the author say sounds ironic?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者说什么听起来很讽刺?
A) 一些捕食者可能经常成为其他捕食者的猎物。
B) 狩猎也可能是解决由狩猎引起的问题的一种方法。
C) 尽管人类狩猎,猎物动物的物种仍在持续变化。
D) 尽管环境变化,猎物动物的数量仍在持续增长。
**判型** 题干 What does the author say sounds ironic? 用 what 直接索取作者点名为讽刺的那件事，无 infer/imply/main idea 字样。
**拆句** What does the author say sounds ironic? 是宾语前置的间接引语：what 是 sounds ironic 的逻辑主语，the author say 作插入语；还原即 the author says (that) what sounds ironic。无陷阱，但要留意它问的是"被作者认为讽刺的事"，不是"讽刺地……"。
**定位** 而且，听起来虽然讽刺：既然人类已经消灭了许多动物天敌，有人就把狩猎看作一种天然手段，用来削减那些如今繁殖数量已超过环境承载力的猎物种群。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Some predators may often turn out to be prey of other predators. 谈"天敌也是别的天敌的猎物"的食物链问题，原文只提 humans 既是 predator 又是 prey，并未讨论天敌之间的相互捕食。
B) ✓ 正确since humans have wiped out many animal predators, some see hunting as a natural way to reduce the herds of prey animals that now reproduce beyond the environment's carrying capacity↔ Hunting may also be a solution to the problem caused by hunting.预判"制造问题的手段反过来变成解决问题的手段"与 Hunting may also be a solution to the problem caused by hunting. 完全等值——problem 对应 overpopulation, solution 对应 a natural way to reduce, caused by hunting 对应 humans have wiped out predators。
C) 答非所问The species of prey animals continue to vary despite humans' hunting. 说"猎物物种持续多样化"，原文未谈物种多样化方向；且即使为真，也回答的是"猎物物种变化"而非"作者觉得讽刺的事"。
D) 偷换概念The number of prey animals keeps rising despite environmental change. 把原文的"超过环境承载力 (beyond the environment's carrying capacity)"偷换成"despite environmental change（不顾环境变化）"，并丢弃了"因人类消灭天敌"这层因果。
questions.quote: And, ironic as it sounds, since humans have wiped out many animal predators, some see hunting as a natural way to reduce the herds of prey animals that now reproduce beyond the environment's carrying capacity.

options.text: Some predators may often turn out to be prey of other predators.
Hunting may also be a solution to the problem caused by hunting.
The species of prey animals continue to vary despite humans' hunting.
The number of prey animals keeps rising despite environmental change.

questions.prompt: What does Glenn Kirk think of charging hunters license fees?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
Glenn Kirk如何看待向猎人收取许可费?
A) 它使猎物种群数量得到控制。
B) 它将狩猎变成了富人的运动。
C) 它导致生态失衡。
D) 它有助于制止以娱乐为目的的猎杀。
**判型** 题干 What does Glenn Kirk think of charging hunters license fees? 索取一个具名人物对一个具体做法的明确观点，原文必有对应表述。
**拆句** What does Glenn Kirk think of charging hunters license fees? 中 charging hunters license fees 是动名词短语作 of 的宾语，charge sb. sth. 即"向某人收取某费"。基础薄弱考生易把 charging 误读为现在分词"正在收费的"，要看清它是名词性结构。
**定位** 他补充说：尽管猎人声称狩猎能让野生动物种群保持平衡，但猎人的执照费实际上被用来"操纵少数狩猎物种过度繁殖，代价是数量大得多的非狩猎物种，结果造成生物多样性、遗传完整性和生态平衡的丧失"。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反It keeps game population under control. 说"让狩猎物种数量受控"，但 Kirk 恰恰指出 license fees 是 manipulate a few game species into overpopulation——是制造过度繁殖，而非控制数量。
B) 无中生有It turns hunting into a sport of the rich. 说"把狩猎变成富人的运动"，原文从未提及收费让狩猎变贵或仅富人可及。
C) ✓ 正确resulting in the loss of biological diversity, genetic integrity and ecological balance ↔It leads to ecological imbalance.预判"执照费导致生态失衡"完整对应 It leads to ecological imbalance.，且把原文三项后果（diversity / integrity / balance）中最具概括性的 ecological balance 留作落点，正是六级正确项的典型做法。
D) 与原文相反It helps stop killing for pleasure. 说"有助于停止为娱乐而杀"，与 Kirk 全篇的批评立场矛盾——他在 P2 上半段还指责 hunters kill for pleasure，根本不可能认为执照费能解决这件事。
questions.quote: He adds that, despite hunters' claims that hunting keeps wildlife populations in balance, hunters' license fees are used to "manipulate a few game species into overpopulation at the expense of a much larger number of non-game species, resulting in the loss of biological diversity, genetic integrity and ecological balance."

options.text: It keeps game population under control.
It turns hunting into a sport of the rich.
It leads to ecological imbalance.
It helps stop killing for pleasure.

questions.prompt: What is the argument of the Humane Society of the United States against hunting?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
美国人道协会反对狩猎的论点是什么?
A) 对于大多数被猎杀的动物来说,过度繁殖不是一个问题。
B) 狩猎剥夺了动物种群的食物来源。
C) 许多鸟类和小型动物正在被不合理地猎杀。
D) 狩猎被普遍认为是一种野蛮行为。
**判型** 题干 What is the argument of the Humane Society of the United States against hunting? 直接索取一个组织的反方理据。
**拆句** What is the argument of the Humane Society of the United States against hunting?是 What is the N? 的判断句；against hunting 修饰 argument，意为"反对狩猎的论点"。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 美国人道协会指出：绝大多数被猎杀的物种——例如水禽、兔子、高地鸟和哀鸽——"营养价值极低，且并不需要被控制数量"。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确the vast majority of hunted species…"…do not require population control." ↔Overpopulation is not an issue for most hunted animals.预判"大多数被猎物种不需控数"与 Overpopulation is not an issue for most hunted animals. 完全对应：not require control（不需要控）= overpopulation is not an issue（不存在过剩问题）。
B) 无中生有Hunting deprives animal populations of their food sources. 说"狩猎剥夺了动物种群的食物来源"，原文 P3 全段未谈"食物来源"问题。
C) 张冠李戴Many birds and small animals are being irrationally killed. 这种"残忍/非理性"表述属于 P2 中 Glenn Kirk 的立场（irrationally cruel），而非 P3 中 Humane Society 的论点。
D) 过度推断Hunting is universally acknowledged as a savage behavior. 把"反方观点"夸张为"普遍公认"，universally 远超 P3 的具体表述，事实上 P2 已说明只是 some 反对者持此立场。
questions.quote: According to the Humane Society of the United States, the vast majority of hunted species—such as waterfowl, rabbits, upland birds and mourning doves—"provide minimal nutrition and do not require population control."

options.text: Overpopulation is not an issue for most hunted animals.
Hunting deprives animal populations of their food sources.
Many birds and small animals are being irrationally killed.
Hunting is universally acknowledged as a savage behavior.

questions.prompt: When is hunting morally justifiable according to Gary E. Varner?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
根据Gary E. Varner的观点,狩猎在什么时候在道德上是正当的?
A) 当它有利于动物及其生态系统时。
B) 当它同时服务于人类和动物的利益时。
C) 当它对人类生存不可或缺时。
D) 当它稳定动物物种的种群数量时。
**判型** 题干 When is hunting morally justifiable according to Gary E. Varner? 用 when 索取一个明确条件，原文必有 Varner 给出的判定标准。
**拆句** When is hunting morally justifiable according to Gary E. Varner? 是 when 引导的特殊疑问句，morally justifiable 是"副词+形容词"作表语，意为"在道德上可被辩护的"。结构清晰，无陷阱。
**定位** Varner 称那种"旨在保障目标物种整体福祉、其生态系统完整性、或二者兼顾"的狩猎为"治疗性狩猎"，认为它是可被辩护的；而生计性狩猎和运动性狩猎——这两者只让人类得益——则不可辩护。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确designed to secure the aggregate welfare of the target species, the integrity of its ecosystem, or both↔ When it benefits animals and their ecosystem.预判"为目标物种与生态系统好"与 When it benefits animals and their ecosystem. 一一对应——target species→animals, its ecosystem→their ecosystem, secure welfare/integrity→benefits。
B) 与原文相反When it serves both human and animal interests. 把答案纳入"既为人也为动物"，但原文 Varner 明确说仅 only benefit human beings 的 subsistence/sport hunting 是不可辩护的；可辩护的那类不包含"为人类利益"。
C) 与原文相反When it is indispensable to humans' subsistence. 直接为 subsistence hunting 辩护，而 Varner 明确把 subsistence hunting 列为"不可辩护"那一类。
D) 以偏概全When it stabilizes the population of animal species. 只截取"控数"这一面（接近 P1论调），而 Varner 的判据更宽——welfare、ecosystem integrity 都算；且"stabilize population"在 P4 并无对应表述。
questions.quote: Hunting "designed to secure the aggregate welfare of the target species, the integrity of its ecosystem, or both"—what Varner terms "therapeutic hunting"—is defensible, while subsistence and sport hunting—both of which only benefit human beings—are not.

options.text: When it benefits animals and their ecosystem.
When it serves both human and animal interests.
When it is indispensable to humans' subsistence.
When it stabilizes the population of animal species.

questions.prompt: What concept are green leaders trying to promote?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
环保领袖们试图推广什么概念?
A) 对动物栖息地的有效保护。
B) 对城市发展的严格控制。
C) 猎人与环保人士的协调努力。
D) 发展与动物保护之间的妥协。
**判型** 题干 What concept are green leaders trying to promote? 索取一个具体主张，原文末段必有对应表述。
**拆句** What concept are green leaders trying to promote? 是 what 作宾语前置的现在进行时疑问句，are trying to promote 表"正在努力推动"。注意 concept 是抽象名词，原文给的将是一个"主张/理念"而非具体行动。
**定位** 或许与公众的趋势相呼应，环保领袖们越来越主张猎人与环保团体之间展开合作：毕竟，双方都谴责城市无序扩张和栖息地破坏。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全Effective protection of animal habitats. 只截取末句 habitat destruction 的一个侧面，而 green leaders 推动的核心是"双方合作"——栖息地保护只是合作理由，不是他们倡导的概念。
B) 以偏概全Strict control over urban development. 同样只截取 urban sprawl 一个侧面，且green leaders 并未单独倡导"严控城市发展"，而是把"deplore urban sprawl"作为双方合作的共同立场。
C) ✓ 正确green leaders are increasingly advocating cooperation between hunters and environmental groups↔ Coordinated efforts of hunters and environmentalists.预判"猎人与环保派联手合作"与 Coordinated efforts of hunters and environmentalists. 一一对应，且选项的抽象度（concept）正好匹配题干 What concept 的提问层级。
D) 无中生有A compromise between development and animal protection. 引入"发展 vs 动物保护的妥协"二元对立，原文从未涉及"开发派 vs 保护派的妥协"。
questions.quote: Perhaps matching the trend among the public, green leaders are increasingly advocating cooperation between hunters and environmental groups: After all, both deplore urban sprawl and habitat destruction.

options.text: Effective protection of animal habitats.
Strict control over urban development.
Coordinated efforts of hunters and environmentalists.
A compromise between development and animal protection.

title: People often discuss the dangers of too much…

sentences.text: People often discuss the dangers of too much stress, but lately a very different view of stress is gaining popularity: this view of stress, held by members of the positive stress movement, argues that stress might actually be beneficial.
The positive stress movement is made up of people such as Zachary Rapp who are looking for an edge in a competitive world, and Rapp's routine is a good example of followers of the movement.
He wakes up most mornings at dawn, goes for a run, sips black coffee while ripping through emails, and then steps into a freezing cold shower.
This is a routine designed to reduce the stress of running simultaneously three different health and biotechnology companies for 18 hours a day.

passage.translation: 人们经常讨论压力过大的危险,但最近一种关于压力的截然不同的观点正在流行:这种由积极压力运动成员持有的压力观点认为,压力实际上可能是有益的。积极压力运动由像Zachary Rapp这样在竞争激烈的世界中寻求优势的人组成,而Rapp的日常作息就是该运动追随者的一个很好的例子。他大多数早晨在黎明时分醒来,去跑步,一边喝着黑咖啡一边快速处理电子邮件,然后进入冰冷的淋浴间。这是一套旨在减轻每天18小时同时经营三家不同的健康和生物技术公司的压力的日常作息。

sentences.text: Although Rapp's practices may sound extreme, he is part of a growing movement, consisting largely of tech industry workers who claim that such radical tactics will help them live better and longer.

Inspired by influential figures in different fields, including entertainers, athletes, entrepreneurs and scientists, positive stress practitioners seek out some combination of extreme temperatures, restrictive diets, punishing exercise routines and general discomfort.

passage.translation: 尽管Rapp的做法可能听起来极端,但他是一个不断壮大的运动的一部分,该运动主要由科技行业从业者组成,他们声称这种激进的策略将帮助他们生活得更好更长久。受到来自不同领域的有影响力人物的启发,包括演艺人员、运动员、企业家和科学家,积极压力实践者寻求极端温度、限制性饮食、高强度锻炼计划和普遍不适感的某种组合。

sentences.text: Rapp argues that positive stress keeps him balanced.

In addition to running and freezing showers, Rapp uses ice baths, hot yoga, and unconventional eating practices such as eliminating dairy, sugar, alcohol and various other foods high in carbohydrates.
He believes that these practices, which put stress on his body, actually make him feel less stress from work.
However, Rapp does not credit anyone in particular for his choices: he said he started using these methods in college, where he got into the habit of taking ice baths to recover from sports.
He got back into it while trying to get his three companies off the ground.

passage.translation: Rapp认为积极压力使他保持平衡。除了跑步和冰冷淋浴,Rapp还使用冰浴、高温瑜伽和非常规的饮食习惯,如不吃乳制品、糖、酒精和各种其他高碳水化合物食物。他相信这些给身体施加压力的做法,实际上使他感到来自工作的压力更少。然而,Rapp并没有将他的选择归功于任何特定的人:他说他在大学时就开始使用这些方法,当时他养成了洗冰浴来从运动中恢复的习惯。在努力让他的三家公司起步时,他又重新开始了这些做法。

sentences.text: Rapp works long hours and sleeps only five to seven hours a night but he said he only gets sick once a year.

For him, the difference between day-to-day stress, like the kind we feel when moving apartments, and positive stress is that the latter involves pushing the body to extremes and forcing it to build up a tolerance.

passage.translation: Rapp工作时间很长,每晚只睡五到七个小时,但他说他一年只生病一次。对他来说,日常压力(比如我们搬家时感受到的那种压力)和积极压力之间的区别在于,后者涉及将身体推向极限并迫使它建立耐受性。

sentences.text: One thought leader in the positive stress world is Dutch extreme athlete Wim Hof, who earned the name "ice man" for his ability to withstand severe cold using deep breathing exercises.
Hof's ideas have become popular among tech industry elites and, thanks to Hof, cold showers are now a trend; indeed, some even call it a form of therapy.

passage.translation: 积极压力领域的一位思想领袖是荷兰极限运动员Wim Hof,他因能够通过深呼吸练习承受严寒而获得了"冰人"的称号。Hof的理念在科技行业精英中变得流行,而且多亏了Hof,冷水淋浴现在成了一种趋势;实际上,有些人甚至称之为一种疗法。

sentences.text: But it is important to note that not everyone agrees with these practitioners; indeed, some medical professionals argue that positive stress is not for everyone, and that it might even be dangerous for people who are unhealthy or older.

passage.translation: 但重要的是要注意,并非每个人都同意这些实践者的观点;事实上,一些医学专业人士认为积极压力并不适合所有人,对于不健康或年长的人来说,它甚至可能是危险的。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about followers of the positive stress movement?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于积极压力运动的追随者,我们了解到什么?
A) 他们通常对不同类型的压力相当敏感。
B) 他们对压力持有与流行观点不同的看法。
C) 他们从过极其忙碌的生活中获得很多乐趣。
D) 他们通过享有良好的健康获得竞争优势。
**判型** What do we learn about followers of the positive stress movement 问的是关于该群体的客观信息，没有 infer/imply/mainly about 等推断或主旨信号。
**拆句** 题干是一般疑问式陈述句：主语 we、谓语 learn、介词短语 about followers of the positive stress movement 指明所问对象。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 人们常讨论压力过大的危害，但最近一种截然不同的压力观正在走红：这种观点由 positive stress movement 的成员所持，主张压力其实可能是有益的。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有sensitive to different types of stress『对不同压力敏感』全文未提；原文只说他们对压力的看法不同，不是对压力本身敏感。
B) ✓ 正确a very different view of stress ↔ a different view on stress from the popular one members of the positive stress movement ↔ They B 选项就是 a very different view of stress 的标准转述，与预判完全吻合。
C) 偷换概念derive much pleasure from living a very hectic life『从极忙生活中获取快乐』偷换了原文 looking for an edge in a competitive world 的概念——是『谋求优势』，不是『以忙为乐』。
D) 与原文相反gain a competitive edge by enjoying good health『靠好身体获得竞争优势』因果倒置：原文是为求竞争优势而做极端做法，不是先有好身体再获优势。
questions.quote: People often discuss the dangers of too much stress, but lately a very different view of stress is gaining popularity: this view of stress, held by members of the positive stress movement, argues that stress might actually be beneficial.

options.text: They are usually quite sensitive to different types of stress.
They hold a different view on stress from the popular one.
They derive much pleasure from living a very hectic life.
They gain a competitive edge by enjoying good health.

questions.prompt: What do followers of the positive stress movement usually do to put their ideas into practice?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
积极压力运动的追随者通常采取什么做法来将他们的理念付诸实践?
A) 他们不断改变自己的生活习惯。
B) 他们与有影响力的人物建立联系。
C) 他们在科技行业寻找工作。
D) 他们采用极端策略。
**判型** What do followers of the positive stress movement usually do to put their ideas into practice 明确问『通常做什么』，是对动作的客观提取。
**拆句** 主句 What do followers...usually do，加目的状语 to put their ideas into practice。注意 usually 是程度词，提醒考生找的是『常态做法』而非个例。
**定位** 在不同领域影响力人物（包括艺人、运动员、企业家和科学家）的启发下，positive stress实践者主动追求极端温度、限制性饮食、严苛锻炼和总体上的不适感的某种组合。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有keep changing their living habits『不断改变生活习惯』全文未出现，原文讲的是采取固定的极端做法，不是频繁更换。
B) 张冠李戴network with influential figures『与影响力人物建立人脉』把原文 Inspired by influential figures『受其启发』偷换为『与其建立关系』，主体关系完全错位。
C) 答非所问seek jobs in tech industries『在科技行业找工作』错读了原文 consisting largely of tech industry workers——后者是描述该群体『大多由科技业从业者组成』的成员构成，不是他们的『做法』。
D) ✓ 正确extreme temperatures, restrictive diets, punishing exercise routines and general discomfort ↔extreme tactics positive stress practitioners seek out ↔ They apply D 用 extreme tactics 一词把原文四个并列做法整体收口，正好对应预判中的『极端手段』。
questions.quote: Inspired by influential figures in different fields, including entertainers, athletes, entrepreneurs and scientists, positive stress practitioners seek out some combination of extreme temperatures, restrictive diets, punishing exercise routines and general discomfort.

options.text: They keep changing their living habits.
They network with influential figures.
They seek jobs in tech industries.
They apply extreme tactics.

questions.prompt: What does Zachary Rapp say about his unconventional practices?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
Zachary Rapp对他的非常规做法是怎么说的?
A) 这些做法帮助他对抗工作压力。
B) 这些做法使他能够减少生活开支。
C) 这些做法使他能够从伤病中恢复。
D) 这些做法帮助他同时让三家公司上市。
**判型** What does Zachary Rapp say about his unconventional practices 问 Rapp 自己怎么说，是观点转述类细节题。
**拆句** What does Zachary Rapp say about his unconventional practices：主语 Rapp、谓语say、about 后是讨论对象。无陷阱。
**定位** 他相信这些给身体施压的做法，反而让他感受到的工作压力变少。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确make him feel less stress from work ↔ combat stress from work these practices ↔ They A 把『让他感觉压力变小』这一结果改写为『帮助他对抗压力』这一动作，是六级细节题典型的『因果同义改写』。
B) 无中生有cut down living expenses『降低生活开销』全文从未涉及任何与花费相关的内容。
C) 偷换概念recover from injuries and illnesses『从伤病中恢复』把原文 taking ice baths to recover from sports『大学时洗冰浴以从运动中恢复』偷换为『从伤病中恢复』，且这是『大学时的起源』而非『现在做法的效果』。
D) 偷换概念get three companies enlisted all at once『让三家公司同时上市』把原文 trying to get his three companies off the ground『让三家公司起步』偷换成『让三家公司上市』；get off the ground 与 enlist 不是一回事。
questions.quote: He believes that these practices, which put stress on his body, actually make him feel less stress from work.

options.text: They help him combat stress from work.
They enable him to cut down living expenses.
They enable him to recover from injuries and illnesses.
They help him get three companies enlisted all at once.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from the passage about day-to-day stress?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （推断题）
**题目译文**
从文章中可以推断出关于日常压力的什么信息?
A) 它对人的身心健康有害。
B) 它在本质上与积极压力没有区别。
C) 它是每个人都必须面对的事情。
D) 它无助于增强人的耐受力。
**判型** What can be inferred from the passage about day-to-day stress 中 inferred 明确点出题型。
**拆句** What can be inferred from the passage about day-to-day stress：主句 What can be inferred、状语 from the passage、about 后是话题对象。注意 can be inferred 是被动语态加情态动词，等于 we can infer。
**定位** 对他来说，日常压力（比如搬家时感受到的那种）与 positive stress 的区别在于：后者会把身体推向极端，迫使身体建立耐受度。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断harmful to one's physical and mental health『对身心健康有害』全文未对 day-to- day stress 作如此强烈的负面判断；首段提到的 dangers of too much stress 也是说『过大压力』而非 day-to-day。
B) 与原文相反does not differ in essence from positive stress『与 positive stress 本质上无区别』恰恰与定位句 the difference between day-to-day stress...and positive stress 强调的『二者有区别』完全相反。
C) 无中生有something everybody has to live with『人人必须忍受』全文未对 day-to-day stress是否普遍作出判断。
D) ✓ 正确the latter involves pushing the body to extremes and forcing it to build up a tolerance ↔does not help build up one's tolerance the difference between day-to-day stress...and positive stress is that the latter ↔ It the latter 独占 build up a tolerance，按对比逻辑前者就缺失该特征——D 正好把这一反向推论说出来。
questions.quote: For him, the difference between day-to-day stress, like the kind we feel when moving apartments, and positive stress is that the latter involves pushing the body to extremes and forcing it to build up a tolerance.

options.text: It is harmful to one's physical and mental health.
It does not differ in essence from positive stress.
It is something everybody has to live with.
It does not help build up one's tolerance.

questions.prompt: What do some medical professionals think of positive stress?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
一些医疗专业人士如何看待积极压力?
A) 其真实效果有待验证。
B) 其副作用不应被忽视。
C) 其效果因人而异,差别很大。
D) 其实践者不应将其作为一种治疗形式。
**判型** What do some medical professionals think of positive stress 问的是该群体的客观观点，可在文中找到对应转述句，不是全文态度题。
**拆句** What do some medical professionals think of positive stress：注意 some 是范围词——只是『一些』医生，不代表全体，提示选项里不要选全称表述。
**定位** 但需要注意的是，并非所有人都赞同这些实践者；事实上，一些医学专业人士主张 positive stress 并不适合所有人，对体质不佳或年长者甚至可能有危险。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Its true effect remains to be verified『真正效果有待验证』全文未提及医生对positive stress 效果是否已被验证的判断。
B) 偷换概念Its side effect should not be ignored『不应忽视其副作用』把 might even be dangerous 偷换为 side effect（副作用）；危险不等于副作用，副作用是医学专门术语。
C) ✓ 正确not for everyone ↔ varies considerably from person to person it might even be dangerous for people who are unhealthy or older ↔ varies considerably原文一边否定『对所有人都适用』，一边指出特定群体可能有危险——这两点合起来就是『效果因人而异』，C 精准命中。
D) 张冠李戴Its practitioners should not take it as a form of therapy『实践者不应把它当作疗法』把 some even call it a form of therapy『有人甚至称其为一种疗法』错配到医生头上，且未在医生口中出现这种反对意见。
questions.quote: But it is important to note that not everyone agrees with these practitioners; indeed, some medical professionals argue that positive stress is not for everyone, and that it might even be dangerous for people who are unhealthy or older.

options.text: Its true effect remains to be verified.
Its side effect should not be ignored.
Its effect varies considerably from person to person.
Its practitioners should not take it as a form of therapy.

title: The United Nations issued a report last week…

sentences.text: The United Nations issued a report last week warning that humans are destroying nature at such a rate that life on Earth is at risk.
When the report came out, it naturally (26)____ headlines.
But obviously it didn't hijack the news agenda in the manner of a major terrorist attack or (27)____ of war.

passage.translation: 联合国上周发布了一份报告，警告人类正在以如此之快的速度破坏自然，以至于地球上的生命面临危险。当该报告发布时，它自然地占据了新闻头条。但显然它并没有像重大恐怖袭击或宣战那样主导新闻议程。

sentences.text: The report from the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES) is clear on what's at (28)____ and what needs to change.
IPBES chair Robert Watson says the " (29)____ evidence" presents an "ominous(凶兆的) picture".
"The health of ecosystems on which we and all other species depend is (30)____ more rapidly than ever," Robert Watson said.
"We are (31)____ the very foundations of our economies, livelihoods, food security, health and quality of life worldwide."
The report says it's not too late if we make "transformative change"—fundamental, system- wide reorganization—at every level from local to global, and we need to focus on how to make that happen.

passage.translation: 生物多样性和生态系统服务政府间科学政策平台（IPBES）的报告清楚地说明了利害关系以及需要改变什么。IPBES主席Robert Watson表示，"压倒性的证据"呈现出一幅"凶兆的画面"。"我们以及所有其他物种赖以生存的生态系统的健康状况正在以前所未有的速度恶化，"Robert Watson说。"我们正在侵蚀全球经济、生计、粮食安全、健康和生活质量的根基。"报告称，如果我们进行"变革性改变"——从地方到全球各个层面进行根本性的、全系统的重组——现在还为时不晚，我们需要关注如何实现这一目标。

sentences.text: First, don't indulge in despair, because despair leads to inertia and doing nothing means certain(32)____ .
Every action to save nature will improve our collective and personal futures and the only way to respond to a threat of this scale is with (33)____ action rooted in headstrong optimism.
Second, we need relentless focus, just like when paramedics(救护人员) arrive on a scene and use the concept of "triage(伤员鉴别分类)" to ensure the most (34)____ cases get treated first.
Saving the natural world needs that kind of thinking.

passage.translation: 首先，不要沉溺于绝望，因为绝望会导致惰性，而无所作为意味着必然的灾难。拯救自然的每一个行动都将改善我们的集体和个人未来，应对这种规模威胁的唯一方法是采取植根于顽强乐观主义的坚定行动。其次，我们需要不懈的专注，就像救护人员到达现场时使用"伤员鉴别分类"的概念来确保最紧急的病例首先得到治疗一样。拯救自然世界需要这种思维方式。我们没有能力同时做所有事情。我们需要做出艰难的选择。

groups.content:
The United Nations issued a report last week warning that humans are destroying nature at such a rate that life on Earth is at risk. When the report came out, it naturally {{26}} headlines. But obviously it didn't hijack the news agenda in the manner of a major terrorist attack or {{27}} of war.

The report from the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES) is clear on what's at {{28}} and what needs to change. IPBES chair Robert Watson says the " {{29}} evidence" presents an "ominous(凶兆的) picture". "The health of ecosystems on which we and all other species depend is {{30}} more rapidly than ever," Robert Watson said. "We are {{31}} the very foundations of our economies, livelihoods, food security, health and quality of life worldwide." The report says it's not too late if we make "transformative change"—fundamental, system- wide reorganization—at every level from local to global, and we need to focus on how to make that happen.

First, don't indulge in despair, because despair leads to inertia and doing nothing means certain{{32}} . Every action to save nature will improve our collective and personal futures and the only way to respond to a threat of this scale is with {{33}} action rooted in headstrong optimism. Second, we need relentless focus, just like when paramedics(救护人员) arrive on a scene and use the concept of "triage(伤员鉴别分类)" to ensure the most {{34}} cases get treated first. Saving the natural world needs that kind of thinking. We don't have the {{35}} to do everything at once. We need to make hard choices.

options.text: capacity
Junction
declaration
Monotonous
deteriorating
overwhelming
determined
stagnation
disaster
stake
eroding
stifled
grabbed
urgent
