questions.explanation:
**答案** K) prematurely 副词
**词性槽** 完整句缺修饰语，需副词修饰动词 died
**依据** 『过早地』正契合污染致死语境上文 The persistent haze over many of our cities is a reminder of the polluted air that we breathe 在讲污染危害，450 万人因户外污染死亡，强调的是『本不该这么早就死却被污染夺命』，prematurely（过早地）正好刻画这种非自然提前死亡。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
L) simply 『仅仅』与死因无逻辑关联simply 意为『仅仅/简单地』，放进 die simply from… 语义空洞，与统计 450 万死亡的严肃语境不搭，且 simply 在第 35 题另有更贴的搭配位（almost double → 几乎），应留给那道空。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) determine 动词
**词性槽** 情态动词 will 后需动词原形
**依据** 『决定』未来生活与健康the decisions that we make now about the design of our cities will __(27)__ the everyday lives and health of the coming generations：『今天的城市设计决定未来几代人的日常生活与健康』，determine（决定/影响走向）正是这种因果定调；与前句 What is more important 也呼应——重要在于现在的决策对未来的『决定性』作用。

**答案** N) synonymous 形容词
**词性槽** 系动词 become 之后需表语形容词
**依据** be synonymous with = 与……几乎等同Traffic has become __(28)__ with air pollution, and many countries intend to ban the sale of petrol and diesel cars 表达『交通已与空气污染密不可分』，这正是 synonymous with 的核心义——两件事在大众认知里几乎划等号；下半句各国禁售燃油车恰是这种『等号印象』的政策回应。

**答案** M) switching 动词
**词性槽** 副词 simply 后需动名词，作主语
**依据** switch to electric cars = 改用电动车，是新闻地道搭配But simply __(29)__ to electric cars will not mean pollution-free cities：上文刚说各国要禁售燃油车，此处转折『仅仅换成电动车也未必无污染』，switch to（改用/切换到）正是描述能源类型转换的标准动词，与下文电力来源、轮胎刹车颗粒物的讨论形成逻辑链。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) opting 搭配错位：opt for 而非 opt to + 名词opt 表『选择』时固定搭配是 opt for sth 或 opt to do sth，而不是 opt to + 名词。这里空后是 to electric cars（介词 to + 名词），与 opt 的语法框架不符。opting 应留给第 32 题的 are opting for other means of travel。
E) locating 义不对：『定位』与切换车型无关locating 意为『确定位置/选址』，与『换成电动车』的语义毫不相干；且 locate 通常作及物动词直接接宾语，不与 to 构成习惯搭配。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— opting 形态对，却被介词 to 卡死。29 题 But simply__(29)__ to electric cars 看到 -ing 词形和『选择电动车』的语义诱惑，容易直接抓opting；但 opt 搭配是 opt for sth，不是 opt to + 名词，正确答案是 switching（switch to）。防坑法：动词搭配看准 for/to/from/of 等介词，一字之差就错。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) generated 动词
**词性槽** be 动词 is 后需过去分词，构成被动
**依据** electricity is generated 是『电是怎么发出来的』标准说法The level of emissions they cause will depend on how the electricity to run them is__(30)__：电动车的排放高低，取决于驱动它们的电是『怎么发出来的』——煤电、风电、核电决定排放——generate electricity（发电）是固定搭配，被动 electricity is generated 完全自然。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) merged 『合并』与发电主题不搭merge 表『合并/融合』，多用于公司、文件、河流；说『电是怎么被合并的』在语义上不通，与上下文谈电力来源的污染影响完全无关。

questions.explanation:
**答案** I) particles 名词
**词性槽** 形容词 + ___ 作宾语，需名词复数
**依据** airborne particles = 空气悬浮颗粒，环境科学固定术语整段在讲电动车也未必让城市无污染：brakes, tyres and roads all create tiny airborne__(31)__ as they wear out，刹车片、轮胎和路面磨损会产生『微小的空气悬浮颗粒』——这正是大气科学里的 PM 颗粒物概念，与全文污染主题严丝合缝。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) miniatures 『微缩模型』与污染语境完全跑题miniatures 指『微型画/微缩模型』，多用于艺术、玩具语境；说刹车和轮胎磨损产生『微缩模型』在物理与语义上都讲不通，是命题人利用『miniature 看着像 mini』设的陷阱。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) opting 动词
**词性槽** are + ___ 进行时，且后接 for
**依据** opt for = 选择，固定搭配young people especially are __(32)__ for other means of travel：年轻人尤其『正在选择其他出行方式』——opt for sth 正是英语里『选择某物/某条路径』的常见动词搭配，与全段年轻人减少开车、转向新出行方式的语境契合。

**答案** J) peak 名词
**词性槽** 形容词性物主代词 its 后需名词
**依据** reach its peak 是固定搭配『达到顶峰』Researchers are already asking if motor vehicle use has reached its __(33)__ and will decline：研究者在问机动车使用是否已『达到顶峰并即将下降』——peak 与紧随其后的decline（下降）构成『顶峰→下降』的逻辑闭环，reach the/its peak 也是英语里最常见的搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
O) trend 『达到趋势』搭配不成立且逻辑反转reach its trend 在英语里不是地道搭配；而且 trend 是『走向/潮流』，与紧跟的 will decline（即将下降）形成不了对照逻辑——下文要表达的是『到顶后下落』，不是『到达趋势』。trend 应留给下题 34 题，其语境正是『这一趋势』。
B) crown 义近 peak 但搭配不当crown 虽有『顶点』之意，但 reach its crown 不是英语固定搭配；同时全段语气偏中性学术，crown 文学色彩过浓，不如 peak 自然。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 B) —— crown『顶点』乍看可填，实为搭配陷阱。crown 在词典里也释为『顶点』，与 reached its __(33)__ and will decline 的『见顶』看似匹配；但 reach its crown 不是地道搭配，reach its peak 才是。防坑法：在词义『差不多』时，优先选择有固定搭配的那个词。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) trend 名词
**词性槽** 指示代词 this 后需名词
**依据** catch up with this trend = 跟上这一趋势上一句刚说 Researchers are already asking if motor vehicle use has reached its__(33)__ and will decline，指明『机动车使用见顶下行』本身就是一个新出现的现象趋势；this trend 正好回指上一句的『见顶下降』，与下文『不再修新路』形成对照。

**答案** L) simply 副词
**词性槽** 情态动词 can 与原形动词 double 之间需副词
**依据** simply double = 简直就是翻倍studies have shown that doubling the size of a road can __(35)__ double the traffic, taking us back to the starting point：研究表明把路加倍，车流量也几乎『简直就翻倍』，simply 在此表示『简直/纯粹地』，强化『扩路反而毫无效果』的反讽，与结尾taking us back to the starting point（回到原点）一拍即合。

title: Here's how the Pacific Northwest is preparing for…

sentences.text: Here's how the Pacific Northwest is preparing for "The Big One".
It's the mother of all disaster drills for what could be the worst disaster in American history.
California has spent years preparing for "The Big One"—the inevitable earthquake that will undoubtedly unleash all kinds of havoc along the famous San Andreas fault(断层).
But what if the fault that runs along the Pacific Northwest delivers a gigantic earthquake of its own?
If the people of the Cascadia region have anything to do with it, they won't be caught unawares.

passage.translation: 以下是太平洋西北地区为"大地震"所做的准备。这是针对美国历史上可能发生的最严重灾难而进行的最大规模灾难演习。加利福尼亚州已经花费数年时间为"大地震"做准备——这场不可避免的地震无疑将沿着著名的圣安德烈亚斯断层释放各种破坏。但如果沿太平洋西北地区延伸的断层也引发一场巨大地震呢?如果Cascadia地区的人们能够有所作为,他们就不会措手不及。

sentences.text: The region is engaged in a multi-day earthquake-and-tsunami(海啸) drill involving around 20,000 people.

The Cascadia Rising drill gives area residents and emergency responders a chance to practice what to do in case of a 9.0 magnitude earthquake and tsunami along one of the nation's dangerous—and underestimated—faults.

passage.translation: 该地区正在进行一场为期多天的地震和海啸演习,约有20000人参与。Cascadia Rising演习为该地区居民和应急响应人员提供了一个机会,让他们练习在发生9.0级地震和海啸时该如何应对,这些灾害可能沿着美国最危险且被低估的断层之一发生。

sentences.text: The Cascadia Earthquake Zone is big enough to compete with San Andreas (it's been called the most dangerous fault in America), but it's much lesser known than its California cousin.
Nearly 700 miles long, the earthquake zone is located by the North American Plate off the coast of Pacific British Columbia, Washington, Oregon and Northern California.

passage.translation: Cascadia地震带的规模足以与圣安德烈亚斯断层相匹敌(它被称为美国最危险的断层),但它远不如其加利福尼亚同类断层那样为人所知。这个地震带长近700英里,位于太平洋不列颠哥伦比亚省、华盛顿州、俄勒冈州和北加利福尼亚海岸外的北美板块附近。

sentences.text: Cascadia is what's known as a "megathrust" fault.
Megathrusts are created in earthquake zones—land plate boundaries where two plates converge.
In the areas where one plate is beneath another, stress builds up over time.
During a megathrust event, all of that stress releases and some of the world's most powerful earthquakes occur.
Remember the 9.1 earthquake and tsunami in the Indian Ocean off Sumatra in 2004?
It was caused by a megathrust event as the India plate moved beneath the Burma micro-plate.

passage.translation: Cascadia是所谓的"巨型逆冲"断层。巨型逆冲断层形成于地震带——即两个板块汇聚的陆地板块边界。在一个板块位于另一个板块下方的区域,压力会随着时间推移而积累。在巨型逆冲事件中,所有这些压力都会释放,世界上一些最强烈的地震由此发生。还记得2004年苏门答腊附近印度洋发生的9.1级地震和海啸吗?它是由印度板块移动到缅甸微板块下方而引发的巨型逆冲事件造成的。

sentences.text: The last time a major earthquake occurred along the Cascadia fault was in 1700, so officials worry that another event could occur any time.
To prevent that event from becoming a catastrophe, first responders will join members of the public in rehearsals that involve communication, evacuation, search and rescue, and other scenarios.

passage.translation: 上一次沿Cascadia断层发生重大地震是在1700年,因此官员们担心另一次地震事件可能随时发生。为了防止该事件演变成灾难,急救人员将与公众成员一起参加演习,演习内容包括通信、疏散、搜救和其他场景。

sentences.text: Thousands of casualties are expected if a 9.0 earthquake were to occur.
First, the earthquake would shake metropolitan areas including Seattle and Portland.
This could trigger a tsunami that would create havoc along the coast.
Not all casualties can necessarily be prevented—but by coordinating across local, state, and even national borders, officials hope that the worst-case scenario can be averted.
On the exercise's website, officials explain that the report they prepare during this rehearsal will inform disaster management for years to come.

passage.translation: 如果发生9.0级地震,预计将有数千人伤亡。首先,地震会震动包括西雅图和波特兰在内的大都市区。这可能引发海啸,在沿海地区造成严重破坏。并非所有伤亡都能够避免——但通过跨地方、州乃至国家边界的协调,官员们希望能够避免最坏的情况发生。在演习网站上,官员们解释说,他们在此次演习期间准备的报告将为未来多年的灾害管理提供信息。

sentences.text: For hundreds of thousands of Cascadia residents, "The Big One" isn't a question of if, only when.
And it's never too early to get ready for the inevitable.

passage.translation: 对于数十万Cascadia居民来说,"大地震"不是会不会发生的问题,而只是何时发生的问题。为不可避免的事情做好准备永远不会太早。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does "The Big One" refer to?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**

A) 一条巨大的地质断层。
B) 一次为灾难做准备的大规模演习。
C) 一场大规模的自然灾难。
D) Caledonia海岸的一次巨大海啸。
**判型** What does "The Big One" refer to? 问的是一个具体称呼的所指，答案就在原文释义里。
**拆句** 句式 What does "The Big One" refer to? 为简单 wh- 疑问句，主语 "The Big One" 借助助动词 does 倒装，refer to 是动词短语；结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 下面是太平洋西北部如何为 "The Big One" 做准备。这是为可能成为美国历史上最严重灾难的一场"灾难演练之母"。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念选项把 "The Big One" 偷换为 A gigantic geological fault；原文虽提到 San Andreas/ Cascadia 断层，但 "The Big One" 指的是断层引发的灾难，而非断层本身。
B) 偷换概念A large-scale exercise to prepare for disasters 描述的是 disaster drills 这件事，而"The Big One" 指的是"将要应对的灾难"，两者是"演练 vs. 演练所应对的灾难"，正好被偷换。
C) ✓ 正确the worst disaster in American history↔ A massive natural catastrophe预判结论是"最严重的自然灾难"，四个选项中只有 A massive natural catastrophe 与之同义对应，其他三项指向断层、演练或海啸（地点错），均偏离释义。
D) 无中生有原文反复出现的是 Cascadia，从未出现 Caledonia；选项 A huge tsunami on the Caledonia coast 用形近词制造混淆，同时把灾难范围缩小为"海啸"，缩窄并改地名。
questions.quote: Here's how the Pacific Northwest is preparing for "The Big One". It's the mother of all disaster drills for what could be the worst disaster in American history.

options.text: A gigantic geological fault.
A large-scale exercise to prepare for disasters.
A massive natural catastrophe.
A huge tsunami on the Caledonia coast. "The Big One"指 的 是 什 么?

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the Cascadia Rising drill?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
Cascadia Rising演习的目的是什么?
A) 让人们为重大地震和海啸做好准备。
B) 提高居民对即将发生的灾难的意识。
C) 教会人们如何适应灾后生活。
D) 应对可能发生的地震的后续影响。
**判型** What is the purpose of the Cascadia Rising drill? 直接询问某个具体演练的目的，答案应在原文显式给出。
**拆句** 句式 What is the purpose of the Cascadia Rising drill? 为 What + be + 主语 的简单疑问句，主语是 the purpose of the Cascadia Rising drill，结构清晰、无歧义。
**定位** Cascadia Rising 演练让本地居民与应急响应人员有机会演练：当沿一条全国最危险且被低估的断层发生 9.0 级地震和海啸时该怎么办。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确practice what to do in case of a 9.0 magnitude earthquake and tsunami ↔To prepare people for a major earthquake and tsunami预判核心是"为地震和海啸做准备"，四项里只有 A 同时含 prepare、earthquake、tsunami 三要素，且对象 people 与原文听众范围吻合；其他三项要么换动作、要么换对象、要么换时机。
B) 偷换概念To increase residents' awareness of imminent disasters 把 practice 偷换为increase...awareness；原文目的是"练习如何应对"这一动作，而非"提升意识"这一心理状态；且 imminent 在原文无依据。
C) 偷换概念To teach people how to adapt to post-disaster life 谈灾后生活适应，与原文 in case of...earthquake and tsunami 谈的灾时应对完全错位；演练发生在灾前，目标动作是灾时反应，不是灾后适应。
D) 以偏概全To cope with the aftermath of a possible earthquake 中 aftermath（后果/余波）指事后处理，与原文"事中应对"错位；且漏掉了 tsunami 这一并列灾种，缩小了演练范围。
questions.quote: The Cascadia Rising drill gives area residents and emergency responders a chance to practice what to do in case of a 9.0 magnitude earthquake and tsunami along one of the nation's dangerous—and underestimated—faults.

options.text: To prepare people for a major earthquake and tsunami.
To increase residents' awareness of imminent disasters.
To teach people how to adapt to post-disaster life.
To cope with the aftermath of a possible earthquake.

questions.prompt: What happens in case of a megathrust earthquake according to the passage?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
根据文章,发生特大逆冲型地震时会出现什么情况?
A) 两个板块合并为一个。
B) 各种力量汇聚在一起。
C) 板块之间的边界变得模糊。
D) 巨大的应力被释放出来。
**判型** What happens in case of a megathrust earthquake according to the passage? 加了according to the passage 直接指明答案在原文有据可查。
**拆句** 句式 What happens in case of a megathrust earthquake according to the passage?主干 What happens，in case of a megathrust earthquake 是表条件的介词短语，according to the passage 是范围状语；in case of 这里相当于 "在...情况下"，与 if 同义，需要识破熟词僻义。
**定位** 在一次巨型逆冲（megathrust）事件中，所有累积的应力一次释放，世界上一些最强的地震就此发生。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断Two plates merge into one 把原文 two plates converge 拔高为 merge into one（合并成一块），但 converge 只是 "在边界处相遇"，并未真合并；且原文 one plate is beneath another 明示一块在另一块下方，并非融合。
B) 张冠李戴A variety of forces converge 把原文唯一的主体 stress 替换成 forces，并把converge 错位安到 forces 头上；原文 converge 描述的是 plates 而非 forces，stress才是被释放的对象。
C) 无中生有Boundaries blur between plates 描述的是 "板块边界变模糊"，原文 land plate boundaries where two plates converge 只说 "板块边界处两板块汇聚"，并未提到边界变模糊，属凭空造词。
D) ✓ 正确all of that stress releases ↔ Enormous stress is released四个选项中只有 D 同时含 stress 与 released 两个核心元素，正好对应原文 all of that stress releases；其余三项要么改主语（plates/forces/boundaries），要么改动词（merge/converge/blur），都没击中过程动作核心。
questions.quote: During a megathrust event, all of that stress releases and some of the world's most powerful earthquakes occur.

options.text: Two plates merge into one.
A variety of forces converge.
Boundaries blur between plates.
Enormous stress is released.

questions.prompt: What do the officials hope to achieve through the drills?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
官员们希望通过演习实现什么目标?
A) 协调各种救灾工作。
B) 减少灾难发生时的人员伤亡。
C) 最大限度地减少灾难造成的财产损失。
D) 建立灾难和应急管理机制。
**判型** What do the officials hope to achieve through the drills? 是对原文具体表态句的事实复述，答案在原文官员发声句里。
**拆句** 句式 What do the officials hope to achieve through the drills? 主干 the officials hope to achieve what，疑问词 what 前置；through the drills 是表方式的介词短语，明确限定"借助演练" 这个手段。
**定位** 并非所有伤亡都能被避免——但通过在地方、州乃至跨国层面进行协调，官员们希望能避免最坏的情况发生。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念Coordinating various disaster-relief efforts 把原文 by coordinating across local, state, and even national borders 即"协调"这一手段当作目标——但原文用 by 引出协调，是手段；用 hope that 引出 averted，才是目标。
B) ✓ 正确Not all casualties can necessarily be prevented↔Reducing casualties in the event of a disaster the worst-case scenario can be averted ↔ in the event of a disaster预判核心是"在灾难发生时减少伤亡"，四项中只有 B 同时含 reduce / casualties /disaster 三要素；A 强调过程而非结果，C 替换为财产损失（原文未提），D 是建立体系（拔高）。
C) 无中生有Minimizing property loss caused by disaster 把原文 casualties（伤亡）替换为property loss（财产损失），但全文从未谈财产损失，只谈人员伤亡（Thousands of casualties）。
D) 过度推断Establishing disaster and emergency management 是说要"建立"灾害与应急管理体系——原文 the report they prepare during this rehearsal will inform disaster management for years to come 只说报告将"为未来的应急管理提供参考（inform）"，并未说要从零建立；inform ≠ establish。
questions.quote: Not all casualties can necessarily be prevented—but by coordinating across local, state, and even national borders, officials hope that the worst-case scenario can be averted.

options.text: Coordinating various disaster-relief efforts.
Reducing casualties in the event of a disaster.
Minimizing property loss caused by disaster.
Establishing disaster and emergency management.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about "The Big One"?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**

作 者 关 于"The Big One"说 了 什 么? A) 它是否会发生还有待观察。
B) 它将如何到来现在预测还为时过早。
C) 它的发生只是时间问题。
D) 它一直困扰着Cascadia的居民。
**判型** What does the author say about "The Big One"? 问的是作者明示态度，原文末段有直接陈述，无须推断。
**拆句** 句式 What does the author say about "The Big One"? 简单 wh- 疑问句，say about X表 "就 X 谈了什么"；介词 about 引出谈论对象，结构无陷阱。
**定位** 对成千上万 Cascadia 居民来说，"The Big One" 不是"会不会发生"的问题，而只是"何时发生"的问题。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反Whether it will occur remains to be seen 等于说 "是否发生还说不准"，正好是原文isn't a question of if 所明确否定的态度——原文恰恰认为 "if" 已不是问题。
B) 偷换概念How it will arrive is too early to predict 把焦点换成"如何到来"，并断言"现在预测还太早"。原文谈的是"何时（when）"且明确说一定会来，并没说 how；且末段最后一句it's never too early to get ready for the inevitable 反对 too early 这一立场。
C) ✓ 正确isn't a question of if, only when↔Its occurrence is just a matter of time预判核心是"必然发生，只是时间问题"，四项中只有 C 同时含"occurrence（必然性默认）"与"matter of time（时间问题）"两要素；其他三项把"是否"或"如何"留作未解，与原文断言相反。
D) 无中生有It keeps haunting Cascadia residents 用 haunt（萦绕、纠缠不去）描写居民的心理被困扰，原文只是冷静陈述 "对居民而言这是个迟早问题"，并没说居民被困扰，属心理状态的无中生有。
questions.quote: For hundreds of thousands of Cascadia residents, "The Big One" isn't a question of if, only when.

options.text: Whether it will occur remains to be seen.
How it will arrive is too early to predict.
Its occurrence is just a matter of time.
It keeps haunting Cascadia residents.

title: "The dangerous thing about lying is people don't…

sentences.text: "The dangerous thing about lying is people don't understand how the act changes us," says Dan Ariely behavioural psychologist at Duke University.
Psychologists have documented children lying as early as the age of two.

Some experts even consider lying a developmental milestone, like crawling and walking, because it requires sophisticated planning, attention and the ability to see a situation from someone else's perspective to manipulate them.
But, for most people, lying gets limited as we develop a sense of morality and the ability to self-regulate.

passage.translation: 杜克大学行为心理学家Dan Ariely说："撒谎的危险之处在于人们不理解这一行为如何改变我们。"心理学家已记录到儿童早在两岁时就会撒谎。一些专家甚至认为撒谎是一个发展里程碑,就像爬行和走路一样,因为它需要复杂的计划、注意力以及从他人视角看待情境以操纵他人的能力。但对大多数人来说,随着我们发展出道德感和自我调节能力,撒谎会受到限制。

sentences.text: Harvard cognitive neuroscientist Joshua Greene says, for most of us, lying takes work.
In studies, he gave subjects a chance to deceive for monetary gain while examining their brains in a functional MRI machine, which maps blood flow to active parts of the brain.
Some people told the truth instantly and instinctively.
But others opted to lie, and they showed increased activity in their frontal parietal(颅腔壁的) control network, which is involved in difficult or complex thinking.
This suggests that they were deciding between truth and dishonesty—and ultimately opting for the latter.

For a follow-up analysis, he found that people whose neural(神经的) reward centers were more active when they won money were also more likely to be among the group of liars – suggesting that lying may have to do with the inability to resist temptation.

passage.translation: 哈佛认知神经科学家Joshua Greene说,对我们大多数人而言,撒谎需要努力。在研究中,他给受试者提供通过欺骗获取金钱利益的机会,同时用功能性核磁共振成像机检查他们的大脑,该机器可以绘制血液流向大脑活跃部位的图像。一些人立即本能地说出真话。但其他人选择撒谎,他们的额顶叶控制网络显示出更高的活跃度,该网络参与困难或复杂的思考。这表明他们在真实和不诚实之间做决定,并最终选择了后者。在后续分析中,他发现那些在赢钱时神经奖励中枢更活跃的人也更有可能属于撒谎者群体,这表明撒谎可能与无法抵抗诱惑有关。

sentences.text: External conditions also matter in terms of when and how often we lie.
We are more likely to lie, when we are able to rationalise it, when we are stressed and fatigued or see others being dishonest.
And we are less likely to lie when we have moral reminders or when we think others are watching.
"We as a society need to understand that, when we don't punish lying, we increase the probability it will happen again," Ariely says.

passage.translation: 外部条件在我们何时以及多久撒一次谎方面也很重要。当我们能够将其合理化、当我们有压力和疲劳或看到他人不诚实时,我们更有可能撒谎。而当我们有道德提醒或认为他人在观察时,我们不太可能撒谎。Ariely说:"作为一个社会,我们需要理解,当我们不惩罚撒谎时,我们就增加了它再次发生的可能性。

sentences.text: In a 2016 study published in the journal Nature Neuroscience, Ariely and colleagues showed how dishonesty alters people's brains, making it easier to tell lies in the future.
When people uttered a falsehood, the scientists noticed a burst of activity in their amygdala.
The amygdala is a crucial part of the brain that produces fear, anxiety and emotional responses including that sinking, guilty feeling you get when you lie.
But when scientists had their subjects play a game—in which they won money by deceiving their partner, they noticed the negative signals from the amygdala began to decrease.
Not only that, but when people faced no consequences for dishonesty, their falsehood tended to get even more sensational.
This means that if you give people multiple opportunities to lie for their own benefit, they start with little lies which get bigger over time.

passage.translation: 在2016年发表于《自然·神经科学》杂志的一项研究中,Ariely和同事展示了不诚实如何改变人们的大脑,使其在未来更容易撒谎。当人们说出谎言时,科学家注意到他们的杏仁核出现了活跃迸发。杏仁核是大脑的关键部分,会产生恐惧、焦虑和情绪反应,包括你撒谎时产生的那种下沉的内疚感。但当科学家让受试者玩一个游戏,在游戏中他们通过欺骗同伴来赢钱时,他们注意到来自杏仁核的负面信号开始减弱。不仅如此,当人们的不诚实行为不会面临任何后果时,他们的谎言往往会变得更加夸张。这意味着如果你给人们多次机会为自己的利益撒谎,他们会从小谎言开始,随着时间推移谎言会变得越来越大。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: Why do some experts consider lying a milestone in a child's development?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
为什么一些专家认为说谎是儿童发展过程中的一个里程碑?
A) 这表明他们有能力从不同角度看待复杂情况。
B) 这表明他们拥有比爬行和走路更非凡的能力。
C) 这代表他们有能力主动与周围的人互动。
D) 这涉及他们心理和身体能力的协调配合。
**判型** 题干 Why do some experts consider lying a milestone in a child's development? 是问「为什么把撒谎视作里程碑」，问的是原文已经写明的事实理由，不是推断。
**拆句** 主干是 Why do some experts consider lying a milestone，consider A B 是「认为 A 是B」的双宾结构；介词短语 in a child's development 修饰 milestone，限定语义场为儿童发展，结构平铺无陷阱。
**定位** 一些专家甚至将撒谎视为一种发育里程碑，类似爬行和走路，因为它需要复杂的规划、注意力，以及从他人视角看待情境以操纵对方的能力。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确the ability to see a situation from someone else's perspective↔the ability to view complex situations from different angles sophisticated planning, attention and the ability to see a situation from someone else's perspective↔ complex situations from different angles预判要的是「综合高级思维」，A 项 view complex situations from different angles把原文 see a situation from someone else's perspective 精确改写出来，命中预判。
B) 偷换概念原文用 like crawling and walking 把撒谎与爬行、走路并列为发育里程碑，并未说撒谎「比 more remarkable than crawling and walking」。
C) 偷换概念原文讲 see a situation from someone else's perspective to manipulate them，重点是「换位思考以操纵」，而非积极地 actively interact with people；选项把「操纵」美化为「互动」。
D) 无中生有原文列举的三项 sophisticated planning, attention and the ability to see a situation from someone else's perspective 全是心智活动，不含体力活动；选项的 both their mental and physical abilities 凭空多出 physical 一维。
questions.quote: Some experts even consider lying a developmental milestone, like crawling and walking, because it requires sophisticated planning, attention and the ability to see a situation from someone else's perspective to manipulate them.

options.text: It shows they have the ability to view complex situations from different angles.
It indicates they have an ability more remarkable than crawling and walking.
It represents their ability to actively interact with people around them.
It involves the coordination of both their mental and physical abilities.

questions.prompt: Why does the Harvard neuroscientist say that lying takes work?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
为什么Harvard的神经科学家说说谎需要费力?
A) 很难从几个选项中做出选择。
B) 很难听起来自然或可信。
C) 这需要血液快速流入大脑。
D) 这涉及大量复杂的心理活动。
**判型** 题干 Why does the Harvard neuroscientist say that lying takes work? 问神经科学家为什么作此判断，理由原文必有交代。
**拆句** 主干 Why does the Harvard neuroscientist say...，that 引导宾语从句 that lying takes work，takes work 这里取「需要付出努力/费劲」的引申义，不是字面的「带去工作」，是典型的熟词僻义点。
**定位** 哈佛认知神经科学家 Joshua Greene 说，对大多数人而言，撒谎是要费劲的。在研究中，他让受试者有机会为金钱回报而撒谎，同时用 fMRI 检查他们的大脑——fMRI 能映射出大脑活跃区域的血流。有些人会即时本能地说真话，但另一些人选择撒谎，他们的颅腔壁控制网络活动增强，而这一区域涉及困难或复杂的思考。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文 deciding between truth and dishonesty 是说撒谎者在「说真说假」之间挣扎，并未说选项 hard to choose from several options 的「多项中难选」；A 把二选一夸大成多选一，且重点偏离了「费劲」的脑科学解释。
B) 无中生有原文讨论的是撒谎时大脑活动加剧，没说撒谎者要 sound natural or plausible（让谎言听起来自然可信）；这种表达层面的难度是常识联想，原文未涉及。
C) 偷换概念原文是说 fMRI 仪器 maps blood flow to active parts of the brain——把血流映射到活跃脑区作观察手段，并非撒谎本身需要 speedy blood flow into one's brain。选项把仪器原理偷换成撒谎的生理条件。
D) ✓ 正确which is involved in difficult or complex thinking ↔ lots of sophisticated mental activity increased activity in their frontal parietal(颅腔壁的) control network ↔involves lots of sophisticated mental activity预判要的是「撒谎牵涉复杂脑活动」，D 项 involves lots of sophisticated mental activity 把原文 complex thinking 用 sophisticated mental activity 精确改写，命中预判。
questions.quote: Harvard cognitive neuroscientist Joshua Greene says, for most of us, lying takes work. In studies, he gave subjects a chance to deceive for monetary gain while examining their brains in a functional MRI machine, which maps blood flow to active parts of the brain. Some people told the truth instantly and instinctively. But others opted to lie, and they showed increased activity in their frontal parietal(颅腔壁的) control network, which is involved in difficult or complex thinking.

options.text: It is hard to choose from several options.
It is difficult to sound natural or plausible.
It requires speedy blood flow into one's brain.
It involves lots of sophisticated mental activity.

questions.prompt: Under what circumstances do people tend to lie?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
在什么情况下人们倾向于说谎?
A) 当他们变得过于情绪化时。
B) 当他们面临过大的同伴压力时。
C) 当诱惑过于强烈时。
D) 当后果不是迫在眉睫时。
**判型** 题干 Under what circumstances do people tend to lie? 问的是原文列举过的具体条件之一，答案就在原文的条件清单里。
**拆句** Under what circumstances 作状语前置，主干 do people tend to lie；tend to do 「倾向于…」，全句无修饰从句，结构平铺无陷阱。
**定位** 我们更容易撒谎——当我们能把它合理化时，当我们承受压力或疲惫时，或者当我们看到别人也不诚实时。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文条件清单是 able to rationalise it、stressed and fatigued、see others being dishonest，没有提到 become too emotional（变得过于情绪化）。stressed 与emotional 不是同义概念，前者特指压力疲劳，后者指情绪失控。
B) 偷换概念原文 see others being dishonest 是「看到别人也不诚实」，重点在「他人行为示范」而非 peer pressure（同辈群体压力要求一致行为）。前者是观察学习，后者是群体强制。
C) ✓ 正确we are able to rationalise it↔ the temptation is too strong the inability to resist temptation↔the temptation is too strong在四个选项里，只有 C 项 the temptation is too strong 能与「rationalise it」「无法抗拒诱惑」这条主线对得上；A/B/D 都不在原文条件清单内，故锁定 C。
D) 张冠李戴原文条件清单里没有 consequences are not imminent（后果不即将到来）这一条；与「后果」相关的内容在第四段讲「不受惩罚谎言会变大」（属 50 题），但那是「不受罚的结果」，不是「撒谎的触发条件」。
questions.quote: We are more likely to lie, when we are able to rationalise it, when we are stressed and fatigued or see others being dishonest.

options.text: When they become too emotional.
When they face too much peer pressure.
When the temptation is too strong.
When the consequences are not imminent.

questions.prompt: When are people less likely to lie?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
什么时候人们不太可能说谎?
A) 当他们精疲力竭并且有压力时。
B) 当他们处于他人密切注视之下时。
C) 当他们以理性方式思考时。
D) 当他们问心无愧时。
**判型** 题干 When are people less likely to lie? 问的是原文列举过的「不易撒谎」的条件，答案是原文事实陈述，不需推断。
**拆句** When 引导状语从句省略形式，主干 are people less likely to lie；less likely 是 likely 的比较级形式，构成反向倾向。
**定位** 当我们有道德提醒、或者认为别人正在注视着我们时，我们就不那么容易撒谎。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反原文 we are stressed and fatigued 出现在 more likely to lie 的条件里——「压力疲惫」是「更易撒谎」的条件，而非「不易撒谎」。选项 worn out and stressed 把它搬到「less likely」侧，正反弄反。
B) ✓ 正确we think others are watching ↔ under watchful eyes预判要的是「认为有人在看」的状态，B 项 under watchful eyes 用名词化短语精确改写了 think others are watching，是同义替换中典型的「动词从句→名词短语」转化，命中预判。
C) 偷换概念think in a rational way（理性思考）与原文 rationalise it（合理化撒谎）措辞相近、语义却相反——前者是冷静客观，后者是为撒谎找借口；并且 rationalise 在原文是 more likely 一侧的条件。
D) 偷换概念原文 moral reminders 是「外部的道德提醒/警示」（如海报、宣誓），不是 a clear conscience（自己问心无愧）。前者是外来刺激，后者是内心状态，且原文从未涉及「良心是否干净」的判断。
questions.quote: And we are less likely to lie when we have moral reminders or when we think others are watching.

options.text: When they are worn out and stressed.
When they are under watchful eyes.
When they think in a rational way.
When they have a clear conscience.

questions.prompt: What does the author say will happen when a liar does not get punished?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者说当说谎者没有受到惩罚时会发生什么?
A) 他们可能觉得理直气壮。
B) 他们会说更大的谎。
C) 他们会变得自满。
D) 他们可能会把谎言和真话混在一起。
**判型** 题干 What does the author say will happen when a liar does not get punished? 问的是原文交代过的后果，答案直接陈述于文中。
**拆句** 主干 What does the author say will happen，What 是 will happen 的主语，作 say 的宾语从句的主句主语；when a liar does not get punished 是时间状语从句，整句虽嵌套但语义清晰。
**定位** 不仅如此，当人们因撒谎而不受任何后果时，他们的谎言会变得越发耸人听闻。这意味着，如果你给人们多次为自身利益撒谎的机会，他们会从小谎开始，谎言会随时间越变越大。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断原文谈的是 negative signals from the amygdala began to decrease——脑区负面信号减弱（是脑层面的反应），并未说撒谎者 feel justified（觉得自己有理、问心无愧）。脑信号减弱不等同于「合理化」心理。
B) ✓ 正确they start with little lies which get bigger over time↔tell bigger lies their falsehood tended to get even more sensational↔They will tell bigger lies预判要的是「谎言规模升级」，B 项 tell bigger lies 把原文「越发耸人听闻」与「小谎变大谎」两条线索精确浓缩为一句，命中预判。
