title: When considering risk factors associated with serious chronic…

sentences.text: When considering risk factors associated with serious chronic diseases, we often think about health indicators such as cholesterol, blood pressure, and body weight.
But poor diet and physical inactivity also each increase the risk of heart disease and have a role to play in the development of some cancers.
Perhaps worse, the (26)____ effects of an unhealthy diet and insufficient exercise are not limited to your body.
Recent research has also shown that (27)____ in a high-fat and high-sugar diet may have negative effects on your brain, causing learning and memory (28)____ .

passage.translation: 在考虑与严重慢性疾病相关的风险因素时，我们常常会想到诸如胆固醇、血压和体重等健康指标。但不良饮食和缺乏运动也各自增加心脏病的风险，并在某些癌症的发展中起到一定作用。也许更糟的是，不健康饮食和运动不足的有害影响并不仅限于你的身体。最近的研究还表明，沉溺于高脂肪和高糖饮食可能会对你的大脑产生负面影响，导致学习和记忆缺陷。

sentences.text: Studies have found obesity is associated with impairments in cognitive functioning, as (29)____ by a range of learning and memory tests, such as the ability to remember a list of words presented some minutes or hours earlier.
There is also a growing body of evidence that diet-induced cognitive impairments can emerge (30)____ —within weeks or even days.
For example, one study found healthy adults (31)____ to a high-fat diet for five days showed impaired attention, memory, and mood compared with a low-fat diet control group.

Another study also found eating a high-fat and high-sugar breakfast each day for as little as four days resulted in problems with learning and memory (32)____ to those observed in overweight and obese individuals.

passage.translation: 研究发现，肥胖与认知功能损害相关，这通过一系列学习和记忆测试进行评估，例如记住几分钟或几小时前呈现的单词列表的能力。也有越来越多的证据表明，饮食引起的认知损害可能会迅速出现——在数周甚至数天内。例如，一项研究发现，被分配进行为期五天高脂肪饮食的健康成年人，与低脂肪饮食对照组相比，表现出注意力、记忆力和情绪受损。另一项研究还发现，每天吃高脂肪和高糖早餐仅仅四天，就会导致与超重和肥胖个体中观察到的类似的学习和记忆问题。

sentences.text: Body weight was not hugely different between the groups eating a healthy diet and those on high fat and sugar diets.
So this shows negative (33)____ of poor dietary intake can occur even when body weight has not changed (34)____ .
Thus, body weight is not always the best indicator of health and a thin person still needs to eat well and exercise (35)____ .

passage.translation: 健康饮食组和高脂肪高糖饮食组之间的体重差异并不是特别大。因此，这表明不良饮食摄入的负面后果即使在体重没有明显变化的情况下也可能发生。因此，体重并不总是健康的最佳指标，瘦人仍然需要良好饮食和定期锻炼。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
When considering risk factors associated with serious chronic diseases, we often think about health indicators such as cholesterol, blood pressure, and body weight. But poor diet and physical inactivity also each increase the risk of heart disease and have a role to play in the development of some cancers. Perhaps worse, the {{26}} effects of an unhealthy diet and insufficient exercise are not limited to your body. Recent research has also shown that {{27}} in a high-fat and high-sugar diet may have negative effects on your brain, causing learning and memory {{28}} .

Studies have found obesity is associated with impairments in cognitive functioning, as {{29}} by a range of learning and memory tests, such as the ability to remember a list of words presented some minutes or hours earlier. There is also a growing body of evidence that diet-induced cognitive impairments can emerge {{30}} —within weeks or even days. For example, one study found healthy adults {{31}} to a high-fat diet for five days showed impaired attention, memory, and mood compared with a low-fat diet control group. Another study also found eating a high-fat and high-sugar breakfast each day for as little as four days resulted in problems with learning and memory {{32}} to those observed in overweight and obese individuals.

Body weight was not hugely different between the groups eating a healthy diet and those on high fat and sugar diets. So this shows negative {{33}} of poor dietary intake can occur even when body weight has not changed {{34}} . Thus, body weight is not always the best indicator of health and a thin person still needs to eat well and exercise {{35}} .

options.text: assessed
excelling
assigned
indulging
consequences
loopholes
conspicuously
rapidly
deficits
redundant
designated
regularly
detrimental
similar
digestion

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) detrimental 形容词
**词性槽** the ___ effects 名词前缺定语
**依据** 与"unhealthy/insufficient"语义同向，"有害的影响"空的左右语境 an unhealthy diet and insufficient exercise 都是负面要素，effects 应承接其"负面影响"基调；detrimental（有害的）正好与"unhealthy/insufficient"在感情色彩上一致，构成 detrimental effects（有害影响）这一医学/科普英语高频搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) redundant 义为"多余的/被裁的"，方向不对redundant effects（多余的影响）不是地道说法，也与全文"危害"主线不相干；这个词在英语里更多用于职位被裁或信息冗余。
O) similar 需要 to 引出对照对象，且语义空洞similar 通常要跟 similar to sth，单独说 the similar effects 既缺对照、又只是"相似的"——填进去等于没说，留给后面真正需要"相似"语义的空（如 32 题）更合适。

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) indulging 动词
**词性槽** that ___ in a ... diet 从句主语后缺谓语动词
**依据** indulge in 沉迷于… 与负面饮食贴合indulge in 是固定搭配，意为"沉溺/纵情于"，常用于不健康行为；indulging in a high-fat and high-sugar diet = "沉溺于高脂高糖饮食"，与下文 may have negative effects on your brain 的负面定性完全吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
I) excelling 义为"擅长"，与高脂高糖饮食感情色彩相悖excel in 表示"在某方面出类拔萃"，是正面感情色彩；"excelling in a high-fat and high-sugar diet"（在高脂高糖饮食上出类拔萃）既不合英语习惯，又与全文负面论调完全对立。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) deficits 名词
**词性槽** causing learning and memory ___ 动词宾语缺名词
**依据** learning and memory deficits 是学术固定说法deficits 在认知科学英语里专指"功能性缺损"，learning and memory deficits 是医学/心理学论文的常见短语，意为"学习与记忆缺陷"，恰好对应 causing 后"造成…"的负面结果。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) digestion 不可数且偏离主题digestion 是"消化"，与 learning and memory 组合既不自然也不指向认知损伤。
K) loopholes 语义场完全错位loopholes（漏洞）一般用在制度/规则语境，learning and memory loopholes 不是英语固定表达，逻辑也不通。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) assessed 动词
**词性槽** as ___ by a range of ... tests 后置定语缺过去分词
**依据** "由测试评估"——assess by tests 学术固定搭配assess（评估）正是科研写作里描述"通过某种测试衡量"的标准动词：as assessed by a range of learning and memory tests = "正如由一系列学习与记忆测试所评估的那样"，与前面 impairments in cognitive functioning 自然衔接。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) assigned 义为"分配/指派"，与 by tests 搭配不通assign 多用于"把人/任务分配给…"，不用于"由测试分配"；as assigned by tests 在语义上不成立。
F) designated 义为"指定"，与"由测试…"逻辑不接designate 一般是"将某物指定为某身份/某用途"，与"由测试…"不构成自然搭配；语义上也无法说"被测试指定"。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) rapidly 副词
**词性槽** can emerge ___ 动词后缺方式副词
**依据** 破折号后"几周乃至几天"=快破折号后 within weeks or even days 直接定义了"多快"，即"很快"；rapidly（迅速地）正是这一速度感的最直接表达。

**答案** B) assigned 动词
**词性槽** adults ___ to a high-fat diet 名词后缺后置分词
**依据** 实验术语：把受试者"分到"某组在临床/对照实验语境里 "participants/adults assigned to … group/diet" 是定式，意为"被分配到 X 饮食组"，与下文 compared with a low-fat diet control group（与低脂对照组比较）的实验设计完全吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) designated "指定"重"命名/身份"，不用于分组designate 强调"指定…为某身份/角色"，如 designated driver；用于"把受试者分到某饮食"既不地道，也与实验术语的常规说法不符。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) similar 形容词
**词性槽** problems ... ___ to those observed in ... 后置定语缺形容词
**依据** similar to 固定搭配 + 与对照实验语义贴合similar to those observed in overweight and obese individuals 意为"与在超重和肥胖人群中观察到的相似"，与本段"短期高脂高糖饮食带来的认知损伤与长期肥胖者类似"的实验结论完全吻合。

**答案** C) consequences 名词
**词性槽** negative ___ of ... 形容词后缺名词中心词
**依据** 与 negative 同款搭配，呼应全文"差饮食的负面后果" negative consequences 是英语高频搭配，意为"负面后果"；本句正在总结前文：体重虽未明显变化，但差饮食的负面后果照样出现，consequences 与 of poor dietary intake、与overview 主旨完全对得上。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) digestion 缩小到"消化"，与主旨不符全文谈"对大脑/认知的负面影响"，把范围缩到"消化"反而偏离主线；且 negative digestion 不是地道搭配。
K) loopholes 义为"漏洞"，与饮食危害无关loopholes 多指法律/规则漏洞，与"差饮食的影响"在语义场上风马牛不相及。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— digestion 词性、与 diet 的话题相关性都合，但主线对不上。看到 of poor dietary intake，digestion 在话题上的"相关感"会诱使主体考生顺手就填；但全文论的是"对大脑/认知的负面后果"，consequences 才是覆盖全文负面影响的总称；防坑点：选名词不仅看搭配，还要看与全文主旨能否对齐。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) conspicuously 副词
**词性槽** has not changed ___ 完成时谓语后缺副词
**依据** 对应前句"体重并无显著差异"——"体重没有显著变化"本段开头 Body weight was not hugely different between the groups eating a healthy diet and those on high fat and sugar diets.——"体重并未有大的差异"；此处 has not changed conspicuously 正是"没有显著地变化"，与上文 not hugely different 同义呼应，强调即便体重看上去没明显变化，差饮食的负面后果照样发生。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
L) rapidly 义为"迅速地"，方向偏离段意本段重点不是"变化快慢"，而是"变化是否显著"；填 rapidly（"没有迅速变化"）就把原文"体重并无显著差异"的论证逻辑改成了"变化速度"，与上下文不接。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 L) —— rapidly 词性也对、读着也通——但偏离段意。body weight has not changed __(34)__ 表面看 rapidly（没有迅速变化）能读通，但本段首句Body weight was not hugely different 已经定调是"没有显著差异"，conspicuously 才是同义回扣；防坑点：副词空一律回看本段首句找同义改写。

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) regularly 副词
**词性槽** 动词 exercise 后缺修饰语
**依据** 与 eat well 对仗，呼应"健康生活方式"本句在告诫"瘦人也仍需好好吃、_____ 地锻炼"，与全文"健康习惯要长期坚持"的主旨相合；regularly（有规律地）正是 exercise 的高频固定搭配——exercise regularly 是英语里"规律锻炼"的最常说法，和 eat well 一起组成完美的健康行为对仗。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
D) conspicuously 义为"显眼地"，与锻炼搭不上conspicuously 修饰的是"显眼、引人注目"，exercise conspicuously（显眼地锻炼）在语义上不成立，也与全文劝诫主旨毫不相干。
L) rapidly 义为"迅速地"，搭配/语义不对rapidly 强调速度快，而本句的对仗目的是"长期坚持"而非"快速"；且 exercise rapidly 不是英语里的常见健康忠告搭配。

title: The future of personal satellite technology is here—are we ready for it?

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Satellites used to be the exclusive playthings of rich governments and wealthy corporations.
But increasingly, as space becomes more democratized, they are coming within reach of ordinary people.
Just like drones(无人机) before them, miniature satellites are beginning to fundamentally transform our conceptions of who gets to do what up above our heads.

passage.translation: 卫星曾经是富裕政府和大型企业的专属玩物。但随着太空变得越来越民主化,它们正逐渐进入普通人的触及范围。就像无人机之前的情况一样,微型卫星正开始从根本上改变我们关于谁有资格在我们头顶上空做什么的观念。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: As a recent report from the National Academy of Sciences highlights, these satellites hold tremendous potential for making satellite-based science more accessible than ever before.
However, as the cost of getting your own satellite in orbit drops sharply, the risks of irresponsible use grow.
The question here is no longer "Can we?" but "Should we?"
What are the potential downsides of having a slice of space densely populated by equipment built by people not traditionally labeled as "professionals"?
And what would the responsible and beneficial development and use of this technology actually look like?
Some of the answers may come from a nonprofit organization that has been building and launching amateur satellites for nearly 50 years.

passage.translation: 正如美国国家科学院最近的一份报告所强调的那样,这些卫星在使基于卫星的科学研究比以往任何时候都更容易获取方面具有巨大潜力。然而,随着将自己的卫星送入轨道的成本急剧下降,不负责任使用的风险也在增长。这里的问题不再是"我们能吗?"而是"我们应该吗?"让一片空间密集地布满由传统上不被称为"专业人士"的人所建造的设备,其潜在的负面影响是什么?这项技术负责任且有益的开发和使用实际上应该是什么样子?一些答案可能来自一个近50年来一直在建造和发射业余卫星的非营利组织。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: Having your personal satellite launched into orbit might sound like an idea straight out of science fiction.
But over the past few decades a unique class of satellites has been created that fits the bill: CubeSats.
The "Cube" here simply refers to the satellite's shape.
The most common CubeSat is a 10cm cube, so small that a single CubeSat could easily be mistaken for a paperweight on your desk.
These mini-satellites can fit in a launch vehicle's formerly "wasted space."
Multiples can be deployed in combination for more complex missions than could be achieved by one CubeSat alone.

passage.translation: 将你的个人卫星发射到轨道上可能听起来像是科幻小说里的想法。但在过去几十年里,一类独特的卫星被创造出来,正好符合这个要求:立方体卫星。这里的"立方体"仅仅指的是卫星的形状。最常见的立方体卫星是一个10厘米的立方体,小到单个立方体卫星很容易被误认为是你桌上的镇纸。这些微型卫星可以装入运载火箭以前"浪费的空间"中。多个立方体卫星可以组合部署,以完成比单个立方体卫星单独完成更复杂的任务。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: Within their compact bodies these minute satellites are able to house sensors and communications receivers/transmitters that enable operators to study Earth from space, as well as space around Earth.

They're primarily designed for Low Earth Orbit (LEO)—an easily accessible region of space from around 200 to 800 miles above Earth, where human-tended missions like the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station (ISS) hang out.
But they can attain more distant orbits; NASA plans for most of its future Earth-escaping payloads (to the moon and Mars especially) to carry CubeSats.

passage.translation: 在它们紧凑的机体内,这些微型卫星能够容纳传感器和通信接收器/发射器,使操作者能够从太空研究地球,以及地球周围的太空。它们主要设计用于近地轨道,这是一个容易到达的空间区域,距离地球表面约200至800英里,像哈勃太空望远镜和国际空间站这样的载人任务就在那里运行。但它们也可以到达更远的轨道;NASA计划让其未来大部分脱离地球的有效载荷(特别是前往月球和火星的)携带立方体卫星。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Because they're so small and light, it costs much less to get a CubeSat into Earth's orbit than a traditional communications or GPS satellite.
For instance, a research group here at Arizona State University recently claimed their developmental small CubeSats could cost as little as $3,000 to put in orbit.
This decrease in cost allows researchers, hobbyists and even elementary school groups to put simple instruments into LEO or even have them deployed from the ISS.

passage.translation: 因为它们如此小巧轻便,将一颗立方体卫星送入地球轨道的成本比传统通信卫星或GPS卫星要低得多。例如,亚利桑那州立大学的一个研究小组最近声称,他们开发的小型立方体卫星送入轨道的成本可能低至3000美元。这种成本的降低使研究人员、爱好者甚至小学生团体都能将简单的仪器送入近地轨道,甚至让它们从国际空间站部署。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: The first CubeSat was created in the early 2000s, as a way of enabling Stanford graduate students to design, build, test and operate a spacecraft with similar capabilities to the USSR's Sputnik(前苏联的人造卫星).
Since then, NASA, the National Reconnaissance Office and even Boeing have all launched and operated CubeSats.
There are more than 130 currently in operation.
The NASA Educational Launch of Nano Satellite program, which offers free launches for educational groups and science missions, is now open to U.S. nonprofit corporations as well.
Clearly, satellites are not just for rocket scientists anymore.

passage.translation: 第一颗立方体卫星创建于21世纪初,作为一种使斯坦福大学研究生能够设计、建造、测试和操作一颗具有与前苏联人造卫星类似能力的航天器的方式。从那时起,NASA、国家侦察局甚至波音公司都发射并操作过立方体卫星。目前有130多颗正在运行。NASA的纳米卫星教育发射计划为教育团体和科学任务提供免费发射,现在也向美国非营利公司开放。显然,卫星不再只是火箭科学家的专属了。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: The National Academy of Sciences report emphasizes CubeSats' importance in scientific discovery and the training of future space scientists and engineers.
Yet it also acknowledges that widespread deployment of LEO CubeSats isn't risk-free.
The greatest concern the authors raise is space debris—pieces of "junk" that orbit the earth, with the potential to cause serious damage if they collide with operational units, including the ISS.

passage.translation: 美国国家科学院的报告强调了立方体卫星在科学发现以及培训未来太空科学家和工程师方面的重要性。然而它也承认,近地轨道立方体卫星的广泛部署并非没有风险。作者提出的最大担忧是太空碎片——围绕地球运行的"垃圾"碎片,如果它们与包括国际空间站在内的运行单元相撞,有可能造成严重损害。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Currently, there aren't many CubeSats and they're tracked closely.
Yet as LEO opens up to more amateur satellites, they may pose an increasing threat.
As the report authors point out, even near- misses might lead to the "creation of a burdensome regulatory framework and affect the future disposition of science CubeSats."

passage.translation: 目前,立方体卫星数量不多,而且它们被密切跟踪。然而,随着近地轨道向更多业余卫星开放,它们可能构成越来越大的威胁。正如报告作者指出的那样,即使是险些相撞也可能导致"创建一个繁琐的监管框架,并影响科学立方体卫星的未来部署"。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: CubeSat researchers suggest that now's the time to ponder unexpected and unintended possible consequences of more people than ever having access to their own small slice of space.
In an era when you can simply buy a CubeSat kit off the shelf, how can we trust the satellites over our heads were developed with good intentions by people who knew what they were doing?
Some "expert amateurs" in the satellite game could provide some inspiration for how to proceed responsibly.

passage.translation: 立方体卫星研究人员建议,现在是时候思考比以往任何时候都更多的人能够获得他们自己的小块太空可能带来的意外和非预期后果了。在一个你可以直接从货架上购买立方体卫星套件的时代,我们如何能相信我们头顶上的卫星是由知道自己在做什么的人怀着良好意图开发的?卫星领域的一些"专家级业余爱好者"可以为如何负责任地推进提供一些启示。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: In 1969, the Radio Amateur Satellite Corporation (AMSAT) was created in order to foster ham radio enthusiasts'(业余无线电爱好者) participation in space research and communication.
It continued the efforts, begun in 1961, by Project OSCAR—a U.S.-based group that built and launched the very first nongovernmental satellite just four years after Sputnik.
As an organization of volunteers, AMSAT was putting "amateur" satellites in orbit decades before the current CubeSat craze.
And over time, its members have learned a thing or two about responsibility.
Here, open-source development has been a central principle.

Within the organization, AMSAT has a philosophy of open sourcing everything making technical data on all aspects of their satellites fully available to everyone in the organization, and when possible, the public.

According to a member of the team responsible for FOX 1-A, AMSAT's first CubeSat, this means that there's no way to sneak something like explosives or an energy emitter into an amateur satellite when everyone has access to the designs and implementation.

passage.translation: 1969年,无线电业余卫星公司成立,目的是促进业余无线电爱好者参与太空研究和通信。它延续了始于1961年的Project OSCAR的努力——这是一个美国团体,在Sputnik升空仅四年后就建造并发射了第一颗非政府卫星。作为一个志愿者组织,AMSAT在当前立方体卫星热潮之前的几十年里就一直在将"业余"卫星送入轨道。随着时间的推移,其成员已经学到了关于责任的一两件事。在这里,开源开发一直是一个核心原则。在该组织内部,AMSAT有一个将一切开源的理念,使其卫星各个方面的技术数据完全向组织内的每个人开放,并在可能的情况下向公众开放。据负责FOX 1-A(AMSAT的第一颗立方体卫星)的团队成员说,这意味着当每个人都能访问设计和实施方案时,不可能偷偷将爆炸物或能量发射器之类的东西放入业余卫星中。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: However, they're more cautious about sharing information with nonmembers, as the organization guards against others developing the ability to hijack and take control of their satellites.
This form of "self-governance" is possible within long-standing amateur organizations that, over time, are able to build a sense of responsibility to community members, as well as society in general.
But what happens when new players emerge, who don't have deep roots within the existing culture?

passage.translation: 然而,他们对与非成员分享信息更为谨慎,因为该组织要防范其他人发展出劫持和控制其卫星的能力。这种形式的"自我管理"在长期存在的业余组织中是可能的,这些组织随着时间的推移,能够建立起对社区成员以及整个社会的责任感。但当新的参与者出现,而他们在现有文化中没有深厚根基时,会发生什么?

passage.label: L

sentences.text: Hobbyists and students are gaining access to technologies without being part of a long-standing amateur establishment.
They're still constrained by funders, launch providers and a series of regulations—all of which rein in what CubeSat developers can and cannot do.
But there's a danger they're ill-equipped to think through potential unintended consequences.
What these unintended consequences might be is admittedly far from clear.
Yet we know innovators can be remarkably creative with taking technologies in unexpected directions.
Think of something as seemingly benign as the cellphone—we have microfinance and text-based social networking at one end of the spectrum, and improvised(临时制作的) explosive devices at the other.

passage.translation: 爱好者和学生正在获得技术的使用权,而不是长期业余机构的一部分。他们仍然受到资助者、发射提供商和一系列法规的约束——所有这些都限制了立方体卫星开发者能做什么和不能做什么。但有一种危险是,他们没有能力充分考虑潜在的非预期后果。诚然,这些非预期后果可能是什么还远不清楚。然而我们知道,创新者在以意想不到的方向使用技术方面可以非常有创造力。想想像手机这样看似无害的东西——我们在光谱的一端有小额信贷和基于文本的社交网络,在另一端有临时制作的爆炸装置。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: This is where a culture of social responsibility around CubeSats becomes important – not simply to ensure that physical risks are minimized, but to engage with a much larger community in anticipating and managing less obvious consequences of the technology.
This is not an easy task.
Yet the evidence from AMSAT and other areas of technology development suggests that responsible amateur communities can and do emerge around novel technologies.
The challenge here, of course, is ensuring that what an amateur community considers to be responsible, actually is.

Here's where there needs to be a much wider public conversation that extends beyond government agencies and scientific communities to include students, hobbyists, and anyone who may potentially stand to be affected by the use of CubeSat technology.

passage.translation: 这就是围绕立方体卫星的社会责任文化变得重要的地方——不仅仅是为了确保物理风险最小化,而是要与更广泛的社区一起预测和管理该技术不太明显的后果。这不是一项容易的任务。然而来自AMSAT和其他技术发展领域的证据表明,负责任的业余社区能够而且确实围绕新技术出现。当然,这里的挑战是确保业余社区认为负责任的东西实际上是负责任的。这就是需要进行更广泛的公众对话的地方,这种对话不仅限于政府机构和科学界,还包括学生、爱好者以及任何可能受到立方体卫星技术使用影响的人。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: Given the easier accessibility to space, it is time to think about how to prevent misuse of satellites.
questions.explanation:
**答案** I 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
鉴于进入太空变得更加容易,现在是时候考虑如何防止卫星被滥用了。
**锚点** 易得后防止误用
**定位** CubeSat 研究者建议，眼下正是要思考这样一件事的时候：当比以往任何时候都更多的人能够拥有头顶这一小片太空时，可能带来什么意想不到、非本意的后果。
**改写** it is time to think about how to prevent misuse of satellites ↔now's the time to ponder unexpected and unintended possible consequences时间催促句+宾语上位Given the easier accessibility to space ↔more people than ever having access to their own small slice of space易得性的同义重写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段的落点是把问题从能不能改写为该不该，是论域转换；Q36 强调此刻就要思考如何防止——动作和时间标记都更贴 now's the time to ponder The question here is no longer "Can we?" but "Should we?" M M 段已经在谈 a culture of social responsibility around CubeSats becomes important 这样的解决路径与 a much wider public conversation，是承接呼吁后的对策章节；而 Q36 锁定的是初次发出此刻该思考误用的提醒，源头仍在 I 段This is where a culture of social responsibility around CubeSats becomes important
questions.quote: CubeSat researchers suggest that now's the time to ponder unexpected and unintended possible consequences of more people than ever having access to their own small slice of space.

questions.prompt: A group of mini-satellites can work together to accomplish more complex tasks.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
一组微型卫星可以协同工作以完成更复杂的任务。
**锚点** 迷你卫星组合完成复杂任务
**定位** 多颗 CubeSat 可以组合部署，去完成单颗 CubeSat 独自无法达成的更复杂任务。
**改写** A group of mini-satellites ↔ Multiples can be deployed数量词同义work together ↔ in combination协同方式同义accomplish more complex tasks ↔for more complex missions than could be achieved by one CubeSat alone目标短语近义+对比补足
questions.quote: Multiples can be deployed in combination for more complex missions than could be achieved by one CubeSat alone.

questions.prompt: The greater accessibility of mini-satellites increases the risks of their irresponsible use.
questions.explanation:
**答案** B 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
微型卫星更容易获取增加了其被不负责任使用的风险。
**锚点** 易得性提升不负责任使用风险
**定位** 然而，随着把自家卫星送入轨道的成本大幅下降，被不负责任使用的风险也在增大。
**改写** The greater accessibility of mini-satellites ↔as the cost of getting your own satellite in orbit drops sharply易得性与成本下降互为表里increases the risks of their irresponsible use ↔ the risks of irresponsible use grow近乎逐词对应
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
I I 段确实呼应了风险话题，但用的是 more people than ever having access to their own small slice of space 来引出此刻该思考的号召；首次把 accessibility increases the risks of irresponsible use 这层因果落到纸上的是 B 段，I 段更对应 Q36 now's the time to ponder unexpected and unintended possible consequences of more people than ever having access to their own small slice of space
questions.quote: However, as the cost of getting your own satellite in orbit drops sharply, the risks of irresponsible use grow.

questions.prompt: Even school pupils can have their CubeSats put in orbit owing to the lowered launching cost.
questions.explanation:
**答案** E 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
由于发射成本降低,即使是在校学生也能将他们的CubeSats送入轨道。
**锚点** 小学生借成本下降把 CubeSat 送上轨
**定位** 这种成本下降使研究人员、爱好者乃至小学生团体也能把简单的仪器送入低地球轨道，甚至从国际空间站释放。
**改写** Even school pupils ↔ even elementary school groups用词不同的同义群体have their CubeSats put in orbit ↔put simple instruments into LEO or even have them deployed from the ISS上位概括+具体场景owing to the lowered launching cost ↔ This decrease in cost allows因果指示词同义
questions.quote: This decrease in cost allows researchers, hobbyists and even elementary school groups to put simple instruments into LEO or even have them deployed from the ISS.

questions.prompt: AMSAT is careful about sharing information with outsiders to prevent hijacking of their satellites.
questions.explanation:
**答案** K 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
AMSAT对与外部人员分享信息持谨慎态度,以防止其卫星被劫持。
**锚点** AMSAT 对外谨慎以防劫持
**定位** 然而，他们在向非成员分享信息这件事上更为谨慎，因为该组织在防范他人获得劫持并接管其卫星的能力。
**改写** AMSAT is careful about sharing information with outsiders ↔they're more cautious about sharing information with nonmembers形近词+同义群体to prevent hijacking of their satellites ↔guards against others developing the ability to hijack and take control of their satellites防御性动词同源
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
J J 段说的是 making technical data on all aspects of their satellites fully available to everyone in the organization，是对内开源；而 sharing information with outsiders to prevent hijacking 的关键词在对外+防劫持，与 J 段方向相反，应配K 段AMSAT has a philosophy of open sourcing everything making technical data on all aspects of their satellites fully available to everyone in the organization
questions.quote: However, they're more cautious about sharing information with nonmembers, as the organization guards against others developing the ability to hijack and take control of their satellites.

questions.prompt: NASA offers to launch CubeSats free of charge for educational and research purposes.
questions.explanation:
**答案** F 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
NASA为教育和研究目的免费提供CubeSats发射服务。
**锚点** NASA 免费发射教育与科研 CubeSat
**定位** NASA 的纳卫星教育发射计划为教育团体和科研任务提供免费发射，如今也对美国的非营利机构开放。
**改写** NASA offers to launch CubeSats ↔The NASA Educational Launch of Nano Satellite program, which offers free launches主体专名同形free of charge ↔ free launches免费用语同义for educational and research purposes ↔ for educational groups and science missions用途词同义
questions.quote: The NASA Educational Launch of Nano Satellite program, which offers free launches for educational groups and science missions, is now open to U.S. nonprofit corporations as well.

questions.prompt: Even with constraints, it is possible for some creative developers to take the CubeSat technology in directions that result in harmful outcomes.
questions.explanation:
**答案** L 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
即使存在限制,一些富有创造力的开发者仍有可能将CubeSat技术引向导致有害后果的方向。
**锚点** 约束之下仍可能走向有害方向
**定位** 他们仍然受到资助方、发射方和一系列法规的约束——这些都限制了 CubeSat 开发者能做什么、不能做什么。但是，他们可能没准备好去思考潜在的意外后果，这本身就是风险。
**改写** Even with constraints ↔They're still constrained by funders, launch providers and a series of regulations约束类型清单回收为名词some creative developers to take the CubeSat technology in directions that result in harmful outcomes↔ innovators can be remarkably creative with taking technologies in unexpected directions走偏方向+创造性同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
I now's the time to ponder unexpected and unintended possible consequences强调的是该思考的时机，而 Q42 强调的是即便有约束仍可能走向有害方向；后者必须落在有明确约束清单+但仍可能的 L 段now's the time to ponder unexpected and unintended possible consequences of more people than ever having access to their own small slice of space
questions.quote: They're still constrained by funders, launch providers and a series of regulations—all of which rein in what CubeSat developers can and cannot do. But there's a danger they're ill- equipped to think through potential unintended consequences.

questions.prompt: While making significant contributions to space science, CubeSats may pose hazards to other space vehicles.
questions.explanation:
**答案** G 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
CubeSats在为空间科学做出重大贡献的同时,可能对其他航天器构成危险。
**锚点** 重大贡献的同时威胁其他航天器
**定位** 但报告也承认，在低地球轨道大规模部署 CubeSat 并非毫无风险。作者最大的担忧是太空碎片——绕地球运行的垃圾，一旦与正在运行的设备（包括国际空间站）相撞，可能造成严重损坏。
**改写** making significant contributions to space science ↔emphasizes CubeSats' importance in scientific discovery and the training of future space scientists and engineers贡献语同义改写pose hazards to other space vehicles ↔cause serious damage if they collide with operational units, including the ISS威胁词+对象上位
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
H H 段确实谈论威胁，但接着 near-misses 谈 creation of a burdensome regulatory framework，重点落在监管后果而非首次把贡献与威胁并列；Q43 的 while 句式要求贡献与威胁并列出现，这只在 G 段同时具备even near-misses might lead to the "creation of a burdensome regulatory framework and affect the future disposition of science CubeSats"
questions.quote: Yet it also acknowledges that widespread deployment of LEO CubeSats isn't risk-free. The greatest concern the authors raise is space debris—pieces of "junk" that orbit the earth, with the potential to cause serious damage if they collide with operational units, including the ISS.

questions.prompt: Mini-satellites enable operators to study Earth from LEO and space around it.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
微型卫星使操作者能够从近地轨道研究地球及其周围空间。
**锚点** 在 LEO 同时研究地球与周边空间
**定位** 在迷你身躯之内，这些微型卫星能够容纳传感器以及通信收发设备，使操作者得以从太空研究地球，同时也研究地球周边的空间。
**改写** Mini-satellites enable operators ↔these minute satellites are able to house sensors and communications receivers/transmitters that enable operators主体词+动词同义to study Earth from LEO and space around it ↔to study Earth from space, as well as space around Earth并列宾语近乎逐字
questions.quote: Within their compact bodies these minute satellites are able to house sensors and communications receivers/transmitters that enable operators to study Earth from space, as well as space around Earth.

questions.prompt: AMSAT operates on the principle of having all its technical data accessible to its members, preventing the abuse of amateur satellites.
questions.explanation:
**答案** J 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
AMSAT的运作原则是使其所有技术数据对成员开放,以防止业余卫星被滥用。
**锚点** AMSAT 内部数据全开放防滥用
**定位** 在组织内部，AMSAT 奉行将一切开源的理念，把卫星各方面的技术数据完全向组织内每一个人开放，并在可能时面向公众。据 AMSAT 第一颗 CubeSat（FOX 1-A）负责团队的成员介绍，这意味着——只要所有人都能接触到设计和实现，就没有办法偷偷把炸药或能量发射器这类东西塞进一颗业余卫星里。
**改写** AMSAT operates on the principle ↔ AMSAT has a philosophy of open sourcing everything原则与理念同义having all its technical data accessible to its members↔making technical data on all aspects of their satellites fully available to everyone in the organization近乎逐字对应preventing the abuse of amateur satellites↔there's no way to sneak something like explosives or an energy emitter into an amateur satellite when everyone has access to the designs and implementation防滥用的具体场景上位概括
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
K more cautious about sharing information with nonmembers 与 guards against others developing the ability to hijack and take control of their satellites 强调的是对非成员不分享、防被劫持，而 Q45 的关键是 accessible to its members +preventing abuse，源头段必须是对内全面开放的 J 段they're more cautious about sharing information with nonmembers, as the organization guards against others developing the ability to hijack and take control of their satellites
questions.quote: Within the organization, AMSAT has a philosophy of open sourcing everything making technical data on all aspects of their satellites fully available to everyone in the organization, and when possible, the public. According to a member of the team responsible for FOX 1- A, AMSAT's first CubeSat, this means that there's no way to sneak something like explosives or an energy emitter into an amateur satellite when everyone has access to the designs and implementation.

title: Companies Are Working with Consumers to Reduce Waste

passage.label: A

sentences.text: As consumers, we are very wasteful.
Annually, the world generates 1.3 billion tons of solid waste.
This is expected to go up to 2.2 billion by 2025.
The developed countries are responsible for 44% of waste, and in the U.S. alone, the average person throws away their body weight in rubbish every month.

passage.translation: 作为消费者,我们非常浪费。每年,全世界产生13亿吨固体废物。预计到2025年,这一数字将上升到22亿吨。发达国家造成了44%的废物,仅在美国,平均每人每月扔掉相当于自己体重的垃圾。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: Conventional wisdom would seem to suggest that companies have no incentive to lengthen the life cycle of their products and reduce the revenue they would get from selling new goods.
Yet, more and more businesses are thinking about how to reduce consumer waste.
This is partly driven by the rising price of raw materials and metals.
It is also partly due to both consumers and companies becoming more aware of the need to protect our environment.

passage.translation: 传统观念似乎表明,企业没有动力延长其产品的生命周期并减少销售新商品所获得的收入。然而,越来越多的企业正在思考如何减少消费者废物。这部分是由原材料和金属价格上涨所推动的。这也部分归因于消费者和企业都越来越意识到保护环境的必要性。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: When choosing what products to buy and which brands to buy from, more and more consumers are looking into sustainability.
This is opposed to just price and performance they were concerned about in the past.
In a survey of 54 of the world's leading brands, almost all of them reported that consumers are showing increasing care about sustainable lifestyles.
At the same time, surveys on consumers in the U.S. and the U.K. show that they also care about minimizing energy use and reducing waste.

passage.translation: 在选择购买什么产品以及从哪些品牌购买时,越来越多的消费者正在关注可持续性。这与他们过去只关心价格和性能不同。在对全球54个领先品牌的调查中,几乎所有品牌都报告说消费者对可持续生活方式表现出越来越多的关注。与此同时,对美国和英国消费者的调查显示,他们也关心最大限度地减少能源使用和减少废物。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: For the most part, consumers control what happens to a product.

But some companies are realizing that placing the burden of recycling entirely on the consumer is not an effective strategy, especially when tossing something away seems like the easiest and most convenient option.

passage.translation: 在大多数情况下,消费者控制着产品会发生什么。但一些公司意识到,将回收的负担完全放在消费者身上并不是一种有效的策略,尤其是当扔掉某物似乎是最简单、最方便的选择时。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Some retailers and manufacturers in the clothing, footwear, and electronics industries have launched environmental programs.
They want to make their customers interested in preserving their products and preventing things that still have value from going to the garbage dump.
By offering services to help expand the longevity of their products, they're promising quality and durability to consumers, and receiving the reputational gains for being environmentally friendly.

passage.translation: 服装、鞋类和电子行业的一些零售商和制造商已经启动了环保项目。他们希望让顾客对保护其产品感兴趣,并防止仍有价值的物品进入垃圾场。通过提供服务来帮助延长其产品的使用寿命,他们向消费者承诺质量和耐用性,并因环保而获得声誉收益。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: For example, the Swedish jeans company Nudie Jeans offers free repair at twenty of their shops.
Instead of discarding their old worn-out jeans, customers bring them in to be renewed.
The company even provides mail-order repair kits and online videos, so that customers can learn how to fix a pair of jeans at home.
Their philosophy is that extending the life of a pair of jeans is not only great for the environment, but allows the consumer to get more value out of their product.
When customers do want to toss their pair, they can give them back to the store, which will repurpose and resell them.
Another clothing company, Patagonia, a high-end outdoor clothing store, follows the same principle.
It has partnered with DIY website iFixit to teach consumers how to repair their clothing, such as waterproof outerwear, at home.
The company also offers a repair program for their customers for a modest fee.
Currently, Patagonia repairs about 40,000 garments a year in their Reno, Nevada, service center.
According to the company's CEO, Rose Marcario, this is about building a company that cares about the environment.
At the same time, offering repair supports the perceived quality of its products.

passage.translation: 例如,瑞典牛仔裤公司Nudie Jeans在其二十家商店提供免费维修服务。顾客不是丢弃他们破旧的旧牛仔裤,而是把它们带来翻新。该公司甚至提供邮购维修套件和在线视频,以便顾客可以学习如何在家修理一条牛仔裤。他们的理念是,延长一条牛仔裤的使用寿命不仅对环境有益,而且使消费者能够从其产品中获得更多价值。当顾客确实想扔掉他们的牛仔裤时,他们可以把它们退还给商店,商店将重新利用并转售它们。另一家服装公司Patagonia,一家高端户外服装店,遵循同样的原则。它与DIY网站iFixit合作,教消费者如何在家修理他们的衣物,如防水外套。该公司还以适度的费用为其顾客提供维修服务。目前,Patagonia在其位于内华达州里诺的服务中心每年维修约40000件服装。据该公司首席执行官Rose Marcario说,这是为了建立一家关心环境的公司。与此同时,提供维修支持了其产品的感知质量。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: In Brazil, the multinational corporation Adidas has been running a shoe-recycling program called "Sustainable Footprint" since 2012.
Customers can bring shoes of any brand into an Adidas store to be shredded and turned into alternative fuels for energy creation instead of being burned as trash.
They are used to fuel cement ovens.

To motivate visitors to bring in more old shoes, Adidas Brazil promotes the program in stores by showing videos to educate customers, and it even offers a discount each time a customer brings in an old pair of shoes.
This boosts the reputation and image of Adidas by making people more aware of the company's values.

passage.translation: 在巴西,跨国公司Adidas自2012年以来一直在运营一个名为"可持续足迹"的鞋类回收项目。顾客可以将任何品牌的鞋子带到Adidas商店进行粉碎,并转化为替代燃料用于能源创造,而不是作为垃圾焚烧。它们被用来为水泥窑提供燃料。为了激励访客带来更多旧鞋,Adidas巴西通过在商店播放视频来教育顾客以推广该项目,甚至每次顾客带来一双旧鞋时都提供折扣。这通过让人们更加了解公司的价值观来提升Adidas的声誉和形象。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Enormous opportunities also lie with e-waste.

It is estimated that in 2014 the world produced some 42 million metric tons of e-waste (discarded electrical and electronic equipment and its parts) with North America and Europe accounting for 8 and 12 million metric tons respectively.
The materials from e-waste include iron, copper, gold, silver, and aluminum materials that could be reused, resold, salvaged, or recycled.
Together, the value of these metals is estimated to be about $52 billion.
Electronics giants like Best Buy and Samsung have provided e-waste take-back programs over the past few years, which aim to refurbish(翻新) old electronic components and parts into new products.

passage.translation: 电子废物也蕴藏着巨大的机会。据估计,2014年世界产生了约4200万公吨电子废物(废弃的电气和电子设备及其部件),其中北美和欧洲分别占800万和1200万公吨。电子废物中的材料包括铁、铜、金、银和铝等可以重复使用、转售、回收或再循环的材料。这些金属的总价值估计约为520亿美元。像百思买和三星这样的电子产品巨头在过去几年中提供了电子废物回收项目,旨在将旧电子元件和部件翻新成新产品。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: For other companies interested in reducing waste, helping the environment, and providing the sustainable lifestyles that consumers seek, here are some first steps for building a relationship with customers that focuses on recycling and restoring value to products.

passage.translation: 对于其他有兴趣减少废物、帮助环境并提供消费者寻求的可持续生活方式的公司,以下是建立与顾客关系的一些初步步骤,这些关系侧重于回收和恢复产品价值。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: Find partners.
If you are a manufacturer who relies on outside distributors, then retailers are the ideal partner for collecting old products.
Power tool maker DeWalt partners with companies, such as Lowes and Napa Auto Parts, to collect old tools at their stores for recycling.

The partnership benefits both sides by allowing unconventional partners (for example, two companies from two different industries) to work together on a specific aspect of the value chain, like, in this example, an engine firm with an accessory one.

passage.translation: 寻找合作伙伴。如果你是依赖外部分销商的制造商,那么零售商是收集旧产品的理想合作伙伴。电动工具制造商DeWalt与Lowes和Napa Auto Parts等公司合作,在其商店收集旧工具进行回收。这种合作关系使双方受益,允许非传统合作伙伴(例如,来自两个不同行业的两家公司)在价值链的特定方面进行合作,例如在这个例子中,一家发动机公司与一家配件公司合作。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: Create incentives.
Environmental conscientiousness isn't always enough to make customers recycle old goods.

For instance, DeWalt discovered that many contractors were holding on to their old tools, even if they no longer worked, because they were expensive purchases and it was hard to justify bringing them in to recycle.
By offering instant discounts worth as much as $100, DeWalt launched a trade-in program to encourage people to bring back tools.
As a result, DeWalt now reuses those materials to create new products.

passage.translation: 创造激励措施。环保意识并不总是足以让顾客回收旧商品。例如,DeWalt发现许多承包商一直保留着他们的旧工具,即使这些工具不再工作,因为它们是昂贵的购买品,很难证明将它们带来回收是合理的。通过提供价值高达100美元的即时折扣,DeWalt启动了一个以旧换新项目来鼓励人们带回工具。因此,DeWalt现在重复使用这些材料来创造新产品。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: Start with a trial program, and expect to change the details as you go.
Any take-back program will likely change over time, depending on what works for your customers and company goals.
Maybe you see low customer participation at first, or conversely, so much success that the cost of recycling becomes too high.
Best Buy, for instance, has been bearing the lion's share of e-waste volume since two of its largest competitors, Amazon and Wal-mart, do not have their own recycling programs.
Since the launch of its program, Best Buy changed its policy to add a $25 fee for recycling old televisions in order to keep the program going.

passage.translation: 从试点项目开始,并预期在进行过程中改变细节。任何回收项目都可能随着时间的推移而改变,这取决于什么对你的顾客和公司目标有效。也许你一开始看到顾客参与度很低,或者相反,取得了如此大的成功以至于回收成本变得过高。例如,百思买一直承担着电子废物量的最大份额,因为其最大的两个竞争对手亚马逊和沃尔玛没有自己的回收项目。自该项目启动以来,百思买改变了其政策,增加了25美元的旧电视回收费用,以保持项目的运行。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: Build a culture of collective values with customers.
A stronger relationship between the retailer/producer and the consumer isn't just about financial incentives.

By creating more awareness around your efforts to reduce waste, and by developing a culture of responsibility, repair, and reuse, you can build customer loyalty based on shared values and responsibilities.

passage.translation: 与顾客建立集体价值观文化。零售商/生产商与消费者之间更牢固的关系不仅仅是关于经济激励。通过提高人们对你减少废物努力的认识,并通过培养责任、维修和重复使用的文化,你可以基于共同的价值观和责任建立顾客忠诚度。

passage.label: N

sentences.text: These examples are just the tip of the iceberg, but they demonstrate how helping customers get more use of their materials can transform value chains and operations.

Reducing waste by incorporating used materials into production can cut costs and decrease the price of procurement(采购): less to be procured from the outside and more to be re-utilized from the inside.

passage.translation: 这些例子只是冰山一角,但它们展示了帮助顾客更多地使用其材料如何改变价值链和运营。通过将使用过的材料纳入生产来减少废物可以降低成本并降低采购价格:从外部采购的更少,从内部重新利用的更多。

passage.label: O

sentences.text: Companies play a big role in creating a circular economy, in which value is generating less from extracting new resources and more from getting better use out of the resources we already have—but they must also get customers engaged in the process.

passage.translation: 公司在创建循环经济中发挥着重要作用,在循环经济中,价值的产生更少来自开采新资源,更多来自更好地利用我们已经拥有的资源——但它们也必须让顾客参与到这个过程中。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: Some companies believe that products' prolonged lifespan benefits both the environment and customers.
questions.explanation:
**答案** F 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
一些公司认为产品使用寿命的延长对环境和消费者都有益。
**锚点** prolonged lifespan + 双赢
**定位** 他们的理念是，延长一条牛仔裤的寿命不仅有利于环境，还能让消费者从产品中获得更多价值。
**改写** products' prolonged lifespan ↔ extending the life of a pair of jeans名词化展开成动词短语benefits both the environment and customers ↔not only great for the environment, but allows the consumer to get more value out of their product both A and B 与 not only A but B 同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E E 段说零售商和制造商 want to make their customers interested in preserving their products，强调的是「让消费者珍惜产品」与「品牌美誉度」，并没有把「对环境 + 对消费者」并列起来作为公司理念表述出来；F 段的 Their philosophy is that …才是题干「Some companies believe that」的同义改写。They want to make their customers interested in preserving their products and preventing things that still have value from going to the garbage dump
questions.quote: Their philosophy is that extending the life of a pair of jeans is not only great for the environment, but allows the consumer to get more value out of their product.

questions.prompt: A survey shows shoppers today are getting more concerned about energy conservation and environmental protection when deciding what to buy.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
一项调查显示,如今的购物者在决定购买什么时越来越关注节能和环境保护。
**锚点** A survey + 节能环保购物
**定位** 与此同时，针对美国和英国消费者的调查显示，他们也关心尽量减少能源使用和减少废弃物。
**改写** A survey shows shoppers today are getting more concerned ↔surveys on consumers in the U.S. and the U.K. show that they also care about survey/show/care about 原样复现energy conservation ↔ minimizing energy use节约能源 = 最小化能源使用environmental protection ↔ reducing waste上位概念与下位行为when deciding what to buy ↔When choosing what products to buy and which brands to buy from买什么 = 购物决策语境
questions.quote: At the same time, surveys on consumers in the U.S. and the U.K. show that they also care about minimizing energy use and reducing waste.

questions.prompt: Companies can build customer loyalty by creating a positive culture of environmental awareness.
questions.explanation:
**答案** M 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
公司可以通过创造积极的环保意识文化来建立客户忠诚度。
**锚点** customer loyalty + culture of environmental awareness
**定位** 通过让人们更关注你们减少废弃的努力，并培养一种以责任、修补和再利用为内核的文化，你可以基于共同的价值观与责任来建立客户忠诚度。
**改写** build customer loyalty ↔ build customer loyalty短语原样复现creating a positive culture of environmental awareness ↔creating more awareness around your efforts to reduce waste, and by developing a culture of responsibility, repair, and reuse上位概念 = 多个具体行为的概括
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E E 段焦点是企业层面 receiving the reputational gains for being environmentally friendly，并未提到培育顾客忠诚度；M 段才是把环保文化与 customer loyalty 直接挂钩的段落。receiving the reputational gains for being environmentally friendly
questions.quote: By creating more awareness around your efforts to reduce waste, and by developing a culture of responsibility, repair, and reuse, you can build customer loyalty based on shared values and responsibilities.

questions.prompt: When companies launch environmental programs, they will have their brand reputation enhanced.
questions.explanation:
**答案** E 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
当公司推出环保项目时,他们的品牌声誉会得到提升。
**锚点** environmental programs → brand reputation enhanced
**定位** 通过提供帮助延长产品寿命的服务，他们在向消费者承诺品质与耐用性，同时也因环保形象获得了口碑收益。
**改写** launch environmental programs ↔ launched environmental programs动词与名词短语原样复现they will have their brand reputation enhanced ↔receiving the reputational gains for being environmentally friendly「口碑被提升」= 「获得口碑收益」
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
G G 段的口碑提升 This boosts the reputation and image of Adidas 是「针对一家公司的具体结论」，而题干 companies 用复数泛指任何启动环保项目的企业，应当落到总论性的 E 段。This boosts the reputation and image of Adidas by making people more aware of the company's values
questions.quote: By offering services to help expand the longevity of their products, they're promising quality and durability to consumers, and receiving the reputational gains for being environmentally friendly.

questions.prompt: One multinational company offers discounts to customers who bring in old footwear to be used as fuel.
questions.explanation:
**答案** G 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
一家跨国公司向带来旧鞋类用作燃料的顾客提供折扣。
**锚点** multinational + footwear + discounts + fuel
**定位** 顾客可以把任意品牌的鞋子带到阿迪达斯门店，鞋子会被粉碎并转化为用于能源生产的替代燃料，而不是被当作垃圾烧掉。这些燃料用于水泥窑供能。为了鼓励顾客带来更多旧鞋，阿迪达斯巴西在门店通过视频做宣传教育顾客，并且每带来一双旧鞋都会给一次折扣。
**改写** multinational company ↔ multinational corporation Adidas company 与 corporation 同义offers discounts to customers ↔offers a discount each time a customer brings in an old pair of shoes短语原样复现bring in old footwear ↔ shoes of any brand 与 brings in an old pair of shoes footwear 上位概括 shoes to be used as fuel ↔ turned into alternative fuels for energy creation 与 fuel cement ovens「用作燃料」= 「转化为燃料并烧」
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
K K 段说 DeWalt launched a trade-in program to encourage people to bring back tools，对象是电动工具而非鞋，作用是回收材料制造新产品而非作燃料，跨国身份也未提，不能与 G 段的四元齐落相比。By offering instant discounts worth as much as $100, DeWalt launched a trade-in program to encourage people to bring back tools
questions.quote: Customers can bring shoes of any brand into an Adidas store to be shredded and turned into alternative fuels for energy creation instead of being burned as trash. They are used to fuel cement ovens. To motivate visitors to bring in more old shoes, Adidas Brazil promotes the program in stores by showing videos to educate customers, and it even offers a discount each time a customer brings in an old pair of shoes.

questions.prompt: Recycling used products can help manufacturers reduce production costs.
questions.explanation:
**答案** N 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
回收利用旧产品可以帮助制造商降低生产成本。
**锚点** Recycling used products → reduce production costs
**定位** 把使用过的材料纳入生产以减少浪费，可以降低成本并降低采购价格——外部采购变少、内部再利用变多。
**改写** Recycling used products ↔ incorporating used materials into production「回收旧产品」= 「把使用过的材料并入生产」reduce production costs ↔ cut costs and decrease the price of procurement动词同义 + 名词上位概括
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
H H 段说金属材料 could be reused, resold, salvaged, or recycled，强调材料价值；但并未把「回收 → 制造商生产成本下降」这一因果链明说出来，因此不是题干的源头段。Together, the value of these metals is estimated to be about $52 billion
questions.quote: Reducing waste by incorporating used materials into production can cut costs and decrease the price of procurement(采购): less to be procured from the outside and more to be re- utilized from the inside.

questions.prompt: Electronic products contain valuable metals that could be recovered.
questions.explanation:
**答案** H 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
电子产品含有可以回收的贵重金属。
**锚点** Electronic products + valuable metals
**定位** 电子垃圾里的材料包括铁、铜、金、银和铝——这些材料可以被再利用、再出售、回收或循环使用。
**改写** Electronic products ↔ discarded electrical and electronic equipment and its parts上下位 + 形容词换名词valuable metals ↔iron, copper, gold, silver, and aluminum 与 the value of these metals is estimated to be about$52 billion形容词 valuable = 「估值 520 亿美元」的概括could be recovered ↔ could be reused, resold, salvaged, or recycled上位动词 recovered = 多个具体动词清单
questions.quote: The materials from e-waste include iron, copper, gold, silver, and aluminum materials that could be reused, resold, salvaged, or recycled.

questions.prompt: It seems commonly believed that companies are not motivated to prolong their products' lifespan.
questions.explanation:
**答案** B 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
人们似乎普遍认为公司没有动力延长其产品的使用寿命。
**锚点** commonly believed + not motivated to prolong lifespan
**定位** 常识似乎会让人认为：企业没有动力去延长产品的生命周期，因为那会减少他们卖新产品的收入。
**改写** It seems commonly believed ↔ Conventional wisdom would seem to suggest「commonly believed」与「Conventional wisdom」同义not motivated to prolong their products' lifespan ↔have no incentive to lengthen the life cycle of their products「motivated」= 「have incentive」、「prolong lifespan」= 「lengthen life cycle」
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
D D 段说 consumers control what happens to a product，但讨论的是「消费者控制产品命运、把回收负担全压消费者无效」，并未谈及企业是否被激励去延长产品寿命，与题干不对应。placing the burden of recycling entirely on the consumer is not an effective strategy
questions.quote: Conventional wisdom would seem to suggest that companies have no incentive to lengthen the life cycle of their products and reduce the revenue they would get from selling new goods.

questions.prompt: It is advisable for companies to partner with each other in product recycling.
questions.explanation:
**答案** J 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
建议公司在产品回收方面相互合作。
**锚点** advisable + partner with each other in recycling
**定位** 寻找合作伙伴。如果你是依赖外部分销商的制造商，那么零售商是收集旧产品的理想伙伴。电动工具制造商德伟特与劳氏、纳帕汽配等公司合作，在它们的门店收集旧工具用于回收。
**改写** It is advisable for companies to partner with each other ↔Find partners 与 DeWalt partners with companies, such as Lowes and Napa Auto Parts建议口吻 vs 段首祈使式建议in product recycling ↔ to collect old tools at their stores for recycling「in product recycling」= 「for recycling」
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
L L 段的小标题是 Start with a trial program, and expect to change the details as you go，谈的是项目从小规模试点起步、随时调整，并未给出「公司之间合作」的建议，不与题干吻合。Start with a trial program, and expect to change the details as you go
questions.quote: Find partners. If you are a manufacturer who relies on outside distributors, then retailers are the ideal partner for collecting old products. Power tool maker DeWalt partners with companies, such as Lowes and Napa Auto Parts, to collect old tools at their stores for recycling.

questions.prompt: Some businesses have begun to realize it may not be effective to let consumers take full responsibility for recycling.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
一些企业已经开始意识到让消费者对回收承担全部责任可能并不有效。
**锚点** not effective + consumers take full responsibility
**定位** 但一些公司正在意识到：把回收的责任完全压到消费者身上并不是一个有效的策略，尤其是当扔掉东西看起来是最容易、最方便的做法时。
**改写** Some businesses have begun to realize ↔ some companies are realizing businesses ↔ companies、begun to realize ↔ are realizing it may not be effective ↔ is not an effective strategy「not effective」原样复现to let consumers take full responsibility for recycling ↔placing the burden of recycling entirely on the consumer「let X take full responsibility」= 「place the burden entirely on X」
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段虽然也含「companies + 否定」的元素，但是「常识认为企业没动力」，与题干的「企业自己意识到把责任压消费者无效」主语不同、论点也不同，因此不是源头段。Conventional wisdom would seem to suggest that companies have no incentive to lengthen the life cycle of their products
questions.quote: But some companies are realizing that placing the burden of recycling entirely on the consumer is not an effective strategy, especially when tossing something away seems like the easiest and most convenient option.

title: The Best Retailers Combine Bricks and Clicks

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Retail profits are falling sharply.
Stores are closing.
Malls are emptying.
The depressing stories just keep coming.
Reading the earnings announcements of large retail stores like Macy's, Nordstrom, and Target is about as uplifting as a tour of an intensive care unit.
The internet is apparently taking down yet another industry.
Brick and mortar stores(实体店) seem to be going the way of the yellow pages.
Sure enough, the Census Bureau just released data showing that online retail sales surged 15.2 percent between the first quarter of 2015 and the first quarter of 2016.

passage.translation: 零售利润正在急剧下降。商店纷纷关闭。购物中心日渐空荡。令人沮丧的消息接连不断。阅读Macy's、Nordstrom和Target等大型零售商店的收益公告，就像参观重症监护病房一样令人压抑。互联网显然正在摧毁又一个行业。实体店似乎正在走向黄页那样的命运。果然,人口普查局刚刚发布的数据显示,2015年第一季度至2016年第一季度期间,在线零售销售额激增了15.2%。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: But before you dump all of your retail stocks, there are more facts you should consider.
Looking only at that 15.2 percent "surge" would be misleading.
It was an increase that was on a small base of 6.9 percent.
Even when a tiny number grows by a large percentage terms, it is often still tiny.

passage.translation: 但在你抛售所有零售股票之前,还有更多事实需要考虑。仅仅看那15.2%的"激增"会产生误导。这是在6.9%的小基数上的增长。即使一个微小的数字按百分比增长很大,它往往仍然很小。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: More than 20 years after the internet was opened to commerce, the Census Bureau tells us that brick and mortar sales accounted for 92.3 percent of retail sales in the first quarter of 2016.
Their data show that only 0.8 percent of retail sales shifted from offline to online between the beginning of 2015 and 2016.

passage.translation: 在互联网向商业开放20多年后,人口普查局告诉我们,2016年第一季度实体店销售额占零售销售额的92.3%。他们的数据显示,从2015年初到2016年,只有0.8%的零售销售额从线下转移到了线上。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: So, despite all the talk about drone(无人机) deliveries to your doorstep, all the retail executives expressing anxiety over consumers going online, and even a Presidential candidate exclaiming that Amazon has a "huge antitrust problem," the Census data suggest that physical retail is thriving.
Of course, the closed stores, depressed executives, and sinking stocks suggest otherwise.
What's the real story?

passage.translation: 因此,尽管人们都在谈论无人机送货上门,尽管所有零售高管都在表达对消费者转向线上的焦虑,甚至有一位总统候选人声称亚马逊存在"巨大的反垄断问题",但人口普查数据表明实体零售正在蓬勃发展。当然,关闭的商店、沮丧的高管和下跌的股票则表明情况并非如此。真实情况是什么?

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Many firms operating brick and mortar stores are in trouble.
The retail industry is getting reinvented, as we describe in our new book Matchmakers.
It's standing in the path of what Schumpeter called a gale(大⻛) of creative destruction.
That storm has been brewing for some time, and as it has reached gale force, most large retailers are searching for a response.
As the CFO of Macy's put it recently, "We're frankly scratching our heads."

passage.translation: 许多经营实体店的公司陷入困境。正如我们在新书《撮合者》中所描述的那样,零售业正在被重新塑造。它正站在熊彼特所说的创造性破坏大风的路径上。这场风暴已经酝酿了一段时间,当它达到大风强度时,大多数大型零售商都在寻找应对之策。正如Macy's的首席财务官最近所说:"坦率地说,我们正在抓耳挠腮。"

passage.label: F

sentences.text: But it's not happening as experts predicted.
In the peak of the dot-com bubble, brick and mortar retail was one of those industries the internet was going to kill—and quickly.
The dot-com bust discredited most predictions of that sort and in the years that followed, conventional retailers' confidence in the future increased as Census continued to report weak online sales.
And then the gale hit.

passage.translation: 但事情的发展并非如专家所预测的那样。在互联网泡沫的高峰期,实体零售是互联网将要扼杀的行业之一——而且会很快。互联网泡沫破裂使大多数此类预测失去了可信度,在随后的几年里,随着人口普查局持续报告疲软的在线销售数据,传统零售商对未来的信心增强了。然后大风袭来了。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: It is becoming increasingly clear that retail reinvention isn't a simple battle to the death between bricks and clicks.
It is about devising retail models that work for people who are making increasing use of a growing array of internet-connected tools to change how they search, shop, and buy.
Creative retailers are using the new technologies to innovate just about everything stores do from managing inventory, to marketing, to getting paid.

passage.translation: 越来越清楚的是,零售业的重塑并非实体店与网店之间简单的生死之战。它关乎设计适合那些越来越多地使用日益增长的互联网连接工具来改变搜索、购物和购买方式的人们的零售模式。富有创意的零售商正在利用新技术创新商店所做的几乎所有事情,从管理库存到营销再到收款。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: More than drones dropping a new supply of underwear on your doorstep, Apple's massively successful brick-and-mortar-and-glass retail stores and Amazon's small steps in the same direction are what should keep old-fashioned retailers awake at night.
Not to mention the large number of creative new retailers, like Bonobos, that are blending online and offline experiences in creative ways.

passage.translation: 比起无人机在你家门口投放新的内衣,苹果公司极为成功的实体加玻璃零售店以及亚马逊在同一方向上迈出的小步,才是应该让老式零售商彻夜难眠的东西。更不用说大量富有创意的新零售商,如Bonobos,正在以创造性的方式融合线上和线下体验。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Retail reinvention is not a simple process, and it's also not happening on what used to be called "Internet Time."
Some internet-driven changes have happened quickly, of course.
Craigslist quickly overtook newspaper classified ads and turned newspaper economics upside down.
But many widely anticipated changes weren't quick, and some haven't really started.
With the benefit of hindsight(后⻅之明), it looks like the internet will transform the economy at something like the pace of other great inventions like electricity.
B2B commerce, for example, didn't move mainly online by 2005 as many had predicted in 2000, nor even by 2016, but that doesn't mean it won't do so over the next few decades.

passage.translation: 零售业的重塑不是一个简单的过程,它也不是按照过去所谓的"互联网时间"发生的。当然,一些由互联网驱动的变化发生得很快。Craigslist迅速超越了报纸分类广告,并彻底颠覆了报业经济。但许多被广泛预期的变化并不快,有些甚至还没有真正开始。有了后见之明,互联网似乎将以类似于电力等其他伟大发明的速度改变经济。例如,企业对企业电子商务并没有像许多人在2000年预测的那样在2005年之前主要转移到线上,甚至在2016年也没有,但这并不意味着它不会在未来几十年内实现。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: But the gale is still blowing.
The sudden decline in foot traffic in recent years, even though it hasn't been accompanied by a massive decline in physical sales, is a critical warning.
People can shop more efficiently online and therefore don't need to go to as many stores to find what they want.
There's a surplus of physical shopping space for the crowds, which is one reason why stores are downsizing and closing.

passage.translation: 但大风仍在吹。近年来客流量的突然下降,尽管并未伴随实体销售的大规模下降,却是一个关键警告。人们可以更高效地在线购物,因此不需要去那么多商店来找到他们想要的东西。相对于人流而言,实体购物空间过剩,这是商店缩小规模和关闭的原因之一。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: The rise of the mobile phone has recently added a new level of complexity to the process of retail reinvention.
Even five years ago most people faced a choice.
Sit at your computer, probably at home or at the office, search and browse, and buy.
Or head out to the mall, or Main Street, look and shop, and buy.
Now, just about everyone has a smartphone, connected to the internet almost everywhere almost all the time.
Even when a retailer gets a customer to walk in the store, she can easily see if there's a better deal online or at another store nearby.

passage.translation: 移动电话的兴起最近为零售业重塑的过程增添了新的复杂性。即使在五年前,大多数人还面临一个选择。坐在你的电脑前,可能在家里或办公室,搜索和浏览,然后购买。或者前往购物中心或主街,看和逛,然后购买。现在,几乎每个人都有智能手机,几乎随时随地都连接到互联网。即使零售商让顾客走进商店,她也可以轻松查看网上或附近其他商店是否有更好的交易。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: So far, the main thing many large retailers have done in response to all this is to open online stores, so people will come to them directly rather than to Amazon and its smaller online rivals.
Many are having the same problem that newspapers have.
Even if they get online traffic, they struggle to make enough money online to compensate for what they are losing offline.

passage.translation: 到目前为止,许多大型零售商为应对这一切所做的主要事情是开设在线商店,这样人们就会直接来找他们,而不是去亚马逊及其较小的在线竞争对手那里。许多零售商遇到了与报纸相同的问题。即使他们获得了在线流量,他们也难以在线上赚到足够的钱来弥补线下的损失。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: A few seem to be making this work.
Among large traditional retailers, Walmart recently reported the best results, leading its stock price to surge, while Macy's, Target, and Nordstrom's dropped.
Yet Walmart's year-over-year online sales only grew 7 percent, leading its CEO to lament(哀叹), "Growth here is too slow."
Part of the problem is that almost two decades after Amazon filed the one-click patent, the online retail shopping and buying experience is filled with frictions.
A recent study graded more than 600 internet retailers on how easy it was for consumers to shop, buy, and pay.
Almost half of the sites didn't get a passing grade and only 18 percent got an A or B.

passage.translation: 少数几家似乎正在让这种模式奏效。在大型传统零售商中,沃尔玛最近报告了最好的业绩,导致其股价飙升,而Macy's、Target和Nordstrom的股价则下跌了。然而沃尔玛的同比在线销售额仅增长了7%,导致其首席执行官哀叹:"这里的增长太慢了。"部分问题在于,在亚马逊申请一键购买专利近二十年后,在线零售购物和购买体验仍然充满摩擦。最近一项研究对600多家互联网零售商在消费者购物、购买和支付的便捷程度方面进行了评分。近一半的网站未能获得及格分数,只有18%获得了A或B。

passage.label: N

sentences.text: The turmoil on the ground in physical retail is hard to square with the Census data.
Unfortunately, part of the explanation is that the Census retail data are unreliable.
Our deep look into those data and their preparation revealed serious problems.
It seems likely that Census simply misclassifies a large chunk of online sales.

It is certain that the Census procedures, which lump the online sales of major traditional retailers like Walmart with "non-store retailers" like food trucks can mask major changes in individual retail categories.
The bureau could easily present their data in more useful ways.
But they have chosen not to.

passage.translation: 实体零售业实地的动荡很难与人口普查数据相吻合。不幸的是,部分解释是人口普查零售数据不可靠。我们对这些数据及其准备工作的深入研究揭示了严重的问题。人口普查局似乎很可能只是错误地分类了大量在线销售。可以肯定的是,人口普查程序将沃尔玛等主要传统零售商的在线销售与餐车等"非店铺零售商"混为一谈,这可能掩盖了个别零售类别的重大变化。该局可以很容易地以更有用的方式呈现他们的数据。但他们选择了不这样做。

passage.label: O

sentences.text: Despite the turmoil, brick and mortar won't disappear any time soon.

The big questions are which, if any, of the large traditional retailers will still be on the scene in a decade or two because they have successfully reinvented themselves, which new players will operate busy stores on Main Streets and maybe even in shopping malls, and how the shopping and buying experience will have changed in each retail category.
Investors shouldn't write off brick and mortar.
Whether they should bet on the traditional players who run those stores now is another matter.

passage.translation: 尽管动荡不安,实体店不会很快消失。重大问题是,如果有的话,哪些大型传统零售商将在一二十年后仍然存在,因为它们成功地重塑了自己,哪些新参与者将在主街甚至购物中心经营繁忙的商店,以及每个零售类别中的购物和购买体验将如何改变。投资者不应该放弃实体店。至于他们是否应该押注于现在经营这些商店的传统参与者,则是另一回事。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: Although online retailing has existed for some twenty years, nearly half of the internet retailers still fail to receive satisfactory feedback from consumers, according to a recent survey.
questions.explanation:
**答案** M 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
根据最近的一项调查,尽管在线零售已经存在了大约二十年,仍有近一半的互联网零售商未能收到消费者满意的反馈。
**锚点** 二十年 + 近一半网店反馈不佳
**定位** 一项最近的研究以"消费者购物、下单、支付的难易程度"为标准给 600 多家网店打了分。几乎一半的网站没有及格，只有 18% 拿到 A 或 B。
**改写** online retailing has existed for some twenty years ↔almost two decades after Amazon filed the one-click patent时间表述的同义改写nearly half of the internet retailers still fail to receive satisfactory feedback from consumers ↔Almost half of the sites didn't get a passing grade近一半 + 不及格 = 反馈不佳according to a recent survey ↔ A recent study graded more than 600 internet retailers survey / study 同义替换
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
C C 谈的是 brick and mortar sales accounted for 92.3 percent of retail sales——实体店占总零售的份额；并未涉及网店是否让消费者满意，与题干 fail to receive satisfactory feedback from consumers 没有交集，仅因"也带百分比"易诱人。More than 20 years after the internet was opened to commerce, the Census Bureau tells us that brick and mortar sales accounted for 92.3 percent of retail sales A A 关注的是 online retail sales surged 15.2 percent——增长速度；与题干 fail to receive satisfactory feedback from consumers 的"满意度"完全是两件事，话题相邻但所述事件不同。online retail sales surged 15.2 percent between the first quarter of 2015 and the first quarter of 2016
questions.quote: A recent study graded more than 600 internet retailers on how easy it was for consumers to shop, buy, and pay. Almost half of the sites didn't get a passing grade and only 18 percent got an A or B.

questions.prompt: Innovative retailers integrate internet technologies with conventional retailing to create new retail models.

F F 强调 conventional retailers' confidence in the future increased，而非变化是否快；尽管 internet was going to kill—and quickly 提到"快"，但它讲的是"预言"本身，不是 Q39 所说"变化没那么快"。conventional retailers' confidence in the future increased as Census continued to report weak online sales J J 关注 The sudden decline in foot traffic in recent years 与 stores are downsizing and closing——这是结果性变化，而非把变化速度与预期对比。The sudden decline in foot traffic in recent years

questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（强锚点）
