questions.explanation:
**答案** I) pouring 动词
**词性槽** others ___ money 与 some developing 平行
**依据** pour money into = 把钱砸进others __(26)__ money into jetpacks 正是 pour money into sth 这一固定搭配——“向…砸钱/投入大量资金”，与“另一些发明者把钱投入喷气背包研发”语义完全吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
L) repressing “压制金钱”讲不通repress 意为“压制（情感/抗议）”，与 money into 这一搭配在语义上完全错位。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) ultimate 形容词
**词性槽** the___symbol：定冠词后、名词前作定语
**依据** “终极象征”=个人交通自由的最高代表the flying car has always remained the __(27)__ symbol of personal transport freedom 配 ultimate 形成固定搭配 ultimate symbol（终极象征），与 has always remained 的“始终如一”语气也吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) autonomous “自动驾驶”修饰 symbol 不通autonomous 形容车辆/系统能自主，不能形容“象征”这一抽象名词。
C) dual “双重”留给后面 C 类两用控制dual symbol 不构成常见搭配，且 dual 的核心义“两用/双重”在后文 30 题 dual controls 处才用得上。
E) imminent “即将到来”与 always remained 时间冲突imminent 指“迫在眉睫的”，与“一直以来都是…象征”这种长期状态矛盾。
H) outrageous “离谱的”带贬义，与 freedom 不搭outrageous 含负面色彩，用来修饰“个人交通自由的象征”语义/感情色彩都不对。
K) random “随机的”与“恒久象征”矛盾random 表“随意的”，与 has always remained 的稳定性完全相反。

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) prototypes 名词
**词性槽** have produced 后缺宾语，定语从句修饰
**依据** “能开能飞的样品”=飞行汽车原型Several companies around the world have produced __(28)__ that can drive on roads and fly 描述的正是各家公司造出的“试制样品”，prototypes（原型机）与“能在路上开、又能飞”完美吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
D) glamour 抽象“魅力”不能 drive/fly glamour 是抽象名词，不可数也无法成为 drive on roads and fly 的逻辑主语，搭配不成立。
F) odds “概率/不和”与造车无关odds 常用于 the odds are/at odds with，意为“可能性/不一致”，无法被公司 produce，也不能开飞。
G) opposites “对立面”语义跑偏opposites 表“相反事物”，与“能开能飞的实体”毫无关联。
N) spectrum “范围/光谱”不可被开飞spectrum 抽象指“范围”，公司不能造出一个 spectrum 来开和飞。

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) detached 动词
**词性槽** be ___ from：被动结构作过去分词
**依据** “与底盘分离”=detach from chassis a passenger capsule that can be __(29)__ from the road-going chassis and picked up by a helicopter-type machine 描写“客舱可从底盘上拆下、由直升机吊起”——detach from 正是“从…拆下/分离”的标准搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) segmented “被切分”≠“被拆下”segmented 强调“分段/被切分成段”，描述把整体切成数块，而原文是“把舱体从底盘上整体分离”，方向不一致。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) dual 形容词
**词性槽** need ___ controls：名词前作定语
**依据** “地空两用”需要“双重控制”require safety certification standards for road and air, need __(30)__ controls 上文反复强调“既要能开路、又要能上天”，dual controls（双重/两用控制系统）正契合“地空两套操控”这一现实需求。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) imminent “迫在眉睫的控制”不通imminent 修饰事件、危险等抽象概念，不与 controls 搭配。
H) outrageous 贬义+ controls 不搭outrageous 表“离谱的”，与中性的“控制系统”语义不合。
K) random “随机控制”与安全相悖上文谈到 safety certification standards，random controls 反而暗示无序，与安全语境矛盾。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) random 形容词
**词性槽** another ___ street：名词前作定语
**依据** “some street → another random street”对仗takes off from some London street and lands in another __(31)__ street，some 与another random 形成“随便起飞/随便降落”的对照，强调“在城市任意街道起降不现实”，random 完美承接。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) imminent “迫近的街道”不通imminent 不修饰地点，语义不搭。
H) outrageous “离谱街道”偏离主旨原句重点不是街道夸张，而是“随意”，outrageous 偏离论点。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) outrageous 形容词
**词性槽** their sometimes ___ schemes：副词后修饰名词
**依据** “有时离谱的方案”=贬义评价But that won't stop inventors from dreaming up new ways to fly and trying to persuade investors to back their sometimes __(32)__ schemes 的转折语气里，sometimes 提示“偶尔离谱”，outrageous（骇人听闻的、离谱的）精确捕捉作者对发明者“天马行空”的微讽。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) imminent “迫在眉睫的方案”逻辑不通imminent 形容“即将发生”，但 sometimes（有时）与之冲突，且文意是“离谱”而非“即将发生”。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 E) —— imminent 易被误选为“即将出现”。their sometimes__(32)__ schemes，imminent 看似形容“即将到来的方案”有诱惑力；防坑要抓 sometimes这一频率副词——它要求形容词指“偶发性质”，而 imminent 强调“迫近”，逻辑冲突；语气也偏轻讽，应选 outrageous。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) glamour 名词
**词性槽** speed, romanticism and ___：三者并列名词
**依据** “速度、浪漫、魅力”三位一体not by the age-old desires for speed, romanticism and __(33)__ 列举民航历来追逐的感性诉求，glamour（魅力/光鲜）与 speed、romanticism 同属“感官与浪漫”范畴，三词同列十分自然。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) opposites “对立面”与“渴望”逻辑断裂对“对立面”的渴望不构成连贯语义，且 opposites 通常以复数表“对立事物”，与列举的抽象诉求不同层级。
N) spectrum “光谱/范围”与浪漫诉求不同层级spectrum 偏中性技术词，对它的“古老渴望”不成立。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) autonomous 形容词
**词性槽** and ___ systems：名词前作定语
**依据** “AI + 自主系统”是当下绿色民航主线New electric engines coupled with artificial intelligence and __(34)__ systems will contribute to a more efficient, integrated transport system——人工智能搭配“自主/自动驾驶系统”才能撑起更高效低碳的整合交通，autonomous systems 是这一语境下的固定表达。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) imminent “即将发生的系统”不通imminent 不修饰 system 这种实体技术，搭配不成立。
H) outrageous 贬义不合“高效环保”语境全文此句正面评价新技术，outrageous 反义。
K) random “随机系统”与“高效整合”相悖下文紧接 more efficient, integrated，random 反义。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) odds 名词
**词性槽** at ___ with：固定搭配 at odds with
**依据** at odds with 固定搭配That's completely at __(35)__ with how I feel today 表达“这与我今天的感受完全不一致”，at odds with 正是“与…不一致/相矛盾”的标准短语，由 completely 强化矛盾程度。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) opposites opposites 不进 at…with 模板opposites 表“对立面”，惯用 be opposites/opposite to，不与 at…with 搭。
N) spectrum spectrum 与 at…with 不搭spectrum 常用 a spectrum of/across the spectrum，不能填入 at…with。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 G) —— opposites 偷换“对立”概念。completely at __(35)__ with how I feel today，opposites 词性相符、词义也带“对立”味，最易诱导；防坑只看搭配模板：能填 at___with 的只有 odds，opposites 不进该框架。

title: The market for products designed specifically for older…

sentences.text: The market for products designed specifically for older adults could reach $30 billion by next year, and startups(初创公司) want in on the action.
What they sometimes lack is feedback from the people who they hope will use their products.

So Brookdale, the country's largest owner of retirement communities, has been inviting a few select entrepreneurs just to move in for a few days, show off their products and hear what the residents have to say.

passage.translation: 专为老年人设计的产品市场到明年可能达到300亿美元，初创公司希望从中分一杯羹。它们有时缺乏的是来自那些他们希望会使用其产品的人的反馈。因此，美国最大的退休社区所有者Brookdale一直在邀请一些精选的创业者搬进来住几天，展示他们的产品，并听取居民的意见。

sentences.text: That's what brought Dayle Rodriguez, 28, all the way from England to the dining room of Brookdale South Bay in Torrance, California.
Rodriguez is the community and marketing manager for a company called Sentab.
The startup's product, SentabTV, enables older adults who may not be comfortable with computers to access email, video chat and social media using just their televisions and a remote control.

passage.translation: 这就是让28岁的Dayle Rodriguez从英国一路来到加利福尼亚州托伦斯市Brookdale South Bay餐厅的原因。Rodriguez是一家名为Sentab的公司的社区和市场经理。这家初创公司的产品SentabTV能够让可能不熟悉电脑的老年人仅使用电视和遥控器就能访问电子邮件、视频聊天和社交媒体。

sentences.text: "It's nothing new, it's nothing too complicated and it's natural because lots of people have TV remotes," says Rodriguez.

passage.translation: Rodriguez说："这不是什么新东西，也不是太复杂的东西，而且很自然，因为很多人都有电视遥控器。"

sentences.text: But none of that is the topic of conversation in the Brookdale dining room.
Instead, Rodriguez solicits residents' advice on what he should get on his cheeseburger and how he should spend the afternoon.
Playing cards was on the agenda, as well as learning to play mahjong(麻将).

passage.translation: 但这些都不是Brookdale餐厅里的谈话话题。相反，Rodriguez征求居民关于他应该在芝士汉堡上加什么以及他应该如何度过下午的建议。日程上有打牌，还有学习打麻将。

sentences.text: Rodriguez says it's important that residents here don't feel like he's selling them something.
"I've had more feedback in a passive approach," he says.
"Playing pool, playing cards, having dinner, having lunch," all work better "than going through a survey of questions.
When they get to know me and to trust me, knowing for sure I'm not selling them something—there'll be more honest feedback from them."

passage.translation: Rodriguez说，重要的是这里的居民不要觉得他在向他们推销什么东西。他说："我通过被动的方法得到了更多反馈。""打台球、打牌、吃晚饭、吃午饭，"所有这些都比"进行一系列问题调查"效果更好。"当他们了解我、信任我，确信我不是在向他们推销什么东西时——就会有来自他们的更诚实的反馈。"

sentences.text: Rodriguez is just the seventh entrepreneur to move into one of Brookdale's 1,100 senior living communities.
Other new products in the program have included a kind of full-body blow dryer and specially designed clothing that allows people with disabilities to dress and undress themselves.

passage.translation: Rodriguez只是搬入Brookdale旗下1100个老年生活社区之一的第七位创业者。该项目中的其他新产品包括一种全身式吹风机和专门设计的服装，这些服装让残障人士能够自己穿脱衣服。

sentences.text: Mary Lou Busch, 93, agreed to try the Sentab system.
She tells Rodriguez that it might be good for someone, but not for her.
"I have the computer and FaceTime, which I talk with my family on," she explains.
She also has an iPad and a smartphone.
"So I do pretty much everything I need to do."

passage.translation: 93岁的Mary Lou Busch同意试用Sentab系统。她告诉Rodriguez，这可能对某些人有好处，但对她来说不是。她解释说："我有电脑和FaceTime，我用它们和家人交谈。"她还有一台iPad和一部智能手机。"所以我做我需要做的几乎所有事情。"

sentences.text: To be fair, if Rodriguez had wanted feedback from some more technophobic(害怕技术的) seniors, he might have ended up in the wrong Brookdale community.
This one is located in the heart of Southern California's aerospace corridor.
Many residents have backgrounds in engineering, business and academic circles.

passage.translation: 公平地说，如果Rodriguez想从一些更害怕技术的老年人那里得到反馈，他可能最终去了错误的Brookdale社区。这个社区位于南加州航空航天走廊的中心地带。许多居民具有工程、商业和学术界背景。

sentences.text: But Rodriguez says he's still learning something important by moving into this Brookdale community: "People are more tech-proficient than we thought."

passage.translation: 但Rodriguez说，通过搬进这个Brookdale社区，他仍在学习一些重要的东西："人们比我们想象的更精通技术。"

sentences.text: And besides, where else would he learn to play mahjong?

passage.translation: 而且，他还能在哪里学打麻将呢？

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about the startups?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
文章关于初创公司说了什么?
A) 它们从不浪费时间为老年人升级产品。
B) 它们想要在老年人商品市场中占有一席之地。
C) 它们邀请老年人到公司试用其产品。
D) 它们试图通过向老年人推广数字产品来获利。
**判型** 题干 What does the passage say about the startups 直问「文章关于 X 说了什么」，指向原文某句客观陈述。
**拆句** 题干 What does the passage say about the startups 是简单特殊疑问句，主干 the passage say what about the startups，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 专门为老年人设计的产品市场明年可能达到 300 亿美元，初创公司想要在这块蛋糕里分一杯羹。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有选项 They never lose time in upgrading products for seniors 说「绝不浪费时间升级产品」，原文从未提及「升级速度」或 never lose time 这一信息。
B) ✓ 正确The market for products designed specifically for older adults could reach \$30 billion by next year↔ the seniors' goods market startups want in on the action ↔ want to have a share of预判「初创公司想进入老年市场分蛋糕」，与 They want to have a share of the seniors' goods market 在话题（老年市场）和动作（分一份）两个维度上完全等值，无其他选项能同时满足。
C) 与原文相反选项 They invite seniors to their companies to try their products 说创业公司请老人去公司，但原文 Brookdale, the country's largest owner of retirement communities, has been inviting a few select entrepreneurs just to move in for a few days 是养老社区 Brookdale 邀请创业者入住社区，方向完全相反。
D) 以偏概全选项 They try to profit from promoting digital products to seniors 把范围缩成「数字产品」，但原文 products designed specifically for older adults 并未限定为数字产品；后文也提到全身吹风机、自助穿衣这类非数字产品。
questions.quote: The market for products designed specifically for older adults could reach $30 billion by next year, and startups want in on the action.

options.text: They never lose time in upgrading products for seniors.
They want to have a share of the seniors' goods market.
They invite seniors to their companies to try their products.
They try to profit from promoting digital products to seniors.

questions.prompt: Some entrepreneurs have been invited to Brookdale to______.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
一些企业家被邀请到Brookdale去______。
A) 与潜在客户进行面谈
B) 对退休社区进行调查
C) 收集居民对其产品的反馈
D) 向老年居民展示如何使用信息技术产品
**判型** 题干 Some entrepreneurs have been invited to Brookdale to 是不完整陈述句，问目的，需要从原文找邀请的目的状语。
**拆句** 题干 Some entrepreneurs have been invited to Brookdale to 是被动语态待补全句，have been invited to do 中 to 后面接选项补完，考生须把选项当作目的状语来读。
**定位** 因此，全美最大的养老社区运营商 Brookdale 一直邀请少数精选的创业者入住几天，展示产品，听取居民的意见。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念选项 have an interview with potential customers 把「听取反馈」偷换成「采访潜在客户」；原文 Brookdale 居民是「试用者」，且交流方式是聊天、玩牌等非正式途径（Playing pool, playing cards, having dinner），不是正式采访。
B) 张冠李戴选项 conduct a survey of retirement communities 把调查对象错挂到「养老社区」上；原文要求创业者听取的是居民对产品的反馈，调查对象是产品，不是社区。
C) ✓ 正确hear what the residents have to say↔ collect residents' feedback show off their products↔ on their products预判中「听取居民意见」是邀请的根本目的，collect residents' feedback on their products 正是这个目的的标准书面表达，其他选项要么动作错（A、B、D），要么对象错。
D) 与原文相反选项 show senior residents how to use IT products 说创业者来「教老人用 IT 产品」；原文方向相反，是创业者来「听老人怎么说自己的产品」，且产品类型不限于 IT。
questions.quote: So Brookdale, the country's largest owner of retirement communities, has been inviting a few select entrepreneurs just to move in for a few days, show off their products and hear what the residents have to say.

options.text: have an interview with potential customers
conduct a survey of retirement communities
collect residents' feedback on their products
show senior residents how to use IT products

questions.prompt: What do we know about SentabTV?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于SentabTV我们了解到什么?
A) 它是一档迎合老年人兴趣的电视节目。
B) 它是一款在老年人中广受欢迎的数字电视。
C) 它是一款专为老年人观看节目而设计的电视。
D) 它是一个通过电视而非电脑实现的通信系统。
**判型** 题干 What do we know about SentabTV 问对 SentabTV 已知什么，找原文对该产品的客观描述句。
**拆句** 题干 What do we know about SentabTV 结构简单，主干 we know what about SentabTV，无陷阱。
**定位** 这家初创公司的产品 SentabTV，让那些不熟悉电脑的老年人，只用电视和遥控器就能收发邮件、视频聊天和使用社交媒体。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念选项 It is a TV program catering to the interest of the elderly 把 SentabTV 偷换为「电视节目」；原文是产品（通讯系统），不是节目。
B) 无中生有选项 It is a digital TV which enjoys popularity among seniors 说「数字电视且广受老人欢迎」；原文既未说它是数字电视，也未提及「广受欢迎」——恰恰相反，P7 中Busch 表示她不需要。
C) 偷换概念选项 It is a TV specially designed for seniors to view programs 说 SentabTV 是「专为老人看节目设计的电视」；原文是「通讯系统」，不是看节目的电视。
D) ✓ 正确enables older adults who may not be comfortable with computers to access email, video chat and social media↔ a communication system using just their televisions and a remote control ↔ via TV instead of a computer预判的「功能（通讯）+ 介质（电视）+ 对比项（电脑）」三要素，只有 It is a communication system via TV instead of a computer 同时覆盖；其他三项要么对象错，要么属性错。
questions.quote: The startup's product, SentabTV, enables older adults who may not be comfortable with computers to access email, video chat and social media using just their televisions and a remote control.

options.text: It is a TV program catering to the interest of the elderly.
It is a digital TV which enjoys popularity among seniors.
It is a TV specially designed for seniors to view programs.
It is a communication system via TV instead of a computer.

questions.prompt: What does Rodriguez say is important in promoting products?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
Rodriguez说在推广产品时什么是重要的?
A) 赢得潜在客户的信任。
B) 了解客户的好恶。
C) 当场展示其优越性。
D) 及时回应客户反馈。
**判型** 题干 What does Rodriguez say is important in promoting products 问 Rodriguez 的原话，是原文直接引语的转述。
**拆句** 题干 What does Rodriguez say is important in promoting products 中 What 既是 say的宾语从句主语，又是 is important 的主语，结构是 What [is important in promoting products] does Rodriguez say？考生易把它读成两个分立的疑问，实际只问一件事：什么东西在推销中重要。
**定位** 当他们开始了解我、信任我，确信我不是来卖东西的——就会有更诚实的反馈。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确to trust me ↔ Winning trust residents ↔ prospective customers整段两次出现 trust / not selling 的对立，trust 是 Rodriguez 反复强调的核心；Winning trust from prospective customers 是这一核心的精准书面表达。
B) 无中生有选项 Knowing the likes and dislikes of customers 说「了解客户喜好」；原文Rodriguez 强调的是「信任」，不是「了解喜好」——尽管聊汉堡配料、玩牌看似在了解喜好，但 Rodriguez 自己点名的核心是 trust。
C) 与原文相反选项 Demonstrating their superiority on the spot 说「当场展示产品优势」；恰恰相反，原文 residents here don't feel like he's selling them something 强调不能让人觉得在推销，更不能当场炫耀。
D) 无中生有选项 Responding promptly to customer feedback 说「及时回应反馈」；原文Rodriguez 谈的是「如何拿到诚实反馈」，没有谈「拿到之后如何回应」。
questions.quote: When they get to know me and to trust me, knowing for sure I'm not selling them something—there'll be more honest feedback from them.

options.text: Winning trust from prospective customers.
Knowing the likes and dislikes of customers.
Demonstrating their superiority on the spot.
Responding promptly to customer feedback.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the seniors in the Brookdale community?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于Brookdale社区的老年人我们了解到什么?
A) 他们中的大多数人对使用Sentab感兴趣。
B) 他们对高科技产品感到相当自在。
C) 他们与其他地方的老年人有很多共同点。
D) 他们中的大多数人比普通人享有更长的寿命。
**判型** 题干 What do we learn about the seniors in the Brookdale community 问对该社区老人已知什么，找原文对该群体的特征描述句。
**拆句** 题干 What do we learn about the seniors in the Brookdale community 中 in the Brookdale community 是修饰 seniors 的后置介词短语，限定为「这一个社区里的老人」，考生须读出限定关系，不要泛化成「所有老人」。
**定位** 但 Rodriguez 说他入住这个 Brookdale 社区还学到了一件重要的事：「人们比我们想象的更精通科技」。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反选项 Most of them are interested in using the Sentab 说「大多数人对 Sentab 感兴趣」；原文 She tells Rodriguez that it might be good for someone, but not for her 表明个案明确表示自己不需要，全文无任何「多数感兴趣」的证据。
B) ✓ 正确People are more tech-proficient than we thought↔They are quite at ease with high-tech products Many residents have backgrounds in engineering, business and academic circles↔quite at ease with high-tech products预判「该社区老人比想象中更懂科技」，与 They are quite at ease with high-tech products 在评价对象（科技产品）和评价程度（quite/more than thought）两个维度完全等值，独此一项。
C) 与原文相反选项 They have much in common with seniors elsewhere 说「与他处老人有很多共同点」；原文 To be fair, if Rodriguez had wanted feedback from some more technophobic seniors, he might have ended up in the wrong Brookdale community 恰恰是说这一社区特殊、不代表别处。
D) 无中生有选项 Most of them enjoy a longer life than average people 说「多数人比常人长寿」；全文从未提及寿命，唯一年龄数字 Mary Lou Busch, 93 是个案，不能推出群体寿命结论。
questions.quote: But Rodriguez says he's still learning something important by moving into this Brookdale community: "People are more tech-proficient than we thought."

options.text: Most of them are interested in using the Sentab.
They are quite at ease with high-tech products.
They have much in common with seniors elsewhere.
Most of them enjoy a longer life than average people.

title: Professor Stephen Hawking has warned that the creation…

sentences.text: Professor Stephen Hawking has warned that the creation of powerful artificial intelligence (AI) will be "either the best, or the worst thing, ever to happen to humanity", and praised the creation of an academic institute dedicated to researching the future of intelligence as "crucial to the future of our civilisation and our species".

passage.translation: Stephen Hawking教授警告说，强大人工智能（AI）的诞生将是"人类有史以来发生的最好或最坏的事情"，并赞扬致力于研究智能未来的学术机构的创建对"我们文明和我们物种的未来至关重要"。

sentences.text: Hawking was speaking at the opening of the Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence (LCFI) at Cambridge University, a multi-disciplinary institute that will attempt to tackle some of the open-ended questions raised by the rapid pace of development in AI research.
"We spend a great deal of time studying in history," Hawking said, "which, let's face it, is mostly the history of stupidity.
So it's a welcome change that people are studying instead the future of intelligence."

passage.translation: Hawking在Cambridge大学Leverhulme未来智能中心（LCFI）的开幕式上发表讲话。该中心是一个多学科研究所，将试图解决AI研究快速发展所引发的一些开放性问题。Hawking说："我们花大量时间研究历史，坦白说，历史大多是愚蠢的历史。所以人们转而研究智能的未来，这是一个可喜的变化。"

sentences.text: While the world-renowned physicist has often been cautious about AI, raising concerns that humanity could be the architect of its own destruction if it creates a super-intelligence with a will of its own, he was also quick to highlight the positives that AI research can bring.
"The potential benefits of creating intelligence are huge," he said.
"We cannot predict what we might achieve when our own minds are amplified by AI.
Perhaps with the tools of this new technological revolution, we will be able to undo some of the damage done to the natural world by the last one—industrialisation.
And surely we will aim to finally eradicate disease and poverty.
And every aspect of our lives will be transformed.
In short, success in creating AI could be the biggest event in the history of our civilisation."

passage.translation: 虽然这位世界著名的物理学家经常对AI持谨慎态度，担心如果人类创造出具有自主意志的超级智能，可能会成为自身毁灭的缔造者，但他也很快强调了AI研究可能带来的积极意义。他说："创造智能的潜在好处是巨大的。当我们自己的思维被AI增强时，我们无法预测可能取得什么成就。也许借助这场新技术革命的工具，我们将能够消除上一场革命——工业化——对自然世界造成的一些破坏。我们肯定会致力于最终消除疾病和贫困。我们生活的方方面面都将被改变。简而言之，成功创造AI可能是我们文明史上最重大的事件。"

sentences.text: Huw Price, the centre's academic director and the Bertrand Russell professor of philosophy at Cambridge University, where Hawking is also an academic, said that the centre came about partially as a result of the university's Centre for Existential Risk.
That institute examined a wider range of potential problems for humanity, while the LCFI has a narrow focus.

passage.translation: 该中心的学术主任、Cambridge大学Bertrand Russell哲学教授Huw Price说，该中心的成立部分源于该校的存在风险中心。Hawking也在Cambridge大学任职。那个研究所审视了人类面临的更广泛的潜在问题，而LCFI则专注于狭窄的领域。

sentences.text: AI pioneer Margaret Boden, professor of cognitive science at the University of Sussex, praised the progress of such discussions.
As recently as 2009, she said, the topic wasn't taken seriously, even among AI researchers.
"AI is hugely exciting," she said, "but it has limitations, which present grave dangers given uncritical use."

passage.translation: AI先驱、Sussex大学认知科学教授Margaret Boden赞扬了此类讨论的进展。她说，就在2009年，即使在AI研究人员中，这个话题也没有被认真对待。她说："AI令人极度兴奋，但它有局限性，如果不加批判地使用，就会带来严重危险。"

sentences.text: The academic community is not alone in warning about the potential dangers of AI as well as the potential benefits.
A number of pioneers from the technology industry, most famously the entrepreneur Elon Musk, have also expressed their concerns about the damage that a super-intelligent AI could do to humanity.

passage.translation: 学术界并非唯一对AI的潜在危险和潜在好处发出警告的群体。科技行业的一些先驱，最著名的是企业家Elon Musk，也表达了对超级智能AI可能对人类造成伤害的担忧。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What did Stephen Hawking think of artificial intelligence?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
Stephen Hawking对人工智能有何看法?
A) 它对人类文明的进步至关重要。
B) 它可能是一种福祉,也可能是一场正在酝酿的灾难。
C) 它可能既带来挑战也带来机遇。
D) 它将是人类智能的重大拓展。
**判型** 题干 What did Stephen Hawking think of artificial intelligence? 问的是某人对某事物的具体看法，要求回原文找观点句。
**拆句** 题干 What did Stephen Hawking think of artificial intelligence? 是 wh-疑问句，主干「X think of Y」，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 霍金教授警告说，创造强大的人工智能将会是「发生在人类身上最好或最坏的事」。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全vital to the progress of human civilisation 只取了「好」的一面，丢掉了 worst thing 的另一面。
B) ✓ 正确the best, or the worst thing↔ a blessing or a disaster ever to happen to humanity ↔ in the making预判「可能最好可能最坏」，与 a blessing or a disaster in the making 在结构和语义上都完全对应，锁定 B。
C) 范围程度偷改challenges as well as opportunities 听起来很对，但 challenges 远弱于 worst thing，opportunities 远弱于 best thing，程度被显著削弱。
D) 答非所问a significant expansion of human intelligence 与 our own minds are amplified by AI 近似，但那是 Q46 之外的内容，且 Q46 问的是首段的总体评价，不是 P3 的局部细节。
questions.quote: Professor Stephen Hawking has warned that the creation of powerful artificial intelligence (AI) will be "either the best, or the worst thing, ever to happen to humanity".

options.text: It would be vital to the progress of human civilisation.
It might be a blessing or a disaster in the making.
It might present challenges as well as opportunities.
It would be a significant expansion of human intelligence.

questions.prompt: What did Hawking say about the creation of the LCFI?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
Hawking对LCFI的创建有何评论?
A) 它将加速人工智能研究的进展。
B) 它将标志着人工智能产业向前迈进了一步。
C) 它对人类的命运极其重要。
D) 它是多学科合作的成果。
**判型** 题干 What did Hawking say about the creation of the LCFI? 问具体陈述，走常规细节定位。
**拆句** What did Hawking say about the creation of the LCFI?，主干 「X say about Y」，creation of the LCFI 作介词宾语，结构简单。
**定位** （霍金）赞扬创立一所致力于研究未来智能的学术机构，称其「对我们文明和物种的未来至关重要」。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Hawking 只说该机构对人类未来至关重要，并未提及它会加速 AI 研究的进度。
B) 偷换概念Hawking 强调对 civilisation 与 species 重要，不是对 AI industry 重要。
C) ✓ 正确crucial ↔ extremely important the future of our civilisation and our species ↔ the destiny of humankind预判「对人类未来至关重要」，与 extremely important to the destiny of humankind 在程度和对象上完全对应，锁定 C。
D) 答非所问原文 multi-disciplinary institute 只是描述机构属性，并非 Hawking 对 LCFI 的评价；Hawking 评价的是其重要性，不是其合作成就。
questions.quote: praised the creation of an academic institute dedicated to researching the future of intelligence as "crucial to the future of our civilisation and our species".

options.text: It would accelerate the progress of AI research.
It would mark a step forward in the AI industry.
It was extremely important to the destiny of humankind.
It was an achievement of multi-disciplinary collaboration.

questions.prompt: What did Hawking say was a welcome change in AI research?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
Hawking认为人工智能研究中的哪一变化值得欢迎?
A) 研究重点从过去转向未来。
B) 研究从理论转向实施。
C) 更加强调人工智能的负面影响。
D) 人类对自身过去愚蠢行为的认识日益增强。
**判型** 题干 What did Hawking say was a welcome change in AI research? 是问 Hawking 所说的具体内容，定位句一句话即可作答。
**拆句** What did Hawking say was a welcome change in AI research? 含套层从句：主句What did Hawking say，宾语从句省略主语 「(what) was a welcome change」。即问Hawking 所说的「那个 welcome change」是什么。
**定位** 「我们花大量时间研究历史，」霍金说，「而历史多半是一部愚蠢史。所以人们改去研究未来智能，是一个可喜的变化。」
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确studying in history ↔ from the past studying instead the future of intelligence ↔ to the future welcome change ↔ shift of research focus预判「研究对象由历史转向未来」，与 The shift of research focus from the past to the future. 完全对位，锁定 A。
B) 无中生有原文谈的是「历史 vs 未来」，与「理论 vs 实施」完全不在一个维度。
C) 偷换概念Hawking 称可喜变化是研究 future of intelligence，而不是着重 AI 的负面影响。
D) 答非所问原文 mostly the history of stupidity 只是 Hawking 的一句吐槽，用来对比为何研究未来反而是 welcome change，并不是 welcome change 本身。
questions.quote: "We spend a great deal of time studying in history," Hawking said, "which, let's face it, is mostly the history of stupidity. So it's a welcome change that people are studying instead the future of intelligence."

options.text: The shift of research focus from the past to the future.
The shift of research from theory to implementation.
The greater emphasis on the negative impact of AI.
The increasing awareness of mankind's past stupidity.

questions.prompt: What concerns did Hawking raise about AI?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
Hawking对人工智能提出了哪些担忧?
A) 它迟早可能超越人类智能。
B) 它可能最终过度放大人类思维。
C) 超级智能可能导致其自身的毁灭。
D) 超级智能可能最终毁灭人类。
**判型** 题干 What concerns did Hawking raise about AI? 是细节，答 Hawking 担忧的具体内容。
**拆句** What concerns did Hawking raise about AI? 主干 「X raise concerns about Y」，raise 是搭配动词，about AI 指明话题范围。结构清晰。
**定位** 这位享誉世界的物理学家在 AI 问题上常常小心翼翼，他担忧：如果人类造出有自己意志的超级智能，人类可能会成为自我毁灭的设计师。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Hawking 谈的是自我意志的超级智能毁灭人类，不是 AI 何时迟早超过人类智能的时间预测。
B) 与原文相反原文 our own minds are amplified by AI 是正面预期，B 选项加了 over- 变成负面over-amplify，与原文相反。
C) 偷换概念原文是 super-intelligence 毁灭人类（destruction of humanity），C 改成 super- intelligence 毁灭 its own——主体宾语反了。
D) ✓ 正确humanity could be the architect of its own destruction ↔ ruin mankind super-intelligence with a will of its own ↔ Super-intelligence if it creates ↔ eventually预判「超级智能或将毁灭人类」，与 Super-intelligence may eventually ruin mankind. 完全对位，锁定 D。
questions.quote: the world-renowned physicist has often been cautious about AI, raising concerns that humanity could be the architect of its own destruction if it creates a super-intelligence with a will of its own.

options.text: It may exceed human intelligence sooner or later.
It may ultimately over-amplify the human mind.
Super-intelligence may cause its own destruction.
Super-intelligence may eventually ruin mankind.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about some entrepreneurs from the technology industry?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于科技行业的一些企业家,我们了解到什么?
A) 他们深受学术界的影响。
B) 他们最有可能从人工智能发展中获益。
C) 他们与学术界对人工智能有着相同的担忧。
D) 他们相信自己能够让人工智能处于人类的控制之下。
**判型** What do we learn about some entrepreneurs from the technology industry? 问的是关于该群体的具体陈述，走细节路径。
**拆句** What do we learn about some entrepreneurs from the technology industry? 主干「learn about X」；from the technology industry 是后置定语修饰 entrepreneurs。无陷阱。
**定位** 学术界并非唯一发出 AI 警示的群体。来自科技业的一批先驱（其中最著名的是企业家埃隆·马斯克）也表达了对超级智能 AI 可能给人类带来损害的担忧。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断原文只说两群体不约而同地担忧，并未说企业家是受学术界影响才担忧的——立场一致≠ 受影响。
B) 无中生有原文未提及科技业企业家「最可能受益于 AI 发展」，纯属臆造。
C) ✓ 正确The academic community is not alone in warning↔share the same concerns about AI as academics have also expressed their concerns↔share the same concerns academic community ↔ academics预判「与学术界同样担忧」，与 They share the same concerns about AI as academics. 在立场、对象、群体三方面都对位，锁定 C。
D) 与原文相反原文表达的是科技业企业家担忧 AI 危害，D 却说他们相信能控制 AI——方向反转。
questions.quote: The academic community is not alone in warning about the potential dangers of AI as well as the potential benefits. A number of pioneers from the technology industry, most famously the entrepreneur Elon Musk, have also expressed their concerns about the damage that a super- intelligent AI could do to humanity.

options.text: They are much influenced by the academic community.
They are most likely to benefit from AI development.
They share the same concerns about AI as academics.
They believe they can keep AI under human control.

title: Pasta is no longer off the menu, after…

sentences.text: Pasta is no longer off the menu, after a new review of studies suggested that the carbohydrate can form part of a healthy diet, and even help people lose weight.
For years, nutritionists have recommended that pasta be kept to a (26)____ , to cut calories, prevent fat build-up and stop blood sugar (27)____up.

passage.translation: 意大利面不再是禁忌食物，一项新的研究综述表明，这种碳水化合物可以成为健康饮食的一部分,甚至有助于人们减肥。多年来,营养学家一直建议将意大利面的摄入量控制在最低限度,以减少卡路里摄入、防止脂肪堆积并阻止血糖飙升。

sentences.text: The low-carbohydrate food movement gave birth to such diets as the Atkins, Paleo and Keto, which advised swapping foods like bread, pasta and potatoes for vegetables, fish and meat.
More recently the trend of swapping spaghetti for vegetables has been (28)____ by clean-eating experts.

passage.translation: 低碳水化合物饮食运动催生了Atkins、Paleo和Keto等饮食法,这些饮食法建议用蔬菜、鱼类和肉类替代面包、意大利面和土豆等食物。最近,用蔬菜替代意大利面条的趋势得到了清洁饮食专家的推崇。

sentences.text: But now a (29)____ review and analysis of (30)____ studies by Canadian researchers found that not only does pasta not cause weight gain, but three meals a week can help people drop more than half a kilogram over four months.
The reviewers found that pasta had been unfairly demonized(妖魔化) because it had been 30 in with other, more fat-promoting carbohydrates.

passage.translation: 但现在,加拿大研究人员对30项研究进行的系统综述和分析发现,意大利面不仅不会导致体重增加,而且每周吃三顿意大利面可以帮助人们在四个月内减重超过半公斤。研究综述者发现,意大利面被不公平地妖魔化了,因为它被归入了其他更容易促进脂肪堆积的碳水化合物之列。

sentences.text: "The study found that pasta didn't (31)____ to weight gain or increase in body fat," said lead author Dr.
John Sievenpiper.
"In (32)____ the evidence, we can now say with some confidence that pasta does not have an (33)____ effect on body weight outcomes when it is consumed as part of a healthy dietary pattern."
In fact, analysis actually showed a small weight loss (34)____ to concerns.
Perhaps pasta can be part of a healthy diet.

passage.translation: 主要作者John Sievenpiper博士说:"该研究发现,意大利面不会导致体重增加或体脂增加。在权衡证据后,我们现在可以相当有把握地说,当意大利面作为健康饮食模式的一部分食用时,不会对体重结果产生不利影响。"事实上,分析实际上显示了轻微的体重下降,这与人们的担忧相反。也许意大利面可以成为健康饮食的一部分。

sentences.text: Those involved in the (35)____ trials on average ate 3.3 servings of pasta a week instead of other carbohydrates, one serving equaling around half a cup.
They lost around half a kilogram over an average follow-up of 12 weeks.

passage.translation: 参与临床试验的人平均每周吃3.3份意大利面来代替其他碳水化合物,一份相当于大约半杯。在平均12周的随访期间,他们减重约半公斤。

Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
Pasta is no longer off the menu, after a new review of studies suggested that the carbohydrate can form part of a healthy diet, and even help people lose weight. For years, nutritionists have recommended that pasta be kept to a {{26}} , to cut calories, prevent fat build-up and stop blood sugar {{27}}up.

The low-carbohydrate food movement gave birth to such diets as the Atkins, Paleo and Keto, which advised swapping foods like bread, pasta and potatoes for vegetables, fish and meat. More recently the trend of swapping spaghetti for vegetables has been {{28}} by clean-eating experts.

But now a {{29}} review and analysis of {{30}} studies by Canadian researchers found that not only does pasta not cause weight gain, but three meals a week can help people drop more than half a kilogram over four months. The reviewers found that pasta had been unfairly demonized(妖魔化) because it had been 30 in with other, more fat-promoting carbohydrates.

"The study found that pasta didn't {{31}} to weight gain or increase in body fat," said lead author Dr. John Sievenpiper. "In {{32}} the evidence, we can now say with some confidence that pasta does not have an {{33}} effect on body weight outcomes when it is consumed as part of a healthy dietary pattern." In fact, analysis actually showed a small weight loss {{34}} to concerns. Perhaps pasta can be part of a healthy diet.

Those involved in the {{35}} trials on average ate 3.3 servings of pasta a week instead of other carbohydrates, one serving equaling around half a cup. They lost around half a kilogram over an average follow-up of 12 weeks.

options.text: adverse
minimum
championed
radiating
clinical
ration
contrary
shooting
contribute

intimate
systematic

questions.explanation:
**答案** I) minimum 名词
**词性槽** be kept to a ___ 结构里 a 后缺名词
**依据** 固定搭配 keep sth to a minimum pasta be kept to a __(26)__, to cut calories, prevent fat build-up and stop blood sugar __(27)__ up——目的是减少卡路里、防脂肪堆积、稳血糖，正是『把意面摄入控制在最低』的语义，keep ... to a minimum 是地道固定搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
K) ration ration 偏战时/物资配给语境ration 指被分配的『定量配给』，多用于物资紧缺时的配给制；keep to a ration 不是常见搭配，与营养师建议减量的语境不贴。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) shooting 动词
**词性槽** stop sth ___ up，stop 后宾语 + 动名词或现在分词作宾补
**依据** shoot up 表『（数值）急剧上升』，正合描述血糖飙升to cut calories, prevent fat build-up and stop blood sugar __(27)__ up——并列三个目的：减卡、防脂、阻止血糖飙升，stop blood sugar shooting up（阻止血糖飙升）语义完全契合。

**答案** B) championed 动词
**词性槽** has been ___ by clean-eating experts，be done by 被动语态需要过去分词
**依据** champion 作动词意为『力挺、拥护』，正合 experts 倡导的语境More recently the trend of swapping spaghetti for vegetables has been championed by clean-eating experts——『用蔬菜替代意面的潮流被清洁饮食专家所推崇』，与 P2 上文 The low-carbohydrate food movement gave birth to such diets as the Atkins, Paleo and Keto 关于低碳饮食运动的叙述一脉相承。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) lumped 搭配方向不对，且应留给 30 题lump 多用在 lump in with（混为一谈），不直接 be lumped by sb；且 30 题 it had been__(30)__ in with other ... carbohydrates 空后紧跟 in with，是 lump 的『正穴』。
H) magnified 语义偏差magnify 是『放大、夸大』，说『潮流被专家放大』勉强能搭、但与 P2『专家积极倡导』的正向语境对不齐——上下文是专家在推这套做法，不是在『夸大』它。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— magnified 看似也能填，实则方向反。has been __(28)__by clean-eating experts 中 H magnified 词性、被动语态都对，且『被专家放大』勉强能解；但 P2 上下文 The low-carbohydrate food movement gave birth to such diets as the Atkins, Paleo and Keto 显示专家在积极倡导这股潮流，应该是 championed（推崇），不是 magnified（放大）。防坑：看段落的感情走向，专家在 P2 里是『支持』而非『夸大』。

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) systematic 形容词
**词性槽** 冠词 a 与名词 review 之间，缺一个形容词作定语
**依据** 学术固定搭配 systematic review（系统综述）P3 说这是 a __(29)__ review and analysis of 30 studies by Canadian researchers——对30 项研究做综述与分析，正是学术领域里 systematic review（系统综述）的标准表达，与下文 found that not only does pasta not cause weight gain 提到的研究结论也契合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) adverse 感情色彩与全文正面定调相反adverse 是负面词（不利的），而本段是用这项研究为意面平反，整体是正面定调；而且adverse review（差评）与下文 not only does pasta not cause weight gain 的肯定性结论矛盾。
C) clinical留给 35 题的 clinical trials clinical 虽可作形容词，但 P5 Those involved in the __(35)__ trials 那处的 clinical trials（临床试验）是更典型的固定搭配，把它留给 35 题更合理；29 题这里若填 clinical review 并非通用学术术语。
D) contrary 留给 34 题的 contrary to 搭配contrary 更常用在 contrary to 结构里，34 题 a small weight loss __(34)__ to concerns 后面紧跟 to，是 contrary 的『正穴』，这里不应抢用。
F) intimate 语义不搭：intimate review 不成立intimate 表『亲密的、私人的』，用在『对 30 项研究的综述』上语义不通，不符合学术语境。
I) minimum 更适合作名词搭配 keep ... to a minimum minimum 在本卷里被 26 题 pasta be kept to a __(26)__ 锁定为名词搭配 keep to a minimum，不参与本空的形容词竞争。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) lumped 动词
**词性槽** had been ___ in with，被动语态需过去分词
**依据** 固定搭配 lump in with（混为一谈）pasta had been unfairly demonized(妖魔化) because it had been lumped in with other, more fat-promoting carbohydrates——意面被妖魔化，是因为它被『和其他更易致脂肪堆积的碳水化合物混为一谈』，lump in with 是高度固定的短语搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) magnified 搭配不成立magnified in with 不是英语固定搭配，magnify 不与 in with 同现；语义上『把意面和其他碳水化合物放大在一起』也不通。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) contribute 动词
**词性槽** didn't ___ to，助动词 didn't 后接动词原形
**依据** contribute to 表『导致、促成』，是体重增加这种结果型语境的固定搭配The study found that pasta didn't contribute to weight gain or increase in body fat——研究发现意面没有『促成』体重增加或体脂上升；contribute to + 结果 是六级阅读和写作高频搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) subscribe subscribe to 是『赞同观点』，主语不能是食物subscribe to 通常表示『订阅；赞同某一观点/理论』，主语必须是有意识主体（人/机构）；这里主语是 pasta（意面），意面无法『赞同体重增加』，逻辑荒谬。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 M) —— subscribe to 形似 contribute to，但主语不对。pasta didn't __(31)__ to weight gain 中 M subscribe 是动词原形且能接 to，词性、搭配都过关；但 subscribe to 表『订阅/赞同观点』，主语得是人或机构。pasta 是食物，不可能『赞同体重增加』。防坑：看到 ___ to 时，先看主语是『有意识主体』还是『客观事物』——客观因果优先 contribute to。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) weighing 动词
**词性槽** 介词 In 后需要动名词，构成 In ___ the evidence 的状语结构
**依据** 固定搭配 weigh the evidence（权衡证据）In weighing the evidence, we can now say with some confidence that pasta does not have an adverse effect on body weight outcomes——『在权衡了证据之后，我们能够有把握地说……』，weigh the evidence 是学术与法律语境的固定搭配，与下文研究者confident 表态衔接自然。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
J) radiating 搭配与语义都不对radiate the evidence『辐射证据』在英语里不成立，radiate 多用于 radiate heat/light/confidence 之类的搭配，宾语必为可辐射的事物或抽象品质。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) adverse 形容词
**词性槽** an ___ effect 结构，an 与名词 effect 之间缺形容词
**依据** 固定搭配 adverse effect（不利影响）we can now say with some confidence that pasta does not have an adverse effect on body weight outcomes when it is consumed as part of a healthy dietary pattern——意面在健康饮食模式下对体重结果『没有不利影响』，adverse effect 是医学/营养学里极常见的固定搭配。

**答案** D) contrary 形容词
**词性槽** weight loss ___ to concerns 中需要个能接 to 的形容词
**依据** 固定搭配 contrary to（与……相反）In __(32)__ the evidence, we can now say with some confidence that pasta does not have an __(33)__ effect on body weight outcomes ... In fact, analysis actually showed a small weight loss contrary to concerns.——人们本来担心吃意面会胖，结果分析显示却出现轻微减重，与人们的担忧『恰恰相反』，contrary to concerns 完美贴合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) intimate 搭配与语义都不成立intimate to 不是固定搭配，且 intimate 表『亲密』，与 concerns 语义不通。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) clinical 形容词
**词性槽** 定冠词 the 与名词 trials 之间，缺形容词作定语
**依据** 固定搭配 clinical trials（临床试验）Those involved in the __(35)__ trials on average ate 3.3 servings of pasta a week 描述受试者饮食安排，正是医学/营养学研究的典型场景；clinical trial 是不可拆的固定术语。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) adverse 感情色彩冲突adverse trials『不利的试验』语义生硬，且与下文 They lost around half a kilogram 这一肯定性结果格调不合；adverse 应留给 33 题的 adverse effect。
D) contrary 搭配不当且应留给 34 题contrary trials 不是固定搭配，且 contrary 的『正穴』是 34 题 contrary to concerns。
F) intimate 语义不搭intimate trials（亲密的试验）在科研语境里说不通。
I) minimum 应留给 26 题的名词搭配minimum 在 26 题作名词 keep to a minimum，不与本空竞争。

title: Resilience Is About How You Recharge, Not How You Endure

passage.label: A

sentences.text: As constant travelers and parents of a 2-year-old, we sometimes fantasize about how much work we can do when one of us gets on a plane, undistracted by phones, friends, or movies.
We race to get all our ground work done: packing, going through security, doing a last-minute work call, calling each other, then boarding the plane.
Then, when we try to have that amazing work session in flight, we get nothing done.
Even worse, after refreshing our email or reading the same studies over and over, we are too exhausted when we land to soldier on with(继续处理) the emails that have inevitably still piled up.

passage.translation: 作为经常旅行且有一个2岁孩子的父母，我们有时会幻想当我们其中一人登上飞机时能完成多少工作，不被手机、朋友或电影分心。我们争分夺秒地完成所有地面准备工作：打包、通过安检、进行最后一分钟的工作电话、互相通话，然后登机。然而，当我们试图在飞行中进行那场精彩的工作时，我们却什么也做不成。更糟糕的是，在反复刷新邮件或一遍又一遍地阅读相同的研究报告后，我们在落地时已精疲力竭，无力继续处理那些不可避免地堆积起来的邮件。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: Why should flying deplete us?
We're just sitting there doing nothing.
Why can't we be tougher, more resilient(有复原力的) and determined in our work so we can accomplish all of the goals we set for ourselves?

Based on our current research, we have come to realize that the problem is not our hectic schedule or the plane travel itself; the problem comes from a misconception of what it means to be resilient, and the resulting impact of overworking.

passage.translation: 为什么飞行会让我们精疲力竭？我们只是坐在那里什么也没做。为什么我们不能在工作中更坚韧、更有复原力、更有决心，从而完成我们为自己设定的所有目标？基于我们目前的研究，我们开始意识到问题不在于我们繁忙的日程或飞机旅行本身；问题来自对复原力含义的误解，以及过度工作所带来的影响。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: We often take a militaristic, "tough" approach to resilience and determination like a Marine pulling himself through the mud, a boxer going one more round, or a football player picking himself up off the ground for one more play.
We believe that the longer we tough it out, the tougher we are, and therefore the more successful we will be.
However, this entire conception is scientifically inaccurate.

passage.translation: 我们经常对复原力和决心采取一种军事化的"强硬"方法，就像海军陆战队员在泥地中爬行、拳击手再打一回合，或足球运动员从地上爬起来再比赛一次。我们相信坚持得越久，我们就越坚韧，因此我们就会越成功。然而，这整个概念在科学上是不准确的。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: The very lack of a recovery period is dramatically holding back our collective ability to be resilient and successful.
Research has found that there is a direct correlation between lack of recovery and increased incidence of health and safety problems.
And lack of recovery—whether by disrupting sleep with thoughts of work or having continuous cognitive arousal by watching our phones—is costing our companies $62 billion a year in lost productivity.

passage.translation: 恰恰是缺乏恢复期这一点极大地阻碍了我们的集体复原力和成功能力。研究发现，缺乏恢复与健康和安全问题发生率增加之间存在直接关联。而缺乏恢复——无论是因工作思绪而扰乱睡眠，还是因看手机而持续认知觉醒——每年给我们的公司造成620亿美元的生产力损失。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: And just because work stops, it doesn't mean we are recovering.

We "stop" work sometimes at 5 pm, but then we spend the night wrestling with solutions to work problems, talking about our work over dinner, and falling asleep thinking about how much work we'll do tomorrow.
In a study just released, researchers from Norway found that 7.8% of Norwegians have become workaholics(工作狂).

The scientists cite a definition of "workaholism" as "being overly concerned about work, driven by an uncontrollable work motivation, and investing so much time and effort in work that it impairs other important life areas."

passage.translation: 仅仅因为停止工作，并不意味着我们正在恢复。我们有时在下午5点"停止"工作，但随后整晚都在努力寻找工作问题的解决方案，在晚餐时谈论我们的工作，入睡时想着明天要做多少工作。在一项刚刚发布的研究中，来自挪威的研究人员发现7.8%的挪威人已成为工作狂。科学家们引用的"工作狂"定义是"过度关注工作，被不可控制的工作动机驱使，在工作上投入如此多的时间和精力，以至于损害了其他重要的生活领域。"

passage.label: F

sentences.text: We believe that the number of people who fit that definition includes the majority of American workers, which prompted us to begin a study of workaholism in the U.S.

Our study will use a large corporate dataset from a major medical company to examine how technology extends our working hours and thus interferes with necessary cognitive recovery, resulting in huge health care costs and turnover costs for employers.

passage.translation: 我们相信符合该定义的人数包括大多数美国工人，这促使我们开始在美国进行一项关于工作狂的研究。我们的研究将使用一家大型医疗公司的大型企业数据集，来研究技术如何延长我们的工作时间，从而干扰必要的认知恢复，导致雇主承担巨额医疗成本和人员流动成本。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: The misconception of resilience is often bred from an early age.
Parents trying to teach their children resilience might celebrate a high school student staying up until 3 am to finish a science fair project.
What a distortion of resilience!
A resilient child is a well-rested one.

When an exhausted student goes to school, he risks hurting everyone on the road with his impaired driving; he doesn't have the cognitive resources to do well on his English test; he has lower self-control with his friends; and at home, he is moody with his parents.
Overwork and exhaustion are the opposite of resilience and the bad habits we acquire when we're young only magnify when we hit the workforce.

passage.translation: 对复原力的误解往往从小就开始培养。试图教导孩子复原力的父母可能会称赞一名高中生熬夜到凌晨3点完成科学展览项目。这是对复原力多么大的扭曲！一个有复原力的孩子是一个休息充分的孩子。当一个精疲力竭的学生去上学时，他可能因驾驶能力受损而伤害路上的每个人；他没有认知资源在英语考试中表现良好；他与朋友相处时自制力较低；在家里，他对父母情绪不佳。过度工作和疲惫是复原力的对立面，而我们年轻时养成的坏习惯只会在我们进入职场后被放大。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: As Jim Loehr and Tony Schwartz have written, if you have too much time in the performance zone, you need more time in the recovery zone, otherwise you risk burnout.
Gathering your resources to "try hard" requires burning energy in order to overcome your currently low arousal level.
It also worsens exhaustion.
Thus the more imbalanced we become due to overworking, the more value there is in activities that allow us to return to a state of balance.
The value of a recovery period rises in proportion to the amount of work required of us.

passage.translation: 正如Jim Loehr和Tony Schwartz所写，如果你在表现区域待的时间太长，你需要在恢复区域待更多时间，否则你就有倦怠的风险。聚集你的资源来"努力尝试"需要燃烧能量以克服你目前的低觉醒水平。这也会加剧疲惫。因此，由于过度工作，我们变得越不平衡，那些能让我们恢复平衡状态的活动就越有价值。恢复期的价值与我们所需完成的工作量成正比。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: So how do we recover and build resilience?

Most people assume that if you stop doing a task like answering emails or writing a paper, your brain will naturally recover, so that when you start again later in the day or the next morning, you'll have your energy back.
But surely everyone reading this has had times when you lie in bed for hours, unable to fall asleep because your brain is thinking about work.
If you lie in bed for eight hours, you may have rested, but you can still feel exhausted the next day.
That's because rest and recovery are not the same thing.

passage.translation: 那么我们如何恢复并建立复原力？大多数人认为，如果你停止做某项任务，比如回复邮件或写论文，你的大脑就会自然恢复，这样当你当天晚些时候或第二天早上重新开始时，你就会恢复精力。但阅读本文的每个人肯定都有过这样的经历：你在床上躺了几个小时，无法入睡，因为你的大脑在思考工作。如果你在床上躺了8个小时，你可能休息了，但第二天你仍然会感到精疲力竭。这是因为休息和恢复不是一回事。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: If you're trying to build resilience at work, you need adequate internal and external recovery periods.

As researchers Zijlstra, Cropley and Rydstedt write in their 2014 paper: "Internal recovery refers to the shorter periods of relaxation that take place within the frames of the work day or the work setting in the form of short scheduled or unscheduled breaks, by shifting attention or changing to other work tasks when the mental or physical resources required for the initial task are temporarily depleted or exhausted.
External recovery refers to actions that take place outside of work—e.g. in the free time between the work days, and during weekends, holidays or vacations."

If after work you lie around on your bed and get irritated by political commentary on your phone or get stressed thinking about decisions about how to renovate your home, your brain has not received a break from high mental arousal states.
Our brains need a rest as much as our bodies do.

passage.translation: 如果你想在工作中建立复原力，你需要充足的内部和外部恢复期。正如研究人员Zijlstra、Cropley和Rydstedt在他们2014年的论文中所写："内部恢复是指在工作日或工作环境框架内进行的较短放松时期，形式为短暂的计划内或计划外休息，通过转移注意力或在初始任务所需的心理或身体资源暂时耗尽或用尽时转换到其他工作任务。外部恢复是指在工作之外进行的活动——例如，在工作日之间的空闲时间、周末、假期或休假期间。"如果下班后你躺在床上，被手机上的政治评论激怒，或因思考如何翻新房屋的决定而感到压力，你的大脑就没有从高度精神觉醒状态中得到休息。我们的大脑和身体一样需要休息。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: If you really want to build resilience, you can start by strategically stopping.
Give yourself the resources to be tough by creating internal and external recovery periods.
Amy Blankson describes how to strategically stop during the day by using technology to control overworking.
She suggests downloading the Instant or Moment apps to see how many times you turn on your phone each day.
You can also use apps like Offtime or Unplugged to create tech free zones by strategically scheduling automatic airplane modes.
The average person turns on their phone 150 times every day.
If every distraction took only 1 minute, that would account for 2.5 hours a day.

passage.translation: 如果你真的想建立复原力，你可以从战略性地停止开始。通过创造内部和外部恢复期，为自己提供坚韧的资源。Amy Blankson描述了如何在白天使用技术来控制过度工作，从而战略性地停止。她建议下载Instant或Moment应用程序，看看你每天打开手机多少次。你还可以使用Offtime或Unplugged等应用程序，通过战略性地安排自动飞行模式来创建无技术区域。普通人每天打开手机150次。如果每次分心只需1分钟，那么每天就会占用2.5小时。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: In addition, you can take a cognitive break every 90 minutes to charge your batteries.
Try to not have lunch at your desk, but instead spend time outside or with your friends—not talking about work.
Take all of your paid time off, which not only gives you recovery periods, but raises your productivity and likelihood of promotion.

passage.translation: 此外，你可以每90分钟进行一次认知休息来充电。尽量不要在办公桌前吃午饭，而是在户外或与朋友共度时光——不要谈论工作。利用你所有的带薪休假，这不仅能给你恢复期，还能提高你的生产力和晋升可能性。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: As for us, we've started using our plane time as a work-free zone, and thus time to dip into the recovery phase.
The results have been fantastic.
We are usually tired already by the time we get on a plane, and the crowded space and unstable internet connection make work more challenging.
Now, instead of swimming upstream, we relax, sleep, watch movies, or listen to music.
And when we get off the plane, instead of being depleted, we feel recovered and ready to return to the performance zone.

passage.translation: 至于我们，我们已开始将飞机时间作为无工作区域，因此也是进入恢复阶段的时间。结果非常棒。通常我们登上飞机时已经很累了，拥挤的空间和不稳定的网络连接使工作更具挑战性。现在，我们不再逆流而上，而是放松、睡觉、看电影或听音乐。当我们下飞机时，我们不再精疲力竭，而是感到恢复了活力，准备好重返表现区域。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: It has been found that inadequate recovery often leads to poor health and accidents.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
研究发现,恢复不足往往会导致健康状况不佳和事故发生。
**锚点** inadequate recovery → poor health and accidents
**定位** 研究发现，缺乏恢复与健康和安全问题发生率上升之间存在直接关联。
**改写** inadequate recovery ↔ lack of recovery inadequate ↔ lack of 的同义改写often leads to poor health and accidents ↔a direct correlation between lack of recovery and increased incidence of health and safety problems因果 ↔ 相关 + accidents ↔ safety problems
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
G G 段确实提到 he risks hurting everyone on the road with his impaired driving，看似触及「事故」，但它只是熬夜学生的个案例证，落点是 Overwork and exhaustion are the opposite of resilience 的 resilience 概念，而非「恢复不足与健康安全问题相关」的研究结论。When an exhausted student goes to school, he risks hurting everyone on the road with his impaired driving
questions.quote: Research has found that there is a direct correlation between lack of recovery and increased incidence of health and safety problems.

questions.prompt: Mental relaxation is much needed, just as physical relaxation is.
questions.explanation:
**答案** J 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
精神放松和身体放松一样,都是非常必要的。
**锚点** Mental relaxation 与 physical relaxation 类比
**定位** 我们的大脑和身体一样，都需要休息。
**改写** Mental relaxation is much needed ↔ Our brains need a rest mental ↔ brains 的「抽象 ↔ 具体器官」替换just as physical relaxation is ↔ as much as our bodies do类比连词 just as ↔ as much as 的句式转换
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
I I 段同样出现 brain 与 rest，但其核心论点是 rest and recovery are not the same thing，与陈述句「心理放松和身体放松一样必要」的类比主张不同。If you lie in bed for eight hours, you may have rested, but you can still feel exhausted the next day. That's because rest and recovery are not the same thing.
questions.quote: Our brains need a rest as much as our bodies do.

questions.prompt: Adequate rest not only helps one recover, but also increases one's work efficiency.
questions.explanation:
**答案** L 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
充分的休息不仅有助于恢复,还能提高工作效率。
**锚点** rest 同时 recover + raise efficiency
**定位** 把你所有的带薪假都休完，这不仅能给你恢复期，还能提升你的效率和升职可能。
**改写** Adequate rest ↔ Take all of your paid time off抽象 ↔ 具体的概括关系helps one recover ↔ gives you recovery periods动词 recover ↔ 名词 recovery periods increases one's work efficiency ↔ raises your productivity increase ↔ raise、efficiency ↔ productivity
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
D D 段说 $62 billion a year in lost productivity，是从反面讲「恢复不足导致生产力损失」，未正向陈述「充足休息会带来恢复 + 效率提升」的双重效应。lack of recovery K K 段聚焦 strategically stopping，给出的是 Instant/Moment、Offtime/Unplugged 等具体工具，并没有陈述「足够休息提升 productivity」这一双重效应。Give yourself the resources to be tough by creating internal and external recovery periods
questions.quote: Take all of your paid time off, which not only gives you recovery periods, but raises your productivity and likelihood of promotion.

questions.prompt: The author always has a hectic time before taking a flight.
questions.explanation:
**答案** A 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
作者在乘飞机前总是忙得不可开交。
**锚点** before taking a flight 的 hectic time
**定位** 我们在登机前马不停蹄地把所有地面工作搞定：打包、过安检、打最后一通工作电话、彼此通话，然后才登机。
**改写** hectic time ↔We race to get all our ground work done: packing, going through security, doing a last-minute work call, calling each other形容词概括 ↔ 动作清单具体化before taking a flight ↔ then boarding the plane时间范围对应
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
M M 段开篇 we've started using our plane time as a work-free zone，描述的是机上时段和下飞机后的恢复感，与陈述句限定的 before taking a flight 这一登机前时段不符。we've started using our plane time as a work-free zone
questions.quote: We race to get all our ground work done: packing, going through security, doing a last-minute work call, calling each other, then boarding the plane.

questions.prompt: Recovery may not take place even if one seems to have stopped working.
questions.explanation:
**答案** E 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
即使一个人看起来已经停止工作,恢复也可能不会发生。
**锚点** stopped working 但 recovery 未发生
**定位** 仅仅是工作停下了，并不意味着我们就在恢复。
**改写** Recovery may not take place ↔ it doesn't mean we are recovering may not ↔ doesn't mean 的含蓄否定对应even if one seems to have stopped working ↔ just because work stops even if ↔ just because 的让步对应
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
I I 段核心句 rest and recovery are not the same thing 谈的是「休息（如躺床）」与「恢复」的不等，陈述句 even if one seems to have stopped working 强调的是「停工」这一动作与恢复的不等，归宿应在 E 段。rest and recovery are not the same thing
questions.quote: And just because work stops, it doesn't mean we are recovering.

questions.prompt: It is advised that technology be used to prevent people from overworking.
questions.explanation:
**答案** K 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
建议利用技术手段来防止人们过度工作。
**锚点** technology 用来 prevent overworking
**定位** Amy Blankson 描述了如何利用技术控制过度工作，在白天有策略地停下来。
**改写** It is advised that technology be used to prevent people from overworking ↔Amy Blankson describes how to strategically stop during the day by using technology to control overworking被动建议 ↔ 主动方法 + prevent ↔ control
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
F F 段说 how technology extends our working hours，把 technology 视为加剧过劳的因素，而陈述句要求的是把 technology 当作 prevent overworking 的工具，方向相反。how technology extends our working hours and thus interferes with necessary cognitive recovery
questions.quote: Amy Blankson describes how to strategically stop during the day by using technology to control overworking.

questions.prompt: Contrary to popular belief, rest does not equal recovery.
questions.explanation:
**答案** I 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
与普遍看法相反,休息并不等于恢复。
**锚点** rest does not equal recovery
**定位** 那是因为休息和恢复不是一回事。
**改写** Contrary to popular belief ↔Most people assume that if you stop doing a task like answering emails or writing a paper, your brain will naturally recover「反大众认知」 ↔ 「大多数人以为」的对照rest does not equal recovery ↔ rest and recovery are not the same thing does not equal ↔ are not the same thing 的同义否定
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E E 段命题为 just because work stops, it doesn't mean we are recovering，对比对象是「停工 vs 恢复」；本题要求的是 rest does not equal recovery，对比对象是「休息 vs 恢复」。just because work stops, it doesn't mean we are recovering
questions.quote: That's because rest and recovery are not the same thing.

questions.prompt: The author has come to see that his problem results from a misunderstanding of the meaning of resilience.
questions.explanation:
**答案** B 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
作者逐渐认识到,他的问题源于对韧性含义的误解。
**锚点** author 自陈：误解 resilience 才是问题源头
**定位** 基于当前的研究，我们意识到：问题不在于繁忙的日程或飞行本身；问题在于对「具有复原力」含义的误解，以及由此产生的过度工作的影响。
**改写** has come to see that his problem results from a misunderstanding of the meaning of resilience ↔we have come to realize that the problem三组同义替换叠加
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
C C 段写 We often take a militaristic 与 this entire conception is scientifically inaccurate，描述的是大众错误观念，而陈述句要求的是「作者自己意识到」这一第一人称顿悟，归宿在 B 段的 we have come to realize。this entire conception is scientifically inaccurate
questions.quote: Based on our current research, we have come to realize that the problem is not our hectic schedule or the plane travel itself; the problem comes from a misconception of what it means to be resilient, and the resulting impact of overworking.

questions.prompt: People's distorted view about resilience may have developed from their upbringing.
questions.explanation:
**答案** G 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
人们对韧性的扭曲看法可能源自他们的成长经历。
**锚点** distorted view of resilience 源自 upbringing
**定位** 对复原力的误解往往是从小被培养出来的。
**改写** distorted view about resilience ↔ The misconception of resilience distorted view ↔ misconception developed from their upbringing ↔ bred from an early age developed ↔ bred、upbringing ↔ from an early age
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
C C 段只给出 a militaristic, "tough" approach to resilience 这一已成型的大众错觉，没有追溯到 bred from an early age 这一养育起源；本题答案锁在 G 段。a militaristic, "tough" approach to resilience
questions.quote: The misconception of resilience is often bred from an early age.

questions.prompt: People tend to think the more determined they are, the greater their success will be.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
人们往往认为自己越有决心,就会取得越大的成功。
**锚点** more determined → greater success 的大众信念
**定位** 我们相信：扛得越久就越硬气，因此也就越成功。
**改写** People tend to think ↔ We believe tend to think ↔ believe 的大众信念句对应the more determined they are, the greater their success will be ↔the longer we tough it out, the tougher we are, and therefore the more successful we will be determined ↔ tough it out / tougher，greater success ↔ more successful
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段说 we have come to realize that the problem 之后的归因句，这是作者反思的结论，而陈述句要求呈现的是大众尚未被反思的信念 the longer we tough it out, the tougher we are, and therefore the more successful we will be，归宿在 C 段。we have come to realize that the problem
questions.quote: We believe that the longer we tough it out, the tougher we are, and therefore the more successful we will be.

title: A Pioneering Woman of Science Re-Emerges after 300 Years

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Maria Sibylla Merian, like many European women of the 17th century, stayed busy managing a household and rearing children.
But on top of that, Merian, a German-born woman who lived in the Netherlands, also managed a successful career as an artist, botanist, naturalist and entomologist( 昆虫

passage.translation: 学家 ). Maria Sibylla Merian与17世纪许多欧洲女性一样,忙于操持家务和抚养子女。但除此之外,这位出生于德国、生活在荷兰的女性还成功地从事着艺术家、植物学家、博物学家和昆虫学家的职业。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: "She was a scientist on the level with a lot of people we spend a lot of time talking about," said Kay Etheridge, a biologist at Gettysburg College in Pennsylvania who has been studying the scientific history of Merian's work.
"She didn't do as much to change biology as Charles Darwin, but she was significant."

passage.translation: "她是一位科学家,其水平可与许多我们花大量时间讨论的人物相媲美,"宾夕法尼亚州葛底斯堡学院的生物学家Kay Etheridge说,她一直在研究Merian工作的科学史。"她对生物学的改变不及Charles Darwin那么大,但她的贡献是重要的。"

passage.label: C

sentences.text: At a time when natural history was a valuable tool for discovery, Merian discovered facts about plants and insects that were not previously known.
Her observations helped dismiss the popular belief that insects spontaneously emerged from mud.
The knowledge she collected over decades didn't just satisfy those curious about nature, but also provided valuable insights into medicine and science.
She was the first to bring together insects and their habitats, including food they ate, into a single ecological composition.

passage.translation: 在自然史是一种宝贵的发现工具的时代,Merian发现了关于植物和昆虫的前所未知的事实。她的观察帮助驳斥了昆虫从泥土中自然产生这一流行观念。她数十年间收集的知识不仅满足了那些对自然好奇的人,还为医学和科学提供了宝贵的见解。她是第一个将昆虫及其栖息地(包括它们的食物)整合到单一生态构图中的人。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: After years of pleasing a fascinated audience across Europe with books of detailed descriptions and life-size paintings of familiar insects, in 1699 she sailed with her daughter nearly 5,000 miles from the Netherlands to South America to study insects in the jungles of what is now known as Suriname.
She was 52 years old.
The result was her masterpiece, Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium.

passage.translation: 在用详细描述和真实尺寸的常见昆虫绘画取悦欧洲各地着迷的观众多年之后,1699年她与女儿从荷兰航行近5000英里到达南美洲,研究现今称为苏里南的丛林中的昆虫。当时她52岁。其成果是她的杰作《苏里南昆虫变态》。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: In her work, she revealed a side of nature so exotic, dramatic and valuable to Europeans of the time that she received much acclaim.
But a century later, her findings came under scientific criticism.
Shoddy(粗糙的) reproductions of her work along with setbacks to women's roles in 18th- and 19th- century Europe resulted in her efforts being largely forgotten.
"It was kind of stunning when she sort of dropped off into oblivion(遗忘)," said Dr.
Etheridge.
"Victorians started putting women in a box, and they're still trying to crawl out of it."

passage.translation: 在她的作品中,她揭示了自然界如此奇异、戏剧性且对当时欧洲人如此宝贵的一面,因而获得了广泛赞誉。但一个世纪后,她的发现受到了科学批评。她作品的粗糙复制品,加上18、19世纪欧洲女性角色的倒退,导致她的努力在很大程度上被遗忘。"当她逐渐被遗忘时,这有点令人震惊,"Etheridge博士说。"维多利亚时代的人开始把女性限制在一个框架里,而她们至今仍在努力挣脱出来。"

passage.label: F

sentences.text: Today, the pioneering woman of the sciences has re-emerged.
In recent years, feminists, historians and artists have all praised Merian's tenacity(坚韧), talent and inspirational artistic compositions.
And now biologists like Dr.
Etheridge are digging into the scientific texts that accompanied her art.
Three hundred years after her death, Merian will be celebrated at an international symposium in Amsterdam this June.

passage.translation: 今天,这位科学界的先驱女性重新出现。近年来,女权主义者、历史学家和艺术家都赞扬了Merian的坚韧、才华和富有启发性的艺术构图。现在像Etheridge博士这样的生物学家正在深入研究伴随她艺术作品的科学文本。在她去世300年后,今年6月Merian将在阿姆斯特丹的一场国际研讨会上受到纪念。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: And last month, Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium was republished.
It contains 60 plates(插图) and original descriptions, along with stories about Merian's life and updated scientific descriptions.
Before writing Metamorphosis, Merian spent decades documenting European plants and insects that she published in a series of books.
She began in her 20s, making textless, decorative paintings of flowers with insects.
"Then she got really serious," Dr.
Etheridge said.
Merian started raising insects at home, mostly butterflies and caterpillars.
"She would sit up all night until they came out of the pupa(蛹) so she could draw them," she said.

passage.translation: 上个月,《苏里南昆虫变态》再版了。它包含60幅插图和原始描述,以及关于Merian生平的故事和更新的科学描述。在撰写《变态》之前,Merian花了数十年记录欧洲植物和昆虫,并以一系列书籍出版。她从20多岁开始,绘制无文字的、装饰性的花卉与昆虫画作。"然后她变得真正认真起来,"Etheridge博士说。Merian开始在家饲养昆虫,主要是蝴蝶和毛虫。"她会整夜不睡,直到它们从蛹中出来,这样她就能画下它们,"她说。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: The results of her decades' worth of careful observations were detailed paintings and descriptions of European insects, followed by unconventional visuals and stories of insects and animals from a land that most at the time could only imagine.
It's possible Merian used a magnifying glass to capture the detail of the split tongues of sphinx moths(斯芬克斯⻜蛾) depicted in the painting.
She wrote that the two tongues combine to form one tube for drinking nectar(花蜜).
Some criticized this detail later, saying there was just one tongue, but Merian wasn't wrong.
She may have observed the adult moth just as it emerged from its pupa.
For a brief moment during that stage of its life cycle, the tongue consists of two tiny half-tubes before merging into one.

passage.translation: 她数十年细致观察的成果是对欧洲昆虫的详细绘画和描述,随后是关于一片大多数当时人只能想象的土地上的昆虫和动物的非传统视觉作品和故事。Merian可能使用了放大镜来捕捉画作中描绘的斯芬克斯飞蛾分叉舌头的细节。她写道,两条舌头结合形成一根管子来吸食花蜜。一些人后来批评这一细节,说只有一条舌头,但Merian并没有错。她可能观察到了成年飞蛾刚从蛹中羽化的时刻。在其生命周期的那个短暂阶段,舌头由两条微小的半管组成,之后才合并成一条。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: It may not have been ladylike to depict a giant spider devouring a hummingbird, but when Merian did it at the turn of the 18th century, surprisingly, nobody objected.
Dr.
Etheridge called it revolutionary.

The image, which also contained novel descriptions of ants, fascinated a European audience that was more concerned with the exotic story unfolding before them than the gender of the person who painted it.

passage.translation: 描绘一只巨型蜘蛛吞食蜂鸟可能不符合淑女风范,但当Merian在18世纪之交这样做时,令人惊讶的是,没有人反对。Etheridge博士称其具有革命性。这幅图像还包含了关于蚂蚁的新颖描述,令欧洲观众着迷,他们更关心在他们面前展开的异国故事,而不是绘制它的人的性别。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: "All of these things shook up their nice, neat little view," Dr.
Etheridge said.
But later, people of the Victorian era thought differently.
Her work had been reproduced, sometimes incorrectly.
A few observations were deemed impossible.
"She'd been called a silly woman for saying that a spider could eat a bird," Dr.
Etheridge said.
But Henry Walter Bates, a friend of Charles Darwin, observed it and put it in a book in 1863, proving Merian was correct.

passage.translation: "所有这些事情动摇了他们美好、整洁的小世界观,"Etheridge博士说。但后来,维多利亚时代的人有不同的看法。她的作品被复制,有时不准确。一些观察被认为是不可能的。"她因说蜘蛛可以吃鸟而被称为愚蠢的女人,"Etheridge博士说。但Charles Darwin的朋友Henry Walter Bates观察到了这一现象,并在1863年将其写入一本书中,证明Merian是正确的。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: In the same plate, Merian depicted and described leaf-cutter ants for the first time.
"In America there are large ants which can eat whole trees bare as a broom handle in a single night," she wrote in the description.
Merian noted how the ants took the leaves below ground to their young.
And she wouldn't have known this at the time, but the ants use the leaves to farm fungi(菌类) underground to feed their developing babies.

passage.translation: 在同一幅插图中,Merian首次描绘和描述了切叶蚁。"在美洲有大型蚂蚁,它们能在一夜之间把整棵树啃得像扫帚把一样光秃,"她在描述中写道。Merian注意到蚂蚁如何将叶子带到地下给它们的幼虫。她当时不可能知道这一点,但蚂蚁用叶子在地下培育菌类来喂养它们发育中的幼体。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: Merian was correct about the giant bird-eating spiders, ants building bridges with their bodies and other details.
But in the same drawing, she incorrectly lumped together army and leaf-cutter ants.
And instead of showing just the typical pair of eggs in a hummingbird nest, she painted four.
She made other mistakes in Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium as well: not every caterpillar and butterfly matched.

passage.translation: Merian关于巨型食鸟蜘蛛、用身体搭桥的蚂蚁和其他细节的描述是正确的。但在同一幅画中,她错误地将行军蚁和切叶蚁混为一谈。她没有只画蜂鸟巢中典型的一对卵,而是画了四个。她在《苏里南昆虫变态》中还犯了其他错误:并非每只毛虫和蝴蝶都匹配。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: Perhaps one explanation for her mistakes is that she cut short her Suriname trip after getting sick, and completed the book at home in Amsterdam.
And errors are common among some of history's most-celebrated scientific minds, too.
"These errors no more invalidate Ms.
Merian's work than do well-known misconceptions published by Charles Darwin or Isaac Newton," Dr.
Etheridge wrote in a paper that argued that too many have wrongly focused on the mistakes of her work.

passage.translation: 也许对她错误的一个解释是,她因生病而缩短了苏里南之行,并在阿姆斯特丹的家中完成了这本书。而且错误在一些历史上最著名的科学头脑中也很常见。"这些错误并不比Charles Darwin或Isaac Newton发表的众所周知的错误概念更能使Merian女士的工作失效,"Etheridge博士在一篇论文中写道,该论文认为太多人错误地关注了她作品中的错误。

passage.label: N

sentences.text: Merian's paintings inspired artists and ecologists.

In an 1801 drawing from his book, General Zoology Amphibia, George Shaw, an English botanist and zoologist, credited Merian for describing a frog in the account of her South American expedition, and named the young tree frog after her in his portrayal of it.
It wouldn't be fair to give Merian all the credit.
She received assistance naming plants, making sketches and referencing the work of others.
Her daughters helped her color her drawings.

passage.translation: Merian的绘画启发了艺术家和生态学家。在他的著作《两栖类总动物学》的1801年绘图中,英国植物学家和动物学家George Shaw称赞Merian在她的南美探险记录中描述了一种青蛙,并在他对它的描绘中以她的名字命名了这种幼年树蛙。将所有功劳归于Merian是不公平的。她在命名植物、绘制草图和参考他人的工作方面得到了帮助。她的女儿们帮助她给画作上色。

passage.label: O

sentences.text: Merian also made note of the help she received from the natives of Suriname, as well as slaves or servants that assisted her.
In some instances she wrote moving passages that included her helpers in descriptions.

As she wrote in her description of the peacock flower, "The Indians, who are not treated well by their Dutch masters, use the seeds to abort their children, so that they will not become slaves like themselves.
The black slaves from Guinea and Angola have demanded to be well treated, threatening to refuse to have children.
In fact, they sometimes take their own lives because they are treated so badly, and because they believe they will be born again, free and living in their own land.
They told me this themselves."

passage.translation: Merian还记录了她从苏里南当地人以及协助她的奴隶或仆人那里获得的帮助。在某些情况下,她写下了动人的段落,在描述中包括了她的助手。正如她在对孔雀花的描述中所写:"印第安人没有得到荷兰主人的善待,他们用这种种子堕掉自己的孩子,这样他们就不会像自己一样成为奴隶。来自几内亚和安哥拉的黑奴要求得到善待,威胁拒绝生育。事实上,他们有时会自杀,因为他们受到如此恶劣的对待,并且因为他们相信自己会重生,自由地生活在自己的土地上。他们亲口告诉我这些。"

passage.label: P

sentences.text: Londa Schiebinger, a professor of the history of science at Stanford University, called this passage rather astonishing.
It's particularly striking centuries later when these issues are still prominent in public discussions about social justice and women's rights.
"She was ahead of her time," Dr.
Etheridge said.

passage.translation: 斯坦福大学科学史教授Londa Schiebinger称这段话相当令人震惊。几个世纪后,当这些问题在关于社会正义和妇女权利的公共讨论中仍然突出时,这段话尤其引人注目。"她超越了她的时代,"Etheridge博士说。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: Merian was the first scientist to study a type of American ant.
questions.explanation:
**答案** K 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
Merian是第一位研究某种美洲蚂蚁的科学家。
**锚点** 首次研究某种美洲蚂蚁
**定位** 在同一张插图里，Merian 首次描绘并描述了切叶蚁。她在描述中写道：“在美洲，有一种大蚂蚁能在一夜之间把整棵树啃得像扫帚柄一样光秃。”
**改写** the first scientist to study ↔ depicted and described leaf-cutter ants for the first time first 同义还原a type of American ant ↔ In America there are large ants 与 leaf-cutter ants上位 → 下位 + 地点同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
L L 段确实出现 army and leaf-cutter ants，但说的是“她错把行军蚁和切叶蚁混在一起”，对应的是题干 Q43“偶有错误”，不是 Q36“首次研究”。incorrectly lumped together army and leaf-cutter ants
questions.quote: In the same plate, Merian depicted and described leaf-cutter ants for the first time. "In America there are large ants which can eat whole trees bare as a broom handle in a single night," she wrote in the description.

questions.prompt: The European audience was more interested in Merian's drawings than her gender.
questions.explanation:
**答案** I 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
欧洲观众对Merian的绘画作品比对她的性别更感兴趣。
**锚点** 更关心画作而非性别
**定位** 这幅画还附有对蚂蚁的新颖描述，让欧洲读者深为着迷——他们更关心眼前展开的异域故事，而不是画家本人的性别。
**改写** more interested in ↔ more concerned with情感动词同义替换Merian's drawings ↔ the exotic story unfolding before them指代同一对象her gender ↔ the gender of the person who painted it代词 her 还原成定语从句
questions.quote: The image, which also contained novel descriptions of ants, fascinated a European audience that was more concerned with the exotic story unfolding before them than the gender of the person who painted it.

questions.prompt: Merian's masterpiece came under attack a century after its publication.
questions.explanation:
**答案** E 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
Merian的杰作在出版一个世纪后遭到了批评。
**锚点** 出版一个世纪后遭攻击
**定位** 在她的作品中，她揭示了大自然如此奇异、戏剧化且对当时欧洲人极有价值的一面，使她广受赞誉。但一个世纪后，她的研究发现遭到了科学界的批评。
**改写** came under attack ↔ came under scientific criticism attack ↔ criticism 同义替换a century after its publication ↔ a century later时间状语同义替换Merian's masterpiece ↔ her findings代表作 ↔ 研究发现
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
J J 段确实写到她被骂 silly woman 以及 Henry Walter Bates...in a book in 1863 翻案，但它是 E 段“百年后受攻击”这件事的延伸细节，不是“作品受攻击”这一事件的首次陈述句；题干问的是“何时遭攻击”的首次表述，所以源头段在 E。She'd been called a silly woman for saying that a spider could eat a bird
questions.quote: In her work, she revealed a side of nature so exotic, dramatic and valuable to Europeans of the time that she received much acclaim. But a century later, her findings came under scientific criticism.

questions.prompt: Merian's mistakes in her drawings may be attributed to her shortened stay in South America.
questions.explanation:
**答案** M 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
Merian绘画中的错误可能归因于她在南美洲停留时间缩短。
**锚点** 缩短南美停留导致出错
**定位** 也许她出错的一个解释是：她因病提前结束了苏里南之行，并回到阿姆斯特丹家中完成了这本书。

questions.tip:
**辨邻**
L L 段把 incorrectly lumped together army and leaf-cutter ants、she painted four、not every caterpillar and butterfly matched 一一列出，但完全没解释“为什么”，归因解释在下一段 M 才出现。Merian was correct about the giant bird-eating spiders, ants building bridges with their bodies and other details. But in the same drawing, she incorrectly lumped together army and leaf-cutter ants.
questions.quote: Perhaps one explanation for her mistakes is that she cut short her Suriname trip after getting sick, and completed the book at home in Amsterdam.

questions.prompt: Merian often sat up the whole night through to observe and draw insects.
questions.explanation:
**答案** G 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
Merian经常彻夜不眠地观察和绘制昆虫。
**锚点** 通宵观察绘画
**定位** 她常常彻夜守候，直到蝴蝶、毛毛虫破蛹而出，好趁机把它们画下来。
**改写** sat up the whole night through ↔ sit up all night短语同义to observe and draw insects ↔ until they came out of the pupa so she could draw them动作流程映射
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
H H 段写 The results of her decades' worth of careful observations were detailed paintings and descriptions，强调成果与可能借助 a magnifying glass 的细节，未提“通宵守候”这一工作方式，不承担 Q40 的“通宵 + 画”。The results of her decades' worth of careful observations were detailed paintings and descriptions of European insects
questions.quote: She would sit up all night until they came out of the pupa so she could draw them.

questions.prompt: Merian acknowledged the help she got from natives of South America.
questions.explanation:
**答案** O 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
Merian对她从南美洲当地人那里得到的帮助表示了感谢。
**锚点** 致谢南美原住民
**定位** Merian 还专门记下了她从苏里南原住民那里得到的帮助，以及奴隶或仆人对她的协助。
**改写** acknowledged the help ↔ made note of the help短语同义natives of South America ↔ the natives of Suriname地名上下位
questions.tip:
