N N 段写 She received assistance naming plants, making sketches and referencing the work of others. Her daughters helped her color her drawings，致谢对象是合作者与女儿，不是 natives；题干指明“原住民”，源头段必须在 O。She received assistance naming plants, making sketches and referencing the work of others. Her daughters helped her color her drawings.
questions.quote: Merian also made note of the help she received from the natives of Suriname, as well as slaves or servants that assisted her.

questions.prompt: Merian contributed greatly to people's better understanding of medicine and science.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
Merian为人们更好地理解医学和科学做出了巨大贡献。
**锚点** 促进对医学与科学的理解
**定位** 她数十年间收集的知识不仅满足了那些对自然好奇的人，还为医学和科学提供了有价值的洞见。
**改写** contributed greatly to ↔ provided valuable insights into贡献动词同义people's better understanding of medicine and science ↔valuable insights into medicine and science名词化等值
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段 She didn't do as much to change biology as Charles Darwin, but she was significant 是把她放进科学家序列做对标评价，未提“医学与科学”的具体贡献，无法承担 Q42 的“促进医学与科学理解”。She didn't do as much to change biology as Charles Darwin, but she was significant
questions.quote: The knowledge she collected over decades didn't just satisfy those curious about nature, but also provided valuable insights into medicine and science.

questions.prompt: Merian occasionally made mistakes in her drawings of insects and birds.
questions.explanation:
**答案** L 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
Merian在绘制昆虫和鸟类时偶尔会犯错误。
**锚点** 昆虫与鸟的绘画偶有错
**定位** 但是在同一张画里，她错误地把行军蚁和切叶蚁混在一起。她没有画一窝两枚的典型蜂鸟蛋数量，而是画了四枚。她在《苏里南昆虫变态》里还犯过其他错误：并不是每条毛毛虫都和对应的蝴蝶相配。
**改写** occasionally made mistakes in her drawings ↔she incorrectly lumped together army and leaf-cutter ants 与 She made other mistakes in Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium as well副词 ↔ 错误清单insects and birds ↔ ants 与 in a hummingbird nest上位 ↔ 下位双指代
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
M M 段 she cut short her Suriname trip after getting sick, and completed the book at home in Amsterdam 解释错的成因，并把她错误与达尔文、牛顿做比较，但具体错处罗列在 L 段；问“哪儿画错”必须落在 L。These errors no more invalidate Ms. Merian's work than do well-known misconceptions published by Charles Darwin or Isaac Newton H H 段 Some criticized this detail later, saying there was just one tongue, but Merian wasn't wrong 是她被误批但其实正确的故事，与“偶有犯错”方向相反。Some criticized this detail later, saying there was just one tongue, but Merian wasn't wrong.
questions.quote: But in the same drawing, she incorrectly lumped together army and leaf-cutter ants. And instead of showing just the typical pair of eggs in a hummingbird nest, she painted four. She made other mistakes in Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium as well: not every caterpillar and butterfly matched.

questions.prompt: Now, Merian's role as a female forerunner in sciences has been re-established.
questions.explanation:
**答案** F 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
现在,Merian作为科学界女性先驱的角色已经得到重新确立。
**锚点** 女性先驱地位被重新确立
**定位** 今天，这位科学领域的女性先驱已经重新浮现。
**改写** Now ↔ Today时间副词同义a female forerunner in sciences ↔ the pioneering woman of the sciences同义短语has been re-established ↔ has re-emerged前缀 re- 共享
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段 She was a scientist on the level with a lot of people we spend a lot of time talking about 是肯定她的地位评价，缺少“先被遗忘 → 现在被重新确立”的时间转折。She was a scientist on the level with a lot of people we spend a lot of time talking about
questions.quote: Today, the pioneering woman of the sciences has re-emerged.

questions.prompt: Merian made a long voyage to South America to study jungle insects over three centuries ago.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
三个多世纪以前,Merian进行了一次前往南美洲的长途航行以研究丛林昆虫。
**锚点** 三百多年前远航南美研究昆虫
**定位** 在多年以详尽描述与等大昆虫画作取悦痴迷的欧洲读者之后，1699 年她带着女儿从荷兰航行近 5000 英里来到南美，在今天被称为苏里南的丛林里研究昆虫。
**改写** made a long voyage to South America ↔she sailed with her daughter nearly 5,000 miles from the Netherlands to South America名 ↔ 动 + 量级to study jungle insects ↔ to study insects in the jungles定语前后置等值over three centuries ago ↔ in 1699年份反算成相对时间
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
M M 段 she cut short her Suriname trip after getting sick 讲的是这次远航被缩短，不是“启程远航”的事件本体；远航这一动作本身的源头在 D。she cut short her Suriname trip after getting sick, and completed the book at home in Amsterdam
questions.quote: After years of pleasing a fascinated audience across Europe with books of detailed descriptions and life-size paintings of familiar insects, in 1699 she sailed with her daughter nearly 5,000 miles from the Netherlands to South America to study insects in the jungles of what is now known as Suriname.

title: Do Parents Invade Children's Privacy When They Post Photos Online?

passage.label: A

sentences.text: When Katlyn Burbidge's son was 6 years old, he was performing some ridiculous song and dance typical of a first-grader.
But after she snapped a photo and started using her phone, he asked her a serious question: "Are you going to post that online?"
She laughed and answered, "Yes, I think I will."
What he said next stopped her.
"Can you not?"

passage.translation: 当Katlyn Burbidge的儿子6岁时,他正在表演一些一年级学生典型的滑稽歌舞。但在她拍下一张照片并开始使用手机后,他问了她一个严肃的问题:"你要把那个发到网上吗?"她笑着回答:"是的,我想我会的。"他接下来说的话让她停了下来。"你能不发吗?"

passage.label: B

sentences.text: That's when it dawned on her: She had been posting photos of him online without asking his permission.

"We're big advocates of bodily autonomy and not forcing him to hug or kiss people unless he wants to, but it never occurred to me that I should ask his permission to post photos of him online," says Burbidge, a mom of two in Wakefield, Massachusetts.
"Now when I post a photo of him online, I show him the photo and get his okay."

passage.translation: 就在那时她恍然大悟:她一直在未经他允许的情况下在网上发布他的照片。"我们大力提倡身体自主权,不强迫他去拥抱或亲吻别人,除非他自己愿意,但我从未想过应该征得他的同意才能在网上发布他的照片,"这位来自马萨诸塞州Wakefield的两个孩子的母亲Burbidge说。"现在当我在网上发布他的照片时,我会给他看照片并征得他的同意。"

passage.label: C

sentences.text: When her 8-month-old is 3 or 4 years old, she plans to start asking him in an age-appropriate way, "Do you want other people to see this?"

That's precisely the approach that two researchers advocated before a room of pediatricians(儿科医生) last week at the American Academy of Pediatrics meeting, when they discussed the 21st century challenge of "sharenting," a new term for parents' online sharing about their children.

"As advocates of children's rights, we believe that children should have a voice about what information is shared about them if possible," says Stacey Steinberg, a legal skills professor at the University of Florida Levin College of Law in Gainesville.

passage.translation: 当她8个月大的孩子长到3或4岁时,她计划开始以适合年龄的方式问他:"你想让其他人看到这个吗?"这正是两位研究人员上周在美国儿科学会会议上向一屋子儿科医生所倡导的方法,当时他们讨论了21世纪"晒娃"这一挑战——这是父母在网上分享孩子信息的一个新术语。"作为儿童权利的倡导者,我们认为如果可能的话,儿童应该对分享有关他们的信息拥有发言权,"Gainesville佛罗里达大学Levin法学院法律技能教授Stacey Steinberg说。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: Whether it's ensuring that your child isn't bullied over something you post, that their identity isn't digitally "kidnapped", or that their photos don't end up on a half dozen child pornography(色情) sites, as one Australian mom discovered, parents and pediatricians are increasingly aware of the importance of protecting children's digital presence.

Steinberg and Bahareh Keith, an assistant professor of pediatrics at the University of Florida College of Medicine, say most children will likely never experience problems related to what their parents share, but a tension still exists between parents' rights to share their experiences and their children's rights to privacy.

passage.translation: 无论是确保你的孩子不会因为你发布的内容而被欺凌,他们的身份不会被数字"绑架",还是他们的照片不会出现在六个儿童色情网站上——正如一位澳大利亚母亲发现的那样,家长和儿科医生越来越意识到保护儿童数字形象的重要性。Steinberg和佛罗里达大学医学院儿科助理教授Bahareh Keith表示,大多数儿童可能永远不会遇到与父母分享内容相关的问题,但父母分享自身经历的权利与儿童隐私权之间仍然存在紧张关系。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: "We're in no way trying to silence parents' voices," Steinberg says.
"At the same time, we recognize that children might have an interest in entering adulthood free to create their own digital footprint."
They cited a study presented earlier this year of 249 pairs of parents and their children in which twice as many children as parents wanted rules on what parents could share.
"The parents said, 'We don't need rules—we're fine,' and the children said, 'Our parents need rules,'" Keith says.
"The children wanted autonomy about this issue and were worried about their parents sharing information about them."

passage.translation: "我们绝不是要让父母噤声,"Steinberg说。"与此同时,我们认识到儿童可能有兴趣在进入成年后自由创建自己的数字足迹。"他们引用了今年早些时候发表的一项研究,该研究涉及249对父母及其子女,其中希望对父母可以分享什么制定规则的儿童数量是父母的两倍。"父母说,'我们不需要规则——我们很好',而孩子说,'我们的父母需要规则,'"Keith说。"孩子们希望在这个问题上拥有自主权,并担心父母分享有关他们的信息。"

passage.label: F

sentences.text: Although the American Academy of Pediatrics offers guidelines recommending that parents model appropriate social media use for their children, it does not explicitly discuss oversharing by parents.
"I think this is a very legitimate concern, and I appreciate their drawing our attention to it," David Hill, a father of five, says.
He sees a role for pediatricians to talk with parents about this, but believes the messaging must extend far beyond pediatricians' offices.
"I look forward to seeing researchers expand our understanding of the issue so we can translate it into effective education and policy," he says.

passage.translation: 尽管美国儿科学会提供了建议父母为孩子示范适当社交媒体使用的指南,但它并未明确讨论父母过度分享的问题。"我认为这是一个非常合理的担忧,我感谢他们引起我们对此的关注,"五个孩子的父亲David Hill说。他认为儿科医生可以在这方面与父母交流,但相信信息传递必须远远超出儿科医生诊所的范围。"我期待看到研究人员扩大我们对这个问题的理解,这样我们就可以将其转化为有效的教育和政策,"他说。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: There's been little research on the topic, Steinberg wrote in a law article about this issue.
While states could pass laws related to sharing information about children online, Steinberg feels parents themselves are generally best suited to make these decisions for their families.

"While we didn't want to create any unnecessary panic, we did find some concerns that were troublesome, and we thought that parents or at least physicians should be aware of those potential risks," Steinberg says.
They include photos repurposed for inappropriate or illegal means, identity theft, embarrassment, bullying by peers or digital kidnapping.

passage.translation: 关于这个话题的研究很少,Steinberg在一篇关于这个问题的法律文章中写道。虽然各州可以通过与在网上分享儿童信息相关的法律,但Steinberg认为父母自己通常最适合为他们的家庭做出这些决定。"虽然我们不想制造任何不必要的恐慌,但我们确实发现了一些令人担忧的问题,我们认为父母或至少医生应该意识到这些潜在风险,"Steinberg说。这些风险包括照片被挪作不当或非法用途、身份盗窃、尴尬、同伴欺凌或数字绑架。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: But that's the negative side, with risks that must be balanced against the benefits of sharing.

Steinberg pointed out that parental sharing on social media helps build communities, connect spread- out families, provide support and raise awareness around important social issues for which parents might be their children's only voice.

passage.translation: 但这是负面的一面,必须在风险与分享的好处之间取得平衡。Steinberg指出,父母在社交媒体上的分享有助于建立社区、连接分散的家庭、提供支持,并提高人们对重要社会问题的认识,而在这些问题上父母可能是孩子唯一的代言人。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: A C.S.

Mott survey found among the 56 percent of mothers and 34 percent of fathers who discussed parenting on social media, 72 percent of them said sharing made them feel less alone, and nearly as many said sharing helped them worry less and gave them advice from other parents.
The most common topics they discussed included kids' sleep, nutrition, discipline, behavior problems and day care and preschool.

passage.translation: C.S. Mott调查发现,在56%的母亲和34%的父亲在社交媒体上讨论育儿问题的人中,72%的人表示分享让他们感到不那么孤单,几乎同样多的人表示分享帮助他们减少担忧,并从其他父母那里获得建议。他们讨论的最常见话题包括孩子的睡眠、营养、纪律、行为问题以及日托和学前教育。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: "There's this peer-to-peer nature of health care these days with a profound opportunity for parents to learn helpful tips, safety and prevention efforts, pro-vaccine messages and all kinds of other messages from other parents in their social communities," says Wendy Sue Swanson, a pediatrician and executive director of digital health at Seattle Children's Hospital, where she blogs about her own parenting journey to help other parents.
"They're getting nurtured by people they've already selected that they trust," she says.

passage.translation: "如今医疗保健存在这种点对点的性质,为父母提供了学习有用建议、安全和预防措施、支持疫苗信息以及来自其社交社区中其他父母的各种其他信息的深刻机会,"西雅图儿童医院儿科医生兼数字健康执行主任Wendy Sue Swanson说,她在那里撰写关于自己育儿历程的博客以帮助其他父母。"他们正在从他们已经选择的、他们信任的人那里获得关怀,"她说。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: "How do we weigh the risks, how do we think about the benefits, and how do we alleviate the risks?" she says.
"Those are the questions we need to ask ourselves, and everyone can have a different answer."

passage.translation: "我们如何权衡风险,我们如何思考好处,我们如何减轻风险?"她说。"这些是我们需要问自己的问题,每个人都可以有不同的答案。"

passage.label: L

sentences.text: Some parents find the best route for them is not to share at all.
Bridget O'Hanlon and her husband, who live in Cleveland, decided before their daughter was born that they would not post her photos online.
When a few family members did post pictures, O'Hanlon and her husband made their wishes clear.

"It's been hard not to share pictures of her because people always want to know how babies and toddlers(学走路的孩子) are doing and to see pictures, but we made the decision to have social media while she did not," O'Hanlon said.
Similarly, Alison Jamison of New York decided with her husband that their child had a right to their own online identity.

They did use an invitation-only photo sharing platform so that friends and family, including those far away, could see the photos, but they stood firm, simply refusing to put their child's photos on other social media platforms.

passage.translation: 一些父母发现对他们来说最好的方式是根本不分享。住在克利夫兰的Bridget O'Hanlon和她的丈夫在女儿出生前就决定不会在网上发布她的照片。当一些家庭成员确实发布了照片时,O'Hanlon和她的丈夫明确表达了他们的意愿。"不分享她的照片一直很难,因为人们总是想知道婴儿和学走路的孩子的情况并看照片,但我们做出了使用社交媒体而她没有的决定,"O'Hanlon说。同样,纽约的Alison Jamison与丈夫决定他们的孩子有权拥有自己的网络身份。他们确实使用了仅限邀请的照片分享平台,以便朋友和家人(包括远方的)可以看到照片,但他们立场坚定,坚决拒绝将孩子的照片放在其他社交媒体平台上。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: "For most families, it's a journey.
Sometimes it goes wrong, but most of the time it doesn't," says Swanson, who recommends starting to ask children permission to post narratives or photos around ages 6 to 8.
"We'll learn more and more what our tolerance is.
We can ask our kids to help us learn as a society what's okay and what's not."

passage.translation: "对大多数家庭来说,这是一个过程。有时会出错,但大多数时候不会,"Swanson说,她建议在孩子6到8岁左右开始征求他们的许可来发布叙述或照片。"我们会越来越多地了解我们的容忍度。我们可以请我们的孩子帮助我们作为一个社会学习什么是可以的,什么是不可以的。"

passage.label: N

sentences.text: Indeed, that learning process goes both ways.
Bria Dunham, a mother in Somerville, Massachusetts, was so excited to watch a moment of brotherly bonding while her first-grader and baby took a bath together that she snapped a few photos.
But when she considered posting them online, she took the perspective of her son: How would he feel if his classmates' parents saw photos of him chest-up in the bathtub?
"It made me think about how I'm teaching him to have ownership of his own body and how what is shared today endures into the future," Dunham says.
"So I kept the pictures to myself and accepted this as one more step in supporting his increasing autonomy."

passage.translation: 事实上,这个学习过程是双向的。马萨诸塞州Somerville的母亲Bria Dunham在看到她的一年级孩子和婴儿一起洗澡时的兄弟情谊时刻时非常兴奋,以至于她拍了几张照片。但当她考虑将它们发布到网上时,她站在儿子的角度思考:如果他同学的父母看到他上半身在浴缸里的照片,他会有什么感受?"这让我思考我如何教他对自己的身体拥有所有权,以及今天分享的内容如何延续到未来,"Dunham说。"所以我把照片留给了自己,并接受这是支持他日益增长的自主权的又一步。"
