versatile
obsessed

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) reputed 形容词
**词性槽** 名词 woman 后修饰，且后接 for 引导短语
**依据** 「被认为(创作了它)的那位女性」be reputed for / reputed for 表「以……著称、被认为(做了)……」，与前文 Did Sarah Josepha Hale write “Mary’s Little Lamb” ... This is still disputed 的「作者归属存疑」氛围完全契合——她是「被认为创作了这首诗」的女性。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) supposed 搭配偏好不同 + 留给 28 题更贴supposed 多用作前置定语（如 the supposed author）表「所谓的、据称的」，与 for writing it 的后置搭配不及 reputed 自然；而 28 题正缺一个修饰 author 的前置形容词，supposed author 在此搭配更紧。坚持 M 反而占掉 28 题的最佳答案。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 M) —— supposed 与 reputed 义近，易抢答 M。考生若按词义「两者都通」匆忙选 M，会同时挤掉 28 题最合适的 supposed。防坑法：看句法位置——后置 + for 短语用 reputed，前置定语用 supposed。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) characters 名词
**词性槽** America’s most fascinating ___ 中所有格 + 形容词最高级后缺名词，且需复数
**依据** 「人物」才与「woman/fascinating」对位前文 the woman __(26)__ for writing it was one of America’s most fascinating __(27)__——主语是 the woman（人），one of 之后的复数名词指代同类（人），character 表「人物」恰合：「美国最迷人的人物之一」。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
D) features对象错位features 表「特征/特色」或「专题报道」，描述的是「事物/抽象属性」而非「人」；与主语the woman 的同类指代不能对位。

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) supposed 形容词
**词性槽** the 与名词 author 之间的前置定语位
**依据** 「所谓的/据称的」作者——与争议主题呼应首句 Did Sarah Josepha Hale write “Mary’s Little Lamb” ... This is still disputed 已把「是否真为作者」立成悬念，此处再说 the __(28)__ author’s life 用 supposed 表「据称的作者」在语义上严丝合缝；the supposed author 是英文常见搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) latter需对照项latter 必须有「前者/后者」两项可对照，本句只提一人，搭配不成立。
O) versatile信息越界versatile 强调「多才多艺/多领域」，本段只在引入「作者生平」，尚未铺陈她的多面身份，把判断前置到这里属于过度推断；且要留给 29 题描述她「作家 + 社会倡导者」的多重身份。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 O) —— versatile author 看似合理，实为越界。the versatile author 形态正确、义看似通，但段落定调是「作者存疑」，应选 supposed。防坑法：让形容词色彩与本段首句的定调词对齐，再下笔。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) fierce 形容词
**词性槽** a 与名词 social advocate 之间作前置定语
**依据** 「强势/积极进取」的社会倡导者下一段交代 17 years of advocacy including letters to five presidents 的执着——这种坚定不移、激进游说的形象，正是 a fierce advocate（强势的倡导者）这一固定搭配的典型语境。

**答案** H) obsessed 形容词
**词性槽** was 之后、紧跟 with 短语，需作表语的过去分词形容词
**依据** be obsessed with 是固定搭配she was particularly __(30)__ with an ideal New England, which she associated with abundant Thanksgiving meals——下文用 abundant Thanksgiving meals 描绘她对「理想新英格兰」的痴迷，be obsessed with 表「痴迷于」恰好对位。

**答案** A) campaign 名词
**词性槽** begin 的宾语位置，前有 a 与形容词 nationwide
**依据** begin a nationwide campaign 是固定搭配She began a nationwide __(31)__ to have a national holiday declared 后文紧跟 17 years of advocacy including letters to five presidents，正是「发起一场全国性的游说运动」。begin/launch a campaign 是高频搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) career 义偏宽泛career 指「职业生涯」，与「为推动某节日设立而展开的具体运动」不对位，且无法与nationwide 自然搭配。
C) characters 复数且义不合characters 复数，与 a ___ 的单数框架冲突；「人物」也无法用 nationwide 修饰。
L) rest 义不搭rest 表「剩余/休息」，与「全国性运动」语义不符。

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) traditional 形容词
**词性槽** 定冠词 the 与名词 festivals 之间，缺定语
**依据** 与「感恩节」语境的「惯例节日」最贴上文交代 Hale 把理想的新英格兰与 abundant Thanksgiving meals 联系起来，再去bring families together while celebrating the __(32)__ festivals——感恩节正是美国「传统节日」，traditional festivals 是高频固定搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) fierce感情色彩冲突fierce 表「激烈/凶猛」，与「家人团聚庆祝节日」的温情语境正相反，不能修饰 festivals。
G) latter需「前后两者」对照才能用latter 通常指此前提到过的两者中的「后者」，本句并无两个对照项，语境不成立。
O) versatile义不搭versatile 多才多艺/多用途，用来形容人或工具，搭配 festivals 不成立。

questions.explanation:
**答案** I) proclamation 名词
**词性槽** 动词 issued 后缺宾语，且前有不定冠词 a
**依据** 总统发布的「公告/宣言」总统 issued a __(33)__ setting aside the last Thursday in November for the holiday 描述的正是林肯于 1863 年发布「感恩节公告」这一历史事实，issue a proclamation 是固定搭配：「发布公告」。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) career 语义不通issue a career 不成立，「职业」与「指定某天为节日」逻辑无关。
C) characters 单复数与词义双不合characters 复数，与 a ___ 的单数框架矛盾；且「人物/角色」无法与 issue 及「设节日」逻辑连起来。
L) rest义不搭issue a rest 不成立；rest 在此意为「剩余/休息」，与发布正式文件无关。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) inspired 动词
**词性槽** be 动词 was 之后、by 引出施事，被动语态需过去分词
**依据** 「由真实事件激发」才合逻辑下一句 When young Mary Sawyer was followed to school by a lamb in 1816, it caused some problems 正是给出「真实事件」的具体内容——一只小羊跟着玛丽去上学。这正是「这首诗由一桩真实事件所启发」。be inspired by 是固定搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
J) rectified 逻辑指向反rectify 意为「纠正错误」，「诗被一桩真实事件纠正」于义不通，且 be rectified by 在文学创作语境中不成立。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) rest 名词
**词性槽** for the ___ of her life 介词短语中、of 前缺名词
**依据** for the rest of her life 是固定短语Hale claimed for the __(35)__ of her life that “some other people pretended that someone else wrote the poem”——for the rest of her life 意为「在余生中」，正合「她终生都坚称作品是自己写的」这一语义。

title: Photography was once an expensive, laborious ordeal reserved…

sentences.text: Photography was once an expensive, laborious ordeal reserved for life's greatest milestones.
Now, the only apparent cost to taking infinite photos of something as common as a meal is the space on your hard drive and your dining companion's patience.

passage.translation: 摄影曾经是一项昂贵、费力的工作,只为人生最重要的里程碑时刻保留。现在,对诸如一顿饭这样平常的事物拍摄无数照片,唯一明显的代价就是你硬盘上的空间和用餐同伴的耐心。

sentences.text: But is there another cost, a deeper cost, to documenting a life experience instead of simply enjoying it?

"You hear that you shouldn't take all these photos and interrupt the experience, and it's bad for you, and we're not living in the present moment," says Kristin Diehl, associate professor of marketing at the University of Southern California Marshall School of Business.

passage.translation: 但是,记录生活体验而不是单纯享受它,是否还有另一种代价,一种更深层的代价?"你会听到不应该拍所有这些照片并打断体验,这对你不好,而且我们没有活在当下",南加州大学Marshall商学院市场营销副教授Kristin Diehl说。

sentences.text: Diehl and her fellow researchers wanted to find out if that was true, so they embarked on a series of nine experiments in the lab and in the field testing people's enjoyment in the presence or absence of a camera.
The results, published in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, surprised them.
Taking photos actually makes people enjoy what they're doing more, not less.

passage.translation: Diehl和她的研究同事想要弄清楚这是否属实,于是他们开展了一系列九项实验,在实验室和现场测试人们在有相机或没有相机的情况下的享受程度。发表在《人格与社会心理学杂志》上的研究结果让他们感到惊讶。拍照实际上让人们更享受他们正在做的事情,而不是更不享受。

sentences.text: "What we find is you actually look at the world slightly differently, because you're looking for things you want to capture, that you may want to hang onto," Diehl explains.
"That gets people more engaged in the experience, and they tend to enjoy it more."

passage.translation: "我们发现,你实际上会以稍微不同的方式看待世界,因为你在寻找你想要捕捉的东西,你可能想要留住的东西,"Diehl解释道。"这让人们更投入到体验中,他们往往更享受它。"

sentences.text: Take sightseeing.
In one experiment, nearly 200 participants boarded a double-decker bus for a tour of Philadelphia.
Both bus tours forbade the use of cell phones but one tour provided digital cameras and encouraged people to take photos.
The people who took photos enjoyed the experience significantly more, and said they were more engaged, than those who didn't.

passage.translation: 以观光为例。在一项实验中,近200名参与者登上一辆双层巴士游览费城。两个巴士游览都禁止使用手机,但其中一个游览提供了数码相机并鼓励人们拍照。拍照的人明显更享受这次体验,并表示他们比那些没有拍照的人更投入。

sentences.text: Snapping a photo directs attention, which heightens the pleasure you get from whatever you're looking at, Diehl says.
It works for things as boring as archaeological(考古的) museums, where people were given eye-tracking glasses and instructed either to take photos or not.
"People look longer at things they want to photograph," Diehl says.
They report liking the exhibits more, too.

passage.translation: 拍照能引导注意力,从而增强你从所看事物中获得的愉悦感,Diehl说。它对像考古博物馆这样无聊的东西也有效,在那里人们被给予眼动追踪眼镜并被指示拍照或不拍照。"人们看他们想拍照的东西的时间更长,"Diehl说。他们也表示更喜欢这些展品。

sentences.text: To the relief of Instagrammers(Instagram用戶) everywhere, it can even make meals more enjoyable.
When people were encouraged to take at least three photos while they ate lunch, they were more immersed in their meals than those who weren't told to take photos.

passage.translation: 让各地的Instagram用户松了一口气的是,它甚至可以让用餐更愉快。当人们被鼓励在吃午餐时至少拍三张照片时,他们比那些没有被告知拍照的人更沉浸在用餐中。

sentences.text: Was it the satisfying click of the camera?
The physical act of the snap?
No, they found; just the act of planning to take a photo—and not actually taking it—had the same joy-boosting effect.
"If you want to take mental photos, that works the same way," Diehl says.
"Thinking about what you would want to photograph also gets you more engaged."

passage.translation: 是相机令人满意的咔嚓声吗?是拍照的身体动作吗?不是,他们发现;仅仅是计划拍照的行为——而不是实际拍照——也有同样的提升愉悦感的效果。"如果你想拍心理照片,那也同样有效,"Diehl说。"思考你想拍什么照片也会让你更投入。"

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about photo-taking in the past?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者对过去拍照的看法是什么?
A) 这是一项费力的工作,用于记录人生重大事件。
B) 这是只有少数富人才能享受的奢侈品。
C) 这是保存珍贵影像的好方法。
D) 这是一项需要大量练习才能掌握的技能。
**判型** What does the author say about photo-taking in the past? 问的是作者就"过去拍照"陈述了什么事实，无 infer/imply/suggest 等推断信号词。
**拆句** Q51 是规范疑问句，主干 What does the author say，about photo-taking in the past作 say 的状语宾语；结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 摄影曾经是一桩昂贵、费力的苦差事，专留给人生最重大的里程碑时刻。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确laborious ordeal ↔ painstaking effort reserved for life's greatest milestones ↔ for recording life's major events预判的两层意思"费力"和"为人生大事"在选项 A 里被 painstaking effort 和 for recording life's major events 同时覆盖，无其他选项做得到。
B) 过度推断原文 expensive 只说"昂贵"，并未说"只有少数富人 (only a few wealthy people) 才能享受"——奢侈品属性是选项添加的。
C) 与原文相反原文用 laborious ordeal（费力的苦差事）做负向描述，选项 C 却把过去的拍照说成是a good way to preserve one's precious images（保存珍贵影像的好办法），与原文情感色彩相反。
D) 无中生有原文只说昂贵、费力、专为大事，对"是否需要练习掌握"未置一词。a skill that required lots of practice to master 是无中生有。
questions.quote: Photography was once an expensive, laborious ordeal reserved for life's greatest milestones.

options.text: It was a painstaking effort for recording life's major events.
It was a luxury that only a few wealthy people could enjoy.
It was a good way to preserve one's precious images.
It was a skill that required lots of practice to master.

questions.prompt: Kristin Diehl conducted a series of experiments on photo-taking to find out _______.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
Kristin Diehl进行了一系列关于拍照的实验,以找出_______。
A) 拍照实际上会给拍摄者带来什么样的快乐
B) 人们在观光时是否喜欢拍照
C) 拍照如何帮助丰富人们的生活体验
D) 拍照是否妨碍人们享受正在做的事情
**判型** conducted a series of experiments on photo-taking to find out 是不完整陈述句，待补全的是实验目的，答案必为文中明示的实验动因。
**拆句** Q52 是带空位的不完整陈述：主语 Kristin Diehl + 谓语 conducted + 宾语 a series of experiments，介词短语 on photo-taking 作定语，不定式 to find out _ 表目的；空位处待填实验目的的宾语从句。
**定位** Diehl 和她的研究伙伴想要查清那种说法是否成立，于是着手开展了一系列共九项实验，在实验室与现场测试人们在有相机和无相机时的愉悦感。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文实验初衷是检验负面说法，what kind of pleasure it would actually bring 把研究目的偷换成正向探寻"种类"，方向完全反了。
B) 以偏概全观光只是 P5 列举的多个实验场景之一，不是研究的总目的。把全研究目的窄化到"观光时是否享受"是以偏概全。
C) 答非所问how it could help to enrich people's life experiences 已经预设拍照有积极作用并追问"如何起作用"，而原文的研究意图是中性验证"是否打断"。
D) ✓ 正确wanted to find out if that was true ↔whether it prevented people enjoying what they were doing interrupt the experience ↔ prevented people enjoying what they were doing把 if that was true 的 that 回指还原为 interrupt the experience，只有 D 把"打断享受"这一层语义保留下来；其他三项都丢了 that 的回指。
questions.quote: Diehl and her fellow researchers wanted to find out if that was true, so they embarked on a series of nine experiments in the lab and in the field testing people's enjoyment in the presence or absence of a camera.

options.text: what kind of pleasure it would actually bring to photo-takers
whether people enjoyed it when they did sightseeing
how it could help to enrich people's life experiences
whether it prevented people enjoying what they were doing

questions.prompt: What do the results of Diehl's experiments show about people taking pictures?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
Diehl的实验结果显示,拍照的人会怎样?
A) 他们会从正在做的事情上分心。
B) 他们能更好地记住所看到或所做的事情。
C) 他们更加专注于吸引他们目光的事物。
D) 他们能更好地理解这个世界。
**判型** What do the results of Diehl's experiments show about people taking pictures? 直问实验结果"显示了什么"，是对原文结论句的同义改写。
**拆句** Q53 主干 What do the results show，介词短语 of Diehl's experiments 修饰 results，about people taking pictures 作 show 的宾语补语；about 后接动名词复合结构 people taking pictures，意为"关于拍照者"。
**定位** 我们发现的是：你其实会以略不同的视角看世界，因为你在寻找想抓拍、想留住的东西。这让人在体验中更投入，也更享受。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反distracted from what they are doing 与原文 more engaged in the experience 情感极性完全相反；原文是"更投入"，选项却是"被分散注意力"。
B) 无中生有原文 P4 只讲"看世界的方式不同+更投入"，未提任何"记忆/回忆"的维度。better remember what they see or do 是无中生有。
C) ✓ 正确more engaged in the experience ↔ more absorbed in what catches their eye things you want to capture ↔ what catches their eye预判的"投入"和"想抓拍的事物"两层意思在选项 C 中被 more absorbed 与 what catches their eye 一一对应覆盖。
D) 过度推断you actually look at the world slightly differently 只说"略不同地看"，没说"更懂"。have a better understanding of the world 把视觉层面的差异放大到认知层面，幅度过大。
questions.quote: What we find is you actually look at the world slightly differently, because you're looking for things you want to capture, that you may want to hang onto. That gets people more engaged in the experience, and they tend to enjoy it more.

options.text: They are distracted from what they are doing.
They can better remember what they see or do.
They are more absorbed in what catches their eye.
They can have a better understanding of the world.

questions.prompt: What is found about museum visitors with the aid of eye-tracking glasses?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
借助眼动追踪眼镜,研究发现博物馆参观者有什么特点?
A) 他们拍出了更好的展品照片。
B) 他们在拍照时更加关注展品。
C) 他们对展出的物品有更好的观察视角。
D) 他们更容易理解历史事件。
**判型** What is found about museum visitors with the aid of eye-tracking glasses? 直问"借助眼动眼镜对博物馆参观者发现了什么"，答案是定位段的客观陈述。
**拆句** Q54 被动句：What is found 主干，about museum visitors 限定对象，with the aid of eye-tracking glasses 是表手段的伴随状语；三层介词短语堆叠但语义清晰，无陷阱。
**定位** 即便是无趣如考古博物馆也同样奏效：参与者被发给眼动追踪眼镜，并被指令要么拍照、要么不拍。"人们对自己想拍的东西注视更久，"Diehl 说道。他们也报告说更喜欢这些展品。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有come out with better photographs 谈的是照片成果优劣，而原文测的是注视时长与喜爱度，与照片质量无关。
B) ✓ 正确People look longer at things they want to photograph ↔focus more on the exhibits when taking pictures things they want to photograph ↔ exhibits when taking pictures预判中的"对想拍的看得更久"在 B 选项中由 focus more 和 exhibits 准确对应，其他三项都在概念层走偏。
C) 偷换概念better view of what are on display 谈的是物理或视觉上的"视野更佳"，而原文谈的是注视时长。两者一是 view（视野/景观），一是 look at（注视）——一字之差，所指不同。
D) 无中生有follow the historical events more easily"更容易跟上历史事件"是认知/理解层面的描述，而原文只测"注视时长"与"喜爱度"。本选项还把"博物馆=历史馆"的刻板印象绑了进来，但原文 archaeological（考古的）不等同于 historical events（历史事件）。
questions.quote: It works for things as boring as archaeological museums, where people were given eye- tracking glasses and instructed either to take photos or not. "People look longer at things they want to photograph," Diehl says. They report liking the exhibits more, too.

options.text: They come out with better photographs of the exhibits.
They focus more on the exhibits when taking pictures.
They have a better view of what are on display.
They follow the historical events more easily.

questions.prompt: They follow the historical events more easily.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （推断题）
**题目译文**
他们更容易理解历史事件。
A) 拍照前最好先做好计划。
B) 心理照片可以像快照一样美丽。
C) 摄影师可以从相机的咔嚓声中获得巨大的快乐。
D) 即使只是想到要拍照也能产生积极的效果。
**判型** 题干因疑似录入异常无法直接定题型，但选项 Even the very thought of taking a photo can have a positive effect. 含 even 这一让步推断信号，且对应末段实验拓展性结论，按推断题处理最稳妥。
**拆句** Q55 的字面 They follow the historical events more easily. 是陈述句而非疑问句或不完整陈述，明显与选项体例不匹配，按异常处理；逐字解析其语法无意义。
**定位** 是相机咔嚓声的满足感吗？还是按下快门那个动作？不是，他们发现：仅仅是"打算拍照"这一念头——哪怕并未真拍——就同样带来提升愉悦的效果。"如果你想拍"心理照"，效果也一样，"Diehl 说。"光是去想自己想拍什么，就能让你更投入。"
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文 planning to take a photo 是"打算拍"这一念头本身（与"真拍"对照），并不是"拍前做规划"这一行为。It is better to make plans before taking photos. 把"打算拍"窄化为"做计划"，且加了"更好"这一比较级判断。
B) 偷换概念原文谈"心理照与实拍效果相同"，但相同的是 joy-boosting effect（提升愉悦的效果），不是美学层面的"漂亮"。Mental photos can be as beautiful as snapshots. 把效果维度偷换成美感维度。
C) 与原文相反Was it the satisfying click of the camera?...No, they found——原文用 No 直接否认"咔嚓声是喜悦来源"，而选项 C 却说 Photographers can derive great joy from the click of the camera，正话反说。
D) ✓ 正确just the act of planning to take a photo—and not actually taking it—had the same joy-boosting effect↔ Even the very thought of taking a photo can have a positive effect. Thinking about what you would want to photograph also gets you more engaged ↔Even the very thought of taking a photo can have a positive effect.定位句的核心让步 and not actually taking it 只有选项 D 中的 Even...the very thought 把"哪怕仅是念头"这一层完整表达出来。
questions.quote: Was it the satisfying click of the camera? The physical act of the snap? No, they found; just the act of planning to take a photo—and not actually taking it—had the same joy-boosting effect. "If you want to take mental photos, that works the same way," Diehl says. "Thinking about what you would want to photograph also gets you more engaged."

options.text: It is better to make plans before taking photos.
Mental photos can be as beautiful as snapshots.
Photographers can derive great joy from the click of the camera.
Even the very thought of taking a photo can have a positive effect.

title: The Ebro Delta, in Spain, famous as a…

sentences.text: The Ebro Delta, in Spain, famous as a battleground during the Spanish Civil War, is now the setting for a different contest, one that is pitting rice farmers against two enemies: the rice-eating giant apple snail, and rising sea levels.
What happens here will have a bearing on the future of European rice production and the overall health of southern European wetlands.

passage.translation: 西班牙的埃布罗三角洲因在西班牙内战期间作为战场而闻名,如今成为另一场较量的舞台,这场较量使稻农与两个敌人对抗:以稻米为食的巨型福寿螺和不断上升的海平面。这里发生的事情将对欧洲水稻生产的未来和南欧湿地的整体健康状况产生影响。

sentences.text: Located on the Mediterranean just two hours south of Barcelona, the Ebro Delta produces 120 million kilograms of rice a year, making it one of the continent's most important rice-growing areas.
As the sea creeps into these fresh-water marshes, however, rising salinity(盐分) is hampering rice production.
At the same time, this sea-water also kills off the greedy giant apple snail, an introduced pest that feeds on young rice plants.
The most promising strategy has become to harness one foe against the other.

passage.translation: 埃布罗三角洲位于地中海沿岸,距巴塞罗那以南仅两小时路程,每年生产1.2亿千克水稻,使其成为欧洲大陆最重要的水稻种植区之一。然而,随着海水渗入这些淡水沼泽,不断上升的盐分正在阻碍水稻生产。与此同时,这些海水也杀死了贪婪的巨型福寿螺,这是一种以水稻幼苗为食的外来害虫。最有希望的策略已变成利用一个敌人来对抗另一个敌人。

sentences.text: The battle is currently being waged on land, in greenhouses at the University of Barcelona.

Scientists working under the banner "Project Neurice" are seeking varieties of rice that can withstand the increasing salinity without losing the absorbency that makes European rice ideal for traditional Spanish and Italian dishes.

passage.translation: 这场战斗目前正在巴塞罗那大学的温室里在陆地上进行。在Neurice项目旗号下工作的科学家们正在寻找既能承受不断增加的盐分又不失去吸水性的水稻品种,这种吸水性使欧洲水稻成为传统西班牙和意大利菜肴的理想选择。

sentences.text: "The project has two sides," says Xavier Serrat, Neurice project manager and researcher at the University of Barcelona, "the short-term fight against the snail—and a mid- to long-term fight against climate change.
But the snail has given the project greater urgency."

passage.translation: Neurice项目经理兼巴塞罗那大学研究员Xavier Serrat说:这个项目有两个方面,短期对抗福寿螺,以及中长期对抗气候变化。但福寿螺使这个项目更加紧迫。

sentences.text: Originally from South America, the snails were accidentally introduced into the Ebro Delta by Global Aquatic Technologies, a company that raised the snails for fresh-water aquariums(水族馆), but failed to prevent their escape.
For now, the giant apple snail's presence in Europe is limited to the Ebro Delta.
But the snail continues its march to new territory, says Serrat.
"The question is not whether it will reach other rice-growing areas of Europe, but when."

passage.translation: 这些螺类原产于南美洲,由Global Aquatic Technologies公司意外引入埃布罗三角洲,该公司为淡水水族馆饲养这些螺类,但未能防止它们逃逸。目前,巨型福寿螺在欧洲的存在仅限于埃布罗三角洲。但Serrat说,福寿螺继续向新领地进军。问题不是它是否会到达欧洲其他水稻种植区,而是什么时候到达。

sentences.text: Over the next year and a half investigators will test the various strains of salt-tolerant rice they've bred.
In 2018, farmers will plant the varieties with the most promise in the Ebro Delta and Europe's other two main rice-growing regions—along the Po in Italy, and France's Rhone.
A season in the field will help determine which, if any, of the varieties are ready for commercialization.

passage.translation: 在接下来的一年半时间里,研究人员将测试他们培育的各种耐盐水稻品种。2018年,农民将在埃布罗三角洲和欧洲其他两个主要水稻种植区——意大利的波河沿岸和法国的罗讷河沿岸——种植最有希望的品种。在田间种植一季将有助于确定这些品种中是否有任何品种已为商业化做好准备。

sentences.text: As an EU-funded effort, the search for salt-tolerant varieties of rice is taking place in all three countries.
Each team is crossbreeding a local European short-grain rice with a long-grain Asian variety that carries the salt-resistant gene.
The scientists are breeding successive generations to arrive at varieties that incorporate salt tolerance but retain about 97 percent of the European rice genome(基因组).

passage.translation: 作为欧盟资助的项目,对耐盐水稻品种的研究正在所有三个国家进行。每个团队都在将当地的欧洲短粒水稻与携带抗盐基因的亚洲长粒品种进行杂交。科学家们正在培育连续几代,以获得既具有耐盐性又保留约97%欧洲水稻基因组的品种。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: Why does the author mention the Spanish Civil War at the beginning of the passage?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （例证目的题）
**题目译文**
作者为什么在文章开头提到西班牙内战?
A) 它对西班牙稻农的生活产生了巨大影响。
B) 它在西班牙历史记录中具有重大意义。
C) Ebro三角洲的稻农正在进行一场同样重要的战斗。
D) Ebro三角洲的稻农正在经历与战争时期同样艰难的时期。
**判型** Why does the author mention the Spanish Civil War 直接问作者为什么提到某事，属于典型的写作意图/例证作用类提问。
**拆句** 题干主干是 Why does the author mention the Spanish Civil War，由 at the beginning of the passage 这一介词短语作状语补充位置；句式平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 西班牙的 Ebro 三角洲，曾因是西班牙内战的战场而出名，如今则成为另一场"战斗"的舞台——一场让稻农同时对抗两大敌人（食稻的巨型苹果螺与海平面上升）的对决。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有It had great impact on the life of Spanish rice farmers 把"内战影响稻农生活"当作作者提及内战的目的，但原文并未谈论内战对稻农生活的任何影响。
B) 答非所问It is of great significance in the records of Spanish history 只解释"内战在西班牙史上很重要"，没有回答"作者为何在此处提它"——这是常识，而题问的是写作意图。
C) ✓ 正确is now the setting for a different contest, one that is pitting rice farmers against two enemies ↔Rice farmers in the Ebro Delta are waging a battle of similar importance What happens here will have a bearing on the future of European rice production and the overall health of southern European wetlands↔ a battle of similar importance预判为"用历史战场衬托今日之战同样重要"，C 项的 a battle of similar importance 同时承接 a different contest 与 will have a bearing on the future of European rice production，与预判一致。
D) 过度推断Rice farmers in the Ebro Delta are experiencing as hard a time as in the war 把作者的比喻坐实为"稻农像战时一样艰难"，原文只做"战场"意象的类比，并未比较两个时代生活艰苦程度。
questions.quote: The Ebro Delta, in Spain, famous as a battleground during the Spanish Civil War, is now the setting for a different contest, one that is pitting rice farmers against two enemies: the rice- eating giant apple snail, and rising sea levels.

options.text: It had great impact on the life of Spanish rice farmers.
It is of great significance in the records of Spanish history.
Rice farmers in the Ebro Delta are waging a battle of similar importance.
Rice farmers in the Ebro Delta are experiencing as hard a time as in the war.

questions.prompt: What may be the most effective strategy for rice farmers to employ in fighting their enemies?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
对稻农来说,与敌人作战最有效的策略可能是什么?
A) 先打击较弱的敌人。
B) 一石二鸟。
C) 逐个消灭敌人。
D) 以恶制恶。
**判型** What may be the most effective strategy 问具体做法，可在原文找到一句直接对应的策略陈述。
**拆句** 题干主干 What may be the most effective strategy，后接不定式 to employ in fighting their enemies 作 strategy 的后置修饰，意为"在对抗敌人时所采用的最有效策略"；情态动词 may 表推测，并不改变设问性质。
**定位** 与此同时，这种海水也会杀死贪婪的巨型苹果螺——一种以幼稻为食的外来害虫。最有希望的策略已经变成"用一个敌人去对付另一个敌人"。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Striking the weaker enemy first 凭空增加"先打较弱的那个"，原文从未对两敌人作"强/弱"区分，也未说明先后。
B) 偷换概念Killing two birds with one stone 是"用一种手段达成两个目标"，与原文"让两个敌人相互制约"不是同一回事；这里没有"一个手段"统揽两敌，而是"一个敌人本身"被借用为手段。
C) 与原文相反Eliminating the enemy one by one 是"逐一消灭"，暗示稻农依次单独对付每个敌人；原文恰相反，是让两个敌人同台"互相消耗"。
D) ✓ 正确to harness one foe against the other ↔ Using one evil to combat the other预判是"以一敌制一敌"，D 的 Using one evil to combat the other 与 harness one foe against the other 在动作结构与对象数量上完全对应。
questions.quote: At the same time, this sea-water also kills off the greedy giant apple snail, an introduced pest that feeds on young rice plants. The most promising strategy has become to harness one foe against the other.

options.text: Striking the weaker enemy first.
Killing two birds with one stone.
Eliminating the enemy one by one.
Using one evil to combat the other.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about "Project Neurice"?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于Neurice项目我们了解到什么?
A) 其目标必须以一定代价来实现。
B) 它旨在提高西班牙水稻的产量。
C) 其当务之急是控制害虫。
D) 它试图借助气候变化来杀死蜗牛。
**判型** What do we learn about "Project Neurice" 问对某事物的客观了解，对应原文一处或几处描述。
**拆句** 题干结构 What do we learn about "Project Neurice" 是一个间接疑问句的标准句式，主谓简单、无陷阱。
**定位** "这个项目分两面，"Neurice 项目经理、巴塞罗那大学研究员 Xavier Serrat 说，"短期是对付蜗牛，中长期是对付气候变化。但蜗牛已让这一项目变得更为紧迫。"
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Its goals will have to be realized at a cost 称项目目标必须"以某种代价"实现，原文从未谈成本/代价问题。
B) 偷换概念It aims to increase the yield of Spanish rice 把项目目标改成"提高西班牙水稻产量"，原文目标是"培育抗盐品种"，提到产量数据只是 120 million kilograms of rice a year的背景介绍，并不是项目目标。
C) ✓ 正确the short-term fight against the snail ↔Its immediate priority is to bring the pest under control But the snail has given the project greater urgency ↔ Its immediate priority C 同时对应 short-term fight against the snail 的短期定位与 greater urgency 的紧迫级别，符合预判"当下首要任务是控蜗"。
D) 与原文相反It tries to kill the snails with the help of climate change 把气候变化说成"杀蜗的帮手"，原文 a mid- to long-term fight against climate change 明确把气候变化列为项目要对付的敌人，方向相反。
questions.quote: "The project has two sides," says Xavier Serrat, Neurice project manager and researcher at the University of Barcelona, "the short-term fight against the snail—and a mid- to long-term fight against climate change. But the snail has given the project greater urgency."

options.text: Its goals will have to be realized at a cost.
It aims to increase the yield of Spanish rice.
Its immediate priority is to bring the pest under control.
It tries to kill the snails with the help of climate change.

questions.prompt: What does Neurice project manager say about the giant apple snail?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
Neurice项目经理对大苹果螺说了什么?
A) 它只能在南欧湿地上生存。
B) 它将入侵欧洲其他水稻种植区。
C) 它以超出人类想象的速度繁殖。
D) 它是被故意引入稻田的。
**判型** What does Neurice project manager say about the giant apple snail 直接问某人关于某事的原话，是观点引述类细节题。
**拆句** 题干主干 What does Neurice project manager say，后接介词短语 about the giant apple snail 限定话题范围；陈述对象明确，无嵌套从句。
**定位** 但蜗牛仍在向新地盘扩张，Serrat 说。"问题不是它会不会蔓延到欧洲其他水稻产区，而是何时蔓延过去。"
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全It can survive only on southern European wetlands 用 only 把蜗牛活动范围限死在南欧湿地，原文只说 For now, the giant apple snail's presence in Europe is limited to the Ebro Delta 是"目前"的暂时状况，并未说它"只能"生存于此。
B) ✓ 正确The question is not whether it will reach other rice-growing areas of Europe, but when ↔It will invade other rice-growing regions of Europe预判是"扩散必然发生"，B 的 will invade 把这一必然性直接落到"将会入侵欧洲其他水稻产区"，与定位句完全等值。
C) 无中生有It multiplies at a speed beyond human imagination 谈"繁殖速度惊人"，原文从未提到蜗牛繁殖率/速度的任何描述。
D) 与原文相反It was introduced into the rice fields on purpose 称"有意引入"，原文 the snails were accidentally introduced 明确说"被意外引入"，方向相反。
questions.quote: But the snail continues its march to new territory, says Serrat. "The question is not whether it will reach other rice-growing areas of Europe, but when."

questions.prompt: What is the ultimate goal of the EU-funded program?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
欧盟资助项目的最终目标是什么?
A) 培育理想的抗盐水稻品种。
B) 提高西班牙水稻的吸收能力。
C) 将西班牙水稻引入欧洲其他地区。
D) 推广水稻杂交技术。
**判型** What is the ultimate goal of the EU-funded program 直问项目目标，原文末段一般会有目的状语/不定式直接呼应。
**拆句** 题干主干 What is the ultimate goal of the EU-funded program，of 短语限定 goal 所属对象；结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 作为一项欧盟资助的研究，三国都在寻找耐盐水稻品种。各团队都把本地的欧洲短粒米与一种带耐盐基因的亚洲长粒米进行杂交。科学家通过逐代繁育，最终要培育出既具备耐盐性、又保留约 97% 欧洲水稻基因组的品种。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确to arrive at varieties that incorporate salt tolerance but retain about 97 percent of the European rice genome↔ Cultivating ideal salt-resistant rice varieties the search for salt-tolerant varieties of rice↔salt-resistant rice varieties预判为"培育耐盐稻"，A 的 Cultivating ideal salt-resistant rice varieties 与原文 to arrive at varieties that incorporate salt tolerance 在动作（培育/获得）与对象（耐盐品种）上均等值。
B) 偷换概念Increasing the absorbency of the Spanish rice 把目标说成"提升西班牙水稻的吸水性"，原文只在 can withstand the increasing salinity without losing the absorbency 提到"不能因此丧失吸水性"，是保底条件，不是要去提升的目标。
C) 无中生有Introducing Spanish rice to the rest of Europe 称"把西班牙水稻引入欧洲其他地区"，原文 in all three countries 仅说三国共同研究，并未谈"推广西班牙米"。
D) 偷换概念Popularizing the rice crossbreeding technology 把"杂交技术普及"当目标，原文Each team is crossbreeding… 说明杂交只是培育新品种的手段，目标不是技术本身。
questions.quote: As an EU-funded effort, the search for salt-tolerant varieties of rice is taking place in all three countries. Each team is crossbreeding a local European short-grain rice with a long-grain Asian variety that carries the salt-resistant gene. The scientists are breeding successive generations to arrive at varieties that incorporate salt tolerance but retain about 97 percent of the European rice genome.

options.text: Cultivating ideal salt-resistant rice varieties.
Increasing the absorbency of the Spanish rice.
Introducing Spanish rice to the rest of Europe.
Popularizing the rice crossbreeding technology.

title: Scientists scanning and mapping the Giza pyramids say…

sentences.text: Scientists scanning and mapping the Giza pyramids say they've discovered that the Great Pyramid of Giza is not exactly even.
But really not by much.

passage.translation: 科学家在扫描和测绘吉萨金字塔时表示，他们发现吉萨大金字塔并非完全对称。但实际上差异并不大。这座金字塔是世界七大奇迹中最古老的一座。几个世纪以来，金字塔的精确尺寸一直令专家们困惑，因为最初覆盖在其表面的"超过21英亩的坚硬白色覆面石"早已被移除。工程师Glen Dash在记录Ancient Egypt Research Associates工作的时事通讯"AERAGRAM"最新一期中报告称，他的团队使用了一种新的测量方法，通过寻找任何幸存的覆面石残余来确定原始边缘的位置。他们发现金字塔东侧比西侧最多短5.5英寸。

He says his (34)____ is that the Egyptians laid out their design on a grid, noting that the Great Pyramid is oriented only (35)____ away from the cardinal directions (its north- south axis runs 3 minutes 54 seconds west of due north, while its east-west axis runs 3 minutes 51 seconds north of due east)—an amount that's "tiny, but similar," archeologist Atlas Obscura points out.

passage.translation: 然而，最令他着迷的问题并不是4500年前设计和建造金字塔的埃及人如何出现了偏差，而是他们如何做到如此接近完美。Dash写道："我们只能推测埃及人如何仅使用他们拥有的工具就能如此精确地布设这些线条。"他说，他的假设是埃及人在网格上布置设计，并指出大金字塔的方向仅略微偏离基本方位（其南北轴线在正北方向以西偏离3分54秒，而其东西轴线在正东方向以北偏离3分51秒）——考古学家Atlas Obscura指出，这个偏差量"微小，但相似"。

groups.content:
Scientists scanning and mapping the Giza pyramids say they've discovered that the Great Pyramid of Giza is not exactly even. But really not by much. This pyramid is the oldest of the world's Seven Wonders. The pyramid's exact size has {{26}} experts for centuries, as the "more than 21 acres of hard, white casing stones" that originally covered it were {{27}} long ago. Reporting in the most recent issue of the newsletter "AERAGRAM," which {{28}} the work of the Ancient Egypt Research Associates, engineer Glen Dash says his team used a new measuring approach that involved finding any surviving {{29}} of the casing in order to determine where the original edge was. They found the east side of the pyramid to be a {{30}} of 5.5 inches shorter than the west side.

The question that most {{31}} him, however, isn't how the Egyptians who designed and built the pyramid got it wrong 4,500 years ago, but how they got it so close to {{32}} . "We can only speculate as to how the Egyptians could have laid out these lines with such {{33}} using only the tools they had," Dash writes. He says his {{34}} is that the Egyptians laid out their design on a grid, noting that the Great Pyramid is oriented only {{35}} away from the cardinal directions (its north- south axis runs 3 minutes 54 seconds west of due north, while its east-west axis runs 3 minutes 51 seconds north of due east)—an amount that's "tiny, but similar," archeologist Atlas Obscura points out.

perfect

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) puzzled 动词
**词性槽** have ___ 现在完成时谓语，要过去分词
**依据** “多个世纪以来一直使专家困惑”——puzzle sb. 标准搭配上下文 as the "more than 21 acres of hard, white casing stones" that originally covered it were __(27)__ long ago 解释了为什么尺寸难测——外层石材早就没了，所以专家长期搞不清精确尺寸；puzzle sb.（使某人困惑）正是这种长期未解的语义。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) established “确立专家”宾语不对establish 的宾语通常是“制度、地位、事实”而非“专家”，has established experts 在搭配上讲不通。
M) removed “移走专家”语义荒谬remove experts 字面是“移走专家”，与上下文（尺寸难定）毫无关联；且 M 真正用在 27 题“石材被移走”的语境里。

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) removed 动词
**词性槽** were ___ long ago 被动语态，要过去分词
**依据** casing 石早就被“拆走”了，正解释“尺寸难测”本句解释为何 26 题中“尺寸困扰专家”——因为 the "more than 21 acres of hard, white casing stones" that originally covered it were __(27)__ long ago，外层石材早已被移走，团队才不得不去 finding any surviving __(29)__ of the casing；remove（移走、拆除）与“surviving remnants（残存碎片）”形成自然因果。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) established “石材被确立”不通establish stones 不是合理搭配，且即便译成“被建立”，也无法解释下文为何只能找到残存碎片；语义因果链断裂。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) chronicles 动词
**词性槽** which ___ the work … 关系从句缺谓语，主语单数
**依据** “记录/编录”研究协会的工作——与 newsletter 职能匹配Reporting in the most recent issue of the newsletter "AERAGRAM," which __(28)__the work of the Ancient Egypt Research Associates 中，newsletter（简报）作为定期出版物，最自然的职能就是按时间“记录、记述”研究协会的工作；chronicle 作动词正是“按时间顺序记述”，与 newsletter 的定位严丝合缝。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
D) fascinates “简报使工作着迷”主宾颠倒fascinate 意为“使……着迷”，其宾语应是“人”而非“工作”；the newsletter fascinates the work主宾不通；且 D 真正用在 31 题“最令他着迷的问题”的语境里。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) remnants 名词
**词性槽** any 后＋of 短语限定，定语法槽为可数名词复数
**依据** casing 已被拆除，能找到的只剩“残余物”上下文 the "more than 21 acres of hard, white casing stones" that originally covered it were __(27)__ long ago 表明外层石灰岩早已被拆走，团队只能去找它“surviving 残存的”部分；remnants（残余物）正好与 surviving 同义呼应，复数也匹配 any 后可数名词的形态。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) hypothesis “假说”不会“surviving of the casing”hypothesis 指抽象的“假说”，无法和 of the casing（外层包石的）搭配，本空讲的是物理遗存而非观点。
G) momentum “动量/势头”与考古实物语境无关momentum 多用于物理或抽象“势头”，谈不上 surviving 或属于 casing 的一部分。
J) precision “精度”是抽象属性，不会被“surviving”修饰precision 是不可数抽象名词，且 any surviving precision of the casing 在语义上不通——精度不会“幸存”。
N) revelations “被披露之事”与外层石头物理遗存对不上revelations 指被揭示出来的事实或秘密，属于信息层面，不能用来指物质上仍幸存的外层石材片段。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) maximum 名词
**词性槽** a ___ of 5.5 inches 名词＋of＋数值，空处为名词
**依据** “最多短 5.5 英寸”——a maximum of 标准量词搭配a maximum of + 数值 = “最多……”，与 only by much 的语义（差距不大、最多 5.5 英寸）一致；同时对应开篇 But really not by much. 的总评——差距很小、且是最大值不超过 5.5 英寸。

**答案** D) fascinates 动词
**词性槽** that 引导的定语从句缺谓语，主语 that 指代单数 question
**依据** “最令他着迷的问题”——fascinate sb. 标准搭配下文 isn't how the Egyptians who designed and built the pyramid got it wrong 4,500 years ago, but how they got it so close to __(32)__ 描述 Dash 真正感兴趣的不是“他们怎么错的”而是“他们怎么做得这么准”，正是“最令他着迷的问题”；fascinate sb.（使某人着迷）与 the question 主语搭配自然。

**答案** I) perfect 形容词
**词性槽** be close to ___ 中 to 作介词，空处可为名词或形容词；并列结构定形容词
**依据** close to perfect＝接近完美，正面照应主旨全文主旨即“误差极小、几乎完美”——首段 the Great Pyramid of Giza is not exactly even. But really not by much. 与 33 题 with such precision、35 题 only slightly away三处呼应，全部指向“perfect”而非“complete”；close to perfect 也是英文里描述“近乎完美”的标准搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) complete “完整”谈的是有没有缺件，与“准不准”错位complete 强调“完整、完成”，是“缺不缺零件”的维度；本句的对照是 wrong（错的）↔right/perfect（对的、完美的），是“准不准、对不对齐”的维度，二者不在一条轴上。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 B) —— complete 看似“完整”很对，实为 wrong ↔ ___ 对照轴错位。got it wrong 4,500 years ago, but how they got it so close to __(32)__ 中 wrong是“做错了”，对照的应是“做对了/接近完美”，所以选 perfect 而非 complete；防坑：见到not … wrong, but … ___，立刻在词库里找 wrong 的反义形容词。

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) precision 名词
**词性槽** with such ___ 的固定结构里要名词
**依据** 全段在赞叹“精度”——precision 直对主题下文 its north-south axis runs 3 minutes 54 seconds west of due north 用极细的角度数据具体说明误差极小，与 with such precision（如此精准）正好对应；上文 how they got it so close to __(32)__ 也已铺垫“接近完美”的语义。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) hypothesis “以如此假说画线”不通with such hypothesis 字面意为“以如此假说”，与 lay out lines（放样画线）这一物理动作搭不上；且 hypothesis 后面紧跟 his __(34)__ 处才是它真正的归宿。
G) momentum “动量/势头”与放样动作不搭with momentum 多用于运动、推进语境，与“放样画对齐线”的精细工艺无关；语义指向是“速度/势能”，不是“准确度”。
N) revelations 复数 + 抽象“启示”与 with such 不配revelations 是复数可数名词，with such revelations 也讲不通——古埃及人画线不是靠“启示”而是靠工具与方法。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) hypothesis 名词
**词性槽** his ___ is that … 名词从句作表语，空处必为名词
**依据** “假说”由 that 从句解释其具体内容We can only speculate as to how the Egyptians could have laid out these lines 已用speculate（推测）定调；Dash 提出的“他们用网格放样”只是推测、未经证实，正是hypothesis（假说）。his hypothesis is that … = “他的假说是……”句式典型。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) momentum “他的动量”和 is that 从句对不上momentum 不接“that 内容从句”，his momentum is that … 不成立，且与“推测画线方式”的话题无关。
N) revelations 复数且义为“被揭示之事”，与未经证实的推测相反revelations 暗示已经被披露的事实，而本句明说 We can only speculate（只能推测），与“揭示出来的真相”语义相反；况且复数与 is 单数也不一致。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 N) —— revelations 看似与“想法/发现”相关，实为与 speculate 反义。his __(34)__ is that the Egyptians laid out their design on a grid 中，his + is that句式要求观点类抽象名词，但上句 We can only speculate 已定调“只能推测”，必填hypothesis（未证实的假说）而非 revelations（被披露的事实）；防坑：上文 speculate /guess 等动词出现，就把 revelations / truth / discovery 这类“已确证”名词排除。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) slightly 副词
**词性槽** is oriented only ___ away from … 副词修饰整个介短
**依据** 下文角度差极小——slightly 量上吻合括号里 its north-south axis runs 3 minutes 54 seconds west of due north, while its east-west axis runs 3 minutes 51 seconds north of due east 给出的偏差只有几分秒，archeologist 也评价 an amount that's "tiny, but similar,"——只能说 slightly（略微地）偏离正北/正东，正面回应 32 题“接近完美”的总评。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) mysteriously “神秘地偏离”与作者赞叹精度的态度相悖mysteriously 表“神秘地”，会暗示原因不明、带玄学色彩；而本段重点是用精确数据印证“几乎完美对齐”，态度是赞叹精度而非渲染神秘。

title: Apple's Stance Highlights a More Confrontational Tech Industry

passage.label: A

sentences.text: The battle between Apple and law enforcement officials over unlocking a terrorist's smartphone is the culmination of a slow turning of the tables between the technology industry and the United States government.

passage.translation: 苹果公司与执法官员之间围绕解锁一名恐怖分子智能手机的斗争,是科技行业与美国政府之间力量对比缓慢转变的高潮。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: After revelations by the former National Security Agency contractor Edward J.

Snowden in 2013 that the government both cozied up to(讨好) certain tech companies and hacked into others to gain access to private data on an enormous scale, tech giants began to recognize the United States government as a hostile actor.
But if the confrontation has crystallized in this latest battle, it may already be heading toward a predictable conclusion: In the long run, the tech companies are destined to emerge victorious.

passage.translation: 2013年前国家安全局承包商Edward J. Snowden披露政府既讨好某些科技公司又侵入其他公司以大规模获取私人数据后,科技巨头开始将美国政府视为敌对势力。但如果这场对抗在最近的斗争中明朗化,它可能已经走向一个可预见的结论:从长远来看,科技公司注定会取得胜利。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: It may not seem that way at the moment.
On the one side, you have the United States government's mighty legal and security apparatus fighting for data of the most sympathetic sort: the secrets buried in a dead mass murderer's phone.

The action stems from a federal court order issued on Tuesday requiring Apple to help the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) to unlock an iPhone used by one of the two attackers who killed 14 people in San Bernardino, California, in December.

passage.translation: 目前看来可能并非如此。一方面,你看到美国政府强大的法律和安全机构正在为最具同情色彩的数据而战:埋藏在一名已故大规模杀人犯手机中的秘密。这一行动源于周二发布的联邦法院命令,要求苹果公司帮助联邦调查局解锁12月在加利福尼亚州San Bernardino杀害14人的两名袭击者之一使用的iPhone。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: In the other corner is the world's most valuable company, whose chief executive, Timothy Cook, has said he will appeal the court's order.

Apple argues that it is fighting to preserve a principle that most of us who are addicted to our smartphones can defend: Weaken a single iPhone so that its contents can be viewed by the American government and you risk weakening all iPhones for any government intruder, anywhere.

passage.translation: 另一方是世界上最有价值的公司,其首席执行官Timothy Cook表示他将对法院命令提出上诉。苹果公司辩称,它是在为维护一项我们这些智能手机成瘾者大多数人都能捍卫的原则而战:削弱单一iPhone使其内容可以被美国政府查看,就有削弱所有iPhone、使其面临任何地方任何政府入侵者威胁的风险。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: There will probably be months of legal confrontation, and it is not at all clear which side will prevail in court, nor in the battle for public opinion and legislative favor.
Yet underlying all of this is a simple dynamic: Apple, Google, Facebook and other companies hold most of the cards in this confrontation.
They have our data, and their businesses depend on the global public's collective belief that they will do everything they can to protect that data.

passage.translation: 可能会有数月的法律对抗,而且完全不清楚哪一方会在法庭上胜出,也不清楚在争取公众舆论和立法支持的战斗中谁会获胜。然而所有这一切背后是一个简单的动态:苹果、Google、Facebook和其他公司在这场对抗中掌握着大部分牌。他们拥有我们的数据,而他们的业务依赖于全球公众的集体信念,即他们会竭尽所能保护这些数据。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: Any crack in that front could be fatal for tech companies that must operate worldwide.
If Apple is forced to open up an iPhone for an American law enforcement investigation, what is to prevent it from doing so for a request from the Russians or the Iranians?

If Apple is forced to write code that lets the FBI get into the iPhone 5c used by Syed Rizwan Farook, the male attacker in the San Bernardino attack, who would be responsible if some hacker got hold of that code and broke into its other devices?

passage.translation: 这条战线上的任何裂缝都可能对必须在全球运营的科技公司造成致命打击。如果苹果公司被迫为美国执法调查打开一部iPhone,有什么能阻止它对俄罗斯或伊朗的请求这样做呢?如果苹果公司被迫编写代码让FBI进入San Bernardino袭击中男性袭击者Syed Rizwan Farook使用的iPhone 5c,如果某个黑客获得了那段代码并侵入其他设备,谁该负责?

passage.label: G

sentences.text: Apple's stance on these issues emerged post-Snowden, when the company started putting in place a series of technologies that, by default, make use of encryption(加密) to limit access to people's data.
More than that, Apple—and, in different ways, other tech companies, including Google, Facebook, Twitter and Microsoft—have made their opposition to the government's claims a point of corporate pride.

passage.translation: 苹果公司在这些问题上的立场出现在Snowden事件之后,当时该公司开始实施一系列技术,默认使用加密来限制对人们数据的访问。不仅如此,苹果——以及以不同方式的其他科技公司,包括Google、Facebook、Twitter和Microsoft——已经将他们对政府主张的反对作为企业自豪感的一部分。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Apple's emerging global brand is privacy; it has staked its corporate reputation, not to mention the investment of considerable technical and financial resources, on limiting the sort of mass surveillance that was uncovered by Mr.
Snowden.
So now, for many cases involving governmental intrusions into data, once-lonely privacy advocates find themselves fighting alongside the most powerful company in the world.

passage.translation: 苹果公司新兴的全球品牌是隐私;它将企业声誉,更不用说大量技术和财务资源的投入,押在限制Snowden先生揭露的那种大规模监控上。所以现在,在许多涉及政府侵入数据的案件中,曾经孤独的隐私倡导者发现自己正与世界上最强大的公司并肩作战。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: "A comparison point is in the 1990s battles over encryption," said Kurt Opsahl, general counsel of the Electronic Frontier Foundation, a privacy watchdog group.
"Then you had a few companies involved, but not one of the largest companies in the world coming out with a lengthy and impassioned post, like we saw yesterday from Timothy Cook.
Its profile has really been raised."

passage.translation: 隐私监督组织Electronic Frontier Foundation的总法律顾问Kurt Opsahl说:"一个比较点是20世纪90年代关于加密的斗争。那时你有几家公司参与,但没有一家世界上最大的公司发表冗长而充满激情的帖子,就像我们昨天从Timothy Cook那里看到的那样。它的形象确实得到了提升。"

passage.label: J

sentences.text: Apple and other tech companies hold another ace: the technical means to keep making their devices more and more inaccessible.
Note that Apple's public opposition to the government's request is itself a hindrance to mass government intrusion.

And to get at the contents of a single iPhone, the government says it needs a court order and Apple's help to write new code; in earlier versions of the iPhone, ones that were created before Apple found religion on(热衷于) privacy, the FBI might have been able to break into the device by itself.

passage.translation: 苹果公司和其他科技公司还握有另一张王牌:使其设备越来越难以访问的技术手段。请注意,苹果公司对政府请求的公开反对本身就是对政府大规模侵入的阻碍。为了获取单一iPhone的内容,政府表示它需要法院命令和苹果公司的帮助来编写新代码;在iPhone的早期版本中,那些在苹果公司热衷于隐私之前创建的版本,FBI可能能够自己破解设备。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: You can expect that noose(束缚) to continue to tighten.
Experts said that whether or not Apple loses this specific case, measures that it could put into place in the future will almost certainly be able to further limit the government's reach.

passage.translation: 你可以预期这种束缚会继续收紧。专家表示,无论苹果公司是否在这个具体案件中败诉,它未来可以采取的措施几乎肯定能够进一步限制政府的触及范围。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: That is not to say that the outcome of the San Bernardino case is insignificant.
As Apple and several security experts have argued, an order compelling Apple to write software that gives the FBI access to the iPhone in question would establish an unsettling precedent.

The order essentially asks Apple to hack its own devices, and once it is in place, the precedent could be used to justify law enforcement efforts to get around encryption technologies in other investigations far removed from national security threats.

passage.translation: 这并不是说San Bernardino案件的结果无关紧要。正如苹果公司和几位安全专家所辩称的,强制苹果公司编写软件使FBI能够访问相关iPhone的命令将树立一个令人不安的先例。该命令本质上是要求苹果公司入侵自己的设备,一旦到位,这一先例可能被用来为执法部门在远离国家安全威胁的其他调查中绕过加密技术的努力辩护。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: Once armed with a method for gaining access to iPhones, the government could ask to use it proactively(先发制人地), before a suspected terrorist attack—leaving Apple in a bind as to whether to comply or risk an attack and suffer a public-relations nightmare.
"This is a brand new move in the war against encryption," Mr.
Opsahl said.

"We have had plenty of debates in Congress and the media over whether the government should have a backdoor, and this is an end run(迂回战术) around that—here they come with an order to create that backdoor."

passage.translation: 一旦掌握了获取iPhone访问权限的方法,政府可以要求先发制人地使用它,在疑似恐怖袭击发生之前——这让苹果公司陷入两难,是遵守命令还是冒着遭受袭击和公关噩梦的风险。Opsahl先生说:"这是反加密战争中的全新举措。我们在国会和媒体上就政府是否应该有后门进行了大量辩论,而这是对此的迂回战术——他们带着创建该后门的命令来了。"

passage.label: N

sentences.text: Yet it is worth noting that even if Apple ultimately loses this case, it has plenty of technical means to close a backdoor over time.

"If they are anywhere near worth their salt as engineers, I bet they are rethinking their threat model as we speak," said Jonathan Zdziarski, a digital expert who studies the iPhone and its vulnerabilities.

passage.translation: 然而值得注意的是,即使苹果公司最终在此案中败诉,它也有大量技术手段随着时间推移关闭后门。研究iPhone及其漏洞的数字专家Jonathan Zdziarski说:"如果他们作为工程师有任何价值,我打赌他们现在正在重新思考他们的威胁模型。"

passage.label: O

sentences.text: One relatively simple fix, Mr.

Zdziarski said, would be for Apple to modify future versions of the iPhone to require a user to enter a passcode before the phone will accept the sort of modified operating system that the FBI wants Apple to create.
That way, Apple could not unilaterally introduce a code that weakens the iPhone—a user would have to consent to it.

passage.translation: Zdziarski先生说,一个相对简单的修复方法是,苹果公司修改iPhone的未来版本,要求用户在手机接受FBI希望苹果公司创建的那种修改过的操作系统之前输入密码。这样,苹果公司就不能单方面引入削弱iPhone的代码——用户必须同意它。

passage.label: P

sentences.text: "Nothing is 100 percent hacker-proof," Mr.
Zdziarski said, but he pointed out that the judge's order in this case required Apple to provide "reasonable security assistance" to unlock Mr.
Farook's phone.

If Apple alters the security model of future iPhones so that even its own engineers' "reasonable assistance" will not be able to crack a given device when compelled by the government, a precedent set in this case might lose its lasting force.
In other words, even if the FBI wins this case, in the long run, it loses.

passage.translation: Zdziarski先生说:"没有什么是百分之百防黑客的",但他指出,本案中法官的命令要求苹果公司提供"合理的安全协助"来解锁Farook先生的手机。如果苹果公司改变未来iPhone的安全模型,使得即使是其自己工程师的"合理协助"在受到政府强制时也无法破解特定设备,那么本案树立的先例可能会失去其持久效力。换句话说,即使FBI赢得此案,从长远来看,它输了。

Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

**辨邻**

title: Data sharing: An open mind on open data

passage.label: A

sentences.text: It is a movement building steady momentum: a call to make research data, software code and experimental methods publicly available and transparent.
A spirit of openness is gaining acceptance in the science community, and is the only way, say advocates, to address a 'crisis' in science whereby too few findings are successfully reproduced.
Furthermore, they say, it is the best way for researchers to gather the range of observations that are necessary to speed up discoveries or to identify large- scale trends.

passage.translation: 这是一场正在稳步积聚力量的运动：呼吁将研究数据、软件代码和实验方法公开并透明化。开放精神正在科学界获得认可,倡导者们表示,这是解决科学界"危机"的唯一途径,该危机表现为成功重复的研究发现太少。此外,他们表示,这是研究人员收集加速发现或识别大规模趋势所必需的各种观察结果的最佳方式。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: The open-data shift poses a confusing problem for junior researchers.
On the one hand, the drive to share is gathering official steam.
Since 2013, global scientific bodies have begun to back policies that support increased public access to research.

On the other hand, scientists disagree about how much and when they should share data, and they debate whether sharing it is more likely to accelerate science and make it more robust, or to introduce vulnerabilities and problems.

As more journal and funders adopt data-sharing requirements, and as a growing number of enthusiasts call for more openness, junior researchers must find their place between adopters and those who continue to hold out, even as they strive to launch their own careers.

passage.translation: 开放数据转变给初级研究人员带来了一个令人困惑的问题。一方面,数据共享的推动正在获得官方支持。自2013年以来,全球科学机构已开始支持增加研究公共访问权的政策。另一方面,科学家们对应该共享多少数据以及何时共享存在分歧,他们争论共享数据是更有可能加速科学发展并使其更稳健,还是会引入脆弱性和问题。随着越来越多的期刊和资助机构采用数据共享要求,以及越来越多的热衷者呼吁更大的开放性,初级研究人员必须在采纳者和那些继续坚持不共享的人之间找到自己的位置,同时还要努力开创自己的职业生涯。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: One key challenge facing young scientists is how to be open without becoming scientifically vulnerable.
They must determine the risk of jeopardizing a job offer or a collaboration proposal from those who are wary of—or unfamiliar with—open science.

And they must learn how to capitalize on the movement's benefits, such as opportunities for more citations and a way to build a reputation without the need for conventional metrics, such as publication in high-impact journals.

passage.translation: 年轻科学家面临的一个关键挑战是如何在保持开放的同时不使自己在科学上变得脆弱。他们必须判断是否会危及来自那些对开放科学持谨慎态度或不熟悉开放科学的人提供的工作机会或合作提议的风险。他们还必须学会如何利用这一运动的好处,例如获得更多引用的机会,以及无需依赖传统指标(如在高影响力期刊上发表论文)就能建立声誉的途径。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: Some fields have embraced open data more than others.
Researchers in psychology, a field rocked by findings of irreproducibility in the past few years, have been especially vocal supporters of the drive for more-open science.
A few psychology journals have created incentives to increase interest in reproducible science—for example, by affixing an 'open-data' badge to articles that clearly state where data are available.

According to social psychologist Brian Nosek, executive director of the Center for Open Science, the average data-sharing rate for the journal Psychological Science, which uses the badges, increased tenfold to 38% from 2013 to 2015.

passage.translation: 一些领域比其他领域更接受开放数据。心理学研究人员——这一领域在过去几年因不可重复性的发现而受到冲击——一直是推动更开放科学的特别积极的支持者。一些心理学期刊已经创建了激励措施来增加对可重复科学的兴趣——例如,在清楚说明数据可获取位置的文章上贴上"开放数据"徽章。据开放科学中心执行主任、社会心理学家Brian Nosek称,使用徽章的《心理科学》期刊的平均数据共享率从2013年到2015年增长了十倍,达到38%。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Funders, too, are increasingly adopting an open-data policy.
Several strongly encourage, and some require, a data-management plan that makes data available.
The US National Science Foundation is among these.
Some philanthropic(慈善的) funders, including the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation in Seattle, Washington, and the Wellcome Trust in London, also mandate open data from their grant recipients.

passage.translation: 资助机构也越来越多地采用开放数据政策。一些机构强烈鼓励,有些则要求提供使数据可获取的数据管理计划。美国国家科学基金会就是其中之一。一些慈善资助机构,包括华盛顿州西雅图的比尔及梅琳达·盖茨基金会和伦敦的惠康基金会,也强制要求其受资助者开放数据。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: But many young researchers, especially those who have not been mentored in open science, are uncertain about whether to share or to stay private.
Graduate students and postdocs, who often are working on their lab head's grant, may have no choice if their supervisor or another senior colleague opposes sharing.

passage.translation: 但许多年轻研究人员,尤其是那些没有接受过开放科学指导的研究人员,对是否应该共享或保持私密感到不确定。研究生和博士后通常从事实验室负责人的资助项目,如果他们的导师或其他资深同事反对共享,他们可能别无选择。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: Some fear that the potential impact of sharing is too high, especially at the early stages of a career.
"Everybody has a scary story about someone getting scooped(被抢先)," says New York University astronomer David Hogg.
Those fears may be a factor in a lingering hesitation to share data even when publishing in journals that mandate it.

passage.translation: 一些人担心共享的潜在影响太大,尤其是在职业生涯的早期阶段。"每个人都有关于某人被抢先的可怕故事,"纽约大学天文学家David Hogg说。这些担忧可能是即使在要求数据共享的期刊上发表论文时仍犹豫不决的一个因素。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Researchers at small labs or at institutions focused on teaching arguably have the most to lose when sharing hard-won data.
"With my institution and teaching load, I don't have postdocs and grad students," says Terry McGlynn, a tropical biologist at California State University, Dominguez Hills.
"The stakes are higher to share data because it's a bigger fraction of what's happening in my lab."

passage.translation: 在小型实验室或以教学为重点的机构的研究人员在共享来之不易的数据时可以说损失最大。"以我的机构和教学负荷,我没有博士后和研究生,"加州州立大学多明格斯山分校的热带生物学家Terry McGlynn说。"共享数据的风险更高,因为这在我实验室正在进行的工作中占更大比例。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Researchers also point to the time sink that is involved in preparing data for others to view.
Once the data and associated materials appear in a repository(存储库), answering questions and handling complaints can take many hours.

passage.translation: 研究人员还指出,准备数据供他人查看所需的时间投入。一旦数据和相关材料出现在存储库中,回答问题和处理投诉可能需要许多小时。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: The time investment can present other problems.

In some cases, says data scientist Karthik Ram, it may be difficult for junior researchers to embrace openness when senior colleagues—many of whom head selection and promotion committees—might ridicule what they may view as misplaced energies.
"I've heard this recently—that embracing the idea of open data and code makes traditional academics uncomfortable," says Ram.
"The concern seems to be that open advocates don't spend their time being as productive as possible."

passage.translation: 时间投入可能会带来其他问题。数据科学家Karthik Ram说,在某些情况下,当资深同事——其中许多人领导遴选和晋升委员会——可能嘲笑他们认为是精力错位的行为时,初级研究人员可能难以接受开放性。"我最近听到这样的说法——接受开放数据和代码的理念会让传统学者感到不舒服,"Ram说。"担忧似乎是开放倡导者没有将时间花在尽可能提高生产力上。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: An open-science stance can also add complexity to a collaboration.
Kate Ratliff, who studies social attitudes at the University of Florida, Gainesville, says that it can seem as if there are two camps in a field—those who care about open science and those who don't.
"There's a new area to navigate—'Are you cool with the fact that I'll want to make the data open?'—when talking with somebody about an interesting research idea," she says.

passage.translation: 开放科学立场也可能给合作增加复杂性。在佛罗里达大学盖恩斯维尔分校研究社会态度的Kate Ratliff说,一个领域似乎可以分为两个阵营——关心开放科学的人和不关心的人。"在与某人讨论一个有趣的研究想法时,需要应对一个新领域——'你能接受我想要公开数据这一事实吗?'"她说。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: Despite complications and concerns, the upsides of sharing can be significant.
For example, when information is uploaded to a repository, a digital object identifier (DOI) is assigned.
Scientists can use a DOI to publish each step of the research life cycle, not just the final paper.
In so doing, they can potentially get three citations—one each for the data and software, in addition to the paper itself.
And although some say that citations for software or data have little currency in academia, they can have other benefits.

passage.translation: 尽管存在复杂性和担忧,共享的好处可能是显著的。例如,当信息上传到存储库时,会分配一个数字对象标识符(DOI)。科学家可以使用DOI发布研究生命周期的每个步骤,而不仅仅是最终论文。通过这样做,他们可能获得三次引用——数据和软件各一次,加上论文本身一次。尽管有人说软件或数据的引用在学术界价值不大,但它们可以带来其他好处。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: Many advocates think that transparent data procedures with a data and time stamp will protect scientists from being scooped.

"This is the sweet spot between sharing and getting credit for it, while discouraging plagiarism(剽窃)," says Ivo Grigorov, a project coordinator at the National Institute of Aquatic Resources Research Secretariat in Charlottenlund, Denmark.
Hogg says that scooping is less of a problem than many think.
"The two cases I'm familiar with didn't involve open data or code," he says.

passage.translation: 许多倡导者认为,带有数据和时间戳的透明数据程序将保护科学家免于被抢先。"这是在共享和获得认可之间的最佳平衡点,同时阻止剽窃,"丹麦夏洛滕隆国家水产资源研究秘书处的项目协调员Ivo Grigorov说。Hogg说,抢先发表的问题比许多人想象的要少。"我熟悉的两个案例都不涉及开放数据或代码,"他说。

passage.label: N

sentences.text: Open science also offers junior researchers the chance to level the playing field by gaining better access to crucial data.

Ross Mounce, a postdoc studying evolutionary biology at the University of Cambridge, UK, is a vocal champion of open science, partly because his fossil-based research depends on access to others' data.
He says that more openness in science could help to discourage what some perceive as a common practice of shutting out early-career scientists' requests for data.

passage.translation: 开放科学还为初级研究人员提供了通过更好地获取关键数据来公平竞争的机会。英国剑桥大学研究进化生物学的博士后Ross Mounce是开放科学的积极倡导者,部分原因是他基于化石的研究依赖于获取他人的数据。他说,科学领域更大的开放性可能有助于阻止一些人认为的常见做法,即拒绝早期职业科学家的数据请求。

passage.label: O

sentences.text: Communication also helps for those who worry about jeopardizing a collaboration, he says.
Concerns about open science should be discussed at the outset of a study.
"Whenever you start a project with someone, you have to establish a clear understanding of expectations for who owns the data, at what point they go public and who can do what with them," he says.

passage.translation: 他说,对于那些担心危及合作的人来说,沟通也有帮助。关于开放科学的担忧应该在研究开始时就讨论。"每当你与某人开始一个项目时,你必须就谁拥有数据、数据在什么时候公开以及谁可以用它们做什么等期望建立清晰的理解,"他说。

passage.label: P

sentences.text: In the end, sharing data, software and materials with colleagues can help an early-career researcher to gain recognition—a crucial component of success.
"The thing you are searching for is reputation," says Titus Brown, a genomics(基因组学) researcher at the University of California, Davis.
"To get grants and jobs, you have to be relevant and achieve some level of public recognition.
Anything you do that advances your presence—especially in a larger sphere, outside the communities you know—is a net win."

passage.translation: 最终,与同事共享数据、软件和材料可以帮助早期职业研究人员获得认可——这是成功的关键组成部分。"你所寻求的是声誉,"加州大学戴维斯分校的基因组学研究员Titus Brown说。"要获得资助和工作,你必须保持相关性并达到一定程度的公众认可。你所做的任何提升你存在感的事情——尤其是在更大范围内,在你所知社群之外——都是净收益。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: Astronomer David Hogg doesn't think scooping is as serious a problem as generally thought.
questions.explanation:
**答案** M 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
天文学家David Hogg认为抢先发表问题并不像人们普遍认为的那样严重。
**锚点** 专名 David Hogg + scooping
**定位** Hogg 说，被抢先并不像很多人认为的那样严重。他说：我熟悉的那两起案例都与开放数据或代码无关。
**改写** Astronomer David Hogg ↔ Hogg专名原样复现doesn't think scooping is as serious a problem as generally thought ↔scooping is less of a problem than many think比较句式的同义改写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
G G 段 Everybody has a scary story about someone getting scooped 是借 Hogg之口转述他人恐惧，与陈述句 doesn't think scooping is as serious a problem as generally thought 的弱化态度方向相反，不是源头段。Everybody has a scary story about someone getting scooped
questions.quote: Hogg says that scooping is less of a problem than many think. "The two cases I'm familiar with didn't involve open data or code," he says.

questions.prompt: Some researchers are hesitant to make their data public for fear that others might publish something similar before them.
questions.explanation:
**答案** G 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
一些研究人员不愿公开他们的数据,担心其他人可能会在他们之前发表类似的内容。
**锚点** 怕别人抢先发表
**定位** 纽约大学天文学家 David Hogg 说，每个人都有一个关于别人被抢先的可怕故事。这些恐惧可能是即使在强制要求分享数据的期刊上发表论文也仍然犹豫不决的一个原因。
**改写** hesitant to make their data public ↔ a lingering hesitation to share data形容词转名词的同义替换for fear that others might publish something similar before them ↔Those fears may be a factor in a lingering hesitation to share data用术语 scooped 概括短语
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
M M 段 scooping is less of a problem than many think 是在弱化 scoop 引发的恐惧，与陈述句 for fear that others might publish something similar before them的 担忧 方向相反，因此不是源头段。scooping is less of a problem than many think
questions.quote: "Everybody has a scary story about someone getting scooped," says New York University astronomer David Hogg. Those fears may be a factor in a lingering hesitation to share data even when publishing in journals that mandate it.

questions.prompt: Some psychology journals have offered incentives to encourage authors to share their data.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
一些心理学期刊提供了激励措施以鼓励作者分享他们的数据。
**锚点** 心理学期刊 + 激励
**定位** 一些心理学期刊设立了激励机制以提升人们对可重复科学的兴趣——例如，给清楚说明数据出处的论文贴上一枚开放数据徽章。
**改写** Some psychology journals ↔ A few psychology journals数量词同义have offered incentives to encourage authors to share their data ↔have created incentives to increase interest in reproducible science—for example, by affixing an 'open-data' badge to articles that clearly state where data are available动词同义+例证支撑
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E E 段 Funders, too, are increasingly adopting an open-data policy 的主语是资助方，与题干 Some psychology journals 的主体不符。Funders, too, are increasingly adopting an open-data policy. Several strongly encourage, and some require, a data-management plan that makes data available.
questions.quote: A few psychology journals have created incentives to increase interest in reproducible science—for example, by affixing an 'open-data' badge to articles that clearly state where data are available.

questions.prompt: There is a growing demand in the science community that research data be open to the public.
questions.explanation:
**答案** A 段（弱锚点）
**题目译文**
科学界对研究数据向公众开放的要求日益增长。
**锚点** 科学界对数据公开的呼声日增
**定位** 这是一场势头持续增强的运动：呼吁公开并透明化研究数据、软件代码和实验方法。开放精神正在科学界获得认可，倡导者称这是应对科研可重复性危机的唯一途径。
**改写** a growing demand ↔ a movement building steady momentum增长趋势的同义替换in the science community ↔ in the science community短语原样复现that research data be open to the public ↔a call to make research data, software code and experimental methods publicly available公开化诉求的同义改写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段 scientists disagree about how much and when they should share data 的核心是分歧，与陈述句 a growing demand 的 增长共识 焦点不同，不是源头段。scientists disagree about how much and when they should share data, and they debate whether sharing it is more likely to accelerate science and make it more robust
questions.quote: It is a movement building steady momentum: a call to make research data, software code and experimental methods publicly available and transparent. A spirit of openness is gaining acceptance in the science community, and is the only way, say advocates, to address a 'crisis' in science whereby too few findings are successfully reproduced.

questions.prompt: Sharing data offers early-career researchers the chance to build a certain level of reputation.
questions.explanation:
**答案** P 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
数据共享为早期职业研究人员提供了建立一定声誉水平的机会。
**锚点** early-career + reputation
**定位** 归根结底，与同行分享数据、软件和材料能帮助早期生涯研究者获得认可——这是成功的一项关键组成部分。
**改写** Sharing data ↔ sharing data, software and materials with colleagues宾语上位简化offers early-career researchers the chance to build a certain level of reputation ↔can help an early-career researcher to gain recognition—a crucial component of success动词+名词的双重同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
N N 段 level the playing field by gaining better access to crucial data 谈的是 拿到数据 的机会，与陈述句 build a certain level of reputation 不同方向。Open science also offers junior researchers the chance to level the playing field by gaining better access to crucial data.
questions.quote: In the end, sharing data, software and materials with colleagues can help an early-career researcher to gain recognition—a crucial component of success.

questions.prompt: Data sharing enables scientists to publish each step of their research work, thus leading to more citations.
questions.explanation:
**答案** L 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
数据共享使科学家能够发表他们研究工作的每个步骤,从而获得更多引用。
**锚点** 每一步发布 + more citations
**定位** 例如，当信息上传到存储库时，会被分配一个数字对象标识符（DOI）。科学家可以用 DOI为研究生命周期的每一步发表成果，而不仅是最终论文。这样他们最多可以获得三次引用——数据和软件各一次，加上论文本身一次。
**改写** publish each step of their research work ↔ publish each step of the research life cycle短语原样复现thus leading to more citations ↔they can potentially get three citations—one each for the data and software, in addition to the paper itself数字具体化为 more
questions.quote: For example, when information is uploaded to a repository, a digital object identifier (DOI) is assigned. Scientists can use a DOI to publish each step of the research life cycle, not just the final paper. In so doing, they can potentially get three citations—one each for the data and software, in addition to the paper itself.

questions.prompt: Scientists hold different opinions about the extent and timing of data sharing.
questions.explanation:
**答案** B 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
科学家们对数据共享的范围和时机持有不同意见。
**锚点** 对分享 extent 与 timing 意见不一
**定位** 另一方面，科学家们对应该分享多少以及何时分享意见不一，并就分享究竟更可能加速科学并使其更稳健、还是引入漏洞与问题展开争论。
**改写** Scientists hold different opinions ↔ scientists disagree态度同义about the extent and timing of data sharing ↔about how much and when they should share data疑问词名词化
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
K K 段 two camps in a field—those who care about open science and those who don't 是合作意愿层面的分歧，与陈述句关心的 extent and timing 不在一个维度上。two camps in a field—those who care about open science and those who don't
questions.quote: On the other hand, scientists disagree about how much and when they should share data, and they debate whether sharing it is more likely to accelerate science and make it more robust, or to introduce vulnerabilities and problems.

questions.prompt: Potential problems related to data sharing should be made known to and discussed by all participants at the beginning of a joint research project.
questions.explanation:
**答案** O 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
与数据共享相关的潜在问题应在联合研究项目开始时让所有参与者知晓并进行讨论。
**锚点** 项目开头就讨论问题
**定位** 对开放科学的担忧应在研究一开始就讨论。他说：每当你和别人启动一个项目时，都必须就数据归属、何时公开、谁可以做什么形成清晰的共识。
**改写** Potential problems related to data sharing ↔ Concerns about open science上位概括同义made known to and discussed by all participants ↔Whenever you start a project with someone, you have to establish a clear understanding of expectations for who owns the data, at what point they go public and who can do what with them讨论参与方的同义重构at the beginning of a joint research project ↔ at the outset of a study时间状语同义
questions.quote: Concerns about open science should be discussed at the outset of a study. "Whenever you start a project with someone, you have to establish a clear understanding of expectations for who owns the data, at what point they go public and who can do what with them," he says.

questions.prompt: Sharing data and handling data-related issues can be time-consuming.
questions.explanation:
**答案** I 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
共享数据和处理与数据相关的问题可能很耗时。
**锚点** 分享与处理数据耗时
**定位** 研究者们还指出，为他人查看而准备数据是一种时间消耗。一旦数据与相关材料出现在存储库中，回答问题和处理投诉可能要花很多个小时。
**改写** Sharing data ↔ preparing data for others to view动作过程同义handling data-related issues ↔ answering questions and handling complaints处理事项的同义具体化can be time-consuming ↔ the time sink can take many hours耗时的同义表达
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
J J 段 The time investment can present other problems 引出的是 同行偏见，与陈述句 can be time-consuming 的焦点 时间本身 不同，因此不是源头段。The time investment can present other problems
questions.quote: Researchers also point to the time sink that is involved in preparing data for others to view. Once the data and associated materials appear in a repository, answering questions and handling complaints can take many hours.

questions.prompt: Junior researchers may have no say when it comes to sharing data.
questions.explanation:
**答案** F 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
初级研究人员在数据共享方面可能没有发言权。
**锚点** Junior researchers 无话语权
**定位** 研究生和博士后通常在他们实验室负责人的项目经费下工作，如果其导师或另一位高级同事反对分享，他们可能没有选择。
**改写** Junior researchers ↔ Graduate students and postdocs上位词对下位群体may have no say when it comes to sharing data ↔may have no choice if their supervisor or another senior colleague opposes sharing话语权与选择权的同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
C C 段 They must determine the risk of jeopardizing a job offer or a collaboration proposal 主语是青年学者自己在权衡，与陈述句 no say 的 被动 不同方向。They must determine the risk of jeopardizing a job offer or a collaboration proposal from those who are wary of—or unfamiliar with—open science.
questions.quote: Graduate students and postdocs, who often are working on their lab head's grant, may have no choice if their supervisor or another senior colleague opposes sharing.

title: Who's really addicting you to Technology?

passage.label: A

sentences.text: "Nearly everyone I know is addicted in some measure to the internet," wrote Tony Schwartz in The New York Times.
It's a common complaint these days.
A steady stream of similar headlines accuses the Net and its offspring apps, social media sites and online games of addicting us to distraction.

passage.translation: 托尼·施瓦茨在《纽约时报》上写道："我认识的几乎每个人都在某种程度上沉迷于互联网。"这是当今常见的抱怨。源源不断的类似标题指责互联网及其衍生应用程序、社交媒体网站和网络游戏使我们沉迷于分心。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: There's little doubt that nearly everyone who comes in contact with the Net has difficulty disconnecting.
Many of us, like Schwartz, struggle to stay focused on tasks that require more concentration than it takes to post a status update.
As one person ironically put it in the comments section of Schwartz's online article, "As I was reading this very excellent article, I stopped at least half a dozen times to check my email."

passage.translation: 毫无疑问,几乎每个接触互联网的人都难以断开连接。我们中的许多人,像施瓦茨一样,努力专注于那些比发布状态更新需要更多专注力的任务。正如一个人在施瓦茨网络文章的评论区讽刺地说的那样:"当我阅读这篇非常精彩的文章时,我至少停下来六次查看我的电子邮件。"

passage.label: C

sentences.text: There's something different about this technology: it is both invasive and persuasive.
But who's at fault for its overuse?
To find solutions, it's important to understand what we're dealing with.
There are four parties conspiring to keep you connected: the tech, your boss, your friends and you.

passage.translation: 这项技术有些不同:它既具侵入性又具说服力。但谁该为其过度使用负责?要找到解决方案,重要的是了解我们正在处理什么。有四方共谋让你保持连接:技术、你的老板、你的朋友和你自己。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: The technologies themselves and their makers are the easiest suspects to blame for our diminishing attention spans.
Nicholas Carr, author of The Shallows: what the internet is doing to our brains, wrote, "The Net is designed to be an interruption system, a machine geared to dividing attention."

passage.translation: 技术本身及其制造者是最容易为我们注意力持续时间缩短而受到指责的对象。《浅薄:互联网如何毒化我们的大脑》的作者尼古拉斯·卡尔写道:"互联网被设计成一个中断系统,一台旨在分散注意力的机器。"

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Online services like Facebook, Twitter and the like, are called out as masters of manipulation—making products so good that people can't stop using them.
After studying these products for several years, I wrote a book about how they do it.
I learned it all starts with the business model.
Since these services rely on advertising revenue, the more frequently you use them, the more money they make.
It's no wonder these companies employ teams of people focused on engineering their services to be as engaging as possible.
These products aren't habit-forming by chance; it's by design.
They have an incentive to keep us hooked.

passage.translation: Facebook、Twitter等网络服务被称为操纵大师——制造出如此优秀的产品以至于人们无法停止使用它们。在研究这些产品数年后,我写了一本关于它们如何做到这一点的书。我了解到这一切都始于商业模式。由于这些服务依赖广告收入,你使用它们的频率越高,它们赚的钱就越多。难怪这些公司雇佣专门的团队致力于将他们的服务设计得尽可能吸引人。这些产品不是偶然形成习惯的;而是有意设计的。它们有动机让我们上钩。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: However, as good as these services are, there are simple steps we can take to keep them at bay.
For example, we can change how often we receive the distracting notifications that trigger our urge to check.

According to Adam Marchick, CEO of mobile marketing company Kahuna, less than 15 percent of smartphone users ever bother to adjust their notification settings—meaning the remaining 85 percent of us default to the app makers' every preset trigger.
Google and Apple have made it far too difficult to adjust these settings so it's up to us to take steps to ensure we set these triggers to suit our own needs, not the needs of the app makers.

passage.translation: 然而,尽管这些服务很好,我们可以采取简单的步骤来控制它们。例如,我们可以改变接收分散注意力的通知的频率,这些通知会触发我们查看的冲动。根据移动营销公司Kahuna的首席执行官亚当·马奇克的说法,只有不到15%的智能手机用户费心调整他们的通知设置——这意味着我们其余85%的人默认接受应用程序制造商的每个预设触发器。Google和Apple让调整这些设置变得过于困难,因此我们需要采取措施确保我们设置这些触发器以满足我们自己的需求,而不是应用程序制造商的需求。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: While companies like Facebook harvest attention to generate revenue from advertisers, other technologies have no such agenda.
Take email, for example.
This system couldn't care less how often you use it.
Yet to many, email is the most habit-forming medium of all.
We check email at all hours of the day—we're obsessed.
But why?
Because that's what the boss wants.
For almost all white-collar jobs, email is the primary tool of corporate communication.
A slow response to a message could hurt not only your reputation but also your livelihood.

passage.translation: 虽然像Facebook这样的公司收集注意力以从广告商那里产生收入,但其他技术没有这样的议程。以电子邮件为例。这个系统根本不在乎你多久使用一次它。然而对许多人来说,电子邮件是最容易形成习惯的媒介。我们在一天中的所有时间查看电子邮件——我们对此着迷。但为什么?因为这是老板想要的。对于几乎所有白领工作,电子邮件是企业沟通的主要工具。对消息的缓慢回应不仅可能损害你的声誉,还可能损害你的生计。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Your friends are also responsible.
Think about this familiar scene.
People gathered around a table, enjoying food and each other's company.
There's laughter and a bit of kidding.
Then, during an interval in the conversation, someone takes out their phone to check who knows what.
Barely anyone notices and no one says a thing.

passage.translation: 你的朋友也有责任。想想这个熟悉的场景。人们围坐在桌子旁,享受美食和彼此的陪伴。有笑声和一些玩笑。然后,在谈话间隙,有人拿出手机查看天知道什么。几乎没有人注意到,也没有人说什么。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Now imagine the same dinner, but instead of checking their phone, the person belches(打嗝) loudly.
Everyone notices.
Unless the meal takes place in a beer house, this is considered bad manners.
The impolite act violates the basic rules of etiquette.
One has to wonder: why don't we apply the same social norms to checking phones during meals, meetings and conversations as we do to other antisocial behaviors?
Somehow, we accept it and say nothing when someone offends.

passage.translation: 现在想象同样的晚餐,但这个人不是查看手机,而是大声打嗝。每个人都注意到了。除非这顿饭是在啤酒屋进行的,否则这被认为是不礼貌的。这种不礼貌的行为违反了礼仪的基本规则。人们不得不想:为什么我们不像对待其他反社会行为那样,对在用餐、会议和谈话期间查看手机应用相同的社会规范?不知何故,我们接受它,当有人冒犯时什么也不说。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: The reality is taking one's phone out at the wrong time is worse than belching because, unlike other minor offenses, checking tech is contagious.
Once one person looks at their phone, other people feel compelled to do the same, starting a chain reaction.
The more people are on their phones, the fewer people are talking until finally you are the only one left not reading email or checking Twitter.
From a societal perspective, phone checking is less like belching in public and more like another bad habit.
Our phones are like cigarettes—something to do when we're anxious, bored or when our fingers need something to toy with.
Seeing others enjoy a smoke, or sneak a quick glance, is too tempting to resist and soon everyone is doing it.

passage.translation: 现实是在错误的时间拿出手机比打嗝更糟糕,因为与其他轻微冒犯不同,查看科技产品是会传染的。一旦一个人看他们的手机,其他人就会感到被迫做同样的事情,引发连锁反应。越多人在看手机,说话的人就越少,直到最后你是唯一一个不读电子邮件或查看Twitter的人。从社会角度来看,查看手机不像在公共场合打嗝,而更像另一个坏习惯。我们的手机就像香烟——当我们焦虑、无聊或当我们的手指需要玩点什么时可以做的事情。看到别人享受一支烟,或偷偷瞥一眼,太诱人而难以抗拒,很快每个人都在这样做。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: The technology, your boss, and your friends, all influence how often you find yourself using (or overusing) these gadgets.
But there's still someone who deserves scrutiny—the person holding the phone.

passage.translation: 技术、你的老板和你的朋友,都影响你发现自己使用(或过度使用)这些小工具的频率。但仍有一个人值得仔细审查——拿着手机的人。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: I have a confession.
Even though I study habit-forming technology for a living, disconnecting is not easy for me.
I'm online far more than I'd like.
Like Schwartz and so many others, I often find myself distracted and off task.
I wanted to know why so I began self-monitoring to try to understand my behavior.
That's when I discovered an uncomfortable truth.
I use technology as an escape.
When I'm doing something I'd rather not do, or when I'm someplace I'd rather not be, I use my phone to port myself elsewhere.
I found that this ability to instantly shift my attention was often a good thing, like when passing time on public transportation.
But frequently my tech use was not so benign.
When I faced difficult work, like thinking through an article idea or editing the same draft for the hundredth time, for example, a more sinister screen would draw me in.
I could easily escape discomfort, temporarily, by answering emails or browsing the web under the pretense of so-called "research."
Though I desperately wanted to lay blame elsewhere, I finally had to admit that my bad habits had less to do with new-age technology and more to do with old-fashioned procrastination( 拖

passage.translation: 延).我有一个坦白。尽管我以研究习惯形成技术为生,但断开连接对我来说并不容易。我上网的时间远远超过我想要的。像施瓦茨和许多其他人一样,我经常发现自己分心和偏离任务。我想知道为什么,所以我开始自我监控试图理解我的行为。那时我发现了一个令人不安的事实。我使用技术作为一种逃避。当我做我不想做的事情,或者当我在我不想待的地方时,我用我的手机把自己转移到别处。我发现这种立即转移注意力的能力通常是一件好事,比如在公共交通工具上打发时间。但我使用科技的频率并不总是那么良性。当我面对困难的工作时,比如思考一个文章想法或第一百次编辑同一份草稿,例如,一个更邪恶的屏幕会吸引我。我可以轻松地暂时逃避不适,通过以所谓"研究"为借口回复电子邮件或浏览网页。尽管我迫切想把责任归咎于别处,但我最终不得不承认,我的坏习惯与新时代技术的关系不大,而与老式的拖延症的关系更大。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: It's easy to blame technology for being so distracting, but distraction is nothing new.
Aristotle and Socrates debated nature of "akrasia"—our tendency to do things against our interests.
If we're honest with ourselves, tech is just another way to occupy our time and minds.
If we weren't on our devices, we'd likely do something similarly unproductive.

passage.translation: 责怪技术如此分散注意力很容易,但分心并不新鲜。亚里士多德和苏格拉底辩论过"akrasia"的本质——我们违背自己利益行事的倾向。如果我们对自己诚实,科技只是占据我们时间和思想的另一种方式。如果我们不在设备上,我们可能会做一些同样无生产力的事情。

passage.label: N

sentences.text: Personal technology is indeed more engaging than ever, and there's no doubt companies are engineering their products and services to be more compelling and attractive.
But would we want it any other way?
The intended result of making something better is that people use it more.
That's not necessarily a problem, that's progress.

passage.translation: 个人技术确实比以往任何时候都更吸引人,毫无疑问,公司正在设计他们的产品和服务使其更引人注目和更有吸引力。但我们会想要其他方式吗?让某样东西变得更好的预期结果是人们更多地使用它。这不一定是问题,那是进步。

passage.label: O

sentences.text: These improvements don't mean we shouldn't attempt to control our use of technology.
In order to make sure it doesn't control us, we should come to terms with the fact that it's more than the technology itself that's responsible for our habits.
Our workplace culture, social norms and individual behaviors all play a part.
To put technology in its place, we must be conscious not only of how technology is changing, but also of how it is changing us.

passage.translation: 这些改进并不意味着我们不应该试图控制我们对技术的使用。为了确保它不控制我们,我们应该接受这样一个事实:不仅仅是技术本身对我们的习惯负责。我们的工作场所文化、社会规范和个人行为都发挥作用。为了让技术各就各位,我们必须不仅意识到技术是如何变化的,还要意识到它是如何改变我们的。
