E they rely on advertising revenue 与 required by their employers 不是同一归因。Since these services rely on advertising revenue, the more frequently you use them, the more money they make
questions.quote: We check email at all hours of the day—we're obsessed. But why? Because that's what the boss wants. For almost all white-collar jobs, email is the primary tool of corporate communication.

title: It is the season for some frantic last-minute…

sentences.text: It is the season for some frantic last-minute math—across the country, employees of all stripes are counting backward in an attempt to figure out just how much paid time-off they have left in their reserves.

More of them, though, will skip those calculations altogether and just power through the holidays into 2017: More than half of American workers don't use up all of their allotted vacation days each year.

passage.translation: 现在正是疯狂进行最后时刻计算的季节——全国各地，各行各业的员工都在倒数计算，试图弄清楚自己还剩下多少带薪休假时间。然而，更多的人会完全跳过这些计算，直接度过假期进入2017年：每年超过半数的美国员工都没有用完他们所有的法定休假天数。

sentences.text: Not so long ago, people would have turned up their noses at that kind of dedication to the job.

As marketing professors Silvia Bellezza, Neeru Paharia, and Anat Keinan recently explained in Harvard Business Review (HBR), leisure time was once seen as an indicator of high social status, something attainable only for those at the top.
Since the middle of the 20th century, though, things have turned the opposite way—these days, punishing hours at your desk, rather than days off, are seen as the mark of someone important.

passage.translation: 不久以前，人们还会对这种对工作的投入嗤之以鼻。正如市场营销学教授Silvia Bellezza、Neeru Paharia和Anat Keinan最近在《哈佛商业评论》(HBR)中解释的那样,闲暇时间曾被视为高社会地位的标志,只有那些处于顶层的人才能拥有。然而,自20世纪中叶以来,情况发生了相反的转变——如今,在办公桌前度过艰苦的工作时间,而非休假,被视为重要人物的标志。

sentences.text: In a series of several experiments, the researchers illustrated just how much we've come to admire busyness, or at least the appearance of it.

Volunteers read two passages, one about a man who led a life of leisure and another about a man who was over-worked and over-scheduled; when asked to determine which of the two had a higher social status, the majority of the participants said the latter.

The same held true for people who used products that implied they were short on time: In one experiment, for example, customers of the grocery-delivery service Peapod were seen as of higher status than people who shopped at grocery stores that were equally expensive; in another, people wearing wireless headphones were considered further up on the social ladder than those wearing regular headphones, even when both were just used to listen to music.

passage.translation: 在一系列实验中,研究人员展示了我们有多么推崇忙碌,或者至少是忙碌的表象。志愿者阅读了两段文字,一段是关于一个过着闲适生活的男人,另一段是关于一个过度工作、日程安排过满的男人;当被要求判断两人中谁的社会地位更高时,大多数参与者选择了后者。对于使用暗示他们时间紧张的产品的人也是如此:例如,在一项实验中,杂货配送服务Peapod的顾客被认为比在同等昂贵的杂货店购物的人地位更高;在另一项实验中,佩戴无线耳机的人被认为比佩戴普通耳机的人在社会阶梯上更高,即使两者都只是用来听音乐。

sentences.text: In part, the authors wrote in HBR, this pattern may have to do with the way work itself has changed over the past several decades.

passage.translation: 作者在《哈佛商业评论》中写道,这种模式的部分原因可能与过去几十年工作本身的变化方式有关。

sentences.text: We think that the shift from leisure-as-status to busyness-as-status may be linked to the development of knowledge-intensive economics.

In such economies, individuals who possess the human capital characteristics that employers or clients value (e.g., competence and ambition) are expected to be in high demand and short supply on the job market.
Thus, by telling others that we are busy and working all the time, we are implicitly suggesting that we are sought after, which enhances our perceived status.

passage.translation: 我们认为,从闲暇即地位到忙碌即地位的转变可能与知识密集型经济的发展有关。在这样的经济体中,拥有雇主或客户看重的人力资本特征(如能力和抱负)的个人,预计在就业市场上会供不应求。因此,通过告诉别人我们很忙并且一直在工作,我们暗示自己是被追捧的,这提升了我们被感知的地位。

sentences.text: Even if you feel tempted to sacrifice your own vacation days for fake busyness, though, at least consider leaving your weekends unscheduled.
It's for your own good.

passage.translation: 即使你想为虚假的忙碌牺牲自己的假期,至少也要考虑让周末不被安排满。这是为了你自己好。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What do most employees plan to do towards the end of the year?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
大多数员工计划在年底做什么?
A) 去度假。
B) 继续工作。
C) 为明年设定一个目标。
D) 回顾这一年的成就。
**判型** What do most employees plan to do towards the end of the year? 问的是一个具体行为事实，没有 infer/suggest/imply，属于典型的事实细节询问。
**拆句** 题干主干 What do most employees plan to do 是 do 引导的疑问句，towards the end of the year 是时间状语后置，结构平铺直叙、无陷阱。
**定位** 不过更多的员工会干脆跳过这些核算，硬扛着把节假日推进到 2017 年：超过一半的美国员工每年并没有用完所有获得的休假日。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反Go for a vacation 与定位句 don't use up all of their allotted vacation days 的语义正相反——原文恰恰是说大多数人不去度假。
B) ✓ 正确power through the holidays into 2017 ↔ Keep on working don't use up all of their allotted vacation days↔ Keep on working预判要求 "年末继续工作"，Keep on working 是这一语义最直接、最不绕弯的表述。
C) 无中生有Set an objective for next year 提到的 "为明年定目标" 在原文中没有任何对应——原文只说算剩多少假、然后继续干活，没说任何制定计划的事。
D) 无中生有Review the year's achievements 谈的是 "年终回顾成绩"，原文只在算休假天数（math），从未涉及业绩盘点。
questions.quote: More of them, though, will skip those calculations altogether and just power through the holidays into 2017: More than half of American workers don't use up all of their allotted vacation days each year.

options.text: Go for a vacation.
Keep on working.
Set an objective for next year.
Review the year's achievements.

questions.prompt: How would people view dedication to work in the past?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
过去人们会如何看待对工作的投入?
A) 他们会认为这是理所当然的事。
B) 他们会认为这是成功的必要条件。
C) 他们会对此嗤之以鼻。
D) 他们会认为这是商人的伎俩。
**判型** How would people view dedication to work in the past? 问的是过去人们对一件具体事情的看法，是可在原文找到出处的事实细节。
**拆句** How would people view dedication to work in the past? 中 would 表过去习惯，view是及物动词，宾语 dedication to work 后接时间状语，无难点。
**定位** 不久以前，人们对那种对工作的过度投入是嗤之以鼻的。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反regard it as a matter of course 表示 "视为理所当然"，意味着被默认接受；但定位句turned up their noses at 表达的是嗤之以鼻、不接受。
B) 无中生有consider it a must for success 说过去把忙工作视作成功必经之路；原文从未涉及success / necessary 这一组语义。
C) ✓ 正确turned up their noses at ↔ look upon it with contempt预判要 "看不起"，contempt 是英语里最直接的 "鄙视"，C 是唯一与定位句负面色彩对应的选项。
D) 无中生有deem it a trick of businessmen 说过去把忙工作视作商人的把戏；原文既没出现businessmen，也没把这种 dedication 归为任何 trick。
questions.quote: Not so long ago, people would have turned up their noses at that kind of dedication to the job.

options.text: They would regard it as a matter of course.
They would consider it a must for success.
They would look upon it with contempt.
They would deem it a trick of businessmen.

questions.prompt: What did the researchers find through a series of experiments?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
研究人员通过一系列实验发现了什么?
A) 一个人显得越忙碌,就越能赢得尊重。
B) 一个人工作得越多,就越感到被剥削。
C) 一个人拥有的知识越多,就会越有能力。
D) 一个人的地位越高,享受的假期时间就越多。
**判型** What did the researchers find through a series of experiments? 问的是研究者发现的具体结论，是事实型细节。
**拆句** 主句 What did the researchers find 是一般疑问句的特殊疑问形式，through a series of experiments 是方式状语，无障碍。
**定位** 在一系列实验中，研究者们展示了我们已经多么推崇忙碌，至少是推崇忙碌的外在表现。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确we've come to admire busyness, or at least the appearance of it ↔The busier one appears, the more respect one earns customers of the grocery-delivery service Peapod were seen as of higher status ↔The busier one appears, the more respect one earns the + 比较级，the + 比较级结构精准捕捉到原文 "程度越深→社会评价越高" 的因果，且 "appears" 一词精确对应 the appearance of it——这种对 appearance 的精准吸收是 A 优于其他选项的关键。
B) 无中生有The more one works, the more one feels exploited 引入 "被剥削感"——原文从未涉及任何 exploitation 类负面情绪，反而强调忙碌带来正面评价。
C) 答非所问The more knowledge one has, the more competent one will be 谈知识与能力的关系——这是后文 Q54 的话题，不是本题实验的发现。
D) 与原文相反The higher one's status, the more vacation time one will enjoy 把 "地位与休假" 正向关联——但原文实验恰恰说 "高地位者反而看起来更忙、休假更少"。
questions.quote: In a series of several experiments, the researchers illustrated just how much we've come to admire busyness, or at least the appearance of it.

options.text: The busier one appears, the more respect one earns.
The more one works, the more one feels exploited.
The more knowledge one has, the more competent one will be.
The higher one's status, the more vacation time one will enjoy.

questions.prompt: What may account for the change of people's attitude towards being busy?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
什么可以解释人们对忙碌态度的转变?
A) 现代社会快节奏的生活。
B) 就业市场的激烈竞争。
C) 计算机技术的广泛应用。
D) 知识在现代经济中的作用。
**判型** What may account for the change of people's attitude towards being busy? 问的是变化的具体原因，原因可在原文找到出处，不必跨段推理。
**拆句** 主干 What may account for the change，of people's attitude 与 towards being busy是两层后置定语，逐层修饰 change，需注意修饰链不要断在 attitude 上。
**定位** 我们认为，地位象征从闲暇到忙碌的转变，可能与知识密集型经济的发展有关。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有The fast pace of life in modern society 谈 "现代生活节奏快"——原文并没有把忙碌归因于生活节奏，只归因于经济形态。
B) 偷换概念The fierce competition in the job market 谈的是 "就业市场的激烈竞争"——原文 in high demand and short supply on the job market 强调的是稀缺与抢手（卖方市场），不是 "竞争激烈"。
C) 无中生有The widespread use of computer technology 谈电脑技术普及——原文从未提及computer / technology 这一组概念。
D) ✓ 正确the development of knowledge-intensive economics ↔The role of knowledge in modern economy individuals who possess the human capital characteristics that employers or clients value (e.g., competence and ambition) are expected to be in high demand and short supply↔ The role of knowledge in modern economy预判要求原因是 "知识密集型经济"，四个选项里只有 D 把 knowledge 与 economy 直接绑定，其他选项要么换主词、要么换领域，均不与原文原因端对齐。
questions.quote: We think that the shift from leisure-as-status to busyness-as-status may be linked to the development of knowledge-intensive economics.

options.text: The fast pace of life in modern society.
The fierce competition in the job market.
The widespread use of computer technology.
The role of knowledge in modern economy.

questions.prompt: What does the author advise us to do at the end of the passage?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者在文章结尾建议我们做什么?
A) 合理安排时间以提高效率。
B) 以有意义的方式规划我们的周末。
C) 无论多忙都要找时间放松。
D) 避免在不忙的时候表现得很忙。
**判型** What does the author advise us to do at the end of the passage? 已指明位置在最后一段，问作者的具体建议，是单点细节询问而非全文主旨。
**拆句** What does the author advise us to do 主干清晰，at the end of the passage 是元信息状语，提示在文末找答案，本身不入选项语义。
**定位** 即便你想为 "假装忙碌" 牺牲自己的假期，那也至少考虑把周末空出来不安排事情。这是为你自己好。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Schedule our time properly for efficiency 提 "为效率合理安排时间"——原文从未把建议落在 "efficiency"，恰恰相反，作者建议把周末 unscheduled。
B) 偷换概念Plan our weekends in a meaningful way 表面与 weekends 词面相符，但"meaningful 地安排周末" 是给周末加内容，原文恰恰建议 leaving your weekends unscheduled —— 不安排。
C) ✓ 正确at least consider leaving your weekends unscheduled↔Find time to relax however busy we are Even if you feel tempted to sacrifice your own vacation days for fake busyness↔Find time to relax however busy we are预判要 "无论多忙都要给自己留休息时间"，C 用 however busy + find time to relax精准捕捉这一含义。
D) 答非所问Avoid appearing busy when we are not 与全文 "假装忙碌" 的批评是相关的，但末段作者的具体建议不是 "别装忙"，而是 "无论真忙假忙，至少给自己留休息"。
questions.quote: Even if you feel tempted to sacrifice your own vacation days for fake busyness, though, at least consider leaving your weekends unscheduled. It's for your own good.

options.text: Schedule our time properly for efficiency.
Plan our weekends in a meaningful way.
Find time to relax however busy we are.
Avoid appearing busy when we are not.

title: At the base of a mountain in Tanzania's…

sentences.text: At the base of a mountain in Tanzania's Gregory Rift, Lake Natron burns bright red, surrounded by the remains of animals that were unfortunate enough to fall into the salty water.
Bats, swallows and more are chemically preserved in the pose in which they perished, sealed in the deposits of sodium carbonate in the water.
The lake's landscape is bizarre and deadly—and made even more so by the fact that it's the place where nearly 75 percent of the world's flamingos(火烈⻦) are born.

passage.translation: 在坦桑尼亚Gregory Rift的一座山脚下，Natron湖呈现出鲜艳的红色，周围散落着不幸落入咸水中的动物遗骸。蝙蝠、燕子等动物以它们死亡时的姿态被化学方式保存下来，被封存在水中的碳酸钠沉积物里。这个湖泊的景观既怪异又致命——而更令人惊奇的是，这里是世界上近75%的火烈鸟的出生地。

sentences.text: The water is so corrosive that it can burn the skin and eyes of unadapted animals.
Flamingos, however, are the only species that actually makes life in the midst of all that death.
Once every three or four years, when conditions are right, the lake is covered with the pink birds as they stop flight to breed.

Three-quarters of the world's flamingos fly over from other salt lakes in the Rift Valley and nest on salt- crystal islands that appear when the water is at a specific level—too high and the birds can't build their nests, too low and predators can move briskly across the lake bed and attack.
When the water hits the right level, the baby birds are kept safe from predators by a corrosive ditch.

passage.translation: 湖水的腐蚀性极强,可以灼伤未适应动物的皮肤和眼睛。然而,火烈鸟是唯一真正在这片死亡之地生存的物种。每隔三到四年,当条件适宜时,湖面上就会布满粉红色的鸟群,它们停止飞行来此繁殖。世界上四分之三的火烈鸟从裂谷的其他盐湖飞来,在水位达到特定高度时出现的盐晶岛上筑巢——水位过高鸟类无法筑巢,水位过低捕食者就能快速穿越湖床发起攻击。当水位达到合适高度时,幼鸟就能通过腐蚀性的沟渠免受捕食者的侵害。

sentences.text: "Flamingos have evolved very leathery skin on their legs so they can tolerate the salt water," says David Harper, a professor at the University of Leicester.
"Humans cannot, and would die if their legs were exposed for any length of time."
So far this year, water levels have been too high for the flamingos to nest.

passage.translation: Leicester大学教授David Harper说:"火烈鸟的腿部皮肤已经进化得非常坚韧,所以它们能够忍受盐水。人类则不行,如果腿部长时间暴露在盐水中就会死亡。"今年到目前为止,水位一直过高,火烈鸟无法筑巢。

sentences.text: Some fish, too, have had limited success vacationing at the lake as less salty lagoons(泻湖) form on the outer edges from hot springs flowing into Lake Natron.
Three species of tilapia(罗非⻥) thrive there part-time.
"Fish have a refuge in the streams and can expand into the lagoons when the lake is low and the lagoons are separate," Harper said.
"All the lagoons join when the lake is high and fish must retreat to their stream refuges or die."
Otherwise, no fish are able to survive in the naturally toxic lake.

passage.translation: 一些鱼类在湖中"度假"也取得了有限的成功,因为流入Natron湖的温泉在外围边缘形成了含盐量较低的泻湖。三种罗非鱼在那里部分时间繁衍生息。Harper说:"鱼类在溪流中有避难所,当湖水水位低、泻湖相互分离时,它们可以扩展到泻湖中。当湖水水位高、所有泻湖汇合时,鱼类必须退回到溪流避难所,否则就会死亡。"除此之外,没有鱼类能够在这个天然有毒的湖泊中存活。

sentences.text: This unique ecosystem may soon be under pressure.
The Tanzanian government has once again started mining the lake for soda ash, used for making chemicals, glass and detergents.

Although the planned operation will be located more than 40 miles away, drawing the soda ash in through pipelines, conservationists worry it could still upset the natural water cycle and breeding grounds.
For now, though, life prevails—even in a lake that kills almost everything it touches.

passage.translation: 这个独特的生态系统可能很快就会面临压力。坦桑尼亚政府再次开始在该湖开采纯碱,用于制造化学品、玻璃和洗涤剂。尽管计划中的作业点将位于40多英里之外,通过管道抽取纯碱,但环保人士担心这仍可能扰乱自然水循环和繁殖地。不过,目前生命依然顽强存在——即使在一个几乎杀死所有接触到它的生物的湖泊中。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What can we learn about Lake Natron?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于Natron湖我们能了解到什么?
A) 对大多数动物来说它根本不适宜居住。
B) 外界对它知之甚少。
C) 它是多种鸟类的繁殖地。
D) 它为许多捕食者提供了理想的栖息地。
**判型** What can we learn about Lake Natron 没有 infer/suggest/imply 等推断词，也没有问mainly about/best title，要求的是可从原文直接读出的关于该湖的事实。
**拆句** What can we learn about Lake Natron 是典型一般疑问的特殊问句结构，主干即 we can learn what about Lake Natron，无从句、无否定、无比较，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 蝙蝠、燕子等动物以它们死亡时的姿势被化学性地保存下来，封存于水中的碳酸钠沉积物里。这片湖的景象既奇异又致命——而且全球近 75% 的火烈鸟都在此出生这一事实让它更甚。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确The lake's landscape is bizarre and deadly ↔ It is simply uninhabitable for most animals Bats, swallows and more are chemically preserved in the pose in which they perished ↔for most animals定位句两层信息——动物大量死亡 + 湖本身致命——分别对应选项的 most animals 和uninhabitable，两层全部命中，锁定 A。
B) 无中生有靠扫雷remains little known to the outside world 谈的是该湖对外界的知名度，文章自始至终未涉及外界是否知道这座湖。
C) 数量范围被放大即误原文只说 nearly 75 percent of the world's flamingos are born，仅指火烈鸟一种；选项 a breeding ground for a variety of birds 把单一鸟种夸大成 a variety of birds（多种鸟），与原文不符。
D) 条件性句子被绝对化原文谈到捕食者是在第 2 段——predators can move briskly across the lake bed and attack，且明确这是水位过低时的情况，捕食者并不是把湖当作理想栖息地；选项an ideal habitat for lots of predators 与原文意思相反。
questions.quote: Bats, swallows and more are chemically preserved in the pose in which they perished, sealed in the deposits of sodium carbonate in the water. The lake's landscape is bizarre and deadly—and made even more so by the fact that it's the place where nearly 75 percent of the world's flamingos are born.

options.text: It is simply uninhabitable for most animals.
It remains little known to the outside world.
It is a breeding ground for a variety of birds.
It makes an ideal habitat for lots of predators.

questions.prompt: Flamingos nest only when the lake water is at a specific level so that their babies can____.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
火烈鸟只在湖水处于特定水位时筑巢,以便它们的幼鸟能够____。
A) 更容易找到安全的庇护所
B) 在脚上长出厚厚的羽毛
C) 远离捕食者
D) 适应咸水
**判型** Flamingos nest only when the lake water is at a specific level so that their babies can 是 so that 引导的目的状语待补全，问的是特定水位带来的具体好处，是直接可在原文找到的事实。
**拆句** Flamingos nest only when the lake water is at a specific level so that their babies can 含两层从句：only when 引导时间状语限定筑巢条件，so that 引导目的状语句子未完。理解关键是抓住 so that 后的内容才是待选的目的部分，不要被前面的条件分句带偏。
**定位** 全球四分之三的火烈鸟从裂谷其他盐湖飞来，在水位达到某一特定水平时浮现的盐晶岛上筑巢——水位过高鸟无法筑巢，水位过低则捕食者可在湖床上迅速穿越发起袭击。当水位恰到好处时，幼鸟由一道腐蚀性的水沟与捕食者隔开而得以保全。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴跨段挪用原文 Fish have a refuge in the streams 提到的 refuge 是给罗非鱼的，不是给火烈鸟幼鸟的；find safe shelter more easily 把这一信息张冠李戴到火烈鸟身上。
B) 偷换概念混名词原文 Flamingos have evolved very leathery skin on their legs 讲的是 leathery skin（皮革般皮肤）且部位在 legs（腿）；选项 grow thick feathers on their feet 把皮肤改成羽毛、把腿改成脚，且 grow 是后天动作，与 have evolved 的进化属性不符。
C) ✓ 正确the baby birds are kept safe from predators by a corrosive ditch↔ stay away from predators预判要求选项含 '远离捕食者' 的语义，四个选项里只有 C 直接复现 predators 一词，且stay away from 与 kept safe from 等值，锁定 C。
D) 细节题看主语是谁原文谈适应盐水的是成年火烈鸟（tolerate the salt water），并不是题干所问的幼鸟；get accustomed to the salty water 把幼鸟当成适应主体，主体错位。
questions.quote: Three-quarters of the world's flamingos fly over from other salt lakes in the Rift Valley and nest on salt-crystal islands that appear when the water is at a specific level—too high and the birds can't build their nests, too low and predators can move briskly across the lake bed and attack. When the water hits the right level, the baby birds are kept safe from predators by a corrosive ditch.

options.text: find safe shelter more easily
grow thick feathers on their feet
stay away from predators
get accustomed to the salty water

questions.prompt: Flamingos in the Rift Valley are unique in that_____.
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
Rift Valley的火烈鸟独特之处在于_____。
A) 它们能在泻湖间快速移动
B) 它们能在咸水中很好地生存
C) 它们在腐蚀性沟渠中自然繁殖
D) 它们知道在何处何时筑巢
**判型** Flamingos in the Rift Valley are unique in that 问的是火烈鸟独特性的具体表现，可直接由原文中的对比句得出，不需多步推理。
**拆句** Flamingos in the Rift Valley are unique in that 是 unique in that 结构，相当于 unique because，that 引导原因状语从句而非定语从句，从句句子尚未完整，待选项补齐。
**定位** 然而，火烈鸟是唯一一种真正能在那一片死寂之中扎根生活的物种。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 动作主语被抢原文 predators can move briskly across the lake bed and attack 中 move briskly的主语是 predators（捕食者），不是火烈鸟；they can move swiftly across lagoons把这一动作误归给火烈鸟，且把 lake bed（湖床）改写为 lagoons（泻湖）。
B) ✓ 正确are the only species that actually makes life in the midst of all that death ↔they can survive well in salty water Flamingos have evolved very leathery skin on their legs so they can tolerate the salt water ↔in salty water预判要求选项体现 '唯一能在腐蚀盐湖生活' 的特性，B 既覆盖 survive 又点出 salty water 介质，命中唯一性的核心，锁定 B。
C) 功能误读为场所原文 the baby birds are kept safe from predators by a corrosive ditch 中腐蚀沟是'隔离屏障' 而非火烈鸟的繁殖场所；选项 they breed naturally in corrosive ditches 把屏障误读为繁殖地，与原文意思相反。
D) 客观行为拟人化即过推原文只说火烈鸟在特定水位时筑巢，并未说它们 '知道在哪里、何时筑巢'；they know where and when to nest 把客观事件拟人化为火烈鸟的认知能力，属过度推断。
questions.quote: Flamingos, however, are the only species that actually makes life in the midst of all that death.

options.text: they can move swiftly across lagoons
they can survive well in salty water
they breed naturally in corrosive ditches
they know where and when to nest

questions.prompt: Why can certain species of tilapia sometimes survive around Lake Natron?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
为什么某些种类的罗非鱼有时能在Natron湖周围生存?
A) 它们可以在含盐量较低的水域避难。
B) 它们能足够快地逃离捕食者。
C) 它们能在泻湖之间自由移动。
D) 它们能忍受温泉水的高温。
**判型** Why can certain species of tilapia sometimes survive around Lake Natron 虽以 Why提问，但原因可直接在原文中找到对应句，不需推断。
**拆句** Why can certain species of tilapia sometimes survive around Lake Natron 是Why+can+主语+sometimes+谓语 的疑问句，sometimes 是关键副词，限定 survive 的频率，提示并非任意时刻都能存活，必有前提条件。
**定位** 一些鱼也算在湖里 '度假' 略有小成——温泉注入 Lake Natron 时，在湖外缘形成了盐度较低的泻湖。三种罗非鱼在那里季节性地繁衍。Harper 说：'鱼可以以溪流为庇护，在湖水低、泻湖彼此隔开时扩展到泻湖里去。'
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确less salty lagoons form on the outer edges from hot springs flowing into Lake Natron ↔They can take refuge in the less salty waters Fish have a refuge in the streams ↔ take refuge预判要求选项体现 '可退守较淡水域'，A 把 streams/lagoons 概括为 less salty waters，并把 refuge 保留为核心词，命中预判，锁定 A。
B) 概念跨段挪用原文谈罗非鱼时只提水位与盐度，未涉及捕食者；flee quick enough from predators把第 2 段火烈鸟相关的 predators 概念挪用到罗非鱼身上，属张冠李戴。
C) 条件状语句易被反读原文 All the lagoons join when the lake is high and fish must retreat to their stream refuges or die 明确写道：水位高时泻湖才合并，但此时鱼必须撤回溪流否则会死；选项 move freely from lagoon to lagoon 把这一危急情形误读为鱼可自由游动，与原文相反。
D) 背景信息被读成原因原文 hot springs flowing into Lake Natron 中 hot springs 只是泻湖形成的来源，未说罗非鱼以耐热为生存机制；stand the heat of the spring water 把背景信息夸大为存活原因，属过度推断。
questions.quote: Some fish, too, have had limited success vacationing at the lake as less salty lagoons form on the outer edges from hot springs flowing into Lake Natron. Three species of tilapia thrive there part-time. "Fish have a refuge in the streams and can expand into the lagoons when the lake is low and the lagoons are separate," Harper said.

options.text: They can take refuge in the less salty waters.
They can flee quick enough from predators.
They can move freely from lagoon to lagoon.
They can stand the heat of the spring water.

questions.prompt: What may be the consequence of Tanzanian government's planned operation?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
坦桑尼亚政府计划实施的行动可能带来什么后果?
A) 火烈鸟加速灭绝。
B) 火烈鸟迁徙路线的改变。
C) Natron湖天然碱的过度开采。
D) Natron湖生态系统的破坏。
**判型** What may be the consequence of Tanzanian government's planned operation 问的是可能后果，原文里有专家直接表态的 worry 句作答，是直陈细节而非考生需自行推断。
**拆句** What may be the consequence of Tanzanian government's planned operation 主干是 What may be the consequence，consequence of 后接两层所有格修饰（政府的+计划的），may 是模态动词表可能性，是理解题干的关键。
**定位** 尽管计划中的开采项目将设在 40 多英里以外，通过管道抽取苏打粉，但环保人士担忧这仍可能扰乱该湖的自然水循环和火烈鸟的繁殖地。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 局部影响升级为终极后果原文仅言担忧扰乱 breeding grounds（繁殖地），未涉及火烈鸟物种灭绝；The accelerated extinction of flamingos 把局部影响夸大为物种灭绝，属过度推断。
B) 新维度选项即无中生有原文未提任何关于火烈鸟迁徙路线变化的信息，仅提及它们从其他盐湖飞来繁殖；The change of flamingos' migration route 引入原文未涉及的维度，属无中生有。
C) 前缀加 over- 即过度推断原文只描述了开采计划的距离与方式，未给出 '过度开采' 的信号；The overmining of Lake Natron's soda ash 把 mining 升级为 overmining，属无中生有。
D) ✓ 正确upset the natural water cycle and breeding grounds↔The disruption of Lake Natron's ecosystem预判要求选项体现 '扰乱湖的自然水循环和繁殖地' 的后果，D 用 disruption 名词化原文upset，再用 ecosystem 概括 water cycle 与 breeding grounds，是同义改写的标准范式，锁定 D。
questions.quote: Although the planned operation will be located more than 40 miles away, drawing the soda ash in through pipelines, conservationists worry it could still upset the natural water cycle and breeding grounds.

options.text: The accelerated extinction of flamingos.
The change of flamingos' migration route.
The overmining of Lake Natron's soda ash.
The disruption of Lake Natron's ecosystem.

title: Many European countries have been making the shift…

sentences.text: Many European countries have been making the shift to electric vehicles and Germany has just stated that they plan to ban the sale of vehicles using gasoline and diesel as fuel by 2030.
The country is also planning to reduce its carbon footprint by 80-95% by 2050, (26)____ a shift to green energy in the country.
Effectively, the ban will include the registration of new cars in the country as they will not allow any gasoline (27)____ vehicle to be registered after 2030.

passage.translation: 许多欧洲国家一直在向电动汽车转型，德国刚刚宣布他们计划在2030年之前禁止销售使用汽油和柴油作为燃料的车辆。该国还计划在2050年之前将其碳排放量减少80-95%，从而引发该国向绿色能源的转变。实际上，该禁令将包括该国新车的注册，因为他们在2030年之后将不允许任何汽油动力车辆注册。

sentences.text: Part of the reason this ban is being discussed and (28)____ is because energy officials see that they will not reach their emissions goals by 2050 if they do not (29)____ a large portion of vehicle emissions.
The country is still (30)____ that it will meet its emissions goals, like reducing emissions by 40% by 2020, but the (31)____ of electric cars in the country has not occurred as fast as expected.

passage.translation: 讨论和实施这项禁令的部分原因是能源官员认为，如果不消除大部分车辆排放，他们将无法在2050年之前实现排放目标。该国仍然希望能够实现其排放目标，比如到2020年减少40%的排放，但该国对电动汽车的接受程度并未像预期那样快速发生。

sentences.text: Other efforts to increase the use of electric vehicles include plans to build over 1 million hybrid and electric car battery changing stations across the country.
By 2030, Germany plans on having over 6 million charging stations (32)____ .
According to the International Business Times, electric car sales are expected to increase as Volkswagen is still recovering from its emissions scandal.

passage.translation: 增加电动汽车使用的其他努力包括计划在全国范围内建设超过100万个混合动力和电动汽车电池更换站。到2030年，德国计划安装超过600万个充电站。根据International Business Times的报道，随着大众汽车仍在从其排放丑闻中恢复，电动汽车销量预计将会增加。

sentences.text: There are (33)____ around 155,000 registered hybrid and electric vehicles on German roads, dwarfed by the 45 million gasoline and diesel cars driving there now.
As countries continue setting goals of reducing emissions, greater steps need to be taken to have a (34)____ effect on the surrounding environment.
While the efforts are certainly not (35)____ , the results of such bans will likely only start to be seen by generations down the line, bettering the world for the future.

passage.translation: 目前德国道路上约有15.5万辆注册的混合动力和电动汽车，相比之下，现在行驶的4500万辆汽油和柴油汽车使其相形见绌。随着各国继续设定减少排放的目标，需要采取更大的步骤才能对周围环境产生明显的影响。虽然这些努力当然不是徒劳的，但这类禁令的结果可能只有在未来几代人才能开始看到，为未来创造更美好的世界。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
Many European countries have been making the shift to electric vehicles and Germany has just stated that they plan to ban the sale of vehicles using gasoline and diesel as fuel by 2030. The country is also planning to reduce its carbon footprint by 80-95% by 2050, {{26}} a shift to green energy in the country. Effectively, the ban will include the registration of new cars in the country as they will not allow any gasoline {{27}} vehicle to be registered after 2030.

Part of the reason this ban is being discussed and {{28}} is because energy officials see that they will not reach their emissions goals by 2050 if they do not {{29}} a large portion of vehicle emissions. The country is still {{30}} that it will meet its emissions goals, like reducing emissions by 40% by 2020, but the {{31}} of electric cars in the country has not occurred as fast as expected.

Other efforts to increase the use of electric vehicles include plans to build over 1 million hybrid and electric car battery changing stations across the country. By 2030, Germany plans on having over 6 million charging stations {{32}} . According to the International Business Times, electric car sales are expected to increase as Volkswagen is still recovering from its emissions scandal.

There are {{33}} around 155,000 registered hybrid and electric vehicles on German roads, dwarfed by the 45 million gasoline and diesel cars driving there now. As countries continue setting goals of reducing emissions, greater steps need to be taken to have a {{34}} effect on the surrounding environment. While the efforts are certainly not {{35}} , the results of such bans will likely only start to be seen by generations down the line, bettering the world for the future.

options.text: acceptance
incidentally
currently
installed
disrupting
noticeable
eliminate
powered
exhaust
restoration
futile
skeptical
hopeful
sparking
implemented

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) sparking 动词
**词性槽** 逗号后悬垂分词作伴随状语，需 -ing 形式动词
**依据** spark a shift = 引发一次转向，固定搭配spark + shift/change/debate/interest 是英语高频搭配，意为「引发、催生」；对应 The country is also planning to reduce its carbon footprint by 80-95% by 2050, __(26)__a shift to green energy in the country. 表「减排目标催生绿色能源转向」，语义因果清晰。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) disrupting 义反 + 搭配错位disrupt a shift 是「打断一次转向」，与「减排带动绿色转型」的正向因果相反，且与下文「政府推动」的积极语气不一致。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) powered 形容词
**词性槽** gasoline ___ vehicle 中作复合形容词修饰名词
**依据** gasoline-powered = 以汽油为动力的，固定搭配对应 they will not allow any gasoline __(27)__ vehicle to be registered after 2030：与全文反复出现的 vehicles using gasoline and diesel as fuel 意思完全一致，powered 是「由…驱动」的过去分词作形容词，与 gasoline 复合自然贴合「禁售燃油车」语境。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) disrupting 义反，与禁售燃油车背景不符disrupting 表示「扰乱、颠覆」，gasoline-disrupting vehicle 既无此搭配也与文意（汽油车被淘汰）相反。
F) futile 义不通futile 意为「徒劳的」，gasoline-futile vehicle 不成立。
G) hopeful 搭配与情感色彩均不合hopeful 修饰人或前景，不能修饰汽车的动力来源。
H) implemented 对象不对implemented 修饰的是政策/计划这类抽象事物，不修饰 vehicle。
J) installed 搭配错位installed 通常说「安装的设备」，gasoline-installed vehicle 不是英文表达。
K) noticeable 义不切题noticeable 是「明显的」，与「动力来源」无关。
N) skeptical 对象不对skeptical 用于「人」对某事持怀疑态度，不能修饰 vehicle。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) implemented 动词
**词性槽** being discussed and ___ 并列过去分词
**依据** implement a ban = 实施禁令，常见搭配Part of the reason this ban is being discussed and __(28)__ is because energy officials see that they will not reach their emissions goals by 2050 if they do not __(29)__ a large portion of vehicle emissions.：禁令被「讨论和实施」，implement a ban/policy是固定搭配，递进自然。

**答案** D) eliminate 动词
**词性槽** 情态/助动词 do not + 动词原形
**依据** eliminate emissions = 消除排放，正合减排目标对应 they will not reach their emissions goals by 2050 if they do not __(29)__ a large portion of vehicle emissions：句意为「若不消除大部分车辆尾气排放，就达不到目标」，eliminate 与 emissions goals 语义闭环。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) exhaust 义反 + 形近陷阱exhaust 作动词是「耗尽」（耗尽某资源），名词义「废气」正好关联本文话题，是命题人放出的形近/题域诱饵；但放在 do not exhaust a large portion of vehicle emissions「不耗尽大部分车辆排放」于逻辑上荒谬——你不会「用尽」排放。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 E) —— exhaust 与 emissions 同属「尾气」话题的形 + 域双重迷惑。they will not reach their emissions goals by 2050 if they do not __(29)__ a large portion of vehicle emissions 里看到 vehicle emissions，许多考生直接联想到 exhaust（名词义「废气」）就填上；但本空要的是动词原形，exhaust 作动词是「耗尽」，与减排逻辑完全相反。防坑：填动词时先盯死动词义而非词面话题。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) hopeful 形容词
**词性槽** is still ___ that 从句，表语形容词带 that 同位语从句
**依据** 下文转折 but，主句须正面 → hopeful The country is still __(30)__ that it will meet its emissions goals, like reducing emissions by 40% by 2020, but the __(31)__ of electric cars in the country has not occurred as fast as expected.：but 之后是负面消息，按「正-但-负」逻辑，but 之前必正面，故选 hopeful「乐观相信能达到目标」。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
N) skeptical 极性反若填 skeptical「怀疑」，再用 but 转到「电动车普及没那么快」则成「负-但-负」，逻辑断裂；且下一段还在罗列政府的积极举措，与「政府自己怀疑能否达标」矛盾。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 N) —— be + 形容词 + that 结构里 skeptical 与 hopeful 都合语法。考生若只看 The country is still __(30)__ that it will meet its emissions goals, like reducing emissions by 40% by 2020, but the __(31)__ of electric cars in the country has not occurred as fast as expected. 半句，hopeful 与 skeptical 都讲得通；必须读到but「电动车普及没那么快」才能用极性反推选 hopeful。防坑：见 but 就要回看前句、对齐极性。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) acceptance 名词
**词性槽** the ___ of electric cars 作主语
**依据** the acceptance of electric cars = 电动车的接受度 / 普及，正合上下文对应 the __(31)__ of electric cars in the country has not occurred as fast as expected：与下文 Other efforts to increase the use of electric vehicles include plans to build over 1 million hybrid and electric car battery changing stations across the country. 互相呼应——市场对电动车的「接受/普及」没有预期那么快，故政府要采取更多举措。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) restoration 义不切题restoration「修复、复原」用于古建筑、生态等被破坏后重建的对象，对全新事物电动车没有「恢复」一说。

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) installed 形容词
**词性槽** having over 6 million charging stations ___ 中作宾补
**依据** 充电站「被安装好」的搭配最贴切对应 By 2030, Germany plans on having over 6 million charging stations __(32)__.：充电桩是被安装的对象，install charging stations 是最自然的搭配；having ... stations installed 表「使充电桩安装完毕」。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) disrupting 义反disrupting 是「扰乱的」，让充电桩处于扰乱状态于政策语境完全相反。
F) futile 义反futile「徒劳的」与全段「扩大充电网络」的积极语气冲突。
G) hopeful 对象不对hopeful 修饰人，不能修饰充电桩。
H) implemented 搭配对象不对implemented 多与 policy/plan/measure 搭，不与 station 搭。
K) noticeable 义不切题noticeable「显著的」不解释充电桩状态。
N) skeptical 对象不对skeptical 用于人。

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) currently 副词
**词性槽** There are ___ + 数词+复数名词，修饰系动词 are
**依据** 对照「现状 vs 未来」，需要「目前」作时间状语本段先讲现状 There are __(33)__ around 155,000 registered hybrid and electric vehicles on German roads，再用 As countries continue setting goals of reducing emissions 转向未来；currently「目前」恰好把这串数据与下文未来目标对照起来。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
I) incidentally 插入语义错位incidentally 是「顺便提一句」，多用于话题切换的插入语，与本段「陈述现状以对比未来」的语气不合。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) noticeable 形容词
**词性槽** a ___ effect on... 中修饰 effect 作定语
**依据** have a noticeable effect 高频搭配 + 与 greater steps 呼应have a noticeable/significant effect on... 是常见搭配，对应 greater steps need to be taken to have a __(34)__ effect on the surrounding environment，「采取更大步伐才能产生显著影响」逻辑顺。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) disrupting 极性反disrupting effect「破坏性影响」与「对环境的积极影响」语境冲突。
G) hopeful 搭配错位hopeful 修饰人或前景，不修饰 effect。
H) implemented 搭配对象不对implemented 说「被执行的」，不修饰 effect。
N) skeptical 对象不对skeptical 用于人。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) futile 形容词
**词性槽** be 动词 + not + ___ 作表语
**依据** not futile = 不是徒劳的，正合让步语义While the efforts are certainly not __(35)__, the results of such bans will likely only start to be seen by generations down the line, bettering the world for the future. 形成「努力不白费/将造福未来」的肯定基调；futile「徒劳的」最贴让步从句的反义需求。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) disrupting 义不切题disrupting「破坏的」与「努力是否值得」的让步无关。
G) hopeful 极性反若填 hopeful，「努力并非有希望的」否定整句基调，与下文「造福未来」矛盾。
H) implemented 搭配 + 已用倾向implemented 通常说政策「已被执行」，做 efforts 的表语义不通；后面 28 题也更需要它。
K) noticeable 极性反noticeable 也是正面词，「努力不是显著的」与下句正面预期相悖。
N) skeptical 对象不对skeptical 修饰人或态度，不修饰 efforts。

title: Our world now moves so fast that we…

sentences.text: Our world now moves so fast that we seldom stop to see just how far we have come in just a few years.
The latest iPhone 6s, for example, has a dual-core processor and fits nicely into your pocket.
By comparison, you would expect to find a technological specification like this on your standard laptop in an office anywhere in the world.

passage.translation: 我们的世界现在变化如此之快,以至于我们很少停下来看看仅仅在几年内我们已经走了多远。例如,最新的iPhone 6s拥有双核处理器,并且可以很好地放入你的口袋。相比之下,你会期望在世界任何地方的办公室里的标准笔记本电脑上找到这样的技术规格。

sentences.text: It's no wonder that new applications for the Internet of Things are moving ahead fast when almost every new device we buy has a plug on the end of it or a wireless connection to the internet.
Soon, our current smartphone lifestyle will expand to create our own smart home lifestyle too.

passage.translation: 当我们购买的几乎每一台新设备末端都有一个插头或者有无线连接互联网的功能时,难怪物联网的新应用正在快速推进。很快,我们当前的智能手机生活方式也将扩展为我们自己的智能家居生活方式。

sentences.text: All researchers agree that close to 25 billion devices, things and sensors will be connected by 2020 which incidentally is also the moment that Millennials(千禧一代) are expected to make up 75 percent of our overall workforce, and the fully connected home will become a reality for large numbers of people worldwide.

passage.translation: 所有研究人员都同意,到2020年将有近250亿台设备、物品和传感器连接起来,顺便说一句,这也是千禧一代预计将占我们整体劳动力75%的时刻,而完全连接的家庭将成为全球大量人口的现实。

sentences.text: However, this is just the tip of the proverbial iceberg as smart buildings and even cities increasingly become the norm as leaders and business owners begin to wake up to the massive savings that technology can deliver through connected sensors and new forms of automation coupled with intelligent energy and facilities management.

passage.translation: 然而,这只是众所周知的冰山一角,因为随着领导者和企业所有者开始意识到技术可以通过连接的传感器和新型自动化形式以及智能能源和设施管理带来的巨大节约,智能建筑甚至城市日益成为常态。

sentences.text: Online security cameras, intelligent lighting and a wealth of sensors that control both temperature and air quality are offering an unprecedented level of control, efficiency, and improvements to what were once classed necessary costs when running a business or managing a large building.

passage.translation: 在线安全摄像头、智能照明以及大量控制温度和空气质量的传感器正在提供前所未有的控制、效率和改进水平,这些曾经在经营企业或管理大型建筑时被归类为必要成本。

sentences.text: We can expect that the ever-growing list of devices, systems and environments remains connected, always online and talking to each other.

The big benefit will not only be in the housing of this enormous and rapidly growing amount of data, but will also be in the ability to run real time data analytics to extract actionable and ongoing knowledge.

passage.translation: 我们可以预期,不断增长的设备、系统和环境列表保持连接,始终在线并相互通信。最大的好处不仅在于容纳这些庞大且快速增长的数据量,还在于能够运行实时数据分析以提取可操作和持续的知识。

sentences.text: The biggest and most exciting challenge of this technology is how to creatively leverage this ever-growing amount of data to deliver cost savings, improvements and tangible benefits to both businesses and citizens of these smart cities.

passage.translation: 这项技术最大和最令人兴奋的挑战是如何创造性地利用这些不断增长的数据量,为这些智能城市的企业和市民带来成本节约、改进和实际利益。

sentences.text: The good news is that most of this technology is already invented.

Let's face it, it wasn't too long ago that the idea of working from anywhere and at anytime was some form of a distant Utopian(乌托邦式的) dream, and yet now we can perform almost any office-based task from any location in the world as long as we have access to the internet.

passage.translation: 好消息是,这项技术的大部分已经被发明出来了。让我们面对现实,不久前,在任何地方、任何时间工作的想法还是某种遥远的乌托邦式的梦想,然而现在,只要我们能够访问互联网,我们几乎可以从世界上任何地方执行任何基于办公室的任务。

sentences.text: It's time to wake up to the fact that making smart buildings, cities and homes will dramatically improve our quality of life in the years ahead.

passage.translation: 是时候认识到这样一个事实:建造智能建筑、城市和家居将在未来几年显著改善我们的生活质量。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does the example of iPhone 6s serve to show?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （例证目的题）
**题目译文**
iPhone 6s的例子用来说明什么?
A) 人们现在使用的智能手机的巨大容量。
B) 智能手机在全世界的广泛使用。
C) 新技术对人们日常生活的巨大影响。
D) 在很短时间内快速的技术进步。
**判型** What does the example of iPhone 6s serve to show? 明确问"这个例子用来说明什么"，是典型的例证目的题。
**拆句** 题干主干是 What does the example serve to show，of iPhone 6s 是 example 的后置定语，serve to do 意为"用来做某事"。句子平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 我们的世界如今变化太快，我们几乎不停下来看一看：仅仅几年间我们已经走出了多远。比如最新的 iPhone 6s 配有双核处理器，又能轻松装进口袋；相比之下，你本以为这种技术规格要在世界各地办公室里的标准笔记本电脑上才能见到。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全The huge capacity of the smartphones people now use. 只复述了例子里 dual-core processor 这种"容量大"的细节，没有上升到作者真正要论证的"技术进步快"。
B) 无中生有The widespread use of smartphones all over the world. 谈的是"普及程度"，可原文iPhone 6s 例子只谈"技术规格"，全段也没提"在全世界被广泛使用"。
C) 偷换概念The huge impact of new technology on people's everyday life. 把话题偷换成"新技术对日常生活的巨大影响"，可原文 iPhone 6s 例子只谈"几年前到现在的技术规格变化"，没有展开"对日常生活造成何种影响"。
D) ✓ 正确Our world now moves so fast that we seldom stop to see just how far we have come in just a few years.↔ The rapid technological progress in a very short period of time.预判"短时间内技术进步惊人"与 The rapid technological progress in a very short period of time. 完全对位，rapid = so fast、in a very short period of time = in just a few years。
questions.quote: Our world now moves so fast that we seldom stop to see just how far we have come in just a few years. The latest iPhone 6s, for example, has a dual-core processor and fits nicely into your pocket. By comparison, you would expect to find a technological specification like this on your standard laptop in an office anywhere in the world.

options.text: The huge capacity of the smartphones people now use.
The widespread use of smartphones all over the world.
The huge impact of new technology on people's everyday life.
The rapid technological progress in a very short period of time.

questions.prompt: What can we expect to see by the year 2020?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
到2020年我们可以期待看到什么?
A) 物联网的应用程序。
B) 智能家居的普及。
C) 千禧一代的出现。
D) 世界的全面全球化。
**判型** What can we expect to see by the year 2020? 是问"2020 年会看到什么"，答案就在原文那句话里，不需推断。
**拆句** What 作 see 的宾语，we 是主语，can expect to see 是谓语，by the year 2020 是时间状语；句式简单。
**定位** 所有研究者一致认为，到 2020 年将有近 250 亿台设备、物品和传感器接入互联网；2020年也恰是千禧一代预计将占整体劳动力 75% 的时刻；而"全互联家庭"也将在全球范围内为大量人群所拥有。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴Apps for the Internet of Things. 来自第 2 段 new applications for the Internet of Things are moving ahead fast，是现在进行时"正在快速推进"，并非 2020 才能看到；时间不匹配。
B) ✓ 正确the fully connected home will become a reality for large numbers of people worldwide ↔The popularization of smart homes. The popularization of smart homes. 用 popularization 概括 become a reality for large numbers of people，用 smart homes 概括 fully connected home，完全等值。
C) 偷换概念The emergence of Millennials. 用 emergence（出现/兴起）形容千禧一代，可原文Millennials(千禧一代) are expected to make up 75 percent of our overall workforce 说的是"届时占劳动力 75%"，不是"届时才出现"——千禧一代早已存在。
D) 过度推断Total globalization of the world. 中的 total globalization"完全全球化"是原文从未出现的概念；定位句虽含 worldwide 一词，但是修饰"全互联家庭普及范围"，不等于"全世界已彻底全球化"。
questions.quote: All researchers agree that close to 25 billion devices, things and sensors will be connected by 2020 which incidentally is also the moment that Millennials(千禧一代) are expected to make up 75 percent of our overall workforce, and the fully connected home will become a reality for large numbers of people worldwide.

options.text: Apps for the Internet of Things.
The popularization of smart homes.
The emergence of Millennials.
Total globalization of the world.

questions.prompt: What will business owners do when they become aware of the benefits of the Internet of Things?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
当企业主意识到物联网的好处时,他们会做什么?
A) 在其运营中雇用更少的工人。
B) 获得对其业务的自动控制。
C) 投资更多智能建筑和城市。
D) 拥抱任何新技术。
**判型** What will business owners do when they become aware of the benefits of the Internet of Things? 问的是企业主一旦意识到好处会采取什么行动，答案是原文里的客观陈述。
**拆句** 主干 What will business owners do，when 引导时间状语从句，从句里 they 回指business owners，become aware of "意识到"。注意 when 在这里是"一旦/当……时"，不是疑问词。
**定位** 然而，这只是冰山一角——随着领导者和企业主开始意识到技术可通过互联传感器、新型自动化以及智能能源与设施管理带来的巨大节约，智能楼宇乃至智能城市正越来越成为常态。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断Employ fewer workers in their operations. 把 massive savings"巨大节约"理解成"裁员省钱"，可原文只说技术通过 sensors、automation、智能能源/设施管理带来节约，从未提及"减少员工"。
B) 偷换概念Gain automatic control of their businesses. 把 new forms of automation 这一"技术手段"曲解成"业主获得对企业的自动控制"。原文 automation 是技术带来节约的方式之一，业主并不会因此"获得对生意的自动控制"。
C) ✓ 正确smart buildings and even cities increasingly become the norm ↔Invest in more smart buildings and cities. as leaders and business owners begin to wake up to the massive savings that technology can deliver↔ Invest in more smart buildings and cities.预判"推动智能楼宇/城市变成常态"与 Invest in more smart buildings and cities. 完全对位：invest in more 正是让 smart buildings and even cities ... become the norm这一普及结果发生的业主侧动作。
D) 以偏概全Embrace whatever new technology there is. 把对象从 smart buildings and even cities 这个具体范畴扩大成 whatever new technology there is"凡是新技术全都拥抱"，明显超出原文。原文只说业主意识到"这门技术"带来节约后让"智能楼宇/城市"成为常态，没有承诺"对所有新技术来者不拒"。
questions.quote: However, this is just the tip of the proverbial iceberg as smart buildings and even cities increasingly become the norm as leaders and business owners begin to wake up to the massive savings that technology can deliver through connected sensors and new forms of automation coupled with intelligent energy and facilities management.

options.text: Employ fewer workers in their operations.
Gain automatic control of their businesses.
Invest in more smart buildings and cities.
Embrace whatever new technology there is.

questions.prompt: What is the most exciting challenge when we possess more and more data?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
当我们拥有越来越多的数据时,最令人兴奋的挑战是什么?
A) 如何将其转化为有利可图的用途。
B) 如何进行实时数据分析。
C) 如何连接可操作的系统。
D) 如何设计新的方式来存储它。
**判型** What is the most exciting challenge when we possess more and more data? 问"最激动人心的挑战是什么"，答案就在原文那句"最大的挑战是……"里。
**拆句** 主干 What is the most exciting challenge，when 引导时间状语从句"当我们拥有越来越多数据时"。more and more 表数量递增。
**定位** 这项技术最大、也最激动人心的挑战，是如何创造性地利用这些不断增长的数据，为智能城市中的企业与市民带来成本节约、改善与切实可感的收益。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确how to creatively leverage this ever-growing amount of data to deliver cost savings, improvements and tangible benefits↔ How to turn it to profitable use.预判"把海量数据创造性地变成实际效益"与 How to turn it to profitable use. 完全对位，turn it to profitable use = leverage data to deliver benefits。
B) 张冠李戴How to do real time data analysis. 来自 run real time data analytics to extract actionable and ongoing knowledge，是上一段铺垫的能力，而第 7 段明确把"最大挑战"定义为 how to creatively leverage ... data，不是"如何做实时分析"。
C) 偷换概念How to link the actionable systems. 用 link the actionable systems"连接可行动的系统"，原文 actionable and ongoing knowledge 里 actionable 修饰 knowledge（可付诸行动的知识），并非什么 actionable systems；同时"如何连接系统"也不是原文设定的挑战。
D) 答非所问How to devise new ways to store it. 中的 store data"存储数据"来自 the housing of this enormous and rapidly growing amount of data，但原文紧接着用 not only ... but also ... 把重点放在"运行实时数据分析"上，第 7 段更把"最大挑战"定义为"创造性利用数据"，存储显然不是答案。
questions.quote: The biggest and most exciting challenge of this technology is how to creatively leverage this ever-growing amount of data to deliver cost savings, improvements and tangible benefits to both businesses and citizens of these smart cities.

options.text: How to turn it to profitable use.
How to do real time data analysis.
How to link the actionable systems.
How to devise new ways to store it.

questions.prompt: What does the author think about working from anywhere and at anytime?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者如何看待在任何地方任何时间工作?
A) 只要连接到互联网就是可行的。
B) 它将在智能建筑、城市和家庭中蓬勃发展。
C) 对普通工人来说,它仍然是一个遥远的乌托邦梦想。
D) 它将为老板和工人都带来切实的好处。
**判型** 题干虽含 think，但锁死了具体话题 working from anywhere and at anytime，作者的看法就在那一两句话里，仍走定位路径而非全文串线。
**拆句** 主干 What does the author think about X，about 后跟动名词短语 working from anywhere and at anytime；anywhere 和 anytime 由 and 并列。
**定位** 我们得承认，不久以前"任何时间任何地点办公"还像是遥远的乌托邦梦；可如今只要我们能上网，就几乎能在世界上任何地方完成几乎任何办公任务。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确and yet now we can perform almost any office-based task from any location in the world as long as we have access to the internet↔ It is feasible with a connection to the internet.预判"只要上网就能实现"与 It is feasible with a connection to the internet. 完全对位：feasible 概括"can perform""已经能做到"，with a connection to the internet 等值于 as long as we have access to the internet。
B) 张冠李戴It will thrive in smart buildings, cities and homes. 把 smart buildings, cities and homes 这一全文话题硬粘到"任意时间地点办公"上。原文 P8 明确给出的条件是 access to the internet，并没有说"在智能楼宇/城市/家里才会兴盛"。
C) 与原文相反It is still a distant Utopian dream for ordinary workers. 把作者明确否定的旧状态当成现状。原文以 and yet now 转折，已说明 distant Utopian dream 是 "过去的看法"，作者现在的态度恰恰相反；这是典型"正话反说"。
D) 张冠李戴It will deliver tangible benefits to both boss and worker. 中的 tangible benefits 来自第 7 段 cost savings, improvements and tangible benefits to both businesses and citizens，谈的是"用数据带来收益"的对象，被搬到"任意时间地点办公"上做承诺；同时 boss/worker 这种二分对象也是原文没有的。
questions.quote: Let's face it, it wasn't too long ago that the idea of working from anywhere and at anytime was some form of a distant Utopian(乌托邦式的) dream, and yet now we can perform almost any office-based task from any location in the world as long as we have access to the internet.

options.text: It is feasible with a connection to the internet.
It will thrive in smart buildings, cities and homes.
It is still a distant Utopian dream for ordinary workers.
It will deliver tangible benefits to both boss and worker.

title: In the beginning of the movie I, Robot,…

sentences.text: In the beginning of the movie I, Robot, a robot has to decide whom to save after two cars plunge into the water—Del Spooner or a child.
Even though Spooner screams "Save her!
Save her!" the robot rescues him because it calculates that he has a 45 percent chance of survival compared to Sarah's 11 percent.
The robot's decision and its calculated approach raise an important question: would humans make the same choice?
And which choice would we want our robotic counterparts to make?

passage.translation: 在电影《我，机器人》的开头，一个机器人必须在两辆车坠入水中后决定救谁——Del Spooner还是一个孩子。尽管Spooner大喊"救她!救她!"，机器人还是救了他，因为它计算出他的生存几率为45%，而Sarah的生存几率为11%。机器人的决定及其计算方法引发了一个重要问题：人类会做出同样的选择吗?我们希望我们的机器人同类做出哪种选择?

sentences.text: Isaac Asimov evaded the whole notion of morality in devising his three laws of robotics, which hold that 1.
Robots cannot harm humans or allow humans to come to harm; 2.
Robots must obey humans, except where the order would conflict with law 1; and 3.
Robots must act in self-preservation, unless doing so conflicts with laws 1 or 2.
These laws are programmed into Asimov's robots—they don't have to think, judge, or value.
They don't have to like humans or believe that hurting them is wrong or bad.
They simply don't do it.

passage.translation: Isaac Asimov在设计他的机器人三定律时回避了整个道德概念，这三定律规定：1. 机器人不能伤害人类或允许人类受到伤害；2. 机器人必须服从人类，除非命令与定律1冲突；3. 机器人必须保护自己，除非这样做与定律1或2冲突。这些定律被编入Asimov的机器人程序中——它们不必思考、判断或评估价值。它们不必喜欢人类或相信伤害人类是错误的或不好的。它们只是不会那样做。

sentences.text: The robot who rescues Spooner's life in I, Robot follows Asimov's zeroth law: robots cannot harm humanity (as opposed to individual humans) or allow humanity to come to harm—an expansion of the first law that allows robots to determine what's in the greater good.
Under the first law, a robot could not harm a dangerous gunman, but under the zeroth law, a robot could kill the gunman to save others.

passage.translation: 在《我，机器人》中救了Spooner生命的机器人遵循Asimov的第零定律：机器人不能伤害人类整体(而非个体人类)或允许人类整体受到伤害——这是对第一定律的扩展，允许机器人决定什么符合更大的利益。根据第一定律，机器人不能伤害一个危险的持枪歹徒，但根据第零定律，机器人可以杀死持枪歹徒以拯救其他人。

sentences.text: Whether it's possible to program a robot with safeguards such as Asimov's laws is debatable.
A word such as "harm" is vague (what about emotional harm?
Is replacing a human employee harm?), and abstract concepts present coding problems.
The robots in Asimov's fiction expose complications and loopholes in the three laws, and even when the laws work, robots still have to assess situations.

passage.translation: 是否可能为机器人编入像Asimov定律这样的安全保障措施是有争议的。像"伤害"这样的词是模糊的(情感伤害算不算?取代人类员工算伤害吗?)，而且抽象概念会带来编码问题。Asimov小说中的机器人暴露了三定律中的复杂性和漏洞，即使定律有效，机器人仍然需要评估情况。

sentences.text: Assessing situations can be complicated.
A robot has to identify the players, conditions, and possible outcomes for various scenarios.
It's doubtful that a computer program can do that—at least, not without some undesirable results.
A roboticist at the Bristol Robotics Laboratory programmed a robot to save human proxies(替身) called "H-bots" from danger.
When one H-bot headed for danger, the robot successfully pushed it out of the way.
But when two H-bots became imperiled, the robot choked 42 percent of the time, unable to decide which to save and letting them both "die."
The experiment highlights the importance of morality: without it, how can a robot decide whom to save or what's best for humanity, especially if it can't calculate survival odds?

passage.translation: 评估情况可能很复杂。机器人必须识别参与者、条件以及各种场景的可能结果。计算机程序能否做到这一点令人怀疑——至少，不会没有一些不良结果。Bristol Robotics Laboratory的一位机器人专家为一个机器人编程，让它从危险中拯救被称为"H-bots"的人类替身。当一个H-bot走向危险时，机器人成功地把它推开了。但当两个H-bots陷入危险时，机器人有42%的时间会卡住，无法决定救哪一个，让它们都"死"了。这个实验凸显了道德的重要性：没有道德，机器人如何决定救谁或什么对人类最好，尤其是如果它无法计算生存几率?

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What question does the example in the movie raise?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
电影中的例子提出了什么问题?
A) 机器人能否做出更好的决策。
B) 机器人是否遵循Asimov的第零定律。
C) 机器人可能如何做出错误的判断。
D) 机器人应当如何被编程。
**判型** What question does the example in the movie raise? 直接询问例子引出的具体问题，答案应是原文里那句问句的转述，属于细节定位题。
**拆句** What question does the example in the movie raise? 主语 the example、谓语 raise、宾语 What question 提前作问；structure 平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 机器人的这一决策及其基于计算的处理方式提出了一个重要问题：人类是否会做出同样的选择？以及我们希望我们的机器人同伴做出怎样的选择？
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念Whether robots can reach better decisions. 把原文的"人类会不会做同样选择"偷换成"机器人能否做更好的决定"，引入了原文未提的"更好"这一比较。
B) 张冠李戴Whether robots follow Asimov's zeroth law. 把第三段才出现的 zeroth law 硬塞到第一段问句里，定位错段。
C) 无中生有How robots may make bad judgments. 暗含"机器人做了坏判断"的负面定性，但原文只是中性描述"按概率救人"，并未称之为 bad judgments。
D) ✓ 正确which choice would we want our robotic counterparts to make? ↔How robots should be programmed.预判方向是"机器人应如何被设定决策"，How robots should be programmed 正是这一方向的最精炼上位概括，与定位句意图完全吻合。
questions.quote: The robot's decision and its calculated approach raise an important question: would humans make the same choice? And which choice would we want our robotic counterparts to make?

options.text: Whether robots can reach better decisions.
Whether robots follow Asimov's zeroth law.
How robots may make bad judgments.
How robots should be programmed.

questions.prompt: What does the author think of Asimov's three laws of robotics?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者如何看待Asimov的机器人三定律?
A) 它们显然脱离了现实。
B) 它们没有遵循机器人学的编码系统。
C) 它们为机器人学奠定了坚实的基础。
D) 它们没有将道德问题纳入考虑。
**判型** What does the author think of Asimov's three laws of robotics? 问作者对三定律的具体看法，原文须给出明文评价，本质仍是细节定位+理解。
**拆句** What does the author think of Asimov's three laws of robotics? 主谓宾 the author /think of / X，疑问代词 What 前置；句式平实。
**定位** 艾萨克·阿西莫夫在设计他的机器人三大法则时回避了"道德"这一整个概念。这三条法则是：1. 机器人不能伤害人类，也不能坐视人类受到伤害；2. 机器人必须服从人类，除非命令与法则1冲突；3. 机器人必须自我保全，除非这样做与法则1或法则2冲突。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有They are apparently divorced from reality. 称三定律"明显脱离现实"，原文未给出此评价；作者只说回避了道德，并未否定其现实性。
B) 偷换概念They did not follow the coding system of robotics. 中的 coding system of robotics 在文中并不存在；原文 abstract concepts present coding problems 谈的是编程难题，不是"违背了某套编码系统"。
C) 与原文相反They laid a solid foundation for robotics. 是高度肯定的评价，与原文 evaded the whole notion of morality 的批评口吻完全相反。
D) ✓ 正确Isaac Asimov evaded the whole notion of morality in devising his three laws of robotics ↔They did not take moral issues into consideration.预判方向是"没考虑道德"，D 用 did not take moral issues into consideration 把evade 拆解为否定+考虑，语义完全等值。
questions.quote: Isaac Asimov evaded the whole notion of morality in devising his three laws of robotics, which hold that 1. Robots cannot harm humans or allow humans to come to harm; 2. Robots must obey humans, except where the order would conflict with law 1; and 3. Robots must act in self-preservation, unless doing so conflicts with laws 1 or 2.

options.text: They are apparently divorced from reality.
They did not follow the coding system of robotics.
They laid a solid foundation for robotics.
They did not take moral issues into consideration.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about Asimov's robots?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者如何评价Asimov笔下的机器人?
A) 它们知道什么对人类有益或有害。
B) 它们被编程为不伤害人类。
C) 它们以主人的最大利益履行职责。
D) 当涉及道德问题时它们会停止工作。
**判型** What does the author say about Asimov's robots? 问的是文章如何描述这群机器人，答案能在文本中找到对应原句。
**拆句** What does the author say about Asimov's robots? 直问句，疑问代词 What 作 say 的宾语，about 引出对象；结构简单。
**定位** 这些法则被编程进阿西莫夫笔下的机器人体内——它们不必思考、判断或评价。它们不必喜欢人类，也不必认同伤害人类是错或恶。它们只是"不做"而已。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反They know what is good or bad for human beings. 与原文 They don't have to…believe that hurting them is wrong or bad 直接矛盾——原文说"不必相信伤害人类是错或恶"，即不需要知道善恶。
B) ✓ 正确These laws are programmed into Asimov's robots ↔They are programmed not to hurt human beings. Robots cannot harm humans or allow humans to come to harm ↔ not to hurt human beings正解抓住"被编程进去的就是不伤人"这一最核心机制，是定位句和法则1合并后的同义改写。
C) 无中生有They perform duties in their owners' best interest. 引入"主人最佳利益"这一文中根本没有的角色，原文谈的是 humans/humanity 而非 owners。
D) 过度推断They stop working when a moral issue is involved. 描述了"碰到道德问题就停工"的情景，原文只说机器人不需思考道德，没有任何"停工"的描述。
questions.quote: These laws are programmed into Asimov's robots—they don't have to think, judge, or value. They don't have to like humans or believe that hurting them is wrong or bad. They simply don't do it.

options.text: They know what is good or bad for human beings.
They are programmed not to hurt human beings.
They perform duties in their owners' best interest.
They stop working when a moral issue is involved.

questions.prompt: What does the author want to say by mentioning the word "harm" in Asimov's laws?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （例证目的题）
**题目译文**
作者提及Asimov定律中的"伤害"一词想要说明什么?
A) 抽象概念难以编程。
B) 机器人难以做出决策。
C) 机器人在某些情况下可能造成伤害。
D) Asimov的定律使用了过多模糊的术语。
**判型** What does the author want to say by mentioning the word "harm" in Asimov's laws?明确问"提到 harm 这个词意在说明什么"，是典型例证目的题。
**拆句** What does the author want to say by mentioning the word "harm" in Asimov's laws?主干 the author want to say what；by mentioning… 是方式状语；in Asimov's laws 修饰 harm，定位范围更精确。
**定位** 像"伤害"这样的词含义模糊（情感上的伤害算不算？取代一名人类员工算不算伤害？），而抽象概念在编程上会带来问题。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确abstract concepts present coding problems ↔ Abstract concepts are hard to program.预判方向是"抽象概念难编程"，A 几乎是 abstract concepts present coding problems 的逐词改写，是例证目的题的标准答案形态。
B) 答非所问It is hard for robots to make decisions. 谈的是机器人决策困难，是后续 P5 实验的结论，而非 harm 这个例子的目的。
C) 偷换概念Robots may do harm in certain situations. 谈机器人"在某些情境下会造成伤害"，混淆了 harm 例子的服务对象——这里 harm 是被讨论的词，不是机器人行为本身。
D) 以偏概全Asimov's laws use too many vague terms. 把"举一个模糊词 harm"夸大成"使用太多模糊术语"，原文只举一例并未做"too many"的程度判定。
questions.quote: A word such as "harm" is vague (what about emotional harm? Is replacing a human employee harm?), and abstract concepts present coding problems.

options.text: Abstract concepts are hard to program.
It is hard for robots to make decisions.
Robots may do harm in certain situations.
Asimov's laws use too many vague terms.

questions.prompt: What has the roboticist at the Bristol Robotics Laboratory found in his experiment?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
Bristol机器人实验室的机器人专家在实验中发现了什么?
A) 机器人有朝一日能够被制造得像人类一样智能。
B) 机器人的程序中可以编入道德问题。
C) 机器人在复杂场景中做决策时可能会遇到困难。
D) 机器人可以被编程以感知潜在危险。
**判型** What has the roboticist at the Bristol Robotics Laboratory found in his experiment?问的是实验具体发现，答案可直接在原文找到事实陈述。
**拆句** What has the roboticist at the Bristol Robotics Laboratory found in his experiment?现在完成时 has…found，强调发现这一动作的结果；at the Bristol Robotics Laboratory作 the roboticist 的后置定语，缩小指代范围。
**定位** 但当两个 H-bot 同时陷入险境时，该机器人有 42% 的概率"卡壳"——它无法决定先救哪一个，结果让两个都"死"了。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断Robots can be made as intelligent as human beings some day. 提到"将来"和"和人类一样聪明"，原文实验只给当下结果，未做任何未来预测。
B) 与原文相反Robots can have moral issues encoded into their programs. 说"可以把道德议题编码进程序"，与原文 The experiment highlights the importance of morality——之所以强调道德重要性恰是因为现在没编码进去——的逻辑相反。
C) ✓ 正确when two H-bots became imperiled, the robot choked 42 percent of the time, unable to decide which to save↔ Robots can have trouble making decisions in complex scenarios.选项把"两个 H-bot 同时遇险卡壳"的具体结果，抽象为"复杂场景下做决策困难"，是细节题最规范的同义改写。
D) 偷换概念Robots can be programmed to perceive potential perils. 把"被编程救人于险"偷换为"被编程感知风险"，但实验真正的发现是"在两难情境会卡壳"，而非"能否感知风险"。
questions.quote: But when two H-bots became imperiled, the robot choked 42 percent of the time, unable to decide which to save and letting them both "die."

options.text: Robots can be made as intelligent as human beings some day.
Robots can have moral issues encoded into their programs.
Robots can have trouble making decisions in complex scenarios.
Robots can be programmed to perceive potential perils.

title: The Pacific island nation of Palau has become…

sentences.text: The Pacific island nation of Palau has become home to the sixth largest marine sanctuary in the world.
The new marine reserve, now the largest in the Pacific, will (26)____ no fishing or mining.
Palau also established the world's first shark sanctuary in 2009.

passage.translation: 太平洋岛国帕劳已成为世界第六大海洋保护区的所在地。这个新的海洋保护区现在是太平洋最大的保护区,将禁止任何捕鱼或采矿活动。帕劳还在2009年建立了世界上第一个鲨鱼保护区。

sentences.text: The tiny island nation has set aside 500,000 square kilometres—80 percent—of its maritime(27)____ , for full protection.
That's the highest percentage of an (28)____ economic zone devoted to marine conservation by any country in the world.
The remaining 20 percent of the Palau seas will be reserved for local fishing by individuals and small-scale (29)____ fishing businesses with limited exports.

passage.translation: 这个小岛国已经划出50万平方公里——占其海洋领土的80%——用于全面保护。这是世界上任何国家专属经济区中用于海洋保护的最高比例。帕劳海域剩余的20%将保留给个人进行当地捕鱼以及出口受限的小规模商业捕鱼企业。

sentences.text: "Island (30)____ have been among the hardest hit by the threats facing the ocean," said President Tommy Remengesau Jr. in a statement.
"Creating this sanctuary is a bold move that the people of Palau recognise as (31)____ to our survival.
We want to lead the way in restoring the health of the ocean for future generations."

passage.translation: 总统小汤米·雷门格绍在一份声明中说:"岛屿社区一直是海洋面临威胁的最大受害者之一。创建这个保护区是一个大胆的举措,帕劳人民认识到这对我们的生存至关重要。我们希望在为子孙后代恢复海洋健康方面发挥带头作用。"

sentences.text: Palau has only been an (32)____ nation for twenty years and has a strong history of environmental protection.
It is home to one of the world's finest marine ecosystems, with more than 1,300 species of fish and 700 species of coral.

passage.translation: 帕劳成为独立国家仅有二十年,在环境保护方面有着深厚的历史。它是世界上最优质的海洋生态系统之一的所在地,拥有1300多种鱼类和700多种珊瑚。

These include the centuries-old custom of "bul", where leaders would call a temporary stop to fishing for key species in order to give fish (35)____ an opportunity to replenish(补

passage.translation: 充).帕劳国家海洋保护区法案的主要发起人参议员霍肯斯·鲍尔斯表示,该保护区将"通过尊重我们过去的保护传统,帮助为帕劳人民建设一个安全的未来"。这些传统包括有着数百年历史的"bul"习俗,即领导人会要求暂时停止捕捞关键物种,以便给鱼类种群一个补充的机会。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
The Pacific island nation of Palau has become home to the sixth largest marine sanctuary in the world. The new marine reserve, now the largest in the Pacific, will {{26}} no fishing or mining. Palau also established the world's first shark sanctuary in 2009.

The tiny island nation has set aside 500,000 square kilometres—80 percent—of its maritime{{27}} , for full protection. That's the highest percentage of an {{28}} economic zone devoted to marine conservation by any country in the world. The remaining 20 percent of the Palau seas will be reserved for local fishing by individuals and small-scale {{29}} fishing businesses with limited exports.

"Island {{30}} have been among the hardest hit by the threats facing the ocean," said President Tommy Remengesau Jr. in a statement. "Creating this sanctuary is a bold move that the people of Palau recognise as {{31}} to our survival. We want to lead the way in restoring the health of the ocean for future generations."

Palau has only been an {{32}} nation for twenty years and has a strong history of environmental protection. It is home to one of the world's finest marine ecosystems, with more than 1,300 species of fish and 700 species of coral.

Senator Hokkons Baules, lead {{33}} of the Palau National Marine Sanctuary Act, said the sanctuary will "help build a {{34}} future for the Palauan people by honoring the conservation traditions of our past". questions.explanation:
**答案** I) permit 动词
**词性槽** will __ no fishing or mining：助动词 will + 空 + 宾语
**依据** permit no fishing or mining = 不允许任何渔猎或采矿保护区的核心规则就是"禁渔禁矿"，permit no ... 的句式比 forbid 更地道、也最契合marine sanctuary 的设立目的；且呼应下句 Palau also established the world's first shark sanctuary in 2009.。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) allocate 搭配错乱allocate "分配" 通常带 to 结构（allocate sth to sb），allocate no fishing 既不合搭配，也不能表达"禁"的含义。
H) indulge 语义反向indulge 是"纵容 / 沉溺"，indulge no fishing 字面上像"不纵容捕鱼"，但实际惯用为 indulge in，与本句结构不匹配，且语义远不如 permit 干净。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) territory 名词
**词性槽** its maritime __：物主代词 + 形容词 + 空
**依据** maritime territory = 海洋领土/海域maritime territory 指一国的海洋领土；下句 The remaining 20 percent of the Palau seas 直接把 "its maritime territory" 等同于 "Palau seas"——"海域"正是 territory 在maritime 限定下的含义。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) celebrities 类别完全不符把 80% 的"海上名人"留作保护区在逻辑上不成立。
L) spectacle 可数性与语义偏离spectacle 多用于"具体景象"，与"国家划出 80% 海洋面积"的行政概念不在一个层面。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) exclusive 形容词
**词性槽** an __ economic zone：冠词 + 空 + 名词短语
**依据** 固定术语 exclusive economic zone（专属经济区）本句在讨论一个国家划给海洋保护的面积占比，所修饰对象正是国际法术语 exclusive economic zone（专属经济区），这是把空锁死的固定搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) commercial 搭配不成立commercial economic zone 不是固定术语；下文 small-scale __(29)__ fishing businesses 才是 commercial 的归宿。
E) essential语义偏离essential 表示"必不可少的"，与 economic zone 搭配语义空泛，且与上下文"专属经济区的占比"这一具体行政概念不匹配。
G) independent 概念错位independent 多修饰国家、机构是否独立，independent economic zone 不是约定俗成的术语；它将留给第 32 空 an __(32)__ nation。
K) solitary感情色彩冲突solitary 多用于人或事物"孤零零"的状态，与表示行政划界的 economic zone 完全不在一个语义场。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 G) —— independent 抢戏 exclusive。看到 an __(28)__economic zone，若不熟 exclusive economic zone（专属经济区）这个国际法术语，主体考生很容易随手填 independent"独立的经济区"。防坑：把术语本身记下来，看到economic zone 直接联想 exclusive。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) commercial 形容词
**词性槽** small-scale __ fishing businesses：形容词 + 空 + 名词
**依据** 与 with limited exports 呼应下文 with limited exports（出口受限）把这类企业定位为"商业性渔业"——commercial fishing businesses 是水产业里的固定术语，意指"商业捕捞企业"。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
K) solitary感情色彩与对象不符solitary fishing businesses"孤单的渔业企业"既不是术语，也无法解释 with limited exports这层商业含义。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) communities 名词
**词性槽** Island __ have been ...：形容词/名词 + 空 + 复数动词
**依据** Island communities = 岛屿社区/岛民群体Island communities 是地道说法，指"靠海/居于岛上的人群"；与下文 Creating this sanctuary is a bold move that the people of Palau recognise as __(31)__ to our survival. 中"我们的生存"指代关系吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) celebrities 对象错位Island celebrities"岛上名人"并非常见说法；且与"受海洋威胁打击最重"的群体不符——名人不会因海洋威胁就成为受害群体。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) essential 形容词
**词性槽** recognise ... as __ to our survival：as + 空 + to
**依据** 固定搭配 essential to survival essential to ...（对……至关重要）是高频搭配；与 our survival 组合后，语义"对我们的生存至关重要"与上文"a bold move"的果敢决策完全匹配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) commercial 语义不通commercial to our survival 既不是固定搭配，也无法解释"商业的对生存"这一逻辑。
G) independent 搭配错误independent of/from 才是惯用搭配；independent to our survival 不成立。
K) solitary 语义错位solitary 强调孤单、独自，与"对生存至关重要"的褒义判断不在同一频道。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) independent 形容词
**词性槽** has only been an __ nation：be + 冠词 + 空 + 名词
**依据** an independent nation 是常见搭配全篇反复出现 nation 形容帕劳是一个新兴的太平洋岛国；an independent nation"独立国家"既符合"独立才二十年"的史实，also 与下句"环保历史"对接自然。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) commercial 概念不沾边a commercial nation 不符合本句讨论"建国年限"的语境，把帕劳定性为"商业国"也与全文环保主旨相悖。
K) solitary 感情色彩偏负solitary 带"孤零零"意味，描述国家"独立建国"完全用不上，且与下文积极的环保叙事不协调。

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) sponsor 名词
**词性槽** lead __ of the Palau National Marine Sanctuary Act：形容词 + 空 + of 短语
**依据** lead sponsor of a bill/act = 法案的首席发起人在英美立法语境里，sponsor 指"提案议员/法案发起人"；lead sponsor of the ... Act 是固定政治术语，与"Senator Hokkons Baules"这个参议员身份完全匹配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) celebrities 复数 + 概念错位celebrities 是复数名词，前面 lead 形容词 + 单数冠位（同位语没有 a/an，常用单数）不匹配；"名人"也与立法发起人身份不沾。
L) spectacle 对象错位spectacle 指"奇观"，不能作"法案的领头人"。
O) territory 概念不对territory 指"领土、领地"，与"法案首席发起人"的角色身份毫不相关。

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) secure 形容词
**词性槽** build a __ future：动词 + 冠词 + 空 + 名词
**依据** a secure future 是熟搭配且呼应主旨a secure future for the Palauan people "为帕劳人民构建一个有保障的未来"是固定式表达；与上文 restoring the health of the ocean for future generations 的"为后代"主旨直接呼应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) commercial 感情色彩与主旨冲突commercial future 把"未来"商业化，与全篇"保护、传统、可持续"的基调正相反。
K) solitary 情感方向相反solitary 暗含"孤独的"，把帕劳人的未来描述成"孤单的未来"既不积极、也不符合 honoring conservation traditions 的语境。

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) stocks 名词
**词性槽** give fish __ an opportunity：动词 + 名词 + 空 + 名词短语
**依据** fish stocks = 鱼类种群，固定术语fish stocks 是水产/生态领域的固定术语，意为"鱼类资源、鱼群存量"；后接 an opportunity to replenish (补充)，正是 "让鱼类种群有机会补充"，与 "bul" 暂停捕捞的因果完全吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) celebrities 话题完全不沾celebrities 是"名人"，与鱼群、捕鱼语境毫无关系。
D) communities 已留给第 30 空communities 用作"群体"时，要么指"岛屿社区"——更适配 Island __(30)__，本空与 fish 复合得到 fish communities 并非固定术语，远不及 fish stocks 地道。
L) spectacle 语义偏离spectacle"奇观、景象"与"让鱼类种群有机会补充"语义不搭。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 D) —— communities 想冒充 stocks。give fish __(35)__ an opportunity to replenish(补充)，若不熟 fish stocks，主体考生可能想到 fish communities"鱼群"。防坑：替换法念一遍——"给鱼类群体一个补充的机会" 听上去虽通，但远不如"鱼类种群得以补充"的术语化表达地道；且 communities 已留给第 30 空。

title: Twenty years ago, the Urban Land Institute defined…

sentences.text: Twenty years ago, the Urban Land Institute defined the two types of cities that dominated the US landscape: smaller cities that operated around standard 9-5 business hours and large metropolitan areas that ran all 24 hours of the day.
Analyzing and comparing cities using the lens of this basic divide gives interesting context to how investment capital flows and housing prices have shifted.

passage.translation: 二十年前，Urban Land Institute定义了主导美国景观的两类城市：围绕标准朝九晚五工作时间运转的小型城市，以及全天24小时运转的大都市区。通过这一基本划分的视角来分析和比较城市，为理解投资资本流动和房价变化提供了有趣的背景。

sentences.text: In recent years, many mid-sized cities have begun to adopt a middle-of-the-road approach incorporating the excitement and opportunity of large cities with small cities' quiet after midnight.
These 18-hour cities are beginning to make waves in real estate rankings and attract more real estate investment.
What is underlying this new movement in real estate, and why do these cities have so much appeal?

passage.translation: 近年来，许多中等规模城市开始采取一种折中方式，将大城市的激动人心和机遇与小城市午夜后的宁静结合起来。这些18小时城市开始在房地产排名中引起关注，并吸引更多房地产投资。这一房地产新动向的根源是什么，为什么这些城市有如此大的吸引力？

sentences.text: 18-hour cities combine the best of 24-hour and 9-5 cities, which contributes to downtown revitalization.
For decades, many downtown cores in small to mid-sized cities were abandoned after work hours by workers who lived in the suburbs.
Movement out of city centers was widespread, and downtown tenants were predominantly made up of the working poor.
This generated little commerce for downtown businesses in the evenings, which made business and generating tax revenue for municipal upkeep difficult.

With the rise of a new concept in urban planning that aims to make life easier and more convenient, however, increasing popularity for urban areas that caused the real estate pushes, in major cities like San Francisco or New York, has inspired a type of forward thinking urbanity and policy in smaller cities.

passage.translation: 18小时城市结合了24小时城市和朝九晚五城市的优点，这促进了市中心的复兴。几十年来，许多中小型城市的市中心核心区在下班后被居住在郊区的工人遗弃。人口迁出市中心的现象十分普遍，市中心的租户主要由贫困劳动者构成。这使得市中心商业在晚间几乎没有商业活动，给经营和为市政维护创造税收带来困难。然而，随着旨在让生活更轻松便利的城市规划新理念的兴起，旧金山或纽约等大城市引发的房地产热潮带来的城市地区日益增长的人气，激发了小城市的一种前瞻性城市化思维和政策。

sentences.text: Transforming downtown areas so that they incorporate modern housing and improved walkability to local restaurants, retail, and entertainment—especially when combined with improved infrastructure for cyclists and public transit—makes them appeal to a more affluent demographic.
These adjustments encourage employers in the knowledge and talent industries to keep their offices downtown.

Access to foot traffic and proximity to transit allow the type of entertainment-oriented businesses such as bars and restaurants to stay open later, which attracts both younger, creative workers and baby boomers nearing retirement alike.

Because of their smaller size, most keep hours that allow people to enjoy themselves, then have some quiet after midnight, as opposed to large major cities like New York, where the buzz of activity is ongoing.

passage.translation: 改造市中心区域，使其融合现代住宅和改善的步行可达性，通往当地餐厅、零售店和娱乐场所——尤其是与改善的自行车和公共交通基础设施相结合时——使它们对更富裕的人口群体产生吸引力。这些调整鼓励知识和人才行业的雇主将办公室保留在市中心。人流和交通便利性使酒吧和餐厅等以娱乐为导向的企业能够营业到更晚，这既吸引年轻的创意工作者，也吸引临近退休的婴儿潮一代。由于规模较小，大多数城市的营业时间允许人们享受生活，然后在午夜后享有一些宁静，而不像纽约这样的大城市，活动的喧嚣持续不断。

sentences.text: These 18-hour cities are rapidly on the rise and offer great opportunities for homeowner investment.
In many of these cities such as Denver, a diverse and vigorous economy attracted to the urban core has offered stable employment for residents.
The right urban mix has propped up home occupancy, increased property values, and attracted significant investment capital.

passage.translation: 这些18小时城市正在迅速崛起，为房主投资提供了巨大机遇。在许多这类城市如丹佛，被吸引到城市核心的多元化和充满活力的经济为居民提供了稳定的就业。恰当的城市组合支撑了住房入住率，提高了房产价值，并吸引了大量投资资本。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about American cities twenty years ago?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于二十年前的美国城市,我们了解到什么?
A) 它们被划分为住宅区和商业区。
B) 它们的房价与繁荣程度相关联。
C) 大城市与小城市之间存在明显的分界。
D) 它们是大量投资资本流入的地方。
**判型** 题干 What do we learn about American cities twenty years ago 是对一个明确时间点的事实陈述发问，没有 infer/suggest/imply 一类信号，是典型的细节回指题。
**拆句** What do we learn about American cities twenty years ago? 主句是 What do we learn about X，about 后接介词宾语 American cities，twenty years ago 是修饰 American cities 的时间状语；结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 二十年前，城市土地学会定义了主导美国格局的两类城市：按朝九晚五标准营业时间运转的小城市，以及全天 24 小时不停转的大都市区。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有选项把原文"按运营时间分两类"偷换成"按 residential and business areas 分两类"，城市内部功能分区在原文毫无出处。
B) 强加因果原文只说分析两类城市能给 investment capital flows and housing prices have shifted 提供有趣背景，并未说 Their housing prices were linked with their prosperity；prosperity 这一概念在二十年前那句里并未出现。
C) ✓ 正确the two types of cities that dominated the US landscape ↔There was a clear divide between large and small cities. smaller cities that operated around standard 9-5 business hours and large metropolitan areas that ran all 24 hours of the day↔ between large and small cities预判落点是"大小城市之间存在清晰划分"，There was a clear divide between large and small cities. 把 two types 和 smaller cities ... large metropolitan areas 同时翻译过来，是定位句的同义替换，锁定 C。
D) 以偏概全原文说"用这一划分作镜头去看投资流向"，并不等于"美国城市是大投资流入之地"；places where large investment capital flowed 把"分析角度"偷换成"所有美国城市都是投资目的地"。
questions.quote: Twenty years ago, the Urban Land Institute defined the two types of cities that dominated the US landscape: smaller cities that operated around standard 9-5 business hours and large metropolitan areas that ran all 24 hours of the day.

options.text: They were divided into residential and business areas.
Their housing prices were linked with their prosperity.
There was a clear divide between large and small cities.
They were places where large investment capital flowed.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from the passage about 18-hour cities?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （推断题）
**题目译文**
从文章中可以推断出关于18小时城市的什么信息?
A) 它们特别吸引小型企业。
B) 它们的房地产价格出现了上涨。
C) 它们用兴奋取代了安静。
D) 它们改变了美国的景观。
**判型** 题干 What can be inferred from the passage about 18-hour cities 明示 inferred，要求基于原文做一步合理延伸。
**拆句** What can be inferred from the passage about 18-hour cities? What 作主语补语；can be inferred 是被动语态，from the passage 是来源状语，about 18-hour cities 是宾语补足；语序常规，无陷阱。
**定位** 这些 18 小时城市开始在房地产排行榜上崭露头角，并吸引更多的房地产投资。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有原文第四段说 18-hour cities 吸引 knowledge and talent industries 和entertainment-oriented businesses such as bars and restaurants，从未限定它"特别"吸引 small businesses，更没说"小型企业"是它的目标客群。
B) ✓ 正确attract more real estate investment ↔ They have seen a rise in property prices. make waves in real estate rankings ↔ a rise in property prices预判落点是"房产升值"，They have seen a rise in property prices. 正是这一预判的最佳同义改写——而且"see + n."是英语里非常常见的"经历某种变化"的句式，与原文进行时 are beginning to 在时态上相容。
C) 与原文相反原文是 incorporating the excitement and opportunity of large cities with small cities' quiet after midnight，强调"兼具"二者，选项 replaced quiet with excitement却把它扭曲成"用兴奋取代宁静"，方向与原文相反。
D) 过度推断原文只说 18-hour cities beginning to make waves in real estate rankings，规模和影响都还在起步，并未到 changed America's landscape 这种全国格局被改变的程度；况且"landscape 被改变"是第一段二十年前划分的语境。

questions.prompt: Years ago, many downtown cores in small to mid-sized cities__________.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
多年前,许多中小型城市的市中心核心区__________。
A) 几乎没有任何商业活动
B) 在营业时间内很拥挤
C) 没有表现出任何繁荣的迹象
D) 在晚上看起来很荒凉
**判型** 题干 Years ago, many downtown cores in small to mid-sized cities__________. 是一个待补全的客观事实陈述句，选项是它的延续，属于细节题。
**拆句** Years ago, many downtown cores in small to mid-sized cities__________. Years ago 作时间状语，主语是带介词短语修饰的 many downtown cores in small to mid-sized cities，谓语空缺待选项补齐；无陷阱。
**定位** 几十年来，许多小到中型城市的市中心在下班后被住在郊区的工作者抛弃。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全原文只说 This generated little commerce for downtown businesses in the evenings 是"晚间"商业少，而非"全天 hardly any business activity"。
B) 无中生有原文未对 downtown 在工作时段的状态作任何描述，更没说它在工作时段 crowded。
C) 过度推断原文虽然提到税收困难，但题干问 Years ago downtown 的整体状态，exhibited no signs of prosperity 是对"繁荣"的全盘否定，超出原文论断。
D) ✓ 正确were abandoned after work hours ↔ looked deserted in the evenings by workers who lived in the suburbs ↔ looked deserted in the evenings预判落点是"晚间被抛弃、冷清"，looked deserted in the evenings 是 were abandoned after work hours 的近义直译，锁定 D。
