questions.prompt: What characterizes the new downtown areas in 18-hour cities?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
18小时城市的新市中心区有什么特征?
A) 知识产业的突然兴起。
B) 大量外来务工人员涌入。
C) 现代化的住房和改善的基础设施。
D) 更舒适的生活和更大的向上流动性。
**判型** 题干 What characterizes the new downtown areas in 18-hour cities? 直接问 18-hour cities 新城区的特征，属于客观信息回指。
**拆句** What characterizes the new downtown areas in 18-hour cities? What 作主语，characterizes 是单数及物动词，宾语是 the new downtown areas in 18-hour cities；characterize 意为"成为……的特征"，注意它是"特征→对象"的指向，主语是特征。
**定位** 改造市中心，使其纳入现代住房并提升通往本地餐厅、零售与娱乐场所的步行便利度——尤其结合为骑行者与公共交通而改善的基础设施时——使它们吸引更富裕的人群。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文是 encourage employers in the knowledge and talent industries to keep their offices downtown，强调"留住"既有雇主，而非 A sudden emergence of the knowledge industry 这种"突然出现"。
B) 与原文相反原文吸引的是 a more affluent demographic 和 younger, creative workers and baby boomers nearing retirement，从未提及 migrant workers。
C) ✓ 正确modern housing ↔ Modernized housing and improved infrastructure. improved walkability to local restaurants, retail, and entertainment ↔improved infrastructure improved infrastructure for cyclists and public transit ↔ improved infrastructure预判落点是"现代化住房 + 基础设施改善"，Modernized housing and improved infrastructure. 同时覆盖原文 modern housing 与 improved walkability ... improved infrastructure，两个特征一一对应，锁定 C。
D) 无中生有原文吸引的是"已富裕人群"，并未涉及 upward mobility（阶层向上流动）；upward mobility 是社会学概念，原文没有任何对应句。
questions.quote: Transforming downtown areas so that they incorporate modern housing and improved walkability to local restaurants, retail, and entertainment—especially when combined with improved infrastructure for cyclists and public transit—makes them appeal to a more affluent demographic.

options.text: A sudden emergence of the knowledge industry.
Flooding in of large crowds of migrant workers.
Modernized housing and improved infrastructure.
More comfortable life and greater upward mobility.

questions.prompt: What have 18-hour cities brought to the local residents?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
18小时城市给当地居民带来了什么?
A) 更多的晋升机会。
B) 更健康的生活环境。
C) 更大的文化多样性。
D) 更好的就业机会。
**判型** 题干 What have 18-hour cities brought to the local residents? 直接问已经发生的结果，属于事实回指。
**拆句** What have 18-hour cities brought to the local residents? What 是 brought 的宾语前置，have...brought 是现在完成时，to the local residents 是间接宾语；brought 用现完表明结果延续至今。
**定位** 在许多这样的城市（比如丹佛），被吸引到市中心的多元而充满活力的经济为居民提供了稳定的就业。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有原文只说提供 stable employment，没有任何关于 promotion（晋升）的描述。
B) 过度推断原文未涉及任何健康/生活环境议题；Healthier living environment 与第四段的walkability、cyclists 看似擦边，但原文从未把它落到"健康"上。
C) 偷换概念原文是 a diverse and vigorous economy，diverse 修饰的是 economy（经济），而非选项 Greater cultural diversity 中的 culture（文化）。
D) ✓ 正确has offered stable employment for residents↔Better job opportunities.预判落点是"稳定就业"，Better job opportunities. 是 stable employment 的名词化同义改写，且其他三项都无原文出处，锁定 D。
questions.quote: In many of these cities such as Denver, a diverse and vigorous economy attracted to the urban core has offered stable employment for residents.

options.text: More chances for promotion.
Healthier living environment.
Greater cultural diversity.
Better job opportunities.

title: You may have heard that Coca-Cola once contained…

sentences.text: You may have heard that Coca-Cola once contained an ingredient capable of sparking particular devotion in consumers: cocaine.
The "Coca" in the name referred to the extracts of coca leaf that the drink's originator, chemist John Pemberton, mixed with his sugary syrup(浆汁).
At the time, coca leaf extract mixed with wine was a common tonic(滋补品), and Pemberton's sweet brew was a way to get around local laws prohibiting the sale of alcohol.
But the other half of the name presents another ingredient, less infamous(名声不好的), perhaps, but also strangely potent: the kola nut.

passage.translation: 你可能听说过可口可乐曾经含有一种能够激发消费者特殊热爱的成分：可卡因。名称中的"Coca"指的是这种饮料的创始人、化学家John Pemberton将古柯叶提取物与他的糖浆混合在一起。当时,古柯叶提取物与葡萄酒混合是一种常见的滋补品,而Pemberton的甜味饮品是一种规避当地禁止销售酒精法律的方法。但名称的另一半呈现了另一种成分,也许不那么臭名昭著,但同样奇特而有效:可乐果。

sentences.text: In West Africa, people have long chewed kola nuts as stimulants, because they contain caffeine that also occurs naturally in tea, coffee, and chocolate.
They also have heart stimulants.

passage.translation: 在西非,人们长期以来一直咀嚼可乐果作为兴奋剂,因为它们含有咖啡因,这种物质也天然存在于茶、咖啡和巧克力中。它们还含有心脏兴奋剂。

sentences.text: Historian Paul Lovejoy relates that the cultivation of kola nuts in West Africa is hundreds of years old.
The leafy, spreading trees were planted on graves and as part of traditional rituals.
Even though the nuts, which need to stay moist, can be somewhat delicate to transport, traders carried them hundreds of miles throughout the forests and grasslands.

passage.translation: 历史学家Paul Lovejoy讲述,西非种植可乐果已有数百年历史。这些枝叶繁茂、树冠开阔的树木被种植在坟墓上,并作为传统仪式的一部分。尽管这些果实需要保持湿润,在运输上可能有些脆弱,但商人们仍将它们运送数百英里,穿越森林和草原。

sentences.text: Europeans did not know of them until the 1500s, when Portuguese ships arrived on the coast of what is now Sierra Leone.

And while the Portuguese took part in the trade, ferrying nuts down the coast along with other goods, by 1620, when English explorer Richard Jobson made his way up the Gambia, the nuts were still peculiar to his eyes.

passage.translation: 直到16世纪,当葡萄牙船只抵达现今Sierra Leone的海岸时,欧洲人才知道它们的存在。虽然葡萄牙人参与了这一贸易,将可乐果与其他货物一起沿海岸运送,但到1620年,当英国探险家Richard Jobson沿冈比亚河而上时,这些果实在他眼中仍然很奇特。

sentences.text: By the late 19th century, kola nuts were being shipped by the tonne to Europe and the US.
Many made their way into medicines, intended as a kind of energy boost.
One such popular medicinal drink was Vin Mariani, a French product consisting of coca extract mixed with red wine.
It was created by a French chemist, Angelo Mariani, in 1863.
So when Pemberton created his drink, it represented an ongoing trend.
When cocaine eventually fell from grace as a beverage ingredient, kola-extract colas became popular.

passage.translation: 到19世纪末,可乐果正以吨为单位被运往欧洲和美国。许多进入了药品,旨在作为一种能量补充。其中一种流行的药用饮料是Vin Mariani,这是一种法国产品,由古柯提取物与红葡萄酒混合而成。它由法国化学家Angelo Mariani于1863年创制。因此,当Pemberton创制他的饮料时,它代表了一种持续的趋势。当可卡因最终失去作为饮料成分的地位时,可乐果提取物可乐变得流行起来。

sentences.text: The first year it was available, Coca-Cola averaged nine servings a day across all the Atlanta soda fountains where it was sold.
As it grew more popular, the company sold rights to bottle the soda, so it could travel easily.
Today about 1.9 billion Cokes are purchased daily.
It's become so iconic that attempts to change its taste in 1985—sweetening it in a move projected to boost sales—proved disastrous, with widespread anger from consumers.
"Coca-Cola Classic" returned to store shelves just three months after the "New Coke" was released.

passage.translation: 在上市的第一年,可口可乐在亚特兰大所有销售它的汽水柜台平均每天售出九份。随着它越来越受欢迎,公司出售了装瓶汽水的权利,以便它能够轻松流通。如今,每天约有19亿瓶可口可乐被购买。它已经变得如此具有标志性,以至于1985年改变其口味的尝试——在一项预计会提升销售的举措中使其更甜——被证明是灾难性的,引发了消费者的广泛愤怒。在"新可乐"发布仅三个月后,"可口可乐经典"就重新回到了商店货架上。

sentences.text: These days, the Coca-Cola recipe is a closely guarded secret.
But it's said to no longer contain kola nut extract, relying instead on artificial imitations to achieve the flavour.

passage.translation: 如今,可口可乐的配方是一个严格保密的秘密。但据说它不再含有可乐果提取物,而是依靠人工仿制品来达到这种风味。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about chemist John Pemberton?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于化学家John Pemberton我们了解到什么?
A) 他在一种食品补充剂中使用了一种效力异常强大的成分。
B) 他在不违反法律的情况下制造了一种含酒精的饮料。
C) 他因开发的古柯饮料而变得臭名昭著。
D) 他冒着违反当地法律的风险用古柯叶制作了一种饮料。
**判型** 题干 What do we learn about chemist John Pemberton 是 What do we learn about X句式，问的是文中关于某人的具体陈述，属于典型细节题。
**拆句** 题干 What do we learn about chemist John Pemberton 结构平铺直叙：特殊疑问句What do we learn about + 介宾 chemist John Pemberton，无陷阱。
**定位** 当时，coca 叶提取物兑酒是一种常见滋补品，而 Pemberton 那款甜饮料是绕开当地禁酒法的办法。但名字的另一半呈现了另一种原料——也许不那么臭名昭著，却同样奇异强劲：kola nut。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确another ingredient, less infamous, perhaps, but also strangely potent: the kola nut ↔a strangely potent ingredient Pemberton's sweet brew ↔ a food supplement预判要点是"用了 strangely potent 原料"，a strangely potent ingredient in a food supplement 把这一要点逐字搬入，且 in a food supplement 与定位句的 tonic 语境吻合，故锁定 A。
B) 与原文相反a drink containing alcohol without breaking law 谎称这款饮料"含酒"。原文Pemberton's sweet brew was a way to get around local laws prohibiting the sale of alcohol 恰恰相反——他的甜饮是为了绕开禁酒令，本身不含酒。
C) 张冠李戴He became notorious because of the coca drink he developed 称 Pemberton 因coca 饮变得 notorious。原文 another ingredient, less infamous, perhaps 中infamous 是修饰 ingredient（kola nut 相对 cocaine 较不"声名狼藉"），并未说Pemberton 本人臭名昭著。
D) 偷换概念He risked breaking local law to make a drink with coca leaves 说 Pemberton 冒着违法风险做 coca 饮。原文 a way to get around local laws 中 get around 是"绕开/规避"，并非"冒险触犯"。
questions.quote: At the time, coca leaf extract mixed with wine was a common tonic, and Pemberton's sweet brew was a way to get around local laws prohibiting the sale of alcohol. But the other half of the name presents another ingredient, less infamous, perhaps, but also strangely potent: the kola nut.

options.text: He used a strangely potent ingredient in a food supplement.
He created a drink containing alcohol without breaking law.
He became notorious because of the coca drink he developed.
He risked breaking local law to make a drink with coca leaves.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about kola nuts?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
文章关于可乐果说了什么?
A) 它们的商业价值最早是由葡萄牙定居者发现的。
B) 它们含有某种在任何其他食物中都找不到的能量提升物质。
C) 19世纪末许多可乐果被运往欧洲用于医疗用途。
D) 它们最初从西非进口时对欧洲人来说很陌生。
**判型** 题干 What does the passage say about kola nuts 是询问文中关于某物的客观陈述，属于细节题。
**拆句** 题干 What does the passage say about kola nuts 结构清楚，无难句。
**定位** 到 19 世纪末，kola nuts 已被吨级运往欧洲和美国。许多被用于药物，作为一种能量补给。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断Their commercial value was first discovered by Portuguese settlers 说葡萄牙"定居者"先发现"商业价值"。原文 Europeans did not know of them until the 1500s, when Portuguese ships arrived 只说葡萄牙人最先"知道"，while the Portuguese took part in the trade, ferrying nuts down the coast 只说他们参与贸易，未说"首先发现商业价值"，更无 settlers 一词。
B) 与原文相反They contain some kind of energy boost not found in any other food 说 kola nuts 有种"其他食物里没有的"提神成分。原文 they contain caffeine that also occurs naturally in tea, coffee, and chocolate 明确说咖啡因"也存在于茶、咖啡、巧克力"——恰恰是"其他食物里也有"。
C) ✓ 正确By the late 19th century, kola nuts were being shipped by the tonne to Europe and the US ↔Many were shipped to Europe in the late 19th century Many made their way into medicines ↔ for medicinal use预判要点是"19 世纪末大量运到欧美做药"，C 的 shipped to Europe + in the late 19th century + for medicinal use 三个要素逐一落到 P5 同一处，毫无遗漏，故锁定 C。
D) 偷换概念They were strange to the Europeans when first imported from West Africa 含"首次从西非进口"的时间设定。原文 by 1620, when English explorer Richard Jobson made his way up the Gambia, the nuts were still peculiar to his eyes 中 still peculiar 是说"到 1620 年还是稀奇"，并未把"稀奇"绑定到"首次进口"那一刻；且原文也未明说 1620 年发生"进口"动作。
questions.quote: By the late 19th century, kola nuts were being shipped by the tonne to Europe and the US. Many made their way into medicines, intended as a kind of energy boost.

options.text: Their commercial value was first discovered by Portuguese settlers.
They contain some kind of energy boost not found in any other food.
Many were shipped to Europe in the late 19th century for medicinal use.
They were strange to the Europeans when first imported from West Africa.

questions.prompt: How come kola-extract colas became popular?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
可乐果提取物可乐饮料是如何流行起来的?
A) 可卡因已经变得臭名昭著。
B) 酒精饮料被禁止了。
C) 设立了售卖它们的冷饮柜台。
D) 苏打水的装瓶销售权被出售了。
**判型** 题干 How come kola-extract colas became popular 以 How come 起头，问"为什么变得流行"，是对原文已存因果关系的直接提问。
**拆句** How come kola-extract colas became popular 中 How come = Why，后接陈述结构，结构简单。
**定位** 当 cocaine 作为饮料原料最终失宠时，kola 提取物可乐变得流行起来。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确cocaine eventually fell from grace as a beverage ingredient ↔ Cocaine had become notorious预判要点是"cocaine 失宠"，A 把 fell from grace 改成 became notorious，正是同义事实复述；其他三项都偏离了句内 when 所标定的原因。
B) 答非所问Alcoholic drinks were prohibited 取自 Pemberton's sweet brew was a way to get around local laws prohibiting the sale of alcohol，这是 1880 年代造可乐的背景，不是"cocaine 退场后 kola-extract colas 流行"的原因。
C) 无中生有Fountains were set up to sell them 取自 Coca-Cola averaged nine servings a day across all the Atlanta soda fountains where it was sold。soda fountains 是销售地点，非 kola-extract colas 整体流行的原因；且原文也未说"设立 fountains"是 colas 流行之因。
D) 与原文相反Rights were sold to bottle the soda 取自 As it grew more popular, the company sold rights to bottle the soda——原文用 As it grew more popular 明确把"卖装瓶权"放在"流行起来之后"，是结果不是原因。
questions.quote: When cocaine eventually fell from grace as a beverage ingredient, kola-extract colas became popular.

options.text: Cocaine had become notorious.
Alcoholic drinks were prohibited.
Fountains were set up to sell them.
Rights were sold to bottle the soda.

questions.prompt: What is known about the taste of Coca-Cola?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于Coca-Cola的味道人们知道什么?
A) 它被如此设计以在消费者中产生成瘾性。
B) 它仍然依赖传统的可乐果提取物。
C) 它在老年人中变得更受欢迎。
D) 自诞生以来它基本保持不变。
**判型** 题干 What is known about the taste of Coca-Cola 询问可口可乐口味的客观事实，属于细节题。
**拆句** 题干 What is known about the taste of Coca-Cola 结构清楚：被动疑问句，无难点。
**定位** 它已成为标志性饮品，以至于 1985 年试图改变口味——加甜以期推动销量——彻底失败，引发广泛消费者愤怒。"Coca-Cola Classic" 在 "New Coke" 发布仅三个月后就回到了货架上。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断It was so designed as to create addiction in consumers 说口味是"为了让消费者上瘾"而设计。原文只提到 capable of sparking particular devotion in consumers——"激起特别热爱"，且这是早期 cocaine 配方时代的描述，并非对 taste 的设计意图说明。
B) 与原文相反It still relies on traditional kola nut extract 说仍依赖传统 kola 提取物。原文 it's said to no longer contain kola nut extract, relying instead on artificial imitations 直接相反——已不含 kola，改用人工模拟。
C) 无中生有It has become more popular among the old 说在老年人中更受欢迎。原文 about 1.9 billion Cokes are purchased daily 只给销量数字，没有任何年龄群体的描述。
D) ✓ 正确attempts to change its taste in 1985 ... proved disastrous↔ remained virtually unchanged Coca-Cola Classic returned to store shelves just three months after the New Coke was released↔ since its creation预判要点是"改味失败、保持原样"，D 用 remained virtually unchanged since its creation 精准等值，故锁定 D。
questions.quote: It's become so iconic that attempts to change its taste in 1985—sweetening it in a move projected to boost sales—proved disastrous, with widespread anger from consumers. "Coca- Cola Classic" returned to store shelves just three months after the "New Coke" was released.

options.text: It was so designed as to create addiction in consumers.
It still relies on traditional kola nut extract.
It has become more popular among the old.
It has remained virtually unchanged since its creation.

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （主旨题）
**题目译文**
文章主要讲的是什么?
A) Coca-Cola的演变。
B) Coca-Cola的成功故事。
C) Coca-Cola的药用价值。
D) Coca-Cola的商业策略。
**判型** 题干 What is the passage mainly about 是经典主旨题问法，问全文主要内容。
**拆句** 题干 What is the passage mainly about 结构最简单的主旨疑问句，无陷阱。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确By the late 19th century↔ The evolution of Coca-Cola You may have heard that Coca-Cola once contained an ingredient capable of sparking particular devotion in consumers: cocaine↔ The evolution of Coca-Cola it's said to no longer contain kola nut extract, relying instead on artificial imitations↔The evolution of Coca-Cola B/C/D 都只能覆盖文中某一面（成功/药用/商业），唯有 A 的 evolution 把从起源—传播—改味—今日配方的所有段落功能囊括其中。
B) 以偏概全The success story of Coca-Cola 强调"成功故事"。文中只 Today about 1.9 billion Cokes are purchased daily 与 It's become so iconic 属于成功面，且 attempts to change its taste in 1985 ... proved disastrous 还含明显失败叙事，不构成主旋律。
C) 以偏概全The medicinal value of Coca-Cola 把主旨锁在"药用价值"上。原文 Many made their way into medicines, intended as a kind of energy boost 讲的是 kola nuts 入药，不是 Coca-Cola 本身的药用价值，且只局限在 19 世纪末这一段。
D) 以偏概全The business strategy of Coca-Cola 把主旨锁到"商业策略"。文中仅 the company sold rights to bottle the soda 与 sweetening it in a move projected to boost sales沾点商业策略，且后者还是失败案例；文章主体仍是历史演变，不是策略剖析。

options.text: The evolution of Coca-Cola.
The success story of Coca-Cola.
The medicinal value of Coca-Cola.
The business strategy of Coca-Cola.

title: In the past 12 months, Nigeria has suffered…

sentences.text: In the past 12 months, Nigeria has suffered from a shrinking economy, a sliding currency, and a prolonged fuel shortage.
Now, Africa's largest economy is facing a food crisis as major tomato fields have been destroyed by an insect, leading to a nationwide shortage and escalating prices.

passage.translation: 在过去12个月里,尼日利亚遭受了经济萎缩、货币贬值和长期燃料短缺的困扰。现在,非洲最大的经济体正面临粮食危机,主要番茄田被一种昆虫摧毁,导致全国性短缺和价格飙升。

sentences.text: The insect, Tutaabsoluta, has destroyed 80% of farms in Kaduna, Nigeria's largest tomato producing state, leading the government there to declare a state of (26)____ .
The insect, also known as the tomato leaf miner, devastates crops by (27)____ on fruits and digging into and moving through stalks.
It(28)____ incredibly quickly, breeding up to 12 generations per year if conditions are favorable.
It is believed to have (29)____ in South America in the early 1900s, and later spread to Europe before crossing over to sub-Saharan Africa.

passage.translation: 这种名为Tutaabsoluta的昆虫已经摧毁了尼日利亚最大番茄生产州卡杜纳80%的农场,导致当地政府宣布进入紧急状态。这种昆虫,也被称为番茄潜叶蛾,通过取食果实、钻入并穿行茎秆来破坏作物。它的繁殖速度极快,如果条件适宜,每年可繁殖多达12代。据信它起源于20世纪初的南美洲,后来传播到欧洲,然后越过撒哈拉以南非洲地区。

sentences.text: In Nigeria, where tomatoes are a staple of local diets, the insect's effects are devastating.
Retail prices for a (30)____ of tomatoes at local markets have risen from $0.50 to $2.50.
Farmers are reporting steep losses and a new $20 million tomato-paste factory has (31)____ production due to the shortages.

passage.translation: 在尼日利亚,番茄是当地饮食的主食,这种昆虫的影响是毁灭性的。当地市场上一把番茄的零售价格已从0.50美元上涨至2.50美元。农民们报告了严重的损失,一家耗资2000万美元的新番茄酱工厂因短缺而停产。

sentences.text: Given the moth's ability also to attack crops like pepper and potatoes, Audu Ogbeh, Nigeria's minister of agriculture, has warned that the pest may "create serious problems for food (32)____ " in the country.
Ogbeh says experts are investigating how to control the pest's damage and prevent its spread, which has gone largely (33)____ until now.

passage.translation: 鉴于这种飞蛾还能够攻击辣椒和土豆等作物,尼日利亚农业部长Audu Ogbeh警告说,这种害虫可能会给该国"粮食安全带来严重问题"。Ogbeh表示,专家们正在研究如何控制这种害虫的破坏并防止其传播,而这种传播迄今基本上未受到遏制。

sentences.text: Despite being the continent's second-largest producer of tomatoes, Nigeria is (34)____ on $1 billion worth of tomato-paste imports every year, as around 75% of the local harvest goes to waste thanks to a lack of proper storage facilities.
A further (35)____ in local supplies is yet another unwelcome setback to the industry.

passage.translation: 尽管是非洲第二大番茄生产国,但尼日利亚每年依赖价值10亿美元的番茄酱进口,因为由于缺乏适当的储存设施,大约75%的本地收成被浪费。本地供应的进一步减少对该行业来说是又一个不受欢迎的挫折。

groups.content:
In the past 12 months, Nigeria has suffered from a shrinking economy, a sliding currency, and a prolonged fuel shortage. Now, Africa's largest economy is facing a food crisis as major tomato fields have been destroyed by an insect, leading to a nationwide shortage and escalating prices.

The insect, Tutaabsoluta, has destroyed 80% of farms in Kaduna, Nigeria's largest tomato producing state, leading the government there to declare a state of {{26}} . The insect, also known as the tomato leaf miner, devastates crops by {{27}} on fruits and digging into and moving through stalks. It{{28}} incredibly quickly, breeding up to 12 generations per year if conditions are favorable. It is believed to have {{29}} in South America in the early 1900s, and later spread to Europe before crossing over to sub-Saharan Africa.

In Nigeria, where tomatoes are a staple of local diets, the insect's effects are devastating. Retail prices for a {{30}} of tomatoes at local markets have risen from $0.50 to $2.50. Farmers are reporting steep losses and a new $20 million tomato-paste factory has {{31}} production due to the shortages.

Given the moth's ability also to attack crops like pepper and potatoes, Audu Ogbeh, Nigeria's minister of agriculture, has warned that the pest may "create serious problems for food {{32}} " in the country. Ogbeh says experts are investigating how to control the pest's damage and prevent its spread, which has gone largely {{33}} until now.

Despite being the continent's second-largest producer of tomatoes, Nigeria is {{34}} on $1 billion worth of tomato-paste imports every year, as around 75% of the local harvest goes to waste thanks to a lack of proper storage facilities. A further {{35}} in local supplies is yet another unwelcome setback to the industry.

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) emergency 名词
**词性槽** 介词 of 后接名词
**依据** 固定搭配 state of emergency state of emergency 是新闻里几乎不变的固定表达『紧急状态』，与上文 The insect, Tutaabsoluta, has destroyed 80% of farms in Kaduna, Nigeria's largest tomato producing state 害虫造成 80% 农田被毁的严重程度也吻合——政府宣布紧急状态。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) handful 搭配不成立handful 通常用 a handful of＝一把，不会说 state of handful，搭配上根本不通。
H) multitude 搭配不成立multitude 也常以 a multitude of 出现，state of multitude 没有这种说法。
J) reduction 义不对题reduction 意为『减少』，state of reduction 既非固定搭配，与 80% 农田被毁后政府的反应（应是宣布紧急/告急）也不匹配。
L) security 义反state of security 意为『安全状态』，与害虫摧毁 80% 农田的灾情完全相反。且 L 在第 32 空有更明确归宿 food security。
M) terror 色彩过重state of terror 多指『恐怖状态』（如战乱/恐袭），程度与色彩都过头，新闻里描述农业灾情不会用这种政治化表达。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) feeding 动词
**词性槽** 介词 by + ___ 与并列 -ing 形式
**依据** feed on 以…为食feed on 是描述昆虫/动物『以…为食』的固定搭配，与 on fruits 直接咬合；上下文devastates crops by __(27)__ on fruits and digging into and moving through stalks.讲虫子如何破坏作物，吃果实正是破坏方式之一。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) Embarking 搭配错位embark on 意为『着手、开始（某事/旅程）』，主语应是人或机构开始项目，与 fruits 搭配既不合习惯也与『破坏作物』的语义无关。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) reproduces 动词
**词性槽** 主语 It + ___ + 副词 → 谓语第三人称单数
**依据** 繁殖呼应 12 generations reproduces 意为『繁殖』，紧接的 breeding up to 12 generations per year if conditions are favorable. 用 breeding（繁殖）和 generations（代）做同义复现，几乎是『把答案写在了下半句』。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) grazes 义不对题grazes 指『（食草动物）吃草』或『擦伤』，主语是害虫且后句讲『每年繁殖 12 代』，与吃草毫无关系。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 E) —— 看半句不看全句。只看 It ___ incredibly quickly 时，grazes 也读得通；忽略下半句 breeding up to 12 generations per year 的同义复现就会误选。防坑：选词填空读到逗号、读到 and 都必须读到句尾再下手。

questions.explanation:
**答案** I) originated 动词
**词性槽** 助动词 to have + 过去分词
**依据** originate in 地点 = 起源于originate in + 地点意为『起源于某地』，与下句 and later spread to Europe before crossing over to sub-Saharan Africa. 后来传到欧洲、再传到撒哈拉以南非洲构成『起源→传播』的标准链条。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) halted 义反halted in South America 意为『在南美被中止』，与下文紧接的『传到欧洲再到非洲』完全反向。且 F 在 31 空更贴切。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) handful 名词
**词性槽** a ___ of 名词复数
**依据** 量与价格逻辑相称a handful of tomatoes『一把番茄』的零售价从 0.5 升到 2.5 美元，价格涨幅描述合理；指零售层面消费者买一小把的常见单位。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) multitude 量级错位a multitude of 意为『大量的、众多的』，强调数目庞大，与零售层面『从 0.5 涨到 2.5 美元』的小份零售价对不上：大量番茄不可能只卖 2.5 美元。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— a ___ of 双量词陷阱。G) handful 与 H) multitude 都符合a ___ of N 结构，词性、搭配、形态全过；唯一靠『代入后量级与 from $0.50 to $2.50 价位是否相称』来判别——多数考生不做这一步常识校验。防坑：填完量词一定回头算一算量与数字配不配。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) halted 动词
**词性槽** has + ___ + 名词宾语 → p.p.
**依据** halt production 固定搭配halt production 意为『停产、中止生产』，与 due to the shortages 因番茄短缺逻辑契合，也与上句 Farmers are reporting steep losses 农户损失惨重的语境一致。

**答案** L) security 名词
**词性槽** 名词修饰名词，做后位中心词
**依据** food security 高频术语food security『粮食安全』是国际新闻、农业部官员发言中的固定术语，与 Audu Ogbeh, Nigeria's minister of agriculture, has warned that the pest may create serious problems for food __(32)__ 农业部长口吻完全吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) handful 搭配荒谬food handful 不成词，handful 通常作 a handful of。
H) multitude 搭配荒谬food multitude 不成词，且语义『食物的众多』与『害虫造成严重问题』的指向矛盾。
J) reduction 搭配不通food reduction 不是固定术语；且 J 留给第 35 空『供应进一步减少』更贴。
M) terror 搭配不通food terror 不存在；术语层面与农业部长警告语体不符。

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) unchecked 形容词
**词性槽** has gone + ___ 作系表中的表语
**依据** go unchecked 固定表达go unchecked 意为『一直未受遏制』，与 experts are investigating how to control the pest's damage and prevent its spread 专家正在研究如何控制蔓延形成因果呼应——正因之前未受遏制，现在才急需研究控制。

**答案** A) dependent 形容词
**词性槽** be 动词 + ___ + on 结构
**依据** be dependent on 黄金搭配be dependent on 意为『依赖』，与下句 as around 75% of the local harvest goes to waste thanks to a lack of proper storage facilities. 因储存设施不足、本地番茄大量浪费，所以需依赖进口『天衣无缝』。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
N) unchecked 搭配错位unchecked 意为『未受遏制』，不与 on 搭配；且语义与『每年花 10 亿美元进口番茄酱』毫无关联。N 留给第 33 空 gone unchecked。

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) reduction 名词
**词性槽** 形容词 further + ___ in
**依据** 进一步减少呼应 setback reduction 意为『减少』，与 A further __(35)__ in local supplies is yet another unwelcome setback to the industry. 中 further（进一步）和 setback（挫折）逻辑顺承——本地供应『进一步减少』正是行业的又一打击。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) multitude 义反a further multitude in supplies 等于『供应进一步众多』，与 setback（挫折/打击）方向完全相反，逻辑上矛盾。
M) terror 搭配荒谬a further terror in local supplies 不成英文表达，且 terror 程度过重，与行业供给数据语体不符。

title: Rich Children and Poor Ones Are Raised Very Differently

passage.label: A

sentences.text: The lives of children from rich and poor American families look more different than ever before.

passage.translation: 来自美国富裕家庭和贫困家庭的儿童,其生活状况比以往任何时候都更加不同。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: Well-off families are ruled by calendars, with children enrolled in ballet, soccer and after-school programs, according to a new Pew Research Center survey.
There are usually two parents, who spend a lot of time reading to children and worrying about their anxiety levels and hectic schedules.

passage.translation: 根据Pew研究中心的一项新调查,富裕家庭受日程表支配,孩子们参加芭蕾、足球和课后项目。通常有双亲,他们花大量时间给孩子读书,并担心他们的焦虑水平和繁忙的日程安排。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: In poor families, meanwhile, children tend to spend their time at home or with extended family.
They are more likely to grow up in neighborhoods that their parents say aren't great for raising children, and their parents worry about them getting shot, beaten up or in trouble with the law.

passage.translation: 与此同时,在贫困家庭中,孩子们往往在家中或与大家庭成员一起度过时间。他们更有可能在父母认为不太适合抚养孩子的社区长大,他们的父母担心他们被枪击、被殴打或惹上法律麻烦。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: The class differences in child rearing are growing—a symptom of widening inequality with far- reaching consequences.
Different upbringings set children on different paths and can deepen socioeconomic divisions, especially because education is strongly linked to earnings.
Children grow up learning the skills to succeed in their socioeconomic stratum(阶层), but not necessarily others.

passage.translation: 儿童抚养方面的阶层差异正在扩大——这是不平等加剧的一个症状,具有深远的影响。不同的成长经历使儿童走上不同的道路,并可能加深社会经济分化,尤其是因为教育与收入密切相关。儿童在成长过程中学习在其社会经济阶层中取得成功的技能,但不一定适用于其他阶层。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: "Early childhood experiences can be very consequential for children's long-term social, emotional and cognitive development," said Sean Reardon, professor of poverty and inequality in education at Stanford University.
"And because those influence educational success and later earnings, early childhood experiences cast a lifelong shadow."
The cycle continues: Poorer parents have less time and fewer resources to invest in their children, which can leave children less prepared for school and work, which leads to lower earnings.

passage.translation: Stanford大学贫困与教育不平等教授Sean Reardon说:"早期童年经历对儿童的长期社会、情感和认知发展可能产生重大影响。而且因为这些影响教育成功和日后收入,早期童年经历会投下终生的阴影。"这个循环继续:较贫困的父母投入到孩子身上的时间和资源更少,这可能使孩子在上学和工作方面准备不足,从而导致较低的收入。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: American parents want similar things for their children, the Pew report and past research have found: for them to be healthy and happy, honest and ethical, caring and compassionate.
There is no best parenting style or philosophy, researchers say, and across income groups, 92% of parents say they are doing a good job at raising their children.
Yet they are doing it quite differently.

Middle-class and higher-income parents see their children as projects in need of careful cultivation, says Annette Lareau, whose groundbreaking research on the topic was published in her book Unequal Childhoods: Class, Race and Family Life.
They try to develop their skills through close supervision and organized activities, and teach children to question authority figures and navigate elite institutions.

passage.translation: Pew报告和过去的研究发现,美国父母希望孩子得到类似的东西:健康快乐、诚实有道德、关心他人富有同情心。研究人员表示,没有最好的育儿方式或理念,在各个收入群体中,92%的父母表示他们在抚养孩子方面做得很好。然而他们的做法却大不相同。Annette Lareau说,中产阶级和高收入父母将孩子视为需要精心培养的项目,她关于这一主题的开创性研究发表在她的著作《不平等的童年:阶级、种族与家庭生活》中。他们试图通过密切监督和有组织的活动来培养孩子的技能,并教导孩子质疑权威人物和驾驭精英机构。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: Working-class parents, meanwhile, believe their children will naturally thrive, and give them far greater independence and time for free play.
They are taught to be compliant and respectful to adults.
There are benefits to both approaches.
Working-class children are happier, more independent, complain less and are closer with family members, Ms.
Lareau found.
Higher-income children are more likely to declare boredom and expect their parents to solve their problems.
Yet later on, the more affluent children end up in college and on the way to the middle class, while working-class children tend to struggle.
Children from higher-income families are likely to have the skills to navigate bureaucracies and succeed in schools and workplaces, Ms.
Lareau said.

passage.translation: 与此同时,工人阶级父母相信他们的孩子会自然茁壮成长,给予他们更大的独立性和自由玩耍的时间。他们被教导要顺从并尊重成年人。两种方法都有好处。Lareau女士发现,工人阶级的孩子更快乐、更独立、抱怨更少,与家人更亲近。高收入家庭的孩子更有可能表示无聊,并期望父母解决他们的问题。然而后来,更富裕的孩子最终进入大学并走向中产阶级,而工人阶级的孩子往往挣扎。Lareau女士说,来自高收入家庭的孩子更有可能具备驾驭官僚机构并在学校和工作场所取得成功的技能。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: "Do all parents want the most success for their children?
Absolutely," she said.
"Do some strategies give children more advantages than others in institutions?
Probably they do.
Will parents be damaging children if they have one fewer organized activity?
No, I really doubt it."

passage.translation: 她说:"所有父母都希望孩子获得最大的成功吗?绝对是的。某些策略是否比其他策略在机构中给孩子更多优势?可能是的。如果父母少安排一项有组织的活动,会伤害孩子吗?不,我真的怀疑。"

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Social scientists say the differences arise in part because low-income parents have less money to spend on music class or preschool, and less flexible schedules to take children to museums or attend school events.
Extracurricular activities reflect the differences in child rearing in the Pew survey, which was of a nationally representative sample of 1,807 parents.

Of families earning more than$75,000 a year, 84% say their children have participated in organized sports over the past year, 64%have done volunteer work and 62% have taken lessons in music, dance or art.
Of families earning less than $30,000, 59% of children have done sports, 37% have volunteered and 41% have taken arts classes.

passage.translation: 社会科学家表示,这些差异部分源于低收入父母用于音乐课或学前教育的钱更少,带孩子去博物馆或参加学校活动的日程安排也不够灵活。Pew调查中的课外活动反映了儿童抚养方面的差异,该调查对1807名具有全国代表性的父母样本进行了调查。在年收入超过75000美元的家庭中,84%表示他们的孩子在过去一年参加过有组织的体育活动,64%做过志愿工作,62%上过音乐、舞蹈或艺术课程。在年收入低于30000美元的家庭中,59%的孩子参加过体育活动,37%做过志愿者,41%上过艺术课。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: Especially in affluent families, children start young.
Nearly half of high-earning, college-graduate parents enrolled their children in arts classes before they were 5, compared with one-fifth of low- income, less-educated parents.
Nonetheless, 20% of well-off parents say their children's schedules are too hectic, compared with 8% of poorer parents.

passage.translation: 特别是在富裕家庭中,孩子很早就开始了。近一半高收入、大学毕业的父母在孩子5岁前就让他们参加艺术课程,而低收入、教育程度较低的父母中只有五分之一这样做。尽管如此,20%的富裕父母表示孩子的日程太繁忙,而较贫困父母中只有8%这样认为。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: Another example is reading aloud, which studies have shown gives children bigger vocabularies and better reading comprehension in school. 71% of parents with a college degree say they do it every day, compared with 33% of those with a high school diploma or less.
White parents are more likely than others to read to their children daily, as are married parents.
Most affluent parents enroll their children in preschool or day care, while low-income parents are more likely to depend on family members.
Discipline techniques vary by education level: 8% of those with a postgraduate degree say they often beat their children, compared with 22% of those with a high school degree or less.

passage.translation: 另一个例子是大声朗读,研究表明这能让孩子拥有更大的词汇量和更好的学校阅读理解能力。71%拥有大学学位的父母表示他们每天都这样做,而拥有高中文凭或更低学历的父母中只有33%这样做。白人父母比其他人更有可能每天给孩子读书,已婚父母也是如此。大多数富裕父母让孩子上学前班或日托,而低收入父母更有可能依赖家庭成员。管教技巧因教育水平而异:8%拥有研究生学位的人表示他们经常打孩子,而拥有高中学历或更低学历的人中有22%这样做。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: The survey also probed attitudes and anxieties.
Interestingly, parents' attitudes toward education do not seem to reflect their own educational background as much as a belief in the importance of education for upward mobility.
Most American parents say they are not concerned about their children's grades as long as they work hard.
But 50% of poor parents say it is extremely important to them that their children earn a college degree, compared with 39% of wealthier parents.

passage.translation: 该调查还探究了态度和焦虑。有趣的是,父母对教育的态度似乎不太反映他们自己的教育背景,而更多地反映对教育对于向上流动的重要性的信念。大多数美国父母表示,只要孩子努力学习,他们就不担心孩子的成绩。但50%的贫困父母表示,孩子获得大学学位对他们来说极其重要,而较富裕父母中只有39%这样认为。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: Less-educated parents, and poorer and black and Latino parents are more likely to believe that there is no such thing as too much involvement in a child's education.
Parents who are white, wealthy or college-educated say too much involvement can be bad.
Parental anxieties reflect their circumstances.
High-earning parents are much more likely to say they live in a good neighborhood for raising children.
While bullying is parents' greatest concern overall, nearly half of low-income parents worry their child will get shot, compared with one-fifth of high-income parents.
They are more worried about their children being depressed or anxious.

passage.translation: 教育程度较低的父母,以及较贫困、黑人和拉丁裔父母更有可能认为,在孩子的教育中不存在过度参与这回事。白人、富裕或受过大学教育的父母则表示过度参与可能是坏事。父母的焦虑反映了他们的处境。高收入父母更有可能表示他们生活在适合抚养孩子的好社区。虽然欺凌是父母总体上最关心的问题,但近一半的低收入父母担心孩子会被枪击,而高收入父母中只有五分之一担心这一点。他们更担心孩子会抑郁或焦虑。

passage.label: N

sentences.text: In the Pew survey, middle-class families earning between $30,000 and $75,000 a year fell right between working-class and high-earning parents on issues like the quality of their neighborhood for raising children, participation in extracurricular activities and involvement in their children's education.

passage.translation: 在Pew调查中,年收入在30000至75000美元之间的中产阶级家庭,在诸如抚养孩子的社区质量、参与课外活动以及参与孩子教育等问题上,正好处于工人阶级和高收入父母之间。

passage.label: O

sentences.text: Children were not always raised so differently.
The achievement gap between children from high- and low-income families is 30–40% larger among children born in 2001 than those born 25 years earlier, according to Mr.
Reardon's research.
People used to live near people of different income levels; neighborhoods are now more segregated by income.

More than a quarter of children live in single-parent households—a historic high, according to Pew—and these children are three times as likely to live in poverty as those who live with married parents.
Meanwhile, growing income inequality has coincided with the increasing importance of a college degree for earning a middle- class wage.

passage.translation: 儿童的抚养方式并非总是如此不同。根据Reardon先生的研究,2001年出生的儿童与25年前出生的儿童相比,来自高收入和低收入家庭儿童之间的成就差距扩大了30-40%。人们过去住在不同收入水平的人附近;现在社区按收入更加隔离。根据Pew的数据,超过四分之一的儿童生活在单亲家庭中——这是历史最高水平——这些儿童生活在贫困中的可能性是与已婚父母一起生活的儿童的三倍。与此同时,收入不平等的加剧与大学学位对获得中产阶级工资的重要性日益增加同时发生。

passage.label: P

sentences.text: Yet there are recent signs that the gap could be starting to shrink.
In the past decade, even as income inequality has grown, some of the socioeconomic differences in parenting, like reading to children and going to libraries, have narrowed.

passage.translation: 然而,最近有迹象表明差距可能开始缩小。在过去十年中,即使收入不平等有所加剧,育儿方面的一些社会经济差异,如给孩子读书和去图书馆,已经缩小。

passage.label: Q

sentences.text: Public policies aimed at young children have helped, including public preschool programs and reading initiatives.
Addressing differences in the earliest years, it seems, could reduce inequality in the next generation.

passage.translation: 针对幼儿的公共政策有所帮助,包括公共学前教育项目和阅读倡议。看来,解决最早期的差异可能会减少下一代的不平等。

Probably they do，是承认某些策略更占优，并非'两种方式都有好处'的对称评价。Do some strategies give children more advantages than others in institutions? Probably they do. title: Elite Math Competitions Struggle to Diversify Their Talent Pool

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Interest in elite high school math competitions has grown in recent years, and in light of last summer's U.S. win at the International Math Olympiad (IMO)—the first for an American team in more than two decades—the trend is likely to continue.

passage.translation: 近年来，人们对精英高中数学竞赛的兴趣日益增长，鉴于去年夏天美国队在国际数学奥林匹克竞赛(IMO)中获胜——这是美国队二十多年来的首次胜利——这一趋势很可能会持续下去。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: But will such contests, which are overwhelmingly dominated by Asian and white students from middle-class and affluent families, become any more diverse?
Many social and cultural factors play roles in determining which promising students get on the path toward international math recognition.

But efforts are in place to expose more black, Hispanic, and low-income students to advanced math, in the hope that the demographic pool of high-level contenders will eventually begin to shift and become less exclusive.

passage.translation: 但是，这些竞赛会变得更加多元化吗?目前这些竞赛绝大多数由来自中产阶级和富裕家庭的亚裔和白人学生主导。许多社会和文化因素在决定哪些有前途的学生走上国际数学认可之路方面发挥着作用。但目前正在努力让更多黑人、西班牙裔和低收入家庭学生接触高等数学,希望高水平竞争者的人口构成最终能开始转变,变得不那么排他。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: "The challenge is if certain types of people are doing something, it's difficult for other people to break into it," said Po-Shen Loh, the head coach of last year's winning U.S.
Math Olympiad team.
Participation grows through friends and networks and if "you realize that's how they're growing, you can start to take action" and bring in other students, he said.

passage.translation: 去年获胜的美国数学奥林匹克队主教练罗博深说:"挑战在于,如果某些类型的人在做某事,其他人就很难打入其中。"参与度通过朋友和网络增长,如果"你意识到他们就是这样增长的,你就可以开始采取行动"并引入其他学生,他说。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: Most of the training for advanced-math competitions happens outside the confines of the normal school day.
Students attend after-school clubs, summer camps, online forums and classes, and university-based "math circles", to prepare for the competitions.

passage.translation: 大多数高等数学竞赛的训练都发生在正常上学日之外。学生们参加课后俱乐部、夏令营、在线论坛和课程,以及大学的"数学圈",为竞赛做准备。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: One of the largest feeders for high school math competitions—including those that eventually lead to the IMO—is a middle school program called Math Counts.
About 100,000 students around the country participate in the program's competition series, which culminates in a national game-show- style contest held each May.
The most recent one took place last week in Washington, D.C.
Students join a team through their schools, which provide a volunteer coach and pay a nominal fee to send students to regional and state competitions.
The 224 students who make it to the national competition get an all-expenses-paid trip.

passage.translation: 高中数学竞赛——包括那些最终通向IMO的竞赛——最大的生源之一是一个名为Math Counts的初中项目。全国约有10万名学生参加该项目的系列竞赛,竞赛在每年五月举行的一场全国游戏节目式比赛中达到高潮。最近的一场比赛上周在华盛顿特区举行。学生通过学校加入一个团队,学校提供志愿教练并支付少量费用将学生送往地区和州级竞赛。进入全国竞赛的224名学生可获得全额报销的旅行。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: Nearly all members of last year's winning U.S.
IMO team took part in Math Counts as middle school students, as did Loh, the coach.
"Middle school is an important age because students have enough math capability to solve advanced problems, but they haven't really decided what they want to do with their lives," said Loh.
"They often get hooked then."

passage.translation: 去年获胜的美国IMO队的几乎所有成员在初中时都参加过Math Counts,教练罗博深也是如此。"初中是一个重要的年龄段,因为学生有足够的数学能力解决高难度问题,但他们还没有真正决定要如何度过一生,"罗博深说。"他们往往在那时被吸引住。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: Another influential feeder for advanced-math students is an online school called Art of Problem Solving, which began about 13 years ago and now has 15,000 users.
Students use forums to chat, play games, and solve problems together at no cost, or they can pay a few hundred dollars to take courses with trained teachers.
According to Richard Rusczyk, the company founder, the six U.S. team members who competed at the IMO last year collectively took more than 40 courses on the site.
Parents of advanced-math students and Math Counts coaches say the children are on the website constantly.

passage.translation: 另一个对高等数学学生有影响力的生源是一所名为Art of Problem Solving的在线学校,该校始于约13年前,现在有1.5万名用户。学生使用论坛免费聊天、玩游戏和一起解决问题,或者他们可以支付几百美元与受过培训的教师一起上课。据公司创始人Richard Rusczyk说,去年在IMO参赛的六名美国队成员在该网站上总共学习了40多门课程。高等数学学生的家长和Math Counts教练说,孩子们一直在这个网站上。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: There are also dozens of summer camps—many attached to universities—that aim to prepare elite math students.
Some are pricey—a three-week intensive program can cost $4,500 or more—but most offer scholarships.

The Math Olympiad Summer Training Program is a three-week math camp held by the Mathematical Association of America that leads straight to the international championship and is free for those who make it.
Only about 50 students are invited based on their performance on written tests and at the USA Math Olympiad.

passage.translation: 还有数十个夏令营——其中许多附属于大学——旨在培养精英数学学生。有些价格昂贵——一个为期三周的强化项目可能花费4500美元或更多——但大多数提供奖学金。数学奥林匹克夏季培训项目是由美国数学协会举办的为期三周的数学夏令营,直接通向国际锦标赛,对于入选者免费。只有约50名学生根据他们在笔试和美国数学奥林匹克竞赛中的表现受邀参加。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Students in university towns may also have access to another lever for involvement in accelerated math: math circles.

In these groups, which came out of an Eastern European tradition of developing young talent, professors teach promising K-12 students advanced mathematics for several hours after school or on weekends.
The Los Angeles Math Circle, held at the University of California, Los Angeles, began in 2007 with 20 students and now has more than 250.
"These math circles cost nothing, or they're very cheap for students to get involved in, but you have to know about them," said Rusczyk.
"Most people would love to get students from more underserved populations, but they just can't get them in the door.
Part of it is communication; part of it is transportation."

passage.translation: 大学城的学生也可能有另一个参与加速数学的途径:数学圈。在这些小组中,教授在放学后或周末向有前途的K-12学生教授高等数学数小时,这源于东欧培养年轻人才的传统。位于加州大学洛杉矶分校的洛杉矶数学圈于2007年开始时有20名学生,现在有250多名。"这些数学圈不花钱,或者学生参与的成本非常低,但你必须了解它们,"Rusczyk说。"大多数人都希望从更缺乏服务的人群中招收学生,但他们就是无法让他们进门。部分原因是沟通;部分原因是交通。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: It's no secret in the advanced-math community that diversity is a problem.

According to Mark Saul, the director of competitions for the Mathematical Association of America, not a single African- American or Hispanic student—and only a handful of girls—has ever made it to the Math Olympiad team in its 50 years of existence.
Many schools simply don't prioritize academic competitions.
"Do you know who we have to beat?" asked Saul.
"The football team, the basketball team—that's our competition for resources, student time, attention, school dollars, parent efforts, school enthusiasm."

passage.translation: 在高等数学界,多样性是一个问题已不是什么秘密。据美国数学协会竞赛主任Mark Saul说,在数学奥林匹克队存在的50年里,没有一个非裔美国人或西班牙裔学生——只有少数女孩——进入过该队。许多学校根本不优先考虑学术竞赛。"你知道我们必须击败谁吗?"Saul问道。"足球队、篮球队——那是我们在资源、学生时间、注意力、学校资金、家长努力、学校热情方面的竞争对手。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: Teachers in low-income urban and rural areas with no history of participating in math competitions may not know about advanced-math opportunities like Math Counts—and those who do may not have support or feel trained to lead them.

passage.translation: 在没有参加数学竞赛历史的低收入城市和农村地区的教师可能不了解像Math Counts这样的高等数学机会——即使了解的人也可能没有支持或感觉没有受过培训来领导它们。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: But there are initiatives in place to try to get more underrepresented students involved in accelerated math.

A New York City-based nonprofit called Bridge to Enter Mathematics runs a residential summer program aimed at getting underserved students, mostly black and Hispanic, working toward math and science careers.
The summer after 7th grade, students spend three weeks on a college campus studying advanced math for seven hours a day.
Over the next five years, the group helps the students get into other elite summer math programs, high-performing high schools, and eventually college.
About 250 students so far have gone through the program, which receives funding from the Jack Kent Cooke Foundation.

passage.translation: 但是,已有举措试图让更多代表性不足的学生参与加速数学。一个名为Bridge to Enter Mathematics的纽约市非营利组织运营一个住宿暑期项目,旨在让缺乏服务的学生(主要是黑人和西班牙裔)朝着数学和科学职业努力。在七年级后的暑假,学生在大学校园里度过三周,每天学习七小时的高等数学。在接下来的五年里,该组织帮助学生进入其他精英暑期数学项目、高水平高中,最终进入大学。到目前为止,约有250名学生完成了该项目,该项目获得Jack Kent Cooke基金会的资助。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: "If you look at a lot of low-income communities in the United States, there are programs that are serving them, but they're primarily centered around 'Let's get these kids' grades up', and not around'Let's get these kids access to the same kinds of opportunities as more-affluent kids,'" said Daniel Zaharopol, the founder and executive director of the program.
"We're trying to create that pathway."
Students apply to the program directly through their schools.
"We want to reach parents who are not plugged into the system," said Zaharopol.

passage.translation: "如果你看看美国许多低收入社区,有一些项目在为他们服务,但这些项目主要围绕'让我们提高这些孩子的成绩',而不是'让我们让这些孩子获得与更富裕的孩子相同的机会',"该项目创始人兼执行董事Daniel Zaharopol说。"我们正在努力创造那条道路。"学生直接通过学校申请该项目。"我们想接触那些没有融入体系的家长,"Zaharopol说。

passage.label: N

sentences.text: In the past few years, Math Counts added two new middle school programs to try to diversify its participant pool—the National Math Club and the Math Video Challenge.
Schools or teachers who sign up for the National Math Club receive a kit full of activities and resources, but there's no special teacher training and no competition attached.

passage.translation: 在过去几年中,Math Counts增加了两个新的初中项目,试图使其参与者群体多样化——全国数学俱乐部和数学视频挑战赛。报名参加全国数学俱乐部的学校或教师会收到一个装满活动和资源的工具包,但没有特殊的教师培训,也没有附带竞赛。

passage.label: O

sentences.text: The Math Video Challenge is a competition, but a collaborative one.
Teams of four students make a video illustrating a math problem and its real-world application.

After the high-pressure Countdown round at this year's national Math Counts competition, in which the top 12 students went head to head solving complex problems in rapid fire, the finalists for the Math Video Challenge took the stage to show their videos.
The demographics of that group looked quite different from those in the competition round—of the 16 video finalists, 13 were girls and eight were African-American students.
The video challenge does not put individual students on the hot seat—so it's less intimidating by design.
It also adds the element of artistic creativity to attract a new pool of students who may not see themselves as "math people".

passage.translation: 数学视频挑战赛是一场竞赛,但是一场协作性竞赛。四名学生组成的团队制作一个视频,展示一个数学问题及其现实世界应用。在今年全国Math Counts竞赛的高压倒计时环节之后(前12名学生快速解决复杂问题进行正面交锋),数学视频挑战赛的决赛选手登台展示他们的视频。该组的人口构成与竞赛环节中的看起来大不相同——在16名视频决赛选手中,13名是女孩,8名是非裔美国学生。视频挑战赛不会让个别学生处于被审查的境地——所以从设计上来说不那么令人生畏。它还增加了艺术创造力的元素,以吸引可能不认为自己是"数学人"的新学生群体。

Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: Middle school is a crucial period when students may become keenly interested in advanced mathematics.
