J lack of enthusiasm could stem from concerns about privacy and security 与 18 percent have even returned devices 谈的是更广义的隐私安全担忧和退货比例，没有把「为换定制服务而交数据」这条因果链单独点出，对应度不如 H 段精准。concerns about privacy and security
questions.quote: And when it comes to the hyper-connected super-smart world that technology firms are painting for us, it seems that consumers are growing more uneasy about handing over the massive amounts of consumer data needed to provide the personalized, customized solutions that companies need to improve their services.

questions.prompt: The Consumer Technology Association is the sponsor of the annual Consumer Electronics Show.
questions.explanation:
**答案** E 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
消费者技术协会是年度消费电子展的赞助方。
**锚点** CTA是CES的主办方
**定位** DuBravac 任职于 CTA——这家机构正是每年主办这场展会的——他说，这种「转向寻找解决方案」的趋势在他做 2016 年预测时已经很明显。
**改写** The Consumer Technology Association ↔ CTA全称对应缩写is the sponsor of the annual Consumer Electronics Show ↔ puts on the show each year主办年度展会对应每年举办这场展会
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
C Gary Shapiro, president and chief executive of the Consumer Technology Association (CTA) 只交代了人物在 CTA 的身份，未陈述 CTA 与 CES 之间的主办关系。Gary Shapiro, president and chief executive of the Consumer Technology Association (CTA)
questions.quote: DuBravac works for CTA—which puts on the show each year—and said that this shift to a search for solutions has been noticeable as he researched his predictions for 2016.

questions.prompt: Many consumers wonder about the necessity of having their fitness monitored.
questions.explanation:
**答案** I 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
许多消费者对监测自己的健康状况的必要性感到疑惑。
**锚点** 对自己健身被监测的必要性产生质疑
**定位** 然而，「我为什么需要这个？」——或更耐人寻味的「你为什么需要知道这些？」——这一持续不去的质问，仍然纠缠着许多新企业前行的脚步。
**改写** Many consumers wonder about the necessity ↔ Why do I need that?质疑必要性对应我为什么需要这个having their fitness monitored ↔ tracking our steps and our very heartbeats健身被监测对应追踪步数和心跳
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
J concerns about privacy and security 与 safer guarantees against having their sensitive information hacked 谈的是隐私和安全风险，不是 wonder about the necessity 的「质疑必要性」。lack of enthusiasm could stem from concerns about privacy and security
questions.quote: Yet the persistent question of Why do I need that?—or, perhaps more tellingly, Why do you need to know that?—dogs the steps of many new ventures.

questions.prompt: The electronic industry is maturing even though no wonder products hit the market.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
尽管没有令人惊叹的产品上市,电子行业正在走向成熟。
**锚点** 无爆款但行业在成熟
**定位** 「没有任何一鸣惊人的爆款，未来几年内也不会有，」消费技术协会（CTA）总裁兼首席执行官 Gary Shapiro 说。然而在他看来，这并不意味着创新已经停止，它只是稍微长大了一点。「许多行业正从婴儿期走向青春期，」Shapiro 说道。
**改写** The electronic industry is maturing ↔Many industries are going out of infancy and becoming adolescents成熟中对应脱离婴儿期走向青春期no wonder products hit the market ↔There is not any one-hit wonder, and there will not be one for years to come无爆款上市对应没有一鸣惊人的爆款even though ↔ that doesn't necessarily mean that innovation has stopped让步关系对应虽然没爆款但创新没停在成长
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B slower growth curves—or shrinking markets in some cases 描述的是市场需求指标的变化，而非「行业从婴儿期走向青春期」那种结构成熟。these segments are looking at slower growth curves—or shrinking markets in some cases
questions.quote: There is not any one-hit wonder, and there will not be one for years to come, said Gary Shapiro, president and chief executive of the Consumer Technology Association (CTA). In his eyes, however, that doesn't necessarily mean that innovation has stopped. It has just grown up a little. Many industries are going out of infancy and becoming adolescents, Shapiro said.

sentences.text: What a waste of money!
In return for an average of £44,000 of debt, students get an average of only 14 hours of lecture and tutorial time a week in Britain.
Annual fees have risen from £1,000 to£9,000 in the last decade, but contact time at university has barely risen at all.
And graduating doesn't even provide any guarantee of a decent job: six in ten graduates today are in non-graduate jobs.

passage.translation: 真是浪费钱！英国学生平均背负44,000英镑的债务，换来的却是平均每周仅14小时的讲座和辅导时间。在过去十年里，年度学费从1,000英镑涨到了9,000英镑，但大学的面授时间几乎没有增加。而且毕业甚至无法保证获得一份体面的工作：如今十分之六的毕业生从事的是非毕业生工作。

sentences.text: No wonder it has become fashionable to denounce many universities as little more than elaborate con-tricks(骗术).

There's a lot for students to complain about: the repayment threshold for paying back loans will be frozen for five years, meaning that lower-paid graduates have to start repaying their loans; and maintenance grants have been replaced by loans, meaning that students from poorer backgrounds face higher debt than those with wealthier parents.

passage.translation: 难怪谴责许多大学不过是精心设计的骗术已成为一种时尚。学生有很多可抱怨的：偿还贷款的起征点将冻结五年，这意味着收入较低的毕业生必须开始偿还贷款；而且助学金已被贷款取代，这意味着来自贫困家庭的学生比那些父母富裕的学生面临更高的债务。

sentences.text: Yet it still pays to go to university.
If going to university doesn't work out, students pay very little—if any—of their tuition fees back: you only start repaying when you are earning £21,000 a year.
Almost half of graduates—those who go on to earn less—will have a portion of their debt written off.
It's not just the lectures and tutorials that are important.
Education is the sum of what students teach each other in between lectures and seminars.
Students do not merely benefit while at university; studies show—they go on to be healthier and happier than non-graduates, and also far more likely to vote.

passage.translation: 然而上大学仍然是值得的。如果上大学不成功，学生只需偿还极少的学费——如果有的话：只有当你年收入达到21,000英镑时才开始偿还。近一半的毕业生——那些后来收入较低的人——将有一部分债务被免除。重要的不仅仅是讲座和辅导。教育是学生在讲座和研讨会之间相互传授的知识的总和。学生不仅在大学期间受益；研究表明——他们会比非毕业生更健康、更快乐，而且更有可能去投票。

sentences.text: Whatever your talents, it is extraordinarily difficult to get a leading job in most fields without having been to university.
Recruiters circle elite universities like vultures(兀鹰).
Many top firms will not even look at applications from those who lack a 2.1, i.e., an upper-second class degree, from an elite university.
Students at university also meet those likely to be in leading jobs in the future, forming contacts for life.
This might not be right, but school-leavers who fail to acknowledge as much risk making the wrong decision about going to university.

passage.translation: 无论你有什么才能，在大多数领域，如果没有上过大学，要获得一份领导职位是极其困难的。招聘人员像兀鹰一样盘旋在精英大学周围。许多顶级公司甚至不会看那些没有从精英大学获得2.1学位(即二等一级学位)的人的申请。大学里的学生还会遇到那些未来可能担任领导职务的人，建立终身联系。这也许不对,但那些未能认识到这一点的中学毕业生可能会在上大学的决定上犯错。

sentences.text: Perhaps the reason why so many universities offer their students so little is they know studying at a top university remains a brilliant investment even if you don't learn anything.
Studying at university will only become less attractive if employers shift their focus away from where someone went to university—and there is no sign of that happening anytime soon.
School-leavers may moan, but they have little choice but to embrace university and the student debt that comes with it.

passage.translation: 也许如此多的大学给学生提供如此少的原因是,它们知道在顶尖大学学习仍然是一项绝佳的投资,即使你什么都没学到。只有当雇主将关注点从某人上的哪所大学转移开时,大学学习才会变得不那么有吸引力——而且没有迹象表明这种情况会很快发生。中学毕业生可能会抱怨,但他们别无选择,只能接受大学以及随之而来的学生债务。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What is the author's opinion of going to university?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （主旨题）
**题目译文**
作者对上大学持什么看法?
A) 归根结底还是值得的。
B) 这纯粹是浪费时间。
C) 很难说是好是坏。
D) 对大多数年轻人来说太贵了。
**判型** What is the author's opinion of going to university 没有任何细节性钩子，直接问作者对整件事的态度/结论，属于全文性的主旨/态度判断。
**拆句** 题干主干 What is the author's opinion of going to university 极简：疑问代词 What 作表语 + be 动词 + 主语 the author's opinion + of 引导对象。无从句、无否定、无比较，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确Yet it still pays to go to university ↔ It is worthwhile after all they have little choice but to embrace university ↔ It is worthwhile after all it still pays = worthwhile，still/after all 共同承载"虽有抱怨但终究如此"的让步语气，正是先抑后扬全文的最大公约数。
B) 以偏概全simply a waste of time 只对应第 1、2 段的负面铺垫，忽略了 Yet it still pays 之后的整片正向论证；且 simply（仅仅是）口吻过强，与作者两面权衡的立场相反。
C) 与原文相反作者立场清晰——"上大学仍然值得"——并非"不好说"。hard to say whether it is good or bad 把先抑后扬误读成"作者也没立场"，掩盖了 Yet it still pays 这一明确表态。
D) 以偏概全too expensive for most young people 借用首段 £44,000 of debt 的事实，但作者从未下结论"对大多数年轻人太贵"——相反，他在第 3 段提示 you only start repaying when you are earning £21,000 a year，承认还款门槛对低收入毕业生友好。把数字事实直接抬到"作者总观点"是局部冒充整体。

options.text: It is worthwhile after all.
It is simply a waste of time.
It is hard to say whether it is good or bad.
It is too expensive for most young people.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about the employment situation of British university graduates?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于英国大学毕业生的就业状况,作者说了什么?
A) 他们中很少有人对所获得的工作感到满意。
B) 他们通常需要很长时间才能找到一份体面的工作。
C) 精英大学的毕业生通常能找到体面的工作。
D) 他们中的大多数人从事不需要大学学历的工作。
**判型** What does the author say about the employment situation 问的是作者就具体话题陈述了什么事实，无 infer/imply/main idea 标记，属于细节题。
**拆句** 题干主干 What does the author say about the employment situation of British university graduates：助动词 does + 主语 the author + 实义动词 say + 介词短语about ... 引出话题。of 短语充当 employment situation 的后置定语，框定主体范围。结构清晰、无从句、无陷阱。
**定位** 而且毕业也根本不能保证一份体面的工作：如今十个毕业生里有六个干的是不需要大学学历的活儿。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有原文只提及"工作是否需要学历"这一客观属性，从未谈及毕业生对工作"满意/不满意"的主观感受。
B) 无中生有原文谈的是"找到的工作够不够体面"，从未提"找一份工作要花多久"，时间维度是凭空引入的。
C) 张冠李戴原文确有 Recruiters circle elite universities like vultures 一句，但那是"招聘者围猎名校生"，是 Q54 的素材，与本题问"整体毕业生就业现状"错位。
D) ✓ 正确six in ten graduates today are in non-graduate jobs ↔Most of them take jobs which don't require a college degree六成被同义量化为 Most，non-graduate jobs 被关系从句解释，两端语义等值，与预判完全吻合。
questions.quote: And graduating doesn't even provide any guarantee of a decent job: six in ten graduates today are in non-graduate jobs.

options.text: Few of them are satisfied with the jobs they are offered.
It usually takes a long time for them to find a decent job.
Graduates from elite universities usually can get decent jobs.
Most of them take jobs which don't require a college degree.

questions.prompt: What does the author say is important for university students besides classroom instruction?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者认为除了课堂教学之外,对大学生来说什么是重要的?
A) 确保获得二等一级学位。
B) 他们未来职业生涯中需要的实用技能。
C) 他们之间在课堂外的互动交流。
D) 培养独立和创造性思维能力。
**判型** What does the author say is important ... besides classroom instruction 问的是某具体方面（非课堂的重要因素）作者说了什么，答案应能从一两句原文中直接读出。
**拆句** 题干 What does the author say is important for university students besides classroom instruction 中 What 同时充当 say 的宾语和后置 is 的主语，是一个省略关系代词的嵌套结构——本质等于 "What [the author says] is important ... besides ..."。besides 引导的介词短语作状语，表示"除……之外"。这是六级常见的嵌入式疑问句，结构稍密，但理解为"作者说什么东西很重要"即可。
**定位** 重要的并不只是课堂讲授与辅导。教育，等于学生们在课堂与讨论课之间相互教给对方的一切之和。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴lack a 2.1, i.e., an upper-second class degree 出现在第 4 段说"用人单位会卡 2.1 学位线"，是顶级岗位招聘的硬门槛、不是"课堂之外什么对学生重要"。
B) 无中生有原文从未提及 practical skills / future careers 这一组合；这是套用了"大学应教实用技能"的常识，与文本无关。
C) ✓ 正确what students teach each other in between lectures and seminars ↔Interactions among themselves outside the classroom "互相教对方"是一种最典型的 interaction；"课堂之间"自然落在"课堂之外"，与预判完全吻合。
D) 无中生有Developing independent and creative thinking abilities 是国内素质教育语境的高频套话，原文从头到尾未出现 independent 或 creative 的对应表述。
questions.quote: It's not just the lectures and tutorials that are important. Education is the sum of what students teach each other in between lectures and seminars.

options.text: Making sure to obtain an upper-second class degree.
Practical skills they will need in their future careers.
Interactions among themselves outside the classroom.
Developing independent and creative thinking abilities.

questions.prompt: What is said to be an advantage of going to university?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
上大学的一个优势是什么?
A) 学习如何在不断变化的世界中承担风险。
B) 结识将来对你有帮助的人。
C) 有机会在社会中发挥领导作用。
D) 获得科学技术领域的最新知识。
**判型** What is said to be an advantage 用被动 is said 引出，问的是某一项被陈述的具体好处，属可在原文直接找到的细节。
**拆句** 题干 What is said to be an advantage of going to university：被动语态 is said to be，What 作表语；of going to university 是 advantage 的后置定语。语态被动但内容明确，无陷阱。
**定位** 在大学里，学生还能结识那些未来可能身居要职的人，由此结下一辈子的人脉。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Learning how to take risks in an ever-changing world 整句话原文未提；take risks与 ever-changing world 都是凭空添加的现代叙事词。
B) ✓ 正确meet those likely to be in leading jobs in the future, forming contacts for life ↔Meeting people who will be helpful to you in the future未来身居要职者结成终身人脉 → 对自己将来有帮助，是定位句直接的同义改写。
C) 过度推断原文是 meet those likely to be in leading jobs——上大学的人是"结识"将来身居要职者，并非自己"扮演 leading role"。把 meet leading-job people 推到 play a leading role 多走了一步。
D) 无中生有原文谈"人脉"与"招聘"，从未提及 up-to-date knowledge in science and technology；这是"上大学就学最新知识"的常识脑补。
questions.quote: Students at university also meet those likely to be in leading jobs in the future, forming contacts for life.

options.text: Learning how to take risks in an ever-changing world.
Meeting people who will be helpful to you in the future.
Having opportunities of playing a leading role in society.
Gaining up-to-date knowledge in science and technology.

questions.prompt: What can we infer from the last paragraph?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （推断题）
**题目译文**
我们能从最后一段推断出什么?
A) 学生对大学教育提出抱怨是很自然的。
B) 很少有学生愿意承担在大学期间产生的债务负担。
C) 大学教育正变得对有能力负担的学生具有吸引力。
D) 大学的声望影响雇主的招聘决策。
**判型** What can we infer from the last paragraph 的 infer 是推断题硬标志，需要从末段陈述出发做一步推理。
**拆句** 题干 What can we infer from the last paragraph：情态动词 can + 主语 we + 动词 infer+ 介词短语 from the last paragraph 指明推理来源。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 也许那么多大学之所以给学生提供得那么少，是因为他们清楚：哪怕你什么都没学到，在顶级大学念书仍然是一笔绝佳投资。只有当用人单位不再以"你出自哪所大学"作为录用焦点时，上大学才会变得不再吸引人——而短期内看不到任何这种迹象。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问原文 School-leavers may moan 只是承接前文情绪化描述，并非"末段推断"的核心；"学生抱怨大学是常态"是文字面表层意思，不算 infer。
B) 与原文相反原文末句明说 they have little choice but to embrace university and the student debt that comes with it——学生别无选择只能接受债务；选项 Few students are willing to bear the burden of debt 把"被迫接受"偷换成"几乎没人愿意承担"。"被迫接受" ≠ "不愿承担"，且原文是"接受"，选项是"不接受"，方向相反。
C) 与原文相反原文是"大学投资回报仍丰、雇主标准未变 ⇒ 上大学仍然吃香"——是"持续吸引人"，选项 becoming attractive to students who can afford it 暗示"正在变得吸引（之前不太吸引）"且把范围缩到"付得起的人"，两处都与原文不符。"付得起的人"在原文也无对应。
D) ✓ 正确Studying at university will only become less attractive if employers shift their focus away from where someone went to university↔ The prestige of the university influences employers' recruitment decisions studying at a top university remains a brilliant investment even if you don't learn anything↔The prestige of the university influences employers' recruitment decisions把"only ... if ..."和"no sign of that"合起来读，等于雇主当前仍以出身院校论英雄，与预判完全吻合。
questions.quote: Perhaps the reason why so many universities offer their students so little is they know studying at a top university remains a brilliant investment even if you don't learn anything. Studying at university will only become less attractive if employers shift their focus away from where someone went to university—and there is no sign of that happening anytime soon.

options.text: It is natural for students to make complaints about university education.
Few students are willing to bear the burden of debt incurred at university.
University education is becoming attractive to students who can afford it.
The prestige of the university influences employers' recruitment decisions.

title: Any veteran nicotine addict will testify that fancy…

sentences.text: Any veteran nicotine addict will testify that fancy packaging plays no role in the decision to keep smoking.
So, it is argued, stripping cartons of their branding will trigger no mass movement to quit.

passage.translation: 任何资深尼古丁成瘾者都会证明，精美的包装在继续吸烟的决定中不起任何作用。因此,有人认为,剥去烟盒的品牌标识不会引发大规模的戒烟运动。

sentences.text: But that isn't why the government—under pressure from cancer charities, health workers and the Labour party—has agreed to legislate for standardised packaging.
The theory is that smoking should be stripped of any appeal to discourage new generations from starting in the first place.
Plain packaging would be another step in the reclassification of cigarettes from inviting consumer products to narcotics(麻

passage.translation: 醉剂 ).但这并不是政府在癌症慈善机构、卫生工作者和工党的压力下同意立法实行标准化包装的原因。该理论认为,吸烟应当被剥夺任何吸引力,以阻止新一代人从一开始就接触吸烟。素包装将是香烟从诱人的消费品重新归类为麻醉剂的又一步骤。

sentences.text: Naturally, the tobacco industry is violently opposed.
No business likes to admit that it sells addictive poison as a lifestyle choice.
That is why government has historically intervened, banning advertising, imposing health warnings and punitive(惩罚性的) duties.
This approach has led over time to a fall in smoking with numbers having roughly halved since the 1970s.
Evidence from Australia suggests plain packaging pushes society further along that road.
Since tobacco is one of the biggest causes of premature death in the UK, a measure that tames the habit even by a fraction is worth trying.

passage.translation: 自然,烟草行业强烈反对。没有哪个企业愿意承认自己将成瘾性毒药作为一种生活方式选择来销售。这就是为什么政府历来进行干预,禁止广告、强制健康警示和征收惩罚性税。这种做法随着时间推移导致吸烟人数下降,自20世纪70年代以来数量大约减半。来自澳大利亚的证据表明,素包装推动社会在这条道路上走得更远。由于烟草是英国过早死亡的最大原因之一,即使只能在一定程度上遏制这一习惯的措施也值得一试。

sentences.text: So why has it taken so long?
The Department of Health declared its intention to consider the move in November 2010 and consulted through 2012.
But the plan was suspended in July 2013.
It did not escape notice that a lobbying firm set up by Lynton Crosby, David Cameron's election campaign director, had previously acted for Philip Morris International.
(The prime minister denied there was a connection between his new adviser's outside interests and the change in legislative programme.)
In November 2013, after an unnecessary round of additional consultation, health minister Jane Ellison said the government was minded to proceed after all.
Now we are told Members of Parliament (MPs) will have a free vote before parliament is dissolved in March.

passage.translation: 那么为什么花了这么长时间?卫生部于2010年11月宣布其考虑此举的意向,并在2012年进行了咨询。但该计划在2013年7月被暂停。人们注意到,由David Cameron的竞选活动主任Lynton Crosby创建的一家游说公司此前曾为Philip Morris International工作。(首相否认其新顾问的外部利益与立法计划的改变之间存在联系。)2013年11月,在经过一轮不必要的额外咨询后,卫生部长Jane Ellison表示政府毕竟倾向于继续推进。现在我们被告知,议会议员将在议会于3月解散前进行自由投票。

sentences.text: Parliament has in fact already authorised the government to tame the tobacco trade.
MPs voted overwhelmingly in favour of Labour amendments to the children and families bill last February that included the power to regulate for plain packaging.
With sufficient will in Downing Street this would have been done already.
But strength of will is the missing ingredient where Mr.
Cameron and public health are concerned.
His attitude to state intervention has looked confused ever since his bizarre 2006 lament(叹惜) that chocolate oranges placed seductively at supermarket checkouts fueled obesity.

passage.translation: 事实上,议会已经授权政府管控烟草贸易。去年2月,议会议员以压倒性多数投票赞成工党对儿童和家庭法案的修正案,其中包括实施素包装监管的权力。如果唐宁街有足够的意愿,这本应已经完成。但在Cameron先生和公共卫生问题上,意志力正是缺失的要素。自从他在2006年发出的那番古怪叹惜——即超市收银台处诱人摆放的巧克力橙子助长了肥胖——以来,他对国家干预的态度一直显得混乱。

sentences.text: The government has moved reluctantly into a sensible public health policy, but with such obvious over-cautiousness that any political credit due belongs to the opposition.
Without sustained external pressure it seems certain Mr.
Cameron would still be hooked on the interests of big tobacco companies.

passage.translation: 政府已经不情愿地转向一项明智的公共卫生政策,但表现出如此明显的过度谨慎,以至于任何应得的政治功劳都属于反对党。如果没有持续的外部压力,Cameron先生似乎肯定仍会受制于大型烟草公司的利益。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What do chain smokers think of cigarette packaging?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
老烟民如何看待卷烟包装?
A) 花哨的包装能够帮助吸引新烟民。
B) 它与卷烟的质量或口味关系不大。
C) 素包装能阻止非吸烟者开始吸烟。
D) 它对他们是否戒烟的决定影响不大。
**判型** What do chain smokers think of cigarette packaging? 直接问某人群对某事物的具体看法，不含 infer/suggest/imply，是典型细节题。
**拆句** What do chain smokers think of cigarette packaging? 是标准 what 引导的特殊疑问句，主语 chain smokers、谓语 think of、宾语 cigarette packaging，结构平铺、无陷阱。
**定位** 任何资深烟民都会作证，花哨的包装在是否继续吸烟的决定中起不到任何作用。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念：偷换观点持有者原文谈的是"老烟民对包装的看法"，A 把视角偷换成"包装能否拉新烟民"（engage new smokers），这是 P2 政府视角，不是题干所问 chain smokers 的视角。
B) 无中生有：原文话题外的属性B 项中的 the quality or taste of cigarettes 在全文中没有任何陈述——原文从头到尾讨论的是包装与吸烟行为的关系，从未提及香烟本身的品质或口味。
C) 偷换概念：偷换观点持有者 + 偷换话题对象C 项谈的是 Plain packaging discourages non-smokers from taking up smoking，对应 discourage new generations from starting in the first place，这是政府视角对plain packaging 的功能阐述，而题干问的是 chain smokers 对一般 cigarette packaging 的看法。
D) ✓ 正确fancy packaging plays no role in the decision to keep smoking ↔It has little impact on their decision whether or not to quit smoking D 项在两端做了等值改写：no role → little impact、keep smoking → whether or not to quit smoking，与预判完全吻合。
questions.quote: Any veteran nicotine addict will testify that fancy packaging plays no role in the decision to keep smoking.

options.text: Fancy packaging can help to engage new smokers.
It has little to do with the quality or taste of cigarettes.
Plain packaging discourages non-smokers from taking up smoking.
It has little impact on their decision whether or not to quit smoking.

questions.prompt: What has the UK government agreed to do concerning tobacco packaging?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
英国政府在烟草包装方面同意做什么?
A) 通过一项法律使卷烟包装标准化。
B) 清除烟盒上的所有广告。
C) 补贴企业采用素包装。
D) 根据包装对卷烟重新分类。
**判型** What has the UK government agreed to do concerning tobacco packaging? 直接问政府同意做的一件具体事，是细节复述题。
**拆句** What has the UK government agreed to do concerning tobacco packaging? 主干为What has the UK government agreed to do，介词短语 concerning tobacco packaging 限定话题范围，结构清晰、无陷阱。
**定位** 但这并不是政府在癌症慈善机构、卫生工作者和工党的压力下同意为标准化包装立法的原因。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确has agreed to legislate for standardised packaging ↔Pass a law to standardise cigarette packaging A 项在动作词（legislate→pass a law）与对象词（standardised packaging→standardise cigarette packaging）两端都做了等值改写，与预判一一对应。
B) 偷换概念：用历史动作冒充本次承诺原文政府承诺的是 legislate for standardised packaging（立法实现标准化包装），并非 Rid cigarette cartons of all advertisements（去掉烟盒上所有广告）；广告禁令在banning advertising 中提及，但那是政府的历史动作，不是 P2 这次新承诺的内容。
C) 无中生有：杜撰未提及的执行手段C 项 Subsidise companies to adopt plain packaging 中"补贴企业去采用 plain packaging" 在原文中完全没有依据——政府是用立法强制，不是用补贴诱导。
D) 偷换概念：颠倒手段与目的的指向原文 Plain packaging would be another step in the reclassification of cigarettes from inviting consumer products to narcotics 提到的 reclassification 是"把香烟从消费品重新分类为麻醉剂"，分类的依据是产品属性而非包装本身；D 项 Reclassify cigarettes according to packaging 颠倒了因果，把 plain packaging 推动重新分类的过程，偷换成"按包装来分类香烟"。
questions.quote: But that isn't why the government—under pressure from cancer charities, health workers and the Labour party—has agreed to legislate for standardised packaging.

options.text: Pass a law to standardise cigarette packaging.
Rid cigarette cartons of all advertisements.
Subsidise companies to adopt plain packaging.
Reclassify cigarettes according to packaging.

questions.prompt: What has happened in Australia where plain packaging is implemented?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
在实施素包装的澳大利亚发生了什么?
A) 吸烟导致的过早死亡率下降了。
B) 吸烟者人数的下降幅度比英国更大。
C) 烟草替代品的销售大幅增加。
D) 卷烟销量的下降速度远快于英国。
**判型** What has happened in Australia where plain packaging is implemented? 问澳大利亚在执行该政策后发生了什么，是事实复述。
**拆句** What has happened in Australia where plain packaging is implemented? 主句问what has happened，where 引导定语从句修饰 Australia、说明背景；要识别"在已执行该政策的澳大利亚发生了什么"这一限制条件。
**定位** 这种做法长期以来使吸烟人数下降，自 1970 年代以来吸烟人数大约减半。来自澳大利亚的证据表明，plain packaging 会让社会沿这条路走得更远。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念：偷换结果指标原文 plain packaging pushes society further along that road 中 that road 指"吸烟人数下降"，并非"过早死亡率下降"——虽然 tobacco is one of the biggest causes of premature death in the UK 提到了 premature death，但那是"为何值得尝试 plain packaging"的论据，不是"澳大利亚发生的结果"。
B) ✓ 正确plain packaging pushes society further along that road ↔The number of smokers has dropped more sharply than in the UK B 项把 further（更远）转写为 more sharply（更陡），并显化了 that road 所指的英国吸烟下降，与预判完全吻合。
C) 无中生有：杜撰未提及的相关概念C 项中的 tobacco substitutes（烟草替代品）在全文中没有任何对应——文中讨论的是plain packaging 对吸烟率的影响，而非任何替代产品的销量。
D) 偷换概念：相近但不等值的指标替换D 项 Cigarette sales have been falling far more quickly than in the UK 有两处偏差：其一，原文谈的是吸烟者人数（numbers 指吸烟人数），不是 cigarette sales（香烟销量）；其二，原文 plain packaging pushes society further along that road 在澳大利亚的语境是"已经实现的结果"，但 "销量下降" 与 "吸烟人数下降" 并非同一指标——前者衡量市场，后者衡量行为。
questions.quote: This approach has led over time to a fall in smoking with numbers having roughly halved since the 1970s. Evidence from Australia suggests plain packaging pushes society further along that road.

options.text: Premature death rates resulting from smoking have declined.
The number of smokers has dropped more sharply than in the UK.
The sales of tobacco substitutes have increased considerably.
Cigarette sales have been falling far more quickly than in the UK.

questions.prompt: Why has it taken so long for the UK government to consider plain packaging?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
为什么英国政府考虑素包装用了这么长时间?
A) 首相Cameron一直不愿采取行动。
B) 资深尼古丁成瘾者的强烈反对。
C) 许多国会议员对吸烟上瘾。
D) 来自烟草制造商的压力依然很大。
**判型** Why has it taken so long for the UK government to consider plain packaging? 问"为何拖这么久"，原文有显性陈述，不需推断。
**拆句** Why has it taken so long for the UK government to consider plain packaging? 主句Why has it taken so long，it 为形式主语，真正主语是不定式 for the UK government to consider plain packaging，要识别这一形式主语结构。
**定位** 但在 Cameron 先生与公共健康问题上，意志的强度正是缺失的那一味要素。从 2006 年他离奇地为超市收银台旁诱人摆放的巧克力橘子"助长肥胖"而叹惜以来，他对国家干预的态度一直显得迷茫。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确But strength of will is the missing ingredient where Mr. Cameron and public health are concerned.↔ Prime Minister Cameron has been reluctant to take action The government has moved reluctantly into a sensible public health policy ↔Prime Minister Cameron has been reluctant to take action A 项 reluctant to take action 与 P5 的 strength of will is the missing ingredient 等值，与 P6 的 moved reluctantly 直接呼应，是预判的同义改写。
B) 偷换概念：偷换原文人物的角色原文 Any veteran nicotine addict will testify that fancy packaging plays no role in the decision to keep smoking. 中 veteran nicotine addicts 是被引证的旁观者，他们"作证"包装与戒烟无关，并未"强烈反对"立法；B 项把这一旁观引证偷换成了"老烟民构成强烈反对"。
C) 无中生有：杜撰人物的私人属性C 项 Many Members of Parliament are addicted to smoking 在全文找不到依据——原文 MPs voted overwhelmingly in favour of Labour amendments 谈的是MPs 投票支持立法，恰恰与"自己沉迷吸烟"相反。
D) 偷换概念：背景常态冒充直接原因原文 Naturally, the tobacco industry is violently opposed. 确实说烟草业激烈反对，但这是行业的常态立场，作者并未把它列为"拖延了 5 年"的直接原因；P5 给出的拖延归因是 Cameron 缺意志，并非烟草厂商的压力。
questions.quote: But strength of will is the missing ingredient where Mr. Cameron and public health are concerned. His attitude to state intervention has looked confused ever since his bizarre 2006 lament(叹惜) that chocolate oranges placed seductively at supermarket checkouts fueled obesity.

options.text: Prime Minister Cameron has been reluctant to take action.
There is strong opposition from veteran nicotine addicts.
Many Members of Parliament are addicted to smoking.
Pressure from tobacco manufacturers remains strong.

questions.prompt: What did Cameron say about chocolate oranges at supermarket checkouts?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
Cameron对超市收银台处的巧克力橙子说了什么?
A) 它们引发了许多争议。
B) 它们吸引了许多吸烟者。
C) 它们使更多英国人变得肥胖。
D) 它们缺少某些成分。
**判型** What did Cameron say about chocolate oranges at supermarket checkouts? 问Cameron 对一件具体物品的具体表态，是细节题。
**拆句** What did Cameron say about chocolate oranges at supermarket checkouts? 主干What did Cameron say about chocolate oranges，介词短语 at supermarket checkouts 修饰 chocolate oranges、说明地点，结构清晰、无陷阱。
**定位** 自从他在 2006 年离奇地叹惜超市收银台旁诱人摆放的巧克力橘子"助长了肥胖"以来，他对国家干预的态度一直显得迷茫。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念：把作者评价说成事件结果原文 his bizarre 2006 lament(叹惜) 中的 bizarre 是作者对 Cameron 该言论的评价（离奇），而非该言论本身"引发了大量争议"——A 项 They fueled a lot of controversy 把作者主观评价偷换成"该物品引起了争议"这一客观事件结果。
B) 偷换概念：用全文主话题压局部话题原文谈的是 chocolate oranges 与 obesity（肥胖）的关系，B 项 They attracted a lot of smokers 把对象偷换成 smokers——这一替换利用了全文主话题是吸烟，强行把局部话题（肥胖）拉回主话题。
C) ✓ 正确chocolate oranges placed seductively at supermarket checkouts fueled obesity↔They made more British people obese C 项 made more British people obese 与原文 fueled obesity 等值，名词→形容词转换 + 动词同义替换，是细节题正确项最常见的形态。
D) 偷换概念：把抽象比喻误读为字面原文 strength of will is the missing ingredient where Mr. Cameron and public health are concerned 中 missing ingredient 是"缺失的要素"的比喻，对应的是Cameron 缺意志，而非 chocolate oranges 这一具体物品有什么成分缺失。D 项 They had certain ingredients missing 把比喻拽回了字面意义。
questions.quote: His attitude to state intervention has looked confused ever since his bizarre 2006 lament(叹惜) that chocolate oranges placed seductively at supermarket checkouts fueled obesity.

options.text: They fueled a lot of controversy.
They attracted a lot of smokers.
They made more British people obese.
They had certain ingredients missing.

title: Small communities, with their distinctive character—where life is…

sentences.text: Small communities, with their distinctive character—where life is stable and intensely human—are disappearing.
Some have (26)____ from the face of the earth, others are dying slowly, but all have(27)____ changes as they have come into contact with an (28)____ machine civilization.
The merging of diverse peoples into a common mass has produced tension among members of the minorities and the majority alike.

passage.translation: 具有独特性格的小型社区——那里的生活稳定且充满人情味——正在消失。一些社区已从地球表面消失,其他社区正在缓慢死亡,但所有社区在与不断扩张的机器文明接触时都经历了变化。不同民族融合成一个共同的群体,在少数群体和多数群体的成员中都产生了紧张关系。

sentences.text: The Old Order Amish, who arrived on American shores in colonial times, have (29)____ in the modern world in distinctive, small communities.
They have resisted the homogenization (30)____ more successfully than others.
In planting and harvesting time one can see their bearded men working the fields with horses and their women hanging out the laundry in neat rows to dry.
Many American people have seen Amish families, with the men wearing broad-brimmed black hats and the women in long dresses, in railway or bus (31)____ .
Although the Amish have lived with (32)____ America for over two and a half centuries, they have moderated its influence on their personal lives, their families, communities, and their values.

passage.translation: 在殖民时期抵达美国海岸的Old Order Amish人,在现代世界中以独特的小型社区形式生存了下来。他们比其他群体更成功地抵制了同质化进程。在播种和收获季节,人们可以看到他们留着胡须的男人用马匹耕作田地,他们的女人把洗好的衣物整齐成排地挂出来晾干。许多美国人在火车站或汽车站见过Amish家庭,男人戴着宽边黑帽,女人穿着长裙。尽管Amish人与工业化的美国共同生活了两个半世纪以上,但他们调节了工业化对其个人生活、家庭、社区和价值观的影响。

sentences.text: The Amish are often (33)____ by other Americans to be relics of the past who live a simple, inflexible life dedicated to inconvenient out-dated customs.
They are seen as abandoning both modern(34)____ and the American dream of success and progress.
But most people have no quarrel with the Amish for doing things the old-fashioned way.
Their conscientious objection was tolerated in wartime, for after all, they are good farmers who (35)____ the virtues of work and thrift.

passage.translation: Amish人常被其他美国人视为过去的遗迹,过着简单、僵化的生活,致力于不便的过时习俗。他们被视为既放弃了现代便利设施,也放弃了成功和进步的美国梦。但大多数人并不反对Amish人以老式方式做事。他们的良心拒服兵役在战时得到了容忍,毕竟,他们是践行勤劳和节俭美德的好农民。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
Small communities, with their distinctive character—where life is stable and intensely human—are disappearing. Some have {{26}} from the face of the earth, others are dying slowly, but all have{{27}} changes as they have come into contact with an {{28}} machine civilization. The merging of diverse peoples into a common mass has produced tension among members of the minorities and the majority alike.

The Old Order Amish, who arrived on American shores in colonial times, have {{29}} in the modern world in distinctive, small communities. They have resisted the homogenization {{30}} more successfully than others. In planting and harvesting time one can see their bearded men working the fields with horses and their women hanging out the laundry in neat rows to dry. Many American people have seen Amish families, with the men wearing broad-brimmed black hats and the women in long dresses, in railway or bus {{31}} . Although the Amish have lived with {{32}} America for over two and a half centuries, they have moderated its influence on their personal lives, their families, communities, and their values.

The Amish are often {{33}} by other Americans to be relics of the past who live a simple, inflexible life dedicated to inconvenient out-dated customs. They are seen as abandoning both modern{{34}} and the American dream of success and progress. But most people have no quarrel with the Amish for doing things the old-fashioned way. Their conscientious objection was tolerated in wartime, for after all, they are good farmers who {{35}} the virtues of work and thrift.

options.text: accessing
progress
conveniences
respective
destined
survived
expanding
terminals
industrialized
undergone
perceived
universal
practice
vanished
process

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) vanished 动词
**词性槽** have + 空 + from，空作现在完成时的过去分词
**依据** vanish from = 从…消失，与上下文"消失"主线呼应Small communities, with their distinctive character—where life is stable and intensely human—are disappearing.点题"消失"，紧接Some have __(26)__ from the face of the earth, others are dying slowly，与 disappearing 同义、与 dying slowly 形成程度递进，vanish from 是固定搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) perceived 及物动词且义不通perceive 通常及物，意为"察觉到"，与 from 不搭，也与小社区"消失"的语义无关。
K) survived 感情色彩相反survive 表"幸存"，与并列分句 others are dying slowly 形成"幸存 vs 慢慢死去"的反义对照，但前面 disappearing 已定调"消失"，本句需要的是与 dying 同向的递进词。
M) undergone 及物且义不切题undergo（经历）通常及物，需直接接宾语如 undergo changes，与 from 搭配不自然。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 K) —— survived 与 vanished 感情色彩相反。26 题 Some have__(26)__ from the face of the earth, others are dying slowly中，survived与 from 也能搭（survive from），且"幸存"与"渐死"看似对照诱人，但前句 disappearing 已定调"消失"，本句需与 dying slowly 形成程度递进而非反义。防坑：先看上一句基调，再决定动词同向还是反向。

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) undergone 动词
**词性槽** have + 空 + changes，空作现在完成时及物动词的过去分词
**依据** undergo changes = 经历变化，固定搭配but all have __(27)__ changes as they have come into contact with an __(28)__machine civilization.描述小社区在接触机器文明的过程中"经历变化"，undergo changes是常见标准搭配，与 as 引导的原因状语吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) perceived 语义不通perceived changes 意为"感知到变化"，但句子主语是 communities（小社区）本身，主语不会"感知"变化，而是"经历"变化。
K) survived 搭配不成立survive changes（经受住变化）虽语法可通，但与 but 引导的让步逻辑（有的消失、有的渐死，但都……）不一致——这里需要的是"都受到了影响"，而非"都活下来了"。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) expanding 形容词
**词性槽** an + 空 + machine civilization，空作 machine civilization 的前置定语
**依据** an expanding machine civilization = 不断扩张的机器文明Small communities, with their distinctive character—where life is stable and intensely human—are disappearing.点明小社区在消失，原因正是they have come into contact with an __(28)__ machine civilization.——一个不断扩张的机器文明吞噬小社区，expanding 既满足 an 后元音音素，也契合"扩张"压迫小社区的因果。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) destined 搭配不自然且首音非元音destined machine civilization 不构成自然表达，且 destined 以辅音开头与 an 不匹配。
J) respective 义不切题respective 表"各自的"，需复数语境，且 an respective 也读音不顺。
N) universal 首音非元音、义偏universal 读音以辅音 /j/ 起，与 an 不搭；且"普遍的机器文明"不如"扩张的机器文明"贴合"小社区被冲击"的因果。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) survived 动词
**词性槽** have + 空 + in，空作现在完成时不及物动词的过去分词
**依据** survive in = 在…中存续，呼应主题反例The Old Order Amish, who arrived on American shores in colonial times, have__(29)__ in the modern world in distinctive, small communities.描述阿米什人作为"小社区在现代化中消失"的反例，他们"在现代世界里以小社区方式存续"，survive in 与 P1 主题形成对照。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) perceived 义不通且需补语perceive 表"感知/认为"，若作被动需补 as + 名词或形容词，本句没有该补语，且"感知在现代世界里"语义不通。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) process 名词
**词性槽** the + 空 + 比较状语，空作 homogenization 的同位/补语名词
**依据** homogenization process = 同质化进程，固定搭配原文谈They have resisted the homogenization __(30)__ more successfully than others.，与首段all have __(27)__ changes as they have come into contact with an__(28)__ machine civilization呼应，作者强调阿米什人在现代化"进程"中抵抗同质化，process 与 homogenization 构成常见搭配 homogenization process。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) conveniences 义不通且为复数conveniences 指便利设施，与 homogenization（同质化）不构成语义搭配，也无法解释"抵抗"的对象。
I) progress 感情色彩与逻辑相反progress 是褒义"进步"，阿米什人抵抗的不是进步本身，而是把所有人变成一样的"进程"，且homogenization progress 不构成自然搭配。
L) terminals 义项不匹配且为复数terminals 指终点站/航站楼，是具体名词，无法与抽象名词 homogenization 复合。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 I) —— process vs progress 形近混淆。30 题 the homogenization ___ 处，progress与process形近且都为名词，主体考生极易选成progress。防坑：homogenization process（同质化进程）是固定搭配，且本句主语是"抵抗"，宾语应为中性"进程"而非褒义"进步"。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) terminals 名词
**词性槽** 介词 in + railway or bus ___，空作介词宾语中心名词
**依据** railway/bus terminals = 火车站/汽车终点站，标准搭配原文描述美国人常在in railway or bus __(31)__见到阿米什家庭，terminals 既能与 railway（火车终点站）也能与 bus（汽车终点站）搭配，且为复数与 or 连接的两类终点呼应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) conveniences 搭配与语义不成立conveniences 不能与 railway/bus 构成"火车便利/公交便利"的合理表达，也无法承担"地点"语义。
I) progress 抽象名词与地点语义冲突progress 是抽象进步义，无法被 railway/bus 修饰为可观察到的地点。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) industrialized 形容词
**词性槽** with + 空 + America，空作前置定语修饰 America
**依据** industrialized America = 工业化的美国，呼应首段"machine civilization"首段铺垫all have __(27)__ changes as they have come into contact with an __(28)__machine civilization.，第二段进一步说阿米什人have lived with __(32)__ America for over two and a half centuries，工业化美国正是他们抵抗同质化的对象，与上文"machine civilization"语义一致。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) destined 搭配不成立destined 多用作 be destined to/for，作前置定语修饰国家不自然，且无法承接"被抵抗的对象"的语义。
J) respective 需复数对象respective 表"各自的"，必须修饰复数名词指代多方各自所有，单独修饰 America 不合常理。
N) universal 义不切题universal America（普遍的美国）不符合常识表达，也未承接前文对工业化、机器文明的强调。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) perceived 动词
**词性槽** are + 空 + by，被动语态过去分词
**依据** be perceived by sb. to be = 被某人认为是，标准句式The Amish are often __(33)__ by other Americans to be relics of the past即"阿米什人常被其他美国人认为是过去的遗物"，perceive 作"认为/视…为"时正可接 to be 补语。

**答案** B) conveniences 名词
**词性槽** modern + 空 + and，形容词后并列结构中的名词
**依据** modern conveniences = 现代便利设施，固定搭配They are seen as abandoning both modern __(34)__ and the American dream of success and progress.说阿米什人被视作放弃了"现代便利"与"美国梦"，modern conveniences 是英语里常见搭配，正与下文 inconvenient out-dated customs（不便的过时习俗）形成 convenience ↔ inconvenient 的呼应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
I) progress 并列项重复且无法呼应 inconvenient progress 已紧跟在 and the American dream of success and progress 中出现，本空再用progress 会出现"放弃现代进步与美国成功与进步的梦想"的语义冗余；且 progress 无法与下文inconvenient out-dated customs 形成 convenience/inconvenient 的同根呼应。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) practice 动词
**词性槽** who + 空 + the virtues，关系从句中的谓语动词
**依据** practice the virtues = 践行美德，标准搭配they are good farmers who __(35)__ the virtues of work and thrift.即"他们是践行勤劳与节俭美德的好农夫"，practice virtues 是常用搭配，与上文阿米什人"传统而踏实"的形象贴合。

title: More than 100 years ago, American sociologist W.…

sentences.text: More than 100 years ago, American sociologist W.
E.
B.
Du Bois was concerned that race was being used as a biological explanation for what he understood to be social and cultural differences between different populations of people.
He spoke out against the idea of "white" and "black" as distinct groups, claiming that these distinctions ignored the scope of human diversity.

passage.translation: 100多年前,美国社会学家W. E. B. Du Bois担心种族被用作生物学解释,而他认为这实际上是不同人群之间的社会和文化差异。他公开反对将"白人"和"黑人"作为不同群体的观点,声称这些区分忽视了人类多样性的范围。

sentences.text: Science would favor Du Bois.
Today, the mainstream belief among scientists is that race is a social construct without biological meaning.
In an article published in the journal Science, four scholars say racial categories need to be phased out.

passage.translation: 科学支持Du Bois的观点。如今,科学家中的主流信念是种族是一种没有生物学意义的社会建构。在《科学》杂志发表的一篇文章中,四位学者表示种族分类需要被逐步淘汰。

sentences.text: "Essentially, I could not agree more with the authors," said Svante Pääbo, a biologist and director of the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology in Germany.

In one example that demonstrated genetic differences were not fixed along racial lines, the full genomes(基因组) of James Watson and Craig Venter, two famous American scientists of European ancestry, were compared to that of a Korean scientist, Seong-Jin Kim.
It turned out that Watson and Venter shared fewer variations in their genetic sequences than they each shared with Kim.

passage.translation: 德国马克斯·普朗克进化人类学研究所所长、生物学家Svante Pääbo说:"从本质上讲,我完全同意作者们的观点。"一个证明遗传差异并非沿种族界限固定的例子是,两位著名的欧洲血统美国科学家James Watson和Craig Venter的全基因组与一位韩国科学家Seong-Jin Kim的基因组进行了比较。结果发现,Watson和Venter之间共有的基因序列变异少于他们各自与Kim共有的变异。

sentences.text: Michael Yudell, a professor of public health at Drexel University in Philadelphia, said that modern genetics research is operating in a paradox: on the one hand, race is understood to be a useful tool to illuminate human genetic diversity, but on the other hand, race is also understood to be a poorly defined marker of that diversity.

passage.translation: 费城Drexel大学公共卫生教授Michael Yudell说,现代遗传学研究正处于一个悖论之中:一方面,种族被理解为阐明人类遗传多样性的有用工具,但另一方面,种族也被理解为该多样性的一个定义不清的标记。

sentences.text: Assumptions about genetic differences between people of different races could be particularly dangerous in a medical setting.
"If you make clinical predictions based on somebody's race, you're going to be wrong a good chunk of the time," Yudell told Live Science.
In the paper, he and his colleagues used the example of cystic fibrosis, which is underdiagnosed in people of African ancestry because it is thought of as a "white" disease.

passage.translation: 关于不同种族的人之间遗传差异的假设在医疗环境中可能特别危险。Yudell告诉Live Science:"如果你基于某人的种族做出临床预测,你很多时候都会出错。"在论文中,他和同事以囊性纤维化为例,这种疾病在非洲血统的人群中诊断不足,因为它被认为是一种"白人"疾病。

sentences.text: So what other variables could be used if the racial concept is thrown out?

Yudell said scientists need to get more specific with their language, perhaps using terms like "ancestry" or "population" that might more precisely reflect the relationship between humans and their genes, on both the individual and population level.
The researchers also acknowledged that there are a few areas where race as a construct might still be useful in scientific research: as a political and social, but not biological, variable.

passage.translation: 那么如果抛弃种族概念,可以使用哪些其他变量呢?Yudell说科学家需要在语言上更加具体,或许使用"祖源"或"人群"等术语,这些术语可能更精确地反映人类与其基因之间在个体和群体层面的关系。研究人员也承认,在科学研究中有少数领域种族作为一个建构可能仍然有用:作为政治和社会变量,而非生物学变量。

sentences.text: "While we argue phasing out racial terminology(术语) in the biological sciences, we also acknowledge that using race as a political or social category to study racism, although filled with lots of challenges, remains necessary given our need to understand how structural inequities and discrimination produce health disparities(差异) between groups."
Yudell said.

passage.translation: Yudell说:"虽然我们主张在生物科学中逐步淘汰种族术语,但我们也承认,使用种族作为政治或社会类别来研究种族主义,尽管充满许多挑战,但鉴于我们需要理解结构性不平等和歧视如何在群体之间产生健康差异,这仍然是必要的。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: Du Bois was opposed to the use of race as ________.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
Du Bois反对将种族用作________
A) 解释人类基因多样性的基础
B) 理解不同人群的辅助手段
C) 对社会和文化差异的解释
D) 描述个体人类特征的术语
**判型** Du Bois was opposed to the use of race as ________ 问的是某人具体反对把 race 当作什么，是对原文一句话的客观转述。
**拆句** Du Bois was opposed to the use of race as ________：be opposed to 是被动结构的固定搭配，意为「反对」；as ________ 引出反对的对象身份（把 race 当作什么）。空格处填的内容是 as 的宾语补足语，对应「race 被用作什么」。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 美国社会学家 W. E. B. Du Bois 担心的是：race（种族）正在被用作一种生物学解释，去解释他所理解的本质上是社会和文化层面的群体差异。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴a basis for explaining human genetic diversity 把 race 与 genetic diversity 挂钩——这是文章后半段 Yudell 等人的现代议题，而非 Du Bois 一百多年前反对的内容。
B) 与原文相反an aid to understanding different populations 把 race 包装成「理解不同人群的助力」，但 Du Bois 反对的恰是这种「用 race 来理解群体」的做法，而非把它当工具。
C) ✓ 正确race was being used as a biological explanation for what he understood to be social and cultural differences↔ an explanation for social and cultural differences预判「反对把 race 当社会文化差异的解释」与 an explanation for social and cultural differences 句意完全重合，直接锁 C。
D) 偷换概念a term to describe individual human characteristics 强调「描述个体特征」，而原文Du Bois 反对的是用 race 解释不同 populations（群体）之间的差异，与「个体特征」无关。
questions.quote: American sociologist W. E. B. Du Bois was concerned that race was being used as a biological explanation for what he understood to be social and cultural differences between different populations of people.

options.text: a basis for explaining human genetic diversity
an aid to understanding different populations
an explanation for social and cultural differences
a term to describe individual human characteristics

questions.prompt: The study by Svante Pääbo served as an example to show ________.
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （例证目的题）
**题目译文**
Svante Pääbo的研究被用作例证来说明________
A) 现代遗传学研究可能会加剧种族冲突
B) 种族是人类基因多样性的一个定义不清的标记
C) 种族作为生物学术语可以解释人类基因多样性
D) 遗传学研究应当考虑社会和文化变量
**判型** served as an example to show 明确问「这个例子是为了说明什么」，考查例子背后的论点。
**拆句** The study by Svante Pääbo served as an example to show ________：主干是 The study served as an example；by Svante Pääbo 是后置定语修饰 study；to show________ 是不定式作 example 的目的状语，空格处填的是「这个例子要说明的论点」，而不是例子本身。
**定位** 在一个用来证明「基因差异并非沿种族界线分布」的例子里，两位欧裔美国科学家 Watson和 Venter 的完整基因组被拿来与韩国科学家 Kim 的基因组做比较。结果显示：Watson 与Venter 之间共享的基因序列变异，反而少于他们各自与 Kim 之间共享的变异。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有modern genetics research is likely to fuel racial conflicts 把现代遗传学说成会「助长种族冲突」，原文从未表达此意——文章主旨恰是用遗传学证据淡化种族界线，而非煽动冲突。
B) ✓ 正确genetic differences were not fixed along racial lines ↔race is a poorly defined marker of human genetic diversity race is also understood to be a poorly defined marker of that diversity ↔race is a poorly defined marker of human genetic diversity预判「race 不能准确反映基因多样性」与 race is a poorly defined marker of human genetic diversity 句意一致；P3 的例子论点与 P4 的概括相互印证，B 是唯一同时贴合两处的表述。
C) 与原文相反race as a biological term can explain human genetic diversity 等于承认「race 这个生物学概念能解释基因多样性」，恰是 Pääbo 例子要否定的命题，与论点完全相反。
D) 答非所问genetics research should consider social and cultural variables 是 Yudell 在 P6、P7 才提出的另一议题，与 Pääbo 例子本身要证明的「基因差异不沿种族界线」无直接关系。
questions.quote: In one example that demonstrated genetic differences were not fixed along racial lines, the full genomes of James Watson and Craig Venter, two famous American scientists of European ancestry, were compared to that of a Korean scientist, Seong-Jin Kim. It turned out that Watson and Venter shared fewer variations in their genetic sequences than they each shared with Kim.

options.text: modern genetics research is likely to fuel racial conflicts
race is a poorly defined marker of human genetic diversity
race as a biological term can explain human genetic diversity
genetics research should consider social and cultural variables

questions.prompt: The example of the disease cystic fibrosis underdiagnosed in people of African ancestry demonstrates that ________.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （例证目的题）
**题目译文**
囊性纤维化疾病在非洲裔人群中诊断不足的例子表明________
A) 在做出诊断时将种族放在一边是绝对必要的
B) 在遗传学研究中纳入社会变量很重要
C) 用于基因多样性的种族分类可能导致错误的临床预测
D) 对黑人的歧视可能导致临床治疗中的疏忽
**判型** The example of the disease cystic fibrosis underdiagnosed in people of African ancestry demonstrates that ________ 明问「这个例子说明了什么」，是典型的例证目的题。
**拆句** The example of the disease cystic fibrosis underdiagnosed in people of African ancestry demonstrates that ________：主干是 The example demonstrates that ____；of the disease cystic fibrosis 是 example 的同位语；underdiagnosed in people of African ancestry 是后置分词定语修饰 disease；demonstrates 是核心动词，提示后面要找的是论点。
**定位** 「如果你基于一个人的种族去做临床预判，那你会有相当大比例的时候判错，」Yudell 对Live Science 说。在论文里，他和同事用了囊性纤维化为例：这种病在非裔人群中被漏诊，因为它被当作一种「白人病」。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断it is absolutely necessary to put race aside in making diagnosis 用 absolutely necessary 把原文意思推到「在诊断中必须完全抛开 race」，但 Yudell 只是说基于race 预判会经常出错，并未主张诊断中完全排除 race。
B) 答非所问it is important to include social variables in genetics research 是 Yudell 后文 P6、P7 才提到的另一类建议（race 作为社会政治变量仍有用），但 P5 的囊性纤维化例子不是用来论证「应纳入社会变量」的。
C) ✓ 正确If you make clinical predictions based on somebody's race, you're going to be wrong a good chunk of the time↔ racial categories for genetic diversity could lead to wrong clinical predictions cystic fibrosis, which is underdiagnosed in people of African ancestry because it is thought of as a "white" disease↔ racial categories for genetic diversity could lead to wrong clinical predictions预判「按种族做临床预判会出错」与 racial categories for genetic diversity could lead to wrong clinical predictions 的因果结构完全一致，且例子（漏诊）也落进wrong clinical predictions，锁 C。
D) 偷换概念discrimination against black people may cause negligence in clinical treatment把漏诊归因为「对黑人的歧视导致疏忽治疗」，但原文给出的原因是「把 cystic fibrosis当 white disease 的认知偏差」，是分类错误而非歧视性疏忽。
questions.quote: "If you make clinical predictions based on somebody's race, you're going to be wrong a good chunk of the time," Yudell told Live Science. In the paper, he and his colleagues used the example of cystic fibrosis, which is underdiagnosed in people of African ancestry because it is thought of as a "white" disease.

options.text: it is absolutely necessary to put race aside in making diagnosis
it is important to include social variables in genetics research
racial categories for genetic diversity could lead to wrong clinical predictions
discrimination against black people may cause negligence in clinical treatment

questions.prompt: What is Yudell's suggestion to scientists?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
Yudell对科学家的建议是什么
A) 他们应该更精确地使用语言
B) 他们避免使用政治敏感术语
C) 他们在研究中摒弃不相关的概念
D) 他们在研究中检验所有可能的变量
**判型** What is Yudell's suggestion to scientists? 问的是一句话能答的具体建议，属于对原文say 引语的客观转述。
**拆句** What is Yudell's suggestion to scientists?：主干 What is Yudell's suggestion；to scientists 是介词短语作 suggestion 的对象状语，相当于「Yudell 给 scientists 提的建议是什么」。结构清晰，无陷阱。
**定位** Yudell 说科学家需要在用词上更精确，或许可以采用 ancestry（祖源）或 population（人群）这类词，它们也许能更准确地反映人类与基因之间的关系，无论在个体层面还是群体层面。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确scientists need to get more specific with their language ↔They should be more precise with the language they use.预判「用词更精确」与 They should be more precise with the language they use.句意一致，且原句的每个成分（主语、情态、核心形容词、宾语）都在选项里同义保留，锁 A。
B) 无中生有They refrain from using politically sensitive terms. 让科学家「避免使用政治敏感词」，原文从未提及 sensitive 一词；Yudell 实际是承认 race 作为政治社会变量仍有用（P7），并非要避开政治色彩词。
C) 过度推断They throw out irrelevant concepts in their research. 让科学家「抛弃无关概念」，但原文并未让 Yudell 主张丢弃 race，而是建议用更精确的词替代；且 race 在 P7 中仍被认为对某些研究 useful，并非 irrelevant。
D) 答非所问They examine all possible variables in their research. 让科学家「考察所有可能的变量」，原文 Yudell 谈的是用词更精确（语言层面），不是要考察更多变量（研究方法层面）。
questions.quote: Yudell said scientists need to get more specific with their language, perhaps using terms like "ancestry" or "population" that might more precisely reflect the relationship between humans and their genes, on both the individual and population level.

options.text: They should be more precise with the language they use.
They refrain from using politically sensitive terms.
They throw out irrelevant concepts in their research.
They examine all possible variables in their research.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from Yudell's remark in the last paragraph?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （推断题）
**题目译文**
从Yudell在最后一段的评论中可以推断出什么
A) 坚持种族主义会延续不公平和歧视
B) 各种族之间的生理差异相当显著
C) 消除种族歧视具有挑战性
D) 种族术语在某些研究领域仍然有用
**判型** What can be inferred from Yudell's remark in the last paragraph? 中 inferred 是推断题的硬标志。
**拆句** What can be inferred from Yudell's remark in the last paragraph?：被动式 can be inferred 表示「能够被推断出什么」；from Yudell's remark in the last paragraph 是推断的来源限定（末段 Yudell 的话）。结构清晰，关键是认出 inferred 这个题型信号。
**定位** 「虽然我们主张在生物科学中逐步淘汰种族术语，但我们也承认：把 race 作为一种政治或社会范畴来研究种族主义，尽管面临大量挑战，但仍然是必要的——因为我们需要理解结构性不平等和歧视如何在不同群体间造成健康差异。」
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反Clinging to racism prolongs inequity and discrimination. 把话题反转成「死守种族主义会延长不平等」，但 Yudell 末段是承认研究 racism 仍有必要，并未谈到「死守racism」会怎样。
B) 偷换概念Physiological disparities are quite striking among races. 说「种族间生理差异相当明显」，但原文 health disparities 指的是「健康差异」，而且这些差异是结构性不平等和歧视造成的（社会原因），并非由生理差异主导。
C) 偷换概念Doing away with racial discrimination is challenging. 把 challenging 安到「消除种族歧视」上，但原文 filled with lots of challenges 修饰的是「把 race 作为政治社会范畴去研究 racism」这件事，不是「消除歧视」。
D) ✓ 正确using race as a political or social category to study racism, although filled with lots of challenges, remains necessary↔ Racial terms are still useful in certain fields of study. there are a few areas where race as a construct might still be useful in scientific research↔Racial terms are still useful in certain fields of study.预判「race 在某些领域仍有用」与 Racial terms are still useful in certain fields of study. 完全一致，且 P6 与 P7 双重印证 still useful 与 certain fields 两个核心点，锁 D。
questions.quote: "While we argue phasing out racial terminology in the biological sciences, we also acknowledge that using race as a political or social category to study racism, although filled with lots of challenges, remains necessary given our need to understand how structural inequities and discrimination produce health disparities between groups."

options.text: Clinging to racism prolongs inequity and discrimination.
Physiological disparities are quite striking among races.
Doing away with racial discrimination is challenging.
Racial terms are still useful in certain fields of study.

sentences.text: Dr.
Donald Sadoway at MIT started his own battery company with the hope of changing the world's energy future.
It's a dramatic endorsement for a technology most people think about only when their smartphone goes dark.
But Sadoway isn't alone in trumpeting energy storage as a missing link to a cleaner, more efficient, and more equitable energy future.

passage.translation: MIT的Donald Sadoway博士创办了自己的电池公司,希望改变世界的能源未来。对于一项大多数人只有在智能手机没电时才会想到的技术来说,这是一个引人注目的认可。但Sadoway并非唯一一个大力宣扬储能是通往更清洁、更高效、更公平的能源未来的缺失环节的人。

sentences.text: Scientists and engineers have long believed in the promise of batteries to change the world.
Advanced batteries are moving out of specialized markets and creeping into the mainstream, signaling a tipping point for forward-looking technologies such as electric cars and rooftop solar panels.

passage.translation: 科学家和工程师长期以来一直相信电池改变世界的前景。先进的电池正在从专业市场走出,逐渐进入主流,标志着电动汽车和屋顶太阳能电池板等前瞻性技术的转折点。

sentences.text: The ubiquitous(无所不在的) battery has already come a long way, of course.
For better or worse, batteries make possible our mobile-first lifestyles, our screen culture, our increasingly globalized world.
Still, as impressive as all this is, it may be trivial compared with what comes next.
Having already enabled a communications revolution, the battery is now poised to transform just about everything else.

passage.translation: 当然,无所不在的电池已经走过了很长的路。无论好坏,电池使我们的移动优先生活方式、我们的屏幕文化、我们日益全球化的世界成为可能。然而,尽管这一切令人印象深刻,但与接下来将要发生的事情相比,这可能微不足道。电池已经促成了一场通信革命,现在它准备改变几乎所有其他事物。

sentences.text: The wireless age is expanding to include not just our phones, tablets, and laptops, but also our cars, homes, and even whole communities.
In emerging economies, rural communities are bypassing the wires and wooden poles that spread power.
Instead, some in Africa and Asia are seeing their first lightbulbs illuminated by the power of sunlight stored in batteries.

passage.translation: 无线时代正在扩展,不仅包括我们的手机、平板电脑和笔记本电脑,还包括我们的汽车、住宅,甚至整个社区。在新兴经济体中,农村社区正在绕过传输电力的电线和木杆。相反,非洲和亚洲的一些地区正看到他们的第一批灯泡被储存在电池中的太阳能点亮。

sentences.text: Today, energy storage is a $33 billion global industry that generates nearly 100 gigawatt-hours of electricity per year.

By the end of the decade, it's expected to be worth over $50 billion and generate 160 gigawatt-hours, enough to attract the attention of major companies that might not otherwise be interested in a decidedly pedestrian technology.
Even utility companies, which have long viewed batteries and alternative forms of energy as a threat, are learning to embrace the technologies as enabling rather than disrupting.

passage.translation: 如今,储能是一个价值330亿美元的全球产业,每年产生近100吉瓦时的电力。到这个十年结束时,预计其价值将超过500亿美元,产生160吉瓦时,足以吸引那些原本可能对这项明显平凡的技术不感兴趣的大公司的注意。即使是长期以来将电池和替代能源形式视为威胁的公用事业公司,也正在学习将这些技术视为促进因素而非破坏因素。

sentences.text: Today's battery breakthroughs come as the world looks to expand modern energy access to the billion or so people without it, while also cutting back on fuels that warm the planet.
Those simultaneous challenges appear less overwhelming with increasingly better answers to a centuries-old question: how to make power portable.

passage.translation: 当今的电池突破出现之时,世界正寻求将现代能源接入扩展到大约十亿没有电力的人口,同时也减少使地球变暖的燃料。随着对一个存在了几个世纪的问题的答案越来越好,这些同时存在的挑战显得不那么令人难以承受:如何使电力便携化。

sentences.text: To be sure, the battery still has a long way to go before the nightly recharge completely replaces the weekly trip to the gas station.
A battery-powered world comes with its own risks, too.
What happens to the centralized electric grid, which took decades and billions of dollars to build, as more and more people become "prosumers," who produce and consume their own energy onsite?

passage.translation: 可以肯定的是,在每晚充电完全取代每周去加油站之前,电池还有很长的路要走。电池驱动的世界也伴随着自身的风险。随着越来越多的人成为在现场生产和消费自己能源的'产消者',那个花费了数十年时间和数十亿美元建造的集中式电网会发生什么?

sentences.text: No one knows which—if any—battery technology will ultimately dominate, but one thing remains clear.
The future of energy is in how we store it.

passage.translation: 没有人知道哪种电池技术(如果有的话)最终会占主导地位,但有一件事仍然很清楚。能源的未来在于我们如何储存它。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does Dr. Sadoway think of energy storage?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
Sadoway博士如何看待能源储存?
A) 它涉及复杂技术的应用。
B) 它是能源发展应当遵循的方向。
C) 它将被证明是一项有利可图的业务。
D) 它是一项造福每个人的技术。
**判型** What does Dr. Sadoway think of energy storage? 直接问具体人物的具体观点，属于可在原文中找到原句出处的细节题。
**拆句** Q46 是常规 What 引导的特殊疑问句，主干 Dr. Sadoway think of energy storage 中think of 是固定短语「对……的看法」，无陷阱。
**定位** 但 Sadoway 并不是唯一一个把储能鼓吹为通向更清洁、更高效、更公平能源未来之关键缺口的人。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有It involves the application of sophisticated technology. 谈的是「涉及高深技术」，而定位句只评价储能在能源未来中的地位，未提及技术是否 sophisticated。
B) ✓ 正确a missing link to a cleaner, more efficient, and more equitable energy future ↔the direction energy development should follow cleaner, more efficient, and more equitable energy future ↔ energy development预判说「储能是能源未来必经之路」，B 选项 the direction energy development should follow 是同一意思的抽象表达，逻辑等值。
C) 偷换概念It will prove to be a profitable business. 把储能定义为「会被证明是赚钱的生意」，而 P1 Sadoway 表述的是其能源价值，并未评判利润前景。
D) 过度推断It is a technology benefiting everyone. 把储能升格为「让每个人都受益」，但 P1 只提到 more equitable 这一个限定，并未做「人人受益」的全称承诺。
questions.quote: But Sadoway isn't alone in trumpeting energy storage as a missing link to a cleaner, more efficient, and more equitable energy future.

options.text: It involves the application of sophisticated technology.
It is the direction energy development should follow.
It will prove to be a profitable business.
It is a technology benefiting everyone.

questions.prompt: What is most likely to happen when advanced batteries become widely used?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
当先进电池被广泛使用时,最有可能发生什么?
A) 移动优先的生活方式将变得流行。
B) 全球化进程将被加速。
C) 通信将采取更多样化的形式。
D) 世界将经历革命性变化。
**判型** What is most likely to happen when advanced batteries become widely used? 虽含most likely，但仍指向原文已表态的明确预言，不需要考生自行推理。
**拆句** Q47 主干 What is most likely to happen 是 What 作主语的疑问句；when 引导的时间状语从句 when advanced batteries become widely used 限定时机，无陷阱。
**定位** 电池已成就了一场通信革命，如今则势将变革几乎所有其他领域。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问Mobile-first lifestyles will become popular. 把 mobile-first lifestyles 当作未来电池广泛使用后才会发生的事，但 batteries make possible our mobile-first lifestyles 表明这是电池已经实现的、属于「过去/现在」的事，不是「未来」的预言。
B) 答非所问The globalization process will be accelerated. 同样把已发生的 globalized world 当成未来才会发生，且原文只说 increasingly globalized world，并未承诺加速会延续到电池广泛使用的未来。
C) 偷换概念Communications will take more diverse forms. 谈的是「通信形式将更多样」，但原文 Having already enabled a communications revolution 已经把通信革命定位为「已经发生」的事，且下一步是 transform everything else（除通信之外的领域），不是通信本身继续多样化。
D) ✓ 正确transform just about everything else ↔ The world will undergo revolutionary changes. Having already enabled a communications revolution ↔ revolutionary changes预判「几乎所有领域将被变革」即 The world will undergo revolutionary changes.——the world 覆盖 everything else 的范围、revolutionary changes 对应 transform。
questions.quote: Having already enabled a communications revolution, the battery is now poised to transform just about everything else.

options.text: Mobile-first lifestyles will become popular.
The globalization process will be accelerated.
Communications will take more diverse forms.
The world will undergo revolutionary changes.

questions.prompt: In some rural communities of emerging economies, people have begun to ___________.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
在新兴经济体的一些农村社区,人们已经开始___________。
A) 发现数字设备简直不可或缺
B) 主要通过移动电话进行交流
C) 用储存的太阳能为家庭照明
D) 用电线和木杆分配电力
**判型** In some rural communities of emerging economies, people have begun to___________. 是要求补全谓语行为的不完整陈述句，本质上仍在问「这些社区做了什么具体的事」。
**拆句** Q48 主干 people have begun to 用现在完成时表已开始的动作，前置状语 In some rural communities of emerging economies 双层限定场景，无从句、无陷阱。
**定位** 相反，非洲和亚洲的部分地区，第一盏灯泡正被电池中储存的阳光所点亮。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有find digital devices simply indispensable 谈「数字设备不可或缺」，但 P4 谈的是电力供应方式而非数字设备的依赖度。
B) 偷换概念communicate primarily by mobile phone 谈手机通讯，但 P4 讨论的是供电而非通讯方式。
C) ✓ 正确their first lightbulbs illuminated ↔ light their homes the power of sunlight stored in batteries ↔ stored solar energy预判「用储存的太阳能点亮家」与 light their homes with stored solar energy 的主谓宾完全对应，无歧义。
D) 与原文相反distribute power with wires and wooden poles 与原文 rural communities are bypassing the wires and wooden poles that spread power 直接矛盾——原文说「跳过电线杆」，选项说「用电线杆配电」。
questions.quote: Instead, some in Africa and Asia are seeing their first lightbulbs illuminated by the power of sunlight stored in batteries.

options.text: find digital devices simply indispensable
communicate primarily by mobile phone
light their homes with stored solar energy
distribute power with wires and wooden poles

questions.prompt: Utility companies have begun to realize that battery technologies ___________.
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
公用事业公司已经开始意识到电池技术___________。
A) 有利于它们的业务
B) 传输电力更快
C) 促进创新
D) 鼓励竞争
**判型** Utility companies have begun to realize that battery technologies ___________. 问电力公司「意识到电池技术怎样了」，是有原文出处的客观细节，不是推断。
**拆句** Q49 主干 Utility companies have begun to realize 后接 that 引导宾语从句，从句主语battery technologies 缺谓语和宾语，待选项补全；无否定无比较，无陷阱。
**定位** 就连一向把电池和替代能源视作威胁的电力公司，如今也在学着把这些技术视作赋能而非颠覆。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确enabling rather than disrupting ↔ benefit their business utility companies ↔ their business预判「赋能而非颠覆」即「对其业务有利」，与 benefit their business 同义。
B) 无中生有transmit power faster 谈「更快输电」，但 P5 只评判技术对电力公司的「敌/友」属性，未提任何输电速度。
C) 过度推断promote innovation 谈「促进创新」，但定位句只评判技术对电力公司业务的影响，未升级到创新维度。
D) 答非所问encourage competition 谈「鼓励竞争」，但定位句焦点在「不再被视作威胁」，未提竞争维度。
questions.quote: Even utility companies, which have long viewed batteries and alternative forms of energy as a threat, are learning to embrace the technologies as enabling rather than disrupting.

options.text: benefit their business
transmit power faster
promote innovation
encourage competition

questions.prompt: What does the author imply about the centralized electric grid?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （推断题）
**题目译文**
作者对集中式电网暗示了什么?
A) 它可能会成为过去的事物。
B) 它可能会成为一个"产消者"。
C) 它将更容易操作和维护。
D) 它将不得不被彻底改造。
**判型** What does the author imply about the centralized electric grid? 含 imply，明确要求考生在原文表态基础上做一步推断。
**拆句** Q50 主干 What does the author imply about the centralized electric grid，imply about 表「对……作出何种暗示」，无从句、无否定、无陷阱。
**定位** 当越来越多的人成为「产消者」——自产自用能源——耗费数十年和数十亿美元建成的集中电网，将何去何从？
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确What happens to the centralized electric grid … as more and more people become "prosumers,"↔ It might become a thing of the past. took decades and billions of dollars to build↔a thing of the past预判「集中电网可能走向终结」即 It might become a thing of the past.——might体现「推断而非断言」的克制，a thing of the past 体现「淡出、被取代」的语义。
B) 张冠李戴It might turn out to be a "prosumer". 把电网当成 prosumer，但 as more and more people become "prosumers," 明确把 prosumers 限定为「人」——集中电网是被产消者削弱的对象，而不是产消者本身。
C) 与原文相反It will be easier to operate and maintain. 暗示电网未来更易运维，但全段以 risks 起头、以 What happens to the centralized electric grid 作反问收束——作者隐含的是「集中电网的处境堪忧」，与「更易运维」相反。
D) 过度推断It will have to be completely transformed. 中 will have to 与 completely 把作者克制的反问/隐忧夸大为「必须彻底改造」的强断言——原文只表「命运不明」，未承诺「必须、彻底」。
questions.quote: What happens to the centralized electric grid, which took decades and billions of dollars to build, as more and more people become "prosumers," who produce and consume their own energy onsite?

options.text: It might become a thing of the past.
It might turn out to be a "prosumer".
It will be easier to operate and maintain.
It will have to be completely transformed.

title: The tree people in the Lord of the…

sentences.text: The tree people in the Lord of the Rings—the Ents—can get around by walking.
But for real trees, it's harder to uproot.
Because they're literally rooted into the ground, they are unable to leave and go(26)____ .

passage.translation: 《指环王》中的树人——Ents——可以通过行走来四处移动。但对于真正的树木来说，连根拔起要困难得多。因为它们实实在在地扎根于地下,无法离开并前往别处。

sentences.text: When a tree first starts growing in a certain area, it's likely that the (27)____ envelope—the temperature, humidity, rainfall patterns and so on—suits it.
Otherwise, it would be unable to grow from a seedling.
But as it (28)____ , these conditions may change and the area around it may no longer be suitable for its (29)____ .

passage.translation: 当一棵树最初开始在某个地区生长时,很可能那里的气候条件——温度、湿度、降雨模式等等——适合它。否则,它就无法从幼苗长大。但随着树龄增长,这些条件可能会改变,它周围的地区可能不再适合其后代生长。

sentences.text: When that happens, many trees like walnuts, oaks and pines, rely (30)____ on so-called "scatter hoarders," such as birds, to move their seeds to new localities.
Many birds like to store food for the winter, which they (31)____ retrieve.
When the birds forget to retrieve their food—and they do sometimes—a seedling has a chance to grow.

The bird Clark's nutcracker, for example, hides up to 100,000 seeds per year, up to 30 kilometers away from the seed source, and has a very close symbiotic(共生的) relationship with several pine species, most (32)____ the whitebark pine.

passage.translation: 当这种情况发生时,许多树木如核桃树、橡树和松树,完全依赖所谓的"贮藏散布者",比如鸟类,将它们的种子搬运到新的地点。许多鸟类喜欢为冬天储存食物,之后再取回。当鸟类忘记取回它们的食物时——它们有时确实会忘记——幼苗就有机会生长。例如,星鸦每年藏匿多达10万颗种子,最远可达距离种子来源30公里的地方,并与几种松树有着非常紧密的共生关系,其中最显著的是白皮松。

sentences.text: As trees outgrow their ideal (33)____ in the face of climate change, these flying ecosystem engineers could be a big help in (34)____ trees.
It's a solution for us—getting birds to do the work is cheap and effective—and it could give (35)____ oaks and pines the option to truly "make like a tree and leave."

passage.translation: 随着树木在气候变化面前超出其理想栖息地,这些会飞的生态系统工程师可能在重新种植树木方面提供巨大帮助。这对我们来说是一个解决方案——让鸟类来做这项工作既便宜又有效——而且它可以给脆弱的橡树和松树提供真正"像树一样离开"的选择。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
The tree people in the Lord of the Rings—the Ents—can get around by walking. But for real trees, it's harder to uproot. Because they're literally rooted into the ground, they are unable to leave and go{{26}} .

When a tree first starts growing in a certain area, it's likely that the {{27}} envelope—the temperature, humidity, rainfall patterns and so on—suits it. Otherwise, it would be unable to grow from a seedling. But as it {{28}} , these conditions may change and the area around it may no longer be suitable for its {{29}} .

When that happens, many trees like walnuts, oaks and pines, rely {{30}} on so-called "scatter hoarders," such as birds, to move their seeds to new localities. Many birds like to store food for the winter, which they {{31}} retrieve. When the birds forget to retrieve their food—and they do sometimes—a seedling has a chance to grow. The bird Clark's nutcracker, for example, hides up to 100,000 seeds per year, up to 30 kilometers away from the seed source, and has a very close symbiotic(共生的) relationship with several pine species, most {{32}} the whitebark pine.

As trees outgrow their ideal {{33}} in the face of climate change, these flying ecosystem engineers could be a big help in {{34}} trees. It's a solution for us—getting birds to do the work is cheap and effective—and it could give {{35}} oaks and pines the option to truly "make like a tree and leave."

legacy
