questions.explanation:
**答案** D) elsewhere 副词
**词性槽** 不及物动词 go 后缺地点状语
**依据** elsewhere 正是"到别处"，与 leave 完美互补句意为"树木无法离开后去别处"，they are unable to leave and go __(26)__ 里 leave +go elsewhere 是英语里典型搭配，完整呼应上文"树人能走、真树不能"的对比。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) exclusively 表"专门地"，与位移无关exclusively 修饰"仅、专门"，go exclusively 无法表达"去别处"，与上下文 leave 不构成位移呼应。
F) forever 表"永远"是时间副词forever 表时间长度，go forever 不能传达"去别的地方"这一空间含义，与前面"无法离开"的空间逻辑不接。
J) notably 表"显著地"是评价副词notably 一般修饰程度或引出突出例子，与 go 搭配无地点义，更适合后文 32 题 most __ 这种引出代表性例子的语境。
M) subsequently 表"随后"是时间副词subsequently 表时间先后，go subsequently 表达不了"去别处"，留给后文 31 题描述"鸟随后再取回食物"的时序语境。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) climatic 形容词
**词性槽** the ___ envelope 中冠词与名词之间
**依据** 破折号列举正是"气候要素" the __(27)__ envelope—the temperature, humidity, rainfall patterns and so on 同位列举的全是气候要素，故 envelope 前必为 climatic，构成 climatic envelope（气候包络）这一生态学搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) fruitful表"多产的"与气候要素无关fruitful envelope 在语义上无法概括温度湿度，且后文谈"是否适合种子生长"，并非"是否多产"。
N) vulnerable 表"脆弱的"修饰对象多为生命体vulnerable envelope 不成立；且 vulnerable 的真实用武之地是后文 35 题修饰"易受气候威胁的橡树/松树"。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) ages 动词
**词性槽** as it ___ 中需谓语动词第三人称单数
**依据** ages = "年岁增长、变老"，正对应"环境变迁" But as it __(28)__, these conditions may change and the area around it may no longer be suitable for its offspring 表"随着树木变老，环境可能改变"，ages（变老/生长）与 it（树）作主语完美契合，紧扣下文"原栖地不再适合后代"的因果。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
O) withdraws withdraws 表"撤退/撤回"，与扎根的树矛盾withdraws 主体应是能主动撤离的对象，但开篇早已强调真树 they are unable to leave and go __(26)__，树不可能 withdraw；语义直接撞墙。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 O) —— withdraws 第三单现挂面好看，语篇直接撞墙。as it__(28)__ 的形态槽容得下 ages 和 withdraws；但开篇 they are unable to leave and go__(26)__ 已为全文定调"真树不能动"，withdraws 与全文逻辑相反。看到形态对的候选，先回首段查"前提"。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) offspring 名词
**词性槽** 形容词性物主代词 its 后
**依据** offspring = 后代，与上文 seedling 同链前句 it would be unable to grow from a seedling 已点出"幼苗"，本句 suitable for its offspring 自然指"是否还适合它的后代生长"，与下段"鸟搬种子"的因果链对接。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) ages ages 名义为"年龄/时代"，与适生环境不搭suitable for its ages 语义空洞，且 A 作动词"成长"的义在 28 题更对路。
H) habitats habitats 是"栖息地"本身、不是"被栖息的对象"句式说"the area…suitable for its ___"——its 指代的应是"被栖息的对象"（后代）而非"栖息地"，否则等于"地区适合它的栖息地"语义打架。H 留给 33 题 ideal ___ 直接表"栖息地"。
I) legacy legacy 偏"遗产/遗留"抽象义suitable for its legacy 不构成生态语境的常用搭配，且后文谈的是"幼苗能否长出"这一具体繁衍问题，不是抽象遗产。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) exclusively 副词
**词性槽** rely ___ on 中嵌入的副词位
**依据** exclusively on = "完全依赖" rely exclusively on 是固定搭配，强调"除此之外别无他法"，与文中"许多树就是只能靠散播储藏的鸟来搬运种子"语义吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) forever 时间副词与"程度依赖"不搭rely forever on 不是英语固定搭配，forever 描述时间持续，无法表达"完全/仅"这一程度义。
J) notably notably 强调"显著地"，不修饰"依赖程度" rely notably on 极少见，notably 多用于举出突出的例子（见 32 题），不是描述依赖比例。
M) subsequently 时间副词，表先后非程度subsequently 表"随后"，rely subsequently on 不构成搭配，留给 31 题描述"鸟随后再取回"。

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) subsequently 副词
**词性槽** 助动词 they 与实义动词 retrieve 之间
**依据** subsequently 呼应"先存、后取"时序Many birds like to store food for the winter, which they subsequently retrieve 中store 在前、retrieve 在后，subsequently（随后）正是这一时间链的关键过渡词，与下文"有时候忘了取"的转折也自然衔接。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) forever forever 表"永远"与一次性"取回"动作冲突they forever retrieve 表"它们永远在取回"，与"先储存、再取回"这一两段式动作不合；且forever 在本卷无更合适的空可安放，但仍不能反过来把不合适的位置硬塞给它。

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) notably 副词
**词性槽** most ___ the whitebark pine 中 most 后
**依据** most notably = "尤其值得一提的是" several pine species, most __(32)__ the whitebark pine 是"先泛指几种松、再举出最突出那一种"的经典引例句式，most notably 正是"尤其是（其中）……"，举出白皮松作为最突出的共生伙伴。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) forever 时间副词无法引例most forever 不构成固定搭配，无法承担"尤其是"的引例功能。
M) subsequently 时间副词表"随后" most subsequently 不是英语习惯搭配；M 留给 31 题描述"鸟随后再取回食物"。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) habitats 名词
**词性槽** 形容词 ideal 后接名词复数
**依据** habitats 与 ideal/outgrow 完美契合ideal habitats（理想栖息地）是生态学固定表达；As trees outgrow their ideal habitats in the face of climate change 表"在气候变化下树木超出其理想栖息地范围"，与上段"原栖地已不再适合后代"的因果完全连贯。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) ages ideal ages 表"理想年龄"与气候话题脱节outgrow their ideal ages 语义混乱，A 的真正用法是后文 28 题的动词"成长/变老"。
I) legacy legacy 抽象义不接 outgrow outgrow their ideal legacy 语义不成立，legacy 也不在"栖息地变化"这一具体话题链上。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) replanting 动词
**词性槽** 介词 in 后需动名词
**依据** replanting trees = 让树木在新地点重新扎根上文 these flying ecosystem engineers could be a big help in __(34)__ trees 紧跟讨论"鸟把种子带到新地方"，replanting trees 正是"重新栽种树木"——鸟通过遗忘的食物种子完成的"无意中的重栽"，与全文主线吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) breathing breathing trees 语义错位help in breathing trees 字面是"帮树呼吸"，与全文"搬运/重栽"主题完全脱节，是形态对、语义错的典型陷阱。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 B) —— breathing 形态完全合身，却被主旨一票否决。in __(34)__trees 这一框架同时容得下 breathing 和 replanting，单看半句几乎五五开；但只要回扣these flying ecosystem engineers could be a big help in __(34)__ trees 紧接其后的"鸟把种子搬去新地"，就知道答案必是 replanting。防坑口诀：选词填空形态对≠语境对，必回主旨。

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) vulnerable 形容词
**词性槽** give ___ oaks and pines 中复合宾语的修饰位
**依据** vulnerable 呼应"气候变化下处境艰难"全文一直在讲气候变化让原栖地不再适合树木 As trees outgrow their ideal __(33)__ in the face of climate change，因此这里的橡树和松树正是"易受气候威胁的"——vulnerable oaks and pines 与"给它们一条生路"的语义完美呼应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) fruitfulfruitful 表"多产"与"需要援救"反向fruitful oaks and pines 表"多产的橡松"，无法解释"为什么还需要鸟帮它们搬家"，与上下文逻辑相反。

title: Teenagers at risk of depression, anxiety and suicide…

sentences.text: Teenagers at risk of depression, anxiety and suicide often wear their troubles like a neon(霓虹灯) sign.
Their risky behaviors—drinking too much alcohol, using illegal drugs, smoking cigarettes and skipping school—can alert parents and teachers that serious problems are brewing.

passage.translation: 有抑郁、焦虑和自杀风险的青少年往往像霓虹灯一样显露出他们的烦恼。他们的危险行为——过度饮酒、使用非法药物、吸烟和逃学——能够提醒家长和教师严重的问题正在酝酿。

sentences.text: But a new study finds that there's another group of adolescents who are in nearly as much danger of experiencing the same psychiatric symptoms: teens who use tons of media, don't get enough sleep and have a sedentary(不爱活动的) lifestyle.

passage.translation: 但一项新研究发现,还有另一群青少年也几乎面临同样大的危险,可能出现相同的精神症状:那些大量使用媒体、睡眠不足并且过着不爱活动的生活方式的青少年。

sentences.text: Of course, that may sound like a description of every teenager on the planet.
But the study warns that it is teenagers who engage in all three of these practices in the extreme who are truly in jeopardy.
Because their behaviors are not usually seen as a red flag, these young people have been dubbed the "invisible risk" group by the study's authors.

passage.translation: 当然,这听起来可能像是对地球上每个青少年的描述。但该研究警告说,真正处于危险之中的是那些极端地从事这三种行为的青少年。因为他们的行为通常不被视为危险信号,这些年轻人被该研究的作者称为"隐形风险"群体。

sentences.text: "In some ways they're at greater risk of falling through the cracks," says researcher Vladimir Carli.
"While most parents, teachers and clinicians would react to an adolescent using drugs or getting drunk, they may easily overlook teenagers who are engaging in inconspicuous behaviors."

passage.translation: "在某些方面,他们面临着更大的被忽视的风险,"研究人员Vladimir Carli说。"虽然大多数家长、教师和临床医生会对使用药物或醉酒的青少年做出反应,但他们可能很容易忽视那些从事不显眼行为的青少年。"

sentences.text: The study's authors surveyed 12,395 students and analyzed nine risk behaviors, including excessive alcohol use, illegal drug use, heavy smoking, high media use and truancy(逃学).
Their aim was to determine the relationship between these risk behaviors and mental health issues in teenagers.

passage.translation: 该研究的作者调查了12395名学生,并分析了九种危险行为,包括过度饮酒、非法药物使用、大量吸烟、高度使用媒体和逃学。他们的目的是确定这些危险行为与青少年心理健康问题之间的关系。

sentences.text: About 58% of the students demonstrated none or few of the risk behaviors.
Some 13% scored high on all nine of the risk behaviors.
And 29%, the "invisible risk" group, scored high on three in particular: They spent five hours a day or more on electronic devices.
They slept six hours a night or less.
And they neglected "other healthy activities."

passage.translation: 约58%的学生表现出没有或很少有危险行为。约13%的学生在全部九种危险行为上得分都很高。而29%的学生,即"隐形风险"群体,在三种行为上得分特别高:他们每天花五小时或更多时间使用电子设备。他们每晚睡眠六小时或更少。而且他们忽视了"其他健康活动"。

sentences.text: The group that scored high on all nine of the risk behaviors was most likely to show symptoms of depression; in all, nearly 15% of this group reported being depressed, compared with just 4% of the low-risk group.
But the invisible group wasn't far behind the high-risk set, with more than 13% of them exhibiting depression.

passage.translation: 在全部九种危险行为上得分都很高的群体最有可能表现出抑郁症状;总体而言,这一群体中近15%的人报告有抑郁,相比之下低风险群体中只有4%。但隐形群体与高风险群体相差不远,他们中超过13%的人表现出抑郁。

sentences.text: The findings caught Carli off guard.
"We were very surprised," he says.
"The high-risk group and low-risk group are obvious.
But this third group was not only unexpected, it was so distinct and so large—nearly one third of our sample—that it became a key finding of the study."

passage.translation: 这些发现让Carli感到意外。"我们非常惊讶,"他说。"高风险群体和低风险群体是显而易见的。但这第三个群体不仅出乎意料,而且如此独特、如此庞大——几乎占我们样本的三分之一——以至于它成为了该研究的一个关键发现。"

sentences.text: Carli says that one of the most significant things about his study is that it provides new early- warning signs for parents, teachers and mental health-care providers.
And early identification, support and treatment for mental health issues, he says, are the best ways to keep them from turning into full-blown disorders.

passage.translation: Carli说,他的研究最重要的意义之一是它为家长、教师和心理健康护理提供者提供了新的预警信号。他说,对心理健康问题的早期识别、支持和治疗是防止它们演变成全面疾病的最佳方式。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does the author mean by saying "Teenagers at risk of depression, anxiety and suicide often wear their troubles like a neon sign" (Lines 1–2, Para. 1)?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （词义句意题）
**题目译文**
作者说"有抑郁、焦虑和自杀风险的青少年往往像霓虹灯一样显露他们的问题"(第1段第1-2行)是
什 么 意 思? A) 心理问题现在可以在大量青少年中发现。
B) 青少年的心理问题正得到越来越多的关注。
C) 青少年的心理问题往往过于明显以至于不可能不被观察到。
D) 抑郁和焦虑是心理问题最常见的症状。
**判型** 题干 What does the author mean by saying 明确要求解释一句话的真实含义，标志着这是一道考查整句修辞含义的句意题。
**拆句** 主干是 What does the author mean by saying...?：宾语从句省略，引号内是被动语态like 引导明喻，句子结构平铺直叙，无陷阱，重心在 like a neon sign 这个比喻。
**定位** 面临抑郁、焦虑与自杀风险的青少年，常常把自己的烦恼像霓虹灯一样挂在身上。他们的危险行为——酗酒、吸毒、抽烟、逃学——能提醒家长和老师严重问题正在酝酿。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念Mental problems can now be found in large numbers of teenagers 把焦点偷换为”患病人数多”，而原句讲的是”症状显眼”，与人数规模无关。
B) 无中生有Teenagers' mental problems are getting more and more attention 谈”日益受到重视”，原文只字未提社会关注度的变化。
C) ✓ 正确wear their troubles like a neon(霓虹灯) sign ↔ too conspicuous not to be observed can alert parents and teachers ↔ not to be observed预判要点是”显眼+能被发现”，C 项 too conspicuous not to be observed 把两点压成一句，是定位句的精准同义改写。
D) 答非所问Depression and anxiety are the most common symptoms 讨论”哪种症状最常见”，与题干所问的”霓虹灯句意”无关。
questions.quote: Teenagers at risk of depression, anxiety and suicide often wear their troubles like a neon(霓虹灯) sign. Their risky behaviors—drinking too much alcohol, using illegal drugs, smoking cigarettes and skipping school—can alert parents and teachers that serious problems are brewing.

options.text: Mental problems can now be found in large numbers of teenagers.
Teenagers' mental problems are getting more and more attention.
Teenagers' mental problems are often too conspicuous not to be observed.
Depression and anxiety are the most common symptoms of mental problems.

questions.prompt: What is the finding of the new study?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
新研究的发现是什么?
A) 青少年的生活方式近年来发生了很大变化。
B) 许多青少年求助于毒品或酒精来获得心理解脱。
C) 经历心理问题的青少年倾向于大量使用媒体。
D) 许多迄今未被观察到的年轻人可能存在心理问题。
**判型** What is the finding 指向一个具体的事实性结论，不是要推断也不是主旨概括。
**拆句** What is the finding of the new study? 单主谓宾的极简疑问句，无修饰、无陷阱。
**定位** 但一项新研究发现，还有另一群青少年同样处于经历这些精神症状的危险中：那些大量使用媒体、睡眠不足、久坐少动的青少年。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Teenagers' lifestyles have changed greatly in recent years 是一个时序变化论断，原文仅描述一群少年的当前状态，未做时序对比。
B) 张冠李戴Many teenagers resort to drugs or alcohol for mental relief 描述的是 P1 中的高风险组特征，且原文从未说他们靠毒品酒精”自我缓解”，而是说这些行为本身是危险征兆。
C) 与原文相反Teenagers experiencing psychological problems tend to use a lot of media 把因果方向颠倒：原文是”高媒介使用等行为→精神风险”，C 把”已有精神问题→倾向使用媒体”反着说。
D) ✓ 正确another group of adolescents ↔ Many hitherto unobserved youngsters in nearly as much danger of experiencing the same psychiatric symptoms ↔may have psychological problems预判两要点：①一群被忽视的少年 ②同样有精神问题风险，D 项用 hitherto unobserved 与 may have psychological problems 一一对应。
questions.quote: But a new study finds that there's another group of adolescents who are in nearly as much danger of experiencing the same psychiatric symptoms: teens who use tons of media, don't get enough sleep and have a sedentary(不爱活动的) lifestyle.

options.text: Teenagers' lifestyles have changed greatly in recent years.
Many teenagers resort to drugs or alcohol for mental relief.
Teenagers experiencing psychological problems tend to use a lot of media.
Many hitherto unobserved youngsters may have psychological problems.

questions.prompt: Why do the researchers refer to teens who use tons of media, don't get enough sleep and have a sedentary lifestyle as the "invisible risk" group?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
为什么研究人员将大量使用媒体、睡眠不足且久坐不动的青少年称为"隐形风险"群体?
A) 他们的行为可能对社会构成隐形威胁。
B) 他们的行为不构成警示信号。
C) 他们的行为不倾向于导致心理问题。
D) 他们的行为可以在地球上几乎所有青少年身上发现。
**判型** Why do the researchers refer to...as the "invisible risk" group 问的是作者为何这样称呼，答案就在命名句旁边的解释里。
**拆句** 宾语从句 teens who use tons of media, don't get enough sleep and have a sedentary lifestyle 是三个并列动词词组作 who 的定语，描述同一群青少年，结构清晰、无陷阱。
**定位** 因为他们的行为通常不被视为危险信号，这些少年被研究的作者们称为”隐性风险”组。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Their behaviors can be an invisible threat to society 把”隐性”嫁接到”社会威胁”上，原文只谈对个人精神健康的风险，从未上升到社会危害。
B) ✓ 正确not usually seen as a red flag ↔ do not constitute a warning signal预判要点是”不被当作危险信号”，B 项就是 not...a red flag 的字面同义翻译。
C) 与原文相反Their behaviors do not tend towards mental problems 说他们的行为不会导致精神问题，而原文整段都在强调这些行为同样会引发精神症状——方向完全相反。
D) 以偏概全Their behaviors can be found in almost all teenagers on earth 借用了 every teenager on the planet，但原文紧接着用 But 强调”只有把三项都做到极端的少年才真正危险”，D 把这条限定吞掉了。
questions.quote: Because their behaviors are not usually seen as a red flag, these young people have been dubbed the "invisible risk" group by the study's authors.

options.text: Their behaviors can be an invisible threat to society.
Their behaviors do not constitute a warning signal.
Their behaviors do not tend towards mental problems.
Their behaviors can be found in almost all teenagers on earth.

questions.prompt: What does the new study find about the invisible group?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
新研究对隐形群体有什么发现?
A) 他们患抑郁症的可能性几乎与高风险群体一样大。
B) 他们患有抑郁症但不表现出任何症状。
C) 他们不像同龄人那样经常表现出危险行为。
D) 他们不像高风险群体那样吸引媒体关注。
**判型** What does the new study find about the invisible group 仍是问一个具体的客观发现，不需要推断。
**拆句** What does the new study find about the invisible group? 介词 about 引出对象限定，单层疑问句，无陷阱。
**定位** 在九种风险行为上得分都高的那一组最容易表现出抑郁症状；总体而言，这一组中近 15%的人报告称自己抑郁，而低风险组仅 4%。但隐性风险组并不比高风险组落后多少，超过13% 的人表现出抑郁。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确the invisible group wasn't far behind the high-risk set ↔almost as liable to depression as the high-risk group more than 13% of them exhibiting depression ↔ liable to depression预判要点是”几乎不亚于高风险组”，A 项用 almost as...as 与 the high-risk group 把对比关系与对比对象一并写出。
B) 与原文相反They suffer from depression without showing any symptoms 说他们抑郁却”无症状”，而原文清清楚楚说 13% of them exhibiting depression，恰恰是有症状被研究观察到。
C) 答非所问They do not often demonstrate risky behaviors as their peers 答的是”隐性”何来，是 53 题层面问题，而非 54 题问的”新研究关于他们的发现”。
D) 无中生有They do not attract the media attention the high-risk group does 谈媒体注意度，原文从未谈及媒体对两组的报道差异。
questions.quote: The group that scored high on all nine of the risk behaviors was most likely to show symptoms of depression; in all, nearly 15% of this group reported being depressed, compared with just 4% of the low-risk group. But the invisible group wasn't far behind the high-risk set, with more than 13% of them exhibiting depression.

options.text: They are almost as liable to depression as the high-risk group.
They suffer from depression without showing any symptoms.
They do not often demonstrate risky behaviors as their peers.
They do not attract the media attention the high-risk group does.

questions.prompt: What is the significance of Vladimir Carli's study?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
Vladimir Carli的研究有什么意义?
A) 它为青少年心理问题提供了一种新的治疗方法。
B) 它为识别有问题的青少年提供了新的预警信号。
C) 它可能找到了处理有行为问题的青少年的理想方法。
D) 它为不健康行为如何引发心理健康问题提供了新的见解。
**判型** What is the significance of Vladimir Carli's study 问的是研究者本人在文中陈述的研究意义，是明示性陈述，不必推断。
**拆句** What is the significance of Vladimir Carli's study? 简单主系表疑问句，of 短语作定语限定 study，无陷阱。
**定位** Carli 说，他研究最重要的意义之一在于，它为家长、老师和心理保健工作者提供了新的早期预警信号。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断It offers a new treatment for psychological problems among teenagers 把”早期预警信号”升级为”新治疗方法”，原文末句虽提及 treatment，但研究本身提供的是预警而非治疗。
B) ✓ 正确provides new early-warning signs for parents, teachers and mental health-care providers ↔provides new early-warning signals for identifying teens in trouble预判要点是”提供新的早期预警信号”，B 项几乎原词复现 early-warning signals，把信号面向的目的写出。
C) 过度推断It may have found an ideal way to handle teenagers with behavioral problems 把研究的意义升级为”找到了理想的处置办法”，原文只说”提供新的早期预警信号”，远没有ideal way 这种程度。
D) 无中生有It sheds new light on how unhealthy behaviors trigger mental health problems谈”揭示不健康行为如何引发心理问题的机制”，原文未做任何机制层面的解释。
questions.quote: Carli says that one of the most significant things about his study is that it provides new early- warning signs for parents, teachers and mental health-care providers.

options.text: It offers a new treatment for psychological problems among teenagers.
It provides new early-warning signals for identifying teens in trouble.
It may have found an ideal way to handle teenagers with behavioral problems.
It sheds new light on how unhealthy behaviors trigger mental health problems.

title: The Paris climate agreement finalised in December last…

sentences.text: The Paris climate agreement finalised in December last year heralded a new era for climate action.
For the first time, the world's nations agreed to keep global warming well below 2℃.

passage.translation: 去年12月最终达成的巴黎气候协定预示着气候行动新时代的到来。这是世界各国首次同意将全球变暖幅度控制在远低于2摄氏度的水平。

sentences.text: This is vital for climate-vulnerable nations.
Fewer than 4% of countries are responsible for more than half of the world's greenhouse gas emissions.
In a study published in Nature Scientific Reports, we reveal just how deep this injustice runs.

passage.translation: 这对气候脆弱国家至关重要。不到4%的国家造成了全球一半以上的温室气体排放。在《自然科学报告》发表的一项研究中,我们揭示了这种不公正现象的严重程度。

sentences.text: Developed nations such as Australia, the United States, Canada, and European countries are essentially climate "free-riders": causing the majority of the problems through high greenhouse gas emissions, while incurring few of the costs such as climate change's impact on food and water.
In other words, a few countries are benefiting enormously from the consumption of fossil fuels, while at the same time contributing disproportionately to the global burden of climate change.

passage.translation: 澳大利亚、美国、加拿大和欧洲国家等发达国家本质上是气候"搭便车者":通过高温室气体排放造成了大部分问题,却只承担少量成本,如气候变化对食物和水的影响。换句话说,少数国家从化石燃料消费中获得了巨大利益,同时却对全球气候变化负担做出了不成比例的贡献。

sentences.text: On the flip side, there are many "forced riders", who are suffering from the climate change impacts despite having scarcely contributed to the problem.
Many of the world's most climate vulnerable countries, the majority of which are African or small island states, produce a very small quantity of emissions.
This is much like a non-smoker getting cancer from second-hand smoke, while the heavy smoker is fortunate enough to smoke in good health.

passage.translation: 另一方面,存在许多"被迫承受者",他们几乎没有对问题做出贡献,却正在遭受气候变化的影响。世界上许多最易受气候影响的国家,其中大多数是非洲国家或小岛国,产生的排放量非常少。这很像一个不吸烟者因二手烟而患癌,而重度吸烟者却有幸在健康状态下吸烟。

sentences.text: The Paris agreement has been widely hailed as a positive step forward in addressing climate change for all, although the details on addressing "climate justice" can be best described as sketchy.

passage.translation: 巴黎协定被广泛誉为在为所有人应对气候变化方面迈出的积极一步,尽管关于解决"气候正义"的细节充其量只能说是粗略的。

sentences.text: The goal of keeping global temperature rise "well below" 2℃ is commendable but the emissions-reduction pledges submitted by countries leading up to the Paris talks are very unlikely to deliver on this.

passage.translation: 将全球气温上升幅度控制在"远低于"2摄氏度的目标值得赞扬,但各国在巴黎会谈前提交的减排承诺很难实现这一目标。

sentences.text: More than $100 billion in funding has been put on the table for supporting developing nations to reduce emissions.
However, the agreement specifies that there is no formal distinction between developed and developing nations in their responsibility to cut emissions, effectively ignoring historical emissions.
There is also very little detail on who will provide the funds or, importantly, who is responsible for their provision.
Securing these funds, and establishing who is responsible for raising them will also be vital for the future of climate-vulnerable countries.

passage.translation: 已有超过1000亿美元的资金被投入用于支持发展中国家减少排放。然而,该协定明确规定发达国家和发展中国家在减排责任方面没有正式区别,实际上忽略了历史排放。关于谁将提供资金,或者更重要的是谁负责提供资金,也几乎没有详细说明。确保这些资金以及确定谁负责筹集这些资金,对于气候脆弱国家的未来也至关重要。

sentences.text: The most climate-vulnerable countries in the world have contributed very little to creating the global disease from which they now suffer the most.

There must urgently be a meaningful mobilisation of the policies outlined in the agreement if we are to achieve national emissions reductions while helping the most vulnerable countries adapt to climate change.

passage.translation: 世界上最易受气候影响的国家对造成这种全球性疾病的贡献微乎其微,而它们现在却承受着最严重的后果。如果我们要在帮助最脆弱国家适应气候变化的同时实现国家减排目标,就必须紧急有效地动员协定中概述的政策。

sentences.text: And it is clearly up to the current generation of leaders from high-emitting nations to decide whether they want to be remembered as climate change tyrants or pioneers.

passage.translation: 显然,当前这一代高排放国家的领导人需要决定,他们是想被后人铭记为气候变化的暴君还是先驱。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: The author is critical of the Paris climate agreement because______.
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者批评巴黎气候协定是因为______。
A) 它对那些易受气候影响的国家不公平
B) 它仅旨在将气温上升控制在2℃以下
C) 它仅对不到4%的国家有利
D) 它让发达国家独自承担责任
**判型** 题干 The author is critical of the Paris climate agreement because 用 because 让考生在原文找出作者批评的具体理由，是典型的因果细节题。
**拆句** Q46 是一个待补全的陈述句：主句 "The author is critical of the Paris climate agreement" 后接 because 引导的原因状语从句，空格处填的是作者批评协议的原因。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 另一方面，存在着许多 "被迫搭车者"——他们几乎没有制造问题，却在承受气候变化的冲击。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确suffering from the climate change impacts despite having scarcely contributed to the problem ↔unfair to those climate-vulnerable nations Many of the world's most climate vulnerable countries ↔ climate-vulnerable nations预判答案 "协定对气候脆弱国家不公" 与 it is unfair to those climate-vulnerable nations 字面一致，直接锁定。
B) 与原文相反it aims to keep temperature rise below 2℃ only 把 keep global warming well below 2℃ 这一目标本身当作批评对象，但作者在 The goal of keeping global temperature rise "well below" 2℃ is commendable 明确说这一目标是commendable 值得肯定的，与批评相反。
C) 偷换概念原文 Fewer than 4% of countries are responsible for more than half of the world's greenhouse gas emissions 说的是 "不到 4% 的国家造成过半排放"——是责任比例，而非协议受益比例；选项 beneficial to only fewer than 4% of countries 把责任偷换成 "协议只让不到 4% 的国家受益"。
D) 与原文相反原文 the agreement specifies that there is no formal distinction between developed and developing nations in their responsibility to cut emissions 明确说协议没有把责任只压到发达国家头上，反而抹平了区别；选项 burdens developed countries with the sole responsibility 正好相反。
questions.quote: On the flip side, there are many "forced riders", who are suffering from the climate change impacts despite having scarcely contributed to the problem.

options.text: it is unfair to those climate-vulnerable nations
it aims to keep temperature rise below 2℃ only
it is beneficial to only fewer than 4% of countries
it burdens developed countries with the sole responsibility

questions.prompt: Why does the author call some developed countries climate "free-riders"?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者为什么称一些发达国家为气候"搭便车者"?
A) 它们不必担心自己消耗的食物和水。
B) 它们更有能力应对全球气候变化。
C) 它们几乎不为自己造成的问题付出任何代价。
D) 它们不受影响"被迫搭车者"的温室效应影响。
**判型** 题干 Why does the author call some developed countries climate "free-riders" 用Why 问作者这样称呼的依据，要的是原文对应解释句，属细节题。
**拆句** Q47 是 why 引导的疑问句，宾补结构 "call some developed countries climate free- riders"——把发达国家 "称为" 气候搭便车者，问的是这样称呼的原因。结构清晰，无陷阱。
**定位** 诸如澳大利亚、美国、加拿大及欧洲国家这些发达国家本质上就是气候上的 "搭便车者"：通过高温室气体排放制造了绝大多数问题，却几乎不承担诸如气候变化对食物与水资源冲击之类的代价。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文 climate change's impact on food and water 中的 food and water 是气候变化冲击的对象，并非他们 "消费" 的对象；选项 They needn't worry about the food and water they consume 把 food/water 偷换成 "自己消费的食物和水"。
B) 无中生有原文从未说发达国家 better able to cope with the global climate change 应对能力更强——它谈的是 "承担成本少" 而非 "应对能力强"，二者不能等同。
C) ✓ 正确incurring few of the costs such as climate change's impact on food and water ↔hardly pay anything for the problems they have caused causing the majority of the problems ↔ the problems they have caused预判答案 "造成问题却不承担代价" 直接对应 hardly pay anything for the problems they have caused，锁定 C。
D) 偷换概念题干和原文里 free-riders 中的 free 来自 free-rider（搭便车，免责），不是 free from（免受影响）；选项 free from the greenhouse effects affecting "forced riders" 利用一词多义把 "免责" 改造成 "免受影响"，与原文相反。
questions.quote: Developed nations such as Australia, the United States, Canada, and European countries are essentially climate "free-riders": causing the majority of the problems through high greenhouse gas emissions, while incurring few of the costs such as climate change's impact on food and water.

options.text: They needn't worry about the food and water they consume.
They are better able to cope with the global climate change.
They hardly pay anything for the problems they have caused.
They are free from the greenhouse effects affecting "forced riders".

questions.prompt: Why does the author compare the "forced riders" to second-hand smokers?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者为什么将"被迫搭车者"比作二手烟受害者?
A) 他们对公共健康问题几乎不负有责任。
B) 他们容易受到不健康环境条件的影响。
C) 他们必须承担他们并不负有责任的后果。
D) 他们没有意识到自己正面临的潜在风险。
**判型** 题干 Why does the author compare the "forced riders" to second-hand smokers 问作者打这个比喻是为说明什么，答案在比喻句邻近的解释/类比说明里。
**拆句** Q48 是 Why 疑问句，主干 "the author compare the forced riders to second-hand smokers"——"compare A to B" 表示把 A 比作 B；问的是这个类比想表达什么。结构无陷阱。
**定位** 另一方面，有许多 "被迫搭车者"，他们几乎未制造问题，却在承受气候变化冲击……这就好比一个不吸烟的人因为二手烟得了癌症，而吸烟成性的人却幸运地一边抽烟一边健康如常。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问题干问的是为何把 forced riders 比作 second-hand smokers，要的是受害与责任之间的对比；little responsibility for public health problems 跑到 public health（公共卫生）这个无关领域，没有回答比喻意图。
B) 以偏概全vulnerable to unhealthy environmental conditions 只说出 "易受不健康环境影响" 这一表层结果，丢掉了比喻的核心——"非由自己造成"；只取一半语义，构成以偏概全。
C) ✓ 正确suffering from the climate change impacts despite having scarcely contributed to the problem ↔bear consequences they are not responsible for二手烟比喻的核心点是 "受害者非责任方"，They have to bear consequences they are not responsible for 正是这一核心的直接转述，锁定 C。
D) 无中生有原文从未提 forced riders unaware of the potential risks "不知道潜在风险"——他们恰恰深受其害，对风险心知肚明；意识与否是凭空添加的命题。
questions.quote: On the flip side, there are many "forced riders", who are suffering from the climate change impacts despite having scarcely contributed to the problem. ... This is much like a non- smoker getting cancer from second-hand smoke, while the heavy smoker is fortunate enough to smoke in good health.

options.text: They have little responsibility for public health problems.
They are vulnerable to unhealthy environmental conditions.
They have to bear consequences they are not responsible for.
They are unaware of the potential risks they are confronting.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about the $100 billion funding?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者对1000亿美元的资金有何看法?
A) 它将激励所有国家减少碳排放。
B) 关于这笔资金的来源没有最终协议。
C) 关于这笔资金将如何使用没有明确说明。
D) 它将有效减少全球温室气体排放。
**判型** 题干 What does the author say about the \$100 billion funding 问作者就这笔钱说了什么具体事实，是典型细节题。
**拆句** Q49 是 What 引导的疑问句，宾语 "the \$100 billion funding" 是询问对象。结构清晰，注意 \$ 是美元符号，无陷阱。
**定位** 至于由谁出资，更关键的是谁来负责筹措这些资金，协议也几乎没有任何细节。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断原文 supporting developing nations to reduce emissions 只说资金用于支持发展中国家减排，并未承诺这能 motivate all nations to reduce carbon emissions "激励所有国家减排"；从 "支持部分国家" 推到 "激励所有国家" 是过度推断。
B) ✓ 正确very little detail on who will provide the funds ↔no final agreement on where it will come from预判 "出资方尚无定论" 与 There is no final agreement on where it will come from一一对应，直接锁定 B。
C) 偷换概念原文 who will provide the funds or... who is responsible for their provision 谈的是"谁出钱" 的来源问题，选项 no clarification of how the money will be spent 偷换成"钱怎么花" 的去向问题，方向不一致。
D) 无中生有effectively reduce greenhouse emissions worldwide 在原文里找不到对应——P7 反而暗示协议在减排责任划分上模糊，无法效力全球减排；这是凭空添加的乐观结论。
questions.quote: There is also very little detail on who will provide the funds or, importantly, who is responsible for their provision.

questions.prompt: What urgent action must be taken to realise the Paris climate agreement?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
要实现巴黎气候协定必须采取什么紧急行动?
A) 鼓励高排放国家采取主动行动。
B) 呼吁所有相关国家共同努力。
C) 推动当前世界领导人达成共识。
D) 立即实施协定中的政策。
**判型** 题干 What urgent action must be taken to realise the Paris climate agreement 问的是具体待采取的措施，原文有明确对应的祈使/必须句，按细节题处理。
**拆句** Q50 是 What 引导的疑问句，主干 "What urgent action must be taken" 用被动语态问什么紧迫行动必须被采取；不定式 "to realise the Paris climate agreement" 作目的状语。结构清晰，无陷阱。
**定位** 如果我们想在实现各国减排的同时帮助最脆弱的国家适应气候变化，就必须紧急且切实地把协定所述政策动员起来落到实处。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问Encouraging high-emitting nations to take the initiative 来源是 it is clearly up to the current generation of leaders from high-emitting nations to decide，那是一句关于 "由谁拍板" 的尾段呼吁，不是题干所问的 "urgent action"；urgent action 在原文中明确锁在 P8 的 must urgently 一句。
B) 无中生有Calling on all the nations concerned to make joint efforts 是听起来很顺耳的常识口号，原文 P8 强调的是 "把已写入协定的政策动员起来"，并非 "号召所有国家联合"——号召联合属于无中生有。
C) 无中生有Pushing the current world leaders to come to a consensus 的 "达成共识" 来源是脑补——P9 谈的是高排放国领导者将被历史如何评价，不是要他们 "达成共识"；原文没有任何 consensus 相关诉求。
D) ✓ 正确a meaningful mobilisation of the policies outlined in the agreement↔Putting in effect the policies in the agreement urgently ↔ at once预判 "立刻落实协议政策" 与 Putting in effect the policies in the agreement at once字面一致，直接锁定 D。

title: It is important that scientists be seen as…

sentences.text: It is important that scientists be seen as normal people asking and answering important questions.
Good, sound science depends on (26)____ , experiments and reasoned methodologies.
It requires a willingness to ask new questions and try new approaches.
It requires one to take risks and experience failures.
But good science also requires (27)____ understanding, clear explanation and concise presentation.

passage.translation: 科学家被视为提出并回答重要问题的普通人，这一点很重要。优秀、可靠的科学依赖于假设、实验和合理的方法论。它需要愿意提出新问题并尝试新方法。它需要人们承担风险并经历失败。但优秀的科学还需要语境理解、清晰的解释和简明的陈述。

sentences.text: Our country needs more scientists who are willing to step out in the public (28)____ and offer their opinions on important matters.
We need more scientists who can explain what they are doing in language that is (29)____ and understandable to the public.
Those of us who are not scientists should also be prepared to support public engagement by scientists, and to (30)____ scientific knowledge into our public communications.

passage.translation: 我们的国家需要更多愿意走进公共舞台并就重要事务发表意见的科学家。我们需要更多能够用令人信服且公众可理解的语言解释自己工作的科学家。我们这些非科学家也应该准备好支持科学家的公众参与，并将科学知识纳入我们的公共传播中。

sentences.text: Too many people in this country, including some among our elected leadership, still do not understand how science works or why robust, long-range investments in research vitally matter.
In the 1960s, the United States (31)____ nearly 17% of discretionary(可酌情支配的) spending to research and development, (32)____ decades of economic growth.
By 2008, the figure had fallen into the single(33)____ .
This occurs at a time when other nations have made significant gains in their own research capabilities.

passage.translation: 这个国家有太多的人,包括我们民选领导层中的一些人,仍然不理解科学如何运作,或者为什么强有力的长期研究投资至关重要。在20世纪60年代,美国将近17%的可酌情支配的支出用于研究与开发,收获了数十年的经济增长。到2008年,这一数字已降至个位数。这种情况发生在其他国家在自身研究能力方面取得重大进展的时期。

sentences.text: At the University of California (UC), we (34)____ ourselves not only on the quality of our research, but also on its contribution to improving our world.
To (35)____ the development of science from the lab bench to the market place, UC is investing our own money in our own good ideas.

passage.translation: 在加州大学,我们不仅为研究质量感到自豪,也为其对改善我们世界的贡献感到自豪。为了加速科学从实验室到市场的发展,加州大学正在将我们自己的资金投入到我们自己的优秀创意中。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
It is important that scientists be seen as normal people asking and answering important questions. Good, sound science depends on {{26}} , experiments and reasoned methodologies. It requires a willingness to ask new questions and try new approaches. It requires one to take risks and experience failures. But good science also requires {{27}} understanding, clear explanation and concise presentation.

Our country needs more scientists who are willing to step out in the public {{28}} and offer their opinions on important matters. We need more scientists who can explain what they are doing in language that is {{29}} and understandable to the public. Those of us who are not scientists should also be prepared to support public engagement by scientists, and to {{30}} scientific knowledge into our public communications.

Too many people in this country, including some among our elected leadership, still do not understand how science works or why robust, long-range investments in research vitally matter. In the 1960s, the United States {{31}} nearly 17% of discretionary(可酌情支配的) spending to research and development, {{32}} decades of economic growth. By 2008, the figure had fallen into the single{{33}} . This occurs at a time when other nations have made significant gains in their own research capabilities.

At the University of California (UC), we {{34}} ourselves not only on the quality of our research, but also on its contribution to improving our world. To {{35}} the development of science from the lab bench to the market place, UC is investing our own money in our own good ideas.

incorporate

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) hypotheses 名词
**词性槽** depends on ___, experiments and reasoned methodologies——三项并列的第一项
**依据** hypotheses 与 experiments、methodologies 同属"科研三件套" Good, sound science depends on __(26)__, experiments and reasoned methodologies. 谈"好科学的根基"，hypotheses（假说）+ experiments（实验）+methodologies（方法论）正是科研标准三步：先提假说、再做实验、再用合理方法。与下文 It requires a willingness to ask new questions and try new approaches. "提新问题、试新方法"完全呼应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
L) inertia 惯性/惰性义，与"好科学的基础"完全相反inertia 是负面词，意为"惰性、不愿改变"，若代入则成"好科学依赖惰性"，与下文 try new approaches 鼓励创新的基调直接冲突，感情色彩相反。

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) contextual 形容词
**词性槽** requires ___ understanding——动词 + 空 + 名词，空作 understanding 的定语
**依据** contextual understanding = 情境/背景化的理解，是科学传播的标准要素之一But good science also requires __(27)__ understanding, clear explanation and concise presentation. 强调好科学还需要"理解 + 清楚解释 + 简洁呈现"三件；contextual understanding 强调"结合背景去理解"，正是科学传播被广泛讨论的能力；并列三项色彩一致。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
J) indefinite 义"模糊的、无限期的"，与"科学严谨"完全相反indefinite understanding 表"模糊不清的理解"，与本段倡导的"好科学"立场冲突；且与 clear explanation、concise presentation 这两个褒义表达色彩相反，并列不协调。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 J) —— indefinite 是形容词，词性也对，但色彩与并列项相反。requires __(27)__ understanding, clear explanation and concise presentation. 三项并列要求同向褒义，indefinite"模糊不清"与 clear/concise 直接冲突。防坑：三项并列形容词题，第一动作不是查词义，而是查色彩是否与已给项一致；不一致直接淘汰，再在剩下的同向词里辨义。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) arena 名词
**词性槽** the public ___ 后接介词 and offer——空前是定冠词 + public，空后跟着并列动词offer，本空只能是名词
**依据** the public arena = 公共领域/舞台，是固定搭配，贴合"走出来面向公众发声" scientists who are willing to step out in the public __(28)__ and offer their opinions on important matters 强调科学家"走出去"对重要议题发声，public arena "公共舞台/公共领域" 正是固定表达；与下文"explain what they are doing in language ... understandable to the public"形成呼应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) digits 数字义，与"公共发声"语境完全无关digits 指"数字、位数"，更适合后文 By 2008, the figure had fallen into the single __(33)__.谈百分比下降的语境，放在 the public ___ 里完全说不通。
G) hypotheses 假说义，是科学家工作的对象而不是公共平台hypotheses 是科学研究的"假说"，更应出现在第一段 Good, sound science depends on__(26)__, experiments and reasoned methodologies. 谈科研根基的位置；the public hypotheses 既不成搭配，也偏离"出面发声"语义。
L) inertia 惰性/惯性义，感情色彩与全段呼吁恰好相反inertia 表"惰性、不愿改变"，本段是"鼓励科学家主动走向公众"，若填 inertia 则成"走进公共惰性"，逻辑指向反、且 the public inertia 不是惯用搭配。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) convincing 形容词
**词性槽** is ___ and understandable——系动词 is 后并列两个表语形容词
**依据** convincing 与 understandable 并列，构成"有说服力且易懂"，呼应"科学家要用公众能接受的语言" scientists who can explain what they are doing in language that is __(29)__ and understandable to the public. 强调科学家解释工作要面向公众，convincing（令人信服的）与 understandable（易懂的）正是科学传播两大要求；与第一段 But good science also requires __(27)__ understanding, clear explanation and concise presentation.中"清楚的解释、简洁的呈现"互相呼应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) contextual 义"语境/上下文的"，描述 language 时不自然contextual 多用作 contextual understanding/analysis，描述"理解/分析"的属性；用来修饰language 说"语境化的语言"既不地道，也与"让公众听懂"的目的不直接相关。它更贴合 27 题前文 But good science also requires __(27)__ understanding 那一空。
J) indefinite 义"不确定的、无限期的"，与"易懂"并列时方向相反indefinite language 意为"模糊不清的语言"，与 understandable 并列就成"既模糊又易懂"，自相矛盾；显然不合。

questions.explanation:
**答案** I) incorporate 动词
**词性槽** and to ___ scientific knowledge into ...——并列 to 不定式，空是动词原形
**依据** incorporate sth. into sth. = 把……纳入到……，是与 into 严格匹配的固定搭配and to __(30)__ scientific knowledge into our public communications. 表达"把科学知识纳入到我们的公共交流中"；incorporate ... into ... 是英语母语者写这一意思时最高频的搭配，介词 into 直接喊出了答案。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
K) indulge 搭配 in 而非 into；感情色彩负面indulge oneself in sth. 是"沉溺"，介词是 in 不是 into；语义"沉溺科学知识于公共交流"完全说不通。
O) warrant 义"使……有必要"，不接 into 框架warrant 是"使有必要、值得"，不与 X into Y 框架共现；语义"保证科学知识到公共交流中"也不通顺。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) devoted 动词
**词性槽** 主语 the United States 后缺谓语，时间状语 In the 1960s 决定一般过去时
**依据** devote X to Y = 把 X 投入到 Y，且 devoted 已是过去式，时态契合In the 1960s, the United States __(31)__ nearly 17% of discretionary(可酌情支配的) spending to research and development 说"60 年代美国把近 17% 的可支配支出投入研发"；devote sth. to sth. 是固定搭配，devoted 形式直接满足 In the 1960s 要求的过去时；与下一句 By 2008, the figure had fallen into the single __(33)__. 形成"过去高—后来跌"的对比链条。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) hasten 义"加快"，且不与"17% 支出 to 研发"搭配hasten 一般接动作（hasten the process），不是"加快 17% 到研发"；语义和搭配都不通。
I) incorporate 搭配是 into 不是 to incorporate A into B 才是地道搭配，本句介词是 to，不匹配；且语义"把 17% 并入研发"不如"投入"自然。
K) indulge 义"沉溺/纵容"，与国家拨款语境感情色彩冲突indulge in 表负面"沉溺"，谈国家投入研发用 indulge 听起来像"放任挥霍"，与文段赞美"长远研发投入"的立场相反。
O) warrant 义"使……有必要/保证"，与"分配支出"动作不对应warrant 表"使有必要、值得"，不表"分配"；warrant 17% to research 也不是英语固定表达。

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) reaping 动词
**词性槽** 句末逗号后接 ___ decades of economic growth——独立分词作状语
**依据** reap ... economic growth = 收获经济增长，与"投入研发"形成正向因果the United States __(31)__ nearly 17% of discretionary(可酌情支配的) spending to research and development, __(32)__ decades of economic growth. 表达"美国把大量支出投入研发，从而收获了数十年的经济增长"；reap ... growth 是常见正向搭配（reap the rewards/benefits/growth），逻辑顺、感情色彩正。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) impairing 义"损害"，与上文"加大研发投入"的逻辑方向完全相反impair 表"损害"，若代入则成"投入研发，损害了几十年的经济增长"，与文段"长远研发投入很重要"的立场冲突；六级常用这种"感情色彩反向词"来设陷阱，要警惕。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— impairing 与 reaping 同为 -ing 分词，词性完全对得上。devoted nearly 17% of discretionary(可酌情支配的) spending to research and development, __(32)__ decades of economic growth. 这里只看语法，H 和 N 都合法；但 H 是"损害"、N 是"收获"，方向相反。防坑：分词作结果状语，逻辑必须沿主句方向走——主句在赞美"加大研发投入"，结果只能是正向"收获经济增长"，立即排除 impairing。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) digits 名词
**词性槽** the single ___ 句末，single 作前置定语，本空是中心名词
**依据** single digits = 个位数，是英语谈百分比/数字下降的固定表达上文 nearly 17% 已给出基准比例，By 2008, the figure had fallen into the single__(33)__. 说"到 2008 年这一数字跌入 single digits"，恰好与"17% → 个位数"形成数值对比；fall into the single digits 是固定表达。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) hypotheses 义指"假说"，与百分比下降毫无关系hypotheses 谈科研假设，搭配 single 也不成立——the single hypotheses 既不像固定表达，也无法解释 fallen into 的"下降"动作。
L) inertia惯性/惰性，无法被"single"修饰inertia 是抽象概念，没有 the single inertia 这种搭配；而且本句要的是"数值"信息（与 17%呼应），inertia 给不出。

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) pride 动词
**词性槽** 主语 we 后缺谓语，且后面跟反身代词 ourselves——"pride oneself on"句型
**依据** pride oneself on sth. = 以……自豪，是固定句型At the University of California (UC), we __(34)__ ourselves not only on the quality of our research, but also on its contribution to improving our world. 强调 UC 对自身研究质量和对世界的贡献"引以为豪"；pride oneself on 是固定搭配，与后面 not only ... but also on ... 完美咬合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) hasten 义"加快"，无 hasten oneself on 的搭配hasten 后接动作或事物，没有 hasten oneself on sth. 这种用法；且"使自己加快研究质量"语义不通。
I) incorporate 义"纳入"，搭配是 incorporate sth. into sth. incorporate 的固定搭配是 incorporate A into B（把 A 纳入 B），不接反身代词加 on；将其代入则"把自己纳入研究质量上"完全说不通。
K) indulge 义"沉溺/纵容"，搭配是 indulge oneself in，不是 on indulge oneself in sth. 表"沉溺于……"，介词是 in 不是 on；且"沉溺于研究质量"感情色彩偏负面，与本段对 UC 的赞美口吻矛盾。
O) warrant 义"使……有必要/保证"，不与反身代词搭配warrant 后常接事物宾语（warrant attention/further study），不是 warrant oneself on；语义"使自己有必要在质量上"也不成立。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) hasten 动词
**词性槽** 不定式 to ___ the development——to 后接动词原形
**依据** hasten the development = 加快……发展，与"投入资金推动落地"完全咬合To __(35)__ the development of science from the lab bench to the market place, UC is investing our own money in our own good ideas. 是说"为了加快科学从实验室走向市场，UC 拿出自己的钱投入好点子"；hasten 表"加速"，与"from the lab bench to the market place"（从实验室到市场）的进程感、与下半句的"投入推动"动作完美对应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
I) incorporate 义"纳入"，搭配 into 而非 from ... to ... incorporate 强调"并入/整合"，常与 into 连用；本句结构是 from ... to ...（从 X 到 Y），是"加速过程"的动词更搭，incorporate 与目的状语"为了纳入科学发展……"也讲不通。本空incorporate 的真正归属在 30 题。
K) indulge 义"沉溺/纵容"，感情色彩与"推动落地"相反indulge 表负面"放纵"，谈"为了纵容科学发展"完全不合本段对 UC 投资行为的赞许口吻。
O) warrant 义"使有必要、保证"，不表"加速过程" warrant 表"使……有必要、值得"，目的状语"为了使科学发展从实验室到市场"语义模糊，且与下半句"投钱推动"的动作链不对应。

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Americans are deeply concerned about the relentless rise in health care costs and health insurance premiums.
They need to know if reform will help solve the problem.
The answer is that no one has an easy fix for rising medical costs.
The fundamental fix—reshaping how care is delivered and how doctors are paid in a wasteful, abnormal system—is likely to be achieved only through trial and error and incremental(渐进的) gains.

passage.translation: 美国人对医疗费用和健康保险费的持续上涨深感担忧。他们需要知道改革是否有助于解决这个问题。答案是,没有人能轻易解决医疗费用上涨的问题。根本性的解决办法——重塑这个浪费、不正常的体系中医疗服务的提供方式和医生的报酬方式——很可能只能通过反复试验和渐进式的进步来实现。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: The good news is that a bill just approved by the House and a bill approved by the Senate Finance Committee would implement or test many reforms that should help slow the rise in medical costs over the long term.
As a report in The New England Journal of Medicine concluded, "Pretty much every proposed innovation found in the health policy literature these days is contained in these measures."

passage.translation: 好消息是,众议院刚刚通过的一项法案和参议院财政委员会通过的一项法案将实施或测试许多改革措施,这些措施应该有助于从长远来看减缓医疗费用的上涨。正如《新英格兰医学杂志》的一篇报告所总结的:"如今卫生政策文献中几乎所有提出的创新都包含在这些措施中。"

passage.label: C

sentences.text: Medical spending, which typically rises faster than wages and the overall economy, is propelled by two things: the high prices charged for medical services in this country and the volume of unnecessary care delivered by doctors and hospitals, which often perform a lot more tests and treatments than a patient really needs.

passage.translation: 医疗支出通常比工资和整体经济增长得更快,它由两个因素推动:美国医疗服务收取的高价格,以及医生和医院提供的不必要医疗服务的数量,它们往往进行比患者真正需要的多得多的检查和治疗。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: Here are some of the important proposals in the House and Senate bills to try to address those problems, and why it is hard to know how well they will work.

passage.translation: 以下是众议院和参议院法案中试图解决这些问题的一些重要提案,以及为什么很难知道它们会有多大效果。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Both bills would reduce the rate of growth in annual Medicare payments to hospitals, nursing homes and other providers by amounts comparable to the productivity savings routinely made in other industries with the help of new technologies and new ways to organize work.
This proposal could save Medicare more than $100 billion over the next decade.
If private plans demanded similar productivity savings from providers, and refused to let providers shift additional costs to them, the savings could be much larger.
Critics say Congress will give in to lobbyists and let inefficient providers off the hook(放过).
That is far less likely to happen if Congress also adopts strong "pay- go" rules requiring that any increase in payments to providers be offset by new taxes or budget cuts.

passage.translation: 两项法案都将把Medicare对医院、疗养院和其他医疗服务提供者的年度支付增长率降低到与其他行业借助新技术和新的工作组织方式常规实现的生产率节约相当的水平。这项提案可能在未来十年为Medicare节省超过1000亿美元。如果私人医保计划也要求医疗服务提供者实现类似的生产率节约,并拒绝让提供者将额外成本转嫁给它们,节省的资金可能会大得多。批评者说,国会会向游说者屈服,放过低效率的提供者。如果国会同时采用严格的"现收现付"规则,要求对提供者支付的任何增加都必须由新税收或预算削减来抵消,那么这种情况发生的可能性就会小得多。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: The Senate Finance bill would impose an excise tax(消费税) on health insurance plans that cost more than $8,000 for an individual or $21,000 for a family.
It would most likely cause insurers to redesign plans to fall beneath the threshold.
Enrollees would have to pay more money for many services out of their own pockets, and that would encourage them to think twice about whether an expensive or redundant test was worth it.
Economists project that most employers would shift money from expensive health benefits into wages.
The House bill has no similar tax.
The final legislation should.

passage.translation: 参议院财政法案将对个人花费超过8000美元或家庭花费超过21000美元的健康保险计划征收消费税。这很可能会导致保险公司重新设计计划以低于这个门槛。参保人将不得不自掏腰包为许多服务支付更多费用,这将鼓励他们在进行昂贵或重复的检查是否值得时三思而后行。经济学家预测,大多数雇主会将资金从昂贵的健康福利转移到工资上。众议院法案没有类似的税收。最终立法应该有。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: Any doctor who has wrestled with multiple forms from different insurers, or patients who have tried to understand their own parade of statements, know that simplification ought to save money.
When the health insurance industry was still cooperating in reform efforts, its trade group offered to provide standardized forms for automated processing.
It estimated that step would save hundreds of billions of dollars over the next decade.
The bills would lock that pledge into law.

passage.translation: 任何与来自不同保险公司的多种表格打过交道的医生,或试图理解自己一连串账单的患者,都知道简化应该能节省资金。当健康保险行业还在配合改革努力时,其行业协会提出为自动化处理提供标准化表格。它估计这一步骤将在未来十年节省数千亿美元。这些法案将把这一承诺写入法律。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: The stimulus package provided money to convert the inefficient, paper-driven medical system to electronic records that can be easily viewed and transmitted.
This requires open investments to help doctors convert.
In time it should help restrain costs by eliminating redundant tests, preventing drug interactions, and helping doctors find the best treatments.

passage.translation: 经济刺激计划提供资金,将低效率的、以纸质为主的医疗系统转换为可以轻松查看和传输的电子记录。这需要公开投资来帮助医生转型。假以时日,它应该通过消除重复检查、防止药物相互作用以及帮助医生找到最佳治疗方法来帮助控制成本。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Virtually all experts agree that the fee-for-service system—doctors are rewarded for the quantity of care rather than its quality or effectiveness—is a primary reason that the cost of care is so high.
Most agree that the solution is to push doctors to accept fixed payments to care for a particular illness or for a patient's needs over a year.
No one knows how to make that happen quickly.
The bills in both houses would start pilot projects within Medicare.

They include such measures as accountable care organizations to take charge of a patient's needs with an eye on both cost and quality, and chronic disease management to make sure the seriously ill, who are responsible for the bulk of all health care costs, are treated properly.
For the most part, these experiments rely on incentive payments to get doctors to try them.

passage.translation: 几乎所有专家都同意,按服务收费制度——医生因医疗服务的数量而非质量或有效性而获得报酬——是医疗费用如此之高的主要原因。大多数人同意,解决办法是推动医生接受固定付款,以治疗特定疾病或满足患者一年内的需求。没有人知道如何快速实现这一目标。两院的法案都将在Medicare内启动试点项目。它们包括诸如负责任的医疗组织来负责患者的需求并兼顾成本和质量,以及慢性病管理以确保负责大部分医疗费用的重症患者得到适当治疗等措施。在大多数情况下,这些实验依靠激励性支付来让医生尝试它们。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: Testing innovations do no good unless the good experiments are identified and expanded and the bad ones are dropped.
The Senate bill would create an independent commission to monitor the pilot programs and recommend changes in Medicare's payment policies to urge providers to adopt reforms that work.
The changes would have to be approved or rejected as a whole by Congress, making it hard for narrow-interest lobbies to bend lawmakers to their will.

passage.translation: 除非能够识别和扩大好的实验并放弃坏的实验,否则测试创新就没有用处。参议院法案将设立一个独立委员会来监督试点项目,并建议改变Medicare的支付政策,以敦促医疗服务提供者采用有效的改革。这些变化必须由国会整体批准或拒绝,这使得狭隘利益集团的游说者很难让立法者屈从于他们的意愿。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: The bills in both chambers would create health insurance exchanges on which small businesses and individuals could choose from an array of private plans and possibly a public option.
All the plans would have to provide standard benefit packages that would be easy to compare.
To get access to millions of new customers, insurers would have a strong incentive to lower their prices, perhaps by accepting slimmer profit margins or demanding better deals from providers.

passage.translation: 两院的法案都将建立健康保险交易所,小企业和个人可以在上面从一系列私人计划中选择,可能还有公共选项。所有计划都必须提供易于比较的标准福利套餐。为了获得数百万新客户,保险公司将有强烈的动机降低价格,或许通过接受更低的利润率或要求从医疗服务提供者那里获得更好的交易。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: The final legislation might throw a public plan into the competition, but thanks to the fierce opposition of the insurance industry and Republican critics, it might not save much money.
The one in the House bill would have to negotiate rates with providers, rather than using Medicare rates, as many reformers wanted.

passage.translation: 最终立法可能会将公共计划纳入竞争,但由于保险行业和共和党批评者的激烈反对,它可能不会节省很多钱。众议院法案中的那个计划将不得不与医疗服务提供者协商费率,而不是像许多改革者所希望的那样使用Medicare费率。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: The president's stimulus package is pumping money into research to compare how well various treatments work.
Is surgery, radiation or careful monitoring best for prostate(前列腺) cancer?
Is the latest and most expensive cholesterol-lowering drug any better than its common competitors?
The pending bills would spend additional money to accelerate this effort.

passage.translation: 总统的经济刺激计划正在向研究投入资金,以比较各种治疗方法的效果。对于前列腺癌,手术、放疗还是仔细监测最好?最新最昂贵的降胆固醇药物比其常见竞争对手好吗?待决的法案将投入额外资金来加快这一努力。

passage.label: N

sentences.text: Critics have charged that this sensible idea would lead to rationing of care.
(That would be true only if you believed that patients should have an unrestrained right to treatments proven to be inferior.)
As a result, the bills do not require, as they should, that the results of these studies be used to set payment rates in Medicare.

passage.translation: 批评者指责说,这个明智的想法会导致医疗配给。(只有当你相信患者应该有不受限制的权利接受被证明是劣等的治疗时,这才是真的。)因此,这些法案没有像它们应该做的那样,要求将这些研究的结果用于设定Medicare的支付费率。

passage.label: O

sentences.text: Congress needs to find the courage to allow Medicare to pay preferentially for treatments proven to be superior.
Sometimes the best treatment might be the most expensive.
But overall, we suspect that spending would come down through elimination of a lot of unnecessary or even dangerous tests and treatments.

passage.translation: 国会需要找到勇气,允许Medicare优先为被证明优越的治疗方法付费。有时最好的治疗可能是最昂贵的。但总体而言,我们怀疑通过消除许多不必要甚至危险的检查和治疗,支出会下降。

passage.label: P

sentences.text: The House bill would authorize the secretary of health and human services to negotiate drug prices in Medicare and Medicaid.
Some authoritative analysts doubt that the secretary would get better deals than private insurers already get.
We believe negotiation could work.
It does in other countries.

passage.translation: 众议院法案将授权卫生与公众服务部部长在Medicare和Medicaid中协商药品价格。一些权威分析人士怀疑部长是否能获得比私人保险公司已经获得的更好的交易。我们相信谈判可行。其他国家就是这样做的。

passage.label: Q

sentences.text: Missing from these bills is any serious attempt to rein in malpractice costs.

Malpractice awards do drive up insurance premiums for doctors in high⁃risk specialties, and there is some evidence that doctors engage in "defensive medicine" by performing tests and treatments primarily to prove they are not negligent should they get sued.

passage.translation: 这些法案中缺少的是任何认真尝试控制医疗事故成本的内容。医疗事故赔偿确实推高了高风险专科医生的保险费,并且有一些证据表明,医生从事"防御性医疗",主要通过进行检查和治疗来证明如果他们被起诉,他们没有疏忽。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: With a tax imposed on expensive health insurance plans, most employers will likely transfer money from health expenses into wages.
questions.explanation:
**答案** F 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
对昂贵的健康保险计划征税后，大多数雇主可能会将资金从医疗支出转移到工资中。
**锚点** 「对昂贵保险计划征税 + 雇主把钱从医疗福利转入工资」双锚点
**定位** 经济学家预测，大多数雇主会把钱从昂贵的健康福利转移到工资中。
**改写** a tax imposed on expensive health insurance plans ↔an excise tax(消费税) on health insurance plans that cost more than $8,000 for an individual or$21,000 for a family「税 + 昂贵保险计划」对应most employers will likely transfer money from health expenses into wages ↔most employers would shift money from expensive health benefits into wages「同义动词 + 同指名词」逐词对照
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E 本段虽谈节省成本，但机制是reduce the rate of growth in annual Medicare payments to hospitals——削减 Medicare 给医院的付款增速，与「对昂贵保险计划征税 + 雇主把钱挪到工资」毫无对应；且本段主体是 Medicare 与提供方，不是雇主与员工工资。Both bills would reduce the rate of growth in annual Medicare payments to hospitals, nursing homes and other providers by amounts comparable to the productivity savings routinely made in other industries
questions.quote: Economists project that most employers would shift money from expensive health benefits into wages.

questions.prompt: Changes in policy would be approved or rejected as a whole so that lobbyists would find it hard to influence lawmakers.
questions.explanation:
**答案** J 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
政策变化将作为一个整体被批准或否决，这样游说者就很难影响立法者。
**锚点** 「政策变更整体表决 + 游说者难影响立法者」双锚点
**定位** 这些变更必须由国会整体批准或否决，使得狭隘利益的游说集团难以让立法者按其意志行事。
**改写** Changes in policy would be approved or rejected as a whole ↔The changes would have to be approved or rejected as a whole by Congress核心程序短语原样复现lobbyists would find it hard to influence lawmakers ↔making it hard for narrow-interest lobbies to bend lawmakers to their will「lobbyists/lobbies」同源 +「influence/bend…to their will」近义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E 本段确实出现了游说话题，但讲的是国会在被游说时会give in to lobbyists and let inefficient providers off the hook(放过)——也就是「国会被说服后放过低效提供方」；而陈述句要的是「整体表决程序使游说难以奏效」，机制是程序设计而非妥协警告，故本段不是源头段。Critics say Congress will give in to lobbyists and let inefficient providers off the hook(放过)
questions.quote: The changes would have to be approved or rejected as a whole by Congress, making it hard for narrow-interest lobbies to bend lawmakers to their will.

questions.prompt: It is not easy to curb the rising medical costs in America.
questions.explanation:
**答案** A 段（弱锚点）
**题目译文**
遏制美国不断上涨的医疗费用并非易事。
**锚点** 「难以遏制美国医疗成本上涨」总论判断
**定位** 根本性修复——重新塑造一个浪费而反常体系中医疗服务的提供方式和医生的报酬方式——很可能只有通过反复试错和渐进式收益才能实现。
**改写** It is not easy to curb the rising medical costs in America ↔no one has an easy fix for rising medical costs「难治」态度词的同义改写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B 本段The good news is that a bill just approved by the House and a bill approved by the Senate Finance Committee would implement or test many reforms that should help slow the rise in medical costs over the long term强调法案带来的乐观前景，是「能减缓」的正面态度；陈述句要的是「不易遏制」的负面态度，方向相反。The good news is that a bill just approved by the House and a bill approved by the Senate Finance Committee would implement or test many reforms that should help slow the rise in medical costs over the long term C 本段Medical spending, which typically rises faster than wages and the overall economy, is propelled by two things只在分析「被什么推动」，并未就「能否遏制」表明态度；陈述句要的是「不易遏制」这一态度判定，本段不承载该判定。Medical spending, which typically rises faster than wages and the overall economy, is propelled by two things: the high prices charged for medical services in this country and the volume of unnecessary care delivered by doctors and hospitals
questions.quote: The fundamental fix—reshaping how care is delivered and how doctors are paid in a wasteful, abnormal system—is likely to be achieved only through trial and error and incremental(渐进的) gains.

questions.prompt: Standardization of forms for automatic processing will save a lot of medical expenses.
questions.explanation:
**答案** G 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
用于自动处理的表格标准化将节省大量医疗费用。
**锚点** 「表单标准化 + 自动化处理 + 省钱」三重锚点
**定位** 在健康保险业还配合改革之时，其行业协会曾提议提供标准化表单用于自动化处理。
**改写** Standardization of forms for automatic processing ↔standardized forms for automated processing同根词词形互换save a lot of medical expenses ↔ save hundreds of billions of dollars over the next decade「概括省钱」对应「具体省多少钱」
questions.quote: When the health insurance industry was still cooperating in reform efforts, its trade group offered to provide standardized forms for automated processing.

questions.prompt: Republicans and the insurance industry are strongly opposed to the creation of a public insurance plan.
questions.explanation:
**答案** L 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
共和党人和保险业强烈反对创建公共保险计划。
**锚点** 「共和党人 + 保险业 + 反对公共保险计划」三重锚点
**定位** 最终立法或许会把一项公共计划投入竞争，但由于保险业和共和党批评者的强烈反对，它可能省不下多少钱。
**改写** Republicans and the insurance industry are strongly opposed ↔the fierce opposition of the insurance industry and Republican critics动词 strongly opposed 与名词 fierce opposition 等值the creation of a public insurance plan ↔ a public plan概括上位词 public plan 对应 public insurance plan
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
K 本段small businesses and individuals could choose from an array of private plans and possibly a public option只是说交易所里可能有公共选项，并未陈述谁反对公共计划，与陈述句的「Republicans 与保险业反对」无对应。small businesses and individuals could choose from an array of private plans and possibly a public option
questions.quote: The final legislation might throw a public plan into the competition, but thanks to the fierce opposition of the insurance industry and Republican critics, it might not save much money.

questions.prompt: Conversion of paper to electronic medical records will help eliminate redundant tests and prevent drug interactions.
questions.explanation:
**答案** H 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
将纸质病历转换为电子病历将有助于消除重复检查并防止药物相互作用。
**锚点** 「纸质转电子病历 + 消除冗余检查 + 防止药物相互作用」三重锚点
**定位** 假以时日，它应能通过消除冗余检查、预防药物相互作用，以及帮助医生找到最佳治疗方案来抑制成本。
**改写** Conversion of paper to electronic medical records ↔convert the inefficient, paper-driven medical system to electronic records名词化 conversion ↔ 动词 convert eliminate redundant tests ↔ eliminating redundant tests动词形态切换（-ing ↔ 原型）prevent drug interactions ↔ preventing drug interactions动词形态切换（-ing ↔ 原型）
questions.quote: In time it should help restrain costs by eliminating redundant tests, preventing drug interactions, and helping doctors find the best treatments.

questions.prompt: The high cost of medical services and unnecessary tests and treatments have driven up medical expenses.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
医疗服务的高昂费用以及不必要的检查和治疗推高了医疗支出。
**锚点** 「医疗服务高价 + 不必要的检查与治疗」双因锚点
**定位** 医疗开支通常涨得比工资和整体经济还快，它由两件事推动：本国医疗服务收取的高价格，以及医生和医院提供的不必要诊疗量——它们经常做远超患者真正所需的检查与治疗。
**改写** The high cost of medical services ↔the high prices charged for medical services in this country cost ↔ prices 同指 +「医疗服务」原样unnecessary tests and treatments ↔the volume of unnecessary care delivered by doctors and hospitals, which often perform a lot more tests and treatments than a patient really needs「不必要的检查与治疗」原样落地driven up medical expenses ↔ Medical spending … is propelled by two things推动类动词同义 +「医疗开支」上位词对应
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
I 本段the fee-for-service system…is a primary reason that the cost of care is so high只给出一项制度性根因（按服务量付费），与陈述句的「高价 + 不必要诊疗」两项并列结构不符。the fee-for-service system—doctors are rewarded for the quantity of care rather than its quality or effectiveness—is a primary reason that the cost of care is so high
questions.quote: Medical spending, which typically rises faster than wages and the overall economy, is propelled by two things: the high prices charged for medical services in this country and the volume of unnecessary care delivered by doctors and hospitals, which often perform a lot more tests and treatments than a patient really needs.

questions.prompt: One main factor that has driven up medical expenses is that doctors are compensated for the amount of care rather than its effect.
questions.explanation:
**答案** I 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
推高医疗费用的一个主要因素是医生的报酬取决于医疗服务的数量而非其效果。
**锚点** 「医生按数量而非效果获报」的根因判断
**定位** 几乎所有专家都同意：按服务量付费的制度——医生按其医疗服务的数量而非质量或效果获报——是医疗成本如此之高的一项主要原因。
**改写** doctors are compensated for the amount of care rather than its effect ↔doctors are rewarded for the quantity of care rather than its quality or effectiveness对照框架原样 + 三对同义词One main factor that has driven up medical expenses ↔is a primary reason that the cost of care is so high「主因 + 推高开支」同义改写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
C 本段the high prices charged for medical services in this country and the volume of unnecessary care delivered by doctors and hospitals给的两项原因都不涉及「按服务量而非质量/效果付费」这一独特对照，与陈述句的「rather than effect」对照结构不符。the high prices charged for medical services in this country and the volume of unnecessary care delivered by doctors and hospitals
questions.quote: Virtually all experts agree that the fee-for-service system—doctors are rewarded for the quantity of care rather than its quality or effectiveness—is a primary reason that the cost of care is so high.

questions.prompt: Contrary to analysts' doubts, the author believes drug prices may be lowered through negotiation.
questions.explanation:
**答案** P 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
与分析师的质疑相反,作者认为药品价格可能通过谈判降低。
**锚点** 「分析师存疑 vs 作者相信谈判可降药价」观点反差锚点
**定位** 一些权威分析人士怀疑卫生部长能否谈到比私营保险公司已经拿到的更好的价；我们相信谈判是可行的。
**改写** Contrary to analysts' doubts ↔Some authoritative analysts doubt that the secretary would get better deals than private insurers already get名词化 doubts 对应动词 doubt 的并列前句the author believes drug prices may be lowered through negotiation ↔We believe negotiation could work「We → the author」人称转换 +「negotiation could work → 谈判可降药价」语境补完
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
O 本段Congress needs to find the courage to allow Medicare to pay preferentially for treatments proven to be superior主张按疗效优劣付款，并未提及「药价谈判」这一独特机制；与陈述句的「谈判降药价」无对应。Congress needs to find the courage to allow Medicare to pay preferentially for treatments proven to be superior
questions.quote: Some authoritative analysts doubt that the secretary would get better deals than private insurers already get. We believe negotiation could work.

questions.prompt: Fair competition might create a strong incentive for insurers to charge less.
questions.explanation:
**答案** K 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
公平竞争可能会为保险公司降低收费创造强大的激励。
**锚点** 「公平竞争催生保险公司降价激励」机制锚点
**定位** 为打入数以百万计的新客户，保险公司将有强烈动机降价，办法可能是接受更薄的利润率或向提供方索要更好的条件。
**改写** a strong incentive for insurers to charge less ↔insurers would have a strong incentive to lower their prices「strong incentive」原样 +「charge less」与「lower their prices」同义Fair competition ↔health insurance exchanges on which small businesses and individuals could choose from an array of private plans and possibly a public option. All the plans would have to provide standard benefit packages that would be easy to compare抽象概念「公平竞争」对应具体制度「交易所 + 标准化 + 可选」
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
L 本段it might not save much money给出反向结论；且全段讨论的是「公共计划本身能不能省钱」，而非「公平竞争催生私营保险公司降价激励」这一机制；与陈述句的正向机制不符。The final legislation might throw a public plan into the competition, but thanks to the fierce opposition of the insurance industry and Republican critics, it might not save much money
questions.quote: To get access to millions of new customers, insurers would have a strong incentive to lower their prices, perhaps by accepting slimmer profit margins or demanding better deals from providers.

passage.label: A

sentences.text: It turns out today's teenagers aren't so scary after all.
Results of USA WEEKEND's Teens & Parents survey reveal a generation of young people who get along well with their parents and approve of the way they're being raised.
They think of their parents with affection and respect.
They speak with Mom or Dad when they have a problem.
Most feel that their parents understand them, and they believe their family is the No. 1 priority in their parents' lives.
Many even think their parents are cool!
Although more than a third have an object in their rooms they would like to keep secret from their parents, rarely is it anything more alarming than a diary or off-color(低俗的) book or CD.

passage.translation: 事实证明,如今的青少年并没有那么可怕。USA WEEKEND的"青少年与父母"调查结果显示,这一代年轻人与父母相处融洽,并认可自己的成长方式。他们怀着喜爱和尊重之情看待父母。遇到问题时,他们会与母亲或父亲交谈。大多数人觉得父母理解自己,并且相信家庭是父母生活中的第一要务。许多人甚至认为自己的父母很酷!虽然超过三分之一的青少年房间里有不想让父母知道的物品,但很少有比日记或低俗书籍、CD更令人担忧的东西。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: Such results may seem surprising against the background of shocking incidents that color the way the mass media portray the young.

In October 2000, the same month the survey was taken, the Washington-based Center for Media and Public Affairs wrote in its publication Media Monitor that, in a recent month of TV news coverage of American youth, just 2% of teens were shown at home, and just 1% were portrayed in a work setting.
In contrast, the criminal justice system accounted for nearly one out of every five visual backgrounds.
No wonder parents worry their own kids might spin out of control once they hit the turbulent waters of adolescence.

passage.translation: 在大众传媒描绘年轻人的那些骇人事件的背景下,这样的结果似乎令人惊讶。2000年10月,也就是调查进行的同一个月,总部位于华盛顿的媒体与公共事务中心在其出版物《媒体观察》中写道,在最近一个月关于美国青少年的电视新闻报道中,只有2%的青少年被展示在家中,只有1%被描绘在工作场景中。相比之下,刑事司法系统占据了近五分之一的视觉背景。难怪父母担心自己的孩子一旦进入动荡的青春期就会失控。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: The overall facts ought to reassure us.
The survey shows us that today's teens are affectionate, sensible and far happier than the angry and tortured souls that have been painted for us by stereotypes.
From other sources, we also know teenage crime, drug abuse and premarital sex are in general decline.
We, of course, need to pay attention to youngsters who are filled with discontent and hostility, but we should not allow these extreme cases to distort our view of most young people.

passage.translation: 总体事实应该让我们安心。调查向我们表明,如今的青少年充满感情、通情达理,并且比刻板印象为我们描绘的那些愤怒和痛苦的灵魂要快乐得多。从其他来源我们也了解到,青少年犯罪、吸毒和婚前性行为总体上呈下降趋势。当然,我们需要关注那些充满不满和敌意的年轻人,但我们不应该让这些极端案例扭曲我们对大多数年轻人的看法。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: My own research at the Stanford Center on Adolescence uses in-depth interviews with small samples of youngsters rather than large-scale surveys.
Still, in my studies and others I have read, I find the same patterns as in USA WEEKEND's survey.

Today's teenagers admire their parents and welcome parental guidance about important matters such as career choice—though certainly not Mom and Dad's advice on matters of personal taste, such as music or fashion.
When we ask teens to choose a hero, they usually select an older family member rather than a remote public figure.
Most teens say they enjoy the company of both parents and friends.

passage.translation: 我自己在斯坦福大学青少年研究中心的研究采用对小样本年轻人的深度访谈,而非大规模调查。尽管如此,在我的研究和我读过的其他研究中,我发现了与USA WEEKEND调查相同的模式。如今的青少年钦佩父母,并欢迎父母在职业选择等重要事项上的指导——尽管在音乐或时尚等个人品味方面,他们肯定不会接受父母的建议。当我们让青少年选择一位英雄时,他们通常会选择年长的家庭成员,而非遥远的公众人物。大多数青少年表示,他们既喜欢与父母相处,也喜欢与朋友相处。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Contrary to some stereotypes, most adolescents believe they must be tolerant of differences among individuals (though they do not always find this easy in the cliquish(拉帮结派的) environment of high school).
Many of them volunteer for community service with disadvantaged people.
One prevalent quality we have found in teens' statements about themselves, their friends and their families is a strikingly positive emotional tone.
By and large, these are very nice kids, and as the band The Who used to sing, "The kids are alright."

passage.translation: 与某些刻板印象相反,大多数青少年认为他们必须容忍个体之间的差异(尽管在拉帮结派的高中环境中,他们并不总能轻易做到这一点)。他们中的许多人为弱势群体提供社区服务志愿工作。我们在青少年关于自己、朋友和家庭的陈述中发现的一个普遍特质是显著积极的情感基调。总的来说,这些都是非常好的孩子,正如The Who乐队曾经唱的那样,"孩子们很好"。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: How much is today's spirit of harmony a change from our more turbulent past?
A mere generation ago, parent-child relations were described as "the generation gap".
Yet even then reports of widespread youth rebellion were overdone: Most kids in the '60s and '70s shared their parents' basic values.
Still, it is true that American families are growing closer at the dawn of this new millennium(千年).
Perhaps there is less to fight about, with the country in a period of tranquility and the dangers of drug abuse and other unwholesome behavior well known.
Perhaps in the face of impersonal and intimidating globalization, a young person's family feels more like a friendly haven than an oppressive trap.
And perhaps parents are acting more like parents than in the recent past.

Within just the past five years, I have noticed parents returning to a belief that teenagers need the guidance of elders rather than the liberal, "anything goes" mode of child-rearing that became popular in the second half of the 20th century.

passage.translation: 今天的和谐氛围与我们更动荡的过去相比有多大变化?仅仅一代人之前,亲子关系还被描述为"代沟"。然而即使在那时,关于大范围青年叛逆的报道也被夸大了:20世纪60年代和70年代的大多数孩子与父母有着基本相同的价值观。不过,美国家庭确实在这个新千年的开端变得更加亲密。也许在国家处于平静时期、吸毒和其他不良行为的危险广为人知的情况下,可争吵的事情少了。也许面对冷漠和令人生畏的全球化,年轻人的家庭感觉更像是一个友好的避风港,而非压迫性的陷阱。也许父母比最近的过去更像父母了。就在过去五年里,我注意到父母们重新相信青少年需要长辈的指导,而非20世纪下半叶流行的那种自由放任的"随便怎样都行"的育儿模式。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: But missing from all these data is the sense that today's young care very much about their country, about the broader civic and political environment, or about the future of their society.

They seem to be turning inward-generally in a pro-social manner, certainly with positive benefits for intimate relationships, but too often at the expense of a connection with the present and future world beyond, including the society they will one day inherit.

passage.translation: 但所有这些数据中缺失的是,如今的年轻人非常关心自己的国家、更广泛的公民和政治环境,或者社会未来的感觉。他们似乎在转向内心——总体上以亲社会的方式,当然对亲密关系有积极益处,但往往以牺牲与当下和未来世界(包括他们有朝一日将继承的社会)的联系为代价。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Recently, we examined more than 400 essays on the "laws of life" that teens from two communities had written as part of an educational program initiated by the John Templeton Foundation in Radnor, Pa.
In those essays, and in follow-up interviews with a few of the teenagers, we found lots of insight, positive feeling and inspirational thinking.
But we also found little interest in civic life beyond the tight circles of their family and immediate friends.

passage.translation: 最近,我们审查了来自两个社区的青少年撰写的400多篇关于"生活法则"的文章,这些文章是位于宾夕法尼亚州Radnor的John Templeton基金会发起的一项教育项目的一部分。在那些文章以及对部分青少年的后续访谈中,我们发现了许多洞察力、积极情感和鼓舞人心的思考。但我们也发现,他们对家庭和亲密朋友小圈子之外的公民生活兴趣寡淡。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: For example, only one boy said he would like to be president when he grows up.
When I was in high school, dozens in my class alone would have answered differently.

In fact, other recent studies have found there has never been a time in American history when so small a proportion of young people have sought or accepted leadership roles in local civic organizations.

It is also troubling that voting rates among our youngest eligible voters—18- to 24-year-olds—are way down: Little more than one in four now go to the polls, even in national elections, compared with almost twice that many when 18-year-olds were first given the vote.

passage.translation: 例如,只有一个男孩说他长大后想当总统。我上高中时,仅我们班就有几十人会给出不同的答案。事实上,其他最近的研究发现,美国历史上从未有过如此小比例的年轻人在地方公民组织中寻求或接受领导职位。同样令人担忧的是,我们最年轻的合格选民——18至24岁的人——的投票率大幅下降:即使在全国选举中,现在也只有略高于四分之一的人去投票,而当18岁的人首次获得投票权时,这一比例几乎是现在的两倍。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: In our interviews, many students viewed politics with suspicion and distaste.
"Most politicians are kind of crooked(不诚实的)," one student declared.
Another, discussing national politics, said, "I feel like one person can't do that much, and I get the impression most people don't think a group of people can do that much."

Asked what they would like to change in the world, the students mentioned only personal concerns such as slowing down the pace of life, gaining good friends, becoming more spiritual, becoming either more materially successful or less materially oriented (depending on the student's values), and being more respectful of the Earth, animals and other people.
One boy said, "I'd rather be concentrating on artistic efforts than saving the world or something."

passage.translation: 在我们的访谈中,许多学生以怀疑和厌恶的态度看待政治。"大多数政客都有点不诚实,"一名学生声称。另一名学生在讨论国家政治时说,"我觉得一个人做不了多少事,而且我觉得大多数人认为一群人也做不了多少事。"当被问到他们想改变世界的什么时,学生们只提到了个人关切,如放慢生活节奏、获得好朋友、变得更有灵性、在物质上更成功或更不注重物质(取决于学生的价值观),以及更尊重地球、动物和他人。一个男孩说,"我宁愿专注于艺术创作,也不愿拯救世界或什么的。"

passage.label: K

sentences.text: It is fine and healthy for teens to cultivate their personal interests, and it is good news when young people enjoy harmonious relations with their family and friends.
But there is also a place in a young life for noble purposes that include a dedication to the broader society, a love of country and an aspiration to make their own leadership contributions.

passage.translation: 青少年培养个人兴趣是好事,也是健康的,年轻人与家人和朋友享有和谐关系也是好消息。但年轻人的生活中也应该有崇高的目标,包括对更广泛社会的奉献、对国家的热爱以及做出自己领导贡献的抱负。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: In the past, the young have eagerly participated in national service and civic affairs, often with lots of energy and idealism.
If this is not happening today, we should ask why.
Our society needs the full participation of its younger citizens if it is to continue to thrive.
We know the promise is there—this is a well-grounded, talented, warm-hearted group of youngsters.
We have everything to gain by encouraging them to explore the world beyond their immediate experience and to prepare themselves for their turn at shaping that world.

passage.translation: 过去,年轻人热衷于参与国家服务和公民事务,往往充满活力和理想主义。如果今天没有发生这种情况,我们应该问为什么。我们的社会需要年轻公民的充分参与才能继续繁荣。我们知道潜力是存在的——这是一群基础扎实、才华横溢、热心肠的年轻人。我们鼓励他们探索眼前经验之外的世界,并为塑造那个世界的轮次做好准备,这样做我们将获益良多。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: Not many young people eligible for voting are interested in local or national elections these days.
questions.explanation:
**答案** I 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
如今没有多少有投票资格的年轻人对地方或全国选举感兴趣。
**锚点** 可投票年轻人 + 选举
**定位** 同样令人不安的是，我们最年轻的有投票资格者——18 到 24 岁——的投票率严重下滑：哪怕在全国大选中，现在去投票的也只比四分之一多一点，约为 18 岁刚获选举权时的一半。
**改写** Not many young people eligible for voting ↔our youngest eligible voters—18- to 24-year-olds—are way down数量极少 ↔ 投票率严重下滑are interested in local or national elections ↔ go to the polls, even in national elections感兴趣 ↔ 去投票 的行为化改写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
J J 段讲学生 viewed politics with suspicion and distaste，属于态度描写；题干要的是 选举参与度低 的事实数据，与 J 段不对应。Most politicians are kind of crooked(不诚实的)
questions.quote: It is also troubling that voting rates among our youngest eligible voters—18- to 24-year-olds—are way down: Little more than one in four now go to the polls, even in national elections, compared with almost twice that many when 18-year-olds were first given the vote.

questions.prompt: Parents are concerned that their children may get involved in criminal offences once they reach their teens.
questions.explanation:
**答案** B 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
父母担心他们的孩子一旦进入青少年时期可能会卷入刑事犯罪。
**锚点** 父母担心孩子犯罪
**定位** 难怪父母会担心自家孩子一旦进入波涛汹涌的青春期就会失控。
**改写** Parents are concerned ↔ parents worry concerned ↔ worry 同义词替换their children may get involved in criminal offences ↔ their own kids might spin out of control犯罪 ↔ 失控 的上下位改写once they reach their teens ↔ once they hit the turbulent waters of adolescence进入青春期 ↔ 进入波涛汹涌的青春期
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
C C 段说 teenage crime, drug abuse and premarital sex are in general decline，落点是 趋势安抚，与题干 父母担心 正好相反。teenage crime, drug abuse and premarital sex are in general decline
questions.quote: No wonder parents worry their own kids might spin out of control once they hit the turbulent waters of adolescence.

questions.prompt: Even during the turbulent years of last century, youth rebellion was often exaggerated in the media.
questions.explanation:
**答案** F 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
即使在上个世纪的动荡岁月里,青年叛逆也常常被媒体夸大。
**锚点** 上世纪青年叛逆被夸大
**定位** 可即便在那时候，关于青年大规模叛逆的报道也是被过度渲染的：60、70 年代的大多数孩子其实认同父母的基本价值观。
**改写** Even during the turbulent years of last century ↔ Most kids in the '60s and '70s上世纪动荡岁月 ↔ 60、70 年代youth rebellion ↔ widespread youth rebellion原样复现often exaggerated in the media ↔ reports of widespread youth rebellion were overdone exaggerated ↔ overdone + reports ↔ in the media
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段聚焦 In October 2000 当下的媒体呈现，与题干所问的 上世纪叛逆是否被夸大 时段错位。in a recent month of TV news coverage of American youth
questions.quote: Yet even then reports of widespread youth rebellion were overdone: Most kids in the '60s and'70s shared their parents' basic values.

questions.prompt: Teenagers of today often turn to their parents for advice on such important matters as career choice.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
当今的青少年在职业选择等重要事项上常常向父母寻求建议。
**锚点** 在择业等大事上找父母
**定位** 今天的青少年钦佩父母，并欢迎父母在诸如择业之类重要事情上的指导——当然不是音乐、时尚等个人品味方面的意见。
**改写** turn to their parents for advice ↔ welcome parental guidance向父母求教 ↔ 欢迎父母指导on such important matters as career choice ↔ important matters such as career choice such ... as 与 such as 的近乎逐字重合
questions.quote: Today's teenagers admire their parents and welcome parental guidance about important matters such as career choice—though certainly not Mom and Dad's advice on matters of personal taste, such as music or fashion.

questions.prompt: The incidence of teenage crime and misbehavior is decreasing nowadays.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
如今青少年犯罪和不当行为的发生率正在下降。
**锚点** 青少年犯罪与不良行为下降
**定位** 从其他来源我们也知道，青少年犯罪、吸毒和婚前性行为整体上在下降。
**改写** teenage crime and misbehavior ↔ teenage crime, drug abuse and premarital sex misbehavior 概括 drug abuse 与 premarital sex is decreasing nowadays ↔ are in general decline在下降 的两种表达
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段说 the criminal justice system accounted for nearly one out of every five visual backgrounds，是统计电视新闻画面，与 青少年实际犯罪率下降 不是同一回事。the criminal justice system accounted for nearly one out of every five visual backgrounds
questions.quote: From other sources, we also know teenage crime, drug abuse and premarital sex are in general decline.

questions.prompt: Young people should have lofty ideals in life and strive to be leaders.
questions.explanation:
**答案** K 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
年轻人应该有崇高的人生理想并努力成为领导者。
**锚点** 崇高理想 + 立志为领袖
**定位** 但年轻人的生活里也应该有崇高的目标——包括对更广阔社会的奉献、对国家的热爱，以及做出自身领导贡献的志向。
**改写** lofty ideals in life ↔ noble purposes lofty ↔ noble 同义词替换strive to be leaders ↔ an aspiration to make their own leadership contributions动词短语 ↔ 名词化短语
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
L L 段强调 Our society needs the full participation of its younger citizens，落脚是参与社会、塑造未来；题干 strive to be leaders 的直接出处仍在 K 段。Our society needs the full participation of its younger citizens if it is to continue to thrive
questions.quote: But there is also a place in a young life for noble purposes that include a dedication to the broader society, a love of country and an aspiration to make their own leadership contributions.

questions.prompt: Some young people like to keep something to themselves and don't want their parents to know about it.
questions.explanation:
**答案** A 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
有些年轻人喜欢对自己保留一些事情,不想让父母知道。
**锚点** 私藏不让父母知道的东西
**定位** 尽管超过三分之一的青少年房间里有件不愿让父母知道的东西，但很少比一本日记、一本低俗的书或 CD 更可怕。
**改写** Some young people like to keep something to themselves ↔more than a third have an object in their rooms they would like to keep secret持有私物 = 留东西给自己don't want their parents to know about it ↔ keep secret from their parents对父母保密 ↔ 不想让父母知道
