groups.content:
Let's say you love roller-skating. Just the thought of {{26}} on your roller-skates brings a smile to your face. You also know that roller-skating is excellent exercise. You have a {{27}} attitude toward it.

This description of roller-skating {{28}} the three components of an attitude: affect, cognition, and behavior. You love the activity; it's great fun. These feelings {{29}} the affective or emotional component; they are an important ingredient in attitudes. The knowledge we have about the object constitutes the cognitive component of an attitude. You understand the health {{30}} that the activity can bring. Finally, attitudes have a behavioral component. Our attitudes {{31}} us to go outside to enjoy roller-skating.

Now, we don't want to leave you with the {{32}} that these three components always work together {{33}} . They don't; sometimes they clash. For example, let's say you love pizza (affective component); however, you have high cholesterol and understand (knowledge component) that eating pizza may be bad for your health. Which behavior will your attitude result in, eating pizza or {{34}} it? The answer depends on which component happens to be stronger. If you are walking past a pizza restaurant at lunchtime, your emotions and feelings probably will be stronger than your knowledge that pizza may not be the best food for your health. In that instance, you have pizza for lunch. If you are at home trying to decide where to go for dinner, however, the knowledge component may {{35}} , and you decide to go where you can eat a healthier meal.

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) strapping 动词
**词性槽** 介词 of 后接动名词
**依据** strap on 穿上（旱冰鞋）strap on one's roller-skates 指'系紧、穿上旱冰鞋'，与 on your roller-skates 和'一想到就微笑'的语境吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) avoiding 避免，与'微笑'矛盾avoiding on your roller-skates 不通，且'避免'是消极义，与 brings a smile 矛盾。
G) inquiring 询问，语义完全不通inquiring 是'询问'，与穿旱冰鞋毫无关系。

questions.explanation:
**答案** I) positive 形容词
**词性槽** a 与名词 attitude 之间填形容词
**依据** positive attitude 积极态度上文说喜欢轮滑、它是很好的运动，对它的态度自然是 positive，positive attitude 也是高频搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) inquiring 好问的，对象不符inquiring attitude 是'爱探究的态度'，与'喜爱某项运动'的语境不符。
O) typical 典型的，语义偏离typical attitude 是'典型态度'，文中强调喜爱而非'典型'。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) illustrates 动词
**词性槽** 单数主语缺三单谓语，后接宾语
**依据** 说明、体现三种成分illustrate 意为'说明、例证'，'这段对轮滑的描述说明了态度的三种成分'与下文逐一介绍三成分吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) improves 改善，与'说明'语义不符improves the three components 是'改善三种成分'，文中并非改善、而是举例说明。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— improves 冒充 illustrates。improves 同是三单动词，但'改善成分'偏离'举例说明三成分'的原意。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) highlight 动词
**词性槽** 复数主语缺原形谓语，后接宾语
**依据** 凸显情感成分highlight the affective component 意为'凸显情感成分'，'这些喜爱的感受凸显了态度的情感成分'语义贴切。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
J) prevail 不及物，不能接宾语prevail 后不能直接跟 the component 作宾语，结构不成立。

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) benefits 名词
**词性槽** the+名词修饰+空+that，缺中心名词
**依据** health benefits 固定搭配health benefits 是高频搭配，指活动'能带来的健康益处'，与 the activity can bring 完全吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) highlight 亮点，不与 health 搭配highlight 作名词是'最精彩处'，没有 health highlight 的说法。
E) impression 印象，对象不符impression 是人对事物的主观印象，不是活动'带来'的东西。
M) specifications 规格参数，语义不搭specifications 指规格/参数，与健康无关。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) prompt 动词
**词性槽** 复数主语缺谓语，后接 us to do
**依据** prompt sb to do 促使某人做prompt us to go outside 意为'促使我们外出'，正是态度的'行为成分'在起作用。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) highlight 突出，不接 sb to do highlight 是'强调某事物'，不能说 highlight us to go。
J) prevail 不及物，不能带宾语prevail 通常不及物，后面不能直接接 us to go。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) impression 名词
**词性槽** the+空+that 同位语从句，缺名词
**依据** leave sb with the impression that leave you with the impression that… 是固定表达'给你留下…的印象'，impression 能接that 同位语从句。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) specifications 规格说明，搭配语义双不符specifications 是'规格参数'，既不与 leave…with 搭配，也不能引出'三种成分总是协同'这类印象。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) perfectly 副词
**词性槽** 修饰 work together 的副词
**依据** 完美地配合下一句 They don't; sometimes they clash 是转折，说明上句假设的是'三者总是完美协同'，故用 perfectly。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
K) primarily 主要地，与转折不呼应primarily 是'主要地'，'主要地一起作用'与下文'其实会冲突'的反差不自然，只有 perfectly 才托得出转折。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 K) —— primarily 冒充 perfectly。两者都是副词、都能接在 work together 后，但只有 perfectly 能与下文'其实会冲突'形成反差。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) avoiding 动词
**词性槽** 与 eating 并列的动名词
**依据** eating 与 avoiding 对举句意是'吃 pizza 还是不吃（避免）它'，avoiding it 与 eating pizza 正好相对。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) inquiring 询问，与吃/不吃无关inquiring it 不通，inquire 是'询问'，与'吃或避免'的对立无关。

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) prevail 动词
**词性槽** 情态动词 may 后接原形
**依据** 知识成分占上风prevail 意为'占上风、占主导'，'此时知识成分可能占上风，于是选更健康的一餐'语义连贯。

title: What can be done about mass unemployment?…

sentences.text: What can be done about mass unemployment?
All the wise heads agree: there're no quick or easy answers.
There's work to be done, but workers aren't ready to do it—they're in the wrong places, or they have the wrong skills.
"Our problems are structural," and will take many years to solve.

passage.translation: 对于大规模失业能做些什么?所有明智的头脑都一致认为:没有快速或简单的答案。有工作要做,但工人们还没有准备好去做——他们在错误的地方,或者他们拥有错误的技能。"我们的问题是结构性的",需要多年时间才能解决。

sentences.text: But don't bother asking for evidence that justifies this bleak view.
There isn't any.
On the contrary, all the facts suggest that high unemployment in America is the result of inadequate demand.
Saying that there're no easy answers sounds wise, but it's actually foolish: our unemployment crisis could be cured very quickly if we had the intellectual clarity and political will to act.
In other words, structural unemployment is a fake problem, which mainly serves as an excuse for not pursuing real solutions.

passage.translation: 但不要费心寻找证据来证明这种悲观的观点是正确的。根本没有任何证据。相反,所有事实都表明美国的高失业率是需求不足的结果。说没有简单的答案听起来很明智,但实际上很愚蠢:如果我们有智识上的清晰认识和政治意愿去行动,我们的失业危机可以很快得到解决。换句话说,结构性失业是一个虚假的问题,主要用作不追求真正解决方案的借口。

sentences.text: The fact is job openings have plunged in every major sector, while the number of workers forced into part-time employment in almost all industries has soared.
Unemployment has surged in every major occupational category.
Only three states, with a combined population not much larger than that of Brooklyn, have unemployment rates below 5%.
So the evidence contradicts the claim that we're mainly suffering from structural unemployment.
Why, then, has this claim become so popular?

passage.translation: 事实是,每个主要部门的职位空缺都急剧下降,而几乎所有行业中被迫从事兼职工作的工人数量都在飙升。每个主要职业类别的失业率都在激增。只有三个州的失业率低于5%,这些州的总人口加起来也不比布鲁克林大多少。因此,证据与我们主要遭受结构性失业的说法相矛盾。那么,为什么这一说法变得如此流行?

sentences.text: Part of the answer is that this is what always happens during periods of high unemployment—in part because experts and analysts believe that declaring the problem deeply rooted, with no easy answers, makes them sound serious.

passage.translation: 部分答案是,在高失业率时期总是会发生这种情况——部分原因是专家和分析师们相信,宣称问题根深蒂固、没有简单的答案,会让他们听起来很严肃。

sentences.text: I've been looking at what self-proclaimed experts were saying about unemployment during the Great Depression; it was almost identical to what Very Serious People are saying now.
Unemployment cannot be brought down rapidly, declared one 1935 analysis, because the workforce is "unadaptable and untrained.
It cannot respond to the opportunities which industry may offer."
A few years later, a large defense buildup finally provided a fiscal stimulus adequate to the economy's needs—and suddenly industry was eager to employ those "unadaptable and untrained" workers.

passage.translation: 我一直在查看自称专家的人在大萧条期间对失业问题的看法;这与非常严肃的人士现在所说的几乎一模一样。1935年的一项分析宣称,失业率无法迅速降低,因为劳动力"不适应且未经培训。它无法对工业可能提供的机会做出回应。"几年后,一次大规模的国防建设终于提供了经济所需的充分财政刺激——突然之间,工业界急于雇用那些"不适应且未经培训"的工人。

sentences.text: But now, as then, powerful forces are ideologically opposed to the whole idea of government action on a sufficient scale to jump-start the economy.

And that, fundamentally, is why claims that we face huge structural problems have been multiplying: they offer a reason to do nothing about the mass unemployment that is crippling our economy and our society.

passage.translation: 但现在,就像当时一样,强大的力量在意识形态上反对政府采取足够规模行动来启动经济的整个想法。从根本上说,这就是为什么声称我们面临巨大结构性问题的说法不断增多的原因:它们提供了一个理由,让我们对正在削弱我们经济和社会的大规模失业无所作为。

sentences.text: So what you need to know is that there's no evidence whatsoever to back these claims.
We aren't suffering from a shortage of needed skills; we're suffering from a lack of policy resolve.
As I said, structural unemployment isn't a real problem, it's an excuse—a reason not to act on America's problems at a time when action is desperately needed.

passage.translation: 所以你需要知道的是,没有任何证据可以支持这些说法。我们不是遭受所需技能短缺的困扰;我们遭受的是缺乏政策决心的困扰。正如我所说,结构性失业不是一个真正的问题,它是一个借口——一个在迫切需要行动的时候不对美国的问题采取行动的理由。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does the author think is the root cause of mass unemployment in America?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者认为美国大规模失业的根本原因是什么?
A) 企业管理不善。
B) 需求不足。
C) 技术进步。
D) 工人适应缓慢。
**判型** What does the author think is the root cause 问的是作者明示的判断，原文必有一句直白表态，属于细节题而非推断题。
**拆句** What does the author think is the root cause of mass unemployment in America?主干是 What does the author think，宾语从句省略 that，从句主干 the root cause of mass unemployment in America is what；难点仅在 think 后接的是嵌套疑问句，无陷阱。
**定位** 恰恰相反，所有事实都表明，美国的高失业率是需求不足造成的。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Corporate mismanagement."企业管理失当"在原文从未出现，纯属考生常识联想。
B) ✓ 正确inadequate demand ↔ Insufficient demand.预判"需求不够"与 Insufficient demand. 字面一致，无需扩展即可锁定。
C) 无中生有Technological advances. 是经济类话题常见的"标准嫌疑人"，但本文未提任何技术变革，属无中生有。
D) 与原文相反Workers' slow adaptation. 复述的是 they're in the wrong places, or they have the wrong skills 这一专家立场，而作者在 structural unemployment is a fake problem已明确否定。
questions.quote: On the contrary, all the facts suggest that high unemployment in America is the result of inadequate demand.

options.text: Corporate mismanagement.
Insufficient demand.
Technological advances.
Workers' slow adaptation.

questions.prompt: What does the author think of the experts' claim concerning unemployment?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （态度题）
**题目译文**
作者如何看待专家关于失业的说法?
A) 不言自明的。
B) 发人深省的。
C) 不理性的。
D) 毫无根据的。
**判型** What does the author think of the experts' claim 中 think of 直接问态度/评价，选项Self-evident.、Groundless. 都是评价性形容词，进一步坐实态度题。
**拆句** What does the author think of the experts' claim concerning unemployment? 主干What does the author think of …；concerning unemployment 作 claim 的后置修饰，等于 about unemployment；句式平铺，无陷阱。
**定位** 换句话说，结构性失业是个伪问题，它的主要作用不过是为"不去追求真正解决方案"提供借口。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反Self-evident.（不言自明、显而易见）暗示作者认同专家说法，与 structural unemployment is a fake problem 完全对立。
B) 与原文相反Thought-provoking. 意为"发人深思"，隐含一定肯定，与作者的全面否定态度不符。
C) 偷换概念Irrational."非理性"指向"逻辑错乱、无道理"，作者却始终在指责对方 there's no evidence whatsoever"无证据"，攻击点错位，属偷换概念。
D) ✓ 正确a fake problem ↔ Groundless. there's no evidence whatsoever to back these claims ↔ Groundless.全文极性词都指向"无事实支撑"，Groundless. 恰是这一极性的形容词概括。
questions.quote: In other words, structural unemployment is a fake problem, which mainly serves as an excuse for not pursuing real solutions.

options.text: Self-evident.
Thought-provoking.
Irrational.
Groundless.

questions.prompt: What does the author say helped bring down unemployment during the Great Depression?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者认为大萧条期间什么因素帮助降低了失业率?
A) 蓬勃发展的国防工业。
B) 智者们的福利方案。
C) 全国范围的工人培训。
D) 产业的彻底重组。
**判型** What does the author say helped bring down unemployment during the Great Depression 限定在大萧条这一时段问"是什么帮忙降的失业"，需要的就是原文那一句的客观转述。
**拆句** What does the author say helped bring down unemployment during the Great Depression? What 既是宾语从句主语又是 helped 的逻辑主语，相当于 What helped bring down unemployment（the author says）；during 短语作时间状语，无陷阱。
**定位** 几年后，一次大规模的国防扩张终于带来了与经济需要相称的财政刺激——产业界突然就乐于雇用那些"难以适应、未受训练"的工人了。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确a large defense buildup ↔ The booming defense industry.预判"国防扩张刺激经济"与 The booming defense industry. 字面对齐，逻辑一步即到。
B) 无中生有The wise heads' benefit package. 把 All the wise heads agree 的讽刺称呼当成具体人物，且"福利方案"原文从未出现，属无中生有。
C) 与原文相反Nationwide training of workers. 与作者立场相反——作者强调 We aren't suffering from a shortage of needed skills，培训根本不是降失业的钥匙。
D) 无中生有Thorough restructuring of industries."产业的彻底重组"在原文中从未出现，且与作者"需求拉动"的诊断方向不符。
questions.quote: A few years later, a large defense buildup finally provided a fiscal stimulus adequate to the economy's needs—and suddenly industry was eager to employ those "unadaptable and untrained" workers.

options.text: The booming defense industry.
The wise heads' benefit package.
Nationwide training of workers.
Thorough restructuring of industries.

questions.prompt: What has caused claims of huge structural problems to multiply?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
是什么导致了关于巨大结构性问题的说法大量增加?
A) 对政府刺激措施的强烈反对。
B) 非常严肃人士试图削弱经济。
C) 从工业许多部门收集的证据。
D) 经济学家未能及时发现问题。
**判型** What has caused … 是直接问"是什么导致 X"的因果问句，原文几乎必然有一句"because/that is why"形式的明示因果，按细节题处理。
**拆句** What has caused claims of huge structural problems to multiply? 主干 What has caused X to do；现在完成时强调结果延续到现在，to multiply 是 cause 后的不定式宾补，无陷阱。
**定位** 但今天和当年一样，强势力量在意识形态上反对政府以足够规模采取行动来重启经济。从根本上说，这就是为何"我们面临巨大结构性问题"这类说法越来越多——它们为"不对正在摧垮经济和社会的大规模失业采取任何行动"提供了借口。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确powerful forces are ideologically opposed to the whole idea of government action ↔Powerful opposition to government's stimulus efforts. government action on a sufficient scale to jump-start the economy ↔government's stimulus efforts预判"强势力量反对政府出手"与 Powerful opposition to government's stimulus efforts. 字面同义，直接锁定。
B) 张冠李戴Very Serious People's attempt to cripple the economy. 把原文 mass unemployment that is crippling our economy 中"摧垮经济"的施动者从"失业"偷换为Very Serious People，且原文也没说他们"企图"摧垮经济。
C) 与原文相反Evidence gathered from many sectors of the industries. 与作者立场矛盾——P3 的全行业证据恰恰被作者用来推翻"结构性"说法，证据不会让"结构性说法"增多，而是反向打击。
D) 无中生有Economists' failure to detect the problems in time. 原文没有任何一句指控"经济学家未能及时发现"，作者批评的是"明知证据不足却仍鼓吹结构性"，性质完全不同。
questions.quote: But now, as then, powerful forces are ideologically opposed to the whole idea of government action on a sufficient scale to jump-start the economy. And that, fundamentally, is why claims that we face huge structural problems have been multiplying: they offer a reason to do nothing about the mass unemployment that is crippling our economy and our society.

options.text: Powerful opposition to government's stimulus efforts.
Very Serious People's attempt to cripple the economy.
Evidence gathered from many sectors of the industries.
Economists' failure to detect the problems in time.

questions.prompt: What is the author's purpose in writing the passage?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （主旨题）
**题目译文**
作者写这篇文章的目的是什么?
A) 证明专家对美国问题的分析。
B) 为结构性失业提供可行的解决方案。
C) 表明政府采取行动的迫切需要。
D) 提醒美国工人适应的紧迫性。
**判型** What is the author's purpose in writing the passage? 中 purpose in writing 是典型主旨题信号，正确项要能覆盖全文论证链而非某一段。
**拆句** What is the author's purpose in writing the passage? 主干 What is the purpose；in writing the passage 是介词短语作 purpose 的后置定语，等同于 of writing；无陷阱。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反To testify to the experts' analysis of America's problems."为专家分析作证"与作者立场完全相反——他全文都在反驳 structural unemployment is a fake problem。
B) 偷换概念To offer a feasible solution to the structural unemployment. 把作者眼中根本不存在的问题（fake problem）当作要解决的对象，且作者也没给出具体方案，属"以伪问题为前提"的偷换概念。
C) ✓ 正确action is desperately needed↔ To show the urgent need for the government to take action. powerful forces are ideologically opposed to the whole idea of government action↔for the government to take action预判"呼吁政府赶紧行动"与 To show the urgent need for the government to take action. 完全对齐，且 C 同时覆盖前 6 段的"破谬"和末段的"呼吁"。
D) 张冠李戴To alert American workers to the urgency for adaptation. 把呼吁对象从"政府"偷换成"工人"，且 adaptation 正是作者反对的说法（unadaptable and untrained 是被嘲讽的话术）。

options.text: To testify to the experts' analysis of America's problems.
To offer a feasible solution to the structural unemployment.
To show the urgent need for the government to take action.
To alert American workers to the urgency for adaptation.

title: Interactive television advertising, which allows viewers to use…

sentences.text: Interactive television advertising, which allows viewers to use their remote controls to click on advertisements, has been pushed for years.
Nearly a decade ago it was predicted that viewers of "Friends", a popular situation comedy, would soon be able to purchase a sweater like Jennifer Aniston's with a few taps on their remote control.
"It's been the year of interactive television advertising for the last ten or twelve years," says Colin Dixon of a digital-media consultancy.

passage.translation: 互动电视广告允许观众使用遥控器点击广告,这一技术已经被推广了多年。近十年前就有人预测,热门情景喜剧《老友记》的观众很快就能通过遥控器轻点几下购买到像Jennifer Aniston那样的毛衣。数字媒体咨询公司的Colin Dixon说:"在过去十到十二年里,每年都被称作互动电视广告年。"

sentences.text: So the news that Cablevision, an American cable company, was rolling out interactive advertisements to all its customers on October 6th was greeted with some skepticism.
During commercials, an overlay will appear at the bottom of the screen, prompting viewers to press a button to request a free sample or order a catalogue.
Cablevision hopes to allow customers to buy things with their remote controls early next year.

passage.translation: 因此,当美国有线电视公司Cablevision宣布将于10月6日向其全部客户推出互动广告时,这一消息受到了一些质疑。在广告播放期间,屏幕底部会出现一个覆盖层,提示观众按下按钮以索取免费样品或订购产品目录。Cablevision希望在明年初让客户能够用遥控器购物。

sentences.text: Television advertising could do with a boost.
Spending fell by 10% in the first half of the year.
The popularization of digital video recorders has caused advertisers to worry that their commercials will be skipped.
Some are turning to the Internet, which is cheaper and offers concrete measurements like click-through rates—especially important at a time when marketing budgets are tight.
With the launch of interactive advertising, "many of the dollars that went to the Internet will come back to the TV," says David Kline of Cablevision.
Or so the industry hopes.

passage.translation: 电视广告确实需要提振。今年上半年广告支出下降了10%。数字录像机的普及让广告商担心他们的广告会被跳过。一些广告商转向互联网,互联网成本更低,并能提供点击率等具体的衡量指标——这在营销预算紧张的时期尤为重要。Cablevision的David Kline表示,随着互动广告的推出,"许多流向互联网的资金将回流到电视"。至少业界是这样希望的。

sentences.text: In theory, interactive advertising can engage viewers in a way that 30-second spots do not.
Unilever recently ran an interactive campaign for its Axe deodorant(除臭剂), which kept viewers engaged for more than three minutes on average.

passage.translation: 从理论上讲,互动广告能以30秒广告无法做到的方式吸引观众。Unilever最近为其Axe除臭剂开展了一场互动营销活动,平均让观众参与了三分钟以上。

sentences.text: The amount spent on interactive advertising on television is still small.
Magna, an advertising agency, reckons it will be worth about $138 million this year.
That falls far short of the billions of dollars people once expected it to generate.
But DirecTV, Comcast and Time Warner Cable have all invested in it.
A new effort led by Canoe Ventures, a coalition of leading cable providers, aims to make interactive advertising available across America later this year.
BrightLine ITV, which designs and sells interactive ads, says interest has surged: it expects its revenues almost to triple this year.
BSkyB, Britain's biggest satellite-television service, already provides 9 million customers with interactive ads.

passage.translation: 目前在电视互动广告上的支出仍然很少。广告代理公司Magna估计今年这一数字约为1.38亿美元。这远远低于人们曾经预期它能产生的数十亿美元。但DirecTV、Comcast和Time Warner Cable都对此进行了投资。由主要有线电视供应商组成的联盟Canoe Ventures领导的一项新举措,旨在今年晚些时候让互动广告在全美范围内普及。设计和销售互动广告的BrightLine ITV表示,兴趣激增:预计其今年收入将增长近两倍。英国最大的卫星电视服务商BSkyB已经向900万客户提供互动广告。

sentences.text: Yet there are doubts whether people watching television, a "lean back" medium, crave interaction.
Click-through rates have been high so far (around 3-4%, compared with less than 0.3%online), but that may be a result of the novelty.
Interactive ads and viewers might not go well together.

passage.translation: 然而,人们怀疑观看电视这种"后仰"媒介的人是否渴望互动。到目前为止点击率一直很高(约为3-4%,而在线点击率不到0.3%),但这可能是新鲜感带来的结果。互动广告和观众可能无法很好地结合。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does Colin Dixon mean by saying "It's been the year of interactive television advertising for the last ten or twelve years" (Lines 4, Para. 1)?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （词义句意题）
**题目译文**
Colin Dixon说"过去十年或十二年里，每年都是互动电视广告年"(第1段第4行)是什么意思?
A) 互动电视广告将在10-12年后变得流行。
B) 互动电视广告在过去十年左右一直处于争论之中。
C) 互动电视广告在融入情景喜剧时是成功的。
D) 互动电视广告没有取得预期的效果。
**判型** 题干结构是 What does Colin Dixon mean by saying "..."，问的是某人说某句话是什么意思，本质是对一句原文的语义解读。
**拆句** 题干主干为 What does Colin Dixon mean by saying "..."，宾语从句问的是"说这句话意指什么"。by saying 是介词短语作方式状语，引号内整句是 saying 的宾语。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 交互式电视广告——让观众用遥控器点击广告——已被力推多年。差不多十年前就有预测说，《老友记》这部热门情景喜剧的观众很快就能用遥控器轻点几下，买到一件像 Jennifer Aniston 同款的毛衣。某数字媒体咨询机构的 Colin Dixon 说："过去十到十二年里，每一年都被说成是交互式电视广告之年。"
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反will become popular in 10-12 years 把原文的过去时 has been ... for the last ten or twelve years（过去十到十二年里）扭成未来 10-12 年才会流行，时间方向反了。
B) 无中生有under debate"被争论"在文中找不到依据，原文只说"被力推"和"被预测"，没有提及辩论或争议。
C) 与原文相反原文只是举 "Friends" 为预言中的例子，并未说交互广告"嵌入情景喜剧"就成功了；is successful 与原句的反讽完全相反。
D) ✓ 正确"It's been the year of interactive television advertising for the last ten or twelve years"↔has not achieved the anticipated results Nearly a decade ago it was predicted that viewers ... would soon be able to purchase↔the anticipated results预判中"喊了十几年没真兑现"的两个要素——"被预期"和"未达成"——分别对应 the anticipated results 与 has not achieved，因此 D 即为定位句的同义改写。
questions.quote: Interactive television advertising, which allows viewers to use their remote controls to click on advertisements, has been pushed for years. Nearly a decade ago it was predicted that viewers of "Friends", a popular situation comedy, would soon be able to purchase a sweater like Jennifer Aniston's with a few taps on their remote control. "It's been the year of interactive television advertising for the last ten or twelve years," says Colin Dixon of a digital-media consultancy.

options.text: Interactive television advertising will become popular in 10-12 years.
Interactive television advertising has been under debate for the last decade or so.
Interactive television advertising is successful when incorporated into situation comedies.
Interactive television advertising has not achieved the anticipated results.

questions.prompt: What is the public's response to Cablevision's planned interactive TV advertising program?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
公众对Cablevision计划推出的互动电视广告项目有何反应?
A) 相当积极。
B) 完全漠不关心。
C) 有些怀疑。
D) 颇为批判。
**判型** What is the public's response to Cablevision's planned interactive TV advertising program? 问的是一个明确事实——公众的反应，四个选项各对应一种态度词。
**拆句** 主干 What is the public's response，介词短语 to Cablevision's planned interactive TV advertising program 作 response 的修饰，限定反应对象。planned 是过去分词作前置定语，修饰 program。结构无陷阱。
**定位** 于是，美国有线电视公司 Cablevision 将于 10 月 6 日向所有客户推出交互广告这件事，遭到了一些怀疑。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反Pretty positive 与原文 skepticism 极性相反；原文是负面态度。
B) 与原文相反Totally indifferent 意为"完全漠不关心"，但原文明确有 skepticism 这一反应，绝非漠然。
C) ✓ 正确was greeted with some skepticism ↔ Somewhat doubtful预判中"怀疑但不强烈"两个特征——语义"怀疑"和程度"一些"——分别落到 doubtful 与Somewhat，故选 C。
D) 偷换概念Rather critical"相当批评"比原文 some skepticism"一些怀疑"程度重；some≠rather，skepticism 是"怀疑"不是"批评"。
questions.quote: So the news that Cablevision, an American cable company, was rolling out interactive advertisements to all its customers on October 6th was greeted with some skepticism.

options.text: Pretty positive.
Totally indifferent.
Somewhat doubtful.
Rather critical.

questions.prompt: What is the impact of the wide use of digital video recorders on TV advertising?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
数字录像机的广泛使用对电视广告有何影响?
A) 它使观众更容易接触到电视广告。
B) 它帮助广告商衡量点击率。
C) 它使电视广告处于极大的劣势。
D) 它使观众能够轻松查看促销商品。
**判型** What is the impact of the wide use of digital video recorders on TV advertising? 直接问"X 对 Y 的影响是什么"，是明确的事实查询。
**拆句** 主干 What is the impact；of 短语 of the wide use of digital video recorders 限定impact 的来源，on 短语 on TV advertising 限定影响对象。两层介词修饰，方向清晰：A影响 B，问 A 对 B 的作用。
**定位** 数字录像机的普及让广告商担心他们的广告会被跳过。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反easily accessible to viewers 是正向描述"更容易被观众接触到"，与原文广告被跳的负面后果完全相反。
B) 张冠李戴helps advertisers to measure the click-through rates 把段中介绍 the Internet, which is cheaper and offers concrete measurements like click-through rates 这件互联网的事，扣到 digital video recorders 头上。
C) ✓ 正确has caused advertisers to worry that their commercials will be skipped ↔placed TV advertising at a great disadvantage has caused ↔ has ... placed预判中"广告处境变差"与选项 placed TV advertising at a great disadvantage 表达完全一致，选 C。
D) 无中生有enables viewers to check the sales items with ease 在原文找不到对应：原文没有说DVR 让观众查看促销商品。
questions.quote: The popularization of digital video recorders has caused advertisers to worry that their commercials will be skipped.

options.text: It has made TV advertising easily accessible to viewers.
It helps advertisers to measure the click-through rates.
It has placed TV advertising at a great disadvantage.
It enables viewers to check the sales items with ease.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about Unilever's interactive campaign?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于Unilever的互动营销活动,我们了解到什么?
A) 它证明了电视广告的优势。
B) 它在吸引观众方面做得很好。
C) 它有助于吸引对公司的投资。
D) 它推动了电视广告行业的发展。
**判型** What do we learn about Unilever's interactive campaign? 是"关于这件事我们了解到什么"——回到原文该例证句直接读取。
**拆句** What do we learn about Unilever's interactive campaign? 主干 What do we learn，about 介词短语指明话题对象。Unilever's 是名词所有格，限定 campaign 的归属。结构无陷阱。
**定位** 联合利华最近为旗下 Axe 除臭剂做了一个交互广告活动，它平均让观众持续投入超过三分钟。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问proves the advantage of TV advertising 把话题从"Unilever 这次活动如何"扩大成"电视广告整体优势"；原句讨论的只是这一次具体的交互广告效果，不证明 TV 广告整体优势。
B) ✓ 正确kept viewers engaged for more than three minutes on average ↔done well in engaging the viewers for more than three minutes on average ↔ done well预判中"在吸引观众投入上效果好"与 done well in engaging the viewers 完全一致，选 B。
C) 无中生有helps attract investments in the company 谈"吸引对公司的投资"，原文只字未提投资。
D) 过度推断has boosted the TV advertising industry 把单次广告的效果扩大成"带动了整个电视广告行业"；原文只是单一例证，没有行业层面推断。
questions.quote: Unilever recently ran an interactive campaign for its Axe deodorant(除臭剂), which kept viewers engaged for more than three minutes on average.

options.text: It proves the advantage of TV advertising.
It has done well in engaging the viewers.
It helps attract investments in the company.
It has boosted the TV advertising industry.

questions.prompt: How does the author view the hitherto high click-through rates?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （态度题）
**题目译文**
作者如何看待迄今为止的高点击率?
A) 它们可能是由于新颖的广告方式。
B) 它们表明了互动广告的受欢迎程度。
C) 它们指向电视观众日益增长的好奇心。
D) 它们指明了媒体改革的未来方向。
**判型** How does the author view the hitherto high click-through rates? 是"作者如何看待X"，标准的态度评判题。
**拆句** How does the author view the hitherto high click-through rates? 主干 How does the author view X。hitherto（到目前为止）是副词修饰形容词 high，强调"迄今为止还高"的隐含时态张力——暗示作者可能不看好这个高数据的持续性。
**定位** 迄今点击通过率一直较高（约 3-4%，相比之下网上不到 0.3%），但这可能只是新鲜感造成的结果。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确but that may be a result of the novelty↔may be due to the novel way of advertising预判中"作者怀疑这只是新鲜感造成"两要素——情态 may 和原因 novelty——分别对应may be due to 与 the novel way of advertising，故选 A。
B) 过度推断signify the popularity of interactive advertising 把高点击率直接读成"交互广告流行"，但作者通篇态度是质疑：Interactive ads and viewers might not go well together。
C) 偷换概念point to the growing curiosity of TV viewers 把"新鲜感"偷换成"日益增长的好奇心"；原文只说新鲜，而且暗示"会过去"，并非"growing"。
D) 无中生有indicate the future direction of media reform 把高点击率说成"媒体改革的未来方向"，原文从未谈媒体改革。

title: Pursuing a career is an essential part of…

sentences.text: Pursuing a career is an essential part of adolescent development.
"The adolescent becomes an adult when he (26)____ a real job."
To cognitive researchers like Piaget, adulthood meant the beginning of an(27)____ .

passage.translation: 追求职业是青少年发展的重要组成部分。"当青少年承担起一份真正的工作时，他就成为了成年人。"对于像Piaget这样的认知研究者来说，成年意味着职业生涯的开始。

sentences.text: Piaget argued that once adolescents enter the world of work, their newly acquired ability to form hypotheses allows them to create representations that are too ideal.

The (28)____ of such ideals, without the tempering of the reality of a job or profession, rapidly leads adolescents to become (29)____ of the non-idealistic world and to press for reform in a characteristically adolescent way.
Piaget said: "True adaptation to society comes (30)____ when the adolescent reformer attempts to put his ideas to work."

passage.translation: Piaget认为，一旦青少年进入工作世界，他们新获得的形成假设的能力使他们能够创造过于理想化的表征。这种理想的存在，如果没有工作或职业的现实来调和，会迅速导致青少年对非理想化的世界变得不能容忍，并以典型的青少年方式要求改革。Piaget说："当青少年改革者试图将他的想法付诸实践时，对社会的真正适应就会自然而然地到来。"

sentences.text: Of course, youthful idealism is often courageous, and no one likes to give up dreams.
Perhaps, taken (31)____ out of context, Piaget's statement seems harsh.
What he was (32)____ , however, is the way reality can modify idealistic views.
Some people refer to such modification as maturity.
Piaget argued that attaining and accepting a vocation is one of the best ways to modify idealized views and to mature.

passage.translation: 当然，年轻人的理想主义往往是勇敢的，没有人愿意放弃梦想。也许，稍微脱离语境来看，Piaget的陈述似乎有些苛刻。然而，他所强调的是现实可以修正理想主义观点的方式。有些人将这种修正称为成熟。Piaget认为，获得并接受一份职业是修正理想化观点和走向成熟的最佳方式之一。

sentences.text: that attaining and accepting a vocation is one of the best ways to modify idealized views and to mature.
As careers and vocations become less available during times of (33)____ , adolescents may be especially hard hit.
Such difficult economic times may leave many adolescents (34)____ about their roles in society.
For this reason, community interventions and government job programs that offer summer and vacation work are not only economically (35)____ but also help to stimulate the adolescent's sense of worth.

passage.translation: 获得并接受一份职业是修正理想化观点和走向成熟的最佳方式之一。当经济衰退时期职业和工作变得不那么容易获得时，青少年可能会受到特别严重的打击。这样困难的经济时期可能会让许多青少年对他们在社会中的角色感到困惑。因此，提供暑期和假期工作的社区干预措施和政府就业项目不仅在经济上有益，而且有助于激发青少年的价值感。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
Pursuing a career is an essential part of adolescent development. "The adolescent becomes an adult when he {{26}} a real job." To cognitive researchers like Piaget, adulthood meant the beginning of an{{27}} .

Piaget argued that once adolescents enter the world of work, their newly acquired ability to form hypotheses allows them to create representations that are too ideal. The {{28}} of such ideals, without the tempering of the reality of a job or profession, rapidly leads adolescents to become {{29}} of the non-idealistic world and to press for reform in a characteristically adolescent way. Piaget said: "True adaptation to society comes {{30}} when the adolescent reformer attempts to put his ideas to work."

Of course, youthful idealism is often courageous, and no one likes to give up dreams. Perhaps, taken {{31}} out of context, Piaget's statement seems harsh. What he was {{32}} , however, is the way reality can modify idealistic views. Some people refer to such modification as maturity. Piaget argued that attaining and accepting a vocation is one of the best ways to modify idealized views and to mature.

that attaining and accepting a vocation is one of the best ways to modify idealized views and to mature. As careers and vocations become less available during times of {{33}} , adolescents may be especially hard hit. Such difficult economic times may leave many adolescents {{34}} about their roles in society. For this reason, community interventions and government job programs that offer summer and vacation work are not only economically {{35}} but also help to stimulate the adolescent's sense of worth.

options.text: automatically
incidentally
beneficial
intolerant
capturing
occupation
confused
promises
emphasizing
recession
entrance
slightly
excited
undertakes
existence

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) undertakes 动词
**词性槽** 主语 he 后缺第三人称单数谓语
**依据** "承担一份真正的工作"贴合"踏入成年"的定义The adolescent becomes an adult when he __(26)__ a real job. 给青少年走向成年下定义——开始"承担"一份真正的工作，undertake a job 是地道搭配，表示主动去做、担起责任，正契合"成年=能担当工作"的论点。

**答案** K) occupation 名词
**词性槽** 不定冠词 an 后名词位
**依据** 与上句"real job"同义复指上一句 The adolescent becomes an adult when he __(26)__ a real job. 给出"真正的工作"，紧接着皮亚杰把"成年"定义为 the beginning of an occupation，occupation 与 real job 形成同义复指，主题词"职业"一锤定音。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) entrance "入口"与"开始"语义冗余entrance 本身已含"进入"之意，与前面的 the beginning of 在语义上叠床架屋，"开始一个入口"逻辑别扭。
H) existence "生存"过于宏大，背离"职业"焦点existence 指"生存状态"，意涵宽泛；本段聚焦点是"a real job"，非"开始一种生存"——过于宏大反而偏题。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) existence 名词
**词性槽** 定冠词 The + ___ + of 名词位
**依据** "理想的存在/产生"对应皮亚杰"形成假设之后才出现理想"上一句 their newly acquired ability to form hypotheses allows them to create representations that are too ideal. 说青少年才有了构建过度理想化表征的能力，本句承接说"这些理想的 existence（产生/存在）若没有现实磨砺，就会让他们对非理想世界intolerant"——existence 表达"理想已经在心里存在/出现"这一状态，是承接 create representations 的最佳抽象名词。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) entrance "入口"无法搭 of such ideals entrance of such ideals 字面成"这些理想的入口"，意象不通；entrance 通常指物理或场景的进入处，与抽象"理想"无法搭配。

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) intolerant 形容词
**词性槽** become + ___ + of 形容词位
**依据** "理想 vs 现实"语境配 intolerant of前文说青少年理想化、缺少现实磨砺，紧接着 rapidly leads adolescents to become__(29)__ of the non-idealistic world and to press for reform in a characteristically adolescent way. 描述青少年迫切想改革——这是对"非理想世界"无法忍受的典型表现；intolerant of 正好搭配 of 介词，且语义对接"按青少年式做派激烈推动改革"。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) beneficial义为"有益的"，与下文"press for reform"语气反向beneficial 是褒义且通常搭 to 而非 of；说"对非理想世界有益"既不通搭配，也与紧随其后的"急于改革"语气拧反。
D) confused 义为"困惑的"，与"激进改革"语义不合困惑者会犹豫不决，而原文描述的是"激切推动改革"——情绪是义愤而非茫然；且 confused 多搭 by/about，不搭 of。
G) excited 义为"兴奋的"，搭配为 excited about/at excited 表对某事兴奋好奇，常搭 about/at，不与 of 搭配；语义上对非理想世界"兴奋"也讲不通。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) automatically 副词
**词性槽** 动词 comes 后缺状语
**依据** 对应"理想唯有付诸实践才自然而然达成适应"全句 True adaptation to society comes __(30)__ when the adolescent reformer attempts to put his ideas to work. 强调真正的社会适应不是凭空而来，而是在青少年把理想付诸实践时"自动"发生，automatically 正好表达这种条件触发、不待外力的自然发生关系。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
I) incidentally义为"顺便地"，与论点焦点冲突incidentally 表示话题之外的附带补充或偶然发生，本句要讲的是"适应"这件大事的实现机制，绝非顺带顺便，语义直接拧反。
N) slightly义为"轻微地"，搭不上"True adaptation" True adaptation 已用 True 强调彻底、真正的适应，再用 slightly 表示"轻微地达成"逻辑自相矛盾，语义不通。

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) slightly 副词
**词性槽** 过去分词 taken 前修饰位
**依据** "稍稍脱离语境"贴让步语气前句 Of course, youthful idealism is often courageous, and no one likes to give up dreams. 在为青少年辩护，作者紧接着用 Perhaps 缓和措辞，承认皮亚杰的话"如果稍微脱离语境"才显得严厉；slightly 与 Perhaps 协同营造出轻度让步的语气，正好替皮亚杰打圆场。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
I) incidentally义为"顺便地"，与 out of context 不搭incidentally 修饰整句作"顺便说一句"的话题转换语，不修饰程度，也无法说"顺便地脱离语境"，搭配根本不成立。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 I) —— incidentally 看似"-ly"就行，实则语义反。第 31 题Perhaps, taken __(31)__ out of context, Piaget's statement seems harsh. 若没注意到 Perhaps 的让步语气，很容易随手填 incidentally；防坑一句话——见到 Perhaps、to some extent 等让步标志，副词优先选 slightly 这种程度词，而非 incidentally 这种插话词。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) emphasizing 动词
**词性槽** was + ___ 进行时谓语
**依据** "皮亚杰要强调的是现实磨理想"对应 emphasize本段在为皮亚杰"开脱"——他原话听上去严厉，但 What he was __(32)__, however, is the way reality can modify idealistic views. 真正想强调（emphasize）的是"现实如何修正理想化观点"。emphasize sth. 直接以观点为宾语，是最常用的学术评述动词。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) capturing 义为"捕捉"，多用于具体形象或注意capture 常搭具体宾语（捕获敌人、捕捉瞬间、抓住注意）；说"皮亚杰在捕捉现实修正理想的方式"语义别扭，且不是"反驳听上去严厉"这层语境惯用动词。

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) recession 名词
**词性槽** 介词 of 后名词位
**依据** 对接"职业减少 + 经济艰难"双重语境本句给出因果链 As careers and vocations become less available during times of__(33)__, adolescents may be especially hard hit.，下一句又点出 Such difficult economic times may leave many adolescents __(34)__ about their roles in society.——"职业减少"加"经济艰难"两条线都指向 recession（经济衰退），这是唯一与因果链严丝合缝的名词。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) entrance "入口/进入"，与"职业减少"反向entrance 表示"进入"或"入口"，times of entrance 含义不明、且与下文 difficult economic times 完全脱节。
H) existence "存在/生存"，本题已锁定第 27 题existence 虽可表"生存状态"，但下一题第 27 题的语义只与 existence 严丝合缝（详见后），此处把它留给第 27 题；且 times of existence 也并非地道英文搭配。
K) occupation "职业"，与本句 careers 内容重复occupation 与 careers and vocations 同义重复，且 times of occupation 在英语里多指"被占领时期"，与经济语境严重错位。
L) promises "承诺"，与"职业短缺"无关promises 表"承诺"，times of promises 既不是固定搭配，也无法解释下文"adolescents may be especially hard hit"的打击来源。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) confused 形容词
**词性槽** leave + 宾语 + ___ 形容词补足语
**依据** "经济困难令青少年对自己的社会角色感到困惑"本句承接"经济衰退"语境，Such difficult economic times may leave many adolescents__(34)__ about their roles in society. 说艰难时世让许多青少年对其社会角色"困惑"——confused about one's role 是地道搭配，且与下句"政府就业项目以激发自我价值感"形成因果关联：因为先 confused，所以才需要刺激 sense of worth。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) beneficial义为"有益的"，主语本应是"事物"非"人" beneficial 修饰物或措施而非人；"使青少年有益的"语法不通，且搭配为 beneficial to，不接 about。
G) excited 义为"兴奋的"，与"艰难经济"语境反向经济衰退令人沮丧、迷茫，不可能 excited about 自己的社会角色；语义和语气都正好反过来。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 G) —— excited 形态合规但情绪反向。第 34 题 leave many adolescents ___ about their roles 形态上 excited 也对，但句子语境是"难时世+需要刺激价值感"的负面语境，excited 反过来了；防坑一句话——形容词补足语先校正情感色彩，再校正搭配介词。

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) beneficial 形容词
**词性槽** are not only … but also … 并列形容词位
**依据** "经济上有益"对仗后半句"激发自我价值感"并列结构 not only economically beneficial but also help to stimulate the adolescent's sense of worth 在"经济收益"与"心理价值"两侧对仗——beneficial 表"有益的"恰好概括项目的经济正面效益；且 economically beneficial 是高频学术搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) excited 义为"激动的"，主语应是人非项目excited 通常描述人的情绪；说"政府就业项目在经济上是激动的"主语错位、搭配不成立，且与not only … but also 的并列对仗（经济效益 + 心理效益）严重不匹配。

title: Climate change may be real, but it's still not easy being green How do we convince our inner caveman to be greener? We ask some outstanding social scientists.

passage.label: A

sentences.text: The road to climate hell is paved with our good intentions.
Politicians may tackle polluters while scientists do battle with carbon emissions.
But the most pervasive problem is less obvious: our own behaviour.
We get distracted before we can turn down the heating.
We break our promise not to fly after hearing about a neighbour's trip to India.
Ultimately, we can't be bothered to change our attitude.
Fortunately for the planet, social science and behavioural economics may be able to do that for us.

passage.translation: 通往气候地狱的道路由我们的良好意愿铺就。政治家们可能会对付污染者,而科学家们则与碳排放作斗争。但最普遍的问题却不那么明显:我们自己的行为。我们在调低暖气之前就分心了。我们在听说邻居去印度旅行后就违背了不坐飞机的承诺。最终,我们懒得改变自己的态度。幸运的是,对于地球而言,社会科学和行为经济学或许能够为我们做到这一点。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: Despite mournful polar bears and charts showing carbon emissions soaring, most people find it hard to believe that global warming will affect them personally.
Recent polls by the Pew Research Centre in Washington, DC, found that 75-80 percent of participants regarded climate change as an important issue.
But respondents ranked it last on a list of priorities.

passage.translation: 尽管有悲伤的北极熊和显示碳排放飙升的图表,大多数人仍然难以相信全球变暖会对他们个人产生影响。华盛顿特区Pew研究中心最近的民意调查发现,75%至80%的参与者认为气候变化是一个重要议题。但受访者在优先事项清单上将其排在最后。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: This inconsistency largely stems from a feeling of powerlessness.

"When we can't actually remove the source of our fear, we tend to adapt psychologically by adopting a range of defense mechanisms," says Tom Crompton, change strategist for the environmental organization World Wide Fund for Nature.

passage.translation: 这种不一致很大程度上源于一种无力感。环境组织世界自然基金会的变革策略师Tom Crompton说:'当我们实际上无法消除恐惧的根源时,我们往往会通过采用一系列防御机制来进行心理适应。'

passage.label: D

sentences.text: Part of the fault lies with our inner caveman.
Evolution has programmed humans to pay most attention to issues that will have an immediate impact.

"We worry most about now because if we don't survive for the next minute, we're not going to be around in ten years' time," says Professor Elke Weber of the Centre for Research on Environmental Decisions at Columbia University in New York.
If the Thames were lapping around Big Ben, Londoners would face up to the problem of emissions pretty quickly.
But in practice, our brain discounts the risks—and benefits—associated with issues that lie some way ahead.

passage.translation: 部分责任在于我们内心的穴居人。进化已经将人类编程为最关注那些会产生即时影响的问题。纽约Columbia大学环境决策研究中心的Elke Weber教授说:'我们最担心现在,因为如果我们无法在下一分钟存活下来,我们就不会在十年后还在这里。'如果泰晤士河拍打着大本钟,伦敦人会很快直面排放问题。但实际上,我们的大脑会低估与未来一段时间的问题相关的风险和收益。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Matthew Rush worth, of the Department of Experimental Psychology at the University of Oxford, sees this in his lab every day.
"One of the ways in which all agents seem to make decisions is that they assign a lower weighting to outcomes that are going to be further away in the future," he says.
"This is a very sensible way for an animal to make decisions in the wild and would have been very helpful for humans for thousands of years."

passage.translation: 牛津大学实验心理学系的Matthew Rushworth每天都在他的实验室里看到这一点。他说:'所有行为主体似乎做出决策的方式之一是,他们对未来更远的结果赋予较低的权重。这对于动物在野外做出决策来说是一种非常明智的方式,并且在数千年来对人类非常有帮助。'

passage.label: F

sentences.text: Not any longer.
By the time we wake up to the threat posed by climate change, it could well be too late.
And if we're not going to make rational decisions about the future, others may have to help us to do so.

passage.translation: 但现在不再如此了。当我们意识到气候变化带来的威胁时,很可能已经太晚了。如果我们不打算对未来做出理性决策,其他人可能必须帮助我们这样做。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: Few political libraries are without a copy of Nudge: Improving Decisions About Health, Wealth and Happiness, by Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein.
They argue that governments should persuade us into making better decisions—such as saving more in our pension plans—by changing the default options.
Professor Weber believes that environmental policy can make use of similar tactics.
If, for example, building codes included green construction guidelines, most developers would be too lazy to challenge them.

passage.translation: 很少有政治图书馆没有Richard Thaler和Cass Sunstein所著《助推:改善关于健康、财富和幸福的决策》的副本。他们认为,政府应该通过改变默认选项来说服我们做出更好的决策,例如在养老金计划中储蓄更多。Weber教授认为环境政策可以利用类似的策略。例如,如果建筑法规包括绿色建筑指南,大多数开发商会懒得挑战它们。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Defaults are certainly part of the solution.
But social scientists are most concerned about crafting messages that exploit our group mentality(心态).
"We need to understand what motivates people, what it is that allows them to make change," says Professor Neil Adger, of the Tyndall Centre for Climate Change Research in Norwich.
"It is actually about what their peers think of them, what their social norms are, what is seen as desirable in society."
In other words, our inner caveman is continually looking over his shoulder to see what the rest of the tribe are up to.

passage.translation: 默认选项当然是解决方案的一部分。但社会科学家最关心的是精心设计利用我们群体心态的信息。Norwich廷德尔气候变化研究中心的Neil Adger教授说:'我们需要了解什么激励人们,什么使他们能够做出改变。这实际上关乎他们的同伴对他们的看法,他们的社会规范是什么,在社会中什么被视为理想的。'换句话说,我们内心的穴居人不断回头看部落其他成员在做什么。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: The passive attitude we have to climate change as individuals can be altered by counting us in—and measuring us against—our peer group.
"Social norms are primitive and elemental," says Dr.
Robert Cialdini, author of Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion.
"Birds flock together, fish school together, cattle herd together…" just perceiving norms is enough to cause people to adjust their behavior in the direction of the crowd.

passage.translation: 我们作为个人对气候变化持有的被动态度可以通过将我们纳入并与我们的同伴群体进行比较来改变。《影响力:说服心理学》的作者Robert Cialdini博士说:'社会规范是原始和基本的。鸟儿成群,鱼儿成群,牛群成群……'仅仅感知规范就足以使人们朝着群体的方向调整他们的行为。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: These norms can take us beyond good intentions.
Cialdini conducted a study in San Diego in which coat hangers bearing messages about saving energy were hung on people's doors.
Some of the messages mentioned the environment, some financial savings, others social responsibility.
But it was the ones that mentioned the actions of neighbours that drove down power use.

passage.translation: 这些规范可以让我们超越良好意愿。Cialdini在圣地亚哥进行了一项研究,在人们的门上挂上印有节能信息的衣架。一些信息提到环境,一些提到经济节约,其他提到社会责任。但正是那些提到邻居行为的信息降低了用电量。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: Other studies show that simply providing the facility for people to compare their energy use with the local average is enough to cause them to modify their behaviour.
The Conservatives plan to adopt this strategy by making utility companies print the average local electricity and gas usage on people's bills.

passage.translation: 其他研究表明,仅仅提供让人们将自己的能源使用与当地平均水平进行比较的设施,就足以使他们改变自己的行为。保守党计划通过让公用事业公司在人们的账单上打印当地平均用电和用气量来采用这一策略。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: Social science can also teach politicians how to avoid our collective capacity for self-destructive behaviour.
Environmental campaigns that tell us how many people drive SUVs unwittingly(不经意地) imply that this behaviour is widespread and thus permissible.
Cialdini recommends some careful framing of the message.

"Instead of normalising the undesirable behaviour, the message needs to marginalise it, for example, by stating that if even one person buys yet another SUV, it reduces our ability to be energy-independent."

passage.translation: 社会科学还可以教政治家如何避免我们集体的自我毁灭行为能力。告诉我们有多少人驾驶SUV的环境宣传活动不经意地暗示这种行为很普遍,因此是允许的。Cialdini建议对信息进行一些仔细的框架设定。'信息不应该使不良行为正常化,而需要将其边缘化,例如,通过声明即使有一个人再买一辆SUV,也会降低我们实现能源独立的能力。'

passage.label: M

sentences.text: Tapping into how we already see ourselves is crucial.
The most successful environmental strategy will marry the green message to our own sense of identity.
Take your average trade union member, chances are they will be politically motivated and be used to collective action—much like Erica Gregory.

A retired member of the Public and Commercial Services Union, she is setting up one of 1,100 action groups with the support of Climate Solidarity, a two-year environmental campaign aimed at trade unionists.

passage.translation: 利用我们已经如何看待自己是至关重要的。最成功的环境战略将把绿色信息与我们自己的身份认同结合起来。以你的普通工会成员为例,他们很可能有政治动机并习惯于集体行动,就像Erica Gregory一样。作为公共和商业服务工会的退休成员,她正在Climate Solidarity的支持下建立1100个行动小组中的一个,这是一项为期两年、针对工会成员的环境运动。

passage.label: N

sentences.text: Erica is proof that a great-grandmother can help to lead the revolution if you get the psychology right—in this case, by matching her enthusiasm for the environment with a fondness for organising groups.
"I think it's a terrific idea," she says of the campaign.
"The union backing it makes members think there must be something in it."
She is expecting up to 20 people at the first meeting she has called, at her local pub in the Cornish village of Polperro.

passage.translation: Erica证明,如果你的心理策略正确,一位曾祖母也可以帮助领导这场革命——在这种情况下,通过将她对环境的热情与对组织团体的喜爱相匹配。她谈到这项运动时说:'我认为这是个很棒的想法。工会支持它让成员们觉得其中一定有些道理。'她预计将有多达20人参加她在康沃尔郡Polperro村当地酒吧召集的第一次会议。

passage.label: O

sentences.text: Nick Perks, project director for Climate Solidarity, believes this sort of activity is where the future of environmental action lies.
"Using existing civil society structures or networks is a more effective way of creating change… and obviously trade unions are one of the biggest civil society networks in the UK," he says.
The "Love Food, Hate Waste" campaign entered into a collaboration last year with another such network—the Women's Institute.
Londoner Rachel Taylor joined the campaign with the aim of making new friends.
A year on, the meetings have made lasting changes to what she throws away in her kitchen.
"It's always more of an incentive if you're doing it with other people," she says.
"It motivates you more if you know that you've got to provide feedback to a group."

passage.translation: Climate Solidarity的项目主任Nick Perks认为,这种活动是环境行动的未来所在。他说:'利用现有的公民社会结构或网络是创造变革的更有效方式……显然工会是英国最大的公民社会网络之一。''爱惜食物,拒绝浪费'运动去年与另一个这样的网络——妇女协会——展开了合作。伦敦人Rachel Taylor加入该运动的目的是结交新朋友。一年后,这些会议对她在厨房里扔掉的东西产生了持久的改变。她说:'如果你和其他人一起做,总是更有动力。如果你知道你必须向一个小组提供反馈,这会更激励你。'

passage.label: P

sentences.text: The power of such simple psychology in fighting climate change is attracting attention across the political establishment.
In the US, the House of Representatives Science Committee has approved a bill allocating $10 million a year to studying energy-related behaviour.
In the UK, new studies are in development and social scientists are regularly spotted in British government offices.
With the help of psychologists, there is fresh hope that we might go green after all.

passage.translation: 这种简单心理学在应对气候变化方面的力量正在吸引整个政治机构的关注。在美国,众议院科学委员会已批准一项法案,每年拨款1000万美元用于研究与能源相关的行为。在英国,新的研究正在开发中,社会科学家经常出现在英国政府办公室。在心理学家的帮助下,我们终究可能走向绿色,这带来了新的希望。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: When people find they are powerless to change a situation, they tend to live with it.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
当人们发现自己无力改变某种情况时,他们往往会接受现状。
**锚点** powerless + live with it 因果对
**定位** 这种言行不一主要源于无力感。'当我们无法真正消除恐惧的源头时，我们倾向于通过采取一系列防御机制在心理上加以适应，'世界自然基金会的变革策略师 Tom Crompton 说。
**改写** powerless to change a situation ↔ When we can't actually remove the source of our fear powerless ≈ can't actually remove they tend to live with it ↔we tend to adapt psychologically by adopting a range of defense mechanisms live with ↔ adapt psychologically
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段陈述了民调里 75-80 percent 认为重要却 ranked it last on a list of priorities 的现象，但没说'powerless → 只能接受'这一原因机制，与 Q36 的因果配对对不上。But respondents ranked it last on a list of priorities.
questions.quote: This inconsistency largely stems from a feeling of powerlessness. "When we can't actually remove the source of our fear, we tend to adapt psychologically by adopting a range of defense mechanisms," says Tom Crompton, change strategist for the environmental organization World Wide Fund for Nature.

questions.prompt: To be effective, environmental messages should be carefully framed.
questions.explanation:
**答案** L 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
为了有效,环境信息应当谨慎措辞。
**锚点** environmental messages + carefully framed
**定位** Cialdini 建议要精心包装信息：'信息不该把不良行为常态化，而要把它边缘化，比如可以说，哪怕只多一个人再买一辆 SUV，都会削弱我们能源自给自足的能力。'
**改写** environmental messages should be carefully framed ↔Cialdini recommends some careful framing of the message should ↔ recommends 建议骨架To be effective ↔Instead of normalising the undesirable behaviour, the message needs to marginalise it效果意识 ↔ 反命题指导
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
H H 段的核心是 crafting messages that exploit our group mentality 与 what motivates people, what it is that allows them to make change，焦点在'懂得人靠什么被驱动'，没出现 framing 这一具体技法。But social scientists are most concerned about crafting messages that exploit our group mentality
questions.quote: Cialdini recommends some careful framing of the message. "Instead of normalising the undesirable behaviour, the message needs to marginalise it, for example, by stating that if even one person buys yet another SUV, it reduces our ability to be energy-independent."

questions.prompt: It is the government's responsibility to persuade people into making environment-friendly decisions.
questions.explanation:
**答案** G 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
说服人们做出环保决策是政府的责任。
**锚点** government 责任 + persuade 决策
**定位** 他们主张政府应该通过改变默认选项来劝导我们做出更好的决策，比如在养老金计划中存更多钱。
**改写** It is the government's responsibility ↔ They argue that governments should responsibility ↔ should 同义表态persuade people into making environment-friendly decisions ↔persuade us into making better decisions people↔us、environment-friendly↔better 替换
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
F F 段的 others may have to help us to do so 中 others 是泛指，并未点名government；本题题干的责任主体明确是 government，必须排除。And if we're not going to make rational decisions about the future, others may have to help us to do so.
questions.quote: They argue that governments should persuade us into making better decisions—such as saving more in our pension plans—by changing the default options.

questions.prompt: Politicians are beginning to realise the importance of enlisting psychologists' help in fighting climate change.
questions.explanation:
**答案** P 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
政治家们开始意识到在应对气候变化中寻求心理学家帮助的重要性。
**锚点** Politicians + psychologists' help
**定位** 这种简单心理学在对抗气候变化中的力量，正在吸引整个政界的关注。
**改写** Politicians are beginning to realise the importance of ↔attracting attention across the political establishment视角翻转的同义表达enlisting psychologists' help in fighting climate change ↔The power of such simple psychology in fighting climate change psychologists' help ↔ simple psychology 名词化对应
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
G G 段是 Thaler 和 Sunstein 等学者主张 governments should persuade us，是规范主张；而 Q39 要的是政客正在意识到心理学的重要并开始行动，对应的应是 P 段的现实进展。They argue that governments should persuade us into making better decisions
questions.quote: The power of such simple psychology in fighting climate change is attracting attention across the political establishment.

questions.prompt: To find effective solutions to climate change, it is necessary to understand what motivates people to make change.
questions.explanation:
**答案** H 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
要找到应对气候变化的有效解决方案,有必要理解是什么促使人们做出改变。
**锚点** understand what motivates people
**定位** '我们需要理解是什么驱动着人们、是什么让他们能够做出改变，'Tyndall 气候变化研究中心的 Neil Adger 教授说。
**改写** To find effective solutions to climate change, it is necessary to ↔ We need to understand目的-必要 ↔ 直接需要表态understand what motivates people to make change ↔understand what motivates people, what it is that allows them to make change压缩式同义改写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
G G 段强调 by changing the default options，属于外部机制层；本题问的是 what motivates people to make change，属于内部驱动层，路径不一致。governments should persuade us into making better decisions—such as saving more in our pension plans—by changing the default options
questions.quote: "We need to understand what motivates people, what it is that allows them to make change," says Professor Neil Adger, of the Tyndall Centre for Climate Change Research in Norwich.

questions.prompt: In their evolution, humans have learned to pay attention to the most urgent issues instead of long- term concerns.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
在进化过程中,人类学会了关注最紧迫的问题而非长期关切。
**锚点** evolution + urgent vs long-term
**定位** 部分原因要怪我们体内的穴居人。进化已经把人类编程为最关注那些会产生即时影响的问题。'我们最担心当下，因为如果我们撑不过下一分钟，就不会再活到十年后，'哥伦比亚大学环境决策研究中心的 Elke Weber 教授说。
**改写** pay attention to the most urgent issues ↔pay most attention to issues that will have an immediate impact urgent ↔ immediate impact 同义instead of long-term concerns ↔our brain discounts the risks—and benefits—associated with issues that lie some way ahead long-term ↔ lie some way ahead
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E E 段的核心是 Matthew Rushworth 实验室的发现 all agents seem to make decisions is that they assign a lower weighting to outcomes that are going to be further away in the future，没有出现 evolution 这一进化命题，与题干 In their evolution 不匹配。One of the ways in which all agents seem to make decisions is that they assign a lower weighting to outcomes that are going to be further away in the future
questions.quote: Part of the fault lies with our inner caveman. Evolution has programmed humans to pay most attention to issues that will have an immediate impact. "We worry most about now because if we don't survive for the next minute, we're not going to be around in ten years' time," says Professor Elke Weber of the Centre for Research on Environmental Decisions at Columbia University in New York.

questions.prompt: One study shows that our neighbours' actions are influential in changing our behaviour.
questions.explanation:
**答案** J 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
一项研究表明,我们邻居的行为对改变我们的行为有影响力。
**锚点** neighbours' actions 影响行为
**定位** 但真正压低用电量的，是那些提到邻居做法的信息。
**改写** our neighbours' actions ↔ the actions of neighbours所有格语序的等值One study shows ↔Cialdini conducted a study in San Diego in which coat hangers bearing messages about saving energy were hung on people's doors One study ↔ conducted a study 上下位influential in changing our behaviour ↔ drove down power use抽象影响 ↔ 具体行为结果
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
K K 段是用 compare their energy use with the local average，对照的是'本地平均'这一统计概念；本题题干钉的是 our neighbours' actions 这种具体邻里行为，对照对象不同。simply providing the facility for people to compare their energy use with the local average is enough to cause them to modify their behaviour
questions.quote: But it was the ones that mentioned the actions of neighbours that drove down power use.

questions.prompt: Despite clear signs of global warming, it is not easy for most people to believe climate change will affect their own lives.
questions.explanation:
**答案** B 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
尽管有明显的全球变暖迹象,大多数人仍然很难相信气候变化会影响他们自己的生活。
**锚点** global warming 自身不易相信
**定位** 尽管有忧伤的北极熊和显示碳排放飙升的图表，大多数人仍然觉得很难相信全球变暖会影响到自己。
**改写** Despite clear signs of global warming ↔Despite mournful polar bears and charts showing carbon emissions soaring上位概括 ↔ 下位具体意象it is not easy for most people to believe ↔ most people find it hard to believe not easy ↔ hard 直接同义affect their own lives ↔ affect them personally their own lives ↔ personally 等值
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
D D 段以 Evolution has programmed humans to pay most attention to issues that will have an immediate impact 给出原因机制；本题 Q43 只问'人们不易相信会影响自己'这一现象的陈述出处，应回到现象本身的 B 段。Evolution has programmed humans to pay most attention to issues that will have an immediate impact
questions.quote: Despite mournful polar bears and charts showing carbon emissions soaring, most people find it hard to believe that global warming will affect them personally.

questions.prompt: We should take our future into consideration in making decisions concerning climate change before it is too late.
questions.explanation:
**答案** F 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
在做关于气候变化的决策时,我们应当在为时已晚之前将我们的未来考虑在内。
**锚点** before it is too late + 考虑未来
**定位** 等我们意识到气候变化所带来的威胁时，很可能已经为时已晚。如果我们自己不打算就未来做出理性决策，那别人就只能来帮我们做。
**改写** take our future into consideration in making decisions ↔make rational decisions about the future考虑未来 ↔ 就未来做决策before it is too late ↔By the time we wake up to the threat posed by climate change, it could well be too late before too late ↔ by the time…it could well be too late
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E E 段只是中性陈述 assign a lower weighting to outcomes that are going to be further away in the future，没有'我们应该考虑未来、否则太迟'的价值判断，与should 的态度不匹配。they assign a lower weighting to outcomes that are going to be further away in the future
questions.quote: By the time we wake up to the threat posed by climate change, it could well be too late. And if we're not going to make rational decisions about the future, others may have to help us to do so.

questions.prompt: Existing social networks can be more effective in creating change in people's behaviour.
questions.explanation:
**答案** O 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
现有的社交网络在促成人们行为改变方面可以更加有效。
**锚点** Existing social networks 更有效
**定位** '借用既有的公民社会结构或网络，是一种更有效的促成变革的方式……显然，工会是英国最大的公民社会网络之一，'他说。
**改写** Existing social networks ↔ existing civil society structures or networks social ↔ civil society 上下位more effective in creating change in people's behaviour ↔a more effective way of creating change more effective + creating change 原样保留
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
M M 段是举例陈述 Erica Gregory. A retired member of the Public and Commercial Services Union, she is setting up one of 1,100 action groups，没有给出'更有效'这一比较判断，本题题干要的是评价句，应回 O 段。Take your average trade union member, chances are they will be politically motivated and be used to collective action
questions.quote: "Using existing civil society structures or networks is a more effective way of creating change… and obviously trade unions are one of the biggest civil society networks in the UK," he says.

passage.label: A

sentences.text: When Nijay Williams entered college last fall as a first-generation student and Jamaican immigrant, he was academically unprepared for the rigors of higher education.

Like many first-generation students, he enrolled in a medium-sized state university many of his high school peers were also attending, received a Pell Grant, and took out some small federal loans to cover other costs.
Given the high price of room and board and the closeness of the school to his family, he chose to live at home and worked between 30 and 40 hours a week while taking a full class schedule.

passage.translation: 去年秋天，当Nijay Williams作为第一代大学生和牙买加移民进入大学时，他在学业上还没有为高等教育的严格要求做好准备。像许多第一代大学生一样，他进入了一所中等规模的州立大学，他的许多高中同学也在那里就读，他获得了Pell助学金，并申请了一些小额联邦贷款来支付其他费用。考虑到住宿费用高昂以及学校离家很近，他选择住在家里，每周工作30到40小时，同时修满全部课程。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: What Nijay didn't realize about his school—Tennessee State University—was its frighteningly low graduation rate a mere 29 percent for its first-generation students.
At the end of his first year, Nijay lost his Pell Grant of over $5,000 after narrowly missing the 2.0 GPA cut-off, making it impossible for him to continue paying for school.

passage.translation: Nijay没有意识到他的学校——Tennessee State University——有着可怕的低毕业率，其第一代大学生的毕业率仅为29%。在第一学年结束时，Nijay因为勉强未达到2.0的GPA分数线而失去了超过5000美元的Pell助学金，这使他无法继续支付学费。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: Nijay represents a large and growing group of Americans: first-generation college students who enter school unprepared or behind.
To make matters worse, these schools are ill-equipped to graduate these students—young adults who face specific challenges and obstacles.
They typically carry financial burdens that outweigh those of their peers, are more likely to work while attending school, and often require significant academic remediation(补习).

passage.translation: Nijay代表了一个庞大且不断增长的美国群体：那些毫无准备或起点落后就进入大学的第一代大学生。更糟糕的是，这些学校没有能力让这些学生毕业——这些年轻人面临着特定的挑战和障碍。他们通常承担着超过同龄人的经济负担，更有可能在上学期间打工，并且常常需要大量的学业补习。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: Matt Rubinoff directs I'm First, a nonprofit organization launched last October to reach out to this specific population of students.
He hopes to distribute this information and help prospective college- goers find the best post-secondary fit.

And while Rubinoff believes there are a good number of four- year schools that truly care about these students and set aside significant resources and programs for them, he says that number isn't high enough.

passage.translation: Matt Rubinoff负责管理I'm First，这是一个去年十月启动的非营利组织，旨在接触这一特定的学生群体。他希望传播这些信息，帮助未来的大学申请者找到最适合的高等教育选择。尽管Rubinoff相信有相当数量的四年制大学真正关心这些学生，并为他们预留了大量资源和项目，但他表示这个数量还不够高。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: "It's not only the selective and elite institutions that provide those opportunities for a small subset of this population," Rubinoff said, adding that a majority of first-generation undergraduates tend toward options such as online programs, two-year colleges, and commuter state schools.
"Unfortunately, there tends to be a lack of information and support to help students think bigger and broader."

passage.translation: "不仅仅是那些精英名校为这一群体中的一小部分人提供这些机会，"Rubinoff说，他补充道，大多数第一代本科生倾向于选择在线课程、两年制学院和通勤州立大学等选项。"不幸的是，往往缺乏信息和支持来帮助学生思考得更远更广。"

passage.label: F

sentences.text: Despite this problem, many students are still drawn to these institutions—and two-year schools in particular.
As a former high school teacher, I saw students choose familiar, cheaper options year after year.
Instead of skipping out on higher education altogether, they chose community colleges or state schools with low bars for admittance.

passage.translation: 尽管存在这个问题，许多学生仍然被这些院校所吸引——尤其是两年制学校。作为一名前高中教师，我看到学生们年复一年地选择熟悉的、更便宜的选项。他们没有完全放弃高等教育，而是选择了社区大学或录取门槛较低的州立学校。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: "They underestimate themselves when selecting a university," said Dave Jarrat, a marketing executive for Inside Track, a for-profit organization that specializes in coaching low-income students and supporting colleges in order to help students thrive.
"The reality of it is that a lot of low-income kids could be going to elite universities on a full ride scholarship and don't even realize it."

passage.translation: "他们在选择大学时低估了自己，"Dave Jarrat说，他是Inside Track的营销主管，这是一家营利性组织，专门为低收入学生提供指导并支持大学帮助学生取得成功。"现实情况是，很多低收入家庭的孩子本可以获得全额奖学金去精英大学，但他们甚至没有意识到这一点。"

passage.label: H

sentences.text: "Many students are coming from a situation where no one around them has the experience of successfully completing higher education, so they are coming in questioning themselves and their college worthiness," Jarrat continued.
That helps explain why, as I'm First's Rubinoff indicated, the schools to which these students end up resorting can end up being some of the poorest matches for them.
The University of Tennessee in Knoxville offers one example of this dilemma.
A flagship university in the South, the school graduates just 16 percent of its first-generation students, despite its overall graduation rate of 71 percent.
Located only a few hours apart, the University of Tennessee and Tennessee State are worth comparing.
Tennessee State's overall graduation rate is a tiny 39 percent, but at least it has a smaller gap between the outcomes for first-generation students and those of their peers.

passage.translation: "许多学生来自这样的环境：他们周围没有人有成功完成高等教育的经历，所以他们带着对自己和自己是否配得上大学的质疑进入校园，"Jarrat继续说道。这有助于解释为什么，正如I'm First的Rubinoff所指出的，这些学生最终选择的学校可能恰恰是最不适合他们的。位于Knoxville的University of Tennessee就提供了一个这种困境的例子。作为南方的一所旗舰大学，该校第一代大学生的毕业率仅为16%，尽管其整体毕业率为71%。University of Tennessee和Tennessee State相距仅几个小时，值得比较。Tennessee State的整体毕业率仅为39%，但至少它在第一代学生和其他学生的结果之间的差距较小。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Still, the University of Tennessee deserves credit for being transparent.
Many large institutions keep this kind of data secret—or at least make it incredibly difficult to find.

The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, for instance, admits only that the graduation rate for its first-generation pupils is "much lower" than the percentage of all students who graduate within four years (81 percent).

passage.translation: 尽管如此，University of Tennessee因其透明度值得肯定。许多大型院校对这类数据保密——或者至少让人很难找到。例如，University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill只承认其第一代学生的毕业率"远低于"四年内毕业的所有学生的比例(81%)。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: It is actually quite difficult to find reliable statistics on the issue for many schools.

Higher education institutions are, under federal law, required to report graduation rates, but these reports typically only include Pell recipient numbers—not necessarily rates specific to first-generation students.
Other initiatives fail to break down the data, too.
Imagine how intimidating it can be for prospective students unfamiliar with the complexities of higher education to navigate this kind of information and then identify which schools are the best fit.

passage.translation: 实际上，对于许多学校来说，很难找到关于这个问题的可靠统计数据。根据联邦法律，高等教育机构需要报告毕业率，但这些报告通常只包括Pell助学金获得者的数量——不一定是专门针对第一代学生的比率。其他项目也未能细分数据。想象一下，对于不熟悉高等教育复杂性的未来学生来说，浏览这类信息然后确定哪些学校最适合他们是多么令人生畏。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: It was this lack of information that prompted the launch of I'm First in 2013, originally as an arm of its umbrella organization, the Center For Student Opportunity.

"If we can help to direct students to more of these types of campuses and help students to understand them to be realistic and accessible places, have them apply to these schools at greater frequency and ultimately get in and enroll, we are going to raise the success rate," Rubinoff said, citing a variety of colleges ranging from large state institutions to smaller private schools.

passage.label: L

sentences.text: Chelsea Jones, who now directs student programming at I'm First, was a first-generation college student at Howard.

"There wasn't really a college-bound culture at my high school," she said.
"I wanted to go to college but I didn't really know the process."

passage.label: M

sentences.text: She was fortunate, though.

Howard, a well-regarded historically black college, had an array of resources for its first-generation students, including matching kids with counselors, connecting first- generation students to one another, and TRIO, a national program that supported 200 students on Howard's campus.

Still, Jones represents a small percentage of first-generation students who are able to gain entry into more elite universities, which are often known for robust financial aid packages and remarkably high graduation rates for first-generation students.
(Harvard, for example, boasts a six-year graduation rate for underrepresented minority groups of 98 percent).

title: The Impossibility of Rapid Energy Transitions

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Politicians are fond of promising rapid energy transitions.
Whether it is a transition from imported to domestic oil or from coal-powered electricity production to natural-gas power plants, politicians love to talk big.

Unfortunately for them (and often the taxpayers), our energy systems are a bit like an aircraft carrier: they are unbelievably expensive, they are built to last for a very long time, they have a huge amount of inertia (meaning it takes a lot of energy to set them moving), and they have a lot of momentum once they are set in motion.
No matter how hard you try, you can't turn something that large on a dime(10美分硬币), or even a few thousand dimes.

passage.translation: 政治家们喜欢承诺快速的能源转型。无论是从进口石油向国产石油转型,还是从煤电生产向天然气发电厂转型,政治家们都喜欢说大话。不幸的是,对他们(通常也对纳税人)而言,我们的能源系统有点像航空母舰:它们极其昂贵,建造时就是为了使用很长时间,它们具有巨大的惯性(意味着需要大量能量才能使它们运动起来),而且一旦开始运动就具有很大的动量。无论你多么努力,你都无法让这么大的东西在10美分硬币上转向,甚至几千枚硬币上也不行。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: In physics, moving objects have two characteristics relevant to understanding the dynamics of energy systems: inertia and momentum.
Inertia is the resistance of objects to efforts to change their state of motion.
If you try to push a boulder(大圆石), it pushes you back.
Once you have started the boulder rolling, it develops momentum, which is defined by its mass and velocity.
Momentum is said to be "conserved," that is, once you build it up, it has to go somewhere.
So a heavy object, like a football player moving at a high speed, has a lot of momentum—that is, once he is moving, it is hard to change his state of motion.

If you want to change his course, you have only a few choices: you can stop him, transferring (possibly painfully) some of his kinetic energy(动能) to your own body, or you can approach alongside and slowly apply pressure to gradually alter his course.

passage.translation: 在物理学中,运动的物体有两个与理解能源系统动力学相关的特征:惯性和动量。惯性是物体对改变其运动状态的努力所表现出的阻力。如果你试图推动一块大圆石,它会推回来。一旦你让大圆石滚动起来,它就产生了动量,动量由其质量和速度决定。动量被认为是"守恒的",也就是说,一旦你积累起动量,它必须有去处。因此,一个重物体,比如一名高速移动的橄榄球运动员,具有很大的动量——也就是说,一旦他运动起来,就很难改变他的运动状态。如果你想改变他的路线,你只有几个选择:你可以阻止他,将他的一些动能(可能是痛苦地)转移到你自己的身体上,或者你可以从旁边靠近并缓慢施加压力以逐渐改变他的路线。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: But there are other kinds of momentum as well.
After all, we don't speak only of objects or people as having momentum; we speak of entire systems having momentum.
Whether it's a sports team or a presidential campaign, everybody relishes having the big momentum, because it makes them harder to stop or change direction.

passage.translation: 但还有其他种类的动量。毕竟,我们不仅把物体或人说成具有动量;我们说整个系统具有动量。无论是运动队还是总统竞选活动,每个人都喜欢拥有强大的动量,因为这使他们更难被阻止或改变方向。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: One kind of momentum is technological momentum.
When a technology is deployed, its impacts reach far beyond itself.
Consider the incandescent(白炽灯的) bulb, an object currently hated by many environmentalists and energy-efficiency advocates.
The incandescent light bulb, invented by Thomas Edison, which came to be the symbol of inspiration, has been developed into hundreds, if not thousands, of forms.
Today, a visit to a lighting store reveals a stunning array of choices.
There are standard-shaped bulbs, flame-shaped bulbs, colored globe-shaped bulbs, and more.
It is quite easy, with all that choice, to change a light bulb.

passage.translation: 一种动量是技术动量。当一项技术被部署时,它的影响远远超出其本身。以白炽灯泡为例,这是一个目前被许多环保主义者和能效倡导者憎恨的物品。白炽灯泡由Thomas Edison发明,后来成为灵感的象征,已经发展出数百种甚至数千种形式。今天,访问一家灯具店会发现令人惊叹的各种选择。有标准形状的灯泡、火焰形状的灯泡、彩色球形灯泡等等。有了这么多选择,更换灯泡是相当容易的。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: But the momentum of incandescent lighting does not stop there.

All of those specialized bulbs led to the building of specialized light fixtures, from the desk lamp you study by, to the ugly but beloved hand-painted Chinese lamp you inherited from your grandmother, to the ceiling fixture in your closet, to the light in your oven or refrigerator, and to the light that the dentist points at you.
It is easy to change a light bulb, sure, but it is harder to change the bulb and its fixture.

passage.translation: 但白炽灯照明的动量并不止于此。所有这些专用灯泡导致了专用灯具的建造,从你学习时用的台灯,到你从祖母那里继承的丑陋但心爱的手绘中国灯,到你壁橱里的吊顶灯具,到你烤箱或冰箱里的灯,以及牙医对着你照的灯。换灯泡确实很容易,但更换灯泡及其灯具就更难了。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: And there is more to the story, because not only are the devices that house incandescent bulbs shaped to their underlying characteristics, but rooms and entire buildings have been designed in accordance with how incandescent lighting reflects off walls and windows.

passage.translation: 故事还有更多内容,因为不仅容纳白炽灯泡的设备是根据其基本特性设计的,而且房间和整栋建筑的设计都是根据白炽灯照明如何从墙壁和窗户反射而来的。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: As lighting expert Howard Brandston points out, "Generally, there are no bad light sources, only bad applications."

There are some very commendable characteristics of the CFL [compact fluorescent(荧光的) light bulb], yet the selection of any light source remains inseparable from the luminaire(照明装置) that houses it, along with the space in which both are installed, and lighting requirements that need to be satisfied.
The lamp, the fixture, and the room, all three must work in concert and for the true benefits of end-users.
If the CFL should be used for lighting a particular space, or an object within that space, the fixture must be designed to work with that lamp, and that fixture with the room.
It is a symbiotic(共生的) relationship.
A CFL cannot be simply installed in an incandescent fixture and then expected to produce a visual appearance that is more than washed out, foggy, and dim.
The whole fixture must be replaced—light source and luminaire—and this is never an inexpensive proposition.

passage.translation: 正如照明专家Howard Brandston所指出的,"一般来说,没有不好的光源,只有不好的应用。"CFL(紧凑型荧光灯泡)具有一些非常值得称赞的特性,然而任何光源的选择都与容纳它的照明装置以及两者所安装的空间和需要满足的照明要求密不可分。灯、灯具和房间,这三者必须协同工作,才能真正造福最终用户。如果CFL要用于照亮特定空间或该空间内的物体,灯具必须设计为与该灯配合使用,而该灯具要与房间配合。这是一种共生关系。CFL不能简单地安装在白炽灯具中,然后期望产生一种不只是褪色、模糊和昏暗的视觉效果。整个灯具必须更换——光源和照明装置——这从来都不是一个便宜的提议。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: And Brandston knows a thing or two about lighting, being the man who illuminated the Statue of Liberty.

passage.translation: 而Brandston对照明颇有研究,他就是照亮自由女神像的人。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Another type of momentum we have to think about when planning for changes in our energy systems is labor-pool momentum.
It is one thing to say that we are going to shift 30 percent of our electricity supply from, say, coal to nuclear power in 20 years.
But it is another thing to have a supply of trained talent that could let you carry out this promise.

That is because the engineers, designers, regulators, operators, and all of the other skilled people needed for the new energy industry are specialists who have to be trained first (or retrained, if they are the ones being laid off in some related industry), and education, like any other complicated endeavor, takes time.
And not only do our prospective new energy workers have to be trained, they have to be trained in the right sequence.
One needs the designers, and perhaps the regulators, before the builders and operators, and each group of workers in training has to know there is work waiting beyond graduation.
In some cases, colleges and universities might have to change their training programs, adding another layer of difficulty.

passage.translation: 在规划能源系统变革时,我们必须考虑的另一种动量是劳动力储备动量。说我们将在20年内把30%的电力供应从煤炭转向核能是一回事。但拥有能让你兑现这一承诺的训练有素的人才储备则是另一回事。这是因为新能源产业所需的工程师、设计师、监管者、操作员以及所有其他技术人员都是必须首先接受培训(或者如果他们是在某些相关行业被裁员的人,则需要重新培训)的专业人员,而教育像任何其他复杂事业一样需要时间。而且我们未来的新能源工作者不仅要接受培训,还必须按正确的顺序接受培训。在建设者和操作员之前,需要设计师,也许还需要监管者,而每组受训工作者都必须知道毕业后有工作在等待。在某些情况下,学院和大学可能必须改变其培训项目,这增加了另一层难度。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: By far the biggest type of momentum that comes into play when it comes to changing our energy systems is economic momentum.
The major components of our energy systems, such as fuel production, refining, electrical generation and distribution, are costly installations that have lengthy life spans.
They have to operate for long periods of time before the costs of development have been recovered.
When investors put up money to build, say, a nuclear power plant, they expect to earn that money back over the planned life of the plant, which is typically between 40 and 60 years.
Some coal power plants in the United States have operated for more than 70 years!
The oldest continuously operated commercial hydro-electric plant in the United States is on New York's Hudson River, and it went into commercial service in 1898.

passage.translation: 到目前为止,在改变我们的能源系统时起作用的最大动量类型是经济动量。我们能源系统的主要组成部分,如燃料生产、炼制、发电和配电,都是成本高昂且使用寿命长的设施。它们必须运行很长时间才能收回开发成本。当投资者出资建造比如一座核电站时,他们期望在该电站的计划寿命期内收回这笔钱,通常是40到60年。美国的一些煤电厂已经运行了70多年!美国最古老的持续运营的商业水电站位于纽约的Hudson River,它于1898年投入商业运营。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: As Vaclav Smil points out, "All the forecasts, plans, and anticipations cited above have failed so miserably because their authors and promoters thought the transitions they hoped to implement would proceed unlike all previous energy transitions, and that their progress could be accelerated in an unprecedented manner."

passage.translation: 正如Vaclav Smil所指出的,"上述所有预测、计划和预期都如此惨败,是因为它们的作者和推动者认为他们希望实施的转型将不同于所有以往的能源转型,并且他们的进程可以以前所未有的方式加速。"

passage.label: L

sentences.text: When you hear people speaking of making a rapid transition toward any type of energy, whether it is a switch from coal to nuclear power, or a switch from gasoline-powered cars to electric cars, or even a switch from an incandescent to a fluorescent light, understanding energy system inertia and momentum can help you decide whether their plans are feasible.

passage.translation: 当你听到人们谈论快速向任何类型的能源转型时,无论是从煤炭转向核能,还是从汽油动力汽车转向电动汽车,甚至是从白炽灯转向荧光灯,理解能源系统的惯性和动量可以帮助你判断他们的计划是否可行。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

**改写** Not only moving objects and people ↔we don't speak only of objects or people as having momentum Not only…but 改写为 don't…only all systems have momentum ↔ we speak of entire systems having momentum all systems 与 entire systems 同义替换

questions.prompt: Energy systems, like an aircraft carrier set in motion, have huge momentum.

能源系统就像启动的航空母舰一样,具有巨大的动量。

questions.quote: our energy systems are a bit like an aircraft carrier: they are unbelievably expensive, they are built to last for a very long time, they have a huge amount of inertia (meaning it takes a lot of energy to set them moving), and they have a lot of momentum once they are set in motion.

F 该段强调 rooms and entire buildings have been designed in accordance with how incandescent lighting reflects off walls and windows，方向是讲灯影响建筑，没有明说问题不在光源而在应用这一对立。rooms and entire buildings have been designed in accordance with how incandescent lighting reflects off walls and windows

能源转型的最大障碍是现有能源系统更换成本过高。

E 该段展示 specialized light fixtures 这种技术影响的范围扩散，但没有把这一现象抽象为 a technology can impact areas beyond itself 这一普遍论断，论断在 D 段。All of those specialized bulbs led to the building of specialized light fixtures F 该段把白炽灯影响推到 rooms and entire buildings，仍属于举例延伸，没有承担技术影响超出自身这一总论断。rooms and entire buildings have been designed in accordance with how incandescent lighting reflects off walls and windows

运动物体的物理特性有助于解释能源系统的动力学。

A 该段用 our energy systems are a bit like an aircraft carrier 来类比，并未明说由moving objects 的物理特性来解释 dynamics of energy systems。our energy systems are a bit like an aircraft carrier
