questions.explanation:
**答案** D) fair 形容词
**词性槽** it's ___ to say that …，形式主语 it 后系动词 + 表语
**依据** It's fair to say 是英语高频习语「可以这样说、说……不为过」it's __(26)__ to say that music moves people in special ways. 前文用「有些音乐让你想跳舞，有些激励你改变世界」铺陈，再来一句「可以说音乐以特别的方式打动人心」做总结，正是 it's fair to say 的标准用法。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) manageable manageable 修饰「可控、可处理」，和 to say 接不上manageable 通常修饰任务、症状（make symptoms more manageable），用来说一件事「可控」；说一句话「可控」语义荒谬。
M) taxing taxing 是「费神的」，说一句话费神在语境里不通taxing 多修饰任务、工作量；it's taxing to say 字面虽通，但与前文铺陈「音乐打动人」的语气完全相反，开篇就泼冷水不合逻辑。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) feels 动词
**词性槽** your brain does … which ___ to you like a sting，which 引导的定语从句缺谓语
**依据** feel like 是固定搭配「感觉像」which __(27)__ to you like a sting in your brain 后面跟 like a sting（像针刺），feels (to you) like … 正是「（对你来说）感觉像……」的标准表达，对人称 sb. 用 feels to sb. like 也通。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) mends mend 是「修补」，与 like a sting 不搭mend 通常修补衣服、关系，无法「mend to you like a sting」，搭配和语义都不成立。
N) tends tend 后接 to do，不接 to you like tends 常见结构是 tends to do sth.（往往做某事），后面接动词原形；这里后面是介词 to you+ like + 名词，结构对不上。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) recently 副词
**词性槽** a ___ published study，冠词与过去分词之间填副词修饰 published
**依据** recently published「最近发表」是学术文献标配搭配According to a __(28)__ published study，引用研究时强调「最近发表的一项研究」是英语中极高频的表达 a recently published study；时间副词 recently 与 published 在意义上紧密呼应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) actually actually 表「实际上」，修饰 published 语义空洞actually published「实际上发表的」在英语里几乎不用——研究要么发表了要么没有，没有「实际上发表」这种说法，搭配不自然。
B) consequently consequently 表因果，前文无因，逻辑不接consequently 用来连接前因后果，这里 According to a … published study 是引出依据，并非承接因果；且 a consequently published study 不是英语习惯搭配。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 A) —— L 还是 A？三个副词都「看着能用」。a __(28)__published study 中考生可能凭直觉填 actually 表「实际上发表」，但英语习惯是 recently published；防坑点：a + 时间副词 + V-ed 名词是学术语境的强搭配模板，时间副词优先于强调副词。

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) tends 动词
**词性槽** Alzheimer's ___ to put people …，主语后缺谓语，第三人称单数
**依据** tends to do 表「倾向于、往往」，契合阿尔茨海默症常见症状Alzheimer's __(29)__ to put people into layers of confusion，「阿尔茨海默症往往让人陷入层层困惑」，tends to 表常发性、规律性，符合医学论述的口吻。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) mends mend 不接 to do，且语义反向mend 是「修补、痊愈」，不接 to do；而且 Alzheimer's mends people 意思是「阿尔茨海默症治愈人」，与下文「陷入困惑」完全矛盾。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) actually 副词
**词性槽** music can sometimes ___ lift people out of …，情态动词 + 副词 + 实义动词
**依据** actually 强调「真的、的确」，呼应前文研究证实the study confirms that music can sometimes __(30)__ lift people out of the Alzheimer's haze，研究「证实」音乐有时确实能把患者从混沌中拉出来，actually 强调这种效果是真实存在的，与 confirms 的语气一致。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) consequently consequently 是因果连接副词，本句无因果链consequently 通常放句首/分句首引出结果（…, consequently, …）；这里没有「因为某事 →所以 lift」的因果，硬塞进 can sometimes consequently lift 既不合习惯也不合逻辑。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) observed 动词
**词性槽** This phenomenon has been ___ several times，被动语态，has been + 过去分词
**依据** observed「被观察到」与并列的 studied 同属研究动作This phenomenon has been __(31)__ several times but rarely studied properly. 中 but连接转折，前后都讲科研动作：「被观察到多次，却很少被认真研究」，observed 与studied 是天然的近义并列。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
O) yielded yield 不及物或表「产生/屈服」，与 phenomenon 主语不搭yield 表「产生（结果）」时用法是 A yielded B；表「屈服」时是 yield to。This phenomenon has been yielded 字面意思「这种现象被产生了」语义荒谬，主被动语义都对不上。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) contributing 形容词
**词性槽** ___ author on the study，冠词位 + 名词 author 前作定语
**依据** contributing author 是学术文献固定身份「参与撰写的作者」associate professor in Radiology at the University of Utah and __(32)__ author on the study，介绍 Jeff Anderson 的双重身份，「副教授」+「该研究的参与撰写作者」逻辑自然；contributing author 是学术论文署名中的标准说法。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
J) plottingplotting 是「密谋/绘图」，修饰 author 语义荒诞plotting author 字面是「正在密谋的作者」或「在画图的作者」，作为学术身份描述完全不通；学术场合无此搭配。
M) taxing taxing 形容「繁重的」，不能用来形容人的身份taxing 通常修饰任务、工作（a taxing job），用来形容 author（人）逻辑不通，且语义偏负面，与正面介绍学者的语境冲突。

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) taxing 动词
**词性槽** the diagnoses of dementia are ___ resources，be 动词后缺谓语成分，与后面resources 形成动宾
**依据** tax resources「使资源吃紧」是固定搭配，与 to the maximum 呼应the diagnoses of dementia are __(33)__ resources to the maximum，「痴呆诊断正在最大限度地消耗资源」；tax 作动词意为「使……负担沉重」，tax resources 在医疗/财政语境是标准说法，to the maximum「到极限」直接强化这种「榨干资源」的意味。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
J) plottingplot resources 不是搭配，且语义对不上「占用资源」plot 表「策划/绘制」，plot resources 字面像「策划资源、绘制资源」，与「消耗社会资源」的语境完全错位。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 J) —— M 还是 J？「熟词僻义」盲区。are __(33)__ resources to the maximum 中考生若不知 tax 还有动词义「使吃紧」，会怀疑 taxing，转去试plotting；防坑点：看到 resources、energy、patience 等被「耗」对象，taxing 比plotting 自然得多，平时多积累一词多义。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) manageable 形容词
**词性槽** make the symptoms more ___，make + 宾语 + 形容词比较级，空填形容词
**依据** make symptoms more manageable「让症状更可控」医学语境标配it might make the symptoms more __(34)__, decrease the cost of care and improve a patient's __(35)__ of life.，三件好事并列：症状更可控、护理成本下降、生活质量提升；manageable 与「降低成本、改善质量」语气完全一致。

**答案** K) quality 名词
**词性槽** improve a patient's ___ of life，所有格+of 锁定名词
**依据** quality of life 是英语固定搭配improve a patient's __(35)__ of life 中，quality of life「生活质量」是医学/社科语境里的高频固定表达，与前文 decrease the cost of care 并列，逻辑顺。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
I) phase phase of life 偏「人生阶段」，与「改善」不搭phase of life 表示「人生的某个阶段」，可以「进入」一个 phase 但谈不上 improve a phase of life；这里要的是生活的「品质」可以被提升，phase 在搭配上和语义上都对不上。

title: Katharine Abraham, an economics professor, was chatting with…

sentences.text: Katharine Abraham, an economics professor, was chatting with her hairdresser(理发师) about retirement plans.
The economist said she plans to continue working because she wants to.
The hairdresser agreed but for a different reason: She needs the money.

passage.translation: 经济学教授Katharine Abraham正在与她的理发师闲聊退休计划。这位经济学家说她计划继续工作，因为她想这样做。理发师表示同意，但原因不同：她需要钱。

sentences.text: Both scenarios(情况) are contributing to a big increase in the number of people in the U.S. working into their 70s.
Over the past 20 years, the share of Americans working in their 70s has risen from less than 10% to nearly 15%.

passage.translation: 这两种情况都促使美国70多岁仍在工作的人数大幅增加。在过去20年里，70多岁仍在工作的美国人比例已从不到10%上升到近15%。

sentences.text: In addition to people being healthier and living much longer, economists say that a combination of financial considerations such as years of slow rise in real wages and a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector are some of the reasons people delay retirement.

The decline of manufacturing and the increase in the number of people working in less labor-intensive occupations also has contributed to the trend, says Abraham, who researches work and retirement decisions of older Americans.

passage.translation: 除了人们更健康、寿命更长之外，经济学家表示，实际工资多年缓慢增长以及私营部门传统养老金制度的转变等一系列财务因素，是人们推迟退休的部分原因。制造业的衰落和从事劳动密集程度较低职业的人数增加也促成了这一趋势，研究美国老年人工作和退休决策的Abraham说。

sentences.text: "Which matters more depends on what your history up until that point has been in the type of work you're doing," Abraham says.

passage.translation: Abraham说："哪个因素更重要取决于你在那之前从事的工作类型的历史。"

sentences.text: The overall trend is hitting Americans of all different levels of educational attainment, although the percentages vary by category.
The share of Americans with bachelor's degrees who were working into their 70s reached nearly 20% in 2018.
For those with a high school degree or less, the proportion of those working in their 70s had risen to around 10%, while those with some college education were in the middle at around 15%.

passage.translation: 这一总体趋势正影响着所有不同教育程度的美国人，尽管各类别的百分比有所不同。拥有学士学位的美国人中，在70多岁仍在工作的比例在2018年达到近20%。对于那些拥有高中或更低学历的人，70多岁仍在工作的比例已上升至约10%,而那些受过一些大学教育的人则处于中间水平，约为15%。

sentences.text: Martin Neil Baily, an economist who is leading a research project on retirement security, notes that quitting a career can lead to feelings of isolation and loneliness, particularly for men.
He suggests that many college-educated workers are choosing to stay in the labor force more for social benefits than for financial reasons.
They're also more likely to be in professional occupations where they tend to enjoy their work more.

passage.translation: 正在领导一项退休保障研究项目的经济学家Martin Neil Baily指出，结束职业生涯可能会导致孤立感和孤独感，尤其是对男性而言。他认为，许多受过大学教育的工作者选择留在劳动力市场更多是为了社交利益而非经济原因。他们也更有可能从事专业职业，往往更享受自己的工作。

sentences.text: Workers in more physical jobs, meanwhile, may be more likely to look forward to retiring, Baily says, suggesting those who stay on are more likely doing so for financial reasons.

passage.translation: 与此同时,从事体力工作的工作者可能更倾向于期待退休，Baily说，这表明那些继续工作的人更有可能是出于经济原因。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about the economics professor and her hairdresser?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
从文章中我们了解到关于经济学教授和她的理发师什么信息?
A) 他们继续工作的原因不同。
B) 他们都致力于工作到70多岁。
C) 他们对目前的财务状况感到满意。
D) 他们对推迟退休持有不同的看法。
**判型** 题干 What do we learn from the passage about the economics professor and her hairdresser 锁定两位具体人物，要在原文里抓他们各自的具体说法，属于事实型细节题。
**拆句** 句子主干是 What do we learn from the passage about ...，about 引出涉及的对象；并列结构 the economics professor and her hairdresser 由 and 连接两个名词短语，无从句、无否定，结构平直无陷阱。
**定位** 经济学家说她打算继续工作，因为她想这样做。理发师也同意继续工作，但理由不同：她需要钱。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确The hairdresser agreed but for a different reason ↔They differ in their reasons for continuing to work预判强调 "两人继续工作的理由不同"，A 项 They differ in their reasons for continuing to work 恰好对此点 100% 命中，无引申无超纲，可直接锁定。
B) 答非所问B 项 They are both committed to working into their 70s 把题目焦点偏到 "是否都坚持工作到 70 多岁"，但题目问的是 "对照两人有何不同"，不是问共同点。
C) 无中生有C 项 They are happy about their current financial situation 说两人都对当前财务状况满意，但理发师明确说 She needs the money，怎么也谈不上 happy。
D) 偷换概念D 项 They hold different views about postponing retirement 似乎与 A 相近，但different views about postponing retirement 意为 "在是否推迟退休这件事上观点不同"，而原文里两人都决定继续工作，差异在理由而不在观点。
questions.quote: The economist said she plans to continue working because she wants to. The hairdresser agreed but for a different reason: She needs the money.

options.text: They differ in their reasons for continuing to work.
They are both committed to working into their 70s.
They are happy about their current financial situation.
They hold different views about postponing retirement.

questions.prompt: What is one of the reasons for people to delay retirement?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
人们推迟退休的原因之一是什么?
A) 越来越多的人转向了智力挑战性较低的工作。
B) 私营部门适合老年人的工作岗位数量增加了。
C) 多年来,按购买力计算的工资增长率有所放缓。
D) 职场中越来越多的人发现难以依靠传统养老金。
**判型** 题干 What is one of the reasons for people to delay retirement 询问具体原因，要在原文清单里点对清单项，属典型细节题。
**拆句** 主干 What is one of the reasons，后接介词短语 for people to delay retirement 作后置定语；for 引导原因方向，不定式 to delay 表逻辑动作，结构清晰，无难点。
**定位** 除了人们更健康、寿命更长之外，经济学家说，多重经济因素的叠加——例如实际工资多年增长缓慢，以及私人部门远离传统养老金——是人们延迟退休的部分原因。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文说 the increase in the number of people working in less labor-intensive occupations——是 "从事劳动强度小的职业的人变多"，A 项 less intellectually challenging jobs 偷换为 "智力上挑战较小的工作"，labor-intensive（体力密集）与intellectually challenging（智力挑战）不是一回事。
B) 无中生有B 项 The number of jobs suitable for older people has increased in the private sector 说私人部门里适合老年人的岗位增多，但原文 a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector 谈的是养老金机制远离传统模式，并未谈岗位数量的变化。
C) ✓ 正确years of slow rise in real wages ↔The rate of wage increase in terms of purchasing power has slowed down for years预判锁定 "实际工资多年涨得慢"，C 项 The rate of wage increase in terms of purchasing power has slowed down for years 把同一信息用购买力的角度表达，是教科书式同义替换。
D) 偷换概念原文 a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector 是 "私人部门正在远离传统养老金"——指制度变化；D 项 find it hard to rely on traditional pensions偷换成 "人们觉得难以依赖传统养老金"——指主观感受。两者方向虽近，但原文从未谈及人们的主观难度感。
questions.quote: In addition to people being healthier and living much longer, economists say that a combination of financial considerations such as years of slow rise in real wages and a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector are some of the reasons people delay retirement.

options.text: More and more people have switched to less intellectually challenging jobs.
The number of jobs suitable for older people has increased in the private sector.
The rate of wage increase in terms of purchasing power has slowed down for years.
More and more people in the workplace find it hard to rely on traditional pensions.

questions.prompt: What is the general trend in people delaying retirement?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
人们推迟退休的总体趋势是什么?
A) 收入越高,他们越有可能倾向于推迟退休。
B) 工作满意度更高的人往往比满意度较低的人退休得更晚。
C) 留在劳动力市场直到70多岁的男性可能多于女性。
D) 教育水平越高,他们越有可能推迟退休。
**判型** 题干 What is the general trend in people delaying retirement 询问的是原文里已经写明的整体规律，去找总括句即可，不需越级推断。
**拆句** 主干 What is the general trend，介词短语 in people delaying retirement 中 people delaying retirement 是 in 的复合宾语（动名词短语带逻辑主语），结构平直、无从句。
**定位** 这一整体趋势影响着所有学历层次的美国人，尽管各类别的比例有所不同。拥有本科学历、且仍在 70 多岁工作的美国人比例在 2018 年达到近 20%；高中及以下学历者比例约10%；有部分大学经历者居中，约 15%。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有A 项 The higher their earnings, the more likely they are tempted to delay retirement 把维度换成 earnings（收入），原文 all different levels of educational attainment 谈的是学历，没有任何收入分层数据。
B) 张冠李戴B 项 Those who have more job satisfaction tend to retire later than those who have less 谈职业满意度的影响，但本段只有学历分层数据，没有关于 job satisfaction的对比；此话题虽在第 6 段简短出现，与 "general trend" 不是同一议题。
C) 张冠李戴C 项 More men than women are likely to stay in the labor force until their late seventies 涉及性别差异，原文虽然第 6 段提到 particularly for men，但那是讲孤独感、不是 general trend 数据；本段从未做性别对比。
D) ✓ 正确The share of Americans with bachelor's degrees who were working into their 70s reached nearly 20%↔ The higher their educational level, the more likely they are to delay retirement预判出 "学历越高，延迟退休比例越高"，D 项 The higher their educational level, the more likely they are to delay retirement 正是这一规律的语句化，无遗漏无超纲。
questions.quote: The overall trend is hitting Americans of all different levels of educational attainment, although the percentages vary by category. The share of Americans with bachelor's degrees who were working into their 70s reached nearly 20% in 2018. For those with a high school degree or less, the proportion of those working in their 70s had risen to around 10%, while those with some college education were in the middle at around 15%.

options.text: The higher their earnings, the more likely they are tempted to delay retirement.
Those who have more job satisfaction tend to retire later than those who have less.
More men than women are likely to stay in the labor force until their late seventies.
The higher their educational level, the more likely they are to delay retirement.

questions.prompt: What is the chief reason for college-educated workers delaying retirement according to an economist?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
根据一位经济学家的说法,受过大学教育的工人推迟退休的主要原因是什么?
A) 享有财务保障。
B) 保持社交联系。
C) 在专业方面做出更多贡献。
D) 增加社会保障金支付。
**判型** 题干 What is the chief reason for college-educated workers delaying retirement 询问原文中经济学家明确给出的主因，按细节题处理即可。
**拆句** 主干 What is the chief reason，介词短语 for college-educated workers delaying retirement 作后置定语，分词 delaying 修饰 workers 表正在延迟；末尾 according to an economist 是插入限定信息源，结构清晰。
**定位** 他指出，许多受过大学教育的劳动者选择继续留在劳动力市场，更多是出于社交方面的好处，而不是经济原因。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反A 项 Enjoying financial security 把主因说成 "享受经济保障"，但原文明确 more for social benefits than for financial reasons —— financial 恰恰是被否定的次要原因，A 项正好反向。
B) ✓ 正确more for social benefits than for financial reasons ↔ Staying connected socially预判抓 social benefits，B 项 Staying connected socially 正面命中；其余选项均与social 无直接对应，可一眼锁定。
C) 过度推断C 项 Contributing more professionally 说 "在专业上贡献更多"，原文 in professional occupations where they tend to enjoy their work more 只说他们多从事专业职业、并享受工作，并未提 "为了贡献更多" 才不退休。
D) 无中生有D 项 Increasing social security payments 把 social 与 financial 拼成 "提高社会保障金"，是基于熟词 social 的乱凑，原文从未提及社会保障金（social security 是美国福利专名）。
questions.quote: He suggests that many college-educated workers are choosing to stay in the labor force more for social benefits than for financial reasons.

options.text: Enjoying financial security.
Staying connected socially.
Contributing more professionally.
Increasing social security payments.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about people doing manual work?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
文章关于从事体力劳动的人说了什么?
A) 他们渴望退休后享受生活。
B) 他们可能会遇到财务困难。
C) 他们通常不喜欢做这种工作。
D) 他们倾向于期待退休。
**判型** 题干 What does the passage say about people doing manual work 直接问原文对该群体的具体说法，按细节题处理。
**拆句** 主干 What does the passage say about ...，about 引出对象；现在分词短语 doing manual work 后置修饰 people，相当于 who do manual work，无从句无难点。
**定位** 另一方面，从事体力劳动较多的工人则可能更期待退休；Baily 说，那些继续留下来的多半是出于经济原因。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断A 项 They are eager to enjoy life after retiring 把原文 "期待退休" 引申到 "渴望享受退休后的生活"，原文只说期待退休、未提退休后做什么，引申了一步。
B) 过度推断B 项 They are likely to have financial troubles 把原文 those who stay on are more likely doing so for financial reasons 推到 "会陷入经济困境"，但 for financial reasons 只说 "出于经济原因"，不等同于 financial troubles。
C) 无中生有C 项 They generally don't enjoy doing it 说 "他们通常不喜欢做这工作"，但原文只说他们更期待退休、并未直接评价是否喜欢工作；不能由 "期待退休" 直接等同 "不喜欢工作"。
D) ✓ 正确may be more likely to look forward to retiring↔They tend to anticipate retirement预判抓 "期待退休"，D 项 They tend to anticipate retirement 是 look forward to retiring 的标准英英同义替换，选定无误。
questions.quote: Workers in more physical jobs, meanwhile, may be more likely to look forward to retiring, Baily says, suggesting those who stay on are more likely doing so for financial reasons.

options.text: They are eager to enjoy life after retiring.
They are likely to have financial troubles.
They generally don't enjoy doing it.
They tend to anticipate retirement.

title: All living organisms on Earth are exposed to…

sentences.text: All living organisms on Earth are exposed to a 24-hour day-night cycle.
This cycle is the reason why people rest at night and are active during the day.
Consequently, all human body functions also follow this daily rhythm, and the timing of behaviors like exercise or food intake can significantly influence your health.
For example, eating at night can lead to weight gain over time because food intake at night leads to increased fat storage.

passage.translation: 地球上所有生物都暴露在24小时昼夜循环之中。这种循环是人们夜间休息、白天活动的原因。因此,所有人体功能也遵循这一日常节律,而运动或进食等行为的时间安排可以显著影响您的健康。例如,夜间进食会随着时间推移导致体重增加,因为夜间摄入食物会导致脂肪储存增加。

sentences.text: Many drug targets in the body follow a 24-hour cycle, too.
This means that the specific proteins a drug is designed to modify can react differently to the medicine over the course of a 24-hour time period.

Because how the body responds to a drug can differ depending on the time it is taken, it logically follows that taking medicines at specific times could help increase their effectiveness and reduce unwanted side effects.

passage.translation: 体内许多药物靶点也遵循24小时周期。这意味着药物旨在修饰的特定蛋白质在24小时时间段内对药物的反应可能有所不同。由于身体对药物的反应会因服药时间而异,因此合乎逻辑的是,在特定时间服药可能有助于提高药效并减少不良副作用。

sentences.text: When doctors prescribe medicine for people, they rarely consider the best time to take it.
There are two main reasons for that oversight.
First, many physicians are not aware that some drugs work better during a specific time of the day.
And second, most drugs have not been studied for possible different effects during a 24-hour cycle.
Therefore, patients are directed to take most drugs during the morning or evening primarily to ensure compliance.

passage.translation: 当医生为患者开药时,他们很少考虑最佳服药时间。这种疏忽有两个主要原因。首先,许多医生不知道某些药物在一天中的特定时间效果更好。其次,大多数药物尚未就24小时周期内可能产生的不同效果进行研究。因此,患者被指示在早晨或晚上服用大多数药物,主要是为了确保依从性。

sentences.text: Over 50 years ago, researchers found that the cholesterol drug simvastatin is more effective at lowering cholesterol levels when taken at night rather than during the day.
This is because the liver enzyme(酶) these drugs target is more active at night.

passage.translation: 50多年前,研究人员发现降胆固醇药物辛伐他汀在夜间服用比白天服用更能有效降低胆固醇水平。这是因为这些药物针对的肝酶在夜间更为活跃。

sentences.text: Taking medicine at the wrong time can even cause harm.
My colleagues and I wondered whether midazolam, the most common sedative(镇静剂) used in surgical procedures worldwide, might interfere with the internal clock that protects the heart at night.
Currently, there are no guidelines regarding when midazolam should be administered.

passage.translation: 在错误的时间服药甚至可能造成伤害。我和同事们想知道咪达唑仑——全球外科手术中最常用的镇静剂——是否会干扰夜间保护心脏的内部时钟。目前,关于何时应给予咪达唑仑尚无指南。

sentences.text: More research is needed to determine the best times to administer treatments for different diseases.
I believe taking drug timing into account could help make treatments more effective and help more people worldwide.

passage.translation: 需要更多研究来确定针对不同疾病实施治疗的最佳时间。我相信将药物给药时间纳入考虑可以帮助使治疗更有效,并帮助全世界更多的人。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about the timing of our behaviors?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
从文章中我们了解到关于我们行为时机的什么信息?
A) 它对我们的健康有相当大的影响。
B) 它将我们限制在24小时昼夜周期中。
C) 它要求我们遵循特定的节律。
D) 它掌握着所有人体功能的关键。
**判型** What do we learn from the passage about ... 问的是文章就「行为时机」明说了什么，答案应能在原文直接找到对应句，不需推断。
**拆句** 题干 What do we learn from the passage about the timing of our behaviors? 是一个what 引导的特殊疑问句，主干是「我们从文中得知什么」，about 短语把范围锁定在「我们行为的时机」上。结构平铺直叙，无从句、无否定，唯一要抓的是 about 后面的话题词，它指明这道题只问「行为时机」相关的内容。
**定位** 因此，人体的所有功能也都遵循这一日常节律，而锻炼、进食等行为的时机会显著影响你的健康。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确can significantly influence your health ↔ It has a considerable impact on our health预判「行为时机大大影响健康」与 It has a considerable impact on our health 完全吻合，故锁定该项。
B) 偷换概念原文是「昼夜周期导致行为有节律」，It confines us to a 24-hour day-night cycle 却说「行为时机把我们限制在 24 小时周期里」，把因当成了果，与原文 This cycle is the reason why people rest at night and are active during the day 相悖。
C) 张冠李戴It requires us to follow a particular rhythm 说「行为时机要求我们遵循某节律」，但原文里「遵循节律」的主体是人体功能（all human body functions also follow this daily rhythm），并非由「行为时机」提出要求。
D) 过度推断It holds the key to all human body functions 称行为时机「掌握着人体所有功能的关键」，原文只说人体功能遵循节律、行为时机影响健康，从未说时机决定一切功能，all与 holds the key 属夸大。
questions.quote: Consequently, all human body functions also follow this daily rhythm, and the timing of behaviors like exercise or food intake can significantly influence your health.

options.text: It has a considerable impact on our health.
It confines us to a 24-hour day-night cycle.
It requires us to follow a particular rhythm.
It holds the key to all human body functions.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about the proteins in our body?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者关于我们体内的蛋白质说了什么?
A) 它们能以不同方式改变药物的效果。
B) 它们能减少某些药物不想要的副作用。
C) 它们对药物的反应在昼夜周期中会发生变化。
D) 它们的设计决定了它们对药物反应的不同方式。
**判型** What does the author say about the proteins 问作者对蛋白质的明确陈述，答案落在讲蛋白质的那句话里，属客观查找而非推断。
**拆句** 题干 What does the author say about the proteins in our body? 主干是「作者关于我们体内的蛋白质说了什么」，say about 后面的 the proteins in our body 是话题。注意四个选项都是完整句子，需要逐个判断哪句和原文一致，题干本身无陷阱。
**定位** 这意味着，药物所要作用的那些特定蛋白质，在 24 小时的进程中对药物的反应可能各不相同。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反They can modify the effects of medicines in different ways 说「蛋白质改变药物的效果」，但原文是药物去作用（modify）蛋白质（the specific proteins a drug is designed to modify），施受关系正好相反。
B) 张冠李戴They can reduce unwanted side effects of certain medicines 把「减少副作用」说成蛋白质的能力，可原文里减副作用的是「按特定时间服药」这一做法（taking medicines at specific times could help increase their effectiveness and reduce unwanted side effects），与蛋白质无关。
C) ✓ 正确can react differently to the medicine over the course of a 24-hour time period ↔Their reaction to medicines changes during the day-night cycle预判「蛋白质对药反应随时段变化」正是 Their reaction to medicines changes during the day-night cycle 所述，锁定该项。
D) 无中生有Their design determines how differently they react to medicines 称「蛋白质的设计决定其反应差异」，原文从未谈蛋白质有何 design，更没说设计决定反应，纯属臆造。
questions.quote: This means that the specific proteins a drug is designed to modify can react differently to the medicine over the course of a 24-hour time period.

options.text: They can modify the effects of medicines in different ways.
They can reduce unwanted side effects of certain medicines.
Their reaction to medicines changes during the day-night cycle.
Their design determines how differently they react to medicines.

questions.prompt: What do doctors do when prescribing medicine for people?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
医生在为人们开药时会做什么?
A) 他们很少考虑服药时间以达到最大效果。
B) 他们很少考虑哪种药物对哪个患者更有效。
C) 他们告诉患者药物在24小时内可能产生的副作用。
D) 他们告诉患者遵守药品生产商的说明。
**判型** What do doctors do when prescribing medicine 问医生实际做了什么，是可在原文直接核对的事实。
**拆句** 题干 What do doctors do when prescribing medicine for people? 主干「医生开药时做什么」，when prescribing 是时间状语（现在分词作状语，相当于 when they prescribe）。结构清晰，关键是抓 doctors 与 prescribing 这一动作场景。
**定位** 医生给人们开药时，很少考虑服药的最佳时间。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确they rarely consider the best time to take it ↔They give little thought to the time of taking it for maximum effect预判「医生很少考虑最佳服药时间」与 They give little thought to the time of taking it for maximum effect 一致，锁定该项。
B) 偷换概念They rarely consider which medicine works better for which patient 把疏忽的对象换成「哪种药对哪个病人更好」，而原文疏忽的是服药「时间」，话题被悄悄换掉。
C) 偷换概念They tell patients its possible side effects during a period of 24 hours 说医生告知24 小时内的副作用，原文讲的是药物未被研究其昼夜差异（most drugs have not been studied for possible different effects during a 24-hour cycle），并非医生告知副作用。
D) 偷换概念They tell patients to comply with the directions of drug manufacturers 说让病人遵从药厂说明，但原文 compliance 指病人遵从医嘱按时服药（patients are directed to take most drugs during the morning or evening primarily to ensure compliance），并未提 drug manufacturers。
questions.quote: When doctors prescribe medicine for people, they rarely consider the best time to take it.

options.text: They give little thought to the time of taking it for maximum effect.
They rarely consider which medicine works better for which patient.
They tell patients its possible side effects during a period of 24 hours.
They tell patients to comply with the directions of drug manufacturers.

questions.prompt: Why do doctors advise patients to take most drugs in the morning or in the evening?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
为什么医生建议患者在早上或晚上服用大多数药物?
A) 为了阻止他们提出投诉。
B) 为了确保他们按照指示服药。
C) 为了严格遵守新的研究发现。
D) 为了保证药物的最大效果。
**判型** Why do doctors advise ... 问的是原文已经给出的理由，定位到目的状语即可作答，不需自己推因果。
**拆句** 题干 Why do doctors advise patients to take most drugs in the morning or in the evening? 是 why 引导的因果问句，主干「医生为何建议病人在早上或晚上服大多数药」。advise sb. to do 是「建议某人做某事」结构。问 why 意味着答案是原文里这一建议背后的目的或原因。
**定位** 因此，病人被指示在早上或晚上服用大多数药物，主要是为了确保遵医服药。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有To discourage them from making complaints 说目的是「阻止病人投诉」，原文目的只有 ensure compliance，从未提 complaints，凭空捏造。
B) ✓ 正确to ensure compliance ↔ To ensure they take the drugs as instructed预判「为确保病人按医嘱服药」与 To ensure they take the drugs as instructed 同义，锁定该项。
C) 与原文相反To comply with new research findings strictly 说目的是严格遵循新研究成果，但原文恰恰指出多数药未做昼夜研究（most drugs have not been studied），医生让早晚服药并非依据研究，方向相反。
D) 与原文相反To guarantee the maximum effect of the drugs 说目的是保证药效最大，但全文论点正是医生没考虑增效时机（they rarely consider the best time to take it），早晚服药并非为了药效最大化，正好相反。
questions.quote: Therefore, patients are directed to take most drugs during the morning or evening primarily to ensure compliance.

options.text: To discourage them from making complaints.
To ensure they take the drugs as instructed.
To comply with new research findings strictly.
To guarantee the maximum effect of the drugs.

questions.prompt: What does the author suggest near the end of the passage?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （主旨题）
**题目译文**
作者在文章结尾处建议了什么?
A) 在为患者开药时考虑服药时机。
B) 通过将服药时机纳入考虑使治疗变得不那么复杂。
C) 开展更多研究以找出治疗不同疾病的最佳时机。
D) 通过进一步研究找出治疗疾病最有效的药物。
**判型** What does the author suggest near the end 问作者在收尾处的整体主张，需要把末段的呼吁概括出来，而非抓某个孤立细节。
**拆句** 题干 What does the author suggest near the end of the passage? 主干「作者在文章接近结尾处建议了什么」，suggest 在此是「建议、主张」，near the end of the passage是地点状语，明确把答案锁在文章末段。这是一道带位置提示的建议题。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全Considering drug-taking timing when prescribing drugs for patients 是第三段对医生开药的观点延伸，而题干问的是 near the end 的建议；末段真正的呼吁是「做更多研究」，而非这条局部主张。
B) 无中生有Making treatments less complex by taking drug timing into account 称考虑服药时机可让治疗「不那么复杂」，原文末段只说能让治疗更有效、惠及更多人（could help make treatments more effective and help more people worldwide），从未提less complex。
C) ✓ 正确More research is needed to determine the best times to administer treatments for different diseases↔ Conducting more studies to find out the best timing for treating different diseases预判「需更多研究找最佳给药时机」与 Conducting more studies to find out the best timing for treating different diseases 完全对应，锁定该项。
D) 偷换概念Finding out the most effective drugs for treating diseases through further research 说要研究「最有效的药物」，可末段研究的目标是「最佳给药时间」（the best times to administer treatments），全文谈的是时机而非药物本身，对象被偷换。

options.text: Considering drug-taking timing when prescribing drugs for patients.
Making treatments less complex by taking drug timing into account.
Conducting more studies to find out the best timing for treating different diseases.
Finding out the most effective drugs for treating diseases through further research.

title: People tend to want as many choices as…

sentences.text: People tend to want as many choices as possible.
They believe this will maximize their (26)____of making the best decision.
But research shows that, when it comes to actually making a (27)____from all of these choices, people can become (28)____ and avoid making a decision altogether.
Even worse, when people finally do decide, they are generally less satisfied with their decision and feel more regretful over whatever choice they made.

passage.translation: 人们往往希望有尽可能多的选择。他们认为这将最大化他们做出最佳决策的机会。但研究表明，当真正要从所有这些选择中做出选择时，人们可能会感到困惑并完全避免做决定。更糟糕的是，当人们最终做出决定时，他们通常对自己的决定不太满意，并对他们所做的任何选择感到更加后悔。

sentences.text: Why does this happen?
Research shows that when people choose from many options, they(29)____ more in the decision, but feel less confident in their ability to decide well.
In other words, when we are (30)____ with more choices, making the "right" or "correct" decision begins to feel more(31)____ and, at the same time, more difficult to do.
This may contribute to the deep fear that we will make the wrong decision.

passage.translation: 为什么会发生这种情况?研究表明，当人们从许多选项中进行选择时，他们在决策上投入更多，但对自己做出正确决定的能力却感到不那么自信。换句话说，当我们面临更多选择时，做出"正确"或"恰当"的决定开始变得更加关键，同时也更加难以做到。这可能导致我们深深担心会做出错误的决定。

sentences.text: How can we solve this problem?
I believe this fear could be tempered by putting decisions into perspective.

It might help to remember that many of the choices you make, such as what to have for lunch, will not (32)____ much in the future and that, even more important choices, like accepting a new job, can (33)____ be changed.

It could also help to (34)____ these situations with clear guidelines and ideas of what you want from the (35)____ of options, which can narrow the possible choices, and also make you more confident about your ability to make the right decision.

passage.translation: 我们如何解决这个问题?我认为通过正确看待决策可以缓解这种恐惧。记住你所做的许多选择，比如午餐吃什么，在未来不会有太大影响，可能会有所帮助；而且，即使是更重要的选择，比如接受一份新工作，最终也是可以改变的。在这些情况下，带着明确的指导方针和你想从一系列选项中获得什么的想法进入，也可能会有所帮助，这可以缩小可能的选择范围，也会让你对自己做出正确决定的能力更有信心。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
People tend to want as many choices as possible. They believe this will maximize their {{26}}of making the best decision. But research shows that, when it comes to actually making a {{27}}from all of these choices, people can become {{28}} and avoid making a decision altogether. Even worse, when people finally do decide, they are generally less satisfied with their decision and feel more regretful over whatever choice they made.

Why does this happen? Research shows that when people choose from many options, they{{29}} more in the decision, but feel less confident in their ability to decide well. In other words, when we are {{30}} with more choices, making the "right" or "correct" decision begins to feel more{{31}} and, at the same time, more difficult to do. This may contribute to the deep fear that we will make the wrong decision.

How can we solve this problem? I believe this fear could be tempered by putting decisions into perspective. It might help to remember that many of the choices you make, such as what to have for lunch, will not {{32}} much in the future and that, even more important choices, like accepting a new job, can {{33}} be changed. It could also help to {{34}} these situations with clear guidelines and ideas of what you want from the {{35}} of options, which can narrow the possible choices, and also make you more confident about your ability to make the right decision.

matter

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) chance 名词
**词性槽** 形容词 their 物主代词后 + of 短语，名词性短语中心词
**依据** chance of doing sth = 做……的可能性原句意为「他们相信这样能最大化做出最佳决定的可能性」，maximize the chance of doing sth 是非常稳定的搭配，C 完美契合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) case case of doing 不是「可能性」case 表示「案例、情况」，maximize their case of making 既不成搭配，也与「最大化可能性」的语义不符。
N) selection selection 表「选择动作/选出物」，与 maximize 不搭selection of making the best decision 语义混乱（做最佳决定本身不是「被选出物」），且 N在 27 题处与 making a ___ 搭配更稳，应留给 27 题。

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) selection 名词
**词性槽** 不定冠词 a 后 + from 短语前，名词作宾语
**依据** make a selection from = 从……中做出选择make a selection 是英语里表「做出一次选择」的高频搭配，from all of these choices 表「从所有这些选项中」，正好契合 when it comes to actually making a __(27)__ from all of these choices 想表达的「真要在这些选项里挑一个」。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) case make a case 义为「论证、辩护」，方向跑偏make a case for sth 表「为某事辩护、提出论据」，与「从一堆选项里挑一个」的语义完全不沾边。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) confused 形容词
**词性槽** become 后接形容词/过去分词作表语
**依据** confused = 困惑、不知所措，正好引出「干脆不决定」people can become __(28)__ and avoid making a decision altogether，「变得困惑 →索性不做决定」是顺承的因果，confused 描述心理状态贴合上文 when it comes to actually making a __(27)__ from all of these choices 的为难感。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) crucial 义为「重要的」，与「不做决定」矛盾若代入「become crucial」=「变得重要」，与并列动作「干脆不做决定」逻辑相反，明显方向错位；且 E 更适合后面 31 题描述「决定本身变得重要」。
L) regular 义为「定期的、常规的」，与心理状态不沾边regular 描述事物的频率/规律，「become regular」（变得规律）与本句心理负担的语境毫无关系。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) invest 动词
**词性槽** 主语 people 后缺谓语，且与 feel less confident 并列
**依据** invest more in sth = 在……上投入更多they __(29)__ more in the decision 想说「在这个决定上投入更多（精力/心思）」，invest more in sth 是固定搭配，与下文 but feel less confident 形成「投入更多 → 反而更没信心」的转折，是文章解释「选择悖论」的关键句。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) enter enter in 不成搭配enter 通常直接接宾语（enter a room）或接 into，没有 enter more in the decision 的说法；语义上也无法表达「投入精力」。
I) matter matter 是不及物动词「要紧」，不能接 more in matter 表「要紧」时句式是「sth matters」，不可说「they matter more in the decision」；且 I 的「要紧」义应留给 32 题。
M) seize seize 是「抓住」，常与机会搭配，与「投入更多」不符seize the chance/opportunity 是常用搭配，seize more in the decision 既不成搭配也不合语义。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— F deposited 与 H invest 都跟「投入」沾边，最迷惑。they __(29)__ more in the decision，考生看到 deposited 也有「存放、投入」之意会犹豫；防坑：先看形态——will/they 现在时后只能接动词原形，deposited 直接淘汰；再看搭配——invest in 才是正解。

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) presented 形容词
**词性槽** be 动词 are 后 + 介词 with，典型「be + 形容词 + with」结构
**依据** be presented with 是固定搭配，表「被给予/面对……」when we are __(30)__ with more choices 要表达「当我们被给予/面对更多选择时」，be presented with sth 正是英语里表「被呈上/面对某物」的标准搭配，与下文 making the "right" or "correct" decision begins to feel more __(31)__ 形成「面对多选 → 决定显得更重要」的因果链。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
D) confused confused with 表「把……与……搞混」，方向反了，且已被 28 题用走confused 形容人 confused by/about 才地道，confused with 多用于「把 A 和 B 搞混」（confuse A with B），与本句「面对更多选择」语义不符；并且按解题顺序 D 已先被 28 题people can become __(28)__ 用走，不可再选。
E) crucial义为「至关重要的」，与 with 不搭crucial 后通常接 to/for/in，没有 be crucial with 的用法；意思也偏离「面对更多选择」的语境。
L) regular 义为「定期的、常规的」，与上下文无关regular 与「面对更多选择」毫无语义勾连，be regular with 也不构成本句所需的「面对/被给予」之意。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) crucial 形容词
**词性槽** feel + more + 空，feel 后接形容词作表语
**依据** 和 difficult 并列：决定既「显得更重要」又「更难做」feel more __(31)__ and, at the same time, more difficult to do 用 and 连接两个并列形容词，crucial（重要的）与 difficult（困难的）一起描绘「正确决定变得既重要又难做」，正好引出下文 the deep fear that we will make the wrong decision 的「深深的恐惧」。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
L) regular 义为「常规的」，与「深深的恐惧」逻辑不通若说「正确决定显得更常规、更难做」既自相矛盾（常规的事不该难），也无法解释下文为何会引出「害怕选错」的恐惧。

questions.explanation:
**答案** I) matter 动词
**词性槽** 助动词 not 后 + 副词 much，需要动词原形
**依据** matter much = 关系重大、要紧many of the choices you make, such as what to have for lunch, will not __(32)__much in the future 想说「你做的很多选择，比如午餐吃什么，将来不会有什么要紧的」，will not matter much 是常见表达，与作者主张「把选择放进合适视角」的对策正相呼应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) seize seize 是及物动词，与不及物结构不符seize 后通常接具体宾语（机会、权力），will not seize much in the future 既缺宾语也不合「不重要」之意。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) ultimately 副词
**词性槽** 情态动词 can 后 + 被动语态 be changed 前，副词作状语
**依据** ultimately 表「最终归根到底」，弱化决定的不可逆感even more important choices, like accepting a new job, can __(33)__ be changed 想说「就算是接受新工作这种更重要的选择，归根到底也是可以变的」，与上句 will not__(32)__ much in the future 共同构成「把选择放进合适视角」的两条理由。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) approximately approximately 表「大约」，修饰数字而非动作approximately 用来修饰数量（approximately 100 people），用在 can approximately be changed 既语义不通，也与「最终也可以改」的安抚作用不符。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) enter 动词
**词性槽** 并列 to + 空，需动词原形；与上句 to remember 并列
**依据** enter these situations with ... = 带着……进入这些情境to __(34)__ these situations with clear guidelines and ideas of what you want，「带着清晰的指引和想法去进入/着手这些情境」，enter a situation with sth 是地道说法，表「以某种状态/准备去面对一个局面」，与下文 which can narrow the possible choices 形成「带着准备进入 → 缩小可能选项」的因果链。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) seizeseize 是「抓住、夺取」，对象多为机会/权力seize these situations 表「抓住/夺取这些情境」语义生硬，且与 with clear guidelines 这种「带着方法论」的伴随状语搭不上——seize 强调瞬间、强力的占有，不是「带着准备去面对」。
**易错**

title: "Phantom" Traffic Jams Are Real—And Scientists Know How to Stop Them

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Traffic jams are a common problem of most big cities, either in developed or in developing countries, but one kind of traffic jams in particular can be especially frustrating.
These are generally known as "phantom" traffic jams, in which dense traffic crawls to a halt for no apparent reason at all.

passage.translation: 交通堵塞是大多数大城市的常见问题,无论是在发达国家还是在发展中国家,但有一种交通堵塞尤其令人沮丧。这种堵塞通常被称为"幽灵"交通堵塞,在这种情况下,密集的车流会毫无明显原因地缓慢爬行直至停止。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: "When caught in such a traffic jam, it is common for drivers to assume that there must be an accident, or construction or something," said Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) computer science professor Berthold Horn.
"And then you drive and drive and drive… and there isn't anything there."

passage.translation: "当遇到这种交通堵塞时,司机通常会认为前方一定发生了事故,或者有施工或其他什么情况,"Massachusetts Institute of Technology(MIT)计算机科学教授Berthold Horn说。"然后你不停地开、不停地开、不停地开……结果前面什么都没有。"

passage.label: C

sentences.text: The exact cause of these phantom traffic jams has long remained a mystery.

But now, new research has found the cause and researchers may have come up with a solution for this frustrating traffic pattern: maintaining equal spacing between cars on the road, rather than driving so closely behind another vehicle that a collision(碰撞) is likely if that vehicle brakes suddenly.

passage.translation: 这些幽灵交通堵塞的确切原因长期以来一直是个谜。但现在,新的研究发现了原因,研究人员可能已经找到了解决这种令人沮丧的交通模式的方法:在道路上保持车辆之间的等距间隔,而不是紧紧跟在另一辆车后面,以至于如果前车突然刹车就很可能发生碰撞。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: Horn said phantom traffic jams are an emergent property of the flow of vehicles down a highway.

A phantom jam begins when a car in dense traffic slows down even slightly, which causes the car behind that vehicle to slow even more—and the slowing action spreads backward through the lane of traffic like a wave, getting worse the farther it spreads.
Eventually, the cars far behind are forced to stop completely or risk hitting the slower vehicles ahead—and so the traffic grinds to a halt over nothing, Horn said.

passage.translation: Horn说,幽灵交通堵塞是车辆在高速公路上行驶流量的一个涌现性质。幽灵堵塞始于密集交通中的一辆车哪怕只是轻微减速,这导致该车后面的车减速得更多——减速行为像波浪一样向后传播到整个车道,传播得越远就越严重。最终,远处后面的车被迫完全停下来,否则就有撞上前面较慢车辆的风险——于是交通无缘无故地陷入停滞,Horn说。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Horn has been working on the problem of phantom traffic jams for years, and he has come up with a solution: By splitting the difference between the cars in front and the cars behind, the spacing of cars in a stream of traffic can act as a damper(抑制) on phantom traffic jams.
That is, it can prevent the slow-down effect from being amplified(增强) by the cars that follow behind, he said.
In essence, each driver would constantly make adjustments to keep their car roughly halfway between the car in front and the car behind.

passage.translation: Horn多年来一直在研究幽灵交通堵塞问题,他提出了一个解决方案:通过折中前方车辆和后方车辆之间的距离,车流中车辆的间距可以对幽灵交通堵塞起到抑制作用。也就是说,它可以防止减速效应被后面跟随的车辆增强,他说。从本质上讲,每个司机都会不断调整,使自己的车大致保持在前车和后车之间的中间位置。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: Horn calls this method of vehicle spacing bilateral(双边的) control, and he said it could be achieved with relatively simple modifications to the adaptive cruise control that many new cars already have.
Adaptive cruise control is a driver assistance technology that sets a maximum speed for vehicles and automatically slows the speed of the car when traffic is sensed in front of the vehicle.
The technology is also known as autonomous cruise control.
Such modifications, Horn said, could help fight phantom jams within a few years, maybe decades before an alternative solution, such as networked self-driving cars, becomes a reality on the roads.

passage.translation: Horn将这种车辆间距方法称为双边控制,他说这可以通过对许多新车已经配备的自适应巡航控制系统进行相对简单的改进来实现。自适应巡航控制是一种驾驶辅助技术,它为车辆设定最高速度,并在感应到车辆前方有交通时自动降低车速。该技术也被称为自主巡航控制。Horn说,这种改进可以在几年内帮助对抗幽灵堵塞,这可能比另一种解决方案(如联网自动驾驶汽车)在道路上成为现实早几十年。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: Traffic jams are caused by a number of factors, such as roads that are poorly designed or over- capacity, localized factors like city traffic-lighting patterns, and events like accidents and construction.
But phantom traffic jams can make all those problems worse, Horn said.

And the researchers in the new study have calculated that solving phantom jams could save at least some of the estimated $121 billion per year that traffic jams are estimated to cost the U.S. economy, Horn told Live Science.

passage.translation: 交通堵塞是由许多因素造成的,例如设计不良或超负荷的道路、城市交通信号灯模式等局部因素,以及事故和施工等事件。但幽灵交通堵塞会使所有这些问题变得更糟,Horn说。新研究中的研究人员计算出,解决幽灵堵塞可以节省交通堵塞估计给美国经济造成的每年1210亿美元损失中的至少一部分,Horn告诉Live Science。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: New research by Horn and MIT postdoctoral associate Liang Wang, published in the journal IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems, shows how bilateral control can fight the problem.
The researchers made computer models of real-world traffic conditions, showing how a typical U.S. freeway could benefit from cars using bilateral control.
That would be in place when human drivers fail to slow down, thus avoiding tailgating(紧跟) the car in front, Horn said.
"Under reasonable conditions today, you might get 1,800 cars per lane per hour throughput (the volume of traffic passing through)," he added.
"But with bilateral control, you could almost double that."
Horn和MIT博士后研究员Liang Wang发表在IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation

passage.translation: Systems期刊上的新研究显示了双边控制如何对抗这个问题。研究人员建立了真实交通状况的计算机模型,展示了典型的美国高速公路如何能从使用双边控制的汽车中受益。当人类司机未能减速从而避免紧跟前车时,双边控制就会发挥作用,Horn说。"在今天的合理条件下,你每小时每车道可能获得1800辆车的通行量(通过的交通流量),"他补充道。"但有了双边控制,你几乎可以将其翻倍。"

passage.label: I

sentences.text: The main alternative to increasing traffic throughput per lane has been to build more lanes and more highways, and putting in new roads is very expensive, he said.
"If we can increase the throughput on major highways, even if it's only by 50 percent, that would be a big deal," Horn said.

passage.translation: 增加每车道交通通行量的主要替代方案是修建更多车道和更多高速公路,而铺设新道路非常昂贵,他说。"如果我们能增加主要高速公路的通行量,即使只增加50%,那也将是一件大事,"Horn说。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: With the help of engineering students at high schools in Maine, Horn and Wang have also built a robot simulation(模拟) that shows how bilateral control can suppress phantom traffic jams.
Increasing the spacing of vehicles dampens the effect of slowdowns by cars in front of a given car, so that the slowing is not worsened until it becomes a phantom jam, the researchers said.

passage.translation: 在Maine州高中工程学生的帮助下,Horn和Wang还建立了一个机器人模拟,展示双边控制如何抑制幽灵交通堵塞。增加车辆间距可以抑制给定车辆前方汽车减速的影响,从而使减速不会恶化到形成幽灵堵塞,研究人员说。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: A video from the project shows a train of autonomous robots running along a track without bilateral control; they eventually back up in phantom jams.

But when the robots are switched over to bilateral control (by flashing the lights in the room), each autonomous robot tries to keep itself halfway between the robot in front and the one behind; the phantom jams disappear as a result, Horn said.

passage.translation: 该项目的一段视频显示,一列自主机器人在没有双边控制的情况下沿轨道行驶;它们最终在幽灵堵塞中倒退。但当机器人切换到双边控制(通过闪烁房间内的灯光)时,每个自主机器人都试图将自己保持在前面和后面机器人之间的中间位置;结果幽灵堵塞消失了,Horn说。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: Since starting his research on phantom traffic jams, Horn has learned that schools of fish and flocks of birds and bats use similar spacing strategies to avoid hitting each other while swimming or flying in densely packed groups.

In particular, studies of millions of bats emerging at dusk from caves in Southeast Asia showed that each bat used a form of bilateral control to reduce the likelihood of collisions with other bats in the densely packed swarm(一大群), Horn said.

passage.translation: 自从开始研究幽灵交通堵塞以来,Horn了解到鱼群、鸟群和蝙蝠群使用类似的间距策略,以避免在密集群体中游泳或飞行时相互碰撞。特别是,对东南亚洞穴中黄昏时涌出的数百万只蝙蝠的研究表明,每只蝙蝠都使用一种双边控制形式来减少在密集群体中与其他蝙蝠碰撞的可能性,Horn说。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: Unlike bats, birds and fish, however, humans have difficulty judging distances behind them.

To address that weakness, Horn is now working with the car company Toyota to enable a form of bilateral control via modifications to existing adaptive cruise control systems, which use forward- facing sensors to judge the distance to the vehicle ahead.
The bilateral control approach would include adding rear-facing sensors to determine the distance to the vehicle following a car.

passage.translation: 然而,与蝙蝠、鸟类和鱼类不同,人类很难判断身后的距离。为了解决这一弱点,Horn现在正与汽车公司Toyota合作,通过改进现有的自适应巡航控制系统来实现一种双边控制形式,该系统使用前向传感器来判断与前方车辆的距离。双边控制方法将包括添加后向传感器来确定与跟随车辆的距离。

passage.label: N

sentences.text: But until those systems become standard, human drivers can help reduce phantom traffic jams simply by not following the car in front so closely.
As Horn argues, "There's absolutely no advantage of tailgating the car in front of you."

passage.translation: 但在这些系统成为标准配置之前,人类司机可以通过不那么紧地跟随前车来帮助减少幽灵交通堵塞。正如Horn所说,"紧跟前车绝对没有任何好处。"

title: Is juicing actually good for you?

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Freshly juiced fruit has become a basic dietary item—especially for busy, health-conscious consumers who can save time on making (and perhaps even chewing) their food without missing out on nutrients.
Fruit juice also has been linked to claims that it can help you both lose weight and stay healthy.
All of which, of course, has made it highly profitable.
The global fruit and vegetable juices market was valued at $154 billion in 2016 and is expected to grow.

passage.translation: 鲜榨果汁已成为一种基本的膳食品——尤其是对于忙碌、注重健康的消费者而言,他们可以节省制作(甚至咀嚼)食物的时间,同时又不会错过营养。果汁还与有助于减肥和保持健康的说法联系在一起。所有这些当然使其极具盈利性。2016年全球水果和蔬菜汁市场价值为1540亿美元,预计还将增长。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: But is juicing really as healthy as we think?
Most foods containing fructose—a naturally occurring sugar found in all fruits and fruit juices—don't seem to have harmful effects as long as they're not contributing to excess daily calories.
This is because the fibre found in whole fruits is intact, and the sugar is contained within the fruit's cells.
It takes our digestive system a while to break these cells down and for fructose to enter the bloodstream.

passage.translation: 但榨汁真的像我们认为的那样健康吗?大多数含有果糖的食物——一种天然存在于所有水果和果汁中的糖——只要不导致每日卡路里过量,似乎就没有有害影响。这是因为完整水果中的纤维是完好的,糖被包含在水果的细胞内。我们的消化系统需要一段时间来分解这些细胞,果糖才能进入血液。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: But this is not the case with fruit juice.
Unlike whole fruit, fruit juice has most of the fibre removed.
This is why the fructose in fruit juices counts as 'free sugars'—which also include honey and the sugars added to foods.
It's recommended by the World Health Organisation that adults have no more than 30g of added sugar, the equivalent of 150ml of fruit juice, per day.
The problem is that, with the fibre removed, fruit juice's fructose is absorbed more quickly.
Sudden increases in blood sugar cause the release of insulin(胰岛素) to bring it back down to a stable level.
Over time, this mechanism can wear out, increasing the risk of developing type 2 diabetes.
In 2013, researchers analysed the health data of 100,000 people collected between 1986 and 2009 and found that fruit juice consumption was linked with increased risk of type 2 diabetes.
Another study found a relationship between fruit juice and type 2 diabetes after following the diets and diabetes status of more than 70,000 nurses over 18 years.
The researchers explain that the possible reason for this may partly have been the lack of the other components found in whole fruit, like fibre.

passage.translation: 但果汁的情况并非如此。与完整水果不同,果汁已去除了大部分纤维。这就是为什么果汁中的果糖被算作"游离糖"——其中还包括蜂蜜和添加到食品中的糖。世界卫生组织建议成年人每天摄入的添加糖不超过30克,相当于150毫升果汁。问题在于,去除纤维后,果汁中的果糖被更快地吸收。血糖的突然升高会导致胰岛素释放,使其降回稳定水平。随着时间的推移,这种机制可能会失效,增加患2型糖尿病的风险。2013年,研究人员分析了1986年至2009年间收集的10万人的健康数据,发现饮用果汁与2型糖尿病风险增加有关。另一项研究在跟踪超过7万名护士18年的饮食和糖尿病状况后,发现了果汁与2型糖尿病之间的关系。研究人员解释说,造成这种情况的可能原因可能部分在于缺乏完整水果中的其他成分,如纤维。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: Juices containing vegetables can provide more nutrients and less sugar than juices made up of just fruit—but they still lack valuable fibre.
Diets high in fibre have been linked to a lower risk of developing heart disease, stroke, high blood pressure and diabetes, and it's recommended adults consume 30g per day.

passage.translation: 含有蔬菜的果汁可以提供比纯水果汁更多的营养和更少的糖——但它们仍然缺乏宝贵的纤维。高纤维饮食与降低患心脏病、中风、高血压和糖尿病的风险有关,建议成年人每天摄入30克。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Aside from the link to type 2 diabetes, many studies agree that fruit juice is harmful if it contributes to an excess in calories.

In an analysis of 155 studies, John Sievenpiper, associate professor at the University of Toronto's Department of Nutritional Sciences, set out to understand if the associations between sugary soft drinks and health—including risk of diabetes and heart disease—were applicable to the food and drink we generally consume as part of a healthy diet.
He compared studies looking into the effects of fructose-containing sugars with control diets free from or lower in these sugars.
His aim?
To isolate the effects of consuming too many calories from the effects of foods containing different sugars.

passage.translation: 除了与2型糖尿病的关联外,许多研究都认为,如果果汁导致卡路里过量,它就是有害的。在对155项研究的分析中,多伦多大学营养科学系副教授John Sievenpiper着手了解含糖软饮料与健康之间的关联——包括糖尿病和心脏病风险——是否适用于我们通常作为健康饮食一部分而摄入的食物和饮料。他比较了研究含果糖糖类影响的研究与不含或较少含这些糖类的对照饮食。他的目的?将摄入过多卡路里的影响与含有不同糖类的食物的影响分离开来。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: He found negative effects on blood sugar and insulin levels when food provided excess calories from sugars, including fruit juice.
However, when the calories weren't in excess overall, there were some advantages to consuming whole fruit—and even fruit juice.
Sievenpiper concludes that the recommended 150ml of fruit juice per day, which is an average serving, is reasonable.
The paper concluded that foods containing fructose may have some small benefits for long-term blood sugar control when they don't lead to over-consumption of calories.
But when they do lead to too many calories, they risk raising blood sugar and insulin levels.

passage.translation: 他发现,当食物提供来自糖(包括果汁)的过量卡路里时,会对血糖和胰岛素水平产生负面影响。然而,当卡路里总体上没有过量时,摄入完整水果——甚至果汁——有一些好处。Sievenpiper得出结论,推荐的每天150毫升果汁(这是平均份量)是合理的。该论文得出结论,当含果糖的食物不导致卡路里过度摄入时,可能对长期血糖控制有一些小的益处。但当它们确实导致过多卡路里时,就有升高血糖和胰岛素水平的风险。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: So while we know that fruit juice can cause diabetes if it's part of a diet that has more calories overall, it's less clear how juice affects the long-term health of those who aren't overweight.
But we have a higher risk of consuming more than the recommended daily number of calories (around 2,000 for women and 2,500 for men) on the days we drink juice, according to research.
Numerous studies have shown that drinking fruit juice doesn't make us consume any less of other foods throughout the day.

passage.translation: 因此,虽然我们知道如果果汁是整体卡路里过多的饮食的一部分,它可能导致糖尿病,但对于那些不超重的人,果汁如何影响其长期健康就不太清楚了。但根据研究,在我们喝果汁的日子里,我们摄入超过建议的每日卡路里数(女性约2000,男性约2500)的风险更高。大量研究表明,喝果汁并不会让我们全天减少其他食物的摄入。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: As it is easy to consume large amounts of fruit juice quite quickly, extra calories are taken in.
And extra calories can contribute to weight gain.

One way we can improve the effects of fruit juice on our health is making sure we select ripe fruit to retain as much of its goodness as possible, according to Roger Clemens, professor of pharmaceutical(药物的) sciences at the University of Southern California.

passage.translation: 由于很容易快速摄入大量果汁,就会摄入额外的卡路里。而额外的卡路里会导致体重增加。南加州大学药物科学教授Roger Clemens表示,我们可以通过确保选择成熟的水果来尽可能保留其营养价值,从而改善果汁对我们健康的影响。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Another reason for fruit juice's recent popularity is the argument that it can help to remove poisonous or harmful substances from the body.
However, "the whole concept of a juice diet helping to remove poisonous or harmful substances from the body is completely false," says Clemens.
"We consume compounds every day that may be poisonous and our bodies do a wonderful job of removing and eliminating anything harmful from our bodies."

passage.translation: 果汁最近流行的另一个原因是,它可以帮助清除体内有毒或有害物质的说法。然而,"果汁饮食有助于清除体内有毒或有害物质的整个概念是完全错误的,"Clemens说。"我们每天都会摄入可能有毒的化合物,而我们的身体在清除和排出体内任何有害物质方面做得非常好。"

passage.label: J

sentences.text: And juice isn't a cure-all for getting your nutrients, either.
"There are a lot of nutrients contained in the parts of the fruits, such as in apple skins, that are excluded when you juice them," says Heather Ferris, a professor of medicine.
"You end up with sugary water with some vitamins."

passage.translation: 果汁也不是获取营养的万能药。医学教授Heather Ferris说:"水果的某些部分含有大量营养成分,比如苹果皮,但当你榨汁时这些部分被排除在外了。""你最终得到的是含有一些维生素的糖水。"

passage.label: K

sentences.text: Plus, she adds, it's not an ideal way to reach the advised 'five a day'.
"People try to get five servings of fruit and vegetables per day and don't realise this isn't just about getting vitamins," she says.
"It's also about reducing the amount of grain carbs(碳水化合物) and protein and fats in our diet, and increasing fibre."
So while fruit juice is better than no fruit at all, there are limits.
It particularly comes with risks when we consume more than 150ml of free sugars per day, or when it puts us over our recommended calorie intake.
It provides us with vitamins—but fruit juice is far from a quick fix.

passage.translation: 此外,她补充说,这不是达到建议的"每天五份"的理想方式。"人们试图每天摄入五份水果和蔬菜,却没有意识到这不仅仅是为了获取维生素,"她说。"这也是为了减少我们饮食中谷物碳水化合物、蛋白质和脂肪的量,并增加纤维。"因此,虽然果汁总比完全不吃水果好,但也有其局限性。特别是当我们每天摄入超过150毫升游离糖,或当它使我们超过建议的卡路里摄入量时,就会带来风险。它为我们提供维生素——但果汁远非速效药。
