sentences.text: Recently, a leading design federation in the UK warned that the UK could face a creative skills shortage, after the latest figures revealed a drop of almost 10 percent in students studying Design and Technology.
These figures showed that the number of pupils that sat exams in Design and Technology fell 10 percent from 204,788 to 185,279 last year.

passage.translation: 最近,英国一家领先的设计联合会警告说,在最新数据显示学习设计与技术的学生人数下降近10%之后,英国可能面临创意技能短缺。这些数据显示,去年参加设计与技术考试的学生人数从204,788人下降到185,279人,降幅达10%。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: Chief executive John Kampfner of the Creative Industries Federation thinks that this drop in figures has worrying implications for the skills pipeline in Britain's hugely successful arts and creative industries.
He said, "We already have skills shortages in many jobs such as animation(动画制作) and special effects."
He added: "Engineering, which requires a similar mix of creative and technical skills, also has recruitment problems."

passage.translation: Creative Industries Federation的首席执行官John Kampfner认为,这一数字下降对英国极为成功的艺术和创意产业的技能储备有令人担忧的影响。他说:"我们在许多工作岗位上已经出现技能短缺,比如动画制作和特效。"他补充道:"工程领域也需要类似的创意和技术技能组合,同样存在招聘问题。"

passage.label: C

sentences.text: Many other designers and architects have expressed concern over the future supply of home-grown talent for UK firms, and industry bodies have pointed out that there has been a lack of roots-level support.
However, if these designers had visited the Design Museum shop in London earlier this year their fears may have been eased.
With £10 to spend, they could have bought a fascinating children's toy called "Dazzle Racer".
An automotive cylinder(圆柱体), it included a wind-up, elastic(有弹性的)- band-powered mechanism, minimal parts, all 100 percent recycled, and lots of stickers.
It was good fun, simple, eye-catching and very original.

passage.translation: 许多其他设计师和建筑师对英国公司未来本土人才的供应表示担忧,行业机构也指出基础层面的支持一直不足。然而,如果这些设计师今年早些时候参观过伦敦Design Museum的商店,他们的担忧可能会得到缓解。只需花10英镑,他们就能买到一款名为"Dazzle Racer"的迷人儿童玩具。这是一个汽车圆柱体,包含一个上发条的橡皮筋动力机制,零件极少,全部100%可回收,还有很多贴纸。它很有趣、简单、引人注目,而且非常新颖。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: Well, you'd expect the Design Museum to commission and make some interesting items, but this one was different.

Designed by a group of six Year 9 and Year 10 boys from Finchley Catholic High School, the toy was the winning entry in the museum's 2015 Design Ventura competition, which brings the business of design to life for students aged 13 to 16 by challenging them to develop a new creative, sustainable and commercially feasible product for the Design Museum shop and attracts hundreds of entries nationwide.

passage.translation: 当然,你会期待Design Museum委托制作一些有趣的物品,但这个不同。这款玩具由Finchley Catholic High School六名九年级和十年级男生组成的小组设计,是该博物馆2015年Design Ventura竞赛的获奖作品。该竞赛通过挑战13至16岁学生为Design Museum商店开发新的创意、可持续且商业可行的产品,将设计业务带入学生生活,吸引了全国数百个参赛作品。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: "We did Design Ventura in my previous school," says Liam Hourican, Finchley Catholic High School's design technology curriculum leader.
"Then when I changed schools four years ago, I introduced it here because it helps to develop so many skills."

passage.translation: Finchley Catholic High School的设计技术课程负责人Liam Hourican说:"我在之前的学校参加过Design Ventura。四年前当我换学校时,我在这里引入了它,因为它有助于培养很多技能。"

passage.label: F

sentences.text: The theme for last year's competition was "Move", and Hourican began with three groups working in lunch breaks and after school before selecting the group with the most innovative idea.
Each participating school may submit just one proposal.
"It's the taking part and doing the work which is important," he says.
"And I never dreamt we'd win."

passage.translation: 去年竞赛的主题是"移动",Hourican最初让三个小组在午休和放学后工作,然后选择了创意最具创新性的小组。每所参赛学校只能提交一份提案。他说:"重要的是参与和做这项工作。我从未想过我们会赢。"

passage.label: G

sentences.text: Catherine Ritman Smith, head of learning at the Design Museum, is expecting around 10,000 participants aged 13 to 16 to take part this year and says that the project—funded by Deutsche Bank as part of its youth engagement programme Born To Be—is the biggest event in the museum's calendar.
"We started Design Ventura with around 800 young people in 2010 and it has grown steadily since," she says.
"Teachers like it because the skills are all transferable and it helps to validate the value of design as a subject," she explains, telling me that nearly 600 schools have taken part so far.

passage.translation: Design Museum学习部主管Catherine Ritman Smith预计今年将有约10,000名13至16岁的参与者参加,并表示该项目是博物馆日程中最大的活动,由Deutsche Bank作为其青年参与计划Born To Be的一部分资助。她说:"我们在2010年以约800名年轻人的规模启动Design Ventura,此后一直在稳步增长。教师喜欢它,因为这些技能都是可转移的,它有助于验证设计作为一门学科的价值。"她告诉我,到目前为止已有近600所学校参加。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: So how does the competition work?
A single-word theme is announced in the summer.
This year it is "Change".
Schools work with groups to produce imaginative design ideas for a product in simple materials that could sell for £10 in the Design Museum shop.
Participating schools then register by November and eventually submit their design idea.
Along the way there is training and support for teachers and tutoring for students from designers.
An additional bonus is when the winners see their design on sale in the spring of the following year.

passage.translation: 那么竞赛如何运作?夏季会公布一个单词主题。今年的主题是"改变"。学校与小组合作,为一个可以在Design Museum商店以10英镑价格出售的简单材料产品提出富有想象力的设计创意。参赛学校随后在11月前注册,最终提交他们的设计创意。在此过程中,设计师为教师提供培训和支持,为学生提供辅导。另一个额外奖励是获奖者在次年春季看到他们的设计在商店出售。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Hourican and his pupils have happy memories of spending a whole day at the museum, having been selected as one of 10 shortlisted schools to present their idea to a panel of judges, including designer Jasper Conran.
Then they worked with the Kin Design Studio in Shoreditch, met designers at their school and attended a lunch with Deutsche Bank employees.
The students helped to make decisions and there were plenty of discussions—they changed the product's name, for example.

passage.translation: Hourican和他的学生对在博物馆度过一整天有美好的回忆,他们作为入围的10所学校之一被选中,向包括设计师Jasper Conran在内的评委小组展示他们的创意。然后他们与Shoreditch的Kin Design Studio合作,在学校与设计师见面,并参加了与Deutsche Bank员工的午餐会。学生们帮助做决定,进行了大量讨论——例如,他们更改了产品的名称。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: "One of the really useful things about this competition," says Hourican, "is that there's a commercial element because the product is going on sale for real and the boys had to learn about budgeting and marketing, as well as designing their game."
Profits go to charity.
"The winning team chooses where it wants the profits to go," says Ritman Smith.
"The Finchley Catholic High School product raised about £1,000 for Great Ormond Street Hospital."
Winning entries in past years have included a make- your-own cloth kit called Dove Bunting and a threefold, wallet-sized travel game with goals at each end, called Badoiiing.

passage.translation: Hourican说:"这个竞赛真正有用的一点是它有商业元素,因为产品要真正销售,男孩们必须学习预算和营销,以及设计他们的游戏。"利润用于慈善。Ritman Smith说:"获胜团队选择利润的去向。Finchley Catholic High School的产品为Great Ormond Street Hospital筹集了约1,000英镑。"过去几年的获奖作品包括一个名为Dove Bunting的自制布料套装和一个钱包大小的三折旅行游戏,两端都有球门,名为Badoiiing。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: It costs the schools nothing to participate in Design Ventura; the professional designers provide their services for free.
Among them are architect Asif Khan, a Design Museum trustee who has worked as designer-in-residence at the museum, helping emerging architects.
He has recently been commissioned to design the new Museum of London building in Smithfield.

passage.translation: 学校参加Design Ventura无需任何费用;专业设计师免费提供服务。其中包括建筑师Asif Khan,他是Design Museum的受托人,曾在博物馆担任驻馆设计师,帮助新兴建筑师。他最近受委托设计位于Smithfield的新Museum of London建筑。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: Another is television presenter and interior designer Naomi Cleaver, who is one of the competition's judges.
"I'm very keen to encourage young people," she says, observing that design brings together other subjects such as literature, art, history, geography and science.
"Now that design education is limited in the curriculum, I'm all in favour of competitions such as Design Ventura, which helps to bring the standard curriculum to life," says Cleaver.
"And the judging day is terrific fun.
Some of these students are very imaginative.
One group presented their idea in the form of a puppet show and we see some marvelous demonstration models.
I'm always impressed by the levels of confidence and the support the students get from their teachers."

passage.translation: 另一位是电视主持人和室内设计师Naomi Cleaver,她是竞赛的评委之一。她说:"我非常热衷于鼓励年轻人。"她观察到设计将文学、艺术、历史、地理和科学等其他学科结合在一起。Cleaver说:"现在设计教育在课程中受到限制,我完全支持像Design Ventura这样的竞赛,它有助于使标准课程生动起来。评审日非常有趣。这些学生中有些人非常富有想象力。一个小组以木偶戏的形式展示了他们的创意,我们看到了一些精彩的演示模型。学生们的自信水平和他们从教师那里得到的支持总是让我印象深刻。"

passage.label: M

sentences.text: Ritman Smith adds: "Design technology has become a tricky subject to make a case for, and we've heard of departments closing in some schools.

We find that if pupils take part in Design Ventura in Year Nine it can be the trigger which leads them to opt for it at General Certificate of Secondary Education, so we are helping to keep alive something which is crucial to industry and entrepreneurship."

passage.translation: Ritman Smith补充说:"设计技术已成为一门难以证明其价值的学科,我们听说一些学校的相关部门正在关闭。我们发现,如果学生在九年级参加Design Ventura,这可能成为促使他们选择参加General Certificate of Secondary Education考试的触发因素,因此我们正在帮助保持对工业和创业至关重要的东西的活力。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: During the course of preparing for Design Ventura, teachers receive training and support while students get tutoring from designers.
questions.explanation:
**答案** H 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
在准备Design Ventura的过程中,教师接受培训和支持,而学生则得到设计师的指导。
**锚点** 教师培训+学生由设计师辅导
**定位** 在这一过程中，老师能获得培训和支持，学生则由设计师提供辅导。
**改写** teachers receive training and support ↔ training and support for teachers主动句↔存在句换位students get tutoring from designers ↔ tutoring for students from designers受动方与施动方都对得上
questions.quote: Along the way there is training and support for teachers and tutoring for students from designers.

questions.prompt: A visit to the Design Museum shop in London can reduce the designers' fears about the future supply of talents educated in Britain.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
参观伦敦Design Museum商店可以减轻设计师对英国培养的人才未来供应的担忧。
**锚点** 参观博物馆商店缓解担忧
**定位** 不过，如果这些设计师今年早些时候去过伦敦设计博物馆商店，他们的担忧本可以得到缓解。
**改写** A visit to the Design Museum shop in London ↔if these designers had visited the Design Museum shop in London earlier this year名词化↔动词化can reduce the designers' fears about the future supply of talents educated in Britain ↔their fears may have been eased reduce↔ease+talent复述前文
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
D D段讲的是这款玩具是2015年Design Ventura比赛获胜作品the toy was the winning entry in the museum's 2015 Design Ventura competition，并未提到'参观商店—缓解担忧'这条因果，仅与C段共享'设计博物馆'这个话题。the toy was the winning entry in the museum's 2015 Design Ventura competition
questions.quote: However, if these designers had visited the Design Museum shop in London earlier this year their fears may have been eased.

questions.prompt: One of Design Ventura's judges says the competition adds vigour to the standard curriculum in schools.
questions.explanation:
**答案** L 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
Design Ventura的一位评委表示,该竞赛为学校的标准课程增添了活力。
**锚点** 评委说比赛给课程添活力
**定位** 鉴于设计教育在课程中受到限制，我非常支持像Design Ventura这样的比赛，它能让标准课程焕发生气。
**改写** One of Design Ventura's judges ↔ one of the competition's judges Design Ventura=the competition adds vigour to the standard curriculum in schools ↔ bring the standard curriculum to life添活力=让其活起来
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
G G段说话人是博物馆学习部门主管Catherine Ritman Smith, head of learning at the Design Museum，并非评委；她讲的是老师为何喜欢这个项目，话题相邻但身份与判断都对不上陈述句。Teachers like it because the skills are all transferable and it helps to validate the value of design as a subject
questions.quote: Now that design education is limited in the curriculum, I'm all in favour of competitions such as Design Ventura, which helps to bring the standard curriculum to life.

questions.prompt: Enrollment in Design and Technology decreased by nearly ten percent last year in the UK.
questions.explanation:
**答案** A 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
去年英国设计与技术学科的注册人数下降了近百分之十。
**锚点** 设计与技术报考人数降近10%
**定位** 这些数据显示，去年参加设计与技术科目考试的学生人数下降了10%，从204,788人减至185,279人。
**改写** Enrollment in Design and Technology ↔the number of pupils that sat exams in Design and Technology报名人数=参加考试的学生数decreased by nearly ten percent last year ↔ fell 10 percent from 204,788 to 185,279 last year decrease↔fall+nearly↔精确数字
questions.quote: These figures showed that the number of pupils that sat exams in Design and Technology fell 10 percent from 204,788 to 185,279 last year.

questions.prompt: Participation of ninth graders in Design Ventura can motivate them to choose design technology as their subject.
questions.explanation:
**答案** M 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
九年级学生参与Design Ventura可以激励他们选择设计技术作为自己的学科。
**锚点** 九年级参赛促其选这门课
**定位** 我们发现，如果学生在九年级参加Design Ventura，这可能成为一个契机，促使他们在英国普通中等教育证书阶段选修该科目，因此我们正在让一件对产业和创业都至关重要的事保持活力。
**改写** Participation of ninth graders in Design Ventura ↔if pupils take part in Design Ventura in Year Nine名词化↔条件句can motivate them to choose design technology as their subject ↔it can be the trigger which leads them to opt for it at General Certificate of Secondary Education motivate=trigger+leads to+opt=choose
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E E段说话人Liam Hourican讲的是他作为老师为何引入比赛——I introduced it here because it helps to develop so many skills，停在'培养技能'层面，并没有讲学生因此选这门课的因果链。I introduced it here because it helps to develop so many skills
questions.quote: We find that if pupils take part in Design Ventura in Year Nine it can be the trigger which leads them to opt for it at General Certificate of Secondary Education, so we are helping to keep alive something which is crucial to industry and entrepreneurship.

questions.prompt: Design Ventura is welcomed by teachers because it helps to prove the worth of design as a school subject.
questions.explanation:
**答案** G 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
Design Ventura受到教师欢迎,因为它有助于证明设计作为学校学科的价值。
**锚点** 老师认可：证明学科价值
**定位** 老师们喜欢这个项目，因为这些技能都可迁移，而且它有助于证明设计作为一门学科的价值。
**改写** welcomed by teachers ↔ Teachers like it被动近义↔主动helps to prove the worth of design as a school subject ↔helps to validate the value of design as a subject prove↔validate+worth↔value
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
L L段是评委Naomi Cleaver的发言I'm all in favour of competitions such as Design Ventura，讲的是评委对比赛的态度，并非'老师欢迎'，与陈述句锁定的态度主体对不上。I'm all in favour of competitions such as Design Ventura, which helps to bring the standard curriculum to life
questions.quote: Teachers like it because the skills are all transferable and it helps to validate the value of design as a subject.

questions.prompt: The schools don't have to pay anything to take part in the Design Ventura competition.
questions.explanation:
**答案** K 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
学校参加Design Ventura竞赛无需支付任何费用。
**锚点** 学校参赛零费用
**定位** 学校参加Design Ventura不花一分钱；专业设计师免费提供服务。
**改写** The schools don't have to pay anything ↔ It costs the schools nothing付钱方视角↔成本方视角to take part in the Design Ventura competition ↔ to participate in Design Ventura take part in=participate in
questions.quote: It costs the schools nothing to participate in Design Ventura; the professional designers provide their services for free.

questions.prompt: Participants in Design Ventura are challenged to create sustainable and marketable products.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
Design Ventura的参与者面临创造可持续且适销产品的挑战。
**锚点** 可持续且可销售的产品
**定位** 这款玩具由Finchley Catholic High School的六名9、10年级男生设计，是博物馆2015年Design Ventura比赛的获胜作品；该赛事面向13到16岁的学生，挑战他们为设计博物馆商店开发一款全新、有创意、可持续且商业上可行的产品，吸引了全国数百份参赛作品。
**改写** Participants in Design Ventura are challenged to create ↔ challenging them to develop被动主语化↔现在分词sustainable and marketable products ↔a new creative, sustainable and commercially feasible product单词↔短语+sustainable原样复现
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
H H段讲的是赛事流程produce imaginative design ideas for a product in simple materials that could sell for £10，落脚点是'10英镑可售的设计构想'，没有sustainable+marketable的并列形容词描述，与陈述句对'产品属性'的聚焦不符。produce imaginative design ideas for a product in simple materials that could sell for £10 in the Design Museum shop
questions.quote: Designed by a group of six Year 9 and Year 10 boys from Finchley Catholic High School, the toy was the winning entry in the museum's 2015 Design Ventura competition, which brings the business of design to life for students aged 13 to 16 by challenging them to develop a new creative, sustainable and commercially feasible product for the Design Museum shop and attracts hundreds of entries nationwide.

questions.prompt: Students benefit from Design Ventura because they can learn about budgeting and marketing in addition to game design.
questions.explanation:
**答案** J 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
学生从Design Ventura中受益,因为除了游戏设计之外,他们还可以学习预算编制和市场营销。
**锚点** 除游戏设计外还学预算和营销
**定位** 这场比赛真正有用的一点是，它有商业元素：因为产品要真的上架销售，所以孩子们除了设计游戏，还得学预算和营销。
**改写** budgeting and marketing in addition to game design ↔budgeting and marketing, as well as designing their game并列项原样+连接词同义Students benefit from Design Ventura because they can learn about ↔the boys had to learn about受益与学到的事等值
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
H H段讲的是流程层面的支持there is training and support for teachers and tutoring for students from designers，只到'设计师辅导'层面，没有触及budgeting/marketing这类商业技能并列，与陈述句锁定的三连收益不符。Along the way there is training and support for teachers and tutoring for students from designers
questions.quote: One of the really useful things about this competition is that there's a commercial element because the product is going on sale for real and the boys had to learn about budgeting and marketing, as well as designing their game.

questions.prompt: According to an officer of the Creative Industries Federation, there is difficulty now in recruiting engineers in the UK.
questions.explanation:
**答案** B 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
根据Creative Industries Federation的一名官员所说,英国目前在招聘工程师方面存在困难。
**锚点** 创意产业联合会官员说工程师难招
**定位** 他说：'我们在动画、特效等许多岗位上已经面临技能短缺。'他还补充道：'工程领域需要相似的创意与技术混合能力，同样存在招聘困难。'
**改写** an officer of the Creative Industries Federation ↔Chief executive John Kampfner of the Creative Industries Federation officer是chief executive的上位词difficulty now in recruiting engineers in the UK ↔Engineering, which requires a similar mix of creative and technical skills, also has recruitment problems difficulty in recruiting engineers=Engineering has recruitment problems
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
A A段虽提到a leading design federation in the UK warned that the UK could face a creative skills shortage，但落脚点是科目报考人数下降数据，并未由具体官员说'工程师难招'，与陈述句锁定的'官员发言+招工程师难'对不上。a leading design federation in the UK warned that the UK could face a creative skills shortage
questions.quote: He said, "We already have skills shortages in many jobs such as animation(动画制作) and special effects." He added: "Engineering, which requires a similar mix of creative and technical skills, also has recruitment problems."

title: Plant-based meats are coming soon to a dinner…

sentences.text: Plant-based meats are coming soon to a dinner table near you, but do they deserve a spot on your plate?
If you tried a vegetable burger years ago and dismissed it as rubbery and flavorless, it's a good time to give meatless meat another chance.
Newer varieties imitate the look, flavor, and texture of meat.
Analysts don't expect the meat-free movement to slow anytime soon; a 2021 report predicts the market will skyrocket to $74 billion by 2030—a 957 percent surge.

passage.translation: 植物基肉类即将出现在你附近的餐桌上,但它们值得在你的盘子里占有一席之地吗?如果你几年前尝试过蔬菜汉堡并认为它像橡胶一样且毫无味道,现在是再给无肉肉类一次机会的好时机。较新的品种模仿了肉类的外观、风味和质地。分析师预计无肉运动不会很快放缓;2021年的一份报告预测,到2030年该市场将飙升至740亿美元——增长957%。

sentences.text: Plant-based meats are no longer just for vegetarians.

Companies such as Impossible Foods and Beyond Meat—the current superstars of the alternative protein sector—are pursuing consumers who enjoy meat but want to reduce their meat consumption for animal rights, health, or environmental reasons.
So far, it's a winning strategy: More than nine out of ten consumers who buy Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products also eat meat.

passage.translation: 植物基肉类不再只是素食主义者的选择。Impossible Foods和Beyond Meat等公司——目前替代蛋白质领域的超级明星——正在追求那些喜欢肉类但出于动物权利、健康或环境原因想要减少肉类消费的消费者。到目前为止,这是一个成功的策略:购买Beyond Burger和Impossible Foods产品的消费者中,超过十分之九的人也吃肉。

sentences.text: Many vegetarians don't actually care for food that resembles meat.
When reporter Joan Solsman, a longtime vegetarian, tried a dish from Impossible Foods, she felt so sick that she couldn't finish it.
"Maybe the best sign that Impossible Foods has cracked the code to realistic fake meat is that I couldn't stand to take another bite," she wrote.

passage.translation: 许多素食主义者实际上并不喜欢类似肉类的食物。当记者Joan Solsman——一位长期素食主义者——尝试Impossible Foods的一道菜时,她感到非常恶心以至于无法吃完。她写道:"也许Impossible Foods已经破解了逼真假肉密码的最好标志就是我无法再咬一口。"

sentences.text: Meatless meats are generally a healthier choice than beef because they are cholesterol-free, plus they're a good source of vitamins, minerals, protein, and fiber.

passage.translation: 无肉肉类通常比牛肉更健康,因为它们不含胆固醇,而且是维生素、矿物质、蛋白质和纤维的良好来源。

sentences.text: If meatless meat can help you stick to a plant-based diet, that in itself can lead to better health.
Not only has red meat been linked to cancer, but studies show that people who ditch meat have lower blood pressure, lower average blood sugar, and lower cholesterol levels.

passage.translation: 如果无肉肉类可以帮助你坚持植物性饮食,那本身就能带来更好的健康。红肉不仅与癌症有关,而且研究表明,不吃肉的人血压更低、平均血糖更低、胆固醇水平也更低。

sentences.text: However, just because it's plant-based doesn't mean it's health food.
Most imitation meats are highly processed and contain high amounts of sodium(钠) compared to traditional beef.

passage.translation: 然而,仅仅因为它是植物基的并不意味着它是健康食品。与传统牛肉相比,大多数仿制肉类都经过高度加工,并含有大量钠。

sentences.text: These new generations of alternate meat get all the attention, but don't forget about whole grains and vegetables.
Beans are an especially excellent protein substitute.
They're nutritious, inexpensive, and far more sustainable than any of the processed meatless substitutes on the market today.

passage.translation: 这些新一代替代肉类获得了所有关注,但不要忘记全谷物和蔬菜。豆类是特别优秀的蛋白质替代品。它们营养丰富、价格低廉,而且比当今市场上任何加工过的无肉替代品都更可持续。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What can we expect of plant-based meats?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
我们对植物基肉类有什么期待?
A) 人们对其分析的兴趣日益增长。
B) 为推广它们付出巨大努力。
C) 其消费量大幅增长。
D) 其品种显著激增。
**判型** What can we expect of plant-based meats? 没有出现 infer/imply/suggest，问的是一个文中已表述的预期结果，属于事实细节题。
**拆句** What can we expect of plant-based meats? 结构是 expect sth of sb/sth（对……抱有什么期待/预期），of 后接被期待的对象。考生熟悉的 expect sth from sb 在此处换成 of，含义相近，不必紧张。
**定位** 分析师们不预期植物肉浪潮短期内会放缓；一份 2021 年的报告预测，到 2030 年该市场将猛增至 740 亿美元——增幅高达 957%。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念An increasing interest in their analyses 把原文里「分析师们的预期」偷换成「对它们分析的兴趣增长」，文章并未说人们对植物肉的分析研究兴趣上升。
B) 无中生有An enormous effort in their promotion 谈的是「推广上的巨大努力」，原文只说市场规模会增长，没提企业或政府投入推广，属无中生有。
C) ✓ 正确the market will skyrocket to $74 billion by 2030—a 957 percent surge ↔A huge boost in their consumption预判要的是「消费规模大增」，A huge boost in their consumption 正是这个语义，锁定 C。
D) 偷换概念A noticeable surge in their varieties 把 surge 的对象从原文的「市场规模」换成「种类」，原文仅提到 Newer varieties imitate the look, flavor, and texture of meat，说新品种已出现，但没说种类会激增。
questions.quote: Analysts don't expect the meat-free movement to slow anytime soon; a 2021 report predicts the market will skyrocket to $74 billion by 2030—a 957 percent surge.

options.text: An increasing interest in their analyses.
An enormous effort in their promotion.
A huge boost in their consumption.
A noticeable surge in their varieties.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about consumers buying Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于购买Beyond Burger和Impossible Foods产品的消费者,我们了解到什么?
A) 他们大多不是素食者。
B) 他们大多是动物权利倡导者。
C) 他们中的大多数出于健康原因不吃肉。
D) 他们中的大多数吃无肉肉类是为了保护环境。
**判型** What do we learn about consumers buying Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products? 是 learn about + 名词结构，问关于该人群在原文中已写明的属性。
**拆句** What do we learn about consumers buying Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products? 主干 What do we learn about consumers，buying ... 是后置的现在分词短语作 consumers 的定语，相当于 who buy ...，结构无陷阱。
**定位** 在购买 Beyond Burger 和 Impossible Foods 产品的消费者中，有超过十分之九的人同时也吃肉。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确More than nine out of ten consumers who buy Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products also eat meat↔ They are mostly non-vegetarians预判说的「多数也吃肉」正对应「多数非素食者」，A 命中。
B) 以偏概全They are mostly animal-rights advocates 把动物权利说成消费者的主要身份，但原文animal rights, health, or environmental reasons 是并列的三类动机之一，没有说大多数是动物权利倡导者。
C) 以偏概全Most of them refrain from eating meat for health reasons 同样把并列三动机里的「健康」拎出来说大多数，且 refrain from eating meat（克制吃肉）与原文 reduce their meat consumption 程度被夸大。
D) 以偏概全Most of them eat meatless meat to protect the environment 同样犯「三选一拎为主因」的错误，无原文比例支撑。
questions.quote: More than nine out of ten consumers who buy Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products also eat meat.

options.text: They are mostly non-vegetarians.
They are mostly animal-rights advocates.
Most of them refrain from eating meat for health reasons.
Most of them eat meatless meat to protect the environment.

questions.prompt: What can we conclude about Impossible Foods' products from Joan Solsman's remark?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （推断题）
**题目译文**
从Joan Solsman的评论中,我们可以对Impossible Foods的产品得出什么结论?
A) 它们更常吸引肉食者。
B) 它们非常像动物肉。
C) 有些已成为其招牌菜。
D) 它们大多作为真正的假肉出售。
**判型** What can we conclude about Impossible Foods' products from Joan Solsman's remark? 中 conclude from ... remark 表示要从她的话里推出关于产品的判断。
**拆句** What can we conclude about Impossible Foods' products from Joan Solsman's remark? 主干 What can we conclude about X from Y，about 引出推断对象（产品），from 引出推断依据（她的话）；这是固定结构。
**定位** 或许 Impossible Foods 成功破解「逼真假肉」密码的最有力信号，就是连我（这个素食者）都没法再吃一口。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问题目要求从她的话推断 Impossible Foods 的「产品本身」特性，They more often appeal to meat-eaters 说的是「产品更受肉食者欢迎」，那是 Q52 答案，不是 Q53的推断方向。
B) ✓ 正确Impossible Foods has cracked the code to realistic fake meat ↔They very much resemble animal meat预判要的是「产品逼真像真肉」，They very much resemble animal meat 直接对应，锁 B。
C) 无中生有Some have become its signature dishes 说这些菜成了「招牌菜」，原文只说她试吃了 a dish from Impossible Foods，并未说哪些是招牌。
D) 偷换概念Most of them are sold as true fake meat 把 realistic fake meat（逼真的假肉）改成sold as true fake meat（作为「真假肉」出售），不仅商业化（销售行为）是原文没有的，true 修饰 fake meat 的逻辑也与「产品像真肉」相违。
questions.quote: Maybe the best sign that Impossible Foods has cracked the code to realistic fake meat is that I couldn't stand to take another bite.

options.text: They more often appeal to meat-eaters.
They very much resemble animal meat.
Some have become its signature dishes.
Most of them are sold as true fake meat.

questions.prompt: Why can the habit of eating a plant-based diet lead to better health?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
为什么植物基饮食习惯能带来更好的健康?
A) 它使人们摆脱任何已知的癌症关联。
B) 它提供保持健康所需的全部营养。
C) 它有助于维持正常的血压和血糖。
D) 它降低肉类消费带来的各种健康风险。
**判型** Why can the habit of eating a plant-based diet lead to better health? 用 Why 提问，原文有明确因果链时仍属细节题。
**拆句** Why can the habit of eating a plant-based diet lead to better health? 中主语是 the habit of doing sth（做某事的习惯）这个抽象名词短语，谓语 lead to 表示导致，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 不仅红肉被发现与癌症相关，研究还显示放弃吃肉的人血压更低、平均血糖更低、胆固醇水平也更低。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断It frees people from any known link to cancer 中 frees ... from any known link 表示「完全免除任何已知关联」，但原文只说红肉与癌症「被发现相关」（red meat been linked to cancer），并未说弃肉就能彻底斩断所有癌症关联。
B) 过度推断It provides all the nutrients for staying healthy 说植物饮食提供「所有保持健康所需的营养」，P4 只列了维生素、矿物质、蛋白质、纤维四项，没说「全部」。
C) 以偏概全It helps maintain normal blood pressure and blood sugar 只提血压和血糖，漏了胆固醇和癌症，且 maintain normal 意为「维持正常」，比 lower 表达的「降低」程度还弱。
D) ✓ 正确Not only has red meat been linked to cancer, but studies show that people who ditch meat have lower blood pressure, lower average blood sugar, and lower cholesterol levels.↔ It reduces various health risks posed by meat consumption预判要「综合性下降」，D 的 various health risks 正好覆盖了四种风险，是唯一概括项。
questions.quote: Not only has red meat been linked to cancer, but studies show that people who ditch meat have lower blood pressure, lower average blood sugar, and lower cholesterol levels.

options.text: It frees people from any known link to cancer.
It provides all the nutrients for staying healthy.
It helps maintain normal blood pressure and blood sugar.
It reduces various health risks posed by meat consumption.

questions.prompt: What does the author recommend we eat at the end of the passage?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者在文章结尾建议我们吃什么?
A) 天然生产的食物。
B) 加工蛋白质替代品。
C) 传统牛肉之类的红肉。
D) 新一代替代肉类。
**判型** What does the author recommend we eat at the end of the passage? 位置写死、动作写死，只问被推荐的事物，不涉及推断。
**拆句** What does the author recommend we eat at the end of the passage? 中 recommend (that) we eat 省略 that，we eat 是宾语从句；at the end of the passage 是位置状语，结构无陷阱。
**定位** 这些新一代的肉类替代品备受关注，但不要忘了全谷物和蔬菜。豆类是格外出色的蛋白替代品。它们营养丰富、价格便宜，可持续性远胜于今天市面上任何加工过的植物肉替代品。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确whole grains and vegetables↔ Naturally produced foods far more sustainable than any of the processed meatless substitutes↔Naturally produced foods预判要「天然食物」，Naturally produced foods 同时覆盖三类推荐对象的共同属性，是唯一合适项。
B) 与原文相反Processed protein substitutes 说的正是作者要反对的加工蛋白替代品，far more sustainable than any of the processed meatless substitutes 明确把这类产品当对照面。
C) 与原文相反Red meats like traditional beef 是全文反复劝退的对象（red meat been linked to cancer），作者绝不会在结尾推荐它。
D) 与原文相反New generations of alternate meat 与 These new generations of alternate meat原词复现，但原文用 but 转折表示「它们抢了风头但作者另有所荐」，并非推荐对象。
questions.quote: These new generations of alternate meat get all the attention, but don't forget about whole grains and vegetables. Beans are an especially excellent protein substitute. They're nutritious, inexpensive, and far more sustainable than any of the processed meatless substitutes on the market today.

options.text: Naturally produced foods.
Processed protein substitutes.
Red meats like traditional beef.
New generations of alternate meat.

title: Our society places a high value on physical…

sentences.text: Our society places a high value on physical beauty.
Americans spend an average of over $722 each year on their appearance.
One in ten Americans has tried to look like a star.

passage.translation: 我们的社会高度重视外在美。美国人平均每年在外表上花费超过722美元。每十个美国人中就有一个试图让自己看起来像明星。

sentences.text: There's nothing wrong with trying to look our best, but excessive focus on physical appearance misses the soulful aspects of what it means to be beautiful.
Trying to look like the magazine pictures can take us on a long ride away from what beauty is really about.

passage.translation: 努力让自己看起来最好并没有什么错,但过度关注外表会忽略美的真正含义中那些关乎灵魂的方面。试图看起来像杂志照片中的样子可能会让我们远离美的真正意义。

sentences.text: Many of us spend far too much time, energy, and money trying to polish an image of what we think will bring attention, love, and connection.
In the process, we may fail to attend to ourselves in a way that would move us toward deeper intimacy, fulfillment, and meaning.

passage.translation: 我们中的许多人花费了太多时间、精力和金钱来打磨一个我们认为能带来关注、爱和联系的形象。在这个过程中,我们可能无法以一种能让我们走向更深层次的亲密、满足和意义的方式来关注自己。

sentences.text: It may sound trite(老生常谈的), but beauty is only skin deep; it's not what brings love toward us.
Just read about the latest Hollywood starlets whose seeming love turns into resentment and bitter court battles.

passage.translation: 这可能听起来老生常谈,但美只是肤浅的;它不是给我们带来爱的东西。只需读读好莱坞最新明星们的故事,她们看似的爱情变成了怨恨和激烈的法庭争斗。

sentences.text: Outer beauty can be as much of a curse as a blessing.
We may develop a habit of being so focused on maintaining a perfect appearance that we never cultivate the inner qualities necessary to sustain and deepen intimacy and connection.
As I describe in my book, The Authentic Heart, it is the courage to be authentic that connects us in a deeper way.

passage.translation: 外在美既可能是诅咒也可能是祝福。我们可能养成一种习惯,过于专注于保持完美的外表,以至于从未培养维持和深化亲密关系和联系所必需的内在品质。正如我在《真实的心》一书中所描述的,正是真实的勇气以更深刻的方式将我们联系在一起。

sentences.text: While our initial attraction may be based, in part, on physical chemistry, it is the meeting of our inner worlds that creates the lasting intimacy and spiritual connection for which we long.
If we redirect our attention toward cultivating inner qualities, we might find a magnetic attraction that moves us from something superficial to something that connects us to our depths.

passage.translation: 虽然我们最初的吸引力可能部分基于身体上的化学反应,但正是我们内心世界的相遇创造了我们渴望的持久亲密和精神联系。如果我们将注意力转向培养内在品质,我们可能会发现一种磁性吸引力,使我们从肤浅的东西走向与我们内心深处相连的东西。

sentences.text: The path toward cultivating inner beauty is really simple.
But what is simple is not always easy.
Not everyone will see us and appreciate us as we take the courageous risk to allow ourselves to be seen as we really are.
But if they don't, it is their loss, not ours.
Eventually we'll find those compatible souls who appreciate us as we are.

passage.translation: 培养内在美的道路其实很简单。但简单的事情并不总是容易的。当我们冒着勇敢的风险让自己以真实的样子被看见时,不是每个人都会看到我们并欣赏我们。但如果他们不欣赏,那是他们的损失,而不是我们的。最终我们会找到那些欣赏真实的我们的志同道合的灵魂。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about American society from the first paragraph?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
从第一段我们对美国社会了解到什么?
A) 它认为大量个人收入浪费在美容产品上。
B) 它认为一个人的外表非常重要。
C) 它高度重视明星的身体健康状况。
D) 它期望每个人都展现出自己最好的外表。
**判型** What do we learn about American society from the first paragraph? 是 what...learn型客观信息问答，且范围锁定首段，属于典型细节题。
**拆句** Q46 主干是 What do we learn about American society，from the first paragraph 是状语限定信息来源；句子平铺直叙、无陷阱。
**定位** 我们的社会高度看重外貌。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有It sees lots of personal income wasted on beauty products. 把 over $722 each year on their appearance 的客观花费篡改为 "被浪费"，原文从未做此评价。
B) ✓ 正确places a high value on physical beauty ↔considers one's physical appearance very important预判 "美国社会把外貌看得很重要" 与 considers one's physical appearance very important 字面贴合，无需推断。
C) 偷换概念places a high value on the physical fitness of stars 把 "看重外貌" 的主体悄悄换成"明星的 physical fitness"；原文 One in ten Americans has tried to look like a star只说有人想模仿明星，未谈明星本身的体魄。
D) 过度推断It expects every individual to look their very best. 把 Our society places a high value on physical beauty 升级为 "要求每一个人都做到最好"，强度与范围都被拔高。
questions.quote: Our society places a high value on physical beauty.

options.text: It sees lots of personal income wasted on beauty products.
It considers one's physical appearance very important.
It places a high value on the physical fitness of stars.
It expects every individual to look their very best.

questions.prompt: What happens when people strive to look better?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
当人们努力让自己看起来更好时会发生什么?
A) 他们必须为怨恨和激烈的法庭斗争做好准备。
B) 他们能够更好地获得关注、爱和人际联系。
C) 他们可能会忽视培养更重要的内在品质。
D) 他们觉得自己大量宝贵的时间、精力和资源被浪费了。
**判型** What happens when people strive to look better? 询问某动作引发的客观后果，是典型的因果型细节题。
**拆句** Q47 主干 What happens 后接 when 引导的时间状语从句，提示发生条件；结构简单无陷阱。
**定位** 我们当中许多人花了过多的时间、精力和金钱去打磨一个我们以为会带来关注、爱与连结的形象。在这个过程中，我们可能会忽略对自己的关照，错过本可带来更深亲密、满足与意义的方式。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴They have to get prepared for resentment and bitter court battles. 把第 4 段说明影星案例的 resentment and bitter court battles 强行移植到 Q47 的情境中，但原文从未把这描述为追求外表的 "必然准备"。
B) 与原文相反They are better able to gain attention, love, and personal connection. 把原文what we think will bring attention, love, and connection 中 "我们以为会带来" 的主观期待包装成客观事实，方向恰好与作者批评意图相反。
C) ✓ 正确fail to attend to ourselves in a way that would move us toward deeper intimacy, fulfillment, and meaning↔ neglect to cultivate the inner qualities that matter more预判 "疏于关照内在更要紧的部分" 几乎逐字对应 neglect to cultivate the inner qualities that matter more。
D) 偷换概念They feel much of their precious time, energy and resources is wasted. 把作者对time, energy, and money 的客观描述换成 "他们自己觉得被浪费"，主体变成 they feel；原文未提及当事人有此自觉。
questions.quote: Many of us spend far too much time, energy, and money trying to polish an image of what we think will bring attention, love, and connection. In the process, we may fail to attend to ourselves in a way that would move us toward deeper intimacy, fulfillment, and meaning.

options.text: They have to get prepared for resentment and bitter court battles.
They are better able to gain attention, love, and personal connection.
They may neglect to cultivate the inner qualities that matter more.
They feel much of their precious time, energy and resources is wasted.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about outer beauty?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者对外在美有何看法?
A) 它可能是遗传的或培养的。
B) 它可能导致坏习惯也可能导致好习惯。
C) 它可能创造联系也可能造成孤立。
D) 它可能带来的伤害和好处一样多。
**判型** What does the author say about outer beauty? 询问作者就某概念的明确陈述，归入细节题。
**拆句** Q48 主干 What does the author say，about outer beauty 是介词短语状语；无难句结构。
**定位** 外在美既可能是祝福，也同样可能是诅咒。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有It may be inherited or cultivated. 谈外貌的来源（遗传/后天培养），原文从未讨论外貌的获得方式。
B) 偷换概念It may lead to bad as well as good habits. 把 Outer beauty can be as much of a curse as a blessing. 改成 "导致好坏习惯"，对象层面从 "对人生整体的祸福" 缩到 "习惯"。原文确实提到 develop a habit，但说的是 "只关注外表的习惯"，并非 "好习惯/坏习惯" 的对照。
C) 与原文相反It may create connection or isolation. 称外貌可能创造 connection；但 P5 P6 都说 connection 来自 inner qualities / meeting of inner worlds，外貌不直接创造 connection。
D) ✓ 正确as much of a curse as a blessing ↔ do as much harm as good预判 "坏处与好处一样多" 直接命中 do as much harm as good，无需推断。
questions.quote: Outer beauty can be as much of a curse as a blessing.

options.text: It may be inherited or cultivated.
It may lead to bad as well as good habits.
It may create connection or isolation.
It may do as much harm as good.

questions.prompt: What brings about spiritual connection?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
是什么带来精神上的联系?
A) 思想的交汇。
B) 一见钟情的吸引。
C) 身体上的化学反应。
D) 频繁的互动。
**判型** What brings about spiritual connection? 询问导致某结果的原因，对应原文中一处明确的因→果叙述。
**拆句** Q49 主干 What brings about spiritual connection，brings about=cause/lead to，是一个三个单词的简单疑问句。
**定位** 虽然最初的吸引可能在一定程度上源于身体的化学反应，但真正创造我们所渴求的长久亲密与精神连结的，是内在世界的相遇。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确the meeting of our inner worlds ↔ Meeting of minds.预判 "内在世界相遇" 几乎逐字对应 Meeting of minds.。
B) 与原文相反Attraction at first sight. 对应 our initial attraction，但原文明确说这只是 "in part" 的初始吸引，并非 spiritual connection 的来源。
C) 与原文相反Physical chemistry. 直接抓取 physical chemistry 这一原词，但原文用 While 让步结构说明它只贡献 initial attraction，不是 spiritual connection 的来源。
D) 无中生有Frequent interaction. 谈交往频率，原文从未提及 spiritual connection 来自频繁互动。
questions.quote: While our initial attraction may be based, in part, on physical chemistry, it is the meeting of our inner worlds that creates the lasting intimacy and spiritual connection for which we long.

options.text: Meeting of minds.
Attraction at first sight.
Physical chemistry.
Frequent interaction.

questions.prompt: What happens when we take the path toward cultivating inner beauty?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
当我们走上培养内在美的道路时会发生什么?
A) 我们可能会找到通往他人灵魂的路径。
B) 我们可能会更被周围的人欣赏。
C) 我们会遇到那些因我们本来的样子而珍视我们的人。
D) 我们会被劝阻不要展现真实的自己。
**判型** What happens when we take the path toward cultivating inner beauty? 仍是 what happens when 的因果型问法，问的是文章对此动作所述的结果。
**拆句** Q50 主干 What happens，when 从句中 take the path toward cultivating inner beauty用了介词短语作 path 的修饰，toward 后接动名词 cultivating，提示这是个比喻：把培养内在美比作走一条路。
**定位** 最终我们会遇到那些欣赏真实的我们的契合灵魂。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反We may find a route toward other people's souls. 让 "我们走向别人的灵魂"；原文P7 描述的是别人走向真实的我们，方向与重点都不一致。
B) 以偏概全We may be appreciated more by people around us. 把 "被那些契合的人欣赏" 扩大为 "被周围所有人更多地欣赏"；原文紧前一句明说 Not everyone will see us and appreciate us，恰好否定 "被周围人普遍更欣赏"。
C) ✓ 正确Eventually we'll find those compatible souls who appreciate us as we are.↔We will meet people who value us for who we are.预判 "最终遇到欣赏真实自我的人" 与 We will meet people who value us for who we are. 几乎逐字对应。
D) 与原文相反We will be discouraged from revealing our true selves. 称我们会被打消展露真我的念头；但原文 if they don't, it is their loss, not ours 是鼓励继续展露自我，与选项方向相反。
questions.quote: Eventually we'll find those compatible souls who appreciate us as we are.

options.text: We may find a route toward other people's souls.
We may be appreciated more by people around us.
We will meet people who value us for who we are.
We will be discouraged from revealing our true selves.

title: The human brain has the ability to constantly…

sentences.text: The human brain has the ability to constantly form new networks and connections between brain cells.
This means the brain has an almost magical ability to change.
This characteristic is (26)____apparent in a new study, focusing on people who underwent a hemispherectomy, a surgical procedure in which half of the brain is removed to treat illness.

passage.translation: 人类大脑具有在脑细胞之间不断形成新网络和新连接的能力。这意味着大脑具有几乎神奇的改变能力。这一特征在一项新研究中尤为明显,该研究关注的是接受过大脑半球切除术的人群,这是一种切除半个大脑以治疗疾病的外科手术。

sentences.text: The findings showed that, despite missing half of this critical (27)____ , participants could function well.
This was because the (28)____ half of their brain strengthened.

In fact, researchers found that connections and thus communication—between parts of different brain networks are actually stronger in people who had hemispherectomies than in people with intact brains.
This (29)____ that the brain is able to compensate for loss of certain brain structure.

passage.translation: 研究结果显示,尽管缺失了这一关键器官的一半,参与者仍能够正常运作。这是因为他们大脑的剩余半部分得到了强化。事实上,研究人员发现,在接受过大脑半球切除术的人群中,不同脑网络部分之间的连接以及由此产生的交流,实际上比拥有完整大脑的人更强。这表明大脑能够补偿某些脑结构的缺失。

sentences.text: There are many other cases in the medical (30)____ that document the brain's amazing ability to(31)____ For example, a young boy had a significant portion of his brain removed for medical reasons, which included the part of the brain (32)____ for sight.
But a few years after his surgery, scientists found that he could (33)____ see.
They determined that this was because other parts of his brain took over the missing part's (34)____ tasks.
Another study involved people who could smell, despite missing the region in the brain that processes information about smells.
Though they are not sure how these individuals (35)____ the ability to smell, scientists believe it is possible that another part of the brain took on that task.

passage.translation: 医学文献中还有许多其他案例记录了大脑惊人的适应能力。例如,一名年轻男孩因医疗原因切除了大脑的很大一部分,其中包括负责视觉的大脑部分。但在手术几年后,科学家们发现他仍然能够看见。他们确定这是因为他大脑的其他部分接管了缺失部分的视觉任务。另一项研究涉及的人群虽然缺失大脑中处理气味信息的区域,却仍能闻到气味。尽管科学家们不确定这些个体是如何保留嗅觉能力的,但他们认为可能是大脑的另一部分承担了这项任务。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
The human brain has the ability to constantly form new networks and connections between brain cells. This means the brain has an almost magical ability to change. This characteristic is {{26}}apparent in a new study, focusing on people who underwent a hemispherectomy, a surgical procedure in which half of the brain is removed to treat illness.

The findings showed that, despite missing half of this critical {{27}} , participants could function well. This was because the {{28}} half of their brain strengthened. In fact, researchers found that connections and thus communication—between parts of different brain networks are actually stronger in people who had hemispherectomies than in people with intact brains. This {{29}} that the brain is able to compensate for loss of certain brain structure.

There are many other cases in the medical {{30}} that document the brain's amazing ability to{{31}} For example, a young boy had a significant portion of his brain removed for medical reasons, which included the part of the brain {{32}} for sight. But a few years after his surgery, scientists found that he could {{33}} see. They determined that this was because other parts of his brain took over the missing part's {{34}} tasks. Another study involved people who could smell, despite missing the region in the brain that processes information about smells. Though they are not sure how these individuals {{35}} the ability to smell, scientists believe it is possible that another part of the brain took on that task.

options.text: adapt
responsible
hardly
retained
indicates
still
insist
strategy
literature
transformed
organ
underlines
