questions.explanation:
**答案** D) complex 形容词
**词性槽** the kinds of 后接名词，空与 strategic 并列修饰名词
**依据** 与 strategic 同属「高级心智」语义场the kinds of __(26)__ and strategic self-presentation behaviour we see in adults：作者强调成年人的自我呈现是「复杂的、有策略的」，complex（复杂的）与 strategic（策略性的）语义并列、相互呼应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
K) solemn 感情色彩与上下文不符solemn 意为「庄严的、肃穆的」，多用于仪式或表情，和「自我呈现行为」的认知性描述不搭边，也无法和 strategic 构成自然的并列。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) previously 副词
**词性槽** than 后修饰过去分词 known
**依据** 与 New findings 形成「新 vs 旧」对照New findings suggest that ... appear at a much younger age than __(27)__ known. 强调「新发现」与「以往所知」对比，previously known = 此前所知，正好把「新发现 vs 旧认知」对照起来。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) suddenly 语义和逻辑都不通suddenly known（突然被知道）既不是固定表达，也和「比以往认为更早」的对比语境不沾边，明显逻辑错位。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) accepted 动词
**词性槽** be 动词后接过去分词作被动谓语
**依据** 符合「被认同/接纳」的社会心理语境kids want to be __(28)__ by those they admire 谈孩子希望「被自己崇拜的人认可、接纳」，accepted by 是地道搭配，对应「获得社会认同」这个本段的主线。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
J) selected选拔语义与「被仰慕者接纳」不匹配selected by 多指「被挑中」（比赛、选拔），带筛选意味，而孩子对「自己崇拜的人」的需求是被接纳、被认可，不是被挑选；语境不符。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) constitutes 动词
**词性槽** what 引导从句需要谓语动词
**依据** what constitutes X = 何为 X 的构成learn about what __(29)__ a desirable reputation 即「了解什么构成了好名声」，constitute 在学术英语里恰好用作「构成、等同于」，是描述抽象概念边界的常用动词。

**答案** C) building 动词
**词性槽** 介词 for 后接动名词作宾语
**依据** build a reputation 是固定搭配strategies that are effective for __(30)__ a good reputation，build a good reputation（建立好名声）是英语里的高频固定搭配，对应「塑造形象」的本段主题。

**答案** O) vary 动词
**词性槽** 情态动词 will 后接动词原形
**依据** vary one's behaviour = 改变/调整自己的行为They will __(31)__ their behaviour in order to appear moral or socially good in the eyes of key observers. 主题是「为博得好印象而调整行为」，vary 作及物动词意为「使……变化、改变」，vary their behaviour 正对应「策略性地改变行为」。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
N) understand 理解自己行为 ≠ 改变以塑形象understand their behaviour 表「理解自己的行为」，与 in order to appear moral（为了显得有道德）这个目的状语不构成因果——理解了并不一定就显得有道德。understand 此处被32 题预留，更不该提前用掉。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 N) —— understand their behaviour 看似合理，实则脱离目的状语。They will __(31)__ their behaviour in order to appear moral or socially good：understand 同为动词原形且能带宾语，但「理解自己的行为」无法导致「显得有道德」这个目的；vary 才符合「调整行为以塑形象」的逻辑。识破靠用 in order to 的目的反推动词。

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) understand 动词
**词性槽** whether children ___ and use ... 谓语动词
**依据** 和 use 构成「理解并运用」的递进whether children __(32)__ and use the fact that different attributes are valuable at different times：understand and use a fact 是英语里「先理解、再运用」的常见递进，正对应「是否懂得并利用不同属性的价值」。

**答案** B) audiences 名词
**词性槽** different 后 + to 介词宾语的复数名词
**依据** 与「印象管理对象」的语境直接对应adults use a large variety of attributes to manage and create impressions 与different attributes are valuable at different times to different __(33)__ 谈的都是「在不同观察者面前营造印象」，audiences（受众/观众）正指「印象呈现给谁看」，逻辑严丝合缝。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) deputies 语义偏离「印象管理」主题deputies 指「副手、代理人」，是政治/职务术语，与本文讨论的「印象的接收者」毫无关联。
I) samples 样本不属于印象管理对象samples（样本）多用于实验或商品场景，无法承担「在不同对象面前调整形象」里的「对象」角色。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 I) —— different samples 形式上完美，语义却偏题。different attributes are valuable at different times to different __(33)__：samples 是复数名词、与 different times 形式平行，但本段主题是「在不同观察者面前展示形象」，audiences才是真正的受众。识破靠回到段落主旨词 impressions/observers 锚定语义。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) struggle 动词
**词性槽** where 从句缺谓语动词，与 succeed 对照
**依据** struggle 与 succeed 形成对照where ... children succeed in controlling their reputation and where they __(34)__：struggle（挣扎、感到吃力）正是 succeed（成功）的反面，「在哪里成功、在哪里受挫」是典型的研究问题表述。

**答案** M) suddenly 副词
**词性槽** 动词 pop 后修饰其方式的成分
**依据** 强调「凭空冒出」的反逻辑Children don't just show up to the first day of kindergarten and have the idea of reputation pop __(35)__ into existence. 作者要否定的正是「名声观念会突然蹦出来」这种说法，suddenly 精准对应「突然冒出」。

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Most people have a dream in life, a vision of who or what they'd like to be in the future.
At a minimum, everyone has interests and values that determine what they want out of their lives.
Even so, trying to set achievable goals that you'll work for over the course of many years can be extremely challenging.
It can be hard to know where to even begin, and the things you hope to achieve may seem impossible.
But, if you're well prepared you may be able to set goals for your life that are just as fulfilling to work toward as to achieve.

passage.translation: 大多数人在生活中都有一个梦想,对未来自己想成为什么样的人或想做什么有一个憧憬。至少,每个人都有决定自己想从生活中得到什么的兴趣和价值观。即便如此,试图设定你将在许多年中为之努力的可实现目标可能极具挑战性。很难知道从哪里开始,而你希望实现的目标可能看起来不可能。但是,如果你准备充分,你也许能够为自己的人生设定这样的目标:朝着它们努力的过程与实现它们一样令人满足。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: We all have goals that we want to achieve in our lives.
These goals may include learning a new language, eating healthier and losing weight, becoming a better parent, saving more money, and so on.
It can be easy to assume that the gap between where you are now and where you want to be in the future is caused by a lack of knowledge.
This is why we buy courses on how to start a business or how to lose weight fast or how to learn a new language in three months.
We assume that if we knew about a better strategy, then we would get better results.
We believe that a new result requires new knowledge.

passage.translation: 我们都有想在生活中实现的目标。这些目标可能包括学习一门新语言、更健康地饮食和减肥、成为更好的父母、存更多的钱,等等。人们很容易认为,你现在所处的位置与你未来想要达到的位置之间的差距是由于缺乏知识造成的。这就是为什么我们购买关于如何创业、如何快速减肥或如何在三个月内学会一门新语言的课程。我们认为如果我们知道更好的策略,那么我们就会获得更好的结果。我们相信新的结果需要新的知识。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: What I'm starting to realize, however, is that new knowledge does not necessarily drive new results.
In fact, learning something new can actually be a waste of time if your goal is to make progress and not simply gain additional knowledge.

passage.translation: 然而,我开始意识到,新知识并不一定带来新结果。事实上,如果你的目标是取得进步而不仅仅是获得额外知识,那么学习新东西实际上可能是浪费时间。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: It all comes down to the difference between learning and practicing.
Thomas Sterner, in his book*The Practicing Mind*, explains the key difference between practicing and learning.
He says: "When we practice something, we are involved in the deliberate repetition of a process with the intention of reaching a specific goal."
Here the words "deliberate" and "intention" are key, because they define the difference between actively practicing something and passively learning it.

passage.translation: 这一切归结为学习和练习之间的区别。Thomas Sterner在他的书《练习的心态》中解释了练习和学习之间的关键区别。他说:"当我们练习某件事时,我们在有意识地重复一个过程,意图达到一个特定的目标。"这里"有意识"和"意图"这两个词是关键,因为它们定义了主动练习某事和被动学习它之间的区别。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Learning something new and practicing something new may seem very similar, but these two methods can have profoundly different results.
Here are some additional ways to think about the difference.
Let's say your goal is to get stronger and more fit.
You can research the best instructions on weight lifting technique, but the only way to build strength is to practice lifting weights.
Let's say your goal is to grow your startup.
You can learn about the best way to make a sales pitch, but the only way to actually land customers is to practice making sales calls.
Let's say your goal is to write a book.
You can talk to a best-selling author about writing, but the only way to become a better writer is to practice publishing consistently.

passage.translation: 学习新东西和练习新东西可能看起来非常相似,但这两种方法可能产生截然不同的结果。以下是一些思考这种区别的其他方式。假设你的目标是变得更强壮、更健康。你可以研究关于举重技术的最佳指导,但增强力量的唯一方法是练习举重。假设你的目标是发展你的初创企业。你可以学习关于如何做销售推介的最佳方法,但真正获得客户的唯一方法是练习打销售电话。假设你的目标是写一本书。你可以和一位畅销书作家谈论写作,但成为更好作家的唯一方法是练习持续发表作品。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: Passive learning creates knowledge.
Active practice creates skill.
Let's consider a couple more reasons to prioritize active practice over passive learning.
First, passive learning can be a stick that supports inaction.
In many cases, learning is actually a way to avoid taking action on the goals and interests that we say are important to us.
For example, let's say you want to learn a foreign language.
Reading a book on how to learn a foreign language quickly allows you to feel like you are making progress ("Hey, I'm figuring out the best way to do this!").
Of course, you're not actually practicing the action that would deliver your desired outcome (speaking the foreign language).

passage.translation: 被动学习创造知识。主动练习创造技能。让我们再考虑几个优先选择主动练习而不是被动学习的理由。首先,被动学习可能成为支持不作为的拐杖。在很多情况下,学习实际上是一种避免对我们声称对自己重要的目标和兴趣采取行动的方式。例如,假设你想学习一门外语。阅读一本关于如何快速学习外语的书让你感觉自己正在取得进步("嘿,我正在找出做这件事的最佳方法!")。当然,你实际上并没有在练习能带来你期望结果的行动(说这门外语)。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: In situations like this one, we often claim that we are preparing or researching the best method, but these rationalizations allow us to feel like we are moving forward when we are merely spinning our wheels.
We make the mistake of being in motion rather than taking action.
Learning is valuable until it becomes a form of procrastination(拖延).

passage.translation: 在这样的情况下,我们经常声称自己正在准备或研究最佳方法,但这些合理化借口让我们在仅仅原地打转时感觉自己正在前进。我们犯了处于运动状态而不是采取行动的错误。学习是有价值的,直到它变成一种拖延形式。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Another point to consider is that practice is learning, but learning is not practice.
Passive learning is not a form of practice because although you gain new knowledge, you are not discovering how to apply that knowledge.
Active practice, meanwhile, is one of the greatest forms of learning because the mistakes you make while practicing reveal important insights.

passage.translation: 另一个需要考虑的要点是,练习是学习,但学习不是练习。被动学习不是一种练习形式,因为尽管你获得了新知识,但你没有发现如何应用那些知识。与此同时,主动练习是最伟大的学习形式之一,因为你在练习时犯的错误揭示了重要的见解。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Even more importantly, practice is the only way to make a meaningful contribution with your knowledge.

You can watch an online course about how to build a business or read an article about a terrible disaster in a developing nation, but that knowledge is unproductive unless you actually launch your business or donate to those in need.
Learning by itself can be valuable for you, but if you want to be valuable to others, then you have to express your knowledge in some way.

passage.translation: 更重要的是,练习是用你的知识做出有意义贡献的唯一方式。你可以观看关于如何创业的在线课程,或阅读一篇关于发展中国家可怕灾难的文章,但除非你真正启动你的业务或向有需要的人捐款,否则那些知识是无用的。学习本身对你来说可能是有价值的,但如果你想对他人有价值,那么你必须以某种方式表达你的知识。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: The last important point to consider is that practice focuses your energy on the process.
Thomas Sterner once said, "Progress is a natural result of staying focused on the process of doing anything."
The state of your life right now is a result of the habits and beliefs that you have been practicing each day.
When you realize this and begin to direct your focus toward practicing better habits day-in and day-out, continual progress will be the logical outcome.
It is not the things we learn nor the dreams we visualize that determine our results, but rather the habits that we practice each day.
Fall in love with boredom and focus your energy on the process, not the product.

passage.translation: 最后一个需要考虑的重要要点是,练习将你的精力集中在过程上。Thomas Sterner曾经说过:"进步是保持专注于做任何事情的过程的自然结果。"你现在生活的状态是你每天一直在练习的习惯和信念的结果。当你意识到这一点并开始将注意力导向日复一日地练习更好的习惯时,持续进步将是合乎逻辑的结果。决定我们结果的不是我们学到的东西,也不是我们想象的梦想,而是我们每天练习的习惯。爱上无聊,将你的精力集中在过程上,而不是产品上。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: What does this all mean?
Is passive learning useless?
Of course not.
In many cases, learning for the sake of learning can be a beautiful thing.
Not to mention that soaking up new information can help you make more informed decisions when you do decide to take action.
That said, the main point of this article is that learning by itself does not lead to progress.
We often hide behind information and use learning as an excuse to delay the more difficult and more important choice of actually doing something.
Spend less time passively learning and more time actively practicing.
Stop thinking and start doing.

passage.translation: 这一切意味着什么?被动学习是无用的吗?当然不是。在很多情况下,为了学习而学习可能是一件美好的事情。更不用说吸收新信息可以帮助你在决定采取行动时做出更明智的决定。也就是说,本文的主要观点是,学习本身并不能带来进步。我们经常躲在信息背后,用学习作为借口来延迟实际做某事这个更困难、更重要的选择。少花时间被动学习,多花时间主动练习。停止思考,开始行动。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: Acquisition of new knowledge may not guarantee the progress that you aim to make.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
获取新知识可能无法保证你实现所追求的进步。
**锚点** new knowledge ↔ progress 的否定连接
**定位** 然而，我开始意识到的是：新的知识未必能带来新的结果。
**改写** Acquisition of new knowledge ↔ new knowledge名词化等价may not guarantee ↔ does not necessarily drive弱否定同义替换the progress that you aim to make ↔ new results上下位等价
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段是 We assume that if we knew about a better strategy, then we would get better results，只是把 大众的设想 摆出来；陈述句要的是 不能保证 的判断，这一判断只出现在 C 段。We believe that a new result requires new knowledge K K 段的 the main point of this article is that learning by itself does not lead to progress 是 收束重申，本文 反直觉新结论 的首次提出在 C 段。learning by itself does not lead to progress
questions.quote: What I'm starting to realize, however, is that new knowledge does not necessarily drive new results.

questions.prompt: Your current situation in life is built on the beliefs and habits you have been practicing daily.
questions.explanation:
**答案** J 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
你当前的生活状况建立在你每天践行的信念和习惯之上。
**锚点** current situation = beliefs and habits
**定位** 你此刻的人生状态，是你每天所践行的习惯和信念的结果。
**改写** Your current situation in life ↔ The state of your life right now同义短语替换beliefs and habits ↔ habits and beliefs并列项顺序调换practicing daily ↔ practicing each day副词与短语等值
questions.quote: The state of your life right now is a result of the habits and beliefs that you have been practicing each day.

questions.prompt: Knowing the best way to learn a foreign language will not enable you to speak it without actual practice.
questions.explanation:
**答案** F 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
了解学习外语的最佳方法并不能使你在没有实际练习的情况下说这门语言。
**锚点** foreign language 案例
**定位** 比如，假设你想学一门外语。读一本 怎样快速学外语 的书会让你觉得自己在进步（嘿，我正在搞清楚最好的方法！）。但其实，你并没有在实际练习那能带来你想要的结果的那个动作——说这门外语。
**改写** Knowing the best way to learn a foreign language ↔Reading a book on how to learn a foreign language quickly学习手段同位替换will not enable you to speak it without actual practice ↔you're not actually practicing the action that would deliver your desired outcome (speaking the foreign language)否定关系等价
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E E 段的例子是 get stronger and more fit、grow your startup、write a book，与foreign language 无关。Let's say your goal is to get stronger and more fit
questions.quote: For example, let's say you want to learn a foreign language. Reading a book on how to learn a foreign language quickly allows you to feel like you are making progress ("Hey, I'm figuring out the best way to do this!"). Of course, you're not actually practicing the action that would deliver your desired outcome (speaking the foreign language).

questions.prompt: People may find it demanding to create a goal which will take a long time to achieve.
questions.explanation:
**答案** A 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
人们可能会发现创建一个需要很长时间才能实现的目标很困难。
**锚点** 长时间才能达成的目标 + demanding
**定位** 即便如此，要为你需要奋斗多年才能达成的目标设立可实现的方案，可能极其困难。
**改写** create a goal ↔ to set achievable goals动宾同义替换which will take a long time to achieve ↔ over the course of many years时长表达同义替换demanding ↔ extremely challenging形容词等价
questions.quote: Even so, trying to set achievable goals that you'll work for over the course of many years can be extremely challenging.

questions.prompt: Learning and practicing seem to be very much alike, but the two processes can lead to quite different outcomes.
questions.explanation:
**答案** E 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
学习和练习似乎非常相似,但这两个过程可能会导致截然不同的结果。
**锚点** alike but different outcomes
**定位** 学新东西与练新东西看起来非常相似，但这两种方式可能带来极为不同的结果。
**改写** Learning and practicing seem to be very much alike ↔Learning something new and practicing something new may seem very similar同义重述the two processes can lead to quite different outcomes ↔these two methods can have profoundly different results整句同义重述
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
H H 段是 Another point to consider is that practice is learning, but learning is not practice——讨论的是包含关系，不是 看起来相似但结果不同。practice is learning, but learning is not practice
questions.quote: Learning something new and practicing something new may seem very similar, but these two methods can have profoundly different results.

questions.prompt: Absorbing new information is helpful in making better decisions prior to action.
questions.explanation:
**答案** K 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
吸收新信息有助于在行动之前做出更好的决策。
**锚点** absorbing information → better decisions
**定位** 更不用说，吸收新的信息有助于你在真正决定行动时做出更明智的决策。
**改写** Absorbing new information ↔ soaking up new information动词族同义替换helpful in making better decisions ↔ help you make more informed decisions形容词转动词同义prior to action ↔ when you do decide to take action时间状语同义
questions.quote: Not to mention that soaking up new information can help you make more informed decisions when you do decide to take action.

questions.prompt: Sometimes we may feel like we are making progress by doing some research or making preparations, but actually we are staying at the starting point.
questions.explanation:
**答案** G 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
有时我们可能会觉得通过做一些研究或准备工作正在取得进步,但实际上我们还停留在起点。
**锚点** feel like progress but actually staying at starting point
**定位** 在这种情形下，我们常声称自己在做准备或研究最佳方法，但这些自我合理化让我们觉得自己在前进，其实只是原地空转。
**改写** doing some research or making preparations ↔ preparing or researching the best method并列动词同义替换feel like we are making progress ↔ feel like we are moving forward短语等价staying at the starting point ↔ spinning our wheels比喻与字面同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
F F 段的 Reading a book on how to learn a foreign language quickly allows you to feel like you are making progress 是 具体例子，陈述句 Q42 的 评论性概括 出现在承接段 G。Reading a book on how to learn a foreign language quickly allows you to feel like you are making progress
questions.quote: In situations like this one, we often claim that we are preparing or researching the best method, but these rationalizations allow us to feel like we are moving forward when we are merely spinning our wheels.

questions.prompt: We are inclined to think that a lack of knowledge prevents us from advancing to a better future.
questions.explanation:
**答案** B 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
我们倾向于认为缺乏知识阻碍我们走向更美好的未来。
**锚点** lack of knowledge 阻碍进步
**定位** 我们很容易这样设想：你当下所处的位置与你将来想到达的位置之间的差距，是由知识不足造成的。
**改写** We are inclined to think ↔ It can be easy to assume倾向表达同义a lack of knowledge prevents us from advancing to a better future ↔the gap between where you are now and where you want to be in the future is caused by a lack of knowledge因果链对位
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
C C 段以 What I'm starting to realize, however 开头是 反驳的转折，与陈述句 倾向于认为 的口吻相反。What I'm starting to realize, however, is that new knowledge does not necessarily drive new results
questions.quote: It can be easy to assume that the gap between where you are now and where you want to be in the future is caused by a lack of knowledge.

questions.prompt: Learning can benefit you by itself, but only practice can turn what you learn into meaningful contributions.
questions.explanation:
**答案** I 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
学习本身可以使你受益,但只有练习才能将你所学的东西转化为有意义的贡献。
**锚点** for you vs meaningful contributions
**定位** 学习本身对你自己可能有价值，但如果你想对他人产生价值，就必须以某种方式把你所学的表达出来。
**改写** Learning can benefit you by itself ↔ Learning by itself can be valuable for you同义重述only practice can turn what you learn into meaningful contributions ↔practice is the only way to make a meaningful contribution with your knowledge唯一路径同义重述
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
H H 段的 Passive learning is not a form of practice 是 包含关系判断，不涉及meaningful contribution 这一价值出口。Passive learning is not a form of practice because although you gain new knowledge, you are not discovering how to apply that knowledge
questions.quote: Learning by itself can be valuable for you, but if you want to be valuable to others, then you have to express your knowledge in some way.

questions.prompt: Practice involves repeating a process intentionally to attain a particular objective.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
练习涉及有意识地重复一个过程以达到特定目标。
**锚点** 练习的定义：重复以达目标
**定位** 他说：当我们练习某事时，我们是在带着达成某个具体目标的意图，刻意地重复一个过程。
**改写** repeating a process ↔ repetition of a process动名词与名词同义intentionally ↔ deliberate repetition of a process with the intention of reaching a specific goal副词与原文 deliberate/intention 对应to attain a particular objective↔ reaching a specific goal动宾同义替换
questions.quote: He says: "When we practice something, we are involved in the deliberate repetition of a process with the intention of reaching a specific goal."

title: If we care about plastic waste, why won't we stop drinking bottled water? We have all seen the damage plastic waste is doing around the world, but sales of bottled water have continued to grow.

passage.label: A

sentences.text: For all the innovation and choice that define the food and drink industries, if you want to make money, you could do a lot worse than fill a bottle with water and sell it.
A litre of tap water, the stuff we have cleverly piped into our homes, costs less than half a penny.
A litre of bottled water can cost well over a pound, especially for something fancy that has been sucked through a mountain.

passage.translation: 尽管食品和饮料行业充满创新和选择，但如果你想赚钱，往瓶子里灌水去卖可能是最稳妥的办法之一。一升自来水，也就是我们巧妙地通过管道引入家中的水，成本不到半便士。而一升瓶装水的售价可能远超一英镑，尤其是那些号称经过山体过滤的高档水。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: Yet the bottled water market is livelier than ever.
It defies our increasing awareness of the harm plastics do to the environment and a broader, growing sense that something has to change.
Sales in the UK were worth a record £558.4 million this past year, an increase of 7%, according to the latest figures from the market analyst Kantar.
Separate data from other analysts show that last year the British consumed more than 2.2 billion litres of bottled water, including "take-home" and "on-the-go" products.
That's an annual rise in volume of 8.5%.

passage.translation: 然而，瓶装水市场比以往任何时候都更加活跃。它无视我们对塑料危害环境的日益认识，也无视一种更广泛、日益增长的变革意识。根据市场分析机构Kantar的最新数据，英国去年的销售额达到创纪录的5.584亿英镑，增长了7%。其他分析机构的独立数据显示，去年英国人消费了超过22亿升瓶装水，包括"家用"和"即饮"产品。这相当于销量年增长8.5%。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: Environmental campaigners are struggling to understand why nations blessed with clean tap water grow only fonder of the bottle.
"It's very surprising to me," says Sam Chetan-Walsh, a political adviser at Greenpeace and campaigner against ocean plastic.
"Public awareness has never been higher, but the message is not quite reaching all the people it needs to."
Where it is heard, the message is causing concern.
Plastic water bottles require oceans of fossil fuels to make and ship.
Additionally, single-use plastics of all types are polluting our cities and seas.
Numerous documentaries have shown how plastic is ultimately killing wildlife.

passage.translation: 环保活动人士难以理解，为什么拥有清洁自来水的国家却对瓶装水愈发青睐。Greenpeace政治顾问兼海洋塑料反对运动者Sam Chetan-Walsh说："这让我非常惊讶。公众意识从未如此之高，但信息并没有完全传达到所有需要听到的人。"在听到这一信息的地方，它正引发担忧。塑料水瓶的制造和运输需要消耗大量化石燃料。此外，各类一次性塑料正在污染我们的城市和海洋。众多纪录片已展示塑料最终如何杀死野生动物。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: Moves against various plastics have gathered pace, from shopping bags to straws and plastic-lined coffee cups.
Chetan-Walsh argues that bottled water is different because the alternatives are so obvious.
"If a product that is so nakedly unnecessary can exist, then the whole system is failing," he says.

passage.translation: 针对各类塑料制品的行动正在加速推进，从购物袋到吸管再到塑料内衬咖啡杯。Chetan-Walsh认为瓶装水与众不同，因为替代品显而易见。他说："如果一种如此明显不必要的产品都能存在，那么整个体系就是失败的。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Hope is not entirely out of reach.
The rate of growth has begun to ease (sales were up 7% in the year, compared with 8% the previous year).

passage.translation: 希望并非完全遥不可及。增长速度已开始放缓(当年销售额增长7%,而前一年为8%)。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: But even if large numbers of people are quitting bottled water because of care for the environment, others are taking it up.
The introduction of the "sugar tax" on juices and soda drinks has pushed more people to bottled water, while health awareness has boosted its desirability.
Tap water consumption is growing at roughly the same pace (UK consumers still drink almost three times as much tap water as bottled water).

passage.translation: 但即使大量人群因关心环境而放弃瓶装水,其他人却开始使用它。针对果汁和碳酸饮料征收的"糖税"促使更多人转向瓶装水,而健康意识也提升了它的吸引力。自来水消费量正以大致相同的速度增长(英国消费者饮用的自来水仍然几乎是瓶装水的三倍)。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: So the plastic tide only creeps higher.
The industry is quick to point out that all its bottles are recyclable.
"But collection rates are, at the most generous estimates, 56%, so the actual recycling rate will be lower than that," Chetan-Walsh says.
And while bottles may be recyclable, very few are made of recycled plastic.
One water bottle company launched recycled half-litre "eco" bottles alongside its standard bottles.
Another has pledged to use only recycled plastic across its range by 2025.
Chetan-Walsh believes in a ban on single-use bottles.
Bans do exist in some places.
Organisers of a famous music festival announced that water bottles will not be sold this summer.
San Francisco has banned them from city property and events.
Last year, the UK government set out plans to ban single-use plastic from its estate.

passage.translation: 因此塑料洪流只会越涨越高。该行业迅速指出其所有瓶子都可回收。"但回收率按最乐观估计也只有56%,所以实际回收率会更低,"Chetan-Walsh说。虽然瓶子可能是可回收的,但很少由回收塑料制成。一家瓶装水公司推出了回收材料制成的半升"环保"瓶,与其标准瓶并行销售。另一家公司承诺到2025年在其全系列产品中只使用回收塑料。Chetan-Walsh主张禁止一次性瓶装水。某些地方确实存在禁令。一个著名音乐节的组织者宣布今年夏天将不再销售瓶装水。San Francisco已在市政财产和活动中禁止使用。去年,英国政府制定了在其管辖范围内禁止一次性塑料的计划。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Water bottlers, unsurprisingly, don't support bans.
But they raise concerns about health rather than profit margins.

Last month one chief executive of a water bottling company said that bans would "result in greater consumption of sugary drinks, adding to all the health dangers of obesity, diabetes and tooth decay".
Kinvara Carey, general manager of an association of the biggest bottled water manufacturers, cites a survey in which people were asked what they would do if bottled water were not available.
"Forty-four per cent would buy another drink, which is not great, 14% would go without and 4.5% said they would find a fountain," she says.
"The choice is important."

passage.translation: 不出所料,瓶装水生产商不支持禁令。但他们提出的担忧涉及健康而非利润率。上月一家瓶装水公司的首席执行官表示,禁令将"导致含糖饮料消费增加,加剧肥胖、糖尿病和蛀牙等所有健康危害"。几家最大瓶装水制造商协会的总经理Kinvara Carey引用了一项调查,询问人们如果没有瓶装水会怎么做。她说:"44%的人会购买其他饮料,这并不理想,14%会不喝,4.5%表示会去找饮水机。选择很重要。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: What if fountains were more numerous, and tap water more clearly available in cafes, restaurants and elsewhere?
Dozens of fountains are being installed in London.
There are similar initiatives elsewhere.
Before plastic and the marketing that made people think they needed bottled water in the first place, fountains were an urban fixture.
Greenpeace, among others, is also pushing for a "deposit return" scheme.
This would mean tax on bottled water would be refunded to customers who returned the plastic for recycling.

passage.translation: 如果饮水机更多,自来水在咖啡馆、餐厅和其他地方更容易获得会怎样?伦敦正在安装数十个饮水机。其他地方也有类似举措。在塑料和让人们认为自己首先需要瓶装水的营销出现之前,饮水机曾是城市的固定设施。Greenpeace等组织也在推动"押金返还"计划。这意味着瓶装水税款将退还给那些归还塑料用于回收的顾客。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: Even if bottled water sales are growing slightly more slowly, the industry is racing to adapt to changing concerns and tastes.
Flavoured water is booming: sales of the sparkling variety shot up by 20%, according to the latest analyst data.
Meanwhile, international water brands, as well as a range of new companies, are selling high-end reusable bottles.
And if you must fill them with tap water, why not add flavouring?

passage.translation: 即使瓶装水销售增长略有放缓,该行业仍在竞相适应不断变化的关切和口味。风味水正在蓬勃发展:根据最新分析数据,气泡水销量飙升了20%。与此同时,国际水品牌以及一系列新公司正在销售高端可重复使用水瓶。如果你必须用自来水灌装它们,为什么不添加调味剂呢?

passage.label: K

sentences.text: As the owner of multiple sugary drink brands and bottled water, PepsiCo is facing challenges on health and environmental fronts.
Last year, the company bought SodaStream (a drinks company that sells machines for making tap water bubbly and then consumers add flavours) for $3.2 billion.
It also launched a range of fancy bottles that work with tap water and flavour packets.
The bottle is reusable.
The packets?
Not so much, and, yes, they are made of plastic, although the company invites users to post them back for recycling.

passage.translation: 作为多个含糖饮料品牌和瓶装水的所有者,PepsiCo在健康和环保方面都面临挑战。去年,该公司以32亿美元收购了SodaStream(一家销售使自来水变气泡水的机器,然后消费者添加风味剂的饮料公司)。它还推出了一系列与自来水和风味包配套使用的高档水瓶。瓶子可重复使用。风味包呢?不太行,而且,是的,它们由塑料制成,尽管该公司邀请用户将其寄回回收。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: As is so often the case, clever marketing can beat reason; awareness is rarely enough.
"There is always this kind of slip between concern, intent and changed behaviour," says Giles Quick, an analyst of bottled water.
"The best example is five a day, the recommendation to have at least five portions of fruit and vegetables every day.
Almost everyone is aware of this, but something like 15%of us achieve it."
Unless a far-reaching bottle ban does come into force, it will be up to consumers to not only demand change—but to act themselves.

passage.translation: 正如常见的情况,巧妙的营销可以战胜理性;意识往往是不够的。瓶装水分析师Giles Quick说:"关切、意图和行为改变之间总是存在这种脱节。最好的例子是每日五份,即每天至少摄入五份水果和蔬菜的建议。几乎每个人都知道这一点,但我们中只有大约15%的人做到了。"除非出台一项影响深远的瓶装水禁令,否则这将取决于消费者不仅要求变革,而且要自己采取行动。

Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: Judging from the slowing rate of sales growth, there is still hope to combat bottled water.
questions.explanation:
**答案** E 段（强锚点）

questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段的重点是 Sales in the UK were worth a record £558.4 million this past year, an increase of 7%，强调“销售在涨”，没有 slowing 这层意思，也没有 there is still hope 这一对照，所以只是话题相邻、并非源头段。Sales in the UK were worth a record £558.4 million this past year, an increase of 7%

**答案** B 段（强锚点）

questions.prompt: It often happens that people can lack reason when faced with skillful marketing.
questions.explanation:
**答案** L 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
人们在面对巧妙的营销时往往会丧失理性。
**锚点** 营销压过理性
**定位** 正如经常发生的那样，聪明的营销能压过理性；仅有意识远远不够。
**改写** people can lack reason when faced with skillful marketing ↔ clever marketing can beat reason视角翻转的等值改写It often happens that ↔ As is so often the case频度状语同义

questions.prompt: One city on the west coast of America has banned single-use bottles from its property and events.

美国西海岸的一座城市已在其物业和活动中禁止使用一次性瓶装水。
**锚点** 美国西海岸某城禁瓶

**辨邻**

**锚点** 化石燃料消耗
**定位** 塑料水瓶的生产和运输需要消耗海量的化石燃料。
**改写** Manufacturing and shipping of plastic water bottles ↔Plastic water bottles require oceans of fossil fuels to make and ship动词不定式对动名词consume a tremendous amount of fossil fuels ↔ require oceans of fossil fuels夸张量词同义替换

questions.prompt: One large beverage company has adapted its operations when confronted with challenges from health and environmental advocates.
questions.explanation:
**答案** K 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
一家大型饮料公司在面对健康和环保倡导者的挑战时调整了其运营。
**锚点** 一家大饮料公司因双压力做调整
**定位** 百事可乐作为多个含糖饮料品牌和瓶装水的母公司，正面临着来自健康和环保两个方面的挑战。
**改写** One large beverage company ↔ PepsiCo具体公司对应上位描述adapted its operations ↔the company bought SodaStream (a drinks company that sells machines for making tap water bubbly and then consumers add flavours) for $3.2 billion动作概括对具体举措challenges from health and environmental advocates ↔facing challenges on health and environmental fronts原词复现
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
H H 段主语是反对禁令的瓶装水厂商，重点是 they raise concerns about health rather than profit margins——他们打健康牌反对禁令，而非“主动调整”。陈述句要的是“一家大公司被双压力推着做调整”，方向不符。they raise concerns about health rather than profit margins
questions.quote: As the owner of multiple sugary drink brands and bottled water, PepsiCo is facing challenges on health and environmental fronts.

questions.prompt: Bottled water is considerably more expensive than tap water.
questions.explanation:
**答案** A 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
瓶装水比自来水贵得多。
**锚点** 瓶装水比自来水贵很多
**定位** 一升自来水——也就是我们巧妙地通过管道引入家中的那种水——花费不到半便士。一升瓶装水却可能要花掉一英镑多，尤其是那种被吹嘘“从山中取水”的高端货。

questions.prompt: Fountains could be seen in cities before bottled water became popular.
questions.explanation:
**答案** I 段（强锚点）

在瓶装水流行之前,城市里可以看到喷泉。
**锚点** 瓶装水流行前城市里有饮水龙头

questions.prompt: More people have taken to bottled water because of their health awareness.
questions.explanation:
**答案** F 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
由于健康意识,更多人开始饮用瓶装水。
**锚点** 因健康意识转向瓶装水
**定位** 对果汁和苏打饮料征收的“糖税”，把更多人推向了瓶装水；与此同时，健康意识的提升也增强了瓶装水的吸引力。
**改写** More people have taken to bottled water ↔ has pushed more people to bottled water动词同义替换because of their health awareness ↔ health awareness has boosted its desirability原因状语对主谓因果
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
H H 段重点是 they raise concerns about health rather than profit margins——是厂商用健康话术反对禁令；陈述句要的是消费者因健康意识转向瓶装水，施动者与情节都不符。they raise concerns about health rather than profit margins
questions.quote: The introduction of the "sugar tax" on juices and soda drinks has pushed more people to bottled water, while health awareness has boosted its desirability.

title: Why it's wrong to look at work-life balance as an achievement

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Few topics have been so endlessly analysed as work-life balance.
The quest to attain this mysterious state has dominated discussion around careers for years—especially for working parents.
The concept is often presented as something to achieve, or a goal to reach.
And once you've reached it, congratulations: you've made it; you're a successful human being of the 21st century.

passage.translation: 很少有话题像工作与生活的平衡这样被无休止地分析。多年来,获得这种神秘状态的追求一直主导着有关职业的讨论——尤其是对于在职父母而言。这个概念常常被呈现为需要达成的某种东西,或需要到达的目标。一旦你达到了,恭喜你:你成功了;你是21世纪成功的人。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: But the problem is that we often tell ourselves: "I'm going to put in eight hours' worth of work, and then I'm going to put in eight hours' worth of 'me time', which will include my family, my hobbies, my workout, my everything," says Anat Lechner, clinical associate professor of management at New York University.
"I don't think it's such a simple formula."

passage.translation: 但问题在于,我们常常告诉自己:"我要投入八小时的工作,然后我要投入八小时的'自我时间',其中将包括我的家庭、我的爱好、我的锻炼、我的一切",纽约大学管理学临床副教授Anat Lechner说。"我认为这不是如此简单的公式。"

passage.label: C

sentences.text: And, according to new findings, it may not be.
Some researchers are now encouraging us to stop thinking about work-life balance as an achievement that you either hit or don't.
Instead, they suggest it may be more of a lifelong process—a continuous, never-ending exercise that requires self- awareness and timely adjustments.
Researchers Ioana Lupu and Mayra Ruiz-Castro argue that work- life balance is "a cycle, not an achievement".

In their 2020 study, the researchers interviewed nearly 80 employees at two London-based firms—an equal number of men and women between the ages of 30 and 50, all with at least one dependent child—who worked in middle or senior management roles.

passage.translation: 而且,根据新的研究发现,可能并非如此。一些研究人员现在鼓励我们停止将工作与生活的平衡视为一种你要么达到要么达不到的成就。相反,他们认为这更可能是一个终身的过程——一个持续的、永无止境的实践,需要自我意识和及时的调整。研究人员Ioana Lupu和Mayra Ruiz-Castro认为,工作与生活的平衡是"一个循环,而非一项成就"。在他们2020年的研究中,研究人员采访了伦敦两家公司的近80名员工——年龄在30至50岁之间的男性和女性人数相等,都至少有一个需要抚养的孩子——他们担任中层或高层管理职位。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: Although it sounds like the respondents had a lot in common, here's what separated them: about 30%of the men and 50% of the women reported resisting working long hours.
The other respondents, meanwhile, all worked long hours because they thought that's what successful professionals should do.

passage.translation: 虽然听起来受访者有很多共同点,但以下是区分他们的因素:约30%的男性和50%的女性报告说抵制长时间工作。与此同时,其他受访者都长时间工作,因为他们认为这是成功的专业人士应该做的。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Lupu and Ruiz-Castro looked at those who rejected the long hours and they found that those workers actually had strikingly similar strategies for maintaining their work-life balance.
They had a tendency to reflect and question assumptions in the name of self-awareness and regularly took steps to adjust the things standing in their way to work-life balance.

passage.translation: Lupu和Ruiz-Castro研究了那些拒绝长时间工作的人,他们发现这些员工实际上在维持工作与生活平衡方面有着惊人相似的策略。他们倾向于以自我意识的名义反思和质疑假设,并定期采取措施调整阻碍他们实现工作与生活平衡的事情。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: Lupu and Ruiz-Castro identified five steps that the respondents in the study who had better work-life balance used in their jobs.
First, they paused and reconsidered beliefs such as "I'm a professional, so I should work, work, work", and asked themselves questions like, "What's currently causing me stress?"
Second, after identifying the cause, they zeroed in on their resultant emotions.
Did they feel angry, sad, energised?
Third, they reprioritised, asking "Is working long hours really worth cutting back on family time?", for example.
Fourth, they considered their alternatives: is there anything at work that could be changed to accommodate these new priorities?
And finally, they implemented changes, like asking their supervisor for greater flexibility, or deciding not to take on every project that comes their way.

passage.translation: Lupu和Ruiz-Castro确定了研究中工作与生活平衡更好的受访者在工作中使用的五个步骤。首先,他们暂停并重新考虑诸如"我是专业人士,所以我应该工作、工作、工作"之类的信念,并问自己诸如"目前是什么导致我压力"之类的问题。其次,在确定原因后,他们专注于由此产生的情绪。他们是感到愤怒、悲伤还是充满活力?第三,他们重新确定优先级,例如问"长时间工作真的值得减少家庭时间吗?"第四,他们考虑自己的选择:工作中是否有任何可以改变的地方来适应这些新的优先事项?最后,他们实施改变,比如要求主管提供更大的灵活性,或决定不承担每一个项目。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: This five-step process is something anyone can adopt.
Going through the steps, and constantly checking in with yourself, can help you shift and adapt your professional life to something that will better harmonise with your personal one.
"Awareness of your emotional state is essential in order to determine the changes you want to make in your work and in your life," says Lupu.

passage.translation: 这个五步骤过程是任何人都可以采用的。经历这些步骤,并不断与自己核对,可以帮助你转变和调整你的职业生活,使其更好地与你的个人生活协调。"意识到你的情绪状态对于确定你想在工作和生活中做出的改变至关重要",Lupu说。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: New York University's Lechner agrees that finding that balance is an ongoing pursuit.
It's not simply about dividing up the hours in your day between work, the gym, kids and chores.
If the underlying emotional sources of stress are still there, then the time you actually spend at home may not be enjoyable.
"We come home and even though physically we are there, mentally we still may be processing things that happened at work.
We're not present," she says.
What we call "work-life balance" is actually just a substitute to having a sense of fulfillment and contentment.

passage.translation: 纽约大学的Lechner同意找到平衡是一个持续的追求。这不仅仅是在工作、健身房、孩子和家务之间分配你一天中的时间。如果压力的潜在情绪根源仍然存在,那么你实际在家度过的时间可能并不愉快。"我们回到家,尽管身体上我们在那里,但精神上我们可能仍在处理工作中发生的事情。我们并不在场",她说。我们所说的"工作与生活的平衡"实际上只是拥有成就感和满足感的替代品。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Of course, finding that balance probably shouldn't be something you have to do by yourself.
Research by Erin Kelly, professor of work and organisation studies at MIT, shows companies and managers can play a key role in creating a better environment for workers.

For her book Overload: How Good Jobs Went Bad and What to Do about It, she and co-author Phyllis Moen split more than 1,000 employees at a Fortune 500 company into two groups, one that worked under a management redesign and one that continued working within the existing management structure.

passage.translation: 当然,找到那种平衡可能不应该是你必须独自完成的事情。MIT工作与组织研究教授Erin Kelly的研究表明,公司和管理者可以在为员工创造更好的环境方面发挥关键作用。在她的著作《超载:好工作如何变坏以及该怎么办》中,她和合著者Phyllis Moen将《财富》500强公司的1000多名员工分为两组,一组在管理重新设计下工作,另一组继续在现有管理结构内工作。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: Under the management redesign, many steps were taken to ensure better work-life balance and prevent burnout(精疲力竭).
Managers were regularly reminded to explicitly support their employees.
Workers were allowed to make changes, like cancelling 9 am meetings.
All of this was done in the name of increasing job satisfaction and giving workers greater flexibility, and to assure workers that it was something management was committed to.
Unsurprisingly, Kelly and Moen found that employees in the redesign group reported less stress and less burnout.
They were less likely to quit their jobs; indeed, over the next four years, they were 40% less likely to quit than those who kept working under the old policies.

passage.translation: 在管理重新设计下,采取了许多措施来确保更好的工作与生活平衡并防止精疲力竭。管理者被定期提醒要明确支持他们的员工。员工被允许做出改变,比如取消上午9点的会议。所有这一切都是为了提高工作满意度和给予员工更大的灵活性,并向员工保证这是管理层致力于的事情。不出所料,Kelly和Moen发现重新设计组的员工报告压力更小,精疲力竭更少。他们不太可能辞职;实际上,在接下来的四年里,他们辞职的可能性比那些继续在旧政策下工作的人低40%。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: "Work-life balance is understood to be an individual's response, so people think 'it's up to me to manage the craziness of my work life'", says Kelly.
But organisations need to examine the demands they're placing on employees.
"The root problem is not how the two pieces of work and life come together.
It's that we have unrealistic expectations of what we're asked to do on the work side."
If your workplace isn't an environment where work-life balance is possible in the first place, any effort you attempt to make toward it on a personal level will be in vain.

passage.translation: "工作与生活的平衡被理解为个人的反应,所以人们认为'管理我工作生活的疯狂取决于我'",Kelly说。但组织需要审查他们对员工提出的要求。"根本问题不是工作和生活这两部分如何结合在一起。而是我们对工作方面要求我们做的事情抱有不切实际的期望。"如果你的工作场所首先就不是一个可以实现工作与生活平衡的环境,那么你在个人层面上为此做出的任何努力都将是徒劳的。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: That's a conversation that appears to be gathering pace.
The new prevalence of remote and flexible working models will likely all play important roles in how we balance our professional and personal lives.
And if it seems like finding that perfect balance remains difficult to achieve, the experts say that keeping some perspective can help.
For millions of people, work is about being able to put food on the table.
Talking about work-life balance "is a very privileged conversation", says Lechner.
"If we're reflecting, maybe we should also reflect on that."

passage.translation: 这是一场似乎正在加速进行的对话。远程和灵活工作模式的新普及可能都将在我们如何平衡职业和个人生活方面发挥重要作用。如果找到那种完美的平衡似乎仍然难以实现,专家们说保持一些视角可以有所帮助。对于数百万人来说,工作是为了能够把食物摆上餐桌。谈论工作与生活的平衡"是一个非常特权的对话",Lechner说。"如果我们在反思,也许我们也应该反思这一点。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: According to a management expert, work-life balance is not as simple as giving equal amounts of time to work and personal life.
questions.explanation:
**答案** B 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
据一位管理专家所说,工作与生活的平衡并不像给工作和个人生活分配同等时间那样简单。
**锚点** 管理学专家观点+工作生活时间不能简单等分
**定位** 但问题在于，我们常常对自己说："我要投入八小时来工作，然后再投入八小时给"自己的时间"，包括家人、爱好、锻炼、一切。"纽约大学管理学临床副教授 Anat Lechner 说。"我不认为它是一个这么简单的公式。"
**改写** According to a management expert ↔Anat Lechner, clinical associate professor of management at New York University身份概括上位not as simple as giving equal amounts of time to work and personal life ↔eight hours' worth of work, and then I'm going to put in eight hours' worth of 'me time'具体公式被概括为等量时间分配not as simple as ↔ I don't think it's such a simple formula否定结论同义改写
questions.quote: But the problem is that we often tell ourselves: "I'm going to put in eight hours' worth of work, and then I'm going to put in eight hours' worth of 'me time', which will include my family, my hobbies, my workout, my everything," says Anat Lechner, clinical associate professor of management at New York University. "I don't think it's such a simple formula."

questions.prompt: Research found that those who are given greater flexibility at work are less stressed and more likely to stay in their jobs.
questions.explanation:
**答案** J 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
研究发现,那些在工作中被给予更大灵活性的人压力更小,更有可能留在他们的工作岗位上。
**锚点** 更大灵活性+压力更小+更愿留任
**定位** 不出意外，Kelly 和 Moen 发现，重新设计组的员工报告称压力更小、倦怠更少。他们更不容易离职；事实上，在接下来的四年里，他们离职的可能性比那些仍在旧政策下工作的员工低 40%。
**改写** given greater flexibility at work ↔ giving workers greater flexibility几乎逐字同义are less stressed ↔ less stress and less burnout形容词与名词同根改写more likely to stay in their jobs ↔40% less likely to quit than those who kept working under the old policies正话反说
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
I I 段只说 split more than 1,000 employees at a Fortune 500 company into two groups 这种实验设置，未提到"压力更小""更愿留任"，因此尽管同样涉及灵活性话题，也只能算邻段，不是源头段。she and co-author Phyllis Moen split more than 1,000 employees at a Fortune 500 company into two groups, one that worked under a management redesign and one that continued working within the existing management structure
questions.quote: Unsurprisingly, Kelly and Moen found that employees in the redesign group reported less stress and less burnout. They were less likely to quit their jobs; indeed, over the next four years, they were 40% less likely to quit than those who kept working under the old policies.

questions.prompt: Workers who rejected working long hours tended to make regular adjustments in order to achieve work-life balance.
questions.explanation:
**答案** E 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
拒绝长时间工作的员工往往会进行定期调整以实现工作与生活的平衡。
**锚点** 拒绝加班者+常态化调整
**定位** Lupu 和 Ruiz-Castro 研究了那些拒绝长时间工作的人，发现这些人维持工作-生活平衡的策略惊人地相似。他们倾向于在自我觉察的名义下反思并质疑既有假设，并经常采取行动去调整阻碍他们实现工作-生活平衡的因素。
**改写** Workers who rejected working long hours ↔ those who rejected the long hours近乎逐字同义make regular adjustments in order to achieve work-life balance ↔regularly took steps to adjust the things standing in their way to work-life balance副词转形容词的等值改写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
F F 段 five steps 与逐条罗列 paused and reconsidered beliefs 是"方法的具体细化"；陈述句没有提到"五步"也没有提到具体步骤，只说"定期调整"，因此匹配的是 E 段的概括，不是 F 段的清单。Lupu and Ruiz-Castro identified five steps that the respondents in the study who had better work- life balance used in their jobs D D 段 about 30% of the men and 50% of the women reported resisting working long hours 只在分类陈述群体，未提及他们"定期调整"等策略，不能承载陈述句的核心信息。about 30% of the men and 50% of the women reported resisting working long hours
questions.quote: Lupu and Ruiz-Castro looked at those who rejected the long hours and they found that those workers actually had strikingly similar strategies for maintaining their work-life balance. They had a tendency to reflect and question assumptions in the name of self-awareness and regularly took steps to adjust the things standing in their way to work-life balance.

questions.prompt: Talking about work-life balance is said to be a privilege reserved for the better-off, not for those who barely make a living.
questions.explanation:
**答案** L 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
据说谈论工作与生活的平衡是富裕阶层的特权,而不是那些勉强维持生计的人的特权。
**锚点** 特权对话+富裕者vs糊口者
**定位** 对于数百万人来说，工作就是为了能把饭端上桌。谈论工作-生活平衡，"是一场非常特权化的对话"，Lechner 说。"如果我们在反思，或许我们也该反思一下这一点。"
**改写** a privilege reserved for the better-off ↔Talking about work-life balance "is a very privileged conversation"同根词的名词与形容词改写not for those who barely make a living ↔For millions of people, work is about being able to put food on the table习语意义改写
questions.quote: For millions of people, work is about being able to put food on the table. Talking about work- life balance "is a very privileged conversation", says Lechner. "If we're reflecting, maybe we should also reflect on that."

questions.prompt: Knowing one's emotional state is of utmost importance in deciding what changes to make for a better work-life balance.
questions.explanation:
**答案** G 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
了解自己的情绪状态对于决定做出什么改变以实现更好的工作与生活平衡至关重要。
**锚点** 了解情绪状态+最关键+决定改变
**定位** "对自身情绪状态的觉察，对于决定你想在工作与生活中做出什么改变是至关重要的，"Lupu 说。
**改写** Knowing one's emotional state ↔ Awareness of your emotional state动名词与名词同义改写is of utmost importance ↔ is essential近义形容词与名词短语等值in deciding what changes to make for a better work-life balance ↔in order to determine the changes you want to make in your work and in your life目的状语等值改写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
F F 段 they zeroed in on their resultant emotions 只是五步中的第二步，没有说情绪觉察"至关重要"，没有承载"of utmost importance"这层定性。Second, after identifying the cause, they zeroed in on their resultant emotions H H 段 underlying emotional sources of stress are still there 描述情绪未处理的后果，没有提到"了解情绪状态对决定改变最重要"这一定性论断。If the underlying emotional sources of stress are still there, then the time you actually spend at home may not be enjoyable
questions.quote: "Awareness of your emotional state is essential in order to determine the changes you want to make in your work and in your life," says Lupu.

questions.prompt: More female professionals reported being reluctant to work overtime than their male counterparts.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
与男性同行相比,更多女性专业人士表示不愿意加班。
**锚点** 女性比男性更多人不愿加班
**定位** 尽管受访者听起来有很多共同点，但区别他们的关键是：大约 30% 的男性和 50% 的女性表示自己抗拒长时间工作。
**改写** More female professionals reported being reluctant to work overtime than their male counterparts↔ about 30% of the men and 50% of the women reported resisting working long hours数字大小关系转比较级being reluctant to work overtime ↔ resisting working long hours近义词同义替换
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E E 段 those who rejected the long hours 只是接着 D 段往下讲他们的策略，但没有出现 30% 或 50% 这种数字，也没有出现男女对比的字眼，不能承载本题男女比例对比的信息。Lupu and Ruiz-Castro looked at those who rejected the long hours and they found that those workers actually had strikingly similar strategies
questions.quote: Although it sounds like the respondents had a lot in common, here's what separated them: about 30% of the men and 50% of the women reported resisting working long hours.

questions.prompt: Without organisational support, any personal effort to maintain work-life balance will be unsuccessful.
questions.explanation:
**答案** K 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
没有组织支持,任何维持工作与生活平衡的个人努力都将不会成功。
**锚点** 缺乏组织支持+个人努力徒劳
**定位** 如果你的工作场所本身就不是一个能让工作-生活平衡得以实现的环境，那么你在个人层面上做出的任何努力都将徒劳无功。
**改写** Without organisational support ↔If your workplace isn't an environment where work-life balance is possible in the first place if not 等价 without any personal effort to maintain work-life balance will be unsuccessful ↔any effort you attempt to make toward it on a personal level will be in vain in vain 与 unsuccessful 同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
I I 段 companies and managers can play a key role in creating a better environment for workers 只说组织可以起作用，没有给出"如果组织不支持，个人努力将徒劳"的反向结论。companies and managers can play a key role in creating a better environment for workers J J 段 employees in the redesign group reported less stress and less burnout 是数据结论，没有出现"any effort…will be in vain"这种条件式徒劳判断。Unsurprisingly, Kelly and Moen found that employees in the redesign group reported less stress and less burnout
questions.quote: If your workplace isn't an environment where work-life balance is possible in the first place, any effort you attempt to make toward it on a personal level will be in vain.

questions.prompt: The question of how to achieve work-life balance has long been the main subject of discussion among workers.
questions.explanation:
**答案** A 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
如何实现工作与生活的平衡这一问题长期以来一直是员工讨论的主要话题。
**锚点** 长期讨论+主要话题
**定位** 很少有话题像工作-生活平衡这样被无休止地反复分析。多年来，追求这种神秘状态的努力一直主导着围绕职业的讨论——尤其是在职父母中间。
**改写** The question of how to achieve work-life balance ↔ The quest to attain this mysterious state同义短语替换has long been the main subject of discussion among workers ↔has dominated discussion around careers for years动词与名词短语的等值改写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
C C 段 Some researchers are now encouraging us to stop thinking about work- life balance as an achievement 是新研究角度，没有出现"长期/主要话题"这种总起判断。Some researchers are now encouraging us to stop thinking about work-life balance as an achievement that you either hit or don't
questions.quote: Few topics have been so endlessly analysed as work-life balance. The quest to attain this mysterious state has dominated discussion around careers for years—especially for working parents.

questions.prompt: You may not actually experience emotional wellbeing at home if you remain occupied with what happened at work.
questions.explanation:
**答案** H 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
如果你仍然被工作中发生的事情占据心思,你在家中可能不会真正体验到情感上的幸福。
**锚点** 在家但心还在工作+无法享受
**定位** 如果潜在的情绪压力源仍然存在，那么你真正待在家里的时间也可能并不愉快。"我们回到家，即便身体在那里，心里可能仍然在处理工作发生的事情。我们其实并不在场，"她说。
**改写** may not actually experience emotional wellbeing at home ↔the time you actually spend at home may not be enjoyable近义概念替换if you remain occupied with what happened at work ↔mentally we still may be processing things that happened at work比喻句的直陈改写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段 I'm going to put in eight hours' worth of work, and then I'm going to put in eight hours' worth of 'me time' 只是讨论时间公式，没有出现"身体在心理不在"这种意象。I'm going to put in eight hours' worth of work, and then I'm going to put in eight hours' worth of 'me time', which will include my family, my hobbies, my workout, my everything
questions.quote: If the underlying emotional sources of stress are still there, then the time you actually spend at home may not be enjoyable. "We come home and even though physically we are there, mentally we still may be processing things that happened at work. We're not present," she says.

questions.prompt: Some researchers suggest that work-life balance is not a goal to achieve, but a process for life to be adjusted promptly.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
一些研究人员认为,工作与生活的平衡不是一个要实现的目标,而是一个需要及时调整生活的
过 程 。
**锚点** 不是要达成的目标+是要随时调整的过程
**定位** 一些研究者现在鼓励我们不再把工作-生活平衡视为一种要么达成、要么没达成的成就。相反，他们认为它更可能是一个终身的过程——一个需要自我觉察与适时调整、持续不断的实践。研究者 Ioana Lupu 和 Mayra Ruiz-Castro 主张：工作-生活平衡"是一个循环，不是一种成就"。
**改写** not a goal to achieve↔ not an achievement近义词替换but a process for life to be adjusted promptly↔a lifelong process—a continuous, never-ending exercise that requires self-awareness and timely adjustments近义词替换+定语改写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段 I don't think it's such a simple formula 只是否定简单公式，没有正面提出"它是一种循环或过程"这种重新定义。I don't think it's such a simple formula H H 段 What we call "work-life balance" is actually just a substitute to having a sense of fulfillment and contentment 是"替代品"视角，没有出现"过程或循环"这种重新定义。What we call "work-life balance" is actually just a substitute to having a sense of fulfillment and contentment
questions.quote: Some researchers are now encouraging us to stop thinking about work-life balance as an achievement that you either hit or don't. Instead, they suggest it may be more of a lifelong process—a continuous, never-ending exercise that requires self-awareness and timely adjustments. Researchers Ioana Lupu and Mayra Ruiz-Castro argue that work-life balance is "a cycle, not an achievement".

title: Do you ever blend up a protein drink…

sentences.text: Do you ever blend up a protein drink for breakfast, or grab a protein bar following an afternoon workout?
If so, you are likely among the millions of people in search of more protein-rich diets.

passage.translation: 你是否曾在早餐时调制蛋白质饮料,或在下午锻炼后拿一根蛋白棒?如果是这样,你很可能是数百万寻求更多富含蛋白质饮食的人之一。

sentences.text: Protein-enriched products are found everywhere.
But contrary to all the publicity that everyone needs more protein, most Americans get twice as much as they need.

passage.translation: 富含蛋白质的产品随处可见。但与所有宣传每个人都需要更多蛋白质的说法相反,大多数美国人摄入的蛋白质是他们所需量的两倍。

sentences.text: Many of us living in the most developed countries are buying into a myth of protein deficiency created by food companies and self-identified health experts.
Global retail sales of protein supplement products reached an astonishing US$18.9 billion in 2020.

passage.translation: 我们中许多生活在最发达国家的人正在接受由食品公司和自封的健康专家制造的蛋白质缺乏神话。2020年全球蛋白质补充剂产品的零售额达到了惊人的189亿美元。

sentences.text: But are we really in need of more protein?
Physicians in the U.S. have never actually examined a patient with protein deficiency because simply by eating an adequate number of daily calories we are also most likely getting enough protein.

passage.translation: 但我们真的需要更多蛋白质吗?美国的医生实际上从未检查过蛋白质缺乏症患者,因为只要摄入足够的每日卡路里,我们很可能也在获得足够的蛋白质。

sentences.text: In fact, Americans currently consume almost twice the National Academy of Medicine's recommended daily intake of protein although the most desirable protein intake may vary depending on age and activity level.

passage.translation: 事实上,美国人目前摄入的蛋白质几乎是美国国家医学院推荐每日摄入量的两倍,尽管最理想的蛋白质摄入量可能因年龄和活动水平而异。

sentences.text: For example, if you're a dedicated athlete you might need to consume higher quantities of protein.

Generally, though, a 140-pound person should not exceed 120 grams of protein per day, particularly because a high protein diet can strain kidney and liver function and increase risks of developing heart disease and cancer.

passage.translation: 例如,如果你是一名专业运动员,你可能需要摄入更多蛋白质。但通常情况下,一个140磅重的人每天摄入的蛋白质不应超过120克,特别是因为高蛋白饮食会给肾脏和肝脏功能带来压力,并增加患心脏病和癌症的风险。

sentences.text: While fats and sugar have taken the beating in turns since over a century ago, protein has managed to remain our red-hot favorite.

passage.translation: 尽管自一个多世纪前以来脂肪和糖分轮流遭受抨击,但蛋白质一直是我们最受欢迎的营养素。

sentences.text: In the 1970s through the 1990s, protein products remained visible but moved back somewhat with the dietary spotlight firmly fixed on low-calorie, low-fat, sugar-free snack foods and beverages following the publication of studies linking sugar and saturated(饱和的) fat consumption to heart disease.

passage.translation: 在20世纪70年代到90年代,蛋白质产品依然可见,但随着研究发表将糖和饱和脂肪摄入与心脏病联系起来,饮食焦点牢牢锁定在低卡路里、低脂肪、无糖的零食和饮料上,蛋白质有所退居其次。

sentences.text: Later research in 2003, however, suggested high-protein diets could aid in weight loss, and protein quickly regained its former nutrient-superstar status.

passage.translation: 然而,2003年后来的研究表明高蛋白饮食可以帮助减肥,蛋白质迅速恢复了其以前的营养超级明星地位。

sentences.text: Now most people living in high-income nations are consuming enough protein.
When we replace meals with a protein bar or drink, we also risk missing out on the rich sources of antioxidants(抗氧化剂), vitamins and many other benefits of real food.

passage.translation: 现在大多数生活在高收入国家的人摄入了足够的蛋白质。当我们用蛋白棒或饮料代替正餐时,我们也有可能错过真正食物中丰富的抗氧化剂、维生素和许多其他益处。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about publicity over protein in America?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于美国对蛋白质的宣传,我们了解到什么?
A) 它帮助制造了蛋白质缺乏的神话。
B) 它帮助美国人寻找富含蛋白质的饮食。
C) 它在公众中引发了许多健康担忧。
D) 它得到了食品公司和健康专家的资助。
**判型** What do we learn about publicity over protein in America? 是一个 What…learn about 的事实型问句，直接问关于某对象（publicity）的某一事实，没有infer/suggest/imply 等推断信号。
**拆句** 句式平铺直叙：What do we learn about publicity over protein in America? 主干是What do we learn about X，介词短语 over protein 是 publicity 的范围限定，in America 限定地域，无陷阱。
**定位** 我们这些生活在大多数发达国家的人，正在接受一个由食品公司和自封的健康专家制造出来的"蛋白质缺乏"神话。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确buying into a myth of protein deficiency created by food companies and self-identified health experts↔ It has helped to create the myth of protein deficiency. contrary to all the publicity that everyone needs more protein ↔the myth of protein deficiency预判说"宣传促成了蛋白缺乏的迷思"，helped to create the myth of protein deficiency 一字不差地落到这个语义上，是定位句的直接同义替换。
B) 与原文相反原文用 buying into a myth 表明宣传是在"骗"美国人，并非"帮"他们；选项 helped Americans in search of protein-rich diets 把负面后果包装成正面服务，与原作者态度相反。
C) 无中生有原文从未说 publicity "raised health concerns"——P6 的健康风险讲的是高蛋白饮食本身，而非舆论造成的恐慌；选项 raised a lot of health concerns among the public在文中无落点。
D) 偷换概念原文说迷思是 created by food companies and self-identified health experts，主语是"食品公司和自封专家"在制造迷思；选项 funded by food companies and health experts 把 created 偷换成 funded（资助），且把 publicity 当受资助对象，主体与动作都被改写。
questions.quote: Many of us living in the most developed countries are buying into a myth of protein deficiency created by food companies and self-identified health experts.

options.text: It has helped to create the myth of protein deficiency.
It has helped Americans in search of protein-rich diets.
It has raised a lot of health concerns among the public.
It has been funded by food companies and health experts.

questions.prompt: Why have physicians in the U.S. never actually examined a patient with protein deficiency?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
为什么美国医生从未真正诊治过蛋白质缺乏症患者?
A) 美国人可以在各处购买到多种富含蛋白质的食品。
B) 美国人能够摄入食品专家推荐的卡路里量。
C) 美国人只需每天摄入足够的食物就能获得充足的蛋白质。
D) 美国人可以依靠食品补充剂来预防蛋白质缺乏。
**判型** Why have physicians in the U.S. never actually examined a patient with protein deficiency? 用 Why 直问原因，要求按原文给出的解释作答，不需要自行推断。
**拆句** 现在完成时 have…never actually examined，never 是关键否定词，actually 加强语气，提示原文给出的解释是"压根没机会见到"层面的原因；理解时把 never examined 当作"从未见过"即可。
**定位** 美国医生从未真正诊治过蛋白缺乏的病人，因为只要每天摄入足够的卡路里，我们也就极可能获得了足够的蛋白质。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问原文给出的原因是"日常热量摄入足够蛋白也就够了"，与"能否买到"无关；选项purchase many kinds of protein-rich foods everywhere 谈购买便利性，是另一回事。
B) 偷换概念原文说的是 an adequate number of daily calories"日常足量的卡路里"，选项 absorb the number of calories recommended by food experts 偷换为"食品专家推荐的卡路里数"——多了"food experts recommended"这一未出现的限定，且 absorb 与eating 含义偏移。
C) ✓ 正确simply by eating an adequate number of daily calories we are also most likely getting enough protein↔ Americans can get sufficient protein just by eating adequate foods daily.预判说"靠正常饮食的热量就够蛋白"，get sufficient protein just by eating adequate foods daily 几乎逐字对应，是 because 句的同义替换。
D) 与原文相反原文的因果是"正常饮食就够蛋白，所以不必靠补剂"；选项 rely on food supplements to prevent protein deficiency 反过来说"靠补剂预防缺乏"，正是全文批判的对象。
questions.quote: Physicians in the U.S. have never actually examined a patient with protein deficiency because simply by eating an adequate number of daily calories we are also most likely getting enough protein.

options.text: Americans can purchase many kinds of protein-rich foods everywhere.
Americans can absorb the number of calories recommended by food experts.
Americans can get sufficient protein just by eating adequate foods daily.
Americans can rely on food supplements to prevent protein deficiency.

questions.prompt: What should people take into consideration in deciding on the most preferable protein intake?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
人们在决定最理想的蛋白质摄入量时应考虑什么?
A) 他们有多健康以及他们吃什么食物。
B) 他们的年龄以及他们从事什么活动。
C) 他们摄入多少蛋白质以及他们的体重是多少。
D) 他们的蛋白质缺乏有多严重以及他们使用什么补救措施。
**判型** What should people take into consideration in deciding on the most preferable protein intake? 在问决策依据，原文必会以并列形式给出依据项，照搬即可。
**拆句** in deciding on… 是 in doing 结构作状语，表"在做某事的时候"；主干是 What should people take into consideration，把状语剥掉，问句就回归"应考虑什么"，简单。
**定位** 尽管最理想的蛋白摄入量可能因年龄和活动量不同而有所差异，美国人现在的蛋白摄入仍接近美国医学科学院推荐摄入量的两倍。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有原文只列了 age and activity level，并未把"现在健康程度"或"吃什么食物"列入考虑因素；选项 How healthy they are and what food they eat 是凭常识自造的因素。
B) ✓ 正确depending on age and activity level ↔ How old they are and what activities they do.预判的"年龄+活动量"两项，与 How old they are and what activities they do 一一对齐，是最直接的同义替换。
C) 偷换概念原文要讨论的是"理想蛋白摄入量"本身，选项 How much protein they consume and what their body weight is 反过来把"已经摄入多少蛋白"和"体重"作为考量因素，循环定义且无文本依据；P6 提到 140-pound 只是举例上限，并非"决定理想摄入量的因素"。
D) 与原文相反选项 How serious their protein deficiency is and what remedies they use 默认存在"protein deficiency"，但原文 P4 明确说美国医生从未见过蛋白缺乏患者，根本不存在这样的前提。
questions.quote: Americans currently consume almost twice the National Academy of Medicine's recommended daily intake of protein although the most desirable protein intake may vary depending on age and activity level.

options.text: How healthy they are and what food they eat.
How old they are and what activities they do.
How much protein they consume and what their body weight is.
How serious their protein deficiency is and what remedies they use.

questions.prompt: What foods have been largely out of favor for more than a century?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
哪些食物在一个多世纪以来基本上不受欢迎?
A) 无糖零食。
B) 富含蛋白质的食物。
C) 红肉和白肉。
D) 含糖和高脂肪食物。
**判型** What foods have been largely out of favor for more than a century? 是事实型问句，答案就在原文某句的事实陈述里。
**拆句** 现在完成时 have been largely out of favor 表过去到现在的持续状态；largely 是程度副词，表"在很大程度上"，提醒不要选"完全/彻底"等绝对化误读。
**定位** 一个多世纪以来，脂肪和糖轮流挨批，而蛋白质却始终是我们的红人。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反原文 dietary spotlight firmly fixed on low-calorie, low-fat, sugar-free snack foods说"无糖零食"是 1970-90 年代受追捧的对象，不是被嫌弃的对象；选项 Sugar-free snacks 把追捧对象当成 out of favor，颠倒立场。
B) 与原文相反原文 protein has managed to remain our red-hot favorite 明说蛋白质始终是favorite（红人），选项 Protein-rich foods 反过来说它失宠，180 度反向。
C) 无中生有原文 P7-P9 整段都在讲脂肪、糖和蛋白质这几类宏量营养素，从未提到"红肉/白肉"被批的话题；选项 Both red and white meats 是凭健康常识填空。
D) ✓ 正确fats and sugar ↔ Sugary and fatty foods. taken the beating in turns since over a century ago ↔largely out of favor for more than a century预判"脂肪和糖被批了一百多年"，Sugary and fatty foods 对齐对象，题干本身对齐时间与态度，三要素全合。
questions.quote: While fats and sugar have taken the beating in turns since over a century ago, protein has managed to remain our red-hot favorite.

options.text: Sugar-free snacks.
Protein-rich foods.
Both red and white meats.
Sugary and fatty foods.

questions.prompt: What does the author imply people in developed countries should do to keep healthy?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （推断题）
**题目译文**
作者暗示发达国家的人们应该做什么来保持健康?
A) 享用天然食物。
B) 吃素食。
C) 每天摄入足够的蛋白质。
D) 用蛋白质棒代替正餐。
**判型** What does the author imply people in developed countries should do to keep healthy? 题干直接用 imply，是推断题的标准句式。
**拆句** 句式较长但分层清晰：主干 What does the author imply X should do，宾语从句的主语是 people in developed countries，目的状语 to keep healthy；抓住"作者+暗示+发达国家民众+保持健康"四要素即可。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确rich sources of antioxidants(抗氧化剂), vitamins and many other benefits of real food↔Enjoy natural food. When we replace meals with a protein bar or drink, we also risk missing out on…↔Enjoy natural food.预判作者推荐"回到真实食物"，Enjoy natural food 正是这条推断的最贴文表达，且不超过一步推。
B) 过度推断原文只说不要靠补剂代餐、要享受真实食物的好处，从未要求 vegetarian diets（素食）；从"少吃加工补剂"推不到"完全吃素"，跨度过大。
C) 与原文相反全文一直在反驳"应该多吃蛋白"的舆论，Americans currently consume almost twice the National Academy of Medicine's recommended daily intake of protein 明示已经摄入过量；选项 Consume enough protein daily 仍劝读者每天摄入足够蛋白，与作者立场相反。
D) 与原文相反尾段明确告诫 When we replace meals with a protein bar or drink, we also risk missing out on…——"代餐"被定性为风险行为；选项 Replace meals with protein bars 反过来把它当成建议，立场颠倒。

options.text: Enjoy natural food.
Eat vegetarian diets.
Consume enough protein daily.
Replace meals with protein bars.

title: Research in human-vehicle interaction has shown even systems…

sentences.text: Research in human-vehicle interaction has shown even systems designed to automate driving are far from being error-proof.
Recent evidence points to drivers' limited understanding of what these systems can and cannot do as a contributing factor to system misuse.
A recent study tackles the issue of over-trusting drivers and the resulting system misuse from a legal viewpoint.
It looks at what the manufacturers of self-driving cars should legally do to ensure that drivers understand how to use the vehicles appropriately.

passage.translation: 人机交互研究表明,即使是为自动驾驶设计的系统也远非万无一失。最近的证据表明,驾驶员对这些系统能做什么和不能做什么的理解有限,是导致系统误用的一个因素。最近的一项研究从法律角度探讨了驾驶员过度信任以及由此导致的系统误用问题。该研究审视了自动驾驶汽车制造商在法律上应采取什么措施,以确保驾驶员理解如何正确使用车辆。

sentences.text: One solution suggested in the study involves requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements (EULAs), similar to the terms and conditions that require agreement when using new software products.
But this is far from ideal.
The agreement may not provide enough information to the driver, leading to confusion about the nature of the requests for agreement and their implications.
Further, most end users don't read EULAs.
A 2017 study shows 91 percent of people agree to them without reading.
Among young people, 97 percent agree without reviewing the terms.

passage.translation: 研究中提出的一个解决方案是要求购买者签署最终用户许可协议,类似于使用新软件产品时需要同意的条款和条件。但这远非理想。该协议可能无法向驾驶员提供足够的信息,导致对同意请求的性质及其含义产生混淆。此外,大多数最终用户不会阅读最终用户许可协议。2017年的一项研究显示,91%的人在未阅读的情况下就同意了这些协议。在年轻人中,97%的人在未审查条款的情况下就表示同意。

sentences.text: The issue is that, unlike using a smartphone app, operating a car has serious safety risks, whether the driver is human or software.
And human drivers need to consent to take responsibility for the outcomes of the software and hardware.

passage.translation: 问题在于,与使用智能手机应用程序不同,操作汽车具有严重的安全风险,无论驾驶员是人类还是软件。而且人类驾驶员需要同意对软件和硬件的结果承担责任。

sentences.text: "Warning fatigue" and distracted driving are also causes for concern.
For example, a driver, annoyed after receiving continuous warnings, could decide to just ignore the message.
Or, if the message is presented while the vehicle is in motion, it could represent a distraction.

Given these limitations and concerns, even if this mode of obtaining consent is to move forward, it likely won't fully protect automakers from their legal liability should the system malfunction(发生故障) or an accident occur.

passage.translation: "警告疲劳"和分心驾驶也是令人担忧的原因。例如,驾驶员在持续收到警告后感到恼火,可能决定直接忽略这些信息。或者,如果信息在车辆行驶时呈现,它可能会造成分心。鉴于这些局限性和担忧,即使这种获得同意的模式得以推进,它也可能无法在系统发生故障或事故发生时完全保护汽车制造商免受法律责任。

sentences.text: Driver training for self-driving vehicles can help ensure that drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations.
This needs to occur beyond the vehicle purchase.
Recent evidence shows even relying on the information provided by the seller is not going to answer many questions.
All of this considered, the road forward for self-driving cars is not going to be a smooth ride after all.

passage.translation: 针对自动驾驶车辆的驾驶员培训可以帮助确保驾驶员充分理解系统的能力和局限性。这需要在车辆购买之外进行。最近的证据表明,即使依赖销售商提供的信息也无法回答许多问题。考虑到所有这些因素,自动驾驶汽车的前进道路毕竟不会一帆风顺。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from research in human-vehicle interaction?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
我们从人机交互研究中了解到什么?
A) 自动驾驶系统绝非不会出错。
B) 无人驾驶车辆可能会被某些人滥用。
C) 自动驾驶汽车制造商没有意识到所涉及的法律问题。
D) 人类与无人驾驶车辆实现交互还有很长的路要走。
**判型** What do we learn from research in human-vehicle interaction? 直接问研究告诉了我们什么，答案必然是原文一句陈述的客观转述，不需要跨段推理。
**拆句** 结构平铺直叙：主句是 What do we learn from research in human-vehicle interaction，from 引导的介宾短语限定信息来源，无从句、无否定、无陷阱。
**定位** 人车交互领域的研究表明，即便是为自动驾驶而设计的系统，也远远谈不上无差错。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确systems designed to automate driving ↔ Automatic driving systems far from being error-proof ↔ by no means immune to errors预判要的是系统并非无差错，A 项 Automatic driving systems are by no means immune to errors 是对 systems designed to automate driving are far from being error-proof 的逐部分同义替换，无添加无减少，锁定 A。
B) 偷换概念Driverless vehicles are likely to be misused by some people 谈的是车被滥用，而题干问的是研究发现，定位句结论是系统易出错，两者不在同一语义层；滥用确实在system misuse 中提到但只是后续展开，并非首句的研究结论。
C) 无中生有Self-driving car manufacturers are not aware of the legal matters involved 称厂商对法律毫无意识，而原文 A recent study tackles the issue…from a legal viewpoint只是说有研究从法律角度切入，从未说厂商不知情。
D) 偷换概念There is a long way to go before humans can interact with driverless vehicles 把研究结论说成人车交互本身遥不可及，而原文人车交互只是研究领域名，研究真正的发现是系统易错，与是否能交互无关。
questions.quote: Research in human-vehicle interaction has shown even systems designed to automate driving are far from being error-proof.

options.text: Automatic driving systems are by no means immune to errors.
Driverless vehicles are likely to be misused by some people.
Self-driving car manufacturers are not aware of the legal matters involved.
There is a long way to go before humans can interact with driverless vehicles.

questions.prompt: What is the problem with requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
要求购买者签署最终用户许可协议存在什么问题?
A) 无论老少,最终用户都觉得条款难以理解。
B) 大多数最终用户签署时根本不会费心阅读条款。
C) 许多人经常对条款的措辞感到困惑。
D) 大多数最终用户即使通读后也不理解这些条款。
**判型** What is the problem with requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements? 询问一个具体做法的问题所在，属于对原文局部反面描述的提取。
**拆句** 结构清晰：What is the problem with… 主句问的是 problem，with 后跟动名词短语requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements 作 problem 的定语，整体无难点。
**定位** 更何况，大多数终端用户根本不读 EULA。2017 年的一项研究表明，91% 的人未读就同意了。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有End users, young and old alike, find the terms complex to interpret 说所有人都觉得条款难以解读，但原文只说大家压根不读，从未说他们读了之后觉得难懂。
B) ✓ 正确most end users don't read EULAs ↔Most end users sign them without bothering to read the terms 91 percent of people agree to them without reading ↔ Most end users预判要的是签前不读，B 项 Most end users sign them without bothering to read the terms 正是这一行为的标准表述，与原文双句合并对应，锁定 B。
C) 偷换概念Many people are often confused by the wording of the terms 说人们被措辞搞晕，但原文 leading to confusion about the nature of the requests for agreement and their implications 说的是对协议性质与含义的困惑，且这是协议信息不足的后果，不是本题题干问的 EULA 整体的根本问题。
D) 与原文相反Most end users do not understand the terms after reading them through 隐含的前提是用户把条款读完了，只是不懂；而原文 most end users don't read EULAs 的事实是用户根本没读，两者前提相反。
questions.quote: Further, most end users don't read EULAs. A 2017 study shows 91 percent of people agree to them without reading.

options.text: End users, young and old alike, find the terms complex to interpret.
Most end users sign them without bothering to read the terms.
Many people are often confused by the wording of the terms.
Most end users do not understand the terms after reading them through.

questions.prompt: What would drivers do when they suffer from "warning fatigue"?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
当驾驶员遭受"警告疲劳"时会怎么做?
A) 毫不拖延地保持汽车行驶。
B) 休息一会儿以避免疲劳驾驶。
C) 尽管反复警告也不采取行动。
D) 虽然疲劳但仍注意警告信息。
**判型** What would drivers do when they suffer from "warning fatigue"? 问的是在某情境下司机会做出何种动作，属于对原文具体情境的事实提取。
**拆句** 主句 What would drivers do 是常规疑问句，when 引导的时间状语从句 when they suffer from "warning fatigue" 限定情境，suffer from 意为遭受、深受其扰，无陷阱。
**定位** 举例来说，一名司机在接到接连不断的警告后心生厌烦，可能干脆决定无视这条信息。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Waste no time keeping the car moving 是 抓紧时间让车继续走，与原文 ignore the message 描述的不作为完全不是一回事。
B) 偷换概念Rest a while to avoid fatigue driving 在谈疲劳驾驶要休息，但原文 "Warning fatigue" 指对警告厌烦，并非生理疲劳。
C) ✓ 正确could decide to just ignore the message ↔ Take no action despite repeated warnings预判要的是无视警告这一行为，C 项 Take no action despite repeated warnings 把无视＝不作为、反复警告＝重复警告两端都精准对位，锁定 C。
D) 与原文相反Take note of the message though fatigued 是 虽然疲惫但仍留意警告，与原文 just ignore the message 完全相反。
questions.quote: For example, a driver, annoyed after receiving continuous warnings, could decide to just ignore the message.

options.text: Waste no time keeping the car moving.
Rest a while to avoid fatigue driving.
Take no action despite repeated warnings.
Take note of the message though fatigued.

questions.prompt: What does the author think of continuing to ask buyers to sign end-user license agreements?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者如何看待继续要求购买者签署最终用户许可协议?
A) 这可能无法保证发生事故时驾驶员的安全。
B) 这可能无法确保自动驾驶系统正常运行。
C) 这可能无法充分保护汽车制造商免受蓄意欺诈的指控。
D) 这可能无法为制造商提供充分的法律责任保护。
**判型** What does the author think of continuing to ask buyers to sign end-user license agreements? 虽问作者看法，但锁定于 EULAs 这一局部做法，仍以一句明确表态句为答案依据，属细节题。
**拆句** What does the author think of continuing to ask buyers to sign end-user license agreements? 中 think of 后接动名词 continuing，continuing 再接动词不定式 to ask buyers to sign…，是动名词+不定式连用的链式结构，意为对继续要求买家签 EULA 这件事，作者怎么看。
**定位** 鉴于这些局限与担忧，即使继续推行这种取得同意的方式，万一系统发生故障或事故发生，它也很可能无法在法律责任上充分保护汽车制造商。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴It will probably not guarantee the safety of drivers in case of accidents 谈的是事故中司机的安全保障，但原文 protect automakers from their legal liability 谈的是保护厂商免于法律责任，对象与内容都错位。
B) 偷换概念It likely won't ensure that the automatic driving system functions properly 谈的是系统能否正常运行，但原文谈的是法律层面对厂商的保护，二者根本不是一回事。
C) 偷换概念It likely won't fully protect automakers against accusations of deliberate cheating谈的是免于被指故意欺诈，但原文 legal liability 仅指法律责任，未涉及 deliberate cheating 故意欺诈这一更窄、更带主观恶意的范畴。
D) ✓ 正确it likely won't fully protect automakers from their legal liability ↔It will probably not provide manufacturers adequate protection from legal responsibilities automakers ↔ manufacturers预判要的是不能充分保护厂商的法律责任，D 项 It will probably not provide manufacturers adequate protection from legal responsibilities 与定位句逐字对位，锁定 D。
questions.quote: Given these limitations and concerns, even if this mode of obtaining consent is to move forward, it likely won't fully protect automakers from their legal liability should the system malfunction(发生故障) or an accident occur.

questions.prompt: What should be done to help drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
应该做什么来帮助驾驶员充分了解系统的功能和局限性?
A) 培训他们成为车辆自动化方面的专家。

C) 拓宽他们对事故预防机制的了解。
D) 便利他们获取销售方提供的信息。
**判型** What should be done to help drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations? 直接问该做什么以达成目的，属于对原文解决方案句的提取。
**拆句** 主句 What should be done 是被动疑问句，to help 引导的不定式作目的状语，help drivers 后接动词原形 fully understand…，整句意思是：为帮司机充分理解系统能力与局限，应该做什么。
**定位** 针对自动驾驶汽车的司机培训，能够帮助确保司机充分了解系统的能力与局限。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断Training them to be experts in vehicle automation 把目标拔到成为车辆自动化领域专家的高度，而原文只要求 fully understand system capabilities and limitations，是理解层级而非专家层级。
B) ✓ 正确Driver training for self-driving vehicles can help ensure that drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations↔ Familiarizing them with the systems through training fully understand system capabilities and limitations↔Familiarizing them with the systems预判要的是通过培训让司机熟悉系统，B 项 Familiarizing them with the systems through training 与定位句双层等值，锁定 B。
C) 无中生有Broadening their knowledge of accident-prevention mechanisms 谈的是扩大防事故机制的知识面，但原文谈的是理解系统的能力与局限，accident-prevention mechanisms 在文中并未出现。
D) 与原文相反Facilitating their access to the information provided by the seller 主张方便司机获取卖家信息，但原文 even relying on the information provided by the seller is not going to answer many questions 明确指出哪怕依赖卖家信息也无法解答许多问题，二者方向相反。

title: Super realistic masks are made from flexible materials…

sentences.text: Super realistic masks are made from flexible materials such as silicone and are designed to imitate real human face—down to every last detail.

passage.translation: 超级逼真的面具由硅胶等柔性材料制成,旨在模仿真实的人脸——精确到每一个细节。

sentences.text: In a study by the Universities of York and Kyoto, researchers asked participants to look at pairs of photographs and decide which showed a (26)____ face and which showed a person wearing a mask.

passage.translation: 在York大学和京都大学的一项研究中,研究人员要求参与者观看成对的照片,并判断哪张显示的是正常面孔,哪张显示的是戴着面具的人。

sentences.text: Surprisingly, participants made the wrong call in one-in-five cases.

passage.translation: 令人惊讶的是,参与者在五分之一的情况下做出了错误的判断。

sentences.text: The 20% error rate (27)____ in the study likely underestimates the extent to which people would struggle to tell an (28)____ face from the real thing outside of the lab.

passage.translation: 研究中观察到的20%的错误率很可能低估了人们在实验室外区分人造面孔和真实面孔的困难程度。

sentences.text: The researchers collected data from participants from both the UK and Japan to (29)____ any differences according to race.
When trial participants were asked to choose between photographs of faces of a different race from theirs, response times were slower and selections were 5% less (30)____ .

passage.translation: 研究人员从英国和日本的参与者那里收集数据,以确定种族方面的差异。当试验参与者被要求在与自己不同种族的面孔照片之间进行选择时,反应时间更慢,准确率降低了5%。

sentences.text: There are now dozens of criminal cases in which offenders have (31)____ themselves off as people of a different age, race or gender, sending police investigations down the wrong path.

passage.translation: 现在有数十起刑事案件,犯罪者冒充不同年龄、种族或性别的人,将警方的调查引向错误的方向。

sentences.text: In one recent case, an international gang used an (32)____ realistic mask to pose as a French minister, (33)____ business executives out of millions of pounds.

passage.translation: 在最近的一起案件中,一个国际犯罪团伙使用极其逼真的面具冒充一位法国部长,从企业高管那里骗取了数百万英镑。

sentences.text: Dr Jet Sanders, who worked on the study while a PhD student at the University of York, said: "Failure to detect synthetic faces may have important implications for security and crime prevention as super realistic masks may (34)____ the key characteristics of a person's appearance to be (35)____identified."

passage.translation: Jet Sanders博士在York大学攻读博士学位期间参与了这项研究,他说:"无法检测出合成面孔可能对安全和犯罪预防产生重要影响,因为超级逼真的面具可能会导致一个人外貌的关键特征被错误识别。"

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
Super realistic masks are made from flexible materials such as silicone and are designed to imitate real human face—down to every last detail.

In a study by the Universities of York and Kyoto, researchers asked participants to look at pairs of photographs and decide which showed a {{26}} face and which showed a person wearing a mask.
