Surprisingly, participants made the wrong call in one-in-five cases.

The 20% error rate {{27}} in the study likely underestimates the extent to which people would struggle to tell an {{28}} face from the real thing outside of the lab.

The researchers collected data from participants from both the UK and Japan to {{29}} any differences according to race. When trial participants were asked to choose between photographs of faces of a different race from theirs, response times were slower and selections were 5% less {{30}} .

There are now dozens of criminal cases in which offenders have {{31}} themselves off as people of a different age, race or gender, sending police investigations down the wrong path.

In one recent case, an international gang used an {{32}} realistic mask to pose as a French minister, {{33}} business executives out of millions of pounds.

Dr Jet Sanders, who worked on the study while a PhD student at the University of York, said: "Failure to detect synthetic faces may have important implications for security and crime prevention as super realistic masks may {{34}} the key characteristics of a person's appearance to be {{35}}identified."

options.text: accurate
incorrectly
allow
normal
artificial
observed
cheating
passed
deserted
reminding
establish
reparable
extremely
resolve
immediately

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) normal 形容词
**词性槽** showed a + ___ + face，名词 face 前缺修饰词
**依据** 与 'a person wearing a mask' 形成「真脸 vs 戴面具」对照decide which showed a __(26)__ face and which showed a person wearing a mask 后半句已经指明对照面是「戴面具的人」，前半句必然是「没戴面具、正常人脸」的意思，normal（正常的）正好表达「未经面具伪装的真实人脸」。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) accurate accurate 修饰判断/数据，不修饰 face accurate 意为「准确的」，常修饰 description、answer、data，搭配 face 极其别扭，且无法与「戴面具」形成对照。
C) artificial方向反了，artificial 反而是面具一侧artificial（人造的、假的）应当对应「面具脸」，但这里要的恰恰是与「戴面具」相对的「真脸」，方向反了；artificial 会留给后面 __(28)__ 用。
E) deserted deserted 修饰场所，与 face 不搭deserted 多指「废弃的街道/房子」，不和 face 搭配，主体考生只要记住它常修饰地点就能排掉。
N) reparable 「可修复的」修饰损坏物，不修饰人脸reparable 意为「可修复的」，对象是机器、损伤、错误，跟「真人脸」语义毫无连接。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) observed 动词
**词性槽** 名词短语 + ___ + in the study，过去分词作后置定语
**依据** observe sth. in the study 是研究类文本的常见说法，被动语义贴合「研究中观察到的 20% 误差率」直接对应 'The 20% error rate observed in the study'，observed 是 observe（观察/注意到）的过去分词，与 in the study 构成自然的「在研究中被观察到的」语义；下文 participants made the wrong call in one-in-five cases 正是这一数据的实验来源。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
L) passed passed 与 error rate 搭配不合理passed 常搭 pass an exam/test 或 pass sth. off as（冒充），与「误差率」无法构成「pass+ in the study」的合理被动结构；它会留到 __(31)__ 那里发挥 passed sb. off as 的固定搭配作用。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) artificial 形容词
**词性槽** an + ___ + face，再一次「冠词 + 空 + 名词」的形容词槽
**依据** 与 the real thing 形成「假 vs 真」精准对照tell an __(28)__ face from the real thing 字面就是「把 ___ 脸与真东西区分开」，与 the real thing 直接相对的就是 artificial（人造的、假的）；上下文 Super realistic masks ... designed to imitate real human face 一直在讨论「人造仿真脸」这一主题，呼应完美。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) accurate accurate 不与 real 形成对照accurate 是「准确的」，与 the real thing 没有反义关系，构成不了 tell A from B 的对照逻辑。
E) deserted deserted 修饰场所，与 face 搭配不当deserted（废弃的）几乎只修饰地点/建筑，配 face 既不搭配也不形成对照。
N) reparable 「可修复的脸」语义荒诞reparable（可修复的）对象是损坏物，不修饰人脸；且与 real 不构成对照。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 A) —— 看到 'an ___ face' 误认 accurate「精确的脸」。考生若忽视 tell an __(28)__ face from the real thing 的 tell A from B 对照，就可能凭 a + 形容词+ face 直接抓 accurate；防坑：先找 from 后面的已知端（the real thing），再到候选里挑它的反义形容词 artificial。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) establish 动词
**词性槽** to + ___ + any differences，不定式 to 后缺动词原形
**依据** establish + differences：查明/确认是否存在差异The researchers collected data from participants from both the UK and Japan to__(29)__ any differences according to race 表「研究者收集两国数据，以便查明是否存在因种族不同而产生的差异」，establish 有「确立、查明、证实」之义，与「研究目的」直接对应；后文 response times were slower and selections were 5% less __(30)__ 即「查明后得出的差异」。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
O) resolve resolve 是「解决问题」，不是「查明差异」resolve 意为「解决/化解」，搭配是 resolve a problem/conflict；「解决差异」与研究语境不符——研究者是要「弄清是否存在差异」，而非「化解差异」。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) accurate 形容词
**词性槽** be 动词 were + 5% less + ___，less 后修饰程度的形容词
**依据** selections 5% less accurate：选择结果准确率低 5%response times were slower and selections were 5% less __(30)__ 与前半句「反应时间更慢」是并列两项负面表现；accurate（准确的）正好对接「判断/选择」类主语，整体语义是「跨种族判断时选择准确率低 5%」，呼应 participants made the wrong call in one-in-five cases 的误判主线。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) deserted deserted 修饰场所，与 selections 风马牛不相及deserted（废弃的）只搭配地点/建筑，「废弃的选择」语义不通。
N) reparable 「可修复的选择」不成立，且与对照逻辑无关reparable（可修复的）对象是损坏物，搭 selections 完全说不通；本题要的是「准确度高低」的对照。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) passed 动词
**词性槽** have + ___ + themselves off as，完成时被动后接 off as 的固定搭配
**依据** passed themselves off as：把自己冒充成另一种身份offenders have passed themselves off as people of a different age, race or gender 译为「罪犯把自己冒充成不同年龄、种族或性别的人」，与下文 sending police investigations down the wrong path 「误导警方调查」的逻辑链条扣得严丝合缝。

**答案** G) extremely 副词
**词性槽** an + ___ + 形容词 realistic，缺一个修饰形容词的副词
**依据** 唯一能合理修饰 realistic 程度的程度副词整篇文章一直在强调面具「逼真到极致」的特点，imitate real human face—down to every last detail，an __(32)__ realistic mask 自然取「极其逼真」之意，extremely 是程度副词，与 realistic 直接构成 'extremely realistic'（极其逼真）这一高频搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) immediately 时间副词，与 realistic 语义不搭immediately 表「立刻、立即」，是时间副词，用来修饰动作的发生时点，an __(32)__ realistic mask 这里不是说面具「立刻」逼真，逻辑不通。
I) incorrectly 方式副词且方向相反，不可能修饰 realistic incorrectly 是「错误地、不正确地」，本身和 realistic（逼真的）方向相反，「错误地逼真」语义自相矛盾；它后面要修饰的应是动作类成分，这里也派不上用场。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) cheating 动词
**词性槽** 逗号后紧贴主句的伴随性动名词短语，缺一个 -ing 形式动词
**依据** 正好套进 cheat sb. out of money 的固定搭配，且与「冒充行骗」逻辑吻合__(33)__ business executives out of millions of pounds 完全是 'cheat sb. out of sth.'（骗某人钱财）的固定结构，意思是「骗走商界高管数百万英镑」；offenders have__(31)__ themselves off as people of a different age, race or gender 上下文也明确指向「行骗」这条主线。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) reminding 搭配是 remind sb. of sth.，不接 out of money reminding 意为「提醒、使想起」，常见搭配是 'remind sb. of/about sth.'，不可能搭 'out of millions of pounds'；与「行骗」语义也不符。

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) allow 动词
**词性槽** 情态动词 may 后缺动词原形
**依据** allow sth. to be done：使关键特征得以被（错误地）识别masks may __(34)__ the key characteristics of a person's appearance to be __(35)__identified 完整成「面具可能让一个人外表的关键特征被错误地识别」，对应「allow + 宾+ to be done」固定搭配；且 Failure to detect synthetic faces may have important implications for security and crime prevention 的「负面后果」语义也由 allow 承担——是面具「使得」误识别成为可能。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) establish 不接 sth. to be done 结构，语义也偏正面establish 意为「确立、查明」，搭配 establish sth.（事实/制度），不能跟 'sth. to be done'这种使役结构；且 establish 强调「确认正确的事实」，与下文「被错误识别」语义冲突。
O) resolve resolve 是「解决问题」，与「让特征被识别」无关resolve 意为「解决（问题/争端）」，常搭 resolve a problem/dispute，与本句「面具让特征被识别」逻辑无连接，且也不接 'sth. to be done'。

questions.explanation:
**答案** I) incorrectly 副词
**词性槽** to be + ___ + identified，被动语态里修饰过去分词需要副词
**依据** 与「面具威胁识别、辨认失败」的负面主旨完全对齐Failure to detect synthetic faces may have important implications for security and crime prevention 已经定调是「识别失败」；面具会让关键面部特征被 incorrectly（错误地）识别，正是「认错人」的核心威胁；与 participants made the wrong call in one-in- five cases 「误判率高」的实验数据也相互呼应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) immediately immediately 表「立刻」，与文章「识别错误」主旨不符immediately（立刻、立即）只表时间速度，「特征被立刻识别」反而是好事，与 Failure to detect synthetic faces 的负面忧虑方向反了。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— 看到 to be ___ identified 误选 immediately「立刻被识别」。to be __(35)__ identified 中 immediately 词性也对、语义看着合理，但与 Failure to detect synthetic faces may have important implications for security and crime prevention 的负面主旨方向相反；防坑：在词性已定的两个副词之间，看段落是「担忧/批评」还是「赞扬」，担忧场景取负面 incorrectly。

title: Chocolates save us from many things, especially emotional…

sentences.text: Chocolates save us from many things, especially emotional distress.
They comfort us in times of trouble, calming down a racing heart by channelling happy calories inside us.
We all have faith in chocolates to delight us in an instant!

passage.translation: 巧克力拯救我们于许多事物之中,尤其是情感困扰。它们在困难时期安慰我们,通过向我们体内输送快乐的卡路里来平复狂跳的心脏。我们都相信巧克力能瞬间给我们带来愉悦!

sentences.text: Recently, chocolate lovers were heartbroken as scientists claimed that they can become extinct by 2050!
But hey, we have some happy news for you.
Scientists can still help save chocolates from dying out!
If you are not aware as to why scientists made the statement about the death of this wonderful thing, let us tell you the facts.
Chocolate trees, whose seeds are used to make chocolate, grow in the tropical plant world and require very specific weather conditions to prosper.

passage.translation: 最近,巧克力爱好者们心碎了,因为科学家声称巧克力可能在2050年灭绝!但是,我们有一些好消息要告诉你。科学家仍然可以帮助拯救巧克力免于消亡!如果你不知道科学家为什么对这一美妙事物的消亡做出声明,让我们告诉你事实。巧克力树的种子被用来制作巧克力,它们生长在热带植物世界中,需要非常特定的天气条件才能繁荣生长。

sentences.text: Now, fifty percent of the world's cocoa(可可) beans come from two countries in West Africa: Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana.
Scientists believe that both of these countries will experience a 3.8°F temperature increase by 2050 due to global warming, endangering the cacao(可可树) farms in the rainforests.
These farms will then have to be shifted to cooler mountainous areas, which are the natural habitat of wildlife.
This will lead to some tough decisions: whether to grow chocolate or save wildlife.

passage.translation: 现在,世界上百分之五十的可可豆来自西非的两个国家:科特迪瓦和加纳。科学家认为,由于全球变暖,到2050年这两个国家都将经历3.8华氏度的温度上升,危及雨林中的可可树种植园。这些种植园将不得不转移到更凉爽的山区,而那里是野生动物的天然栖息地。这将导致一些艰难的决定:是种植巧克力还是拯救野生动物。

sentences.text: Unfortunately, the crisis of global warming has already had a serious negative impact on cacao farms' yields, leading to the prices of chocolates skyrocketing.

passage.translation: 不幸的是,全球变暖危机已经对可可种植园的产量产生了严重的负面影响,导致巧克力价格飙升。

sentences.text: Scientists, however, are trying to find a long-term and eco-friendly solution to this problem!
They are trying to modify the species with a gene-editing technology, which will transform the seedlings into a species that survives even in a drier and warmer climate.

passage.translation: 然而,科学家正在努力寻找一个长期且环保的解决方案来应对这个问题!他们正在尝试用基因编辑技术改造物种,这将把幼苗转变为即使在更干燥和更温暖的气候中也能存活的物种。

sentences.text: According to a report by The Business Insider, in the University of California's new bio-sciences building, tiny green cacao seedlings are lined up in refrigerated greenhouses for a new experiment by using a technology called CRISPR.
By manipulating the DNA of plants, this technology is already being used across the world to make plants tougher and cheaper.
Similarly, in this unconventional experiment, scientists will make tiny, precise changes to the DNA of the seedlings to make the cocoa crops survive in warmer and drier climates.

passage.translation: 根据The Business Insider的一份报告,在加利福尼亚大学的新生物科学大楼里,微小的绿色可可幼苗在冷藏温室中排列成行,用于一项使用CRISPR技术的新实验。通过操纵植物的DNA,这项技术已经在世界各地被用来使植物更强壮、更便宜。同样,在这项非常规实验中,科学家将对幼苗的DNA进行微小而精确的改变,以使可可作物在更温暖和更干燥的气候中存活。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What do people believe chocolates can do?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
人们认为巧克力能做什么?
A) 立即让他们振奋起来。
B) 制造快乐的卡路里。
C) 掩盖情绪困扰。
D) 缓解他们的心脏问题。
**判型** What do people believe chocolates can do? 问的是巧克力能干什么这一具体功能，没有infer/imply/mainly 等信号词。
**拆句** 题干主干 What do people believe chocolates can do? 是一个嵌套宾语从句的特殊疑问句：What 是 do 的宾语，people 是主语，believe 后跟省略 that 的宾语从句 chocolates can do (what)。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 我们都相信巧克力能在一瞬间让我们开心起来！
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确delight us in an instant↔ Cheer them up instantly「瞬间让人开心」的预判与 Cheer them up instantly 在语义上完全重合，无差量，直接锁定。
B) 偷换概念识别Create happy calories 把原文 channelling happy calories inside us 中「输送/导入愉快卡路里」当成「创造卡路里」，把比喻动作偷换成 create。
C) 与原文相反识别原文是 They comfort us in times of trouble——「安抚」情绪，而 Conceal emotional distress 说「隐藏」情绪，安抚≠隐藏，意思相反。
D) 过度推断识别原文 calming down a racing heart 是比喻「让狂跳的心平静下来」，而 Relieve them of heart trouble 把 racing heart 强行解为「心脏疾病」并把 calming down 换成relieve…of，属于过度推断。
questions.quote: We all have faith in chocolates to delight us in an instant!

options.text: Cheer them up instantly.
Create happy calories.
Conceal emotional distress.
Relieve them of heart trouble.

questions.prompt: What was scientists' recent assertion about chocolates?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
科学家最近关于巧克力的断言是什么?
A) 在不久的将来它们可能会成为稀罕物。
B) 在危机时期它们可以让人们稍微平静下来。
C) 它们可以防止人们心碎。
D) 在不到30年的时间里它们可能会变得无法获得。
**判型** What was scientists' recent assertion about chocolates? 问的是科学家断言的具体内容，原文中可定位一句即可作答。
**拆句** 题干 What was scientists' recent assertion about chocolates? 是 What…be 句型，主语scientists' recent assertion 由所有格 + 形容词 + 名词构成，about chocolates 是后置介词短语修饰 assertion。结构简单，无陷阱。
**定位** 最近，巧克力爱好者们伤心欲绝，因为科学家声称巧克力到 2050 年可能灭绝！
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断识别They could become a rare treat in the near future 说巧克力会变成「稀有美食」，但原文是 extinct（灭绝/绝种），不是 rare（稀少），属于程度上的过度推断与偷换。
B) 答非所问识别They could calm people down a bit in times of crisis 描述的是巧克力的安抚功能，是首段的内容；题干问的是「科学家最近的断言」，不在第一段范围内。
C) 与原文相反识别They could prevent people from getting heartbroken 利用 chocolate lovers were heartbroken 中的 heartbroken 反向拼凑，把「伤心」错改为「防止伤心」，与原文方向完全相反。
D) ✓ 正确they can become extinct by 2050 ↔ They could become unavailable in less than 30 years「2050 年前灭绝」的预判与 They could become unavailable in less than 30 years完全重合，时间值与「灭绝/不可得」均对得上。
questions.quote: Recently, chocolate lovers were heartbroken as scientists claimed that they can become extinct by 2050!

options.text: They could become a rare treat in the near future.
They could calm people down a bit in times of crisis.
They could prevent people from getting heartbroken.
They could become unavailable in less than 30 years.

questions.prompt: What would happen if the cacao farms were shifted to cooler mountainous areas?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
如果可可农场转移到更凉爽的山区会发生什么?
A) 那里野生动物的自然栖息地将被破坏。
B) 可可农民适应起来会很艰难。
C) 热带雨林将急剧缩小。
D) 可可豆的质量将大受影响。
**判型** What would happen if the cacao farms were shifted to cooler mountainous areas?是 if 条件下的客观结果，可直接到原文条件句中找到表述。
**拆句** 题干 What would happen if the cacao farms were shifted to cooler mountainous areas? 是 What + 虚拟条件句：主句 what would happen 用 would，从句 were shifted是被动语态，整体表达「假设农场被迁走，会发生什么」。要注意 were shifted 是被动结构，主体是农场而非农民。
**定位** 这些农场届时将不得不被迁到更凉爽的山区，而那里正是野生动物的自然栖息地。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确cooler mountainous areas, which are the natural habitat of wildlife ↔The natural habitat of wildlife there would be ruined whether to grow chocolate or save wildlife ↔ would be ruined「侵占并破坏野生动物栖息地」的预判与 The natural habitat of wildlife there would be ruined 完全重合。
B) 无中生有识别The cacao farmers would have a tough time to adapt 谈的是「农民适应困难」，原文从未提及农民的适应问题，纯属编造。
C) 答非所问识别The rainforests would be shrinking dramatically 谈的是雨林萎缩，但题干问的是「农场迁到凉爽山区之后」，迁出地（雨林）的变化并不是题干问的「会发生什么」的核心后果，且原文未说雨林会因此显著萎缩。
D) 无中生有识别The quality of cocoa beans would suffer greatly 说可可豆质量会大幅下降，原文从未谈及「质量」问题，只提到产量（yields）下降；属于无中生有。
questions.quote: These farms will then have to be shifted to cooler mountainous areas, which are the natural habitat of wildlife.

options.text: The natural habitat of wildlife there would be ruined.
The cacao farmers would have a tough time to adapt.
The rainforests would be shrinking dramatically.
The quality of cocoa beans would suffer greatly.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the cacao farms in the crisis of global warming?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于全球变暖危机中的可可农场我们了解到什么?
A) 它们试图向基因编辑科学家寻求帮助。
B) 它们决定搬到更凉爽的山区。
C) 由于产量下降它们遭受了很大损失。
D) 它们通过提高可可豆价格而获益。
**判型** What do we learn about the cacao farms in the crisis of global warming? 问的是文中告诉我们的客观事实，可在原文找一句直接陈述。
**拆句** 题干 What do we learn about the cacao farms in the crisis of global warming? 主干为What do we learn about Y，about 后接 the cacao farms in the crisis of global warming，in 引导的介词短语充当 farms 的处境状语。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 不幸的是，全球变暖危机已经严重负面地影响了可可园的产量，导致巧克力价格飙升。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有识别They try to seek help from gene-editing scientists 说农场主动求助科学家，原文第五、六段是科学家自己在研究、不是农场求助，属无中生有。
B) 时态偷换识别They decide to move to cooler mountainous areas 把原文第三段 will then have to be shifted 这一未来「将不得不被迁」错读为已经「决定迁移」，时态与主动性都被改了。
C) ✓ 正确had a serious negative impact on cacao farms' yields ↔They have suffered a lot due to a decrease in produce「农场产量受严重负面影响」的预判与 They have suffered a lot due to a decrease in produce 在语义上一致；C 把「产量下滑」前移为原因，更贴合题干「What do we learn about the cacao farms」的视角。
D) 与原文相反识别They have benefited by raising prices of cocoa beans 说农场因涨价获益，但原文是「产量下降→巧克力价格飙升」，价格飙升是消极后果而非农场获益；属与原文相反。
questions.quote: Unfortunately, the crisis of global warming has already had a serious negative impact on cacao farms' yields, leading to the prices of chocolates skyrocketing.

options.text: They try to seek help from gene-editing scientists.
They decide to move to cooler mountainous areas.
They have suffered a lot due to a decrease in produce.
They have benefited by raising prices of cocoa beans.

questions.prompt: What are scientists trying to do in the University of California's new bio-sciences building?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
科学家们正试图在加州大学的新生物科学大楼里做什么?
A) 建造成排的冷藏温室用于可可幼苗研究。
B) 对可可幼苗进行基因编辑使其能够承受更干燥、更温暖的气候。
C) 用最新的基因编辑技术生产巧克力。
D) 将更强韧植物的基因移植到可可幼苗中。
**判型** What are scientists trying to do in the University of California's new bio-sciences building? 问的是科学家在特定地点的具体行动，可在原文末段直接找到。
**拆句** 题干 What are scientists trying to do in the University of California's new bio- sciences building? 是 What + 进行时疑问句：trying to do 表达科学家此刻正努力做某事，in 引导的地点状语限定场景。结构清晰，无陷阱。
**定位** 在这个非常规实验中，科学家将对种苗的 DNA 做出细微而精确的改变，以使可可作物能在更暖、更干的气候中存活。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问识别Build rows of refrigerated greenhouses for research on cacao seedlings 把原文tiny green cacao seedlings are lined up in refrigerated greenhouses 中的「冷藏温室」错读为科学家在「建造温室」，但温室只是已有的实验环境，不是科学家正在做的目的。
B) ✓ 正确make tiny, precise changes to the DNA of the seedlings↔Gene-edit cacao seedlings to make the cocoa crops survive in warmer and drier climates↔for them to withstand a drier, warmer climate「基因编辑可可种苗 + 让其耐暖耐旱」的预判与 Gene-edit cacao seedlings for them to withstand a drier, warmer climate 在两个语义成分上都重合。
C) 过度推断识别Produce chocolates with the latest gene-editing technology 把目标直接定为「生产巧克力」，但原文目的是先改造种苗使可可作物耐气候，距离「生产巧克力」还有多步，属过度推断。
D) 无中生有识别Transplant the genes of tougher plants to cacao seedlings 说把更耐性强植物的基因移植到可可种苗，原文只说对种苗 DNA 做精细修改，未提「移植其他物种基因」，属无中生有。
questions.quote: in this unconventional experiment, scientists will make tiny, precise changes to the DNA of the seedlings to make the cocoa crops survive in warmer and drier climates.

options.text: Build rows of refrigerated greenhouses for research on cacao seedlings.
Gene-edit cacao seedlings for them to withstand a drier, warmer climate.
Produce chocolates with the latest gene-editing technology.
Transplant the genes of tougher plants to cacao seedlings.

title: As a university student, I've come to realise…

sentences.text: As a university student, I've come to realise just how little I know about money.
I've come to the brutal realisation that Australia's youth are being done a great disservice by not receiving any consistent financial education.

passage.translation: 作为一名大学生,我逐渐意识到自己对金钱知之甚少。我残酷地认识到,澳大利亚的年轻人因未能接受任何系统的金融教育而遭受了巨大的损失。

sentences.text: Diving headfirst into the crash course of starting university, I've quickly tried to get myself up to speed with the financial terms of the modern era to help manage my personal finances.

passage.translation: 在开始大学生活的速成课程中一头扎进去后,我迅速努力让自己跟上现代金融术语的步伐,以帮助管理我的个人财务。

sentences.text: I've read some financial education books, done some online learning, and have spoken to my nearest and dearest for their pearls of financial wisdom.

passage.translation: 我读了一些金融教育书籍,进行了一些在线学习,并向我最亲近的人请教他们的金融智慧。

sentences.text: There are undoubtedly hundreds of great resources out there for those wishing to improve their financial literacy, but while I was researching, I still kept wishing that I didn't have to play catch-up with the money world.
I felt that I was sailing the financial seas with no skills and no life jacket!

passage.translation: 对于那些希望提高金融素养的人来说,无疑有数百种优秀的资源,但在我研究的过程中,我仍然不断希望自己不必在金钱世界中急起直追。我感觉自己在金融的海洋中航行,既没有技能也没有救生衣!

sentences.text: However, after talking to my friends who felt the same, I quickly realised that it wasn't my ignorance but the lack of financial education in our schooling system that is leaving high schoolers seriously behind in the modern world of money.

passage.translation: 然而,在与有同样感受的朋友交谈后,我很快意识到,不是我的无知,而是我们学校教育体系中缺乏金融教育,导致高中生在现代金钱世界中严重落后。

sentences.text: Let's compare a theoretical financial education subject to the standard compulsory English class.
On average, English may not be the most popular subject, but it's consistently on the schedule throughout high school, with all students graduating fluent in English.

passage.translation: 让我们把一门理论上的金融教育课程与标准的必修英语课进行比较。平均而言,英语可能不是最受欢迎的科目,但它在整个高中阶段都持续出现在课程表上,所有学生毕业时都能流利使用英语。

sentences.text: A financial education subject should do just the same.

It shouldn't be just a one-day event but a course integrated throughout the whole of high school that would allow students to gradually expand their financial literacy, and would prevent the need for a 'catch up' phase once we're out on our own after graduation.

passage.translation: 金融教育课程也应该做到同样的事情。它不应该只是一次性活动,而应该是一门贯穿整个高中阶段的课程,让学生逐步扩展他们的金融素养,并防止我们毕业独立后需要经历一个'追赶'阶段。

sentences.text: In the same way that learning a language or new skills takes time, building financial skills requires practice and years to gradually accumulate bits and pieces of knowledge.

passage.translation: 正如学习一门语言或新技能需要时间一样,培养金融技能需要实践和多年时间来逐步积累零散的知识。

sentences.text: Giving young people the opportunity to become familiar with the world of money would provide them with a great advantage to enter adulthood with confidence and security so that they are able to manage their own money and look after themselves.

passage.translation: 给年轻人提供熟悉金钱世界的机会,将为他们带来巨大优势,使他们能够自信而安全地进入成年期,从而能够管理自己的金钱并照顾好自己。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What has the author come to realise since entering university?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
自从进入大学以来,作者意识到了什么?
A) 他需要金融术语速成课程。
B) 他非常缺乏金融素养。
C) 实现财务独立需要持续的教育。
D) 为所有澳大利亚青年提供金融教育是不现实的。
**判型** What has the author come to realise直接问一个具体认知结果，不含infer/imply/mainly about等推断或主旨信号词。
**拆句** What has the author come to realise since entering university?主干是What ... has come to realise，What作realise的宾语；since entering university是时间状语，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 作为一名大学生，我已经意识到自己对金钱了解得有多么少。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念He needs a crash course on financial terms说作者需要一门速成课，而原文Diving headfirst into the crash course of starting university里的crash course指的是大学开学这件事本身像速成课，不是金融术语速成课。
B) ✓ 正确just how little I know about money ↔ lacking in financial literacy预判说我钱的知识少，He is very much lacking in financial literacy里的lacking in financial literacy正是这层意思的标准表达。
C) 答非所问It requires consistent education to be financially independent谈的是要做到financially independent的条件，而题干问的是作者意识到什么，P1里realise的宾语并不是这个条件论。
D) 与原文相反It is unrealistic to give all Australian youth a financial education说给澳洲青年金融教育不现实，而原文Australia's youth are being done a great disservice by not receiving any consistent financial education恰恰是在痛心他们没有得到金融教育，作者立场是该给而不是不现实。
questions.quote: As a university student, I've come to realise just how little I know about money.

options.text: He needs a crash course on financial terms.
He is very much lacking in financial literacy.
It requires consistent education to be financially independent.
It is unrealistic to give all Australian youth a financial education.

questions.prompt: How did the author feel in today's money world?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者在当今货币世界中感觉如何?
A) 生存装备严重不足。
B) 对金融文献一无所知。
C) 几乎没有能力向前发展。
D) 被在线资源压得喘不过气来。
**判型** How did the author feel直接问感受，是关于感受这个事实的细节题，不含推断信号词。
**拆句** How did the author feel in today's money world?主干How did the author feel，in today's money world是地点/情境状语；结构简单，无陷阱。
**定位** 我感觉自己正在金融的海洋上航行，却既没有技能也没有救生衣！
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确sailing the financial seas with no skills and no life jacket ↔ Badly equipped to survive预判说作者缺装备处境危险，Badly equipped to survive里badly equipped to survive正是这层意思的标准等值表达。
B) 偷换概念Ignorant of financial literature里financial literature是金融文献，而原文谈的是financial literacy/skills，文献和素养是两回事，选项偷换了对象。
C) 程度副词偷换Barely capable of moving ahead说勉强能前进，原文no skills and no life jacket描绘的是完全无装备的处境，是不能前进而不是勉强能。
D) 答非所问Overwhelmed by the resources online说被网络资源压垮，而原文hundreds of great resources out there并没有说作者被压垮，反而是肯定资源很多，作者的负面感受来自缺装备不是资源多。
questions.quote: I felt that I was sailing the financial seas with no skills and no life jacket!

options.text: Badly equipped to survive.
Ignorant of financial literature.
Barely capable of moving ahead.
Overwhelmed by the resources online.

questions.prompt: What did the author realise after talking to his friends?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者在与朋友交谈后意识到了什么?
A) 他们和他一样热衷于金融事务。
B) 学校教育制度应该为他的困境负责。
C) 高中生对现代金融世界一无所知。
D) 金融课程和必修英语课一样不受欢迎。
**判型** What did the author realise after talking to his friends问的是一个具体认知结果，没有infer/imply等信号词。
**拆句** What did the author realise after talking to his friends?主干What did the author realise，after talking to his friends是时间状语；结构平直，无陷阱。
**定位** 然而，和有同感的朋友们聊过之后，我很快意识到，让高中生在现代金钱世界里严重落后的，不是我的无知，而是我们学校系统里金融教育的缺失。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断They were as keen as he was on financial matters说朋友们也对金融问题热心，而原文my friends who felt the same只说朋友们有同感（同样觉得吃力），并没说他们热心研究金融。
B) ✓ 正确not...but the lack of financial education in our schooling system ↔The schooling system was to blame for his trouble预判说学校系统背锅，The schooling system was to blame for his trouble里was to blame正是这层归因意思。
C) 以偏概全High schoolers knew nothing about the modern financial world说高中生对金融世界一无所知，而原文leaving high schoolers seriously behind说的是严重落后不是一无所知，knew nothing是把落后扩大成零知识。
D) 无中生有Financial courses were as unpopular as compulsory English classes说金融课和必修英语一样不受欢迎，原文English may not be the most popular subject只是承认英语不算最受欢迎，从未说金融课不受欢迎或两者并列，且这点出现在48题区间之外，纯属无中生有。
questions.quote: However, after talking to my friends who felt the same, I quickly realised that it wasn't my ignorance but the lack of financial education in our schooling system that is leaving high schoolers seriously behind in the modern world of money.

options.text: They were as keen as he was on financial matters.
The schooling system was to blame for his trouble.
High schoolers knew nothing about the modern financial world.
Financial courses were as unpopular as compulsory English classes.

questions.prompt: What is the author's idea of a financial education course?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者对金融教育课程的想法是什么?
A) 它应该预见学生毕业后的需求。
B) 它应该为学生提供一些基础知识。
C) 它应该像英语教学那样授课。
D) 它应该融入高中教育。
**判型** What is the author's idea of a financial education course?问的是作者明确提出的具体主张，原文应有should句直接对应，不需推断。
**拆句** What is the author's idea of a financial education course?主干What is the author's idea，of短语限定idea的对象，结构平直无陷阱。
**定位** 它不该只是一个一日活动，而该是一门贯穿整个高中阶段的课程，让学生逐步拓展自己的金融素养，从而避免我们毕业独立生活后还得补课。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念It should foresee students' needs after graduation说该课该预见学生毕业后的需求，而原文prevent the need for a 'catch up' phase once we're out on our own after graduation说的是避免毕业后补课，不是预见学生需求，foresee needs偷换了prevent the need这层因果。
B) 以偏概全It should provide students with some basic knowledge说该课只该提供基础知识，而原文gradually expand their financial literacy说的是逐步拓展金融素养，且years to gradually accumulate bits and pieces of knowledge强调长期积累，some basic把整个长期拓展过程缩成基础知识，是范围偷小。
C) 过度推断It should be taught the same way as English is taught说该课该用和英语一样的教法，而原文Let's compare a theoretical financial education subject to the standard compulsory English class只是拿英语做类比强调持续性，并没有说要在教法上完全一样，taught the same way是把类比推过头。
D) ✓ 正确a course integrated throughout the whole of high school ↔It should be integrated into high school education预判说该课应融入高中始终，It should be integrated into high school education里integrated into high school education正是这层意思的同义表达。
questions.quote: It shouldn't be just a one-day event but a course integrated throughout the whole of high school that would allow students to gradually expand their financial literacy, and would prevent the need for a 'catch up' phase once we're out on our own after graduation.

options.text: It should foresee students' needs after graduation.
It should provide students with some basic knowledge.
It should be taught the same way as English is taught.
It should be integrated into high school education.

questions.prompt: What would financial literacy do to young people?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
金融素养会给年轻人带来什么?
A) 让他们在经济有保障的情况下步入成年。
B) 使他们能够照顾自己而无需担心金钱问题。
C) 使他们在资金管理方面自信而有安全感。
D) 帮助他们熟悉货币世界。
**判型** What would financial literacy do to young people问的是金融素养对年轻人的具体作用，原文应有直接对应句。
**拆句** What would financial literacy do to young people?主干What would financial literacy do，to young people是间接宾语；结构平直无陷阱。
**定位** 让年轻人有机会熟悉金钱世界，会让他们带着自信和安全感步入成年，并因此能够自己管理钱财、照顾好自己。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全Allow them to enter adulthood with financial security只保留了security丢掉了confidence，且把confidence and security压缩为financial security一项，原文是双重收益而不是只有金融安全。
B) 过度推断Enable them to look after themselves without worrying about money里without worrying about money是说不必为钱发愁，而原文able to manage their own money只说能管理钱，不等于不必为钱发愁，without worrying是从能管理钱推过头。
C) ✓ 正确enter adulthood with confidence and security so that they are able to manage their own money↔ Render them confident and secure in terms of money management预判说在金钱管理上自信且有安全感，Render them confident and secure in terms of money management里confident and secure in terms of money management正是这层意思最完整的同义替换。
D) 答非所问Help them become familiar with the world of money说帮他们熟悉金钱世界，而原文Giving young people the opportunity to become familiar with the world of money里熟悉金钱世界是金融素养这件事的前提条件而不是它带来的后果，题干问的是financial literacy带来什么，不是它是什么。
questions.quote: Giving young people the opportunity to become familiar with the world of money would provide them with a great advantage to enter adulthood with confidence and security so that they are able to manage their own money and look after themselves.

options.text: Allow them to enter adulthood with financial security.
Enable them to look after themselves without worrying about money.
Render them confident and secure in terms of money management.
Help them become familiar with the world of money.

title: Scientists have known that depriving adult mice of…

sentences.text: Scientists have known that depriving adult mice of vision can increase the sensitivity of individual neurons(神经元) in the part of the brain devoted to hearing.

New research from biologists at the University of Maryland (26)____ that sight deprivation also changes the way brain cells (27)____ with one another, shifting the mice's sensitivity to different frequencies.

passage.translation: 科学家们已经知道,剥夺成年小鼠的视觉可以提高大脑中负责听觉部分的单个神经元的敏感性。马里兰大学生物学家的最新研究揭示,视觉剥夺还会改变脑细胞相互作用的方式,从而改变小鼠对不同频率的敏感性。

sentences.text: "This study (28)____ what we are learning about how manipulating vision can have a (29)____effect on the ability of an animal to hear long after the window for auditory(听觉的) learning was thought to have (30)____ ," said Patrick Kanold, senior author of the study.

passage.translation: 该研究的资深作者Patrick Kanold说:"这项研究强化了我们正在了解的一点,即在人们认为听觉学习窗口已经关闭很久之后,操纵视觉仍能对动物的听力产生重大影响。"

sentences.text: It was once thought that the sensory regions of the brain were not (31)____ after a critical period in childhood.
This is why children learn languages much more (32)____ than adults.

Kanold's earlier research disproved this idea by showing that depriving adult mice of vision for a short period increased the sensitivity of individual neurons in the auditory cortex(皮质), which is devoted to hearing.

passage.translation: 人们曾经认为,大脑的感觉区域在童年的关键期之后就不再具有适应性。这就是为什么儿童学习语言比成年人容易得多的原因。Kanold早期的研究推翻了这一观点,他的研究表明,短期剥夺成年小鼠的视觉会提高听觉皮质中单个神经元的敏感性,而听觉皮质负责听觉。

sentences.text: Young brains wire themselves according to the sounds they hear frequently, assigning areas of the auditory cortex to (33)____ frequencies based on what they are used to hearing.
The researchers found that, in adult mice, a week in the dark also changed the (34)____ of space to different frequencies.

passage.translation: 年幼的大脑会根据它们经常听到的声音进行自我连接,根据它们习惯听到的内容,将听觉皮质的区域分配给特定的频率。研究人员发现,在成年小鼠中,在黑暗中待一周也会改变分配给不同频率的空间分布。

sentences.text: "We don't know why we are seeing these patterns," Kanold said.
"We (35)____ that it may have to do with what the mice are paying attention to while they are in the dark."

passage.translation: Kanold说:"我们不知道为什么会看到这些模式。我们推测这可能与小鼠在黑暗中关注什么有关。"

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
Scientists have known that depriving adult mice of vision can increase the sensitivity of individual neurons(神经元) in the part of the brain devoted to hearing. New research from biologists at the University of Maryland {{26}} that sight deprivation also changes the way brain cells {{27}} with one another, shifting the mice's sensitivity to different frequencies.

"This study {{28}} what we are learning about how manipulating vision can have a {{29}}effect on the ability of an animal to hear long after the window for auditory(听觉的) learning was thought to have {{30}} ," said Patrick Kanold, senior author of the study.

It was once thought that the sensory regions of the brain were not {{31}} after a critical period in childhood. This is why children learn languages much more {{32}} than adults. Kanold's earlier research disproved this idea by showing that depriving adult mice of vision for a short period increased the sensitivity of individual neurons in the auditory cortex(皮质), which is devoted to hearing.

Young brains wire themselves according to the sounds they hear frequently, assigning areas of the auditory cortex to {{33}} frequencies based on what they are used to hearing. The researchers found that, in adult mice, a week in the dark also changed the {{34}} of space to different frequencies.

"We don't know why we are seeing these patterns," Kanold said. "We {{35}} that it may have to do with what the mice are paying attention to while they are in the dark."

options.text: adaptable
readily
closed
registered
distribution
reinforces
interact
revealed
narration
significant
neutral
specific
permanently
speculate
prescribes

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) revealed 动词
**词性槽** 主语 New research 后缺谓语，需要单数动词
**依据** research revealed that... 是科研报道高频搭配句子是典型的"新研究揭示……"句式，New research from biologists at the University of Maryland __(26)__ that sight deprivation also changes the way brain cells __(27)__with one another，research revealed/showed that 是四级和考研阅读里科普类语料最常见的引出研究结论的搭配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) prescribes 义为"开处方/规定"，与"研究揭示"不沾边prescribe 多用于医生开药或权威机构"规定"，与 research 做主语完全不搭，且其内容 that 从句是研究结论，不是规定。
K) reinforces 义为"加强"，需要被加强的对象，与本句"首次揭示"不符reinforce 是"加强、强化已有事物"，常见结构 reinforces the idea/finding/argument that...；本句是直接给出"新研究"的发现，并非在加强某个先前结论，更适合放在第 28 空。
O) speculate 原形动词，主谓不一致；且语气是"推测"不是"揭示" speculate 是原形，主语 New research 为三单需要 -s 形式，形态先不符；语义上"推测"也弱于"揭示"，与前句已知事实并列叙述的语气不匹配。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) interact 动词
**词性槽** 主语 brain cells 后做谓语，需原形动词
**依据** interact with one another = "相互作用"，神经科学固定搭配changes the way brain cells __(27)__ with one another 描述的是脑细胞之间的相互作用方式，interact with one another"彼此相互作用"是生物/神经科学的标准说法，与全文主旨"剥夺视觉改变脑细胞间互动"完美对应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) prescribes三单 -es 形态与复数主语 brain cells 冲突prescribes 是三单形式，主语是复数 brain cells，主谓数不一致；且语义"开处方/规定"也与脑细胞行为不搭。
K) reinforces三单形态错 + 语义需要宾语reinforces 一是三单形态不匹配复数主语；二是 reinforce 是及物动词需要直接宾语，本句空后是 with one another 而非名词宾语，搭配不成立。
O) speculate义为"推测"，脑细胞不会"推测" speculate 是有意识主体的认知行为，与无意识的 brain cells 主语在语义上违和，且 speculate with 也不是常用搭配。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) reinforces 动词
**词性槽** 主语 This study 后缺谓语，需要三单形式
**依据** study reinforces what we are learning ="研究强化/印证了我们的认识"上一段已经讲了"剥夺视觉影响脑细胞相互作用"，本句作者引述研究者评价"这项研究 ___ 我们正在学到的东西"，逻辑上是"再次印证/强化"既有认识，reinforces what we are learning 搭配地道，This study __(28)__ what we are learning about how manipulating vision can have a __(29)__ effect on the ability of an animal to hear。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) prescribes义为"开处方/规定"，与"印证研究发现"完全不搭prescribe 用于医生开药或权威给出规定，主语一般是人或机构，且不与 what we are learning这种"我们正在学到的东西"搭配，语义荒谬。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— prescribes 形态对、三单一致，主体考生不认词义时易蒙。This study __(28)__ what we are learning 处，prescribes 与正确答案 reinforces 在形态上都是三单 -es，许多四级考生对 prescribe 只记得"开处方"半个义项，会怀疑"是不是有别的意思"而硬选；防坑要点是看主语 study 和宾语 what we are learning——"研究"只会"印证/强化"，不会"规定"。

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) significant 形容词
**词性槽** 冠词 a 与名词 effect 之间，要填形容词作定语
**依据** 搭配 have a significant effect on 是四级高频固定表达have a significant effect on "对……有显著影响" 是四级阅读和写作里反复出现的高频搭配，配合上下文 manipulating vision can have a __(29)__ effect on the ability of an animal to hear，作者要强调操控视觉对听觉能力的影响"重大"，significant 正是这层意思。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) adaptable 义为"可适应的"，与 effect 不搭adaptable 通常修饰人或系统（如 an adaptable learner），说"一个可适应的影响"在中英文里都不通顺，搭配错位。
F) neutral "中立的影响"在科学语境里反向且无意义neutral effect 表示"既不正也不负、没什么作用"，但作者全篇都在强调剥夺视觉"确实改变了"听觉皮层，正话反说，与主旨冲突。
N) specific义为"特定的"，文中并未限定某一种影响specific effect 强调"某一具体的影响"，需要后文点明是哪一种；而本句只是泛指"有影响"，逻辑上不需要这种限定，且 specific 在第 33 空有更典型的归属（specific frequencies）。

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) closed 动词
**词性槽** have to have + ___，需要过去分词，构成完成时态被动表达
**依据** the window has closed ="窗口已关闭"，比喻关键期结束原文用 the window for auditory learning 比喻"听觉学习的关键期"，long after the window for auditory learning was thought to have __(30)__ 说"这个窗口被认为早已关闭"，对应下段第 31 空所讨论的"过了关键期后不可塑"的传统观点；window has closed是"关键期/机会窗口已关"的固定比喻。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
J) registered义为"登记"，与"窗口关闭"语义无关registered 多用于"注册、登记、记录在案"，搭配 the window 在英语里没有对应的固定比喻，意思完全跑偏。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) adaptable 形容词
**词性槽** 系动词 were 后做表语
**依据** 下一段反驳"不可塑"，正好对应 adaptable本段是先立后破：先说"曾经认为感觉区在童年关键期后就不再 ___"，紧接着 Kanold's earlier research disproved this idea by showing that depriving adult mice of vision for a short period increased the sensitivity of individual neurons in the auditory cortex 用 disproved 反驳，证明成年后大脑仍可被改变。adaptable"可塑、可适应"恰好是被反驳的那种属性，否定的就是"不可塑"。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) neutral neutral 与上下文论辩焦点无关上下文的对立面是"可塑 vs 固定"，不是"中性 vs 偏向"；填 neutral 后整句变成"曾认为大脑感觉区不是中性的"，与下文用 disproved 反驳的语义完全对不上。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— neutral 词性、形态都对，迷惑性强。the sensory regions of the brain were not __(31)__ 处 be 动词后填形容词，A 和 F 都是合格形容词；考生若不抓住下句 disproved 的反驳逻辑，容易被 neutral 的"中性、不偏不倚"误导；防坑靠回看下一句反驳的是什么。

questions.explanation:
**答案** I) readily 副词
**词性槽** 修饰动词 learn，且夹在 more 比较级里
**依据** readily ="容易地、轻松地"，对应"小孩学语言比成人快"的常识全段强调"成年大脑感觉区曾被认为不再可塑"，这是为什么 children learn languages much more __(32)__ than adults——比较的是"学得容易、学得快"，readily"轻易地、迅速地"正中靶心。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) permanently 义为"永久地"，与"比成人……"的比较语义不搭permanently 强调"持续不断"，但语境对比的是儿童 vs 成人"学语言这件事做得怎么样"，需要的是"快 / 容易"，不是"持久"；填 permanently 后整句变成"小孩比成人更永久地学语言"，逻辑混乱。

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) specific 形容词
**词性槽** 形容词修饰复数名词 frequencies
**依据** specific frequencies = "特定频率"，正中神经科学语境上下文说"幼年大脑根据常听到的声音连线，把听觉皮层的区域分配给"___ 的频率，意思是"对应到某些特定的频率"，specific frequencies 是听觉/神经科学论文中的高频搭配，意思贴合 assigning areas of the auditory cortex to __(33)__ frequencies based on what they are used to hearing。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) adaptable "可适应的频率"逻辑不通频率本身是物理量，不存在"可不可适应"，adaptable 通常修饰生命体或系统，搭配在常识层面就不成立。
F) neutral "中性频率"与上下文"基于听到的声音"逻辑相反neutral 强调"无偏好"，但句子明说大脑是"基于它们常听到的声音"做分配，恰恰是有偏好、有针对性的分配，方向相反。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) distribution 名词
**词性槽** the ___ of space to different frequencies，定冠词 the 后 of 短语前的名词位
**依据** distribution of space to frequencies ="空间向不同频率的分配"上文 Young brains wire themselves according to the sounds they hear frequently, assigning areas of the auditory cortex to __(33)__ frequencies based on what they are used to hearing. 刚说幼年大脑把皮层区域"分配给"特定频率，本句紧跟着说成年大鼠经过一周黑暗后也改变了"空间对不同频率的分配"，distribution of … to … 与上文assigning … to … 概念呼应，搭配地道。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) narration 义为"叙述"，与神经科学语境无关narration 用于讲述故事、电影旁白等，本文是讨论听觉皮层的空间分配，narration of space to frequencies 在语义上完全跑题。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) speculate 动词
**词性槽** 主语 We 后缺谓语，原形动词作一般现在时
**依据** speculate that ="推测"，与从句的 may have to do with 完美呼应从句里有 may，表明说话人不下定论，主句的动词应同样表"推测、猜测"，We __(35)__that it may have to do with what the mice are paying attention to while they are in the dark. 整句意思是"我们推测这可能与小鼠在黑暗中注意什么有关"，speculate 既贴合语气又契合上下文。

title: Engineering in the U.S. has long been a…

sentences.text: Engineering in the U.S. has long been a male-dominated profession.
Fifty years ago, it looked like that might change.

passage.translation: 长期以来,美国的工程学一直是一个男性主导的专业。五十年前,这种情况看起来可能会改变。

sentences.text: In 1970, the percentage of women majoring in engineering was less than 1%.
In 1979, that number was 9%.
Many hoped women would continue to enter the field at the same rate.
But that's not what happened.
Today, only 21% of engineering majors are women, a number largely unchanged since 2000.

passage.translation: 1970年,主修工程学的女性比例不到1%。1979年,这一数字为9%。许多人希望女性能够以同样的速度继续进入该领域。但事实并非如此。如今,只有21%的工程学专业学生是女性,这一数字自2000年以来基本保持不变。

sentences.text: I am a historian who, along with my colleagues, surveyed 251 women engineers who graduated from college in the 1970s.
These pioneers reflected on the challenges they faced—and had advice for women entering the field today.

passage.translation: 我是一名历史学家,与我的同事们一起对251名在20世纪70年代大学毕业的女性工程师进行了调查。这些先驱者反思了她们所面临的挑战,并为今天进入该领域的女性提供了建议。

sentences.text: One survey taker explained, "The greatest challenge for me was continuing to believe in myself, when all the messages I was getting were that I would never be taken seriously or promoted or given raises at the same rate as men, who were clearly less qualified and not as smart as I was."

passage.translation: 一位受访者解释说:"对我来说最大的挑战是继续相信自己,而我收到的所有信息都是,我永远不会被认真对待,也不会像男性那样得到晋升或加薪,而那些男性明显不如我有资格,也没有我聪明。"

sentences.text: A chemical engineer who worked in manufacturing agreed, "You have to prove yourself just because you are female.
And you have to work twice as hard!"

passage.translation: 一位从事制造业的化学工程师也表示同意:"仅仅因为你是女性,你就必须证明自己。而且你必须付出双倍的努力!"

sentences.text: A civil engineer said, "We are 'women engineers.' People don't refer to a man as a 'man engineer'—he's an engineer.
We are constantly reminded that we don't truly belong."
Another civil engineer stated, "On many levels, you're never quite one of the groups."

passage.translation: 一位土木工程师说:"我们是'女性工程师'。人们不会把男性称为'男性工程师',他就是工程师。我们不断被提醒,我们并不真正属于这里。"另一位土木工程师表示:"在许多层面上,你永远不完全是群体中的一员。"

sentences.text: Women also talked about family caregiving responsibilities.

A retired vice president from a major chemical company stated, "Young women engineers are on an equal footing until they have children, then they struggle to balance work and family—and compete with men who don't have the same household responsibilities."

passage.translation: 女性还谈到了家庭照料责任。一家大型化工公司的退休副总裁表示:"年轻的女性工程师在生孩子之前处于平等地位,然后她们就要努力平衡工作和家庭,并与没有相同家庭责任的男性竞争。"

sentences.text: But over the years things have changed a lot.
Young women engineers are more accepted mostly because there are just more of them.

passage.translation: 但多年来情况已经发生了很大变化。年轻的女性工程师更容易被接受,主要是因为她们的人数更多了。

sentences.text: Many women engineers hailed the benefits of their chosen career.
A program manager in manufacturing stated that engineering is the best degree.
A mechanical engineer said, "It will give you the flexibility to do almost anything.
It is also satisfying to see the effects of what you have done."

passage.translation: 许多女性工程师赞扬了她们所选择职业的好处。一位制造业项目经理表示,工程学是最好的学位。一位机械工程师说:"它会给你几乎可以做任何事情的灵活性。看到你所做工作的成效也很令人满意。"

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about the engineering profession in the United States?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
这篇文章对美国工程行业有何论述?
A) 自1979年以来,该行业对女性工程师的态度发生了变化。
B) 该行业在20世纪70年代见证了女性工程师数量的显著增长。
C) 该行业经历了男性主导地位的逐渐削弱。
D) 该行业在2000年拥有数量最多的工程专业学生。
**判型** What does the passage say about the engineering profession in the United States 没有 infer/imply/mainly about 等推断或主旨标志，问 "the passage say"，是对原文已陈述事实的核对，属四级最高频的细节题。
**拆句** 题干主干是 What does the passage say about ...，是 say about 后接宾语的特殊疑问句，结构平铺直叙、无陷阱，只要知道 say about="就……说了什么"即可。
**定位** 1970 年，主修工程的女性占比不到 1%；1979 年这一数字升至 9%。许多人本希望女性能以同样速度持续进入这一行业，但事实并非如此。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有原文只给比例数据，没有提任何"对待女工程师态度的变化"，a change in attitude towards women engineers since 1979 属于凭空添加新概念。
B) ✓ 正确In 1970, the percentage of women majoring in engineering was less than 1%. In 1979, that number was 9%↔ It witnessed a significant increase in women engineers in the 1970s In 1970 和 In 1979 ↔ in the 1970s预判要的是"70 年代女工程师比例大幅上升"，B 项 significant increase in women engineers in the 1970s 几乎逐词对应，无需犹豫即可锁定。
C) 与原文相反Today, only 21% of engineering majors are women, a number largely unchanged since 2000 明确说自 2000 年起男性主导未弱化，与 gradual weakening of male dominance 直接相反。
D) 偷换概念原文 2000 年只是"21% 未变"的起算点，并未说 2000 年工程专业人数达到最大，boasted the largest number of engineering majors in 2000 属于把时间词原样搬，结论却换了内容。
questions.quote: In 1970, the percentage of women majoring in engineering was less than 1%. In 1979, that number was 9%. Many hoped women would continue to enter the field at the same rate. But that's not what happened.

options.text: It has seen a change in attitude towards women engineers since 1979.
It witnessed a significant increase in women engineers in the 1970s.
It has experienced the gradual weakening of male dominance.
It boasted the largest number of engineering majors in 2000.

questions.prompt: What does one survey taker say was her greatest challenge?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
一位受访者表示她面临的最大挑战是什么?
A) 不对资质较低的男性工程师产生优越感。
B) 不把她收到的所有信息都当真。
C) 在升职或加薪时不过高评价自己的资历。
D) 尽管不断受到打击或遭受不公平待遇,仍不失去自信。
**判型** What does one survey taker say was her greatest challenge 是对原文一句引语的客观还原，属细节题。
**拆句** What does one survey taker say was her greatest challenge 是个嵌套问句，say 后面接的是 "(that) her greatest challenge was ____"，疑问词 What 提到了句首，回原文找"挑战是 ____" 这层语义即可。
**定位** 我最大的挑战是在收到"我永远不会像男性那样被认真对待、被晋升或被加薪——而那些男性明显不如我合格、不如我聪明"这类信息时，仍然继续相信自己。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文受访者只是说"那些男性明显不如我合格"，是事实陈述；Not to feel superior to less qualified male engineers 把它扭曲成"不要觉得自己高人一等"，方向截然不同。
B) 答非所问原文 all the messages I was getting 是"挑战的背景"，不是"挑战本身"；B 项却把"不要把这些信息当真"说成挑战，错把背景当主体。
C) 与原文相反原文说"她被晋升/加薪的待遇不如男性"，C 项却说"在被晋升/加薪时不要看高自己的资历"，既颠倒了情境（她没有被同等晋升），也错读了态度。
D) ✓ 正确continuing to believe in myself ↔ Not to lose self-confidence all the messages I was getting were that I would never be taken seriously or promoted or given raises at the same rate as men↔ though constantly discouraged or unfairly treated预判要"在打压中坚持自信"，D 项 Not to lose self-confidence though constantly discouraged or unfairly treated 两个要素全有，是定位句的精准同义替换。
questions.quote: The greatest challenge for me was continuing to believe in myself, when all the messages I was getting were that I would never be taken seriously or promoted or given raises at the same rate as men, who were clearly less qualified and not as smart as I was.

options.text: Not to feel superior to less qualified male engineers.
Not to take seriously all the messages she was getting.
Not to think highly of her qualifications when promoted or given a pay raise.
Not to lose self-confidence though constantly discouraged or unfairly treated.

questions.prompt: How do women engineers frequently feel according to the two civil engineers?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
根据两位土木工程师的说法,女性工程师经常有何感受?
A) 在许多层面上不具备资格。
B) 被排除在团体之外。
C) 被所在组织过度使用。
D) 被男性同事看不起。
**判型** How do women engineers frequently feel according to the two civil engineers 问的是"她们感觉如何"，依据 according to 直接锁定原文两位 civil engineer 的话，是细节归纳题。
**拆句** How do women engineers frequently feel according to the two civil engineers 主干是 How do women engineers feel，frequently 是状语，according to ... 是介词短语作状语，限定信息来源，没有从句也无否定，是直白的特殊疑问句。
**定位** 一位土木工程师说："我们被叫作'女工程师'。人们不会把男人叫'男工程师'——他就是工程师。我们时刻被提醒：我们并不真正属于这里。"另一位土木工程师说："在很多层面上，你从来不算这个圈子的一员。"
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文 On many levels, you're never quite one of the groups 中的 on many levels 修饰"在多个层面上"不属于群体，A 项 Disqualified on many levels 把它说成"在多个层面上不合格"，是把"不属于群体"换成"不合格"。
B) ✓ 正确We are constantly reminded that we don't truly belong ↔ Excluded from the group you're never quite one of the groups ↔ Excluded from the group预判要"不属于/被排除的情绪"，B 项 Excluded from the group 直接对应两位受访者的核心情感，是最稳的同义替换。
C) 张冠李戴P6 全段谈的是"不属于群体"的归属感问题，根本未涉及工作量；Overworked by their organizations 是从 work twice as hard 借来的概念，硬塞进了 53 题。
D) 过度推断原文两位土木工程师讲的是"被整个圈子提醒不属于"，并未具体说"是男同事看低自己"；Looked down upon by male colleagues 把抽象的群体压缩成"男同事"这一具体施动者。
questions.quote: A civil engineer said, "We are 'women engineers.' People don't refer to a man as a 'man engineer'—he's an engineer. We are constantly reminded that we don't truly belong." Another civil engineer stated, "On many levels, you're never quite one of the groups."

options.text: Disqualified on many levels.
Excluded from the group.
Overworked by their organizations.
Looked down upon by male colleagues.

questions.prompt: What probably makes young women engineers more accepted nowadays?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
什么可能使年轻女性工程师在当今更容易被接受?
A) 她们在获得平等地位方面取得的成功。
B) 她们平衡工作与家庭的能力。
C) 她们职责的改变。
D) 她们数量的增加。
**判型** What probably makes young women engineers more accepted nowadays 看似含probably 像推断，实质问"原文里给出的原因是什么"，原文已经直说理由，仍是细节题。
**拆句** What probably makes young women engineers more accepted nowadays 是 What makes sb. + 形容词 的使役结构，What 作主语，makes 是谓语，young women engineers 是宾语，more accepted nowadays 是宾语补足语，意为"是什么让年轻女工程师如今更被接受"。
**定位** 年轻女工程师之所以如今更被接受，主要是因为她们的人数变多了。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴原文 Young women engineers are on an equal footing until they have children 只说"育前与男性平起平坐"，是过去就存在的状态，不是"如今更被接受"的新原因；A 项Their success in gaining an equal footing 把它包装成新成就，归错原因。
B) 与原文相反原文 then they struggle to balance work and family 明明说"在生育后她们挣扎于平衡工作与家庭"，B 项却说"她们有能力平衡工作与家庭"，方向完全相反。
C) 无中生有原文 compete with men who don't have the same household responsibilities 提到"家庭责任不对等"，但从未说女工程师的责任发生了变化；C 项 The change in their responsibilities 是凭空增添一个变化。
D) ✓ 正确there are just more of them ↔ The increase in their number预判要"人数变多"，D 项 The increase in their number 是这层意思的最贴近名词化表达，无可争议。
questions.quote: Young women engineers are more accepted mostly because there are just more of them.

options.text: Their success in gaining an equal footing.
Their ability to balance work and family.
The change in their responsibilities.
The increase in their number.

questions.prompt: What can we conclude about many female engineers from the statement of a mechanical engineer?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （推断题）
**题目译文**
从一位机械工程师的陈述中,我们可以对许多女性工程师得出什么结论?
A) 她们对所选择的职业深感自豪。
B) 她们获得了灵活工作的好处。
C) 她们享受将工程工作做到最佳程度。
D) 她们已证明能够做几乎任何事情。
**判型** What can we conclude about many female engineers from the statement of a mechanical engineer 中的 conclude+from 是典型推断题信号，需要从一位受访者的具体话语得出"许多女工程师"层面的结论。
**拆句** What can we conclude about many female engineers from the statement of a mechanical engineer 主干为 What can we conclude，about many female engineers是 conclude 的对象，from the statement of a mechanical engineer 是信息来源；问的是"从这位机械工程师的话里能得出关于许多女工程师的什么结论"。
**定位** 许多女工程师都盛赞自己所选职业的好处。一位制造业项目经理说工程是最好的学位。一位机械工程师说："它会给你几乎可以做任何事的灵活度，看到自己所做工作的成果也令人满足。"
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确Many women engineers hailed the benefits of their chosen career↔They take great pride in their chosen career It is also satisfying to see the effects of what you have done↔take great pride in their chosen career预判要"对职业感到自豪"，A 项 take great pride in their chosen career 在态度极性和概括层级上都对得最准，是最贴预判的一项。
B) 偷换概念原文 give you the flexibility to do almost anything 是说"这份职业能给你灵活度"，强调的是职业本身的属性；B 项 reaped the benefits of being flexible 把它说成"她们因"自己"灵活而获益"，把工具属性挪到了人本身。
C) 无中生有原文 engineering is the best degree 是"工程是最好的学位"，整体作主系表；C 项enjoy doing engineering to the best degree 把 the best degree 拆成 to the best degree（=最大程度地）作状语，意思变成"以最高程度享受做工程"，是字面拼凑出的伪意思。
D) 过度推断原文 give you the flexibility to do almost anything 是工程这个职业"能让你"做几乎任何事，是潜在可能；D 项 proved capable of doing almost anything 说她们"已经证明自己能做几乎任何事"，把可能性升级为既定事实。
questions.quote: Many women engineers hailed the benefits of their chosen career. A program manager in manufacturing stated that engineering is the best degree. A mechanical engineer said, "It will give you the flexibility to do almost anything. It is also satisfying to see the effects of what you have done."

options.text: They take great pride in their chosen career.
They have reaped the benefits of being flexible.
They enjoy doing engineering to the best degree.
They have proved capable of doing almost anything.

title: The weakening of the human connection to nature…

sentences.text: The weakening of the human connection to nature might be good for economic growth but is bad for people.
A tipping point was reached in 2020 when human-made materials—such as steel, concrete and plastic—were found to weigh more than all life on Earth.
Continuing to grow concrete forests rather than real ones is shortsighted.
Simply being in the nearest wood has such health benefits that the Woodland Trust successfully lobbied for it to be prescribed by doctors.

passage.translation: 人类与自然联系的削弱可能有利于经济增长,但对人们却是有害的。2020年达到了一个临界点,当时发现人造材料——如钢铁、混凝土和塑料——的重量超过了地球上所有生命的总重量。继续建造混凝土森林而非真正的森林是目光短浅的。仅仅身处最近的树林中就有如此多的健康益处,以至于Woodland Trust成功游说医生开具处方。

sentences.text: Yet slipping from popular culture is the wonder and beauty of the natural world.
For every three nature-related words in hit songs of the 1950s, researchers found, there was only slightly more than one 50 years later.
It is not a moment too soon that teenagers will be able to take a natural history test, given that for decades children have been able to name more video game characters than wildlife species.

passage.translation: 然而,自然世界的奇妙与美丽正在从流行文化中消失。研究人员发现,20世纪50年代热门歌曲中每出现三个与自然相关的词汇,50年后就只有略多于一个了。青少年将能够参加自然历史测试,这一时刻来得正是时候,因为几十年来儿童能说出的电子游戏角色名字比野生动物物种名称要多。

sentences.text: Part of remedying this social disease would be for parliament to pass a "right to grow" law, allowing anyone to turn underused public spaces into vegetable and fruit gardens.
The idea is for people to get back in touch with the soil—while producing food sustainably.

passage.translation: 纠正这种社会疾病的部分措施是议会通过一项'种植权'法律,允许任何人将未充分利用的公共空间变成蔬菜和水果园。其理念是让人们重新接触土壤——同时可持续地生产食物。

sentences.text: Vegetable planting has a respectable tradition.
In April 1649, locals responded to high prices and food shortages by cultivating vegetables on common land in Southern England.

The practice of throwing seed bombs to turn vacant plots of land green took off in 1970s New York, and has been revived(使复活) by green-thumbed(有园艺才能的) social media influencers who defy local US regulations in a war on ugly spots in cities.

passage.translation: 种植蔬菜有着值得尊重的传统。1649年4月,当地人通过在英格兰南部的公共土地上种植蔬菜来应对高物价和食物短缺。在20世纪70年代的纽约,投掷种子弹将空置地块变绿的做法开始流行,并被有园艺才能的社交媒体影响者所复兴,他们无视美国地方法规,向城市中的丑陋地带宣战。

sentences.text: Apart from the urgent task of providing more healthy nutrients to those who increasingly can't afford them, publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens connect what we eat to where it comes from—the means of production, if you will.
They can make unlovely spaces lovely, and marry use and beauty as well as help promote a sense of community.
Plants are also, of course, our first defence against species loss and climate change.
Such planting is a small step for humanity—in the right direction.

passage.translation: 除了为那些越来越无力负担的人提供更多健康营养的紧迫任务外,可公开使用的水果和蔬菜园将我们所吃的食物与其来源——如果你愿意的话,即生产方式——联系起来。它们可以使不美观的空间变得美观,将实用性与美感结合起来,并有助于促进社区意识。当然,植物也是我们抵御物种丧失和气候变化的第一道防线。这种种植对人类来说是朝着正确方向迈出的一小步。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does the author want to emphasise in the first paragraph?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （主旨题）
**题目译文**
作者在第一段想要强调什么?
A) 2020年是人类历史上的一个重大转折点。
B) 从长远来看,经济增长对人们的益处很小。
C) 削弱人类与自然的联系是不明智的。
D) 使用人造材料对人类是有害的。
**判型** What does the author want to emphasise in the first paragraph? 问的是首段作者想强调什么，是段落主旨而非局部细节。
**拆句** What does the author want to emphasise in the first paragraph? 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，want to emphasise 是一个简单的动词短语，无从句无否定，结构清爽，无陷阱。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全The year 2020 was a big turning point in human history. 把段落里一个支撑论据（2020 年的 tipping point）当作主旨，且"in human history"是过度推断——原文只说人造物质量超过生命这一比较点。
B) 偷换概念Economic growth benefits people little in the long run. 把原文"对经济或许有利"扭曲成"经济增长对人没好处"，攻击点从"与自然的连接"偷换到了"经济增长本身"，并把短期权衡偷换为 in the long run。
C) ✓ 正确The weakening of the human connection to nature might be good for economic growth but is bad for people.↔ It is unwise to weaken the human connection to nature. Continuing to grow concrete forests rather than real ones is shortsighted. ↔It is unwise to weaken the human connection to nature.预判要的是"削弱与自然的连接是不明智的"，It is unwise to weaken the human connection to nature. 正好是这一判断的同义表达，且覆盖整段而不偏向某个论据。
D) 过度推断It is harmful to mankind to use human-made materials. 把"人造物总质量超过生命"这一比较事实，推断成"使用人造物本身就有害"，原文从未否定使用人造物，只是反对以此取代真实自然。

options.text: The year 2020 was a big turning point in human history.
Economic growth benefits people little in the long run.
It is unwise to weaken the human connection to nature.
It is harmful to mankind to use human-made materials.

questions.prompt: What did researchers find about popular culture?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
研究人员关于流行文化发现了什么?
A) 它与自然界日益脱节。
B) 它充斥着各种电子游戏角色。
C) 它特别迎合青少年的口味。
D) 它仍然受到20世纪50年代热门歌曲的影响。
**判型** What did researchers find about popular culture? 直接问研究者发现了什么客观事实，属于细节题。
**拆句** What did researchers find about popular culture? 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，主谓researchers find，about popular culture 限定 find 的对象，结构平铺，无陷阱。
**定位** 对于 1950 年代流行歌曲里每三个与自然相关的词，研究人员发现，50 年后只剩下略多于一个。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确For every three nature-related words in hit songs of the 1950s, researchers found, there was only slightly more than one 50 years later.↔ It is increasingly detached from the natural world. Yet slipping from popular culture is the wonder and beauty of the natural world. ↔It is increasingly detached from the natural world.预判要的是"自然内容大量减少"，A 项用 increasingly detached 这一抽象升级精确对应该数据，所以锁定 A。
B) 偷换概念It is filled with all kinds of video game characters. 把原文"孩子认识的游戏角色比野生动物多"偷换成"流行文化里充斥着游戏角色"——研究比较的是孩子的认知，不是流行文化的内容构成。
C) 无中生有It is especially appealing to the taste of teenagers. 全句"对青少年口味格外有吸引力"在 P2 中没有任何对应；原文只是提到青少年将能参加自然史考试，并未谈流行文化对青少年的吸引力。
D) 与原文相反It is still impacted by the hit songs of the 1950s. 说流行文化仍受 50 年代流行歌曲影响，但原文用 50 年代和 50 年后的数据对比，恰恰说明这种影响在减弱、自然主题在流失，方向相反。
questions.quote: For every three nature-related words in hit songs of the 1950s, researchers found, there was only slightly more than one 50 years later.

options.text: It is increasingly detached from the natural world.
It is filled with all kinds of video game characters.
It is especially appealing to the taste of teenagers.
It is still impacted by the hit songs of the 1950s.

questions.prompt: What does the author propose people do?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者建议人们做什么?
A) 采取措施确保可持续的食物发展。
B) 通过种植权利重新与自然建立联系。
C) 支持议会对抗社会疾病。
D) 用果树和蔬菜植物覆盖公共空间。
**判型** What does the author propose people do? 问作者具体提议人们做什么，定位到对应主张句即可作答，属于细节题。
**拆句** What does the author propose people do? 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，propose 后接"people do"是"propose sb do sth"句型省略了 that 与情态的简略问法，相当于问"作者建议人们做什么"，无陷阱。
**定位** 矫正这一社会病的一部分举措，是让议会通过一项"种植权"法案，允许任何人把利用不足的公共空间改造成菜园和果园。其理念在于让人们重新接触土壤——同时可持续地生产粮食。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全Take measures to ensure sustainable food development. 把原文末尾"while producing food sustainably"这一附带的从属信息抬升成了核心主张，掩盖了"重新接触土壤、与自然重连"这一真正的主诉。
B) ✓ 正确Part of remedying this social disease would be for parliament to pass a "right to grow" law ↔Reconnect with nature through the right to grow. The idea is for people to get back in touch with the soil ↔Reconnect with nature through the right to grow.预判要的两层信息——"通过种植权"和"重新接触自然"——B 项用 through 和reconnect with nature 一并覆盖，所以是答案。
C) 偷换概念Stand by the parliament in fighting social diseases. 把"议会通过法案"偷换成"人们站在议会一边"，方向完全反过来——原文是作者建议议会行动，不是建议民众站队议会。
D) 过度推断Cover public spaces with fruit trees and vegetable plants. 把原文"allowing anyone to turn underused public spaces"的"利用不足的公共空间"扩展到"所有公共空间"，并把"允许"扭曲为"全面覆盖"，方式与范围都被放大。
questions.quote: Part of remedying this social disease would be for parliament to pass a "right to grow" law, allowing anyone to turn underused public spaces into vegetable and fruit gardens. The idea is for people to get back in touch with the soil—while producing food sustainably.

options.text: Take measures to ensure sustainable food development.
Reconnect with nature through the right to grow.
Stand by the parliament in fighting social diseases.
Cover public spaces with fruit trees and vegetable plants.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about vegetable planting?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
我们从文章中了解到关于蔬菜种植的什么信息?
A) 这一切始于1649年的英格兰南部。
B) 它受到美国政府法规的保护。
C) 它长期以来一直被用于增加食物供应和改善城市景观。
D) 随着社交媒体影响力的增加,它已在全球范围内普及。
**判型** What do we learn from the passage about vegetable planting? 问从文章中获取的事实信息，属于细节题。
**拆句** What do we learn from the passage about vegetable planting? 主干 What do we learn，from the passage 与 about vegetable planting 都是介词短语作状语，前者点出来源、后者点出话题对象，结构清晰。
**定位** 1649 年 4 月，英国南部居民为应对高物价与粮食短缺，在公共土地上种植蔬菜。把种子炸弹扔到空地以使其变绿的做法在 1970 年代的纽约兴起，并被有园艺天分的社交媒体网红重新带火，他们无视当地美国法规，向城市里的丑陋角落"开战"。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全It all started in 1649 in Southern England. 把段内一个时间点放大为"全部起源"，原文只说 1649 年发生过一次，并未说蔬菜种植起源于此。
B) 与原文相反It is protected by US government regulations. 与原文 defy local US regulations 直接相反：原文说网红"无视"美国当地法规，选项说"受其保护"。
C) ✓ 正确locals responded to high prices and food shortages by cultivating vegetables on common land in Southern England↔ It has long been used to increase food supply and improve urban landscape. throwing seed bombs to turn vacant plots of land green ↔It has long been used to increase food supply and improve urban landscape. Vegetable planting has a respectable tradition. ↔It has long been used to increase food supply and improve urban landscape.预判要的"补食物 + 美化城市"两条线，C 项用 food supply 与 urban landscape 并列，正好两条都覆盖，所以是答案。
D) 过度推断It has been popularised worldwide with the increasing influence of social media.把原文里"1970 年代纽约 + 美国网红重新带火"扩张为"全球普及"，并把"重振"延伸为"日益增长的影响力"，超出原文范围。
questions.quote: In April 1649, locals responded to high prices and food shortages by cultivating vegetables on common land in Southern England. The practice of throwing seed bombs to turn vacant plots of land green took off in 1970s New York, and has been revived by green-thumbed social media influencers who defy local US regulations in a war on ugly spots in cities.

options.text: It all started in 1649 in Southern England.
It is protected by US government regulations.
It has long been used to increase food supply and improve urban landscape.
It has been popularised worldwide with the increasing influence of social media.

questions.prompt: What can publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens do apart from their practical functions?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
除了实用功能外,可公开访问的果蔬园还能做什么?
A) 提高人们的环保意识。
B) 增加植物物种的多样性。
C) 充当抵御自然灾害的第一道防线。
D) 增强人们的社区精神。
**判型** What can publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens do apart from their practical functions? 问的是除实用功能之外这些菜园还能做什么，是对应原文并列项的细节题。
**拆句** What can publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens do apart from their practical functions? 主干 What can ... gardens do，apart from their practical functions 作状语限定范围，相当于把"实用功能"这一已知项排除出去；其中 publicly accessible 是副词修饰形容词，整体修饰 gardens。
**定位** 它们能化丑为美，把实用与美感融合在一起，并有助于增强一种社区感。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念Raise people's environmental awareness. 把"连接食物与产地、对抗物种丧失"偷换成"提升环保意识"，前者是行为层面的连接和效用，后者是心理认知层面的意识。
B) 无中生有Add to the great variety of plant species. 说菜园会增加植物物种多样性，原文从未谈"增加植物物种多样性"这一功能。
C) 偷换概念Act as the first defence against natural disasters. 把 first defence against species loss and climate change 偷换成"对抗自然灾害"——物种丧失和气候变化不等于"自然灾害"，并且选项主语 act as 暗示把整个菜园当成防线，与原文 Plants are 也对不上。
D) ✓ 正确help promote a sense of community↔ Enhance people's community spirit.预判要的"增强社区感"在原文里有直接对应的 "help promote a sense of community"，D 项把 promote 替换为 enhance、sense of community 替换为community spirit，是高保真同义替换，可锁定。
questions.quote: They can make unlovely spaces lovely, and marry use and beauty as well as help promote a sense of community.

options.text: Raise people's environmental awareness.
Add to the great variety of plant species.
Act as the first defence against natural disasters.
Enhance people's community spirit.

title: When Toni Morrison died in 2019, the world…

sentences.text: When Toni Morrison died in 2019, the world lost one of its most influential authors.
But Morrison was not an early success.
Her first novel was not published until she was 39, and her last appeared when she was 84.
And Morrison was not (26)____ in this regard.
Numerous writers produce masterpieces well into their 70s and beyond.
Such (27)____ accomplishments highlight an important point.
Our capacity to speak, write and learn new vocabulary does not seem to (28)____ with age.
Our eyesight may dim and our recall may weaken, but, by comparison, our ability to produce and to(29)____ language is well preserved into older adulthood.

passage.translation: 当托妮·莫里森于2019年去世时,世界失去了一位最具影响力的作家。但莫里森并非早年成名。她的第一部小说直到39岁才出版,而她的最后一部作品问世时她已84岁。莫里森在这方面并非独一无二。许多作家在70多岁及以后仍创作出杰作。这些文学成就凸显了一个重要观点。我们说话、写作和学习新词汇的能力似乎不会随年龄增长而衰退。我们的视力可能减弱,记忆力可能下降,但相比之下,我们产生和理解语言的能力在老年期仍保持良好。

sentences.text: Indeed, the latest research that has emerged on language and aging shows that language mastery is a(30)____ that we begin as infants and continue on for the rest of our lives.
Some aspects of our language abilities, such as our knowledge of word meanings, (31)____ improve during middle and late adulthood.
One study, for example, found that adults over sixty had an average vocabulary size of over 21,000 words.
The researchers also studied a (32)____ of college students and found that their average vocabulary contained (33)____ 16,000 words.
In another study, older adults, with an average age of 75,(34)____ better than participants in their youth or middle years on tasks that required them to determine the meaning of words.
Thus, language seems to be a skill that, contrary to what many might (35)____ , does not weaken with age.

passage.translation: 事实上,关于语言和衰老的最新研究表明,掌握语言是一段旅程,我们从婴儿时期开始,并在余生中持续进行。我们语言能力的某些方面,例如我们对词汇含义的认知,实际上在中年和老年期有所提高。例如,一项研究发现,60岁以上的成年人平均词汇量超过21000个单词。研究人员还对大学生样本进行了研究,发现他们的平均词汇量约为16000个单词。在另一项研究中,平均年龄为75岁的老年人在需要确定单词含义的任务上表现优于青年或中年参与者。因此,语言似乎是一种技能,与许多人可能认为的相反,它不会随年龄增长而减弱。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
When Toni Morrison died in 2019, the world lost one of its most influential authors. But Morrison was not an early success. Her first novel was not published until she was 39, and her last appeared when she was 84. And Morrison was not {{26}} in this regard. Numerous writers produce masterpieces well into their 70s and beyond. Such {{27}} accomplishments highlight an important point. Our capacity to speak, write and learn new vocabulary does not seem to {{28}} with age. Our eyesight may dim and our recall may weaken, but, by comparison, our ability to produce and to{{29}} language is well preserved into older adulthood.

Indeed, the latest research that has emerged on language and aging shows that language mastery is a{{30}} that we begin as infants and continue on for the rest of our lives. Some aspects of our language abilities, such as our knowledge of word meanings, {{31}} improve during middle and late adulthood. One study, for example, found that adults over sixty had an average vocabulary size of over 21,000 words. The researchers also studied a {{32}} of college students and found that their average vocabulary contained {{33}} 16,000 words. In another study, older adults, with an average age of 75,{{34}} better than participants in their youth or middle years on tasks that required them to determine the meaning of words. Thus, language seems to be a skill that, contrary to what many might {{35}} , does not weaken with age.

options.text: actually
literary
approximately
performed
assume
rarely
component
sample
comprehend
undermined
deteriorate
unique
equivalent
unit
journey

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) unique 形容词
**词性槽** be 动词 was 后作表语
**依据** 下一句正解释「并不罕见」Numerous writers produce masterpieces well into their 70s and beyond. 紧跟其后说明「许多作家年逾古稀仍出杰作」，正是在否定 Morrison 在大器晚成上的「独一无二性」，因此 And Morrison was not __(26)__ in this regard. 应为「并非独一无二的」。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) equivalent 缺少对比对象equivalent 表「与...等同」，须有比较对象（equivalent to sb.）；本句只给出 in this regard这一抽象限定，没有具体参照物，且 was not equivalent 与下一句「许多人也如此」逻辑反向，行不通。

questions.explanation:
**答案** I) literary 形容词
**词性槽** 形容词修饰名词 accomplishments
**依据** 上文全在谈作家与小说前文反复提到 When Toni Morrison died in 2019, the world lost one of its most influential authors. 与 Her first novel was not published until she was 39，accomplishments 指的就是「文学成就」，所以 literary 与上下文最贴合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) equivalent 语义不通equivalent 意为「等同的」，需要与另一参照对象比较，这里并未出现可比物，「等同的成就」放进 Such __(27)__ accomplishments highlight an important point. 不知与什么等同，逻辑断裂。
N) unique 已被 26 题选用unique 在解 26 题时已被划走（见 26 题），整套词库每词只能用一次，本空不再考虑。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) deteriorate 动词
**词性槽** to 后接动词原形
**依据** deteriorate with age 固定搭配deteriorate with age「随年龄退化」是英语中描述衰老的标准表达；Our capacity to speak, write and learn new vocabulary does not seem to __(28)__ with age.「我们的语言能力似乎并不随年龄退化」精准契合全文主旨。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) comprehend 语义与 with age 不搭comprehend 表「理解」，「不随年龄理解」语义不通；且 comprehend 是及物动词，后面缺少宾语；同时 29 题正需要 comprehend 与 produce 并列。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) comprehend 动词
**词性槽** to produce and to ___ 并列结构
**依据** produce 与 comprehend 对仗produce language（产出语言）与 comprehend language（理解语言）构成语言能力的「输出—输入」标准对子，是语言学领域常用搭配；our ability to produce and to__(29)__ language is well preserved into older adulthood. 顺势承接主旨「老年仍保留语言能力」。

**答案** H) journey 名词
**词性槽** is a ___ that 主表结构
**依据** 把语言习得比作终身旅程language mastery is a __(30)__ that we begin as infants and continue on for the rest of our lives.，begin... continue... for the rest of our lives 正是 journey 的典型语境（人生/学习的「旅程」），与「终身学习」的喻体完全匹配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
D) component 组成部分 ≠ 终身过程component 表「组成部分」，与「从婴儿开始持续一生」的连续性语义不搭——人不会「开始并持续一生地做一个 component」。
O) unit 单位/单元静态unit 指静态的「单位/单元」，无法承载「begin and continue for life」这一动态过程，搭配不当。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) actually 副词
**词性槽** 情态结构里修饰动词
**依据** 强调「与预期相反」全文核心论点是「语言能力不随年龄衰退」，本句进一步给出强例证：词义知识在中老年还会提高，与「人老智衰」的常识相反，正好用 actually「实际上」来强调反预期；与下一句One study, for example, found that adults over sixty had an average vocabulary size of over 21,000 words. 的举例链衔接通顺。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
K) rarely 与论点反向rarely improve「很少提升」会让本句意思翻转为「中老年词汇几乎不提升」，与下一句「60 岁以上成人词汇量超 21,000 词」的研究例证、以及全文「语言能力不衰退」主旨直接矛盾。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 K) —— actually vs rarely 反向陷阱。knowledge of word meanings, __(31)__ improve，rarely 词性与 actually 完全一致，光看语法位置无法区分；不少考生若没读到下一句的研究数据，会想当然填 rarely「很少提升」与「人老智衰」的常识匹配，正中陷阱。防坑：本题副词类二选一时先回全文找主旨，再决定方向。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) sample 名词
**词性槽** studied 的宾语 a ___ of...
**依据** 研究语境的「样本」上下文是 The researchers also studied a __(32)__ of college students，researcher +studied 已经标明这是科研场景，a sample of college students「一份大学生样本」是研究文献的固定表达。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
D) component 搭配不成立component 指「组成部分」，常说 a component of a system，与 college students 搭配生硬；研究语境里也极少说「一组学生组件」。
H) journey 需留给 30 题的「过程」journey 在此句搭配 a journey of college students 不通；同时本词在 30 题（语言学习是一段历程）有更贴切的归宿，先做的 32 题不应抢用它。
O) unit 搭配语义不准a unit of college students 听起来像「一队学生」，多用于军事/组织编制，而非研究取样语境；研究里通常说 sample。

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) approximately 副词
**词性槽** 数字 16,000 前需副词修饰
**依据** approximately + 数字是常用搭配contained __(33)__ 16,000 words，「大约 16,000 个单词」对应研究里给出的平均值估算，搭配自然、语义合理。

**答案** J) performed 动词
**词性槽** 主语后缺谓语动词
**依据** performed better 是典型搭配perform 在科研语境中常表「在测试/任务中的表现」，performed better than participants in their youth or middle years on tasks 是英语固定搭配 perform better on tasks「在任务上表现更好」，语义、时态均贴合。

**答案** C) assume 动词
**词性槽** 情态动词 might 后接动词原形
**依据** contrary to what people assume 固定逻辑contrary to what many might __(35)__ 是英语经典「与人们想当然的看法相反」句式，assume 表「想当然地以为」最贴合；与后面 does not weaken with age 形成「常识 vs事实」对照，呼应 overview 反预期立意。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) comprehend 要留给 29 题comprehend 在 29 题与 produce 并列搭配 produce and to ___ language，是该空唯一通顺选择；本空若先抢走，会让 29 题无解。同时本句语义重点是「设想/猜想」，不是「理解」。
F) deteriorate 要留给 28 题deteriorate 是 28 题「does not seem to ___ with age」的固定答案；放到本空 what many might deteriorate 语法不通（deteriorate 通常作不及物动词），既错位又抢走了 28 题的唯一选择。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 E) —— comprehend 错位抢词。contrary to what many might__(35)__, does not weaken with age，comprehend 与 might 语法上完全搭得上，「与许多人可能理解的相反」乍看也通，但它会抢走 29 题唯一的答案；并且本句核心是「想当然」而非「理解」。防坑：定动词时不仅看本空通不通，也要扫一眼别的空有没有更需要这个词的位置。

title: No escape as 'snow day' becomes 'e-learning day'

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Certain institutions, such as schools, are likely to close when bad weather, such as snow, flooding or extreme heat or cold, causes travel difficulties, power outages(断供), or otherwise endangers public safety.

When snowy weather arrives in the US, it means the chance of school children benefiting from the long-standing tradition of the "snow day", when schools are forced to close and students get an unexpected day off.

passage.translation: 某些机构,如学校,在恶劣天气(如降雪、洪水或极端高温或低温)导致交通困难、电力中断或以其他方式危及公共安全时,很可能会关闭。当降雪天气到达美国时,这意味着学校儿童有机会受益于由来已久的"雪天"传统,即学校被迫关闭,学生获得意外的一天假期。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: The criterion for a snow day is primarily the inability of school buses to operate safely on their routes and danger to children who walk to school.
Often, the school remains officially open even though buses do not run and classes are canceled.
Severe weather that causes cancellation or delay is more likely in regions that are less able to handle the situation.
Snow days are less common in more northern areas of the United States that are used to heavy winter snowfall, because municipalities are well equipped to clear roads and remove snow.
In areas less accustomed to snow even small snowfalls of an inch or two may render roads unsafe.

passage.translation: 雪天的标准主要是校车无法在其线路上安全运行以及对步行上学的儿童构成危险。通常,即使校车不运行且课程被取消,学校仍然正式开放。在处理这种情况能力较弱的地区,导致取消或延迟的恶劣天气更有可能发生。在习惯于冬季大雪的美国北部地区,雪天不太常见,因为市政当局有充足的设备来清理道路和清除积雪。在不太习惯降雪的地区,即使一两英寸的小雪也可能使道路不安全。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: Snow days are a familiar theme in American film and TV shows, with children getting the good news and then running outside for some seasonal snowman-building and snowball throwing, against a background of joyful pop music.
But the tradition is now over for pupils in several US states such as South Carolina, Nevada, Georgia and Indiana.
This academic year, many school boards have introduced policies which require students to work from home if the school is shut by snow or extreme weather.
They are known as "e-learning days", which certainly sounds less fun than a snow day.

passage.translation: 雪天是美国电影和电视节目中的一个熟悉主题,孩子们得到好消息后跑到外面堆雪人和打雪仗,背景是欢快的流行音乐。但这一传统现在对South Carolina、Nevada、Georgia和Indiana等几个美国州的学生来说已经结束了。本学年,许多学校董事会出台了政策,要求学生在学校因降雪或极端天气关闭时在家学习。它们被称为"电子学习日",这听起来确实不如雪天有趣。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: Teachers are also losing their snow days and instead will be expected to be on hand to take a virtual register and answer students' questions online.
A pilot programme in a school district in Anderson County, South Carolina, has supplied students with electronic tablets loaded with assignments to complete in the event of a school closure.
If it is successful, it could be rolled out across the state.

passage.translation: 教师也失去了他们的雪天,相反,他们将被要求随时待命以进行虚拟点名并在线回答学生的问题。South Carolina州Anderson County一个学区的试点项目已向学生提供了装载有作业的电子平板电脑,以便在学校关闭时完成。如果成功,它可能会在全州推广。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: But some parents object to the new policy if the vigorous debate on the Facebook page of Anderson County school district is anything to go by.
"When it snows, let the kids enjoy it," said one commenter.
Another said the decision would "ruin school even more", and someone else called snow days "a fun part of childhood".
But supporters of the policy say it means children will miss fewer days of school.

It will also bring to an end a less popular US high school tradition: the "make-up day", which requires students in many states to make up the time lost due to weather by working during school holidays.

passage.translation: 但一些家长反对这项新政策,如果Anderson County学区Facebook页面上的激烈辩论能说明什么的话。一位评论者说:"下雪时,让孩子们享受吧。"另一位说这个决定会"让学校更加糟糕",还有人称雪天是"童年有趣的一部分"。但该政策的支持者表示,这意味着孩子们将减少缺课天数。它还将结束一个不太受欢迎的美国高中传统:"补课日",它要求许多州的学生通过在学校假期学习来弥补因天气而损失的时间。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: Students in North Carolina already have several make-up days scheduled because of school closures during Hurricane Florence, which struck in September.
Tom Wilson, the superintendent(主管) of Anderson County school district, said the change away from snow days makes practical and financial sense.
He said technology has changed every profession, so it makes sense to use it to "eliminate" make-up days.
Adam Baker of the Department of Education in Indiana said e-learning days were proving a "great success".
He said most Indiana schools already use digital devices during lessons, so it was an "easy decision" to extend this to days when schools are closed.
He denies the decision is depriving children of the chance to enjoy the snow.
"Students are still able to enjoy snow days and outside time," he said.
"Many have PE and science assignments that have them out enjoying the weather."
But local school superintendents in Ohio are resisting proposals to adopt e-learning days.
They fear that students without internet access at home will be disadvantaged by the policy, and superintendent Tom Roth is concerned that e-learning days will offer a lower quality of education.

passage.translation: North Carolina的学生已经安排了几个补课日,因为9月袭击的飓风Florence导致学校关闭。Anderson County学区主管Tom Wilson表示,放弃雪天的改变在实际和财务上都有意义。他说技术已经改变了每个行业,因此使用它来"消除"补课日是有道理的。Indiana州教育部的Adam Baker表示,电子学习日被证明是"巨大的成功"。他说大多数Indiana学校已经在课堂上使用数字设备,因此将其扩展到学校关闭的日子是一个"容易的决定"。他否认这个决定剥夺了孩子们享受雪的机会。他说:"学生仍然能够享受雪天和户外时间。许多人有体育和科学作业,让他们出去享受天气。"但Ohio当地的学校主管正在抵制采用电子学习日的提议。他们担心家中没有互联网接入的学生将因该政策而处于不利地位,主管Tom Roth担心电子学习日将提供较低质量的教育。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: There are also so-called "blizzard bags", with assignments that children take home ahead of an expected snow closure.
But Mr Roth says it is not sufficient as a replacement.
"I think we still need the class time to give our kids the education that they deserve," he said.
"You can't get that with a blizzard bag or doing the work from home like that.
It's not going to be as effective."

passage.translation: 还有所谓的"暴风雪袋",其中包含孩子们在预期的雪天关闭之前带回家的作业。但Roth先生说这作为替代是不够的。他说:"我认为我们仍然需要课堂时间来给我们的孩子他们应得的教育。你无法通过暴风雪袋或像那样在家做作业来获得这些。这不会那么有效。"

passage.label: H

sentences.text: There is a long-running debate on whether missing days of school affects attainment.
In England, there has been a focus on tackling absenteeism(旷课) from school.
The Department for Education (DFE) published research in 2016 arguing that missing any days at school could have a negative impact on results.
Even a few days lost in a year could be enough to miss out on getting a good exam grade, the DFE's research concluded.
