title: How Climate Change Will Affect What You Eat

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Earlier this year, scientists warned that one in six animal species could go extinct(灭绝的) due to climate change.
Could the same thing happen to our crops and other foodstuffs too?

passage.translation: 今年早些时候,科学家警告说,由于气候变化,六分之一的动物物种可能会灭绝。我们的农作物和其他食品也会发生同样的事情吗?

passage.label: B

sentences.text: It's clear that farmers in many parts of the world are going to find things harder in the coming decades.
Last week, BBC Future explored one scientist's efforts to help crops cope with the increased probability of droughts.
By using the genes from resurrection(复活) plants, Jill Farrant of the University of Cape Town is exploring whether she can design crops to survive for much longer periods without water.

passage.translation: 显然,世界许多地区的农民在未来几十年里将面临更大的困难。上周,BBC Future探讨了一位科学家帮助农作物应对干旱概率增加的努力。开普敦大学的Jill Farrant正在利用复活植物的基因,探索她能否设计出在更长时间内无需水分也能存活的农作物。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: But if we can't find ways to protect other foods, will they survive climate change?
Fortunately, there is some good news on this front.
Despite alarmist headlines about "foods that are going extinct," there is no evidence that major food types like beans, chocolate, wine, corn or wheat will cease to exist.

passage.translation: 但如果我们找不到保护其他食物的方法,它们能在气候变化中存活下来吗?幸运的是,在这方面有一些好消息。尽管有关于"正在灭绝的食物"的危言耸听的标题,但没有证据表明豆类、巧克力、葡萄酒、玉米或小麦等主要食物类型会不复存在。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: But that doesn't mean it's all good news for future food.
We will probably have to change where we grow certain crops, as some regions get too hot.
The disadvantage, obviously, is that local farmers will suffer under this situation.
And some people may struggle to get the same access to certain foods.
"Even if overall food production may be unaffected, food security can still be impacted," says Margaret Walsh, a scientist at the US Department of Agriculture's Climate Change Program Office.
In other words, even if a certain food is still grown on some corner of the Earth, it doesn't mean that everyone will continue to have the same degree of access as today.

passage.translation: 但这并不意味着未来食物的一切都是好消息。随着一些地区变得过热,我们可能不得不改变某些农作物的种植地点。显然,不利之处在于当地农民将在这种情况下遭受损失。而且有些人可能难以获得与现在相同的某些食物。美国农业部气候变化项目办公室的科学家Margaret Walsh说:"即使总体粮食生产可能不受影响,粮食安全仍然可能受到影响。"换句话说,即使某种食物仍然在地球的某个角落种植,也不意味着每个人都将继续拥有与今天相同程度的获取途径。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Overall, the yields of many foods, from staples to life-enhancing extras such as coffee and chocolate, will likely be impacted by climate change too.

How those decreases will be felt will depend on the degree of warming and the crop in question, but in general, "anything over about 30 ℃ is very bad for crops," says Wolfram Schlenker, an associate professor of international and public affairs at Columbia University.
For example, statistical studies that he and a colleague built of corn and soybean(大豆) production in the US show a steep decline after crossing the 30℃ temperature threshold(临界点).

passage.translation: 总体而言,从主食到提升生活品质的额外食品如咖啡和巧克力,许多食物的产量也可能受到气候变化的影响。这些减产将如何被感受到取决于变暖的程度和相关作物,但总的来说,"任何超过约30℃的温度对农作物都非常不利",哥伦比亚大学国际与公共事务副教授Wolfram Schlenker说。例如,他和一位同事对美国玉米和大豆生产进行的统计研究显示,在超过30℃的温度临界点后,产量急剧下降。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: In the US—the world's largest producer of corn and soybeans—farms can move north to some degree, Schlenker says.
But eventually, yields will likely suffer because the soil north of Iowa declines in quality—a legacy of glacial(冰川的) expansion.
Other studies, including studies of wheat in India and corn in Africa, also found that there is a threshold above which yields sharply decline: crops can adapt and move, but only to a point.
"What's common to all studies is the finding that extreme heat is damaging to crop growth, although exact cutoffs vary by crop," Schlenker says.
"If predictions for the end of the century are true, though, I think a lot of agricultural areas in the US will see significant hits."

passage.translation: Schlenker说,在美国——世界上最大的玉米和大豆生产国——农场可以在一定程度上向北迁移。但最终,产量可能会受到影响,因为爱荷华州以北的土壤质量下降——这是冰川扩张的遗留问题。其他研究,包括对印度小麦和非洲玉米的研究,也发现存在一个临界点,超过该临界点产量就会急剧下降:农作物可以适应和迁移,但只能到一定程度。Schlenker说:"所有研究的共同点是发现极端高温对作物生长有害,尽管确切的临界值因作物而异。不过,如果对本世纪末的预测是真的,我认为美国的许多农业地区将遭受重大打击。"

passage.label: G

sentences.text: Under current conditions, about 4% of the world's croplands experience drought in any given year, but by the end of the century those conditions are forecasted to jump to about 18% per year.
Some studies indicate that horticulture crops—generally, everything besides staples—may be impacted most severely, largely because they tend to be confined to a smaller geographic area.

Researcher Andrew Jarvis and his colleagues found that 80% of coffee-growing zones in Central America and Brazil could become unsuitable by 2050, for example, while climate change will likely have "great impacts" on cocoa(可可粉) production in West Africa.
"High quality chocolate will be less available in the future, and if you want it, you'll have to pay a lot more for it," Jarvis says.

passage.translation: 在目前的条件下,世界上约4%的农田在任何给定年份都会经历干旱,但到本世纪末,这些条件预计将跃升至每年约18%。一些研究表明,园艺作物——通常是除主食以外的所有作物——可能受影响最严重,主要是因为它们往往局限于较小的地理区域。研究员Andrew Jarvis和他的同事发现,例如,到2050年,中美洲和巴西80%的咖啡种植区可能变得不适宜,而气候变化可能对西非的可可粉生产产生"巨大影响"。Jarvis说:"未来优质巧克力将不那么容易获得,如果你想要它,你将不得不为此支付更多的钱。"

passage.label: H

sentences.text: This means that, for those who can afford it, some foods will simply cost them more in the future.
But for poorer people, those same price jumps will likely cause certain foods to go extinct from their diets.
"The more you reduce, the shorter the supply, and the higher the price will jump," Schlenker says.

passage.translation: 这意味着,对于那些负担得起的人来说,未来一些食物只会让他们花费更多。但对于较贫穷的人来说,同样的价格跳涨可能会导致某些食物从他们的饮食中消失。Schlenker说:"你减少得越多,供应就越短,价格就会跳得越高。"

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Another potential climate change-induced problem is our dependence on commodity crops—wheat, soybeans, corn and rice—which currently provide humanity with 75% of its calories, either directly or indirectly through the animals we raise on those crops.

Jarvis and his colleagues also found that, over the past five decades, the world has seen an increasing standardisation of diets; the foods we eat globally today are 36% more similar than they were in 1961.

While this can be good news for the world's poorest people who now consume more calories, protein and fat than in the past, homogeneity(同一性) and over-dependence on a handful of staples leave us vulnerable to threats such as drought, disease and pests—all of which are predicted to worsen in many parts of the world as a result of climate change.

passage.translation: 另一个潜在的气候变化引发的问题是我们对商品作物的依赖——小麦、大豆、玉米和大米——这些作物目前直接或通过我们用这些作物饲养的动物间接为人类提供75%的卡路里。Jarvis和他的同事还发现,在过去的五十年里,世界饮食的标准化程度不断提高;我们今天在全球吃的食物比1961年相似度高36%。虽然这对世界上最贫穷的人来说可能是个好消息,他们现在比过去消耗更多的卡路里、蛋白质和脂肪,但同一性和对少数几种主食的过度依赖使我们容易受到干旱、疾病和害虫等威胁——所有这些威胁预计都会因气候变化而在世界许多地区恶化。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: There are ways we could soften the coming blow to the global food supply, however.

Like Farrant's work with resurrection crops, a number of companies, organisations and researchers are aiming to create drought and temperature-resistant crops through genetic engineering and conventional breeding.
For now, the jury is still out as to how successful those endeavours will be.
"The people at Monsanto who I've talked to are much more optimistic that they'll be able to engineer heat-tolerant crops," Schlenker says.
"On the other hand, scientists at the USDA who I've spoken with are much more cautious."

passage.translation: 然而,有一些方法可以减轻即将到来的对全球粮食供应的打击。像Farrant对复活作物的研究一样,许多公司、组织和研究人员正致力于通过基因工程和传统育种创造耐旱和耐温作物。目前,这些努力将取得多大成功还有待观察。Schlenker说:"我交谈过的Monsanto公司的人对他们能够培育出耐热作物要乐观得多。另一方面,我与之交谈过的美国农业部的科学家则要谨慎得多。"

passage.label: K

sentences.text: Until genetic engineering comes to fruition, other strategies might also help in some places, including applying more fertiliser, implementing better irrigation, using machinery that gets crops out of the field faster or installing storage facilities to delay spoilage.
"Many places could benefit a great deal just by using technologies that already exist," Walsh says.
"General farm management can go a long way toward easing changes."

passage.translation: 在基因工程取得成果之前,其他策略在某些地方也可能有所帮助,包括施用更多肥料、实施更好的灌溉、使用能更快将作物运出田间的机械,或安装储存设施以延缓腐败。Walsh说:"许多地方仅仅通过使用已经存在的技术就能获得很大的好处。一般的农场管理可以在很大程度上缓解变化。"

passage.label: L

sentences.text: Finally, diversifying our diet away from heat-sensitive wheat, corn, rice and other crops could also help.
"We've seen profound changes in the last decades in what we eat largely as a result of international trade, and I think that trend toward more diversification will continue," M Jarvis says.
"Depending on a greater number of plant species creates a more vigorous and less risky food system—and one that provides a broader range of nutritional requirements."

passage.translation: 最后,使我们的饮食从对热敏感的小麦、玉米、大米和其他作物多样化也可能有所帮助。Jarvis说:"在过去几十年里,我们所吃的食物发生了深刻的变化,这主要是国际贸易的结果,我认为这种走向更多样化的趋势将继续下去。依赖更多的植物物种可以创造一个更有活力、风险更低的食物系统——一个提供更广泛营养需求的系统。"

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

**改写** some people may not have adequate access to certain foods ↔some people may struggle to get the same access to certain foods “难以获取”改写为“获取不足”One consequence of climate change ↔ food security can still be impacted气候变化导致的后果

**定位** 施伦克尔说，在美国——世界最大的玉米和大豆生产国——农场可以在一定程度上北移。但最终产量很可能受损，因为爱荷华以北的土壤质量下降，这是冰川扩张的遗留问题。

**辨邻**
E E 段 a steep decline after crossing the 30℃ temperature threshold 是温度阈值角度，缺“向北迁移”这一锚点，故非 41 题源头。statistical studies that he and a colleague built of corn and soybean(大豆) production in the US show a steep decline after crossing the 30℃ temperature threshold(临界点)
questions.quote: In the US—the world's largest producer of corn and soybeans—farms can move north to some degree, Schlenker says. But eventually, yields will likely suffer because the soil north of Iowa declines in quality—a legacy of glacial(冰川的) expansion.

questions.prompt: One possible solution to the food security problem is diversification of diet.
questions.explanation:
**答案** L 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
食品安全问题的一个可能解决方案是饮食多样化。
**锚点** 饮食多样化解决粮食安全
**定位** 最后，让我们的饮食多样化、远离对热敏感的小麦、玉米、水稻等作物，也会有所帮助。
**改写** diversification of diet ↔diversifying our diet away from heat-sensitive wheat, corn, rice and other crops “饮食多样化”名词—动词对应One possible solution to the food security problem ↔diversifying our diet away from heat-sensitive wheat, corn, rice and other crops could also help “一种可能的解决办法”=“也会有所帮助”
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
I I 段 over-dependence on a handful of staples leave us vulnerable 讲的是单一依赖的风险，而 42 题要的是“多样化作为解决方案”，落在 L 段。homogeneity(同一性) and over-dependence on a handful of staples leave us vulnerable to threats
questions.quote: Finally, diversifying our diet away from heat-sensitive wheat, corn, rice and other crops could also help.

questions.prompt: It remains unsettled whether the global food supply problem can be solved by creating heat-tolerant crops through genetic engineering.
questions.explanation:
**答案** J 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
通过基因工程创造耐热作物能否解决全球粮食供应问题仍未确定。
**锚点** 基因工程培育耐热作物前景未定
**定位** 像法兰特对复活作物的研究一样，许多公司、组织和研究者正力图通过基因工程和常规育种培育抗旱耐热作物。目前，这些努力能否成功仍无定论。
**改写** It remains unsettled whether the global food supply problem can be solved ↔the jury is still out as to how successful those endeavours will be “仍未确定”=“尚无定论”creating heat-tolerant crops through genetic engineering ↔create drought and temperature-resistant crops through genetic engineering “耐热作物+基因工程”近义对应
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段 is exploring whether she can design crops to survive for much longer periods without water 是描述某人的探索，缺“the jury is still out”这一未定论锚点，故非 43 题源头。Jill Farrant of the University of Cape Town is exploring whether she can design crops to survive for much longer periods without water K K 段 other strategies might also help in some places 讲的是现成技术，不是 43 题“基因工程能否成功尚无定论”，故非源头。Until genetic engineering comes to fruition, other strategies might also help in some places
questions.quote: Like Farrant's work with resurrection crops, a number of companies, organisations and researchers are aiming to create drought and temperature-resistant crops through genetic engineering and conventional breeding. For now, the jury is still out as to how successful those endeavours will be.

questions.prompt: Poor people may have to give up eating certain foods because of their high prices.
questions.explanation:
**答案** H 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
穷人可能不得不因某些食物价格过高而放弃食用它们。
**锚点** 穷人因高价放弃某些食物
**定位** 但对较穷的人来说，同样的价格上涨很可能使某些食物从他们的饮食中彻底消失。
**改写** Poor people may have to give up eating certain foods ↔for poorer people, those same price jumps will likely cause certain foods to go extinct from their diets “被迫放弃吃”=“食物从饮食中消失”because of their high prices ↔ those same price jumps “因高价”=“价格上涨”
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
G G 段 you'll have to pay a lot more for it 是普遍涨价，缺“穷人放弃（give up）”这一落点，故非 44 题源头。if you want it, you'll have to pay a lot more for it D D 段 some people may struggle to get the same access to certain foods 是泛指获取受损，不带“因高价被迫放弃”的因果，故非 44 题源头。some people may struggle to get the same access to certain foods
questions.quote: But for poorer people, those same price jumps will likely cause certain foods to go extinct from their diets.

questions.prompt: A number of existing farming technologies could be used to reduce the negative effect of climate change on food production.
questions.explanation:
**答案** K 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
许多现有的农业技术可用于减少气候变化对粮食生产的负面影响。
**锚点** 现有农业技术减负面影响
**定位** 沃尔什说：“很多地方只要用上已经存在的技术，就能大大获益。”“总体的农场管理大有助于缓解这些变化。”
**改写** A number of existing farming technologies could be used ↔Many places could benefit a great deal just by using technologies that already exist “现有农业技术”=“已经存在的技术”reduce the negative effect of climate change on food production ↔General farm management can go a long way toward easing changes “减少负面影响”=“缓解这些变化”
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
J J 段 aiming to create drought and temperature-resistant crops through genetic engineering 是未来导向的研发，不是 45 题“已存在的现成技术”，故非源头。a number of companies, organisations and researchers are aiming to create drought and temperature-resistant crops through genetic engineering and conventional breeding L L 段 diversifying our diet away from heat-sensitive wheat, corn, rice and other crops could also help 讲的是饮食结构调整，非“现有农业技术”，故非 45 题源头。diversifying our diet away from heat-sensitive wheat, corn, rice and other crops could also help
questions.quote: "Many places could benefit a great deal just by using technologies that already exist," Walsh says. "General farm management can go a long way toward easing changes."

title: People in business often make decisions based on…

sentences.text: People in business often make decisions based on their own personal feelings or instincts.
It is quite horrifying to see people being guided by some unknown force.
But how wise is it, really, to let your instincts drive your decisions?

passage.translation: 商业人士在做决策时经常基于自己的个人感觉或直觉。看到人们被某种未知力量引导是相当可怕的。但是，让你的直觉驱动你的决策，这到底有多明智呢?

sentences.text: In the decision-making process, relying on instincts only makes sense when you have a vast experience to support you.
Simply "feeling" that something is right or should be done is highly subjective and can drown you.

passage.translation: 在决策过程中，依赖直觉只有在你拥有丰富经验支撑时才有意义。仅仅"感觉"某事是对的或应该做是高度主观的，可能会让你陷入困境。

sentences.text: On the other hand, there is a more rational approach to making decisions.
Data and analysis have long been associated with informed decisions.
These reduce the likelihood of errors and increase the chances of success.
Big, systematic data is mostly the foundation of most of our decisions, personal and business alike.
But with its extreme usability comes a complication: what do you do if you strongly feel something should not be done, even if the data insists that it should?

passage.translation: 另一方面，有一种更理性的决策方法。数据和分析长期以来一直与明智的决策相关联。这些能够减少错误的可能性，增加成功的机会。大量系统化的数据主要是我们大多数决策的基础，无论是个人决策还是商业决策。但随着其极高的实用性而来的是一个复杂问题:如果你强烈感觉某事不应该做，即使数据坚持认为应该做，你该怎么办?

sentences.text: This seemingly easy question is what drives the need to understand the relationship between instincts and data in the decision-making process.
Without making things complicated, the solution to this dilemma is using data and instincts in conjunction to arrive at the best possible decisions.

passage.translation: 这个看似简单的问题驱使人们需要理解决策过程中直觉与数据之间的关系。不把事情复杂化的话,这个困境的解决方案是将数据和直觉结合使用，以达成最佳决策。

sentences.text: Instinctive decisions are always backed by previous experiences or information, which acknowledges that instinctive decisions have worked in the past.
Decisions are not about making the choice and braving the consequences because you want to blindly trust your instincts.
They are about combining your inner wisdom with the knowledge of systematic data to make the best decisions.

passage.translation: 直觉决策总是有以往经验或信息作为支撑，这表明直觉决策在过去曾经奏效。决策不是做出选择并勇敢面对后果，因为你想盲目相信自己的直觉。决策是将你的内在智慧与系统化数据的知识相结合，以做出最佳决策。

sentences.text: Sometimes, rational analysis and data are impractical to be employed in certain situations.
Absence of definitive criteria, and time and resource constraints, and novel situations are instances which limit the practicality of data.
The only feasible option is to rely on what your instincts tell you.
In these situations, instincts can help you make effective and quick decisions.

passage.translation: 有时，在某些情况下理性分析和数据不切实际。缺乏明确标准、时间和资源限制以及新颖情况都是限制数据实用性的例子。唯一可行的选择是依赖你的直觉告诉你什么。在这些情况下，直觉可以帮助你做出有效而快速的决策。

sentences.text: Combining instinctive and rational analysis produces well-rounded decisions.
It reduces the chances of making mistakes, and has increasingly become a favorite approach to decision-making among leaders of today.

passage.translation: 将直觉和理性分析相结合能产生全面的决策。它减少了犯错的机会，并且已日益成为当今领导者最喜欢的决策方法。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does the author say businesspeople often do?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者说商界人士经常做什么?
A) 努力理解某些未知力量。
B) 避免被自己的感觉所驱使。
C) 利用丰富的过往经验。
D) 在决策时依赖直觉。
**判型** What does the author say businesspeople often do? 问的是「商人通常做什么」这一可在原文逐字核实的客观行为，不含 infer/imply。
**拆句** 题干主干是 What does the author say businesspeople often do?，what 作宾语前置；the author say 是插入成分，可剥离；剥离后等价于「Businesspeople often do what?」结构平铺，无陷阱。
**定位** 商界人士常常基于自己的个人感觉或直觉做决策。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有原文用 unknown force 比喻直觉的神秘性，并未让商人「弄清未知力量」；Strive to make sense of some unknown forces 凭空给出动作。
B) 与原文相反原文说商人「常凭感觉决策」，Avoid being driven by their own feeling 却说「避免被感觉驱动」，完全反向。
C) 张冠李戴relying on instincts only makes sense when you have a vast experience to support you 是作者给「合理使用直觉」开的条件，并非商人「实际正在做的事」。
D) ✓ 正确make decisions based on their own personal feelings or instincts ↔Rely on instincts in decision-making预判「依赖直觉作决策」与 Rely on instincts in decision-making 高度重合，正确项锁定。
questions.quote: People in business often make decisions based on their own personal feelings or instincts.

options.text: Strive to make sense of some unknown forces.
Avoid being driven by their own feeling.
Draw on a vast wealth of past experience.
Rely on instincts in decision-making.

questions.prompt: What should we take into account in order to make informed decisions?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
为了做出明智的决策,我们应该考虑什么?
A) 出错的可能性。
B) 系统性的数据和分析。
C) 情况的复杂性。
D) 个人感受和商业策略。
**判型** What should we take into account in order to make informed decisions? 问的是「为了做出明智决策应当考虑什么」，答案是原文直接陈述的因素。
**拆句** 题干主干 What should we take into account，what 作 take into account 的宾语前置；in order to make informed decisions 是表目的的不定式状语；句式简单。
**定位** 数据与分析长期以来一直与明智的决策紧密相关。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问原文 These reduce the likelihood of errors 说数据与分析「降低出错概率」，The likelihood of errors 只是数据带来的「结果」，不是「应当考虑的因素」。
B) ✓ 正确Data and analysis ↔ Systematic data and analysis预判「依靠数据与分析」与 Systematic data and analysis 完全对应，且原文 Big, systematic data 进一步加固，正确项锁定。
C) 无中生有原文从未出现 The complexity of circumstances（环境的复杂性）这一表述，与「明智决策的依靠」无关。
D) 偷换概念原文把 personal feelings or instincts 视作「常被依赖却需谨慎」的对象，并未把它与business strategies 并列为「做明智决策的因素」。
questions.quote: Data and analysis have long been associated with informed decisions.

options.text: The likelihood of errors.
Systematic data and analysis.
The complexity of circumstances.
Personal feelings and business strategies

questions.prompt: What should people do in a decision-making process if instincts disagree with data?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
在决策过程中,如果直觉与数据不一致,人们应该怎么做?
A) 用以往的经验解决这个两难困境。
B) 弄清楚两者中哪一个更可靠。
C) 将两者结合起来。
D) 让直觉优先于数据。
**判型** What should people do in a decision-making process if instincts disagree with data?问的是作者给出的具体做法，原文有 using data and instincts in conjunction 直陈方案。
**拆句** 题干 What should people do in a decision-making process if instincts disagree with data? 主句是 What should people do，in a decision-making process 介词短语作地点状语；if instincts disagree with data 是 if 引导的条件状语从句；结构清楚。
**定位** 简单来说，这一难题的解决方案是把数据和直觉结合起来使用，以达成最佳的决策。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴Instinctive decisions are always backed by previous experiences 是「直觉的支撑机制」，不是题干问的「矛盾时的解决办法」。
B) 无中生有原文从未让人「比较谁更可靠」，Figure out which of the two is more reliable 是凭空增加的取舍动作。
C) ✓ 正确using data and instincts in conjunction ↔ Combine the two together预判「把数据与直觉结合使用」与 Combine the two together 完全等价，正确项锁定。
D) 与原文相反原文明确反对盲目信任直觉（you want to blindly trust your instincts 被作者否定），Prioritize instincts over data 却把直觉摆在数据之上，反向。
questions.quote: Without making things complicated, the solution to this dilemma is using data and instincts in conjunction to arrive at the best possible decisions.

options.text: Resolve the dilemma with previous experience.
Figure out which of the two is more reliable.
Combine the two together.
Prioritize instincts over data.

questions.prompt: What should we do when facing various factors that limit the practicality of data?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
当面对限制数据实用性的各种因素时,我们应该怎么做?
A) 进行理性和系统的分析。
B) 探索最可行的选择。
C) 求助于我们内在的智慧。
D) 应用明确的标准。
**判型** What should we do when facing various factors that limit the practicality of data? 问的是特定情境下的做法，仍是定位＋复述。
**拆句** 题干主句 What should we do，when facing various factors 是 when 引导的现在分词时间状语，省略主语 we；that limit the practicality of data 是定语从句，修饰 factors。基础薄弱的同学要看清「factors」才是从句修饰对象，而不是「we」。
**定位** 唯一可行的办法，是依靠你的直觉告诉你的东西。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反原文明说数据在此场合「不可行」，Make a rational and systematic analysis 反让你做理性系统分析，正好走反方向。
B) 偷换概念原文说 The only feasible option is to rely on what your instincts tell you，给出的是「唯一可行的办法」；Explore the most feasible options 把「唯一选项」偷换成「探索多个最可行选项」，且把动作偷换成「探索」。
C) ✓ 正确rely on what your instincts tell you ↔ Resort to our inner wisdom预判「依靠直觉」与 Resort to our inner wisdom（求助内在智慧）通过 P5 给出的等价关系完全对应，正确项锁定。
D) 与原文相反原文 Absence of definitive criteria 指出此场合「没有明确标准」，Apply definitive criteria 反让你「应用明确标准」，与原文完全对立。
questions.quote: The only feasible option is to rely on what your instincts tell you.

options.text: Make a rational and systematic analysis.
Explore the most feasible options.
Resort to our inner wisdom.
Apply definitive criteria.

questions.prompt: What does it take for decisions to become the best according to the author?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
根据作者的观点,决策要成为最佳决策需要什么?
A) 结合运用直觉和数据。
B) 在做出选择时评估所有因素。
C) 回忆过去实际奏效的做法。
D) 避免随意相信直觉。
**判型** What does it take for decisions to become the best according to the author? 问的是「让决策成为最佳」的所需条件，是原文有明确句子可对应的细节，并非要从全文归纳的主旨。
**拆句** 题干 What does it take for decisions to become the best according to the author? 句型为「it takes sth for sb/sth to do sth」，what 替换 sth 提前；for decisions 是 take的逻辑主语；to become the best 是真正的目的不定式。看懂这个句型是关键，否则容易把题干误读成主旨题。
**定位** 把直觉与理性分析结合起来，能产出周全的决策。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确Combining instinctive and rational analysis↔Applying instincts and data in conjunction using data and instincts in conjunction to arrive at the best possible decisions↔Applying instincts and data in conjunction预判「直觉＋理性分析联用」与 Applying instincts and data in conjunction 完全对应，且 P4 与 P7 双句佐证，正确项锁定。
B) 无中生有原文从未要求「评估所有因素」，Assessing all factors when making a choice 是无来源的扩张表述。
C) 以偏概全Instinctive decisions are always backed by previous experiences 只是说直觉以经验为后盾，并不等于「让决策变最佳」的充分条件，Recalling what has actually worked in the past 把直觉一侧的支撑当成全部条件。
D) 以偏概全you want to blindly trust your instincts 提到「不要盲目相信直觉」，但这只是「最佳决策」的一个否定性前提，不是充分条件，Refraining from trusting instincts arbitrarily 把单一前提当成全部条件。
questions.quote: Combining instinctive and rational analysis produces well-rounded decisions.

options.text: Applying instincts and data in conjunction.
Assessing all factors when making a choice.
Recalling what has actually worked in the past.
Refraining from trusting instincts arbitrarily.

title: In the history of horse racing, few horses…

sentences.text: In the history of horse racing, few horses have captured the affection of the British public like Red Rum.
Today, three decades after his retirement, he is still one of the best-known and most beloved racehorses of all time.

passage.translation: 在赛马史上,很少有马能像Red Rum那样赢得英国公众的喜爱。如今,在它退役三十年后,它仍然是有史以来最知名、最受喜爱的赛马之一。

sentences.text: Red Rum was passed around to several owners before being purchased for Noel Le Mar.
The agent who made the purchase was the now-legendary horse trainer Donald "Ginger" McCain.

passage.translation: Red Rum在被Noel Le Mar购买之前曾被转手给几位马主。促成这次购买的经纪人是现已成为传奇的驯马师Donald "Ginger" McCain。

sentences.text: It wasn't apparent at the time, but Red Rum had a serious bone disease in his foot.
For many horses (and many trainers) this would mean the end of a racing career before it even began.
For Ginger and Red Rum, though, it was just an obstacle to greatness that had to be overcome.

passage.translation: 当时并不明显,但Red Rum的蹄部患有严重的骨病。对于许多马(以及许多驯马师)来说,这意味着赛马生涯甚至在开始之前就结束了。但对于Ginger和Red Rum来说,这只是通往伟大道路上必须克服的障碍。

sentences.text: Red Rum's true talent came out in steeplechases(障碍赛⻢).
His power, speed and jumping ability carried him to his first Grand National title in 1973.
The very next year, Red Rum returned to take his second title.
He was the first horse to take successive firsts since Reynoldstown in 1935-1936.
Red Rum's spirit and grace had already begun to charm the leagues of Grand National fans.

passage.translation: Red Rum的真正天赋在障碍赛马中显现出来。它的力量、速度和跳跃能力使它在1973年赢得了首个英国障碍赛马大赛冠军。第二年,Red Rum再次夺冠。它是自1935-1936年的Reynoldstown以来第一匹连续夺冠的马。Red Rum的精神和优雅已经开始征服众多英国障碍赛马大赛的粉丝。

sentences.text: In the following two years, Red Rum lost out on the title, coming in second both times.
When he returned in 1977 to try again, he was largely regarded as past his prime.
He was 12 years old and not expected to place highly.
He surprised sporting fans around the world when he came in a remarkable 25 lengths ahead of the nearest horse, taking his third Grand National win.
To this day, Red Rum's third win is known as one of the greatest moments in horse racing history.

title: When people set out to improve their health,…

sentences.text: When people set out to improve their health, they usually take a familiar path: starting a healthy diet, getting better sleep, and doing regular exercise.

Each of these behaviors is important, of course, but they all (26)____ on physical health—and a growing body of research suggests that social health is just as, if not more, important to (27)____ well-being.

passage.translation: 当人们开始改善健康状况时,他们通常会采取一条熟悉的路径:开始健康饮食、获得更好的睡眠以及进行规律的锻炼。当然,这些行为中的每一种都很重要,但它们都集中在身体健康上——而越来越多的研究表明,社交健康同样重要,甚至对整体幸福感更为重要。

sentences.text: One recent study published in the journal PLOS ONE, for example, found that the strength of a person's social circle was a better (28)____ of self-reported stress, happiness and well-being levels than fitness tracker data on physical activity, heart rate and sleep.
That finding suggests that the " (29)____self" represented by endless amounts of health data doesn't tell the whole (30)____ .

passage.translation: 例如,最近发表在PLOS ONE期刊上的一项研究发现,一个人社交圈的强度比健身追踪器上关于身体活动、心率和睡眠的数据更能预示自我报告的压力、幸福感和健康水平。这一发现表明,由无穷无尽的健康数据所代表的"量化自我"并不能说明问题的全部。

sentences.text: This idea is supported by plenty of (32)____ research.
Studies have shown that social support—whether it comes from friends, family members or a spouse—is (33)____ associated with better mental and physical health.

A rich social life, these studies suggest, can lower stress levels, improve mood, encourage positive health behaviors and discourage damaging ones, boost heart health and improve illness (34)____ rates.

passage.translation: 这一观点得到了大量先前研究的支持。研究表明,社会支持——无论是来自朋友、家庭成员还是配偶——都与更好的心理和身体健康密切相关。这些研究表明,丰富的社交生活可以降低压力水平、改善情绪、鼓励积极的健康行为并抑制有害行为、促进心脏健康并提高疾病康复率。

It's a significant problem, (35)____ since loneliness is emerging as a widespread public health problem in many countries.

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
When people set out to improve their health, they usually take a familiar path: starting a healthy diet, getting better sleep, and doing regular exercise. Each of these behaviors is important, of course, but they all {{26}} on physical health—and a growing body of research suggests that social health is just as, if not more, important to {{27}} well-being.

One recent study published in the journal PLOS ONE, for example, found that the strength of a person's social circle was a better {{28}} of self-reported stress, happiness and well-being levels than fitness tracker data on physical activity, heart rate and sleep. That finding suggests that the " {{29}}self" represented by endless amounts of health data doesn't tell the whole {{30}} .

There's also a qualified self, which is who I am, what are my activities, my social network, and all of these aspects are not {{31}} in any of these measurements.

This idea is supported by plenty of {{32}} research. Studies have shown that social support—whether it comes from friends, family members or a spouse—is {{33}} associated with better mental and physical health. A rich social life, these studies suggest, can lower stress levels, improve mood, encourage positive health behaviors and discourage damaging ones, boost heart health and improve illness {{34}} rates.

Social isolation, meanwhile, is linked to higher rates of physical diseases and mental health conditions. It's a significant problem, {{35}} since loneliness is emerging as a widespread public health problem in many countries.

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) focus 动词
**词性槽** they 后缺谓语动词，且空后紧跟介词 on
**依据** focus on 表「关注/聚焦于」，贴合「这些行为都只关注身体健康」上文列举饮食、睡眠、运动后转折说 they all __(26)__ on physical health，意思是这些做法都「聚焦于」身体健康，引出下文「但社交健康同样重要」的转折，focus on 语义最顺。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) base 搭配语义反了base on 是「把……建立在……之上」，需要「A base B on C」的及物结构（如 base a theory on facts），这里 they all base on 缺宾语、语义也不通，说「这些行为都把自己建立在身体健康上」不合逻辑。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) overall 形容词
**词性槽** 空处在介词 to 后、名词 well-being 前，作定语，要形容词
**依据** overall well-being「整体健康/总体幸福」搭配自然且切题social health is just as, if not more, important to __(27)__ well-being 强调社交健康对「总体」的健康/幸福很重要，overall well-being 正是与前文 physical health（局部）相对的「整体福祉」。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) prior 语义不搭prior「先前的」修饰 well-being 说「先前的幸福」既不通顺也不切题，prior 应留给 32 题prior research「先前的研究」。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) indicator 名词
**词性槽** 空处在 a better 后、of 前，作中心名词
**依据** a better indicator of「更好的……指标」契合「社交圈强度比体测数据更能预示压力幸福」the strength of a person's social circle was a better __(28)__ of self-reported stress, happiness and well-being levels than fitness tracker data，比较社交圈与体测数据谁更能「预示/反映」压力幸福，an indicator of 正是「……的指标」。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
J) puzzle 语义不通a better puzzle of「更好的……谜题」讲不通，本句要的是「衡量/预示」的标志物 indicator，而非 puzzle。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) quantified 形容词
**词性槽** 空处在冠词 the 与名词 self 之间（带引号），作定语，要形容词
**依据** quantified self「量化自我」呼应「海量健康数据」，并与下段 qualified self 形成对照the "__(29)__ self" represented by endless amounts of health data 指「被海量数据量化出来的自我」，即 quantified self；下一段 There's also a qualified self 正与它对照，可反推此处为 quantified。

**答案** N) story 名词
**词性槽** 形容词 whole 后、动词 tell 的宾语位置，需要名词
**依据** the whole story 是固定说法，意为「全部真相/全貌」the "quantified self" represented by endless amounts of health data doesn't tell the whole __(30)__ 说海量健康数据「说不出全貌」，tell the whole story 正是「道出全部真相」的固定表达。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) indicator 搭配不成立没有 tell the whole indicator「说出全部指标」这种说法，indicator 留给 28 题的 a better ___of 更合适。
J) puzzle 义近表象但搭配不对puzzle 是「谜题」，tell the whole puzzle 不成搭配；表「全貌」的固定宾语是 story 而非 puzzle。
L) recovery 语义不沾边recovery「康复」与「数据说不出全貌」毫无关系，且它是 34 题 illness ___ rates 的答案。

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) reflected 动词
**词性槽** 空处在 are not 后、介词 in 前，作系表/被动的核心，是动词（过去分词）
**依据** are not reflected in「未被反映在……中」契合「这些方面没体现在测量数据里」my social network, and all of these aspects are not __(31)__ in any of these measurements，说「我的社交网络等方面都没被这些测量反映出来」，be reflected in 正是「反映/体现在……中」的固定被动搭配。

**答案** H) prior 形容词
**词性槽** 空处在 plenty of 与名词 research 之间，作定语，要形容词
**依据** prior research「先前/已有的研究」契合「这一想法得到大量已有研究支持」This idea is supported by plenty of __(32)__ research，本段承接前文观点并用研究背书，prior research（已有研究）语义最顺。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
K) quantified 语义被占且不切此处quantified「被量化的」修饰 self（量化自我）成立，但 quantified research 不是常见说法、也偏离此处「已有研究」之意；它是 29 题答案。
M) reflected语义不通reflected research「被反映的研究」讲不通，reflected 应留给 31 题 are not reflected in。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 K) —— quantified 词性也对、又是本篇出现过的词，易误填。32空 plenty of __(32)__ research 要形容词，quantified 正好是形容词、又在 29 题刚见过「量化」概念，考生易顺手填它；但 quantified research 不是常见搭配、也偏离「已有研究」之意，正确的是 prior research——防坑点是别被刚出现的词带跑，回到 research 的常见修饰词。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) strongly 副词
**词性槽** 空处在 is 与过去分词 associated 之间，修饰形容词性成分，要副词
**依据** strongly associated「密切相关」是固定搭配is __(33)__ associated with better mental and physical health 要表达「社会支持与更好的身心健康密切相关」，strongly associated with 是论文里描述相关性的标准说法。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) eagerly 感情色彩不搭eagerly「急切地」修饰的是人主动的意愿（eagerly waiting），不能修饰 associated「被关联」这种客观关系。
C) especially语义指向错especially「尤其」用于举例强调，不表示关联的「强度」，且它是 35 题 especially since 的答案，应留给那处。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) recovery 名词
**词性槽** 空处在名词 illness 与名词 rates 之间，构成复合名词修饰语，要名词
**依据** illness recovery rates「疾病康复率」契合「丰富社交能改善健康结果」boost heart health and improve illness __(34)__ rates 与前面 lower stress、improve mood、boost heart health 并列，都是积极结果，improve illness recovery rates「提高疾病康复率」语义最顺。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) indicator 搭配不成立illness indicator rates 不是常见说法，且 improve indicator rates 语义空洞；indicator 应留给 28 题 a better ___ of。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 E) —— indicator 名词性也对，易抢填到 34。34 空 illness ___rates 要名词，indicator 是名词易被代入，但 illness indicator rates 不成搭配、且会害得28 题 a better ___ of 没词可用；正确是 recovery，防坑点是看清并列里要的是「正向结果」的康复率，并为 28 题留出 indicator。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) especially 副词
**词性槽** 空处在逗号后、引导 since 从句前，作状语，要副词
**依据** especially since「尤其是因为」引出强化原因It's a significant problem, __(35)__ since loneliness is emerging as a widespread public health problem，especially since 是常见连用，表「这问题很严重，尤其因为孤独正成为普遍的公共健康问题」。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) eagerly 语义与位置都不通eagerly「急切地」表人的态度，放在 since 从句前既无 eagerly since 的说法，也说不通「急切地因为」，逻辑不成立。

title: A multitasker is one who can perform two…

sentences.text: A multitasker is one who can perform two or more tasks effectively at the same time, which—apart from the obvious differences—is similar to what a computer does.
The concept does indeed come from the realms of technology, where it is used to refer to an operating system that can execute multiple tasks at the same time.
However, the question is: can a person really be a multitasker?

passage.translation: 多任务处理者是指能够同时有效完成两项或更多任务的人，这与计算机所做的事情相似，只是存在明显的差异。这个概念确实来自技术领域，用于指代能够同时执行多项任务的操作系统。然而,问题是:一个人真的能成为多任务处理者吗?

sentences.text: For most scientists, the answer is no.
So much so that, according to experts in neuroscience(神经系统科学), our brains do not handle multitasking situations well.
As soon as two tasks require our attention, productivity suffers.
What we call multitasking, therefore, is in reality the ability to move more or less quickly from one task to another.
This requires two essential conditions: that one of the tasks needs to be automatic, like walking or eating, and that they both need different mental processes.
Answering the phone and writing at the same time, for example.

passage.translation: 对于大多数科学家来说,答案是否定的。以至于根据神经系统科学专家的说法,我们的大脑无法很好地处理多任务情况。一旦两项任务需要我们的注意力,生产力就会下降。因此,我们所说的多任务处理,实际上是或多或少快速地从一项任务转换到另一项任务的能力。这需要两个基本条件:其中一项任务需要是自动的,比如走路或吃饭,并且两项任务都需要不同的心理过程。例如,同时接电话和写作。

sentences.text: However, on the other side of the coin there are people who maintain that it is possible to be, or at least seem to be, multitasking.

A recent study concluded that regardless of whether people are actually handling several tasks or not, the mere fact that they perceive this activity as multitasking has a positive effect on their performance.

passage.translation: 然而,从另一个角度来看,有些人坚持认为成为或至少看起来像是多任务处理者是可能的。最近的一项研究得出结论,无论人们是否真正在处理多项任务,仅仅是他们将这种活动视为多任务处理这一事实,就对他们的表现产生了积极影响。

sentences.text: The business perspective offers a different view: multitasking is understood as the ability to adapt to all types of environment within a company and effectively undertake different activities within a set time frame.
Indeed, many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking to improve their productivity.

From this different perspective, you can not only be multitasking but this ability can also be taught: something that is easier in fluid organisations, which favour flexibility in their working practices.

passage.translation: 商业视角提供了不同的观点:多任务处理被理解为适应公司内所有类型环境并在规定时间框架内有效承担不同活动的能力。事实上,许多公司寻找擅长多任务处理的人来提高生产力。从这个不同的角度来看,你不仅可以进行多任务处理,而且这种能力也可以被传授:这在灵活的组织中更容易实现,这些组织在工作实践中倾向于灵活性。

sentences.text: The benefits of multitasking are clear.
Being quicker and more efficient increases our performance and the number of tasks completed.
But having to pay attention to several things at once means that the powers of concentration are reduced and that can lead to more mistakes.

passage.translation: 多任务处理的好处是显而易见的。更快更高效地工作可以提高我们的表现和完成的任务数量。但是必须同时注意几件事意味着注意力会降低,这可能导致更多错误。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does a "multitasker" originally refer to?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （词义句意题）
**题目译文**
"多任务处理者"最初指的是什么?
A) 一种能够同时执行多项任务的操作系统。
B) 一名同时执行多项任务的熟练工人。
C) 一种能同时有效完成多项任务的复杂技术。
D) 一个能够同时执行多项任务的高效率的人。
**判型** 题干 What does a "multitasker" originally refer to 直接问一个词「原本指什么」，考的是文中对该词来源含义的界定。
**拆句** 句子主干是 What does a "multitasker" originally refer to，结构平铺，refer to 意为「指代、指的是」，originally 作状语修饰 refer to，意为「最初指的是」。无陷阱。
**定位** 这个概念确实来自科技领域，在那里它被用来指一种能够同时执行多项任务的操作系统。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确an operating system that can execute multiple tasks at the same time ↔An operating system capable of doing several tasks at once预判要的「能同时多任务的操作系统」与 An operating system capable of doing several tasks at once 完全吻合，主体、能力、同时性三点都对上。
B) 偷换概念A skilled worker（熟练工人）把主体说成人，而原词最初指的是操作系统，主体张冠李戴。
C) 偷换概念A sophisticated technology（一种复杂技术）只取了原文「来自科技领域」的背景，却没说成「操作系统」，主体被放大成笼统的「技术」，与原文具体所指不符。
D) 答非所问An efficient person（高效的人）把主体说成人，对应的是首句对 multitasker 的「现今」描述，而非题干要的「最初」所指，时间与主体都错。
questions.quote: The concept does indeed come from the realms of technology, where it is used to refer to an operating system that can execute multiple tasks at the same time.

options.text: An operating system capable of doing several tasks at once.
A skilled worker executing more than one task at the same time.
A sophisticated technology doing several tasks effectively at once.
An efficient person able to perform multiple tasks at the same time.

questions.prompt: Why can't people really be multitaskers according to neuroscientists?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
根据神经科学家的观点,为什么人们实际上无法成为多任务处理者?
A) 他们没有充分接触多任务处理的情境。
B) 他们无法与机械操作系统相比。
C) 他们的大脑不允许他们进行多任务处理。
D) 他们的注意力持续时间无法延长。
**判型** 题干 Why can't people really be multitaskers according to neuroscientists 问的是某方观点下的具体理由，答案能在原文直接找到对应句。
**拆句** Why can't people really be multitaskers according to neuroscientists：主干是 why ... can't people be multitaskers（人为什么不能成为多任务者），really 加强语气，according to neuroscientists 是状语，限定「按神经科学家的看法」。really 易让人误读为「真的能吗」，其实它服务于全句的否定，意为「人确实当不了」。
**定位** 以至于，按照神经科学专家的说法，我们的大脑并不能很好地处理多任务情境。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有not sufficiently exposed to multitasking situations（接触多任务情境不够）文中从未提及，原文讲的是大脑机能，不是接触多少。
B) 答非所问not comparable to mechanical operating systems（无法与机械操作系统相比）只是首段把人和电脑作类比的延伸，并非神经科学家给出的不能多任务的理由。
C) ✓ 正确our brains do not handle multitasking situations well ↔Their brains do not allow them to multitask预判的「大脑处理不好」与 Their brains do not allow them to multitask 一致，把原因归于大脑这一生理层面，正合定位句。
D) 无中生有attention span cannot be expanded（注意力广度无法扩展）文中并无此说，原文只说两项任务争夺注意力时效率下降，没谈注意力能否扩展。
questions.quote: So much so that, according to experts in neuroscience(神经系统科学), our brains do not handle multitasking situations well.

options.text: They are not sufficiently exposed to multitasking situations.
They are not comparable to mechanical operating systems.
Their brains do not allow them to multitask.
Their attention span cannot be expanded.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the conclusion of a recent study on multitasking?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
从最近一项关于多任务处理的研究结论中我们了解到什么?
A) 人们通过保持他们正在做的事情是多任务处理这一认知而取得更大成就。
B) 人们对他们正在做的事情作为多任务处理的感知使其表现受益。
C) 人们活跃的心理过程对他们的多任务处理产生积极影响。
D) 人们可以通过处理多任务处理情境来提高他们的能力。
**判型** 题干 What do we learn from the conclusion of a recent study 问一项具体研究的结论，原文有对应明示句，属可直接定位的细节。
**拆句** What do we learn from the conclusion of a recent study on multitasking：主干 what do we learn（我们了解到什么），from the conclusion of a recent study 是状语，on multitasking 修饰 study，指「一项关于多任务的近期研究的结论」。结构平铺，无陷阱。
**定位** 一项近期研究得出结论：无论人们是否真的在处理多项任务，仅仅是他们把这一活动感知为多任务这个事实，就对他们的表现有正面影响。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念maintaining whatever they are doing is multitasking 用 maintaining（坚持主张/坚持做）替换原文的 perceive（感知），「坚称是多任务」不等于「感知为多任务」，把主观认知偷换成口头主张。
B) ✓ 正确they perceive this activity as multitasking↔the perception of what they are doing as multitasking has a positive effect on their performance ↔ performance benefits from预判的「感知为多任务即提升表现」与 People's performance benefits from the perception of what they are doing as multitasking 完全对应，落点都在「感知」这一主观因素。
C) 张冠李戴active mental processes（积极的心理过程）借的是第二段讲切换需要不同 mental processes 的内容，与本研究结论的「感知」无关。
D) 与原文相反improve their capabilities by handling multitasking situations 说「靠处理多任务来提升能力」，而原文强调的恰是「无论是否真在处理多任务」，重点在感知而非实际处理，方向相反。
questions.quote: A recent study concluded that regardless of whether people are actually handling several tasks or not, the mere fact that they perceive this activity as multitasking has a positive effect on their performance.

options.text: People make greater achievements by maintaining whatever they are doing is multitasking.
People's performance benefits from the perception of what they are doing as multitasking.
People's active mental processes exert a positive effect on their multitasking.
People can improve their capabilities by handling multitasking situations.

questions.prompt: How does the business world view multitasking?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
商业界如何看待多任务处理?
A) 它是一种在灵活组织中常见的稀有技能。
B) 它是所有员工都需要具备的适应性能力。
C) 它是许多员工缺乏的一种基本素质。
D) 它是一种可以培养的理想能力。
**判型** 题干 How does the business world view multitasking 问商业界如何看待多任务，原文有专段陈述该立场，属可定位细节。
**拆句** How does the business world view multitasking：view 在此是动词「看待」，主干为the business world view multitasking（商业界如何看待多任务）。需注意 view 此处不是名词「景观」而是动词，属熟词的常见用法。
**定位** 从这一不同视角看，你不仅可以做到多任务，而且这种能力还可以被传授：这在灵活的组织里更容易做到，这类组织在工作方式上崇尚灵活性。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反a rare skill（罕见技能）与原文 many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking 矛盾——能被许多公司寻得且可传授，说明并不罕见。
B) 以偏概全required of all workers（对所有员工的要求）把范围夸大成「全体员工」，原文只说many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking，是企业青睐某些人，而非要求所有人都具备。
C) 无中生有many employees lack（许多员工缺乏）文中并无此说，原文谈的是公司想要、能力可教，没有说员工普遍缺乏这种能力。
D) ✓ 正确many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking ↔ a desirable ability this ability can also be taught ↔ that can be developed预判的「可培养的实用能力」与 a desirable ability that can be developed 两点全中：desirable 对应被公司追求，can be developed 对应可教。
questions.quote: From this different perspective, you can not only be multitasking but this ability can also be taught: something that is easier in fluid organisations, which favour flexibility in their working practices.

options.text: It is a rare skill often found in fluid organisations.
It is an adaptable capability required of all workers.
It is an essential quality many employees lack.
It is a desirable ability that can be developed.

questions.prompt: What does the author imply we should do if we have to focus on some task and do it well?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （推断题）
**题目译文**
如果我们必须专注于某项任务并把它做好,作者暗示我们应该做什么?
A) 以灵活的方式工作。
B) 从错误中学习。
C) 避免多任务处理。
D) 提高效率。
**判型** 题干 What does the author imply we should do 用 imply 问作者「暗示」我们该怎么做，答案需基于原文推理而非直接摘录。
**拆句** What does the author imply we should do if we have to focus on some task and do it well：主干 what does the author imply we should do（作者暗示我们该做什么），if引导条件状语从句 if we have to focus on some task and do it well（如果我们必须专注某项任务并把它做好）。从句是答案成立的前提，须连同主句一起理解。
**定位** 但不得不同时关注好几件事，意味着专注力会下降，而这会导致更多错误。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴Work in a flexible way（以灵活方式工作）取自第四段商业视角的 favour flexibility in their working practices，与末段「要专注做好该怎么办」无关。
B) 无中生有Learn from mistakes（从错误中学习）只是借了末段 mistakes 一词，原文说的是多任务会「导致」更多错误，从未建议「从错误中学习」。
C) ✓ 正确having to pay attention to several things at once means that the powers of concentration are reduced↔ Avoid multitasking预判的「别同时做多件事」与 Avoid multitasking 一致——既然多任务降低专注、引发错误，那要做好就该避免它。
D) 答非所问Increase efficiency（提高效率）对应原文 Being quicker and more efficient，但那是多任务的「好处」一面，并非「要专注做好」的对策；况且追求效率与多任务相伴，恰是降低专注的根源。
questions.quote: But having to pay attention to several things at once means that the powers of concentration are reduced and that can lead to more mistakes.

options.text: Work in a flexible way.
Learn from mistakes.
Avoid multitasking.
Increase efficiency

title: Having a rival can keep you committed to…

sentences.text: Having a rival can keep you committed to achieving your goals and enhance your overall performance.
But before you go out and find an entrepreneur to outcompete, it's important to understand and avoid the traps that often come with rivalry.
After all, competitive rivalry can also hinder effective decision-making and increase your willingness to take risks, behaviors that can ultimately hurt your venture's success.

passage.translation: 拥有一个竞争对手可以让你保持对实现目标的投入,并提升你的整体表现。但在你出去寻找一个要超越的企业家之前,重要的是要理解并避免竞争关系常常带来的陷阱。毕竟,竞争性对抗也可能妨碍有效决策,并增加你承担风险的意愿,这些行为最终可能损害你企业的成功。

sentences.text: Finding someone you're committed to outcompeting can be a great way to stay focused on your goals and push your venture to the next level.
But when you're intently focused on outperforming your rivals, you may begin to develop a "win-at-all-costs" mentality that causes you to ignore how you achieve success.
One group of researchers, for example, examined the link between rivalry and unethical behavior.
They found that when people compete against their rivals, they are more willing to behave unethically to win.
But such behavior may stain your reputation and strain relationships important to your success.
One way to avoid this trap is to stop and reflect on what's important.
While outperforming your rivals may provide short-term benefits, the loss of your integrity will have long-term consequences.

passage.translation: 找到一个你致力于超越的人可以是保持专注于目标并将你的企业推向新高度的好方法。但当你专注于超越竞争对手时,你可能开始形成一种"不惜一切代价取胜"的心态,导致你忽视如何获得成功。例如,一组研究人员考察了竞争关系与不道德行为之间的联系。他们发现,当人们与竞争对手竞争时,他们更愿意采取不道德行为来获胜。但这种行为可能玷污你的声誉,并使对你成功至关重要的关系变得紧张。避免这一陷阱的一种方法是停下来反思什么是重要的。虽然超越竞争对手可能带来短期利益,但丧失诚信将产生长期后果。

sentences.text: One reason having a rival can enhance your venture's performance is that it creates a level of excitement that drives you to work harder.
But this eagerness to win may also hurt your venture's success, particularly when it causes you to make impulsive, insensible decisions.

But it's possible to avoid such costly mistakes by making a habit of engaging in critical thinking, such as considering opposing viewpoints and conducting cost-benefit analyses, especially for those decisions that are complex and can determine the future of your venture.

passage.translation: 拥有竞争对手能够提升你企业表现的一个原因是,它创造了一种兴奋感,驱使你更加努力工作。但这种求胜的渴望也可能损害你企业的成功,特别是当它导致你做出冲动、不明智的决策时。但通过养成批判性思维的习惯,可以避免这种代价高昂的错误,比如考虑对立观点和进行成本效益分析,尤其是对那些复杂且能够决定你企业未来的决策。

sentences.text: The sense of eagerness that comes with having a rival can not only cause you to make poorer decisions, but it can also lead you to take greater risks that put your venture in peril.

One way you can overcome the risk-inducing effects of rivalry that stand to endanger your venture's success is to remain attentive to your emotional state and actively monitor how such feelings are affecting your decision- making.

passage.translation: 拥有竞争对手带来的渴望感不仅会导致你做出更糟糕的决策,还可能使你承担更大的风险,从而危及你的企业。你可以克服竞争关系引发的风险效应以保护企业成功的一种方法是,保持对自己情绪状态的关注,并积极监控这些情绪如何影响你的决策。

questions.prompt: How can competitive rivalry benefit entrepreneurs according to the passage?

questions.tip:

questions.prompt: What is one of the traps entrepreneurs may often fall into when competing with rivals?

questions.tip:

**拆句** What are entrepreneurs advised to do to avoid traps that often accompany rivalry：被动结构 are advised to do（被建议做某事），to avoid… 是目的状语，that often accompany rivalry 是定语从句修饰 traps，accompany 意为"伴随"。

questions.tip:

questions.prompt: How can entrepreneurs avoid making impulsive and insensible decisions?

创业者如何避免做出冲动和不明智的决策?

**拆句** How can entrepreneurs avoid making impulsive and insensible decisions：avoid 后接动名词 making（avoid doing 固定用法），impulsive"冲动的"、insensible"不明智的"两个形容词并列修饰 decisions。结构清晰，无陷阱。

**选项**

questions.quote: But it's possible to avoid such costly mistakes by making a habit of engaging in critical thinking, such as considering opposing viewpoints and conducting cost-benefit analyses, especially for those decisions that are complex and can determine the future of your venture.

title: A number of studies have looked at how…

sentences.text: A number of studies have looked at how family life can affect productivity and satisfaction in the workplace.
However, there has been (26)____ little research on the influence of leisure activities.
So Ciara Kelly and colleagues recruited 129 hobbyists to look at how the time spent on their hobbies(27)____ their work life.

passage.translation: 许多研究探讨了家庭生活如何影响工作场所的生产力和满意度。然而，关于休闲活动影响的研究却少得令人惊讶。因此，Ciara Kelly及其同事招募了129名爱好者，以研究他们在爱好上花费的时间如何塑造他们的工作生活。

sentences.text: The researchers found that when participants spent longer than (28)____ on their leisure activity, their belief in their ability to perform their job was strengthened.
But this was only the (29)____ when they had a serious hobby that was dissimilar to their job, or when their hobby was similar to their work but they only did it (30)____ .
When their hobby was both serious and similar to their job, then spending more time on it actually decreased their work (31)____ .

passage.translation: 研究人员发现，当参与者在休闲活动上花费的时间比平常更长时，他们对自己履行工作能力的信念得到了增强。但这种情况仅发生在他们拥有与工作不同的严肃爱好时，或者当他们的爱好与工作相似但只是随意为之时。当他们的爱好既严肃又与工作相似时，在其上花费更多时间实际上会降低他们的工作效率。

sentences.text: Why might that be?

To maintain a serious hobby, people need to invest significant psychological resources, say the authors—so if the activity has the same kinds of demands as their work, they may be left (32)____ and unable to perform well at their job.
But if their hobby is quite different from their career, it may not (33)____ in the same way but instead help them develop other knowledge and skills that can (34)____ their confidence at work.
"Consider a scientist who is a keen rock climber," says Kelly.
"Since climbing is so far (35)____ from their day-to-day work activities, they can still recover from the demands of their job with plenty of resources."

passage.translation: 这是为什么呢？作者指出，为了维持一个严肃的爱好，人们需要投入大量的心理资源——因此，如果该活动与他们的工作有相同类型的要求，他们可能会感到精疲力竭，无法在工作中表现良好。但如果他们的爱好与职业截然不同，它可能不会以同样的方式产生干扰，反而帮助他们发展其他知识和技能，从而增强他们在工作中的信心。Kelly说："想象一位热衷于攀岩的科学家。由于攀岩与他们的日常工作活动相去甚远，他们仍然可以从工作需求中恢复过来，并保有充足的资源。"

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
A number of studies have looked at how family life can affect productivity and satisfaction in the workplace. However, there has been {{26}} little research on the influence of leisure activities. So Ciara Kelly and colleagues recruited 129 hobbyists to look at how the time spent on their hobbies{{27}} their work life.

The researchers found that when participants spent longer than {{28}} on their leisure activity, their belief in their ability to perform their job was strengthened. But this was only the {{29}} when they had a serious hobby that was dissimilar to their job, or when their hobby was similar to their work but they only did it {{30}} . When their hobby was both serious and similar to their job, then spending more time on it actually decreased their work {{31}} .

Why might that be? To maintain a serious hobby, people need to invest significant psychological resources, say the authors—so if the activity has the same kinds of demands as their work, they may be left {{32}} and unable to perform well at their job. But if their hobby is quite different from their career, it may not {{33}} in the same way but instead help them develop other knowledge and skills that can {{34}} their confidence at work. "Consider a scientist who is a keen rock climber," says Kelly. "Since climbing is so far {{35}} from their day-to-day work activities, they can still recover from the demands of their job with plenty of resources."
