**改写** Job satisfaction ↔ how you feel about your work名词 ↔ how 从句has a lot to do with company culture ↔Company culture can have a big impact on how you feel about your work have a lot to do with = have a big impact on
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B I simply didn't get along with the company culture 是个案陈述（"我"和这家公司文化合不来），没有把"文化 ↔ 满意度"提升到普遍道理，所以承担陈述的是把规律点透的 C 段，而不是 B 段。They favored a more rigid, closed-door, corporate atmosphere, while I would have preferred something more collaborative and open N you're still trying to determine whether or not the company is a good fit for you 强调的是"判断是否合适"，并未涉及"对工作的感受/满意度"这一陈述。you should also look at the process through a similar lens
questions.quote: Company culture can have a big impact on how you feel about your work, so you want to make sure you sign an offer letter with an organization you're truly excited about.

questions.prompt: A chat with an insider of a company can give job applicants very useful information when they prepare for an interview.
questions.explanation:
**答案** J 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
与公司内部人员的交谈可以在求职者准备面试时为他们提供非常有用的信息。
**锚点** 与公司内部人员聊有助于面试准备
**定位** 在 LinkedIn 上或通过邮件给这家公司的现任或前任员工发一条短消息，问他们是否愿意和你简短聊聊关于这家公司的事情。如果对方答应了你的聊天请求，你就会带着相当强大、相当有用的信息走进面试现场！
**改写** A chat with an insider of a company ↔Send a quick message to a current or previous company employee on LinkedIn or by email and ask if they would be willing to have a quick conversation with you insider ↔ current or previous company employee；chat ↔ quick conversation can give job applicants very useful information when they prepare for an interview ↔you'll be armed with some pretty powerful and helpful information heading into your interview very useful ↔ pretty powerful and helpful；prepare for ↔ heading into
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
K that part at the end of a job interview when the hiring manager asks if you have any questions 已经在"面试当中"了，与 prepare for an interview 的"面试前"时间节点不一致。That's the perfect opportunity to speak up and get your burning company culture questions answered!
questions.quote: Send a quick message to a current or previous company employee on LinkedIn or by email and ask if they would be willing to have a quick conversation with you about the organization in general. If you get a yes to your request for a chat, you'll be armed with some pretty powerful and helpful information heading into your interview!

title: In the coming era of budget cuts to…

sentences.text: In the coming era of budget cuts to education, distance learning could become the norm.

passage.translation: 在即将到来的教育预算削减时代,远程教学可能会成为常态。

sentences.text: The temptation for those in charge of education budgets to trade teachers for technology could be so strong that they ignore the disadvantages of distance learning.
School facilities are expensive to build and maintain, and teachers are expensive to employ.

Online classes do not require buildings and each class can host hundreds of people simultaneously, resulting in greater savings, thus increasing the temptation of distance education for those concerned more about budgets than learning.
But moving away from a traditional classroom in which a living, breathing human being teaches and interacts with students daily would be a disaster.
Physically attending school has hidden benefits: getting up every morning, interacting with peers, and building relationships with teachers are essential skills to cultivate in young people.
Moreover, schools should be more than simple institutions of traditional learning.
They are now places that provide meals.
They are places where students receive counseling and other support.

passage.translation: 对于那些负责教育预算的人来说,用技术取代教师的诱惑可能会如此强烈,以至于他们忽视了远程学习的弊端。学校设施的建设和维护成本高昂,而雇用教师也很昂贵。在线课程不需要建筑物,每个班级可以同时容纳数百人,从而节省更多开支,这增加了那些更关心预算而非学习的人对远程教育的诱惑。但是,抛弃传统课堂——在那里有一个活生生的人每天教学并与学生互动——将是一场灾难。实际到校上学有着隐藏的益处:每天早上起床、与同龄人互动以及与教师建立关系,这些都是年轻人需要培养的基本技能。此外,学校应该不仅仅是传统学习的简单机构。它们现在是提供餐食的地方,是学生接受咨询和其他支持的地方。

sentences.text: Those policy-makers are often fascinated by the latest technology in education and its potential to "transform" education overnight.
But online education does not allow a teacher to keep a struggling student after class and offer help.
Educational videos may deliver academic content, but they are unable to make eye contact or assess a student's level of engagement.
Distance education will never match the personal teaching in a traditional classroom.
In their first 18 years of life, American children spend only 9% of their time in school.

Yet teachers are expected to prepare them to be responsible citizens, cultivate their social skills, encourage successful time management, and enhance their capacity to flourish in an increasingly harsh labor market.
Given these expectations, schools should not become permanently "remote".

passage.translation: 这些政策制定者往往痴迷于教育领域的最新技术及其一夜之间"改变"教育的潜力。但在线教育无法让教师在课后留住一个有困难的学生并提供帮助。教育视频可能传递学术内容,但它们无法进行眼神交流或评估学生的参与程度。远程教育永远无法匹敌传统课堂中的个人化教学。在生命的前18年里,美国儿童只有9%的时间在学校度过。然而,教师却被期望让他们做好成为负责任公民的准备,培养他们的社交技能,鼓励成功的时间管理,并增强他们在日益严酷的劳动力市场中蓬勃发展的能力。鉴于这些期望,学校不应该永久地变成"远程"的。

sentences.text: The power of the classroom is rooted in the humanity of the people gathered in the same place, at the same time.
Personal teaching is about teachers showing students a higher path, and about young people going through the process together.
Technology, no matter how advanced, should simply be a tool of a good teacher.

passage.translation: 课堂的力量植根于在同一地点、同一时间聚集在一起的人们的人性。个人化教学是关于教师向学生展示一条更高的道路,也是关于年轻人共同经历这一过程。技术无论多么先进,都应该只是一位好教师的工具。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What mainly accounts for the possibility that distance learning could become the norm?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
远程学习有可能成为常态,这主要是什么原因造成的?
A) 教育技术的进步。
B) 财政资源缩减。
C) 学校设施短缺。
D) 缺乏合格的教师。
**判型** What mainly accounts for the possibility that distance learning could become the norm?问「是什么导致」，是对文本中明确陈述事实的提取，不是态度也不是推断。
**拆句** 题干主干是What mainly accounts for the possibility，that引导同位语从句解释possibility的内容；that distance learning could become the norm整体作possibility的同位语；副词mainly限定account for，提示要找「主要」原因而非次要原因。结构清晰、无陷阱。
**定位** 在即将到来的教育预算削减时代，远程教育可能成为常态。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有原文未提及教育技术本身的进步是导致远程教育常态化的原因；P1只字未提技术进步，只谈预算。
B) ✓ 正确budget cuts to education ↔ Shrinking financial resources预判「教育预算削减」与Shrinking financial resources「财政资源缩水」是同一概念的不同表述，是细节题最典型的同义替换。
C) 偷换概念Shortage of school facilities是「校舍短缺」，而原文School facilities are expensive to build and maintain说的是校舍「造价高、维护贵」，是「贵」不是「缺」；且这是第二段提到的，并非第一段中远程教育常态化的原因。
D) 无中生有原文从未提及「合格教师短缺」是远程教育常态化的原因；teachers are expensive to employ说的是教师「贵」，不是「缺」或「不合格」。
questions.quote: In the coming era of budget cuts to education, distance learning could become the norm.

options.text: Advances in education technology.
Shrinking financial resources.
Shortage of school facilities.
Lack of qualified teachers.

questions.prompt: What does the author say is one possible benefit of students attending school physically?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者认为学生实地到校上学可能带来的一个好处是什么?
A) 养成早起的习惯。
B) 吃营养均衡的饭菜。
C) 成长为有生命、会呼吸的人。
D) 培养与同龄人和教师的关系。
**判型** What does the author say is one possible benefit问「作者说了什么好处」，是对作者明示信息的提取。
**拆句** 题干主干是What does the author say is one possible benefit，省略了关系代词的宾语从句结构「the author say (that) [what] is one possible benefit」；介词of短语of students attending school physically作benefit的定语，其中students是动名词attending的逻辑主语。结构无陷阱，注意one possible暗示文中可能列了多个好处，选项里只要有一个对得上即可。
**定位** 实地上学有隐性的好处：每天早起、与同伴互动、与老师建立关系，这些都是年轻人需要培养的关键能力。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全Developing the habit of getting up early虽然对应原文getting up every morning，但原文这只是三项并列好处之一，且作者强调的核心是skills to cultivate，而getting up属于日常生活动作；将「早起」提炼为「养成早起的习惯」是把动作误读成了一种习惯养成训练，与原文核心语义有偏差。
B) 张冠李戴原文末尾They are now places that provide meals提到学校提供餐食，但作者并未说「营养均衡的餐食」是attending school physically的benefit；nutritionally well- balanced属于无中生有的修饰语，且provide meals被原文归入「学校的社会职能」而非「实地上学的好处」——主体不同。
C) 偷换概念原文a living, breathing human being teaches and interacts with students中living, breathing是修饰teacher的形容词，强调「活生生的」教师；选项Growing into living and breathing human beings把「形容老师的状态词」偷换成「学生成长的目标」，且growing into是「成长为」的方向性动词，原文完全没有这层意思。
D) ✓ 正确interacting with peers, and building relationships with teachers ↔Cultivating relationships with peers and teachers选项Cultivating relationships with peers and teachers精准合并了预判中的第二、三项内容，且与原文cultivate呼应。
questions.quote: Physically attending school has hidden benefits: getting up every morning, interacting with peers, and building relationships with teachers are essential skills to cultivate in young people.

options.text: Developing the habit of getting up early.
Eating nutritionally well-balanced meals.
Growing into living and breathing human beings.
Cultivating relationships with peers and teachers.

questions.prompt: What does the author think of the latest technology in education?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （态度题）
**题目译文**
作者如何看待教育领域的最新技术?
A) 它可能有潜在的弊端。
B) 它可能使许多教师失业。
C) 它可能增加学生的经济负担。
D) 它可能彻底改变课堂教学。
**判型** What does the author think of直问作者对某事物的看法，是典型态度类信号。
**拆句** 题干主干是What does the author think of the latest technology in education，think of是固定搭配「对……怎么看」；the latest是形容词最高级作定语。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 那些政策制定者常常被教育领域最新技术及其「一夜变革」教育的潜力所迷住。但在线教育不允许教师把学习吃力的学生留下来课后辅导。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确online education does not allow a teacher to keep a struggling student after class and offer help↔ It may have potential disadvantages Distance education will never match the personal teaching in a traditional classroom ↔It may have potential disadvantages预判得出作者对新技术持质疑或保留态度，It may have potential disadvantages恰好用「可能有不足」概括了这种保留立场，与原文极性一致。
B) 无中生有原文未提及新技术会「让教师失业」；作者讨论的是技术替代教师在功能上的局限，不是技术造成教师失业的社会后果。
C) 张冠李戴原文谈的是节约预算者的成本动机resulting in greater savings，从未提及学生的财务负担会因此增加；把「学校省钱」误读为「学生多花钱」，方向完全相反。
D) 与原文相反It may revolutionize classroom teaching即「可能彻底变革课堂教学」是政策制定者的看法，不是作者的；原文用"transform"加引号、用But转折、用Distance education will never match the personal teaching in a traditional classroom反驳，明确否定了这种乐观看法。考生若把fascinated误读成作者本人也「被迷住」，就会反选此项。
questions.quote: Those policy-makers are often fascinated by the latest technology in education and its potential to "transform" education overnight. But online education does not allow a teacher to keep a struggling student after class and offer help.

options.text: It may have potential disadvantages.
It may render many teachers jobless.
It may add to students' financial burden.
It may revolutionize classroom teaching

questions.prompt: What does the author say teachers are expected to do?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者说教师被期望做什么?
A) 增强学生的领导能力。
B) 提升学生到管理岗位。
C) 使学生能够适应生活中的变化。
D) 让学生为未来的竞争做好准备。
**判型** What does the author say teachers are expected to do?问「教师被期望做什么」，是对原文明示信息的客观提取。
**拆句** 题干主干是What does the author say teachers are expected to do，author say后省略了that引导的宾语从句；从句主干是「teachers are expected to do (what)」，be expected to do是固定结构「被期望做」。结构无陷阱。
**定位** 然而，教师却被期望让他们成为有责任感的公民，培养他们的社交能力，鼓励他们成功管理时间，并增强他们在日益严酷的劳动力市场上立足发展的能力。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有原文四项期望中没有提到培养「领导力」（leadership capacity）；社交能力不等于领导力，二者不可等同。
B) 偷换概念原文没有任何「把学生提升到管理岗位」的内容；该项利用原文management一词（time management）做望文生义的偷换——time management是「时间管理」，managerial positions是「管理职位」，二者只是共享management词根，语义完全不同。
C) 无中生有原文四项期望中没有「让学生适应生活变化」（adapt to the changes in life）这一项；adapt to changes是常见教育鸡汤，但原文未提及。
D) ✓ 正确enhance their capacity to flourish in an increasingly harsh labor market ↔Prepare students to be competitive in the future预判得出最后一项enhance their capacity to flourish in an increasingly harsh labor market，选项Prepare students to be competitive in the future恰是此项的抽象提炼。
questions.quote: Yet teachers are expected to prepare them to be responsible citizens, cultivate their social skills, encourage successful time management, and enhance their capacity to flourish in an increasingly harsh labor market.

options.text: Enhance students' leadership capacity.
Elevate students to managerial positions.
Enable students to adapt to the changes in life.
Prepare students to be competitive in the future.

questions.prompt: Why couldn't technology replace a good teacher?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
为什么技术不能取代一位好教师?
A) 它缺乏人性。
B) 它尚不成熟。
C) 它无法追踪学生的成长。
D) 它无法满足个人需求。
**判型** Why couldn't technology replace a good teacher?问「为什么不能」，是对原文中给出的明确原因的提取；末段P4给出了直接答案句，不需推断。
**拆句** 题干主干是Why couldn't technology replace a good teacher?，否定情态动词couldn't与why连用，表达「为何不能」，注意这不是疑问句的常规反问，而是给定「不能取代」的前提下追问原因。结构无陷阱，重点抓couldn't的否定意味。
**定位** 课堂的力量根植于聚集在同一地点、同一时间的人们身上的人性。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确The power of the classroom is rooted in the humanity of the people gathered in the same place, at the same time↔ It lacks humanity Technology, no matter how advanced, should simply be a tool of a good teacher↔It lacks humanity预判得出原因为「技术缺乏人性」，选项It lacks humanity使用与原文同一个抽象名词humanity，是同根词的正反极性替换，匹配度最高。
B) 与原文相反原文未提及技术「尚不成熟」（still immature）；作者用no matter how advanced反而承认了技术可以非常先进，否定的是技术的本质属性（非人性），不是技术的发展阶段。
C) 无中生有原文没有任何关于「技术无法追踪学生成长」的表述；track students' growth这一说法是作者批评教育技术时未涉及的另一个方向。
D) 以偏概全It cannot cater to personal needs即「不能满足个性化需求」听起来很对，且与第三段online education does not allow a teacher to keep a struggling student after class and offer help有局部对应，但题目55题问的是技术为何不能取代好教师，根本原因应回末段P4的humanity，而不是第三段的某个具体功能局限；选It cannot cater to personal needs是把局部理由当作根本理由，犯以偏概全的错误。这是本题最有迷惑性的干扰项。
questions.quote: The power of the classroom is rooted in the humanity of the people gathered in the same place, at the same time.

options.text: It lacks humanity.
It is still immature.
It cannot track students' growth.
It cannot cater to personal needs.

title: Social media can be a powerful communication tool…

sentences.text: Social media can be a powerful communication tool for employees, helping them to collaborate, share ideas and solve problems.
Research has shown that 82% of employees think social media can improve work relationships and 60% believe it can support decision-making processes.
These beliefs contribute to a majority of workers connecting with colleagues on social media, even during work hours.

passage.translation: 社交媒体对员工来说可以是一种强大的沟通工具,帮助他们协作、分享想法和解决问题。研究表明,82%的员工认为社交媒体可以改善工作关系,60%的员工相信它可以支持决策过程。这些信念促使大多数员工在社交媒体上与同事建立联系,甚至在工作时间也是如此。

sentences.text: Employers typically worry that social media is a productivity killer; more than half of U.S. employers reportedly block access to social media at work.
In my research with 277 employees of a healthcare organization I found these concerns to be misguided.
Social media doesn't reduce productivity nearly as much as it kills employee retention.

passage.translation: 雇主通常担心社交媒体会扼杀生产力;据报道,超过半数的美国雇主在工作场所屏蔽社交媒体访问。在我对一家医疗机构277名员工的研究中,我发现这些担忧是误导性的。社交媒体对生产力的削弱远不及它对员工留任率的损害。

sentences.text: In the first part of the study I surveyed the employees about why and how they used platforms like Facebook, Twitter, or LinkedIn.
Respondents were then asked about their work behaviors, including whether they felt motivated in their jobs and showed initiative at work.
I found employees who engage in online social interactions with co-workers through social media blogs tend to be more motivated and come up with innovative ideas.
But when employees interact with individuals outside the organization, they are less motivated and show less initiative.

passage.translation: 在研究的第一部分,我调查了员工使用Facebook、Twitter或LinkedIn等平台的原因和方式。然后要求受访者回答他们的工作行为,包括他们是否在工作中感到有动力并表现出主动性。我发现通过社交媒体博客与同事进行在线社交互动的员工往往更有动力并提出创新想法。但当员工与组织外部的个人互动时,他们的动力较弱,主动性也较差。

sentences.text: In the second part of the study I found 76% of employees using social media for work took an interest in other organizations they found on social media.

When I examined how respondents expressed openness to new careers and employers, I found that they engaged in some key activities including researching new organizations and making new work connections.

passage.translation: 在研究的第二部分,我发现76%在工作中使用社交媒体的员工对他们在社交媒体上发现的其他组织产生了兴趣。当我考察受访者如何表达对新职业和雇主的开放态度时,我发现他们参与了一些关键活动,包括研究新组织和建立新的工作联系。

sentences.text: These findings present a dilemma for managers: employees using social media at work are more engaged and more productive, but they are also more likely to leave your company.
Managers should implement solutions that neutralize the retention risk caused by social media.

passage.translation: 这些发现给管理者带来了一个两难困境:在工作中使用社交媒体的员工更投入、更高效,但他们也更有可能离开你的公司。管理者应该实施能够消除社交媒体造成的留任风险的解决方案。

sentences.text: They can create social media groups in which employees will be more likely to collaborate and less likely to share withdrawal intentions or discussions about external job opportunities.
Managers can also use social media to directly reduce turnover(跳槽) intentions, by recognizing employees' accomplishments and giving visibility to employees' success stories.

passage.translation: 他们可以创建社交媒体群组,在这些群组中员工更有可能协作,而不太可能分享离职意向或讨论外部工作机会。管理者还可以利用社交媒体直接降低跳槽意向,通过认可员工的成就并让员工的成功故事获得关注。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does previous research about social media reveal?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
先前关于社交媒体的研究揭示了什么?
A) 大多数员工对其持积极看法。
B) 它提高了员工的工作效率。
C) 它使员工能够建立联系。
D) 员工在工作时间花费大量时间使用它。
**判型** What does previous research about social media reveal? 用 what...reveal 直接问研究揭示的事实，没有 infer/imply 等推断信号，是典型细节题。
**拆句** 题干主干 What does previous research about social media reveal? 结构平铺：what 作reveal 的宾语前置，about social media 是修饰 research 的介词短语。无陷阱。
**定位** 已有研究表明：82% 的员工认为社交媒体能改善工作关系，60% 的员工相信它有助于决策过程。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确82% of employees think social media can improve work relationships and 60% believe it can support decision-making processes↔ Most employees think positively of it原文两条数据都是正面态度的多数比例，恰好对应预判中的"多数员工肯定它"，整段不含工作效率提升或工作时间被占用的客观数据，故锁定选项首字母为 A。
B) 偷换概念原文只说员工"认为"社交媒体能改善关系和决策，是主观看法；It improves employees' work efficiency 把这种看法说成了已被证明的客观事实，且把 work relationships 偷换成 efficiency。
C) 以偏概全It enables employees to form connections 把原文 improve work relationships 改成"建立联系"，并把"员工的看法"偷换成"它实际能够"，只触及关系一项却丢了决策，且把主观信念伪装成已证事实。
D) 无中生有原文只说员工 connecting with colleagues on social media, even during work hours，并没有给出"花费大量工作时间在上面"的程度判断；Employees spend much of their work time on it 凭空加上了"花费大量时间"的数量评估。
questions.quote: Research has shown that 82% of employees think social media can improve work relationships and 60% believe it can support decision-making processes.

options.text: Most employees think positively of it.
It improves employees' work efficiency.
It enables employees to form connections.
Employees spend much of their work time on it.

questions.prompt: What did the author's own research find about social media?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者自己的研究发现社交媒体有什么影响?
A) 它对员工的工作产生负面影响。
B) 它对员工忠诚度造成很大损害。
C) 它扼杀了员工的工作动力。
D) 它影响雇主的决策。
**判型** What did the author's own research find about social media? 用 what...find 问研究的客观发现，是典型细节题。
**拆句** 题干 What did the author's own research find about social media? 主语 the author's own research，谓语 find，about social media 是 find 后的话题状语。结构清楚，无陷阱。
**定位** 社交媒体降低生产力的程度，远远比不上它对员工留任的杀伤力。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全原文 Social media doesn't reduce productivity nearly as much as it kills employee retention 已点明社交媒体并不显著降低生产力，所以"对工作产生负面影响"过于宽泛——它只在留任这一面有显著负面，工作本身（生产力、动力）并没有受到普遍负面影响。
B) ✓ 正确Social media doesn't reduce productivity nearly as much as it kills employee retention ↔It does much harm to employee loyalty not...as much as... 句式的语义重心在后半句"as much as"之后，定位句的论点核心是"对员工留任的杀伤更大"，恰好对应预判与首字母 B 的选项。
C) 张冠李戴原文第 2 段并未谈及对员工动力（motivation）的杀伤——动力一词出现在第 3 段，且第 3 段中社交媒体反而是"使员工 more motivated"。本选项把作者研究的核心结论说成"扼杀动力"，与原文位置和方向都不符。
D) 答非所问原文第 1 段提及社交媒体被员工认为 can support decision-making processes，主语是"员工的决策"，而非"雇主的决策"；本选项把"对雇主决策的影响"放进作者己研结论里，既错位也答非所问。
questions.quote: Social media doesn't reduce productivity nearly as much as it kills employee retention.

options.text: It influences employees' work negatively.
It does much harm to employee loyalty.
It kills employees' motivation for work
It affects employers' decision-making.

questions.prompt: What did the author find in his study about the effect of online social interactions?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者在研究中发现在线社交互动有什么影响?
A) 它因员工而异。
B) 它往往随使用的平台而变化。
C) 它与员工与谁互动有很大关系。
D) 当员工与外部人员互动时很难衡量。
**判型** What did the author find in his study about the effect of online social interactions?同样是 what...find 句式，问研究中的具体发现。
**拆句** 题干主干是 What did the author find，in his study 是状语，about the effect of online social interactions 是 find 的宾语介词短语，进一步限定要找的发现内容。结构略长，但层层并列，无陷阱。
**定位** 我发现：通过社交媒体博客与同事进行在线社交互动的员工，往往更有动力、能想出更多新点子；但当员工与组织外的人互动时，他们反而动力下降、缺少主动性。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文并未说"因人而异"或"每个员工不一样"，而是把员工按互动对象分成两类得出两种结果；It differs from employee to employee 把分类标准偷换成"员工个体差异"。
B) 无中生有原文 platforms like Facebook, Twitter, or LinkedIn 仅作为研究背景，没有把不同平台作为造成结果差异的原因；It tends to vary with the platform used 把背景信息硬升级成变量来源。
C) ✓ 正确employees who engage in online social interactions with co-workers ... tend to be more motivated / when employees interact with individuals outside the organization, they are less motivated↔ It has much to do with whom employees interact with原文两个分句除了对象不同（同事 vs. 外部人士）几乎所有别的条件都相同，结果却完全相反——这正是"效果取决于互动对象"的最直接证据，故锁定首字母 C。
D) 与原文相反原文恰恰已经测量出员工与外部人士互动会导致 less motivated and show less initiative，研究是给出了明确结果的，并不"难以衡量"。本选项与原文方向相反。
questions.quote: I found employees who engage in online social interactions with co-workers through social media blogs tend to be more motivated and come up with innovative ideas. But when employees interact with individuals outside the organization, they are less motivated and show less initiative.

options.text: It differs from employee to employee.
It tends to vary with the platform used.
It has much to do with whom employees interact with.
It is hard to measure when employees interact with outsiders.

questions.prompt: What problem was found with employees using social media for work?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
员工使用社交媒体工作发现了什么问题?
A) 他们很少表达内心想法。
B) 他们中的大多数人探索新的工作机会。
C) 他们不愿意与他人合作。
D) 他们中的许多人最终生产力下降。
**判型** What problem was found with employees using social media for work? 用what...found 问研究中发现的问题，仍是问客观事实。
**拆句** 题干 What problem was found with employees using social media for work? 是 what作主语的被动疑问句：problem 与 what 共同作主语，be found 是谓语，with employees using social media for work 是介词短语修饰 problem。读不顺时把它倒过来想成 "researchers found what problem with these employees" 即可。
**定位** 我发现：76% 用社交媒体办公的员工会关注他们在社交媒体上看到的其他组织。当我考察这些受访者如何表达对新职业、新雇主的开放态度时，我发现他们会从事几项关键活动，包括研究新公司、建立新的工作联系。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有原文第 4 段没有提到员工"是否表达内心想法"——只说他们关注其他组织、研究新公司、建立新人脉，这些都是外向行为；They seldom expressed their inner thoughts把不存在的话题拉进来。
B) ✓ 正确76% of employees using social media for work took an interest in other organizations they found on social media↔ Most of them explored new job opportunities openness to new careers and employers ↔ explored new job opportunities 76% 的覆盖面+关注新公司、研究新公司、建立新人脉、对新职业开放等多项行为同向叠加，正对应"多数人在物色新工作"，故锁定首字母 B。
C) 与原文相反原文第 3 段已说与同事互动会让员工 more motivated and come up with innovative ideas，本身就是合作意愿强；They were reluctant to collaborate with others 与之方向相反。
D) 与原文相反原文第 2 段已经否定 Social media doesn't reduce productivity nearly as much as it kills employee retention，社交媒体并未明显降低生产力；本选项却说"很多人最终生产力降低"，是把作者明确否定的结论又重新放回来。
questions.quote: I found 76% of employees using social media for work took an interest in other organizations they found on social media. When I examined how respondents expressed openness to new careers and employers, I found that they engaged in some key activities including researching new organizations and making new work connections.

options.text: They seldom expressed their inner thoughts.
Most of them explored new job opportunities.
They were reluctant to collaborate with others.
Many of them ended with lower productivity.

questions.prompt: What does the author suggest managers do to neutralize the retention risk?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者建议管理者做什么来消除留任风险?
A) 因员工的成就而给予晋升。
B) 为员工创造分享成功故事的机会。
C) 通过社交媒体认可员工的成就。
D) 鼓励员工提高在社交媒体上的知名度。
**判型** What does the author suggest managers do to neutralize the retention risk? 虽含suggest，但问的是作者明文给出的建议方案，原文必有对应句，仍属细节题。
**拆句** 题干主干 What does the author suggest managers do，managers do 是 suggest 后省略 that 的虚拟语气从句（suggest sb. do），to neutralize the retention risk 是表目的的不定式。难点在虚拟语气省略 that 的结构，主体考生易把 managers 看成全句主语。
**定位** 管理者还可以利用社交媒体直接降低跳槽意向：方法是表彰员工取得的成就、让员工的成功故事更被看见。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文动作是 recognizing employees' accomplishments（公开承认成就），不是"提拔"；Give promotions to employees for their accomplishments 把"承认"偷换成"提拔"，并丢掉了"通过社交媒体"这一关键媒介。
B) 张冠李戴原文是管理者借社交媒体 giving visibility to employees' success stories——动作发起者是管理者；Create opportunities for employees to share success stories 把动作主体换成员工自己分享，与原文恰好对调，且回避了"用社交媒体"这一关键媒介。
C) ✓ 正确Managers can also use social media to directly reduce turnover(跳槽) intentions, by recognizing employees' accomplishments and giving visibility to employees' success stories↔ Acknowledge employees' achievements through social media预判要求"用社交媒体表彰成就"中的动作与媒介两要素同时对齐，只有首字母 C 把"承认成就"与"借助社交媒体"都准确保留，其余选项要么换错动作、要么丢掉媒介。
D) 偷换概念原文是管理者 giving visibility to employees' success stories——是"让员工的事迹可见"，主导者是管理者；Encourage employees to increase their visibility on social media 把"被表彰的事迹"偷换成"员工的曝光度"，且把管理者的动作变成鼓励员工自己增加曝光，正好是文章想抑制的"个人外向行为"。
questions.quote: Managers can also use social media to directly reduce turnover(跳槽) intentions, by recognizing employees' accomplishments and giving visibility to employees' success stories.

options.text: Give promotions to employees for their accomplishments.
Create opportunities for employees to share success stories.
Acknowledge employees' achievements through social media.
Encourage employees to increase their visibility on social media.

title: If you've ever looked at the ingredients list…

sentences.text: If you've ever looked at the ingredients list while grocery shopping, chances are you've seen the term "natural flavors".
But have you taken a (26)____ to consider what these natural flavors actually are?

passage.translation: 如果你在购物时曾经看过配料表,你很可能见过"天然香料"这个术语。但你是否停下来想过这些天然香料究竟是什么?

sentences.text: Most of us might think that "natural flavors" are, well, naturally good for us.
A recent study in the journal Appetite found that when the word "natural" appears on packaging, people (27)____ that the food within is indeed healthier.
In truth, natural flavors do not (28)____ much, at least chemically speaking, from their flavor-boosting (29)____ : artificial flavors.
Both can be made in a lab by trained flavorists, but artificial flavors use chemicals to give a product a (30)____ smell or taste.

passage.translation: 我们大多数人可能认为"天然香料"自然对我们有益。最近发表在《食欲》期刊上的一项研究发现,当"天然"一词出现在包装上时,人们会认为其中的食物确实更健康。事实上,天然香料与其增味对应物人工香料在化学成分上并无太大差异。两者都可以由训练有素的调味师在实验室制造,但人工香料使用化学物质赋予产品特定的气味或味道。

sentences.text: Natural flavors come from plant or animal (31)____ , like fruit, vegetable, meat, fish or milk that is then processed or refined in some way.
In short, natural flavors are (32)____ from plants and animals to create specific flavors for processed foods.
But that does not (33)____ make it easier to tell what is really in your food.
Because the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has not (34)____ the term, companies can use it to refer to pretty much anything derived from a plant or animal.
And natural flavors can also include a variety of chemical additives, such as preservatives.
The FDA doesn't require companies to reveal what additional chemicals a specific item (35)____ .

passage.translation: 天然香料来自植物或动物来源,如水果、蔬菜、肉类、鱼类或牛奶,然后以某种方式加工或提炼。简而言之,天然香料是从植物和动物中提取的,用于为加工食品制造特定风味。但这并不一定能让你更容易知道食物中到底有什么。因为食品药品监督管理局(FDA)没有对该术语进行定义,公司可以用它来指代几乎任何源自植物或动物的物质。而且天然香料还可以包含多种化学添加剂,如防腐剂。FDA不要求公司披露特定产品含有哪些额外化学物质。

sentences.text: So if you want to know for certain what you're getting with your groceries, you might want to stick to the farmer's market.

passage.translation: 所以,如果你想确切知道你购买的食品里有什么,你可能需要去农贸市场购物。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
If you've ever looked at the ingredients list while grocery shopping, chances are you've seen the term "natural flavors". But have you taken a {{26}} to consider what these natural flavors actually are?

Most of us might think that "natural flavors" are, well, naturally good for us. A recent study in the journal Appetite found that when the word "natural" appears on packaging, people {{27}} that the food within is indeed healthier. In truth, natural flavors do not {{28}} much, at least chemically speaking, from their flavor-boosting {{29}} : artificial flavors. Both can be made in a lab by trained flavorists, but artificial flavors use chemicals to give a product a {{30}} smell or taste.

Natural flavors come from plant or animal {{31}} , like fruit, vegetable, meat, fish or milk that is then processed or refined in some way. In short, natural flavors are {{32}} from plants and animals to create specific flavors for processed foods. But that does not {{33}} make it easier to tell what is really in your food. Because the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has not {{34}} the term, companies can use it to refer to pretty much anything derived from a plant or animal. And natural flavors can also include a variety of chemical additives, such as preservatives. The FDA doesn't require companies to reveal what additional chemicals a specific item {{35}} .

So if you want to know for certain what you're getting with your groceries, you might want to stick to the farmer's market.

options.text: acknowledge
implies
chance
necessarily
contains
particular
counterparts
perceive
defined
second
differ
sources
especially
strange
extracted

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) second 名词
**词性槽** 动词 take + 不定冠词 a 后，要填名词作宾语
**依据** take a second = 花点时间，固定搭配have you taken a __(26)__ to consider 意为"你有没有花点时间去想想"，take a second（second 此处指"片刻、一会儿"）是地道搭配，单数可数也吻合 "a"。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) chance 搭配指向不对take a chance 意为"冒险、碰运气"，放进 taken a __(26)__ to consider 成了"冒险去考虑"，与"花时间思考"的语境不符。
D) counterparts 复数，与 a 冲突counterparts 是复数形式，前面却是单数冠词 a，语法上就过不去；词义"对应物"也接不上。
N) sources 复数且词义不符sources 同样是复数，与 a 不配；"来源"也无法和 "to consider" 构成通顺意思。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) perceive 动词
**词性槽** 主语 people 后缺谓语，要填动词
**依据** "人们认为食物更健康"是主观感知people __(27)__ that the food within is indeed healthier，承接前句 "natural" 带来的错觉，这里说人们"认为/觉得"里面的食物更健康，perceive（主观认为、感知）正贴这层"误以为"的语境。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) acknowledge "承认"含已确认事实，与误解语境反acknowledge 是"承认（某事属实）"，暗示那是被证实的事实；但本文恰恰要说"更健康"只是人们的错觉、并非事实，用 acknowledge 逻辑指向反了。
F) differ不接 that 从句，搭配不成立differ 表"不同"，固定接 differ from，不能接 that 从句；语法上就接不上 that the food within is indeed healthier。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 A) —— acknowledge 词性对、能接 that，最易误填。它和perceive 一样是动词、能接 that 从句，但表"承认事实"，而本文讲的是"人们误以为更健康"。防坑：判断语境是客观事实还是主观感知——讲误解就选 perceive。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) differ 动词
**词性槽** 助动词 do not 后接动词原形
**依据** differ from = 与……不同，搭配定死natural flavors do not __(28)__ much, at least chemically speaking, from their flavor- boosting __(29)__: artificial flavors，意为"天然香精与人工香精差别不大"，differ from 是固定搭配，且呼应全文"两者其实差不多"的主旨。

**答案** D) counterparts 名词
**词性槽** 形容词 flavor-boosting 后、their 之后作名词中心词
**依据** 人工香精是天然香精的"对应物" natural flavors do not differ much ... from their flavor-boosting __(29)__: artificial flavors，把 artificial flavors 称作 natural flavors 的 counterparts（对应物/对等物），正是两类香精互为对照的关系，词义最贴。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
N) sources "来源"指向错，且后文要用sources 意为"来源"，但 artificial flavors 是与天然香精"并列对照"的另一类，不是它的来源；且 sources 在 31 题指"植物动物来源"才真正贴切，此处用掉会顶掉后面的空。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 N) —— sources 词性也对、义看着也沾边，易抢答。sources 是复数名词、配 their，"来源"似乎也通；但 artificial flavors 与天然香精是"对照"而非"来源"关系，应选 counterparts，并把 sources 留给 31 题。防坑：前瞻哪个词在别处更对口。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) particular 形容词
**词性槽** 空在名词 smell/taste 前作定语，要填形容词
**依据** "给产品某种特定气味"逻辑顺use chemicals to give a product a __(30)__ smell or taste，人工香精用化学物质赋予产品一种"特定的"气味或味道，particular（特定的）正契合"定制某种风味"的语境。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
O) strange 感情色彩偏负面，与语境冲突strange 意为"奇怪的、古怪的"，带贬义；本句在客观说明香精"赋予特定风味"，并无"气味古怪"之意，色彩对不上。

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) sources 名词
**词性槽** from plant or animal 后作介词宾语中心词
**依据** "来自植物或动物来源" Natural flavors come from plant or animal __(31)__, like fruit, vegetable, meat, fish or milk，sources（来源）指天然香精的"植物或动物来源"，后面列举的水果、蔬菜、肉、鱼、奶正是这些来源的具体例子。

**答案** H) extracted 动词
**词性槽** be 动词 are 后接过去分词构成被动
**依据** "从动植物中被提取出来" natural flavors are __(32)__ from plants and animals to create specific flavors for processed foods，be extracted from（从……中被提取）正是天然香精的制取方式，搭配与语义双双吻合。

**答案** J) necessarily 副词
**词性槽** does not 与实义动词 make 之间，要填副词
**依据** not necessarily = 未必，固定搭配But that does not __(33)__ make it easier to tell what is really in your food，意为"但这未必就让你更容易弄清食物里到底有什么"，not necessarily（未必、不一定）是地道搭配，且与转折 But 及后文"FDA 没定义"的语境吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) especially "尤其"不与 not 构成此意，逻辑不顺especially 意为"尤其、特别"，does not especially make 读作"不特别使……"，既不地道也接不上"了解成分其实没变容易"的转折语气。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) defined 动词
**词性槽** has not + 空 + the term，要填过去分词
**依据** FDA 没有"定义"这个术语Because the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has not __(34)__ the term, companies can use it to refer to pretty much anything，正因 FDA 没给"natural flavors"这个术语下定义，企业才能随便用——define the term（给术语下定义）逻辑严丝合缝。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) extracted "提取术语"搭配讲不通extracted 是"提取、萃取"，宾语应是物质（如从植物 extracted 出香精），与 the term（术语）搭配成"提取术语"不成立；且 extracted 该留给 32 题。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) contains 动词
**词性槽** what 从句里 a specific item 后缺谓语
**依据** 某产品"含有"哪些额外化学物The FDA doesn't require companies to reveal what additional chemicals a specific item __(35)__，意为"FDA 不要求企业披露某个产品含有哪些额外化学物"，contains（含有）正对应"产品里有什么成分"，且单三与 a specific item 一致。

title: In the age of the internet, there's no…

sentences.text: In the age of the internet, there's no such thing as a private debate.
But is that bad for science?
Some scientists have had concerns.

When debates in any sector move beyond the halls of universities and government agencies, there's potential for information to be used incorrectly, leading to public confusion; yet, open debate can also promote communication between the scientific community and the public.
Recent open debates on scientific research, health, and policy have aroused greater public attention and encouraged more diverse voices.

If this trend spurs scientists to agree more quickly about the best solutions to our problems—and at the same time helps the public observe the process of scientific discourse more clearly—then this is good for everyone, including scientists.

passage.translation: 在互联网时代,不存在私密的辩论这回事。但这对科学来说是坏事吗?一些科学家对此表示担忧。当任何领域的辩论超出大学和政府机构的范围时,信息就有可能被错误使用,导致公众困惑;然而,开放的辩论也能促进科学界与公众之间的交流。近期关于科学研究、健康和政策的公开辩论引起了更广泛的公众关注,并鼓励了更多元化的声音。如果这一趋势促使科学家更快地就解决问题的最佳方案达成一致,同时帮助公众更清楚地观察科学讨论的过程,那么这对包括科学家在内的每个人都有益。

sentences.text: A recent debate published in The New York Times discussed the question of how quickly medicine should be developed and produced.
Issues such as safety of the product and perception of the public were examined and considered.

But some experts worried that such public speculation might lead people to believe that disagreement about the details meant a lack of adequate scientific consensus over the safety and efficiency of modern-day medicine.

passage.translation: 《纽约时报》最近发表的一场辩论探讨了药物应以多快速度研发和生产的问题。产品的安全性和公众的认知等议题得到了审视和考量。但一些专家担心,这种公开推测可能会让人们认为,对细节的分歧意味着在现代药物的安全性和有效性方面缺乏充分的科学共识。

sentences.text: The anxiety seems misplaced.
Gone are the days of going to a conference and debating scientific issues, and that's good because those gatherings were not diverse enough and excluded many important voices.
These days, the public can access debates about science regardless of where they take place.

passage.translation: 这种焦虑似乎是多余的。去会议上辩论科学问题的日子已经一去不复返了,这是好事,因为那些聚会不够多元化,排除了许多重要的声音。如今,无论辩论在哪里进行,公众都可以接触到关于科学的辩论。

sentences.text: For many scientists, public debate is a new frontier and it may feel like a place with few restraints or rules.
But rather than avoiding such conversations, let the debates be transparent and vigorous, wherever they are held.
If the public is to understand that science is an honorably self- correcting process, the idea that science is a fixed set of facts in a textbook needs to be dismissed.
With the validity of science coming under attack, there's a need for scientific debates to be perceived as open and true to life.
Let everyone see the noisy, messy deliberations that advance science and lead to decisions that benefit us all.

passage.translation: 对许多科学家来说,公开辩论是一个新领域,可能感觉像是一个几乎没有限制或规则的地方。但与其回避这类对话,不如让辩论无论在哪里举行都保持透明和充满活力。如果要让公众理解科学是一个值得尊敬的自我纠正过程,就需要摒弃科学是教科书中一套固定事实的观念。随着科学的有效性受到攻击,科学辩论需要被视为开放和真实的。让每个人都看到那些推动科学进步并做出有益于我们所有人的决策的嘈杂、混乱的讨论过程。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does the author think open debate can do?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者认为公开辩论能做什么?
A) 帮助公众更好地理解科学。
B) 消除科学界的困惑。
C) 解决大学与政府机构之间的争议。
D) 防止信息被公众错误使用。
**判型** What does the author think open debate can do是一个具体的做什么问题，不含infer、imply、mainly about等推断或主旨信号词，属于围绕一个话题点的细节定位题
**拆句** 主干是What does the author think open debate can do，think后省略that，引出宾语从句open debate can do (what)。问句的What其实是宾语从句里do的宾语，被前置到句首。结构简单、无陷阱。
**定位** 如果这一趋势能推动科学家更快地就我们面临问题的最佳解决方案达成一致，并同时帮助公众更清楚地观察科学讨论的过程，那么对所有人，包括科学家在内，都是好事。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确helps the public observe the process of scientific discourse more clearly ↔Help the public to better understand science预判让公众更清楚地观察、理解科学讨论与Help the public to better understand science在语义上同构，仅是observe到understand、scientific discourse到science的上下位替换
B) 偷换概念Clear up confusion in the scientific community说的是消除科学界内部的困惑，但原文potential for information to be used incorrectly, leading to public confusion点明confusion存在于公众一侧、而非科学界内部
C) 无中生有Settle disputes between universities and government agencies声称开放辩论能解决高校与政府机构之间的纠纷；原文虽提及halls of universities and government agencies，但只是说辩论的发生地，并未说要去settle什么disputes
D) 与原文相反Prevent information from being used incorrectly by the public把防止信息被误用说成open debate的功能；但原文there's potential for information to be used incorrectly, leading to public confusion里，这一可能性是开放辩论的副作用而非它的解决目标
questions.quote: If this trend spurs scientists to agree more quickly about the best solutions to our problems—and at the same time helps the public observe the process of scientific discourse more clearly—then this is good for everyone, including scientists.

options.text: Help the public to better understand science.
Clear up confusion in the scientific community.
Settle disputes between universities and government agencies.
Prevent information from being used incorrectly by the public.

questions.prompt: Why did a recent debate published in The New York Times arouse concerns among experts?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
为什么《纽约时报》上发表的一场近期辩论在专家中引起了担忧?
A) 它可能会阻碍医学研究的进展。
B) 它可能会滋生公众对现代医学的不信任。
C) 它可能会增加获取研究资金的难度。
D) 它可能会妨碍医学科学家达成共识。
**判型** Why did a recent debate published in The New York Times arouse concerns among experts问的是某一具体事件下专家担心的具体原因，原因可在文中直接找到，不需要跨段推断
**拆句** 主干是Why加did加a recent debate加arouse加concerns。a recent debate后带过去分词短语published in The New York Times作后置定语，限定是哪一场debate；among experts限定concerns的范围。理清后题干即那场登在某报上的辩论，为何让专家担心。
**定位** 但一些专家担心，这种公开揣测可能让人们相信：对细节的分歧意味着科学界对现代医药的安全与效率缺乏足够的共识。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有It might hinder the progress in medical research谈的是阻碍医学研究的进展，原文只说公开辩论可能让公众产生误解，并未说会拖慢医学研究本身
B) ✓ 正确might lead people to believe that disagreement about the details meant a lack of adequate scientific consensus over the safety and efficiency of modern-day medicine↔ It might breed public distrust in modern medicine预判中的对现代医药产生不信任正好对应public distrust in modern medicine；原文的多步表述被压缩成一个名词distrust，是典型的名词化同义替换
C) 无中生有It might add to the difficulty of getting research funds说会增加获得研究经费的难度；原文从未提及funds、funding、money相关概念
D) 偷换概念It might prevent medical scientists reaching consensus说会阻止医学科学家达成共识；原文是meant a lack of adequate scientific consensus——即让公众以为科学界没共识，但事实是科学界已有共识，并不是公开辩论会真的让科学家无法达成共识
questions.quote: But some experts worried that such public speculation might lead people to believe that disagreement about the details meant a lack of adequate scientific consensus over the safety and efficiency of modern-day medicine.

options.text: It might hinder the progress in medical research.
It might breed public distrust in modern medicine.
It might add to the difficulty of getting research funds.
It might prevent medical scientists reaching consensus.

questions.prompt: Why does the author say some experts' anxiety seems misplaced?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
为什么作者说一些专家的焦虑似乎是错位的?
A) 在会议上辩论科学问题现在已经过时了。
B) 科学家和公众都可以辩论各种话题。
C) 无论如何公众都能接触到关于科学的辩论。
D) 科学家可以用任何他们喜欢的方式表达自己的观点。
**判型** Why does the author say some experts' anxiety seems misplaced问的是作者下此判断的依据，依据明示在原文紧随其后的句子中，属于因果细节
**拆句** Why does the author say后接一个宾语从句some experts' anxiety seems misplaced。anxiety前是some experts'所有格作定语；seems是系动词、misplaced是表语形容词。理解为为什么作者说某些专家的担心是放错地方的。
**定位** 去开会、在会上辩论科学问题的日子已经过去了，这是好事，因为那些聚会不够多元，把许多重要的声音排除在外。如今，无论辩论在哪里举行，公众都能接触到。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全Debating scientific issues at a conference is now old-fashioned只是原文Gone are the days of going to a conference的复述，确实存在于文中，但它只是支撑句之一，不是作者用来回答为什么misplaced的核心理由；核心理由是公众如今随处可获取辩论
B) 偷换概念Diverse topics can be debated by both scientists and the public说的是多元话题可被科学家与公众共同辩论；原文diverse是修饰those gatherings本身（聚会不够多元），并不是说话题多元，更没说公众能与科学家共同辩论
C) ✓ 正确the public can access debates about science regardless of where they take place↔Debates about science are accessible to the public anyway预判中的无论在哪都能接触到正是accessible to the public anyway的内涵；从access（动词）到accessible（形容词）的词性转换加主被动互换是四级最典型的同义替换手法
D) 张冠李戴Scientists can voice their opinions whatever way they like说的是科学家可以以他们喜欢的方式发声；原文谈论的是公众能接触到辩论，主语和动作都不是科学家
questions.quote: Gone are the days of going to a conference and debating scientific issues, and that's good because those gatherings were not diverse enough and excluded many important voices. These days, the public can access debates about science regardless of where they take place.

options.text: Debating scientific issues at a conference is now old-fashioned.
Diverse topics can be debated by both scientists and the public.
Debates about science are accessible to the public anyway.
Scientists can voice their opinions whatever way they like.

questions.prompt: What does the author suggest scientists do about public debate?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者建议科学家如何对待公开辩论?
A) 对此进行更多讨论。
B) 张开双臂拥抱它。
C) 为它制定新规则。
D) 将它限制在理性的程度。
**判型** What does the author suggest scientists do about public debate问的是一个具体建议，答案在原文祈使句中能直接找到，无需推断
**拆句** 主干What does the author suggest scientists do。suggest后接的是宾语从句省略that，scientists是从句主语、do是从句动词（虚拟语气省略should），about public debate是范围状语。句意：作者建议科学家们对于公共辩论应该怎么做。
**定位** 但与其回避这类对话，不如让辩论变得透明而有力，无论它们在哪里举行。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念Have more discussions about it说对公共辩论本身展开更多讨论——它把公共辩论变成被讨论的对象；原文是要科学家参与到公共辩论中，而不是开会讨论公共辩论应不应该做
B) ✓ 正确rather than avoiding such conversations, let the debates be transparent and vigorous↔Embrace it with open arms预判拥抱并积极参与与Embrace it with open arms在意象与态度极性上完全一致；rather than avoiding的反面正是embrace
C) 与原文相反Formulate new rules for it说要为公共辩论制定新规则；原文it may feel like a place with few restraints or rules承认公共辩论缺规则，但下一句紧接着以But rather than avoiding such conversations转向拥抱而非立规则，作者并未建议立新规
D) 与原文相反Restrain it to a rational degree说要把公共辩论约束到一个合理程度；原文却用let the debates be transparent and vigorous强调放开而非约束，方向相反
questions.quote: But rather than avoiding such conversations, let the debates be transparent and vigorous, wherever they are held.

options.text: Have more discussions about it.
Embrace it with open arms.
Formulate new rules for it.
Restrain it to a rational degree.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about science in the last paragraph?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者在最后一段关于科学说了什么?
A) 它是通过教科书传播的。
B) 它是被证明有效且符合实际的东西。
C) 它是一个动态的自我完善过程。
D) 它是事实和既定规则的集合。
**判型** What does the author say about science in the last paragraph问的是末段里关于science的具体描述，不问全文主旨也不问态度极性，定位段已给出，属段内细节题
**拆句** 主干What does the author say about science。in the last paragraph是地点状语限定回答范围。say about science是动词搭配对…作出说明。理解为在末段里作者关于science说了什么。
**定位** 如果想让公众明白科学是一个光荣的自我修正过程，那么科学就是教科书里一组固定事实这一观念就必须被抛弃。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反It is transmitted through textbooks说科学通过教科书传播；原文the idea that science is a fixed set of facts in a textbook needs to be dismissed恰好是作者要否定的观念
B) 张冠李戴It is what proves valid and true to life说科学是被证明有效且符合现实的东西；原文there's a need for scientific debates to be perceived as open and true to life里true to life修饰的是scientific debates（辩论）如何被感知，而不是用来定义science本身
C) ✓ 正确science is an honorably self-correcting process↔It is a dynamic and self-improving process预判自我修正的动态过程与a dynamic and self-improving process逐字对应；self- correcting对应self-improving是同根同义的复合形容词替换
D) 与原文相反It is a collection of facts and established rules说科学是事实与既定规则的集合——这与原文science is a fixed set of facts in a textbook想抛弃的旧观念完全对齐
questions.quote: If the public is to understand that science is an honorably self-correcting process, the idea that science is a fixed set of facts in a textbook needs to be dismissed.

options.text: It is transmitted through textbooks.
It is what proves valid and true to life.
It is a dynamic and self-improving process.
It is a collection of facts and established rules.

title: Online classes began to be popularized just a…

sentences.text: Online classes began to be popularized just a few decades ago.
They are advertised as a way for adults to finish their education and students to learn the material at their own pace—it is far more compatible for people with busy schedules.

passage.translation: 在线课程仅在几十年前才开始普及。它们被宣传为成年人完成学业和学生按照自己的节奏学习材料的一种方式——对于日程繁忙的人来说，这种方式要兼容得多。

sentences.text: But after being enrolled in an online course last fall semester, I came to realize online classes were merely a means to fulfil course requirements.

passage.translation: 但在上个秋季学期注册了一门在线课程之后,我开始意识到在线课程仅仅是完成课程要求的一种手段。

sentences.text: First of all, students lack the desire to learn, and they simply complete their assignments to receive credit for a passing grade rather than genuinely engage with the course material.

passage.translation: 首先,学生缺乏学习的欲望,他们只是完成作业以获得及格分数的学分,而不是真正地参与课程材料。

sentences.text: As online courses tend to have more than 100 students, most of the assignments are short and simple.
They are not designed for students to interact with the material in depth but designed to be graded easily to accommodate such a large number of students.

passage.translation: 由于在线课程往往有超过100名学生,大多数作业都简短而简单。它们的设计目的不是让学生深入地与材料互动,而是为了易于评分以适应如此大量的学生。

sentences.text: Perhaps the biggest disadvantage of taking an online class is the absence of face-to-face interaction between the teacher and their students.
Live sessions are infrequent and are often scheduled during the middle of the day when students have to attend other classes or work.
The office hours of the professor may also be during inconvenient times for many students as well.
Most interaction with the professor has to be through email which is often impersonal.
It is nearly impossible for students to build a relationship with their professor.

passage.translation: 也许参加在线课程最大的劣势是教师和学生之间缺乏面对面的互动。实时课程很少,而且经常安排在学生必须上其他课或工作的白天。教授的办公时间对许多学生来说也可能不方便。与教授的大多数互动必须通过电子邮件进行,这往往缺乏人情味。学生几乎不可能与教授建立关系。

sentences.text: There is also little interaction amongst students.
It can be harder for students to create study groups and form relationships with their peers.

passage.translation: 学生之间的互动也很少。学生更难创建学习小组并与同学建立关系。

sentences.text: Online classes also require either a computer or laptop and a reliable internet connection.
Not all students have access to these types of resources, whether it is for financial or other reasons, and some students can be put at a disadvantage.

passage.translation: 在线课程还需要一台计算机或笔记本电脑以及可靠的互联网连接。并非所有学生都能获得这些类型的资源,无论是出于经济原因还是其他原因,一些学生可能会处于劣势。

sentences.text: Offering online classes certainly helps students who would otherwise not be able to attend classroom sessions.
However, they fail to provide a genuine education with an emphasis on convenience rather than critical thinking.
We need restructured online classes in which students can have a learning experience that will actually provide quality education.

passage.translation: 提供在线课程当然有助于那些原本无法参加课堂授课的学生。然而,它们未能提供真正的教育,强调的是便利性而非批判性思维。我们需要重组在线课程,让学生能够获得真正提供优质教育的学习体验。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about students enrolled in online classes?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于参加在线课程的学生,作者说了什么?
A) 他们可以轻松获取课程材料。
B) 他们缺乏学习动力。
C) 他们可以按照自己的节奏学习。
D) 他们很少完成课程要求。
**判型** What does the author say about students enrolled in online classes? 在问「就上网课的学生这件事，作者具体说了什么」，是对单一陈述的事实核对。
**拆句** 题干主干是 What does the author say about X，标准的 say about 双宾结构，关于 X 的对象是 students enrolled in online classes，其中 enrolled in online classes 是过去分词短语作 students 的后置定语，等于 students who are enrolled in online classes，无陷阱。
**定位** 首先，学生缺乏学习的欲望，他们只是完成作业以拿到及格分数，而不是真正与课程内容打交道。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴：宣传方观点≠作者观点They can access course materials easily. 取自 P1 对网课的宣传性描述，并非作者本人就「学生」给出的评价，问的是作者对学生说了什么，不是对网课说了什么。
B) ✓ 正确lack the desire to learn↔ unmotivated to learn预判要找「学生没有学习动力」的表达，四个选项里只有 They are unmotivated to learn. 直接对应 lack the desire to learn，故锁定。
C) 张冠李戴：照抄被驳斥的卖点They can learn at their own pace. 原句正是 learn the material at their own pace 的近乎照抄，是作者列为反驳对象的卖点，不是作者对学生的论断。
D) 与原文相反：rarely 类否定词反转事实They rarely fulfil the course requirements. 说学生很少完成课程要求，但 they simply complete their assignments to receive credit for a passing grade 明示他们恰恰会完成作业、只是为拿学分，方向相反。
questions.quote: First of all, students lack the desire to learn, and they simply complete their assignments to receive credit for a passing grade rather than genuinely engage with the course material.

options.text: They can access course materials easily.
They are unmotivated to learn.
They can learn at their own pace.
They rarely fulfil the course requirements.

questions.prompt: What does the author think of online course assignments?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者如何看待在线课程作业?
A) 它们被设计得便于批改。
B) 它们旨在促进互动。
C) 它们基于容易获取的材料。
D) 它们是为了适应学生的需求而布置的。
**判型** What does the author think of online course assignments? 指向作者对某一具体事物的判断句，仍属细节核对。
**拆句** 主干 What does the author think of X，think of 在此意为「认为…如何」，相当于 What is the author’s opinion of X，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 这些作业的设计不是为了让学生深入与材料互动，而是为了便于打分，以应对如此庞大的学生群体。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确designed to be graded easily ↔ made convenient to mark预判锁定「便于打分」的语义，仅 They are made convenient to mark. 直接对应；其他选项要么扯到互动，要么扯到材料/学生需求，不在 designed to 的目的范围。
B) 与原文相反：not…but… 的前半句反着用They are meant to facilitate interaction. 把作业说成「促进互动」，但 not designed for students to interact with the material in depth 明确否定了「互动」目的。
C) 无中生有：制造原文未提及的属性They are based on easily accessible material. 说作业基于「容易获取的材料」，原文P4 没有任何句子谈论材料的获取难易，凭空捏造。
D) 偷换概念：动词宾语被替换They are given to accommodate students' needs. 把 accommodate 的对象从原文to accommodate such a large number of students 中的「大量学生（人数）」偷换成「学生的需求」，目的指向被改。
questions.quote: They are not designed for students to interact with the material in depth but designed to be graded easily to accommodate such a large number of students.

options.text: They are made convenient to mark.
They are meant to facilitate interaction.
They are based on easily accessible material.
They are given to accommodate students' needs.

questions.prompt: What does the author say is one disadvantage of online classes?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者说在线课程的一个缺点是什么?
A) 它们经常被安排在不规律的时间。
B) 它们使得教授的办公室难以接近得多。
C) 它们往往会增加教授回复学生邮件的负担。
D) 它们几乎不为学生提供相互建立关系的机会。
**判型** What does the author say is one disadvantage of online classes? 中 one disadvantage 是单数，明示只问其中一个具体缺点，是定点取信息的细节题。
**拆句** 题干主干 What does the author say is one disadvantage of online classes，say 后是省略 that 的宾语从句 (that) one disadvantage of online classes is what，what 提前到句首形成疑问，需注意「what 在从句里实为表语」这一点，否则容易把 say 误读成不及物。
**定位** 学生之间的互动也很少。要想组建学习小组、和同伴建立关系会更难。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念 + 与原文相反They are frequently scheduled at irregular times. 说直播课「频繁地」被安排在不规律时间，原文 Live sessions are infrequent 恰恰说直播课很少，且原文谈的是「时间冲突」而非「时间不规律」。
B) 偷换概念：时间不便 ≠ 空间不可达They make professors' offices much less accessible. 把焦点放在「办公室更不可达」，但 The office hours of the professor may also be during inconvenient times只说「办公时间不便」，没有说办公室不可达，accessible 与 convenient times 不是同义。
C) 无中生有：从一个事实派生未提及的后果They tend to increase professors' burden of responding to students' emails. 谈教授回邮件「负担加重」，原文 Most interaction with the professor has to be through email which is often impersonal 只说邮件互动「冷冰冰」，并未提教授负担。
D) ✓ 正确form relationships with their peers ↔ students to build relationships with each other It can be harder for students to create study groups ↔ provide little chance预判核心是「学生 + 学生之间难建立关系」，They provide little chance for students to build relationships with each other 在主体、动作、方向上全部命中。
questions.quote: There is also little interaction amongst students. It can be harder for students to create study groups and form relationships with their peers.

options.text: They are frequently scheduled at irregular times.
They make professors' offices much less accessible.
They tend to increase professors' burden of responding to students' emails.
They provide little chance for students to build relationships with each other

questions.prompt: What problem may arise if classes go online?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
如果课程转到线上可能会出现什么问题?
A) 更多学生可能会发现容易缺课。
B) 教师会担心网络连接不佳。
C) 一些学生参加课程可能会有困难。
D) 资源有限的学校将处于不利地位。
**判型** What problem may arise if classes go online? 问「在网课条件下会出现什么问题」，问的是文中已写明的某一具体后果，不需要推论。
**拆句** 主干 What problem may arise，后接 if 条件状语从句 if classes go online，arise 为不及物动词「出现」，结构清晰；注意 go online 这个搭配指「转为线上」，不要望文生义译作「上网」。
**定位** 并非所有学生都能用上这些资源，无论是出于经济还是其他原因，有些学生因此可能处于不利地位。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有：把后果嫁接到主观行为More students may find it easy to be absent from them. 谈学生「更容易缺席」，原文从未谈学生主观逃课难易，凭空添加。
B) 张冠李戴：替换受影响主体Teachers will worry about poor internet connections. 把网络问题的担忧者换成teachers，原文 P7 通篇是 students 受影响，无任何关于教师担忧的描述。
C) ✓ 正确Not all students have access to these types of resources ↔Some students may have difficulty attending them some students can be put at a disadvantage ↔ may have difficulty预判核心「部分学生上不了网课」，选项 Some students may have difficulty attending them 主体、动作、可能性三要素与原文一一对位。
D) 张冠李戴：把人替换成机构Schools with limited resources will be at a disadvantage. 把 at a disadvantage的主体换成 schools，但 some students can be put at a disadvantage 明确主语是 students。
questions.quote: Not all students have access to these types of resources, whether it is for financial or other reasons, and some students can be put at a disadvantage.

options.text: More students may find it easy to be absent from them.
Teachers will worry about poor internet connections.
Some students may have difficulty attending them.
Schools with limited resources will be at a disadvantage.

questions.prompt: What does the author think constitutes a key part of genuine education?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者认为什么构成了真正教育的关键部分?
A) 获取有用的知识。
B) 在校园进行实际生活技能的训练。
C) 发展学生的个性。
D) 培养分析思维能力。
**判型** What does the author think constitutes a key part of genuine education? 仍是问作者明示的具体内容，文末已直接点出，无需推断。
**拆句** 题干主干 What does the author think X constitutes Y，think 后为宾语从句，从句里What 同时是 constitutes 的主语，constitutes = 构成；该结构需要把 What 还原到从句主语位才能读顺，是四级长难句的小考点。
**定位** 然而，网课未能提供真正的教育，因为它强调便利而非批判性思维。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全：用常识替代作者主张Acquisition of useful knowledge. 把「真教育」化约为「获取有用知识」，但 P8 强调的是思维而非知识，且原文也未把「有用知识」列为真教育的关键。
B) 无中生有：用文章主题的相邻概念造干扰Training of real-life skills on campus. 强调「校园里」「真实生活技能」两个限定，但P8 既未谈 real-life skills 也未谈 on campus，是利用「网课—线下」对立常识捏造的对立项。
C) 无中生有：搬用流行教育口号Development of students' personalities. 把真教育的关键说成「学生人格的发展」，原文 P8 通篇未涉及 personalities/character 之类的人格概念。
D) ✓ 正确critical thinking↔analytical thinking ability预判核心是 critical thinking，四个选项里只有 Cultivation of analytical thinking ability. 直接对应 critical thinking 的同义改写，故锁定。
questions.quote: However, they fail to provide a genuine education with an emphasis on convenience rather than critical thinking.

options.text: Acquisition of useful knowledge.
Training of real-life skills on campus.
Development of students' personalities.
Cultivation of analytical thinking ability.

title: You might think of your teeth as tools,…

sentences.text: You might think of your teeth as tools, like built-in knives and forks, but if they are mere tools, why do they feel pain and wouldn't it be better if they could just (26)____ under any condition?
In spite of our (27)____ discomfort, it turns out there's a good reason our teeth are so sensitive.
Tooth pain is a (28)____ mechanism that ensures when a tooth is being damaged we'll notice and do something about it.

passage.translation: 你可能会把牙齿看作工具，就像内置的刀叉一样，但如果它们仅仅是工具，为什么会感到疼痛呢？如果它们能在任何条件下咀嚼，岂不是更好？尽管我们有牙齿不适，但事实证明我们的牙齿如此敏感是有充分理由的。牙痛是一种防御机制，确保当牙齿受到损伤时我们会注意到并采取措施。

sentences.text: If we eat something too hot or too cold, or if the tooth is worn down enough where the tissue(29)____ is exposed, all of those things cause pain, and then the pain causes the person not to use that tooth to try to protect it a little bit more.
So it's really a protective mechanism more than anything else.
If teeth didn't feel pain, we might (30)____ to use them in situations that damage them, and for humans, damaging (31)____ teeth is a problem because, unlike crocodiles, we can't (32)____ them.

passage.translation: 如果我们吃的东西太烫或太冷，或者如果牙齿磨损到足以暴露下面的组织，所有这些都会引起疼痛，然后疼痛会导致人不使用那颗牙齿，试图更多地保护它。所以这实际上更多是一种保护机制。如果牙齿感觉不到疼痛，我们可能会在损害它们的情况下继续使用它们，而对人类来说，损坏成年牙齿是个问题，因为与鳄鱼不同，我们无法替换它们。

sentences.text: Teeth have three layers, only one of which—the innermost layer of the tooth—can hurt, as that layer of the tooth (33)____ both blood vessels and nerves.
Pain is the only feeling to which the nerves in that layer respond.
Whereas people with tooth sensitivity may complain, for example, of tooth pain(34)____ by heat or cold, the nerves in the inner layer don't sense temperature.
Rather, they feel pain, which may be (35)____ with, say, drinking something very cold.

passage.translation: 牙齿有三层，其中只有一层——牙齿的最内层——会疼痛，因为牙齿的这一层既包含血管也包含神经。疼痛是这一层神经唯一会做出反应的感觉。虽然牙齿敏感的人可能会抱怨，例如，由冷热引发的牙痛,但内层的神经并不感知温度。相反，它们感受疼痛，这种疼痛可能与喝非常冷的东西等情况有关。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
You might think of your teeth as tools, like built-in knives and forks, but if they are mere tools, why do they feel pain and wouldn't it be better if they could just {{26}} under any condition? In spite of our {{27}} discomfort, it turns out there's a good reason our teeth are so sensitive. Tooth pain is a {{28}} mechanism that ensures when a tooth is being damaged we'll notice and do something about it.

If we eat something too hot or too cold, or if the tooth is worn down enough where the tissue{{29}} is exposed, all of those things cause pain, and then the pain causes the person not to use that tooth to try to protect it a little bit more. So it's really a protective mechanism more than anything else. If teeth didn't feel pain, we might {{30}} to use them in situations that damage them, and for humans, damaging {{31}} teeth is a problem because, unlike crocodiles, we can't {{32}} them.

Teeth have three layers, only one of which—the innermost layer of the tooth—can hurt, as that layer of the tooth {{33}} both blood vessels and nerves. Pain is the only feeling to which the nerves in that layer respond. Whereas people with tooth sensitivity may complain, for example, of tooth pain{{34}} by heat or cold, the nerves in the inner layer don't sense temperature. Rather, they feel pain, which may be {{35}} with, say, drinking something very cold.

emotional
associated
implies

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) chew 动词
**词性槽** 情态动词 could 后接动词原形
**依据** 把牙比作刀叉，自然就是"咀嚼"上文 You might think of your teeth as tools, like built-in knives and forks把牙比作刀叉，刀叉是用来切割食物、对应牙齿的功能正是咀嚼。"如果牙不痛、能在任何情况下随便____"——填 chew（咀嚼）最贴合牙齿"工具"的本职。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) continue 语义空泛、接不上刀叉的比喻could just continue（只是继续）缺少明确对象，对不上前文把牙比作"刀叉"这个咀嚼工具的语境。
M) swallow 义偏，刀叉不"吞" swallow 是"吞咽"，主语是喉咙而非牙齿；把牙比作刀叉强调的是咀嚼切割，不是吞咽，故不选。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) dental 形容词
**词性槽** 物主代词 our 与名词 discomfort 之间作定语
**依据** dental discomfort=牙齿带来的不适，扣牙痛主题全文讲牙痛，In spite of our dental discomfort——"尽管我们有牙齿带来的不适"，dental（牙齿的）修饰 discomfort 正好点出不适来自牙齿，与全文主题一致。

**答案** F) defense 名词
**词性槽** 冠词 a 与名词 mechanism 之间作定语的名词
**依据** defense mechanism 固定说法 + 紧扣"保护"主旨defense mechanism（防御机制）是地道固定搭配，且下文反复点明 So it's really a protective mechanism more than anything else，"防御=保护"正好呼应。牙痛是一种"防御机制"，主旨契合度最高。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
I) emotional 义偏，与"保护牙齿"主旨冲突emotional mechanism（情感机制）说的是情绪，而本文讲的是牙痛"保护牙齿"的生理防御功能，与情感无关；下文 protective mechanism 也证明该填"防御/保护"类词，故排除。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) underneath 形容词
**词性槽** 名词 tissue 后作后置定语
**依据** the tissue underneath=下面（深层）的组织，对应"磨损露出内层"句意是牙"磨损到 ____ 的组织暴露出来"。underneath 作后置定语表"在下面的"，the tissue underneath 即"下层组织"，牙被磨损后露出的正是深层组织，与第三段"内层有神经会痛"一致。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) downward 义偏"向下运动"，不表静态位置downward 强调"朝下的方向/运动"（如 a downward trend），不用来表示"位于下方的"静态组织。the tissue downward 不通，故选表静态方位的 underneath。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— downward 与 underneath 都含"下"义，易选错。空 29要的是"下面的组织"，downward 也带"向下"且词性可作定语，迷惑性高；防坑：要的是静态"位于下方"用 underneath，downward 表运动方向，记住"方向词≠方位词"。

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) continue 动词
**词性槽** 情态动词 might 后接动词原形
**依据** continue to do 搭配成立 + 逻辑通：会"继续"用受损的牙句意是"如果牙不会痛，我们可能会 ____ 在伤牙的情况下用它们"。continue to use（继续使用）搭配地道，逻辑也对——没有痛感的警示，人就会继续乱用牙导致受损，正好呼应主旨"疼痛是保护机制"。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) swallow 搭配不成立、语义不通swallow to use 搭配不存在（swallow 后不接 to do 表此意），且"吞咽去使用牙齿"语义荒谬，与上下文"继续用受损的牙"完全对不上。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) adult 形容词
**词性槽** 名词 teeth 前作定语的修饰语
**依据** adult teeth=恒牙，对应"换不了牙"的难题adult teeth 指"恒牙（成年人的牙）"。紧接下句 unlike crocodiles, we can't replace them——恒牙坏了换不了，所以"damaging adult teeth is a problem"，逻辑完整。adult 在这里取"成年的、恒久的"义，正好与"不可替换"对应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
G) dental 语义冗余：dental 本就是"牙的"，修饰 teeth 重复dental 意为"牙齿的"，dental teeth（牙齿的牙齿）语义重复、不通；况且 dental 已是空 27 "dental discomfort"的答案，按"用过即划"也不能再用。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) replace 动词
**词性槽** 情态动词 can't 后必跟动词原形
**依据** 对比鳄鱼"换牙"，人类不能"替换"牙齿上文说牙受损是个问题，紧接 unlike crocodiles, we can't __(32)__ them：鳄鱼牙掉了能长新的，而人"不能 ____它们"。能与"鳄鱼能、人不能"这层对比对上的只有 replace（替换牙齿），逻辑正好解释了为什么"damaging adult teeth is a problem"。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) chew 与上下文逻辑相反we can't chew them（不能咀嚼牙齿）说不通，牙是用来咀嚼食物的，不是被咀嚼的对象，且与"鳄鱼"的对比毫无关系。
E) continue 搭配与语义都不成立we can't continue them 意思含糊（无法继续它们？），既接不上 them=牙齿这个宾语的逻辑，也对不上"鳄鱼能换牙"的对比。
M) swallow 义不对，与对比脱节swallow them（吞下牙齿）与"damaging adult teeth is a problem"的因果完全无关，纯属误填。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) contains 动词
**词性槽** 主语后缺谓语，需第三人称单数动词
**依据** 形态唯一 + 语义吻合：内层"含有"血管和神经that layer of the tooth __(33)__ both blood vessels and nerves——牙的内层"含有"血管和神经，contains（含有）与宾语 blood vessels and nerves 搭配自然，且为单三形式，主谓一致，是唯一答案。

**答案** N) triggered 形容词
**词性槽** 名词 pain 后作后置定语的过去分词
**依据** triggered by=由……引发，与"冷热"作诱因搭配pain triggered by heat or cold——"由冷热引发的疼痛"。triggered by 表"被……触发/引发"，heat or cold 是疼痛的直接诱因，搭配精准、语义通顺。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) associated associated with 而非 associated by associated 的固定搭配是 associated with（与……相关），不和 by 连用。这里空后是 by heat or cold，搭配不合；况且 associated 更适合空 35 的 associated with，此处该选 triggered。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 B) —— associated 与 triggered 都表"相关/引发"，极易混填。空34 pain __(34)__ by heat or cold里，associated（相关的）词性也对、词义也沾"与冷热有关"，看着也通；防坑：associated 只搭 with、不搭 by，空后是 by 就必须选triggered，把这对词的固定介词背死。

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) associated 形容词
**词性槽** be 动词 + 空 + with，需过去分词作表语
**依据** be associated with=与……相关联，固定搭配 + 余下唯一候选be associated with 是地道固定搭配，表"与……相关"。they feel pain, which may be associated with, say, drinking something very cold——这种痛"可能与喝很凉的东西相关"，语义通顺，且空后正是 with，搭配完全吻合。

title: Why it matters that teens are reading less

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Most of us spend much more time with digital media than we did a decade ago.
But today's teens have grown up with smartphones.
Compared with teens a couple of decades ago, the way they interact with traditional media like books and movies is fundamentally different.

passage.translation: 我们大多数人使用数字媒体的时间比十年前多得多。但今天的青少年是伴随着智能手机成长起来的。与几十年前的青少年相比，他们与书籍和电影等传统媒体互动的方式有着根本性的不同。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: Analysis of surveys of over one million teens in the United States collected since 1976 reveals a major shift in how teens are spending their leisure time.
Paper books are being ignored, in favor of screens.
Digital devices are changing other behaviors, too.
More and more, young people choose spending time on their electronic devices over engaging in other activities, regardless of the type.
Indeed, by 2016, the average American high school senior said they spent six hours a day writing text messages, on social media, and online during their free time.
And that covers just three activities, and if other digital media activities were included, that estimate would no doubt rise.

passage.translation: 对自1976年以来在美国收集的超过一百万青少年的调查分析揭示了青少年消磨闲暇时间方式的重大转变。纸质书籍正被忽视，人们转而青睐屏幕。数字设备也在改变其他行为。越来越多的年轻人选择把时间花在电子设备上，而不是参与其他活动，无论活动类型如何。事实上,到2016年,美国高中毕业班学生平均表示他们每天在空闲时间花六个小时发短信、使用社交媒体和上网。而这只涵盖三种活动,如果包括其他数字媒体活动,这一估计无疑会上升。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: Teens did not always spend that much time with digital media.
Online time has doubled since 2006, and social media use has moved from a periodic activity to a daily one in the same period.
By 2016, nearly nine out of ten young women in the 12th grade said they visited social media sites every day.
Meanwhile, time spent playing video games rose from under an hour a day to an hour and a half on average.
One out of ten American 8th grade students in 2016 spent 40 hours a week or more playing video games.
Let me emphasize that this is equal to the time most adults spend per week at work.

passage.translation: 青少年并非一直在数字媒体上花费那么多时间。自2006年以来,上网时间翻了一番,社交媒体的使用在同一时期从偶尔为之的活动变成了每日活动。到2016年,12年级的年轻女性中近十分之九表示她们每天访问社交媒体网站。与此同时,玩电子游戏的时间从每天不到一小时增加到平均一个半小时。2016年,十分之一的美国8年级学生每周玩电子游戏40小时或更长时间。让我强调一下,这相当于大多数成年人每周的工作时间。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: If teens are spending so much time using electronic devices, does that mean they have to give up some other activities?
Maybe not.
Over the years, many scholars have insisted that time online does not necessarily take away time spent engaging with traditional media or on other activities.
Some people, they argue, are just more interested in certain kinds of media and entertainment.
Thus, using more of one type of media does not necessarily mean less of the other.

passage.translation: 如果青少年花那么多时间使用电子设备,这是否意味着他们不得不放弃其他一些活动?也许不是。多年来,许多学者坚持认为,上网时间不一定会占用参与传统媒体或其他活动的时间。他们认为,有些人只是对某些类型的媒体和娱乐更感兴趣。因此,更多地使用一种类型的媒体并不一定意味着减少使用另一种。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: That may be true, but that still does not tell us much about what happens across a whole generation of people when time spent on digital media grows.
Large surveys conducted over the course of many years tell us that American youth are not going to the cinema nearly as often as they did in the past.
While 70 percent of 8th and 10th grade students used to go to the movies once a month or more, now only about half do this.
More and more, watching a movie is something teens choose to do on their electronic devices.
Why is this a problem?
One reason is that going to the cinema is generally a social activity.
Now, watching movies is something that most teens do alone.
This fits a larger pattern.
In another analysis, researchers found that today's teens go out with their friends much less often than previous generations did.

passage.translation: 这也许是对的,但这仍然没有告诉我们当整整一代人在数字媒体上花费的时间增长时会发生什么。多年来进行的大型调查告诉我们,美国年轻人去电影院的频率远不如过去。虽然过去70%的8年级和10年级学生每月至少去看一次电影,但现在只有大约一半的人这样做。越来越多的青少年选择在他们的电子设备上看电影。为什么这是一个问题?原因之一是去电影院通常是一种社交活动。现在,看电影是大多数青少年独自做的事情。这符合一个更大的模式。在另一项分析中,研究人员发现,今天的青少年与朋友外出的频率远低于前几代人。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: But the trends related to movies are less disturbing compared with the change in how teens spend their time.
Research has revealed an enormous decline in reading.
In 1980, about 60 percent of senior high school students said they read a book, newspaper or magazine every day that was not assigned for school.
By 2016, only 16 percent did.
This is a huge drop and it is important to note that this was not merely a decline in reading paper books, newspapers or magazines.
The survey allowed for reading materials on a digital device.

passage.translation: 但与电影相关的趋势与青少年时间分配方式的变化相比,令人不安的程度要轻一些。研究揭示了阅读量的巨大下降。1980年,大约60%的高中毕业班学生表示他们每天阅读一本书、报纸或杂志,而这些不是学校布置的作业。到2016年,只有16%的人这样做。这是一个巨大的下降,值得注意的是,这不仅仅是纸质书籍、报纸或杂志阅读量的下降。该调查允许在数字设备上阅读材料。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: Indeed, the number of senior high school students who said they had not read any books for pleasure in the last year was one out of three by 2016.
That is triple the number from two decades ago.
For today's youth, books, newspapers and magazines have less and less of a presence in their daily lives.
Of course, teens are still reading.
But they are generally reading short texts.
Most of them are not reading long articles or books that explore deep themes and require critical thinking and reflection.
Perhaps not accidentally, in 2016 reading scores were the lowest they have ever been since 1972.

passage.translation: 事实上,到2016年,表示在过去一年中没有读过任何消遣书籍的高中毕业班学生人数达到三分之一。这是二十年前数字的三倍。对于今天的年轻人来说,书籍、报纸和杂志在他们的日常生活中越来越缺乏存在感。当然,青少年仍在阅读。但他们通常阅读的是短文本。他们中的大多数人没有阅读探讨深层主题、需要批判性思维和反思的长篇文章或书籍。也许并非偶然,2016年的阅读成绩是自1972年以来的最低水平。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: This might present problems for young people later on.
When high school students go on to college, their past and current reading habits will influence their academic performance.
Imagine going from reading texts as short as one or two sentences to trying to read entire books written in complex language and containing sophisticated ideas.
Reading and comprehending longer books and chapters takes practice, and American teens are no longer getting that practice.

passage.translation: 这可能会给年轻人日后带来问题。当高中生进入大学时,他们过去和现在的阅读习惯将影响他们的学业表现。想象一下,从阅读短至一两句话的文本到试图阅读用复杂语言写成、包含深奥思想的整本书。阅读和理解较长的书籍和章节需要练习,而美国青少年不再进行这种练习。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: So how can this problem be solved?
Should parents and teachers take away teens' smartphones and replace them with paper books?
Probably not.
Research has shown that smartphones are currently American teens' main form of social communication.
This means that, without a smartphone, teens are likely to feel isolated from their peers.
However, that does not mean teens need to use electronic devices as often as they do now.

Data connecting excessive digital media time to mental health issues suggests a limit of two hours a day of free time spent with screens, a restriction that will also allow time for other activities—like going to the movies with friends or reading longer, more complicated texts.

passage.translation: 那么如何解决这个问题呢?父母和教师应该拿走青少年的智能手机并用纸质书籍替换吗?可能不行。研究表明,智能手机目前是美国青少年社交交流的主要形式。这意味着,没有智能手机,青少年很可能会感到与同龄人隔绝。然而,这并不意味着青少年需要像现在这样频繁地使用电子设备。将过度使用数字媒体时间与心理健康问题联系起来的数据表明,空闲时间使用屏幕的时间应限制在每天两小时,这一限制也将为其他活动留出时间——比如和朋友去看电影或阅读更长、更复杂的文本。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: The latter is especially important.

I would argue that of all the changes brought about by the widespread use of digital devices, the huge decline in reading is likely to have the biggest negative impact on today's teens because reading books and longer articles is one of the best ways to learn critical thinking.
It helps people to understand complex issues and to separate fact from fiction.
Thus, deep reading is crucial for being a good citizen, a successful college student and a productive employee.
If serious reading dies, a lot will go with it.

passage.translation: 后者尤其重要。我认为,在数字设备广泛使用带来的所有变化中,阅读量的大幅下降可能对今天的青少年产生最大的负面影响,因为阅读书籍和较长的文章是学习批判性思维的最佳方式之一。它帮助人们理解复杂问题并区分事实与虚构。因此,深度阅读对于成为一个好公民、一个成功的大学生和一个高效的员工至关重要。如果严肃阅读消亡,许多东西也将随之消失。
