儿童需要付出巨大努力才能掌握数词的概念。
**锚点** 孩子掌握数字词需付出巨大努力
**定位** 事实上，孩子要真正掌握数字词的确切含义，是一个让他们要花上数年的艰苦过程。
**改写** It takes great efforts for children ↔ a painstaking process that takes children years “painstaking + takes years”=“great efforts”grasp the concept of number words ↔ acquiring the exact meaning of number words动词同义替换
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
G Number words and their written forms transform our quantitative reasoning as they are introduced into our cognitive experience by our parents, peers and school teachers虽然提及孩子的学习来源，但落点在“后天获得”，并未刻画孩子掌握数字词的“数年艰辛”。Number words and their written forms transform our quantitative reasoning as they are introduced into our cognitive experience by our parents, peers and school teachers.
questions.quote: In fact, acquiring the exact meaning of number words is a painstaking process that takes children years.

title: The start of high school doesn't have to be stressful

passage.label: A

sentences.text: This month, more than 4 million students across the nation will begin high school.
Many will do well.
But many will not.
Consider that nearly two-thirds of students will experience the "ninth-grade shock," which refers to a dramatic drop in a student's academic performance.
Some students cope with this shock by avoiding challenges.
For instance, they may drop difficult coursework.
Others may experience a hopelessness that results in failing their core classes, such as English, science and math.

passage.translation: 本月,全国将有超过400万学生开始高中生活。许多人会表现良好,但许多人不会。考虑到近三分之二的学生将经历"九年级冲击",这指的是学生学业表现的急剧下降。一些学生通过逃避挑战来应对这种冲击。例如,他们可能会放弃困难的课程。其他人可能会经历一种绝望感,导致他们的核心课程(如英语、科学和数学)不及格。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: This should matter a great deal to parents, teachers and policymakers.

Ultimately it should matter to the students themselves and society at large, because students' experience of transitioning(过渡) to the ninth grade can have long-term consequences not only for the students themselves but for their home communities.
We make these observations as research psychologists who have studied how schools and families can help young people thrive.

passage.translation: 这对家长、教师和政策制定者来说应该非常重要。最终它应该对学生自己和整个社会都很重要,因为学生过渡到九年级的经历不仅对学生自己,而且对他们的家庭社区都可能产生长期影响。我们作为研究学校和家庭如何帮助年轻人茁壮成长的心理学研究者提出这些观察结果。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: In the new global economy, students who fail to finish the ninth grade with passing grades in college preparatory coursework are very unlikely to graduate on time and go on to get jobs.
One study has calculated that the lifetime benefit to the local economy for a single additional student who completes high school is half a million dollars or more.
This is based on higher earnings and avoided costs in health care, crime, welfare dependence and other things.

passage.translation: 在新的全球经济中,未能以合格成绩完成九年级大学预备课程的学生极不可能按时毕业并继续找到工作。一项研究计算出,一个额外完成高中学业的学生为当地经济带来的终身收益是50万美元或更多。这是基于更高的收入以及在医疗保健、犯罪、福利依赖和其他方面避免的成本。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: The consequences of doing poorly in the ninth grade can impact more than students' ability to find a good job.
It can also impact the extent to which they enjoy life.
Students lose many of the friends they turned to for support when they move from the eighth to the ninth grade.
One study of ninth- grade students found that 50 percent of friendships among ninth graders changed from one month to the next, signaling striking instability in friendships.

passage.translation: 九年级表现不佳的后果不仅影响学生找到好工作的能力,还可能影响他们享受生活的程度。当学生从八年级升入九年级时,他们失去了许多曾经寻求支持的朋友。一项关于九年级学生的研究发现,50%的九年级学生友谊每月都在变化,这表明友谊的显著不稳定性。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: In addition, studies find the first year of high school typically shows one of the greatest increases in depression of any year over the lifespan.
Researchers think that one explanation is that ties to friends are broken while academic demands are rising.
Furthermore, most adult cases of clinical depression first emerge in adolescence(⻘春期).
The World Health Organization reports that depression has the greatest burden of disease worldwide, in terms of the total cost of treatment and the loss of productivity.

passage.translation: 此外,研究发现高中第一年通常显示出人一生中抑郁症增长最显著的时期之一。研究人员认为,一个解释是与朋友的联系被打破,而学业要求却在上升。此外,大多数成人临床抑郁症病例首次出现在青春期。世界卫生组织报告称,就治疗总成本和生产力损失而言,抑郁症在全球范围内具有最大的疾病负担。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: Given all that's riding on having a successful ninth grade experience, it pays to explore what can be done to meet the academic, social and emotional challenges of the transition to high school.

So far, our studies have yielded one main insight: Students' beliefs about change—their beliefs about whether people are stuck one way forever, or whether people can change their personalities and abilities—are related to their ability to cope, succeed academically and maintain good mental health.

Past research has called these beliefs "mindsets(思维模式)," with a "fixed mindset" referring to the belief that people cannot change and a "growth mindset" referring to the belief that people can change.

passage.translation: 鉴于成功的九年级经历关系重大,探索可以做些什么来应对过渡到高中的学业、社交和情感挑战是值得的。到目前为止,我们的研究产生了一个主要见解:学生关于变化的信念——他们关于人是否永远固定不变,还是人可以改变其性格和能力的信念——与他们应对、学业成功和保持良好心理健康的能力有关。过去的研究将这些信念称为"思维模式",其中"固定型思维模式"指的是人们不能改变的信念,"成长型思维模式"指的是人们可以改变的信念。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: In one recent study, we examined 360 adolescents' beliefs about the nature of "smartness"—that is, their fixed mindsets about intelligence.
We then assessed biological stress responses for students whose grades were dropping by examining their stress hormones(荷尔蒙).

Students who believed that intelligence is fixed—that you are stuck being "not smart" if you struggle in school—showed higher levels of stress hormones when their grades were declining at the beginning of the ninth grade.

If students believed that intelligence could improve—that is to say, when they held more of a growth mindset of intelligence—they showed lower levels of stress hormones when their grades were declining.
This was an exciting result because it showed that the body's stress responses are not determined solely by one's grades.
Instead, declining grades only predicted worse stress hormones among students who believed that worsening grades were a permanent and hopeless state of affairs.

passage.translation: 在最近的一项研究中,我们考察了360名青少年关于"聪明"本质的信念——即他们关于智力的固定型思维模式。然后,我们通过检查压力荷尔蒙来评估成绩下降学生的生物压力反应。那些相信智力是固定的学生——即如果你在学校学习困难,你就会一直"不聪明"——在九年级开始时成绩下降时显示出更高水平的压力荷尔蒙。如果学生相信智力可以提高——也就是说,当他们对智力持有更多成长型思维模式时——他们在成绩下降时显示出较低水平的压力荷尔蒙。这是一个令人兴奋的结果,因为它表明身体的压力反应并非完全由一个人的成绩决定。相反,成绩下降只在那些相信成绩恶化是一种永久且无望的状态的学生中预示着更糟糕的压力荷尔蒙。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: We also investigated the social side of the high school transition.
In this study, instead of teaching students that their smartness can change, we taught them that their social standing—that is, whether they are bullied or excluded or left out—can change over time.
We then looked at high school students' stress responses to daily social difficulties.
That is, we taught them a growth mindset about their social lives.
In this study, students came into the laboratory and were asked to give a public speech in front of upper-year students.
The topic of the speech was what makes one popular in high school.
Following this, students had to complete a difficult mental math task in front of the same upper-year students.

passage.translation: 我们还调查了高中过渡的社交方面。在这项研究中,我们没有教学生他们的聪明才智可以改变,而是教他们他们的社交地位——即他们是否被欺凌、排斥或冷落——可以随时间改变。然后我们观察了高中生对日常社交困难的压力反应。也就是说,我们教给他们关于社交生活的成长型思维模式。在这项研究中,学生来到实验室,被要求在高年级学生面前发表公开演讲。演讲的主题是什么使一个人在高中受欢迎。在此之后,学生必须在同样的高年级学生面前完成一项困难的心算任务。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Experiment results showed that students who were not taught that people can change showed poor stress responses.

When these students gave the speech, their blood vessels contracted and their hearts pumped less blood through the body—both responses that the body shows when it is preparing for damage or defeat after a physical threat.
Then they gave worse speeches and made more mistakes in math.
But when students were taught that people can change, they had better responses to stress, in part because they felt like they had the resources to deal with the demanding situation.

Students who got the growth mindset intervention(干预) showed less-contracted blood vessels and their hearts pumped more blood—both of which contributed to more oxygen getting to the brain, and, ultimately, better performance on the speech and mental math tasks.

passage.translation: 实验结果显示,没有被教导人可以改变的学生表现出不良的压力反应。当这些学生发表演讲时,他们的血管收缩,心脏泵送的血液减少——这两种反应都是身体在遭受身体威胁后为损伤或失败做准备时表现出的。然后他们的演讲更差,数学错误更多。但当学生被教导人可以改变时,他们对压力有更好的反应,部分原因是他们觉得自己有资源来应对这种要求高的情况。接受成长型思维模式干预的学生显示出较少收缩的血管,他们的心脏泵送更多血液——这两者都有助于更多氧气到达大脑,并最终在演讲和心算任务上取得更好的表现。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: These findings lead to several possibilities that we are investigating further.
First, we are working to replicate(复制) these findings in more diverse school communities.
We want to know in which types of schools and for which kinds of students these growth mindset ideas help young people adapt to the challenges of high school.
We also hope to learn how teachers, parents or school counselors can help students keep their ongoing academic or social difficulties in perspective.

We wonder what would happen if schools helped to make beliefs about the potential for change and improvement a larger feature of the overall school culture, especially for students starting the ninth grade.

passage.translation: 这些发现带来了我们正在进一步调查的几种可能性。首先,我们正在努力在更多样化的学校社区中复制这些发现。我们想知道在哪些类型的学校以及对哪些类型的学生,这些成长型思维模式理念能帮助年轻人适应高中的挑战。我们还希望了解教师、家长或学校辅导员如何帮助学生正确看待他们持续的学业或社交困难。我们想知道,如果学校帮助使关于变化和改进潜力的信念成为整体学校文化的一个更大特征,尤其是对于刚开始九年级的学生,会发生什么。

questions.prompt: In one study, students were told their social position in school is not unchangeable.
questions.explanation:
**答案** H 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
在一项研究中,学生被告知他们在学校的社会地位并非一成不变。
**锚点** 被告知其在校的社交地位并非不可改变
**定位** 我们告诉他们，他们的社交地位——也就是说，他们是否被霸凌、被排斥或被冷落——是可以随时间改变的。
**改写** students were told ↔ we taught them被告知=我们教他们their social position in school ↔ their social standing校内社交位置=社交地位is not unchangeable ↔ can change over time并非不可改变=可以随时间改变
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
F F段讨论的是whether people can change their personalities and abilities，并未提及social standing或bully/exclude等具体社交内容。a "growth mindset" referring to the belief that people can change
questions.quote: we taught them that their social standing—that is, whether they are bullied or excluded or left out—can change over time

questions.prompt: It is reported that depression results in enormous economic losses worldwide.
questions.explanation:
**答案** E 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
据报道,抑郁症在全球造成巨大的经济损失。
**锚点** 抑郁造成全球巨大经济损失
**定位** 世界卫生组织报告称，抑郁是全球疾病负担最重的，体现在治疗的总成本和生产力的损失上。
**改写** It is reported ↔ The World Health Organization reports被动据报道=具名机构的reports depression results in enormous economic losses ↔depression has the greatest burden of disease worldwide, in terms of the total cost of treatment and the loss of productivity巨大经济损失=治疗成本+生产力损失这一负担worldwide ↔ worldwide原样复现
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
C C段讨论the lifetime benefit to the local economy，是单个学生对地方经济的正向贡献，与全球性的经济损失方向相反。the lifetime benefit to the local economy for a single additional student who completes high school is half a million dollars or more
questions.quote: The World Health Organization reports that depression has the greatest burden of disease worldwide, in terms of the total cost of treatment and the loss of productivity.

questions.prompt: One study showed that friendships among ninth graders were far from stable.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
一项研究显示,九年级学生之间的友谊远非稳定。
**锚点** 九年级生友谊远谈不上稳定
**定位** 一项针对九年级学生的研究发现，九年级生之间百分之五十的友谊在前后两个月间发生了变化，显示出友谊明显的不稳定。
**改写** friendships among ninth graders ↔ friendships among ninth graders原样复现far from stable ↔ striking instability in friendships绝非稳定=显著不稳定
questions.quote: One study of ninth-grade students found that 50 percent of friendships among ninth graders changed from one month to the next, signaling striking instability in friendships.

questions.prompt: More than half of students will find their academic performance declining sharply when they enter the ninth grade.
questions.explanation:
**答案** A 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
超过半数的学生在进入九年级时会发现自己的学业表现急剧下降。
**锚点** 过半数学生进入九年级后学业表现急剧下滑
**定位** 想想看：将近三分之二的学生会经历所谓的九年级冲击——指学生学业表现的急剧下滑。
**改写** More than half of students ↔ nearly two-thirds of students过半=接近三分之二their academic performance declining sharply ↔a dramatic drop in a student's academic performance学业表现急剧下滑=学业表现显著下降when they enter the ninth grade ↔ experience the "ninth-grade shock"进入九年级即九年级冲击发生时点
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
G G段聚焦Students who believed that intelligence is fixed这一部分学生的反应，未给出涵盖整体的过半数比例。Students who believed that intelligence is fixed—that you are stuck being "not smart" if you struggle in school—showed higher levels of stress hormones when their grades were declining at the beginning of the ninth grade
questions.quote: Consider that nearly two-thirds of students will experience the "ninth-grade shock," which refers to a dramatic drop in a student's academic performance.

questions.prompt: Researchers found through experiments that students could be taught to respond to stress in a more positive way.
questions.explanation:
**答案** I 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
研究人员通过实验发现,可以教会学生以更积极的方式应对压力。
**锚点** 实验发现学生可被教导以更积极方式应对压力
**定位** 但是当学生被教导人可以改变时，他们对压力的反应变得更好，部分原因在于他们感到自己拥有应对挑战情境的资源。
**改写** through experiments ↔ Experiment results showed that通过实验=实验结果显示students could be taught ↔ when students were taught可以被教导=被教导这一假设条件respond to stress in a more positive way ↔ they had better responses to stress更积极方式应对压力=对压力的反应更好
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
H H段交代的是研究流程：students came into the laboratory and were asked to give a public speech，并未陈述更好的压力反应这一结果。we taught them a growth mindset about their social lives G G段考察的是学生原本就持有的信念差异下的反应，关键句是If students believed that intelligence could improve，并未实施教导干预。If students believed that intelligence could improve—that is to say, when they held more of a growth mindset of intelligence—they showed lower levels of stress hormones when their grades were declining
questions.quote: But when students were taught that people can change, they had better responses to stress, in part because they felt like they had the resources to deal with the demanding situation.

questions.prompt: It is beneficial to explore ways to cope with the challenges facing students entering high school.
questions.explanation:
**答案** F 段（弱锚点）
**题目译文**
探索应对刚进入高中的学生所面临挑战的方法是有益的。
**锚点** 探索如何应对高中新生面对的挑战是有益的
**定位** 鉴于成功度过九年级这件事关乎甚多，探索能采取哪些措施以应对升入高中所带来的学业、社交和情感挑战是值得的。
**改写** It is beneficial to explore ways ↔ it pays to explore what can be done值得探索=有益地探索可做什么cope with the challenges ↔ meet the academic, social and emotional challenges应对挑战=直面学业社交情感挑战students entering high school ↔ the transition to high school进入高中的学生=向高中过渡这一过程的主体
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B段的核心表态是This should matter a great deal to parents, teachers and policymakers，关注点在该不该被重视，而非探索方法的有益性。This should matter a great deal to parents, teachers and policymakers J J段说的是研究者下一步要做什么、想知道什么，未给出beneficial这种价值判断；其表述如We want to know in which types of schools都属于具体计划。We want to know in which types of schools and for which kinds of students these growth mindset ideas help young people adapt to the challenges of high school
questions.quote: Given all that's riding on having a successful ninth grade experience, it pays to explore what can be done to meet the academic, social and emotional challenges of the transition to high school.

title: Can you remember what you ate yesterday?…

sentences.text: Can you remember what you ate yesterday?
If asked, most people will be able to give a vague description of their main meals: breakfast, lunch, dinner.
But can you be sure you've noted every snack bar in your car, or every handful of nuts at your desk?
Most people will have a feeling that they've missed something out.

passage.translation: 你能记得自己昨天吃了什么吗？如果被问到，大多数人能够给出对其主餐的模糊描述：早餐、午餐、晚餐。但你能确定自己记下了车里的每一根零食棒，或者办公桌前的每一把坚果吗？大多数人会觉得自己遗漏了一些东西。

sentences.text: We originally had this suspicion back in 2016, puzzled by the fact that national statistics showed calorie consumption falling dramatically over past decades.
We found reliable evidence that people were drastically under-reporting what they ate.

passage.translation: 我们最初在2016年就有了这种怀疑，当时对国家统计数据显示过去几十年卡路里消耗量急剧下降这一事实感到困惑。我们发现可靠证据表明，人们对自己的饮食存在严重的少报现象。

sentences.text: Now the Office for National Statistics has confirmed that we are consuming 50% more calories than our national statistics claim.

passage.translation: 现在，国家统计局已经证实，我们摄入的卡路里比国家统计数据声称的多50%。

sentences.text: Why is this happening?
We can point to at least three potential causes.
One is the rise in obesity levels itself.
Under-reporting rates are much higher for obese people, because they simply consume more food, and thus have more to remember.

passage.translation: 为什么会发生这种情况？我们至少可以指出三个潜在原因。一个是肥胖水平本身的上升。肥胖人群的少报率要高得多，因为他们摄入的食物更多，因此需要记住的也更多。

sentences.text: Another cause is that the proportion of people who are trying to lose weight has been increasing over time.
People who want to lose weight are more likely to under-report their eating—regardless of whether they are overweight or not.
This may be driven partly by self-deception or "wishful thinking".

passage.translation: 另一个原因是试图减肥的人群比例随着时间推移一直在增加。想要减肥的人更有可能少报自己的饮食——无论他们是否超重。这可能部分是由自我欺骗或"一厢情愿的想法"驱动的。

sentences.text: The final potential cause is an increase in snacking and eating out over recent decades—both in terms of how often they happen and how much they contribute to our overall energy intake.
Again, there is evidence that food consumed out of the home is one of the most poorly recorded categories in surveys.

passage.translation: 最后一个潜在原因是近几十年来吃零食和外出就餐的增加——无论是在发生频率方面还是在对我们总体能量摄入的贡献方面。同样，有证据表明，在家以外消费的食物是调查中记录最不准确的类别之一。

sentences.text: So, what's the message conveyed?
For statistics, we should invest in more accurate measurement options.
For policy, we need to focus on options that make it easy for people to eat fewer calories.
If people do not know how much they are eating, it can be really hard for them to stick to a diet.
Also, we should be looking for new ways to ensure what people eat wouldn't have much impact on their waistlines.
If this works, it won't matter if they can't remember what they ate yesterday.

passage.translation: 那么，传达的信息是什么？在统计方面，我们应该投资于更准确的测量方法。在政策方面，我们需要关注让人们更容易摄入更少卡路里的选项。如果人们不知道自己吃了多少，他们可能真的很难坚持节食。此外，我们应该寻找新方法来确保人们吃的东西不会对他们的腰围产生太大影响。如果这奏效，他们能否记得昨天吃了什么就不重要了。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What did the author suspect back in 2016?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者在2016年怀疑什么?
A) 几十年来卡路里摄入量已经大幅下降。
B) 大多数受访者不愿透露他们吃了什么。
C) 国家统计数据没有反映实际的卡路里摄入量。
D) 大多数人在报告卡路里摄入量时没有包括零食。
**判型** What did the author suspect back in 2016 问的是一个具体过去时间点上的具体事实，没有 infer/imply 之类信号词，属于事实细节题。
**拆句** 题干 What did the author suspect back in 2016? 是一个简单的特殊疑问句，主语 the author，谓语 suspect，宾语用 what 提问，back in 2016 是时间状语，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 我们最初是在 2016 年产生这种怀疑的——我们困惑于一个事实：国家统计数据显示，过去几十年里热量消费在大幅下降。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反Calorie consumption had fallen drastically over the decades. 复述的是统计数据本身的表象，作者恰恰是怀疑这个表象不可信，而非相信它。
B) 无中生有原文只说人们 drastically under-reporting——漏报，没有任何文字表明他们 reluctant to reveal——主观上不愿透露；后文第 5 段更解释为自我欺骗或愿景式思维，而非拒绝回答。
C) ✓ 正确national statistics showed calorie consumption falling dramatically over past decades↔The national statistics did not reflect the actual calorie consumption.预判落点是“统计与现实不符”，四个选项里只有 The national statistics did not reflect the actual calorie consumption. 直接说统计没有反映真实情况，与预判完全吻合。
D) 张冠李戴Most people did not include snacks when reporting their calorie intake. 接近第 1段 every snack bar in your car 和第 6 段 snacking 的内容，但那些不是 2016 年的怀疑，而是后续展开的具体机制。
questions.quote: We originally had this suspicion back in 2016, puzzled by the fact that national statistics showed calorie consumption falling dramatically over past decades.

options.text: Calorie consumption had fallen drastically over the decades.
Most people surveyed were reluctant to reveal what they ate.
The national statistics did not reflect the actual calorie consumption.
Most people did not include snacks when reporting their calorie intake.

questions.prompt: What has the Office for National Statistics verified?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
国家统计局证实了什么?
A) 人们的卡路里摄入量远未被准确报告。
B) 遗漏正餐导致了吃零食的习惯。
C) 国家的肥胖水平与卡路里摄入量有很大关系。
D) 卡路里摄入量与一个人吃零食的量有关。
**判型** What has the Office for National Statistics verified? 直问某机构核实了什么事实，无推断信号词，属事实细节题。
**拆句** 题干 What has the Office for National Statistics verified? 是现在完成时的特殊疑问句，主语是机构名，谓语 verified，结构清晰，无障碍。
**定位** 如今国家统计局已证实：我们实际摄入的热量比国家统计声称的高出 50%。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确we are consuming 50% more calories than our national statistics claim ↔People's calorie intake was far from accurately reported. People's calorie intake was far from accurately reported. 把“实际比上报高出 50%”这件事精确概括为“摄入量远未被准确上报”，与预判一一对应。
B) 无中生有The missing out of main meals leads to the habit of snacking. 把“漏掉正餐”和“养成吃零食的习惯”绑成因果，原文从未提及这种因果链——文中说的是“忘记零食”而非“漏掉正餐导致吃零食”。
C) 张冠李戴The nation's obesity level has much to do with calorie intake. 涉及肥胖与热量摄入的关系，那是第 4 段 rise in obesity levels 后面的讨论，不是国家统计局证实的内容。
D) 张冠李戴Calorie consumption is linked to the amount of snacks one eats. 类似第 6 段对零食的讨论，但那是作者推论的“潜在原因之一”，不是国家统计局已证实的事实。
questions.quote: Now the Office for National Statistics has confirmed that we are consuming 50% more calories than our national statistics claim.

options.text: People's calorie intake was far from accurately reported.
The missing out of main meals leads to the habit of snacking.
The nation's obesity level has much to do with calorie intake.
Calorie consumption is linked to the amount of snacks one eats.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about obese people from the passage?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
从文章中我们对肥胖者了解到什么?
A) 他们通常对自己的饮食习惯保密。
B) 他们忽视了肥胖的潜在原因。
C) 他们情不自禁地吃得比应该吃的多。
D) 他们难以回忆起自己吃过什么。
**判型** What do we learn about obese people from the passage? 限定主体为某类人，问关于他们的文本陈述，仍是文中明示的细节而非推断。
**拆句** 题干 What do we learn about obese people from the passage? 是 What 引导的疑问句，about obese people 限定 learn 的对象，from the passage 是出处状语，句意直白。
**定位** 肥胖人群的漏报率要高得多，因为他们吃得本来就多，需要回想的食物也就更多。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念They usually keep their eating habits a secret. 把客观上的漏报误读成主观上对外保密，原文没有任何表示故意隐瞒的字眼。
B) 张冠李戴They overlook the potential causes of obesity. 把“忽视肥胖原因”安到肥胖人群头上，但全文中“指出潜在原因”的是作者（We can point to at least three potential causes），与肥胖人群无关。
C) 过度推断They cannot help eating more than they should. 加入了 cannot help（情不自禁）和 more than they should（超出应吃的量）两个主观限制，原文只是说 simply consume more food——“就是吃得多些”，并未涉及自控力或应有量。
D) ✓ 正确they simply consume more food, and thus have more to remember ↔They have difficulty recalling what they have eaten.预判落在“记不清吃了什么”，四个选项中只有 They have difficulty recalling what they have eaten. 直接说回忆困难，与预判完美对应。
questions.quote: Under-reporting rates are much higher for obese people, because they simply consume more food, and thus have more to remember.

options.text: They usually keep their eating habits a secret.
They overlook the potential causes of obesity.
They cannot help eating more than they should.
They have difficulty recalling what they have eaten.

questions.prompt: What often goes unnoticed in surveys on food consumption?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
在食物消费调查中什么常常被忽视?
A) 外出就餐的增长趋势。
B) 吃零食的潜在原因。
C) 人们的家庭能源消耗。
D) 人们多年来不断变化的饮食。
**判型** What often goes unnoticed in surveys on food consumption? 问的是调查中常被漏掉的某个具体类别，属于事实细节而非推断。
**拆句** 题干 What often goes unnoticed in surveys on food consumption? 主语 what，goes unnoticed 是系表结构（go + 形容词，表“处于…状态”），in surveys on food consumption 是地点状语限定情境，结构无陷阱，关键要识别 go unnoticed 的固定搭配含义。
**定位** 再者，有证据表明：在家以外吃的东西，是调查中被记得最差的类别之一。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确food consumed out of the home ↔ The growing trend of eating out. an increase in snacking and eating out over recent decades ↔The growing trend of eating out.段末明确说在家外吃饭是漏报最严重的类别之一，只有 The growing trend of eating out. 把“外出就餐”作为答案给出，与定位句完全对应。
B) 答非所问题干问“调查中常被漏掉的是什么”，The potential causes of snacking. 谈的是“吃零食的潜在原因”，方向跑偏；且原文也没说零食的“原因”被漏报。
C) 偷换概念People's home energy consumption. 字面上像“家庭能源消费”，与“在家吃饭”完全是两个领域；原文谈的是 energy intake（能量摄入），不是 energy consumption（能源消费）。
D) 以偏概全People's changing diet over the years. 用“饮食习惯随年份变化”这种大词把整篇主旨偷换上来，原文段落讲的是某一类食物在调查中被漏报，不是泛泛“饮食变化”。
questions.quote: Again, there is evidence that food consumed out of the home is one of the most poorly recorded categories in surveys.

options.text: The growing trend of eating out.
The potential causes of snacking.
People's home energy consumption.
People's changing diet over the years.

questions.prompt: What does the author suggest policymakers do about obesity?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者建议政策制定者就肥胖问题采取什么措施?
A) 提醒人们减少吃零食。
B) 确保人们吃不增肥的食物。
C) 确保人们不会错过正餐。
D) 确保人们不坚持同样的饮食。
**判型** What does the author suggest policymakers do about obesity? 问作者对决策者的具体建议，文中尾段已明示，属细节题而非主旨题。
**拆句** 题干 What does the author suggest policymakers do about obesity? 是 What 引导的疑问句，谓语 suggest 后接的是省略 that 的宾语从句 policymakers do ...，从句动词用原形 do（suggest 类动词的虚拟语气），about obesity 限定建议主题。
**定位** 此外，我们应当寻找新方法，确保人们吃下去的东西不会对腰围产生多大影响。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Remind people to cut down on snacking. 让人们少吃零食，仅来自 snacking and eating out 的现象描述，文中并未在 P7 提出“提醒减少零食”这一具体政策建议。
B) ✓ 正确what people eat wouldn\'t have much impact on their waistlines↔Make sure people eat non-fattening food. Make sure people eat non-fattening food. 把“吃了不会胖到腰围”换说成“吃不发胖的食物”，是从定位句的反向角度切入同一件事——与预判正对。
C) 与原文相反Ensure people don\'t miss their main meals. 让人们别漏掉正餐，与全文主旨方向相反——文章说人们漏报、吃得多，不是吃得少，更不存在“应该多吃几顿正餐”的建议。
D) 偷换概念See that people don\'t stick to the same diet. 让人们不要长期保持同一种饮食，原文从未提及对单一饮食的看法；唯一相关的 stick to a diet 谈的是减肥者难以坚持节食，与让大众放弃单一饮食毫无关系。
questions.quote: Also, we should be looking for new ways to ensure what people eat wouldn't have much impact on their waistlines.

options.text: Remind people to cut down on snacking.
Make sure people eat non-fattening food.
Ensure people don't miss their main meals.
See that people don't stick to the same diet.

sentences.text: Boredom has become trendy.
Studies point to how boredom is good for creativity and innovation, as well as mental health.
It is found that people are more creative following the completion of a tedious task.
When people are bored, they have an increase in "associative thought"—the process of making new connections between ideas, which is linked to innovative thinking.
These studies are impressive, but in reality, the benefits of boredom may be related to having time to clear your mind, be quiet, or daydream.

passage.translation: 无聊已经成为一种趋势。研究指出无聊有益于创造力和创新，也有益于心理健康。研究发现，人们在完成一项乏味的任务后会更有创造力。当人们感到无聊时,他们的"联想思维"会增加——这是在不同想法之间建立新联系的过程,与创新思维相关。这些研究令人印象深刻,但实际上,无聊的好处可能与有时间理清思绪、保持安静或做白日梦有关。

sentences.text: In our stimulation-rich world, it seems unrealistic that boredom could occur at all.
Yet, there are valid reasons boredom may feel so painful.
As it turns out, boredom might signal the fact that you have a need that isn't being met.

passage.translation: 在我们这个刺激丰富的世界里,无聊似乎根本不可能发生。然而,无聊让人感觉如此痛苦是有正当理由的。事实证明,无聊可能预示着你有某种需求没有得到满足。

sentences.text: Our always-on world of social media may result in more connections, but they are superficial and can get in the way of building a real sense of belonging.
Feeling bored may signal the desire for a greater sense of community and the feeling that you fit in with others around you.
So take the step of joining an organization to build face-to-face relationships.
You'll find depth that you won't get from your screen no matter how many likes you get on your post.

passage.translation: 我们这个永远在线的社交媒体世界可能会带来更多联系,但这些联系是肤浅的,可能会妨碍建立真正的归属感。感到无聊可能预示着渴望获得更强的社群意识以及你与周围他人契合的感觉。因此,迈出加入一个组织的步伐,建立面对面的关系。你会发现深度,这是你无论在帖子上获得多少点赞都无法从屏幕上得到的。

sentences.text: Similar to the need for belonging, bored people often report that they feel a limited sense of meaning.
It's a fundamental human need to have a larger purpose and to feel like we're part of something bigger than ourselves.
When people are bored, they're more likely to feel less meaning in their lives.
If you want to reduce boredom and increase your sense of meaning, seek work where you can make a unique contribution, or find a cause you can support with your time and talent.

passage.translation: 与归属需求类似,感到无聊的人常常报告说他们感到意义感有限。拥有更宏大的目标并感觉自己是比自身更伟大事物的一部分,是人类的基本需求。当人们感到无聊时,他们更有可能觉得自己的生活缺乏意义。如果你想减少无聊并增强意义感,寻找你可以做出独特贡献的工作,或者找到一项你可以用时间和才能支持的事业。

sentences.text: If your definition of boredom is being quiet, mindful, and reflective, keep it up.
But if you're struggling with real boredom and the emptiness it provokes, consider whether you might seek new connections and more significant challenges.
These are the things that will genuinely relieve boredom and make you more effective in the process.

passage.translation: 如果你对无聊的定义是安静、专注和反思,那就继续保持。但如果你正在与真正的无聊及其引发的空虚感作斗争,考虑一下你是否可以寻求新的联系和更有意义的挑战。这些才是真正能够缓解无聊并让你在此过程中变得更加高效的事情。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What have studies found about boredom?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
研究发现了关于无聊的什么情况?
A) 它促进创新思维。
B) 它是做无聊任务的结果。
C) 它帮助人们与他人建立联系。
D) 它对人的心理健康有害。
**判型** 题干 What have studies found about boredom? 直接问研究的客观发现，未出现infer/imply/mainly about 等推断或主旨信号
**拆句** 现在完成时一般疑问句 What have studies found about boredom?，主干是 studies have found what about boredom；about boredom 是 found 的范围状语，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱
**定位** 研究指出无聊有益于创造力和创新（思维），也有益于心理健康。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确boredom is good for creativity and innovation ↔ It facilitates innovative thinking.预判的「无聊带来好处+创新」两要素在 It facilitates innovative thinking. 中都被精确还原——facilitates 对应 is good for，innovative thinking 对应 creativity and innovation
B) 与原文相反原文说 people are more creative following the completion of a tedious task——是完成无聊任务之后人更有创造力，并非无聊本身是做无聊任务的结果；It is a result of doing boring tasks. 把因果方向倒过来，是典型的与原文相反
C) 无中生有P1 谈的是无聊与创造力、创新、心理健康的关系，未提及无聊「帮人和他人连接」；It helps people connect with others. 的内容在 P1 中没有任何对应句
D) 与原文相反原文明确说无聊 as well as mental health（与心理健康并列在 good for 之后，意为对心理健康有益），It does harm to one's mental health. 说的是「有害」——评价极性完全反转
questions.quote: Studies point to how boredom is good for creativity and innovation, as well as mental health.

options.text: It facilitates innovative thinking.
It is a result of doing boring tasks.
It helps people connect with others.
It does harm to one's mental health.

questions.prompt: What does the author say boredom might indicate?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者说无聊可能表明什么?
A) 需要独处。
B) 渴望得到满足。
C) 需要解决的冲突。
D) 需要被认可的感受。
**判型** 题干 What does the author say boredom might indicate? 是对作者陈述的直接发问，无推断或主旨信号
**拆句** 宾语从句 What does the author say boredom might indicate?，主句 the author say +宾语从句 boredom might indicate what；what 是宾语从句里 indicate 的宾语前移；结构常见，无陷阱
**定位** 事实证明，无聊可能是在告诉你：你有一种需求没有被满足。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有原文未提「希望独处」；A need to be left alone. 是把后文 P3 关于「真实连接」的话题反向推断出来的伪命题，但 P2 中根本没有这层意思
B) ✓ 正确a need that isn't being met ↔ A desire to be fulfilled.预判的「需求+未被满足」两要素被 A desire to be fulfilled. 完整保留——desire 替换need，to be fulfilled 替换被动定语从句
C) 偷换概念A conflict to be resolved. 谈「冲突」，但 P2 全段未提任何 conflict（冲突）的概念——need 是「需求」不是「冲突」，两者不能等同
D) 偷换概念A feeling to be validated. 说「需要被确认的感觉」，但原文说的是「需求未被满足」——「确认感觉」与「满足需求」不是一回事；validate 与 meet 不能等价替换
questions.quote: As it turns out, boredom might signal the fact that you have a need that isn't being met.

options.text: A need to be left alone.
A desire to be fulfilled.
A conflict to be resolved.
A feeling to be validated.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about social media from the passage?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
从文章中我们了解到关于社交媒体的什么情况?
A) 它可能是拓展人际关系的障碍。
B) 它可能妨碍提升社会地位。
C) 它可能阻碍人们培养真正的社群归属感。
D) 它可能使人们觉得自己应该融入外部世界。
**判型** 题干 What do we learn about social media from the passage? 问文章告诉我们关于social media 的什么事实，无推断或主旨信号
**拆句** 一般疑问句 What do we learn about social media from the passage?，主干 we learn what about social media；from the passage 是状语，提示答案在文章里有明文，结构无陷阱
**定位** 我们这个永远在线的社交媒体世界可能带来更多连接，但这些连接是肤浅的，会妨碍建立真正的归属感。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反原文 may result in more connections 说的是社交媒体带来更多连接（在数量上扩大），而 It may be an obstacle to expanding one's connections. 说它「妨碍扩大连接」——评价方向反转
B) 偷换概念原文未提 social status（社会地位）；It may get in the way of enhancing one's social status. 中「妨碍提升社会地位」在 P3 中无任何对应——social 一词共用但status 完全没出现
C) ✓ 正确can get in the way of building a real sense of belonging ↔It may prevent people from developing a genuine sense of community.预判的「妨碍」+「真正的归属感」两要素被 prevent people from developing a genuine sense of community 完整对应——动词短语、形容词、核心名词全部同步同义替换
D) 偷换概念It may make people feel that they ought to fit in with the outside world. 说「让人觉得自己必须融入外部世界」，但原文 the feeling that you fit in with others around you 把 fit in 作为「归属感」的一部分（是好事），不是说社交媒体让人觉得「必须迎合」
questions.quote: Our always-on world of social media may result in more connections, but they are superficial and can get in the way of building a real sense of belonging.

options.text: It may be an obstacle to expanding one's connections.
It may get in the way of enhancing one's social status.
It may prevent people from developing a genuine sense of community.
It may make people feel that they ought to fit in with the outside world.

questions.prompt: What does the author suggest people do to get rid of boredom?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者建议人们做什么来摆脱无聊?
A) 计算他们的帖子获得的点赞数。
B) 反思他们与他人的关系。
C) 参与现实生活中的互动。
D) 参加在线讨论。
**判型** 题干 What does the author suggest people do to get rid of boredom? 问作者明文给出的建议，无推断信号
**拆句** 宾语从句 + 不定式状语 What does the author suggest people do to get rid of boredom?，主句 the author suggest + 宾语 people do what；to get rid of boredom是目的状语；结构稍复杂但无陷阱
**定位** 所以请采取行动，加入一个组织，去建立面对面的关系。你会从中获得屏幕给不了的深度——无论你的帖子收到多少点赞。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反原文 no matter how many likes you get on your post 明确否定「数点赞」的价值；Count the likes they get on their posts. 反而把「数点赞」当作建议——完全反向
B) 答非所问Reflect on how they relate to others. 说「反思自己如何与他人相处」，但作者的建议是「采取行动加入组织」，不是「反思」；reflect 与 take action 是两种完全不同的应对方式
C) ✓ 正确build face-to-face relationships ↔ Engage in real-life interactions.预判的「面对面/线下」+「关系/互动」两要素被 Engage in real-life interactions. 整体保留，且未做任何延伸
D) 与原文相反Participate in online discussions. 说「参与线上讨论」——而原文恰恰让人远离屏幕，转向 build face-to-face relationships；线上与线下方向反转
questions.quote: So take the step of joining an organization to build face-to-face relationships. You'll find depth that you won't get from your screen no matter how many likes you get on your post.

options.text: Count the likes they get on their posts.
Reflect on how they relate to others.
Engage in real-life interactions.
Participate in online discussions.

questions.prompt: What should people do to enhance their sense of meaning?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
人们应该做什么来增强意义感?
A) 尝试做一些原创的事情。
B) 面对重大挑战。
C) 以独特的方式定义无聊。
D) 致力于有价值的事业。
**判型** 题干 What should people do to enhance their sense of meaning? 直接问该做什么，无推断信号
**拆句** 情态动词疑问句 + 不定式状语 What should people do to enhance their sense of meaning?，主干 people should do what；to enhance... 是目的状语；结构清晰，无陷阱
**定位** 如果你想减少无聊、增强意义感，就去寻找一份你能做出独特贡献的工作，或者找到一项你能用时间和才华去支持的事业。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念Try to do something original. 说「做原创的事」，但原文 make a unique contribution 强调的是「做独特贡献」——unique contribution（独特贡献）与something original（原创之物）不是同一概念，前者强调贡献的「不可替代性」，后者强调内容的「首创性」
B) 张冠李戴Confront significant challenges. 说「直面重大挑战」，但 P4 通篇未提 challenge（挑战）；该词只在 more significant challenges 出现，是 P5 谈「摆脱无聊」的总建议，不是 P4 谈「增强意义感」的具体做法
C) 答非所问Define boredom in their unique way. 说「用自己独特的方式定义无聊」——这与题目所问的「增强意义感」无关；该项把 If your definition of boredom is being quiet, mindful, and reflective 中的 definition 一词嫁接到本题
D) ✓ 正确find a cause you can support with your time and talent↔Devote themselves to a worthy cause.原文给的两个建议中，选项命中第二个 find a cause you can support with your time and talent——Devote themselves to a worthy cause. 是它的精准凝练
questions.quote: If you want to reduce boredom and increase your sense of meaning, seek work where you can make a unique contribution, or find a cause you can support with your time and talent.

options.text: Try to do something original.
Confront significant challenges.
Define boredom in their unique way.
Devote themselves to a worthy cause.

title: Nowadays you can't buy anything without being asked…

sentences.text: Nowadays you can't buy anything without being asked to provide a rating of a company's performance on a five-star scale.

passage.translation: 如今，你买任何东西都会被要求用五星制为公司的表现评分。

sentences.text: I've been asked to rate my "store (26)____ " on the EFTPOS terminal before I can pay.
Even the most (27)____ activities, such as calling Telstra or picking up a parcel from Australia Post, are followed by texts or emails with surveys asking, "How did we do?"

passage.translation: 我甚至在EFTPOS终端机上被要求为"购物体验"评分后才能付款。即使是最普通的活动，比如致电Telstra或从Australia Post取包裹，之后也会收到短信或邮件调查，询问"我们做得怎么样？"

sentences.text: Online purchases are (28)____ followed up by a customer satisfaction survey.
Companies are so(29)____ for a hit of stars that if you delete the survey the company sends you another one.

passage.translation: 网上购物后通常会有客户满意度调查跟进。公司如此渴望获得星级评价，如果你删除调查问卷，公司还会再给你发一份。

sentences.text: We're (30)____ to rate our apps when we've barely had a chance to use them.
One online course provider I use asks you what you think of the course after you've only completed (31)____ 2 per cent of it.

passage.translation: 我们刚开始使用应用程序时就被提示进行评分。我使用的一家在线课程提供商在你只完成大约百分之二的课程后就询问你对课程的看法。

sentences.text: Economist Jason Murphy says that companies use customer satisfaction ratings because a (32)____display of star feedback has become the nuclear power source of the modern economy.

passage.translation: 经济学家Jason Murphy表示，公司使用客户满意度评分是因为光鲜亮丽的星级反馈展示已成为现代经济的核心动力源。

sentences.text: However, you can't help but (33)____ if these companies are basing their business on fabrications(捏造的东西).
I (34)____ that with online surveys I just click the (35)____ that's closest to my mouse cursor(光标) to get the damn thing off my screen.
Often the star rating I give has far more to do with the kind of day I'm having than the purchase I just made.

passage.translation: 然而，你不禁会怀疑这些公司是否将其业务建立在虚假信息之上。我承认，对于在线调查，我只是点击离鼠标光标最近的选项，好把这该死的东西从屏幕上弄走。我给出的星级评分往往更多地与我当天的心情有关，而非我刚刚完成的购买。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
Nowadays you can't buy anything without being asked to provide a rating of a company's performance on a five-star scale.

I've been asked to rate my "store {{26}} " on the EFTPOS terminal before I can pay. Even the most {{27}} activities, such as calling Telstra or picking up a parcel from Australia Post, are followed by texts or emails with surveys asking, "How did we do?"

Online purchases are {{28}} followed up by a customer satisfaction survey. Companies are so{{29}} for a hit of stars that if you delete the survey the company sends you another one.

We're {{30}} to rate our apps when we've barely had a chance to use them. One online course provider I use asks you what you think of the course after you've only completed {{31}} 2 per cent of it.

Economist Jason Murphy says that companies use customer satisfaction ratings because a {{32}}display of star feedback has become the nuclear power source of the modern economy.

However, you can't help but {{33}} if these companies are basing their business on fabrications(捏造的东西). I {{34}} that with online surveys I just click the {{35}} that's closest to my mouse cursor(光标) to get the damn thing off my screen. Often the star rating I give has far more to do with the kind of day I'm having than the purchase I just made.

options.text: announce
roughly
commonplace
routinely
confess
shining
desperate
showering
experience
variety
fascinated
voyage
option
wonder
prompted

questions.explanation:
**答案** E) experience 名词
**词性槽** 引号内 store 后作复合名词
**依据** 为「购物体验」打分rate my "store __(26)__"，被要求打分的对象正是「store experience（购物体验）」——这是英语里固定说法。结合全文都在讲「给体验/服务打星」，experience 完全契合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) variety 义不搭，不评「种类」variety 是「种类、多样性」，「store variety」指商品种类，但作者通篇评的是服务/体验的星级，不是评商品多不多；与 rate 的对象不符。
N) voyage 义不搭，航行无关voyage 是「航行、海上旅程」，与在 EFTPOS 刷卡机上为购物打分的场景毫无关系，明显是干扰词。

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) commonplace 形容词
**词性槽** the most 后、名词 activities 前作定语
**依据** 「最平常的」活动也被评分Even the most __(27)__ activities, such as calling Telstra or picking up a parcel…，连「最司空见惯的」活动——打个电话、取个包裹——都被要求评分。commonplace（平常的、司空见惯的）正好和 Even（连……都）形成「连最普通的也不放过」的强调。

**答案** J) routinely 副词
**词性槽** be 与过去分词间修饰动词，要副词
**依据** 「例行地」跟进调查Online purchases are __(28)__ followed up by a customer satisfaction survey，网购后「例行地、惯常地」会收到满意度调查——routinely（例行地）正好表达这种司空见惯、每次都来的常态，呼应全文「评分无处不在」。

**答案** D) desperate 形容词
**词性槽** be 动词 so 后作表语，要形容词
**依据** 急切渴望星星Companies are so __(29)__ for a hit of stars that if you delete the survey the company sends you another one.，公司「极度渴望」一点点好评，以至于你删了问卷它再发一份。desperate for（极度渴望……）是固定搭配，正好表达这种不顾一切的迫切。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) fascinated搭配是 by，不搭 for fascinated（着迷的）一般搭 fascinated by/with，不说 fascinated for；而且「着迷」程度上达不到「删了再发」的那种迫切，与 so…that 的夸张语气不符。
K) shining义不搭，留给 32 题shining 是「闪亮的」，描述物体发光，不能描述公司「渴望」的心理状态；它更适合 32 题 a__(32)__ display of star feedback 修饰星星的「闪亮陈列」。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— fascinated 看着也像「热衷」。29 题 Companies are so__(29)__ for a hit of stars 处，fascinated（着迷的）词性对、也像「热衷好评」，颇具迷惑性。但它搭 by 不搭 for，且程度达不到「删了再发」的迫切。防坑：desperate for 才是固定搭配，fascinated 用 by。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) prompted 动词
**词性槽** be 后接过去分词作被动谓语
**依据** 被「催促/提示」去评分We're __(30)__ to rate our apps when we've barely had a chance to use them，我们刚下载、还没怎么用，就被「催着/提示着」去给 app 打分。be prompted to do（被提示/被催促去做）是固定搭配，正好表达这种被系统弹窗催评分的场景。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
L) showering 搭配反向，且非分词形shower 表「倾泻、大量给予」常用 shower sb. with sth.，是「往某人身上倒东西」，方向是给予而非催促；这里需要的是「我们被催去评分」，be showering to rate 既不合搭配也讲不通。

questions.explanation:
**答案** I) roughly 副词
**词性槽** 数字前修饰百分比，要副词
**依据** 修饰数字表「大约」completed __(31)__ 2 per cent of it，作者强调「只完成大约 2%」就被要求评分，roughly（大约）恰好修饰具体数字 2 per cent，语义和搭配都顺。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
J) routinely 义不搭，不修饰数字routinely 意为「例行地、惯常地」，修饰的是反复发生的动作，不能用来修饰一个具体数字 2 per cent。说「例行地 2%」讲不通。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) shining 形容词
**词性槽** 冠词 a 后、名词 display 前作定语
**依据** 「闪亮的」星级陈列a __(32)__ display of star feedback has become the nuclear power source of the modern economy，把星级好评比作现代经济的核电源，用 shining（闪亮的）修饰这种「星星陈列」既贴合星星发光的意象，又有夸张的修辞色彩。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) fascinated 只修饰人，不修饰物fascinated（着迷的）描述的是人「被吸引」的心理状态，不能修饰 display（陈列）这样的事物。「a fascinated display」不成立。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) wonder 动词
**词性槽** 情态短语后接动词原形
**依据** 忍不住「纳闷/想知道」you can't help but __(33)__ if these companies are basing their business on fabrications，作者忍不住「纳闷」这些公司是不是在拿捏造的数据做生意。wonder if（想知道是否、纳闷）是固定搭配，正好引出这个疑问。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) announce 义反，不接 if 表疑问announce 是「宣布」，表示对外公开声明，与「忍不住产生疑问」的语气相反，也不和 if 从句构成「想知道是否」的搭配。
C) confess 义偏，且要留给 34 题confess 是「坦白、承认」，更适合 34 题 I __(34)__ that… 那种「我承认……」的坦白语境；can't help but confess if… 语义也别扭。它要留给后面真正坦白的空。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 C) —— confess 也是动词易抢位。33 题 you can't help but__(33)__ if… 处，confess（坦白）词性也对、也像在「说什么」，容易被误填。但 wonder if（纳闷是否）才是固定搭配，且 confess 要留给 34 题。防坑：认准 wonder if 表内心疑问，confess 接的是 that 从句的招供。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) confess 动词
**词性槽** 主语 I 后缺谓语，要动词
**依据** 坦白自己打分很随意I __(34)__ that with online surveys I just click the __(35)__ that's closest to my mouse cursor，作者要「坦白」一件不太光彩的事——自己评分时只是随手乱点。confess that（坦白、承认）正好引出这种自我招供的语气。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) announce 语气不符，非自我招供announce（宣布）是正式对外公布，而这里是作者私下坦白自己的小毛病，带点不好意思的口吻。用「宣布我随便乱点」语气完全不对。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) option 名词
**词性槽** the 后作宾语，要名词
**依据** 点最近的「选项」I just click the __(35)__ that's closest to my mouse cursor(光标)，作者说自己随便点离光标最近的那个——评分时点的正是星级「选项」。option（选项）和 click、closest to my mouse cursor 完全自洽。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) experience 已用且义不搭experience（体验）已在 26 题用掉，且「click the experience」语义不通——你点的是屏幕上一个可点的东西，不是「体验」。
M) variety 义不搭，无法被「点」variety 意为「多样、种类」，「click the variety」讲不通——光标最近的不是「多样性」，而是一个具体可点的选项。

title: Success was once defined as being able to…

sentences.text: Success was once defined as being able to stay at a company for a long time and move up the corporate ladder.
The goal was to reach the top, accumulate wealth and retire to a life of ease.
My father is a successful senior executive.
In 35 years, he worked for only three companies.

passage.translation: 成功曾经被定义为能够在一家公司长期工作并沿着企业阶梯向上攀升。目标是达到顶峰，积累财富，然后退休过上安逸的生活。我的父亲是一位成功的高级管理人员。在35年里，他只为三家公司工作过。

sentences.text: When I started my career, things were already different.
If you weren't changing companies every three or four years, you simply weren't getting ahead in your career.
But back then, if you were a consultant or freelancer(自由职业者), people would wonder what was wrong with you.
They would assume you had problems getting a job.

passage.translation: 当我开始职业生涯时，情况已经不同了。如果你不是每三四年就换一次公司,你根本无法在职业生涯中取得进步。但在那时,如果你是顾问或自由职业者,人们会怀疑你有什么问题。他们会认为你找工作有困难。

sentences.text: Today, consulting or freelancing for five businesses at the same time is a badge of honor.
It shows how valuable an individual is.
Many companies now look to these "ultimate professionals" to solve problems their full-time teams can't.
Or they save money by hiring "top-tier(顶尖的) experts" only for particular projects.

passage.translation: 如今,同时为五家企业提供咨询或自由职业服务是一种荣誉徽章。它显示了一个人有多么宝贵。许多公司现在寻求这些"终极专业人士"来解决他们全职团队无法解决的问题。或者他们通过仅为特定项目雇用"顶尖专家"来节省资金。

sentences.text: Working at home or in cafes, starting businesses of their own, and even launching business ventures that eventually may fail, all indicate "initiative," "creativity," and "adaptability," which are desirable qualities in today's workplace.

Most important, there is a growing recognition that people who balance work and play, and who work at what they are passionate about, are more focused and productive, delivering greater value to their clients.

passage.translation: 在家或在咖啡馆工作,创办自己的企业,甚至发起最终可能失败的商业项目,这些都表明了"主动性"、"创造力"和"适应能力",这些都是当今职场中令人向往的品质。最重要的是,人们越来越认识到,那些平衡工作与娱乐、从事自己热爱的工作的人更加专注和高效,为客户提供更大的价值。

sentences.text: Who are these people?
They are artists, writers, programmers, providers of office services and career advice.
What's needed now is a marketplace platform specifically designed to bring freelancers and clients together.
Such platforms then become a place to feature the most experienced, professional, and creative talent.

This is where they conduct business, where a sense of community reinforces the culture and values of the gig economy(零工经济), and where success is rewarded with good reviews that encourage more business.

passage.translation: 这些人是谁?他们是艺术家、作家、程序员、办公服务提供者和职业建议提供者。现在需要的是一个专门设计用来将自由职业者和客户聚集在一起的市场平台。这样的平台随后成为展示最有经验、最专业和最有创造力的人才的地方。这是他们开展业务的地方,在这里社区意识强化了零工经济的文化和价值观,成功会获得良好评价的奖励,从而鼓励更多业务。

sentences.text: Slowly but surely, these platforms create a bridge between traditional enterprises and this emerging economy.
Perhaps more important, as the global economy continues to be disrupted by technology and other massive change, the gig economy will itself become an engine of economic and social transformation.

passage.translation: 这些平台正在缓慢但稳定地在传统企业和这个新兴经济体之间搭建桥梁。也许更重要的是,随着全球经济继续被技术和其他重大变革所颠覆,零工经济本身将成为经济和社会转型的引擎。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does the author use the example of his father to illustrate?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （例证目的题）
**题目译文**
作者用他父亲的例子来说明什么?
A) 人们花多长时间到达职业生涯的顶峰。
B) 在他父亲的时代,人们如何积累财富。
C) 在他父亲的时代,人们如何看待成功。
D) 人们通常在一家公司待多久。
**判型** 题干What does the author use the example of his father to illustrate?里use the example...to illustrate是例证目的题的标志句式。
**拆句** What does the author use the example of his father to illustrate?主干是What does the author use...to illustrate，宾语the example of his father插在use和to illustrate之间，可还原为The author uses the example of his father to illustrate what？句子结构清晰，无陷阱。
**定位** 成功曾经被定义为能在一家公司长期任职、并沿企业晋升阶梯向上攀升。其目标是登上顶峰、积累财富、退休享福。我父亲是一位成功的高级主管。35年里他只为三家公司工作过。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 把例子局部细节当成例证目的=以偏概全A项How long people took to reach the top of their career.只截取了例子里"长期任职"这层片面信息，且"花多久到顶"是文中未直接给出的时间细节。
B) 拎走并列项里的一个=以偏概全B项How people accumulated wealth in his father's time.把原文里accumulate wealth截出来做主旨，但accumulate wealth只是论点中目标的一个并列项，并非例子要说明的核心。
C) ✓ 正确Success was once defined as being able to stay at a company for a long time and move up the corporate ladder.↔ How people viewed success in his father's time. C项把"父辈时代人们如何看待成功"完整对应原文论点句的语义，例子（35年三家公司）正是这个看法的证据。
D) 把例子字面=目的，是答非所问D项How long people usually stayed in a company.几乎是父亲例子（he worked for only three companies 35年）的复述，问的是"例子表面讲了啥"，而题问的是"例子用来证明啥"。
questions.quote: Success was once defined as being able to stay at a company for a long time and move up the corporate ladder. The goal was to reach the top, accumulate wealth and retire to a life of ease. My father is a successful senior executive. In 35 years, he worked for only three companies.

options.text: How long people took to reach the top of their career.
How people accumulated wealth in his father's time.
How people viewed success in his father's time.
How long people usually stayed in a company.

questions.prompt: Why did people often change jobs when the author started his career?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
当作者开始他的职业生涯时,为什么人们经常换工作?
A) 这在当时被认为是一种时尚。
B) 这是一种在职业生涯中晋升的方式。
C) 这是对不断变化的就业市场的回应。
D) 长期保住一份工作很困难。
**判型** Why did people often change jobs when the author started his career?问的是当时换工作背后的具体原因，答案能在原文里找到对应表述。
**拆句** Why did people often change jobs when the author started his career?主干Why did people change jobs，后接when引导的时间状语从句，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 如果你没在每三四年换一次公司，那你的职业基本就没在前进。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有A项It was considered a fashion at that time.里的fashion（流行风尚）在原文中无任何对应表述，作者强调的是"不换就升不上去"的功利动因，而非流行潮流。
B) ✓ 正确If you weren't changing companies every three or four years, you simply weren't getting ahead in your career.↔ It was a way to advance in their career.从预判"换工作是为了职业前进"出发，B项直接以a way to advance in their career对位，完全覆盖定位句的正面含义。
C) 偷换概念C项It was a response to the changing job market.把换工作说成是对"职场变化"的被动响应，原文给出的是主动追求职业前进的内在动因，逻辑方向相反。
D) 与原文相反D项It was difficult to keep a job for long.说当时"很难长期保住一份工作"，原文说的是"如果想前进就得自己换"，并非工作保不住；D项把主动换岗读成被动失业。
questions.quote: If you weren't changing companies every three or four years, you simply weren't getting ahead in your career.

options.text: It was considered a fashion at that time.
It was a way to advance in their career.
It was a response to the changing job market.
It was difficult to keep a job for long.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about people now working for several businesses at the same time?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于现在同时为几家企业工作的人,作者说了什么?
A) 他们常被视为最宝贵的人才。
B) 他们能够更充分地发挥自己的潜力。
C) 他们能够掌控自己的生活和工作日程。
D) 他们为自己是杰出的问题解决者而感到自豪。
**判型** What does the author say about people now working for several businesses at the same time?问的是作者对该群体的具体评价，原文应有直接陈述。
**拆句** What does the author say about people now working for several businesses at the same time?主干What does the author say about people，working for several businesses at the same time是people的现在分词后置定语；now是时间副词，把范围限定在当下。
**定位** 如今，同时为五家公司做咨询或自由职业是一种荣誉徽章，它显示一个人有多么有价值。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确It shows how valuable an individual is. ↔They are often regarded as most treasured talents. a badge of honor ↔ are often regarded as从预判出发，A项把badge of honor+how valuable汇总成most treasured talents，最贴合作者对这群人的评价。
B) 张冠李戴（错段拼接）B项They are able to bring their potential into fuller play.说他们"能把潜力发挥得更充分"，原文未在53题的定位段说这件事，潜力发挥要到P4再讨论focused and productive。
C) 过度推断C项They have control over their life and work schedules.说他们"掌控自己的生活和工作日程"，原文虽提到为多家公司打工，但没说他们对日程有控制权——这层引申是读者的主观联想。
D) 偷换概念（叙述视角+部分原因）D项They feel proud of being outstanding problem solvers.说他们"为自己作为解决问题者而自豪"，原文里badge of honor是社会对他们的视角，不是他们自己feel proud；problem solvers也只是企业聘他们的部分原因。
questions.quote: Today, consulting or freelancing for five businesses at the same time is a badge of honor. It shows how valuable an individual is.

options.text: They are often regarded as most treasured talents.
They are able to bring their potential into fuller play.
They have control over their life and work schedules.
They feel proud of being outstanding problem solvers.

questions.prompt: What have businesses come to recognize now?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
企业现在认识到了什么?
A) 谁能够轻松地解决问题。
B) 人们如何能更加专注和高效。
C) 什么样的人能为它们做出更多贡献。
D) 为什么有些人对工作更有热情。
**判型** What have businesses come to recognize now?问当下企业认识到了什么，是问事实细节，不是推断。
**拆句** What have businesses come to recognize now?现在完成时have come to recognize表示从过去到现在累积形成的认识，now强调当下状态，结构无陷阱。
**定位** 最重要的是，人们越来越认识到：那些工作与休息平衡、并从事自己所热爱之事的人，更专注、更高产，能给客户带来更大的价值。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴+偷换程度A项Who is capable of solving problems with ease.里solving problems with ease（轻松解决问题）来自solve problems their full-time teams can't，但P3说的是"解决全职团队搞不定的问题"，并非"轻松"，且和"现在认识到的"语境不符。
B) 答非所问（偷换疑问词）B项How people can be more focused and productive.问的是"如何变得更专注高产"，而原文给的是"哪类人更专注高产"，疑问词错位，且companies的认知对象是人，不是方法。
C) ✓ 正确people who balance work and play, and who work at what they are passionate about, are more focused and productive, delivering greater value to their clients↔ What kind of people can contribute more to them.原文that从句的真正主语是people who...，整句重心是这类人能为客户贡献更多价值；C项的"What kind of people can contribute more to them"精准对位该重心。
D) 答非所问+偷换重心D项Why some people are more passionate about work.问"为什么有些人对工作更热情"，但原文里passionate只是描述这类人的特征之一，并未解释"原因"，且重心是其价值，不是热情的成因。
questions.quote: Most important, there is a growing recognition that people who balance work and play, and who work at what they are passionate about, are more focused and productive, delivering greater value to their clients.

options.text: Who is capable of solving problems with ease.
How people can be more focused and productive.
What kind of people can contribute more to them.
Why some people are more passionate about work.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about the gig economy?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
关于零工经济,作者说了什么?
A) 它可能迫使企业改革其商业实践。
B) 它可能很快取代传统的经济模式。
C) 它将在全球范围内推动技术进步。
D) 它将带来彻底的经济和社会变革。
**判型** What does the author say about the gig economy?问的是作者对零工经济的具体陈述；答案直接在原文有对应句而非需要推断。
**拆句** What does the author say about the gig economy?结构简单：主干What does the author say，about the gig economy是介词短语修饰say，无陷阱。
**定位** 或许更重要的是，随着全球经济持续被技术和其他剧变所颠覆，零工经济本身将成为经济与社会变革的引擎。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断A项It may force companies to reform their business practice.说零工经济会"迫使企业改革其业务实践"，原文并未提到"迫使企业改革"这一动作，create a bridge between traditional enterprises and this emerging economy说的是搭桥而非迫使改革。
B) 与原文相反B项It may soon replace the traditional economic model.说零工经济会"很快取代传统经济模式"，原文里始终是"搭桥""成为引擎"，从未表达替代关系。
C) 与原文相反（因果颠倒）C项It will drive technological progress on a global scale.说零工经济"将驱动全球技术进步"，但原文里是"global economy被technology颠覆"，技术是动因、零工经济是结果之一，方向被反过来。
D) ✓ 正确the gig economy will itself become an engine of economic and social transformation↔It will bring about radical economic and social changes.从预判"将带来经济与社会变革"出发，D项把engine of transformation改写成bring about radical changes，逐字段语义匹配，是定位句的直接同义替换。
questions.quote: Perhaps more important, as the global economy continues to be disrupted by technology and other massive change, the gig economy will itself become an engine of economic and social transformation.

options.text: It may force companies to reform their business practice.

questions.prompt: What did Harvard scientists do 50 years ago?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
50年前哈佛大学的科学家们做了什么?
A) 他们提高了公众对心脏病可能致病因素的认识。
B) 他们将公众的注意力从糖的健康风险转移到脂肪上。
C) 他们用新发现将糖业置于聚光灯下。
D) 他们就糖在人体健康中的作用进行了大规模研究。
**判型** What did Harvard scientists do 50 years ago? 问的是过去某个具体行为，答案应是定位段对该行为的客观陈述。
**拆句** What did Harvard scientists do 50 years ago? 是 what 引导的一般疑问句，主语Harvard scientists，时间状语 50 years ago，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 糖业震惊。这描述了本周许多美国人在得知一桩内幕后的反应——50 年前，糖业出钱请哈佛科学家做研究，把心脏病的责任焦点从糖身上挪开，狠狠地压在了膳食脂肪头上。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有raised public awareness of the possible causes of heart disease 说哈佛科学家"提高了公众对心脏病病因的认知"，但原文只说他们"转移焦点"，从未提及"提高认知"，且行为方向相反——是误导而非启蒙。
B) ✓ 正确shifted the focus away from sugar's role in heart disease—and put the spotlight(注意的中心) squarely on dietary fat↔ turned public attention away from the health risks of sugar to fat预判内容"把心脏病矛头从糖转向脂肪"与 turned public attention away from the health risks of sugar to fat 在框架、对象、方向上完全重合，即同义替换型正确项。
C) 与原文相反placed the sugar industry in the spotlight with their new findings 说研究让"糖业"成为焦点，与原文 put the spotlight(注意的中心) squarely on dietary fat 恰恰相反——焦点是脂肪而非糖业。
D) 无中生有conducted large-scale research on the role of sugar in people's health 强调"大规模"研究，但原文未提及研究规模，只说糖业出钱资助；且研究内容不是"糖与健康的作用"而是"转移焦点"。

That describes the reaction of many Americans this week following revelations that, 50 years ago, the sugar industry paid Harvard scientists for research that shifted the focus away from sugar's role in heart disease—and put the spotlight(注意的中心) squarely on dietary fat.

They turned public attention away from the health risks of sugar to fat.

questions.prompt: What does Marion Nestle say about present-day nutrition studies?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
Marion Nestle对当今营养学研究有何看法?
A) 这些研究花了她整整一年时间来追踪和分析。
B) 它们大多基于系统性综述。
C) 它们依赖于食品行业的资助。
D) 几乎所有研究都服务于资助方的目的。
**判型** What does Marion Nestle say about present-day nutrition studies? 直接索取一个人对一事的具体说法，答案应是文中该人原话的转述。
**拆句** What does Marion Nestle say about present-day nutrition studies? 主干 What...does Marion Nestle say，about 引出宾语补足语限定 say 的内容范围；句法直白。
**定位** Nestle 告诉我们："在近 170 项研究里，约 90% 的结果都偏向了资助方的利益。"
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问They took her a full year to track and analyze 说"研究花了她一整年追踪"，对应原文spent a year informally tracking，但这是关于 Nestle 的研究方法，不是她对"present-day nutrition studies"本身的看法，答非所问。
B) 张冠李戴Most of them are based on systematic reviews 把"systematic reviews"安到"present-day nutrition studies"头上，但原文 Other systematic reviews support her conclusions 是说"其他系统性综述支持 Nestle 的结论"，systematic reviews 是支持她的工具，不是被她评论的研究的本质。
C) 偷换概念They depend on funding from the food industries 说"研究依赖食品业资助"，是"资金来源"层面的事实，而原文 Nestle 强调的是"研究结论偏向资助方"——把"结论偏袒"偷换成了"资金依赖"。两者层面不同。
D) ✓ 正确Roughly 90% of nearly 170 studies favored the sponsor's interest ↔Nearly all of them serve the purpose of the funders预判"九成研究服务资助方利益"与 Nearly all of them serve the purpose of the funders 在数量级、动作、对象三层全部对齐，是教科书级同义替换正确项。
questions.quote: "Roughly 90% of nearly 170 studies favored the sponsor's interest," Nestle tells us.

options.text: They took her a full year to track and analyze.
Most of them are based on systematic reviews.
They depend on funding from the food industries.
Nearly all of them serve the purpose of the funders.

questions.prompt: What did Coca-Cola-funded studies claim?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
可口可乐资助的研究声称什么?
A) 运动对健康的重要性超过饮食。
B) 选择吃什么和喝什么是控制体重的关键。
C) 饮用可口可乐不会导致体重增加。
D) 食品行业在对抗肥胖方面发挥着重要作用。
**判型** What did Coca-Cola-funded studies claim? 问被可口可乐资助的研究主张了什么，答案是文中明示的论断。
**拆句** What did Coca-Cola-funded studies claim? 主语 Coca-Cola-funded studies 是"名词- funded 复合形容词+名词"结构，意为"被可口可乐资助的研究"；句意直白。
**定位** 去年《纽约时报》披露，可口可乐资助知名科学家和组织，宣扬这样一种主张：在对抗体重增长的战斗中，人们应更看重运动，而不是吃了什么、喝了什么。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确in the battle against weight gain, people should pay more attention to exercise and less to what they eat and drink↔ Exercise is more important to good health than diet预判"重运动而轻饮食"与 Exercise is more important to good health than diet 的"运动比饮食更重要"严格等价；定位句的 more/less 平行结构本身就是隐性比较。
B) 与原文相反Choosing what to eat and drink is key to weight control 说"吃喝选择是控重关键"，与原文 less to what they eat and drink"少在乎吃喝"完全相反——可口可乐研究恰恰要弱化饮食责任。
C) 无中生有Drinking Coca-Cola does not contribute to weight gain 凭空捏造一句"喝可乐不会增重"，原文从未出现此论断；可口可乐资助研究只是"转移注意力"到运动，并未直接为可乐本身辩护。
D) 偷换概念The food industry plays a major role in fighting obesity 说"食品业在抗肥胖中起重要作用"，看似与原文相关，但原文是说"可口可乐资助研究让人忽视饮食"，并未把食品业塑造为"抗肥胖功臣"；把"产业操纵议程"偷换成了"产业贡献抗肥胖"。

Choosing what to eat and drink is key to weight control.
Drinking Coca-Cola does not contribute to weight gain.

questions.prompt: What does Liebman say about industry-funded research?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
Liebman对行业资助的研究有何看法?
A) 它只关注营养和健康。
B) 它在消费者中造成困惑。
C) 它很少产生客观的研究结果。
D) 它违背公共利益。
**判型** What does Liebman say about industry-funded research? 同 Q47 同款句式，仍是细节题，定位到 Liebman 引语即可。
**拆句** What does Liebman say about industry-funded research? 结构同 Q47；industry- funded 是"名词-过去分词"复合形容词，表被动"被产业资助的"。
**定位** "当食品业出钱做研究时，它常常能买到自己想要的结论。"而它想买的，往往是一个对产业有利的结果。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问It simply focuses on nutrition and health 只说研究"聚焦营养健康"，是话题描述，未触及 Liebman 对"业内资助偏袒"的核心评价；属答非所问。
B) 无中生有It causes confusion among consumers 说"造成消费者困惑"，原文 P5 Liebman 谈的是"研究结论偏袒产业"，未提及消费者困惑这一后果——"困惑"是后文（P6）作者建议引出的语境，但不是 Liebman 的直接评价。
C) ✓ 正确what it pays for is often a pro-industry finding↔ It rarely results in objective findings When the food industry pays for research, it often gets what it pays for↔It rarely results in objective findings预判"买到的多是偏袒产业的结论"与 It rarely results in objective findings 是同一事实的正反描述：常偏袒=极少客观。
D) 过度推断It runs counter to the public interest 跨越"研究偏袒产业"直接推到"与公众利益对立"——这是合理但过度的引申。原文只说结论亲产业，没有明示"对立于公众利益"，且 Liebman 所在机构名 Center for Science in the Public Interest 是机构名而非她的论断。
questions.quote: "When the food industry pays for research, it often gets what it pays for." And what it pays for is often a pro-industry finding.

questions.prompt: What is the author's advice to consumers?

作者对消费者的建议是什么?
A) 在决定吃什么时遵循自己的直觉。
B) 对饮食专家的建议持怀疑态度。
C) 忽略新闻推送中的无关信息。
D) 对新的营养学研究发现要三思而后行。
**判型** What is the author's advice to consumers? 问的是一项具体行动建议，答案是文末作者明示的劝告，仍属细节题（非笼统主旨）。
**拆句** What is the author's advice to consumers? What is 主系表结构，主语 the author's advice，介词短语 to consumers 修饰 advice 表对象；无难点。
**定位** 鉴于这种环境，消费者读到营养科学的最新发现时应当保持怀疑，并对新闻推送里冒出来的最新研究置之不理。
questions.tip:

B) 与原文相反Be doubtful of diet experts' recommendations 让消费者"怀疑膳食专家的建议"，但原文恰恰相反 Rely on health experts who've reviewed all the evidence——要怀疑的是"业内出资的最新研究"，不是"健康专家"。
C) 偷换概念Ignore irrelevant information on their news feed 让消费者"忽略新闻推送里的无关信息"，但原文 ignore the latest study that pops up on your news feed 让消费者忽略的是"新闻推送里冒出的最新研究"——把"最新研究"偷换成"无关信息"，对象被偷偷扩大并改性质。
D) ✓ 正确consumers should be skeptical(怀疑的) when reading the latest finding in nutrition science↔Think twice about new nutrition research findings预判"对新研究保持怀疑"与 Think twice about new nutrition research findings 在态度（怀疑↔三思）与对象（最新营养发现↔新营养研究结论）两层都对齐。

groups.content:
Social isolation poses more health risks than obesity or smoking 15 cigarettes a day, according to research published by Brigham Young University. The {{26}} is that loneliness is a huge, if silent, risk factor.

Loneliness affects physical health in two ways. First, it produces stress hormones that can lead to many health problems. Second, people who live alone are less likely to go to doctor {{27}} , to exercise or to eat a healthy diet.

Public health experts in many countries are {{28}} how to address widespread loneliness in our society. Last year Britain even appointed a minister for loneliness. "Loneliness {{29}} almost every one of us at some point," its minister for loneliness Baroness Barran said. "It can lead to very serious health {{30}} for individuals who become isolated and disconnected."

Barran started a "Let's Talk Loneliness" campaign that {{31}} difficult conversations across Britain. He is now supporting " {{32}} benches," which are public seating areas where people are encouraged to go and chat with one another. The minister is also {{33}} to stop public transportation from being cut in ways that leave people isolated.

More than one-fifth of adults in both the United States and Britain said in a 2018 {{34}} that they often or always feel lonely. More than half of American adults are unmarried, and researchers have found that even among those who are married, 30% of relationships are {{35}} strained. A quarter of Americans now live alone, and as the song says, one is the loneliest number.
