**答案** I) implication 名词
**词性槽** 定冠词 The 后作主语的名词
**依据** "言外之意/启示是……" The __(26)__ is that loneliness is a huge, if silent, risk factor：承接首句"孤独危害比肥胖吸烟还大"的研究，这里说"由此得出的含意／启示是：孤独是巨大却无声的风险因素"，implication（言外之意、启示）正是对前述研究结论的提炼，单数与 The...is 一致。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) dimensions 义不对且数不合dimensions 指"维度"，"这个维度是孤独是风险因素"语义不通；且 dimensions 为复数，与"The ___ is" 的单数 is 不一致。
H) idiom 义不对：习语idiom（习语）与"研究得出的结论/含意"无关，"这个习语是……"读不通。

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) appointments 名词
**词性槽** go to doctor 后接名词作宾语
**依据** doctor appointments = 看病预约go to doctor __(27)__：doctor appointments 是地道固定搭配，指"去看医生的预约"。本段在说独居者"不太会去看病、运动或健康饮食"，"看病预约"正好与 exercise、healthy diet 并列成三件健康行为。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) dimensions 搭配不成立"go to doctor dimensions"（去看医生维度）不成句，dimensions 与 go to 不搭。
N) survey 义不对：调查"去做医生调查"不合本句"看病"的语境；survey 留给空 34 更合适。
H) idiom 义不对：习语idiom（习语）与"去看病"毫无关联。
I) implication 义不对且已被占用implication（含意）既不搭 go to doctor，又已是空 26 的答案。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) debating 动词
**词性槽** be 动词 are 后接 -ing 作谓语
**依据** "正在讨论如何应对" experts ... are __(28)__ how to address widespread loneliness：专家们"正在争论／讨论如何应对孤独"，debating（讨论、争论）后接 "how to ..." 地道，语义正是"探讨对策"，与下文"英国甚至任命了孤独事务大臣"的应对行动衔接。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
J) pushing 搭配指向不同pushing 表"推动、努力争取"，常接 to do，不直接接 "how to" 表"讨论怎么做"；且 push 更贴空 33。
M) splitting义不对：分裂"正在分裂如何应对孤独"语义讲不通，splitting 与本句逻辑无关。
O) touches 形态不符touches 是单数现在时，无法跟在 are 后构成进行时，形态先被排除。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) touches 动词
**词性槽** 主语 Loneliness 后缺谓语，宾语 us
**依据** "孤独影响着我们几乎每个人" Loneliness touches almost every one of us at some point：touches 在此取"触及、影响"义，"孤独在某些时刻几乎触及我们每一个人"，单三形态与主语 Loneliness 一致，语义贴合"孤独普遍"这一全文论点。

**答案** C) consequences 名词
**词性槽** 形容词 serious 后接名词
**依据** "导致严重后果"是固定搭配lead to very serious health __(30)__：lead to（导致）后接的、又能被 serious（严重的）修饰的、还是讲健康层面的，正是 consequences（后果）。"严重的健康后果" 语义最顺，且与全文"孤独危害健康"的主旨完全咬合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) dimensions 义不对：维度而非后果dimensions 指"维度／方面"，"严重的健康维度"不通；这里要的是 lead to 导出的结果，不是某个方面。
I) implication 已被空 26 用掉implication 是空 26 的答案，已从词库划走，按"每词最多用一次"不再参与。
B) appointments 搭配不成立appointments 指"预约"，"严重的健康预约"讲不通，且它另有归属（空 27）。
H) idiom 义不对：习语idiom 是"习语"，与 lead to 导致的健康结果毫无关系。
N) survey 义不对：调查survey 是"调查"，"严重的健康调查"不合逻辑；它更贴空 34。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) sparked 动词
**词性槽** that 引导定语从句缺谓语
**依据** "引发了……对话" campaign that __(31)__ difficult conversations across Britain：一场运动"在英国各地引发／激起了难以启齿的对话"，sparked（引发、激起）与 conversations 搭配地道，sparked discussions/conversations 是高频组合，语义指向"运动带来积极效果"。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
O) touches 时态与搭配都差touches 是单数现在时，与本段过去语境不符，且"触及对话"不如"引发对话"自然；touches 更贴空 29。
G) hindered 逻辑指向相反hindered（阻碍）意思反了——运动是要促进而非阻碍交流，与积极主旨冲突。
M) splitting形态与义都不对splitting 是 -ing 形式不能直接作过去式谓语，且"分裂对话"语义怪异。
J) pushing 形态不合且另有归属pushing 为 -ing 形式，作 that 从句谓语需 pushed，形态不对；且 push 更贴空 33 的"pushing to"。
D) debating 形态不合且另有归属debating 为 -ing 形式，此处需过去式谓语；debating 更贴空 28 的进行时结构。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 G) —— hindered 形态对、逻辑反。空 31 要过去式动词，hindered 形态完全合规，光看语法分不出对错。防坑：回到语义方向——"Let's Talk Loneliness" 运动是要"引发"对话而非"阻碍"对话，逻辑指向决定选 sparked。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) friendly 形容词
**词性槽** 名词 benches 前作定语
**依据** "友好长椅"鼓励陌生人交谈"friendly benches," which are public seating areas where people are encouraged to go and chat with one another：后面的定语从句解释这是"鼓励人们去和彼此聊天的公共座椅"，正好印证 friendly（友好的）——"友好长椅"，主题是化解孤独、促进交流。

**答案** J) pushing 动词
**词性槽** be 动词 is 后接 -ing，再接 to do
**依据** push to do = 努力争取做某事is also __(33)__ to stop public transportation from being cut：pushing to stop（努力争取阻止）地道，"大臣还在努力争取阻止削减公共交通"，push to do 是固定搭配，语义指向"主动推动政策"，与上文"支持友好长椅"的积极行动并列。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) splitting搭配与义都不对splitting 不与 to do 构成"努力做某事"的搭配，且"分裂去阻止"语义讲不通。

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) survey 名词
**词性槽** 冠词 a 后、介词 that 从句前的名词
**依据** "在一项调查中表示" said in a 2018 __(34)__ that they often or always feel lonely：人们"在 2018 年的一项调查中表示……"，survey（调查）正是承载"超五分之一成年人说常感孤独"这类数据结论的载体，搭配 said in a survey 地道自然。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
I) implication 义不对且已被占用implication（含意）不是人们"在其中说话"的场合，且已是空 26 答案。
E) dimensions 义不对：维度"在一个 2018 维度中说"不通，dimensions 与 said in 不搭。
H) idiom 义不对：习语idiom（习语）无法承载调查数据，语义不符。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) severely 副词
**词性槽** 修饰形容词 strained 的状语
**依据** "严重紧张"程度副词30% of relationships are __(35)__ strained：severely（严重地）修饰 strained，"30%的关系严重紧张"，程度副词与"strained（紧张）"语义同向、自然加强，呼应本段"即便已婚也有大量关系出问题"的论点。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) abruptly 义不对：突然 vs 程度abruptly 表"突然地"，强调方式/时间，不是程度；"突然紧张"与 strained 这种持续状态不搭，这里要的是"紧张的严重程度"。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 A) —— abruptly 词性对、易抢答。空 35 副词只有 abruptly 与severely 两候选，词性都对，慌乱中可能凭眼熟选 abruptly。防坑：先问空修饰的是"程度"还是"方式"——are __(35)__ strained 要的是"严重程度"，选程度副词 severely。

title: Being an information technology, or IT, worker is…

sentences.text: Being an information technology, or IT, worker is not a job I envy.
They are the ones who, right in the middle of a critical meeting, are expected to instantly fix the projector that's no longer working.
They have to tolerate the bad tempers of colleagues frustrated at the number of times they've had to call the help desk for the same issue.
They are also the ones who know there are systems that are more powerful, reliable and faster, but their employer simply will not put up the funds to buy them.

passage.translation: 作为一名信息技术或IT工作者，这不是我羡慕的工作。他们是那些在关键会议进行到一半时，被期望立即修好不再工作的投影仪的人。他们必须忍受同事们的坏脾气，这些同事因为同一个问题不得不多次致电服务台而感到沮丧。他们也是那些知道存在更强大、更可靠、更快速的系统，但他们的雇主就是不愿出资购买的人。

sentences.text: According to a recent survey, employees who have a job reliant on IT support consider IT a major source of job dissatisfaction.
Through no fault of their own, they can suddenly find their productivity deteriorating or quality control non-existent.
And there's little they can do about it.

passage.translation: 根据最近的一项调查,依赖IT支持的员工认为IT是工作不满的主要来源。他们会突然发现自己的生产力在下降或质量控制不复存在,而这并非他们自己的过错。对此他们几乎无能为力。

sentences.text: The experience of using IT penetrates almost the entire work field.
It has become a crucial part of employees' overall work experience.
When IT is operating as it should, employee self-confidence swells.
Their job satisfaction, too, can surge when well-functioning machines relieve them of dull tasks or repetitive processes.

But if there's one thing that triggers widespread employee frustration, it's an IT transformation project gone wrong, where swollen expectations have been popped and a long list of promised efficiencies has been reversed.
This occurs when business leaders implement IT initiatives with little consideration of how those changes will impact the end user.

passage.translation: 使用IT的体验几乎渗透到整个工作领域。它已成为员工整体工作体验的关键部分。当IT按其应有的方式运行时,员工的自信心会增强。当运转良好的机器使他们摆脱枯燥的任务或重复性流程时,他们的工作满意度也会飙升。但如果有一件事会引发广泛的员工挫败感,那就是IT转型项目出了问题,膨胀的期望被打破,一长串承诺的效率提升被逆转。这种情况发生在业务领导者实施IT举措时很少考虑这些变化将如何影响最终用户。

sentences.text: Which is why managers should appreciate just how influential the IT user experience is to their employees, and exert substantial effort in ensuring their IT team eliminates programming errors and application crashes.
Adequate and timely IT support should also be available to enable users to cope with technological issues at work.
More importantly, IT practitioners need to understand what employees experience mentally when they use IT.

passage.translation: 这就是为什么管理者应该认识到IT用户体验对员工的影响有多大,并付出大量努力确保他们的IT团队消除编程错误和应用程序崩溃。还应提供充分及时的IT支持,使用户能够应对工作中的技术问题。更重要的是,IT从业者需要了解员工在使用IT时的心理体验。

sentences.text: Therefore, businesses need to set up their IT infrastructure so that it is designed to fit in with their employees' work, rather than adjust their work to fit in with the company's IT limitations.

passage.translation: 因此,企业需要建立其IT基础设施,使其设计与员工的工作相适应,而不是调整员工的工作以适应公司的IT限制。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about working in IT?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者对从事IT工作有何看法?
A) 这份工作令许多人羡慕。
B) 这份工作对他没有吸引力。
C) 这份工作经济回报丰厚。
D) 这份工作与他的能力不匹配。
**判型** What does the author say about working in IT? 用 what 引导，问作者对某一具体对象的明确表态，属于带主观色彩的细节题，而不是 infer/imply。
**拆句** 题干是简单疑问句，主干为 What does the author say about working in IT?，about 引出话题，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 成为一名信息技术（即 IT）工作者，不是一份我会羡慕的工作。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反It is envied by many. 把作者 not a job I envy 的态度改成"很多人羡慕"，方向完全相反，且原文也没说"很多人羡慕"。
B) ✓ 正确not a job I envy ↔ does not appeal to him预判"作者不羡慕 IT 工作"与 It does not appeal to him. 同义；其余选项与作者表态相反或与文意无关。
C) 无中生有It is financially rewarding. 称 IT 工作"经济回报丰厚"，但全文从未谈及薪资或金钱收益，纯属编造。
D) 偷换概念It does not match his abilities. 说 IT 工作"与他的能力不匹配"，原文只说作者不羡慕、并描述 IT 工作辛苦，从未涉及作者本人的能力是否够格。
questions.quote: Being an information technology, or IT, worker is not a job I envy.

options.text: It is envied by many.
It does not appeal to him.
It is financially rewarding.
It does not match his abilities.

questions.prompt: What is the finding of a recent survey on employees who have a job reliant on IT support?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
最近一项针对工作依赖IT支持的员工的调查有何发现?
A) IT有助于提高生产力。
B) IT有助于改善质量控制。
C) 许多员工对IT深感沮丧。
D) 大多数员工在工作中严重依赖IT。
**判型** What is the finding of a recent survey 直接问一项调查的发现，是对原文具体信息的复述，属于细节题。
**拆句** 主干 What is the finding of a recent survey on employees，on 引出调查对象、who 从句进一步限定。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 根据一项最新调查，工作依赖 IT 支持的员工把 IT 视为工作不满的主要来源。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反IT helps boost productivity. 说 IT 提升生产力，与原文 their productivity deteriorating（生产力下降）完全相反。
B) 与原文相反IT helps improve quality control. 说 IT 改善质量控制，但原文是 quality control non-existent，质控"不复存在"，方向反转。
C) ✓ 正确consider IT a major source of job dissatisfaction ↔Many employees are deeply frustrated by IT预判"员工对 IT 极度不满"与 Many employees are deeply frustrated by IT. 完全吻合；其他三项要么把 IT 说成正面作用，要么扯到使用频率，均偏离结论。
D) 答非所问Most employees rely heavily on IT in their work. 说"大多数员工严重依赖 IT"，但题干问的是调查的 finding，而原文 finding 是"员工不满"，不是"员工依赖"；"依赖"只是调查对象的限定条件，不是调查结论。
questions.quote: According to a recent survey, employees who have a job reliant on IT support consider IT a major source of job dissatisfaction.

options.text: IT helps boost productivity.
IT helps improve quality control.
Many employees are deeply frustrated by IT.
Most employees rely heavily on IT in their work.

questions.prompt: What is said to happen when IT is functioning properly?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
据说当IT正常运行时会发生什么?
A) 员工的工作效率会大幅提升。
B) 员工变得更加依赖机器。
C) 不再有任何枯燥或重复性的任务。
D) 员工对自己的工作变得更有信心。
**判型** What is said to happen when IT is functioning properly? 问在某条件下会发生什么具体结果，是原文已有陈述的复述题，属细节题。
**拆句** 题干主干 What is said to happen，when 从句修饰 happen，is said 是被动语态，弱化作者主观色彩，照常按客观细节处理。
**定位** 当 IT 像它本应那样运转时，员工的自信心便会膨胀。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 过度推断There is a big boost in employees' work efficiency. 把答案换成"工作效率大幅提升"，原文只说自信和工作满意度上升，并未在 IT 正常运转时给出"效率大幅提升"的结论；"a big boost"也属于原文未表达的程度夸大。
B) 偷换概念Employees become more dependent on machines. 说员工"更依赖机器"，原文谈的是 IT 正常时员工"自信增强"，未涉及依赖加深；"依赖加深"通常是负面评价，与本段 IT正常时的正向描述也不符。
C) 过度推断原文 well-functioning machines relieve them of dull tasks or repetitive processes说机器"减轻"枯燥重复任务，There are no longer any boring or repetitive tasks. 却说"不再有任何"重复任务，把"缓解"夸大为"彻底消除"。
D) ✓ 正确employee self-confidence swells ↔ Employees become more confident in their work预判"员工自信增强"与 Employees become more confident in their work. 几乎逐字同义；其余选项不是过度推断就是与原文相反。
questions.quote: When IT is operating as it should, employee self-confidence swells.

options.text: There is a big boost in employees' work efficiency.
Employees become more dependent on machines.
There are no longer any boring or repetitive tasks.
Employees become more confident in their work.

questions.prompt: What should business leaders do before implementing new IT initiatives?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
企业领导者在实施新的IT举措之前应该做什么?
A) 考虑客户的各种期望。
B) 列出承诺要实现的各项效率提升。
C) 评估培训员工的高昂成本。
D) 考虑对员工可能产生的影响。
**判型** What should business leaders do before implementing new IT initiatives? 问"应当做什么"，对应原文里直接给出建议/批评的句子，是细节题。
**拆句** 主干 What should business leaders do，before 引导时间状语 before implementing new IT initiatives，implementing 是动名词作介词宾语。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 正因如此，管理者应当意识到 IT 用户体验对员工有多大影响，并下大力气确保 IT 团队消除程序错误与应用崩溃。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴Consider the various expectations of their customers. 把考虑对象从员工换成"客户"，但全文从未谈及 customers，关注点始终是 employees/end user。
B) 与原文相反Draw up a list of the efficiencies to be promised. 把"承诺的效率"列成清单，原文恰恰批评 a long list of promised efficiencies has been reversed，即"承诺过的效率被打回原形"，是失败之处而非应做之事。
C) 无中生有Assess the swollen cost of training the employees. 借用 swollen expectations have been popped 中的 swollen 拼出"激增的培训成本"，但原文 swollen 形容的是expectations（被吹胀的预期），从未提培训成本。
D) ✓ 正确with little consideration of how those changes will impact the end user ↔Think about the possible effects on their employees managers should appreciate just how influential the IT user experience is to their employees ↔Think about the possible effects on their employees预判"先考虑对员工的影响"和 Think about the possible effects on their employees.高度吻合；A/B/C 要么换错对象，要么偏离核心动作。
questions.quote: Which is why managers should appreciate just how influential the IT user experience is to their employees, and exert substantial effort in ensuring their IT team eliminates programming errors and application crashes.

options.text: Consider the various expectations of their customers.
Draw up a list of the efficiencies to be promised.
Assess the swollen cost of training the employees.
Think about the possible effects on their employees.

questions.prompt: How can a business help improve its employees' experience in using IT?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
企业如何帮助改善员工使用IT的体验?
A) 通过设计适合他们需求的系统。
B) 通过确保他们的心理健康状况良好。
C) 通过调整他们的工作以适应IT系统。
D) 通过为他们提供定期的在职培训。
**判型** How can a business help improve its employees' experience in using IT? 问公司具体如何改善，对应原文给出的具体做法句，属细节题。
**拆句** 主干 How can a business help improve its employees' experience，in using IT 是后置介词短语修饰 experience。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 因此，企业需要这样搭建其 IT 基础设施：使其设计去适配员工的工作，而不是让员工调整工作去迁就公司的 IT 局限。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确set up their IT infrastructure so that it is designed to fit in with their employees' work↔By designing systems that suit their needs预判"IT 去适配员工"严丝合缝对应 By designing systems that suit their needs.；B/C/D 要么扯心理健康、要么取了 rather than 后的反向做法、要么属于无中生有的培训。
B) 偷换概念By ensuring that their mental health is sound. 借用 what employees experience mentally when they use IT 里的 mentally 拼出"确保心理健康"，但原文是"理解员工使用 IT 时的心理体验"，不是"维护员工心理健康"，且这一点也不是末段给出的总对策。
C) 与原文相反By adjusting their work to suit the IT system. 把 rather than 后的反面做法 adjust their work to fit in with the company's IT limitations 当成对策，方向完全反转。
D) 无中生有By offering them regular in-service training. 提到"定期在职培训"，全文从未谈及培训这件事，纯属新概念。
questions.quote: Therefore, businesses need to set up their IT infrastructure so that it is designed to fit in with their employees' work, rather than adjust their work to fit in with the company's IT limitations.

options.text: By designing systems that suit their needs.
By ensuring that their mental health is sound.
By adjusting their work to suit the IT system.
By offering them regular in-service training.

title: Educators and business leaders have more in common…

sentences.text: Educators and business leaders have more in common than it may seem.
Teachers want to prepare students for a successful future.
Technology companies have an interest in developing a workforce with the STEM (science, technology, engineering and math) skills needed to grow the company and advance the industry.
How can they work together to achieve these goals?
Play may be the answer.

passage.translation: 教育工作者和企业领导者之间的共同点可能比表面看起来更多。教师希望为学生的成功未来做好准备。科技公司有兴趣培养一支具备STEM(科学、技术、工程和数学)技能的劳动力队伍,以发展公司并推动行业进步。他们如何共同合作来实现这些目标?玩耍可能就是答案。

sentences.text: Focusing on STEM skills is important, but the reality is that STEM skills are enhanced and more relevant when combined with traditional, hands-on creative activities.
This combination is proving to be the best way to prepare today's children to be the makers and builders of tomorrow.
That is why technology companies are partnering with educators to bring back good, old-fashioned play.

passage.translation: 关注STEM技能很重要,但现实是,当STEM技能与传统的动手创造性活动相结合时,它们会得到增强并变得更加相关。事实证明,这种结合是让今天的孩子为成为明天的创造者和建设者做好准备的最佳方式。这就是为什么科技公司正在与教育工作者合作,让美好的老式玩耍重新回归。

sentences.text: In fact many experts argue that the most important 21st-century skills aren't related to specific technologies or subject matter, but to creativity; skills like imagination, problem-finding and problem- solving, teamwork, optimism, patience and the ability to experiment and take risks.
These are skills acquired when kids tinker(鼓捣小玩意).
High-tech industries such as NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory have found that their best overall problem solvers were master tinkerers in their youth.

passage.translation: 事实上,许多专家认为,最重要的21世纪技能与特定技术或学科无关,而是与创造力有关;这些技能包括想象力、发现问题和解决问题的能力、团队合作、乐观精神、耐心以及实验和冒险的能力。这些都是孩子们在鼓捣小玩意时获得的技能。NASA喷气推进实验室等高科技行业发现,他们最优秀的综合问题解决者在年轻时都是鼓捣小玩意的高手。

sentences.text: There are cognitive(认知的) benefits of doing things the way we did as children—building something, tearing it down, then building it up again.
Research shows that given 15 minutes of free play, four- and five-year-olds will spend a third of this time engaged in spatial, mathematical, and architectural activities.
This type of play—especially with building blocks—helps children discover and develop key principles in math and geometry.

passage.translation: 以我们儿时的方式做事——建造某样东西,拆掉它,然后再重新建造——具有认知上的益处。研究表明,给予15分钟的自由玩耍时间,四五岁的孩子会将其中三分之一的时间用于空间、数学和建筑活动。这种类型的玩耍——尤其是玩积木——帮助儿童发现和发展数学和几何学中的关键原理。

sentences.text: If play and building are critical to 21st-century skill development, that's really good news for two reasons: Children are born builders, makers, and creators, so fostering(培养) 21st-century skills may be as simple as giving kids room to play, tinker and try things out, even as they grow older.
Secondly, it doesn't take 21st-century technology to foster 21st-century skills.
This is especially important for under- resourced schools and communities.
Taking whatever materials are handy and tinkering with them is a simple way to engage those important "maker" skills.
And anyone, anywhere, can do it.

passage.translation: 如果玩耍和建造对21世纪技能发展至关重要,那么这确实是个好消息,原因有二:孩子天生就是建造者、创造者和制作者,因此培养21世纪技能可能就像给孩子们留出空间去玩耍、鼓捣和尝试事物一样简单,即使他们逐渐长大也是如此。其次,培养21世纪技能不需要21世纪的技术。这对资源不足的学校和社区尤其重要。利用手头任何材料进行鼓捣,是激发那些重要的"创造者"技能的简单方法。而且任何人在任何地方都可以做到。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about educators?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者关于教育工作者说了什么?
A) 他们向科技公司寻求建议以实现教学目标。
B) 他们在为企业培养劳动力方面取得了成功。
C) 他们帮助学生获得未来成功所需的技能。
D) 他们与科技公司合作以提高教学效率。
**判型** 题干 What does the author say about educators 问的是作者对教育者说了什么客观陈述，没有 infer/imply/mainly about，是定位 + 转述型细节题。
**拆句** What does the author say about educators 主干是 "the author say what about educators" 的疑问倒装，about 后面跟话题对象，结构简单、无陷阱。
**定位** 教师想让学生为成功的未来做好准备。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有They seek advice from technology companies to achieve teaching goals 说教师向科技公司寻求建议，原文只说双方有共同点 Educators and business leaders have more in common than it may seem，并没有任何「教师向公司讨教」的方向性陈述。
B) 与原文相反They have been successful in preparing the workforce for companies 用现在完成时说教师已经成功地把劳动力交付给公司，原文只说 Teachers want to prepare students for a successful future——是 want to 的愿望，不是已实现的成果。
C) ✓ 正确Teachers want to prepare students for a successful future ↔They help students acquire the skills needed for their future success预判要求「准备 + 未来 + 学生」三要素齐全，They help students acquire the skills needed for their future success 把三个要素一一对应，无新增也无遗漏，是定位句的标准同义替换。
D) 偷换概念They partner with technology companies to enhance teaching efficiency 说教师与公司合作以提升教学效率，原文虽然提到 technology companies are partnering with educators to bring back good, old-fashioned play，但目的是把游戏带回课堂，不是「提升教学效率」。
questions.quote: Teachers want to prepare students for a successful future.

options.text: They seek advice from technology companies to achieve teaching goals.
They have been successful in preparing the workforce for companies.
They help students acquire the skills needed for their future success.
They partner with technology companies to enhance teaching efficiency.

questions.prompt: How can educators better develop students' STEM skills, according to the author?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
根据作者的观点,教育工作者如何才能更好地培养学生的STEM技能?
A) 通过将它们与传统的、富有启发性的活动相结合。
B) 通过邀请企业领导者帮助设计课程。
C) 通过增强学生批判性思考的能力。
D) 通过向学生展示最好的学习方式是通过玩耍。
**判型** 题干 How can educators better develop students' STEM skills 问的是具体方法，需要回原文找一句明确的「办法」陈述，属于方法型细节题。
**拆句** How can educators better develop students' STEM skills, according to the author：主干 educators develop STEM skills，better 是副词修饰 develop，according to the author 是插入语，整句问的是方法，结构简单。
**定位** 关注 STEM 技能很重要，但事实是，只有当 STEM 技能与传统的、动手的创造性活动相结合时，这些技能才能得到强化，也才更具相关性。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确STEM skills are enhanced and more relevant when combined with traditional, hands-on creative activities↔ By blending them with traditional, stimulating activities预判的三要素「结合 + 传统 + 动手/创意」，By blending them with traditional, stimulating activities 命中「结合」「传统」两项硬词，「动手创意」被合理上位化为stimulating，整体语义等值。
B) 无中生有By inviting business leaders to help design curriculums 说请商业领袖来帮忙设计课程，原文只说商业领袖与教师有共同利益、且科技公司与教师合作把游戏带回来technology companies are partnering with educators to bring back good, old- fashioned play，没有任何「商业领袖设计课程」的说法。
C) 偷换概念By enhancing students' ability to think in a critical way 把方法说成「增强批判性思维」，但原文里 the most important 21st-century skills aren't related to specific technologies or subject matter, but to creativity 列出的是 creativity、imagination、problem-solving，并没有 critical thinking 这一项。
D) 过度推断By showing students the best way to learn is through play 说告诉学生学习的最佳方式是玩，原文虽然反复肯定 play 的价值 Play may be the answer，但用 may 表推测，且没有把 play 表述为 the best way to learn，属于对原文力度的放大。
questions.quote: Focusing on STEM skills is important, but the reality is that STEM skills are enhanced and more relevant when combined with traditional, hands-on creative activities.

options.text: By blending them with traditional, stimulating activities.
By inviting business leaders to help design curriculums.
By enhancing students' ability to think in a critical way.
By showing students the best way to learn is through play.

questions.prompt: How do children acquire the skills needed for the 21st century?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
儿童如何获得21世纪所需的技能?
A) 通过参与涉及特定技术的活动。
B) 通过摆弄物品来自行解决问题。
C) 通过熟悉高科技设备。
D) 通过团队合作掌握基本原理。
**判型** 题干 How do children acquire the skills needed for the 21st century 是 How + 一般疑问，问获得方式，定位 → 同义替换即可，不需要主旨级归纳。
**拆句** How do children acquire the skills needed for the 21st century：主干 children acquire the skills，needed for the 21st century 是过去分词后置定语修饰 skills，等价于the skills which are needed for the 21st century。
**定位** 这些（21 世纪所需的）能力，正是孩子们在鼓捣小玩意时获得的。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反By engaging in activities involving specific technologies 说通过涉及具体技术的活动来获得能力，但 the most important 21st-century skills aren't related to specific technologies or subject matter, but to creativity 明确说不是关联于 specific technologies，选项与原文方向相反。
B) ✓ 正确These are skills acquired when kids tinker ↔By playing with things to solve problems on their own预判核心「自己动手 + 鼓捣 / 玩耍」在 By playing with things to solve problems on their own 中以 playing with things + on their own 完整复现，并把要获得的能力具体化为 solve problems，与同段的 problem-solving 完全一致。
C) 与原文相反By familiarizing themselves with high-tech gadgets 说让孩子熟悉高科技装置，但 it doesn't take 21st-century technology to foster 21st-century skills 明确说培养这些技能并不需要 21 世纪的高科技。
D) 张冠李戴By mastering basic principles through teamwork 把方式说成「通过团队合作掌握基本原理」，原文同段列出的能力清单 skills like imagination, problem-finding and problem-solving, teamwork, optimism, patience and the ability to experiment and take risks 里虽然出现 teamwork，但 teamwork 是要获得的能力之一，不是获得能力的途径，且 basic principles 出现在第四段说的是数学几何，与 21 世纪技能不是同一回事。
questions.quote: These are skills acquired when kids tinker.

options.text: By engaging in activities involving specific technologies.
By playing with things to solve problems on their own.
By familiarizing themselves with high-tech gadgets.
By mastering basic principles through teamwork.

questions.prompt: What can we do to help children learn the basics of math and geometry?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
我们可以做些什么来帮助儿童学习数学和几何的基础知识?
A) 尽早激发他们的兴趣。
B) 花更多时间与他们一起玩游戏。
C) 鼓励他们动手制作东西。
D) 允许他们自由摆弄计算器。
**判型** 题干 What can we do to help children learn the basics of math and geometry 问的是建议性做法，回原文找一句明确的做法陈述即可，属于方法型细节题。
**拆句** What can we do to help children learn the basics of math and geometry：主干 we do what，to help 是目的状语，help children learn 是 help sb. do 结构，learn the basics of math and geometry 是 help 的宾补，无难点。
**定位** 这种游戏——尤其是搭积木——能帮助孩子发现并掌握数学和几何中的关键原理。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Stimulate their interest as early as possible 说要尽早激发兴趣，原文虽提到 four- and five-year-olds Research shows that given 15 minutes of free play, four- and five-year-olds will spend a third of this time engaged in spatial, mathematical, and architectural activities，但并没有提出「激发兴趣」这一做法，更没有「越早越好」的表态。
B) 偷换概念Spend more time playing games with them 说大人花更多时间陪孩子玩游戏，原文的关键是「孩子自己搭建」 This type of play—especially with building blocks—helps children discover and develop key principles in math and geometry，并未要求大人陪玩，更没说 more time 这一程度。
C) ✓ 正确This type of play—especially with building blocks—helps children discover and develop key principles in math and geometry↔ Encourage them to make things with hands预判核心「动手 + 搭建/制作」，Encourage them to make things with hands 同时命中 make（建造/制作）与 with hands（动手），无新增信息，是 building blocks 的合理上位概括。
D) 与原文相反Allow them to tinker freely with calculators 把鼓捣的对象换成计算器，原文却强调building blocks 这类纯动手物件；且 it doesn't take 21st-century technology to foster 21st-century skills 已经否定了高科技工具的必要性，calculators 属于反向。
questions.quote: This type of play—especially with building blocks—helps children discover and develop key principles in math and geometry.

options.text: Stimulate their interest as early as possible.
Spend more time playing games with them.
Encourage them to make things with hands.
Allow them to tinker freely with calculators.

questions.prompt: What does the author advise disadvantaged schools and communities to do?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者建议条件不利的学校和社区做什么?
A) 培训学生成为创造者以满足未来市场需求。
B) 利用现有资源培养学生的创造性技能。
C) 让学生参与具有挑战性的任务以培养他们的创造力。
D) 与企业合作改善他们的教学设施。
**判型** 题干 What does the author advise disadvantaged schools and communities to do 是定向问作者建议，需要找一句明确针对弱势学校的建议句，是定位型细节题，不需要全篇归纳。
**拆句** What does the author advise disadvantaged schools and communities to do：主干the author advise sb. to do sth.，advise sb. to do 是固定搭配，disadvantaged ... communities 整体作 advise 的宾语，结构清晰。
**定位** 这一点对于资源匮乏的学校和社区尤为重要。拿手边任何能找到的材料动手鼓捣，就是激发这些重要「制造者」能力的一种简单办法。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Train students to be makers to meet future market demands 把目的设为「满足未来市场需求」，原文里反复说的是培养 maker / creator 等能力 Children are born builders, makers, and creators，从未出现 market demands 这类商业目的。
B) ✓ 正确Taking whatever materials are handy and tinkering with them is a simple way to engage those important "maker" skills↔ Develop students' creative skills with the resources available it doesn't take 21st-century technology to foster 21st-century skills↔Develop students' creative skills with the resources available预判的「现有/手边资源 + 创造性能力」，Develop students' creative skills with the resources available 同时命中 with the resources available（现有资源）与 creative skills（创造性能力），两项语义点齐全且力度匹配。
C) 与原文相反Engage students with challenging tasks to foster their creativity 说让学生做有挑战性的任务，原文却强调 fostering 21st-century skills may be as simple as giving kids room to play, tinker and try things out，用的是 as simple as，方向是「越简单越好」。
D) 张冠李戴Work together with companies to improve their teaching facilities 说与公司合作改善教学设施，原文虽然在首段提到 Educators and business leaders have more in common than it may seem，但末段给资源匮乏地区的建议只是用手边材料鼓捣，从未提到「与公司合作改善设施」。
questions.quote: This is especially important for under-resourced schools and communities. Taking whatever materials are handy and tinkering with them is a simple way to engage those important "maker" skills.

options.text: Train students to be makers to meet future market demands.
Develop students' creative skills with the resources available.
Engage students with challenging tasks to foster their creativity.
Work together with companies to improve their teaching facilities.

title: Most animals seek shade when temperatures in the…

sentences.text: Most animals seek shade when temperatures in the Sahara Desert soar to 120 degrees Fahrenheit.
But for the Saharan silver ant, (26)____ from their underground nests into the sun's brutal rays to(27)____ for food, this is the perfect time to seek lunch.
In 2015 these ants were joined in the desert by scientists from two Belgian universities, who spent a month in the (28)____ heat tracking the ants and digging out their nests.
The goal was simple, to discover how the (29)____ adapted to the kind of heat that can (30)____ melt the bottom of shoes.

passage.translation: 当撒哈拉沙漠的温度飙升到华氏120度时，大多数动物都会寻找阴凉处。但对于撒哈拉银蚁来说，从地下巢穴爬出来进入太阳的酷热光线中寻找食物，这正是寻找午餐的完美时机。2015年，来自比利时两所大学的科学家在沙漠中加入了这些蚂蚁的行列，他们在极端高温中度过了一个月的时间追踪蚂蚁并挖掘它们的巢穴。目标很简单，就是发现这个物种如何适应那种能够真正融化鞋底的高温。

sentences.text: Back in Belgium, the scientists looked at the ants under an electronic microscope and found that their (31)____ , triangular hair reflects light like a prism(棱镜), giving them a metallic reflection and protecting them from the sun's awful heat.
When Ph.D. student Quentin Willot (32)____ the hair from an ant with a (33)____ knife and put it under a heat lamp, its temperature jumped.

passage.translation: 回到比利时后,科学家们在电子显微镜下观察这些蚂蚁,发现它们厚实的三角形毛发像棱镜一样反射光线,使它们产生金属反射效果,并保护它们免受太阳的可怕高温伤害。当博士生Quentin Willot用一把小刀从一只蚂蚁身上移除毛发并将其放在热灯下时,它的温度骤升。

sentences.text: The ants' method of staying cool is (34)____ among animals.
Could this reflective type of hair protect people?

Willot says companies are interested in (35)____ these ants' method of heat protection for human use, including everything from helping to protect the lives of firefighters to keeping homes cool in summer.

passage.translation: 蚂蚁保持凉爽的方法在动物中是独一无二的。这种反射型毛发能否保护人类呢?Willot说,一些公司对将这些蚂蚁的热保护方法应用于人类使用很感兴趣,包括从帮助保护消防员的生命到在夏季保持房屋凉爽等各个方面。

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
Most animals seek shade when temperatures in the Sahara Desert soar to 120 degrees Fahrenheit. But for the Saharan silver ant, {{26}} from their underground nests into the sun's brutal rays to{{27}} for food, this is the perfect time to seek lunch. In 2015 these ants were joined in the desert by scientists from two Belgian universities, who spent a month in the {{28}} heat tracking the ants and digging out their nests. The goal was simple, to discover how the {{29}} adapted to the kind of heat that can {{30}} melt the bottom of shoes.

Back in Belgium, the scientists looked at the ants under an electronic microscope and found that their {{31}} , triangular hair reflects light like a prism(棱镜), giving them a metallic reflection and protecting them from the sun's awful heat. When Ph.D. student Quentin Willot {{32}} the hair from an ant with a {{33}} knife and put it under a heat lamp, its temperature jumped.

The ants' method of staying cool is {{34}} among animals. Could this reflective type of hair protect people? Willot says companies are interested in {{35}} these ants' method of heat protection for human use, including everything from helping to protect the lives of firefighters to keeping homes cool in summer.

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) crawling 动词
**词性槽** 逗号后补充说明主语动作，缺现在分词
**依据** 蚂蚁「爬出」地巢钻进烈日crawling「爬行」描述银蚁 from their underground nests into the sun's brutal rays 从地下巢穴爬向烈日的动作，符合蚂蚁的行进方式与全文觅食情境。

**答案** F) hunt 动词
**词性槽** 不定式 to 后，缺动词原形
**依据** to hunt for food = 觅食，正合主旨全文开头点明银蚁外出 to seek lunch，hunt 与 for food 构成 hunt for「搜寻、觅食」，与「这是觅食好时机」完全一致。

**答案** E) extreme 形容词
**词性槽** 名词 heat 前作定语，缺形容词
**依据** 形容沙漠「极端」高温最贴全文反复渲染 120 degrees Fahrenheit 的酷热，extreme「极端的、极度的」修饰 heat表「极端高温」，与主旨完全契合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) moderate 义反，温和与酷热相悖moderate「适度的、温和的」恰与沙漠 120 华氏度的极热相反。
M) thick thick 不修饰 heat thick「厚的」不与 heat 搭配，且应留给 __(31)__ 的毛发。
I) remote 偏远修饰不了热量remote「偏远的」用于地点而非热度，语义不搭。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) species 名词
**词性槽** 定冠词 the 后作宾语，缺名词
**依据** 指银蚁这一「物种」如何适应酷热全文研究对象是 the Saharan silver ant 这种蚂蚁，species「物种」指代这一生物种类如何adapted to 高温，与主旨吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
L) specimens 标本是死物，不会主动「适应」specimens「标本、样本」指采集的实物样品，没有生命，不能作 adapted to「适应」的主语；这里讲的是活体物种如何适应酷热。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 L) —— specimens 与 species 形近、都搭科研语境，最易错选。两词同为名词、都能跟在 the 后，且「标本」与科学家研究高度相关，但 the __(29)__adapted to the kind of heat 的谓语是「适应」，只有活物种能适应，死标本不能；防坑：看谁能当这个谓语的主语。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) literally 副词
**词性槽** 助动词 can 与实义动词 melt 之间，缺副词
**依据** 强调「真能把鞋底融化」非夸张can __(30)__ melt the bottom of shoes 在渲染高温之极，literally「确确实实地、简直」强调这是字面意义上真会发生，强化酷热程度。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) consciously高温无意识可言，主语错位consciously「有意识地」用于有思维的主体，而这里主语是 heat（热量），热不会「有意识地」融鞋，语义荒谬。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 B) —— consciously 词性对、位置也能放，易当副词随手填。consciously 与 literally 同为副词、都能塞进 can __(30)__ melt the bottom of shoes，但主语是 heat（热量），热不会「有意识地」融鞋；防坑：副词必须和被修饰动词的施动者语义相容，无意识主体排除 consciously。

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) thick 形容词
**词性槽** 与 triangular 并列修饰 hair，缺形容词
**依据** 描述毛发「浓密/粗」，与三角形、反光相称下文说这种毛 reflects light like a prism 像棱镜反光，thick「厚的、浓密的、粗的」描述毛发的物理形态，与三角形截面、强反光相配。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) moderate 「适度的毛发」无意义moderate「适度的」修饰 hair 不传递任何形态信息，不贴。
I) remote 偏远修饰不了毛发remote「偏远的」与 hair 完全不搭。

questions.explanation:
**答案** J) removed 动词
**词性槽** 从句主语 Willot 后缺谓语动词（过去式）
**依据** 「去掉/移除」蚂蚁毛发再加热做实验后文 put it under a heat lamp, its temperature jumped 是把取下的毛发拿去加热，removed「移除、去掉」正描述「从蚂蚁身上取下毛发」这一动作。

**答案** N) tiny 形容词
**词性槽** 冠词 a 与名词 knife 之间，缺形容词作定语
**依据** 蚂蚁毛发极细，配「微小的」刀刃才合理上文 Quentin Willot __(32)__ the hair from an ant 是从一只蚂蚁身上取毛发，这等精细操作要用极小的刀，tiny「极小的」最贴。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) thick 义反，厚刀切不下蚂蚁毛thick「厚的、粗的」与精细取毛的语境相反，且 thick 已为 __(31)__ 描述毛发留着，更不该填这里。
E) extreme 搭配不通，无 extreme knife 之说extreme「极端的」不修饰刀具，且要留给 __(28)__/__(30)__ 处的酷热语境。
H) moderate 语义空泛，与精细取毛无关moderate「适度的」修饰刀毫无信息，不贴语境。
I) remote 义不搭，偏远修饰不了刀remote「偏远的」用于地点，配 knife 不成立。
O) unique 义不搭，且要留给 __(34)__unique「独特的」修饰刀无意义，且该词是 __(34)__ 处「方法独特」的最佳人选。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) unique 形容词
**词性槽** 系动词 is 后作表语，缺形容词
**依据** 反光毛降温在动物中「独特」，引出可否用于人类下文紧接 Could this reflective type of hair protect people? 用反问凸显其稀有可贵，unique「独一无二的」正点出该方法在动物界少见、值得借鉴。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) thick 厚不能修饰「方法」thick「厚的」修饰 method 不通，且要留给 __(31)__ 的毛发。
E) extreme 极端的方法语义偏，且留给酷热extreme「极端的」不贴「独特罕见」的语气，且是 __(28)__/__(30)__ 酷热语境的强候选。
H) moderate 「适度的方法」无信息且不引出后文moderate「适度的」既空泛，又无法支撑下句「能否用于人类」的转折。
I) remote 义不搭，偏远修饰不了方法remote「偏远的」与 method 语义不相关。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) adapting 动词
**词性槽** 介词 in 后接动名词，需 -ing 动词
**依据** 企业有意「改造」银蚁防热法供人类用下文 these ants' method of heat protection for human use 是把蚂蚁方法改用于人，adapting「改造、使适用」正对这层意思。

title: The History of the Lunch Box

passage.label: A

sentences.text: It was made of shiny, bright pink plastic with a Little Mermaid sticker on the front, and I carried it with me nearly every single day.
My lunch box was one of my first prized possessions, a proud statement to everyone in my kindergarten: "I love Mermaid-Ariel on my lunch box."

passage.translation: 它是由闪亮的亮粉色塑料制成的,正面贴着一张小美人鱼的贴纸,我几乎每天都带着它。我的饭盒是我最早的珍贵物品之一,向幼儿园里的每个人骄傲地宣告:"我喜欢我饭盒上的美人鱼爱丽儿。"

passage.label: B

sentences.text: That bulky container served me well through my first and second grades, until the live-action version of 101 Dalmatians hit theaters, and I needed the newest red plastic box with characters like Pongo and Perdita on the front.
I know I'm not alone here—I bet you loved your first lunchbox, too.

passage.translation: 那个笨重的容器陪伴我度过了一年级和二年级,直到真人版《101斑点狗》上映,我需要最新的红色塑料盒,正面印着Pongo和Perdita这样的角色。我知道我不是唯一一个——我敢说你也喜欢过你的第一个饭盒。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: Lunch boxes have been connecting kids to cartoons and TV shows and super-heroes for decades.
But it wasn't always that way.
Once upon a time, they weren't even boxes.
As schools have changed in the past century, the midday meal container has evolved right along with them.

passage.translation: 几十年来,饭盒一直将孩子们与卡通、电视节目和超级英雄联系在一起。但情况并非一直如此。曾几何时,它们甚至不是盒子。随着学校在过去一个世纪中发生变化,午餐容器也随之演变。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: Let's start back at the beginning of the 20th century—the beginning of the lunch box story, really.
While there were neighborhood schools in cities and suburbs, one-room schoolhouses were common in rural areas.
As grandparents have been saying for generations, kids would travel miles to school in the countryside (often on foot).

passage.translation: 让我们回到20世纪初——这确实是饭盒故事的开端。虽然城市和郊区有社区学校,但单间校舍在农村地区很常见。正如祖父母们世世代代所说的那样,农村的孩子们要走很远的路去上学(通常是步行)。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: "You had kids in rural areas who couldn't go home from school for lunch, so bringing your lunch wrapped in a cloth, in oiled paper, in a little wooden box or something like that was a very long- standing rural tradition," says Paula Johnson, head of food history section at the Smithsonian National Museum of American History in Washington, D.C.

passage.translation: "在农村地区,孩子们无法回家吃午饭,所以用布包着、用油纸包着、用小木盒之类的东西带午餐是一个由来已久的农村传统,"位于华盛顿特区的Smithsonian国立美国历史博物馆食品历史部门负责人Paula Johnson说。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: City kids, on the other hand, went home for lunch and came back.
Since they rarely carried a meal, the few metal lunch buckets on the market were mainly for tradesmen and factory workers.

passage.translation: 另一方面,城市的孩子们会回家吃午饭,然后再回来。由于他们很少携带饭食,市场上为数不多的金属饭盒主要是供工匠和工厂工人使用的。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: After World War II, a bunch of changes reshaped schools—and lunches.
More women joined the workforce.
Small schools consolidated into larger ones, meaning more students were farther away from home.
And the National School Lunch Act in 1946 made cafeterias much more common.
Still, there wasn't much of a market for lunch containers—yet.
Students who carried their lunch often did so in a re-purposed bucket or tin of some kind.

passage.translation: 第二次世界大战后,一系列变化重塑了学校和午餐。更多女性加入劳动力队伍。小学校合并成更大的学校,意味着更多学生离家更远。1946年的《国家学校午餐法案》使食堂变得更加普遍。尽管如此,午餐容器的市场还不大——至少当时如此。携带午餐的学生通常使用某种改装的桶或罐头盒。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: And then everything changed in the year of 1950.
You might as well call it the Year of the Lunch Box, thanks in large part to a genius move by a Nashville-based manufacturer, Aladdin Industries.
The company already made square metal meal containers, the kind workers carried, and some had started to show up in the hands of school kids.

passage.translation: 然后在1950年,一切都改变了。你不妨称它为饭盒之年,这在很大程度上要归功于Nashville的制造商Aladdin Industries的天才之举。该公司已经生产方形金属餐盒,就是工人们携带的那种,其中一些开始出现在学校孩子们手中。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: But these containers were really durable, lasting years on end.
That was great for the consumer, not so much for the manufacturer.
So executives at Aladdin hit on an idea that would harness the newfound popularity of television.
They covered lunch boxes with striking red paint and added a picture of TV and radio cowboy Hopalong Cassidy on the front.

passage.translation: 但这些容器真的很耐用,可以使用很多年。这对消费者来说很好,但对制造商来说就不那么好了。因此Aladdin的高管们想出了一个主意,利用电视新兴的流行度。他们用醒目的红色油漆涂覆饭盒,并在正面添加了电视和广播牛仔Hopalong Cassidy的图片。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: The company sold 600,000 units the first year.
It was a major "Ah-ha!" moment, and a wave of other manufacturers jumped on board to capitalize on new TV shows and movies.
"The Partridge Family, the Addams Family, the Six Million Dollar Man, the Bionic Woman—everything that was on television ended up on a lunch box," says Allen Woodall.
He's the founder of the Lunch Box Museum in Columbus, Georgia.
"It was a great marketing tool because kids were taking that TV show to school with them, and then when they got home they had them captured back on TV," he says.

passage.translation: 该公司第一年就售出了60万个。这是一个重大的"啊哈!"时刻,其他制造商纷纷加入,利用新的电视节目和电影。"Partridge Family、Addams Family、Six Million Dollar Man、Bionic Woman——电视上播出的所有内容最终都出现在饭盒上,"Allen Woodall说。他是位于Georgia州Columbus的饭盒博物馆的创始人。"这是一个很好的营销工具,因为孩子们把那个电视节目带到学校,然后当他们回家时,他们又在电视上看到了它们,"他说。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: And yes, you read that right: There is a lunch box museum, right near the Chattahoochee River.
Woodall has more than 2,000 items on display.
His favorite?
The Green Hornet lunch box, because he used to listen to the radio show back in the 1940s.

passage.translation: 是的,你没看错:确实有一个饭盒博物馆,就在Chattahoochee河附近。Woodall展出了2000多件物品。他最喜欢的?青蜂侠饭盒,因为他曾在1940年代听过这个广播节目。

passage.label: L

sentences.text: The new trend was also a great example of planned obsolescence, that is, to design a product so that it will soon become unfashionable or impossible to use and will need replacing.
Kids would beg for a new lunch box every year to keep up with the newest characters, even if their old lunchbox was perfectly usable.

passage.translation: 这一新趋势也是计划性淘汰的一个很好的例子,即设计一种产品,使其很快就会变得过时或无法使用,需要更换。孩子们每年都会乞求买一个新饭盒,以跟上最新的角色,即使他们的旧饭盒完全可以使用。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: The metal lunch box craze lasted until the mid-1980s, when plastic took over.
Two theories exist as to why.
The first—and most likely—is that plastic had simply become cheaper.
The second theory—possibly an urban myth—is that concerned parents in several states proposed bans on metal lunch boxes, claiming kids were using them as "weapons" to hit one another.
There's a lot on the internet about a state-wide ban in Florida, but a few days worth of digging by a historian at the Florida State Historical Society found no such legislation.
Either way, the metal lunch box was out.

passage.translation: 金属饭盒热潮持续到1980年代中期,当时塑料取而代之。关于原因有两种理论。第一种——也是最有可能的——是塑料变得更便宜了。第二种理论——可能是都市传说——是几个州担心的家长提议禁止金属饭盒,声称孩子们用它们作为"武器"互相击打。互联网上有很多关于Florida全州禁令的信息,但Florida州历史学会的一位历史学家经过几天的挖掘,没有发现任何此类立法。无论如何,金属饭盒退出了舞台。

passage.label: N

sentences.text: The last few decades have brought a new lunch box revolution, of sorts.
Plastic boxes changed to lined cloth sacks, and eventually, globalism brought tiffin containers from India and bento boxes from Japan.
Even the old metal lunch boxes have regained popularity.
"I don't think the heyday(鼎盛时期) has passed," says D.J.
Jayasekara, owner and founder of lunchbox.com, a retailer in Pasadena, California.
"I think it has evolved.
The days of the ready-made, 'you stick it in a lunchbox and carry it to school' are kind of done."

passage.translation: 过去几十年在某种程度上带来了新的饭盒革命。塑料盒变成了内衬布袋,最终,全球化从印度带来了tiffin容器,从日本带来了bento盒。即使是旧的金属饭盒也重新流行起来。"我不认为鼎盛时期已经过去,"lunchbox.com的所有者和创始人D.J. Jayasekara说,这是位于California州Pasadena的一家零售商。"我认为它已经演变了。那种现成的、'你把它放进饭盒里带到学校'的日子已经过去了。"

passage.label: O

sentences.text: The introduction of backpacks changed the lunch box scene a bit, he adds.
Once kids started carrying book bags, that bulky traditional lunch box was hard to fit inside.
"But you can't just throw a sandwich in a backpack," Jayasekara says.
"It still has to go into a container."
That is, in part, why smaller and softer containers have taken off—they fit into backpacks.

passage.translation: 背包的引入在一定程度上改变了饭盒的格局,他补充道。一旦孩子们开始背书包,那种笨重的传统饭盒就很难放进去了。"但你不能只是把三明治扔进背包里,"Jayasekara说。"它仍然必须装进一个容器里。"这在一定程度上解释了为什么更小、更软的容器开始流行——它们可以放进背包。

passage.label: P

sentences.text: And don't worry—whether it's a plastic bento box or a cloth bag, lunch containers can still easily be covered with popular culture.
"We keep pace with the movie industries so we can predict which characters are going to be popular for the coming months," Jayasekara says.
"You know, kids are kids."

passage.translation: 别担心——无论是塑料bento盒还是布袋,午餐容器仍然可以轻松印上流行文化。"我们与电影行业保持同步,这样我们就可以预测未来几个月哪些角色会受欢迎,"Jayasekara说。"你知道,孩子就是孩子。"

Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: Lunch containers were not necessary for school kids in cities.

城市里的学生不需要午餐盒。

在午餐盒上印上电视角色被证明是一种有效的营销策略。
