questions.tip:
**辨邻**
I I 段讲的是 Aladdin 因为盒子太耐用、销售吃亏，所以才想到「借电视红人印盒」这一点子——内容停留在动机和点子本身，没出现销量爆发、同行跟随这类「结果性」信息，不能承担 proved an effective marketing strategy 这一对「结果」的判断。executives at Aladdin hit on an idea that would harness the newfound popularity of television. They covered lunch boxes with striking red paint and added a picture of TV and radio cowboy Hopalong Cassidy on the front
questions.quote: It was a major "Ah-ha!" moment, and a wave of other manufacturers jumped on board to capitalize on new TV shows and movies. "It was a great marketing tool because kids were taking that TV show to school with them, and then when they got home they had them captured back on TV," he says.

questions.prompt: Smaller lunch boxes are preferred because they fit easily into backpacks.
questions.explanation:
**答案** O 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
更小的午餐盒更受欢迎,因为它们很容易装进背包。
**锚点** 更小盒 + 塞进书包
**定位** 这在一定程度上解释了为什么更小、更软的容器开始流行——它们能塞进书包。
**改写** Smaller lunch boxes are preferred ↔ smaller and softer containers have taken off被动偏好 ↔ 主动走红fit easily into backpacks ↔ they fit into backpacks几乎原样复现
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
N N 段讲塑料盒过渡到布袋、tiffin、bento 的整体演变，并引用 I don't think the heyday 的判断，但并未出现「书包」这一原因抓手，无法承担 fit easily into backpacks 这一具体因果。Plastic boxes changed to lined cloth sacks, and eventually, globalism brought tiffin containers from India and bento boxes from Japan
questions.quote: That is, in part, why smaller and softer containers have taken off—they fit into backpacks.

questions.prompt: Lunch boxes have evolved along with the transformation of schools.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
午餐盒随着学校的变革而演变。
**锚点** 随学校转型而演变
**定位** 随着过去一个世纪里学校发生变化，午间饭盒也随之一同演变。
**改写** Lunch boxes have evolved along with the transformation of schools ↔As schools have changed in the past century, the midday meal container has evolved right along with them句式重构 + 词性变换
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
G G 段列举二战后学校的几项具体变化 More women joined the workforce、Small schools consolidated into larger ones、the National School Lunch Act in 1946，这些都是「学校变了」的事实例证，未给出「午餐盒与学校共同演变」这一全景式总论，承载不了 Q39 的判断。After World War II, a bunch of changes reshaped schools—and lunches N N 段虽然有 I think it has evolved 这种「演变」措辞，但开头限定在 The last few decades have brought a new lunch box revolution——只是近几十年的局部演变，且并未把「学校转型」作为驱动因素，无法承担 transformation of schools 这一总论。The last few decades have brought a new lunch box revolution, of sorts
questions.quote: As schools have changed in the past century, the midday meal container has evolved right along with them.

questions.prompt: Around the beginning of the nineteen fifties, some school kids started to use metal meal containers.
questions.explanation:
**答案** H 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
大约在二十世纪五十年代初,一些学生开始使用金属餐盒。
**锚点** 1950 年前后 + 学生用金属饭盒
**定位** 1950 年一切都变了。你不妨把那一年称为「午餐盒元年」，这在很大程度上要归功于位于纳什维尔的制造商 Aladdin Industries 的一次妙招。这家公司当时已经生产方形金属饭盒——就是工人们用的那种——其中一些已开始出现在学生手里。
**改写** Around the beginning of the nineteen fifties ↔ in the year of 1950年份精确对应some school kids started to use metal meal containers ↔some had started to show up in the hands of school kids学生使用 ↔ 出现在学生手中
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
I I 段讲的是金属盒因为太耐用，于是被 covered with striking red paint 并加上Hopalong Cassidy 头像——这是金属盒进入学生手之后的下一步动作，承载不了some school kids started to use 这一「刚开始用」的语义。They covered lunch boxes with striking red paint and added a picture of TV and radio cowboy Hopalong Cassidy on the front
questions.quote: And then everything changed in the year of 1950. You might as well call it the Year of the Lunch Box, thanks in large part to a genius move by a Nashville-based manufacturer, Aladdin Industries. The company already made square metal meal containers, the kind workers carried, and some had started to show up in the hands of school kids.

questions.prompt: School kids are eager to get a new lunch box every year to stay in fashion.
questions.explanation:
**答案** L 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
学生们渴望每年得到一个新午餐盒以保持时尚。
**锚点** 每年换新盒 + 追潮流
**定位** 孩子们会每年央求换一只新午餐盒，好跟上最新角色，哪怕旧盒还完全能用。
**改写** eager to get a new lunch box every year ↔ Kids would beg for a new lunch box every year渴望 ↔ 央求stay in fashion ↔ keep up with the newest characters上位概念 ↔ 下位具体
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
J J 段主体是厂商和博物馆创办人的话 everything that was on television ended up on a lunch box，讲的是厂商如何利用 TV 角色，没有给出「孩子每年换新盒以追潮流」这一行为描述，承载不了 eager to get a new lunch box every year。a wave of other manufacturers jumped on board to capitalize on new TV shows and movies
questions.quote: Kids would beg for a new lunch box every year to keep up with the newest characters, even if their old lunchbox was perfectly usable.

questions.prompt: Rural kids used to walk a long way to school in the old days.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
农村孩子过去常常走很长的路去上学。
**锚点** 乡村孩子 + 步行很远去学校 + 旧时代
**定位** 正如祖辈们世代以来反复念叨的：乡下孩子上学常常要走好几英里路（往往是步行）。
**改写** Rural kids ↔ kids would travel miles to school in the countryside形容词 ↔ 地点状语walk a long way to school ↔kids would travel miles to school in the countryside (often on foot)动作 = 距离 + 方式 组合in the old days ↔ Let's start back at the beginning of the 20th century宽泛时代词 ↔ 具体世纪
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E E 段也涉及 rural kids，但内容是 bringing your lunch wrapped in a cloth, in oiled paper, in a little wooden box 这一中午带饭传统，没有触及「步行长距离上学」这一具体动作，无法承担 walk a long way to school。You had kids in rural areas who couldn't go home from school for lunch
questions.quote: As grandparents have been saying for generations, kids would travel miles to school in the countryside (often on foot).

questions.prompt: The author was proud of using a lunch box in her childhood.
questions.explanation:
**答案** A 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
作者为自己童年时使用午餐盒感到自豪。
**锚点** 作者本人 + 童年用盒很自豪
**定位** 我的午餐盒是我最早的珍宝之一，是我向幼儿园里每个人发出的骄傲宣言：「我爱我盒子上的美人鱼艾莉儿。」
**改写** The author was proud of using a lunch box ↔My lunch box was one of my first prized possessions, a proud statement to everyone in my kindergarten同根形容词 + 自豪情绪的直接吐露in her childhood ↔ in my kindergarten上位时代词 ↔ 下位时段词
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段虽然也是作者本人回忆，但讲的是 I needed the newest red plastic box 这一升级动作和 I bet you loved your first lunchbox, too 这一对读者的猜测，没有出现proud / pride 这种自豪情绪，无法承担 was proud 这一情感判断。That bulky container served me well through my first and second grades, until the live-action version of 101 Dalmatians hit theaters, and I needed the newest red plastic box
questions.quote: My lunch box was one of my first prized possessions, a proud statement to everyone in my kindergarten: "I love Mermaid-Ariel on my lunch box."

questions.prompt: The most probable reason for the popularity of plastic lunch boxes is that they are less expensive.
questions.explanation:
**答案** M 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
塑料午餐盒流行的最可能原因是它们更便宜。
**锚点** 塑料盒流行 + 最可能原因是便宜
**定位** 第一种——也是可能性最大的——解释是：塑料只是变得更便宜了。
**改写** popularity of plastic lunch boxes ↔ plastic took over走红 ↔ 取代The most probable reason ↔ The first—and most likely最高级近义less expensive ↔ plastic had simply become cheaper比较级近义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
N N 段虽然提到 Plastic boxes changed to lined cloth sacks 这一塑料盒的后续演变，但全段未给出「塑料盒为什么流行 / 取代金属」的原因，无法承担 The most probable reason for the popularity of plastic lunch boxes 这一对「原因」的判断。Plastic boxes changed to lined cloth sacks, and eventually, globalism brought tiffin containers from India and bento boxes from Japan
questions.quote: The first—and most likely—is that plastic had simply become cheaper.

questions.prompt: The durability of metal meal containers benefited consumers.
questions.explanation:
**答案** I 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
金属餐盒的耐用性使消费者受益。
**锚点** 金属饭盒耐用 + 利于消费者
**定位** 但这些饭盒非常耐用，能用上好多年。对消费者来说这是好事，对厂商就不那么好了。
**改写** The durability of metal meal containers↔these containers were really durable, lasting years on end名词化 ↔ 形容词谓语benefited consumers ↔ That was great for the consumer动词 ↔ 形容词短语
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
H H 段虽然提到 square metal meal containers，但全段聚焦「1950 年金属盒首次进入学生手」这一节点，未涉及 durable / great for the consumer 这一属性 + 评价判断，承担不了 Q45 的「耐用利消费者」语义。The company already made square metal meal containers, the kind workers carried, and some had started to show up in the hands of school kids
questions.quote: But these containers were really durable, lasting years on end. That was great for the consumer, not so much for the manufacturer.

title: Poverty Is a Story About Us, Not Them

passage.label: A

sentences.text: Too often still, we think we know what poverty looks like.
It's the way we've been taught, the images we've been force-fed for decades.
The chronically homeless.
The undocumented immigrant.
The urban poor, usually personified as a woman of color, the "welfare queen" politicians still too often reference.

passage.translation: 我们仍然常常认为自己知道贫困是什么样子。这是我们被教导的方式,是几十年来被强行灌输给我们的形象。长期无家可归者。无证移民。城市贫民,通常被塑造成有色人种女性,即政客们仍然经常提及的"福利女王"。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: But as income inequality rises to record levels in the United States, even in the midst of a record economic expansion, those familiar images are outdated, hurtful, and counterproductive to focusing attention on solutions and building ladders of opportunity.

passage.translation: 但随着美国收入不平等上升到创纪录水平,即使是在创纪录的经济扩张之中,那些熟悉的形象已经过时、具有伤害性,并且不利于将注意力集中在解决方案上和建立机会阶梯上。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: Today's faces of income inequality and lack of opportunity look like all of us.
It's Anna Landre, a disabled Georgetown University student fighting to keep health benefits that allow her the freedom to live her life.
It's Tiffanie Standard, a counselor for young women of color in Philadelphia who want to be tech entrepreneurs—but who must work multiple jobs to stay afloat.

It's Ken Outlaw, a welder in rural North Carolina whose dream of going back to school at a local community college was dashed by Hurricane Florence—just one of the extreme weather events that have tipped the balance for struggling Americans across the nation.

passage.translation: 今天收入不平等和缺乏机会的面孔看起来就像我们所有人。她是Anna Landre,一位Georgetown University的残疾学生,为保留让她能够自由生活的健康福利而奋斗。她是Tiffanie Standard,费城有色人种年轻女性的顾问,这些女性想成为科技企业家——但必须打多份工才能维持生计。他是Ken Outlaw,北卡罗来纳州农村的一名焊工,他回到当地社区大学上学的梦想被飓风Florence摧毁——这只是使全国陷入困境的美国人失去平衡的极端天气事件之一。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: If these are the central characters of our story about poverty, what layers of perceptions, myths, and realities must we unearth to find meaningful solutions and support?
In pursuit of revealing this complicated reality, Mothering Justice, led by women of color, went last year to the state capital in Lansing, Michigan, to lobby on issues that affect working mothers.

One of the Mothering Justice organizers went to the office of a state representative to talk about the lack of affordable childcare—the vestiges(痕迹) of a system that expected mothers to stay home with their children while their husbands worked.
A legislative staffer dismissed the activist's concerns, telling her "my husband took care of that—I stayed home."

passage.translation: 如果这些是我们关于贫困故事的中心人物,那么我们必须揭示哪些层次的认知、神话和现实才能找到有意义的解决方案和支持?为了揭示这一复杂现实,由有色人种女性领导的Mothering Justice去年前往密歇根州首府Lansing,就影响职业母亲的问题进行游说。Mothering Justice的一位组织者前往一位州代表的办公室,谈论缺乏负担得起的儿童保育问题——这是一个期望母亲在丈夫工作时留在家里照顾孩子的制度的痕迹。一位立法助手对这位活动人士的担忧不屑一顾,告诉她"我丈夫处理了那件事——我待在家里"。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: That comment, says Mothering Justice director Danielle Atkinson, "was meant to shame" and relied on the familiar notion that a woman of color concerned about income inequality and programs that promote mobility must by definition be a single mom, probably with multiple kids.
In this case, the Mothering Justice activist happened to be married.

And in most cases in the America of 2019, the images that come to mind when we hear the words poverty or income inequality fail miserably in reflecting a complicated reality: poverty touches virtually all of us.
The face of income inequality, for all but a very few of us, is the one we each see in the mirror.

passage.translation: Mothering Justice主任Danielle Atkinson说,那句评论"意在羞辱",并依赖于一个熟悉的观念,即关心收入不平等和促进流动性项目的有色人种女性从定义上来说一定是单身母亲,可能还有多个孩子。在这个案例中,Mothering Justice的活动人士恰好是已婚的。而在2019年美国的大多数情况下,当我们听到贫困或收入不平等这些词时脑海中浮现的形象,在反映复杂现实方面惨败:贫困实际上触及我们所有人。除了极少数人之外,收入不平等的面孔就是我们每个人在镜子里看到的那张脸。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: How many of us are poor in the U.S.?
It depends on who you ask.
According to the Census Bureau, 38 million people in the U.S. are living below the official poverty thresholds.
Taking into account economic need beyond that absolute measure, the Institute for Policy Studies found that 140 million people are poor or low-income.
That's almost half the U.S. population.

passage.translation: 美国有多少人是贫困的?这取决于你问谁。根据Census Bureau的数据,美国有3800万人生活在官方贫困线以下。考虑到超出绝对衡量标准的经济需求,Institute for Policy Studies发现1.4亿人是贫困或低收入人群。这几乎是美国人口的一半。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: Whatever the measure, within that massive group, poverty is extremely diverse.
We know that some people are more affected than others, like children, the elderly, people with disabilities, and people of color.

passage.translation: 无论采用何种衡量标准,在这个庞大的群体中,贫困是极其多样化的。我们知道有些人比其他人受到的影响更大,比如儿童、老年人、残疾人和有色人种。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: But the fact that 4 in 10 Americans can't come up with $400 in an emergency is a commonly cited statistic for good reason: economic instability stretches across race, gender, and geography.
It even reaches into the middle classes, as real wages have stagnated(不增⻓) for all but the very wealthy and temporary spells of financial instability are not uncommon.

passage.translation: 但十分之四的美国人在紧急情况下拿不出400美元,这是一个被频繁引用的统计数据,原因充分:经济不稳定跨越种族、性别和地域。它甚至延伸到中产阶级,因为除了非常富有的人之外,所有人的实际工资都停滞不前,暂时的经济不稳定并不罕见。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Negative images remain of who is living in poverty as well as what is needed to move out of it.
The big American myth is that you can pull yourself up by your own efforts and change a bad situation into a good one.
The reality is that finding opportunity without help from families, friends, schools, and community is virtually impossible.
And the playing field is nothing close to level.

passage.translation: 关于谁生活在贫困中以及需要什么才能摆脱贫困的负面形象依然存在。美国的大神话是你可以通过自己的努力提升自己,把糟糕的处境变成好的处境。现实是,没有来自家庭、朋友、学校和社区的帮助,找到机会几乎是不可能的。而且竞争环境远非公平。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: The FrameWorks Institute, a research group that focuses on public framing of issues, has studied what sustains stereotypes and narratives of poverty in the United Kingdom.
"People view economic success and wellbeing in life as a product of choice, willpower, and drive," says Nat Kendall-Taylor, CEO of FrameWorks.
"When we see people who are struggling," he says, those assumptions "lead us to the perception that people in poverty are lazy, they don't care, and they haven't made the right decisions."

passage.translation: FrameWorks Institute是一个专注于公共议题框架的研究小组,研究了在英国是什么维持了关于贫困的刻板印象和叙事。FrameWorks的首席执行官Nat Kendall-Taylor说:"人们将经济成功和生活幸福视为选择、意志力和动力的产物。"他说,当我们看到正在挣扎的人时,这些假设"使我们认为贫困人口是懒惰的,他们不在乎,他们没有做出正确的决定"。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: Does this sound familiar?
Similar ideas surround poverty in the U.S.
And these assumptions give a false picture of reality.
"When people enter into that pattern of thinking," says Kendall-Taylor, "it's cognitively comfortable to make sense of issues of poverty in that way.
It creates a kind of cognitive blindness—all of the factors external to a person's drive and choices that they've made become invisible and fade from view."

passage.translation: 这听起来熟悉吗?美国对贫困也存在类似的观念。而这些假设给出了错误的现实图景。Kendall-Taylor说:"当人们进入那种思维模式时,用那种方式理解贫困问题在认知上是舒适的。它创造了一种认知盲目性——一个人的动力和所做选择之外的所有外部因素变得不可见并从视野中消失。"

passage.label: L

sentences.text: Those external factors include the difficulties accompanying low-wage work or structural discrimination based on race, gender, or ability.
Assumptions get worse when people who are poor use government benefits to help them survive.
There is a great tension between "the poor" and those who are receiving what has become a dirty word: "welfare."

passage.translation: 这些外部因素包括伴随低工资工作的困难,或基于种族、性别或能力的结构性歧视。当贫困人口使用政府福利来帮助他们生存时,假设会变得更糟。在"穷人"和那些接受已经成为脏字的东西——"福利"——的人之间存在巨大的紧张关系。

passage.label: M

sentences.text: According to the General Social Survey, 71 percent of respondents believe the country is spending too little on "assistance to the poor".
On the other hand, 22 percent think we are spending too little on "welfare": 37 percent believe we are spending too much.

passage.translation: 根据General Social Survey,71%的受访者认为国家在"对穷人的援助"上花费太少。另一方面,22%的人认为我们在"福利"上花费太少:37%的人认为我们花费太多。

passage.label: N

sentences.text: "Poverty has been interchangeable with people of color—specifically black women and black mothers," says Atkinson of Mothering Justice.
It's true that black mothers are more affected by poverty than many other groups, yet they are disproportionately the face of poverty.
For example, Americans routinely overestimate the share of black recipients of public assistance programs.

passage.translation: Mothering Justice的Atkinson说:"贫困一直与有色人种——特别是黑人女性和黑人母亲——互换使用。"确实,黑人母亲比许多其他群体更受贫困影响,但她们不成比例地成为贫困的面孔。例如,美国人经常高估公共援助项目中黑人受益者的比例。

passage.label: O

sentences.text: In reality, most people will experience some form of financial hardship at some point in their lives.
Indeed, people tend to dip in and out of poverty, perhaps due to unexpected obstacles like losing a job, or when hours of a low-wage job fluctuate.

passage.translation: 实际上,大多数人在生命中的某个时刻会经历某种形式的经济困难。确实,人们往往会陷入和摆脱贫困,可能是由于意外障碍,如失业,或者当低工资工作的时数波动时。

passage.label: P

sentences.text: Something each of us can do is to treat each other with the dignity and sympathy that is deserved and to understand deeply that the issue of poverty touches all of us.

passage.translation: 我们每个人都可以做的事情是以应有的尊严和同情对待彼此,并深刻理解贫困问题触及我们所有人。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: One legislative staffer assumed that a woman of color who advocated affordable childcare must be a single mother.
questions.explanation:
**答案** E 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
一位立法工作人员认为,一位倡导平价托儿服务的有色人种女性一定是单身母亲。
**锚点** 立法助理与单亲母亲的成见
**定位** Mothering Justice 主任 Danielle Atkinson 说，那番话'意在让人难堪'，依赖于一种熟悉的观念：一个关心收入不平等和促进流动性项目的有色人种女性，按定义必然是单亲妈妈，而且很可能带着好几个孩子。
**改写** One legislative staffer ↔ A legislative staffer近乎原样复现assumed that a woman of color who advocated affordable childcare must be a single mother ↔relied on the familiar notion that a woman of color concerned about income inequality and programs that promote mobility must by definition be a single mom assumed=relied on the notion
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
D 该段虽提到a legislative staffer dismissed the activist's concerns，也是与立法助理的对话现场，但只引用了助理my husband took care of that—I stayed home这句私人说法，并未点明她'假设这位活动家是单亲母亲'——把成见上升为'单亲母亲'的判断是下一段才做的。A legislative staffer dismissed the activist's concerns, telling her "my husband took care of that—I stayed home."
questions.quote: That comment, says Mothering Justice director Danielle Atkinson, "was meant to shame" and relied on the familiar notion that a woman of color concerned about income inequality and programs that promote mobility must by definition be a single mom, probably with multiple kids.

questions.prompt: People from different races, genders and regions all suffer from a lack of financial security.
questions.explanation:
**答案** H 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
来自不同种族、性别和地区的人都遭受着缺乏经济保障的困扰。
**锚点** 种族/性别/地域三维并列
**定位** 但是十分之四的美国人无法在紧急情况下拿出400美元这一事实是被频繁引用的数据，原因充分：经济不稳定横跨种族、性别和地域。
**改写** different races, genders and regions ↔ across race, gender, and geography并列三元同义对位all suffer from a lack of financial security ↔ economic instability stretches across缺乏金融安全等于经济不稳
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
G 该段说poverty is extremely diverse并列举了children, the elderly, people with disabilities, and people of color，谈的是'哪类群体更受影响'，并未陈述'种族/性别/地域三维都受影响'这一横跨维度的判断。poverty is extremely diverse. We know that some people are more affected than others, like children, the elderly, people with disabilities, and people of color.
questions.quote: But the fact that 4 in 10 Americans can't come up with $400 in an emergency is a commonly cited statistic for good reason: economic instability stretches across race, gender, and geography.

questions.prompt: According to a survey, while the majority believe too little assistance is given to the poor, more than a third believe too much is spent on welfare.
questions.explanation:
**答案** M 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
根据一项调查,虽然大多数人认为给予穷人的援助太少,但超过三分之一的人认为在福利上花费
过 多 。
**锚点** 三分之一以上认为福利花太多
**定位** 根据综合社会调查，71%的受访者认为国家在'对穷人的援助'上花得太少。另一方面，22%认为'福利'花得太少，37%认为花得太多。
**改写** the majority believe too little assistance is given to the poor ↔71 percent of respondents believe the country is spending too little on "assistance to the poor" majority等于71%more than a third believe too much is spent on welfare ↔37 percent believe we are spending too much more than a third等于37%
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
F 该段数据38 million people、140 million people是穷人人口规模统计，并非a survey中关于'花得多少'的态度调查，对象与陈述句不一致。Taking into account economic need beyond that absolute measure, the Institute for Policy Studies found that 140 million people are poor or low-income.
questions.quote: According to the General Social Survey, 71 percent of respondents believe the country is spending too little on "assistance to the poor". On the other hand, 22 percent think we are spending too little on "welfare": 37 percent believe we are spending too much.

questions.prompt: A research group has found that Americans who are struggling are thought to be lazy and to have made the wrong decisions.
questions.explanation:
**答案** J 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
一个研究小组发现,处境艰难的美国人被认为是懒惰的,并且做出了错误的决定。
**锚点** 研究机构定性挣扎者懒惰
**定位** 他说，当我们看到正在挣扎的人时，那些假设'让我们形成这样的认知：贫困中的人懒惰、不在乎、没有做出正确的决定'。
**改写** A research group has found ↔The FrameWorks Institute, a research group that focuses on public framing of issues, has studied research group原词复现Americans who are struggling are thought to be lazy ↔When we see people who are struggling," he says, those assumptions "lead us to the perception that people in poverty are lazy are thought to be等于lead us to the perception have made the wrong decisions ↔ haven't made the right decisions wrong等于haven't加right
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
K 该段承接J段继续引用Kendall-Taylor的话谈cognitive blindness，但没有给出'挣扎者被认为懒惰且做错了决定'这一研究结论本身，只是对前段结论的延伸评价。When people enter into that pattern of thinking, it's cognitively comfortable to make sense of issues of poverty in that way. It creates a kind of cognitive blindness
questions.quote: When we see people who are struggling," he says, those assumptions "lead us to the perception that people in poverty are lazy, they don't care, and they haven't made the right decisions.

questions.prompt: Under the old system in America, a mother was supposed to stay home and take care of her children.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
在美国的旧制度下,母亲应该待在家里照顾孩子。
**锚点** 旧体系下母亲在家
**定位** Mothering Justice 的一位组织者去州众议员办公室谈论可负担育儿服务的缺失——那是一个体系的遗痕：这个体系预期母亲在家照看孩子，而丈夫外出工作。
**改写** Under the old system in America ↔ the vestiges(痕迹) of a system vestiges暗示旧体系a mother was supposed to stay home and take care of her children ↔expected mothers to stay home with their children supposed to与expected to同义
questions.quote: One of the Mothering Justice organizers went to the office of a state representative to talk about the lack of affordable childcare—the vestiges(痕迹) of a system that expected mothers to stay home with their children while their husbands worked.

questions.prompt: It was found that nearly 50% of Americans are poor or receive low pay.
questions.explanation:
**答案** F 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
研究发现,近50%的美国人贫困或收入微薄。
**锚点** 近半数美国人贫困或低薪
**定位** 考虑到绝对指标之外的经济需求，政策研究所发现有1.4亿人贫困或低收入。那几乎占美国人口的一半。
**改写** nearly 50% of Americans ↔ almost half the U.S. population nearly 50%等于almost half are poor or receive low pay ↔ are poor or low-income receive low pay等于low-income
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
M 71 percent、22 percent、37 percent描述的是对援助/福利支出态度的受访比例，而非'穷或低收入的人占总人口比例'，对象与题干不符。71 percent of respondents believe the country is spending too little on "assistance to the poor"
questions.quote: Taking into account economic need beyond that absolute measure, the Institute for Policy Studies found that 140 million people are poor or low-income. That's almost half the U.S. population.

questions.prompt: Americans usually overestimate the number of blacks receiving welfare benefits.
questions.explanation:
**答案** N 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
美国人通常高估了接受福利救济的黑人数量。
**锚点** 高估黑人福利受益者数量
**定位** 例如，美国人经常高估公共援助项目中黑人受益者的比例。
**改写** overestimate the number of blacks receiving welfare benefits ↔overestimate the share of black recipients of public assistance programs number约等于share, welfare benefits等于public assistance programs usually ↔ routinely usually等于routinely
questions.quote: For example, Americans routinely overestimate the share of black recipients of public assistance programs.

questions.prompt: It is impossible for Americans to lift themselves out of poverty entirely on their own.
questions.explanation:
**答案** I 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
美国人完全靠自己摆脱贫困是不可能的。
**锚点** 无法独自摆脱贫困
**定位** 美国的一个大神话是：你可以靠自己的努力把自己拉上去，把坏境况变成好境况。现实是：如果没有家人、朋友、学校和社区的帮助，几乎不可能找到机会。
**改写** It is impossible for Americans to lift themselves out of poverty entirely on their own ↔finding opportunity without help from families, friends, schools, and community is virtually impossible lift themselves等于pull yourself up
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
O 该段说大多数人会经历经济困难、dip in and out of poverty，描述的是贫困流动现象，并未陈述'靠自己能否脱贫'这一论断。Indeed, people tend to dip in and out of poverty, perhaps due to unexpected obstacles like losing a job
questions.quote: The big American myth is that you can pull yourself up by your own efforts and change a bad situation into a good one. The reality is that finding opportunity without help from families, friends, schools, and community is virtually impossible.

questions.prompt: Nowadays, it seems none of us can get away from income inequality.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（弱锚点）
**题目译文**
如今,我们似乎没有人能够摆脱收入不平等。
**锚点** 没人能逃脱收入不平等
**定位** 今天收入不平等和机会缺失的面孔，长得就像我们所有人。
**改写** none of us can get away from income inequality ↔Today's faces of income inequality and lack of opportunity look like all of us正反同义Nowadays ↔ Today's时间副词同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
E E段poverty touches virtually all of us和the one we each see in the mirror承接C段'all of us'的论断进一步铺陈，但本话题首次明确提出是在C段开头一句，E段仅是延展。poverty touches virtually all of us. The face of income inequality, for all but a very few of us, is the one we each see in the mirror. P the issue of poverty touches all of us与陈述句意思接近，但P段是结尾的总结呼吁，话题首次明确陈述是在C段。to understand deeply that the issue of poverty touches all of us
questions.quote: Today's faces of income inequality and lack of opportunity look like all of us.

questions.prompt: Assumptions about poor people become even more negative when they live on welfare.
questions.explanation:
**答案** L 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
当穷人依靠福利生活时,关于他们的假设变得更加负面。
**锚点** 靠福利时成见更负面
**定位** 当贫困者依靠政府福利来维生时，对他们的种种假设会变得更糟。
**改写** Assumptions about poor people become even more negative ↔ Assumptions get worse become more negative等于get worse when they live on welfare ↔when people who are poor use government benefits to help them survive live on welfare等于use government benefits to survive
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
J J段说people in poverty are lazy, they don't care, and they haven't made the right decisions，是基础的负面假设，但并未陈述'靠福利时这些假设变得更糟'这一增量条件。lead us to the perception that people in poverty are lazy, they don't care, and they haven't made the right decisions
questions.quote: Assumptions get worse when people who are poor use government benefits to help them survive.

title: The Place Where the Poor Once Thrived

passage.label: A

sentences.text: This is the land of opportunity.

If that weren't already implied by the landscape—rolling green hills, palm trees, sun-kissed flowers—then it's evident in the many stories of people who grew up poor in these sleepy neighborhoods and rose to enormous success.
People like Tri Tran, who fled Vietnam on a boat in 1986, showed up in San Jose with nothing, made it to MIT, and then founded the food- delivery start-up Munchery, which is valued at $300 million.

passage.translation: 这里是充满机遇的土地。如果这一点还不能从景观中得到暗示——起伏的绿色山丘、棕榈树、阳光亲吻的花朵——那么从许多人的故事中就能清楚地看出,他们在这些宁静的社区中贫困长大,却取得了巨大的成功。比如Tri Tran,1986年乘船逃离越南,身无分文地来到圣何塞,后来进入MIT,然后创办了食品配送初创公司Munchery,该公司估值达3亿美元。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: Indeed, data suggests that this is one of the best places to grow up poor in America.

A child born in the early 1980s into a low-income family in San Jose had a 12.9 percent chance of becoming a high earner as an adult, according to a landmark study released in 2014 by the economist Raj Chetty and his colleagues from Harvard and Berkeley.

That number—12.9 percent—may not seem remarkable, but it was: Kids in San Jose whose families fell in the bottom quintile(五分位数) of income nationally had the best shot in the country at reaching the top quintile.

passage.translation: 事实上,数据表明这里是美国穷人孩子成长的最佳地区之一。根据经济学家Raj Chetty及其来自哈佛和伯克利的同事们在2014年发布的一项里程碑式研究,20世纪80年代初出生在圣何塞低收入家庭的孩子,成年后成为高收入者的概率为12.9%。这个数字——12.9%——也许看起来并不显著,但实际上很显著:在圣何塞,家庭收入处于全国最低五分之一的孩子,拥有全国最高的机会进入最高五分之一收入阶层。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: By contrast, just 4.4 percent of poor kids in Charlotte moved up to the top; in Detroit the figure was 5.5 percent.
San Jose had social mobility comparable to Denmark's and Canada's and higher than other progressive cities such as Boston and Minneapolis.

passage.translation: 相比之下,夏洛特只有4.4%的贫困孩子向上流动到顶层;底特律这一数字为5.5%。圣何塞的社会流动性可与丹麦和加拿大相媲美,高于波士顿和明尼阿波利斯等其他进步城市。

passage.label: D

sentences.text: The reasons kids in San Jose performed so well might seem obvious.

Some of the world's most innovative companies are located here, providing opportunities such as the one seized by a 12-year- old Mountain View resident named Steve Jobs when he called William Hewlett to ask for spare parts and subsequently received a summer job.
This is a city of immigrants—38 percent of the city's population today is foreign-born—and immigrants and their children have historically experienced significant upward mobility in America.
The city has long had a large foreign-born population (26.5 percent in 1990), leading to broader diversity, which, the Harvard and Berkeley economists say, is a good predictor of mobility.

passage.translation: 圣何塞的孩子们表现如此出色的原因似乎显而易见。世界上一些最具创新性的公司坐落于此,提供了各种机会,例如一位名叫Steve Jobs的12岁Mountain View居民所抓住的机会,他给William Hewlett打电话要零件,随后获得了一份暑期工作。这是一座移民城市——如今该市38%的人口出生在国外——移民及其子女在美国历史上经历了显著的向上流动。该市长期以来拥有大量外国出生人口(1990年为26.5%),带来了更广泛的多样性,哈佛和伯克利的经济学家们表示,这是流动性的良好预测指标。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: Indeed, the streets of San Jose seem, in some ways, to embody the best of America.

It's possible to drive in a matter of minutes from sleek(光亮的) office towers near the airport where people pitch ideas to investors, to single-family homes with orange trees in their yards, or to a Vietnamese mall.

The libraries here offer programs in 17 languages, and there are areas filled with small businesses owned by Vietnamese immigrants, Mexican immigrants, Korean immigrants, and Filipino immigrants, to name a few.

passage.translation: 事实上,圣何塞的街道在某些方面似乎体现了美国最好的一面。在几分钟内就可以从机场附近人们向投资者推销创意的光亮办公大楼,开车到院子里种着橙树的独栋住宅,或是到越南购物中心。这里的图书馆提供17种语言的项目,有些区域遍布越南移民、墨西哥移民、韩国移民和菲律宾移民等拥有的小企业。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: But researchers aren't sure exactly why poor kids in San Jose did so well.

The city has a low prevalence of children growing up in single-parent families, and a low level of concentrated poverty, both factors that usually mean a city allows for good intergenerational mobility.
But San Jose also performs poorly on some of the measures correlated with good mobility.
It is one of the most unequal places out of the 741 that the researchers measured, and it has high degrees of racial and economic segregation(隔离).

Its schools underperform based on how much money there is in the area, said Ben Scuderi, a predoctoral fellow at the Equality of Opportunity Project at Harvard, which uses big data to study how to improve economic opportunities for low-income children.
"There's a lot going on here which we don't totally understand," he said.
"It's interesting, because it kind of defies our expectations."

passage.translation: 但研究人员并不确切知道为什么圣何塞的贫困孩子表现如此出色。该市在单亲家庭中成长的儿童比例较低,集中贫困程度也较低,这两个因素通常意味着一个城市允许良好的代际流动。但圣何塞在一些与良好流动性相关的指标上表现不佳。在研究人员测量的741个地方中,它是最不平等的地方之一,并且存在高度的种族和经济隔离。哈佛大学机会平等项目的博士前研究员Ben Scuderi表示,根据该地区的资金状况,其学校表现不佳,该项目利用大数据研究如何改善低收入儿童的经济机会。他说:"这里发生了很多我们并不完全理解的事情。这很有趣,因为它有点违背我们的预期。"

passage.label: G

sentences.text: The Chetty data shows that neighborhoods and places mattered for children born in the San Jose area of the 1980s.
Whether the city still allows for upward mobility of poor kids today, though, is up for debate.
Some of the indicators such as income inequality, measured by the Equality of Opportunity Project for the year 2000, have only worsened in the past 16 years.

passage.translation: Chetty的数据显示,对于20世纪80年代出生在圣何塞地区的儿童来说,社区和地方很重要。然而,该市今天是否仍然允许贫困儿童向上流动,尚有争议。机会平等项目为2000年测量的一些指标,如收入不平等,在过去16年中只是恶化了。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Some San Jose residents say that as inequality has grown in recent years, upward mobility has become much more difficult to achieve.
As Silicon Valley has become home to more successful companies, the flood of people to the area has caused housing prices to skyrocket.
By most measures, San Jose is no longer a place where low-income, or even middle-income families, can afford to live.
Rents in San Jose grew 42.6 percent between 2006 and 2014, which was the largest increase in the country during that time period.
The city has a growing homelessness problem, which it tried to address by shutting down "The Jungle," one of the largest homeless encampments(临时住地) in the nation, in 2014.
Inequality is extreme.

The Human Development Index—a measure of life expectancy, education and per capita(人均的) income—gives East San Jose a score of 4.85 out of 10, while nearby Cupertino, where Apple's headquarters sits, receives a 9.26.

San Jose used to have a happy mix of factors—cheap housing, closeness to a rapidly developing industry, tightly-knit immigrant communities—that together opened up the possibility of prosperity for even its poorest residents.
But in recent years, housing prices have skyrocketed, the region's rich and poor have segregated, and middle-class jobs have disappeared.
Given this, the future for the region's poor doesn't look nearly as bright as it once did.

passage.translation: 一些圣何塞居民表示,随着近年来不平等的加剧,向上流动已变得更加难以实现。随着硅谷成为更多成功公司的所在地,涌入该地区的人潮导致房价飙升。从大多数标准来看,圣何塞不再是低收入甚至中等收入家庭负担得起的地方。2006年至2014年间,圣何塞的租金增长了42.6%,是该时期全国最大的增幅。该市的无家可归问题日益严重,为此在2014年关闭了全国最大的无家可归者临时住地之一"丛林"。不平等现象极为严重。人类发展指数——衡量预期寿命、教育和人均收入的指标——给东圣何塞打分为4.85分(满分10分),而附近的Cupertino(苹果公司总部所在地)得分为9.26分。圣何塞曾经拥有令人愉快的因素组合——廉价住房、靠近快速发展的产业、紧密团结的移民社区——这些因素共同为即使是最贫困的居民打开了繁荣的可能性。但近年来,房价飙升,该地区的富人和穷人出现隔离,中产阶级工作岗位消失。鉴于此,该地区贫困人口的未来看起来远不如从前光明。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: Leaders in San Jose are determined to make sure that the city regains its status as a place where even poor kids can access the resources to succeed.
With Silicon Valley in its backyard, it certainly has the chance to do so.

"I think there is a broad consciousness in the Valley that we can do better than to leave thousands of our neighbors behind through a period of extraordinary success," San Jose Mayor Sam Liccardo said.

passage.translation: 圣何塞的领导人决心确保该市重新获得其作为一个即使贫困孩子也能获得成功资源之地的地位。有硅谷作为后盾,它当然有机会做到这一点。圣何塞市长Sam Liccardo说:"我认为硅谷普遍意识到,在这段非凡成功的时期,我们可以做得更好,而不是抛下数千名邻居。"

passage.label: J

sentences.text: But in today's America—a land of rising inequality, increasing segregation, and stagnating(不增⻓的) middle-class wages—can the San Jose region really once again become a place of opportunity?

passage.translation: 但在今天的美国——一个不平等加剧、隔离加深、中产阶级工资停滞不前的国度——圣何塞地区真的能再次成为一个充满机遇的地方吗?

passage.label: K

sentences.text: The idea that those at the bottom can rise to the top is central to America's ideas about itself.
That such mobility has become more difficult in San Jose raises questions about the endurance of that foundational belief.
After all, if the one-time land of opportunity can't be fixed, what does that say for the rest of America?

passage.translation: 底层人士可以升至顶层的理念是美国自我认知的核心。这种流动性在圣何塞变得更加困难,这引发了关于这一基础信念持久性的质疑。毕竟,如果这片曾经充满机遇的土地都无法修复,那对美国其他地方意味着什么?

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.prompt: According to some people living in San Jose, it has become much harder for the poor to get ahead due to the increased inequality.
questions.explanation:
**答案** H 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
据一些生活在圣何塞的人说,由于不平等加剧,穷人要出人头地变得更加困难了。
**锚点** 穷人变难 + 不平等加剧
**定位** 一些圣何塞居民表示，随着近些年不平等加剧，向上流动变得困难得多。
**改写** According to some people living in San Jose ↔ Some San Jose residents say同源引语者改写due to the increased inequality ↔ as inequality has grown in recent years状语从句到名词短语的等值改写much harder for the poor to get ahead ↔upward mobility has become much more difficult to achieve动词短语 vs 名词化的同义改写
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
G G 段表述为 Whether the city still allows for upward mobility of poor kids today, though, is up for debate，只是把今天能否上升流动作为 "有争议" 来呈现，并没有以居民为发声主体说 "因为不平等加剧所以穷人难上升"，因此不是 36 题的源头段。Whether the city still allows for upward mobility of poor kids today, though, is up for debate. Some of the indicators such as income inequality, measured by the Equality of Opportunity Project for the year 2000, have only worsened in the past 16 years. F F 段提到 one of the most unequal places 与 racial and economic segregation，但语境是研究者承认 "按这些指标本不该流动性高，可它当年偏偏高"——是讲历史反常之谜，不是讲 "今天因不平等加剧所以难上升"，故非源头段。It is one of the most unequal places out of the 741 that the researchers measured, and it has high degrees of racial and economic segregation
questions.quote: Some San Jose residents say that as inequality has grown in recent years, upward mobility has become much more difficult to achieve.

questions.prompt: In American history, immigrants used to have a good chance to move upward in society.
questions.explanation:
**答案** D 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
在美国历史上,移民过去有很好的机会在社会中向上流动。
**锚点** 历史上移民有良好上升机会
**定位** 这是一座移民之城——如今 38% 的人口是外国出生的——而移民及其子女在历史上一直在美国经历着显著的向上流动。
**改写** In American history ↔ historically experienced significant upward mobility in America时间副词与介词短语等值immigrants used to have a good chance to move upward in society ↔immigrants and their children have historically experienced significant upward mobility主语扩展与动名化等值
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
A A 段以个体故事 Tri Tran 引入主题，重在叙事，未给出 "移民群体在美国历史上向上流动" 这一概括论断。故不是 37 题源头段。Tri Tran, who fled Vietnam on a boat in 1986, showed up in San Jose with nothing, made it to MIT, and then founded the food-delivery start-up Munchery, which is valued at $300 million. E E 段罗列 Vietnamese immigrants, Mexican immigrants, Korean immigrants, and Filipino immigrants 等族裔小生意的现状，呈现的是 "今天街景"，并未做 "移民在美国历史上有上升机会" 的论断，所以不是 37 题源头段。there are areas filled with small businesses owned by Vietnamese immigrants, Mexican immigrants, Korean immigrants, and Filipino immigrants, to name a few
questions.quote: This is a city of immigrants—38 percent of the city's population today is foreign-born—and immigrants and their children have historically experienced significant upward mobility in America.

questions.prompt: If the problems of San Jose can't be solved, one of America's fundamental beliefs about itself can be shaken.
questions.explanation:
**答案** K 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
如果圣何塞的问题无法解决,美国关于自身的一个基本信念可能会动摇。
**锚点** 问题解不开 + 动摇美国根本信念
**定位** 向上流动在圣何塞变得更困难，这件事引发了对那一根本信念能否持续的质疑。毕竟，如果这片曾经的机会之地都修复不了，那对美国其他地方又意味着什么？
**改写** If the problems of San Jose can't be solved ↔ if the one-time land of opportunity can't be fixed上下位概念的指称等值one of America's fundamental beliefs about itself can be shaken ↔raises questions about the endurance of that foundational belief同义形容词与因果方向相同
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
J J 段反问 can the San Jose region really once again become a place of opportunity? 只针对圣何塞这一城市层级的疑问，没说 "美国关于自身的根本信念被动摇"，故不是 38 题源头段。But in today's America—a land of rising inequality, increasing segregation, and stagnating middle- class wages—can the San Jose region really once again become a place of opportunity?
questions.quote: That such mobility has become more difficult in San Jose raises questions about the endurance of that foundational belief. After all, if the one-time land of opportunity can't be fixed, what does that say for the rest of America?

questions.prompt: San Jose was among the best cities in America for poor kids to move up the social ladder.
questions.explanation:
**答案** B 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
圣何塞曾是美国最适合穷人孩子攀登社会阶梯的城市之一。
**锚点** 圣何塞在全美数一数二利于穷孩子向上
**定位** 在圣何塞，家庭收入全国处于最底层五分位的孩子，在全国范围内拥有进入最顶层五分位的最佳机会。
**改写** San Jose was among the best cities in America ↔had the best shot in the country at reaching the top quintile全国最佳=全美最好之一for poor kids to move up the social ladder ↔Kids in San Jose whose families fell in the bottom quintile of income nationally had the best shot...at reaching the top quintile隐喻与数据指标等值
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
C C 段是 just 4.4 percent of poor kids in Charlotte moved up to the top; in Detroit the figure was 5.5 percent 这种与他城对比的论述（这恰好是 43 题的源头），但 39题问的是 "在全美最好之一" 的绝对定位，需要 B 段中 the best shot in the country这种 "全国" 字样，不是 C 段的横比。By contrast, just 4.4 percent of poor kids in Charlotte moved up to the top; in Detroit the figure was 5.5 percent. San Jose had social mobility comparable to Denmark's and Canada's and higher than other progressive cities such as Boston and Minneapolis.
questions.quote: Kids in San Jose whose families fell in the bottom quintile of income nationally had the best shot in the country at reaching the top quintile.

questions.prompt: Whether poor kids in San Jose today still have the chance to move upward is questionable.
questions.explanation:
**答案** G 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
如今圣何塞的穷人孩子是否仍有向上流动的机会是值得怀疑的。
**锚点** 今日穷孩子是否还能上升 = 有疑问
**定位** 不过，这座城市今天是否仍然允许穷孩子向上流动，是有待商榷的。
**改写** Whether poor kids in San Jose today still have the chance to move upward ↔Whether the city still allows for upward mobility of poor kids today主从语态互换、信息完全对齐is questionable ↔ is up for debate习语与单词的同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
H H 段最后明确判断 the future for the region's poor doesn't look nearly as bright as it once did——这已经是确定性结论，不是 "is questionable / up for debate" 的疑问语气；故不是 40 题源头段。Given this, the future for the region's poor doesn't look nearly as bright as it once did. J J 段 can the San Jose region really once again become a place of opportunity?反问的主语是 "圣何塞地区" + "再次成为机会之地"，与 40 题 "穷孩子今天是否还有上升机会" 的主语和谓语都不完全对齐；G 段才是直接对应的陈述存疑。can the San Jose region really once again become a place of opportunity?
questions.quote: Whether the city still allows for upward mobility of poor kids today, though, is up for debate.

questions.prompt: San Jose's officials are resolved to give poor kids access to the resources necessary for success in life.
questions.explanation:
**答案** I 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
圣何塞的官员们决心让穷人孩子获得人生成功所需的资源。
**锚点** 官员决心给穷孩子提供资源
**定位** 圣何塞的领导者们决心确保这座城市重新成为连穷孩子都能获取成功所需资源的地方。
**改写** San Jose's officials are resolved ↔ Leaders in San Jose are determined同义名词+同义形容词to give poor kids access to the resources necessary for success in life ↔place where even poor kids can access the resources to succeed施动方向互换+不定式同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
J J 段 can the San Jose region really once again become a place of opportunity?是质疑性的反问，主语和发声者并非 "官员/领导"，态度也不是 "决心"，故不是 41 题源头段。can the San Jose region really once again become a place of opportunity?
questions.quote: Leaders in San Jose are determined to make sure that the city regains its status as a place where even poor kids can access the resources to succeed.

questions.prompt: San Jose appears to manifest some of the best features of America.
questions.explanation:
**答案** E 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
圣何塞似乎体现了美国的一些最佳特征。
**锚点** 体现美国最好的一面
**定位** 确实，从某种程度上说，圣何塞的街道似乎体现了美国最好的一面。
**改写** San Jose appears to manifest some of the best features of America ↔the streets of San Jose seem, in some ways, to embody the best of America整句结构与选词逐对等值
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
A A 段开篇 This is the land of opportunity 只是给圣何塞贴 "机会之地" 的标签，并没有像 E 段那样把它概括为 "体现美国最好一面"。故 A 段不是 42 题源头段。This is the land of opportunity.
questions.quote: Indeed, the streets of San Jose seem, in some ways, to embody the best of America.

questions.prompt: As far as social mobility is concerned, San Jose beat many other progressive cities in America.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
就社会流动性而言,圣何塞超过了美国许多其他进步城市。
**锚点** 圣何塞胜过其他进步城市
**定位** 圣何塞的社会流动性可与丹麦、加拿大相提并论，并且高于波士顿、明尼阿波利斯等其他进步城市。
**改写** As far as social mobility is concerned ↔ San Jose had social mobility话题界定的等值San Jose beat many other progressive cities in America ↔higher than other progressive cities such as Boston and Minneapolis比较动词与比较结构的同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段 the best shot in the country at reaching the top quintile 只给出 "全美最高" 的定位，没有把波士顿、明尼阿波利斯等其他进步城市拿来比较，故不是 43 题源头段。Kids in San Jose whose families fell in the bottom quintile of income nationally had the best shot in the country at reaching the top quintile.
questions.quote: San Jose had social mobility comparable to Denmark's and Canada's and higher than other progressive cities such as Boston and Minneapolis.

questions.prompt: Due to some changes like increases in housing prices in San Jose, the prospects for its poor people have dimmed.
questions.explanation:
**答案** H 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
由于圣何塞房价上涨等一些变化,其穷人的前景已经变得黯淡。
**锚点** 房价上涨等变化 → 穷人前景黯淡
**定位** 圣何塞曾经有一套很合拍的有利因素——便宜的住房、毗邻高速发展的产业、紧密团结的移民社区——这些因素一起为最贫穷的居民也打开了通向繁荣的可能。但近年来，房价飙升、贫富分化加剧、中产工作消失。鉴于此，这一地区穷人的未来已远不如从前看上去那么光明。
**改写** Due to some changes like increases in housing prices in San Jose ↔But in recent years, housing prices have skyrocketed因果连词与时间副词的等值the prospects for its poor people have dimmed ↔the future for the region's poor doesn't look nearly as bright as it once did光暗隐喻的同义
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
G G 段表述为 Some of the indicators such as income inequality, measured by the Equality of Opportunity Project for the year 2000, have only worsened in the past 16 years，谈的是收入不平等等指标，并未把 "房价上涨" 作为具体因素列出，故不是 44 题源头段。Some of the indicators such as income inequality, measured by the Equality of Opportunity Project for the year 2000, have only worsened in the past 16 years.
questions.quote: San Jose used to have a happy mix of factors—cheap housing, closeness to a rapidly developing industry, tightly-knit immigrant communities—that together opened up the possibility of prosperity for even its poorest residents. But in recent years, housing prices have skyrocketed, the region's rich and poor have segregated, and middle-class jobs have disappeared. Given this, the future for the region's poor doesn't look nearly as bright as it once did.

questions.prompt: Researchers do not have a clear idea why poor children in San Jose achieved such great success several decades ago.
questions.explanation:
**答案** F 段（强锚点）
**题目译文**
研究人员不清楚为什么圣何塞的穷人孩子在几十年前取得了如此巨大的成功。
**锚点** 研究者说不清几十年前穷孩子为何成功
**定位** 但研究者并不能确切说明，圣何塞的穷孩子为什么当年表现这么好。
**改写** Researchers do not have a clear idea ↔ researchers aren't sure exactly why同义否定表达poor children in San Jose achieved such great success several decades ago ↔poor kids in San Jose did so well结果论断同义+时间隐含等值
questions.tip:
**辨邻**
B B 段 the best shot in the country at reaching the top quintile 是给出 "穷孩子表现好" 的数据结果，并未承认 "研究者不确定为什么" 这一认知缺口，故不是 45 题源头段。A child born in the early 1980s into a low-income family in San Jose had a 12.9 percent chance of becoming a high earner as an adult D D 段 The reasons kids in San Jose performed so well might seem obvious 之后罗列了创新公司、移民比例、多元化等具体原因解释，是在给原因；而 45 题要的是"研究者不清楚原因"，论旨方向相反，故不是源头段。The reasons kids in San Jose performed so well might seem obvious.
questions.quote: But researchers aren't sure exactly why poor kids in San Jose did so well.

title: The terms "global warming" and "climate change" are…

sentences.text: The terms "global warming" and "climate change" are used by many, seemingly interchangeably.
But do they really mean the same thing?

passage.translation: "全球变暖"和"气候变化"这两个术语被许多人使用,似乎可以互换。但它们真的意思相同吗?

sentences.text: Scientists shaped the history of the terms while attempting to accurately describe how humans continue to alter the planet.
Later, political strategists adopted the terms to influence public opinion.

passage.translation: 科学家在试图准确描述人类如何持续改变地球的过程中塑造了这些术语的历史。后来,政治策略家采用这些术语来影响公众舆论。

sentences.text: In 1975, geochemist Wallace Broecker introduced the term "climate change" in an article published by Science.

In 1979, a National Academy of Sciences report used the term "global warming" to define increases in the Earth's average surface temperature, while "climate change" more broadly referred to the numerous effects of this increase, such as sea-level rise and ocean acidification(酸化).

passage.translation: 1975年,地球化学家Wallace Broecker在Science发表的一篇文章中引入了"气候变化"这一术语。1979年,美国国家科学院的一份报告使用"全球变暖"来定义地球平均表面温度的上升,而"气候变化"则更广泛地指代这种上升带来的众多影响,如海平面上升和海洋酸化。

sentences.text: During the following decades, some industrialists and politicians launched a campaign to sow doubt in the minds of the American public about the ability of fossil-fuel use, deforestation and other human activities to influence the planet's climate.

passage.translation: 在随后的几十年里,一些实业家和政治家发起了一场运动,试图在美国公众心中播下怀疑的种子,质疑化石燃料使用、森林砍伐和其他人类活动影响地球气候的能力。

sentences.text: Word use played a critical role in developing that doubt.
For example, the language and polls expert Frank Luntz wrote a memo encouraging the use of "climate change" because the phrase sounded less scary than "global warming," reported the Guardian.

passage.translation: 词语使用在制造这种怀疑方面发挥了关键作用。例如,据Guardian报道,语言和民意调查专家Frank Luntz写了一份备忘录,鼓励使用"气候变化",因为这个短语听起来不如"全球变暖"那么可怕。

sentences.text: However, Luntz's recommendation wasn't necessary.
A Google Ngram Viewer chart shows that by 1993 climate change was already more commonly used in books than global warming.
By the end of the next decade both words were used more frequently, and climate change was used nearly twice as often as global warming.

passage.translation: 然而,Luntz的建议并非必要。Google Ngram Viewer图表显示,到1993年,"气候变化"在书籍中的使用已经比"全球变暖"更常见。到下一个十年末,这两个词的使用频率都更高了,而"气候变化"的使用频率几乎是"全球变暖"的两倍。

sentences.text: NASA used the term "climate change" because it more accurately reflects the wide range of changes to the planet caused by increasing amounts of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.

passage.translation: NASA使用"气候变化"这一术语,因为它更准确地反映了大气中温室气体增加对地球造成的广泛变化。

sentences.text: The debate isn't new.
A century ago, chemist Svante Arrhenius started one of the first debates over the potential for humans to influence the planet's climate.
Arrhenius calculated the capability of carbon dioxide to trap heat in the Earth's atmosphere, but other chemists disagreed.
Some argued that humans weren't producing enough greenhouse gases, while others claimed the effects would be tiny.
Now, of course, we know that whatever you call it, human behavior is warming the planet, with grave consequences ahead.

passage.translation: 这场争论并不新鲜。一个世纪前,化学家Svante Arrhenius发起了关于人类影响地球气候潜力的首批争论之一。Arrhenius计算了二氧化碳在地球大气中捕获热量的能力,但其他化学家持不同意见。一些人认为人类产生的温室气体不够多,而另一些人则声称其影响微乎其微。当然,现在我们知道,无论你怎么称呼它,人类行为正在使地球变暖,严重的后果即将到来。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: Why did politicians use the two terms "global warming" and "climate change"?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
政治家为什么使用"全球变暖"和"气候变化"这两个术语?
A) 影响公众对人类活动对地球影响的看法。
B) 更准确地描述人类活动的后果。
C) 在竞选活动中赢得更多民众选票。
D) 向公众保证现有产业的安全性。
**判型** Why did politicians use the two terms 问的是政客使用这两个词的具体原因，属对文中明示原因的事实性提问。
**拆句** 题干 Why did politicians use the two terms "global warming" and "climate change"?主干是 "Why did politicians use the two terms"，引号里的两个术语只是 the two terms的同位补充，句式平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 后来，政治策略家们采用这些术语，是为了影响公众舆论。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确to influence public opinion ↔ To sway public opinion how humans continue to alter the planet ↔ the impact of human activities on Earth把 to influence public opinion 改成 To sway public opinion 再叠加上文 "how humans alter the planet" 的名词化转述，正好等价于 To sway public opinion of the impact of human activities on Earth.。
B) 张冠李戴To more accurately describe the consequences of human activities. 这是Scientists shaped the history of the terms while attempting to accurately describe how humans continue to alter the planet. 里科学家的目的，被错配到政客头上。
C) 无中生有To win more popular votes in their campaign activities. 文章只字未提选举或拉票；launched a campaign 中的 campaign 指"运动"而非"竞选活动"。
D) 与原文相反To assure the public of the safety of existing industries. 与原文相反——launched a campaign to sow doubt 表明政客是制造怀疑、并非给公众吃定心丸。
questions.quote: Later, political strategists adopted the terms to influence public opinion.

options.text: To sway public opinion of the impact of human activities on Earth.
To more accurately describe the consequences of human activities.
To win more popular votes in their campaign activities.
To assure the public of the safety of existing industries.

questions.prompt: As used in a National Academy of Sciences report, the term "climate change" differs from "global warming" in that_________.
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
在美国国家科学院报告中使用的"气候变化"一词与"全球变暖"的不同之处在于_________。
A) 听起来不那么模糊
B) 看起来更科学
C) 涵盖更多现象
D) 更接近现实
**判型** As used in a National Academy of Sciences report, the term "climate change" differs from "global warming" in that_________. 问的是该报告里两词的具体差异，属事实层提问。
**拆句** 题干 As used in a National Academy of Sciences report, the term "climate change" differs from "global warming" in that_________. 是个待补全的陈述句，主干 "the term climate change differs from global warming in that ..."，As 引导的状语限定范围；空格由 in that 引导的从句填，选项即从句内容。
**定位** 1979 年，美国国家科学院的一份报告用 global warming 这个术语来指地球地表平均温度的上升，而 climate change 则更广泛地指这一升温带来的诸多影响，例如海平面上升和海洋酸化。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问it sounds less vague 谈的是"听起来更不含糊"，可这个报告本身比较的是两术语的指代范围，不是听感；听感是 P5 里 Luntz 的话题，与本题报告无关。
B) 无中生有it looks more scientific 谈"显得更科学"，原文从未比较两术语的科学性观感，纯属编造。
C) ✓ 正确more broadly referred to the numerous effects ↔ it covers more phenomena预判已经定调"climate change 范围更宽"，四个选项里只有 it covers more phenomena 直接讲范围差异，与定位句中 more broadly + numerous effects 一一对位。
D) 无中生有it is much closer to reality 说"更贴近现实"，原文并未在该报告中比较两术语谁更接近实际，是无中生有。
questions.quote: In 1979, a National Academy of Sciences report used the term "global warming" to define increases in the Earth's average surface temperature, while "climate change" more broadly referred to the numerous effects of this increase, such as sea-level rise and ocean acidification(酸化).

options.text: it sounds less vague
it looks more scientific
it covers more phenomena
it is much closer to reality

questions.prompt: What did industrialists of the late 20th century resort to in order to mislead Americans?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
20世纪末的实业家采取了什么手段来误导美国人?
A) 编造的调查结果。
B) 虚假的研究发现。
C) 雇用气候专家。
D) 刻意选择措辞。
**判型** What did industrialists of the late 20th century resort to in order to mislead Americans? 问的是实业家采取的具体手段，属对文中明示信息的事实性提问。
**拆句** 题干 What did industrialists of the late 20th century resort to in order to mislead Americans? 主干 "What did industrialists resort to"，of the late 20th century 修饰industrialists，in order to mislead Americans 是目的状语；resort to 意为"诉诸于"，是高频四级词组。
**定位** 用词起到了关键作用，造就了那种怀疑。例如，语言与民调专家 Frank Luntz 写了一份备忘录，建议使用 climate change，因为它听起来不像 global warming 那么吓人——《卫报》报道。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Made-up survey results. 说"伪造调查结果"，原文只字未提调查造假，纯属编造。
B) 无中生有False research findings. 说"虚假的研究发现"，原文从未提及实业家发布假研究，只提了使用词汇上的策略。
C) 张冠李戴Hired climate experts. 把 the language and polls expert Frank Luntz 的身份错置——Luntz 是语言与民调专家，并非气候专家，且原文未说他被实业家雇佣。
D) ✓ 正确Word use played a critical role in developing that doubt.↔ Deliberate choice of words.预判已明确"在用词上做手脚"，四个选项里只有 Deliberate choice of words. 谈选词，其他三个分别引到调查、研究、专家，都不是文中点出的手段。
questions.quote: Word use played a critical role in developing that doubt. For example, the language and polls expert Frank Luntz wrote a memo encouraging the use of "climate change" because the phrase sounded less scary than "global warming," reported the Guardian.

options.text: Made-up survey results.
False research findings.
Hired climate experts.
Deliberate choice of words.

questions.prompt: Why did NASA choose the term "climate change"?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
NASA为什么选择"气候变化"这个术语?
A) 为了获得更多资金。
B) 为了更精确。
C) 出于政治需要。
D) 为了避免争论。
**判型** Why did NASA choose the term "climate change"? 是 Why 提问，问 NASA 选这个术语的原因，原文必有直接对应句。
**拆句** 题干 Why did NASA choose the term "climate change"? 是简单疑问句，主干 "Why did NASA choose the term"，引号短语作 choose 的宾语，句式无陷阱。
**定位** 美国国家航空航天局之所以使用 climate change 这个术语，是因为它能更准确地反映由大气中温室气体增加所引发的地球范围广泛的变化。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有To obtain more funds. 谈"获取更多资金"，原文从未提及 NASA 的预算或经费问题。
B) ✓ 正确more accurately reflects ↔ For greater precision预判已经给出"为了更准确"这个核心，四个选项里只有 For greater precision 谈精准度，其他三个引到资金、政治、避免争论，都没在 P7 中出现过。
C) 张冠李戴For political needs. 谈"出于政治需要"，这是 political strategists 与 industrialists and politicians 的动机，而非 NASA 的；NASA 的选词理由是科学准确性。
D) 无中生有To avoid debate. 说"为了避免争论"，原文 P7 只字未提 NASA 想回避争论；P8 反而表明争论一直存在、不可回避。
questions.quote: NASA used the term "climate change" because it more accurately reflects the wide range of changes to the planet caused by increasing amounts of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.

options.text: To obtain more funds.
For greater precision.
For political needs.
To avoid debate.

questions.prompt: What is the author's final conclusion?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （主旨题）
**题目译文**
作者的最终结论是什么?
A) 全球变暖是更准确的术语。
B) 术语的准确性在科学中很重要。
C) 人类活动对地球有严重影响。
D) 政治干扰严肃的科学辩论。
**判型** What is the author's final conclusion? 问的是作者的最终结论，是对全文中心的提问，不靠某一句的细节解决。
**拆句** 题干 What is the author's final conclusion? 是 What is 句型，主干极简，author's final是 conclusion 的双层修饰，提示找全文末尾的总结表态。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反Global warming is the more accurate term. 说 global warming 更准确，恰好和NASA used the term "climate change" because it more accurately reflects the wide range of changes 与 whatever you call it 的立场相反。
B) 以偏概全Accuracy of terminology matters in science. 把"术语精确度"当作全文主旨，但这只是 P3、P7 这两个局部所谈，作者在末段已明确越过术语之争，落点在"人类影响"。
C) ✓ 正确human behavior is warming the planet, with grave consequences ahead↔Human activities have serious effects on Earth. Human activities have serious effects on Earth. 既概括了 P8 末句的核心判断，也覆盖前文 P3 提到的海平面上升、海洋酸化等具体后果，是唯一兼顾主线与全文铺垫的选项。
D) 以偏概全Politics interferes with serious scientific debate. 说"政治干预严肃科学辩论"，这只是P4\~P5 局部话题，且原文未给出"干预了严肃科学辩论"这样的明确价值判断，更不是作者最终结论。

options.text: Global warming is the more accurate term.
Accuracy of terminology matters in science.
Human activities have serious effects on Earth.
Politics interferes with serious scientific debate.

title: A growing number of U.S. bike riders are…

sentences.text: A growing number of U.S. bike riders are attracted to electric bikes for convenience, health benefits and their fun factor.
Although ebikes first appeared in the 90s, cheaper options and longer-lasting batteries are breathing new life into the concept.

passage.translation: 越来越多的美国自行车骑行者因便利性、健康益处和趣味性而被电动自行车所吸引。尽管电动自行车最早出现在90年代,但更便宜的选择和更持久的电池正为这一概念注入新的活力。

sentences.text: Established bike companies and startups are embracing ebikes to meet demand.
About 34 million ebikes were sold worldwide last year, according to data from eCycleElectric Consultants.
Most were sold in Europe and China, where the bikes already have exploded in popularity.
Recently, the U.S. market has grown to 263,000 bikes, a 25% gain from the prior year.

passage.translation: 老牌自行车公司和初创企业都在接纳电动自行车以满足需求。根据eCycleElectric Consultants的数据,去年全球售出约3400万辆电动自行车。大部分销往欧洲和中国,在这些地方电动自行车已经爆发式流行。最近,美国市场已增长至26.3万辆,比前一年增长25%。

sentences.text: The industry is benefiting from improved batteries as suppliers over the years developed technology for laptops, smartphones and electric cars.
In 2004, the price of batteries used on ebikes fell, spurring European sales.

passage.translation: 该行业正受益于改进的电池,供应商多年来为笔记本电脑、智能手机和电动汽车开发了相关技术。2004年,电动自行车所用电池的价格下降,刺激了欧洲的销售。

sentences.text: But lower cost options are emerging, too.
This month, three U.S. bikeshare companies, Motivate, LimeBike and Spin, announced electric bicycles will be added to their fleets.
New York-based Jump Bikes is already operating an electric bikeshare in Washington, D.C., and is launching in San Francisco Thursday.
Rides cost $2 for 30 minutes.

passage.translation: 但成本更低的选择也正在出现。本月,三家美国共享单车公司Motivate、LimeBike和Spin宣布将在其车队中增加电动自行车。总部位于纽约的Jump Bikes已在华盛顿特区运营电动共享单车,并将于周四在旧金山推出。骑行30分钟收费2美元。

sentences.text: The system works like existing dockless bikeshare systems, where riders unlock bikes through a smartphone app.
"This is the beginning of a long-term shift away from regular pedal(踏板) to electric bikes," said Jump Bikes CEO Ryan Rzepecki.
"When people first jump on an ebike, their face lights up.
It's exciting and joyful in a way that you don't get from a regular bike."

passage.translation: 该系统的运作方式类似现有的无桩共享单车系统,骑行者通过智能手机应用解锁自行车。Jump Bikes首席执行官Ryan Rzepecki表示:"这是从普通脚踏自行车向电动自行车长期转变的开始。当人们第一次骑上电动自行车时,他们脸上会露出光彩。这种兴奋和愉悦是普通自行车无法带来的。"

sentences.text: Two years ago, CEO Chris Cocalis of Pivot Cycles, which sells high-end mountain bikes, found that U.S. bike shops weren't interested in stocking ebikes.
Some retailers warned Cocalis that they'd drop the brand if it came out with an electric bike.

passage.translation: 两年前,销售高端山地自行车的Pivot Cycles公司首席执行官Chris Cocalis发现,美国自行车商店对储备电动自行车不感兴趣。一些零售商警告Cocalis,如果他推出电动自行车,他们就会放弃该品牌。

sentences.text: Now that sales are taking off, the vast majority of bike dealers are asking Cocalis when he'll make an ebike available.
"There's tremendous opportunity to get a generation of people for whom suffering isn't their thing," Cocalis said.
"Ebike riders get the enjoyable part of cycling without the massive suffering of climbing huge hills."

passage.translation: 现在销售开始腾飞,绝大多数自行车经销商都在询问Cocalis何时推出电动自行车。Cocalis说:"这是一个巨大的机会,可以吸引那些不喜欢吃苦的一代人。电动自行车骑行者能享受到骑行的乐趣,而无需忍受爬陡坡的巨大痛苦。"

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about ebikes?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
从文章中我们了解到关于电动自行车的什么信息?
A) 它们的健康益处和趣味价值超过了成本。
B) 直到20世纪90年代,它们才在美国引起公众关注。
C) 直到改进电池出现后,它们才变得流行。
D) 它们的广泛使用归因于人们的环保意识。
**判型** What do we learn from the passage about ebikes? 没有 infer/imply/mainly about，问的是文中陈述的客观信息，四个选项各对应一处事实，属于综合性细节判断。
**拆句** What do we learn from the passage about ebikes? 是常规疑问句：主干是 What do we learn，about ebikes 是介词短语限定话题，from the passage 提示答题范围在通篇，无陷阱结构。
**定位** 尽管电动自行车早在 90 年代就出现了，但更便宜的款式和更耐用的电池正在为这个概念注入新的生命力。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文只说 convenience, health benefits and their fun factor 是吸引人骑电动车的几个并列原因，并没有把「健康与乐趣」与「成本」放在一起比，更没说「前者超过后者」。
B) 偷换概念原文 ebikes first appeared in the 90s 是说「90 年代才首次出现」，没有「在那之前美国人不知道、之后才关注」的意思；而 They did not catch public attention in the United States until the 1990s. 把「出现」偷换成了「引起公众关注」。
C) ✓ 正确Although ebikes first appeared in the 90s, cheaper options and longer-lasting batteries are breathing new life into the concept.↔ They did not become popular until the emergence of improved batteries.预判的「电池变好才流行」与 They did not become popular until the emergence of improved batteries. 的「直到电池改良才流行」语义完全一致；首段又用 The industry is benefiting from improved batteries 强化「电池→产业受益」的因果，可二次确认。
D) 无中生有全文只字未提 environmental awareness（环保意识），原文给出的流行原因是convenience, health benefits and their fun factor 与电池改进，没有任何句子把「环保」列为推动因素。
questions.quote: Although ebikes first appeared in the 90s, cheaper options and longer-lasting batteries are breathing new life into the concept.

options.text: Their health benefits and fun values outweigh their cost.
They did not catch public attention in the United States until the 1990s.
They did not become popular until the emergence of improved batteries.
Their widespread use is attributable to people's environmental awareness.

questions.prompt: What brought about the boost in ebike sales in Europe at the beginning of the century?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
是什么在世纪之初促成了欧洲电动自行车销量的增长?
A) 自行车制造技术的更新。
B) 电动自行车电池价格的下降。
C) 短途出行方式的改变。
D) 制造电动汽车成本的上升。
**判型** What brought about the boost in ebike sales in Europe at the beginning of the century? 是 What brought about 句式，问引起某事件的具体原因，是一道指向明确的因果细节题。
**拆句** What brought about the boost in ebike sales in Europe at the beginning of the century? 主干是 What brought about the boost，in ebike sales 修饰 boost，in Europe 与 at the beginning of the century 是两个并列状语，分别给出地点与时间，结构清晰、无陷阱。
**定位** 2004 年，用于电动自行车的电池价格下降，促使欧洲销量大增。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念原文谈的是 The industry is benefiting from improved batteries as suppliers over the years developed technology for laptops, smartphones and electric cars.——技术进步发生在电池领域（且来自笔记本、手机、电动汽车），不是 bike manufacture（自行车制造）。
B) ✓ 正确In 2004, the price of batteries used on ebikes fell, spurring European sales.↔The falling prices of ebike batteries.预判「电池价格下降」与 The falling prices of ebike batteries. 完全一致；spurring这个分词正好把「价格下降」与「欧洲销量」用因果绑在一起，无需推理。
C) 无中生有原文从未提及 short-distance travel（短途出行）这个概念，更未把它和欧洲销量增长挂钩；考生若凭「电动车=城市短途」的常识硬选，就掉进无中生有陷阱。
D) 偷换概念原文只说电池技术是从 laptops, smartphones and electric cars 这些领域延伸过来的，并没说「电动汽车制造成本上升」导致电动自行车在欧洲热销；选项把不相关的两件事强行拼接。
questions.quote: In 2004, the price of batteries used on ebikes fell, spurring European sales.

options.text: Updated technology of bike manufacture.
The falling prices of ebike batteries.
Changed fashion in short-distance travel.
The rising costs for making electric cars.

questions.prompt: What is the prospect of the bike industry according to Ryan Rzepecki?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
根据Ryan Rzepecki的说法,自行车行业的前景如何?
A) 将有更多资金投入到自行车电池研究中。
B) 电动自行车的销量将增加。
C) 该行业将从电动自行车共享中获益。
D) 该行业将对人们的日常生活产生影响。
**判型** What is the prospect of the bike industry according to Ryan Rzepecki? 用 according to + 人名，问的是他对前景的具体看法，答案应在他的原话里直接拿到，是定向细节题。
**拆句** What is the prospect of the bike industry according to Ryan Rzepecki? 是简单疑问句：主干 What is the prospect，of the bike industry 修饰 prospect，according to Ryan Rzepecki 限定信息源，无陷阱。
**定位** 这是从普通脚踏自行车向电动自行车长期转变的开端。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有CEO 原话谈的是「骑行体验」和「长期转向」，与「投资电池研究」无关；原文第 3 段提到电池技术从其他行业受益，但从未说会加大对电池研究的投入。
B) ✓ 正确This is the beginning of a long-term shift away from regular pedal(踏板) to electric bikes.↔The sales of ebikes will increase.预判的「销量会持续增长」与 The sales of ebikes will increase. 在语义上一致；且第 2段已铺垫 the U.S. market has grown to 263,000 bikes, a 25% gain from the prior year，这种「长期转向」在 CEO 嘴里说出，结合销量背景，必然指向「销量上升」。
C) 偷换概念原文确实在 P4 P5 介绍了 Jump Bikes 等公司的共享业务，但 CEO 的原话谈的是「骑行体验与长期转向」，没有说整个产业会「靠共享盈利」。
D) 过度推断CEO 原话只说「是一次长期转向的开端」，并未上升到「改变人们日常生活」的层级；考生若把「长期转向」凭印象拔高，就会过度推断。
questions.quote: This is the beginning of a long-term shift away from regular pedal(踏板) to electric bikes.

options.text: More will be invested in bike battery research.
The sales of ebikes will increase.
It will profit from ebike sharing.
It will make a difference in people's daily lives.

questions.prompt: What prevented Chris Cocalis from developing ebikes sooner?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
是什么阻止了Chris Cocalis更早开发电动自行车?
A) 零售商拒绝经营电动自行车。
B) 传统自行车带来的高额利润。
C) 用户对骑行电动自行车风险的担忧。
D) 他专注于销售昂贵的山地自行车。
**判型** What prevented Chris Cocalis from developing ebikes sooner? 问的是阻碍发生在过去的具体事实，需要在原文找到对应的客观陈述，属典型细节题。
**拆句** What prevented Chris Cocalis from developing ebikes sooner? 主干是 What prevented Chris Cocalis，from developing ebikes sooner 是 prevent sb from doing sth 的固定搭配，意为「阻止他更早开发电动车」；考生若没掌握这个搭配，容易把prevent ... from 理解反，需特别留意。
**定位** 两年前，主营高端山地车的 Pivot Cycles 公司 CEO Chris Cocalis 发现，美国的自行车商店并没有兴趣进电动自行车。一些零售商警告 Cocalis，如果他出电动车，他们就停售他的品牌。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确Some retailers warned Cocalis that they'd drop the brand if it came out with an electric bike. ↔Retailers' refusal to deal in ebikes.预判的「零售商不愿进货+威胁停售」与 Retailers' refusal to deal in ebikes. 完全等值；refusal to deal in（拒绝经营）是 weren't interested in stocking + warned ... they'd drop the brand 的概括。
B) 无中生有原文只说 Pivot Cycles, which sells high-end mountain bikes，介绍公司业务，未提及「传统车带来高利润」或他舍不得放弃高利润；考生凭「高端=高利润」的常识硬补，是无中生有。
C) 无中生有全文从未提到 risk of ebike riding（电动车骑行风险）或 users' concern（用户担忧）；阻碍来自零售商，而不是用户的安全顾虑。
D) 偷换概念Pivot Cycles, which sells high-end mountain bikes 只是介绍公司业务的非限制性定语从句，是背景；并不是「他专注卖高端山地车」导致他没做电动车——阻碍来自零售商，不来自他自己。
questions.quote: Two years ago, CEO Chris Cocalis of Pivot Cycles, which sells high-end mountain bikes, found that U.S. bike shops weren't interested in stocking ebikes. Some retailers warned Cocalis that they'd drop the brand if it came out with an electric bike.

options.text: Retailers' refusal to deal in ebikes.
High profits from conventional bikes.
Users' concern about risks of ebike riding.
His focus on selling costly mountain bikes.

questions.prompt: What makes Chris Cocalis believe there is a greater opportunity for ebike sales?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
是什么让Chris Cocalis相信电动自行车销售有更大的机会?
A) 电动自行车价格的进一步降低。
B) 公众对健康的关注。
C) 对登山运动日益增长的兴趣。
D) 年轻一代对舒适骑行的追求。
**判型** What makes Chris Cocalis believe there is a greater opportunity for ebike sales? 问的是导致他形成某观点的具体理由，答案应在他原话里给出，属于定向细节题。
**拆句** What makes Chris Cocalis believe there is a greater opportunity for ebike sales? 主干What makes Chris Cocalis believe ...，make sb do sth 表「使某人……」，believe 后接that 从句（that 省略），从句主干是 there is a greater opportunity，for ebike sales 修饰 opportunity；结构层级清晰，但 make sb believe 后接长从句，基础薄弱考生可能把believe 误当成名词，需提醒。
**定位** 存在一个巨大的机会，能争取到一整代不愿吃苦的人。骑电动车的人可以享受骑行的乐趣，而不必承受爬大坡那种痛苦折磨。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 答非所问电动车价格下降在 cheaper options 与 the price of batteries used on ebikes fell 中出现过，但 Cocalis 在 P7 谈到机会时，理由是「一代人不愿吃苦」，与价格无关。
B) 答非所问health benefits 确实是电动车整体吸引力之一，但 Cocalis 在 P7 谈机会时，给出的理由是「不愿吃苦」，与公众健康关注无关。
C) 与原文相反原文 without the massive suffering of climbing huge hills 说的是骑电动车可以免去爬坡的折磨——也就是说人们想避开爬坡，而不是对爬山兴趣上升。
D) ✓ 正确There's tremendous opportunity to get a generation of people for whom suffering isn't their thing.↔ The younger generation's pursuit of comfortable riding.预判的「新一代不愿吃苦、追求舒适」与 The younger generation's pursuit of comfortable riding. 完全对应；原话两句一起构成完整因果：「有一代人不愿吃苦」+「电动车让骑行享受而不痛苦」——这正是他看到机会的依据。
questions.quote: There's tremendous opportunity to get a generation of people for whom suffering isn't their thing. Ebike riders get the enjoyable part of cycling without the massive suffering of climbing huge hills.

The public's concern for their health.
The increasing interest in mountain climbing.
