title: The things people make, and the way they…

sentences.text: The things people make, and the way they make them, determine how cities grow and decline, and influence how empires rise and fall.
So, any disruption to the world's factories (26)____ .
And that disruption is surely coming.
Factories are being digitised, filled with new sensors and new computers to make them quicker, more (27)____ , and more efficient.

passage.translation: 人们制造的东西以及他们制造这些东西的方式，决定了城市如何发展和衰落，并影响着帝国如何兴起和衰亡。因此，世界工厂的任何disruption都很重要。而这种disruption必将到来。工厂正在被数字化，配备新的传感器和新的计算机，使它们更快、更灵活、更高效。

sentences.text: Robots are breaking free from the cages that surround them, learning new skills and new ways of working.
And 3D printers have long (28)____ a world where you can make anything, anywhere, from a computerised design.
That vision is (29)____ closer to reality.
These forces will lead to cleaner factories, producing better goods at lower prices, personalised to our individual needs and desires.
Humans will be(30)____ many of the dirty, repetitive, and dangerous jobs that have long been a (31)____ of factory life.

passage.translation: 机器人正在摆脱围绕它们的围栏，学习新技能和新的工作方式。而3D打印机长期以来一直承诺一个世界，在那里你可以根据计算机化的设计在任何地方制造任何东西。这一愿景正在更加接近现实。这些力量将带来更清洁的工厂，以更低的价格生产更好的商品，并根据我们个人的需求和愿望进行个性化定制。人类将免于许多肮脏、重复和危险的工作,这些工作长期以来一直是工厂生活的特征。

sentences.text: Greater efficiency (32)____ means fewer people can do the same work.
Yet factory bosses in many developed countries are worried about a lack of skilled human workers—and see (33)____ and robots as a solution.
But economist Helena Leurent says this period of rapid change in manufacturing is a(34)____ opportunity to make the world a better place.
"Manufacturing is the one system where you have got the biggest source of innovation, the biggest source of economic growth, and the biggest source of great jobs in the past.
You can see it changing.
That's an opportunity to (35)____ that system differently, and if we can, it will have tremendous significance."

passage.translation: 更高的效率不可避免地意味着更少的人可以完成同样的工作。然而,许多发达国家的工厂老板担心缺乏熟练的人类工人——并将自动化和机器人视为解决方案。但经济学家Helena Leurent说,制造业的这一快速变革时期是让世界变得更美好的绝佳机会。"制造业是一个系统,在过去你拥有最大的创新来源、最大的经济增长来源和最大的优质就业来源。你可以看到它正在改变。这是一个以不同方式塑造该系统的机会,如果我们能做到,它将具有巨大的意义。"

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
The things people make, and the way they make them, determine how cities grow and decline, and influence how empires rise and fall. So, any disruption to the world's factories {{26}} . And that disruption is surely coming. Factories are being digitised, filled with new sensors and new computers to make them quicker, more {{27}} , and more efficient.

Robots are breaking free from the cages that surround them, learning new skills and new ways of working. And 3D printers have long {{28}} a world where you can make anything, anywhere, from a computerised design. That vision is {{29}} closer to reality. These forces will lead to cleaner factories, producing better goods at lower prices, personalised to our individual needs and desires. Humans will be{{30}} many of the dirty, repetitive, and dangerous jobs that have long been a {{31}} of factory life.

Greater efficiency {{32}} means fewer people can do the same work. Yet factory bosses in many developed countries are worried about a lack of skilled human workers—and see {{33}} and robots as a solution. But economist Helena Leurent says this period of rapid change in manufacturing is a{{34}} opportunity to make the world a better place. "Manufacturing is the one system where you have got the biggest source of innovation, the biggest source of economic growth, and the biggest source of great jobs in the past. You can see it changing. That's an opportunity to {{35}} that system differently, and if we can, it will have tremendous significance."

options.text: automation
interaction
concerns
leaning
enormously
matters
fantastic
moving
fascinated
promised
feature
shape
flexible
spared
inevitably

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) matters 动词
**词性槽** any disruption + ___ 缺谓语动词
**依据** matter 作不及物动词 = 「至关重要」承接前句 The things people make, and the way they make them, determine how cities grow and decline, and influence how empires rise and fall.——既然制造决定城市与帝国兴衰，那么对世界工厂的任何破坏「就是大事/至关重要」，matters 作不及物动词正是这个意思。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) concerns concerns 作动词通常需要宾语concerns 表「涉及/使担心」时一般是及物动词（concerns sth./sb.），独立作谓语收尾不自然；而 matter 是典型的不及物动词，可直接以句号结尾。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) flexible 形容词
**词性槽** 并列三个 more+形容词，唯一槽位要形容词
**依据** 数字化工厂的核心卖点是「更灵活」Factories are being digitised, filled with new sensors and new computers to make them quicker, more __(27)__, and more efficient. 三个并列形容词在描述「数字化升级后工厂的优点」，「更快、更灵活、更高效」是制造业话题里最常见的三件套。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
D) fantasticfantastic 是评价性形容词，不与 more 自然搭配fantastic 本身就含有「极好的」最高级语义，英文里几乎不说 more fantastic；而且这里要的是可度量的属性（快/灵活/高效），不是主观评价。

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) promised 动词
**词性槽** have long ___ 完成时缺过去分词
**依据** promise a world 表「许诺/预示一个世界」3D 打印机长期以来一直「许诺/预示」一个「任何东西都能在任何地方制造出来」的世界——promise 在英文里有「让人期待、预示前景」的引申义，与紧随其后的 That vision is__(29)__ closer to reality.「那个愿景正在更接近现实」完美呼应：先 promise（许诺愿景）→ 后 vision（愿景）。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) fascinated fascinate 的宾语应是「人」而非「世界」fascinate 表「使……着迷」，宾语通常是人（fascinated us）；3D printers have long fascinated a world 把世界当宾语既不自然，也无法引出后句「那个 vision 接近现实」的呼应。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 E) —— fascinated 形态对、搭配错。fascinated 是 -ed 过去分词，能放进 have long ___ 的完成时框架，主体考生若只看形态极易选错；防坑点是看后面宾语 a world——fascinate 的宾语应是人，而 promise 才能带 a world 这种「愿景」类宾语，并与下句 vision 形成呼应链。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) moving 动词
**词性槽** is + ___ closer，be + V-ing 进行时
**依据** moving closer to 是「越来越接近」的固定表达「is moving closer to reality」是英文里描述「愿景/目标正在越来越接近现实」的固定说法，承接 28 题的 promised a world：先许诺一个愿景，如今这个愿景 is moving closer to reality.。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
J) leaning lean 表「倾斜/倾向」，方向感不对lean closer 字面是「向前倾得更近」，多用于身体动作；表达抽象的「愿景接近现实」用 move closer to 才地道，leaning closer to reality 不是英文里的常见搭配。

questions.explanation:
**答案** O) spared 动词
**词性槽** Humans will be ___ + 名词，被动语态
**依据** be spared sth. = 被免去某事spare sb. sth. 表「使某人免遭某事」，被动 be spared sth. 表「被免去某事」；这里说人类将被免去那些「脏、重复、危险的工作」——正好对应第二段开头机器人接管这些活的语境。

**答案** F) feature 名词
**词性槽** a + ___ of factory life，冠词后必为名词
**依据** a feature of … 是固定搭配，表「…的一大特征」句意是「肮脏、重复、危险的工作长期以来是工厂生活的一大__」，a feature of factory life 正好等于「工厂生活的一个特征」，与 have long been（长期以来一直是）的时间感完美贴合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
I) interaction interaction 指「互动」，与「脏活累活」语义不搭interaction 强调双方相互作用，把「dirty, repetitive, and dangerous jobs」称为 a interaction of factory life 在语义上讲不通，工作本身不是「互动」。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) inevitably 副词
**词性槽** 副词修饰整句/动词 means
**依据** 「效率提高」与「人变少」是必然因果句意是「效率提高 __ 意味着同样的工作用更少的人就能完成」，逻辑上是一个必然推论，而非强调程度。Greater efficiency __(32)__ means fewer people can do the same work. 用 inevitably（必然地、不可避免地）来标记这种因果必然性最贴。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) enormously enormously 强调「程度大」而非「必然性」enormously means 在英文里几乎不成立——它通常修饰量/程度（如 enormously expensive），与 mean 这种逻辑判断动词搭配不自然；这里也不是讨论「效率多么巨大地意味着」，而是「必然意味着」。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 C) —— enormously 词性对、逻辑错。enormously 和 inevitably都是副词，都能塞进 Greater efficiency __(32)__ means；防坑点是判断这是「程度」还是「必然性」——mean 这种逻辑判断动词要的是表必然性的副词（inevitably），而非表程度的（enormously）。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) automation 名词
**词性槽** and 连接的并列名词，与 robots 同列
**依据** automation and robots 是制造业话题黄金搭配工厂主担心缺技术工人，把「自动化和机器人」视作 a solution——automation 与robots 同属「替代人工的技术」范畴，是四级与雅思阅读里描述未来工厂的高频搭档。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
I) interactioninteraction 不是替代人工的技术手段interaction 指「互动」，并不构成 a solution（解决缺工的方案）；把 interaction and robots 并列既不合搭配，也违背「缺人 → 用技术替人」的因果。

questions.explanation:
**答案** D) fantastic 形容词
**词性槽** a + ___ + opportunity，冠词后名词前作定语
**依据** 评价 opportunity 用褒义强词「绝佳的」经济学家说「这是一个 __ 的机会去让世界更好」，结合后文 if we can, it will have tremendous significance. 的强烈褒义，用 fantastic（绝佳的）来评价 opportunity 在语义强度与感情色彩上都贴合。

**答案** N) shape 动词
**词性槽** to ___ that system，不定式 to 后接动词原形
**依据** shape the system = 塑造这个体系shape 作动词表「塑造、使成形」，shape the system differently 即「以不同的方式塑造这个体系」，正好承接 That's an opportunity to __(35)__ that system differently, and if we can, it will have tremendous significance. 的「重大意义」——主动重塑制造业是经济学家眼里的重大机会。

title: Forests in countries like Brazil and the Congo…

sentences.text: Forests in countries like Brazil and the Congo get a lot of attention from environmentalists, and it is easy to see why.
South America and sub-Saharan Africa are experiencing deforestation on an enormous scale: every year almost 5 million hectares are lost.
But forests are also changing in rich Western countries.
They are growing larger, both in the sense that they occupy more land and that the trees in them are bigger.
What is going on?

passage.translation: 像巴西和刚果这样的国家的森林受到环保人士的广泛关注，原因显而易见。南美洲和撒哈拉以南非洲正在经历大规模的森林砍伐：每年损失近500万公顷。但在富裕的西方国家，森林也在发生变化。它们正在扩大，既体现在占据更多土地，也体现在树木变得更大。这是怎么回事？

sentences.text: Forests are spreading in almost all Western countries, with the fastest growth in places that historically had rather few trees.
In 1990 28% of Spain was forested; now the proportion is 37%.
In both Greece and Italy, the growth was from 26% to 32% over the same period.
Forests are gradually taking more land in America and Australia.
Perhaps most astonishing is the trend in Ireland.
Roughly 1%of that country was forested when it became independent in 1922.
Now forests cover 11% of the land, and the government wants to push the proportion to 18% by the 2040s.

passage.translation: 森林在几乎所有西方国家都在扩展，在历史上树木较少的地区增长最快。1990年西班牙有28%的森林覆盖率；现在这一比例为37%。在希腊和意大利，同期增长率都是从26%到32%。森林在美国和澳大利亚也逐渐占据更多土地。也许最令人惊讶的是爱尔兰的趋势。该国在1922年独立时大约只有1%的森林覆盖率。现在森林覆盖了11%的土地，政府希望到2040年代将这一比例推进到18%。

sentences.text: Two things are fertilising this growth.
The first is the abandonment of farmland, especially in high, dry places where nothing grows terribly well.
When farmers give up trying to earn a living from farming or herding, trees simply move in.
The second is government policy and subsidy.
Throughout history, governments have protected and promoted forests for diverse reasons, ranging from the need for wooden warships to a desire to promote suburban house-building.
Nowadays forests are increasingly welcome because they suck in carbon pollution from the air.
The justifications change, the desire for more trees remains constant.

passage.translation: 有两个因素在促进这种增长。第一个是农田的废弃，尤其是在那些没有什么作物能生长得特别好的高海拔干旱地区。当农民放弃靠耕作或放牧谋生时，树木就会自然进驻。第二个是政府政策和补贴。纵观历史，政府出于各种原因保护和促进森林发展，从建造木制战舰的需要到促进郊区住宅建设的愿望。如今，森林越来越受欢迎，因为它们能吸收空气中的碳污染。理由在变化,对更多树木的渴望始终如一。

sentences.text: The greening of the West does not delight everyone.
Farmers complain that land is being taken out of use by generously subsidised tree plantations.
Parts of Spain and Portugal suffer from terrible forest fires.
Others simply dislike the appearance of forests planted in neat rows.
They will have to get used to the trees, however.
The growth of Western forests seems almost as unstoppable as deforestation elsewhere.

passage.translation: 西方的绿化并非让所有人都感到高兴。农民抱怨土地因获得慷慨补贴的人工林而退出使用。西班牙和葡萄牙的部分地区遭受严重的森林火灾。其他人则只是不喜欢整齐成行种植的森林的外观。然而，他们将不得不习惯这些树木。西方森林的增长似乎几乎与其他地方的森林砍伐一样不可阻挡。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What is catching environmentalists' attention nowadays?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
什么正在引起环保人士的关注?
A) 富裕国家正在掠夺贫穷国家的资源。
B) 许多发展中国家的森林正在迅速缩减。
C) 森林正在吞噬全球肥沃的农田。
D) 富裕国家在应对森林砍伐方面几乎无所作为。
**判型** What is catching environmentalists' attention nowadays? 是直接的特殊疑问句，问的是一个具体事实，不含 infer、suggest、imply，也不问全篇主旨。
**拆句** 题干 What is catching environmentalists' attention nowadays? 是现在进行时的特殊疑问句，主语是疑问代词 What，谓语 is catching 带宾语 environmentalists' attention，时间状语 nowadays 在句末。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 巴西、刚果这些国家的森林正得到环保人士的大量关注，原因不难看出。南美和撒哈拉以南非洲正以巨大规模经历森林砍伐：每年几乎损失 500 万公顷。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有原文只指出环保人士关注发展中地区的森林消失，并没说 Rich countries are stripping poor ones of their resources，这是套用国际关系常见话术编造出的内容。
B) ✓ 正确Brazil and the Congo ↔ many developing countries experiencing deforestation on an enormous scale ↔ fast shrinking预判说「发展中地区森林大规模消失」，Forests are fast shrinking in many developing countries. 在主语、动词、地域限定三处都与原文等值，是定位句的同义替换。
C) 与原文相反原文讲的是森林正在消失，选项却说 Forests are eating away the fertile farmland worldwide——森林在侵蚀农田，主客体关系恰好颠倒；首段也未提及 worldwide farmland 被吞噬。
D) 答非所问题干问的是 What is catching environmentalists' attention nowadays?——环保人士关注的是什么，而 Rich countries are doing little to address deforestation 是对富国不作为的指责，原文首段并没有这一指控。
questions.quote: Forests in countries like Brazil and the Congo get a lot of attention from environmentalists, and it is easy to see why. South America and sub-Saharan Africa are experiencing deforestation on an enormous scale: every year almost 5 million hectares are lost.

options.text: Rich countries are stripping poor ones of their resources.
Forests are fast shrinking in many developing countries.
Forests are eating away the fertile farmland worldwide.
Rich countries are doing little to address deforestation.

questions.prompt: Which countries have the fastest forest growth?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
哪些国家的森林增长最快?
A) 那些新近获得独立的国家。
B) 那些对木材需求最大的国家。
C) 那些过去森林覆盖率最低的国家。
D) 那些提供巨额政府补贴的国家。
**判型** Which countries have the fastest forest growth? 直接问「哪些国家」，是对原文具体信息的客观提取。
**拆句** 题干 Which countries have the fastest forest growth? 是 Which 引导的特殊疑问句，Which countries 作主语，have 作谓语，宾语 the fastest forest growth。结构简单。
**定位** 几乎所有西方国家的森林都在扩展，其中增长最快的地方是那些历史上树木相当稀少的国家。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全原文只用 Ireland 作为戏剧性案例（1922 年独立时 1%、现在 11%），并未说「森林增长最快的是新近独立的国家」这一普遍规律，Those that have newly achieved independence. 是把单一举例拔高为通则。
B) 无中生有the greatest demand for timber 在 P2 全段从未出现，森林增长最快的原因被原文限定为「历史上树少」，而非木材需求。
C) ✓ 正确historically had rather few trees↔ used to have the lowest forest coverage预判说「历史上树木很少的国家」，Those that used to have the lowest forest coverage. 把「过去树少」换说成「过去森林覆盖率最低」，二者完全同义，因此锁定。
D) 张冠李戴enormous government subsidies 对应的是 P3 提到的 government policy and subsidy，那讨论的是「促进森林增长的因素」，不是 Q52 所问的「哪国增长最快」，跨段错位。
questions.quote: Forests are spreading in almost all Western countries, with the fastest growth in places that historically had rather few trees.

options.text: Those that have newly achieved independence.
Those that have the greatest demand for timber.
Those that used to have the lowest forest coverage.
Those that provide enormous government subsidies.

questions.prompt: What has encouraged forest growth historically?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
历史上是什么促进了森林增长?
A) 政府的倡导。
B) 木材用作燃料。
C) 有利的气候。
D) 环保运动。
**判型** What has encouraged forest growth historically? 问的是历史上具体促进森林增长的因素，是对文中事实的提取，不要求多步推理。
**拆句** 题干 What has encouraged forest growth historically? 是现在完成时特殊疑问句，What作主语，has encouraged 作谓语，forest growth 作宾语，historically 是时间状语。现在完成时强调「从过去延续到现在」的累积效应。
**定位** 纵观历史，政府出于各种理由保护并推动森林的扩张，从制造木质战舰的需要，到希望促进郊区住宅建设。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确governments have protected and promoted forests ↔ The government's advocacy预判说「历史上是政府保护并推动了森林」，The government's advocacy. 用名词形式精准对应原文动词短语 promoted。
B) 偷换概念原文虽提到 the need for wooden warships，但 warships 是用木材造战舰，并非烧木头做燃料；The use of wood for fuel 偷换了用途。
C) 无中生有原文讲历史上促进森林的是政府政策，没有提到 favourable climate 这一自然因素；这是套用常识编造。
D) 张冠李戴The green movement 属于近现代环保运动，对应原文 Nowadays 这一时间段，而题干限定的是 historically 历史范围，时段不匹配。
questions.quote: Throughout history, governments have protected and promoted forests for diverse reasons, ranging from the need for wooden warships to a desire to promote suburban house-building.

options.text: The government's advocacy.
The use of wood for fuel.
The favourable climate.
The green movement.

questions.prompt: What accounts for our increasing desire for forests?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
是什么导致我们对森林的渴望日益增加?
A) 它们独特的景观之美。
B) 它们作为果园的用途。
C) 它们改善空气质量的能力。
D) 它们稳定的建筑材料供应。
**判型** What accounts for our increasing desire for forests? 用 account for 直接问原因，对应文中应有明确的因果句，属于事实信息提取。
**拆句** 题干 What accounts for our increasing desire for forests? 中 account for 是固定短语，意为「解释、是…的原因」。基础薄弱考生易把它误读成「算作」，须当心；除此之外句式简单。
**定位** 如今森林越来越受欢迎，因为它们能吸走空气中的碳污染。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有unique scenic beauty 在 P3 中并不存在；末段反而说 Others simply dislike the appearance of forests planted in neat rows，强调有人对景观不满，把「景观美」作为渴求理由完全是无中生有。
B) 无中生有use as fruit plantations 在 P3 全段未出现，原文用 plantations 是泛指「种植园」，与水果无关。
C) ✓ 正确suck in carbon pollution from the air ↔ capability of improving air quality预判说「森林能净化空气」，Their capability of improving air quality. 是这一句的标准学术化转述，因此锁定。
D) 张冠李戴supply of building materials 对应原文 wooden warships 与 suburban house- building，但那都是 Throughout history 段提及的历史理由，不是 Q54 所问的「如今越发渴求」的理由。
questions.quote: Nowadays forests are increasingly welcome because they suck in carbon pollution from the air.

options.text: Their unique scenic beauty.
Their use as fruit plantations.
Their capability of improving air quality.
Their stable supply of building materials.

questions.prompt: What does the author conclude about the prospects of forestation?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （主旨题）
**题目译文**
作者对造林前景得出了什么结论?
A) 撒哈拉以南非洲的沙漠将逐渐减少。
B) 它将在人们生活中发挥越来越重要的作用。
C) 发展中国家的森林破坏将迅速放缓。
D) 发达国家和发展中国家正朝着相反的方向发展。
**判型** What does the author conclude about the prospects of forestation? 问的是作者对整体前景的结论，覆盖全文走向，不可由单一定位句直接拿到。
**拆句** 题干 What does the author conclude about the prospects of forestation? 是宾语从句结构的特殊疑问句，What 是 conclude 的宾语，about the prospects of forestation 是conclude 的状语，限定结论的话题对象。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念Deserts in sub-Saharan Africa will diminish gradually. 蹭了 sub-Saharan Africa 这一地名，但话题对象从「森林」被偷换为「沙漠」，原文从未讨论沙漠消长。
B) 过度推断It will play a more and more important role in people's lives. 是抒情式价值判断，与原文末句「两条趋势同样不可阻挡」的冷静对照不匹配；原文从未把森林作用提升到「在人们生活中越发重要」的层面。
C) 与原文相反原文末句明说 The growth of Western forests seems almost as unstoppable as deforestation elsewhere——他处毁林同样不可阻挡，而 Forest destruction in the developing world will quickly slow down. 却说「很快放缓」，方向相反。
D) ✓ 正确The growth of Western forests seems almost as unstoppable as deforestation elsewhere↔moving in opposite directions But forests are also changing in rich Western countries. They are growing larger↔Developed South America and sub-Saharan Africa ↔ developing Developed and developing countries are moving in opposite directions. 同时容纳了全文「造林与毁林」两条主线，与末句并置结构完美对齐，是唯一覆盖全文且不与任何区间冲突的选项。

options.text: Deserts in sub-Saharan Africa will diminish gradually.
It will play a more and more important role in people's lives.
Forest destruction in the developing world will quickly slow down.
Developed and developing countries are moving in opposite directions.

title: Boredom has, paradoxically, become quite interesting to academics…

sentences.text: Boredom has, paradoxically, become quite interesting to academics lately.
In early May, London's Boring Conference celebrated seven years of delighting in dullness.
At this event, people flocked to talks about weather, traffic jams and vending-machine sounds, among other sleep-inducing topics.

passage.translation: 矛盾的是,无聊近来已经变得颇令学术界感兴趣。五月初,伦敦无聊大会庆祝了在沉闷中寻找乐趣的第七个年头。在这场活动中,人们蜂拥参加关于天气、交通堵塞和自动售货机声音等令人昏昏欲睡的话题的讲座。

sentences.text: What, exactly, is everybody studying?
One widely accepted psychological definition of boredom is "the distasteful experience of wanting, but being unable, to engage in satisfying activity."
But how can you quantify a person's boredom level and compare it with someone else's?
In 1986, psychologists introduced the Boredom Proneness Scale, designed to measure an individual's overall tendency to feel bored.
By contrast, the Multidimensional State Boredom Scale, developed in 2008, measures a person's feelings of boredom in a given situation.

passage.translation: 人们究竟在研究什么?一个被广泛接受的关于无聊的心理学定义是"想要但无法从事令人满意的活动的令人不快的体验"。但是如何量化一个人的无聊程度并将其与他人进行比较呢?1986年,心理学家引入了无聊倾向量表,旨在测量个体感到无聊的总体倾向。相比之下,2008年开发的多维状态无聊量表则测量一个人在特定情境中的无聊感受。

sentences.text: Boredom has been linked to behavior issues including inattentive driving, mindless snacking, excessive drinking, and addictive gambling.
In fact, many of us would choose pain over boredom.
One team of psychologists discovered that two-thirds of men and a quarter of women would rather self- administer electric shocks than sit alone with their thoughts for 15 minutes.
Researching this phenomenon, another team asked volunteers to watch boring, sad, or neutral films, during which they could self-administer electric shocks.
The bored volunteers shocked themselves more and harder than the sad or neutral ones did.

passage.translation: 无聊与包括注意力不集中驾驶、无意识零食、过度饮酒和成瘾性赌博在内的行为问题有关。事实上,我们中的许多人宁愿选择痛苦也不愿选择无聊。一组心理学家发现,三分之二的男性和四分之一的女性宁愿对自己施加电击,也不愿独自思考15分钟。在研究这一现象时,另一组研究人员要求志愿者观看无聊、悲伤或中性的电影,在此期间他们可以对自己施加电击。感到无聊的志愿者比悲伤或中性的志愿者更频繁、更用力地电击自己。

sentences.text: But boredom isn't all bad.
By encouraging self-reflection and daydreaming, it can spur creativity.
An early study gave participants abundant time to complete problem-solving and word-association exercises.
Once all the obvious answers were exhausted, participants gave more and more inventive answers to combat boredom.
A British study took these findings one step further, asking subjects to complete a creative challenge (coming up with a list of alternative uses for a household item).
One group of subjects did a boring activity first, while the others went straight to the creative task.
Those whose boredom pumps had been primed were more productive.

passage.translation: 但无聊并非全是坏事。通过鼓励自我反思和白日梦,它可以激发创造力。一项早期研究给参与者充足的时间来完成解决问题和词语联想练习。一旦所有明显的答案都用尽后,参与者为了对抗无聊给出了越来越多富有创造性的答案。一项英国研究将这些发现推进了一步,要求受试者完成一项创造性挑战(想出一件家居用品的替代用途清单)。一组受试者首先做了一项无聊的活动,而其他人则直接进行创造性任务。那些无聊感被预先激发的人更有成效。

sentences.text: In our always-connected world, boredom may be a hard-to-define state, but it is a fertile one.
Watch paint dry or water boil, or at least put away your smartphone for a while, and you might unlock your next big idea.

passage.translation: 在我们这个永远在线的世界里,无聊可能是一种难以定义的状态,但它是富有成效的。看着油漆变干或水烧开,或者至少把智能手机放在一边一段时间,你可能会解锁你的下一个重大想法。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: When are people likely to experience boredom, according to an accepted psychological definition?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
根据公认的心理学定义,人们在什么时候可能会感到无聊?
A) 当他们没有机会做自己想做的事时。
B) 当他们不喜欢正在学习的材料时。
C) 当他们经历某些令人不快的事情时。
D) 当他们从事某些例行活动时。
**判型** When are people likely to experience boredom, according to an accepted psychological definition?是 When 引导的事实型疑问句，且明确以according to an accepted psychological definition限定信息来源，答案应是原文定义句的客观转述。
**拆句** 题干主干是 When are people likely to experience boredom，主句问的是「时间/情境」；后置介词短语according to an accepted psychological definition为状语，限定答案来源必须是「公认的心理学定义」，不是作者本人观点或常识。
**定位** 无聊在心理学上一个被广为接受的定义是「想去从事一项令人满足的活动，却无法去做时的那种不快体验」。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确wanting, but being unable, to engage in satisfying activity↔don't have the chance to do what they want When they don't have the chance to do what they want.把原文定义句的两个核心成分「有意愿」与「被阻止」一一保留，且未添加任何原文未给出的限定，是定义句的最忠实改写。
B) 无中生有When they don't enjoy the materials they are studying.把场景限定到「学习材料」，但原文定义未提学习场景，纯属添油加醋。
C) 偷换概念When they experience something unpleasant.把原文里的「不快体验」拿出来当条件，可原文 distasteful experience 描述的是无聊本身（结果），不是触发无聊的条件，因果倒置。
D) 与原文相反When they engage in some routine activities.把无聊触发条件描述为「在做日常活动」，可原文定义明确强调「想做却做不成」，主体是「未能从事」而非「正在从事」。
questions.quote: One widely accepted psychological definition of boredom is "the distasteful experience of wanting, but being unable, to engage in satisfying activity."

options.text: When they don't have the chance to do what they want.
When they don't enjoy the materials they are studying.
When they experience something unpleasant.
When they engage in some routine activities.

questions.prompt: What does the author say boredom can lead to?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者认为无聊会导致什么?
A) 决心。
B) 专注。
C) 精神退化。
D) 有害行为。
**判型** What does the author say boredom can lead to?是 What 引导的事实问句，问的是「无聊会导致什么」，是对原文具体陈述的转述。
**拆句** 句子主干 What ... boredom can lead to，是宾语前置的特殊疑问句；what 是 lead to 的宾语，问的是「后果」。句中嵌入does the author say并非考点，仅说明信息来源是作者陈述，结构无陷阱。
**定位** 无聊与多种行为问题相关，包括驾驶时心不在焉、不动脑子地乱吃东西、过量饮酒以及嗜赌成瘾。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Determination.意为「决心」，原文从未提到无聊会让人变得有决心；整段讨论的全是负面后果，与正向心理品质毫无关联。
B) 与原文相反Concentration.意为「专注」，与原文inattentive driving描述的「分心驾驶」恰好相反；无聊导致的是注意力涣散，不是专注。
C) 过度推断Mental deterioration.意为「精神/智力衰退」，是把原文里的具体行为问题进一步推到「精神层面退化」的程度，原文未提任何精神疾病或认知衰退后果。
D) ✓ 正确behavior issues including inattentive driving, mindless snacking, excessive drinking, and addictive gambling↔ Harmful conduct. Harmful conduct.既保留了 behavior=conduct 的词汇对应，又用 harmful 准确概括了那四个具体后果的共同属性，是对原文罗列最贴切的总括式改写。
questions.quote: Boredom has been linked to behavior issues including inattentive driving, mindless snacking, excessive drinking, and addictive gambling.

options.text: Determination.
Concentration.
Mental deterioration.
Harmful conduct.

questions.prompt: What is the finding of one team of psychologists in their experiment?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
一组心理学家在实验中有什么发现?
A) 志愿者更愿意看一部乏味的电影,而不是独自坐着思考。
B) 许多志愿者选择伤害自己,而不是忍受无聊。
C) 男性志愿者比女性更能抵御无聊的影响。
D) 许多志愿者无法忍受超过十五分钟的无聊。
**判型** What is the finding of one team of psychologists in their experiment?问的是具体实验的结论事实，需回到该实验描述句做同义比对，属典型细节题。
**拆句** 主干 What is the finding，主系表结构；of one team of psychologists 修饰 finding，in their experiment 进一步限定研究情境。三层修饰只是把范围限到「那个团队那次实验的结论」，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
**定位** 一组心理学家发现，三分之二的男性与四分之一的女性宁愿对自己施加电击，也不愿独自静坐沉思 15 分钟。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 张冠李戴Volunteers prefer watching a boring movie to sitting alone deliberating.把后文另一项实验「看无聊片时电击自己」（another team asked volunteers to watch boring, sad, or neutral films）的实验对象混进来——这是另一团队的研究，对应另一题的结论，不是本题考的实验。
B) ✓ 正确would rather self-administer electric shocks than sit alone with their thoughts for 15 minutes↔Many volunteers choose to hurt themselves rather than endure boredom. Many volunteers choose to hurt themselves rather than endure boredom.既保留了原文比较结构两端的方向，又把具体动作恰当上位化，是对实验发现的最忠实概括。
C) 与原文相反Male volunteers are more immune to the effects of boredom than females.把男女比例的差异解读成「男性更能抗无聊」，可原文是「三分之二男性 vs 四分之一女性都选择了电击」——男性选择电击的比例反而更高，意味着男性更难忍无聊，结论方向完全相反。
D) 过度推断Many volunteers are unable to resist boredom longer than fifteen minutes.把 15分钟当成志愿者能忍耐的上限，可原文只是说「实验设定独坐 15 分钟」，并未测出志愿者的耐受阈值——结论从实验时长推到「忍耐极限」，多迈了一步。
questions.quote: One team of psychologists discovered that two-thirds of men and a quarter of women would rather self-administer electric shocks than sit alone with their thoughts for 15 minutes.

options.text: Volunteers prefer watching a boring movie to sitting alone deliberating.
Many volunteers choose to hurt themselves rather than endure boredom.
Male volunteers are more immune to the effects of boredom than females.
Many volunteers are unable to resist boredom longer than fifteen minutes.

questions.prompt: Why does the author say boredom isn't all bad?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者为什么说无聊并非全是坏事?
A) 它刺激记忆。
B) 它为放松提供了时间。
C) 它可能促进创造性思维。
D) 它可能促进自主学习。
**判型** Why does the author say boredom isn't all bad?问作者给出的理由，原文转折句后必紧跟解释，答案是该解释句的转述。
**拆句** 句首 Why 引出原因；主谓 does the author say 套着宾语从句 boredom isn't all bad。从句用 isn't all bad（部分否定）而非 isn't bad，表示「并非完全是坏事」，暗示后面一定有正面意义的展开。
**定位** 但无聊也并非全是坏事。通过促进自省与遐想，它能激发创造力。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有It stimulates memorization.说无聊会刺激记忆，但原文谈的是 self-reflection、daydreaming、creativity，全程没有 memory/memorization 这一概念。
B) 偷换概念It allows time for relaxation.把无聊的好处概括为「有时间放松」，可原文明确说的是促进自省与遐想进而激发创造力，重点是「创造产出」而非「身心放松」。
C) ✓ 正确it can spur creativity ↔ It may promote creative thinking. It may promote creative thinking.两端的动词（spur→promote）和名词（creativity→creative thinking）都做了精准的同义替换，且未引入任何超出原文的限定，是理由句的最忠实改写。
D) 过度推断It may facilitate independent learning.把好处推到「促进自主学习」，但原文谈的是创造力，而非学习或独立学习；从「自我反思」推到「独立学习」多走了一步。
questions.quote: But boredom isn't all bad. By encouraging self-reflection and daydreaming, it can spur creativity.

options.text: It stimulates memorization.
It allows time for relaxation.
It may promote creative thinking.
It may facilitate independent learning.

questions.prompt: What does the author suggest one do when faced with a challenging problem?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者建议人们在面对具有挑战性的问题时应该做什么?
A) 停止闲散,放眼大局。
B) 解锁自己的智能手机。
C) 环顾四周寻找刺激。
D) 允许自己有一些时间感到无聊。
**判型** What does the author suggest one do when faced with a challenging problem?问的是作者给出的具体行动建议，是原文建议句的客观转述，未要求推断。
**拆句** 主干 What does the author suggest one do，其中 one do 是 suggest 后省略 that 与should 的虚拟语气从句；when faced with a challenging problem 是过去分词作时间状语，相当于 when one is faced with ...，意为「当面对难题时」。
**定位** 看油漆变干，看水烧开，或者至少先把手机放下一会儿，你就可能解开下一个大点子。

sentences.text: When my son completes a task, I can't help but praise him.

passage.translation: 当我的儿子完成一项任务时，我忍不住要表扬他。在该表扬的地方给予表扬是很自然的，对吧？但是表扬会不会太多呢？

sentences.text: According to psychologist Katherine Phillip, children don't benefit from (26)____ praise as much as we'd like to think.
"Parents often praise, believing they are building their child's self-confidence.
However, over-praising can have a (27)____ effect," says Phillip.

passage.translation: 心理学家Katherine Phillip认为，孩子们并不像我们想象的那样从持续的表扬中受益。Phillip说："父母经常表扬孩子，认为这样可以建立孩子的自信心。然而，过度表扬可能会产生负面影响。当我们反复使用同样的表扬时，它可能会变得空洞，不再被孩子重视。这也可能会让孩子产生一种期待，认为他们做的任何事情都必须得到表扬作为回报。这可能会导致孩子因害怕让父母失望而避免冒险。"

sentences.text: Does this mean we should do away with all the praise?
Phillip says no.
"The key to healthy praise is to focus on the process rather than the (31)____ .
It is the recognition of a child's attempt, or the process in which they achieved something, that is essential," she says.
"Parents should encourage their child to take the risks needed to learn and grow."

passage.translation: 这是否意味着我们应该摒弃所有的表扬？Phillip说不是。她说："健康表扬的关键在于关注过程而非结果。重要的是认可孩子的尝试，或者他们取得某项成就的过程。父母应该鼓励孩子承担学习和成长所需的风险。"

sentences.text: So how do we break the (32)____ of praise we're all so accustomed to?
Phillip says it's important to (33)____ between "person praise" and "process praise".
"Person praise is (34)____ saying how great someone is.
It's a form of personal approval.
Process praise is acknowledgement of the efforts the person has just (35)____ .
Children who receive person praise are more likely to feel shame after losing," says Phillip.

passage.translation: 那么我们如何打破我们都习以为常的表扬模式呢？Phillip说，区分'人格表扬'和'过程表扬'很重要。她说：'人格表扬只是简单地说某个人有多棒。这是一种个人认可的形式。过程表扬是对一个人刚刚付出的努力的认可。接受人格表扬的孩子在失败后更容易感到羞愧。'

Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
When my son completes a task, I can't help but praise him. It's only natural to give praise where praise is due, right? But is there such a thing as too much praise?

According to psychologist Katherine Phillip, children don't benefit from {{26}} praise as much as we'd like to think. "Parents often praise, believing they are building their child's self-confidence. However, over-praising can have a {{27}} effect," says Phillip. "When we use the same praise{{28}} , it may become empty and no longer valued by the child. It can also become an expectation that anything they do must be {{29}} with praise. This may lead to the child avoiding taking risks due to fear of {{30}} their parents."

Does this mean we should do away with all the praise? Phillip says no. "The key to healthy praise is to focus on the process rather than the {{31}} . It is the recognition of a child's attempt, or the process in which they achieved something, that is essential," she says. "Parents should encourage their child to take the risks needed to learn and grow."

So how do we break the {{32}} of praise we're all so accustomed to? Phillip says it's important to {{33}} between "person praise" and "process praise". "Person praise is {{34}} saying how great someone is. It's a form of personal approval. Process praise is acknowledgement of the efforts the person has just {{35}} . Children who receive person praise are more likely to feel shame after losing," says Phillip.

questions.explanation:
**答案** B) constant 形容词
**词性槽** from + ___ + 名词 praise，定语位
**依据** 对应下文"反复使用""过度表扬"——"持续不断的表扬" over-praising can have a __(27)__ effect 与 When we use the same praise __(28)__ 都在说"表扬太多/太频繁"，故空里要的是"持续不断的"——constant praise 完美对应主旨"过度表扬反成害"。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) disappointing"令人失望的表扬"逻辑反了disappointing 表"令人失望"，下文说孩子从表扬中"得不到我们想象的那么多益处"，原因是"太多"而非"令人失望"，且 C 是第 30 题的钩子（fear of disappointing their parents）。
E) exhausting "令人筋疲力尽的表扬"不通exhausting 多修饰 work/journey 等耗体力的事，不会修饰 praise；且与下文"过度表扬使表扬变空洞"的因果对不上。
F) experienced experienced praise 不是英语搭配experienced 用来修饰人（有经验的医生/老师），不修饰 praise；语义层面也讲不通"有经验的表扬"。
G) negative"负面表扬"自相矛盾，且 G 是 27 题的钩子negative praise 自身就矛盾——表扬本身是正面的。同时 27 题 over-praising can have a__(27)__ effect 才是 negative 的天然落点。
J) plural"复数的表扬"不通plural 是语法术语"复数的"，与表扬的频率/性质完全无关，属于明显干扰词。
L) rewarded rewarded praise 不成搭配，且 L 是 29 题钩子rewarded 是"被奖赏的"，修饰"表扬"本身不通顺；本词更适合 29 题 anything they do must be __(29)__ with praise。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 G) —— G) negative 在 26 题极有迷惑性——词性也对、感情色彩也沾边。考生看到 children don't benefit from __(26)__ praise 容易直接选 negative（负面的表扬），但下文 over-praising can have a __(27)__ effect 里的 effect 才是 negative的正确落点；26 题需要的是"持续不断的"，对应主旨"过度表扬"。防坑——先把整段读完、看到 27 题的 However 再回填 26，能避免抢词。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) negative 形容词
**词性槽** 冠词 a 与名词 effect 之间，定语位
**依据** 与上文"父母以为表扬利于自信"形成 However 转折Parents often praise, believing they are building their child's self-confidence. However, over-praising can have a __(27)__ effect：However 提示语义反转，前句是正面（建立自信），所以 effect 应是反面——negative effect"负面效应"是固定搭配，逻辑严丝合缝。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) disappointing C 是 30 题钩子；这里 negative 更直接更常见disappointing effect 偶尔可见，但 negative effect 是绝对高频且与 However 转折语义最对位；同时 C 在 30 题 fear of __(30)__ their parents 才是正确落点。
E) exhausting "令人筋疲力尽的影响"与上下文无关exhausting effect 多用于体力/精神耗损语境，与"过度表扬使表扬贬值"的因果完全对不上。
F) experienced experienced effect 不成搭配experienced 修饰人，不修饰 effect；语义上也不通。
J) plural "复数的影响"语法术语，与本文无关plural 是"复数形式"，纯语法概念，与教育心理学的语境无关。
L) rewarded rewarded effect 不成搭配rewarded 不能修饰 effect；本词更适合 29 题的 be rewarded with 搭配。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) repeatedly 副词
**词性槽** 动词 use 后修饰动作 → 要副词
**依据** 对应上文"使用同样的表扬"暗含的"反复" When we use the same praise __(28)__, it may become empty："反复地"用同一句表扬，才会让表扬变得空洞无意义；repeatedly 与 the same praise、become empty 三者构成完整因果链。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
M) separately "分开地"与上下文逻辑无关separately 表示"分别、单独"，但句子讨论的是"同一句表扬反复使用"导致贬值，不存在"分开使用"的语义，逻辑对不上。
N) simply "仅仅"无法解释"变空洞"的原因simply 表示"仅仅、只不过"，常作语气副词。但本句要解释表扬为何 become empty，需要的是"次数/频率"信息，simply 给不出这个信息，且 N 在 34 题有更典型的用武之地（提前预判用过即划）。

questions.explanation:
**答案** L) rewarded 形容词
**词性槽** be + ___ + with：被动结构里要过去分词作表语
**依据** be rewarded with 是"被奖以……"的固定搭配anything they do must be __(29)__ with praise："他们做的任何事都必须以表扬作为奖励"，be rewarded with praise 是地道搭配，完美对应上下文"孩子开始期待每件事都得到表扬"。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
C) disappointing be disappointing with 不是英语搭配disappointing 是主动义"令人失望的"，be disappointing with 不成立；且 C 在 30 题才是正确落点。
E) exhausting be exhausting with 不成搭配exhausting 是"令人筋疲力尽的"，与 with praise 完全无关；语义也不通。
F) experienced be experienced with X 是"对 X 有经验"，主语应是人be experienced with 的主语只能是人，而本句主语是 anything they do（事），逻辑不符。

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) disappointing 动词
**词性槽** fear of + 动名词：of 后接 V-ing
**依据** fear of disappointing their parents = "怕让父母失望" the child avoiding taking risks due to fear of __(30)__ their parents：上文说孩子被表扬养成依赖，做事就怕没表扬；逻辑链 = 怕没被表扬 → 怕让父母失望 → 不敢冒险。disappointing 表"使……失望"，逻辑完美闭环。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
E) exhausting exhausting their parents = "使父母疲惫"语义不符exhaust 表"使筋疲力尽"，与上下文"孩子怕得不到表扬、不敢冒险"的心理逻辑无关；本句要表达的是怕父母不开心，不是怕父母累。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) outcome 名词
**词性槽** rather than 后与前面 the process 平行 → 名词
**依据** "过程 vs 结果"是教育心理学经典对立focus on the process rather than the __(31)__：process（过程）的天然反义就是outcome（结果）；下文 It is the recognition of a child's attempt, or the process in which they achieved something, that is essential 也是在强调"过程"对立"结果"。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
I) pattern pattern 与 process 不构成反义对立pattern 表"模式、惯常做法"，process 表"过程"，二者并非常见反义；且 I 在 32 题 the__(32)__ of praise we're all so accustomed to 才是天然落点（习惯化的"模式"）。

questions.explanation:
**答案** I) pattern 名词
**词性槽** the + ___ + of 名词 = 名词中心词
**依据** "打破表扬的（习惯化）模式"——pattern 表惯常做法how do we break the __(32)__ of praise we're all so accustomed to：we're all so accustomed to 提示这是"我们都已习惯的"东西，pattern 正是"惯常模式"；break the pattern 是固定搭配"打破惯例"。

**答案** D) distinguish 动词
**词性槽** 情态动词 important to 后接动词原形
**依据** 固定搭配 distinguish between A and B = 区分两者to __(33)__ between "person praise" and "process praise"：英语中"区分 A 和 B"的标准搭配就是 distinguish between A and B；下文紧接着分别给两者下定义，正是"区分"的展开。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) choose choose between 是"在两者中选一个"，与下文"两者都解释"矛盾choose between A and B 意为"在 A 和 B 中选一个"，而下文 Phillip 同时定义 person praise与 process praise、并未让人二选一，因此 choose 逻辑不符。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 A) —— A) choose 与 between 搭配也成立，是 33 题最经典陷阱。to __(33)__ between "person praise" and "process praise" 表面看 choose between 完全成立；但下文紧接着同时给两个 praise 下定义，并非让人二选一。防坑——看 between 后下文是"选一个"还是"分清楚"，本段是后者，故 distinguish。

questions.explanation:
**答案** N) simply 副词
**词性槽** be 动词与现在分词之间 → 副词作状语
**依据** "仅仅是说某人多棒"——是给 person praise 下定义Person praise is __(34)__ saying how great someone is. It's a form of personal approval.：simply 表"仅仅、只不过"，用来给概念下精简的定义最贴切："person praise不过就是夸某人多棒"。

**答案** O) undertaken 动词
**词性槽** has just + ___：现在完成时要过去分词
**依据** undertake efforts = "付出努力"，是地道动宾搭配acknowledgement of the efforts the person has just __(35)__：undertake 表"承担、从事"，undertake efforts/a task 是常见搭配；"承认这个人刚刚付出的努力"——与上文process praise 关注"过程"完美呼应。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) experienced experience efforts 不是英语搭配experience 常接 success/difficulty/loss 等"经历到的事"，不与 efforts 直接搭配；说"经历了努力"也不符合 process praise"承认所做努力"的核心义。

title: Picture this: You're at a movie theater food…

sentences.text: Picture this: You're at a movie theater food stand loading up on snacks.
You have a choice of a small, medium or large soda.
The small is $3.50 and the large is $5.50.
It's a tough decision: The small size may not last you through the whole movie, but $5.50 for some sugary drink seems ridiculous.
But there's a third option, a medium soda for $5.25.
Medium may be the perfect amount of soda for you, but the large is only a quarter more.
If you're like most people, you end up buying the large (and taking a bathroom break midshow).

passage.translation: 想象一下这个场景：你在电影院的小卖部购买零食。你可以选择小杯、中杯或大杯汽水。小杯3.50美元，大杯5.50美元。这是个艰难的决定：小杯可能不够你喝完整场电影，但花5.50美元买些含糖饮料似乎很荒谬。但还有第三个选择，中杯汽水5.25美元。中杯也许正好是你需要的汽水量，但大杯只贵了两毛五。如果你和大多数人一样，最终会买大杯（然后在电影放映中途去趟洗手间）。

sentences.text: If you're wondering who would buy the medium soda, the answer is almost no one.
In fact, there's a good chance the marketing department purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy(诱饵), making you more likely to buy the large soda rather than the small.

passage.translation: 如果你想知道谁会买中杯汽水，答案是几乎没有人。事实上，营销部门很可能故意将中杯汽水定价为诱饵，让你更有可能购买大杯而不是小杯汽水。

sentences.text: I have written about this peculiarity in human nature before with my friend Dan Ariely, who studied this phenomenon extensively after noticing pricing for subscriptions(订阅) to The Economist.
The digital subscription was $59, the print subscription was $125, and the print plus digital subscription was also $125.
No one in their right mind would buy the print subscription when you could get digital as well for the same price, so why was it even an option?
Ariely ran an experiment and found that when only the two "real" choices were offered, more people chose the less-expensive digital subscription.
But the addition of the bad option made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option.

passage.translation: 我之前曾与朋友Dan Ariely就人性中的这一特点写过文章，他在注意到The Economist的订阅定价后对这一现象进行了广泛研究。电子版订阅是59美元，纸质版订阅是125美元，而纸质版加电子版订阅也是125美元。没有人会在同样价格能获得电子版的情况下购买纸质版订阅，那为什么它还是一个选项呢？Ariely进行了一项实验，发现当只提供两个"真实"选择时，更多人选择了较便宜的电子版订阅。但加入这个糟糕选项后，人们更有可能选择更贵的纸质版加电子版选项。

sentences.text: Brain scientists call this effect "asymmetric dominance" and it means that people gravitate toward the choice nearest a clearly inferior option.
Marketing professors call it the decoy effect, which is certainly easier to remember.
Lucky for consumers, almost no one in the business community understands it.

passage.translation: 脑科学家称这种效应为"不对称优势"，它意味着人们倾向于选择最接近明显较差选项的选择。营销学教授称之为诱饵效应，这显然更容易记住。对消费者来说幸运的是，商界几乎没有人理解它。

sentences.text: The decoy effect works because of the way our brains assign value when making choices.
Value is almost never absolute; rather, we decide an object's value relative to our other choices.
If more options are introduced, the value equation changes.

passage.translation: 诱饵效应起作用是因为我们的大脑在做选择时赋予价值的方式。价值几乎从来不是绝对的；相反，我们是相对于其他选择来决定一个物品的价值。如果引入更多选项，价值等式就会改变。

A) ✓ 正确there's a good chance the marketing department purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy, making you more likely to buy the large soda rather than the small↔ people's peculiar shopping behavior Picture this: You're at a movie theater food stand↔ To illustrate预判到答案是"展示异常购物行为"，选项里只有To illustrate people's peculiar shopping behavior同时覆盖illustrate（举例目的）和peculiar shopping behavior（异常购物行为），与预判完全吻合。
B) 无中生有the increasing variety of snacks说的是零食"种类的增多"，但原文从头到尾只谈大中小三种可乐的定价心理，根本没有讨论零食种类多寡。
C) 偷换概念how hard it can be to choose a drink说的是"选饮料有多难"。原文It's a tough decision确实承认决定难，但这只是引出诱饵效应的铺垫，作者的真正意图不是讲选择之难，而是讲选择被操纵；选项把铺垫当成目的，是偷换。
D) 无中生有how popular snacks are among movie fans说的是"零食在影迷中多受欢迎"，原文完全没有谈零食的受欢迎程度，也没把读者定义为movie fans。
questions.quote: If you're wondering who would buy the medium soda, the answer is almost no one. In fact, there's a good chance the marketing department purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy, making you more likely to buy the large soda rather than the small.

options.text: To illustrate people's peculiar shopping behavior.
To illustrate the increasing variety of snacks there.
To show how hard it can be to choose a drink there.
To show how popular snacks are among movie fans.

questions.prompt: Why is the medium soda priced the way it is?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
中杯汽水为什么这样定价?
A) 为了吸引更多顾客购买它。
B) 为了显示价格与分量相匹配。
C) 为了确保顾客饮用适量的汽水。
D) 为了让顾客相信他们得到了实惠。
**判型** Why is the medium soda priced the way it is问的是文中已明示的因果，是对原文具体信息的再现，属于细节题。
**拆句** Why is the medium soda priced the way it is?主干为被动结构the medium soda is priced，the way it is是方式状语从句简写（=in the way that it is priced），整体问的是"为何如此定价"。考生需读懂被动语态，把priced还原成"被定价"。
**定位** 事实上，营销部门很可能是故意把中杯定价为诱饵，让你更倾向于买大杯而不是小杯。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反To attract more customers to buy it说的是"吸引更多顾客来买中杯"，但If you're wondering who would buy the medium soda, the answer is almost no one明确告诉我们中杯定价的目的恰恰不是为了卖中杯本身。
B) 无中生有To show the price matches the amount说的是"展示价格与分量相符"，但原文从未声称中杯价格合理，反而暗示这种定价是营销操纵。
C) 偷换概念To ensure customers drink the right amount of soda说的是"确保顾客喝合适的量"，体现的是关怀消费者健康的善意动机；原文中营销部门的动机是purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy，即操纵性的，与善意正相反。
D) ✓ 正确purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy, making you more likely to buy the large soda rather than the small↔ To make customers believe they are getting a bargain Medium may be the perfect amount of soda for you, but the large is only a quarter more ↔getting a bargain预判答案是"让顾客觉得大杯划算/占便宜"，make customers believe they are getting a bargain里getting a bargain正是"占便宜"的标准说法，与预判精准匹配。
questions.quote: In fact, there's a good chance the marketing department purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy, making you more likely to buy the large soda rather than the small.

options.text: To attract more customers to buy it.
To show the price matches the amount.
To ensure customers drink the right amount of soda.
To make customers believe they are getting a bargain.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from Dan Ariely's experiment?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
我们从Dan Ariely的实验中了解到什么?
A) 价格较低的商品吸引更多顾客。
B) The Economist的促销策略有效。
C) The Economist的印刷版最终卖得最好。
D) 更多读者选择数字版而非印刷版。
**判型** What do we learn from Dan Ariely's experiment问的是实验本身揭示了什么客观事实，是对原文的转述，属细节题。
**拆句** What do we learn from Dan Ariely's experiment?是what引导的特殊疑问句，主干为we learn，from Dan Ariely's experiment为状语。结构直白，无陷阱。
**定位** Ariely做了一个实验发现：只提供两个"真实"选项时，更多人选了便宜的纯数字订阅。但加入那个糟糕的选项后，人们更倾向于选更贵的纸质加数字组合订阅。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 以偏概全Lower-priced goods attract more customers说的是"低价商品吸引更多顾客"。原文在加诱饵后的结果恰是"更多人选了更贵的"，并非低价更受欢迎；实验的核心是揭示诱饵效应，不是廉价致胜。
B) ✓ 正确the addition of the bad option made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option↔ The Economist's promotional strategy works预判答案是"实验证明诱饵策略有效"，The Economist's promotional strategy works里works即"奏效、起作用"，与预判中"有效"匹配；且promotional strategy恰好概括了The Economist的特殊定价做法。
C) 与原文相反The Economist's print edition turns out to sell the best说的是"纯纸质版卖得最好"，但原文No one in their right mind would buy the print subscription when you could get digital as well for the same price明确指出几乎没人单买纸质版——它根本不是最好卖的，而是诱饵本身。
D) 以偏概全More readers choose the digital over the print edition说的是"更多读者选数字版而非纸质版"。这只在But之前的场景（只有两个真实选项时）成立，But之后the addition of the bad option made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option改变了这个结果——而题问的是从整个实验中学到了什么，应当看But之后的发现。
questions.quote: Ariely ran an experiment and found that when only the two "real" choices were offered, more people chose the less-expensive digital subscription. But the addition of the bad option made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option.

options.text: Lower-priced goods attract more customers.
The Economist's promotional strategy works.
The Economist's print edition turns out to sell the best.
More readers choose the digital over the print edition.

questions.prompt: For what purpose is "the bad option" (Line 7, Para. 3) added?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
添加"劣选项"是为了什么目的?
A) 为了迎合某些顾客的特殊需求。
B) 为了帮助顾客做出更理性的选择。
C) 为了诱使顾客购买价格更高的商品。
D) 为了给顾客提供更多样化的商品。
**判型** For what purpose is "the bad option" added问的是文中明示的添加目的，是对原文信息的客观转述，归为细节题。
**拆句** For what purpose is "the bad option" (Line 7, Para. 3) added?是被动疑问句，For what purpose是疑问短语前置，主语是the bad option，谓语是is added。括号内的Line 7, Para. 3是位置提示，不算原文成分。
**定位** 但加入那个糟糕的选项使得人们更倾向于选择更贵的"纸质加数字"组合订阅。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有To cater to the peculiar needs of some customers说的是"迎合某些顾客的特殊需求"，但原文中加入诱饵的目的是营销操纵，不是为了满足顾客的任何需求；原文里No one in their right mind would buy the print subscription更直接说明没人需要这个选项。
B) 与原文相反To help customers to make more rational choices说的是"帮助顾客作出更理性的选择"，但原文加入诱饵恰恰让顾客作出了非理性的选择——选了更贵的而非更便宜的；选项把操纵动机说成助人为乐，方向反了。
C) ✓ 正确made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option ↔To trap customers into buying the more pricey item the more expensive print plus digital option ↔ the more pricey item预判答案为"使顾客买更贵的"，To trap customers into buying the more pricey item里trap...into精准对应"诱饵"的负面操纵色彩，more pricey精准对应more expensive，与预判完全匹配。
D) 偷换概念To provide customers with a greater variety of goods说的是"为顾客提供更多种类的商品"。原文中加诱饵不是为了丰富选项种类，而是为了利用对比心理把顾客推向最贵的那个选项。
questions.quote: But the addition of the bad option made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option.

options.text: To cater to the peculiar needs of some customers.
To help customers to make more rational choices.
To trap customers into buying the more pricey item.
To provide customers with a greater variety of goods.

questions.prompt: How do we assess the value of a commodity, according to the passage?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
根据文章,我们如何评估商品的价值?
A) 通过考虑它的实用性。
B) 通过将它与其他选择进行比较。
C) 通过将它的质量纳入考量。
D) 通过检查它的价值等式。
**判型** How do we assess the value of a commodity, according to the passage?末尾according to the passage显式要求从文本中找答案，属细节题。
**拆句** How do we assess the value of a commodity, according to the passage?主干是How do we assess the value，of a commodity是修饰value的后置定语，according to the passage是插入语，表示信息来源。结构清晰。
**定位** 价值几乎从不是绝对的；而是说，我们是相对于自己拥有的其他选项来决定一个物品的价值。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有By considering its usefulness说的是"考虑其用处"，但原文Value is almost never absolute; rather, we decide an object's value relative to our other choices明确指出价值是相对的，从未提到用处这个独立维度。
B) ✓ 正确we decide an object's value relative to our other choices↔By comparing it with other choices decide an object's value↔ assess the value预判答案为"相对于其他选项"，By comparing it with other choices的comparing...with正是"相对"的动作化表达，与预判完全匹配。
C) 无中生有By taking its quality into account说的是"将其质量纳入考量"，原文从头到尾未谈商品质量；这是常识维度而非原文维度。
D) 偷换概念By examining its value equation说的是"通过检视其价值等式"。原文If more options are introduced, the value equation changes里的value equation是对评估过程的命名，不是用来评估的工具；选项把名词搬来制造熟悉，但用错了角色。
questions.quote: Value is almost never absolute; rather, we decide an object's value relative to our other choices.

options.text: By considering its usefulness.
By comparing it with other choices.
By taking its quality into account.
By examining its value equation.

title: Three children in every classroom have a diagnosable…

sentences.text: Three children in every classroom have a diagnosable mental health condition.
Half of these are behavioural disorders, while one third are emotional disorders such as stress, anxiety and depression, which often become outwardly apparent through self-harm.
There was an astonishing 52 percent jump in hospital admissions for children and young people who had harmed themselves between 2009 and 2015.

passage.translation: 每个教室里有三名儿童患有可诊断的心理健康疾病。其中一半是行为障碍,三分之一是情绪障碍,如压力、焦虑和抑郁,这些往往通过自残行为表现出来。2009年至2015年间,因自残而入院的儿童和青少年人数惊人地增长了52%。

sentences.text: Schools and teachers have consistently reported the scale of the problem since 2009.
Last year, over half of teachers reported that more of their pupils experience mental health problems than in the past.
But teachers also consistently report how ill-equipped they feel to meet pupils' mental health needs, and often cite a lack of training, expertise and support from the National Health Service(英国国家医疗服

passage.translation: 务体系 ).自2009年以来,学校和教师一直在报告这一问题的严重程度。去年,超过半数的教师报告称,与过去相比,更多的学生出现心理健康问题。但教师们也一直报告说,他们感到自己没有能力满足学生的心理健康需求,并经常提到缺乏来自National Health Service的培训、专业知识和支持。

sentences.text: Part of the reason for the increased pressure on schools is that there are now fewer 'early intervention(干预)' and low-level mental health services based in the community.
Cuts to local authority budgets since 2010 have resulted in a significant decline of these services, despite strong evidence of their effectiveness in preventing crises further down the line.

passage.translation: 学校压力增加的部分原因是,目前社区中的"早期干预"和低水平心理健康服务减少了。自2010年以来地方政府预算削减导致这些服务大幅减少,尽管有充分证据表明它们在预防后续危机方面非常有效。

sentences.text: The only way to break the pressures on both mental health services and schools is to reinvest in early intervention services inside schools.

passage.translation: 打破心理健康服务和学校双重压力的唯一途径是重新投资校内早期干预服务。

sentences.text: There are strong arguments for why schools are best placed to provide mental health services.
Schools see young people more than any other service, which gives them a unique ability to get to hard- to-reach children and young people and build meaningful relationships with them over time.
Recent studies have shown that children and young people largely prefer to see a counsellor in school rather than in an outside environment.
Young people have reported that for low-level conditions such as stress and anxiety, a clinical setting can sometimes be daunting(令人却步的).

passage.translation: 有充分的理由说明为什么学校最适合提供心理健康服务。学校比任何其他服务机构更多地接触青少年,这使它们具有独特的能力去接触难以触及的儿童和青少年,并随着时间推移与他们建立有意义的关系。最近的研究表明,儿童和青少年大多更愿意在学校而非外部环境中见咨询师。青少年报告说,对于压力和焦虑等低水平疾病,临床环境有时会令人却步。

sentences.text: There are already examples of innovative schools which combine mental health and wellbeing provision with a strong academic curriculum.
This will, though, require a huge cultural shift.
Politicians, policymakers, commissioners and school leaders must be brave enough to make the leap towards reimagining schools as providers of health as well as education services.

passage.translation: 已经有一些创新学校的例子,它们将心理健康和幸福保障与强大的学术课程相结合。然而,这需要巨大的文化转变。政治家、政策制定者、委员和学校领导者必须有足够的勇气迈出这一步,重新将学校设想为健康和教育服务的提供者。

groups.instructions: There are 2 passages in this section.Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements.For each of them there are four choices marked A),B),C)and D).You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.prompt: What are teachers complaining about?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （细节题）
**题目译文**
教师们在抱怨什么?
A) 有太多学生需要特别关注。
B) 他们在为有需求的学生提供咨询时承受了过大的压力。
C) 学校设备不足,无法实施任何干预措施。
D) 他们缺乏必要的资源来解决学生的心理问题。
**判型** 题干 What are teachers complaining about? 用 what 直接问一个客观事实，没有infer/suggest/imply 之类的推断信号词。
**拆句** 题干 What are teachers complaining about? 是现在进行时的特殊疑问句，主语teachers、谓语 are complaining about，介词 about 后被前置疑问词 what 取代，无从句、无否定，结构平铺直叙、无陷阱。
**定位** Service(英国国家医疗服务体系).但是教师们也一贯反映自己在应对学生心理健康需求时装备多么不足，并经常列举培训、专业能力和来自英国国家医疗服务体系支持的缺乏。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 偷换概念There are too many students requiring special attention. 把抱怨内容偷换成学生数量过多，但原文 a lack of training, expertise and support 抱怨的是教师自身资源不足，并未说学生人数太多。
B) 偷换概念They are under too much stress counselling needy students. 把抱怨内容换成教师承受过大压力，但原文 how ill-equipped they feel 抱怨的是装备不足，不是工作压力大。
C) 以偏概全Schools are inadequately equipped to implement any intervention. 用 any intervention（任何干预）把范围放大；原文只说教师在应对心理需求上装备不足，并未说学校不能实施任何干预。
D) ✓ 正确a lack of training, expertise and support ↔ lack the necessary resources to meet pupils' mental health needs ↔ to address pupils' mental problems预判的两个语义点（缺资源、为了应对学生心理问题）都精确落在 They lack the necessary resources to address pupils' mental problems. 里，故锁定。
questions.quote: But teachers also consistently report how ill-equipped they feel to meet pupils' mental health needs, and often cite a lack of training, expertise and support from the National Health

options.text: There are too many students requiring special attention.
They are under too much stress counselling needy students.
Schools are inadequately equipped to implement any intervention.
They lack the necessary resources to address pupils' mental problems.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about community health services in Britain?
questions.explanation:
**答案** A （细节题）
**题目译文**
从文章中我们对英国社区卫生服务了解到什么?
A) 由于预算削减,它们已经恶化。
B) 它们为当地居民的日常生活提供便利。
C) 它们在帮助精神病患者方面被证明无效。
D) 它们为当地居民提供预防性护理。
**判型** What do we learn from the passage about community health services in Britain? 中learn from the passage 是定向取信息，不是推断，问的是文中已陈述的事实。
**拆句** 题干结构为 What + do we learn + from the passage + about + community health services in Britain；about 短语限定要问的对象，in Britain 进一步限定地域。理解时把 What do we learn 视作信息询问的固定外壳，重心放在 about 后面那串名词短语，无陷阱。
**定位** 自 2010 年以来对地方财政预算的削减导致了这些服务的大幅衰退，尽管有强有力的证据证明它们在预防后续危机方面的有效性。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) ✓ 正确Cuts to local authority budgets since 2010 have resulted in a significant decline of these services↔ They have deteriorated due to budget cuts. a significant decline of these services ↔ They have deteriorated预判的两个要点（衰退 + 预算削减为因）都精确落在 They have deteriorated due to budget cuts.，且因果方向一致，故锁定。
B) 无中生有They facilitate local residents' everyday lives. 说社区服务便利居民日常生活，但原文从未谈到对日常生活的便利，只谈预算与衰退。
C) 与原文相反They prove ineffective in helping mental patients. 说服务被证明无效，但原文strong evidence of their effectiveness in preventing crises further down the line明确说有强证据证明其有效——正反相反。
D) 偷换概念They cover preventative care for the local resident. 看似呼应 preventing crises，但 preventative care 通常指预防性医疗保健，与原文 preventing crises further down the line（预防后续危机）不是一回事；且本题问的是文章对社区服务的描述要点，原文重点是衰退，不是预防覆盖。
questions.quote: Cuts to local authority budgets since 2010 have resulted in a significant decline of these services, despite strong evidence of their effectiveness in preventing crises further down the line.

options.text: They have deteriorated due to budget cuts.
They facilitate local residents' everyday lives.
They prove ineffective in helping mental patients.
They cover preventative care for the local resident.

questions.prompt: Where does the author suggest mental health services be placed?
questions.explanation:
**答案** B （细节题）
**题目译文**
作者建议将心理健康服务设置在哪里?
A) 在家里。
B) 在学校。
C) 在医院。
D) 在社区。
**判型** 题干 Where does the author suggest mental health services be placed? 用 where 直问地点，配 suggest 提示要找作者明确写出的建议位置，仍是文章里已有的事实陈述。
**拆句** 题干 Where does the author suggest mental health services be placed? 表层是特殊疑问句，深层是 suggest + that 从句的虚拟语气结构——从句省略了 that，谓语用 (should) be placed 的原形被动，should 被省略。基础薄弱考生易把 be placed 误读成时态错误，其实是 suggest 后建议性虚拟。
**定位** 打破心理健康服务和学校双方压力的唯一办法是把早期干预服务重新投入到学校之内。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有At home. 在家中提供，原文 inside schools 与 Schools see young people more than any other service 反复强调学校，从未提到在家中提供心理服务。
B) ✓ 正确inside schools ↔ At school.预判要求的地点是学校内部，四个选项里只有 At school. 对应，故锁定。
C) 与原文相反In hospitals. 与原文 a clinical setting can sometimes be daunting 的态度相反——作者把医院/诊所环境视为令人却步的，反对在医院里提供低强度服务。
D) 张冠李戴In communities. 看似呼应 low-level mental health services based in the community，但作者讲的是社区服务因预算削减已衰退（Cuts to local authority budgets… have resulted in a significant decline），主张方向已转向学校内部，不是继续放在社区。
questions.quote: The only way to break the pressures on both mental health services and schools is to reinvest in early intervention services inside schools.

options.text: At home.
At school.
In hospitals.
In communities.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the recent studies?
questions.explanation:
**答案** C （细节题）
**题目译文**
我们从最近的研究中了解到什么?
A) 学生更愿意依靠同龄人来缓解压力和焦虑。
B) 年轻人热衷于建立有意义的关系。
C) 学生在学校寻求咨询时感到更自在。
D) 年轻人从各种户外活动中受益。
**判型** What do we learn from the recent studies? 与第 47 题同句型，问的是研究直接给出的结论，不需要跨句推断。
**拆句** 题干 What do we learn from the recent studies? 与第 47 题同构，只是把 the passage换成 the recent studies，结构无陷阱。
**定位** 近期研究表明，儿童和年轻人在很大程度上更愿意在学校里见心理咨询师，而不愿在校外环境中见。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 无中生有Students prefer to rely on peers to relieve stress and anxiety. 称学生倾向于靠同龄人缓解压力焦虑，但研究结论是关于咨询地点（校内 vs 校外），从未谈到同伴这一路径。
B) 张冠李戴Young people are keen on building meaningful relationships. 与 build meaningful relationships with them over time 关键词重合，但原文中这句话的主语是 Schools/them（即提供方），不是青少年自己；且本题问 recent studies 的结论，而不是这句一般性描述。
C) ✓ 正确prefer to see a counsellor in school ↔ more comfortable seeking counselling in school children and young people ↔ Students预判的两个要点（学生群体 + 校内更愿）都精确落在 Students are more comfortable seeking counselling in school.，故锁定。
D) 无中生有Young people benefit from various kinds of outdoor activities. 谈户外活动的益处，原文未出现 outdoor activities 这一概念。
questions.quote: Recent studies have shown that children and young people largely prefer to see a counsellor in school rather than in an outside environment.

options.text: Students prefer to rely on peers to relieve stress and anxiety.
Young people are keen on building meaningful relationships.
Students are more comfortable seeking counselling in school.
Young people benefit from various kinds of outdoor activities.

questions.prompt: What does the author mean by a cultural shift (Line 2, Para. 6)?
questions.explanation:
**答案** D （词义句意题）
**题目译文**
作者所说的文化转变(第6段第2行)是什么意思?
A) 学校学术课程的简化。
B) 家长参与学校的决策制定。
C) 教师对心理健康态度的转变。
D) 对学校概念的转变。
**判型** 题干 What does the author mean by a cultural shift 用 What does … mean by … 这一固定句型直问引文含义，是典型的词义句意题。
**拆句** 题干 What does the author mean by a cultural shift 是特殊疑问句，主干为 What does the author mean，介词短语 by a cultural shift 引出被询问的短语，注意 mean by 在此是固定搭配（凭 X 意指什么），后跟括号注明的行号定位。
**定位** 政界、决策者、采购者和校领导必须有足够的勇气，迈出那一步，把学校重新想象成既提供健康服务、也提供教育服务的场所。
questions.tip:
**选项**
A) 与原文相反Simplification of schools' academic curriculums. 简化学术课程，原文 combine mental health and wellbeing provision with a strong academic curriculum 强调学术课程要保持坚实，不是简化。
B) 无中生有Parents' involvement in schools' policy-making. 家长参与学校决策——原文呼吁的参与者是 Politicians, policymakers, commissioners and school leaders，并不包含家长，且谈的不是决策参与而是学校角色重塑。
C) 以偏概全A change in teachers' attitudes to mental health. 把转变的范围缩窄到教师态度，但原文 Politicians, policymakers, commissioners and school leaders 列出的转变主体不是教师，而是政界、决策者、采购者和校领导——主体错位、范围缩小。
D) ✓ 正确reimagining schools as providers of health as well as education services↔A change in the conception of what schools are.预判的核心（重新定义学校是什么）与 D 的措辞一对一对齐，且 D 的 conception 一词正好对应 cultural shift 中的 cultural（观念层面的）。
questions.quote: Politicians, policymakers, commissioners and school leaders must be brave enough to make the leap towards reimagining schools as providers of health as well as education services.

options.text: Simplification of schools' academic curriculums.
Parents' involvement in schools' policy-making.
A change in teachers' attitudes to mental health.
A change in the conception of what schools are.

sentences.text: Trust is fundamental to life.
If you can't trust anything, life becomes intolerable.
You can't have relationships without trust, let alone good ones.

passage.translation: 信任是生活的基础。如果你不能信任任何事物,生活就会变得无法忍受。没有信任就无法建立关系,更不用说良好的关系了。

sentences.text: In the workplace, too, trust is (26)____ .
An organization without trust will be full of fear and(27)____ .
If you work for a boss who doesn't trust their employees to do things right, you'll have a(28)____ time.
They'll be checking up on you all the time, correcting "mistakes" and (29)____ reminding you to do this or that.
Colleagues who don't trust one another will need to spend more time (30)____their backs than doing any useful work.

passage.translation: 在职场中,信任同样至关重要。一个没有信任的组织将充满恐惧和猜疑。如果你为一个不信任员工能把事情做好的老板工作,你将度过痛苦的时光。他们会一直检查你,纠正"错误",并不断提醒你做这做那。彼此不信任的同事将需要花更多时间提防他人,而不是做任何有用的工作。

sentences.text: Organizations are always trying to cut costs.
Think of all the additional tasks caused by lack of trust.
Audit(审计) departments only exist because of it.
Companies keep large volumes of (31)____because they don't trust their suppliers, their contractors or their customers.
Probably more than half of all administrative work is only there because of an ever-existing sense that "you can't trust anyone these days."
If even a small part of such valueless work could be (32)____ , the savings would run into millions of dollars.

passage.translation: 组织总是试图削减成本。想想缺乏信任所导致的所有额外任务。审计部门的存在只是因为信任缺失。公司保留大量记录是因为他们不信任供应商、承包商或客户。可能超过一半的行政工作存在的唯一原因是一种永远存在的感觉,即"如今你不能信任任何人"。如果能消除哪怕一小部分这种毫无价值的工作,节省下来的开支将达到数百万美元。

sentences.text: All this is extra work we (33)____ onto ourselves because we don't trust people—the checking, following through, doing things ourselves because we don't believe others will do them (34)____ —or at all.
If we took all that away, how much extra time would we suddenly find in our life?
How much of our work (35)____ would disappear?

passage.translation: 所有这些都是我们因为不信任他人而给自己增加的额外工作——检查、跟进、亲自做事,因为我们不相信别人会妥善完成——或者根本不会完成。如果我们把所有这些都去掉,我们的生活中会突然多出多少额外时间?我们的工作压力会减少多少?

groups.instructions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
groups.content:
Trust is fundamental to life. If you can't trust anything, life becomes intolerable. You can't have relationships without trust, let alone good ones.

In the workplace, too, trust is {{26}} . An organization without trust will be full of fear and{{27}} . If you work for a boss who doesn't trust their employees to do things right, you'll have a{{28}} time. They'll be checking up on you all the time, correcting "mistakes" and {{29}} reminding you to do this or that. Colleagues who don't trust one another will need to spend more time {{30}}their backs than doing any useful work.

Organizations are always trying to cut costs. Think of all the additional tasks caused by lack of trust. Audit(审计) departments only exist because of it. Companies keep large volumes of {{31}}because they don't trust their suppliers, their contractors or their customers. Probably more than half of all administrative work is only there because of an ever-existing sense that "you can't trust anyone these days." If even a small part of such valueless work could be {{32}} , the savings would run into millions of dollars.

All this is extra work we {{33}} onto ourselves because we don't trust people—the checking, following through, doing things ourselves because we don't believe others will do them {{34}} —or at all. If we took all that away, how much extra time would we suddenly find in our life? How much of our work {{35}} would disappear?

options.text: constantly
properly
credible
records
essential
removed
exploring
stacks
gather
suspicion
load
tracked
miserable
watching
pressure

questions.explanation:
**答案** C) essential 形容词
**词性槽** 系动词 is 后作表语，要形容词
**依据** 呼应首句「信任是根本」，trust is essential＝信任不可或缺第一段已定调 Trust is fundamental to life.，第二段 too 表示职场同理，所以这里说信任「至关重要」最顺，essential 正是「必不可少」之意。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) credible 语义错位：可信的对象是人/说法，不是「信任」本身credible 意为「可信的」，说 trust is credible（信任是可信的）逻辑打架；句子要表达的是信任的重要性，不是信任可不可信。
G) miserable 感情色彩反：信任本身不会「悲惨」miserable 是负面词「悲惨的」，本句在肯定信任的价值，色彩相反；它真正的归宿是第 28 空you'll have a __(28)__ time。

questions.explanation:
**答案** M) suspicion 名词
**词性槽** and 并列 fear，要与之同为名词
**依据** 「缺乏信任」最直接的结果就是猜疑An organization without trust 没有信任，自然 full of fear and suspicion（充满恐惧与猜疑），suspicion 与 trust 正是反义对子，语义最贴。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
H) pressure 义偏：压力非「不信任」的直接对应，且另有专属空pressure 指「压力」，与「没有信任」不构成直接因果；它真正对应第 35 空 How much of our work __(35)__ would disappear? 的 work pressure（工作压力）。

questions.explanation:
**答案** G) miserable 形容词
**词性槽** 在名词 time 前作定语，要形容词
**依据** 在不信任你的老板手下，日子很难受前提是 If you work for a boss who doesn't trust their employees，被处处盯防、纠错、催促，have a miserable time（日子很难受）色彩与情境吻合。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
B) credible搭配＋色彩双错：credible time 不成立credible「可信的」修饰 time 讲不通（没有「可信的时光」一说），且本句是负面情境，需要贬义词，credible 中性偏褒，色彩也不对。

questions.explanation:
**答案** A) constantly 副词
**词性槽** 修饰现在分词 reminding，要副词
**依据** 呼应「all the time」，描述不停地提醒前句 They'll be checking up on you all the time 已说「一直盯着」，本句 constantly（不断地）reminding 与之同调，刻画不信任的老板没完没了地提醒。

**答案** O) watching 动词
**词性槽** spend time doing 结构，空填动名词
**依据** watch one's back＝提防背后、互相防备上下文是互不信任的同事 Colleagues who don't trust one another，watching their backs（时刻提防）正刻画这种防备，比埋头干活还费时间，语义贴切。

**答案** J) records 名词
**词性槽** 动词 keep 的宾语，且被 large volumes of 修饰，要名词
**依据** 因不信任供应商客户而留存大量「记录/档案」下文给出原因 because they don't trust their suppliers, their contractors or their customers——不信任就要留底，keep large volumes of records（保存大量记录）逻辑最顺。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) load 义不合：load 是「负荷」，公司不会「保存负荷」load 指负担/负荷，keep large volumes of load 讲不通；它对应第 33 空的动词用法，不在此处。
L) stacks搭配冲突：stacks 本身已含「大量」之意，与 volumes of 语义重复stacks 意为「一堆、大量」，large volumes of stacks（大量的『一大堆』）语义叠床架屋，且不指向「因不信任而留底」的具体对象。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 L) —— stacks 词性也对、又含『大量』，最易误选。stacks 是名词且自带「一堆」之意，填进 large volumes of __(31)__ 看着顺；防坑：volumes of 已经表大量，stacks 与之语义重复，且要选「因不信任而留存的东西」——记录(records)才扣题。

questions.explanation:
**答案** K) removed 动词
**词性槽** could be ___ 被动语态，空填过去分词
**依据** 无价值的工作被「去掉」，才能省下数百万下文 the savings would run into millions of dollars——只有把 valueless work 去除（removed）才能省钱，removed（被去除）与「省钱」因果直连。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
N) tracked逻辑反：追踪工作不会带来节省tracked「被追踪」与下文「省下数百万」对不上——追踪只会增加工作而非减少；本句要的是「去掉」这类减负动作。
**易错**
最具迷惑性的错误词是 N) —— tracked 形态对、又像审计『追踪』，迷惑性强。tracked能构成 could be tracked 的被动，且全文提到 audit，易被带偏；防坑：认准结果句 the savings would run into millions，省钱只能靠『去除』(removed)，追踪是增负，方向相反。

questions.explanation:
**答案** F) load 动词
**词性槽** we ___ onto ourselves，主语 we 后缺谓语，要动词
**依据** load ... onto＝把（负担）加到……身上本段说这些都是因不信任而 extra work we __(33)__ onto ourselves，load onto oneself（把额外活儿压到自己头上）是 load 作动词的典型搭配，语义贴切。

**答案** I) properly 副词
**词性槽** 修饰动词 do them，要副词
**依据** 与后文「or at all」对照，意为「把事做对/做好」do them __(34)__—or at all 中 or at all 表「甚至根本不做」，前面应是「好好地做」，properly（妥当地、正确地）正好构成「做不好——甚至不做」的递进。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
A) constantly 义不搭：此处讲「做得好不好」，不是「做得勤不勤」constantly 意为「不断地」，与 or at all（根本不做）形成不了对照；本空要的是质量评价，不是频率，且 constantly 另有归宿（第 29 空）。

questions.explanation:
**答案** H) pressure 名词
**词性槽** 名词 work 后构成复合名词，作主语中心，要名词
**依据** work pressure＝工作压力，固定常见搭配本段说去掉不信任带来的额外活儿后会怎样：How much of our work __(35)__ would disappear?，work pressure（工作压力）是地道搭配，且「压力消失」逻辑顺。
questions.tip:
**竞争词**
F) load 搭配略逊且本词另有更贴的空load 也可作名词，但 work pressure 比 work load 在此更顺，且 load 真正对应第 33 空的动词用法 extra work we __(33)__ onto ourselves，把它留给那里更合理。

title: Why Are Asian Americans Missing From Our Textbooks?

passage.label: A

sentences.text: I still remember my fourth-grade social studies project.
Our class was studying the Gold Rush, something all California fourth-graders learned.
I was excited because I had asked to research Chinese immigrants during that era.
Growing up in the San Francisco Bay Area, I had always known that "San Francisco" translated to "Gold Mountain" in Chinese.
The name had stuck ever since Chinese immigrants arrived on the shores of Northern California in the 1850s, eager to try their luck in the gold mines.
Now I'd have the chance to learn about them.

passage.translation: 我依然记得我四年级时的社会研究项目。我们班正在学习淘金热,这是所有加利福尼亚州四年级学生都会学习的内容。我很兴奋,因为我申请研究那个时代的中国移民。我在旧金山湾区长大,一直都知道"San Francisco"在中文里翻译为"金山"。自从中国移民在19世纪50年代抵达北加利福尼亚海岸、渴望在金矿碰碰运气以来,这个名字就一直沿用至今。现在我终于有机会了解他们了。

passage.label: B

sentences.text: My excitement was short-lived.
I remember heading to the library with my class and asking for help.
I remember the librarian's hesitation.
She finally led me past row after row of books, to a corner of the library where she pulled an oversized book off the shelf.
She checked the index and turned over to a page about early Chinese immigrants in California.
That was all there was in my entire school library in San Francisco, home of the nation's first Chinatown.
That was it.

passage.translation: 我的兴奋很快消退了。我记得和班级一起去图书馆并寻求帮助。我记得图书管理员的犹豫。她最后带着我穿过一排又一排的书架,来到图书馆的一个角落,从书架上抽出一本大开本的书。她查看了索引,翻到关于加利福尼亚早期中国移民的一页。这就是我整个学校图书馆的全部相关资料——而这所学校位于旧金山,美国第一个唐人街的所在地。就这些了。

passage.label: C

sentences.text: I finally had the opportunity to learn about Asian Americans like myself, and how we became part of the fabric of the United States when I took an introductory class on Asian-American history in college.
The class was a revelation.
I realized how much had been missing in my textbooks as I grew up.
My identity had been shaped by years of never reading, seeing, hearing, or learning about people who had a similar background as me.
Why, I wondered, weren't the stories, histories, and contributions of Asian Americans taught in K-12 schools, especially in the elementary schools?
Why are they still not taught?

passage.translation: 我终于有机会了解像我这样的亚裔美国人,以及我们如何成为美国社会组成部分,那是在我上大学时选修了一门亚裔美国史入门课程。这门课令我大开眼界。我意识到在成长过程中我的教科书遗漏了多少内容。我的身份认同是在多年从未阅读、看到、听到或学习过与我有相似背景的人的经历中形成的。我想知道,为什么亚裔美国人的故事、历史和贡献没有在K-12学校教授,尤其是在小学?为什么它们至今仍未被教授?

passage.label: D

sentences.text: Our students—Asian, Latino, African American, Native American, and, yes, white—stand to gain from a multicultural curriculum.
Students of color are more engaged and earn better grades when they see themselves in their studies.
Research has also found that white students benefit by being challenged and exposed to new perspectives.

passage.translation: 我们的学生——亚裔、拉丁裔、非洲裔美国人、美洲原住民,以及没错,白人学生——都能从多元文化课程中受益。有色人种学生在课程中看到自己时,参与度更高,成绩也更好。研究还发现,白人学生通过接受挑战和接触新视角也能受益。

passage.label: E

sentences.text: For decades, activists have called for schools to offer anti-racism or multicultural curricula.
Yet a traditional American K-12 curriculum continues to be taught from a Eurocentric point of view.
Being multicultural often falls back on weaving children of color into photographs, or creating a few supporting characters that happen to be ethnic—an improvement, but superficial nonetheless.
Elementary school classrooms celebrate cultural holidays—Lunar New Year!
Red envelopes!
Lion dancers!—but they're quick to gloss over(掩饰) the challenges and injustices that Asian Americans have faced.
Most students don't, for example, learn about the laws that for years excluded Asians from immigrating to the U.S.
They don't hear the narratives of how and why Southeast Asian refugees(难⺠) had to rebuild their lives here.

passage.translation: 几十年来,活动人士一直呼吁学校提供反种族主义或多元文化课程。然而,传统的美国K-12课程仍然从欧洲中心主义视角进行教授。多元文化往往退化为将有色人种儿童编入照片中,或创造几个恰好是少数族裔的配角人物——这是一种改进,但仍然流于表面。小学教室庆祝文化节日——农历新年!红包!舞狮!——但它们很快就掩饰了亚裔美国人面临的挑战和不公。例如,大多数学生没有了解到多年来禁止亚洲人移民美国的法律。他们没有听到关于东南亚难民如何以及为何必须在这里重建生活的叙述。

passage.label: F

sentences.text: Research into what students learn in school has found just how much is missing in their studies.

In an analysis, Christine Sleeter, a professor in the College of Professional Studies at California State University, Monterey Bay, reviewed California's history and social studies framework, the curriculum determined by state educators that influences what is taught in K-12 classrooms.
Of the nearly 100 Americans recommended to be studied, 77% were white, 18% were African American, 4% were Native American, and 1% were Latino.
None were Asian American.

passage.translation: 对学生在学校学习内容的研究发现,他们的学习中遗漏了多少东西。在一项分析中,加州州立大学蒙特雷湾分校专业研究学院教授Christine Sleeter审查了加利福尼亚的历史和社会研究框架,这是由州教育工作者确定的、影响K-12课堂教学内容的课程。在推荐学习的近100名美国人中,77%是白人,18%是非洲裔美国人,4%是美洲原住民,1%是拉丁裔。没有一个是亚裔美国人。

passage.label: G

sentences.text: Worse, when Asian Americans do make an appearance in lesson books, it is often laced with problems.
"There hasn't been much progress," says Nicholas Hartlep, an assistant professor at Metropolitan State University.
His 2016 study of K-12 social studies textbooks and teacher manuals found that Asian Americans were poorly represented at best, and subjected to racist caricatures(拙劣的模仿) at worst.
The wide diversity of Asian Americans was overlooked; there was very little mention of South Asians or Pacific Islanders, for example.
And chances were, in the images, Asian Americans appeared in stereotypical(模式化的) roles, such as engineers.

passage.translation: 更糟糕的是,当亚裔美国人确实出现在课本中时,往往充满问题。"没有取得多少进展,"大都会州立大学助理教授Nicholas Hartlep说。他2016年对K-12社会研究教科书和教师手册的研究发现,亚裔美国人往好了说是代表性不足,往坏了说是遭受种族主义式的拙劣模仿。亚裔美国人的广泛多样性被忽视了;例如,很少提及南亚裔或太平洋岛民。而且很可能,在图像中,亚裔美国人以模式化的角色出现,比如工程师。

passage.label: H

sentences.text: Teachers with a multicultural background or training could perhaps overcome such curriculum challenges, but they're few and far between.
In California, 65% of K-12 teachers are white, compared with a student population that is 75% students of color.
Nationwide, the gap is even greater.

It isn't a requirement that teachers share the same racial or ethnic background as their students, but the imbalance poses challenges, from the potential for unconscious bias to a lack of knowledge or comfort in discussing race and culture.

passage.translation: 具有多元文化背景或培训的教师或许可以克服这些课程挑战,但这样的教师少之又少。在加利福尼亚,65%的K-12教师是白人,而学生群体中75%是有色人种学生。在全国范围内,这一差距甚至更大。教师与学生拥有相同的种族或族裔背景并非必要条件,但这种不平衡带来了挑战,从潜在的无意识偏见到在讨论种族和文化时缺乏知识或感到不自在。

passage.label: I

sentences.text: How race and ethnicity is taught is crucial, says Allyson Tintiangco-Cubales, an Asian-American studies professor at San Francisco State University.
She added that it's not so much about the teacher's background, but about training.
"You can have a great curriculum but if you don't have teachers dedicated(专注于) to teaching it well," she says, "it won't work as well as you want it to."

passage.translation: 旧金山州立大学亚裔美国研究教授Allyson Tintiangco-Cubales说,种族和族裔如何被教授至关重要。她补充说,这不太关乎教师的背景,而是关乎培训。"你可以有很好的课程,但如果你没有专注于把它教好的教师,"她说,"它就不会像你期望的那样有效。

passage.label: J

sentences.text: Some teachers are finding ways to expose students to Asian-American issues — if not during school hours, then outside of them.
This summer, Wilson Wong will lead a class of rising fifth-graders at a day camp dedicated to Chinese culture and the Chinese-American community in Oakland, California.

His students, for instance, will learn about how Chinese immigrants built the railroads in California, and even have a chance to "experience" it themselves: They will race each other to build a railroad model on the playground, with some students being forced to "work" longer and faster and at cheaper wages.

Wong, a middle school teacher during the school year, hopes he's exposing the students to how Chinese Americans contributed to the U.S., something that he didn't get as a student growing up in the San Francisco Bay Area.
"I planted the seeds early," he says.
"That's what I'm hoping for."

passage.translation: 一些教师正在寻找方法让学生接触亚裔美国人议题——如果不是在上课时间,那就在课外。今年夏天,Wilson Wong将在加利福尼亚州奥克兰一个致力于中国文化和华裔美国人社区的日间夏令营中带领一个即将升入五年级的班级。例如,他的学生将了解中国移民如何在加利福尼亚修建铁路,甚至有机会亲自"体验"它:他们将互相竞赛在操场上建造一个铁路模型,一些学生被迫以更长时间、更快速度和更低工资"工作"。Wong在学年期间是一名中学教师,他希望自己能让学生了解华裔美国人如何为美国做出贡献,这是他在旧金山湾区长大时作为学生没有获得的东西。"我早早地播下了种子,"他说。"这就是我所期望的。

passage.label: K

sentences.text: And, despite setbacks, the tide may finally be turning.
California legislators passed a bill last year that will bring ethnic studies to all its public high schools.
Some school districts, including San Francisco and Los Angeles, already offer ethnic studies at their high schools.
High schools in Portland, Chicago, and elsewhere have either implemented or will soon introduce ethnic studies classes.
And, as more high schools begin teaching it, the door could crack open for middle schools, and, perhaps inevitably, elementary schools, to incorporate a truly more multicultural curriculum.
Doing so will send an important message to the nation's youngest citizens: Whatever your race or ethnicity, you matter.
Your history matters.
Your story matters.

passage.translation: 而且,尽管遭遇挫折,局面可能终于要扭转了。加利福尼亚州立法者去年通过了一项法案,将在所有公立高中引入族裔研究。包括旧金山和洛杉矶在内的一些学区已经在其高中开设了族裔研究课程。波特兰、芝加哥和其他地方的高中要么已经实施,要么即将引入族裔研究课程。而且,随着越来越多的高中开始教授它,这扇门可能会为初中、也许不可避免地为小学打开一道缝,以纳入一个真正更加多元文化的课程。这样做将向国家最年轻的公民传递一个重要信息:无论你的种族或族裔如何,你都很重要。你的历史很重要。你的故事很重要。

groups.instructions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

**改写** more and more high schools in America are including ethnic studies in their curriculums ↔High schools in Portland, Chicago, and elsewhere have either implemented or will soon introduce ethnic studies classes列举上位为趋势including ethnic studies in their curriculums ↔ offer ethnic studies at their high schools include=offer的同义改写
